The Juneli bar is fantastic as was the indian restaurant (you must eat there at least once as the food is fabulous as is the service and live classical indian music)Service is top notch and you are made to feel special by all staff.My only complaint is that some of the staff are a little in your face in terms of expecting tips,  particularly the army of bell boys carrying your luggage. A little subtlety here would go a long way as it kind of spoils the experience when leaving. I prefer to make the choice of tipping myself and it not to appear compulsory! Management and front desk are exemplary though. Highly recommended to the non budget concious traveller.Club rooms were the best in my opinion as they have a lovely seatef large bay window.Wifi great and complimentary use of computers in the "business room" in lobby. Check there are no weddings booked before staying as they can be noisy if you want some peace during your stay.

Its smack on Durbar Marg where all the high endish shops are. You would have KFC and Pizza hut just outside the hotel. There are also several smaller eateries but this street is not for eating - its shopping branded stuff. Round the corner (10min walk is Thamel) There is also the Palace which is the end of Durbar Marg - (3 min walk)Rooms are sufficient - a bit old but ok. The lifts have copper doors and looks like it was done up in the 70's. Service was ok.I would rate this as a great business hotel.

Location of the hotel is very good. Darbar marg has all branded showrooms and restaurants. The hotel is old but nice. While check in one need to specify if smoking room is required. There are very few smoking rooms available and all are in ground floor only. Smoking rooms have disadvantage of not having floor carpets though tariff is same for all rooms. Hence if you opt for smoking rooms, you compromise with the quality of room. Else food and service is good. The palace is very nearby.

It is an old hotel room size is decent and rooms are comfortable too, bed comfort is great but beware of staff they stole one of my perfumes so lock everything when you leave the room. It is a decent hotel and can improve on its cleanliness. Has an casino so has its advantages. Best part of the hotel is its location right Darbar Marg in the heart of the city.

We stayed here twice - and the second time was more like a 5-star experience. Food in the Chinese restaurant was good and so was the coffee (although the menu in the Coffee House only mentioned cold coffee they do it hot as well!). Hot water in most hotels in Nepal appears to be rationed so that is worth checking at check-in time. We had a room with a view (and a window seat) the second time (also worth asking for!). In both stays the staff were great - and the beds comfortable.

Have been to this hotel, 20 years back. Came now, and expected it to have blossomed on its reputation. But no. The rooms were quite small. Had a fantastic lunch in the banquet. The best part about the hotel is the location, on Durbar Marg. The entire business district is only minutes walk away. We were committed breakfast sharp at 6.30, but unfortunately, that wasnt the case. Fine a small blip. Overall, leaves a lot to improve. Rooms did not have free Wifi. Only the reception lobby area had.

Best thing about this hotel is the location. Located on d lively Darbar marg and close to Thamel. Though the prices of this hotel are of 5 star, it is not worthy in terms of infra, service, food.Food: In room dining does not have much option for a vegetarian. Taste wise is also average and nothin great. Breakfast bufdet is also not amusing.Laundry: Laundry like any other hotel of this category is highly priced but quality and service is good.Wifi: Wifi is free and reliable with good speed.Room: Infra of room is average. Maintenance seems to be poor. Big problem is noise from corridor and other rooms like the bell of next room is so clearly heard that it seems it is our and we tend to check.Housekeeping: It is good but depends on d floor you stay.

Staying in the hotel is completely a waste of money..Service at the Coffee Shop is TERRIBLE...First of all, the restaurant is poorly manned..You need to ask for the cutlery individually every time  (knife, fork, spoon). They wont place it on their own.. It looks like they are not aware of the process to be followed to prepare the table for the guest...But they have been taught few very good things - If a guest is carrying an apple with him when he is in a hurry, they will tell him that carrying fruit is not allowed... I have been to so many hotels across the world but have not found a hotel where guests are not allowed to carry an apple with them after breakfast...Then adding to the misery is the room service where people don't understand what you are asking for.. Basic item like bournvita milk (part of menu) was not available in the hotel for four continuous days and they claim that they are the best destination in kathmandu...Apart from the location and infrastructure, the hotel does not have anything else for which a person can think of staying in this hotel...

I've stayed at Annapurna recently for 2 nights - the location is convenient and not too far from the Airport and the hotel offers a shuttle service as well . Although its one of the oldest hotels in KTM, the Rooms are now renovated and comfortable. They could do well to make it a little more functional for a business traveler with a convenient working desk and comfortable chair . The coffee shop is located in another building in the same vicinity and offers a fairly good buffet breakfast . The staff are very helpful .

Stayed for 4 nights.  Centrally located and within walking distance of Thamel.Quiet location, nice pool and very accommodating staff.  Helpful and friendly.Gym was a bit disappointing - one treadmill meant there was a wait in the mornings.I also struggled to turn off the air condioner in the room each night...despite many attempts, which meant it stayed on all night - a bit noisy in the room as a result.Overall, pleased with the stay.

I have been to many hotels around the globe and this year as a tour leader of a bunch of people we had been to Nepal for trekking and to see wonderful Mountains as we have Alps in Europe which has much more less altitude than mountains.Arriving in Nepal we were taken to this wonderful property in Kathmandu which is located in the metropolitan area. Upon entering the hotel  lobby i found the lobby huge comparing most of the ironic hotels in Europe. Upon Checking in i was told the hotel was built long time ago and for me everything looks so well Managed from the lobby elevator to the swimming pool and more especially the hotel Sauna section. While taking a tour of the property i was told Sauna was the  newly added amenities in the hotel which looked fresh and made me feel relaxed  using after my busy schedule. Moreover I would also suggest if they could open a spa in the hotel because people would use for it while they come after trekking as they will be super tired.  The food was great and the service was excellent. I make sure i will be visiting this property again next year with my people.

I stayed at the Annapurna hotel twice. The location is prime. All staff are friendly and nice. But I interacted with Shanti, Sumin and Rebika the most and they were exceptionally professional and friendly. My only comment would be on the airport shuttle service. While complimentary, the drivers try to pick up all  guests in one go.  After being on road for 25 hours, waiting another hour outside the airport is too much. When I informed the pick up person that I am going to take a taxi, he instructed the driver to leave with me only. However, after leaving the airport premises, the driver returned to pick up another guest. It was annoying.

I enjoyed staying in hotel Annapurna very much. The staff are very polite and courteous.The size of the room is immense.The pool next to the bar looks awesome and it even feels good to swim during the afternoon while the climate is hot. The service is excellent. Since the location of the hotel is supremely prime to where I need to go and the staff service being so prompt I have no reason behind choosing Annapurna over other hotels.In short it was home away from home experience for me.

Have looked at the Annapurna several times while visiting KTM in the past because it has a very central location, but have always stayed elsewhere because it looks old. On this trip stayed here for almost a week because I wanted the location. The hotel does desperately need refreshing in the rooms and public spaces - bathrooms with old and cracked fixtures, carpets rather threadbare, just all around tired. If you do stay, ask for a room on the back side, the courtyard rooms that face the pool also face the outdoor party area and can be quite noisy.Only tried the breakfast restaurant, a very limited buffet breakfast selection and other than the usual egg station the selection was very basic, rather plain, and oriented to Asian tastes. This cafe also opens up for dinner and dessert (cake selection looked quite good) and wanted to try it but during my stay it closed up at about 9PM so didn’t get the chance. I wanted to try the main restaurant for dinner but on that night there was live music at such a volume I left the hotel.The bright spot was the staff. All were extremely friendly and helpful in everything from getting a room changed, to front door greetings by the security staff, to management asking if I needed anything. Highest compliments on staff selection!I hope the hotel tries to upscale, at present it’s a 3 star at best and while I want to stay here because it’s local, I wouldn’t unless it renovates; I don’t think it’s as good overall as the nearby Yak and Yeti (which also needs a bit of work in the rooms). While the Annapurna has a great location, is a local small chain worth patronizing and is a historical building it needs be significantly upgraded. If it doesn’t, the upcoming openings of other new large hotels in the area will swallow it up.
６月４日～５日に宿泊しました。正直、古い感じが印象的でした。昔は、カトマンズを代表するホテルだったと思わせるような作りですが、好きな人は好きかもしれません。部屋もやはり古い感じでした。朝食はメニューが豊富でしたが、正直、味は・・・。

I am compelled (!) to stay here. I love this place for many reasons; the most important being the staff. You like to be received by the greetings " Welcome back, sir!, right from the airport, from the reception and from the coffee shop and even at the restaurants.The room service is always with a smile. No need to experiment with newer options when you are happy staying at the same place time and again.

Hotel Annapurna is 50 years old providing services to make sure we have a stay to remember. Rooms are old. Good service and good food. The hotel is in the heart of the city. Located minutes away from both breathtaking heritage sites and many of the diplomatic and business districts. Stayed there twice.

Excellent location in the centre of the city . Good access to the key locations , very good service , front office , but rooms are old and need to be upgraded. Else the property is very popular for events

Me and my husband had our wedding reception there. We stayed there for a night after the event in one of their club rooms which was amazing. After the big event we were pretty tired and the room was a treat. Very comfortable and cosy. The next day we had a lovely breakfast, we could have had on our club room floor which was pretty cool but we decided to join our families (who also stayed there that night) in their restaurant.They had nicely decorated the wedding reception hall and the food very good. The location is the best as you can go to the night clubs and markets very easy. Our family and friends who had traveled from overseas had really good time and we were very happy with how our special day. went

Gut gelegenes ehemaliges Luxushotel im Zentrum Kathmandus. Die 5 Sterne entsprechen schon lange nicht mehr, bei uns wären es höchstens 3 Sterne. Großes Haus mit entsprechendem sehr freundlichem Personal. Die Zimmer nicht sauber, aber für nepalesische Verhältnisse akzeptabel. Frühstück asiatisch orientiert. Sehr gutes indisches Restaurant mit gehobenen Preisen.

When in Kathmandu, always at Hotel Annarpurna! You would never repent for staying at this hotel. Centrally located, well appointed bedroom and just above average bath rooms. ( They need to be refurbished). Breakfast is lavish and well spread. The most outstanding feature of the hotel is its staff. Very friendly, helpful and ever smiling.

This is one of the best hotels in Kathmandu, Nepal. So beautiful and well maintained. Swimming pool adds to it's beauty. Fully wifi enabled. Food is super tasty. Shopping can be done with the premises. Staff is well trained and well behaved as well. Spa is a plus point.

Even-though its an old property, the hotel is well maintained. stayed there for 3 nights. The food was good, rooms were neat and clean. The bathroom can be made much more cleaner. The location of the Hotel is perfect.

Hotel is in a great location. Near all shops and restaurants The room were fine nothing fancy. The bed was really bad... i had a sore back after staying there  The breakfast food was alright. It is a bit old would need some improvements.

We just came back from a short vacation in Kathmandu and we stayed at the Annapurna for a total of 4 nights. Although the hotel and rooms looks and feels old, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay. Very friendly service and the food at the Coffee Shop as well as the food in the Indian restaurant were excellent. Great breakfast buffet. Walking distance to Thamel street. Huge temperature controlled pool. The best thing was that they set up a gourmet dinner by the pool side late night, say 12AM for the 8 of us which was a wonderful experience. By the way the restaurants serves Halal food. Will definitely recommend this hotel to my friends...

Great location in Kathmandu. The staff is super friendly and helpful. The rooms are a bit run down and needs to be renovated. That being said, I do have a huge complaint: they charge 15$ per day for Internet. For god sake, we are in 2017 and all hotels of this standard (and these room prices) have to have Internet included in the rooms. In addition, they issue coupons with codes that stop working and you have to call the receptions 2-3 times a day for new codes. Such a hassle!! Unless they fix this, I will definitely stay somewhere else next time I'm in KTM.

i was told that this is one of the best hotel in Nepal ! Location is superb ! Rooms are good and you can have comfortable stay ! But food is not at all worth in terms of the price they charge ! Buffet breakfast is just in name of options you have ! Needs lots of improvement ! One thing i would like to mention is that though rooms are available ..but the front desk will try to give you the costly rooms with an excuse that rooms are not available ! This is what is not expected from them !

We were made very welcome here at the Annapurna Hotel from the Director Mr. Rana and all his staff. Santi, the reception trainee, was such a joy she always had a lovely smile and shared kind words.The rooms were fine even though they are a little "tired!" We slept well! Buffet breakfast was a real treat in the coffee shop with a large selection of all types of cuisine and we combined leisurely breakfasts and our local meetings. The hotel is within walking distance to Thamel (main city and shopping area) and yet quiet as it is set back from the road and in a garden setting. There is a big pool, bar and choice of Indian or Chinese restaurants. All in all a very pleasant stay! We met up with some Rotarians as this is "home" to one of their chapters.

I was there with my family and stayed at room might be it was their deluxe or normal one.All total 3 rooms, rooms were not to the standard.This was our second visit to kathmandu.Firstly we stayed at radission atleast the room was moderate and cozy but then we changed our plan to stay in diffrent hotel but room was in worst condition more than the room the staff at front desk Ms. Dibya was so rude and not welcoming might be she was incharge on the shift.she messed our problem like the hell. Rather than her receptionist were far better and Ms. Dibya was screaming to her subordinates junior.how can the the management give such customer care responsibility to non efficient and non proffesional staff.save the hotel- Management Team.would not recommend to any one who are looking for hospitality.

We had taken two deluxe rooms..very spacious and well appointed.Hotel is very centrally located and has good service.....the food fell short of our expectations.Otherwise a lovely stay amidst very friendly staff

The reception is handled by couple of young girls who are smart and do a good job. Among them is Shristi, who is great at her job!Then the rooms: comfortable, LCD TVs, toilet amenities, central ACThe swimming pool is large but mostly is utilised due to the weather. Maybe summer months see more swimmers. Good coffee tables laid near the pool.Two restaurants: Indian and Chinese. Both serve fantastic food.Business centre on the first floor serves all the work related issues.Ample parking. Complimentary airport pick and drop on their Toyota vans.The breakfast is from 7-10 am at the Coffee shop. The buffet is one area which they need to improve as options are pretty much limited.The room service is prompt. In room dining is good.Wi-Fi speed is slow, they provide only 328 Kbps speed, which somehow manages to pull data.Overall one of the best hotels in Kathmandu. The staff are extremely warm and courteous. Being located on Darbar Marg makes this hotel easily accessible to the shopping area outside!Nice! Recommend to stay!

Hotel is very good. Ambience is Excellent.Food is also good. Staff is very much courteous.Cleanliness. Hotel is located in heart of city. Rooms are spacious and beautifully decorated. Overall its value for money.

since long time (more than 40 years) I was a regular guest two time in the year at thishotel. Every friendly, like home far from your home. I was there on november from 2 to5 and the people was the same, kind, attentive, <this also after the strong hearthquake that was in Kathmandu on april.. the confort was the same and all the people from thebell captain to the general manager work for your confort and very happy to see meagain. a very good experience because at same level that before tragedy of NepalThank you to all this people.

This is a review for The Coffee Shop rather than Hotel Annapurna itself. I love the Coffee Shop! Try the Pork Chops, they are delightful! The staff here is really courteous.  I love the ambiance at The Coffee Shop, it's just realaxing.

This is one of those grand old places in the 3rd world that was the best available at the time it was built but is in a controlled state of decline.  It's nothing that would keep you from staying there, and it's a great place to base yourself in Katmandu, but this is no 5-star place either.  The rooms are sort of clean, the beds are firm and comfortable, the shower works, there's a safe in each room, all the stuff you would expect.  But if this hotel were in New York or London, it would have been renovated 20 years ago or relegated to the world of hotels that were once great and aren't anymore.  The carpet is old and in need of replacement, the bathroom is functional but quite tired, the cabinets are missing hardware and the drapery and fixtures are vintage.  The breakfast buffet is excellent and the hotel staff are pretty good, although there is that sort of "I'll get to you when I get to you" attitude at the front desk sometimes.  The WiFi is slow, but it works.   All in all, when you consider the central location and the fact that most everything in Katmandu is slowly falling apart, they do a good job of keeping this place going.

very nice hotel, very friendly staff....   this is kathmandu, so you cant compare it to western hotels of similar rating  ...  but i enjoyed my visit very much ...Jumeni Bar feels like a bit of a throwback, but great place for an end of day whiskey

Staying here for 4 days 3 night at room 1022 and experience my first earthquake of 3.6 here. PhewEverything is okay with good services and large swimming pool (It raining and i did not use the pool) and a gym. Room is little worn out but still comfortable. There is plenty of tv channe to choose from. WIfi is acceptable but it only limited to 2 devices. Buffet breakfast is alright. Staff is friendly and very helpful.It is Nepal, so be prepare for frequent power cut but it restore quickly by their generator. There is quite number of restaurant nearby and MAS office is just across the street. Would I stay here again? unlikely as for this price i could get something more better around Thamel area. It a long walk if you want to go to the hustling and bustling area of Thamel

I often stay in this hotel when I have to attend conferences. For Nepalese they tend to give old heritage room, not very clean and lots of dead insects on bathtubs. After earthquake rooms and lobby are now fully renovated and safe to stay. Indian food is excellent and staff are very hospitable with complementary airport drop and pick up service. BF is good and free Wifi. The place near to Thamel for hangouts.

Hotel is a little old but in a warm, comfortable way like an old arm chair - but it could still do with a proper upgrade to the rooms.  Staff friendly and very helpful. Location is convenient and with all the daily challenges they must be facing the standards are pretty good.Breakfast in a separate building is average and with restaurants within walking distance I didn't try any other meals at the hotel.  Bedroom walls are quite thin so you get that 'stereo TV' effect from next doors television.  There are regular power cuts at night and early in the morning, and the emergency lighting comes on in the entranceway to your room each time the power goes off - so expect to be woken several times a night by the lights and the clunking from the old ac system.WIFI is slow - but the fact that it works at all is a bonus.Kathmandu restaurants are famous for adding extra items to your bill - but I didn't expect this at the hotel and just realized in time that the food bill and car hire were not mine.

We rather like best and comfortable beds are in the hotel.The garden face room and wall painting by arts are great.No doubt about best breakfast ever I had.If, you are thinking to travel in Nepal, try your best, it is best location in center point of tourist area of Kathmandu, Nepal.

after the terrible earthquake in Nepal (Kathmandu) it was such a reassuring place to be. you could feel safe and life seemed 'normal'. the staff were just excellent - friendly and helpful - the rooms were great - and the service all up was just 'first class' considering what was going on in the real world outside the hotel. I can recommend this hotel to anyone at anytime.  has a great pool too which I did not use.

Kind of boutique hotel in an old building with an Annex newly built block. Restaurant serves mixed Nepalis and Indian cuisine with live music. Breakfast is good and served in a hall from where you can watch the morning rush of the city. There is a small Casino in the campus, and several small restaurants and cafes outside, including Pizza Hut at walking distance.

We stayed at our " second home " in Kathmandu for two weeks just before the earthquake in April.As always they took such very good care of us!!!! We have stayed there for many years now, and its always so nice to meet everybody again, so many smiles, so much wamth and hospitality from everyone working there!!!We left Nepal on the evening before the first earthquake so we were very lucky, but our thoughts are very much with all the wonderful people in Nepal...I have been following the news and updates from Annapurna -  and they are as usual, taking responsibility, taking care of both their own, their guests and people in the community at such a difficult time!!Once again thankyou so much to this hotel and its staff with so much heart!!

This is an unexceptional hotel with an unwarranted pretension to be a 5-star property. My bed mattress was sagging at the edges (probably because of age or bad manufacture) and I had to insert a pillow below it level it off, and then managed to sleep.For WiFi in the room they wanted an additional $ 12. When I protested they gave me a user name and password but it did not work anyway as the signal in the room was too weak and sporadic. A local beer that can be purchased for $ 1.25 is billed at an astounding $ 11 in the coffee shop. Regular guests are directed to the coffee shop for meals which are limited in taste and range. But not so the price.When I asked the manager about their London-level prices he huffily said that their policy was appropriate for an international-level hotel. Well, actually their hotel would surpass a Best Western in America and has the same bland lack of character that characterizes middling chain hotels.For the same price or a little more you can find hotels with more character and class in Kathmandu -- for example the Yak & Yeti, an excellently managed property.

the hotel is right at darbar marg ( palace road ) very close to thamel area... nice property... good food and crowd.. but the rooms were very small, had to ask for a paid upgrade... also they must change the pillows... rest was ok! slightly high on room tariff... food was great and cheap!

Made a mistake, so I just stayed on for 8 days. I was staying in Everest for 10 days, the problem there was Wi-Fi problem & its chargeable.So I checked into Annapurna as a walk in customer, the very first day I encountered that there was no hot shower they only have semi warm it was very a very cold day, so I made a complain ,they technician came  checked with a gadget & arranged to changed my room, the manager told me it was the boiler issue which they had just changed,looks like every room was like that. Tired of moving around & stacked with it for the next 8 days. If you need hot shower take a shower either between the time 5pm to 7 pm or at 2 am to 6 am.

A very nice hotel , I alway stay here when I in Kathmandu. Nice warm welcome every time I visit , staff is very friendly and helpful . Good Indian food , not very expensive. Just in the centre of the city

I stayed last month in this hotel with my friends and  I must say the hotel was very comfortable, had a Pleasant stay. This hotel is a great experience to Explore. Very nice people and nice food. I would like to thank annapurna team for the valuable experience. Well done Annapurna Team, You have done a great job.

I have had a special relationship with the Staff at the Hotel del Annapurna for many years, this year I met two new staff members with whom I instantly connected ...  Mrs Dybya Pau and the Matre de, Mr Shiva. Because I am an elderly woman, Dybya visited me regularly through my day to see if my needs were being met as did Mr Muni Rana. As I was travelling alone, Mr Shiva, took my order for breakfast and brought it to me. The young gardener, on my way back from breakfast, always had a rose for me. Because of my friendly, patient nature, I attract wonderful people, and have always done so. Nikhibhatia 8, needs to stay home so that they can eat the breakfast they are used to. The two weeks I was there, there was nothing wrong with the temperature of my breakfast. On my first visit 40yrs ago, I stayed in probably a 15American dollars a night room, with a single bed that had a very thin mattress; so I asked staff to go and buy me  another one ... no big deal , Iit was so cheap and was kept for me for the next seven or eight years ... cant remember. People usually travel to experience a 'difference' than the life they live. If they want it to be the same,with hot water that runs exactly when they want it to, then don't go to my beloved Kathmundhu.Go to Singapore. For instance, Bacon will never be the same as it is at home: I don't order bacon. All Nikhi b had to do was enquire to the Maitre de was your favourite breakfast available from the Al la Carte Menue. I found Management, very co-operative with my needs. Wander the streets/other hotels for breakfast.! You wouldn't be on a budget staying at the Annapurna. I am an Australian and bobsmith 198 sounds like he is too. We don't winge when we travel to Third World countries desperately doing their best for their guest, and everyone is just so WILLING. YOU CANT BUY WILLINGNESS, it comes from the heart and is reflected in your eyes. The Nepalese people have to be amongst  the most friendly, willing and lovable peoples in the World ... Namaste and many Tashi da leks dear people of Nepal. Patricia giudice.

We stayed there for 3 nights in December. Overall the hotel rooms are pretty old and the tariffs on a higher side. Also, the hotel seriously needs to do something with their coffees shop food especially the breakfast, which served dishes almost cold and the same ones on all 3 days.The only good part is the location which is the best in Kathmandu and also the room sizes which are pretty generous.

We traveled to Nepal in Oct/Nov and stayed here 3 times over our visit.It was in a great location near the Thamel area, the hotel itself was clean, the staff were very friendly and helpful, we ate in all the restaurants and while they are more expensive than going out the food was great and we couldn't fault the service. The pool area was a nice place to sit and relax after the noise and traffic out in the street.Overall its a good place to stay, we would definitley stay here again if in Kathmandu.

It is not the small room which needs an update, but the other facilities who makes it  a good place to stay for a couple of nights. Real international breakfast and  different restaurants.Many function rooms, for weddings and parties. And then you see the glittering dressed ladies in there sari's and jewelery. A lust for the eyes. Thamel and Durbarplace are in walking distance, with all shopping and restaurant facilities. The staff was very nice and helpful and we do not regret our 3 night stay.

This hotel is one of the oldest "grand" hotels in town. It would need an uplift. Most of the infrastructure looks tired. Rooms below club category are perhaps not to be considered. Walls are thin and you hear neighbors noises. The plumbing could use some new pipes, too, my water came out yellowish most of the time. On the plus side there's a good Indian restaurant. All in all a rather charming old hotel with lots of things to fix - so don't expect a five star.

We stayed here for 3 nights in total and we're very disappointed upon being shown to our room. Very basic and bland decor and very small room.  We informed reception immediately of our disappointment and the staff were very amiable in trying to make us happy. We were straight away escorted to a room on a higher floor which was much better in size and with a large bed rather than 2 singles.  The bed was lovely and comfortable with a view over the pool. The bathroom was still poor in my opinion... smelly and the water here is brown....very off putting so I didn't shower or bathe once on my stay!! The staff are lovely though :)

We arrived at night and left int he morning, but our stay here was very nice. We were on the "Club Floor" and had a private check-in. The room was nice and spacious and comfortable. It was after 10 PM and we were hungry. The Coffee Shop (part of the hotel but you have to exit to get there) was open thankfully, and we had a nice meal. There seemed to bo some other nice dining options had we arrived earlier.The breakfast buffet was very nice and the staff all around was helpful. Although I saw free WiFi advertised, I was told at breakfast that I could not get the password because it "wasn't included in my package."Otherwise, ad very comfortable stay.

Fairly modern, comfortable, yet unremarkable hotel in Central KTM near the old palace. Clean and efficient service, with good buffet breakfast served in an adjacent building. Room was comfortable, if a little tired, however spoiled by view of plant equipment and wires immediately outside. Good sized outside swimming pool was well maintained, with towels supplied. Good value for money.

I visited Kathmandu, Nepal, recently and checked in at Annapurna. The hotel has this really relaxing and casual aura about it, which can be felt as soon as one enters the lounge. The staff is very friendly and helpful and go out of their way to assist customers, they feel happy doing this, and one can sense this instantaneously. The hotel has an Indian restaurant (Ghar - e - Kabab), a Chinese restaurant (Arniko Room), Juneli Bar, a cake shop and a coffee shop. We tried some of the pastries and desserts from their cake shop, and they were yummy!. The Juneli bar is next to their swimming pool (which is pretty big) and one can spend leisurely evenings with drinks and snacks, enjoying the ambiance and the outdoors as well!. There is also a casino within the hotel which is an added pleasure for all of us who like to gamble, just for fun. Unfortunately was closed owing to some tax issues (this was the case with all casinos in Kathmandu), but they would open soon, we were told.We were staying in their club room with a lovely cocktail evening, with wines, cocktails and lots of mouth-watering, delightful and titillating snacks, all part of the awesome package!. The staff took care of all our needs courteously and graciously and chatted around with us amicably. Since this was our first visit to Nepal, during Dussehra (everything was closed), the front office staff took the bother to chart out a rough schedule for our sightseeing and booked transfers for our sightseeing, which made things easier for us. All in all, we had a lovely time, and although we will not visit Nepal again (cause we have seen more or less all there is to see), our experience in the hotel is one we will cherish and remember and I would personally recommend this hotel to anyone thinking of traveling to Kathmandu, for business or for leisure.

We had a deluxe room with breakfast. Free reliable wifi, swimming pool, small gym, three restaurants (Chinese, Indian and a general one), KFC and Pizza Hut just outside hotel. Pleasant helpful staff. All in all a good hotel. Not 5 star by western standards but we were happy to be here. New carpets comfortable bed, clean though furnishings a bit tired. A nice reception area.15 minute walk to Thamel. Note Airport is pretty chaotic. You need you baggage tracking label to get through customs as they check it against the bag you have picked up. Worth getting a visa in advance as the queue was about 200 people long and we were able to walk straight through. Outside airport where drivers and hotels collect people is chaos too and policemen move you along whilst you are searching for your ride. As is to be expected roads are very potholed and pedestrians need to beware of cars rickshaws and motorcycles.

I stayed in Annapurna in February 2014... It was a memorable experience.The building is old, but they have renovated it and hence the rooms and the lobby area are very good.Heaters is a must when you visit Kathmandu almost all round the year... and this hotel provides good heating....The restaurants are awesome, especially the Chinese restaurant... great quality food.The hotel is centrally located and is just 30mins drive from the airport...Its a little expensive.. but worth the money you pay...There is a travel desk who offer you cabs to go around... If you are visiting Kathmandu... there are many places to see... but for sure dont miss the early morning Mountain Flight.. which takes you over the Himalayas and gives you a distant view of Mt Everest...

We have stay several days in that hotel. Great location, in a new area pleanty of new shops anb modern cafes and restaurants (very good theRest. mezze at a penthouse amb with and excellent terrace).Rooms are big. Very clean and with all you need as a traveller. Breakfast is full of diferent options and everything is very good. Also, they may offer you a breakbast bag if you need it or even a breakfast at your room.It also has two special restaurants. One indian and the other chinesse. Both very confortable. There's a good bar were they serve spirits and wines. Very confortable.It's just 5 minutes walking from Thamel neigbourhood.

This is a very centrally located hotel, was really easy to get about, atms resturants,  KFC, coffee everything is just outside the hotel.The Chinese resturant here is to die for, amazing food and great staff. Indian was good as well (different resturant) but I loved the Chinese and so did the family. The outside cafe / resturant which was part of the hotel was great as well.Rooms a nice and spacious, slightly older hotel but well maintained.The hotel staff were just amazing and helpful. Really had a good stay here. Great hotel to start our vacation.

Fantástico establecimiento con personal amable y comida espectacular. Dispone de distintos ambientes para disfrutar y descansar. Terraza y piscina formidable Totalmente recomendable y para volver,  siempre

One of the best Chinese Restaurants in Nepal....Never miss out to try their Chillie Garlic Prawn.....I am fan of it...Visited around 5 times bec of their food....Chef visits your table to understand more of what you like provided you a regular there...

The property is very spacious and it is in main area of Kathmandu and it's safe for family  good rooms are good staff is friendly they serve good breakfast and they have 3-4 restraunt in propety so u don't need to go out for meals you have all in-house they serve excellent cakes in cake shop if u visit this proper and don't have cakes there then it's not worth visiting you must try their cakes

The staff at this hotel is simply one best I've ever seen. I stayed here for 10 days with my family while I was getting married. The gym and amenities needs remodeling but the service of the staff and location makes up for it. As a hotelier, I sincerely thank you for your amazing service.

Homely crew ready to serve you whenever you ask. Good restaurants and coffee shop, Traditional Nepali food also available.The Hotel has its own Casino, frequented mostly by Indian gamblers. In the category of 4 Stars, it has best location in Kathmandu.

We had been to  Nepal for the first time along with my Husband. The time we landed in Nepal we  were taken to this fantastic property. The hotel was in super Rush as we had to wait for some time to get a room. The room that was given to us was not up to the Mark. I along with my husband went down to speak with the Manager on Duty in the Evening( Forgot his name). He calmed us down and told us that the hotel was fully occupied and will make sure he will provide us a good room during our second visit which he did. We also dined in the Chinese Restaurant during our second visit and i found the food is relatively better than what they serve in the Main restaurant which is located outside from the Reception. We were thrilled with the experience we got from the hotel. See you soon next year hopefully.

The staff was so accommodating and gracious to my family and friends in a resort style environment. The breakfasts and lunches with such a variety of flavors quickly became our favorite meeting spot. I've traveled since to big name hotels and none come close to the delicious culinary delights of Hotel Annapurna in Kathmandu. Thank you. We look forward to visiting again next year.

..This is the first time I come to Nepal.and I stayed at annapurna hotel and I feel this hotel has all the facilities you need.When I staying here, I feel safe and comfort ,everyone will take good care of you as you were a relative member of the family ,from the first moment you entered the hotel all staff team here is a professional,In the hotel you will have a swimming pools, gym, spa and many more ,that you can spend the vacation time here as long as you want.I feel the love in this hotel ,thank you very much to all staff and friends,thank you to Mr.Samir Chand, Mr.Rochan, Miss Rojina , Rebika, Buagyashere ,Mr.Tau Prasad Gurung and all Annapurna Team that I met ,you are a wonderful team ever ,Thank you very much for your hospitality ,I wish to see you all again ... with love... Thann :)

I stayed in this hotel for 2 nights in the month of August. This was my 2nd visit to Nepal and my first visit to Hotel Annapurna. The hotel is in the heart of the city and that is the best advantage, just minutes away from both heritage sites, walking distance from casino and and right in middle of market.My first impression was that its an old hotel with old design. The basic rooms are very small in size, but if you upgrade you will get a better size room. The staff were extremely friendly and helpful in everything from getting a room changed, to front door greetings by the security staff, to management.A good hotel with very good staff to make your stay comfortable.

I have stayed at this hotel more than once only because of its location. On my previous visits I have ignored the out dated rooms, the rock solid mattresses, the flat and lifeless pillows, the small bugs that seem to have a permanent residence in the rooms. I even ignored the smell of smoke/mold/ddt that seems to permeate throughout the rooms and the hotel, and the wall thumping music that is often played but I cannot ignore rude and hostile staff. The service staff at the front counter are beyond reproach, they blatantly ignore your inclusions and “gang up” when you try to point out what you’ve already paid for. Also, they seem to have only two taxis they will allow to operate from inside and they will charge you extreme amounts and one of them has no idea where he is going most of the time. I will never stay here again and I recommend that if you want a friendly and welcoming experience then choose somewhere else.

The staff were very friendly and we didn't have any problems checking in. The pool area was also nice and location good. The room itself was okay, but the toilet a little bit dirty and old. The hotel would need to be renovated.

This has to be without doubt my worst ever hotel stay. It is classed as a 5 star hotel but that is a complete misrepresentation. My deluxe room was outdated and dingy. I went to the bar for a drink which with service is very overpriced. Whilst sitting on the sofa and to my horror a rat ran between my feet. I quickly moved to the main bar whilst the manager chased the rat outside. Just 10 minutes later two more rats appeared and casually ran throughout the bar. Needless to say this has serious health issues especially when uncovered peanuts are left on the bar and given to guests. I immediately complained to the manager who apologised. However at checkout there was now no record of my complaint and i was told the only compensation available was a free breakfast! I am now trying to find out how to make an official complaint and to inform their health department as I have real concerns about this. If you do stay here perhaps avoid the bar area!A total disgrace.

This hotel is very conveniently located on the main shopping street of Kathmandu and very good restaurants, cafes and decent bars are just a walk away. It is modern and well maintained.Checking went super-fast. Staff was very efficient but was not at all cheerful. Services delivered, hospitality was missing.I stayed at a Club Room that fell short of general description of suit / club room but was one of the best rooms I ever stayed in Kathmandu. It was spacious enough for a comfortable stay though the bath room is bit smaller. Bed was comfortable, linen was fresh and clean. Centralized air conditioner was bit noisy. I used it on heating mode, which was fine for the prevailing weather. Tea coffee making facility was available and complementary mineral water provided.Bathroom was very clean, all items properly worked. Fresh and clean towels and good quality toiletries provided.I returned from a very long day at work and reached the Indian restaurant around 10.30 p.m. to see the door was closed but live music was still going on. Bar staff was very discourteous and asked me to contact a manager to have some food. (I did not like room services and wanted to dine at a relaxed environment). It took some unpleasant dialogues before food was arranged at a corner of the lobby which I appreciated. Wondering why it was not offered at the beginning.    Breakfast was bit overpriced but was good. Staff at this restaurant were bit more helpful and cheerful. Gentlemen at the egg and waffle station was amazing. Restaurant in-charge offered me fresh pineapple when I told him that bit more variety of fresh fruit would have been nice.Overall, this hotel is among the best in Kathmandu for business and leisure travelers alike.

Gruppenzimmer sind abgewohnt keine 5 Sterne, nach der Ameisenstrasse im Badezimmer wurden wir in den ersten Stock umgezogen. Das Zimmer war deutlich besser. Wunderschön ist die Poolanlage leider ist der Pool ab 1.11 geschlossen.

Stayed here on tour on the way out to hike around Poon Hill. The place is nice don't get me wrong it just doesn't match the photos that you see online or here on TripAdvisor, they have really taken artistic lisence a bit too far. That being said the staff is incredibly friendly and helpful

Have stayed twice in this hotel The last was October 2017. The hotel is around 10 minutes walk to Thamel for your souvenirs hunting and meals. There is a casino about 50 meters walk along the same side of the road from the hotel if you fancy a little wager. The staffs from the front desk to the concierge are very helpful and courteous. As mentioned in some posts, the restaurant on the ground floor serves some delicious North Indian food and the Murg Tandoori chicken and the mutton Rogan Josh with naan bread are my favourite.

Ubicación relativamente buena aunque para ir a cualquiera de los grandes monumentos has de moverte en transporte. Habitaciones tamaño standard con tus botellas de agua, limpio. Buen servicio y atencion por parte de los trabajadores del hotel. El wifi llega bien.

Stayed here for 6 nights for a conference. The place is ok, by and large. The location is great. The age of the place shows in the wear of the smallish rooms, the beds and pillows are lumpy, showers old as well and the mini bar not only empty but out of order as well. Breakfast is not spectacular but edible, and the pool was very nice - overall set-up would have warranted three or even four stars for their attempt at a five-star hotel, considering you’ll be hard pushed to find anything meeting international luxury standards in Kathmandu. What put me off this place however were the repeated mistakes and slips in the service. Before and during organisation of the conference communication was difficult (and often rude) and several mistakes were made with guest pickups, check ins and check outs as well as set-up of the room. The last day of the meeting hotel staff very aggressively told us they expected us to be out of the room at the scheduled end time of the agenda and not a minute later as they had another booking immediately after. After the conference I stayed on and tried to relax which was made difficult; the staff would not respect do not disturb signs on the door, and there were noise disturbances in the middle of the night. The last nail in the coffin was having my sleep interrupted early in the morning of departure with a call from the reception, due to another mix-up. Can’t wait to leave this place.

Stayed in the Club room.Clean comfortable room .Wonderful obliging staff . Buffet breakfast was a good spread but the service was chaotic in the  coffee shop. The club rooms buffet that I  preferred next morning  was simple but the calmer and slow paced environment was a good way to start the day.The  dinner at the Indian restaurant was delicious. The kebabs and entrees were delicios and the service was excellent. The location is great and it is an easy walk to a lot of lovely cafes and restaurants.

We were put up here for 3 nights on full board by our airline after a flight cancellation. My room on the club floor was very comfortable with plenty of amenities : wifi, aircon, room safe, kettle with tea and coffee, iron, good linen and toiletries, comfortable bed and pillows, flat screen tv with English language channels, plenty of sockets for charging. All our meals were buffet style and the choice and quality good. A couple of wedding receptions were held during our stay which added colour to our stay. The Royal Palace is very close. The fitness room needs better aircon as it was very hot in the afternoon and the decent sized pool needs more shade/sun umbrellas.

I stayed at the hotel for 3 weeks on a biz trip in April/May 2018. The hotel is in a great location if you need to have meetings at governments offices. It is also in a fairly good central locations with several restaurants around.Rooms: cleanWIFI: not badOverall accommodation: value for moneyRestaurants at the hotels though are expensive and not great vfm I'm afraid.

This is fantastic place for tourists to stay for luxurious accommodation in the prime location of the Kathmandu city and have a great fun and experiences with very affordable cost.Hey guys just try once to feel the difference.

We stayed in Annapurna many many years ago when I was in college. We decided to stay there again and not much has changed. The rooms here are little small and the decor and fittings are old. But then this is one of the oldest 5 star hotels in Nepal.This is a typical big city hotel, everything is expensive and the staff is very good but they seem a little distracted. The restaurants serve very good food and the service is great too. But the breakfast in the coffee shop is not a good experience. They are way understaffed for dealing with heavy rush during breakfast hours.My kids were a little unwell due to stomach bug and the hotel made arrangement for a doctor to visit, which was very kind of them.Overall its a good place to stay since its location is excellent and the service is also good. Price wise I think its a little over the top for Nepal.

The Annapurna Hotel has at one time been an excellent hotel, however it is showing signs of its age and is in need of some TLC. Having said that  and a very good stay with good food and very good staff. My only real complaint was that the water from the shower and wash basin was initially a delicate shade of brown on every application.

Bodde i samband med trek i Himalaya. Hotellet blir en oas i den oordning som råder i staden, uppskattade läget på en av de finare gatorna med gångavstånd till Thamel.Rymliga och välstädade rum, fantastisk frukost buffé. Det som drar ned betyget något är att vattnet på rummen var lätt gult och att poolen var väl kall.

This property seriously needs renovation. I had some friends staying here and brought me to show their rooms. They call them heritage rooms. Perhaps bad heritage. It's a shame that this such a beautiful property is in such a shame. I was joking people there for lunch and the service and food were both terrible.

The staff here is very rude especially guest manager . They dont know how to talk to their guest , they always ignore you , misbehaves with you . So i wont recommend anybody to this hotel.All they want is to make hole in your pocket and offer you ignorance !

Went there for dinner. The hotel is in a good location but very old and needs a lot of renovation.The food was okay, the ambience and the design need to be changed. Not worthy of being rated a 5 star today.

Hotel:Oldie, But Goldie. It is no modern hotel. But is has style.CEO (of 3 hotels) Mr. Raju Bikram Shah is very friendly and customer oriented. So, all the staff is very friendly too. High level of customer care!!! Starting with security guides and cleaning staff until high educated service staff (e.g. in the Indian Restaurant). This is for me a sign of great leadership. Chapeau!!!Food: Several good restaurants (Indian = very good; Coffe Shop = good; Chinese Restaurant = quite good); Bar:nice bar with great outdoor (pool area) tables, too; drinks & beverages are quite expensive for Nepal;

This was my second stay at this hotel. This hotel has the unique advantage of being centrally located on Durbar Marg. It was by business trip and all my visiting place were located close to the hotel.Every experience of my stay was memorable from the moment I requested for reservation thru the web, the response was prompt. A separate car was waiting at the airport for pick up and check-in was very smooth. The ladies are all very well trained and beautifully dressed.House keeping was more than my expectation, particularly the evening help.The USP of this hotel (apart from very good staff always willing to do a bit extra) is the food. I got my favorite food every time I asked for (Thanks chief chef-Mr. Aga)On the whole perfect place to be called home away from home.

Hotel Annapurna is in Kathmandu town walking distance from Thamel - no views of the mountains and not much interior beauty to recommend it.  But the service and facilities were excellent during my stay, and the staff friendly and helpful, and given that it was a working week,, this was the most I could ask for!

This is my second stay in this hotel which is very short. My first was before five years ago & now so many changes has been done & the hotel is really a good place to stay .Rooms are v. good --equiped with all required materials.location is good --nearby are fast food shops --coffe shops... etc.

It was certainly my first stay in this hotel and is going to be my last one until they bring massive changes in the staff's hospitality, especially at the reception. The check in was very time consuming and no apology at all. No smiles or hospitality whatsoever while dealing with the guest and when asked about any early breakfast later in the evening for tomorrow morning, rather than giving me an option, the receptionist started asking whether I was their guest or not. I mean why would i ask him, if i was not their guest.. very rude and bias. I would not have expected this from a five-star hotel. I would not recommend this Hotel.

Basically everything that I want from a hotel stay when I visit Nepal. Clean, efficient and friendly service. Very central for where I need to go on my trips. Try to get a room at the back of the hotel as it is much quieter, especially if there is a wedding

Stayed in this hotel for 2 nights before and 1 night after an Exodus group tour in Nepal.Nice clean rooms, wifi in reception area and delicious breakfast.Made use of the pool one afternoon when relaxing but not impressed with the cost of poolside drinks - almost £20 for one beer and one coke!!
50年の歴史がある五つ星ということで期待していましたが、微妙なところですね。WiFiも有料の割には使いにくいし、風呂の水も茶色いし、ベッドも小さいし、もちろん良いところもあるのでしょうけど、値段の割にはと思うところが目についてしまいました。

We had an event in the hotel, so the stay was also lined up here. The ambiance is nice. The rooms were clean. A visit to their Jungli Bar is a good option. My colleague stays here regularly and has high opinion for this place. He said the staff is always courteous and helpful. I too have a similar opinion on that. It is centrally located on Durbar Marg and is pretty close to the Museum

Everything about this hotel is first class. The staff is attentive and helpful. The location is central and you can walk to many attractions (if you dare!). The breakfast is delicious and varied and the pool huge and inviting. If only they wouldn't charge for wireless in your room.

Stayed in Hotel Annapurna in early November for four nights as part of my business trip. The hotel is centrally located in the city of Kathmandu and the room that I stayed in was spacious and had all usual amenities. Staff was friendly but buffet breakfast was poor lacking selection and the hotel needs a lot of TLC as rooms need some updating.

Its nice Hotel to Stay in as the Atmosphere and People are so nice.Very Neat and Clean.  Staff is also Good and Well Mannered.If you are Getting Bored .You can go and Spent time in Casino.You have all places near by like Durbar  Square,Royal Palace and if you want to shop Go to Thamel..You  have  Pizza Hut and Kfc,  outside Hotel if you are Fast Food Lover.I would Advice once to Visit and Enjoy Stay Inn.

This hotel is in the main hub of Kathmandu. The best place to stay in Kathmandu. Staff is good and rooms are also very neat and clean. Casino is there in the hotel. Ans if you pizza lovers pizza hut is right outside the hotel. So many choices of fast food outside.  Thamel, main shopping place of Kathmandu is at a walkable distance.

It is located near durbar MARG, this hotel is famous for casino in the world and it is very old casino of Nepal Only foreigners are alloud to play casino Nepal resident are not alloud, it is open Twenty four hour. You can play any amount with any currency different types casino play you will find in the Anna purna hotel.

Good location, Comfortable rooms and very friendly staffs. The bathroom was a bit too small and the shower curtains could not contain the water from flooding the bathroom floors. At the price we paid, we were definitely expecting a lot better.

Very good rooms; reasonable. service is excellent. great food and is walking distance to all the attractions that the city has to offer including the thamel market, palace museums etc. also very close to all the good restaurants and shops

The hotel is centrally located at Durbar Marg in Thamel and right next to New Road. Its an ideal location in center of city for any business traveler since traffic in Kathmandu can be quite an issue. The staff is courteous and helpful and its a clean hotel with good assortment of Indian food. Dinner with live music in their restaurant Ghar-e-kabab as well as their breakfast buffet are good and recommended.

Over the past year and a half, I have stayed four times at the Annapurna and so feel qualified to make an assessment of the hotel. First of all, the reception staff on arrival are consistently  very thoughtful as one is invited to take a seat, offered a refreshing drink while the staff completes the check-in processes. All the hotel staff are helpful, friendly and thoughtful. Any questions are thoughtfully answered and there is a sense of well being which exudes throughout the hotel. My rooms have ranged from small to spacious with the room on my last visit in May of this year, being very spacious with all the amenities that one could wish for. I particularly like the natural soaps. My only wish would be to have my room vacuumed on a daily basis and not once in a while.  I love Indian food and found the Indian restaurant to be one of the best that I have experienced on my travels. The Coffee shop where breakfast is served is absolutely wonderful with a range of western, Nepalese, Indian and Chinese fare offered at breakfast.  I usually mix it all up so that I do not have to choose! Here too one can get an excellent cup of coffee with  an absolutely amazing variety of sweets!  There is a buffet lunch each day with each day having a different theme. I have had the continental, the Chinese and the Indian cuisine and enjoyed them all. Very tasty.  The hotel is a stone's throw from a range of well known designer shops, local well know shops and markets as well as walking distance to a number of temples. The earthquake of last year in April has not dampened the spirit of residents who continue to be welcoming and thoughtful. I look forward to my return visit.

Nice hotel located on the main street Durbar Marg.  Rooms are spacious and beds comfortable.  Tea/coffee service provided in the room.  We stayed for two nights and would definitely recommend this hotel to tourists visiting Kathmandu.  The lobby has live music every evening.  There are a number of restaurants serving Indian and Chinese cuisine.  Reception staff extremely efficient and professional.

Stayed in this property for three days during recent business trip in the city. It is one of the oldest and supposed best hotel in city. Few plus is has is its location, few of the energetic and courteous staff. Minus is it is quite old, room are lot of the Size, interior and amenities what you would expected in a 5 Star, you will smell the hint of we are best attitude among quite of the staff and most it is does not fit in to value for money criteria. There was considerable waiting time during airport pick, check in was smooth, buffet breakfast spread was average,  staff not attentive and courteous to the guests. Wifi speed and connectivity was ok. Lobby is good room was disappointing. Overall not a value for money proposition. Will like to specially mention the professional, alertness and courtesy attitude of Ms.Pragya Shrestha sad same was missing with most of the other staff.

Annapurna is one of the oldest luxury hotels in Kathmandu. It is sprawled over a considerable area in the middle of Darbar Marg (hip, chic part of the city). The hotel is located in front of a mall. Lots of coffee shops and restaurants nearby. Be sure to try Nanglo (right next door). The rooms are a bit run down but not uncomfortable.The staff is stellar - helpful and polite. The breakfast is fantastic! Especially the South Asian selection. I looked forward to a leisurely breakfast every morning.

Stayed in Club Room, 3043, with pool view. The room itself was nice and quite spacious. The bathroom was a bit dated, but fine.I arrived very late in the evening and ordered room service. Delivery was prompt and food quality was quite good.Service at club level breakfast area was excellent. I didn't catch her name, but the server was so enthusiastic and attentive.It appears that the hotel has ongoing renovations, however, this did not disturb my stay in any way.There are some nicer, and newer options in the area, but I would definitely consider staying at this property again.

Not a coffee shop !!  It a restaurant ! I called in just for a coffee and pastry with friends.But un like a coffee shop it was not a relaxed atmosphere in fact it was extreemly formal! What I found was if you bought pastry or cakes in their shop the cost was 160 rps per peice but if you go into the restaurant the cost jumps to 300rps per peice A very small pot of tea 300rps and two coffees cost 600rps !!!

Conveniently placed with less than a 10 minutes walk to Thamel. It's rated as 5 star although it's more a 3 star... The rooms are okay but could use some renovation especially the bathrooms and there's no minibar!Staff are super friendly and make you feel welcome. It has a really nice coffee shop with an impressive menu, 24 hour room service, and the breakfast is also really good at this hotel. The Indian restaurant however is average. The pool is nice- busy on weekends as its open to the public. the gym is decent and they have an in house travel agent which is a plus. My flight was in the evening, they are  very flexible with late check-out, they also didn't me extra for checking out sooner than reserved. They also have free airport transfers.

Stay was comfortable since we booked the suit but really the benchmark of a 5 star not known to them. They made a good effort to service us but few basic were missing and the transportation was not as expected. Quiet close to Thamel the main market and hence get marks of a strategic location. However be clear in your communication with them and don't forget to check couple of times to avoid last minute hassle.

The hotel is avoidable. We purchased 2 stays at this hotel (In and Out) through a reputed internet hotel / holidays package provider. Even though we had confirmed bookings for 2 adults plus 1 child ( 1 double bed + 1 single bed) the counter staff questioned the pricing confirmed to us on our second stay (3 days later).Ms Dibya was  undiplomatic as was a senior male member of the management who remained a mute and uninspiring spectator. Later, we learnt that he was the General Manager of the hotel. That a senior staff member chose not to provide guidance to out of line employee behaviour reflects poorly on the hospitality standards of the hotel. What was appalling was that Ms Dibya spoke to us as if she was doing us a big favour by not charging us for the extra bed even though our confirmed booking included it.While it is legitimate to clarify, the manner in which Ms Dibya went about it was rude and discourteous. In the end, it was a case of staff covering ignorance of hotel packages being sold as mis-pricing and attempting to display righteous indignation where none was called for.The next time we will choose a genuine customer friendly hotel that may not be "starred" as this one but is true to the wonderful hospitality we have been privy to more generally in Nepal. Cheers

The best thing about this hotel is its location. Durbar Marg is supposed to be the most happening place in Kathmandu and you have the pleasure of stepping on it once you come out of the hotel. It is one of the oldest hotel in Kathmandu but it is well maintained. You have very courteous staffs who are willing to help you in every way they can. The in house Indian restaurant offers delicious food. They also have a chinese restaurant but I have not tried it. There is a well stocked Bar adjoining the swimming pool where you can have a mug of beer in the evening.

hotel is located close to most tourist attractions. the lady at the reception who checked us in made special effort to help us with very useful information -unfortunately i have forgotten her name. the complimentary breakfast had lots of variety and the taste of everything i had was great- the hotel really lived up to its name of goddess annapurna! service in room was efficient and friendly. Enjoyed the swimming pool view.

Nice hotel set back from Durbar Marg. The staff are wonderful and will help you with any requests. Rooms are not 5 star but the ambiance and food in the Indian restaurant is very nice. Nice quiet area beside the pool -(large for this area) to escape from the madness of Kathmandu. The hotel does seem to have a lot of functions(business meetings and weddings) so be prepared for a lot of people.

Short review today.This hotel is possibly one of the nicest hotels within kathmandu. Had the pleasure of a couple stays over the years and without a doubt I was only left with fond memories of a country with lovely people who smile with every greeting. "NAMASTE" Food was good, hotel was clean, staff were some of the friendliest I've come across and my overall experience was that of a great one. Rooms were to a good size and no problems what's so ever. Would defo Reccommend the trip to anyone keen to visit this beautiful place. 4 out of 5 at least. :)

This is one of the nicer hotels in KTM. The rooms are not small, but not big. They are a bit dated, but nice and clean. The people are very helpful and the doormen salute you when you go by.  The breakfast was huge and pretty good, with an interesting selection of local and international. Its a 10-15 walk to the center and tourist sites. They charge for wifi unless you have that included. You can use free wifi in parts of the lobby. They have a big pool which I did not use.

I was back in the Annapurna Hotel after about 3 years this past July and it not only survived the earthquake, but has completed renovations that makes it again a real Top Hotel for Kathmandu.The room was well furnished, the lobby is kept at excellent standard, the pool is refreshing and large enough for all.The other advantage that this property has always enjoyed is location. It is an easy 10-15 minute walk to the Thamel tourist area, and additionally has a number of taxi available out front for any trips outside of the city.

Kathmandu is a city of dust congested traffic and no rules. When you walk along the streets for more than an hour you will definitely need a shower. Hotel Annpura with its name gives an extraordinary value to a stay in Nepal.

Centrally located and proximity to trammel is a huge advantage as it's dotted Witt cafes n restaurants discos etc .Has 4 restaurants serving some great food and also serves F&B adjacent to the pool.About 20 minutes from airportYou get ample parking ,good wifi .Breakfast is served at adjoining cafe within the premises and is decent .

It was Nice Experience Staying here With Such a lovely and Friendly Environment!!! Staff Were Co-operative and The Management Staff! Lots of huge space  to go Around and If you Feel hungry and Want to have  Fast food You can go out of Hotel and Enjoy Pizza and Kfc..... The Best part is that Everything is Near by like Airport,Places to Roam Durbar Square ,Royal Palce Museum ,Pashupati Nath Temple,Syambhu( Monkey Temple)... Also for Shopping you have many Shops to Shop Around and For killing your Time you can Have a great time In Casino. Once if you come to Kathmandu,You should Visit this Hotel and Surely you will Like it.

average food - except for the momos. Very frustrating wifi (if you are on business) - you have to enter your username and password every time you move from the room to the coffee shop or if your laptop goes to sleep! One of the cleaners asked for tips from my American colleague!!!

Whilst previous reviews on this hotel indicated that the staff were unfriendly, I found quite the contrary.  One of our party was feeling quite ill and they arranged a doctor quickly and efficiently and followed up regularly to see if there was any further assistance they could provide.  Thamel is only a short distance away.This was the most expensive hotel we stayed at in Nepal, but we felt it was reasonably priced, given the facilities.

I had a wonderful experience. The hotel is spacious and beautiful, with a large, wonderful pool, an exercise room, 3 restaurants, and a bar. The staff are welcoming, helpful, and incredibly friendly. The breakfast, which is included in the room fee, is substantial, with a lot of interesting variety. The room is comfortable, and the Internet is very reliable. I have no complaints whatsoever, and I plan to stay there again if I return to Kathmandu.

We stayed in club room which is very spacious. We stayed around 7 days.  staff was very friendly &after 2nd day they new what we like to have. Anna purna is the best hotel to stay in kathmandu. It is centrally located &suronded by malls &market.

it was a completely satisfying experience of 4 nights at the hotel. From the check-in to check-out, all the services were provided with smiling faces, cooperative and friendly attitude and with efficiency. All the staff of the hotel was eager to help me out.Of course, there is a room for improvement at any level of service and facility. Fortunately, I did close the deal of business at Kathmandu, which will enable me to visit Kathmandu at least six times a year, for 3 to 4 night each time.I recommend this hotel for all - business traveler or a tourist.

Have stayed multiple times here on business trips, and found them to be comfortable and functional. Rooms at the top floor are really small, so should be avoided. They have 2 restaurants, one for indian/nepal cuisine (really nice) which even has gazal shows in evening & a chinese restaurant which was fine too. Taxis are readily available outside, however they charge a premium. The attached casino in the property is frankly average. All in all a comfortable 3 star setup in one of the posh kathmandu areas, but be ready to pay premium price for it.

What a wonderful experience I had at Hotel Annapurna. Like all truly five star properties - and there are too few of them - service was impeccable and effortless. The staff was there with what I needed before I asked, and not around when I didn't want them around. The room was large, really comfortable, and well appointed - the type of room, in fact, that is so pleasant you are reluctant to leave it to go outside. (This might have had something to do with the great air conditioning.) Minibar was well stocked with everything you need and prices for it were reasonable. There is a large, clean outdoor pool, and a well equipped business center. I stayed briefly in the Yak & Yeti hotel prior to this, and Hotel Annapurna was so much nicer, and better, there was simply no comparison. And because I was there during the off season, the room rate was ridiculously reasonable. Hotel Annapurna would be a five star experience in any country on Earth. The fact that it's in lovely, enchanted, but remote and poor Nepal, just adds icing to the cake - and makes their achievement all the more impressive. I'd stay there again in a heartbeat.

I visited Hotel de'l Annapurna as a volunteer worker for the seminar organised by PATA  Nepal Chapter. The hotel provided the quality service including quality food and quality meeting/seminar hall. The hall was facilitated with the necessary technologies. The hall was near the parking space which made every guest to locate the hall easily.

This hotel has reinvented itself. I stayed here about 20 years back and it seems in last few years they have completely modernised which is to be appreciated. I think they were the first 5 star hotel in Kathmandu and want to keep the tag of one of the best if not the best. Its the best location in Kathmandu, on Durbar Marg. Rooms were good size with nice decor so were bathrooms with all modern amenities. The breakfast buffet was very nice. I had dinner in their Indian restaurant (I forget the name) and I can vouch that this is the best Indian restaurant in Kathmandu. Having stayed at several hotels in Kathmandu due to several visits in last couple of years I am happy that this time I stayed at Annapurna. However I must add that we were allotted rooms on the ground floor and they had no view. Reception said they were the better rooms, not sure. And yes Reception staff need to be better, much better.

The hotel is a nice property. Though when we visited it, there was maintenance work going on. The swimming pool is not as big as shown in the pictures. Even the water in the pool wasn't clean. We had selected a queen bed. But when we got there we got two twin beds which the housekeeping joined to form a single bed. The room was cleaned nicely only the first day after which the housekeeping just set the linen and went. Even though we threw our used towels on the floor, the same towels were folded and kept back on the rack. Even the safe wasn't working, we told the reception thrice but they sent nobody so we just gave up. Due to unavailability of a pool facing room we were upgraded to corporate deluxe. The food at the Indian restaurant was quite nice. However it was really expensive. Opposite the hotel, the Sherpa Mall offers a wide variety of cafés and restaurants. Many showrooms are just at walking distance from the hotel.

I stayed one week at this hotel in May 2015.Despite the hard days the country was going through because of the earthquake, the hotel managed to keep a very good quality of service.I was on the ground floor, the room was spacious with high ceiling. Wifi is slow but that's the case everywhere in Nepal.I wish the hotel improves the gym.Tips:If internet speed is important for you, then get a local sim card with data plan. Cheap and efficientA cross the street from the hotel there's an excellent western/nepali/indian fusion cuisine restaurant called "The old house" a visit is a must

Situated next to the US Embassy, one of the luxurious places to stay or take your loved ones to eat. Also the Casino well maintained, and very helpful staff. Also the surrounding area is very nice. You have a shopping mall, a movie theatre and a nice pub just outside the hotel. The best part if that the place is very safe because of the fact it is close to the Embassy and also almost no power cut in the area. Awesome place.

Both of the US Search & Rescue teams stayed here as we were making plans to return home. Then Nepal was hit with the May 12th 7.3 quake, so we returned to action.  The hotel allowed us to use their facility to run all of our operations from. The staff was quick to get as many services as possible operational.  I had the opportunity to eat at the Chinese restaurant which was very good and I heard the same comments from other team members regarding the Indian restaurant.  Unfortunately, neither had reopened following the last quake. A BIG thank you to the entire staff.

I checked into this hotel a few days after the earthquake - it was filled to the brim with people there for earthquake relief, and many of the staff were not there because they'd had to attend to their own families and property.  As a result, the remaining staff were overworked and overtired.  Because the safety of the dining room was in question, they had put up a huge canopy outside and managed to continue serving quality breakfast and dinner out there - even for those who arrived late from working long days.  Within a few days they moved the operation indoors again.  The room was not cleaned for the first few days due to staff shortages, but within a few days this service resumed (they did a good job) and after awhile we even started getting our daily newspaper again, signaling a return to normalcy.Given the personal challenges the staff had to deal with, and all of the issues caused by the earthquake, I think the hotel did remarkably well trying to keep operating and providing services.  When the LA firefighters were staying there to conduct search and rescue after the second major quake, there were clearly not enough rooms, but the hotel worked to find everyone some sort of accommodation and deal with all of their equipment and special requirements - and not once did we run out of food, which was pretty impressive considering the fluctuating guest numbers and all of the logistical challenges caused by the earthquake.  So hats off for a great job during trying times.Having said all of that, I agree with other reviewers who way this hotel's 5-star rating is unwarranted.  During normal times, the single restaurant provides a limited Indian/Nepalese menu which becomes quite boring after a 2-week stay; the rooms are quite small and crowded, the thermostat doesn't really work (control A/C by turning off and on).  The water in the toilet was brown and the water from the shower was yellow - but this may have been caused by the earthquake in all fairness, as it faded over time.  The wi-fi was reliable and decent speed, TV channels had an ok selection, and services overall were good.  I'd give a "3" rating if I hadn't been so impressed by the effort the hotel made to keep things operating post-earthquake.

The best part of the hotel is the location. Its right on Durbarmarg which gives access to the business district as well as shopping & several eating joints. The room was pretty neat & well-stocked with all amenities. Breakfast is something that really disappointed, for a hotel of such quality. Room service was very prompt and food was great as well. All in all a good experience.

Its a good hotel, centrally located. The rooms are good, but its not a five star hotel as people in Nepal claim it to be. The services are good. Staff are friendly, helpful and fluent in english. The food is good. One of the better hotels to stay at in Kathmandu.

Wir waren zu dritt bereits knapp 2 Wochen unterwegs mit dem Rucksack und wollten uns einfach mal etwas Luxus gönnen. Nach einer sehr unangenehmen 16.5 Std Busfahrt erreichten wir Kathmandu im Regen, schnappten uns schnell ein Taxi und verließen uns (leider) auf den Marco Polo Reiseführer.
