Had an incredible time in dusit princess for my friend bachelorette party! Kishor Acharya and Sushant Ranjitkar provided top-notch service. The food was absolutely delicious too! Can't wait to go back for more. Highly recommend! 💕🥂

The hotel is really in the centre. Services are really the best starting from Check in till check out. I got a problem with the in-room internet but the reception staff fixed it for me immediately. Food and beverage are really Dusit standards. One of the best. We for sure will come back to this hotel again. And thank Rajita Shrestha for helping me and informing me about the benefit of the Gold member

our stay was amazing! The hotel food (morning buffet and dinner) were delicious and the staff especially Nisha at the front desk were extremely nice. We had a great time and were well assisted with transportation needs and room service. Highly recommend Dusit Princess

Excellent and courteous service by the staff …. Few call outs by name are the front office desk led by Ayush Sharma, Nisha Thapaliya and the cheerful bell boy Suresh. The set up of the hotel is extremely refreshing and sets up a calm and serene environment for work.

Fantastic treatment . Beautiful and clean place with very experienced staff .Choose Muna for a deep tissue massage . You ll be renowned in/ out 😍🙏🏻.The green tea is served with love in lonby of the SPA.Take the chance to pop in if you are here for business or just leisure

A wonderful stay at the Dusit Princess. The staff were wonderful and went out of their way to make our stay very comfortable. Thank you to Nisha on reception for all the assistance. The rooms were spotless and showers were so powerful. I also had a Trekkers massage at the spa which was amazing value. Our stay at this hotel was the perfect end to an incredible trip to Nepal.

The swimming pool was very clean and non irritating on the skin. The cleanliness of the hotel is top notched.    The hotel had a very aesthetically pleasing environment. The service was impeccable. The staffs were very lovely, poised and efficient. The food was delicious ✨.    Highly recommended. It was an overall pleasant day out for us.

The level of service in this hotel is unbeatable. From the interiors, to the food, to amenities to the location - you get your money’s worth by staying here. My personal favorites: the masamam curry from Soi, their thai restaurant. The pad thai cocktail from Kibu, their rooftop sky lounge. And the cheesecake from Dusit Gourmet, their cafe.

excellent Thai cuisine. Quality food. Very friendly staff.one of best place and environment.First time we came to  this hotel restaurant  and planning to come very soon bar tender richal gurung is very smart and friendly and professional thanks all the staff and management team.

Really great experience, great environment, nice service and hospitality. Staff here are really great. Especially Mr. Rajat Rajbanshi, he is really considerate and make us feel at home. Thank you for everything.

We did our HCPs and DW meet in hotel Dusit Princess Kathmandu and got very good service from Mr Suraj Pokhrel and team for our event. Food was also good quality and taste which was liked by our customers. Everything was very well organised. Keep it up.

We enjoyed a lovely buffet breakfast with great service at Dusit Princess on their one year anniversary month . Its not my first time and it wont be my last. It is a great place and it is highly recommended from my side. We both had a wonderful time. Thanks.

It was pleasure experience, feeling like a new person after professional treatment. This is already my second time coming to Crest Spa. The staff are very supportive and professional. If you come to Kathmandu, you definitely need to visit Crest Spa.

Beautiful hotel with great accommodating staff. Modern rooms and bathrooms with lots of attention to detail. The rooftop pool and bar were a highlight! We had dinner in the restaurant, the food was tasty and delivered quickly. Would recommend!

Jeni, Nisha, Srijana  , Nabin  and all staff were very helpful and polite.Food was good in the soi restaurant  and the roof top bar and restaurant. Room were comfortable and well attended. Basically good and clean place and well located.we recomend this to other.

The Dusit Princess offered a charming stay in a perfect location. The room, while cozy, was spotless and had everything I needed. The rooms are the best than any other hotel. The stay was comfortable and all the staffs were well mannered and well trained. Nisha Thapalia helped us the check-out and she made sure our process was smooth. She is well spoken and well groomed.

I like the hospitality. The ambiance and the room is beyond beautiful. Talking about the food I could not stop eating it. Really liked this hotel. One of my favorites in Nepal. I also like the bar and the swimming pool.

Kishor Achaya was an amazing waiter. We made sure we were happy with our food and he was extremely friendly. Kishor has helped us during our whole stay and is a great team member of Dusti Princess. He always had a smile on his face. I would highly recommend the hotel and his services!

The hotel is modern, clean and comfortable. Friendly staff and good facilities. Cozy sky bar with an outdoor pool. The breakfast is tasty - a mix of Asien and continental food. The standard room is medium sized but big enough. I will probably come again.

A wonderful experience! Starting with our incredible room which was spacious, comfortable and spotless. The Staff are the stars! One of the nicest hotels I have stayed with amazing staff members like Deepak, Kshetri, Navin,Bisal and other. Food was amazing, room was perfect , pool area was very nice and spa was amazing. Had 3 different massages and used the sauna everyday. I recommend this hotel to everyone

Gorgeous hotel with such kind and generous people like Rajat and Sreejana who made checking in and out very smooth. Lots of lovely shops, bars and restaurants near by and the rooms were very clean and well maintained. They also had a nice selection of baked goods in the lobby

By far the best hotel in nepal in my experience over last 6 years. Staff is extremely friendly and have problem solving approach. Food is amazing. Staff in restaurant is also very welcoming and friendly. Hotel is located right in the heart of kathmandu

Would rate the experience 5 on 5. Excellent staff .... friendly and attentive. The spa is a must visit and roof top bar was rocking. Everything was absolutely top notch. The rooms comfortable well appointed. The experience was so good that I am already contemplating my next trip to KTM and Dusit

Excellent service. All my family enjoyed a lot. My daughter and her friend enjoyed foods and the pool. Thank you Sabin luitel bhai was great..Prarthana ji gave us a very good deal.. thank you all the dusit staff for wonderful hospitality…..

One of the best Hotels I have ever stayed.its crystal clean both room and toilets, they have all the necessary toiletries and towels.thier gym, spa, Jacuzzi are top notch. Location is best suited, easy to go to Thamel , Indrachowk and center of the city

Went for a birthday dinner celebration at Kibu, the rooftop lounge at the hotel. Beautiful ambience, good drinks and extremely polite and friendly staff. Our hostess Puspa Gurung was very professional. Extremely attentive and made our experience that much more pleasant.

Stayed for 3 nights after EBC trek. Great location. Clean rooms, great bfast.  Used the sauna and steam room as well which was perfect.  Pool on roof top was also a nice place to relax. This was a great experience. I did try the local THAKALI , was amazing. Compliment Chef Prakash Awasthi. The breakfast spread was awesome. Kishor and Suhana for great service in the restaurant. Nisha at the front desk was courteous. Will definitely come again......... Room 503Uday

Sunita is a star of the Crest Spa!I had a wonderful deep tissue massage and detox scrub....oh my!! Totally chilled out after a full week of work. Good trip and staying in this hotel. Room is big. Ac is cool. Breakfast is good. Prices are acceptable. Nice views on the top. Will come again in September. Services everyone makes you feels well. Five start hotel definitely. Highly recommend to stay here. And near the taimile street

Nisha and all staff is very nice, nice service, pleasant stay, neat and tidy room. Breakfast very nice. Room interiors design was amazing.Manish Bajracharya was was very sweet and professional.Amir is very attentive.Coffee shop was nice and bakery item is delicious.love to come back again.

The stay at Dusit Princess was a beautiful experience- clean and spacious rooms, good location, tasty food and the best of all is the warmth and hospitality by the entire staff! Turned out to be a very good choice for stay! Recommended for a stay in Kathmandu!

Dushit Princess has an elegant lobby and attentive staff. You get stunning views from Kibu Sky Lounge make for a memorable evening. The food here was also great. Perfect for business or leisure. Must visit highly recommended while in Nepal.

Warm and affectionate staff made the stay memorable. Reception staff Rajitha and the Coffee Shop Manager were exceptional. Coffee shop and the restaurant served excellent food. Approach road to the hotel is sketchy, apart from that it was perfect

Everything was so good. Ambience, Food , Comfort, Hospitality everything was excellent. Experience was awesome. I will definitely recommend this hotel to my knowns.Cleanliness is good. The hotel was very beautiful...the decoration and ambience were so cozy food was amazing everything was on top notch. I had a great time in Dusit Princess Kathmandu. It’s a new property and located very close to Thamel. The staff was great. Shout out to Nisha, Amir, Suresh at the front desk. I would highly recommend this hotel to people travelling to Kathmandu for work.

Great ambiance, good view, overall great service from beginning to end. World class experience. Can't miss it. Special shoutout to Thapa ji who is extraordinary. If you are here you must see both restaurant and bar on top

Very nice hotel with kind staff. Good bed and clean room. The Thai restaurant in the hotel has also some very nice food and kind staff. Suited at a good place nearby good restaurants, spa and shops. I recommend this hotel and will be staying here at the end of my trip as well

Good food  the restaurant Soi is designed well and creates good mood. We were there for food only with business colleagues. The energetic girl NIMA SHERPA served us very well. We are fan of her service. Presentation of food especially pineapple rice was excellent.

Stay was excellent.  Staff was courteous and always ready to help.  Dining experience was also excellent and food taste was very good.  Nice choices.  Delicious food.  Spa, sona, gym was nice and clean.  Staff was helpful.  Gym had trainer always ready to help and train guest.Thank you.

Housekeeping service in no 1 in Nepal. Friendly staff and quick follow up. Corridor & Lobby area well maintained. Another hand The hotel is very peaceful enviroments. Scent of  lobby is very nice and feeling well.

Great experience...Good hospitality by the team. Front desk is very helpful, especially Ms. Nisha & Mr. Manish bajracharya. It was an experimental selection of hotel for my recent trip to katmandu, sure will book here next time. Keep it up guys.

Binod Bist is the best server! All the staff was so accommodating and so so nice! We don’t want to leave! Go to the 12th floor!  Magic! Also, the hotel is so beautiful and brand new! The room is beautiful, clean, spacious and brand new! A must stay!

Great staff, courteous front desk , kitchen chefs, service staff. Would strongly recommend to experience! Will come back again!! Very welcoming ambient! Very clean premises. Tasty , plentiful breakfast choices, lunch dinner options also very good.

We went for Saturday brunch and service was excellent and there was a lot of choices in the food. Especially thanks to Kishor acharya who provide us excellent service and help in each and every time. Really appreciate and recommend visit once in the best hotel.

Best hotel I’ve ever stayed in, even compared to  USA. Staff was so friendly and helpful, the food was amazing, the hotel was beautiful and had great amenities. Was welcomed with fresh fruit and a beautiful room. 100% coming back.

Excellent services and polite staff. Nisha and Jeni at the front desk were especially helpful. The 12th floor bar and pool side lounge had a wonderful ambience. The hotel went out of the way to provide food, drinks and snacks to our whole team.

Super impressive. I visited twice (before and after a trek) with a group of mostly Californians. We first stayed in an older hotel in Kathmandu, which was fine. But our trek was delayed so we spent one night at the Dusit Princess before heading to the mountains. Honestly the entire group was blown away. This is an excellent hotel. We asked our tour operator to put us in the Dusit Princess on the way back from Everest, and spent the entire trek talking about how nice it would be to come back. On our return it was such an amazing treat to stay here - the service is top notch (especially the staff’s friendliness and eagerness), the property is brand new and in excellent condition, and the food is among the best we’ve had. I am particularly impressed with the spa. I’ve had massages all over the world. The 90 minute trekkers massage I had with Savitra (?) at the Crest Spa was among the best I’ve had anywhere. There are some rough spots. The staff seems young and new, and we did experience some minor issues (slow service at the pool deck restaurant, a missing dish at the Thai restaurant on the ground floor). But overall we loved the Dusit and wouldn’t hesitate to recommend it to anyone.

We stayed here 5 nights at the end of December 2019, 4 nights in a Heritage de Luxe room and at the end of our trip one night in a Junior Suite. The hotel has 80 rooms and there are plans to add another building with 40 rooms to the complex. Hopefully this will not destroy the nice (small scale) atmosphere of the complex which includes 3 restaurants, an unheated outdoor pool, a Spa and a lounge bar. The hotel is not cheap but worth the money although drinks are very expensive in the bar (€5 for a coca cola in the bar, less expensive in the restaurant). One of the 3 restaurants is very expensive but considered a unique experience. Staff (appr 300 employees) is very friendly and helpful. The Heritage de Luxe room is spacious and nice. The Junior Suite is extremely nice. Without doubt it is worth the additional costs compared to a Heritage de Luxe room. Much more spacious (especially the bathroom), a very nice atmosphere and an additional “day bed”. In both rooms we had a good bed, very good shower and Wi-Fi. Both rooms have a small refrigerator, air-conditioning and a kettle to make coffee or tea. The bathroom is spacious with 2 sinks.Complimentary bottled water and fruit are provided. Breakfast buffet is very good. There are several small restaurants close to the hotel were we had nice dinners for around €2 per person. The city center is 15 min away by taxi (for which we paid €6).

This property not an easy place to get to, but it is so worth the the effort. Hidden up in the hills facing the Himalayas, it offers stunning views of the mountain ranges. Because of its location nestled in the hills, there are hundreds of stairs around the property to get from your room to the many places such as the mediation hall, spa area, yoga hall, and reception area. We spent 5 wonderful days taking advantage of the many activities offered. The experience is both relaxing and invigorating. Our junior suite was private, warm and comfortable with amazing views of the Himalayas. In addition to a sitting area in the suite, there is a private terrace to sit and enjoy the beauty of the property and the view. The staff is so friendly and makes sure you are comfortable. Having stayed at both Dwarika properties in Kathmandu and Dhulikhel, I have become a loyal fan! Can’t wait to return and experience the wonders of Nepal!!

I loved everything about my stay at this Dwarikas hotel.  The architecture is magnificent and everything about the spaces created makes you feel calm.  The food at each restaurant available on the property was delicious.  But most importantly, everyone I came in contact with was extremely pleasant, curteous, helpful and kind.  I highly recommend a visit to The Dwarikas Hotel and Kathmandu!

It certainly is a unique experience when staying at The Dwarika's Hotel.  From the saluting Security Guard on the door to the very personal attention from all the staff, this architecturally restored building offers one a view into a previous time while staying in bustling Kathmandu.   We thought the Fusion Bar was a delightful place to dine and relax your tired feet after a long day and the Courtyard is an enchanting and lush place to dine and sit during your stay.  The courtyard pool is small and can be rather refreshing, as not heated, but is beautifully in keeping with the restored building.However, the Krishnapathan restaurant felt a little gimmicky with the order to remove shoes, wash hands, floor seating and addition of an apron (despite there being a napkin provided) all within minutes of arriving.  It just felt far to canteen-like for our taste.Also, we were in Room 301 which, while huge, was disappointing on so many levels.  It had a severe lack of power points, an incredibly slippery tiled floor and a hairdryer that's plug had to be forced into the power socket by Housekeeping to use it.  More importantly, since the room ran the full width of the property, it had no protection from outside noise.  There was a busy alley down below with the constant buzz of motorbikes and had a tied up dog in the property next door that barked constantly day and night.  It was far from the oasis or sanctuary from the cacophony of Kathmandu that we had hoped for or as referred to in other Reviews.  We can’t be the only people to have reported this problem with this room.  So, I would say, visit this extraordinary Hotel, but perhaps be prepared for less than a 5* experience.

This is probably our favorite hotel we've ever stayed in.  The location is super convenient from the airport.  The grounds are beautiful and immaculate.  For example, the outdoor furniture white cushion covers are never stained or dirty.  The rooms are spacious and bathrooms huge.  All the restaurants we tried had fabulous food, pleasing to the eye and palate.  The pool area is lovely, but it was a little to chilly for us to swim.  The real difference with Dwarika is the incredible staff.  Everyone is exceptionally helpful and accomodating. I needed to borrow an electric voltage converter to charge my camera battery and they found one for me. At breakfast the one day the buffet wasn't available, the waiter notice we weren't eating cheese, which he had observed the week prior, so he brought us a plate of cheese. Prior to our evening flight out, the hotel allowed us the use of a room for an hour to shower and relax.  Everything about this hotel is top notch.  Many hotels are lovely, but the great staff places Dwarika into a class by itself.

Kathmandu was a chaotic city but once we stepped through the doors of Dwarika’s hotel, calmness prevailed. Namaste was the usual greeting which roughly means“I bow to you, equivalent of saying hello but with respect”.The hotel was known for preserving decorative wood carvings from ancient buildings being torn down.The UNESCO Asia-Pacific Heritage Award for Culture Heritage Conservation was given to this most deserving hotel.  The junior suite was beautifully appointed and very spacious.  The gift shop contained beautiful cashmere clothing, interesting books, pottery, stationery, and jewelry.  We bought most of our gifts from this store.The buffet breakfast was wonderful!Achyut Neupane was our favorite server, always a smile on his face.The Sherpa soup was absolutely delicious.  It was fun to try Nepali dishes at their main restaurant.We hired a driver arranged by the hotel to take us to Thamel, Boundhanath Stupa and Pashupatinath Temple.The airport was 2 km away and cost about 500-600 rupee.  Many hotels are not memorable but the Dwarika is an exception. The hotel staff was exceptional as was everything about the hotel.

This hotel is incredible!!! Upon entrance you are greeted with a refreshing towel and hot tea. Check in was very fast and smooth. The rooms are extremely large and very comfortable. The grounds are beautiful. You may think that you are staying at a palace instead of a hotel. The breakfast was great with a large selection to choose from. The service was exceptional. Normally I don’t mention names in my reviews; however, one staff member deserves it. Shiva was a perfect example of staff leadership. He was always available to make our stay memorable. He was very courteous, friendly, knowledgeable, and very professional. Also, the entire staff always went out of their way to ensure our needs were always met with a smile. Their hospitality was greatly appreciated by my wife, daughter, and me. It was a fantastic stay.

From the moment you arrive, you know you’re at a special place. This hotel should be put in the same category as La Mamounia, The Plaza, Del Coronado, The Ritz. The entire staff; front desk, servers, housekeeping, security, just can’t do enough for you. Ram Chandra Gajurel was always at the front of the house to make sure we had everything we needed. By the end of the week, we felt like family. The accommodations are magnificent. An old grand hotel full of antiques & hand crafted art work. Most people prefer staying in the main building but we liked our room in one of the smaller buildings. Very cozy & private. We very much enjoyed the food & ate most of our meals there. Their menus include everything from Continental cruising to Nepalese to Japanese. Don’t miss the 6-30 course set menu restaurant. We chose the 6 courses & couldn’t move afterwards!!! I really can’t find anything wrong with this place.

We stayed for 2 nights at Dwarika’s Hotel. After driving in the dusty and busy Kathmandu, we arrived to the hotel and we were surprised by the beautiful architecture, the excellent service and the great options for dinner.The room was big, nice, with a nepalese architecture.You have all the amenities necessary, such as a full minibar, coffe, tea, complimentary water, toothpaste, toothbrush, ironing board, iron...Absolutely a perfect attention for details.As for the restaurants, we had 2 times dinner at the Japanese Restaurants and it was very good.We had lunch at the international one and it was also very good. We used the laundry and it was impeccable.Absolutely nothing to comment:) would go back in a heartbeat.And i guess you notice that i don’t give 5* easily.

Dwarika's hotel is a 5 star heritage hotel in Kathamandu, Nepal worth staying in if one is looking for a good heritage hotel. The architecture reflects very elaborate carvings and Nepalese culture. Staff are polite and very helpful. The hotel Nepalese restaurant offers a very interesting Nepalese dining experience which serves authentic Nepalese cuisine in traditional Nepalese custom.

I’m so appreciative that there exists a place that still values customer service through out the hotel. I have stayed at dozen of hotels in Nepal . This was on the top of the list of best experiences ever. Staff were very hospitable and there for every need of mine. There is a gentleman in the evening shift in food and beverage depart (Fusion Bar and restaurant) with smiling face called Pramesh Devkota. He is lovely, great asset to the hotel. He is friendly, very through and professional. All the best for him and hope to see you again. I highly recommend to go there during dinner time in his presence. It was a pleasure to stay here. The hotel is located very close to the airport approximately 5 min. I would recommend this hotel for both business or pleasure trips.

The owners of Dwarika's have created a truly original and fascinating hotel that gives visitors an authentic impression of Nepalese culture and architecture.  I arrived during Diwali/Tihar and the hotel was looking particularly beautiful with flowers, rangoli, and lights everywhere.  It was a wonderful introduction to Nepal. On returning from trekking my room was a haven of peace and comfort, providing every comfort anyone could need.  The breakfast buffet is excellent, with a wide range of Asian and Western choices.

My husband and I recently spent 8 nights at the Dwarika.  This is honestly one of the most beautiful hotels we've ever stayed at with genuinely one of the best staffs we've ever experienced.A much delayed trip to Kathmandu, (thanks to COVID :-(   was rewarded with many wonderful experiences, enhanced by this amazing hotel.  The hotel itself is a preservation of amazing Newari architecture thanks to Mr. Dwarika Das Shrestha who rescued, documented, and restored numerous wooden Newari artifacts.  I think some family members actually still live onsite.I can't say enough about the front desk staff, the Toran breakfast staff, housekeeping, Krishnapan, and Fusion restaurant and bar staff.  So welcoming, so attentive, so professional, and so friendly.  The front desk staff was incredibly attentive and their attention to detail was amazing.  We felt like they actually knew us.After a few mornings, the breakfast staff greeted us like old friends and recognized that my husband and I would have three cups of coffee while reading the Kathmandu news, and just as one cup was finished, they'd appear with another cup!The Krishnapan tasting experience is one you shouldn't miss.  We actually ate here twice - the food was just lovely.  My husband did 9 courses non-veg and I did 6 courses veg the first time and the second time, they mixed up the menu so we could try something different.  Delicious and sophisticated Nepali cuisine.Both of our rooms were fantastic (we stayed for 5 nights, flew to Pokhara, then came back for another 3 nights).  First room was a junior suite and second room was a heritage executive suite.  Both so spacious and beautifully appointed.  The housekeeping staff did an amazing job every morning, plus turn down service.The property itself is a peaceful retreat away from busy Kathmandu.  Beautiful landscaping, a quite library, a spacious bar and restaurant.  We tried to enjoy as much of the different spaces as we could.  The bartender and the Fusion staff were outstanding!  My husband actually got a real martini (which is sometimes a challenge in another country).The Dwarika really enhanced our Nepal experience.  I just smile every time I think about our stay.

Every single place of this hotel met magically the highest level of elegance and comfort.Be it the reception, the gym or yoga room, there was order and a unique nepali touch. Temperature in every room was perfect. Subtle music where appropriate. Harmony was the rule.From eggs benedict and cheese variety in the breakfast to the delicate assortment of Nepalese dishes in the evening, all the food was superb (and I also had amazing carbonara in the garden tables).This hotel was the perfect add-on to the beauty of visiting Nepal, and a cozy shelter on rainy afternoons.All the staff was elegant, efficient, friendly and very professional. The security greets you with a military traditional salutation that felt warm and full of respectCongrats to the professional and friendly staff and management!

The experience at Dwarika was truly perfect. From ambiance to the service every bit was filled with warmth and aimed at teaching us about the culture of Nepal. The fixed menu containing Nepali cuisine is worth a try and suitable for adults as well as children. Beautiful room that overlook a beautiful courtyard make the stay extremely relaxing and enjoyable. Some details like the chirping of birds or the flute music playing further added to the wonderful experience.

This hotel is beautiful with its Newari architecture and expert placements of art and antiquities. All the public areas are comfortable and attractive. The staff are exceptionally responsive and looked after us very well. They make good cocktails in their bar and the food we ate was all tasty and well presented. Our room (a junior suite) was restful with muted colours and a day bed and overlooked the inner courtyard.

We only stayed here for dinner and a couple drinks after coming back to Kathmandu from the Dwarika Dhulikhel Resort and waiting for our night flight.  We didn’t get a chance to spend a night at Dwarika Kathmandu but we were super impressive by the property.  The construction took decades as we heard and the attention to details is amazing, every door knob, pillar, window frame were well-considered by the owner and designers.  We enjoyed walking through every corner of this hotel.We had dinner at the main restaurant, not very impressive, run out of steak at 6:30pm (while its sister property at Dhulikhel, which is over an hour from Kathmandu never run out of steak). Had drinks at the bar - Fugion, great service, good cocktail. I will try spending a couple nights here at Dwarika Kathmandu the next time I’m in Nepal, but perhaps not the main restaurant.  I saw the Japanese restaurant have impressive menu including hot pots and Teppanyaki!

We stayed one night in the Dwarika’s Hotel as part of a National Geographic tour and I wish we stayed longer.  The hotel is a tranquil oasis in the midst of a bustling and chaotic cityscape.  The best feature of the hotel was our sensational room — it was huge, beautifully furnished in Nepalese style, and as comfortable a room as one could imagine having in a hotel. Big bathroom with separate shower stall and soaking tub; nice sized closet, spacious combination bedroom and living area with a lot of comfortable furniture.  It was so quiet we felt as though there were no other rooms in the hotel.  The fitness center on the roof is the best equipped I’ve seen on our trip, with a good number of free weights and weight machines, and treadmills. There is also a very attractive yoga deck on the roof.  The swimming pool is modest in size but refreshing.  Hotel staff is extremely attentive.  The hotel has real character and an authentic feel, with a lot of interesting and unusual decorative features (the door handles are fun works of art). The Dwarika is a very special hotel and among the nicest hotels we’ve visited, anywhere.

Dwarika’s is much more than a hotel; it is an experience!  All details have been considered, which has made it a clear oasis in the center of a hectic city.  If travel or business takes you to Kathmandu, only Dwarika’s can offer you respite from the madding crowd.

all rooms face the incredible and huge courtyard; the building itself incorporates exquisite wood antique windows and doors. The city is known for dogs barking all night long. Not here. Totally quiet. Several great restaurant choices. Very attentive service. Beautiful pool. Lovely seating areas - covered and uncovered. Tables offer various games, including the Nepalese board game : Baagh-Chaal, quite the strategic game that involves tigers and goats. Room is sizable and unique but our did not offer privacy except for the toilet. A bit weird that could easily be fixed with a curtain. Comfortable beds and bedding.

We booked a junior suite for 4 nights at Dwarika. We checked in on March 19, early morning.  Our first impressions by far exceeded our expectations. This property is a landmark of Nepalese artwork, style, architecture and taste. It is definitively a must see, worth even a visit just for a dinner in one of its restaurants. Staff was welcoming and extremely charming. We settled in room 309, which was simply said, awesome. Please check the attached pictures for a reference. Our stay was comfortable, regenerating and unforgettable. The property is a sanctuary, a museum transformed in a hotel, but a museum full of life, tradition and positive soul featuring several internal shops that sells clothes, books and artwork. Breakfast is served at the Toran restaurant, facing the reception. Service was excellent, food tasty. We booked a SPA treatment. I personally had an Ayurvedic treatment which specifically deals with sinus/nose ailments which proved very effective. We had dinner at Krishnarpan restaurant and this, too, has been truly a unique experience, worth to spend an extra word about its menu options: from six to twenty-two courses. Upon booking (which is necessary well in advance) after a short mail interactions with the staff, we decided to go for the twelve course menu. Well, be aware that Krishnarpan doesn’t serve nouvelle cuisine European style kind of portions. This were twelve full size courses that left us literally breathless. Because of quality, taste, variety, presentation and, specifically, quantity. We consider a honor having been able to spend four days in Katmandhu while being hosted at Dwarika’s.

Dwarika is a very beautiful hotel. It is unique in that it showcases many exquisite restored Nepali woodworking pieces, and the entirety of the hotel is picturesque and instagrammable. We received excellent service from the hotel staff - especially one of the receptionist trainees (that’s what it says on his badge); he was exceptionally attentive and had an enthusiastic demeanor. Bartender and drinks were also exceptional. On the down-side, we believe to have gotten sick from the room service meals. We believe this because we received room service twice and got sick the morning after. But we can’t exclude it could have been other sources - though unlikely to happen twice from different places. Last, there were too many mosquitos and small spiders; so the place needs a bit better pest control. Overall, we this is definitely the best hotel we stayed at in Kathmandu (we stayed at 3 different).

Old world architecture, superb service and food make this a must respite in a very crowded, dirty city. Park like inner courtyard. Unheated outdoor pool. Rooftop fitness center and yoga room. Food very good. Airport very crowded, too small. Flights often delayed because of lack of space for planes. Kathmandu has not recovered from 2015 earthquake.

As soon as you pass through the high walls sheltering the Dwarika Hotel from the main road, you are transported to a different world. The Dwarika creates a unique atmosphere, blending traditional Nepalese architecture and artwork with first class customer service.Guest rooms are spacious and comfortable. The beautiful grounds allow guests the option to take meals and refreshments outside. There are a number of excellent dining option within the hotel. We enjoyed the Fusion Bar and had a memorable six course meal at the hotel’s signature  restaurant, Krishnarpan. The hotel is located in a central position, close to the airport. It is also a short walk to one of Kathmandu’s extraordinary sights, the Pashupatinath Hindu temple complex, located on the Bagmati River. We were privileged to spend time here witnessing the ceremonies of daily life.The Dwarika is a special place to stay. Its atmosphere is evocative and calming. It is like stepping back in time.

Raunak ji! Thank you for making our engagement ceremony a memorable night 👏 The service you arranged and provided us was greatly appreciated. You’re one of the best Manager who’s very good skill about managing both customer and staff I have ever experienced in my career. Your valued involvement on our big day will be always thankful. Also, looking forward to see you again  in future.

The Dwarikas hotel is one of the best hotel we've stayed.Dwarikas itself is a big name in the city but how can be a hotel be so peaceful in the crowded city with all the busy roads travelled along kathmandu its like a sacred place to be The staffs were so polite and humble they welcomed us with the nepali rituals.Rooms were amazing and it was on unique traditional style.Foods were average but service at the fusion bar was spectacular.Ashim took care of us he was attractive all the way and gave us exceptional service beyond the expectations.Sumit made amazing best cocktails for us it was too delicious.Mr ram briefed us about the establishment of the hotel and he took us to tour of the hotel.everyone here at the hotel they are helpful smiley faces all the time gave us  positive vibes.

I went to the Dwarika's hotel with my daughter. Our experience from start to finish felt like a dream. It was an oasis of peace where every single member of the staff was very hospitable, kind and friendly, especially Rushita who was like an angel. The food was amazing and the complementary yoga classes a very fun experience. If you are looking for a place to stay in Kathmandu, the Dwarika's hotel is definitely the place to be!

The hotel rooms and facilities were excellent with a very relaxing vibe to it.The hotel is close to the airport which is a plus and a short taxi ride, around $6 one way  (or very hazardous  walk)  to shopping and site seeingGood choice of food and restaurants inside and out in the courtyard.All staff friendly and professional and in particular the front office staff.Would recommend a night or two stay.

This hotel brings you back in time and this is the main reason you want to stay here. The hotel’s colonial design, the collection of wood carvings, the serene courtyard that is the remedy from the hustle and bustle of Katmandu, all makes this place a unique stay in Nepal.  The only negative feedback would be about the food at the restaurant.  Our daughters ordered room service and the food was not of standard expected from dwarikas.

This property was a true gem on so many levels.  Physically, the attention to detail and the care that went into restoration is apparent everywhere.  Our room was spacious and attractive and, frankly, quite interesting in detail.  The common areas were very comfortable and welcoming, and we loved the musical offerings in the afternoon.  Even more impressive was the staff.  Without exception, they were gracious, welcoming, and helpful.  From the greeting in the driveway to the waitstaff at the restaurants, we felt appreciated and cared for.  There was no need to leave the premises for dining.  We enjoyed our meals at the outdoor restaurant and a very special meal at Krishnarpan.Many thanks to the Dwarkia's family for a thoroughly enjoyable stay.

I visited the this hotel as part of a longer journey in Nepal. I stayed twice during my trip in October and November of 2021. On both occasions, I had absolutely gorgeous rooms overlooking the courtyard. The staff and service were impeccable,  the rooms and total hotel clean and inviting. The ambience is enchanting, private, and feels far removed from the bustle of Kathmandu Valley, though you're centrally located and need only to walk outside to be immersed.They offer 3 or 4 different dining experiences at the hotel, all of which were fantastic (my heart belongs to C. Momo...). Service was fast, attentive, and prices reasonable. I also recommend you visit their gift shop for wonderful locally made items- everything from incense, jewelry, souvenirs, books, to housewares and even antique furniture. I would never stay anywhere else while in Kathmandu.

spent 2 nights  here to celebrate my wife's birthday! From the moment we checked in to our departure true Nepalese hospitality. Make sure you get a Junior suite and find yourself amidst luxury! Shiva the manager truly embodies the essence of what Dwarika's stands for: a true warm guest experience. We celebrated Nepali New Year with a great outdoor buffet experience and also ate at Mako's also an excellent dining option. You can walk out and a few minutes you are in Pashupatinath UNESCO site. But once inside the facility you will not want to leave. Need to be there! Few places like this exist anymore.

Amazing hotel, with the biggest and most beautiful court yards. Went there for dinner, which was excellent, the service made us feel special, staff was very helpful and professional. The whole place is done tastefully...wish I could afford to stay there, but at 500$ a night (I was told).....not possible

Our stay at Dwarikas Hotel was just perfect in every way.For my birthday-Special cake and dinner table was organised.The staff made us feel like family .Rooms are well appointed and was warmed up every evening with the turn down service .Special dance and flute performances made the evening extra special. The service at breakfast and dinner was just perfect .every need was met to perfection.Same day laundry service was exactly what we needed after our india trip.They even stored our bags for 5 days as we toured the rest of Nepal .Dwarika 's hotel is highly recommended for a Katmandu stay beyond compare.

We stayed in the royal suite. This is surely THE place to stay in Kathmandu. Beautiful hotel, lovely courtyard area, convenient location (airport and sights close). There is nothing the staff won’t do to help.  Management are totally on top of their game.  A very well run hotel with a long history of providing the top end experience in Kathmandu.  Use in conjunction with Kathmandu Travels & Tours who will look after any bespoke top-end experience in Nepal.

We have recently been in Nepal and due to CoVid 19 and many flight cancellations we had to change our bookings at The Dwarika 3 times. The hotel was fantastic, they did not charge us any cancellation fees and in fact upgraded our rooms when we finally landed on their doorstep. I have been wanting to stay at this hotel for sometime and am so pleased I finally got there.  The buildings are beautiful and it is hard to take in all the wonderful details as there are so many.Cannot say enough about the staff, they were friendly, helpful and had amazing attention to detail. We had a few meals at the hotel and the food was delicious.Our room, an Executive Suite, was wonderful.Thank you to all the staff at The Dwarika. We hope to return!

Beautiful traditional hotel in Kathmandu, very close to the airport. Amazing staff throughout the hotel, with great hospitality, friendliness and good service. Junior suite was very spacious, great pool and good massage. The grounds of the hotel are really exceptional, peaceful, serene and clean you feel at home and with nature. Would definitely recommend a stay at Dwarika’s.

I enjoyed excellent service in a lovely atmosphere.  The massage was very relaxing and the singing bowl treatment energizing. I skin feels good after the facial. The spa meets expectations of quality for the unique hotel.   I wish I had time to go for more treatments!

Stayed in the hotel for the first time and really loved it. Restaurants, swimming pool, gift shop, rooms, gym, location. Everything is amazing.Special thanks for the Front Desk Team; Nutan and her amazing colleague ( I forgot her name sorry). And to Madan, he is the one who met us in the airport, concierge team also for their assistance with everything that we need. Our stay was 10 out of 10.Thanks for taking care about us, hope to see you soon again!

We stayed four nights at Dwarika’s while exploring Kathmandu and surrounds. Everywhere you look there is an antique to catch your eye. We were warmly welcomed on arrival.  Our room was spacious with a large bathroom. The room had all of the modern conveniences while maintaining its special charm. The staff was wonderful. Always warm, friendly and eager to please. As others have said it is an oasis in crazy Kathmandu. Magical!

Stayed here on a small group tour   Full of atmosphere beautiful structure. This hotel is quite central yet not noisy except for the pigeons Rooms lovely full of character on our return were upgraded to a suit which was huge & stunning with all facilities. We ate at their Nepali restaurant which we all thoroughly enjoyed. Sitting on cushions on the floor. Wine expensive which is to be expected. Also the Japanese restaurant which was reasonable staff were wonderful. Would have loved to stay longer.

We stayed for 4 nights and had a wonderful experience in every respect. The property has old artifacts lovingly restored and a heritage feel, with something interesting to see at each corner. The service was very good, always delivered with a smile. I liked the breakfast selection, available from 6 am.  We couldn't have asked for a better place from which to explore Nepal.

We took and overland to Kathmandu Nepal while on our world cruise. Kathmandu was a bucket list item and did not disappoint. We stayed in the hotel Dwarika, a little bit of old, but modern. Nice room size and very comfortable. The hotel staff some of the best in our 45 years of travel. Be prepared, replaying in our head Bob Seger’s song “going to Kathmandu”.  Breakfast was a  buffet and very good. Restaurant for dinner was also very good. Hotel would be our first choice if we returned. I alway’s carry an extension cord, was important since plugs where limited.

When we booked we chose 6 courses since that was the only option to be able to chose you courses.  When we got there they told us it was a fixed menu.  So a lot of items we could not eat, the other ones were not good and the food presentation was very poor.   Also it was very expensive.  Btw the restaurant was empty.

We stayed at the Dwarika’s Hotel in Kathmandu on the front end of a Trekking vacation in the Himalayas.  Clean, modern rooms with fantastic architecture throughout.  Phenomenal service by an attentive and helpful staff. The courtyard offers a peaceful and beautiful sanctuary from the noise and congestion of the third world developing urban hustle and bustle only yards away on the outside of the hotel.  Large spacious rooms. Good food. Beautiful pool and bar. Likely the best hotel in Kathmandu.  Highly recommended. I will stay here again, without reservation, if I ever return to Kathmandu.

The hotel was a surprise once entering.  A huge courtyard gives a medieval, but comfortable feel.  There were plenty of open areas to sit in or eat.  The food was well served and exotic to our midwestern tastes, but we loved it.  The hotel room was large, comfortable with many amenities.  A perfect escape for a few days.

Tarika was like stepping into Narnia. From the chaos of the street outside to the serenity inside, it was like another world. Staff is exceptionally attentive. The rooms are elegant and unique. The courtyard is magnificent. It is like a living museum. Everyone should try the Mako Japanese restaurant in addition to the Krishnarpan, both were wonderful. We highly recommend the hotel. We also stayed at the sister property in Dhulikhel. The property in Kathmandu is much more luxurious while the mountain top property is more About activities like singing, bowls, hiking, and meditation.

Beautiful hotel with big, comfortable rooms with heating. A family of 4 (2 kids) can easily fit. Enjoyed our stay. However, check the charges, eg: the airport transfers before signing the bill. We were being overcharged but was rectified after pointing it out.

Everything about this hotel is absolutely wonderful. The architecture, the staff, the food, the rooms....all wonderful. We never wanted to leave the premises! Our room was spacious and there are lots of places in the common areas to sit and relax. The library bar was warm and cozy. Dinner at the Nepalese restaurant was a truly unique experience. The staff could not do enough for us .

Amazing experience!! We loved the food and most of all the service! Lovely people, I highly recommend. Dwarika is also a must if you’re in Nepal. We did the 6 courses so that we were able to eat everything but it was still very filling. Every dish is well thought of

Was blown away when I entered the property at how peaceful and beautiful it was. After spending 12 days trekking this was a nice repose before returning back home. Despite the bustle of the city all around it, it is really quiet inside. The architecture is all traditionally inspired by Nepalese culture. There are great restaurants on site, too. The only reason I give it 4 and not 5 stars is I found the bed to be too firm - after 2 weeks in teahouses I was craving something more comfortable.

Beautiful architecture and exceptional facility!  One of my most favourite hotels. Everything our group needed - well appointed rooms, lots of space for informal meetings, wide choice of food and good pool/fitness area. Highly recommend

On arrival you are welcomed in a peaceful garden and the hotel building and design is a reflection on old Nepal. Whilst the building is new many antique elements were included like old doors and window frames. Antiques everywhere. My room was spacious, comfortable and thoughtful bathroomamenities. They grow a lot of food in their own farm, delicious! There are shops, pool, spa and several restaurants to chose from! Service was attentive, courteus and prompt. I loved the place!

Highly inspired by the Kathmandu's rich Newari culture and lifestyle, the hotel is no less than an architectural museum or better said a replica of an old Malla styled Palace. The restaurant serves organic food and is very clean and hygienic. Highly recommended if you wish to experience Nepal and its vibrant culture.

My second visit here and I was not disappointed.   Gorgeous place, impeccable service, very Nepali atmosphere.  They have been hard hit by COVID and now by the monsoon season, so need more guests!  Please consider staying here, it is unforgettable!

Stayed 3 nights at the hotel and were upgraded. Rooms are very spacious with amenities available,  drinks, and coffee/ tea selection.  Breakfast selection was excellent with staff very attentive and helpful. Had a few drinks at the Fusion bar, but I didn't have dinner at the hotel. Overall, it is a good location not too far away from the airport. Staff are friendly and helpful.

Krishnarpan restaurant 6 course menu was excellent. Ram Pudasaini the bar manager was great in giving us good cocktails. Overall great experience just soaking in the atmosphere. Highly recommended restaurant and bar.

We stayed at Dwarika’s for three nights to celebrate my father’s birthday.  It was nothing short of magical. Make sure you get a Junior suite, it was truly a stunning room. The service and hospitality were the best I’ve experienced! Breakfast and the Bar deserve special mention and so does the entire property!You can walk out and a few minutes you are in Pashupatinath UNESCO site. But once inside the facility you will not want to leave. I would highly recommend Dwarika as a perfect stay, short or long!

We stayed at Dwarika’s twice - once on our way to Pokhara and our Himalayan trek, and again on our way back. Our stays were borderline magical - the hotel itself is utterly beautiful and a peaceful and cool refuge from bustling Kathmandu. The rooms were comfortable, beautiful, immaculately clean, and full of amenities. The staff were, without exception, friendly, caring, and attentive. We were very sad to leave, and hope to come back someday.

Amazing service at reception upon our arrival! The Room was fresh, clean and modern. Great location as it's walking distance from cafés, restaurants, bars, parks and shops. Had great time at this place.

I had a very quick visit to the dwarika's I ordered a lamb shank and dwarika's bliss. Food and drinks was awesome, I love the ambience and nepali architecture which represent nepali heritage, culture and artifacts. I wish to spend 1 night in this beautiful property.

Lovely hotel, I stayed as part of a holiday tour. I arrived a day earlier then the rest of the group and I felt completely at home. Lovely surroundings - splendid room and good food.  The facilities are good too.  The staff were very friendly and attentive.

Fantastic hotel.  I am so happy I chose this oasis of a hotel.  Beautiful and peaceful room and grounds.  Outstanding service.  I spent 2 nights here prior to a trek and 1 night to follow.  I also loved the little bar area- I had several fun evenings chatting with staff over a martini!

A classic boutique hotel centrally located in Katmandu.  Older but very elegant.  Rooms are large and well appointed and maintained. The pool and spa is great and there is a choice of 3 restaurants on property.  Food was excellent.  We totally enjoyed out stay.  Very unique and relaxing.  Easy to walk around nearby streets.

Beautiful hotel in the center of Kathmandu. We were here to go to Everest and the hotel made the lodging experience amazing. Very safe hotel with a lot of security and a very good restaurant. There is a very nice pool in the middle of one of the courtyards. There’s a few cool shops inside the hotel. The rooms are nice but the tub was a little questionable as it’s under the floor level. I’m pretty young but if I was older this could have been an issue.

Kathmandu is so busy it such a nice relaxing feeling coming to the hotel. The staff are exceptional and friendly. The rooms are very large and beds a super comfortable. Don’t miss the dinner at the Nepalese restaurant! Fix 6 course meal with great service. The restaurant for buffet breakfast and all day dinning was wonderful too. Highly recommend this hotel!

Sublime - magical - best massage therapist ever. Such friendly staff, delicious breakfast options, beautiful rooms and architecture. Great location for the airport and all the rest of points of interest. Cannot recommend enough - the oasis in the middle of the craziness of Kathmandu

Excellent service 24/7, beautiful cultural hotel, great diversified food & you won't feel like going out. I loved the decor & the board games here and there. Breakfast was delicious, whole the dinner at the Nepalese restaurant was amazing.

We've stayed at Dwarika's one or two days every time we've visited Nepal (4 times). It is a beautiful haven in the mania that Kathmandu can be. Mr Dwarika rescued lots of remarkable wooden artifacts, from ruined buildings and incorporated them, with information about their history, in the lovely hotel buildings which are arranged around a courtyard. There's a lovely small pool and trees and flowers fill the courtyard. The food is second-to-none! It's right near the airport although not so handy for the main shopping area of Thamel.

We went here twice for dinner.Outdoor by the pool and inside with traditional floor seating.The service, food and decor were all amazing.The scenery here is unreal. Such a beautiful place that can also be quite intimate and romantic.Such a unique experience!

This was a fantastic hotel!  Everyone who worked here was sooo nice!  Our rooms were lovely, and little treats were left for us nightly.  The food  in the restaurant was delicious.  And the huge patio area with music was incredible!  We even ate a meal there.

It's just hard for me to really express the beauty of this hotel. What a grand building this is. So much antiques, arts and architectures within the vicinity. Cannot wait to stay in this hotel again, my favorite of all time.

What a great hotel- beautiful property, great food, excellent staff. I would have loved to have stayed longer. It also has interesting shops. Although the renovation of the property is fairly recent it seems to belong to an earlier time.It is truly an oasis in a busy city.

Superb in every respect.Greeted on arrival and given welcome sash and drink. Everything in the room explained then a historical tour of the hotel.Traditional nepali dinner was excellent.They staff are simply wonderful.The suite was perfect and very comfortable. Highly recommend.

We stayed at wonderful hotels on our trip to India and Nepal,  but this was one of my very favorites! I loved the atmosphere and ambiance. We really enjoyed the restaurant. Our meals were delicious and beautifully presented. I would definitely stay here again!

This place is beyond phenomenal, and I could not advise it more. The service is perfect and the food and accommodations are beyond any expectations. From the first step, everything is extraordinary and we cannot wait to come back!

Extraordinary experience! The food was outstanding and the staff were kind, helpful and accommodating. You must come to this restaurant if you are in Kathmandu. It has been a lovely, memorable dinner to celebrate my daughters birthday and definitely hope to come again!

It is a calm and peaceful place in the busy city. I enjoyed our stay. Especially we are impressed by the Japanese restaurant in this hotel.  Great food and service. I am impressed by Sadhimi and Nikujyaga. All foods are delicious. Appreciate service by Mako-san. She was a very nice person. Thank you very much. We would like to return to this hotel in the near future.

Amazing massage, very relaxing. This massage is very good and thorough. Felt like a truly unique experience that I would definitely want to do again. I suggest this massage for anyone staying in Nepal. Specifically, the oil massage is really great.

Words cannot describe what I lived through at Dwarika's on Sat April 25th--the day the earthquake hit Kathmandu.  The beautifully decorated bedroom will forever be etched in my mind--as it became moving, almost fluid as the quake hit.  While the hotel is a gem for many reasons, I want to post about the incredible staff and owners of Dwarika.  The hotel suffered a significant amount of damage.  Throughout the horrifying day and night, they did whatever they could to care for us...when we were all so scared and saddened for their country, family and loved ones.  We saw the pain and suffering on their faces, yet their kindness and love continued to show through.  Dwarikas is special for many reasons, but what makes it what it truly is has to do with the staff inside... My greatest respect and gratitude goes to everyone at Dwarika's and all of our love and prayers are with you during the most difficult time.  I will for sure return.

Ho avuto la fortuna e la gioia di soggiornare alcune notti in questo meraviglioso albergo alcuni anni or sono: indimenticabile e perfetto: Stanza grandissima arredata con estremo gusto come tutta la struttura. Un 'oasi di pace nel caos della capitale

A friend of mine bought a wedding gift for us and he left it in the room before heading out for lunch. When we got back from lunch, the room had been made by the housekeeping and we realised that the gift was missing!! When we called the manager to look into it, he spent two days looking into it and he claimed that the staff would never steal items from guest's rooms. He was implying that we would lie about such a thing, when we almost paid close to USD400/night/room and we stayed there for 3 nights (3 rooms) spending almost USD4000. You wouldn't think to keep a gift in safe deposit box when you're staying at such a "prestige" hotel.Complete disgrace to the hotel. The least he could have done was made up the loss gift.Would NOT recommend anyone to stay at this overpriced and unsafe hotel.

My wife and I checked into this beautiful hotel less than 4 hours before the earthquake that devastated this wonderful country struck.  It is impossible to fully describe the maelstrom of this tragic event.  Words do not do it justice; it can only be viscerally experienced to understand its overwhelming effect.  Within minutes of the initial shock, the entire staff from owner to housekeeper created a calm in the eye of this storm.  We all knew that while we were in a foreign land, we were safe; that we had people who would protect us.And while words cannot describe the actual quake, there are words that do describe the response of the entire staff from owner to housekeeper.  It started with Ambika Shrestha, the 85 year-old matriarch of the Shrestha family which owns the hotel, who calmly sat in the midst of her guests throughout the entire ordeal as her daughter, Sangita, demonstrated unparallelled leadership as she directed her dedicated staff with absolutely stunning poise, grace, and competence.  Sangrita’s performance under pressure was flawless.  Never once did she raise her voice.  Her presence conveyed a confidence that allowed us all to take a deep breath, and realize that we were going to be fine because she and her mother were not going to let anything prevent that from happening.The hotel staff, cooks, housekeepers and groundsmen, all of whom were personally touched by this catastrophe, subordinated their personal interests and provided us with comfort and protection from the elements.  After spending our first night under a cloudy, and sometimes wet Kathmandu sky, we awoke to a prepared breakfast, along with toothpaste brushes and toothpaste.  Housekeepers made our outdoor beds.  Generators kept cell phones charged.  And it was all done with a matter of fact precision that made it clear that yes, we were going to be all right even as our stay extended another 36 hours.I cannot possibly express our appreciation to all at the Dwarika’s for their concern, support, comfort, and kindness as they balanced the losses that they, their families and country undoubtedly experienced with a collective commitment to their guests.  We were blessed to have been in their company during this tragedy, and can only hope that better days remains ahead for them and all whom we left behind in Nepal.Joe Burke, Wellesley, Massachusetts

I had been to this hotel in 2012, 2014 and now this year.  Arrival in Nepal was normal and I spent my first night at Dwarika's with no problem at all.  The next day we flew to Badrapur and then on to Ilam and finally Dobate for the Red Panda Network project.  Whilst up in the hills the earthquake struck.  We were very lucky.  Somehow we made it back to Kathmandu as planned on the Monday.  We did not know what to expect when arriving at Dwarika's....  We were greeted by a remarkable lady, the owner Mrs Ambica Shrestha, who was in full charge of everything despite the obvious state of flux.  In the circumstances the staff were incredible considering some of them were sleeping in the open in Kathmandu.  They put all those within the confines of the hotel first.  The hotel itself had barely suffered any damage but then it had been properly built.  My room was impeccable but was minus hot water (a minor detail given the circumstances).   The restaurants were out of commission but we were all given as much local food as we could eat in one of the courtyards.  Thank heavens the weather was dry.  The staff then set up beds and duvets in one of the courtyards with an awning and lanterns.  The aftershocks were still very powerful and for security reasons it was best we all slept outside.  I then spent the nest few days there before being able to fly out on my scheduled flight on the 3rd May.  The very next day the hot water was back and we were also given a set menu to chose from.  How they managed to put on such good food in the circumstances I have absolutely no idea.  They also managed to produce a yummy chocolate cake on my birthday.  Mrs Shrestha and her daughter, Sangita Shrestha Einhaus, were omnipresent, seeing to everything from officials from embassies and their young nationals waiting to be repatriated to looking after relief teams and film crews.  Most of all they were part of the Business and Professional Women of Nepal and spent part of their time organizing relief in the shape of basic food parcels for far flung villages.  All in all given the appalling circumstances this place was a haven and run by remarkable women and their staff.  Praises all round.

i found this is run by ruling class family that has pillaged nepal for centuries. too decadent that they live high off the hog while so many people suffer in this country, really suffer!if you like hanging out with rich and uppity then this is for you, but don't expect much culture other than the superficial outer structures.

A dream came true! Waited four years to finally have the opportunity to visit this stunning property and it definitely did not disappoint. The rooms are out of this world beautifully designed in a luxury Nepali way. Staff is well trained to make you feel at ease and comfortable. The hotel design is incredible, you must see it for yourself to believe it! Highly recommended!

The hotel is as you can see in the pictures is beautiful, real traditional Nepalese luxury. But what makes it special is it's people I would spend days looking for words to be fair when describing them and trust me there are no words! We arrived there a day before the earthquake and we experienced the real hospitality, where the guests are the main priority and there are no problems that couldn't be solved immediately. We were served 5-star food with a genuine smile and we never had to ask for anything, they literally expected our needs.During the earthquake we were up in the mountains and our hotel collapsed, when back in Dwarika's exhausted and scared we asked to check out and go to the airport, they could have got rid of us, instead they asked to stay and informed us that the airport was closed. They took very good care of us, stayed up the whole night preparing food and beds for all of us and making sure we were all safe and comfortable. Regarding the damage, there was no serious damage that hotel is really strong so there is nothing to worry about. This is Definitely the best hotel I ever stayed in and I highly recommend it and Nepal as a country as well, it's not only about the incredible Himalayas but this country is special by it's people. A special thank you to all the hotel staff you guys are AMAZING! I wish you all the best and God bless Nepal!

first of all, you need to understand that this hotel does not follow normal conventions for 4/5 star hotels - it h as after been built in many places from reclaimed wood and structures from around the city; it looks ancient but is only about 60 years old or so. the rooms are terrific and the general ambience around the interior cloistered walls is wonderful, relaxing and indulgent. Ive been lucky to visit here many times before but what has struck me recently is how much Krishnarpan restaurant has declined. it is becoming a parody of itself and instead of promoting the best of local cuisine is now becoming a sad, tired but expensive eating joint that supposedly celebrates culinary heritage but there's no heart here any more and all the 'actors' are simply going through their lines. Worst of all though was the spa- dreadful; if you are male and book a spot you are not made aware that only male on male spa treatments are available until you get there and have signed all the paperwork committing you to a treatment. There are no niceties, no tea beforehand nor afterwards , no drinks, no relaxation area and none of the care one expects from a spa in a 5 star hotel. if the management should ever read this; go to the Hotel Tibet in Kathmandu and try their spa - its half the price of yours but ten times better. take your staff too so that they can see what makes a great spa experience. Back in Dwarikas, the bar area is nice and is manned literally by a number of staff who are eager to help- no problem here. So try Dwarikas and see what you think- there are better hotels in this amazing city but Dwarikas should really be punching way above its weight and is currently a disappointing trip. I'm hoping to revisit the city later in the year and won't be staying here but shall drop by for a drink. I hope they can rediscover their passion for excellence throughout.

Need I say more? Two of our travellers got food poisoning from their restaurant and one of our rooms had a broken air conditioning. The front desk did nothing to help except to say open a window! Run don't walk from this poorly run relic! Also, staff has attitude as compared to warm and friendly Napalese we experienced while sight seeing.

Nepal. Kathmandu. Dwarika. Three words that we will never forget. We came in this country to accompany our son to spend a three weeks period in a humanitarian camp. He joined a group of volunteers that give help to children whose families were left in distressed condition by the heartquake of a few years ago. We took the opportunity to spend a few days in the capital of Nepal, where we had never been before. So we were prepared to find a complex situation, but was not exactly as we thought. First of all we have been surprised by how the natural chaos of this city is pervaded by a kind of positive energy. Nepalese people are special. They all emanates a kind feeling towards others. Everywere you go you never feel insecure. They need help in any aspect of the practical life, but they generously give their heart anytime. It is not easy to describe this feeling you have anywhere you go, but believe me it is like if the people here love you as you are part of their family. And with the people at the Dwarika’s Hotel you have the same feeling. This hotel it has been conceived by a very sophisticated person, capable to harmoniously concentrate in a single location all the structural elements of the Nepalese culture and spirituality. And what it surprises it is how being guest of this hotel prepares to positively embrace the complexity of a town like Kathmandu. The enlightened vision of the founder brought him to create a place where a foreign person can leave at the reception the stress brought from abroad, so that when you exit the door of this mansion for the first time you already have a Nepalese spirit in your heart. This hotel is run with a top class international hotelier culture, but preserving all the elements of the local culture. No compromises has been made, and this is what makes this place so special. It feels familiar, but not because you find the aseptic five stars service and elements of the usual international chains of hotels. It feels familiar because the nepalese staff makes you feel to be part of a family. They are trained professionally, but from each of them you can get an individual genuine kind attitude. Like all the people in Nepal naturally do. So if you are planning to go to Kathmandu and you look for a top quality hotel don’t hesitate to book a room in this hotel. We spent four nights in an Heritage junior suite. A room with a lot of space: three sofas, a dining area, a huge bathroom with shower, a bath tub, a toilet room, a walk in wardrobe, and a very big four poster bed. Talking about money in general it is not a cheap hotel, even more if compared with the average hotel of the region. But this is not by far an ordinary hotel. This is one of the best hotel in the world. Have any doubt? Well, if you can afford stay at least one night in the Royal suite (it is expensive, but not more than an ordinary junior suite in a five star hotel in New York or London). What you get it is nothing less that the regal experience of 14th century Malla King of Nepal. It is set over three floors, and it has a huge private rooftop terrace with an incomparable view of the Himalayan peaks. We tried it, and trust me you do really feel like a king. And once in a life it is an experience to be done. In conclusion, this hotel may appear to be a paradox considering the level of poverty that this region of the world still accuses. But it represent just one of the doors through which you may enter in this wonderful country, and it is the door used by the aristocracy. Therefore there are many other ways to have an accommodation in Nepal, but if you want to have a touch of the contradictions that have made the history of this country you don’t have any other choice that staying at the Dwarika’s hotel. And so living Kathmandu outside and inside the walls of this special hotel you will then have the best of the two deep opposites of the wonderful Nepal's heart.

I have been tardy penning my travel experiences  (the last entry was 2008!) but my recent stay at Dwarika persuades me to open this page and share.I have just returned from an 8 night stay at this unique heritage hotel.  Everything, from front desk reception, to the restaurants, souvenir shop, and the spa, was professionally orchestrated with a uniquely personal touch.  The restaurants did not have a laundry list of items to choose, but every dish we ordered we did not have qualms to savour them again in the next meal.  It was in fact so good that we ended up taking almost every meal in the hotel, and inviting our Nepali friends to dine with us too.  Special commendation to the Toran staff who remembered our quirks after a meal and served us to our requirements without much of a reminder.  They were very much willing to share their thoughts and knowledge too.  I have learned a lot about Nepali culture just conversing with them.The spa messuers were excellent too, and definitely a must after a day of trekking.  We commented that the room was a bit cold to our liking despite the air conditioning, and they immediately placed additional electric heater when we next visited.The souvenir shop was like an undiscovered Aladdin's cave situated at the back of the hotel, next to the gym.  We ended up buying most of our souvenirs there, as they not only have a good variety of well curated lcoal products, but the price was no more expensive than the stretches of Thamel area.  And in Thamel area, you will need to haggle intensely for a resoanble price.  Special commendation to the bubbly staff Narendran.  I would say, this man could charm a monkey down a tree and still be well liked.  Speaking to him, friendship is almost immediately bonded.The only shop we did not purchase anything was the cashmere joint.  Although the items were unique, they did not warrant the price tag.Special commendation to Shiva the front office manager.  He could resolve every question and problem we had for him.There were little hiccups here and there during our stay, but none worth mentioning as they were too insignificant.Over all, a great stay.  If we ever return to Nepal, we will not look elsewhere.

We were in and out of this hotel over a two week trip to Bhutan, Nepal, and Tibet four different times. We highly recommend, but I am writing this review to commend their service on April 25, 2015 after the 7.9 magnitude earthquake. With no electricity, running water, and damage to the hotel, the management and staff of this hotel were able to expertly make guests comfortable overnight in their courtyard, and keep us safe, warm, and fed. Kudos to excellent and thoughtful service in a disaster!

Dwarikas is a must visit hotel although be prepared to pay dearly for the experience.  The settings and rooms are amazing although little touches are overlooked such as the bedding is naff for such a quality hotel. Bar food was underwhelming for this class of hotel.Traditional Nepalese Restaurant set menu at circa $50/person with their wine at low tables.  Not bad.WiFi in the bar free otherwise $12/day and did not work very well.  Thought this was an insult given their prices.Summary - worth the experience but incredibly expensive.

We decided to switch from Yak and Yeti to Hotel Dwarika for two nights given the reviews we saw online and tripadvisor.  The hotel is architecturally lovely and definitely an oasis from busy Kathmandu.  We were glad we had a chance to stay here for those experiences.  However, location is not great and realistically the hotel courtyard is very small.  Wifi is not free and very temperamental. Because of its location, we ate most of our meals in the hotel and that was very expensive. Overall, the service and experience was good but not great for a 5 star hotel.

As a self proclaimed 5 star hotel, their service and attitude was pathetic and left a lot to be desired. Ambience was nice in hotel but everything was a "no" with no alternatives or adjustment. I travel about 42 weeks a year (>300,000 airline miles a year) and stay in 100s of hotels. Service and attitude is what drives hospitality and Dwarika was extremely poor. We were returning from out trek upto Everest base Camp. The spa had very limited choices and people,with very limited knowledge.

Dwarikas is by far my favorite hotel in Kathmandu. If you are looking for a boutique style hotel with all of the luxuries of a 5 start hotel this is your place. The courtyard is simply beautiful with all of the reclaimed architectural elements. For a very special dinner, Krishnarpans is an experience that shouldn't be missed.After trekking, there is nothing like arriving at a little oasis of beauty in the middle of the city. The spa offers a variety of treatments, including a trekkers massage. The other stunning feature of the hotel is the swimming pool surrounded by covered daybeds where there is simply no better place to really relax.I have stayed here on three different occasions, and have always had wonderful service. In a city that is so full of activity, Dwarikas is like a little island in paradise. I look forward to my next return!

I only stayed one night bit would go back just to stay in this incredible room in a wonderful hotel with so much ambience.The restaurant food was not to my liking and the breakfast was average.The service was not special either ..But that room......i didnt want to leave

My wife and I stayed here for the three nights just past.  While Kathmandu as a city leaves much to be desired, Dwarika's is an oasis of calm and historical elegance.  It is appointed throughout with artifacts, furnishings, and architecture that evoke insights into the country's culture.  Our room (403) on the top floor was not a suite but was very spacious.  Brick, stone, carved wood, beamed ceiling, good bed and quiet.  Staff is very friendly and attentive, quick to respond to requests for more pillows or help with baggage.  Breakfast is fine -- eggs cooked to order, service efficient.  We dined at their Nepalese specialty restaurant (while the whole diplomatic corps was supping in the banquet hall nearby) one night and were impressed.  It's a bit expensive compared to another restaurant we visited the night before with a somewhat similar menu, but beautifully presented by staff in gorgeous local dress.  We really were surprised and delighted by the bar.  Very clubby atmosphere; lots of cozy nooks to  hunker down and sip a scotch.  A nice upstairs with a view of the beautiful swimming pool and a pool table to boot. We were thoroughly pleased with the place.

The real nepali spirit. Stylish and elegant. Huge rooms. We tryied a heritage suite, which was fabulous.This is not a Chain hotel, could be sometimes air conditioning is not perfect or insulation is not the best...but it is exquisite and this is Nepal. All the staff is very attentive and kind.It is a destination itself

My wife and I stayed here after our trek to unwind and enjoy the luxury.  Good:Rooms are excellentProperty is beautiful and well maintainedQuiet and away from all the traffic and noise on the streetBad:Non-existent customer service at the front desk - no "thank you" on departure, no "how was your stay" - they all just seemed poorly trained.  They just threw paper around and never made eye contact or even attempted to smile.  This was true of all of the reception staff whenever you went by. No hello or good morning if you passed by. Restaurant staff was ok - better than the front desk but all very inconsistently trained - some really good, some really bad.Management was poor when we asked to see the manager about something - all very wishy washy and no follow up.Food quality was average.  The Newari restaurant was nice and food was ok.  The Japanese restaurant food was below average.
