The breakfast buffet was adequate but service was lacking generally.TV in the room was horrible and looked to be from the 1980's - poor reception - not a big deal necessarily but when you're paying $400 USD a night, you expect more.Dwarikas can become a true 5 star with appropriate training and diligence.  Learn from those who train the staff at the Oberoi, Leela and the 4 seasons!!  Shame really as you can see the effort that's gone into building the property - now it just needs to be managed well.

We stayed at this hotel for two nights after spending 2 weeks in Nepal.  It was our last hotel before leaving for home so we saw it as a kind of resting place and as a nice quiet end to our busy trip.  It is indeed a beautiful hotel but I have a few issues with it.  For one thing, I'm not a fan of a bathroom with no door.  Yes, the toilet area has a door but the bath and shower area are wide open and not private at all.  Since I travel with a friend, not a spouse, I find this just a bit annoying.  I'm accustomed to privacy in the bath/shower area and found this a bit bothersome.  Also, the door locking situation is a bit strange.  There is a big padlock on the outside of the room door and there are two deadbolts on the inside.  Now, picture a scenario where one person wants to be out of the room and the other wants to take a nap inside the room.  There is no good locking situation.  Either the person inside is locked in if the padlock is on OR the person outside is locked out if the deadbolts are on. This hotel obviously assumes that every traveler is traveling with a spouse and that both parties will always want to be in or out of the room at the same time.  There is no option for any other scenario.  I found this a bit difficult.  Yes, the hotel is beautiful and the breakfast is great; the pool is beautiful and the lounging areas are wonderful but I wish they would fix those other pesky situations that would keep me from coming back here again.

My visit was back in 2009 (Aug2014 is chosen simply because my date of visit was not available) Traveling to Nepal alone was an unforgettable experience. The long journey was well the spiritual journey I came for. The hotels courtyard is what resonates in my memory. The people, air, plants were amazing. The smells from the wood that the hotel is built on even has a special essence to it.Sipping tea at the courtyard garden felt like a dream, everything was an attack to the senses. I cannot simply say enough about the hotel, the room, the food- which I adore now. One would be assured of a pleasant experience.

I visited Nepal almost 10 years ago and Dwarika's seemed the best choice (April 2014 is chosen simply because the year of my visit was not available in the pull menu).  The hotel is actually better than shown in the photos. Staff, premises, food, cleanness, decoration...simply amazing! Owners did a great job preserving traditional nepalese architecture and art! Like an open air museum. I could spend hours drinking tea in the garden while my sister was impatiently waiting to explore the "outer" world.I don't know how much it costs nowadays and whether I could afford it. If you can't stay there then visit one of the restaurants or have a drink in the garden. You'll remember it for years!

By far nicest and very interesting place in KTM. The architecture is gorgeous and it is nice that the owners have made a conscious Decision to preserve  local items . An oasis of quiet after a busy day in a busy city. Breakfast excellent and fun to try a free yoga class.

We arrived at Dwarika's during the earthquake. Preceding posts have beautifully put into words the feelings generated by such tragedy, as well as the very special treatment offered by this marvelous hotel to its guests. I would like to point out how deeply touched we have been by the selflessness and generosity of both the staff, guides, drivers, and the family of owners, Sangita, her nephew and her lovely mother, who kindly shared their home with us. They all refused to charge for their services, provisions, cell phones, even if, as we are aware, the way they made us feel taken care of and protected was absolutely priceless. We didn't get to visit sites and monuments in Nepal this time, but we had the unique opportunity to make acquaintance with the noble soul of its people. It was a spiritual and unforgettable experience. My profound gratitude and admiration.

from the outside it doesnt look like much but as soon as you pass through the front door you step into a world of calm and beauty completely divorced from the dusty noisy streets outside. The hotel is made up of several buildings each of which has been built using materials salvaged from demolished buildings. So there are all sorts of door and  window styles mostly in wood and the whole place has an antique feel even though it is new. Each room and each building has its own character. If you need Four Seasons pristine fittings this is not for you but if you like charm and comfort it is the best. The compound also has restaurants and bars which based on our experience were far better than anything in town.Everything works, the staff are lovely and after a night's rest you feel serene and recharged to see the sites.

I stayed 2 nights at this hotel with my husband, after 2 nights in the beautiful Dwarika's Resort in Dhulikel. If I had had a choice, I would have visited Kathmandu first (as it is a dusty, noisy city), followed by some peaceful time at the Resort in Dhulikel. As many Tripadvisor members have said, this hotel is truly a sanctuary within Kathmandu. After a day of sightseeing, breathing in the polluted air, and listening to the non-stop sounds of honking car horns, my husband and I were relieved to return to the beautifully designed hotel courtyard for a drink and some peace. You can tell that this hotel is a labour of love, and I am glad that its founder had the foresight to preserve all the antique Nepal wood carvings and other heritage pieces, which are now thoughtfully incorporated into the design of the hotel. Both the public spaces and rooms are beautiful, and I thoroughly enjoyed sitting in the courtyard in the mornings and evenings, admiring the architecture and watching all the people, pigeons and dogs! The owners of the hotel also live on the property, and keep several well-fed and adorable dogs.I was a bit wary of the level of food hygiene in Kathmandu, so we ate all of our meals at Dwarika's. No problems at all there, and food is generally not bad. I would recommend one dinner at their Nepalese restaurant Krishnarpan, which serves 6 to 22 courses covering foods from different parts of Nepal.At the time of this entry, Nepal had just suffered one of the worst earthquakes in its history. I sincerely hope that the Dwarika's staff and property are doing fine.

Everything was perfect....the room, the architecture, the food., the service.....it  as a pleasure to come back here after sightseeing and shopping.   Wouldn't change a thing..Stay here if you can....  Worthy it

Right in busy Katmandu...this place is amazing! Restored old buildings and added buildings that look as old as the old! Beautiful rooms. Personnel were very kind and generous in their time and service. Being saluted each time we came/went was an extra touch😃While keeping the character of an old palace, Dwarika was able to meet all my expectations and more! The open areas were grand and comfortable. A lovely oasis amidst the chaos of Katmandu!People placed chess and had tea, ate in the open courtyard and a brass game with tigers and goats...can't remember the exact name and for sure cannot spell it!All staff were attentive and welcoming....'Naste' the word for every day !

Beautiful building, innthe midle of Kathmandu ...as soon as you enter you forgot all the noisy dusty road outside! Room are nice, some nicer than othre one and difficult to know which one they will give you, missing a nice duvet , they only have blanket which are not the best in a cold night. Heating is not the best, doesn't work very well. Room are sometimes a bit dark. Lovely garden with good restaurants inside the hotel. Lovely tea. Bed are not very comfortable, hard .

Si es un lugar 📍Paradisíaco en pleno Kadmandu  🇳🇵lleno de vida y atenciones con sus áreas 🕊🕊🌳🌲🌳🌳🦜🦜y Tranquiladad un Oasis de ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️                                     Para mi no a sido un hotel 🏨 es un ‼️Hogar ‼️🏠por el trato de su personal cordial y su servicio a 🤵🏻 Tika Ram que sugirió muy buen menú 🧾🍽    La Arquitectura Artesanal que han logrado rescatar y fomentar para seguir dando identidad local 💯 👌🏼Hace de este lugar un OASIS 🌲🌳🕊            Y nuestro agradecimiento por sus atenciones y el pastel 🍰 que a tenido para con nosotros               Doña: ‼️AMBICA SHRESTHA ‼️                             🇳🇵Namaste 🙏🏼 Mima y Eduardo Ochoa 15 Abril 2019Morelia, México 🇲🇽

We felt really privileged during the stay at the hotel. Staff, location, ambience, food.....everything was great.Also, we would like to mention that service provided by Naha (reception) and Yanu (restaurant) was nothing short from superb!

Dwarika's Hotel in Kathmandu is a beautiful respite in an intense city.  The hotel is built around a courtyard with lovely sitting areas, fountains and pool.  My husband and I stayed here one night before going to Chitwan National Park and again after our park visit. During our stay the food, service, and room were all 5 star.  The hotel itself was built with traditional Nepal craftsmanship from reclaimed lumber and carved wood pieces.  Our room was large with plenty of seating, a desk area, closet and large bathroom with two sinks, step down tub, and separate shower.  The hotel has several high end dinner-only restaurants plus a 24 hour restaurant (with courtyard seating) and room service.  They also have a very nice lounge/bar with drinks starting around $12 U.S.  Dwarika's staff was very pleasant and helpful.  We left laundry to be done while we were away and it was ready and waiting for us on our return.  The staff was also helpful in retrieving an item I left at Chitwan (no small task).  In general they were very accommodating.  My only, minor, complaint, is that our bed was not as comfortable as we would have liked.  Overall it was a joy to be there and I highly recommend this hotel.  Dwarika's is one of my favorite hotels anywhere.

I designed a 15-day customized luxury tour of the Himalayas (Nepal, Tibet & Bhutan).  We only stayed in 5-star hotels on the tour.  We stayed at Dwarika's on two different dates, checking in & out while traversing through the other countries.The entrance to the hotel off the busy street did not impress.  There was not much of an entrance, too tight.  I liked the courtyard that greeted us as we stepped inside the hotel though.  I liked that there were a few restaurants & shops within the property.  Unfortunately, these were the only part of the hotel that were interesting to me.  I did not get the luxurious feeling in this hotel.  My comfort level here was lacking.  It was my least favorite of all the hotels we stayed at on the tour.Check-In -- greeting was cordial & efficient the first time we checked in.  There was a big group checking in at the same time we did on our second stay.  Since we arrived earlier than the check-in time, we waited.  After a while, we decided to eat outside the hotel to kill time.  Perhaps the wait was good because our rooms were bigger the second time around.Bellhop service -- was very good, courteous & attentive.  We left our luggages at Dwarika's twice and they were there waiting for us when we came back from the other countries.  They kept them safely for us.Decor theme -- Nepalese, exotic & very nice.  Loved it.Room -- Outdated.  Sizes & configuration are all different.  We stayed 2 different dates and got 2 different rooms in each stay.  Needs more light in the room.  Some rooms are noisier than others.  Best to get a room facing the courtyard for less noise.  My friends stayed on the 4th floor and were not able to sleep because woodpeckers were busy pecking on the roof at night.  It depends on which 4th floor room though because the others who stayed on the same floor did not hear the woodpeckers.  They have a safe, hair dryer, internet & air condition.  No iron or ironing board but you can call and they'll bring it to your room.  Bathroom --  Too dark.  Toiletries were lacking.  They do not have conditioners.  The shampoo is too runny like water and no smell.  It did not feel good to take a shower.Cleanliness -- very good but I cannot explain why I felt "gritty" while staying at Dwarika's.  Cleaning & restaurant staff -- very goodRestaurants -- they have a few to choose from.  The decor of all of them was classy.  I am not into Indian or Nepalese food so I cannot say how good they were but we had a fun evening at Krishnarpan because of the ambiance & company.Location -- not too far from city center and quite close to Tribhuvan airport.  There is nothing outside the hotel worth walking around for.Dwarika's is well-known in Nepal and scored high amongst reviewers.  For this reason, I had to try it.  We also stayed at Hyatt Regency for 4 nights at the beginning of our tour before our stays at Dwarika's.  I was more comfortable at Hyatt.  I am glad that I tried both.

It is a very sweet hotel, but a bit overpriced. Additionally, in late afternoon they have very loud music playing to welcome guests. It is loud enough to prevent you from having a conversation in your room.

This is simply a stunningly beautiful hotel.No detail is spared on the interior design filled with hand carved wooden windows and pillars, offering a truly authentic nepalese experience.  Staff are exceptional ( especially reception who go out of their way to help you, and know every detail of your stay).  Nothing was too difficult ( including lending my husband a pair of gloves for our trek that they had brought from home).  Fluffy pillows, hard pillows, soft pillows, extra towels, ... we had to stop ourselves from having a competition to test them as to what wasnt achievable.Would highly recommend.  They have a sister travel agency who organised tours and treks for us.  (You must have the guide Mark! He was excellent).4 day trip.Day 1... sightseeing in and around kathmandu.  Lunch on rooftop overlooking boudhanath temple.  Visit pashupatinath temple at sun down to watch the cremation rituals.  Hugely moving experience, like varanasi without the hoards.Day 2 - We did sunrise over the himalayas at naggarkot and then hiked to Dhurlikel.  Spectacular.  25k must do.  End up for lunch in the sister Dwarika hotel there which is super pretty ( and you must stay if you have time).  Have the delicious nepali set lunch ... rainbow momo's and currey platter (aloo gobi to die for).  Stop off for a couple of hours in bhaktapur on the way home.  Pick a sunny day.  Drinks in hotel bar.Day 3 - easy heli ride to lukla and everest base camp. (C. $850-1000 per person if u can find another couple to go with).  Stop off at Everest View hotel for tea.   Drinks at phat kath in thamel.Day 4 .... relax in morning,  patan and then shopping in thamel.  Supper at third eye restaurant.Shopping... bhaktapur ... wooden carvings on the streets.Patan ... metal work ... fun masks and statues ...  go north of patan dhurbar square for higher end crafts shops ... south for down n dirty shops filled to the brim with poorly cast bronze and brass objets. Thamel ... best thanka shop is halfway down mandala street, lhs walking up from parytan marg, in the sagarmatha bazaar in thamel,  run by the son of a famous thanka teacher, near the gourmet bakery.  Lovely family and very high quality original designs.Pashminas/cashmere  .... everywhere, buy cheap unless you really know what you are doing ... Warning ... wear a scarf that can cover your nose and mouth in kath and patan as dust/pollution is a nightmare.  Or invest in a mask.  Shame, but it is what it is.

The hotel is basically a UNESCO world heritage site and the owners should be seriously recognized for the work they've done in preserving Nepalese national heritage. The staff is lovely and the rooms are well appointed. Try the 6 course set menu in the restaurant one night for dinner. The food is interesting but not very good - a reflection more on the cuisine of Nepal than the restaurant itself. Only drawback: pigeons! Pigeons were a huge problem all over the city. At the hotel, we were surprised that spikes and fishing line weren't placed as a deterrent. Some areas can't be enjoyed for the fear of being pooped on and other areas are constantly being cleaned of pigeon droppings.

I wrote about this wonderful hotel after my first visit in June 2015. Now, after 6 more visits, I want to commend the management and staff on the attentive and gracious service, the comfort and cleanliness of the bedrooms, and the excellent upkeep of the grounds. This is truly a gem.

To be very honest this hotel helped a lot during my holidays in Nepal. The journey has been difficult , and every night coming back to this small piece of paradise was really a relief. The hotel is stunning, Nepalese architecture , nice garden and pool. The rooms are big , spacious and bright. Very clean. International restaurant and a Nepalese also. Much much nicer that all the others 5 stars international hotels . Strongly recommended.

My second time here and again it didn't disappoint. The service, the size of the rooms, the level of comfort and quality of food and beverage make this a must-do if you're in Kathmandu, particularly if you have spent time in less expensive accommodation on treks or volunteer expeditions. Spend an evening by the fire in the bar, bliss out in the day spa or relax in your spacious room reading, journalling or working before you head home to normality.

I had first heard of Dwarika's from a knowledgable friend, but while both she and the website described its beauty, neither quite convey how magical its experience is.  We were upgraded to a junior suite--each way we turned in the room, there was something lovely to look at--using Nepalese decor with casual elegance.  The service was outstanding--special thanks to Sheba who helped us in a thousand was and to whoever it was helped us pack our voluminous luggage (included a wooden elephant bought at Dwarika's resort in the hills).   Highly recommended visit to shop that sells cashmere pashminas in the courtyard.One more thing to note:  Dwarika's is completely Nepalese owned and managed and has made a refugee camp for a Kathmandu neighborhood ruined in the earthquake.  It is a very good place to spend your money in these difficult times for Nepal.

Beautiful hotel, lovely ethnic decor, unfortunately the personal touch is missing. It also comes as a shock that a hotel in this price range offers free WiFi and breakfast only to guests paying for deluxe rooms.

Touring in Kathmandu is fantastic but intense and exhausting; we were extraordinarily lucky to be staying at this hotel.  You walk into the courtyard and all tensions of the day disappeared : you were in a beautiful setting with wonderfully attentive and caring staff, a lovely spacious room and delicious food.  It is tastefully and lovingly designed with Nepali antiques and treasures that reflect its environs and offer the opportunity to appreciate them in peace.  I would highly recommend to anyone with no hesitations.  Many thanks especially to the concierge named Ruskin.

We loved this hotel from the moment we walked through the doors.  We stayed 3 nights before a trek in the Annapurna foothills and again at the end for 1 night.  Both rooms we had were very comfortable with lots of character.The buildings are all beautiful and the atmosphere quite atmospheric.  Its not a cheap hotel and the restaurants are pricey but the food and service was excellent. A couple of slight negatives - wifi is expensive and the swimming pool, while looking very inviting was freezing cold.  We'd certainly recommend this hotel.

My husband and I have just returned from a 5 night stay at Dwariks's Hotel in Kathmandu.  What a lovely, lovely experience to stay at this special hotel.  Outside is the hustle and bustle of fascinating Kathmandu but as soon as those doors open to the hotel, you are transported to a place of beauty and relaxation.  The staff is amazing!  Each one seemed to know us by name and those smiles were everywhere.  Before we ever arrived, I had the privilege of corresponding with Rojina at the hotel and she was always so punctual and helpful with arrangements for the room as well as for the special dinners.  We tremendously enjoyed the barbeque on Friday night (that is the only night they do it).  We also enjoyed the Napalese dinner at Krishnarpan.  We had the 6 course menu and it was fun.  We had already enjoyed so much curry, etc. during the three days before that it did not seem as unique because we had eaten so many good dishes earlier.  The breakfast buffet was always delicious!!  The staff, especially Ruskill were always available with smiles to help us in any way we wish.  Our room was 408 and it was one of the loveliest rooms we have ever enjoyed.  We are travel agents for a small company and over 20 years, this was one of the loveliest places and rooms we have stayed.  Room 408 is a junior suite and really huge with beautiful view over the courtyard.  We just loved it!!  The hotel is located about 10 minutes from the airport so it was very convenient to catch the early morning flight up to see Mt. Everest.  We had to try for two days to do this, but on the second day, the weather cleared and we were up!  Such fun and they have the flight so well organized so that everyone gets to go forward and view out of the captains' area and each person is seated by a window.  The flight goes one way and returns so that you get to see Mt Everest for sure.  They also sell t-shirts on the plane stating "I did not climb Mt. Everest, but I touched it with my heart."  Sell for 10 USD.  I thought the flight was well worth the money.  We flew on Buddha Air.  Everyone says they are the safest airlines to do this flight seeing trip.  There are still some reservations about safety issues but we risked it and really are happy that we did.  :-)You may pay a little more to stay at Dwarika's Hotel, but it is an experience in itself just to reside here.  If we ever return to Kathmandu, we shall once again look forward to staying at this fairytale hotel.  You will absolutely love it!!

Kathmandu is a bustling city of many faces. This is an oasis in the middle of it all!We arrived after a busy trip in India and were ready for a little break, and the Dwarika's Hotel did not disappoint! It is a beautifully restored Newali complex with authentic and spacious rooms, delicious restaurants and bars to choose from and outside areas that are relaxing and inviting.Everyone was extremely helpful with our arrangements, transfers, and guides of the city.Special Thanks to Alphie ( spelling?) who was friendly, informative and helpful during our stay.It is definitely the place to stay in Kathmandu!

Dwarika's is a special tranquil experience in the midst of chaotic Kathmandu. The mix of architecture, spacious and beautifully decorated rooms, great food and fabulous service combine for a memorable experience. Make sure you try the singing bowl massage. It will help cure whatever ails you. I'd recommend without hesitation.

From the moment we entered the Dwarika's Hotel we knew we were in a most special and Zen like environment... We were greeted with a huge smile by a kind hearted man , Mr. Shiva Devkota, the manager! After our long flight from New York he made us feel most welcome and at home ..assuring us that if  we needed anything at all, he was their to help ...and that he did ,since one of our suitcases were lost and he was able to quickly locate it and have it at our room the following day !!!.We then ventured out to the hotel's cute pub like bar/restaurant ,Fusion bar where we were once again greeted by more lovely smiles, those of Ms.Sujita and Mr.Ram Pudasains who served us a delicious meal and were lots of fun as well,They advised us on all the newest drinks they had to offer .. This entire staff were truly some of the kindest and most  wonderful people we had met throughout our holiday ! We look forward to returning to this true piece of Paradise in NEPAL ...Lauralee Bruce, New York

It is difficult to give this property an overall rating as some aspects are very very good and others are way below acceptable On the plus side the buildings and its gardens are a delight.  The building had been beautifully restored and the rooms are very well appointed with all mod cons. Our Junior Suite is spacious and very well equipped. There are some lovely touches such as a huge range of toiletries including toothbrushes and antiseptic ointment.  We were given a gorgeous chocolate cake and we enjoyed our meal in the Nepalese restaurant. On the minus side, on arrival we decided to have lunch in the pretty courtyard. Two bowls of soup took half an hour to arrive for no obvious reason as there were few customers . There was no apology or explanation for the delay,  The entree was OK and then we waited - and waited - and waited for our bill.  After around 15 minutes of waiting our guide arrived and we expressed our irritation.  He investigated the bill and found it could not be produced as the printer was broken - again no progress report or apology. We then went to our room, which as I mentioned looked beautiful.  However four of the lights were not working. An electrician came quickly and there were a range of explanations including various loose connections.Housekeeping was odd too. Turn down service didn't happen until we requested it at 9.30 as we needed extra bath towels (only two provided) . We were delighted to be left a dish of chocolates by the housekeeper who brought the extra towels. We had eaten more than enough last night so didn't eat them. We were surprised that they disappeared the next day!  Our wifi was free (possibly because we were on a package pre-booked by a travel agent.  The signal is excellent but sadly it is necessary to log in frequently as the wifi disconnected itself if not used for a period of time.Yes, I would return to this hotel again. It is a very special oasis in a bustling city.  But I feel it is let down by its service which is a great pity.

Ho soggiornato una sola notte, al termine del viaggio a Kathmandu.  L' hotel è SUPER TOP! Colazione internazionale con ottima scelta di dolce e salato. La camera ENORME, gran comfort.  Non manca nulla! Squisita la gentilezza e cortesia del personale. Interessanti i massaggi da provare nella SPA.

The first impression of the hotel is it's quite lovely.  Apparently the original owner, Dwarika Das Shrestha, picked up a bunch of architectural carvings in 1950s as people were sawing them off for firewood.  He decided to collect these ancient carvings and constructed a hotel around these architectural elements as people discard them.  Thus the hotel architecturally is a mixture of various styles which can look a bit messy but charming at the same time.Every night around sunset, the hotel has a dancer who would do traditional dance in central courtyard.  I really enjoyed seeing that as it not only reenforced the local culture upon its guests, but also this is a nice way to calm its guests from the hectic Kathmandu right outside the entrance.I stayed in the Heritage Executive Suite which faces the beautiful interior courtyard.  The room obviously can't be compared to Amans or Four Seasons.  It's very rustic.  But everything in the room feels very authentic and not put on.  Everything you need is there; the bed was comfortable; the room is large; the bathroom is almost the same size as the bedroom.  The only complaint I have is I wish bathroom is brighter.  It felt a bit dark especially in the shower area.  I typically like to hang up everything when I check into a hotel room.  Unfortunately the existing clothes rod couldn't take on the weight and fell.  It was quite funny actually.  I ended up requesting clothing racks as I'm sure those will hold weight of several heavy jackets and pants.There are several restaurants available within the Dwarika hotel/ compound.  The Krishnarpan restaurant is a must for someone who's curious about Nepalese food.  From my understanding is that Krishnarpan is one of the best Nepalese restaurant in the city.  In addition, there is a Japanese restaurant called Mako's.  It felt like a neighborhood Japanese restaurant here in the SF Bay Area.  I would say the food is fine. Furthermore, there is a restaurant called Toran.  It basically has some Nepalese food plus other western cuisines.  Among these three restaurants, my favorite is Mako's as it reminded me of typical Japanese food I have at home.  I didn't get a chance to try the Fusion Bar or Kaiser Cafe.I didn't use the pool as it was end of January in Kathmandu.  While I didn't test the water, I assume it's not heated.  I also didn't try the spa.  Although if the spa here is similar to the one at Dwarika's Resort, I would  recommend it.  There is a conglomerate of shops towards the back of the compound.  I think it's probably rented out by the hotel to individual shop owners.  I would say lots of interesting stuff and most look like they have been curated and not junky stuff you find around tourist attraction sites.    Don't expect this place to be luxurious (as in Aman or Four Seasons' way) because it is not.  However, the service standard is as high as any Amans I've been to and I would gladly return to this hotel next time I come back to Kathmandu.If you are interested in a more detail review, click on my profile which will take you to my blog where I have more pictures as well as a video of the sunset dancer!

We stayed here for 1 night at the end of our adventures round Nepal, and wished we could have stayed for longer!So many superlatives that could be used for this incredible property - if you can afford to splurge, then I guarantee you won't be disappointed staying here.The building / grounds are much larger than I pictured them being; there's so much to explore. You can tell how this hotel is a family labour of love over time, and it's so wonderful to stay in such a unique property; such an oasis of calm in the midst of the chaos of Kathmandu a couple of steps away outside the entrance.Rooms: delightful with interesting featuresBeds: incredibly comfyBathrooms: luxurious and spaciousStaff: friendly, welcoming, helpful, efficientBreakfast: the best choice we had in the whole of Nepal by a long wayGym: impressively kitted-out no matter where you are in the worldFree morning yoga: wonderful, with such an entertaining and enthusiastic instructorHotel complex: just incredibleTo be honest I was pretty hesitant before booking this place as it is very expensive, but I'm so glad we did as we had a wonderful 24 hours there and enjoyed our chance to experience this magical property.The only negative is not offering free hotel transfers (MUCH cheaper places in Kathmandu offer this and are much further from the airport, so this is very poor). The hotel is very close to the airport, and it would save guests having the hassle of haggling hard/being ripped off by taxi drivers when you request to be taken to the most expensive hotel in town.
在交通上很方便，雖然價格是加德滿都裡最高的，但與其他開發中國家首都的五星級酒店相比，價格依然實惠。最主要是，旅店內4百多個木雕窗門，現代工匠已難耗費時間去製作，就文化遺產而言，值得入住慢慢品味。雖然，感覺這旅店有想追尋安縵的待客方式，可惜功力不足，還有待加強。

well this is one of the best place to be in has been one of the known place with the renowned newari culture along with luxury. it has been really good to be in and has been doing good into all the services

One of the best, I had never experienced such an Hospitable and friendly staff till now. The Architecture is admirable. Finely designed Executive Suites. Tastey and excellent quality food. Really enjoyed staying at Dwarika's.

Just loved this hotel. Apart from being an oasis amongst the hussle and bussle of Kathmandu it is a quality hotel with large rooms, great restaurants, with high level of service. The decoration using antique wood pieces from Kathmandu is fascinating and truly meets its goal of being a living museum

I stayed recently two days/nights in Dwarika's Hotel in Kathmandu and found this hotel to have the soul of a living culture.  The architectural history and heritage preserved throughout its corridors, rooms, restaurants and patios is an invaluable testimony to the Nepali culture.  Located in a busy area of Nepal's capital city, and within proximity to the airport, the Dwarika's possesses a charm difficult to compare with other unique hotels in Nepal and beyond the country's borders.  Great hospitality permeates the environment at Dwarika's and a peaceful touch of elegance accompanies every moment one spends in this property.  I truly believe every dollar one pays here is worth invested, whether a solo traveller or in groups.  The hotel gift shop has a section, a whole room, with books, a point of distinction that conveys a mission behind the business; the restaurants are varied and serve a variety of foods; the sleeping rooms are uniquely furnished with pieces of carved wood that transport your mind throughout history.  I recommend the Dwarika's even if you can only afford one night.  It is an experience of its own. Do not expect the traditional resort amenities, but be open to cross the tunnel of a spititual journey: do yoga in the mornings, relax by the pool, read the several framed quotes from the founder of this enterprise, experience the cultural events in the patio, or simply walk in silence metitation to enjoy this unique property.

Dwarika's Hotel is a unique place, a real gem inside the busy-noisy-dusty Kathmandu. Step within its walls, and suddenly it becomes quiet - just to let your focus shift to the wooden carvings, antique details, and surrounding greenery. The building as well as the rooms are truly beautiful, and the interiors are arranged with great taste. This is not something achievable by an interior design project order - it takes years of passion.Dwarika's will be a great choice for those in business/ education/ culture, but also for those looking for that special something in their holiday. For holidaymakers, we strongly recommend the City+Country package (check the special offers link on Dwarika's website). If the 5 nights/ 6 days package looks too short, enquire about customising it. Some basics: Rooms are very clean; the hotel has all the facilities, as well as central heating (important during winter months); it also has ample food/ drink options. We review them separately, just a quick overview here: The Fusion bar has a warm atmosphere, a good drinks menu to choose from, and even Premier League shown live:) The traditional Nepali restaurant Krishnarpan serves amazing food. The continental Toran is much more than a safe all-rounder. Kaiser Cafe is based in the Garden of Dreams (15-30mins by car), and will probably work better as a lunch option.Staff are very helpful, polite, and have a great attitude - we would like to thank them for their efforts to make our stay as wonderful as it was. However, frontline staff are not informed enough for a hotel of this standard, and sometimes lose focus when it matters. The hotel management should consider providing more training/ guidance.For the benefit of the readers, below is a quick list of things you should know (and ask for assistance if necessary):- Arrival: You will need Dwarika's address to fill in your visa on arrival form. Make sure you note it down. - City transport: Traffic in Kathmandu is very chaotic, and good drivers/ cars are worth the expense. So get your transfers organised by the hotel as much as you can (a must for business travellers). If you take a taxi from Dwarika's, ask hotel staff to help explain the driver where you would like to go, and understand how much you should pay.- Guided city tours: There's a list under the special offers link (as above), but Dwarika's staff were unable to make any recommendations. It helps to do some research in advance (we recommend the tours of Bhaktapur, Patan, and Boudhanath Stupa). The tours are organised by a contractor - ask to speak to them directly. Our guide Uttam was absolutely great, and we figured out a tour plan in no time. The car/ driving were also very good. A half-day tour for two costs approx. 50 USD (payable by credit card at Dwarika's, includes transfers). - Money: Ask for prices inclusive of service charge (10%) and VAT (13%). Typically, these two are not mentioned, and combined they add a fair amount to your bill. If you plan to withdraw cash from ATM, enquire ab. charges, as they can be significant as well.- Departure: Kathmandu airport is one of those, where it's much easier to arrive at than depart from - and Dwarika's staff should really do a better job preparing people for that. For one, the first security check and the associated queue are at the very entrance to the terminal building. Having your ticket printed is required (and negotiation/ crowd control abilities are desirable - especially if you can't afford to wait a longer while). So, if you haven't done so yourself, ask at the hotel to print your airline tickets. More security checks and formalities pop up in odd places, and 2h before the flight time was just about enough for a mid-week/ mid-day flight. Finally, there is no really such thing as duty free shopping at Kathmandu airport. Buy souvenirs elsewhere - e.g. there's a lovely shop at Dwarika's - but enquire ab. the rules on keeping the receipts/ showing them at the airport.

I would have given this 5 stars if it wasn't for just a couple of small but important things . They say in UK " that 1st impressions are the most important " and things looked good when we were greeted at the airport by the hotel representative as part of the 7 night City and Country package that included this hotel and their beautiful resort in the hills an hour outside Katmandu with uninterrupted views of the Himalayas. The downside was that we were then bundled into an old tired Skoda taxi with a gruff driver that spoke no English . Normally this doesn't register with me , but when we were paying over $4000.00 for the experience I did expect something slightly more in keeping with the standard and quality of the rest of the experience ( which is certainly 5* ! ) I reasoned it must be about the standard in Nepal but when we arrived at the Hotel to see a very new and smart Hotel logo'd van leave I couldn't help but think we had not received the best airport transfer . It was interesting that the same happened when we transferred from the hotel to the resort and on talking  to another guest who was traveling on her own  she also told us about it and how she was a little nervous as a single white female arriving in the evening and almost didn't get in the taxi as she thought it couldn't have been the proper Hotel transfer. On arrival we were shown through a door into an open courtyard and our cases were brought in - we couldn't see a reception and after a while a member of staff said " are you checking in " - once again as we had arrived on hotel transfer and our bags had been carried in so I'm not sure what else they thought we might be doing? We went into an inner reception and to a desk where we were asked for passports - no Nepalese welcome at all ( which we did see others get later in the week ) then we were asked to take a seat nearby . After 10 minutes of then watching the receptionist take telephone calls / get pulled by more senior staff to do other admin - we went back to the desk to ask if it was possible to check us in and then do everything else ?! It became clear the 'reception ' was more the 'office and admin ' centre for all staff - I'd suggest moving customer / guest checkin to the outside courtyard and then take people to their rooms to complete a more personal checkin? I really didn't want to see all the back office stuff going on in front of me and as a new guest didn't feel we were their priority.After that the rest of the stay was just great . Rooms are huge with lots of local artefacts. We found the rooms being heated to 24 degrees but weren't concerned as there were 2 Ac units - until they told us the whole hotel was in winter mode  and so even if we turned the temps down It wouldn't cool . However by turning off and opening windows we were able to get the room more how we liked it - cool ! The rest of the staff ( except reception ) are just amazing and always smile and happy to help - the guys dressed in black and white were exceptionally good . When we asked about a half day tour/ booking Spa and dinner all was just taken Care of  - he created an itinerary , got us a guide and car with driver all for $60 ! And it was a great 4 hours of City highlights The guys in the Spa are young but full of energy and have great technique and we enjoyed all our treatments The Nepalese restaurant and the 5 course Tasting menu (we got in the package ) on our 1st night was superb - a personalised menu and good introduction to their cuisine and culture. The International restaurant that did breakfast and dinner was also good and a welcome respite for those just arrived who need to acclimatise their stomachs . So in short - we loved this place but for a few initial hiccups that do need addressing. I really don't think they market their 5/7 night dual centre packages well - we found it to be a perfect combination and with an all inclusive meal package and daily Spa treatments included at the resort and the meal and all transfers it was actually very good value - shame they don't shout about it on the international / European market more and you had to hunt on the website to find it !

Great place, fantastic hospitality personnel very attentive.... Choices of 3 restaurants on site. Quiet and peaceful hotel. 5 min drive from the International Airport of Kathmandu. The only down side is you need to take taxi to go to Thamel shopping district

When I first arrived to Dwarika's the staff was all over me welcoming me back (I had stayed there previously) and was very warm and friendly.  They gave me a junior suite which was beautiful.  I only stayed one night and changed to a cheaper hotel.  However after two nights at that hotel I decided to return to Dwarika's.  They gave me a 20% discount which was very nice and I had the junior suite again.   But it seemed that the staff had done a 180 in how they treated me.  It was like I was old hat.  Granted, I didn't expect the extremely warm welcome that I got the first time I arrived, but I seemed to get nothing.  The staff seemed sort of depressed and angry.  Then there was a serious monsoon downpour and there was a leak in the ceiling of my room..  The immediately moved me to another room which was also leaking.  Finally a third room which was fine.  Don't get me wrong, the hotel is phenomenal; peaceful, comfortable and luxurious.  You get what you pay for and you pay a lot.  But I just can't shake that feeling of almost being ignored when I returned to the hotel.

Nuestra habitacion era enorme, mas d 100 m2. Equips de música con CD de música local y muebles antiguos.Un detalle tras otro. Nos ofrecieron una sesion privada de cine, donde nos proyectaron la ascension al Everest de Araceli Segarra. Todo muy emotivo.

Angels of Nepal!!!I'm lucky to be one of the few who could see, live and experience of what Dwarikas means. Excellent in everything.... Food, service and the most important... The people!!! Starting with a lovely manager, great staff, friendly, devoted, what can I say? 5 stars is too less.... Just wish to have the opportunity to go back and enjoy.... I fully recommend

Very good and charming hotel. Beautiful garden, big swimming pool, massage centre, cosy bars and restaurants.When we were there, there was a nice nepali dance show at night.We booked yoga class in the morning. I recommend it.Another tipp is to order a masala chai tea in the evening at the swimming pool area

С удовольствием вспоминаем этот отель и свою поездку, приветливый персонал, прекрасная природа, после землетрясения прошло не так много времени, а следов почти нет, будем ждать следующую поездку, рекоменуем!

This is a real 5 star hotel in Kathmandu! By far the best accommodations in Kathmandu. The restaurant in the hotel is 5 star as well. The service is incredible as are the rooms and lobby of this oasis in the chaos of Kathmandu.

I stayed twice at this hotel during my 9 day visit to Nepal.  The service is impeccable, the rooms were large and beautifully appointed and the food is excellent.  I especially enjoyed the Japanese restaurant.  The staff are so helpful and friendly.  Really enjoyed my stays and would stay there again!

Beautiful hotel with charming courtyards. Rooms are spacious and very well decorated. Restaurants an bar are great (must try the Nepalese tradion all set menu). Staff very attentive. Used the guide and driver from sister travel company - very nice and knowledgeable. Would highly recommend

The quiet elegance of Dwarika’s, with its beautiful antique Nepali woodwork, makes it a perfect place to recover from the noise and stress of the city outside. The gracious service makes you feel well cared for and the food is wonderful. Staying at Dwarika’s soothes the soul.

We came in late at night and the place didn't look like much, but everyone was friendly and our rooms were large, comfortable, and quiet.  It has one of the most beautiful courtyard areas you could hope for and a great place to peacefully read a book or have lunch.It was a very relaxing hotel with a couple of restaurants and a cool bar.

Stayed at Dwarika's Hotel while staying the night in Kathmandu, on the way to Bhutan. The courtyard is spectacular, the rooms traditionally furnished and beautiful, and the staff extremely attentive. We enjoyed the spa which was 4 star, and the traditional Nepalese restaurant, Krishnarpan, which was a delight. We were joined at the hotel by David Beckham (and his entourage) who was also visiting Nepal and seemed to enjoy the hotel as well. He is one of many celebs who has frequented the hotel.One of our favourite hotels, ever.

Staying at "Dwarika's Hotel" was like a dream accomplished. This beautiful hotel is itself a monument to the Nepalese traditional architecture, carefully built in the style of the old royal palaces of the Newar Dinasty (13th Century). Anywhere you look, you'll find real jewels of Nepalese art. Precious wood carved windows and doors will immediately catch your eyes and attention: they truly represent the efforts of Dwarika's owners in preserving Nepalese mastership in wood carvings, so special and caractheristic of this Himalayan country.  We stayed at a junior suite (Nr. 205) on the second floor, overlooking the lovely gardens and ponds. Beautiful and comfortable. Room decor consisted of antique items, carefully collected and assembled by Nepalese art experts. Three restaurants cater fine different cuisines: "Krishnarpan" (Nepalese), "Mako's" (Japanese) and "Toran" (International). "Fusion Bar", just by the awesome pool, offers exquisite aperitifs and cosmopolitan atmosphere. Rooms are very clean and well kept. Breakfast is served at international standards on "Toran" (with indoor or outdoor seating possibilities). An extremely gentle and attentive staff completes the scene. At "Pansha Kosha Himalayan Spa" well trained therapists will indulge you moments of relaxation and inner reflexion. Ayurvedic massages will bring wellness to tired bodies and minds. Wifi was charged and quite unstable. If you are still looking for a hotel in Kathmandu, Dwarika's is your new address! I visited Kathmandu on February 2015, nearly two and a half months before the terrible earthquake that devastated Nepal on April 25, 2015. But "Dwarika's Hotel", located very near the "Tribhuvan International Airport" area, operates normally as recently reported by fellow travelers. Enjoy!

My family and I spent five nights at the Dwarika's property in Kathmandu at the start of our trip to Nepal in April. Upon arrival we were immediately struck by the stunning architectural details of this property and the friendliness of the hotel staff. We were greeting warmly and taken promptly to our room which was extremely spacious and shown the features of the room and the hotel itself. We enjoyed our stay at Dwarika's a great deal - the food offerings were excellent, the beds comfortable and the facilities very luxurious. This is an extremely pricey option for Kathmandu but if you are looking for a little luxury in the midst of Kathmandu, Dwarika's does not disappoint!

I'm a business traveller who has stayed in top class hotels all over the world.  We stayed at Dwarika's from 4/17-20 while on our first visit to Nepal.  The staff was attentive and plentiful, even though there were a lot of trainees.  The Nepalese reataurant was amazing- we were stuffed on only the six course meal.  The hotel offers free yoga classes at 7:00 in the morning, but you have to make a reservation- don't worry, though, the most that I had in any of my classes was 4 (including someone that was a hotel employee).  The yogi is awesome; he is flexible in places that I didn't know existed.  The hotel also boasts a fitness center, a pool, and a very pleasant courtyard to hang out in far from the bustle of the nearby city street.  We stayed in a junior suite and a heritage double and both were huge and well appointed (including a nice selection of loose teas...)

We stayed at the Dwarika Hotel 2x during our trip to Nepal. At the beginning of the trip we stayed on the 4th floor. The second time we were assigned to the 3rd floor. The layout of our room on the higher floor was better. Don't get me wrong both stays were very good and we enjoyed the hospitality each time. Namaste is the customary greeting and frankly it makes you smile at this property. The history of the development is interesting. The rooms were clean, the grounds well kept. When I am in town I would stay again.

The Dwarika's is a very special, family owned hotel that aimes to provide a more authentic feel of Nepal then ordinary luxury hotels.  Its grounds are lovely, with courtyards and lots of outdoors seating and a nice swimming pool. The service is good, so is the food.  Light sleepers should bring earplugs - one should not foget that this hotel is in the middle of all of the city's huzzle and buzzle and the airport is not far away either.  Rooms in the inside buildings are quieter.  Those in the South and West face the streets.  WiFi costs exta.

Deeply appreciated this hotel, itself and the mission behind it. Built in traditional style with savaged antique wood carvings the late owner passionately collected, it is like an oasis in an otherwise chaotic city. It was run with great passion by the wonderful staffs. We were upgraded into a giant suite that was beautifully appointed and decorated. The court yard was divine with weeping wisteria in bloom. The public spaces were abundant and tastefully decorated with genuine antiques. Located in the center of the town not far from the airport, it was a very convenient location. We looked forward to going out exploring the city and we equally looked forward to going back to relax.

I have never been to Nepal before and arrived in torrential rain to be taken through the hurly-burly of Kathmandu traffic to the haven of Dwarika’s.  The photographs I had seen before I arrived gave only a vague impression of how wonderful the hotel was.  It did not really feel like staying in a hotel, except that the service was wonderful.  Because the owners have collected so many old architectural items and incorporated them into the various buildings, it feels much more as if one is staying in a part of old Kathmandu (but quieter!) even down to the various stupas and incense burning in the courtyards.  We very much enjoyed our Nepali dinner in the specialist restaurant in the hotel, although we were still slightly jet-lagged, being our first evening.  Our room was fantastic, and the provision of umbrellas at the exit of every building (which were very necessary initially) was a much appreciated touch, and representative of the level of service generally. The hotel was even better when it stopped raining and the sun came out and one could really appreciate one’s surroundings.  If one wants to avoid glittering modern towers which could be anywhere, and really feel that you are in Nepal, this is the hotel for you.

This hotel was absolutely stunning. Amongst the hustle and bustle of the capital, you arrive not far from the airport to a driveway. Once inside you realise this place is like an ancient monument. It is like a mini paradise with artefacts collected by the owners family for years. We were welcomed by the staff in a traditional Nepali manner. Our first room was stunning it was on the ground floor and looked on to the beautiful enchanting gardens. The rooms had the same old feel as he grounds and everything seemed antique. I would say this hotel is for those who are happy in this sort of surroundings rather than needing modern contemporary. But then I would question why visit nepal if you are looking for a modern feel. This hotel gives you the true experience of the city and its culture.I really enjoyed the breakfast as I tried yak cheese and this was new to me. The Nepali resturant was a brilliant experience it is western prices but it's a experience I haven't had anywhere else. The hotel helped arrange city tours which were very well organised, they also helped get taxis which were more upmarket Han those that locals use. Either way it's all an experience. On a downside we had to change rooms due to a water problem. This was disappointing and we had to move closer to the pool on the first floor. These rooms were beautiful but not as fantastic as the first room. I suppose it couldn't be helped it was either stay and have no water or move and be able to wash. Overall this hotel is a must and if you can afford the luxury go for it you should not miss this enchanting experience. We stayed at the Hyatt before we left the country and that was a typical western hotel. It had its modern luxuries but not a touch on this one.

Only stayed for 1 night but from the welcome on our arrival to our departure the staff ensured that we had a most pleasant stay.The room was clean and spacious, and the gardens/pool area looked to be well maintained.The food was excellent and the staff very attentive.

Dwarika's Hotel has deservedly built up a solid reputation for being THE place to stay in Kathmandu.Although not wonderfully located, taxis can easily be obtained by the doormen to transport you around the city.The hotel is not as old as it first looks, having been built in an authentic style using antique wooden windows, doors and fittings. Rooms are large, well appointed, and with comfortable beds.The various restaurants offer excellent choice of Nepali and international foods, and the cozy "Pub" with open fireplace is a warm and comfortable haven for pre or post dinner drinks.Staff are friendly and efficient.

After 5 days at the Hyatt, which we loved,  we walked into the dwarika and were pleasantly surprised by the traditional design and palace type design.  The first words out of the reception were, didn't we want to upgrade to a suite for only $80. Since the hotel was more expensive than the Hyatt, we said no thanks. The standard room was wonderful. Beautiful Nepalese decor, comfy bed, views into the courtyard.  Then, realizing I had no wifi code, I asked for one and it was ONLY $ 10 a day. After a brief send pleasant , although unnecessary at the price of the room, we were granted complimentary wifi.  The buffet breakfast was adequate but the beverage service lacking. It was cold in the city and the lobby was cold. The open areas were beautiful but outdoors. I wonder how they are in the monsoon season.  The Nepalese dinner was excellent. We ate at the hotel a second night in the regular restaurant. Service was good and the waiter very helpful.  The location didn't seem too near any sites . You barely notice the hotel from the street but it is open and spacious past the entry

I've been fortunate enough to have travelled to many different countries, occasionally treating myself to a 5 star hotel. But Dwarikas is simply the best hotel I've ever stayed in. Upgraded to an amazing suite upon arrival, really spacious and total luxury. The hotel has so much character and beauty, ok not in the greatest of locations in crazy Kathmandu, but what an Oasis! The staff were perfectly trained, polite but chatty and friendly. Very,very impressed, huge attention to detail such as the understated but beautiful Christmas decorations. Only whinge was the cost of the mini bar, but this was 5 star plus without a doubt.

Nepal is not what you will expect. It is in the pantheon of the great old cultures….Machu Picchu, Angkor Wat, Petra…wonderful old civilizations that will reward you with novel insights and rich unique cultural highlights.  The hotel is resurrected from the hand-carved windows that were going to be destroyed for kindling and is highly complementary and derivative of Durbar Square, Patan City and Bhaktapur (all ancient palaces/residences).  Some features of the hotel date back to the 13th century. It has some small quirks and missteps but you must absolutely stay here.  The staff will go out of its way to please you and the architecture is one of a kind – there is no comparison to the style.  Every turn is a photographic opportunity and you “feel like you are staying in history”.  There is a high level of environmental concern here including the opportunity to fund dog rescue – aided by a wonderful furry (dog) friend that resides there and initiatives to support the community.Having read many comments about Nepal there are several key points that need to be made.  First there is nonsense that Durbar Square has graffiti and trash which is absolutely not correct.  Yes you will have to pay to walk through the squares (approximately $15) but these are World Heritage Sites that are outdoor museums.  It is well worth the price – for all of them. The funds go to support their upkeep and it is a privilege to be able to view these heritage sites.   Second, they may be highly concerning by appearance, but I would encourage you try the local Nepalese restaurants – no not the tourist sites but the ones down the back alley that have line ups with not an English/American in sight.  Point to what you want, order a beer, and have the best $3 lunch ever.  If you need a name try Chatamari Chhen.  They open around 1:30 pm and stay open until the food is gone – after that you are out of luck.  It is a real shame the tourists are discouraged from such culinary revelations by fear mongering guide books. However, if the concerns remain then try the Nepalese restaurant in the Dwarika hotel – it does a very close approximation but perhaps without the lingering fear. If you can afford a personal guide, then we would suggest Surendra Ranjit who caters to the English and German tourist (surendra2000@hotmail.com) who is outstanding and can certainly share with you his personal favorites. Regarding flights to Everest – they may or may not go.  Your will likely wait hours for the flight to take off so eat breakfast first and be patient.  It would be highly prudent to plan for this over several sequential mornings since these flights are frequently cancelled (7 am is your only option). Our understanding is that you can’t get a refund, but can reschedule, so if you save this for your last day, and it does not happen, you are out of luck. Your only other option is to charter a helicopter to base camp but this around $2,100 per person… Finally, although Everest is clearly a highlight not be missed, some time should be set aside to really visit several real artist studios.  There are some truly unique ones that have hand-carved buffalo bone prayer wheels, truly unique Thanka paintings created by masters (not present at any of the main tourist destinations and are hidden away in back alleys), Hindi goddess statues hand caste in copper and painted in gold, singing bowls (most good ones start around $100), wood sculptures, and of course you can always purchase the Nepal cashmere.

This is THE place to stay before and after trekking the Himalayas. We could forget the noise and pollution of Kathmandu, unwind in impeccable surroundings and had warm greetings from all the staff. We felt we got special attention at the Fusion Bar from Misters Ram, Jawad and Keshav. The room service was a matter of minutes. The only thing that was out of sync was the ability to grab WiFi in the room. It was inconsistent and devices got knocked off. Thank you for our oasis. As another in the circle of friends made there in the courtyard said, "The Dwarika is the favorite hotel of all my travels.

This hotel is an excellent choice when in Kathmandu. Remember where you are. This hotel has very good western standards and a very attentive staff. Adding to what others have already said about the hotel: We enjoyed the bar and restaurant. It was happy hour at the bar which meant if you ordered one drink you got two delivered, not a special price. The food at the restaurant, Krishnarpan, was spectacular. The menu is set up in "courses" and it is far too easy to over order. Both the six course and twelve course dinners never seemed to end. And the food was a great way to sample many dishes. FYI, we have also stayed at the Yak and Yeti and found both to be good, yet different. Dwarika has a very local feeling that we enjoyed.

The hotel is in historical buildings which have been magnificently restored with love for the details. Spacious rooms, several restaurants in the property, a SPA and swimming pool area. Peaceful place especially considering that it is situated in the middle of a chaotic and polluted city. Free access to the business center, however in oder to use WI-FI in the room and in all property you need to buy coupons (12$ a day or 5$ per hour). I think this is unacceptable for such an hotel; to note it was also the only hotel in Nepal charging for use of the Wi-Fi (as such the low rating for value below)

I came to this hotel having done 3 weeks in Tibet including a Mount Everest North Face trek at very high altitude well above base camp. I was very tired and the journey from Tibet had taken 2 days. Kathmandu's Friday rush hour traffic did not help my state of mind....so my surprise was complete on going through the front door of Dwarika's hotel. One leaves the noise, dust and general well meaning chaos of Kathmandu  and is transported into another world of peace, calm and serenity where things work and get done. Having stayed at other far cheaper but far inferior places in Kathmandu I was shocked. This is a beautiful hotel. I learned that it was founded by a visionary who wanted to preserve Nepal's beautiful historic wooden artifacts and over many years this hotel was established to house the collection. The beautiful wood is displayed everywhere but what is more important is that this hotel has character, integrity and soul and executes so well. The inner courtyard, interior lobby and rooms are so well arranged and furnished. This is not a branch of some boring global chain that could be located anywhere but a place where the best of the local character comes through. I stayed in a junior suite; it was large, very well arranged and the perfect place to recover after my prior endeavors. There is a good choice of restaurants within the hotel (the traditional Nepali restaurant was my favorite) and it a great bar to relax in. It was so good just to sit and read a book outside in the warm shade in the calmness of one of the courtyard areas.As a hotel that operates at high standards but preserves the best of the local city it is in, I highly recommend this hotel. Is one of the best city hotels I have stayed at in Asia.

If anyone doesn't find this an enchanting piece of paradise then they are severely jaded and world weary.  This is a little slice of heaven, and a peaceful sanctuary amid the noise and chaos of Kathmandu with resident dogs and gorgeous gardens and wonderful staff.  It's the Nepalese experience rather than a cookie cutter hotel stay, but without compromising on delivering a 5 star product.The rooms are really lovely, the property overall is gorgeous and sure there may be some little glitches such as plumbing draining a tiny bit slow or the hot water not instantaneous, but this is in Nepal where blackouts occur daily. Loved the Fusion bar, wonderful decor (and the great service), and we went there every day for terrific drinks and a cigar (husband).  Had a superb 6 course meal at Krishnarpan their Nepalese restaurant and again, wonderful and gracious service.  It was my husband's birthday and they made him the most decadent and delicious chocolate cake and he really loved it (and ate every bit of it!).  There is a charming and erudite Manager who clearly runs a very well oiled ship as all the staff here are superbly trained and have just the right combination of friendliness and professionalism. On average they have all been at Dwarika's for a number of years, which is a very good sign and it shows in the service levels.Try and get to the Kaiser Cafe (Thamel) which is also run by the same group, as the setting in the Garden of Dreams at nighttime is simply breathtaking.  As you can tell we really enjoyed out 3 nights at Dwarika's and will be back for sure.

Dwarika's Hotel is off the charts in every way.  The location is not ideal for walking around, but taxis are easy to come by and very inexpensive to take you anywhere.  Large rooms, excellent service, healthy food and a fantastic historical setting make this a truly one of a kind resort.

What a hotel, everything down to the smallest detail is perfect. I work in hospitality and have the greatest luck to travel around the world on a regular basis. I never right reviews because i do tend to pick on things that are minor.I wanted to write this review because i was blown away about how good this place really is! My room on the second floor was the biggest room I have seen and the lay out was spectacular. Furnishings were beautiful, day bed with a million different shaped cushions to flop onto after a hard day out. Slate style floors throughout, walk in shower, with a big separate bath area. enough room to put a dining room and chairs lol. big tv on a wall swivel so you can turn it to different ends of the room (bed, or day bed).The grounds are awesome, great seating everywhere with day beds by the pool or courtyard seating all around the place. All with large trees and folige to keep the sting of the sun out and i think the noise of the chaotic streets just outside. A real haven away from it all.The staff were special. Its quit funny, the attention by the staff is over the top, if you want it to be, they will be there every second to top up a drink, have a conversation or just check if everything is alright.(this is fusion bar).On the other hand they get the idea if you want some quiet time and will let you be. Ram the man makes a killer cocktail and will try to force free canapes in you every second. Be careful you wont eat dinner haha, a great conversationalist. He has an exceptional bunch of people with him and is training them well. I recommend this place for all these reasons and alot more. It is a place that will stay at the top of my list for many years im sure.I did stay at two other properties in the same price bracket and its not worth a comparisonthx guys and girls for a great stay. I will be back in the not to distant future.

Этот отель в здании 15-16 века. О его строительстве есть стенд в лобби. Когда после шумной улицы попадаешь во внутренний двор, кажется, что это другая реальность- тихо, спокойно. В отеле 3 ресторана. Японский, мы туда зашли, когда они закрылись после обеда. Но нас накормили. Непальской кухни, вечером они во дворе устроили барбекю, было вкусно. И международной- там проходят и завтраки. Завтраки средние. Есть СПА. В первый день записаться не удалось, не было мест. На следующий - сходили. Не выше четверки. Номера просторные. Дверь номера изнутри закрывается на деревянную задвижку. Ночью был сильный ветер. Дверь распахивалась и мы приставили к ней стул. У душевой кабины дверцы нет, а висит полиэтиленовая шторка. Я не понимаю, как ее моют после каждого, кто жил в номере. Унитазы в отеле самые дешевые. Я понимаю, владельцы отеля собирают антиквариат по всей стране, но сантехника в дорогом отеле должна быть на достойном уровне. Вывод, любителям роскоши и удобств, явно не сюда.

Splendid effort was put into this facility. The restoration of local architecture a gift to the culture by Dwarikas. The enclave of the hotel is simply enchanting. It is set up with  the feel of a small village with 2 shops, a bar, several restaurants, a pool, yoga area, etc. The room was large, lovely, and interesting. The view from it onto the courtyard inviting. The restaurants serve fabulous foods. Service is very good, too.

Food at krishnarpanam is not worth it at allIt's designed to make fools out of foreignersNo tasteNo presentationOnly a high cost gor poor quality of goodIt was a disaster...course by courseNot doable at all

Man glaubt es kaum, wenn man durch das lebendige und aufregende Kathmandu fährt und sich plötzlich in einer anderen Welt wiederfindet. Unser Taxi zweigte von der Hauptstrasse ab, fuhr in eine überdachte, schmale Vorfahrt. Wir wurden herzlich von allen Anwesenden begrüsst (Security, Gepäckboy und Hotelangestellte) und wie wir durch die Eingangstüre des Hotels traten, tauchten wir ein in eine erstaunliche Oase von Luxus und Ruhe! Unvorstellbar: bloss einige Meter zur Hauptstrasse und man tritt in eine völlig andere Welt ein. Wir wurden zu einer Polstergruppe in der Lobby begleitet, wo uns eine warmes, wohlduftendes Erfrischungstuch und ein Willkommensgetränk gereicht wurden. Das Check-In an der Reception übernahm ein Angestellter, während dem uns ein Anderer das Hotel erklärte. Wir wurden ins Zimmer in einem Trakt im Innenhof geführt, begleitet von freundlichen Grüssen der anwesenden Angestellten. Man fühlte sich extrem willkommen und gut aufgehoben in einer wunderbaren, eigenen Atmosphäre. Das Hotel hat einen speziellen Architekturstil, Backsteine durchmischt mit dunklem Holz. Unser Zimmer war geräumig, gross, lang und offen. Zwei gegenüberstehende Waschbecken, separate Dusche, Badewanne und ein separates WC. Auch von dort Ausblick auf den Pool im Innenhof. Die Einrichtung des Zimmers speziell, ausgewählt, hübsch und sehr sauber. Bevor wir unser Nachtessen im Hauptrestaurant einnahmen, gönnten wir uns einen Drink in der Bar. Auch dort, sehr aufmerksames, freundliches Personal und eine gute Stimmung. Was aber der absolute Hammer in diesem Hotel war: ein unübertreffliches und extrem feines Nachtessen im Restaurant. Das Servicepersonal sehr aufmerksam, diskret und ausgesprochen freundlich. Die Vorspeise Trüffelravioli und der Hauptgang Chicken Tikka Masala sind wohl die besten Speisen, die ich je in Asien gegesssen habe! Sehr, sehr geschmackvoll und mundete super. Auch das Frühstücksbuffet liess keine Wünsche offen. Ich bin immer noch begeistert von dieser Wohlfühloase mitten im Getümmel von Kathmandu und will gerne zurückkehren. Dies umso mehr, als wir wegen der Unpassierbarkeit der Strasse über die Grenze von Tibet verspätet in diesem Hotel ankamen und nur eine Nacht bleiben konnten.

Tutto bellissimo. Costruzione in stile locale. Camera molto ampia e molto ben arredata davvero accogliente. Giardino cortile interno all'hotel molto piacevole per bere qualcosa o semplicemente rilassarsi con una lettura. La SPA offre massaggi meravigliosi e non cari. Tornare in hotel la sera dopo le gite e stato sempre un vero piacere. La posizione e ottima e lo staff efficiente e gentile.Vale tutte le 5 stelle.

gran hotelbuena ubicacion  cerca del aeropuerto excelente servicio y desayuno buenas habitaciónes y amplias instalación tipo colonial muy bonitobuenos restaurantes probamos  el nepali  y el japones volveremos

Hotel lindo, bem cuidado e com a proposta de conservar a característica arte de entalhar madeira. Quartos grandes e confortáveis, bom banho, frutas de cortesia, biscoitos e muitas garrafas de água. O wi fi é bom e gratuito. Dispõe de 3 restaurantes- nepalês, japonês e internacional,além de um charmoso bar. Spa, piscina, lojas e biblioteca. Atendimento muito cordial. Um refúgio de paz na agitada cidade. Recomendo!

Usually, no matter how opulent a hotel might be, it is still a hotel. A place where you’re withering away valuable time that could otherwise be spent outside the hotel doors, where you can get the true experience and vibe of a location.The Dwarika’s is so delightfully different. It was a vital part of my overall experience in Kathmandu. You feel the heart and soul of Nepal while on the property. Actually, it’s perhaps an injustice to simply label it a hotel. It is a truly special experience.The rooms are also beautiful. For starters, they are gigantic. More importantly, they reflect the culture and heritage of Nepal. Housekeeping does a great job as well. The toiletries are all natural and smell wonderful— I even bought some shampoo, conditioner, and lotion at the gift shop prior to leaving. And I loved relaxing in the room in the evenings over a cup of Himalayan tea and cookies, admiring the courtyard and the sound of chirping birds.The entire property is majestic, with exquisite attention to detail. I can’t even put into words how gorgeous everything is, no matter which direction you look. Also, I had one of the best massages of my life at the spa.While there are many pretty and sparkly hotels around the world, many can leave you feeling a bit empty if the people of the hotel are aloof.  At the Dwarika’s though, this is the area that puts them over the top. The staff is so warm, always smiling, and always eager to help. I don’t think I ever opened a door for myself in the 5 days I was there. And Shiva, in particular, is a real gem. He went out of his way to ensure that every aspect of our stay was perfect, and always with a smile on his face, and genuine.... the way one would be if they were doing something for their lifelong best friend.I can’t say enough wonderful things about The Dwarika’s. I hope to return one day.

Etwas Besonderes ist das Dwarikas auf jeden Fall, man muss es einfach einmal erlebt haben. Wenn man dieses Haus vesucht nachzumachen dann ist es ein Fehler, einfach so lassen wie das Haus jetzt ist dann macht Mann bestimmt keinen Fehler.KL

De entrada pedimos que nos cambiaran de habitación porque las cortinas no servían. El hotel es caro por lo que se esperan mejores habitaciones pero tienen todo lo necesario y el hotel que es bellísimo se disfruta mucho. Hay un pequeño restaurante japonés sencillo y recomendable. El desayuno no es muy variado pero la cena es muy buena. Por la tarde hay una exhibición de danza nepalesa y tomar el té en el patio es realmente agradable. La atención es muy buena y todo el personal muy amable y dispuesto. A mitad del viaje resulta muy económico dar a lavar la ropa, además de que lo hacen rápido y bien.

Just a short drive from the airport you enter a calm oasis and secluded retreat from the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu.You are welcomed with smiles and wonderful staff.The hotel grounds and facilities are great. Especially the architecture. Rooms are not created equal here. Our first night on our trip we stayed in room 503 which was incredible. The last night we ended up in room 203 which was a lot less exciting. Both were equally well-appointed and comfortable but 503 had beautiful views of the pool from the veranda window. It was clearly empty on our second stay on the trip and we wished we were assigned the same room as it truly captures the beauty of this hotel.The spa is excellent, with great selection of therapies and at extremely reasonable prices. Had a fantastic hour long massage. The F&B program is just ok. Nothing bad but nothing over the top great. The bar had ok drinks.The breakfast selection was great but wasnt amazing either. Nonetheless, I would highly recommend this place as a base in Kathmandu, especially before and after any other inter-Nepali travels you may have as it really exudes calm and serenity within traditional heritage architecture and culture.

Unassuming exterior, interior is a renovated traditional Nepali courtyard. Very tastefully and lovingly restored, stylish and without the standard bling of the high end chains.Rooms are large and well appointed, breakfast is good, service very friendly and attentive.Would do back and do wish we could find similar hotels elsewhere

..... whoever can show a certain budget for travelling should stay there when in Kathmandu.  The Dwarika's is owned and managed by a German Man with his Nepalese wife and mother in law. The presence of the two ladies is omni. Something which man do usually not achieve: The hotel is equipped and decorated which has long to be unparalleled. So many small and beautiful details are to be found in the public areas as well in the extremly spacious rooms. Their smallest rooms are larger than the average rooms in any other 5 star hotel in the world! I have been travelling in 41 countries, but there was only ONE experience like the one at Dwarika's! Maybe because Kathmandu is such a dirty-. traffic plagued city, it helps Dwarika's to stand out? The only one thing I would point out is the breakfast: Given the fact that one of the owners is German, I would expect much better breads and pastries! The breads and bakery products do need much much improvement! Two kinds of honey doe not make the breakfast better if the bread is not good..... but this is (luckily for me) really not a big issue.Expensive stay,1300+ US for two nights and two dinners without Champagne, but worth it!  If back in Kathmandu, we will stay there.

When Mr. Shrestha saw Nerwar carvings being used as firewood, he made up his mind to save as much of the art and Nepali culture as he could. His conservation efforts led to the idea of building a hotel that incorporated as much of the artwork as possible. When you walk into the atrium you are looking at a 13th century mantel and entrance way. Dwarika's (Mr. Sherstha's first name) efforts have resulted in a unique blend of luxury, heritage and culture. His vision extended beyond the hotel, sustainable organic farms supply the restaurants, a workshop to restore and replicate the wood carvings created and each evening Nepali folk dances are performed. The rooms are incredible mini museums, the staff and food excellent. We kept walking into things are we soaked in the artwork that is everywhere. A must stay in Kathmandu. A special call out to Rabina our server Monday 11/11/19, she made dinner a very special occasion.

This hotel is an amazing place where to stay and enjoy your stay in an autentic heritage hotel. Part of Dwarika's group of hotels and resorts in Nepal taking care to provide a unique brand of Nepali hospitality which supports and promote Nepal's rich and diverse heritage. Highly recommended!

The minute you step inside this hotel, you have entered a different world in Katmandu. All the rooms surround a courtyard.
