And the courtyard is sumptuous- restaurants, pool, library, bars,gift shop, seating areas. The rooms are humongous. Nicely decorated in a traditional style. The bathroom is also very large with separated areas for shower, toilet, and sink. The large entrance to the bathroom doesn't have a door. Amenities are plentiful. It's worth spending time at the hotel just to appreciate the hotel itself while in Katmandu

We stayed at the Dwarika for one night only, but it was worthy and we really enjoyed it. The spa is a must!! It is a hotel with a history, all the staff is really helpful and welcoming. The room is very big with a nepali decor.

Based on four lovely nights at Dwarika’s, here is my detailed analysis of this special 5 star property:1. This is a unique luxury hotel. Unique in the world. It features many ancient wood carvings and statues that have been preserved by and incorporated into the hotel. The character of ancient Nepal is brought to life. There are wood carvings and statues in the courtyards, corridors and guest rooms. Dwarika’s must be like staying in an old Nepali king’s palace.2. 5 star hotel! There is no doubt: Dwarika’s is a 5star luxury hotel. I have had the good fortune of staying in many 5 star hotels around the world and Dwarika’s is special. 3. The service is excellent. Knowing service can be subjective, please let me give one example: We checked into the hotel at 9am (jet lagged and tired) - fully expecting a 6 hour wait for our room to be ready. We were greeted by Concierge Ram who advised that our original suite number was changed so that we would have a new suite - with only a minimal wait. Wow! The new suite was ready in one hour. Ram offered cappuccino and kindness as we waited. Ram was a sensational host and ambassador for Dwarika’s. A young trainee (Rama) then took us to our suite with great care. We were quickly relaxing in the room. No hassle or extra charge. (I think of all the famous 5 star hotels where we waited in the lobby for hours for our room to be ready.) Thanks Ram - one more time.4. The food is diverse. We ate at all three restaurants.5. The Japanese Mako’s was excellent - and I do not like sushi or sashimi. Tempura vegetables and shrimp, fried chicken and Japanese pizza carried the day. I liked to maitre’d very much; she runs a tight ship. One needs reservations as Mako’s is small.6. Nepalese restaurant - The Nepalese 6 course meal was a fun “show”. This was my first attempt at Nepalese cuisine and I liked it. Not too spicy. Advice: be careful with the potent rice wine. More advice: the staff will bring you as much of one item as you wish from the set menu.7. The main dining room was OK. We had our best luck with afternoon meals from their extensive menu. Salads were a favorite. Our favorite waiter, Pashant was superb.8. The breakfast buffet was just fair. It could use a few more fruits in my opinion. Better coffee, too. 9. The suite room was top flight. Important: Do not think 2019 high rise modern. Think luxury in the context of historical Nepalese structures and spaces. Our suite had all the goodies from flat screen TV to fast internet. Even, a ceiling fan. We had a king size bed. Huge bath. We were in 408 (a junior suite, I think). Advice:  I would order junior suites or above based  purely on room size. The smaller rooms are - well, kinda small.  10. Strong security - with lots of front guards and high hotel walls. The neighborhood  isn’t  lovely and the hotel seems an oasis in gritty, dirty Kathmandu. 11. Good value - We paid a base B&B room rate of about $400 per night plus taxes. Dwarika’s is a special hotel in Kathmandu.  I can recommend it without hesitation.

the hotel started around  25 years ago and they build it as 'old nepalese style'it's very nice. the rooms are big, clean and nicely decorated. you have all the facilities you may need. the staff is very friendly and helpful. the bar is very cozy. the japanese restaurant is really very good, a class better than the others. can really recommend this hotel. we enjoyed the 5 nights there.

A chaque passage à Katmandou, j aime retrouver le Dwarika pour son architecture, son calme et l immense professionnalisme du personnelJe m y suis rendue pour dîner au Mako’s leur restaurant Japonais, d une excellente qualitéSoirée parfaite

This is by far the best hotel in Kathmandu and probably in the whole subcontinent. The infrastructure is great, woodwork is breathtaking, but perhaps the best part of it all is the service.  Of particular note is Pramesh Devkota that is the most attentive, efficient and courteous guy.  The spa and its staff is also great.

This hotel was such a pleasant surprise that we booked a further 3 nights to extend our stay in Kathmandu.  The hotel staff are courteous, polite and responsive to the requests of guests.  Front desk staff were always helpful when we were looking for a local walk, to visit a temple or specific monument.  They provided a good local map and clear instructions.I used the spa for a well deserved Himalayan massage following walking up to Tiger's Nest Monastery the previous day.  The spa staff were helpful and made my visit enjoyable.  The massage was thorough and met my needs.We had a junior suite overlooking the courtyard, which provided plenty of room.  It was well presented with a day bed and chairs for chilling during the day time. There are double sinks and a separate shower and bath.  Dwarika provides some beautiful soaps and lotions, that are also available for sale.  Dwarika's make most of their furniture and furnishings and this gives each room an individual feel.We had the bbq on Friday night, which was buffet style.  There was plenty of choice, particularly as one of us is vegetarian.  Chefs readily explained ingredients and made alterations to menus to meet our requirements (one didn't like overly spicy food).  The only negative was service was sometimes slow, particularly at breakfast, although I enjoyed the good coffee whilst waiting for my order.This is a gem of a hotel and we totally enjoyed our stay at Dwarika's before the onset of monsoon season.

Not to gush about how much my husband and I loved this hotel. The decor, the wood, the wood carvings, the room, the ambiance were our style. We wanted to move in here immediately. None of that is important if you do not have the staff. The people working here were all great, friendly and helpful. The rooms were clean and so beautiful. I do not know what the mattress or sheets and pillows had in them, but I have never slept so well in my life. I would definitely stay at this hotel again.  By the way the picture on the side does not even begin to show how beautiful this hotel is.

Laut unserem Guide ist es das beste Hotel im gesamten südasischen Raum. Das kann ich nur unterschreiben. Wir hatten ein etwas größeres Zimmer, eine Junior Suite, gebucht, wir hätten es dort locker 14 Tage ausgehalten. Es gibt nicht nur ein Morgen- und ein Abendservice, scheinbar auch ein Nachtservice. Handtücher werden immer ausgetauscht, wann immer wir welche verwendet haben.Möglicherweise ist die Klimaanlage etwas laut, diese kann man aber abschalten bzw. auf Nachtbetrieb umstellen. Die sonstigen Einrichtungen (Fitnessraum, Wellnessbereich) haben wir leider nicht benützt, da wir nur einige Tage dort waren.Das Frühstücksbuffet einfach herrlich. Es gibt nahezu alles was Sie wollen und vor allem einen perfekten Espresso. Wenn man den Bildern glaubt, war hier die halbe Politprominenz der ganzen Welt bereits zu Gast.Gezeichnet Peter Nemeth

This lovely, quiet hotel provided a respite from the noise and smog of Kathmandu.  We stayed at the beginning and at the end of our stay in 2 different rooms. Both were large, with a large bathroom, double sinks, nicely appointed.  The staff were caring, helpful and overall top-notch.A quick word about its history.  The original owner collected artifacts from buildings that were going to be torn down and which now adorn the rooms and restaurants. There are peaceful gardens, a quiet courtyard, fountains...Definitely worth a stay!!

This property is a zen oasis of calm. Beautiful pool, and beautiful gardens, and beautiful windows everywhere you look. This hotel began as an effort to save the elaborate carved windows from demolition during Nepal’s modernization effort. What a tragedy it would have been for these architectural gems to have been lost!  The rooms carry on the Nepalese decor, which is pleasantly rustic. On the downside, the AC never really worked (but we could open a window to the cool spring air) and the WiFi was near useless. The breakfast buffet was really good, enhanced by the beautiful surroundings. We also ate the 9 course dinner. Not sure if it was worth the price, but the food was excellent and plentiful and served in a beautiful dining room. The service was gracious. I would especially like to thank the hotel for helping me search for my lost cell phone. I thought I left it or dropped it at the hotel, but they patiently helped me review security footage which clearly shows I took it with me. How kind they were to a traveler in distress!  This property may be pricy compared to average Kathmandu hotels, but it is not average in any way. Staying here helps preserve the Nepalese cultural treasures and is a delight to all the senses. Should be on 1001 places to visit before you die. Namaste, Dwarika’s Hotel.

The hotel is built to form a very large interior courtyard which isolates guests from the traffic, noise and pollution of Kathmandu. The hotel buildings are very attractive and the courtyard is pleasant and inviting. Restaurants, shops and a great bar are located in the courtyard. The rooms are quite large and comfortable. We stayed here one night before heading to the sister property in Dhulikhet which is equally nice. Highly recommended.

I simply loved staying here, it’s like living in ancient Nepal, but with modern aminities.  The hotel is an ode to the architecture of Nepal.  Not only is it beautiful, the food quality is excellent.  Stay here once to experience something truely unique

Hotel offers access to any amenity a traveler might want. Arguably one of the best Nepali restaurants in the city is on-site. Super clean, well attended, and very friendly staff....highly recommended!

It was a sudden decision to visit Nepal & it was our first visit. Hence we decided to book the best hotel in Kathmandu. Also to celebrate our wedding anniversary with family & friends. Excellent & friendly staffs. The resort is enchanting. I just want to to let people know that it’s their policy that no outside alcohol or beverage is allowed in the restaurants or bar. Well if you bought any from the duty free shop, just drink it in your room.

The Dwarika's hotel is steeped in history and luxury. The rooms are large and absolutely beautiful with great attention to detail. The housekeeping was immaculate with fresh batch of chocolates sent to the room everyday!  Every corner of the property is like a treasure hunt - you come across delightful little things! The service of the staff was exceptional, The food was good. The property is close to the airport and conveniently located. The hotel has a spa and a fitness center.

The hotel grounds are beautiful, and so are the rooms. Service, from the doormen to the chamberladies was top-notch. We like the little extra touches such as complimentary fresh fruits and cookies being sent up to our room.There are 3 restaurants within the hotel. We visited 2 of them and would highly recommend Mako's. Do see my other review of the restaurant.Small things we are concerned about are the lack of adequate wall sockets to charge our multiple devices, and that the bathrooms do not have doors. It could get inconvenient for families who stay at the hotel. The location is very near the airport, and to many major tourist attractions. A cab to Thamel costs around 400 rupees.

Wonderful stay in Kathmandu - best hotel on our trip in Nepal and Bhutan. Staff, rooms, facilities and overall atmosphere were at a very high standard. Recommend the Nepali restaurant for its food, service and genuine Nepalese style.

Das Dwarikas ist ein Hotel, in dem man einmal geschlafen haben muss. Es wurde uns von meinem ehemaligen Arbeitskollegen empfohlen, der Nepalese ist. Es ist keine Kette. Dementsprechend ist das Hotel toll eingerichtet (selbstgemachte Möbel, hinduistische und nepalesische Kunst).Das Hotel verfügt über relativ moderne Zimmer und einen hohen Komfort. Das Hotel ist sehr sauber und sehr gepflegt und es gibt überhaupt nichts zu beklagen. Im Gegenteil: Inhabergeführte Hotels, so unsere Erfahrung, bieten mehr Charme und oft einen besseren Service.Kommen wir wieder einmal nach Kathmandu, dann auf jeden Fall in dieses Hotel Vielen Dank!

Atendimento excelente! Quartos grandes e limpos! Funcionários atenciosas e capacitados! Café da manhã razoavelmente bom ! Restaurantes excelentes, comidas muito boas!!!! Spa adorável!! Arquitetura interessante e peculiar! Volto com certeza!

Whilst Kathmandu was not exactly what I expected this hotel ticked the 5 star boxes. We stayed at this hotel twice during our visit.The hotel is essentially a ring of buildings around a square with some building in the middle.The bedrooms are excellent (try for ones off the main reception lobby - they are bigger) with all the usual facilities and very clean.The hotel has a nice bar in the courtyard and a pleasant swimming pool - we used both.The evening food was excellent, especially in the Nepalese restaurant; but the bar menu was also very good and less formal.Service was first class.Only problem (small) is the hotel is located on a very busy road with nothing to see - you need to get a taxi (very cheap) to the action.I would stay there again.

We were 2 families.  We stayed there 2 nights. The hotel is situated in an ancient well preserved building which is completely different from what we saw so far.Crew was amazing along all our stay. And I mean all crew. Reception managers restaurant and others. All tried to make our stay the best.The hotel offers several restaurants. We tried the Japanese and the barbeque which were very good.Breakfast was relatively simple but much more than sufficient. The only problem I had was pigeons which woke me up at 0530.Rooms were very large and comfortable. Designed in a manner to coincide with the hotel building. Great place great service.

If you are looking for a get away, leaping into another time dimension, solitude and intimate with that special person, then you are at the right zone, right place.This is NOT your average holiday. Place will take you back in time, the architecture, surroundings, views, every piece of furniture and the avatars of Himalayas will beam you to a different planet.I would go again

This hotel is like an island of peace and beauty in the caos and traffic of Katmandu. Everything is very pleasant to our senses and I wish to point to the kindness and sweetness of the people working in the hotel.It is understandably a bit expensive but we found it acceptable and rather compensated by the pleasant staying.Just to find something to improve I would indicate the breakfast which can be richer in variety and perhaps serve a better coffee.I would indicate the Dwarika’s as the first choice in Katmandu, by all means.

I spent one night at Dwarika's during a recent business trip, and only wish that I could have stayed longer. Location:  Heavy traffic can affect travel times.  During off-peak hours, however, Dwarika's is under a 30-minute drive from the airport, and about 15-20 minutes from the Thamel tourist area.  Rooms surround an inner courtyard, and I had no problems with traffic noise.Design:  The property is a thoughtful restoration of a local heritage property.  Rooms combine historic detail with modern conveniences.  My junior suite was huge, and absolutely immaculate.  There was a large bathroom and dressing area, plenty of storage, a desk, and a separate living area, all with ample windows.Service:  Staff members were extremely attentive and responsive.  The hotel pays close attention to details like helping guests with currency exchange at a competitive rate, or offering cookies and chocolates with the turndown service.Food:  The breakfast buffet is quite generous, and includes local options in addition to standard Western fare.The hotel's amenities include a couple of appealing handicraft and souvenir shops, as well as several restaurants.  For me, Dwarika's does everything right.  The hotel is an excellent choice for professional service with traditional architecture and design.

Feeling like one has stepped back in time, the ambiance, architecture, the regal rooms, resplendent to the royal suites of the 14th century Malla kings of Nepal and of course the service; all absolutely superb. This rates as one of the very best hotels I have ever stayed in. With a long list of notable personalities that have chosen to stay here, it is apparent why this was their choice. As the owner informed me, the hotel was built around the collection of ancient and historic window and door frames collected by Mr. Dwarika Das Shrestha, many moons ago. He wanted to preserve the rich artistic and architectural splendor of Nepalese history. The remainder of the hotel finishes are of traditional and mostly historic furniture, fixtures and fittings complemented with fresh flowers on a daily basis. The buildings are set round a series of linked paved courtyards, which are serenly atmospheric and peaceful. A grand outdoor swimming pool, and a 21st Century spa and gym for those inclined. Food superb, in particular the Krishnarpan, the Nepali speciality restaurant at Dwarikas. Quite frankly the only place to stay in Kathmandu!

Absolutely loved this hotel. We felt like Kings and Queens residing in a magnificent ancient palace. The rooms are huge and spacious. The courtyards are inviting and relaxing. The staff are super polite and hospitable. They take care of your every need. We had a 6 course dinner at Krishnapan restaurant which was delicious and a memorable experience. Highly recommend the City Country package offered by the hotel - 2 nights in Dwarika Kathmandu and 3 nights at Dwarikas resort in Dhulikhel. It has many spa and meal inclusions. Kathmandu is a cramped noisy city and Dwarika is an oasis of peace and calm right in the heart of city.

The hotel is only 10 minutes from the airport, and really showcases traditional Nepalese crafts. BUT...the pool is ice cold, the shower fixtures need to be updated, the mattresses are to old and soft, the pillows are too hard and simple things like printing a boarding pass takes 3 requests of the front desk.  I was served by many staff wearing a tag "trainee", but there was n one actually training them.  The breakfast buffet was marginal.  I was told by many that this hotel is known for its atmosphere, but the Hyatt has better service.

Dieses über Jahre hinweg privat aufgebaute Hotel ist wohl einzigartig auf der Welt. Die vom Gründer geretteten handwerklichen Kulturschätze, verbaut in einer traumhaften Anlage, verdienen Respekt. Neben der 5-Sterne Qualität des Hauses leistet man mit dem sicherlich hohen Übernachtungspreis auch einen Beitrag zur Rettung nepalesischer Handwerkskunst.

The entrance to the hotel is not very auspicious being on a busy road about 10 minutes from the airport. But....inside is a peaceful oasis with a warm welcome and excellent service. Our room was large with a good sitting area, a dressing area, two washbasins, a separate bath and shower. The King-size bed was clean and comfortable.  It overlooked the swimming pool. There was complimentary fresh fruit and plenty of bottled water in the room. Ground coffee and a selection of teas were also provided. Service in the hotel was excellent. The breakfast menu was extensive and varied, and eggs were cooked to order. The dinner menu was also good and well-presented. Wine is expensive at the table and in the bar [equating to at least £50 per bottle] - Nepalese beer is much cheaper and very drinkable!  There were a few small shops in the courtyard of the hotel with a range of gifts to take home. The only downside is the lack of parking space, but for most visitors this would be of little consequence. Overall, we were very pleased with this hotel and even more pleased that, when we revisited it after 10 days touring, we were offered the same room. Warmly recommended!

With a building created originally as a museum for ancient Nepali architectural artifacts, I have never seen a hotel like this one. Add in the impeccable service, fabulous food, and great atmosphere,  and you have the recipe for vacation perfection. Every room is different, featuring some old Nepali items. The one odd thing is that the doors are closed by padlocks, so it is difficult for individuals to leave the rooms separately.

This family run hotel is truly an amazing oasis in the midst of Katmandu. We stayed here for three delightful evenings. The restaurants including a traditional Nepalese restaurant were fantastic. Great food Great service. The complex is beautiful furnished with authentic Nepalese furniture. Even the windows have been salvage from historic properties each is a carved masterpiece.Strolling inside Dwarika's compound you would never know that outside is a gritty world still recovering from the effects of the earthQuake in 2015. If you hare in Katmandu stay here its worth it.

How wonderful to arrive here after the general craziness of this vibrant city.  Beautiful design in and out complete with pool and traditional style. Loved the Japanese restaurant which was a surprise to find such great food. They also have a Nepalese restaurant but we didn't have time. Minor gripes: electricity in our room went our at night so I had to run around to find a socket that worked for my phone. Also, the bed was super hard - not sure why - maybe a Nepalese thing but seriously like concrete. We had an extra bed too plus lots of room. Really wonderful overall with just minor niggles.

Un hotel en el que te sentís como en tu propia casa. Muy cómodo. La calidad de atención de todo el personal es muy profesional, todos muy amables. Los restaurantes del hotel son muy buenos. La calidad de la comida que sirven en el desayuno también muy buena.Todo excelente. Estuvimos solo por tres días pero nos hubiéramos quedado un par de días más para poder seguir disfrutando de todo ese bello lugar.

Incredible hotel with fascinting history. A true sanctuary in the crazy beautiful city of Katmandu. Be sure to try out the taster menu (you can go up to 27 courses but we stuck to 9 which was plenty!). Very kind and helpful staff.

Friendly and professional staff.  Sit down check-in.  Room was very comfortable, spacious and quiet.  Bathrooms amenties are provided; including robe and slippers.   Large walk-in closest for carry on luggage and dresser drawer inside.  Safe is easy to use.  Bottle water is provided; loose leaf teas and cookie snacks and fruits daily.  The hotel is centrally located and walkable to the busy streets.  ATMs are nearby as well.  Restaurant offers delicious Nepalese cuisine.   The hotel is minutes from the airport to catch the flight out or catch the chartered plane to Mt Everest.  October was mild weather-wise.  What a delight to have stayed at this hotel!

Stayed total 5 nights in Kathmandu, one in Dhulikhel. Overall experience was just great. Whatever you have in mind, the personnel will do everything to fix. Rooms are roomy, well equipped, beautifully decorated. The whole place and its inner garden is very beautifully designed, with respect of the history, as well as nowadays customer needs. Strong recommendation. The food is ok, I would't say excellent, but good. The spa is also very nice, thought the one in Dhulikhel is even better. Flip flops (in the rooms) could be changed to an ecological Nepalese versions (prepared from leafs). Yes. My kind of place!

Very beautiful heritage type htl with a great service however lication not so satisfactory. Good for short stay if one only need to stay indoors after sights. Pool, restaurants, bar available taxi stand just outside

A luxurious oasis away from the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu. I've been to Nepal twice -- once on a budget friendly trip, and the other on a more luxurious one; and while I've enjoyed both thoroughly, I'd have to admit that staying a few days at the Dwarika does give you the sense of vacation and comfort you'd want from a vacation.Location is a bit further away than other hotels, and for good reason -- you're away from the incessant noise of Kathmandu, but close enough for everything to be a mere 10-minute ride away.Staff are amazing, rooms are incredible and the atmosphere is special -- well worth the cost. I'd go again in a heartbeat.

We visited Nepal last January for my husband's birthday and stayed at the Dwarika's Hotel.This hotel is one of the most magical places I've ever stayed in. Let me start with the reservation process. I had booked through booking.com and then sent the hotel an email requesting several things: a pick up from the airport, a booking in one of their restaurants and a birthday cake and I had requested a tour guide to take us around. My email was answered promptly and all my requests were arranged in the most organised manner. We were also upgraded to a suite upon arrival!Before I continue I just want to say that if youre planning on discovering the city, I recommend hiring a tour guide from the hotel. They own a travel agency called Kathmandu tours and they have the best programs and local guides. We did a 3 day tour that was lovely. Our guide took us around and we felt like we saw alot of things in Kathmandu and the surrounding areas in a very non commercial way. The actual hotel is fascinating. The architecture is traditional Nepalese architecture and the actual hotel has history. The owner Mr.Dwarika wanted to preserve the traditional Nepalese Newari woodwork and in the old days used to collect window frames and doors. He eventually put them in the family home that is today the Dwarikas hotel. The building encloses a very charming courtyard and garden that has lots of ins and outs and that is just lovely to walk in.The reception is great and all the staff are very professional  warm and friendly.  Once you enter the hotel there is a mini reception in a very charming outdoor courtyard. You are then lead into the main reception where they greet you with a white scarf to wear over the neck:) The whole hotel has very warm hues and colors and traditional Nepalese motifs everywhere. The rooms and bathroom are spacious and super clean. They are decorated in such a tasteful yet traditional manner. You just don't want to leave the room! They have the most comfortable Nepalese type slippers in the room, cute small cubes of traditional soap in the bathroom and a selection of traditional teas. These are small touches that really make a difference and makes ones stay very memorable.The restaurants in the hotel are great. I highly recommend you book in the Nepalese restaurant. They serve a set menu that ranges from 7 to 21 courses it has very tasty traditional Nepali food. It's quite a cultural experience. The continental restaurant where breakfast is served has super great food and serves a selection of international food. We tried it for lunch and for dinner .On the weekend they do an open  Nepali buffet and BBQ outdoors in the courtyard. All I can say is that it is EXCELLENT! There is also a Japanese restaurant. Food was good but nothing to really rave about and it was quite empty. There is a beautiful pool surrounded by very nice sun loungers how ever since it was January we did not try it. There is also a spa  where the massage is really very good. I highly recommend this place if you are planning to visit Kathmandu. There are other hotels there that are good and cheaper. But staying at the Dwarikas is not just a regular stay its an experience that is really not to be missed!

The hotel is located on the busy street. But It is unbelievably tranquil once you step into the building. The court yard was beautiful and quiet. The room was beautiful, spacious, luxurious and comfortable. All stuff was very friendly, careful and attentive. They all were very nice to our child also. They treat us like a royal family!! So nice! The restaurant was very special too. I wish I was more hungry to finish all 9 course meal. Every thing was very delicious. It is more pricy if you compare to other luxury hotels in Kathmandu, but it is totally worth!! You wouldn't get this kind of luxury experience with this price in western countries.  I recommend to everyone.  Perfect place to take a break from the chaos of the city. I would love to come back someday!

We stayed at Dwarikas three times during our recent trip to Nepal, Tibet and Bhutan, using it as a base for our travels.   Dwarikas is a little oasis of calm  away from the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu.  The rooms are beautiful, very spacious and well equipped.  The staff are very helpful and the restaurants are excellent.  Sitting out in their beautiful  courtyard or by the pool in the sunshine after a busy day was a highlight of our trip.

De grootste kamer ooit tijdens dit verblijf in een correct gerenoveerd hotel naar historische normen. Contrast met de buitenwereld is wel groot doch hier moet je doorkijken .Ecologisch denken is hier ook aanwezig. Je waant je in één van de tempels van Kathmandu. Echt een leuke topper als afsluiter van onze rondreis.Zou ik er teruggaan, zeker.Opgelet het is een prijzig hotel

Now you are here I guess you have reviewed their website; all I would say about that is believe it!  Since this is a site for personal experiences, here are some of mine:-It is not cheap!  but something like this never is.  The architecture and style are brill , I thought the place was very old; it is not, just 30 to 40 years.  Hence you benefit from the style and fittings and furniture but with such as modern electrics (including AC) and lifts (or elevators if you wish!).  The staff are very very good, nothing is too much trouble; they are there when you want them, invisible when you do not.  Food was good; one time I had lamb shank and no knife required, just twist the fork and meat fell off the bone.  NO complaints.  I would recommend a good guide for getting around Kathmandu

I travel over 100,000 international miles a year, and I stay at the best hotels I can whenever I can, usually Ritz Carlton, Four Seasons and Relais & Chateaux. Having said that, in my opinion, when you add up all the components that make a great hotel, Dwarika's is one of the finest hotels in the world. Rooms:Stunning, huge rooms, incredible design and comfort, everything just where you want it. Big comfy beds, beautiful lighting, steaming full force showers, fluffy towels exactly where they need to be.. couches, day beds, desks.. a true home away from home, where you can spend time working in your room and simply enjoy the warm luxury.Design:The design in absolutely every corner of this entire property is nothing short of extraordinary with an incredible eye for the tiniest detail (whomever designed this hotel, both architecturally and interiors, is a true gifted person/s). Restaurant design is right on point, creating different experiences at each restaurant, without becoming over thematic or kitsch - the colors, objet d'art placed just so, the lighting, tabletop including plateware is just jaw dropping at times. (p.s. I'm a restaurant designer and I'm in awe of the public areas). Eye candy at every turn as you walk from your suite to the elevator, or simply wake up in the morning and brew a cup of loose leaf tea from the selection of five teas in your room.FoodI normally skip hotel restaurants, but when I do get lured in sometimes its always an incredible disappointment - but not a Dwariki's, food is excellent in every restaurant, true to concept and not a lazy step in cuisine anywhere - not an easy task. Congrats!  The Krishnarpan restaurant is a true gem worthy of 4-5 stars anywhere in the world.Wine and LiquorTight wine list to please all palates without overblowing the lists, ample liquor cabinets. nothing like a brandy around the fire in the cozy bar after dinner when its 5C outside.Facilties:After three days in the jungle working and staying with local farmers, I arrived at Dwariki's as a staging point to perhaps catch up on some sights I'd missed previously, and take as tries of meetings - but, for the three days I was there, I did not leave the property. I moved my meetings from local offices to the Library at Dwariki's, I wrote documents in the courtyard, lunching in different spots, service at my fingertips, even when I didn't know I needed it. I walked the property several times to just clear my head and there were surprises in every corner.  I don't know if there was a fitness center as I did not seek it out after three days of heavy exercise in the jungle, but if there was, it would have been first class. Tables and couches are spread all around the property - find your favorite spot and zone out.Staff:I don't know.. the greatest staff of any hotel I've stayed at? Maybe. Definitely the best, most respectful and warm service all around the property. A quick example, after a particularly rough long 4WD drive back into town I had a back muscle spasm the day after arriving at Dwariki's . I called the front desk to get access to a doctor for some heavy duty muscle relaxants, which ended up being only a 45min wait at 5:30pm on a Thursday in Kathmandu! Within 10mins of my call though, two hot water bottles arrived at my room, the girl who brought them commented she'd heard my back was sore and she took in our her own initiative to do what she could to help before the doc arrived. Then, for the rest of my stay, the staff were so incredibly helpful and thoughtful ensuring that I was improving and offering their aid whenever they could - way more than a person could ever expect.I could go on and on about the service and gracefulness of the staff, as there were so many instances during my stay that added up to make me feel so incredibly welcome and relaxed while on property.Location:Only drawback - 15min-20mins to Thamel in a taxi ($5-$6) depending on traffic, but super close to the airport. Getting to and from Thamel is easy - however here you just can't walk out the hotel door and experience an 'old town' experience like Thamel.Make your own mind up - I've stayed at the other great hotel here and it is but a shadow on Dwariki's - I'll never stay elsewhere again in Kathmandu -no point in taking second best.

Sans aucun doute la plus belle et la plus authentique adresse de Katmandou. Non seulement l'endroit est magnifique, mais il est en plus apaisant au milieu de cette ville si intense. Le personnel est parfait, les chambres immenses, luxueuses, très joliment décorées. Cet endroit est vraiment un de nos coups de cœur parmi les nombreux hôtels du monde que nous avons connus. Nous y avons passé 2 puis 3 nuits après un séjour en montagne et c'était un réel plaisir de s'y retrouver. Les restaurants sont au niveau de l'hôtel, nous avons testé le japonais et le classique, tous deux de bonne qualité. On a hâte d'y retourner

absolutely stunning hotel and brilliant service, staff couldn't do enough for you. Food and drinks lovely, some drinks are reasonably priced others are ridiculously priced the food is wistful but just so more expensive than getting out into the culture of it and experiencing the street food and local restaurants and bars.

Spent a week in Nepal traveling around and admit this is the nicest hotel by long long way.  That said I am also a traveler who looks carefully at value for the money and one of the things everyone will note is this is also probably the most expensive hotel in katmundu so the expectations are pretty high. What I loved was the fact this hotel has gone to extreme measures to preserve the heritage of the city and the country which is no small undertaking.  Unfortunately,  outside of Asia,  Nepal is known for trekking and for the horrible earthquake last year.  What I admire is this hotel works to have visitors take more from their visit.  What I wish I had done differently is read and followed all trip advisor posts.  So we did the upgrade to the junior suite using a travel agent.  All of the posts said go on the second floor and face the court yard.  We didn't follow that.  We ended up on the 3rd floor (there are only 3 floors unless some buildings have higher ones but I may not have seen those buildings) and we're facing outside the hotel.  Nothing wrong with that but the courtyard was beautiful and wish I had faced it.Out aircon struggled but eventually worked and net net didn't need it too much.The hotel didn't feel full so not sure entirely why they didn't just put us in a nice room that faced courtyard and all that but am not too worried.  End of day one trip advisor post said "there are no bad rooms" and indeed that is true.Massage treatments were fine --lacked finesse and my husband didn't get what he kept asking for "work on my feet" and instead the therapist worked on his calves.  We would have don't multiple treatments but the first one didn't scream to come back.Food was good, but preference was to go out to Himalayan Java for a great breakfast and coffee.  Truly great so I wouldn't worry about including a breakfast package.We wanted late check out but it was too difficult or they really didn't want to let us so we left at 11 and went to our next hotel in katmundu (which I will also rate and was less then half the price) we likely would have spa'd that day or shopped in some of the amazing boutiques.  I highly recommend musu musu for cashmere ... You will not be disappointed!We will be back -- Dwarika will always be a place I will want to revisit.  Hope next time the kinks are worked out and I have learned my lesson -- always follow advice on trip advisor!

Dwarika's Hotel is a wonderful property and I cannot recommend it highly enough.  I had the base-level room, which was spacious (with a massive bed) and beautiful with nepalese furniture and decorations.  The property itself is beautiful, with lots of little courtyards housing the pool and places to sit.  The staff were exceptional, obviously very well trained.It's been said before, but it's true, that this hotel offers a very quiet and calm oasis from the chaos that is Kathmandu.  Stepping through the door is like stepping into a tardis to another world.The only downside to the hotel is its location, south of central Kathmandu.  It is, however, convenient for the airport (less than 10 minutes' drive away) and it is within walking distance of Pashtupatinath.  It is also a (very long) walk from Bodnath and Patan.  For anywhere else you'll need to get a taxi, although these are very easy to find so I wouldn't consider that a problem.The restaurants and bars were great, although the room service menu was quite limited.  Prices were expensive by nepali standards but quite reasonable by international standards.I stayed here at the end of my trip, and at the Yak & Yeti at the start of my trip. Whilst they are both 5* the difference between the two was massive.  Yak & Yeti had a better location, but overall I would definitely recommend Dwarika's.  You won't regret it.

新婚旅行で1泊しました。スタッフは非常に親切で、笑顔で対応してくれましたし、カトマンズ周辺の小旅行も詳しく相談に乗ってくれました。部屋は綺麗で広く、清潔（これ重要！）で雰囲気も完璧でした（その前にハイアットに泊まったのですが、完全に勝っていました）。ホテル内の食事も雰囲気抜群で美味しかったです。最終日だったのですが、帰国便が深夜になると話すと、チェックアウトして日中観光すると汗をかくだろうと言ってシャワーを浴びれるように部屋をタダで用意してくれました！おかげで妻とシャワーを浴びてフライトまでゆっくりと部屋で過ごせました。普通はない素晴らしい対応で感動しました。また、泊まりたいです！

We stay here whenever we are in Kathmandu, and love the ambience and the friendly service. Rooms are very spacious, with nice bedding and richly appointed. The only thing we can fault is the very very poor lighting in the bathroom area. Surely this can be upgraded?!

Отличное место, чтобы отдохнуть в тишине. Имеется несколько ресторанов на территории. Сервис на высшем уровне, но и цены не маленькие. Все чисто и цивильно. Можно сказать, что это одно из самых "пафосных" мест в Катманду.

Recently visited the Himalayan land for a short business trip and stayed at Dwarika hotel.  The room was Executive standard and it was impressive in terms of traditional feel and the decor, but also had modern fixtures and fittings. Location was good too if you want to be close to the airport.The Japanese restaurant was absolutely fabulous and authentic, coupled with a very polite and understanding Japanese manager.Local markets are nearby too if you fancy bit of souvenir shopping.Breakfast was the only downside in terms of choice of items and their presentation.

Hotel charmoso,uma obra de arte,atendimento nota 10!Eles são muito amáveis e fazem de tudo para sua experiência ser a mais agradável possível.A culinária é boa,com opções de café da manhã.Os quartos são charmosos,as banheiras um convite ao relaxamennto.Spa com diversas massagens,todas ótimas.Simplesmente amei!

We LOVED our stay at Dwarika's in March. I still miss it! We are a family of 4 and were in and out for a total of six nights (back and forth from trekking) and stayed in 208 and 308.We want to extend a special thank you for Maaz, one of the concierges. He made us feel so welcome from the minute we arrived and gave us a special tour of the gorgeous property, teaching us about the building's history and architecture. I want my entire house to look like Dwarika's!We enjoyed learning about the hotel, Kathmandu and Nepal from him. Everyone from the welcoming staff, to laundry, to servers, to front desk were professional and welcoming. We really felt like Dwarika's was a home away from home during our 9 month trip around the world. They set the bar so high, it will be hard to find another spot like Dwarika's!

Dwarika's provided a very relaxing 4 night stay after touring north India for 18 days prior.  The hotel has traditional Nepalese architecture, designed with an enclosed courtyard that provides a quiet place to swim & sunbathe, have lunch or enjoy afternoon tea.  Our room was large with a comfortable bed and tastefully decorated.  I would suggest they switch their bedding to a down (real or alternative) duvet as the blanket was too heavy and restrictive.  The food was delicious and the service, to include reception, wait staff and housekeeping, were all exceptional with a genuine eagerness to please the guest.

Everything was perfect with this hotel. We stayed there three nice and were thrilled with the service, the quality of what they offered. The staff were so nice and helpful. The hotel layout and design was also very nice with artifacts collected around the country and used in building the buildings.

I was here on business and wasn't told where I was staying. Everything about this hotel is grand. My group had the six course meal also and it was especially good. Gotta try the alcohol served during the dinner. It is very......potent.

Для Катманду, с его пылью, шумом, гамом и огромным количеством людей, это просто райский уголок. Тихо, уютно, зелень. А бассейн, это просто фантастика! Про еду и говорить не стоит, все на высшем уровне.Дороговато правда, но оно того стоит!

We stayed in Dwarika's for a few nights whilst visiting Kathmandu at the start of our holiday in Nepal and Bhutan.  It is an oasis of peace and tranquility in the busy city, made from reclaimed Nepalese bricks and woodwork, the saving of which was the aim of the hotel's founder.  Each bedroom is slightly different and each is luxurious and comfortable.  We ate in the flagship restaurant Krishnarpan, although we could only manage the 6-course set menu rather than the 22!  Absolutely delicious Nepalese food.  The Fusion Bar is also a very pleasant place to spend an evening drinking local beer and trying the cuisine.  Breakfast outside in the courtyard is relaxing and tasty.  The staff were all incredibly helpful and attentive.  A wonderful start to a fascinating holiday.

Beautiful hotel with excellent service 😊 the nepalese traditional 9 course dinner is a very nice experience.Rooms are very clean and spacious, and staff are very friendly .From the moment you enter you have full assistance, the concierge is very helpful as well. Breakfast is served starting 6 am which is very convenient for an early start to explore the city

We stayed here of row nights whilst we enjoyed touring round Kathmandu. It is a hugely impressive structure with lovely history. The staff are quite brilliant and our room was to die for, so characterful and well appointed.We ate in the specialist Nepalese restaurant (at the hotel) and we had the 6 course meal which was fun and the food was lovely, but it was very uncomfortable sat so close to the floor for so long.Stay here, they to spend some time doing nothing by the pool and enjoy your surroundings.

Sangita Shrestha Continuing his vision and utilising the sketches through which he had conceived the hotel, his wife and daughter, Sangita Shrestha Einhaus, completed the front building (where the reception is now housed) in 1998. In order to complete the building's façade, they worked closely with a local potter named Hirakaji for close to a year, trying to replicate the horizontally carved designs with terracotta. Using a mold of the carvings from the horizontal reliefs on the door frame that is in front of the Lumbini building, they revived traditional terracotta designs that were used in the valley around the 15th century. These terracotta designs were more economical than wood, but created a similar aesthetic feel to a building's façade. The revival of this tradition has proven to be highly popular, with such designs now being replicated throughout the valley.

Spacious rooms with separate bath and shower. Plenty of restaurants to cater to your food of choice.If you like something a bit spicy, order the Chicken Sandeko, you won't be disappointed.Take time to walk around the hotel and take in the different buildings and wooden features. There are a few friendly dogs wandering around as well if they're not too shy to come out.I will be staying here again in the future.

i loved this hotel . The decor of each roomwas a fabulous mix of antique woods with midern onvieniences . im suprised this hasnt bern a cover of a travel magazine . i didnt expect something this nice  this is designated a 4 star but is nicer than many 5 stars . Food at the restaurants was greatand service was great . i cant wait to go back

Everything about Dwarikas is quintessential!  Amazing history and architecture lovingly maintained.  Very friendly and attentive staff - great food and an atmosphere that radiates calm and serenity.  Nepal is suffering from not only the effects of the earthquake on toureism but also a fuel crisis. I would highly recommend anyone thinking of going to Nepal to not miss this experience!  I traveled solo with Abercrombie and Kent for an 11 day "Images of Nepal" which included Kathmandu, a 4 day trek (with a support crew of 9!!) in the Annapurna and Chitwan National Park.  Rajeev (Dharma Travel) showed me all the sights of Kathmandu and shared his personal experience of the earthquake.  Tanka and Chering cared for me for the 4 day trek (a lot of uphill climbing and rather a lot of leeches) but wonderful scenery and little villages along the way, and Veneeta the lovely naturalist (In Chitwan) enabled me to see a tiger from the back of an elephant !!  A very rare and lucky sighting!!!Please go there - they really need the toursits to help them recover

This hotel is a wonderful oasis. It is a little way away from a lot of what goes on in Kathmandu, but that sort of helps. It is beautiful, and beautifully kept. The rooms are very well appointed, and you really feel as though you are somewhere special with each room having its unique attributes. Mine overlooked the pool and was very spacious. The staff are charming and keen to assist. As across all of Kathmandu, there are frequent power interruptions but backup generation kicks in very quickly. The internet is quick and stable. There are I think 3 restaurant options including a bar. Just a wonderful place to unwind and enjoy some tranquility.

Kathmandu da tarihin içinde kaybolmak ve lezzetli yemeklerini tatmak için kaçırılmayacak bir fırsat . Bu otel çok kaliteli dışarıdaki keşmekeşten uzak pırıl pırıl her tarafı tarih kokan bir otel . Kesinlikle tavsiye ederim.

So look this hotel is definitely an experience, its a beautiful structure, and the rooms are huge (again I booked a suite so Im not too sure about how the normals stay). The bed was comfortable, the bathroom was enviable and the waterfall shower was-dare I say it, yes I will: romantic. The pool is great, the facilities in the property are trendy with affluent locals and guests. the traditional restaurant is amazing, I really recommend splurging and going for the largest tasting menu. Though we couldn't finish it it was worth every precious bite.Location is great and there is quiet (as quiet as it gets in Nepal, we were still woken up by barking dogs twice). You could find a modern and trendier alternative, but people don't really go to Nepal for that kind of stay, so stay here, it is a great hotel, well deserving of the pride that the hotel staff obviously feel for their properties.Also if you leave the hotel and take a left there is a random cafe, I know you shouldn't eat street food in Nepal because of pollution, but you must try their momos. You will get poisoned, and I did get poisoned, but the deliciousness is worth every agonising moment on your throne (none resident stomachs simply can't handle the water quality in the country).

The Dwarika’s Hotel in Kathmandu is literally a ‘living museum’. The décor and the attention to detail are just amazing. The furniture, décor, fixtures and fittings are just really quite extraordinary. The Dwarika’s Hotel is well located for exploring the city. It's not cheap but worth it if you are not restricted by budget. I would say that this is definitely one of the best hotels in Kathmandu.

Um hotel incomum, com uma história que evoca toda sua razão de ser. Foi construido para que possamos admirar a arte de entalhamento das molduras das janelas e portas. E de quebra, é o hotel mais bacana, charmoso e confortável na cidade. Parece incrível que ele se insira dentro do caos de forma tão coerente. Mas o faz. E te deixa feliz!

Although this lovely restored hotel is in the midst of the chaos that is Kathmandu, as soon as you step through the hotel gate it's like a quiet, peaceful oasis, totally separate from the noise, garbage and pollution.  The hotel and grounds are immaculately clean, and beautifully scenic with an outdoor pool and several seating areas, several restaurants to choose from, a nice bar/lounge with free internet access, and impeccable service throughout (we had one small exception to the "impeccable service" rule in the Nepali-style restaurant where the maitre d' displayed a bit of an attitude, but management corrected the problem more than adequately by upgrading our room on our return visit to the hotel during the same trip).  The food in all the restaurants was delicious, and the rooms themselves spacious, comfortable, clean and well-appointed.  I am a very picky traveller when it comes to hotels and service, and I would return to this hotel without hesitation.

Las habitaciones son espaciosas y confortables. Los dueños son encantadores y te hacen sentir como en casa. Los desayunos muy completos y el personal siempre pendiente de todo lo que puedas necesitar. Suelen hacer bbq por la noche por lo que todo es muy familiar. El chofer/guarda que está en la garita es muy amable y educado. La verdad que muy recomendable y si volviera a ir a Katmandú no dudaría en ir a este hotel. La ubicación magnifica.

Outside, high walls that hide the beauty inside. My husband and I stayed 4 days at the hotel. As we entered, we were delighted with the internal gardens, the reception, the lobby of the hotel. All in typical architectural style of Nepal and the hotel strives to preserve pieces of art that tell us the history of the country. Our room, a junior suite, very broad, with comfort and beauty. However, we were somewhat disappointed with the service offered, especially considering the high price paid by the daily. When we reached the hotel we were welcomed by the hotel staff, but the hostess gave us very little information about the services offered by the hotel, not talking about the use of the pool, spa, shops, library, restaurants, limited-only show us the room and inform about the time of breakfast. We had to figure out everything ourselves. Room service is reasonable, short of replacement products in the bathroom and minibar. The hotel's main restaurant, offers a good range of good quality food and very attentive waiters. However, in the restaurant by the pool, the service is very slow. There is a Japanese restaurant and another Nepali, the latter very beautiful in terms of decor and varied menu, but we did not have chance to try. It is worth but needs to improve its services to support the five stars.

I stayed in this incredible hotel for a few days after an Everest base camp trek a couple of years ago and the earthquake has brought the memories flooding back. With all the suffering and carnage wrought by the earthquake in the city, I hope this place wasn't too badly damaged and that the staff are OK.It was a beautiful jewel of a hotel, totally unique, staffed by wonderful locals, and I will hopefully return soon if it's not been destroyed. (I've checked on G**gl* and can't find anything!).If it's still standing and you ever get a chance, stay here even if only for a night or two for one of the most unforgettable hotel experiences you'll ever have.

I had stayed at Dwarikas a few years ago so already knew that it was an exceptional hotel - a unique location and wonderful staff led by the unstoppable Sangeeta. However it was the events of the Kathmandu Earthquake that unexpectedly led me to revisit. The day after the earthquake I spent a fruitless 11 hours at Kathmandu Airport trying to get on a flight to Varanasi which was subsequently cancelled and so went to Dwarikas for the night.Despite the terrible situation and the personal crisis that everyone was facing, I received a warm welcome back and was offered the opportunity to stay with the other guests, sheltering in the garden. For anyone who thinks that spend the night in the garden sounds terrible, you have no idea what living in the aftermath of a quake is like. I was incredibly grateful for their hospitality and for the surprise arrival of hot noodle soup which was much appreciated. The team worked tirelessly around the clock looking after their guests and doing their best to help despite torrential rain, no power supply and continuing shocks throughout the night - all this with many staff having no home of their own to go to or family members who were injured or killed in the earthquake. Nepal is a beautiful country and Kathmandu an incredible location to visit and I would encourage everyone to visit. Since I am writing this only days after the earthquake it may not be the right time to visit straightaway but Im sure that given some breathing time and recovery time it will indeed be restored. Please support Nepal now by donating if you can and by visiting this beautiful country when its safe to do so. And when you're in Kathmandu, please stay at Dwarikas.Thank you.

We stayed at this hotel twice during out time in Kathmandu. First upon arrival from USA and second departing on the morning of the earthquake. We had a wonderful stay both times. Our junior suite 410 was outstanding and probably the largest triple we have ever had in any of our travels worldwide. It was comfortable and spacious, with excellent facilities and beds.Our second stay was in junior suite 308 which was fine but not quite as large or comfortable as 410. Surely if we had never seen 410, 308 would have been a five star as well. It merely lacked some of the extra space and universal plugs that made 410 so, so exceptional. The floor plan had slightly less privacy for three, we were spoiled by 410. In all other respects 308 was great!We ate in several of the restaurants and each was very good. The lamb shank was really tasty and the Japanese restaurant food was good as well. Breakfasts were buffet style with lots of choices and ample quantity. Overall the chef and baking was exceptionally good in each instance.  We would definitely stay again.  Hopefully they sustained little or no damage or injury to staff as the place was beautiful and staff warm and friendly.

J'ai eu l'occasion de séjourner à deux reprises en 2013 dans cet hôtel, dont j'ai gardé un merveilleux souvenir . J'écris cet article aujourd'hui car je craignais qu'il n'ait été sérieusement endommagé par le récent séisme, mais des avis de voyageurs présents la semaine dernière m'ont paru plutôt rassurants . Monsieur Dwarika avait été choqué de voir des trésors d'architecture laissés à l'abandon ou détruits dans les villages népalais ; il avait donc décider de sauver ce qu'il pouvait en les rachetant aux villageois et en les stockant jusqu'à ce qu'il y en eut assez pour construite son hôtel avec . Il eût été triste que ses années de travail aient été anéanties .L'accueil est chaleureux, la famille de Monsieur Dwarika, décédé depuis, dirige l'endroit de main de maître .Les chambres sont très agréables, les différents restaurants de grande qualité, le service efficace, et une fois le seuil franchi, on oublie la quartier fort bruyant et poussiéreux pour se retrouver au milieu des fleurs et des oiseaux .

After two weeks of trekking and staying in lodges and camping, this place was an absolute oasis, but let's face it, it is an oasis anyway.  Away from the madness of Thamel, this is a place to relax and reflect. Built from handmade bricks and rescued carved wood, it is a piece of Nepalese history.  We stayed in a heritage suite which was beautifully appointed, with a huge bed and a day bed, sitting area, an enormous bathroom with a separate toilet and shower. There was a great selection of loose leaf teas and coffee.  There are beautiful courtyards to relax in, and a very nice pool area.  The staff that we met were friendly and attentive. Reliable, quick WiFi.You will probably need to catch a taxi if you want to do any shopping or venture out (make sure you set the fare before you get in! The meters are never used).Highly recommended.

We stayed at this hotel about a month ago.  It truly is a treasure of a hotel and the environment showed the heritage and beauty of the Nepalese culture.  The grounds were very well maintained and showed off the beautiful architecture of the region.  The room by far exceeded our expectations.  The large room had décor of many local pieces of crafts and furniture.  The bathroom was almost as large as some rooms of other hotels.  We hope that if any damage occurred from the earthquake that it was minimal.  This hotel and the whole area of Kathmandu are true wonders of the world and any damage would be a  major loss to all.  Our wishes of a quick recovery to this land go out to all.

This was probably the most unique and beautiful hotel I have ever stayed in.  The rooms are huge and no room is the same as any other and the staff and meals were stunning.  An excellent base in Kathmandu and I would highly recommend staying there.

This has to be the best hotel in Kathmandu. We arrived at night and upon entering the property were amazed by the courtyard all lit up romantically with candle lights. It's a heritage property with so much charm especially on the heritage deluxe room. The staff were very friendly. Only disappointment was that we could not eat at the traditional Nepali restaurant as they required advance booking to prepare the course menu which we wish we were advised in advance . Also the transportation to the dhulikel resort where we stayed for 5 nights was very expensive at 72 usd ++ when the return was only 30 usd ++. This inconsistency was a bit bothersome. Nevertheless I would absolutely recommend this hotel to all Kathmandu travelers. We spent our last night at the Hyatt Regency which was of a much lower standard , but cheaper. bravo!

Firstly, Kathmandu city is filthy, polluted, chaotic & often depressing. Dwarika's is a haven of perfectness. It is spotlessly clean. The staff are delightful & once you step inside the main door you are calmed.We stayed in a Junior Suite, well actually we stayed in 3 different JS. The first, room 27, was a huge disappointment, dark & cramped & nothing like as advertised. We complained & were moved the next day to room 106, which was great. The only fault we could find was there was no separate shower, which really is no fault at all!! Later in the trip on our return to Kat & Dwarika's we were lodged in room 317. Amazing room & being in the same building as reception, the Internet was lightening fast. The food was fine. Breakfast was a buffet, ok but very warm! The main restaurant, same one for breakfast, served food all day & the quality was good, but the service was really slow. The specialty Nepalese restaurant looked ok, but it involed sitting on the floor to eat, so we didn't bother. The standout, however was Mako's!! This Japanese restaurant hidden inside Dwarika's was rarely full & the food was some of the best I have tasted anywhere!!!!!I probably wouldn't return to Kathmandu, but if I did, I would definitely stay at Dwarika's.

Dwarika's Hotel is a stunning place to stay!  We were there for three nights, and I could not recommend it more highly.  The service is excellent, and the accommodations are lovely.  You leave the dusty streets of Kathmandu, and enter a serene courtyard, built and decorated in traditional Nepali style.  Many decorated wooden windows line the walls looking out on the courtyard, and the interior is decorated with many lovely traditional furnishings.  The restaurant serving breakfast is very good, and we ate dinner there, as well.  The service in the restaurant is also excellent.  If you are in Kathmandu, this is the place to be!

Nepal is full of art, culture, character and heritage. Dwarika's hotels have the combination of all these best qualities! I chose to stay at both Dwarika's Kathmandu and Dhulikhel resort for the total of 6 nights, together with 2 days city tour and 4 days hiking package from its sister tour company. It has by far exceeded my expectation given I am quite a demanding traveller. Dwarika's Kathmandu hotel is a master piece - from the wood carving windows to the great service, to the well prepared Nepali cursine. I felt truly indulged in the fine Nepali's lifestyle, livining like a riyal princess. Dwarika's Dhulikhel resort is one of its kind. The whole resort is on a hill itself, with its strategic location you will find yourself facing one of the world greatest view - Himalayas! There is a helipad to take passengers to the base camp if the budget allows. Resort is full of activities, you will find yourself busy running from one location to another and wish you have had more time. One of the highlight was the city tour and hiking package where the company had amazing professionals arranging, leading and guiding me through the ancient towns and safely hiked around Annapurna!I am so glad that I chose Dwarika's group to arrange my entire Nepal trip!

I did not stay here. I was only there for lunch. First the place is so unique with the beautiful architecture and wood carvings. The layout inside the entrance is just so nice with numerous places to sit or lounge (e.g., cabana like units with white flowing curtains), gorgeous flowers and plants, and a swimming pool. There were some nice shops too. The food was fine, service was good, and did I mention the place is beautiful?

On our trip to Bhutan we stayed 2 nights in this hotel. (one night on our way to Bhutan, and one on our return). The hotel is a compound with interior gardens and few different buildings located in it. It is beautifully renovated. The rooms are spacious and very nicely decorated. We had lunch at the main restaurant, the local food was very spicy but in the evenings there is a nice bbq buffet with a big variety of  choices.The staff was very helpful and we could leave some of our stuff in the hotel until we returned a week later. Our son forgot in the room a stuffed toy and they found and kept it also until our return.The inner garden with bars and restaurants are so beautiful that my only regret was that we were only passing through and I would have wished to be able to just spend a whole day enjoying it.

After a week on the road on a volunteer mission, to arrive at this stunning hotel felt like reaching an oasis after a long trek in the desert. A former palace, the hotel (let's call it a resort, that's how it feels) has spacious grounds, beautiful areas to chill on a day bed, ample choice of restaurants and bar areas and beautiful, warm, friendly service. We stayed in a large junior suite overlooking the centre of the resort, with comfy beds, a large bath and big day bed - Perfect for 2 travel companions to spread out. Whilst located outside the central tourist areas, you can easily hire a driver or take cabs to wherever you need to go. We chose the former and paid about $25 Aud for a half day. The day spa here is lovely and has a good range of treatments. Rooms were a bit cold (but it is winter) and the singing bowl therapy is not to be missed. If you are looking for an excellent quality hotel without the blandness of a global hotel chain, this is worth checking out. We plan to return to Nepal same time next year and will without a doubt be returning to this gorgeous haven of style, peace and luxe accomodation.

We were there during mid December 2014 with our family and stayed for 3 nights in this beautiful hotel.Rooms - we were upgraded to family suite which we were thankful to their management. Rooms are large and have enough space with all the amneties. Except dont expect any external views from the windows but can view the internal court yard of this hotel.Service - excellent and always there to assist.Food - breakfast was good and with good number of varieties. they have couple of in house restaurants which are very good but its quite expensive.Power back up - there is always a power cut in KTM but no worries in this hotel as they have 24/7 generator as back up.I will definetely recommend this hotel to anyone who are on leisure holidays and although is not near to Thamel area but taxis are easily available from here at approx NRs 400/.

We were so lucky to discover this boutique gem in Kathmandu .. It's such a beautiful homey place to stay with extraordinary architect as if your living in the old royal palaces with humble sweet helpful and joyful staff 👌and great tasty food and great spa massages done with professional ladies . The best part they did a very nice birthday surprise for my husband 🌹which made our stay there more worthy✨ It was 2nd home in nepal

This is my second time at the hotel and was not disappointed. I think I loved the hotel the second time even more. They have perfected every part of this hotel. From the moment you walk in it smells like heaven. The rooms are spacious and have a great energy in them. Everyone at the hotel goes beyond their way to help you. I love this place and can't wait o go back and makes sure everyone I know who visits that city goes there. Try the spa!

I have never loved a hotel until now.  Kathmandu is dirty, noisy, and crazy.  Dwarikas is another world. Slightly out of center, built as a large compound with all windows facing the huge interior square, Dwarikas is tranquil. Your room is spotless and furnished with antiques. The buildings themselves incorporate thousands of carved wooden windows and other decorative elements salvaged by the founder as Kathmandu transformed into the modernish city it is today. The staff is friendly but not overdoing it and you feel at home.  It's not stuffy and most guests are wearing hiking gear and other casual outfits. The spa is great and the restaurants went out of their way to accommodate an alergy in our party. Cannot emphasize enough how great this hotel is. Because no smaller rooms were available we stayed in a junior suite which is enormous but peaked at the other rooms which were also lovely and very large. Do yourself a favor and stay at Dwarikas. You will be glad you did.

This is a stunning hotel which showcases reclaimed Nepali architecture and artefacts and supports ancient trades by using indigenous artisans for non-reclaimed items.  It is a refreshing change from corporate, homogenous offerings. The hotel was immaculately clean and smelt wonderful - I was told it was citronella.  The staff were welcoming, polite and attentive.  Good food with plenty of choice.Nearly everything about the bedroom was faultless.  It was big, elegant and very comfortable BUT it was Room 209 (I imagine 210 is similarly affected).  It is in an echo chamber so avoid it if you do not want to be woken up at 4.30 every morning.  Our stay would have been perfect except this intrusion.  Simple double/triple glazing would rectify this problem.  We have suggested this to the hotel and I hope that they follow through on the the suggestion.

I recommend The Dwarika's Hotel with my eyes shut.A very beautiful property, nicely decorated and very charming.The rooms are very spacious and comfortable. Food and service are great and the staff very friendly and helpful.It's an oasis in the middle of a busy and noisy city. The location is great, very close to the International airport and to the Pashupatinah Temple.It's worth a visit !!

Tudo no hotel vale a pena...Recepção: atenciosa e muito eficaz nas suas solicitações.Quarto: amplo, com banheira e chuveiro, duas pias, mesa de estar, cama XX King Size (enorme!!), enfim, talvez um dos pontos mais fortes desse hotel!!Restaurantes: comida muito boa! Vale a pena a visita!Ambiente externo: esse sim o ponto mais forte do Hotel! Arquitetura de época perfeitamente restaurada!! Simplesmente lindo e charmoso!!Localização: ao lado do aeroporto, no coração da cidade!

Having spent a week in Nepal, I am completely at ease to recommend the Dwarika Hotels as the best in the country. It is simply a unique place trying to preserve the culture of ancient Nepal. It is refreshing that someone cares about preserving the culture of a country and displays artifacts from times past to show visitors the rich history of this lovely place.The staff is well trained and management is trying to please its customers.The hotel is an oasis in an otherwise maddening city overwhelmed by traffic congestion and pollution.If you go to Kathmandu, this is the place to stay if you have the resources to pay for it.It is more than a 5 star hotel!!!!!!!

O Dwarika já merece atenção pelo papel que exerce na conservação da cultura nepalense (arquitetura e restauro/abrigo de artefatos). O hotel é charmoso e os restaurantes estendem suas mesas pelo páteo central, muito agradável. O café da manhã poderia ser melhor. Às sextas-feiras, é servido um bufê especial de grelhados na área da piscina que eles chamam de churrasco, mas vai bem além em opções (servindo inclusive para os vegetarianos). Ótimo espaço para abrigar festas. Ficamos em uma suíte júnior localizada no terceiro pavimento do prédio central: quarto amplo, bonita vista para o páteo do hotel, bastante agradável. No mesmo período fiquei também no Hyatt, concorrente: menos vibrante mas mais sofisticado e com uma cozinha mais notória. Ainda assim, o Dwarika vale a pena como experiência hoteleira genuinamente local.

As others have written thins hotel truly is a haven in this busy city, you step into the courtyard and leave the busy street behind you and you are in another world. Our room was beautifully appointed with all lights working and AC working. Yes the power flits off but the generator normally backs up within a few seconds. We had a room facing in to the courtyard and it was very quiet but we did have windows closed.We ate at the Nepalese restaurant and the main courtyard one, both very good food, it did though take a while to get the bill each time.One little gripe. Internet in a hotel of this price should be included, not an extra charge, it is complimentary at Dwarika's Resort so why pay at the hotel? WIFI is now as necessary part of a room as soap in the bathroom so this should really be reviewed.Whilst we were there for three nights one night the pool area was cordoned off for an EU cocktail party and the next night the courtyard closed for Standard Bank. The EU function did not impact us as we were booked at the Nepalese that evening for dinner but on our last night we wanted to yes the courtyard but could not and ended up having dinner in the breakfast room which was a bit of a shame.

Dwarikas Hotel is certainly very nice looking,but there are two main drawbacks.Firstly, with its premium position, it rents out the main public area for parties and so that peaceful rest is somewhat difficult with a large noisy party going on within the echo chamber that is the main area. There are obviously limited facilities within Kathmandu for large events so we had kids running round for Spain's National Day and then a bunch of bankers taking over the place and commandeering all the seating outside. The staff actually removed all the tables and chairs except three tables, and roped then into the area for the bank The three tables they left behind were not even remotely sufficient for the dozens of resident guests. We stayed three nights and two of the three were party nights. Paying a small fortune for the best hotel and being told the main outdoor restaurant is effectively closed to people paying to stay, is unacceptable, particularly when a lot of the staff are waiting on the party leaving residents waiting around for service. The only options were the two high end restaurants or the place they serve breakfast - so much for a memorable last night in the hotel. We ended up in a remote overflow room of the breakfast area with some very polite and apologetic staff.The second is that they hold the events right under the windows of the suite rooms, so getting an early nights sleep isn't actually possible while a banks drinks reception rolls on for hours. It went on for four hours and then the staff had to drag the furniture back into position. The whole area is an echo chamber so it's not possible to sleep. They are clearly just trying to make as much money as they can and really don't care about the people staying in, if they can make more money from people from outside at the same time. They will also helpfully arrange a 0600 Everest overflight, while keeping you from sleeping the night before. The rooms are well done and beds are very comfortable, staff are very helpful, but if you want peace and quiet, you have a choice of traffic noise on the outside - or party noise on the inside, and being unable to use the advertised dining facilities as they have been sold to non- residents. Power does go out regularly but only for a few seconds at a time. During the day, you might not even notice it.Internet is pretty poor quality -  a reasonable price for $10 a day, but dreadfully congested, and we had much faster speeds in a remote lodge in the Pokhara region. At times, a simple iM would take a minute to go through.The pool area and cabanas are quiet during the day and you can get a drink poolside if you are patient - the trick is to order one at the Fusion bar, but don't sign, and go back to your sunbed, and the barman will keep coming out to get signatures, and you can order then. Rooms towards the back left corner of the hotel suffer from barking dogs during the day - no idea at night though as the dogs are inside the hotel and not outside. They could have been guests dogs but I doubt it given their state - an overly fat Beagle, an Alsatian or German Shepherd with rear hip problems and what looked like a Labrador.Staff are good, although the concept of drinking plain, boiled water seems to not translate. The staff are the redeeming feature of the hotel - nothing is too difficult for them, although service can be slow, it's not the staff but the kitchens either being slow, or being in the next city.For this basic lack of consideration for paying residents, I would knock them down a grade and would probably stay in the Hyatt next time which while pretty bland, at least our stay there wasn't disrupted by the sounds of a hotel making money at the expense of the residents. At least the Hyatt is big enough that you can hide from any noise - it isn't physically possible here. Opening your window on the second floor and being able to hear  every word of a party attendees conversation isn't a sign of a good hotel. It's a good hotel physically, and organisationally, but let down by the management prioritising guests over residents.A safe hotel which is better to visit than to stay at I think, on balance. Give the place a miss if an event is planned, and fly on to somewhere else would be a better option in my view. The Nepalese restaurant is certainly with visiting.

From past reviews, I knew that a historic hotel like Dwarika's needed to be part of our cultural Nepali adventure, but I underestimated how much I would fall in love with the atmosphere and exceptional warm culture of the staff of the hotel!  The pictures don't truly capture how much the hotel is a complete indoor and outdoor oasis of exceptional craftmanship and artwork, combined with amazing gardens and outdoor space, and topped with a warm, friendly staff that greet you multiple times per day with a peaceful namaste.Our room was both unique and luxurious.  The food in all the restaurants was exceptional.  The hotel takes their mission seriously to create a full Nepali cultural experience...the spa offers exceptional massages...there was a local musician and dancer playing in the courtyard each evening before dinner...free yoga every morning...and Nepali movies set up in the library each evening.  It felt like an artistic, culinary, and relaxing introduction to the magical world of Nepal all within the hotel.I would recommend this hotel highly be part of your Kathmandu itinerary.

Staff and environment makes Dwarika's the best place on earth. I can only express my gratitude for every wonderful moment I spent there. Every room is a different room and great. Totally recomment it!

After our Mount Everest Base Camp Trek, we just wanted to relax for a few days in Kathmandu before going home again. We are so happy we picked the Dwarika's Hotel based upon TripAdvisor reviews. Kathmandu is very loud and busy but once you enter the hotel you do not notice any of that anymore, it's like entering a little private paradise. The architecture is very beautiful and the hotel consists of different buildings and restaurants. We stayed in the newest building in a room with view on the pool. The room was spectacular and so was the bathroom. The Nepalese restaurant was an experience and the food in the other restaurants was very good as well (the surf and turf in the International restaurant is recommended). The service was great as well. We had a very relaxing time here, sunbathing by the pool, reading a book, nice food & drinks. Exactly what we needed after the Mount Everest Base Camp Trek.

This hotel is absolutely gorgeous. A short drive from the airport and not too far from Durbar Square, it is a truly tranquil spot in the middle of a dusty, busy city.
