Our family of three stayed in a well-appointed large room on the fifth floor with a view over the pool and lush courtyard. The food was good, and it was nice to have a selection of restaurants without leaving the property (Nepali, Japanese and International). The only downside was that although we had booked room for three and paid approximately US $80/night for our nine-year-old to share a room with us, we had to call to request that his bed be made up. And actually, after some further miscommunication (they thought we were calling for turndown service), Housekeeping ended up making up a bed for him on the sofa in the room. At $80 extra per night on top of a steep room charge, I would have thought it would be ready and waiting along with extra towels for him. Other than this, all was well and we enjoyed our stay.

We selected Dwarikas after reading Trip Advisor reviews of the hotel. We wanted a safe, centrally located hotel to maximize our limited time in Kathmandu. Dwarikas is located near the airport and also within easy walking distance to the Pashupatinath Temple.  When we arrived at the airport, the Dwarikas shuttle representative was waiting with a sign as promised. Unfortunately one of our suitcases decided not to get on the flight so instead of hopping right in the van and zooming to the hotel we asked the the shuttle representative to help us find the Qatar Airlines office to track down our lost bag. The shuttle representative was extremely accommodating and actually went to the airport the next day and picked up our lost bag for us.  After a short drive through the crazy streets of Kathmandu to the hotel, we were welcomed into the Dwarikas oasis. The center courtyard is a beautiful display of Nepalese architecture and exudes relaxation. Our room was very nice and had a view to the center courtyard. The room was spacious and clean with a comfortable bed and bathroom facilities. We enjoyed dinner in the traditional Nepalese restaurant located on the property and also took advantage of the spa facilities. They have a few different styles of restaurants on the premises. We even ate in the library with a cozy fireplace one evening. The waitstaff was more than gracious.  We also had issues with Qatar airlines canceling our return flight. The Dwarikas shuttle representative helped us out with locating the Qatar airlines office in downtown Kathmandu and getting our flight problems sorted out. The assistance was greatly appreciated and it was easy to tell that the staff cared about making the guests experience in the hotel and also in Nepal a pleasurable one. I don't think the internet issues described in earlier reviews have been sorted out. With the price of the room there is no question that Internet should be complimentary throughout the stay for guests.  At the end of our trip, we had a 12 hour layover in Kathmandu before our international flight out of the country. We decided to come back to Dwarikas, have lunch and drinks by the pool and also get a massage. After spending a significant amount of money on these services and also our multi day stay the previous week it was frustrating that Dwarikas would not give us a complimentary internet coupon so we could check in for our flight. This was our only gripe about the hotel.   We definitely recommend this hotel and would stay again on our next visit to Kathmandu. Just loved the ambiance and overall experience.

Beautiful place. Well located. Plenty of charm. Isolated from the outside noise. Relatively friendly staff. This should be the start of a great review, but it is unfortunately not: I had high expectations upon arrival as the place is really good looking, and I found the rooms to be very "authentic" (in reality quite modern, but with a very nice historic touch) BUT (and I tried two rooms, just to see if the first one was an exception...) a hotel is ultimately there to allow one to rest, and the beds in this one are really bad (I stayed there 3 nights and my back still hurts 3 days later from having slept on a bed which seemed made of solid concrete); the rooms are poorly isolated, so one is subject to any outside noise at any point during the night; and (in my second room) it was impossible to have hot water stable without calling a plumber to fix it morning and evening. Really too bad, as the place "felt" really good and I would have loved to have a great stay there...

Walking off the bustling streets of Kathmandu and through the doors of Dwarika's is a bit like stepping through the  wardrobe in the Secret Garden.  A haven to experience and enjoy like very few other places, especially in a place like KAT.  After three weeks of trekking and traipsing around the country, this was the perfect wind down hotel.  Amazing comforts and service among spectacular architecture and cultural expression.   Loved it!

D une   architecture sidérante lorsque l’on arrive, et même après. Dans un style newar traditionnel, avec de magnifiques fenêtres, moucharabieh, sculptées. Notre chambre était spacieuse et confortable un petit déjeuner très complet et un personnel très très sympathique. Il y a trois restaurants très différent où l’on mange très bien. Il y a 3 restaurants différents qui proposent des spécialités népalaise. C’est pas donné mais c’est bon Merci à toute l’équipe  du Dawrika pour leur accueil.

Un albergo in stile Nepalese con legni cesellati a mano e arredato con mobili preziosi in stile locale.Sontuoso palazzo d’epoca con camere arredate con cura e bagno ampio con vasca e doccia.3 ristoranti : Neplase dove abbiamo cenato benissimo, giapponese ed un altro internazionale Una bellissima piscina ed una Spa.Al mattino presto c’è un corso di yoga Personale gentile è molto professionale È stato al di sopra delle mie aspettative!Meraviglioso

Perhaps there are "fancier" hotels within Kathmandu, but the Dwarika's has more character & soul than any of those "fancier" accommodations.  This place is 75% 5-star hotel and 25% must-see museum!  Dwarika Das Shrestha had quite the vision with this place... It is a one of a kind stay within the bustling city of Kathmandu and I would not considering staying anywhere else on future visits to Nepal.  The attention to detail throughout the property is incredibly unique... the staff does a remarkable job in every respect... and the breakfast is 5/5.  The rooms are impeccably clean and their house-keeping team does as good of a job as I've ever seen to keep them that way.  The only two negatives I could find were the prices on laundry seemed a bit steep (as they often are at higher end hotels), however, I was able to walk about 3 minutes down the road to a local laundromat where everything was cleaned perfectly for a few dollars (highly recommend this location, which is next to Bajeko Sekuwa Battisputali... I was unable to find the actual name during my google searching)... my only other complaint is the lack of flexibility on a later check-out, when the hotel appeared to be at 1/4 capacity.  Those two things do not do anything to diminish our fantastic stay... Lastly, for those of you with any pandemic concerns lingering... the COVID safety standard at Dwarika's is top notch...  (as is the majority of Nepal, to be honest).  I have not seen a hotel in the US/UK that compares to the lengths taken by the Dwarika's.

Cadre magnifique et authentique un véritable musée Newar dans la tumultueuse et tres poluée capitale de Katmandou, tres bon petit déjeuner, magnifique piscine mais non chauffée, plusieurs restaurants mais nous avons essayé que le japonais au passage tres bon, seul petit bémol pour avoir fréquenté d'autres hotels de cette catégorie dans d'autres pays je pense que  le service pourrait être amélioré!

The place is fine Which is not different then any street or temple area and traditional Kathamandian home;Room and food prices are very high.With same atmosphere and food quality  anyone can find several places in Kathmandu.

Dwarika - a true five star hotel. This is more akin to a palace than a hotel in a beautiful city. The rooms are stunning, the original features take you back in time yet the soft touches provide you with everything a modern five star would (and more!). The Dwarikas staff are nothing short of amazing, they're attentive and knew my partner and I across the hotel. We did not have breakfast or dine in the hotel due to the vast amounts of options elsewhere however the reviews of Toran and the likes are outstanding. The gym is a great effort considering you're in such a hotel, a few running machines, free weights, bench, multipurpose machine, barbells etc. To add there is an awesome yoga studio on the fourth floor which has direct sunlight. The gym is also on the fourth floor which gets a lot of light which is great to energise you.The location is perfect from the airport, if theres no traffic its circa 10 mins, if there is traffic anything up to 30 mins. Travelling around Katmandu from here was very easy too, Thamel is only a 15 min drive with no traffic and there are hotel taxis outside who will take you there for around 400NPR. Taxi too and from the airport also 400NPR. Have to provide a thank you to our driver Dev whose car is parked outside the Dwarika (the only blue car in Katmandu which also for anyone who likes to have normal leg room is a dream ride). We hired Dev for the day to take us around Katmandu to all the top attractions including Chandragiri Hill for a very reasonable fare.All in all I couldn't recommend this hotel anymore, if I ever return to Katmandu I wouldn't look any further than here - this is an independent review, we were never asked to leave a review from either the hotel or Dev as mentioned above.

you step off a busy kathmandu street into an incredible oasis..the collection of beautifully preserved traditional newari buildings around a central courtyard..the sheer quantity of precious artefacts preserved..classy, large, airy, comfortable rooms, lovely breakfast..outstanding service..a truly authentic and unique experience

Me and m,y wife stay 3 night in this Hotel. Wow !! what a wonderful staff and their services. The room was suite and everything facilities. Their breakfast was just supper and so many items. Love to have Puri and Curry. They do have different type of restaurant where you get typical food.We really enjoyed and loved this place.

This wonderful hotel is an oasis in the heart of Kathmandu.  The gorgeous room was large and decorated with true artifacts of Nepal.  The central area of the hotel was a relaxing retreat from the hectic city.  The restaurants were exceptional.  We especially enjoyed the six course traditional dinner at Krishnarpan.

We stayed at Dwarika for 3 nights surrounding our travels in Nepal and this was an outstanding hotel. The rooms were lovely, with every amenity you could want. The courtyard in the hotel was an oasis from the busy city after the days of touring. It was quiet, peaceful and beautiful. The breakfast had so many options to try. The best part of the hotel was the staff. Every person was kind, helpful and always with a smile to offer any assistance. You could see they wanted to provide the best service to their guests. This was appreciated.

Positiv- Anlage: Wunderschön, klassischen Gebäuden aus Ziegelsteinen und geschnitztem Holz nachempfunden mit vielen Blumen, Bäumen und Wasserbecken- Anlage: Drei sehr gute Restaurants- Zimmer: Sehr geräumig und gemütlich- Zimmer: Bad ebenfalls groß mit zwei Waschbecken sowie separate Toilette- Zimmer: Viele Steckdosen, teilweise mit Adaptern- Zimmer: Viele nette Details, z.B. Hausschuhe und Badeschuhe- Service: 5 große Flaschen Wasser kostenlos pro Tag; Obstplatte am Anfang und Pralinen jeden Abend- Service: Personal sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit- Service: Bei Halbpension darf man sich im Restaurant Toran beliebig viele Speisen von der umfangreichen Menükarte aussuchenNeutral- Zimmer: Mittelgroßer Fernseher mit wenigen internationalen Kanälen- Service: Das Frühstücksbuffet ist relativ übersichtlich (auf Standard-4-Sterne-Niveau), allerdings gibt es eine Zusatzkarte mit Service am Tisch mit leckeren Speisen und großartigen SmoothiesNegativ- Anlage: Zwar dringen kaum Geräusche von außen rein, aber das Hotel selbst ist relativ hellhörig und eine große Zahl Vögel macht frühmorgens großen Lärm im Innenhof- Zimmer: Betten viel zu hart und unpraktische Bettdecken- Zimmer: Altmodische Elektrik, keine Steuerung vom Bett aus, viele einzelne Lichtschalter

Stayed here on a package with their sister hotel in Dhulikhel.  Great location - about 10 minutes to the airport and close to the Pashpupatinath temple.We had a Junior suite on the fourth floor that overlooked the courtyard which was large and quiet.The staff are really friendly and helpful, great service in all areas of the hotel. The whole ambience is one of tranquility and calm in a very busy part of Kathmandu.

O hotel é maravilhoso principalmente se comparado com a realidade da cidade. Tem quatro restaurantes e um jardim interno encantador. Um conforto voltar para o hotel após um dia pela turbulenta Catmandu

We had the opportunity to stay at the hotel and was not disappointed.  The rooms are large and elegant, plenty of nice touches and multiple restaurant options on site.  We loved all the food and service.  We enjoyed dining in the courtyard and being surround by wonderful architecture. We enjoyed dining in the courtyard and being surround by wonderful architecture.  It was a great way to end the day in beautify, greenery and removed from the city bustle.Enjoyed the spa and benefited from their help in getting tours setup.  Internet access was great, it was easy to use.  We were very happy at the quality of the tours and the guides flexibility with us.  He was patient and ensured we had a great experience.

The hote is located conveniently close to the airport which is great given the traffic jams in Kathmandu. As you enter the hotel from the main dusty road it's amazing to enter into a courtyard style opening that makes you forget the hustle and bustle outside.Rooms were done in traditional Nepalese style and spacious. Food varied depending on where you ate. The Toran and its adjoining courtyard dining is ok but nothing to write home about, whilst the Krishnarpan serves an excellent se course dinner (ranging from 6 - 22 courses!). We ordered 6 and nearly exploded. Advanced booking is highly recommended.The Fusion bar has a nice feel to it for pre or post dinner drinks.So if luxury and being pampered after a long day out sightseeing is what you are looking for then this is the place.I would have given it 5 stars if the quality of the food was better.

An excellent place to stay for family or business travel.  The visitor is pampered from arrival to departure.  Food is excellent and the wine selection is perfect.  The rooms are comfortable, roomy, and equipped with all you need to be comfortable and well rested.  Birdsong and attentive staff make the vast courtyard a place for rejuvenation and relaxation.The spa has many options for comfort and therapeutic massage.  The pool is beautiful.All in all, an excellent place to stay.

Situated about 15 mins from the airport, this hotel is situated on a busy road and you enter through 2 small wooden doors walking into a large open interior courtyard, leaving all the noise and pollution behind you. It is just an amazing place, with beautiful wood carvings everywhere, lots of places to sit either inside or in the various courtyards and you cannot hear any outside noise! Our room was large, huge bed, usual luxuries in the bathroom with plenty of free bottles of water.Staff v friendly and efficient esp in the bar where we all sat and watched Liverpool play one night!There is a small outside pool, v clean and v cold! Great after a day sightseeing with lots of large beds and outdoor sofas to lie on.Breakfast was OK but I would suggest sitting outside as the dining room is a little dark. We ate 1 night in their traditional restaurant choosing the 7 course banquet which was superb with loads of food. You can go up to 22 courses but 7 was ample for us.We really enjoyed our time here and cannot recommend it enough.Many thanks for a great stay.

This hotel is nothing short of amazing.  We stayed at Dwarika's at three different times during our trip to Nepal.  The people who work at Dwarika's are beyond welcoming and professional.  You are greeted upon arrival with a welcome scarf and their signature hot lemon, ginger, and honey drink.  The property is beautiful with traditional wood carvings everywhere, unique furniture, and stunning courtyard.  It's location made getting to the various sites around town convenient and it is close to the airport.  The rooms are equally, well-appointed and spacious.  We stayed in a regular room, junior suite, and suite.  All have ample space and seating areas.  The suites give you a ton of extra room which is nice and the bathrooms are great.  There are several restaurants to choose from, including a Japanese restaurant which is delicious.  We ate there several nights.  There is a nice pool and great bar next to it.  We had drinks there most nights by the fire.  The gift shops are very nice, including a furniture store.  It is a wonderful place to come back to in the evenings and relax.  Again, the people are what make this hotel so lovely and we thoroughly enjoyed our time here.

My wife and I spent three glorious nights at this property.  As others have commented, it is an oasis of fine service and serenity in the midst of Kathmandu.If we return to Kathmandu, this is the only place to stay!

What a fabulous place.  As soon as you enter you are transported to a beautiful space with handcrafted woodworkings, comfortable yet elegant spaces.  We stayed in 2 different rooms at the beginning and end of our trip and both were excellent, well appointed and clean.  The staff truly makes this an exceptional hotel.  Friendly, very attentive to detail and knowledgable.  Excellent food.  If back in Kathmandu would definitely stay again!

La primera vez que visitó un Hotel tan lleno de clase, buen gusto, exquisitez y elegancia.Estás en el paraíso dentro del maravilloso caos de Katmandú.Cada rincón está impregnado de esa paz que se respira en Nepal y todo ello acompañado de la profesionalidad y amabilidad del personal.

First time to Kathmandu, yes, the  Squares and Temples are extremely beautiful. But the city is completely chaotic, dusty and dirty. I cannot even have a fresh breath outside my hotel.Through the wooden entrance to this 5 stars hotel, it's totally a Heaven! Fresh air, friendly and courteous staff, huge and clean Nepalese style room, and the atmosphere here is very spiritual. You can join yoga and meditation here.I had dinner at Mako's Japanese restaurant in hotel and it's very delicious. And the Japanese waitresses are very attentive and polite. I feel like in Kyoto. This is the best meal I had in my 5 days trip in Nepal.The massage is very good in this hotel too. I tried the Himalayan massage in their spa. It's very relaxing and comfortable. Perfect.I highly recommended this hotel for those who visit Nepal for the first time. Although the price is not cheap, you won't regret it, specially for the fresh air!

What a wonderful property--the staff was so eager to please, and the building itself is like a National Treasure, steeped in rich history.  The story of how the hotel got its start, and what it has become, for guests and the community, as well, is heartwarming. The wood carvings on the building are just outstanding--I'd never seen anything like it.We also had an authentic Nepalese dinner at the Krishnarpan Restaurant, on site, and it was very well done.  I believe its about 7 courses, so you won't leave hungry!They were also nice enough to hold our luggage, for three nights.
パシュパティナートからほど近いので、カトマンズに来たら一度は利用したい。伝統的な建築装飾も保存を兼ねて配置されている。ただし、それなりに料金もかかるので、ランチ程度で満足している。

Beautiful and charming hotel. Hidden away within giant brick walls in Kathmandu. Stayed here twice in two different rooms, each was gorgeous with king size comfortable beds, huge bathrooms with tubs and rain showers with soaps and potions from the spa. The rooms had music and fruit/cookies upon my arrival. Ample in room bar and a large assortment of fresh teas and coffee with French press (deluxe room). Plenty of bottled water is provided. The food at the restaurants is excellent and room service is available. Shops on site. Nice pool and spa. Yoga daily in a rooftop studio. The staff were attentive and wonderful. All the amenities you can ask for from a 5 star hotel but with stunning wood a brick work. Absolutely gorgeous and tucked away. I can’t wait to stay again.

Various traditional heritage Newari houses sporting centuries old intricate wood works salvaged by Late Shri Dwarika Das Shreshtha from being burnt as firewood , congregating around courtyards is known all over the world as Dwarika’s Hotel , winner of the PATA Heritage Award and the INTACH-SATTE Award. The  hotel takes immense pride in an extensive collection of artifacts from the 13th century onwards and preserves the aesthetic sensibility  of  Newari  civilization boasting mastery in bronze  crafts , distinctive  temples ,  intricate wood  carvings ,  sculptures ,  terracotta works , etc .  Though we did not stay in the hotel , we went to Krishnarpan for our dinner . Highly impressed by the dining experience which I reviewed earlier , we moved through the complex and learnt many aspects of the hotel , which I am sharing now .There are 87 rooms and suites excuding the earthiness of traditional  life in the Kathmandu valley . The  handmade traditional Nepali terracotta tiles or individually laid wooden panels are used in  the           flooring .  The furniture is made by traditional carpenters .   The upholstery is hand woven and locally produced, and the line is organic The architect of the Royal Suites is inspires by the abodes of Malla kings . The private terrace offers the magnificient views of snow clad  Himalayan peaks as well as hotel’s beautiful courtyard .Heritage Executive Suites combine traditional style with modern convenience and facilitate splendid view of Hotel’s courtyard .Each of the 43 luxurious Heritage Junior Suites is individually designed with local materials including pottery, slate and brass, as well as genuine antiques and artefacts.Heritage Deluxe Rooms capture the essence of such a lifestyle without compromising on comfort .The  Dwarika’s  hotel  has  three restaurants and a bar . Meals , from Newari cuisines to a range of continental dishes and Japanese flavours , are  prepared  with  fresh  produce  from  the  Dwarika’s own  farms,  which  use  toxin-free  and  environmentally friendly production methods. The Toran offers a variety of continental cuisines , to be enjoyed either in the restaurant or in the hotel’s spacious courtyards – an ideal location for all day lounging and informal dining. The Fusion bar overlooks a swimming pool which replicates 12th century royal baths . Whereas Krishnarpan offers never to be forgotten Newari culinary experience , Mako’s can be patronised for authentic Japanese meals .Pancha Kosha Himalayan Spa offers 2000 years old  experience inherited from ancient traditions of care and respect .

This is a wonderful hotel. From the moment we arrived till we left I could not find fault.  The rooms are large and comfortable. The gardens relaxing and well kept.  A quiet haven from the chaos of the city outside.  In all a great stay.  Highly recommended

Rumbeling down the potholed roads of Kathmandu, we eagerly looked forward to immersing ourselves headfirst  in to this oasis amidst the plethora of flora, friendly staff and Mewari history. If you want a history lesson in art and culture of the Nepali people this would be the place to start. The contained hotel on 4 1/2 acres of grounds has plenty for you to do to relax. Everything is well thought of such as a library, travel desk, outdoor tables and chairs, gift shop, swimming pool, spa, bar and the list goes on. The rooms are large and well thought of. The only thing this hotel should have is an in house ATM because you will directed to one about 3 blocks away, walkable but easier if they had one. It has been suggested by many I'm sure. We enjoyed the breakfast but there is a lack of variety and you will end up seeing the same menu day after day, and notice that the dessert,  if you order the Nepali Thali , a variety on a single large plate, will be what was offered at breakfast!! Go figure!! But the staff are ever pleasing and eager to make you comfortable. You will see the owner putsing around as she lives on the property and she and her family are so interested in where people come from and who they are. This makes one feel like family. There is an adequate business center and a spa that is so quiet and relaxing, using organic products mostly prepared in house from natural ingredients. The variety of treatments offered is amazing. Be sure and try their special Nepali dinner, served in Nepali style with the different foods from the different regions of the country. Makes for a wonderful educational experience. We met many people from different parts of the world.

Charming serving staff, tranquil, peaceful atmosphere in beautiful surroundings, yet all in the midst of fascinating, but super busy and dusty Kathmandu (quite the contrast to serene Bhutan where  we had spent most of the trip!)We stayed in a Junior Suite for one night before flying to Bhutan, then for two nights in an Executive Suite at the end.The Junior Suite was a great size and very comfortable, the Executive Suite yes was larger but long and thin, and if anything we preferred the layout of the Junior Suite. As such, we thought it was probably not worth paying the upgrade cost for the Executuve Suite. There are five of the latter ( and we were in suite 35) and all are different, and possibly others are better. Water pressure was low in the bath taps, which we passed on, and the flowers in the room on arrival were in bit of a limp, sorry state. They were changed and both were nothing major, but not quite what you would perhaps expect when paying for the extra.Altogether however we loved our stay at Dwarika’s. It is real heritage property, full of interesting artefacts, corners and seating areas and the best such option in Kathmandu. Not remotely corporate, and the staff were delightfully welcoming. We particularly enjoyed breakfast and cold drinks/ coffees sat outside in the beautiful courtyards and relaxing and reading in the pool area. Pool itself somewhat cool!  Staff were also very helpful in advising us as to how to locate a restaurant in the Thamel area.We were so glad we had chosen to stay there, as a real haven, post sight seeing and we had a delicious six course dinner at their speciality Nepali restaurant. A delicious chocolate birthday cake was also presented to my delighted husband at the end of the meal. Other meals were good, but we felt the Friday nnight bbq by the pool lacked some atmosphere and the bbq food, although good, could have been served  slightly warmer, or hot plates for provided.

Dans cet hôtel magnifiquement construit à l’ancienne tout est parfait ...il n’y a aucune fausse note   Excellente restauration personnel attentionné et aimable et l’emplacement de l’hôtel est unique. Que du rêve dans cette ville partiellement détruite.

This is one of the best hotels that we have stayed at in this part of Asia.  The hotel is a shrine to wood conservation and is certainly worth an explore when you stay there.  The facilities are extremely good and our room was huge, with a massive bathroom and all the necessary facilities.We dined in the Nepalese restaurant and the food was unbelievably good.  the service was fantastic and all the staff greet you and are pleased and eager to help you.  can't fault the place!

Dwarika's Hotel is a welcome oasis in chaotic Katmandu. The staff if welcoming and helpful. The food is delicious, and the rooms are spectacular as are the grounds. It is amazing that this peaceful spot is smack in the middle of a bustling city.

We stayed here three nights with Abercrombie and Kent tour. A beautiful hotel, everything is nice including friendly service, facilities, restaurants and the bar. The elevator is a little slow, but we don’t mind having a relaxing walk to our room:)Top recommended to friends and family if visiting Kathmandu!

We stayed here for about two weeks when Kathmandu was suffering from major pollution (it's always polluted but this time around it was worse). We stayed at the hotel quarters as much as we could since the pollution was so bad. We ate at the restaurants too. The food was overpriced and okay, especially the Japanese restaurant. Small portions. The main restaurant with Nepali food was better, but not Westernized. The hotel is one of a kind. The rooms are decorated with precise Nepali detail. We stayed in the double room. You can take a bath with the provided black salts. Mattress is firm, but other than that, pretty ordinary in terms of amenities. The plus is the architecture. Very noisy with bird sounds in the morning but at night it was relatively quiet. Best is no pollution from outside streets.Right outside the hotel is a busy road but you can't hear it in the hotel premise. Very polluted outside, though, and alot of taxi guys waiting to hover around you. I would stay here again only because of the quiet and the isolated nature of the hotel. Other than that, not much to rave about. There is a massage place and some boutique shops. Super expensive as predicted.For a Nepali hotel, they keep their words. Great customer service and well trained waiters. Oh the breakfast was included but not great. I expected better for the price we were paying. Same breakfast buffet daily and it got boring. I would recommend it though if one can afford this hotel.

We stayed at this hotel at the beginning and end of a visit to Nepal and Bhutan. The Dwarika was amazing in all respects. The entire stunning courtyard with flowers a pool and great places to sit ina peaceful garden were a great respite from the busy dusty Kathmandu scene. We loved it!!

This is a very special hotel that was built over time with old window frames, doors, furniture.  The pool for swimming was wonderful.  The staff was very accommendating and the food delicious.  It is the one perfect place to stay in Kathmandu!

One of the most beautiful hotels in the world. Well run by the family of Dwarika, who spent his life restoring buildings in Kathmandu. Service was excellent, housekeeping was excellent, spa was excellent. I’m thinking about moving into the hotel! The owners were lovely! I will really miss this home away from home!10 stars!

This fine hotel was built about 40 years ago to reflect traditional Nepal. Our room was large and very nice. Only thing below 5 was mattress. All needed amenities are within the walls including a nice selection of dining. An incredible respite from the turmoil just outside.

The Dwarikas is the most beautiful hotel yet. Exquisite in every way. Rooms are huge and meticulously kept. Breakfast is sublime.Service is impeccable.Such a retreat from the busy, noisy Kathmandu. When tou are greeted on the driveway and are escorted into the courtyard, it’s line another world full of quiet music and tranquil seating areas to enjoy.Cannot say anymore except If you go to Kathmandu, you need to stay here.

The service is fa traffic no small thanks to the best staff I have experienced. I am a world traveller, having travelled the world it is a pleasure to be there. I have to say that Mr.Ruskin at the front office, Neeta at Krishna Arpan is amazing as is Prashant Bista at Fusion together these three people have made my stay memorable.May God Bless these three people who treat guests like God. thank you my friends. These three people are truly gifted human beings. They treated me as I were family.

What a beautiful property with amazing gardens and the abbience both in the restaurants and rooms are par excellence. The F/O and F&B staff came across as extremely polite and courteous and looked really passionate about their respective roles.Overall--9/10

Una serata al ristorante di questo tesoro durante il nostro viaggio tra India e Nepal ..Quello che stupisce è la presenza di questa struttura straordinaria dal punto di vista architettonico nel caos di Kathmandu ..Sembra un oasi ...Cena con piatti tipici nepalesi in un atmosfera straordinaria ..personale gentile , una serata da ricordare ..Prezzi ovviamente alla altezza del locale ..In definitiva se siete da queste parti non lasciatevelo  scappare

We stayed at Dwarika for 2 nights upon returning from Pokhara and Chitwan.  It was truly an oasis in a crazy but wonderful city.  The staff was most welcoming and the grounds of the hotel were relaxing and comforting.  Our twin room was spacious, clean and we loved overlooking the beautiful courtyard.We returned to the hotel after our overland trip from Chinese border which was long and on mostly unpaved and bumpy roads.  We left bags here upon leaving Kathmandu the first time and were grateful to be able to store them at Dwarika. Breakfast was quite ample and the other  restaurants were wonderful. We enjoyed laying in the "beds" by the pool reading and relaxing and especially enjoyed walking around the grounds appreciating all the beautiful architecture and Newari wood work.Visit the work shop if you get a chance.

We stayed at Dwarika’s for three nights. We were upgraded to the Jr. suite the last night. Both rooms were well appointed with a large bathroom, comfortable beds and a quiet environment. The Newari architecture is absolutely beautiful! The restaurant serves a variety of items from western, Indian, and Nepalese. A treatment at the spa is a must. Thank you to all the staff who are most gracious and hospitable.

This is now my second stay at Dwarika's and it is always a breath of fresh air in the midst of crazy travel plans. The service is world class, the food is delicious, and the staff goes the extra mile to make your stay as relaxing as possible. The property itself is gorgeous, head to toe Nepali artifice (the owner was a collector and found his hobby to be rather expensive so funneled it into the hotel.) And the rooms are plush, cookies, fruit, waterbottles and chocolates refreshed daily, and they have turn down service nightly. The pictures online simply do not do it justice. You have to see it for yourself.

Had dinner in this hotel and was simply stunned by it's beauty. This place is like a palace of the 1800's. The food we had was excellent and the portions we're great as well. Not many business travelers around as I feel this is more of an splurge hotel. If you have the money.. faunt it. Not able to share much info on the rooms. But I am sure .. it's worth it.The sounds of birds, flowing water etc are classy. You might have to reserve tables in advance to be able to have dinner in any of the 5 restaurants.

If you can afford the price, this is the one for you.  I am certain, given other destinations, you'd have to pay a lot more.  We originally booked for one night only at this hotel, but, upon arrival at the other hotel organised by the travel agent a day prior, we had to ring the Dwarika whether we could come in a day ahead - paying additional for the extra night, of course.  The staff returned call promptly and was offering A$200 for an additional night.  I believe they were doing this out of good will.Unfortunately, the travel agent begged and pleaded that we stayed with their choice of hotel....  The next day, we promptly showed up at the hotel.  The facade of it is nothing to write home about.  In fact, it was dilapidated.  It was on a very busy street, with all the dust and noise to go with it.  However, upon entering the hotel, we were greeted warmly and it was but an oasis... All the facilities were as good as shown in the pictures, and later I relished into reading the records of the hotel and how the owner, though for personal gain and profit purposes, was able to revive the interest in the traditional carving and housing style, while incorporating into the requirements of a first-class hotel facilities.We enquired whether we could extend our stay for half a day, since the flight would not depart till late in the evening.  Next day the young PR lady came back and said we could stay as long as we wished!!  We broached further and she explained that since it is the beginning of the monsoon season, their occupancy rate is very low.  'It's better to have people in the house than no one at all....' she said.

This hotel represents the true heritage of Nepal. The architecture, woodwork, furniture and ambiance is unique. They have some of the finest and traditional cuisines. The rooms are huge and comfortable. Its quite well placed and with in 10 to 15 mins drive from the airport.

Absolutely lovely accommodation - beautiful rooms, pleasant staff, good on-site restaurants, wonderful ambiance in courtyard.  We have traveled a lot and this is one of the most lovely places we have ever stayed.  The purpose of the hotel - to preserve woodwork and other crafts of local people - is evident everywhere in the hotel and makes it very special.  At the same time, the hotel is extraordinarily comfortable and up to date.  The exercise facilities on the roof are good; daily laundry is reliable, everything that you would want it to be. It has lots of comfortable spaces to lounge between activities in a well equipped and large courtyard.  It is obviously a splurge, but worthwhile.

口コミが良かったので初ネパールをこのホテルで５泊過ごしました。空港からホテルは１０分以内で着きました。ホテルに送迎を頼むと片道１１ドルと税金がかかります。明細を見たら１５００ルピーくらいでした。部屋は広く清潔でした。シャンプーもコンディショナーも良い香りでした。水圧の充分でした。歯ブラシが置いてなかったですが頼めば持ってきてくれます。この時歯磨き粉も一緒に持ってこないのがもう一歩のところですかね。スタッフの全体的に親切な方が多いかったです。食事はレストランやルームサービスを利用しましたが全体的に美味しかったですし価格も想像より安かったです。パスタが１２００ルピーから１５００ルピー、モモが６５０ルピーほどです。ここにプラス２３パーセント付きます。ランドリーはTシャツと短パンをだして５００ルピー弱（税込み）だったと思います。１日に数回停電がありましたが数秒で復旧するのでとくに不便は感じませんでした。ターンダウン時、チョコレートが置いてあります。タメルまでのタクシーは一律５００ルピーのようです。良い点スタッフが親切でした。部屋が清潔に保たれてました。食事が美味しかったです。ネパールに行った際、ルピーに両替すると思いますがこの時また日本円やドルに再両替する事を考えなくていけませんがこのホテルではチェックアウト時の支払いを余ったルピーと残りをクレジットカードで支払いできました。（他のホテルもそれが当たり前だったらすいません）水が黄色いとの口コミがありましたが私の時はそれがなかったです。部屋によるのかもしれません。WIFIの速度は問題ありませんでした。悪い点他の方も書いていましたがサービスのスピードが全体的に遅いです。ルームサービスを頼んでも、食べ終わった後のお皿を引き上げてもらうのも電話してから結構時間がかかります。ホテル内でイベントがあったのでたまたまだったのかもしれません。プールの水が冷たすぎて入れませんでした。これは人によると思いますが毎朝８時頃、儀式的なものだと思いますがラッパのような音が鳴ります。これで起きる人は多いかもしれません。テレビのリモコンが分かりにくいし、チャンネル変えるたびに爆音になったりするのが鬱陶しかったです。埃だらけのカトマンズの街から帰ってくると安心できるホテルです。スタッフも最初は冷たい印象の人もいますが慣れると結構話しかけてきたり笑顔を見せてくれます。国民性でしょうか。ホテルで飼ってるゴールデンレトリバーにも癒されました。

This is an astonishingly beautiful hotel, with grandeur in an old colonial style. It is build around a central courtyard with a beautiful refreshing pool, wonderful outdoor four poster beds to laze in (As well as the usual pool chairs), and excellent and attentive service. We were upgraded to a junior suite - a large airy room with a sunken bath, high ceilings, and grand bed scattered with rose petals. The food was the best we ate in Nepal, the atmosphere is easy charm with touches of real luxury, and the on-site massages were wonderful. There are of course many (far) cheaper options in Katmandhu but this was worth every penny.

We had an excellent 3-night stay at Dwarika’s. The hotel is located close to the airport - the drive is only about 10 minutes. The entire staff is friendly and welcoming.The room was beautifully appointed, and we slept well in the comfortable bed. Amenities were perfectly fine, but if you don’t like the smell of lemongrass, be sure to bring your own. Several water bottles were provided each day, so this wasn’t an issue. Cookies, fruit, and chocolate were also in the room.There are several restaurants. The main Fusion restaurant was quite good, but expensive. We found the food at Mako’s even better, and it was cheaper! The shower was excellent - good pressure and always hot. My only complaint with the bathroom area would be that the sink area is fairly dark, even with the lights on. This is  where luggage is stored as well, so we ended up bringing our suitcases into the main part of the room when packing. Also, the daybed had a very strong smell of baby powder.The power kicked off a few times each day and night during our stay, but this very common in Nepal, even if no one will tell you so. It only lasts a few seconds (or at most a few minutes), so just be patient and it will return.

spent few days in this hotel that has been build with old wooden work. You really have the feeling to be in a Nepalese palace. Everything is beautiful and you can't expect such a luxury place from the outside. Have the Yoga lesson in the morning. probably the most beautiful hotel I have visited in my life.

Dwarika's is a paradise in a congested and sadly quite polluted city.  Once entering Dwarika's, you're in a lovely oasis of calm clean beauty.  The rooms are quite spacious and well appointed.  All of the services you could need are available at the hotel.I am disabled and the hotel has quite a lot of stairs, so that was a challenge.  The hotel loaned me a wheelchair and the staff carried me up and down the stairs in the wheelchair with a smile.  Once we got to the level where the elevator was, my husband could push me the rest of the way to our room.I had a massage at the hotel by a wonderful healer.  It was the best massage I have ever had and I have had hundreds of massages.Dwarika's is excellent and highly recommended.

The Dwarika‘s is the perfect spot to relax after a day of sightseeing in Kathmandu. The bedrooms are spacious, perfectly clean and traditionally decorated, the food in the restaurants is of high quality (most of it from the hotel‘s own organic farms), service is polite and helpful and the calm atmosphere is amazing! The place is both: luxury hotel plus museum - the collection of Newa woodwork is impressive!I recommend guided tours organized by the hotel team and dinner at the traditional Nepali restaurant.

The place is bang in the middle of a very busy & noisy intersection. Located at about 10 mins ride from the airport (which is a plus if you’re traveling), the place is an oasis once you enter the doors. Artifacts & art, pillars with embroidery make up the restaurants and the courtyard. Apparently, the owner is renowned for her taste of restoring Nepalese handicrafts & placing them in her Hotel. Food is decent, and they have a good collection in the bar. However, at times - prices make you feel like you’re paying for the ambience & history, and less for the taste, quality of the whiskey being served. I would recommend the Newari restaurant at the place - for the experience. Bring along your (fat) wallet, though.

It's a splurge compared to a few other hotels in Kathmandu but, if you can swing it or have a special occasion, I thought it was worth the price.  The rooms are the most exquisite and authentic of any hotel I've ever stayed in.

As someone who tends to stay in luxurious hotels (Four Seasons, One and Only, Como, Oberoi) I wanted my family and I to stay somewhere beautiful in Kathmandu. There couldn't have been a better place to stay for 5 nights! This property is absolutely stunning. From the moment you walk in, you realize you are in an oasis in what is a very dusty, chaotic city. Rooms - We stayed in Executive Suites and not only are they extremely spacious, but beautifully designed and furnished. The beds were extremely comfortable and the shower pressure was AWESOME (two things that I notice tend to get left out when putting together luxurious hotels). Service - The people who work here treat you like family. The Nepalese (at least in my experience) are a little shy at first, but the minute you warm up to them and flash them a genuine smile, they would do anything to help you be more comfortable. Food - I do NOT like any spicy food (yes I realize I came to the wrong part of the world for that kind of preference) and Dwarika's accommodated me perfectly. My husband is a bodybuilder and was very happy with the food here. No complaints from anyone in the family. I do not think anyone will be disappointed in the choices or preparation of any food here.Gym - Well it is like a "toy box" gym, meaning that it looks like it COULD be a gym, but hasn't yet made it that far. There is very little weight to speak of and only a couple machines. So hopefully you aren't going to Dwarika's to get prepped to summit Everest. Pool - It isn't heated so VERY cold in the winter!Laundry - Yes I know this is a weird thing to comment on, but out of all the places in Nepal that we stayed, this is the ONLY place where our laundry came back to us smelling clean and fresh. It's the little things right?Overall - I would highly recommend this to the viewer that wants a plush place to stay while touring Kathmandu. Everything from the service to the rooms were way above my expectations and the staff made it feel like home. Thank you Dwarika's!

This hotel is a hidden gem amongst the madness that is Kathmandu. The crazy traffic, horrible roads and dust that lingers everywhere in the city is all forgotten once you step through the door into this fabulous hotel. It's clear that the owners of this hotel care about the comfort of their guests. The rooms are all spacious and well-appointed. The interior courtyard and pool area are beautiful. The restaurants and bar are terrific, with great food and service. WiFi is weak in some places around the property, and I was frequently disconnected and had to revert to 4G for communications. There were at least a dozen power outages every day, but that's not the hotel's fault, as it happens everywhere in Kathmandu. I found it odd that the hotel hasn't updated to a modern security system for door locks. It's not difficult to install a cardkey system, even on old doors. Having padlocks on room doors just seemed curious and outdated. Even the key fob was like a large stick that was too big to fit into a pocket. Perhaps this system is used to evoke some historical charm, but in reality it's just annoying.Still, it's definitely worth staying here, if you're in Kathmandu.

Within the chaos of Kathmandu this is a great place to hide and relax.  The rooms are wonderful and the service is excellent.  We enjoyed the food and the atmosphere is very serene compared to what is going on just outside.  I would not go back to Kathmandu unless it was a stop-over because it is so difficult to get around but The hotel make it as easy and pleasurable as possible.  However, there was a lot of renovation work and expansion going on at the hotel when we were there which was fairly noisy during the day.

Well I have to say Kathmandu was not what I expected.  Sleepy mountain villagey sort of place...not a bit of it.Big Asian city with all the crazy carnage that goes with it...and some.The Dwarika’s hotel is an oasis in this turbulence.It’s a lovely interesting hotel with great and helpful staff.  This is 5 stars in local currency....it’s not what you would get for 5 stars in western hotel - but in Nepal it’s fantastic.And actually makes me bring up a point I have wanted to raise for a while - the star rating doesn’t work on Trip Advisor - you are not comparing like with like.  There needs to be some local territory adjustment.  Stay at the Dwarika’s!

Absolutely stunning hotel, like a palace within Kathmandu city. You get wrapped into it's cosy and serene atmosphere and can getaway from the noise and dust of the town. Evereything here is just perfect - antique furniture, great breakfasts, the rooms, the service and a very good SPA. If you look for the best place to stay - it's here. Pricey, too, but worth it for sure. Situated a bit away from the main attaractions, about 15 minutes by car to Tamel.

We stayed at Dwarika’s at the beginning and end of our journey in Kathmandu and found it a haven of peace and comfort.It was an amazing heritage hotel with original architecture. We stayed in both a standard room and a suite, both of which were well appointed and met all our needs.The staff were exceptional and very attentive. The food in the Bhutanese restaurant was lovely and it was a great experience, we only managed the 6 course menu, the 22 course menu is not for the faint hearted! The main restaurant was also very good indeed and served a variety of western and eastern food. We particularly loved the chicken thali. The hotel can certainly cook lovely Indian food.A great breakfast is available and we particularly enjoyed the Nepali food. The hotel is only a short distance from the airport which is very convenient - we would definitely stay here again.

My family of five spent nearly a week at this wonderful hotel.  The artwork alone makes it worth a visit.  In fact, I fell in love with the old yogurt-making vats that are dotted around the public rooms, and charming Shiva at reception went out of his way to help me find one (well, three ultimately!) that I could purchase.  He was so kind and helpful--not just with regards to my antique obsession!--and always had a smile on his face.  A real pleasure to get to know, with a great can-do attitude.  Shriva is tops in my book, but so many people there went out of their way to make our stay memorable--Somina, and another lovely young woman, and two male trainees (sorry I didn't catch the names!) in guest services made all our excursions run seamlessly.  The restaurant staff in all the restaurants were always friendly and thoughtful (the tandoori chicken in the main restaurant is delicious, btw, as are the Nepalese special breakfast items they can make to order).   Mako's Japanese was a real surprise.  It was fun to talk with Mako, and the food there was delicious (I used to live in Tokyo, so I know my Japanese cuisine!)--again, the staff was lovely.  There was also a charming older man with a ponytail who apparently works in PR and he suggested we spend the day at the countryside property--and we really enjoyed it!  The views of the Himalayas are stunning, and we had an absolutely delicious lunch there.  Definitely worth a trip if you have time.The bartender also went out of his way to help us make a reservation at a cool jazz bar in town called Jazz Upstairs.  If you are interested in that kind of music, this is a funky little place to check out Kathmandu's jazz scene. I'm so glad I found Dwarika's.  It really is the best place to return home to after exploring exciting Kathmandu.

What a wonderful place! Visited dusty, dusty Kathmandu for two nights with my family and my jaw dropped as soon as I entered this gorgeous hotel. The entire property is clearly a labour of great love - every corner, rafter, wall is painstakingly designed to showcase the fantastic wooden carvings that are part of Newari heritage. But it isn't just a beautiful museum, the service is really great too. We got upgraded to a suite, staff was always friendly, happy to chat and help. The 6-course meal at the Newari restaurant is excellent (though there was so much food that how people manage to eat the 9-course and 22-course versions is entirely beyond me). The bar is really cool, and the bartenders never bother you with orders, you can just sit and relax. Nice shop as well. Car transfers were easily booked through their travel desk as well.Minor quibble that the wifi could have been better.If you're up for the splurge, you will enjoy every bit of this.

Great hotel for it's ambiance, room, bar, restaurants and staff.  BUT; after checking out of hotel we realized the wife left behind a pair of pants.  Contacted the hotel and asked to forward pants to our final hotel in Mumbai but only if they could guarantee that pants would arrive before our departure for home 2 1/2 weeks later.  Very long story short, Dwarkia filled out the bill of lading incorrectly and it took almost a month for pants to clear customs in Mumbai and another couple of weeks for Dwarkia to finally have pants delivered to my home in California.  What irks me the most, is not only did Dwarkia ask our hotel in Mumbai (The Four Seasons) to help in clearing customs but when the FS asked Dwarkia to reimburse them for a payment that they made to DHL on behalf of the Dwarkia, the Dwarkia did not make the concerted effort to make requested reimbursement.  We checked out of Dwarkia on December 8 and as of today, January 27, payment still has not been made (after to many requests from FS).

Believe all the reviews - Dwarika’s is the most incredible place to stay in Kathmandu. It sits on a dusty, bustling street with an unassuming facade, but once you step through the door, it is the definition of an urban oasis. The grounds and architecture are stunning, with all sorts of hidden corners seemingly overflowing with beautiful wood carvings, sculptures, art works and flowers. Wow. It took an hour just to wander around taking photos. And beyond that, the room itself was also a stunner with traditional art and furniture, plus all the modern conveniences you'd want. The traditional, multi-course dinner at Krishnarpan was absolutely delicious and the service from every single member of the staff - from beginning to end - was over-the-top awesome. If you're willing to pay the price, this is without question THE place to stay in Kathmandu.

A most beautiful hotel built in the traditional style with beautiful carved windows by a man whose passion was preserving Nepali culture but also incorporating all the comforts of our modern world. The best beds in Nepal in my opinion!It is like a haven from the dust of Kathmandu, built round a large courtyard filled with birds and flowers, truly beautiful. The food is great (3 restaurants to choose from)and the staff delightful, nothing is too difficult.Early morning Yoga was a must if you have time, the man who ran the class made it such fun, a perfect way to start the day.

The decoration is hard to explain because everywhere you see there is a picture moment. The carvings and decorations are well organized into ambiance that makes you want to stay. Why go and explore the city when you have so much beauty around you!!! The bar, the restaurants, the store... they are all great. This place is a must. I came here years ago and couldn't wait to come back. And I am leaving thinking the same thing, when am I coming back here again, and again.

Wir haben hier zum Abschluss unserer Nepalreise einem Tag verbracht.Es ist wahrscheinlich der sauberste Ort in Kathmandu. ... eine wahre Oase. Nachdem man eine Zeit im Land war ist dieses Hotel genau das was man braucht. Der Service war zuvorkommend und freundlich.Die Preise sind für Nepal überdurchschnittlich hoch und wir hatten bei den Zimmerpreisen etwas mehr erwartet. Es ist ein Luxushotel jedoch mit kleinen Abstrichen. Störend sind auch die vielen Tauben, die im Innenhof auf den Bäumen leben und dort auch ihr Geschäft verrichten.

An hotel full of character with excellent, attentive staff in a central location We had large heritage bedrooms which were well equipped The Japanese restaurant within the hotel is vey good but our party had mixed views on the Krishnarpan restaurant from enjoyed everything to liked nothing!You sit at low tables and one can get very stiff Excellent breakfast selection for all tastes. Omelettes particularly good and served with a smile

Friendly staff, beautiful sanctuary hotel in our room and the courtyard from the chaos of Kathmandu, would be 5 star (it’s really really close but 5 star to us has to be perfection), if it wasn’t for the breakfast (very limited options) which wasn’t what you’d expect in a top hotel. Club sandwich average but  the super food salad was the best I’ve ever had.

Dwarika's Hotel is an intimate luxury boutique hotel that embraces Nepal's artistic heritage. Every corner seems like a painting. The staff are well-trained to go above and beyond; they anticipate what you need and deliver before you even ask for it. That for me is the true definition of 5 stars This is a place that values service and rapport, above all. Everything is personal, from the moment you check in, to the dining experience. I absolutely love the breakfast spread! What an exquisite selection of organic juices, honey and bread. The omelette and pancake station will fix your craving for comfort. Spend time at the spa, you can thank me later. In a nutshell, Dwarika's has the essence of home, heart of a temple and design of an art museum. Certified as one of Nepal's best kept secrets. Hands down, the most beautiful hotel in Kathmandu.Only the best,Mr. Raven

Stare al Dwarika di Kathmandu è come soggiornare in un museo. Non è comune stare in un albergo che oltre ai comfort ti offre una vera esperienza culturale. Ottima l’attenzione al dettaglio e buono il servizio. Bravi! Consigliatissimo. Ah, il ristorante nepalese è veramente eccellente e merita senza dubbio una visita.

Ambiance, service, food...everything is an oasis to the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu.....architecture is tenderly created and restored making the hotel a perfect place  To stay.Service is impeccable, and the appreciation from the staff is repaid by us in gratitude for such a hotel to be here.There are three restaurants and if time allows try them all, each has it’s ken atmosphere and the food is delicious.

I stayed for 3 nights. Fantastic hotel and so many historic restored pieces that require intricate work. Read the history of the hotel, it’s really amazing that someone has spent their lives putting this hotel together. The restaurant food is average, if you compare to global cities, BUT it’s #1 in Kathmandu for sure. I only went outside one for 1 hour to get a SIM card, but that was a mistake. I should have just stayed at the hotel the entire time. It’s an oasis in a bustling city. Staff was quite helpful even though their level of service isn’t quite up to par of true international 5 star service, but their genuine efforts really make up for the lack of experience. Great stay. Highly recommend it!

A beautiful and immaculately run hotel. Without exception the staff were charming, friendly and efficient. Our Deluxe Heritage room was extremely comfortable with extra touches of complimentary fruit, water and home-made biscuits. The breakfast buffet was superb. Food in the other restaurants was of an equally high standard. I cannot fault Dwarika's.

What a beautiful place and the staff who is always attentive with a big smile!  The spa with INCREDIBLE massages. The heritage of the Dwarikas can be seen everywhere, the room with its antique chests, tapestries, Nepal's history can be felt everywhere. Although the main restaurant menu does not vary the kitchen is always willing to serve you that extra dish. Kathmandu is an incredible city, yes it's noisy and dirty but there is so much to see and it's tons of fun. Need peace and quiet, you just head back.

I cannot say enough good things about this property. I visited for two nights on a quick side trip to Nepal from New Delhi, and stayed in a room with a king-sized bed on the second floor of this property. What to say about this place? It's different from anywhere I've ever been, and every aspect was incredible. The hotel is clad in heritage woodwork, hundreds of years old, recovered from the local area. The décor is local in flavour and beautifully done. The washrooms are lovely, the bed was comfortable, and there was ample seating and workspace. The crowning jewel of the property, in my opinion, is the variety of beautiful outdoor spaces and seating to enjoy what was decent weather when I was there. There are several drinking/dining options; I had sushi and the buffet breakfast, and both were excellent. The pool is lovely to swim in and just as good to lounge beside and look at. Attention to detail was everywhere I looked at this hotel -- flowers throughout, attentive staff, and nice little boutiques. Best of all, the price was extraordinary reasonable. Great value, and I can't wait to stay again someday.

For a hotel, it might be easy to be "luxury" but it will never be easy to be a real heritage.  Dwarika's Hotel is really a "heritage" where you can find "Nepal in dream".  Outside the hotel gate, it might be the "real Nepal" with dirts, terrible traffic and all kinds of noises.  But when you entered the hotel, everything is so different.  That's the most amazing part here.We stayed in the Lumbini building where you can find old bricks and nice wooden windows.  The room is fantastic and we're so relaxed in the room after a long journey from Lumbini to Kathmandu.  The room is decent and clean with all kinds of facilities.  Coffee and tea is complimentary together with some snacks and fruits.  Never miss the traditional Nepal restaurant in the hotel.  We've tried the 6 courses menu which is a great experience.  The dinner might be expensive if compared with the average restaurant price in Kathmandu, but it worth every penny you spent.Love this hotel and it's a pity that we only stayed here for one night.  Will definitely go back if we come back to Nepal again.

L'Hôtel, construit à base de matériaux et ouvrages traditionnels savamment recyclés représente dignement le riche patrimoine culturel de la vallée de Katmandou.Une chambre, une salle de bain spacieuse et décoré avec gout, dépaysement total !Sans conteste le meilleur restaurant du Népal qui sert un menu dégustation en une farandole de plats délicieux qui rendent hommage aux cuisines népalaises, tibétaines et indiennes.Le personnel très chaleureux à l'image des népalais offre un service exceptionnel de qualité irréprochable.

Lovely hotel with a small town-like feel. We felt like we were far away from the traffic and noise/air pollution that was right outside the walls of the Dwarika's.  We were greeted by our very kind driver who picked us up from the airport.  It is a 10 minute drive from the airport and once we reached we were saluted by the uniformed guard at the door.  That was really nice.  It seems we walked through the door and into a different town.  A few hours later we were given a tour by Neha who was very kind and explained the history of the hotel.  Our room was lovely but the white sofa by the window wasn't cleaned as I saw some crumbs on the cushion.  Also immediately there was a lot of noise coming from the roof, as if someone was rolling a bowling ball.  We could hear several voice including a child's coming from the bathroom skylight.  It happened throughout the day every once in a while.  The food was amazing.  I ordered the seasonal barbecue chicken.  The service staff was genuinely helpful and courteous.  I ordered fresh pomegranate juice which was not on the menu but they got it to me anyway.  Since FlyDubai (I will never use this airline again) postponed our flight from 8am to 7pm, I asked one of the gentlemen at the front desk to find out how much the airport business lounge was since the hotel check-out time is 11am.  He never got back to me.  Next day I asked the same from a young lady at the desk (I wish I caught her name) and she was so, so helpful.  Not only did she get me the answer but she managed to get us a "refresher" room so we didn't have to be stuck in the airport between 11am and 7pm.  And it was free.  I will always thank Dwarika's for their understanding about our situation by that silly airline.  Thank you!  I gave it 4 stars because of the roof noise and cleanliness.

This hotel exceed all my expectations. The staff are a delightfully attentive catering to our every need. When you enter you are greeted with smiles. The space it self is a wonder. There are so many area to explore and hang out each having its own purpose.  The pool, pub, four restaurants, spa, out door area and rooms are all just breathe taken spaces.  The artistry/craftsmanship that has been put into every detail of this place is an absolute wonder.  Not to mention a very quick cab ride to the airport.  This place is a must stay for anyone wanting an experince in Nepal.

Dwarika's Hotel is in kathmandu valley, inside the bagmati region. It have nice rooms, 24/7 excellent service. Clean and nice view of kathmandu valley of nepal. I love to visit Dwarika's Hotel in very near future.

Frühstück : unbegreiflich gut und viel uns speziell ( beste Schokocroissants und ein Mega crepe mit Mango ) --- Die Betten war superbequem und das Personal mehr als freundlich .. man fühlt sich wirklich wie zuhause in diesem tollen Hotel ... selten etwas besseres gehabt und ich reise sehr viel !!! Verschieden tolle Restaurants im Hotel ...

I stayed at Dwarika's in June, which is apparently off-season and beginning of the rainy season. The hotel is always clean and the staff polite and always welcoming. The rooms are well kept and the onsite restaurants are tasty. After housekeeping came by, I noticed a couple flys and bugs in the room, but nothing that would change my overall perception the hotel.

This hotel is absolutely beautiful. The service was excellent. We had an issue with the room and immediately they fixed it. The next night there was still a problem and they switched our room no problem. I would highly recommend this hotel

Ayant pas mal voyagé à travers le monde cet hotel est tout simplement un des plus beaux que j ai eu l occasion de visiter.tout y est parfait , le personnel est trés agreable .L'architecture de l 'hotel est magnifique , un havre de paix ds le centre de Katmandou et proche de l'aeroport.

My wife and I stayed for four nights in this sanctuary away from the frantic city outside. We loved all of the restaurants including both the 16 or more course meals at the Nepalese dining room and the very personable Japanese restaurant. The setting is serene and the buildings look to be 400 years old as the attention to detail and the use of old materials make for a beautiful property.We enjoyed the bar and the library as well. The staff took extremely good care of 2 people celebrating their 45th wedding anniversary..having their notable chocolate cake in our room upon our arrival

Another amazing stay at the Oasis in Kathmandu; seriously a sanctuary from the busy streets outside. My only constructive feedback would be that the morning waiters serving breakfast could certainly improve the feeling of being welcome.

Stunning hotel in the middle of Kathmandu. The architecture makes the hotel a destination in itself, as do the multiple world class restaurants and the great bar on premises. Loved it and wouldn't stay anywhere else in Kathmandu.

I could spend hours and hours in the courtyard of Dwarika's Hotel in Kathmandu. What a beautiful setting! My room was enormous and beautifully decorated. The bathroom was as large as a typical hotel room. I loved the unique way of locking the door. Also, I must add that the staff were friendly and helpful. I would definitely choose Dwarika's Hotel if I were ever in Kathmandu again.

We've stayed here before and love the history, design, rooms, and public areas. The buildings, workmanship, and outdoor areas are magnificent.   This time there was a noticeable improvement in the service levels and staff training which made for a perfect experience.  The beds are very comfortable and the AC worked ok but did not have the cooling power needed for the room size.  The bathroom in our suite was magnificent and the shower was great.  Amenities in the bathroom were the best I've seen.  Wifi was little slow and there are too many light switches.  Breakfast is not extravagant but provided everything we wanted.  The Krishnarpan multi course dinner is not to be missed.  While expensive it is a one of a kind event.  Other restaurants by the pool offer a beautiful setting and great food and drinks.  The spa was very good but the massage therapist I had last year who was incredible had left and I received a very good but not great massage.

Este hermoso hotel tiene todo echo al detalle con materiales de la zona, la arquitectura de Nepal y la decoración de ahí , una belleza en detalles y cuidado del hotel que recibe a muchos turistas de occidente , las habitaciones muy cómodas, sensación de estar en una casa típica de Katmandú. limpio, excelente  comida , servicio , detalles como las zapatillas de levantar tejidas a ganchillo, el concierne excelente nos encontró cupo en helicóptero privado para subir al Everest. Han ido ampliando en habitaciones conservando el aspecto, una belleza de patios interiores una gran historia en el restaurant de comida nepalesa que no deben dejar de ir

We stayed here for 7 nights in total, 3 nights at the beginning of our trip and 4 nights at the end. And we stayed here 4 years ago. That experience made us choose again for this hotel. First of all, the hotel looks like a museum filled with Newari heritage stuff like handcarved wooden windows and doors, pottery, stautues, furniture. A real treat to your eyes. Beautiful! And staff is the best and most friendliest in the world (like all Nepali). And you'll wonder how they managed to bring the silence inside the hotel, once you enter through the low front door. And you'll find no dust! Unbelievable in the one of the most dustiest and noisiest cities in the world. I can go on and on about all the positive things, but you better book a room  yourself (the standard ones are already huge, 4 years ago we had a suite and we got lost ;-))

Meant to write this a while ago, but stayed a night in Dwarikas whilst living in Kathmandu. Wonderfully peaceful place with excellent service and large comfortable, traditional, rooms make this an absolute must for anyone wanting to experience Nepali luxury! One night was not enough, and will happily return when i finally get to venture back to beautiful Nepal. Gorgeous hotel and grounds, showing off the true Nepali culture

Sicherlich ist das Hotel in der schmutzigen Stadt eine Oase, wenngleich auch dezentral gelegen. Außen auf traditionell gemacht, innen high tech und die Zimmer durchaus ansprechend. Das ist aber auch schon alles an positivem. Das Essen am Pool dauert lang, schmeckt einfallslos und ist fürchterlich teuer.In der Bar werden deutlich teurere Preise verrechnet als auf der Getränkekarte ausgewiesen("sorry we changed the prices" erfährt man dann beim bezahlen), bei einer Reklamation konnte dann kaum wer mehr englisch... will man spät am Abend dann die Polizei holen? Natürlich nicht denn wer weiß wie lange das dauert. Das Frühstück geschmacklich sicher nicht einem 5 Sterne Hotel entsprechend. Late check out um 2 p.m. nur gegen eine Gebühr von EUR171,50!!!Alles in allem nicht empfehlenswert.

Wewent there to have some quite time and not to have to be inside.Lovely garden, nice sitting areas, the buildings are beautiful.Good place to escape all the noise 😊Actually a better retreat than then Garden of Dreams.And no tourists taking pictures.

This is a beautiful hotel contained within its own compound.  Staff were all friendly and efficient.  Rooms very clean and well appointed.  My room was very spacious.  Outstanding pool area with crystal clear pool.Very comfortable bar area with all manor of drinks available.  Bar staff slightly non-attentive after first encounter.This hotel has three restaurants:  Nepalese, Japanese and coffee shop.  The Japanese restaurant is a sweet surprise!  We had very good Sauvignon Blanc (New Zealand) and Chardonnay (Australia), California Maki (Roll), Praws Tempura and vegetable noodle soup.  All were served promptly, very hot and delicious.  This is a small restaurant and we were accommodated without a reservation but probably best to make reservation if possible.Breakfast buffet is very good if you get there early but empty platters are not promptly refilled.  Come late and you might find only 30%.Note on taxis:  They are not all honest.  Hotel arranged taxi for tour of Patan and Bhaktapur and said taxi would charge 4500 Rupees.  While we did make extra stops this taxi ultimately charged 8500 Rupees.  Another taxi ride to and from the airport for the Mountain Flight (Everest viewing) was supposed to cost 500 Rupees but 1000 was demanded at conclusion.The Mountain Flight on Buddha Air is a "must do" as long as weather is good.  They will refund your ticket if weather is not good so there is no risk of booking.  We were lucky it was clear and had great views of Mount Everest from comfortable large aircraft.Dwarika's is an oasis in busy dusty Kathmandu and a wonderful place to spend a little time.  I actually wished I had booked an extra day.

What a wonderful place.  The history and the feeling of this wonderful hotel takes you totally away from the mayhem of Kathmandu City.  How to feel cocooned in warmth of lovely staff and you just want to drink in the atmosphere of the hotel.

El hotel es muy lindo , tanto  las  areas comunes como las habitacion. Es delicioso el patio con sus mesitas y la tranquilidad y ambiente que se vive.El personal es sumamente amable, profesional y atento.Lamentablemente, descuidan algunas zonas como el business center, que estaba sucio, con maquinas que no funcionaban y cubiertas de polvo.El spa no mantiene el ambiente bello del resto del hotel, son cuartos sencillos, sin mas. Aunque los masajes son muy recomendables.Tiene diferentes opciones de restaurantes muy buenos.A pesar de los pequeños problemas nombrados queda lindísima sensacion por el tan agradable ambiente.

Terrific experience!! We spent 3 wonderfull nights. Excellent service and accommodations. Nepal suffered an strong hit in 2015 but this place was totally recovered. The hotel has godd restaurants. I highly recomend try to enjoy the nepali food in one of them.

I stayed at Dwarika’s for 6 weeks, from early December 2016 to mid January 2017, while on a business trip.  Dwarika’s is by far one of the best hotels I’ve ever experienced, because of the unparalleled quality of service, comfort and attention to detail, and stunning, unique architecture and design.  Whether you’re on vacation or you’re traveling for business, and you need an efficient, quiet, comfortable place to work - in your room or in common areas - or a stylish, well-serviced place to meet colleagues over a drink, it’s impossible to imagine a better place to stay.Rooms: I stayed in a Heritage Deluxe room, and it was spacious and just as pictured on the Dwarika’s website.  The bed, pillows, and sheets were all very comfortable, and there were enough layers on the bed to make it easy to adjust for more or less warmth and weight.  I also appreciated the view of the courtyard and the natural light streaming in during the day.  The bathroom had a huge, deep tub, as well as a separate shower stall and toilet room, two sinks, and a skylight, again bringing natural light during the day.  I appreciated that my room was stocked with enough water and tea at all times, as well as fruit and evening biscuits and chocolates.Service:Staff at Dwarika’s seem to enjoy their work and work well together, which spills over into the friendly way that they interact with guests.  It’s evident that Dwarika’s is a non-chain, family-owned and run establishment, and the owners live on the premises and are frequently in the dining room and courtyard.  During my long stay, the staff assisted me in myriad ways, sometimes offering help even before I could think to ask for something.  For example, after a particularly crappy day, when I wasn’t feeling well, as I mounted the steps to my room, one of the heads of housekeeping saw me, asked if I was doing ok, and immediately offered to bring hot water bottles to my room.  The same staff person was extremely kind and helpful after I spent a weekend being quite ill, even having one of her colleagues call me to remind me to eat!  Service in the courtyard and dining room is equally attentive.  Within the first 2 days of my stay, the breakfast shift staff remembered what kind of tea I like and had worked it out with the omelet chef to make me scrambled tofu and tomatoes instead of eggs.  Within 4 days, they’d remembered my juice preferences and were happy to make me a special order detox juice, if the juice of the day had celery or beets in it (yuk!).  Simply coming into the dining room and having everyone wish me a good morning by name was a very pleasant way to start my long day.  Small touches, like having a side table for my laptop at breakfast or dinner, made it easy to eat, no matter how much work I had to do.  Several times, I was able to order what I wanted in the dining room and then have it delivered to my room, although the item was not on the room service menu.The staff also helped with small errands.  They were willing to make brief phone calls to businesses where staff only speaks Nepali (which I don’t speak), get me batteries one night, recharge my mobile phone credit, and procure medication I needed.  Over time, all of this smoothed my stay considerably.Finally, one of the managers went out of his way to facilitate my spending two nights at the Dwarika’s Resort in Dhulikhel over Christmas weekend.  My schedule was difficult and my budget was tight, but in the end, it all worked out, because the staff wanted to help out a long-term guest and are just plain kind.Food:I found it easy enough to grab a taxi and head out to eat in Thamel or elsewhere.  However, the food at the bar and in the main dining room is quite good and, obviously, convenient.  The breakfast includes omelets made to order (or scrambled tofu), fresh made crepes and juices, as well as a buffet with hot dishes that change every day, multiple kinds of bread and pastries, yogurt, granola, fruit, cheese, and veggies.  If you don’t have time to eat in the dining room, the staff will make you a to-go box with whatever you like, including juice and tea/coffee.  During the day or early evening, the main dining room serves the tables in the courtyard, and the bar serves the daybeds and library, so it’s lovely to sit outside and work or relax and have food.  As a vegetarian who basically sticks to locally grown, organic vegetables and limited dairy in the US, I appreciated the variety on the menu and that the veggies come from Dwarika’s organic farm, which I visited during a weekend at the Dwarika’s Resort in Dhulikhel.  Menu items I really enjoyed were the crepes at breakfast, various whole grain breads, mushroom soup, veggie burgers and momos (from the bar), mixed greens with roasted vegetables and fried goat cheese, the haloumi salad, homemade buckwheat pasta, and the channa (chickpea) curry.  I also ate at the Nepali specialty restaurant one night and enjoyed it, though I found even the small portions in the basic 6 course menu way more food than I could eat, and the Friday night barbecue one night, which is a delicious buffet with a huge variety, but similarly too much food for me.Ambience: 	The photos don’t do justice to how unique and wonderful Dwarika’s.  It rivals the best boutique hotels anywhere in the world.  As other reviews note, every detail has been considered and is beautiful.  Dwarika’s is an oasis of calm in Kathmandu.

We just spent three amazing days in this wonderful hideaway - definitely, one of the best luxury city hotels we've been to. We are traveling a lot - usually in design boutique hotels in Europe - but this hotel is at the top of our list. Wonderful large rooms, beautiful interior, a wide choice at the breakfast menu...this list could be endless. We tried the Japanese and the Nepali restaurant, the food was extremely good. When planning a trip to Nepal, start your journey here - it's the perfect opportunity to dive into the Nepali culture. We will definitely come back.
