The hotel building is so good that it is hard to remember that it was only built recently.The rooms are large but there are few cupboards and those that there are can be found five feet up.The doors are poorly made and and don't shut properly or fit - not the quality of the building itself! Whilst the building provides an oasis from the dirt and filth outside it is miles from the main sights and shopping so a taxi is needed to go anywhere.The staff are a strange mixture of the really welcoming Nepalise people to others who,to be honest,seem to have an attitude problem.Breakfast was disappointing and resturants had a problem when they were busy with groups.However evening meals were good with a choice of western food and local meals.The promised newspaper never arrived,the bins in the room were not always emptied,dust remained around the room over the four days we stayed,EtcSuper building but must do better!

Aún que no queda cerca del centro de Katmandú el hotel es fantástico tiene un restaurante nepalés realmente bueno . Todo en el hotel es cuidado y bonito lleno de detalles que hace de la estadía una experiencia inolvidable!

8 years ago when we were last in Kathmandu we had promised that next time we would treat ourselves to a stay at Dwarika's. This time we did just that and it did not disappoint!Architecturally unique, close to the airport, Dwarika's is a beautiful hotel in every way.It manages to be sophisticated, welcoming and still pay homage to Nepal in so many ways. The central courtyard is an oasis from the city. In the courtyard are pavilions which house the cosy bar (which has a roaring fire in the fireplace every night - magnificent on a cool January evening), the very pretty pool area and the Japanese and Nepali restaurants. The multi-cuisine restaurant is housed adjacent to the main lobby area. The carved wood window frames, brick walls, tiled floors and local woven textiles create restful and comfortable yet interesting surroundings.  We stayed for 5 days and really could have stayed longer. Staff are very friendly and incredibly helpful. Food is delicious too.  We were lucky enough to meet the owner and her daughter who are very gracious and welcoming. I couldn't imagine staying anywhere else in Kathmandu.

We enjoyed our 3 night stay at Dwarika's but I wasn't blown away. Everything I had read had probably meant that I had built up unrealistic expectations but I didn't think it quite matched up to many of the other similar hotels we have stayed at.Rooms are huge and are beautifully furnished. The wifi is excellent and there is a good selection of TV channels. Fruit is provided along with hot drinks.Service is very good, though it seemed to depend upon who you were dealing with. The person who checked us in was exceptional but the attitude of one of the others at the front desk left a little to be desired. The day before we left, I asked for the car to take us to the airport at 4pm the following day. I was immediately told that we would be charged 50% supplement to keep the room beyond 11am. I informed them that we would't require the room but it seemed a strange first reaction. Upon checking out I asked them to collect our luggage from our room. When we came to leave, we were asked where our bags were. It turned out they had not been collected so the bell boy went for them. If the room hadn't been cleaned and so the bags hadn't been collected, I struggle to see why we couldn't have kept the room if we had wanted. A silly little thing, but annoying.Whilst breakfast was quite average, all other food was excellent. The Nepalese, in particular is highly recommended. We opted for the 9 course menu. It was superb. No idea how anyone manages 22 courses.The bar in the hotel is lovely. A real colonial treat.The best thing about the hotel is the fact that it provides a real escape from the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu. Unfortunately it is a little distance away from the main attractions. Normally a 2 or 3 mile distance wouldn't be an issue but this is Kathmandu and the traffic is mad so it can take some time to travel around. It's well worth using the hotel car. It might be more expensive than a taxi but you know what you will be paying and it is far more comfortable.This is a very good hotel and don't let my small issues put you off. It is almost certainly the best hotel in Kathmandu.

Recently I stayed at the Dwarika's Hotel and though my stay was brief it was memorable. The hotel is located very close to the Airport and its every little corner is tastefully decorated in the beautiful Newari style. The rooms are large and very comfortable and the garden a joy to behold. The staff was extremely helpful and very kindly gave us the use of a room to relax before our late evening flight. The breakfast buffet had a good selection of local and Western dishes as did the BBQ buffet dinner. I wish we had more time to stay at this outstanding property.

The best decision ever made to stay in this hotel. Beautiful surroundings, away from hustle bustle. The rooms were nice and well decorated. Staff is really very helpful and ready to help. Wi-Fi is also having a good range.

Staying at the Dwarika Hotel was probably one of the most overwhelmingly positive hotel experiences I've ever had at. First of all, it is a complete oasis from the hustle&bustle of downtown Kathmandu just outside its entrance. The hotel grounds are gorgeous, you truly feel like you are staying in a palace and speaks to the beauty of the local architecture of Nepal. Each and every member of staff was beyond hospitable, and exuded a genuine warmth and friendliness I find is so rare to come by these days in luxury hotels. We were upgraded to a suite upon check-in which was an amazing surprise - the room is simply beautiful, with so much attention to detail with the design. The bathroom was also quite impressive, huge brass sinks and a generously sized shower.  Another huge highlight of our stay at the Dwarika was our meal at their Nepali restaurant 'Krishnarpan'. We decided to go with the 16 course meal, which was an incredible experience! Each dish was served by a different server representing the region of Nepal the dish was from. It was indeed a huge meal (do not expect bite-sized dishes), but nonetheless, it was hands down the best meal of our entire trip. The hotel bar is also so beautiful! Has a charming colonial vibe with vinyl records lining the wall. Our flight was not until midnight from Kathmandu, so the hotel staff was kind enough to give us a refresher room for a couple of hours before we headed to the airport - such high-quality service and hospitality that is rare to come by these days.I could not recommend this hotel more - it was such a delight and we were so well taken care of. It goes way beyond value in terms it providing truly such a unique hotel experience.

This was our treat after a 2-week trek and it was absolutely amazing. I can't speak higher of this place. We loved everything: - staff: very helpful, very professional but approachable and lovely, especially staff at the restaurants and cafes or even in the little souvenir shop- food: yum. We had breakfast, lunch and dinner there and ever meal was lovely. The court yard is magical and having a little afternoon snack there with Masala tea is just perfect- room: amazing, spacious, well decorated, extremely comfortable. There were some fruits and cookies plus tea/ coffee in the room. Lovely place, comfortable bed, great shower- location: great for exploring nearby attractions but the hotel itself is an attraction tooIt is a gem! We will definitely be back!

Our experience has been superbWe chose the royal suite which is a 3 story suite built a a Naware style,decorated as a museum , we spent our 4 days and nights enjoying the inner beauty of the place. There is a large terrace with a view on the city a temple and the Himalayas . Also a small terrace for privacyThe amenities are local and fantasticThe fruits , nuts chips and mini bar is includedThe service is outstanding, twice a day everything is replaced and cleaned and picked up . It has been a royal experience The very best is the staff led by Previn the royal manager whose style is stunning , discrete , caring . He made our tripWe also used their excursion trips Katmandu, Patan, Baktapur,and the helicopter flight over the Everest which is do impressive and leaves you for 1.5 hours at the Everest House hotel a Japanese hotel in the surrounding of the Everest Oxygen is available for those with acute mountain sicknessSo everything was worth the time the effort and the moneyDwarika is more than à hotel , It is a way of life

Perfect location : easy access to airport & historical city. The hotel looks amazing at night & the Nepalese restaurant is worth to try. The junior suite displays modern comfort in a historical environment.

I have been to Kathmandu several times over the last 40 years and stayed in a variety of different hotels. Of all of these hotels Dwarikas has become my favourite. The staff are wonderful and the rooms are superb. If you are going trekking then this is a great base to return to.Beware - Nepal is not as cheap as it was in the past. Government taxes and the included service charge make a beer in Dwarikas as expensive as a beer in Paris! But this is an acceptable price to pay for such a super hotel.

I hesitated to review this hotel since it already has so many stellar reviews. That said, what makes this beautiful spot unique is that it continues to resonate with me even weeks after checking out. Rarely, if ever, do I revisit a hotel. In the case of Dwarika's,  memories continue to resurface and they always make me smile. For those of us who travel for business and spend much of our time in hotels, we are grateful for memories like this. The extra large comfortable rooms with every need covered, the beautiful antique brass touches everywhere, the sound of the wind  all staff make this hotel truly special. For those who check in expecting nothing more than a luxury hotel experience, you may be surprised with the magical memories that continue to last.

We booked last minute for a long weekend which I thought might have been more of a backpackers experience but was delighted to find top class luxury. From check-in the staff were very helpful helping to arrange day tours and book a much needed spa treatment. Friday evening buffet of the local cuisine was a highlight along with the friendly bar staff at the pool. Adventure trips such as downhill cycling and trekking have to be booked externally which is the only part I thought the hotel could have been more knowledgeable on. Overall impression is that it reminds me of the "Best marigold hotel movie" with the location in the heart of the chaos and the fabulous decor and personal touches. Definitely a must visit!

Dwarika's Hotel is tranquil and unique property that is unabashly Nepalese in its architecture and decor, giving it a rustic charm that a contemporary property cannot match. Our 2nd floor Junior Suite room was spacious and comfortable with a nice view of the hotel's inner courtyard. There were a cornucopia of Nepalese furnishings that added to the historic charm, including in the rooms.Service was warm and friendly, and dining options are plenty, including the renowned Krishnarpan restaurant that service amazing Nepalese fare.Our room was a mixed bag. Most of the modern functionalities were not sacrificed in the name of character. A large, king sized bed, dual sinks & vanities, a work desk and chair as well as a comfortable couch were all part of the in-room offerings. However, the light switches were a confusing mess (beware - some of the switches affect the electric sockets, and certain/random combinations of switches turn them on/off), the work chair was incredible uncomfortable and the toilet seat was cheap and worn (although I have no doubt that it's "clean.")The most annoying part was the smell of the bed sheets/comforters (not sure which.) There was damp, musky smell which was off-putting - the type of odor that comes from laundry items that have not been sufficiently dried. Dwarika's might want to replace the beddings a bit more occasionally and dry them thoroughly.Overall, there's every reason to believe that Dwarika's is the top luxury option in Kathmandu, and is a comfortable place to pass the time between tours of the Valley. Given the price, however, a few improvements are necessary for the hotel to reach the level of some of the finer accommodations around the world.

Es un hotel que no solo destaca por su magnífica labor de preservar la esencia de Nepal, sino que también lo hace por la genialidad gracias a la cual lo consigue. Todo está cuidado al detalle, se encargan de que las maderas empleadas sean antiguas, los adornos son elaborados por su propia cadena, y muchos otros son antigüedades. La estética, al igual que la comida, las instalaciones y el personal, son excelentes. Y sin duda alguna otro aspecto destacable es el empeño por parte de la dueña, que además es cónsul honoraria de España, en ayudar a numerosos afectados por el terremoto y en fomentar la educación y la mejora de la situación de las mujeres.

Construído por um arquiteto restaurador. O Hotel parece um palácio. Tudo esta cuidadosamente reformado. Existem varias lojinhas, o restaurante é ótimo, o Spa estava em reforma, mas fiz massagens deliciosas, piscina linda e aulas de yoga nota 1000. Atenção dos funcionários e dicas do guest relations foram øtimas.

Step into the hotel and you step out of the hussle and bussle of Kathmandu into another world. As per its website and other reviews, the hotel is a like a time capsule of Kathmandu in bygone years and a wonderful reminder of the architecture and craftsmanship of years gone by.And the hotel takes this to the 'enth' degree with lots of little touches throughout your stay. This is all very quaint but some of these points are out of date and even a little on the dangerous side. To enter your room you are given a massive key fob which holds the key to the massive padlock on the outside of your door. Once inside, the only way to secure the door is with a bolt latch at the top of the door. If you are traveling with someone and you exit the room separately it means the other person needs to leave the door unlocked or open the door for you when you want to re enter. The shower and bath soaps and shampoos are provided in little clay pots. Problem is they become very slippery when you are wet and are easily broken.The service from the staff was excellent and they were extremely helpful with all requests. The hotel is nearer the airport and a little away from the livelier parts of the town (e.g. Thamel) but taxis are not expensive.  I must also say that for what it provides the hotel is extremely expensive by Kathmandu standards and although very quaint, unless you are going for a special reason (e.g. anniversary or honeymoon) there are a lot of other choices of better value.

We were initially hesitant to book The Dwarika given its room rate, but it proved to be worth every dollar and rupee! We stayed for three nights and were immensely appreciative of the calm and quiet that the hotel offers in an otherwise chaotic city. It allowed us to really dig deep into the city, but still having a restful place to retreat to at night! The location is not great, you're not going to meander around the hotel area and all the attractions of the city is a short taxi ride away. That being said, it is perhaps what makes it such a special retreat. Finding a taxi was never a problem and it was cheap enough to get around. The hotel itself is worthy of being called an attraction too: a lovely history behind it, beautiful architecture and now also focusing on organic food.Our only disappointment was an overwhelming smell of diesel when the generators kicked in: we had one night of lulling about in a whiff of diesel, but with the benefit of 24 hour power, there isn't much to complain about!We were treated like regulars at the Fusion bar and had a wonderful last evening dinner in the Nepali restaurant. It is a must do experience: personalised dinner menus and all, but arrive hungry, wearing loose clothes.

The hotel is one of the most famous ones in Katmandu with the most amazing architecture that you walk hours to see in historical places when you sit in the garden or  go through the buildings you already feel like you are experiencing the history of the city. Everyone is very helpful and kind. The restaurants inside the hotel is a very good option. Rooms are spacious, if you are sensitive with smell avoid entry level rooms.

Dwarika's, in addition to being an excellent five star hotel with everything that ranking entails, is a jewel of Newari architecture and woodwork art. It is almost like a museum, like a place where the time has stopped more than a century ago and an oasis of elegant and exotic tranquility in the crazy, noisy and overcrowded city of Kathmandu. It has a totally different atmosphere than the city itself, a "fine de siecle" feeling of place where the royalty and the nobility of the city used to gather, back then....It is quite away from the place where everything happens, from the indescribably hectic and tiring Thamel, but taxies are easily available to take you there. Even you cannot afford it or if you prefer to stay in Thamel, a coffee or a meal here would expose you to an atmosphere you can no longer experience anywhere else in Nepal …..

LOVE Dwarika’s!  This is an iconic hotel in Kathmandu that has everything you’d ever want including a fabulous spa and multiple restaurants. It’s got a jazz / blues bar and a sushi restaurant in addition to a Nepalese fine dining option (among others).  Splurge on a suite and you won’t be disappointed.  The rooms are HUGE and beyond comfortable. Bathrooms are beautiful and spacious.  Bath amenities are top notch.  I could have stayed there for much longer than we did!  This is the ONLY place to stay in Kathmandu - nothing else will come close in terms of quality or experience!

Absolutely awesome hotel - basically a live in museum with all the wooden work that has been retained and restored.  Rooms are excellent and sizeable - amenities very nice.  Had the 6 course tasting menu dinner - excellent food and an impressive wine list.  Service impeccable.

This hotel is beautiful! The grounds and hotel decoration is requisite! The food is fresh and delicious, and all staff were very courteous and friendly. The rooms are lovely with comfortable beds and so very clean. Highly recommend a stay here!

Beautiful hotel, lovingly created by the original owner with beautiful wood carvings. The staff are polite and courteous and always happy to help. The food is wonderful - from thee traditional banquet experience to ice cream by the pool! A drum destination.

We stayed here as part of a wedding party. Normally it would have been wildly over budget for the likes of us. However if you run to champagne tastes and have pockets to match, look no further.This hotel is a sheer delight. Everything is thought out and presented in exquisite taste. The staff are helpful and efficient, the rooms are spotlessly clean and the hotel is quiet and a real escape from the noise and bustle of Katmandu.What makes Dwarikas such an exception however are the buildings themselves, reconstructed from salvaged materials from traditional homes.

ネパール文化を活かした5つ星ホテル。何よりも素敵なのは庭園のプールとテラス席での食事。ホテルとは思えない文化的な建物の中の庭園・プールはタイムスリップしたかのような気分にさせてくれる。どうせネパールの5つ星ホテルに泊まるのであれば、グループホテルではなく文化を味わえるこのホテルがオススメ。その他、レストランも歴代の偉人が訪れた事のあるレストラン。味はそもそもネパール料理が好きかどうかによるが、外のネパール料理よりも美味しい。部屋も普通のラグジュアリーなホテルとは違い、文化を味わえるラグジュアリーさ。残念だったのは5つ星にも限らず、水が濁っていた事。但しこれはカトマンズ全体で水不足の時期であったため、仕方がない。※他のホテルに宿泊した時はもっと茶色かったのでマシではある。水不足の時期に行ったら5つ星でも綺麗な水は出ないのかなと…スパも素晴らしかったので、是非利用して頂きたい。そしてネパール全体に言える事かもしれないが、スタッフのサービスが素晴らしい。スタッフの笑顔、サービスにも癒やされるよい滞在だった。

I stay in Dwarika's Hotel along with my family for two days and a night. It's becomes my one of the amazing place which I never forget. Really, I get facilities more than I expect. My family feels happy with me for bring her in such pleasant place. I really impressed from the cheerful nature of staffs of hotel. They welcome us with warm greetings. The rooms are amazing and even have huge soaking tubs.We highly recommend Dwarika's Hotel and plan on staying no where else.

We stayed at Dwarika's Hotel for three nights. We found Sakar, his lovely wife and family and staff to be warm, welcoming and caring. My friend had injured her knee and Sakar and his staff went out of their way to care for her , finding medicine at a pharmacy on the holiday of Holi - which is no easy task. They welcomed us with smiles and warm greetings. They accommodated our every need. The food was delicious- great Nepali lunch as well as a great breakfast. Our rooms were old world charm. The antique woodwork is amazing and the garden is lush with flowers. Dwarika's hotel is a short 9 minute walk from Thamel and is situated in Durbar Square ' s rich architectural area teeming with life. We highly recommend Dwarika's Hotel and plan on staying no where else.

We checked in and did not believe the heaven Behring the doors. Beautiful design, wood carvings and art all over the hotel. The rooms are spacious and every thing you need and more are in the room. Shower robs , kettle, coffee, tee, fruits etc. it was our 20th anniversary so they kindly upgraded us and even had a cake with happy anniversary waiting in the room!!!. Amazing and kind service. Highly recommended. Very near  to the two largest temples in Kathmandu. When we arrived we stayed two nights in Tamal and when we left Napal we stayed two nights here. Great decision. Lovvvve this place.

We traveled with a tour group to Nepal.  Dwarika's Hotel was a very pleasant surprise.  The rooms, the grounds, the food, and the staff are all excellent.  Although we used it as a base for sight seeing, I would not hesitate to use it as a great place to just relax for a few days.

Absolutely fabulous hotel in all aspects. Room was beyond large, fabulous huge bath, and extraordinary staff. Spa was lovely as well as massage treatments. Housekeeping staff put hot water bottles in your bed every evening as a special touch. Courtyard was grand, perfect spot for afternoon tea. Do not miss on your trip to Nepal!

We spent 3 nights here earlier this month and our experience was wonderful.  There is an inner courtyard with beautiful restored buildings in it.  Our room was large and clean and I believe all the rooms look into the courtyard.  We did not eat at the Nepalese restaurant, but the food in the Japanese restaurant was great, and the food in the main restaurant was also of good quality and the menu has something for everyone.As many other reviews have noted, this hotel is an quiet oasis away from the hustle & bustle of the city even though it is just off a major roadway.  Also as noted, the architecture is unique and gives a sense of Nepalese culture.

Fabulous design incorporating elements of traditional Nepali design with modern amenities.  Detailed carving is everywhere on  building columns, in rooms on light fixtures.  Inside the compound is a welcome relief from the business and chaos that is Kathmandu /food and service was amazingly great! beautiful swimming pool.  Owners have done a lot to help with the earthquake relief efforts.  Do not miss this hotel -- worth every penny you spend!

Well run facility with - great rooms, Nepalese food & events Nice staff and well researched facility must stay in Kathmandu Pros : Temple nearbyCons : Bit away from the bustling market and roads were not well laid out outside when we visited

Quisimos conocer varios hoteles del lugar, asi que en nuestras 4 y 5 noche elegimos este hotel para conocer. De los tres que visitamos, fue el mejor. Las habitaciones un lujo, el personal muy atento. Un 10 en limpieza. La comida deliciosa. Si pueden conocerlo, dense este gusto!

From the moment you walk through the door you feel like you are in a magical place. This hotel is extraordinary. The original design make you feel like nothing has been touched since it was built. the rooms are simple and comfortable. Even if you don’t stay at this hotel you should go for a dinner/drink just to look around.

美しい建物は気分を高揚させてくれます。中庭が広くゆったり過ごせました。スタッフ達の人柄が良くとても良いホテルだと感じます。もしカトマンズにまた来れたらこのホテルにまた滞在したいです。入り口近くのソファーやプールサイドのベッドソファーの座り心地は最高で、私の家族はミルクティーを頼み長時間チェスやトランプを楽しむ事が出来ました。中庭でゆったり過ごす人達の姿をよく見かけました。ネパール料理のレストランと日本食のレストランに夕食に行きました。どちらもとても美味しいです。ネパール料理のレストランはチャールズ皇太子やヒラリー・クリントンなどのセレブリテイも訪れています。スパもレベル高いトリートメントを受けられます。また、毎朝ヨガレッスンが行われていて、興味深い内容なのでお時間が許せば是非参加されることをお薦めします。ホスピタリティ溢れる素晴らしいホテルだと思います。

Cet hotel allie le confort de la modernité à l'architecture traditionnelle Népalaise.Le chambres sont très grandes avec tout le confort moderne mais avec une touche traditionnelle. Le restaurant est excellent et le personnel très compétent.

We stayed here for three nights, each time we had a different room, always in the main building, top floor, every room was different, large, a nice view into the extremely beautiful courtyard, very typical Nepalese architecture, just a place you want to stay and enjoy life. Breakfast was good, nice to have it outside on the terrace, friendly service. Wie say it seldom: We didn't want to leave.

This hotel is one of the most unusual and memorable I have ever stayed in.  The structure itself is fascinating, the rooms unique and homey and the staff extremely warm and welcoming. Nepal itself is so well worth the trip and Dwarika's Hotel truly enhances the experience.

I had originally meant to stay at Dwarika's before and after our recent trek in the Everest region, but ultimately had not done so due to the view that we needed to be closer to Thamel in order to deal with some things before our trek, and also because I was making all our travel arrangements months in advance and Dwarika's has a rather strict policy on paying their entire tariff at the time of booking, together with a strict and limited refund policy in case of cancellation. At any rate, after returning to Kathmandu from our trek, we made our way to Dwarika's for lunch and spent the entire afternoon eating and drinking in the calm of their beautiful courtyards. The place is everything I had imagined and hoped it would be. The staff are friendly, engaging, and have perfect fluency in English. We particularly enjoyed talking at length to one of our waiters. Food and drink were both superior and delightful. Within the walls of this hotel everything is an oasis of calm, in complete contrast to the chaos of Kathmandu. The staff were happy to show us a standard room, a suite, and the enormous presidential suite. The accommodations are incredibly beautiful and spacious. We definitely will be staying at Dwarika's on our next trip to Nepal, likely next year. I might mention that at least one of the necessities that motivated our staying at a hotel (Yak and Yeti) closer to Thamel - a pharmacy where we could purchase medications for our trek - was in fact available just across the street from Dwarika's, and I suspect we also could have found a bureau de change not too far away from the hotel. Dwarika's is clearly a cultural treasure!

Stayed 2 weeks at Dwarika's and had a great experience. Asked for help getting a SIM card, and they were happy to do everything for me with a local shop and bring me the chip and a receipt. All the restaurants in the compound were good, but the multi-course Nepali food lived up to its reputation.
ネワール文化を基調としたホテル。建物が芸術的で見ていて楽しい。クリシュナルパンの夕飯はとてもおいしかった。しかし、値段の割に部屋が小さめの印象。スタッフの英語がとても上手なので、ストレスが少ない。

This hotel, with its creative architecture and well tended courtyards, is an oasis in Kathmandu. The staff are gracious and attentive to the slightest detail. There is a variety of restaurants and a smallish pool with sun beds around it. I did have some problems with the wifi in the bedroom on my latest (third) visit.

Architecturally this is one of the more interesting and authentic properties anywhere in the world. A night here is sure to delight those seeking an authentic experience in the lap of luxury. The Japanese restaurant was quite remarkable with a well curated menu  and at reasonable prices. I would recommend this hotel to anyone who loves old world charm and a slice of historic in an urban and luxurious setting.

Необычно, комнаты огромные, чисто, красиво, за такой необычный интерьер и ванную комнату прям 5+, внутренний двор тоже отличный, приятно гулять, территория не большая, но мы отлично провели там время. Придраться не к чему, поехала бы еще раз.

I was in Kathmandu with my team of trainers from the United States doing disaster work.  We wanted to spend our last night at a hotel near the airport.   Dwarika's Hotel is a beautiful, elegant and peaceful hotel.  We were surrounded by the antiquities of Nepal and this made the stay even more meaningful.  We had worked very hard and found this hotel to be a true oasis!  The staff were courteous, helpful and went above and beyond the call of duty when I thought I had lost my passport, even finding out exactly what I had to do to get a replacement quickly and even offered to walk with me to the police station to make a "lost report."  Fortunately, my passport was found.  However, I was so appreciative.   To our surprise, the upgraded each one of us to a suite, which was such a delight after our hard work in the field.   The beds, the linens, the towels were luxurious and honestly I only wished we could have stayed longer.  The meals were great too...the BBQ was tasty and had so many choices.   Thank you staff of Dwarika Hotel.   Also the wifi was complimentary....perhaps this has changed.

Viaje de luna de miel en una de las suite de esta hotel que mas se puede pedir.El hotel una maravilla arquitectonica, decorado con gusto, estilo palacio de los reyes Newar, obras de arte por lo pasillos como si fuera un museo. El menu degustacion del restaurante una maravilla, te descalzas al entrar, te dan para lavarte las manos unos paños y despues te acompañan a la mesa casi a ras de suelo y a disfrutar de los platos que van sacando, puedes elegir entre un menu de 15 platos u otro de 25, con el de 15 tuve as que suficiente. tienen detalles con los huespedes como por ejemplo, nos dieron la carta personalizada con nuestros nombres y los platos que habiamos degustado ademas, nos obsequiaron con un objeto decorativo hecho del material con el que esta construido el hotel. Todas las noches nos dejaban unos chocolates junto a la almohada de la cama. Para repetir sin dudar.

Contrary to the media, Nepal is alive and well and this hotel is a great example. The service is absolutely amazing and the staff is very friendly and eager to help and tell you about their country. The rooms are huge and have everything you might need. Good food options with three restaurants. The architecture is beautiful and historic. The city is bustling and desperate for people to come back. I would definitely stay here again.

I have experienced many friendly staffs at hotels and restaurants, but this is the first time I ever wanted waiters and receptionists to stop doing their job just so our family could enjoy their company. Even after the earthquake, Dwarika's is still a beautiful slice of serenity in a very hectic city and it has the best staff I have ever experienced (especially in their food and beverage department). The rooms are wonderful and clean as expected, but it is impossible to go a sentence without mentioning how friendly and helpful the people are at the hotel. I cannot sing higher praises of the establishment and I can say with certainty that I would not consider staying or eating anywhere else in Kathmandu.

Eight years ago I stayed in this amazing hotel. The history of its founding and development was moving and special. The saving of architecture and artefacts from ancient Nepal  with which to build the hotel was a far sighted and noble achievement.The service, welcome, facilities , food were all excellent.I remembered this experience and today found out that the hotel has survived the earthquake intact and is helping their nation recover. I was thrilled to know this and that it is still welcoming guests to their beautiful country.Go !  Go ! Go! you will be rewarded and will be helping them rebuild.

Stayed here for 3nights during our Nepal trip, overall it was an excellent experience. The hotel is beautiful as are the rooms. What we most liked though was the hospitality shown to us by the hotel staff. As well as being both professional and polite, everyone we met was so happy and friendly. We loved our stay in Nepal, if you've never been then please go, you're missing something very special if not…We will return again very soon - Thank you Dwarika

Kathmandu era una città fantastica, per clima, siti culturali, persone amabili e serene. La città è molto povera, ma Dwarika's è un albergo/ristorante che ci fa sognare di essere altrove, in una fiaba o in un ricco palazzo d'altri tempi.

The history of this hotel makes it one of a kind.  Just to walk around and enjoy the fine details and abundance of historical objects makes it worth a visit even if you're not spending the night.  However, as a resident the rooms, spa and commitment to exceptional service by everyone with whom we came in contact makes this a hotel worth collecting in your travels.

Katmandu sehir olarak insanın içini isıtan bir sehir. Şehirclik olarak batılı anlamda geride olmalarına rağmen bu otel başka.. Odamız inanılmaz derece de büyük bir o kadar basit ancak bir o kadar da fonsiyonel ve inceliklerle dolu. Oda iç avluya bakıyordu. Havuzu gece görmek harika. Oda da yatak bölümü, orada geniş bir hol, ve oturma bölümü yer alıyor. Banyo ve tuvalet ayrı ayrı..Hayatım da kaldığım her en iyi yerlerden biri..

This place is so special. The intricate wooden carvings everywhere are so gorgeous; it is indeed a living museum. The rooms and staff are great. The traditional thali dinner is very nice. A tranquil retreat in the otherwise chaotic city of Kathmandu.

El hotel está restaurado tras el terremoto, ya es totalmente seguro volver a alojarse y poder disfrutar de un merecido descanso. Las  habitaciones mantienen todas las comodidades de un hotel verdaderamente exquisito. No es el típico hotel americano impersonal, es un hotel exclusivo para los amantes del verdadero lujo. Es un museo con extraordinarias piezas antiguas labradas en madera. Ventanas , columnas, muebles  ofrecen al visitante una bello trabajo típico local. Las áreas comunes ofrecen al cliente todo lo que necesita además de poder deleitarse comiendo en sus restaurantes.Dentro del hotel se encuentra el más reconocido restaurante Nepalí en el que se han deleitado probando sus platos típicos de las distintas regiones de Nepal personalidades de todo el mundo.Es un hotel en donde la atención del servicio hace que el visitante se siente muy cómodo y como si estuviera en casa.

We stayed here in late March while traveling to an from Pokhara while trekking around the Annapurna foothills. Lovely hotel and great staff. I hope all the staff are safe after the terrible earthquake in April

Beautifully appointed hotel amid the chaos of the city. Quiet and a joy,especially when you have just finished your first trek in Nepal. I hope that the hotel did not suffer much damage. I have very fond memories of the peoples of Nepal.

We spent 3 nights at the Dwarika's few days before the earthquake. The hotel's authentic architecture with original Newar windows, artifacts and decoration overall makes the experience really unique. The room are spacious, well decorated and very clean. The restaurants are also great. The Japanese is run by a very famous Japanese chef offers great dishes. The Nepalese, with its "Hall of Fame" and authentic Nepalese service, food, tableware is also a must-see.We had luch every single day in the hotel's sunny courtyard. The service is also very good, well above the expectations I initially had for a stay in Nepal. We are really sad for the earthquake and hope that the Dwarika, its staff and the Nepalese can bouce back!In any case, Mr Dwarika fully fulfilled his goal of leaving a true legacy.

Considered the best hotel in Nepal, the Dwarika's was built in the Nepalese style and really delights and impresses for the beauty and personality. The suites are spacious, decorated with furniture, tapestries and typical objects, with all the expected amenities of a 5 star. There are four restaurants available and that the local cuisine is especially beautiful. In fact, almost all delights at the hotel with the exception of service and price.It is absurdly expensive for the country standards and staff despite gentle, are not properly trained, so that there are many flaws in the service, as delay in treatment, lack of replacement of daily consumption items in the suite, and other details. Another problem is the location, far from the city center.

Superbe hôtel un vrai hâvre de paix à Katmandou. Nous y avons séjourné 5 jours. L'accueil est chaleureux, le personnel charmant. Tout est fait pour satisfaire le client. Les restaurants sont très bons, le restaurant Krishanrpan sert des plats Népalais sublimes, un menu vous est remis à votre nom!. La piscine très agréable. Wi fi gratuite. La décoration est typiquement Népalaise,  il y a plein de belles choses et de beaux objets à voir partout dans l'hôtel.La literie est très confortable, les chambres super propres. Les sanitaires sont bien équipés et la robinetterie impeccable. L'hôtel est situé près de l'aéroport, mais pas de bruit d'avion. Il est également situé près de Pashupatinath. Le luxe à l'état pur.

Its an old looking structure just 10min from the airport. One of the best hotels in Kathmandu. The windows and door frames are antiques and the courtyard is very relaxing with a small pool and ample lazing beds and chairs (all very properly cared for). The restaurant serves excellent local food - there are 3 outlet. The Nepalese restaurant had very authentic (high end though) cuisine. You can sit on  the floor and there are performances.Breakfast was ample and very personalised.The rooms were very antique looking but extremely comfortable.They also have a spa and some shops. There is also a fireplace although I am not sure if they use it during winter ( I was there in June).Apart from the airport, there is very little you can do in the surrounding area (in fact nothing). Town centre is a good 15 min away with no traffic.

Si buscas autenticidad y originalidad, este hotel es una auténtica maravilla. Las habitaciones son preciosas, y te transportan a una época oriental y rústica maravillosa. Muy original el sistema de la llave de la habitación, si bien es un poco incomodo si vas en pareja (es un candado, tal cual). A destacar el restaurante, con el menú degustación de comida nepalí.Ojo: no hay wi-fi en las habitaciones. Sólo en la zona del bar.Ha sido un auténtico placer!

Wanted to drop some notes on the 10plus stays Rooms on lower floor 101/102/103 are best location Location is next to pashpatinath a short walk around the corner and 15 mins from airport Overall the bedding is not that nice but service is really good Used to love Friday nite barbecue this prices have shot up in recent years simply way over priced Hyatt Kathmandu or the Yak and Yeti is now better value
ホテルの名前にもなっている大富豪が失われつつあるネワール建築の様式をそのまま残したいというコンセプトで、取り壊されていく精緻な彫刻が施された窓枠や調度品などをコツコツと集め、自邸を泊まれる博物館として改装したホテル。建築好きなら鼻血ものであることは間違いない。サービスも設備もカトマンズとは思えないほどの一級品。ただし飛び抜けて高い。ここに泊まるだけに訪れる価値は十分だがいかんせん高すぎる。

Les bâtiments de l'hôtel , en pur style newar , sont de très grande qualité.Beau jardin fleuri et piscine ( même si non chauffée !).Les chambres et sanitaires ont une décoration raffinée et sobre.Nous avons pris les chambres standard , déjà de très grand confort.Bon petit déjeuner buffet.Le dîner au restaurant népalais est une belle expérience.Un seul point est totalement inacceptable: il faut payer le wifi...alors qu'il est gratuit dans la moindre tea house à 200 roupies la nuit.

Resort  lussuoso in cui  trovi un’atmosfera di pace e tranquillità che ti isola dalla caotica Kathmandù. Si viene proiettati magicamente, senza neanche accorgersene, nella cultura e nella spiritualità nepalese. Si trova un po’ lontano dal centro città, ma una volta arrivati si entra in un’atmosfera magica in stile newari. Ambiente caratteristico in legno intagliato con tantissimi pezzi di antiquariato del XIII secolo. L’arredamento è sobrio ed elegante,  sembra di stare dentro un antico castello o un tempio induista ricco di opere d’arte. Giardino - cortile incantevole con annessa piscina circondata da luci soffuse e sottofondo musicale. Bellissime fontane artistiche e variopinti fiori arricchiscono l’arredamento esterno.  Ci sono stata per una cena di gala nella sala del ristorante tipico nepalese gustando un’ottima cibo composto da 6 portate. In questa sala si mangia senza  scarpe, seduti su comodi cuscini posti su bassissimi sgabelli raso terra. Tavoli apparecchiati nei minimi dettagli. Personale garbato e attento. Ambiente pulitissimo. Un vero gioiello tra la polverosa e difficoltosa vita cittadina nepalese. Prezzo un po’ caro, però ne vale la pena. La struttura ha altri 3 punti  ristoro con cucina oltre che nepalese anche internazionale, giapponese e piatti vegani. Ha parcheggio privato gratuito. Centro benessere compreso di massaggi. Le camere dell’hotel sono tutte dotate di Tv satellitare, climatizzatore, bagno e salotto. Le camere che danno sul cortile, in quanto più isolate dal traffico della strada, dovrebbero essere più tranquille. L’Hotel dista 500 metri dal Tempio Pashupatinath e 2 km dall’aeroporto internazionale di Tribhuvan.

When we first arrived and walked through the door from the street, it looked like a little village. They had these beautifully restored unique brick buildings with wooden carved windows overlooking a few courtyards. There were flowering trees overlooking the courtyards and the site was completely idyllic. Even at night the courtyards were brightly lit up and absolutely beautiful. Among the shared facilities there was a library (a building, not a room), tavern overlooking the pool and spa. After a tiring day of sightseeing, there is nothing more wonderful than lounging around in the various buildings and courtyard in the hotel and reading a book or playing chess. Also there are programs in evenings and night. One evening was the flute, another evening we caught the female dancer. This adds to the atmosphere. The spa was average - nothing to boast about. The hotel room was enormous and very nice with a nice lounging day bed as well. Not all rooms are made equal though. The only slight issue is that it is a bit of an open bathroom concept so:1. After a shower, you step out and it can be freezing cold. There is no towel rack inside the shower room which would made a radical difference 2. If you sharing a room, should be with your significant other vs just a friend as you can't bring all your clothes and towel into the shower room as nowhere to hang the clothes. Other issues:1. With service in this environment it is different from western style management. There is no empowerment so they are all very rigid.their key drop is to say no, not yes. 2. There are a few power trips per night but these are quickly restored. 3. It seemed every night the wireless would suddenly stop working. I suspect this is a Nepal issue rather than a hotel issue. 4. The room door closes on a padlock system so theoretically someone could lock you in your room. Eg your hotel mate goes out, pulls the lever, while you are still in the room. 5. Must be only 6 star hotel with no conditioner and body lotion in the rooms- only upon request.  And Nepal has very dry air

Hotel com decoração interessante, jardins internos lindos, piscina excelente, dispõe de 3 restaurantes (todos bons) e serviço eficiente e simpático. A suíte júnior que fiquei era muito boa, mas os quartos standard são muito mais simples e se ficar de frente pra rua extremamente barulhento. Fica um pouco afastado do mercado e da zona turística, mas ainda assim pelo que vi, é o melhor hotel da cidade.

This hotel was a treat at the end of a 3 wk vitamin distribution effort in hill villages. Breakfast was included with room the first night but not thereafter. Free yoga each morning was fun. Spa services were unique and reasonably priced by US standards. The ancient massage was 75 min including passive yoga stretching and ayervedic massage--$60. Gift shops charge top dollar but did deal a little. Shopping is not that easy to access without a taxi ride from this location. The pool is lovely. Spotty free wifi in the bar area only. Creative courtyard lunches for $20. Hotel is within walking distance of Pashipatinath temple area. Clientele was older and perhaps more 'well heeled' than anywhere else we stayed in Nepal. Many nations represented.

Dwarika's - это роскошный отель в Катманду! Если вам хочется отключится от окружающей непальской действительности и не жалко при этом значительной суммы денег, то вам сюда! Роскошное здание с колоритным внутренним двором, несколько ресторанов где все очень вкусно и московские цены, приятное обслуживание, уютный бар с отличным алкоголем (тоже не дешевым, конечно). Номера очень теплые, там есть все необходимое и даже больше. Одна проблема - из Dwarika's не хочется уходить :)

Es un excelente hotel en alimentos, su arquitectura tipica, alberca, descanso, pide una suite en el ultimo piso y usa el CD del hotel para poner musica tipica y te relajes. Los cuartos son comodos y excelentes amenidades, jabon olor a menta. El personal es amable pero no destaca sobremanera, distruta de sus variados restaurantes y hay un lugar para leer, si te gusta lo gozaras. Es tematico y relajante.

Stunning place, we stayed in a suite it was huge and gorgeous. Its an oasis in the middle of busy Kathmandu with a great garden full of lovely trees and plants, a big pool and superb food. The staff were really friendly  and it was pleasure to stay there

i have stayed atdwariks now at least 3 times, not actually a one nightstand stuff but stayed there just to enjoy the inner beauty of dwarikas, the location is just about right near the international airport and the area it is located is slowly getting urbanised.....when i say inner beauty i mean that the courtyard is great and the decoration is beautiful as well.Since i went alone i could not expeirience the restuarnts but the room service was  quite nice and efficient.i guess our tourist friends would certainly enjoy this little paradise with modern facilities to boot

NamasteHerzlich Willkommen!Das Dwarikas Hotel in Kathmandu ist nur 1.6 km vom Internationalem Flughafen entfernt, also sehr gut und zentral gelegen. Der Empfang im Hotel war äusserst freundlich und hilfsbereit. Das Check-in erfolgte rasch und unkompliziert. Die Mitarbeiter strahlen eine harmonische Ruhe und eine glückliche Zufriedenheit aus. Das Zimmer 310 ist ein wahrer Traum, sehr gross und geräumig. Der Lärm von der Strasse verhallt in den Wänden, sodass absolute Ruhe herrscht. Das Buffet zum Morgenessen ist reich und frisch. Das Nachtessen ist hervorragend und das Bier Everest ein Genuss. Ich kann jedem Nepal Reisenden dieses Hotel wärmstens empfehlen,Norbert aus der Schweiz

What a beautiful place!!  Great staff,accomation and surroundings. You would never know you were on a busy street in Katmandu. Only downside is location. For Dubar Square and Thamil,it's a bit of a hike. Traffic can be dreadful. Still loved The Dwarika though

I went to this hotel as a tourist and not as a guest. I must say I was really surprised to see how beautifully it's been built and maintained. We ended up having a light lunch at their restaurant "Toran" and it was decent.  But this hotel is a must visit for those wanted to get a glimpse of some really excellent architecture and woodwork.

Dwarika's Hotel is just so beautiful and very mesmerizing.The hotel has a very wide and spaced out property. The rooms were so spacious and luxurious, and the staff were so caring and always wanted to find an opportunity to help, especially the lady receptionist Mahima. I so loved the architecture and how the hotel was built, it felt as if you're at your own house relaxing.

Absolutamente precioso. Creo que hicimos en él tantas fotos como en cualquiera de las plazas Durbar, por ejemplo. La habitación junior suite era bastante grande, llena de detalles de artesanía con un gusto precioso y bien cuidados. Wifi incluida y también, a pesar de que había leído lo contrario, tiene caja de seguridad en la habitación. Los jardines, la biblioteca, etc.. preciosos. Se corresponde exactamente con las imágenes que se ven en su web, no engañan en absoluto. Además su propietaria es la cónsul honoraria de España en Katmandú y el Consulado Honorario está en el propio edificio del hotel (al lado de la entrada puede verse el mástil con la bandera española y la placa oficial). O sea, que si eres español es un valor añadido en caso de problemas...

We arrived after a long flight and were delighted with the warm welcome and our room - the only major let down was the position of the hotel away from any other good restaurants as the food here was really only average - in retrospect we would have liked to have the comfort of this hotel combined with the ability to eat out without the complications of taxis etc

It is unbelievable that just a few meters from Kathmandu's hustel and bustle there is a place like this. Tranquility and peace, that is what you find here. Each room decorated like a masterpiece. If you want to top it pay a visit to the Spa. No other place to stay when in Kathmandu.

カトマンズの大きな通り沿いにあるとは思えない程、一歩ホテルに入っただけでとても静かな空間でした。敷地内の建物もネワール建築で素晴らしい！カメラのシャッターが止まりません。ネパール最後の夜の記念に…と1人でシングルを予約したのですが、部屋が空いているからとスイートルームにアップグレードして頂きました。日の入り直前に「おやすみの準備です」と言って女性スタッフ2人が訪れ、カーテンを閉めて、ベッドを入りやすいようにほぐしてくれ、バスマットを敷いて下さったのには感動しました！夜にはチョコを持っておやすみの挨拶に来て下さいました。レストランやロビー、プールなどどのスタッフのサービスも最高ランクでした！この感動をスタッフの方に伝えたかったのですが、英語が不慣れなため上手く伝えられなかったのが残念です。是非また泊まりたい、皆にもオススメしたいホテルです！

This is by far the best hotel in Kathmandu. Beautiful architecture, peaceful ambiance, and the most friendly, kind and helpful staff. There are three restaurants and the typical Nepali food one is an experience in itself. If you can afford it, dont hesitate, you wont regret it.

we stayed at the Dwarikas hotel during our stay in Kathmandu. The hotel is an oasis in the heart of the city. The Nepal artifacts through out the hotel adds to the feeling of going back to old Kathmandu. The rooms were great and the staff attentive. I would stay at no other hotel than the Dwarikas.

Beautiful  and peaceful hotel close to Kathmandu airport and convenient for the city centre. Good bar with helpful staff. Lovely rooms. But two criticisms: (1) Why does. A hotel of this quality think it appropriate to give free wifi in the bar and by the swimming pool, but charge for it in the rooms; and (2) the meals in the signature Nepali restaurant are expensive and  a trap for tourists- avoid.

Prachtig hotel, heritage, mooi bewaarde authenticiteit, max service, vriendelijkheid, luxe. Prachtige kamers met alles erop en eraan, pure luxe, schitterend bed, badkamer. Lekker ontbijt, diner, super vriendelijk personeel, rustige ligging, mooie binnentuin met zwembad.

Nous avons séjourné en famille durant 4 nuits, en octobre 2014.Longue attente pour obtenir une chambre, qui finalement est une chambre simple, le bois est omniprésent mais sans luxe. Une armoire et un bureau sans charme, une salle de bain austère, pas de produits  body lotion ni conditioner dans la chambre.Bien sûr, au tarif demandé, tout le monde est poli et courtois, mais vraiment cet hôtel de vaut pas le tarif demandé. Les restaurants de l'hôtel sont plus chers qu'en Europe. Déçu, vraiment nous avons été déçu de la qualité de l'hôtel. Ils vous vendent une histoire, une tradition, etc ...Les voyages précédent à Katmandu nous ont fait découvrir d'autres hôtels, 4 étoiles, 4 fois moins onéreux et tout aussi bien équipés.Yves Jordan, Lyon

An amazing property, beautifully decorated with traditional artefacts! Spacious and charming rooms, excellent service, great food in a beautiful setting. One of the best hotels that I've ever stayed at. I would highly recommend this property to any traveller visiting Kathmandu.

This is a lovely hotel. A feast for the eyes. If you are expecting perfection in systems etc go to the Marriott or whatever globotel is open next. The a/c doesn't work well or at all, the power fails on a regular basis, internet works when it works, the bulbs in the bathroom mirrors don't work (they don't have replacements) and the drain in our bathroom overflowed if there was too much water in the sink when you pulled the plug. BUT this place really has soul. Rooms are large and beautifully furnished. Unusually our mini bar was complimentary. We had a large day bed and a terraceThe decor is astonishing and everywhere you look there is beauty and wonderThere are several restaurants and a bar plus a library.  The main restaurant was ok - reminiscent of the costa brava in the 70's but there are a couple of speciality restaurants. One Nepalese and one Japanese. Both of them were high quality though not cheap. The Nepalese offered set menus between 6 and 22 courses.  We opted for the 16 course and halfway through I couldn't eat any more. The staff are lovely with the only exception being the meeter and greeter when we arrived. She was downright rude which gave a bad first impressionSo if you want a truly unique place to stay and don't mind a few quirks then this is the place to stay in Kathmandu.

Abbiamo soggiornato per tre notti al Dwarika ed è stata un'esperienza veramente splendida.Stanze grandissime, arredate con il meglio dell'artigianato nepalese.Servizi impeccabili, grande attenzione ai clienti anche nelle piccole cose.Bellissimi pezzi di antiquariato un po dovunque, ottima cena nepalese in uno dei ristoranti annessi all'hotel.Tornare stanchi in hotel, dopo un lungo viaggio in Tibet, è stato come tornare a casa!

In the chaos of Kathmandu, Dwarika's is like an oasis of calm, beauty and cleanliness. The hotel grounds are beautiful, the architecture and courtyard inside makes you feel as though you have been transported back in time. We stayed as a family with 2 kids (ages 14 and 3) and found the hotel extremely comfortable and the staff so kind and helpful. After a day on the busy streets of the city, coming back to this hotel is perfect. Rooms extremely spacious and well decorated (we had an Executive Suite). We ate at all 3 restaurants (the Japanese, traditional Nepali and Continental) and each one was great. Hotel gives ample bottled water to get you through your entire stay. Small touches like umbrellas available for all, a full set of toilettries (including toothbrushes, toothpaste, etc) are fantastic. Definitely the #1 place to stay in Kathmandu!

The Dwarikas Hotel is a peaceful oasis in the middle of bustling Kathmandu. It combines the service standards of a five star hotel with the special environment of a boutique hotel. The owners of this hotel have a vision of how their hotel should contribute to the conservation of Nepalese heritage and this is felt in every corner of the hotel. Beautiful work of art can be seen all over the hotel. Staff are very friendly and competent. Foods is excellent, especially the six course Nepalese dinner. If there is one drawback, then it is that wifi is not free. For a hotel in this category, free wifi should simply be part of the service offered.

My husband and I stayed at the Dwarika's Hotel for a few days before and after our trip to Tibet. The hotel is just beautiful. The attention to detail in the construction of the hotel is outstanding. The hand carved dark wood doorways & window coverings/shutters against the red brick and stone patios instantly gives you a relaxing feeling. Then to be greeted so warmly and given a Nepal specialty fruit drink and cool towels and seated and large over sized chairs & couches made it a complete event, and we had only just walked in the doors! This is a place not to be missed. We hope to go back to Nepal and stay at Dawarika's mountain resort which we hear is just as spectacular.

Um hotel lindo e charmoso no coração da cidade caótica e empoeirada.A arquitetura nepalesa é preciosa e sentar no jardim e apreciar seus recortes e janelas entalhadas já é um programa delicioso.Vale a hospedagem ou jantar a noite no seu lindo restaurante ou mesmo tomar um chá da tarde, no lindo pátio em meio aos jardins.A piscina do hotel é deliciosa.Recomendadíssimo

Me quede en este hotel hace poco.Es un edificio muy antiguo recién restaurado. Esta ricamente decorado por objetos en madera tallados.Restaurante japonés muy rico.Gente muy servicial y lista para darte todo tipo de información. Recomiendo ir a Patan pasar el dia y volver a este hotel.

Travelling with small children, after being 'out and about' in Kathmandu during the day, it is wonderful to come home to Dwarika's at the end of the day. The staff are very family friendly, and the girls loved the experience as much as we did.There are lots of dining options that start early for the kids, and the poolside BBQ was fantastic!

Une architecture digne des palais royaux du Nepal, une ambiance reposante à l'abris de l'agitation de Katmandou.. Les chambres sont très belles et grandes. Seul bémol, le restaurant occidental à l'ambiance assez froide.Sinon, le restaurant népalais vaut le détour, très typique et très bon ! Le bar est parfait.Bref, un hôtel au charme fou que je recommande vivement !

My two daughters and I stayed here for only one night but I so wish it was longer.It is one of the coolest, most beautiful hotels I have stayed it.It has separate building on the compound with beautiful woodwork, carvings and lush landscaping. Brick and stone paths take you around the property and the birds are chirping... It's just heaven.The food was FANTASTIC at the small Japanese restaurant and also at the two other restaurants. We stayed in 507 which was great because we could see the city scape. It had a separate tub and shower, plenty of closets, coffee/ tea maker and the beds ( even the extra one ) were super comfy.They have an ok gym ( wish they had a tv by treadmill) and a cool " yogi" who teaches a very basic ( but fun) yoga class at 7am.The front desk staff as well as housekeeping were all great too We had just a great time and we would come back in a heartbeat ...Thanks !

The hotel's architecture is beautiful and the gardens are gorgeous. The rooms are very spacious and nicely decorated. The food is very tasty with ingredients from the owners' farm. Staff was very courteous. The heating was a bit inefficient in many parts of the hotel including the bar. I tried to work in the bar during the day and it was freezing cold. The WiFi system is a bit old fashion. One needs to get a new password from the reception every single day and re-log in. The hotel rates are too high.

This is a beautiful experience. The hotel is a testimony of the dedication of Mr. Dwarikas, who spent a lifetime collecting and renovating architectonic details from the area, who are now a part of the hotel. The level of service, attentive, sincere, is as best as it can get anywhere in the world. Only 5 minutes from the airport. Highly recommended if you go to Kathmandu,

My wife and I had just been on a 8 day trek and needed to unwind, so we booked this hotel to really have a wonderful end to our honeymoon, and we were not disappointed. This was by far and large the best hotel I have ever stayed at in my life. We had a suite that was enormous and the grounds were beautiful. The only thing that surpassed the sheer beauty of the place was the service itself. From the manager right down to the cleaning staff, everyone was excellent. A few things to note:- They do not like tips, there is a tipping box in the lobby that is the best way to ensure your tips to the waiters etc find their way to those working behind the scenes.- It is a luxury 5* hotel, but at the same time it is family run. A testament to how amazing this place is, is that the family still live on the premises (they even came to us in the library to congratulate my wife and I on getting married - nice touch!)- They have a traditional nepalese restaurant that has been frequented by several celebreties and honoured guests (including Prince Philip, Hillary Clinton) and it is AMAZING. We had a lot of local food and this did it justice.- The breakfast is the best I have had anywhere in the world.- The spa is an oasis. - Location is smack in the middle of town, so lots of hustle and bustle, yet no noise in the rooms AT ALL.My wife and I are frequent travellers and have been to several luxury hotels around the world and we will be returning here every year to celebrate our anniversary. Excellent hotel, excellent service, great food.

Very much enjoyed our stay at this hotel, the rooms are comfortable and the hotel has lot of character. The food is awesome and the Nepalese restaurant is excellent. The hotel architecture is amazing and has a very colonial look.

Very much enjoyed my stay at Dwarika's. Beautifully decorated, super friendly staff, lots of character. Generally a great vibe. The building is spectacular, old wood, brick, beautiful carvings...a real feast for the eyes.

Со стороны сразу так и не заметишь, что стоишь, пожалуй, перед самым лучшим и истинно "непальским" отелем в Катманду. Справа шумно кипит жизнь столицы Непала, а с левой стороны вы стоите перед вполне себе обычным входом, перед которым небольшой автомобильный карман, чтобы они могли высадить пассажиров и тут же уехать. Никакой парковки, только пара охранников перед входом. Но стоит только войти внутрь, как вы попадаете в совершенно иной мир, уютный, с прекрасной архитектурой как во внутреннем дворе, так и коридоров отеля. Вокруг сады, журчание небольших искусственных водоёмов, ароматы цветов и других растений, коих очень много во внутреннем дворе, где, помимо этого есть 2-3 ресторана, бар, бассейн и огромное дерево с розовыми листьями перед ним. С противоположной стороны от входа находится корпус с VIP-номерами, где гостями были Хиллари Клинтон, Ричард Гир, Джимми Картер, Дэми Мур, Борис Гребенщиков и другие.Номер бы очень просторный, с большой кроватью, вход в ванную комнату не имеет двери, это просто портал, где по центру находится довольно крупная ванна, а уже по обеим сторонам от неё - душевая и туалет (с дверьми)

Всем советую этот отель! Парадиз в Катманду. Отличный сервиз.Спа не понравилось. Ощущение, что массажиста куда-то спешила. Внутри 2 ресторана типичной непальской кухни.Что самое главное - это ощущение спокойствия. Никто ничего не ворует

A lovely quiet oasis in the middle of Kathmandu. The large comfortable bedrooms are furnished in a traditional and luxurious style. They face into a quiet courtyard where there is a bar and restaurant. Great service.The hotel is conveniently located for the airport so don't miss out on the scenic Buddha Airways Everest flight.We loved Nepal and it was a great add on to our India Northern Triangle itinerary.We arrived via a direct flight from Varanasi which was short and convenient. First we spent 2 nights at the Dwarika Dhulikhel for a uniquely relaxing experience. Then we transferred to this hotel for 2 nights before flying back to New Delhi. This itinerary worked really well and it was especially good to have a day relaxing after Varanasi.Thank you Trinetra for managing our tour.

This is our second trip to Nepal in the past 12 months. On each occasion, we have used Dwarika's Hotel as our main base during our trip. This time, we stayed at Dwarika's on four separate occasions over a 4 week period ... and on each, the service & professionalism of all of the staff was unparalleled as well as the state of our incredible and luxurious rooms. The setting out of the hotel, the Newari architecture, the pieces of local history placed all around the complex are fascinating & beautiful ... it is like walking around a museum, a piece of "living history".When you arrive back at Dwarika's, the feeling is like "coming home" ... from people at the front entrance to the reception desk and the guys who carry your luggage. The genuinely friendly & caring faces and the "welcome back" greetings provide you with a sense of enjoyment and real contentment, as well as a sense of belonging. We believe this is what sets Dwarika's Hotel apart from the other 5 star international hotels in Kathmandu ... its people ... their warmth, their caring attitude and the way they go about doing their job. I am sure the founder of this establishment, Dwarika Das Shrestha would have been very proud how his dream has evolved.There are just too many people who we would like to give special mention to for their assistance and making our stays so memorable, but we would like to name a few:- Shiraj (the Night Manager), Shiva (Hospitality / Reception), Sange (IT - for his help with our computer browsing issues), Alpha, Neeta & Handyha (all Restaurant staff), and Dr. Sanjay (for his professional care & consideration).During this stay at Dwarika's, we used the SPA facilities on a number of occasions due to an ongoing shoulder problem. We found the SPA's menu of services to be quite extensive and what one would expect from a 5 star international hotel. The SPA people were very professional & attentive. We would like to give special mention to Sashi and her magical hands / fingers ... my should will miss you back in Australia. We found the prices for the various treatments to be very reasonable. We certainly look forward to coming back one day to this "oasis". If you are visiting Kathmandu, this is a "must stay" hotel ... you will not be disappointed.

The Dwarika is a renovation on Newari style of an old building. It is simply gorgeous. It frees you from the third world town. Unfortunately, as in all Nepal, the food is quite disappointing. Really a "must go".

Having read of the chaos and pollution of Kathmandu, I felt it important to book a hotel I would be happy to return to and recuperate from the activities of exploring the city.I booked Dwarika's based on the reviews from Tripadvisor, but also beacuse of the photos of this amazing property, the architectural details, the feeling of history that has been recreated, the use of amazing wooden furniture and of art situated everywhere you look. Like Dwarika's Resort this hotel has a soul that makes you feel instantly comfortable and secure in a very foreign environment that is Kathmandu.Arriving late at night we were welcomed and taken straight to our Junior Suite; bigger than my apartment in Hong Kong and furnished in such a unique way, I felt like I was staying in someones very plush house. The way the hotel is decorated makes you just feel welcome and comfortable and it is not like a cookie cutter interantional hotel chain where every room is a carbon copy of the next, with mass produced products.Breakfast was a delight outside in the courtyard, although some of the staff were a little cold and aloof. After 7 hours exploring and walking the mad streets of Kathmandu, I do not believe I have ever been so happy to see the hotel and enter the Lobby and inner courtyard and retreat from the madness I discovered during my long, hot and crazy day.After a long hot shower, and a few hours around the pool dinner was a 6 course Nepalese set course in the Nepalese restaurant in the inner courtyard of Dwarika's. The meal was a wonderful and VERY filling experience and the staff here were lovely, hospitable and friendly.I wanted to experience Dwarika's Resort for my last day and as I had booked directly with Nirdosh (who was exceptionally professional and helpful with my booking) I asked the team to cancel my last night and book at the resort; which was arranged straight away and transfer was arranged the following morning. A great nights sleep and off to Dwarika's Resort in Dhulikel the following day; readers, if you have not heard of Dwarika's Resort then please sepnd a few minutes reading the reviews and I would recommend 100% for you to spend some time here; it is only 1 hours drive away and you will experience an unforgetable and amazing stay.Great stay, thank you

The first time I met my English friend Diana  5 years ago ,in Bali where she lived,  she told me that the most amazing place in the world was Kathmandu .. she was absolutely right.We were in Nepal last March and the beauty of its gorgeous  artistic heritage, the colours  and  perfumes of its streets and markets , the kindness of its smiling people,  so poor but so dignified , not to talk of  the emotion to rise your eyes in the chaos of a little street at sunset and meet the  Boudhanath Stupa ‘s eyes … it is  really breathtaking and worthwhile going.. even if you are not  a tracker…We had only one week so we stayed  mostly in Kathmandu at Dwarika ‘s hotel that I recommend.  It is a bit far from  Durbar square and in a quite anonymous  part of the city but when you pass its  threshold  you enter in an oasis of peace,  full of beautiful Nepali antique  furniture and objects. Rooms are spacious and comfortable and try a  Nepali  dinner at KRISHNARPAN restaurant… it’s a real experience. There is also a nice good Japanese  restaurant..

We stayed at Dwarika's Hotel on our last night in Nepal and from the moment we entered the courtyard, I did not want to leave. We are a family of four with two small children (4 and 6), and after the dusty, smoggy streets of Kathmandu, this place is an oasis of beauty, tranquility and cleanliness. The staff were all exceptionally friendly and kind to our children, our room was enormous and just perfect for the four of us. The beauty of the traditional woodwork and the story behind the restoration were inspiring. The food was fantastic - best coffee I had in Nepal - and there was enough space for our children to run around without being too annoying to other guests and for them to burn off some energy. The three resident dogs kept them amused, particularly the one who shared my daughter's name. This place was pure bliss and we loved every minute spent here.

Hotel maravilhoso, acolhedor, elegante e com o melhor restaurante de Cidade.Preciosidades como as antigas janelas de madeira  de Katmandu, algumas originais, com cerca de 200 anos. Pitoresca área externa, com lindos jardins e piscina. Experiência inesquecível.

I have read all of the reviews and criticisms of this hotel. What trumps all of this is that you will stay in one of the most amazing hotels in the world. There is always a sterile atmosphere in most hotels but in Dwarika's, you feel as though you are staying in someone's home. And what a great feeling to have that in such an exotic faraway location. Each room is unique and every nook and cranny displays such beautiful craftmanship and detail. Also loved the environmentally friendly products and paper. They also supply a local tiger game with instructions on your coffee table. Just strolling around the different buildings and courtyards of the hotel is fascinating. You must have someone explain the history of the collection of all of this fabulous wookwork that was to be discarded if Dwarika did not save it.Although the food was average and the location was a bit far from the center, I would not miss this experience - phenomenal.

This is a charming hotel built in a Nepali rustic style.It is certainly not the Ritz and in truth we thought our room was quite dark but as a very comfortable and easily accessible base in Kathmandu we were quite satisfied.In our opinion the Japanese restaurant was not good and the breakfast was just about adequate but we still enjoyed our stay at Dwarika's and if we were to return to Kathmandu we would probably stay here again.

My father and I spent a night here waiting for our flight to Nepalgunj the next day to head to Tiger Tops at the Bardia National Park.This hotel is gorgeous.  Rooms are very spacious and they gave us a complimentary upgrade to the suite.  Free Wifi.  Friendly service all around.  Clean and spacious rooms.  Wonderful hot water.  A nice breakfast complimented our stay.  What more could you ask for?

The approach to this hotel from the airport and the hectic street on which it is situated do not prepare you for the experience here. Away from the crazy traffic of Kathmandhu you are immediately immersed in a calming, relaxing hotel. It really does feel like someone's home rather than a hotel.The Friday evening barbeque is worth trying with many traditional Nepali dishes. The staff are all charming and always smiling. Kathmandhu is a fascinating destination and this is a treat to stay here.Our only criticism was the daily charge for wi-fi, which we didn't expect in a top end property such as this. Well worth a stay when in KTM.

Darika's service and amenities were excellent but what especially appealed to us is the fact that the hotel's authentic Nepali architectural details and furnishings are visually stunning.  As others have said: museum quality.  I couldn't recommend this hotel enough to the discerning traveller.

This is such a beautiful hotel from the moment you arrive to lobby to rooms to restaurants to outside terraces.    The room was gorgeous and large---- really nicely appointed and very comfortable.   Checkin was fast, and checkout was ok.   However people at reception are not so welcoming/friendly.    Food is ok--- but not exceptional.   Definitely recommend the hotel--- and i'll alternate between Dwarika's and the Hyatt--- both lovely.

Sumi was our hostess. She was knowledgeable about cuisine, had very genuine and pleasant personality made our lunch very relaxing. The food was exceptional and the quality was maintained over years. Just a wonderful place to relax for business or family.

Beautiful traditional hotel with excellent service. An oasis of calm in the middle of the traffic chaos typical of Kathmandu.Absolutely recommended! Anyone visiting Nepal and Kathmandu should treat themselves to at least 2 days here. The hotel also has several very good restaurants and a dedicated wellness department.

The moment you walk into the open-air garden reception, you know Dwarika's is special! It is such an oasis after a day of exploring in Kathmandu. You disappear inside the property and the dust, traffic, and noise vanish. You literally breathe easier. The whole place smells of honeysuckle and lemongrass. The hotel grounds are gorgeous, with three restaurants, a pool, several shops, and a spa. The spa, by the way, is excellent and reasonably priced. The menu of services is huge, which special massages for travelers who have been trekking. Our room was huge and spotless. It had a large walk-in shower, separate tub, and, a first for us, a walk-in closet. Turn down service included fresh fruits and chocolates. There were plentiful bottles of water provided daily. After a couple exhausting days at temples and in Thamel, we dined at Dwarika's main restaurant, with no complaints. The menu is big, so you can enjoy local cuisine, pasta, sandwiches, burger, salads...along with local beers and wines. The location is not walkable for most people to Thamel or Durbar Square, but taxis are cheap and plentiful. Plus, the hotel is located very close to the airport, which is super convenient.

Best hotel I’ve ever stayed at, and I’ve stayed at a lot of luxury hotels. This one is not only luxurious but has amazing character — something not found in a Ritz, 4 Seasons, etc. True to its Nepal heritage, amazing touches that I can’t even describe here. I was here for a business trip but stayed a day beyond for pleasure, and seriously considered extending further just to spend more time at the hotel. Stay here if in Kathmandu!  You won’t regret it!

We couldn't believe how can a hotel be so beautiful.Dwarikas has preserved the history of ancient wood works and  made hotel as a holy place.Rooms are also on traditional style but needs to be cleaned well.Foods are delicious and the service at the Fusion bar is on topnotch Ashim,Sumit,Niles and the team took care of us  and made our stay memorable.We wanted to have dinner on other restaurants but we were so satisfied by the service and the ambience of the fusion bar.This hotel is just perfect i highly recommend this hotel if you are willing to stay here.

After staying at hyatt regency we got to know about dwarikas we stayed here for 1 night after we checked in we tour the property it was phenomenal we were stunned by the beauty of this place we were too tired.Rooms were very clean and tidy so we relaxed there for a while after that we planned to have the dinner by the poolside bar staffs were welcoming and we experienced the best hospitality we enjoyed the perfect old-fashioned cocktail and had really delicious meal over there service was really amazing and was in top notch.In the morning we had delicious breakfast at torun restaurant i liked the way they settled the buffet staffs were welcoming but something was lacking in their service.

The best place ever we've stayed.we had amazing time here in the dwarikas hotel.We felt like we stayed at the living museum.We had delicious Japanese cuisine and after then we went to the bar we had special cocktails made by bartender Ashim he made everything easy for us we wanted to know about the history of the dwarikas he told us everything how and when it was established we enjoyed a lot there at the bar.2nd day we had nepali course menu it didn't disappointed us although the course was too long service was extraordinary.I highly recommend this hotel if you love the history and next timi we will be visiting dwarikas resort to experience holistic wellness forsure....

Eine der besten Adressen in Kathmandu, sei es für ein Abendessen oder für eine Übernachtung.Der Preis entspricht internationalen Standards, was ungewöhnlich für Nepal ist, jedoch war mir diese tolle Erfahrung der Preis definitiv wert!Die Zimmer sind großzügig bemessen und ausgestattet, inkl. Dusch-Badewannen-Bad. Der Pool darf auch nicht außer Acht gelassen werden. Alles in Allem ein gelungener Hotelaufenthalt.

Dwarika is like a sanctuary in the midst of a very busy city. You immediately feel relaxed in a tranquil, peaceful environment. The hotel staff are incredibly attentive and have an excellent eye for detail. Dwarika has traditional Nepali styling which is sensitive to the local culture. Food from all restaurants was delicious (especially the Krishnapathan!) and very reasonably priced. I would thoroughly recommend a visit to Dwarika and rightly deserves all of the fantastic praise this hotel receives on Trip Advisor!

We stayed at this hotel for 3 nights this place made us feel like we were staying at the traditional village.everything here is perfect theres nothing that needs to be improved.for the whole 3 nights we had dinner at fusion bar we experienced the best service,best cocktails and best foods. Thank you Sumet and charming Bartender Asim they made our stay more worthy and reliable there.We had lunch at the courtyard restaurant it went very good and the service was also in top notch.It's totally different than the other hotel but still the best and it wil be forever ❤️

The best place to get away from the Kathmandu traffic and crowded streets, it is more like a hidden oasis in the city, i booked a Junior Suite and been upgraded to Royal Suite.The experience in general was amazing. The hotel takes you to a world and a unique experience. The suite was larger than I imagined, in addition to the facilities and equipment that were more than I expected.
