Living in such a place makes you tend to just relax and enjoy the atmosphere.I enjoyed a massage, in addition to having dinner at the restaurant overlooking the pool. The hotel staff was very helpful, It will be my first choice on my next visit to the city without hesitation

The truly luxury place and only place in Nepal is Dwarika. If you are a traveler with luxury standards that’s the hotel to book. Beautiful traditional architecture, clean and very well maintained property, different choices of in house restaurants, the Mediterranean, the Japanese , the Nepali. I really liked also the F&B service in the library. The staff very attentive , available and very kind. I really recommend this hotel if you are looking for luxury hospitality

We travelled nepal at the time of mid April and our destination was here to have a lunch. Then after entering dwarikas from the entrance felt like we were into another dimension Architectures and ambience was very astonishing then We had lunch at poolside bar it was an amazing experience having the delicious lunch and tasty cocktails Genius barman Asim briefed us about the dwarikas and we acknowledged religious norms and values about the nepali culture it was too interesting and fascinating.Although it was our short time spending there as promised i will be back with my colleagues and will spend more time over there.

The staff are very attentive and welcoming!  They made my birthday special with a birthday serenade, a blessing, a cake with candles that didn’t blow out, and champagne.  When I returned for an unexpected night after missing a flight, the staff treated me as if I had come back home!The grounds include lots of beautiful wooden carvings that were saved by the owner and beautifully incorporated into the rooms and around the property.  The pool area is a wonderful place to relax.The gift shop is expansive with a variety of objects, books, and clothing.Be sure to request a tour of the property to find out more about its history!

We stayed two nights at the Dwarika and it was excellent. The hotel is beautiful and is a great rest from the busy city. The rooms are beautiful. The breakfast is excellent. We also had dinner twice which was very good. The staff was welcoming. Highly recommended.

Hotel davvero molto bello ed unico nella sua architettura e storia. Sorge vicino al tempio di Pashupatinah, non lontano neppure dall' aeroporto di Kathmandu.Oasi di pace nel caos della città,con una piazza al suo interno su cui si affacciano tutti gli ambienti della struttura tra cui 3 ristoranti,dove il più famoso offre il menù nepalese da 6 o 9 portate abbastanza famoso tra i tour del Nepal.Abbiamo soggiornato 1 notte non potendo sfruttare a pieno le potenzialità della struttura,dalla piscina alla spa. Camera Junior suite immensa e dotata di tutti i comfort. Bagno enorme . Personale molto gentile e disponibile. Colazione discreta, ovviamente precedenza al salato ( con il formaggio di yak difficile altrimenti da trovare in altri hotel in città).Unico neo, la sera per due sandwich c è voluta oltre un ora di attesa, fatto presente in reception si sono scusati ed erano dispiaciuti in modo evidente.Provato anche il ristorante Giapponese che ritengo valido e con prezzi onesti .Se cercate una struttura elegante ma con una forte personalità,l avete trovata.

I had the pleasure of staying both at Dwarika's hotel as well as Dwarika's resort a few days ago. Since I'd never been to Nepal before, I didn't quite know what to expect, but chose Dwarika's almost solely due to proximity to the Pashipathunath Temple, as I knew I wanted to explore that - as well as seeing it was close to the airport. In the photos it looked a bit dated, but it doesn't feel it, it's all kinds of lovely really. To the historic and beautiful decor everywhere, to the spacious rooms and beautiful bathrooms - all made to help us guests be comfortable - this hotel is a gem! You can easily spend a day just inside the resort, marveling at their hand carved doors, ornaments, art, decor and courtyard. Really lovely! Staff couldn't have been nicer, always asking if I needed something or of I was comfortable. I asked the hotel for 2 separate days of sightseeing with a driver and a car and they were safe and attentive to my requests. The food was amazing!! I didn't quite expect good gluten-free food in Kathmandu, but Dwarika's provided a really wonderful, gluten-free truffle pasta, and after discovering that - I had it every night. I loved coming back to the hotel and just luxuriate in the hotel surroundings, either to have a swim, a massage or stay on their daybed having a drink. Kathmandu is quite hectic, so having a quiet oasis to come back to after a long day of sightseeing, feels amazing. What a start to my Nepal trip. They were also very helpful when I decided I needed something from Kathmandu whilst staying at Dhulikhel, (you can read about my crazy request at the review for Dwarika's resort.) Go to Dwarika's Kathmandu, you'll be taken well care of there! Kathmandu has so much to offer, I'd stay quite a few days to explore.

stupendo hotel ,camera superconfortevole , pieni di attenzioni, bellissima la piazza interna che ti isola dalla caotica Kathmandu, ottimo il ristorante con specialità nepalesi prezzi adeguati ai servizi offerti. Da non perdere se siete a Kathmandu..

Dieses Hotel ist eine Oase der Ruhe und Freundlichkeit. Alle durch Höfe verbundenen Gebäude sind aus Backsteinen mit Holzelementen errichtet, die Einrichtung besteht aus antiken Stücken. Jedes Zimmer ist individuell geschmackvoll gestaltet. Wir hatten Zimmer Nr. 301 und Aussicht auf drei Seiten, wundervoll hell. Das Essen ist hervorragend. Bei der Massage wurden zwei Wärmeflaschen unter die flauschige Decke gelegt, damit wir es schön gemütlich im ohnehin gut geheizten Raum haben. Besonders hervorzuheben ist die Freundlichkeit aller Mitarbeiter. So wurden wir vom Kellner beim Abendessen gefragt, wie unser Mountainflight war, den wir morgens gemacht und von dem wir ihm einen Tag zuvor erzählt hatten. Als wir den web-checkin gemacht haben, hatte ich bei der Rezeption ersucht, dass der nightservice jetzt gemacht werden kann. Nur 10 Minuten später sind wir ins Zimmer zurückgekehrt und alles war zur vollsten Zufriedenheit erledigt. Einfach TOP!

10th visit to Kathmandu and our 3rd stay at Dwarika's, in our opinion it is the best hotel in Kathmandu for quality of rooms, food and service. Nothing is too much trouble for the staff who go out of their way to be helpful and are always happy and smiling.  Special mention to the Fusion bar team, Dev, Prashanta, Ram and Rupesh for their excellence service and friendship throughout our stay of 5 days at the beginning of our tour and 2 days at the end.

I had the privilege of staying at this incredible resort. This property is family owned and operated. The family is so welcoming and the property is full of history and historic woodworking pieces. Food is incredible, rooms are exquisite, service and property is beyond belief. An oasis in the middle of Kathmandu.

This restaurant provides an enchanting experience in a luxurious setting. The experience is personalized with your own menu with your name printed on the menu. Even the six course meal is too much for most to eat. However, you can choose up to a 20+ course meal. This is fine authentic Nepalese cuisine. Really special and worth the cost.
離機場十分接近坐的士大約只需要十分鐘左右酒店的大堂非常漂亮豪華房間亦很乾淨但只是有點覺得相片比現實的來得好看

I’ve been traveling all around the world for many years. This hotel is the best I have ever been to. You feel history, it’s an hotel museum where you’ll be amazed in every little detail. It’s so relaxing. The staff is so professional, they understand your needs. You feel like home. THE place to go. A must do once in your life. R.F

This a nice hotel with attentive staff.  There are several restaurant within the hotel itself and also a few shops.  There are a couple of nice store with scarves and some nice jewelry.  The rooms were large and comfortable with a clothes steamer in the bathroom that came in very handy. I enjoyed the courtyard and the beautiful private areas around the pool.

We spent 4 nights at Dwarika’s - 2 separate stays, in a Junior Suite and the Executive Suite.  This is one of the most beautiful and memorable hotels in which we have stayed. The architects and interior designers have taken great care to highlight the architecture, arts, and crafts of Nepal.  I enjoyed exploring all the public spaces and admiring it all.    Kathmandu is a very noisy dusty city and we enjoyed returning to our peaceful oasis every day Our room was very lovely with surprisingly good amenities - big tub and shower, fast internet, cable TV.  We ate 3 dinners at different restaurants. The Krishnarpan is especially worth a special splurge - highlighting the best of Nepal cuisine.  Breakfast was very good with plenty of choices.  Finally, the service was exceptionally warm and attentive.  We highly recommend exploring Dwarikas - even if it is just for a meal or drink.

My mouth just dropped open when I saw this hotel. The restored window frames (everyone different and saved from destruction) were magnificent. The whole aura of the hotel is a testament to the love Dwarika had for his country and the carvings that are so much a part of Nepal’s history. Our room (310) was beautiful - large and spacious with a large bathroom. The toiletries provided were great - especially the small squares of mint soap. The decor is lovely as is the ambiance of the entire hotel. The staff is lovely and couldn’t be more helpful. This was truly a fabulous place to stay and I wouldn’t hesitate to return - we loved it!

This is a wonderful hotel full of history and a priceless collection of wood carvings throughout the hotel.  Anyone visiting  Nepal should read the information provided on the hotel's web page.  It is  fascinating.  Decor and furnishings are magnificent.  Service is impeccable.  A true gem hidden away from the bustle of the surrounding city.

This is truly luxurious accommodation to hide away after the hustle and bustle of Khatmandu.  The rooms are spacious and the interior design reflects the cultural beauty of the country.  Staff are extremely helpful.  The food is top-notch and the nightly entertainment in the courtyard is an added bonus.   The spa is also a welcome facility on site.

Our first visit to Nepal and so Dwarika’s was our very first choice.  From the outside, it looked like a rundown-hotel until one steps inside.  It’s gorgeous inside the premises with all the beautiful lush landscapes surrounding the hotel.  So peaceful and serene.  The room are nice and cozy.  Definitely a place where one can relax.  However, the restaurants are not as good.  We dined at their most expensive restaurant in the premises but were left disappointed.  Food was not cheap but reasonable for foreigners.  The food were bland that we hardly touch our food.  The hotel needs to improve the restaurants in the premises.There are restaurants outside the hotel which are a block or two that is so much more cheaper and food was excellent.  Bajeko Restaurant for dinner is excellent.  One can have a nice meal for $10 only.  Rameshwaran Snacks and Restaurant is an excellent place to have breakfast as well as dinner with $10 for two people.  A must visit instead of spending $23pp at Dwarika’s Toran Restaurant for breakfast or their Krisnarpan Restaurant.  I will review both restaurants in more details separately.

Hotel is stunning! Its architecture, services, rooms, food, everything is perfect. You can’t go wrong with this choice. We loved our stay there, and are very grateful to staff for their services and attitude.

Dwarika's is a calm and soothing oasis amid the dusty congestion of Kathmandu.  As soon as you enter the courtyard, you are transported into a different world of rest, relaxation, and heritage.  The hotel buildings are reproductions of traditional Nepali architecture and woodworking, and surround a lush central courtyard that is cool and scented with incense.  The hotel is packed with antiques and reproduction pieces - the courtyard, lobbies, corridors, and guest rooms, and there is nothing cookie-cutter about this - every vista is unique.  The rooms are wonderfully appointed with abundant furnishings and modern conveniences - an electrical strip on the desk with 5 US/European outlets, hair dryer, clothes steamer, satellite TV and sound system.  Housekeeping is attentive, and brings fruit and cookies every day.  We stayed for 6 nights in an executive suite, which was spacious and well furnished.  There is a full service spa that we did not use, although we did use the spa facilities at Dwarika's Resort outside of the city in Dhulikhel, which is run by the same ownership, and that was great, so I am confident that this is as well.The location is just 5-10 minutes from the airport, so very convenient for transfers, but there is nothing of interest in the immediate surroundings, just congested streets and local business, so you really cannot see anything by walking around the vicinity.  Fortunately, taxis are abundant and inexpensive - about 500 NPR or $5 to go most places, and we took them around town multiple times.  Most people visiting will have a tour or guide, but it is nice to get out and see the local reality by yourself, particularly for shopping.  At the suggestion of guest services, we took a taxi to Bodnath one evening to see the lights and walk around the Stupa with locals, and had a great time.The hotel staff was fantastic, and very helpful about everything - they stored bags while we were travelling elsewhere in Nepal, and if you have any purchases that you can't carry home, they will pack up and ship by DHL.There is a signature traditional Nepal restaurant that serves 6+ course dinner, which was a wonderful cultural experience, but too much food most days. There is an elegant Japanese restaurant that is also quite lovely.  The third venue is more casual, with all day dining both indoors and outside in the courtyard, and that is where we ate the most.  The food is good but not spectacular, but we really enjoyed the wide range of Nepali, Indian, and Continental offerings (sometimes you need french fries), and we were always satisfied.  There is a bar next to the pool, and drinks served anytime in the courtyard, all in an amazing setting.Although this is absolutely a 5 star establishment, it is worth pointing out that expectations are a little different in Nepal than in the US or Europe.  The guest rooms contain a lot of old wood furniture and ornaments, and the floors are terra cotta tile.  Although they are clean and washed every day, you may sense a touch of humidity or dust that you wouldn't find at the Four Seasons.  We absolutely did not take this as a negative - it is the charm of being here, and was a commonality that we found when traveling across Nepal.  The same goes for the food - it is a little simpler but still good, and of course that only applies to there continental presentations for tourists.  The hotel is expensive for local standards, but that comes with the territory.This is a truly wonderful place, and it is THE place to stay when in Kathmandu if you want to experience local charm.  I am told by our local travel agency that the better western hotel chains are also good, but are just not as special, so you should decide what kind of experience you want.  We will absolutely stay here again if we ever make it back (and we really do hope to).

We spent our last night in Nepal at this excellent hotelOur suite (201) was spacious and comfortable with a super king sized bed , writing desk,bathroom with walk in shower and bath and twin wash basins and there was a flat screen tv. Wifi worked well throughout the hotel. The staff are really friendly and helpful, nothing was too much trouble We had breakfast,lunch and dinner, all of which were excellent but the 6 course Nepalese feast (which could be expanded up to 22 courses!) was really special. The drinks are very expensive in comparison to other hotels in Nepal, but at a hotel of this quality it is only to be expectedThe carvings and general decor exhibit crafts from a bygone periodWe were there on the second night of Divali and there were some beautiful pavement decorations made by the staff as well as a free hour long dancing show in the courtyard.This really is a wonderful hotel, perfectly situated for the airport and on a future visit I would not hesitate to return to Dwarikas

I spent four nights here in a junior suite.  Wonderful service.  Excellent food at breakfast and dinner.  Wasn't there for lunch.  Everyone was very attentive to my needs.  The room was large and well kept.  Really liked everything about the place.  Location is near the ghats, a bit far from the square, but you aren't going to be walking anyway.  Always taxis waiting right outside.

We stayed for 5 nights.The Hotel has great charm and its own unique personality.The room was quite good.The staff and service were excellent.We were very pleased with the experience and recommend the hotel.

This hotel is a quiet oasis hidden in downtown Kathmandu. The food is excellent, the decor beautiful, and the staff courteous and friendly. The restoration of antique wood relics from the 13th and 15th centuries are priceless and to be able to view and walk among these items is exceptional. The owner, Mrs. Ambica Shrestha, is gracious and makes you feel as if you are her houseguests. Highly recommend!

... Au centre de Katmandou, cet hôtel musée est très bien isolé, il est un havre de paix confort grand luxe à tous les niveaux... le petit déjeuner est très riche et le restaurant Népalais succulent ; mais, l’hôtel est un peu vieillissant au niveau de l’architecture intérieure et des installations... Par exemple, on dort empêtré dans des draps... Sinon le service est un des plus attentionnés et des plus parfaits que j’ai connu...

Il Dwarika's di Kathmandu non è un albergo dove appoggiarsi una notte in transito verso altre destinazioni in Nepal, ma un heritage hotel dove vale la pena di soggiornare almeno una settimana (e alla fine dei sette giorni la tentazione di prolungare il soggiorno sarà forte). Non sono solo i magnifici edifici storici recuperati con gusto e raffinatezza a incantare, ma soprattutto la cura dei dettagli, la sostenibilità, la pulizia, l'efficienza, la gentilezza, la riservatezza mista a una complicità discreta e mai ostentata - quindi sincera. Si ha la sensazione di vivere in una famiglia al Dwarika's, grazie a un team affiatato e disponibile. Il ristorante nepalese è un'esperienza, ma anche la cucina internazionale è da raccomandare (i piatti italiani sono all'altezza delle migliori offerte nostrane). Il Dwarika's (e tutte le sue proprietà nei paraggi, compresi i bar-ristorante a Garden of Dreams e nel museo di Patan, per non parlare del sontuoso resort zen fuori città che sarà meta di un viaggio futuro) usa prodotti coltivati nei propri campi e riceve settimanalmente forniture di pasta e formaggi dall'Italia. Un grazie particolare alla signora Sheba Rana Shrestha, sales manager, che si è adoperata in ogni modo per riassegnarci una stanza all'alba, dopo che il nostro volo per Pokhara era stato impietosamente cancellato, e ai signori Ram, Pramesh e Madan per la loro affettuosa vicinanza durante tutto il soggiorno (e al personale della spa per i consigli). Raramente un hotel è in grado di offrire un soggiorno così pieno di esotismo, confort e spiritualità al pari del Dwarika's. My heart belongs to you all. A prestissimo!

For my last night in Kathmandu I stayed in this outstanding hotel with spacious and well decorated rooms, a swimmingpool, a wellness and very nice restaurant area and terraces. The hotel is built in typical Newari style and is full of cosy corners to discover. The food is excellent, staff very friendly and tere is nothing negative I can find to tell about my stay. Highly recommand this location.

Sobald man durch den Eingang des Hotels geht fühlt man sich schon in einer Oase inmitten der Stadt. Der Empfang ist sehr freundlich wie der Service während des gesamten Aufenthaltes. Die Zimmer und Bäder sind riesig und sehr schön eingerichtet mit tollen Deko-Gegenständen. Die Gartenanlage inklusive des Pools ist wunderschön und wird top gepflegt. Das Frühstücksbuffet war sehr gut und umfangreich. Es gibt drei Restaurants auf dem Gelände (international, nepalesisch und japanisch), das Essen hat uns sehr gut geschmeckt. Wir können das Hotels uneingeschränkt empfehlen und hätten gerne noch mehr Zeit hier entspannt.

This hotel is outstanding you know when we got the entrance of the hotel the staff is very helpful for all our problems.They really provide us a nice room with balcony and private spa,i like that very much and my wife is very happy staying there ,the cuisine over there is really amazing and the best service i got ever in my life of journey.

I was amazed to see the hospitality scenec buty is unmatched location beautiful non comparable staff is courtious and polite naplese hospitality is great will definately come back nepal. Lake nearby is beautiful coffeeshop is amazing just relax and read a book with a sip of coffee

I am so impressed and pleased by the impeccable and sincere service at Dwarikas. The hotel itself is stunning with lots to explore. But what made the experience exceptional was the staff. From Arjun who made our dinner feel special at the restaurant; the breakfast staff who delighted in explaining the exotic local spread; Sumit who answered my call in the middle of the night and assisted my dad; Shekhar who offered fruits and bottles of water to bring to my dad when he was unwell.I wish I could have stayed longer and met more of the wonderful people who made Dwarika’s feel like home.
こちらにある有名レストランで食事するために訪問しましたが、予約時間まで30分以上あったので敷地内を散策しました。伝統的な様式で建てられた建築物はとても趣がありました。ホテル内は小さな町のような感じで、とても心地良く散策出来ました。またレストラン・クリシュナーパンはとても美味しくてサービスが良く期待通りでした。次回カトマンズに来る時には絶対にこちらに宿泊したいと思いました。
歴史的建造物の中にあるネパール高級料理。味も大変美味しくスタッフのサービスも非常によかったです。結婚記念日に伺ったのですが突然の報告にもかかわらずおもてなしをご用意してくれました。ワインのメニューも豊富でした。大変気持ちよく美味しくいただきました。

Suite accommodation was large/neat/clean. Staff provided excellent service. Multiple restaurants on site. Super breakfast buffet. Evening dress was casual. Hotel was booked through tour company. You won't be disappointed staying here.

There is only one hotel in town that contains the style of old Nepal and this is the one. The ambiance is tranquil. Breakfast buffet shouldn't be missed - especially for the cinnamon yogurt. Daily yoga with the funniest yogi you'll ever meet. A salute from the hotel guard when you enter. It is a refuge in the dusty and crowded city.

Wonderful hotel in very busy and hectic Kathmandu. The rooms are big and beautiful with a great bathroom (open but still a bit private). 3 restaurants with great food and a bar. The staff is incredibly friendly and nice, will definitely stay there again. A sanctuary!

just outside centre, great after busyness of central KathmanduGorgeous building with so much history/ old Nepalise carved woodInspiring story of how got built by Dwarika3 restaurants all good foodswimming poolGorgeous central courtyardLarge luxury suitesservice or international hotel, but good feels and built by Nepalese person great for relax before or after trekking

A little oasis very close to the airport. We stayed here for a total of 4 nights- at the start and end of our holiday. The rooms are excellent, staff very welcoming and the pool is excellent. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay.

We stayed at the hotel on our last night in Kathmandu.  The restaurant was the absolute best (we chose a 6 course menu that was spectacular). The entire hotel covers at least a couple of street blocks and it is filled with trees - the birds sing loudly at dusk - a very joyful experience - a total retreat from the busy Kathmandu streets. But the best part is the service - incomparable to any we've seen before. This hotel is magnificent.  Highly recommended.

Very beautiful sorroundings and the room was very nice and pretty big. We had a great stay (would have got 5 stars if the food also would have been that good) after a trekking in the Himalayas, and the staff were very serviceminded. A very beautiful hotel where you can really expect to be relaxed!

This is an amazing place, so unexpected amongst the chaos of the city.  An old palace rescued from destruction and reinvented as a hotel to represent the best of Nepali culture and history.  It does not appear to be part of any chain or hotel association and is so much the better for it.  Absolutely unique.  The rooms are amazing - huge, beautifully decorated, all different.  The service is outstanding, delicious breakfasts and very good food in the main bar in the evening.  What a great place to start and finish our tour of Nepal.

Dwarika's is an island of calm in the often chaotic environment of Kathmandu.  It is close to the K airport and easy to reach shortly after arrival.  The hotel is built around a large open courtyard with guest rooms in the exterior and restaurants and seating areas in the center.  There are five restaurants, from fine dining to bar food.  The rooms are large and nicely appointed.  The staff is excellent.

Très bon restaurant dans un endroit sublime. Décoration traditionnelle népalaise et newari. il parait que les bâtiments ont été démontés de certains endroits pour être remontés en plein Katmandou. Un must. Je n'ai pas testé l'hôtellerie.

Wir sind als Touristen in Nepal unterwegs.Auf unserer Reise waren wir auch im Dwarika‘s Hotel in Kathmandu.Sehr freundliches Personal, immer hilfsbereit, stets aufmerksam und allzeit ansprechbar. Sehr schöner Innenhof. Frühstück ist absolut ausreichend aber auch nicht der Überflieger. Und so ist es überall im Hotel, alles läuft wie immer, ja wie seit Ewigkeiten .In alles Bereichen sollte einfach mal durchgelüftet werden und mit frischem Wind alles angestaubte erneuert werden, zB auch die Zimmer.

Le lieu est une pure merveille en plein cœur de Katmandou. Des chambres magnifique et un accueil personnalisé. Un charme incommensurable avec un personnel attentif La cuisine n’est pas de reste avec un restaurant gastronomique typiquement népalais. La ballade dans les jardins est un véritable régal

Magnifique hôtel situé au centre de Katmandu. Chambre spacieuse et très bien décorée, avec raffinement. Équipement au top grand restaurant gastronomique  piscine et salle de sport bref tout pour passer un séjour incroyable

Having had the privilege to visit many outstanding hotels in my line of work - it is rare that I find myself truly blown away.  This two Dwarika Hotels in Nepal has re set my expectations and definition of 5 Star Luxury.  These two properties are true destination hotels - they are worth visiting on their own merit, but it is certainly a bonus that they happen to be located in the one of the most exciting destinations in the world.  Having brought numerous groups to this hotel on business incentives - I can vouch for the incredible service, attention to detail and passion of the family behind this extraordinary property group.If you have any space left on your bucket list - I would add a visit to Dwarika's right at the very top.

I visited Dwarika's maybe 18 years ago during a trip to Nepal. I had wonderful memories of this magical place in Kathmandu. My nickname for Dwarika's was the princess palace as I remembered feeling like a peaceful princess in crazy Kathmandu. I returned to Nepal 18 years later with my 14-year-old son. My son delivered school supplies to small village schools outside of Lukla for his 8th-grade project. I decided to splurge while we were staying in Kathmandu and see if Dwarika's was the same place that I remembered!We couldn't have been happier with our decision. From the moment you step into Dwarika's from the crazy, busy, dusty streets of Kathmandu you are taken back. The gardens, birds, beautiful smelling plants and flowers, and the very friendly Nepalese staff take over your senses. Dwarika's is as if you have stepped back in time with modern features. Each room is different, so I can only speak about the two different places we stayed in. Our first room was simple with beautiful architecture, comfortable sheets and bed and quite clean. Our room was tranquil even though we are right off a busy Kathmandu street. Our second room, after trekking and not showering was even better! The room was spacious, with a king bed, day bed, desk, minibar, and a large bathroom. We quickly handed off our dirty laundry and took a long, hot, and much-needed shower. Afterward, we headed down to the pool, relaxed on one of the day beds, I had a margarita, and we pet the local, fat, cute, hotel yellow lab. It is easy to grab a taxi from the front to head out exploring for the day. Afterward, you can return for modern cocktails, wine, and other drinks! We enjoyed all 3 of the restaurants on site but often sat outside in the garden by the pool.You can't miss the handsome, long grey haired manager of the property (Mr.  Praveen). He is kind, soft-spoken, knowledgeable, and will help you out with any problems or concerns. His friendly staff is also available to assist with all of your needs.Dwarika's is one of my favorite properties in the world as it is my style!  I love authentic, local, personal, environmental, unique, special, customer service but understated, not a chain hotel, and friendly. If you like this type of environment, then you will love Dwarika's!! I will not wait 18 years to return. In fact, I am already planning our return!

We stayed here for our last night in Kathmandu after spending a week in Nepal, coincidentally on the day of Shivaratri which meant that the city was absolutely heaving with worshippers. Luckily this place makes you feel as if you are miles from everywhere, with great sound insulation. Our room was very well appointed and comfortable; the staff could not have been more helpful; nice bar and two great restaurants. And evening entertainment from two dancers.Sheer heaven!

This was a great start to our trip in Nepal.  The love and restoration that went into this hotel is amazing -- what a special place to stay in.  And as everyone else said on TA, a great escape from busy Kathmandu.  Also the staff was very lovely.  Lastly, we ate dinner at Krishnarpan (upscale Nepalese) which was a highlight.   The food and service was outstanding.   A must go if in Kathmandu.

This boutique hotel feels like a oasis in the middle of busy Kathmandu.Excellent service, beautiful buildings, attention to details, great food, calm surroundings,... just a little piece of heaven. Pool, gym, yoga studio, spa, library and shops are really nice.

There are not enough superlatives to describe this hotel. The art and architecture and craftsmanship in this hotel makes the hotel a destination in itself. The rooms opening onto the courtyard make you forget you are in a city. Service was absolutely perfect. This trip we stayed in Pullman, ITC and Oberoi properties, the Dwarika’s was the best of an amazing collection. The breakfast buffet was excellent- superb pastries and authentic Nepalese treats(loved the Yak cheese).

The Dwarika's Hotel is absolutely magnificent! The hotel itself is clean, authentic and beautiful. But what makes this hotel even better is the STAFF. Management, please give everyone a raise in pay, they deserve it :-) They made our stay very special and they we're extremely helpful with everything. The restaurants were also very pleasant and the food was delicious. I would love to return to this hotel again.

We booked this hotel based on the reviews on TripAdvisor and we were not disappointed.  In fact our experience exceeded our expectations.  The hotel is lovely and tranquil with a lovely back story.  Staff are as good as any 5 star hotel I’ve been too in London or Dubai.  Food very good; we had a BBQ in the court yard on the Friday and tried a wide range of Nepali food.  I would seriously recommend this hotel to anyone not on a budget and looking for a bit of tranquility amongst the intensity of Kathmandu.

This hotel is truly outstanding and from beginning to end we felt like royalty. Some of our highlights below: 1) Staff: the staff were exceptional - it felt like each member of the team had been briefed personally on what you were up too and any requests that were made. 2) Nepalese cuisine; The on-site local restaurant was scummy! We had the 12-course dinner which was as delicious as it was vast. There were so many cute personal touches to this evening that I won't share as it might spoil it. 3) Architecture: The Hotel masters luxury and cosy - it's like a time capsule and just amazing.4) Location: Only 5 minutes from the airport, which was great for us as we only visited for the weekend. 5) Breakfast: Make sure to go for the breakfast included option as it was scrummy!!6) Bar: The bar had a great selection of cocktails and the usual house spirits as you'd expect and a pool table and football table - go upstairs for the cosy armchairsI could go on and on about this hotel - it's honestly the best place i've ever stayed.

I stayed two nights at Dwarika Kathmandu. This was probably one of the best hotel I had the chance to visit during my stay in Nepal.Mainly because it is such a peaceful placeIn the busy Kathmandu, quiet, and nicely decorated.Try to get information from the hotel about the history behind, it is really interesting. The owners of the place are willing to preserve their heritage by keeping the old wooden windows and they have their own workshop to restore them.They do manufacture their own soaps, shampoo on the spot for their guests.I would strongly suggest you to try one of the two restaurants. I tried the traditional Nepali one and it was a great experience to taste the traditional 9 courses dinner.The breakfast is amazing too! A lot of different pastries (many gluten free)  :))They have also spa facilities with traditional Nepali massages that I did not tested.As far as the room are concerned, the one I stayed in was very spacious and confortable,  none of them are on the street side which make them quiet.The hotel is a little far from Thamel on foot but a cab can drop you there for few rupees.

Gran bel hotel arredato con mobili d'epoca e dettagli nepalesi, ottimi ristoranti, servizio quasi impeccabile considerando gli standard di kathmandu. Consiglio le camere sopra la reception, più accoglienti. Assolutamente raccomandato.

We spent three nights at Dwarika’s and fell in love with it immediately. Such a wonderful building with delightful room so and such friendly staff. The food is also absolutely fantastic with the nice course meal at Krishnarpan - a culinary highlight

Great place to visit,nice atmosphere.amazing spa..beautiful decor.yum yum food...very very net and clean place. My little boy is enjoy very much during his stay,he is really happy,what else more..Thanks awesome team..

Dwarika’s is a real gem. A very well thought out hotel that has real character and soul. The staff are friendly, attentive, and welcoming - they are proud of their hotel and it shows in the service you receive. We stayed for three nights as we explored Kathmandu - it is way from the main tourist area but it is easy and inexpensive to get a taxi to the sights you want to see.

Form the moment we arrived we had the most amazing time. The hotel is so beautiful with its heritage incredibly intricate carvings there’s always something to point/look at. We came in December thinking it could be cold but we barely needed the heating on in our room it was nice and warm. It was a lovely touch adding hot water bottles to the really comfy beds though! The staff were all so friendly and welcoming and the Nepali restaurant was one of the most enjoyable dining experiences I’ve ever had (I’ve been to 47 countries so have had my fair share of hotels and meals!). It’s definitely worth paying that little bit extra! Side note- from the airport expect to pay 550-650 NPR. To Thamel it’s 300NPR. If you need a tour guide I have posted Kumar’s details in a photo - he was so knowledgeable, his English is perfect and he can take you through the city or on treks. He took us on a tour of Durbar square for 1.5 hours and it was a highlight of our trip!

When you experience Kathmandu it is loud, hectic, very dusty and dirty. The Dwarikas is an island of calm, relax, upmarket service and a paradise to enjoy. Many antiques in the public area and the rooms, very friendly and attentive staff, an absolute pleasure to stay there - as is their sister hotel, the Dwarikas Spa.

Traveling for business and this place made us feel relaxed. Construction and design brought us back to the historic of Nepal. Room was great and service was attentive.Unfortunately we can spent time here only 3 nights. This place will be recommended.

The service level is second to none without being intrusive. The rooms are magnificent, using traditional wooden art pieces and furniture of the highest quality throughout. The owners have achieved something that is truly amazing and unique. I've stayed here twice now on a tour of Nepal and cannot recommend it highly enough.

We arrived at Dwarika’s hotel from the hustle and bustle of the streets of Kathmandu.  On entering the hotel through a small wooden door is like entering another world, a world of peace and tranquility, a secret garden where the stress of getting to the hotel just instantly disappears.We were staying for three nights before going further into Nepal on tour.  Our room was wonderful with plenty of space to spread out and overlooking the swimming pool.  Everything was there, bath, shower, twin handbasins and separate toilet in this very large bathroom.  The bedroom had plenty of sitting areas with intricate pieces of wood furniture and decorated in a Nepalese style.  We were sorry to have to leave the hotel when the time came to have to go on tour but we were to return again twice before and after our trip to Bhutan and our eventual journey home.  Again on our return we could not fault the rooms we stayed in.  We were welcomed back as if we were family.  The main restaurant had a good choice on the menu and the service was excellent.  The staff are very helpful and friendly and nothing is too much of a problem.  This is a very unusual hotel not like anything we have stayed in before.  It is like living in the past but with modern amenities.  The garden courtyards have a wonderful array of colourful flowers and small temples burning incense.  It is such a peaceful place that you do not want to leave.Until the next time!

after trekking for days and staying in basic mountain lodges and tents me and my husband treated ourselves for the last night in Kathmandu to spend in this luxury hotel. And it did not disappoint, amazing place with beautiful courtyard and rooms. Breakfast was very good too.

Great base for exploring Kathmandu before or after a trek. Wonderful oasis in very busy, dusty and noisy city. Once you step inside the hotel door it's calm and tranquil. We stayed for two nights before our trek and also one night at the end of the trip before flying out very early in the morning. The staff were so friendly and the food so fresh. Mostly sourced from their own farms the flavours were incredible. We ate in Touran, their international restaurant and also had a very special meal in Krishnarpan – the Nepali restaurant. In Krishnarpan the whole experience was wonderful, very theatrical and full of meaning. The waitresses guided us through the numerous courses and explained about the traditions. All in all a very special evening. The swimming pool in the hotel grounds is refreshing and with loungers and beds makes a great place to while away a couple of hours after a tour around the main sights of Kathmandu.We were lucky enough to be upgraded to a suite on our second visit which was heaven although the original heritage room we had on our first visit was also very beautiful and very comfortable. The hotel takes great pride in their plants and the courtyards are filled with the most wonderful flowers and trees.The original owner worked very hard to preserve the incredible wooden carvings of the Newari people and these have been used to great effect to make this hotel a very special place.

I had three nights of self congratulatory over indulgence in the perfect place after our EBC trek. Dwaricas really is head and shoulders over anything I’ve experienced in this part of the world both in terms of quality and admittedly price.My room, number 25, a junior suite was perfect in e every way and had a regular stream of freebies delivered to my door unprompted. Also ate in the Japanese on site, here the food was beyond anything I have sampled in the last two weeks here. Excellent staff, really attentive, without being oppressive, nothing too much trouble a I would definitely recommend staying here if you in Nepal.

Eine Oase in der quirligen und schmutzigen Stadt! Super Service, gutes Essen! Es gibt sogar italienischen Schinken zum Frühstück! Die Chefin des Hauses ist super nett und wir haben uns gefreut, Sie kennen gelernt zu haben! Gern wieder!

The hotel is a living work of art.  The hotel is very unique.  It’s not just a place to stay but a trip back into Nepalese history and culture.   I highly recommend all the restaurants.   However I dined at the main restaurant the two nights I was there.  This is because the excellent service of Pramesh Devkota.  He works at the main restaurant and provides excellent service with a smile. He is enthusiastic about the menu and Nepalese history.   Pramesh made me feel so welcome and special.  The gym is great and I recommend the 7 am yoga class.  The interior courtyard around the pool is spectacular with flowers and birds singing.

As pretty much all others have said it is an oasis in a chaotic city. The room was beautiful and the whole experience was very relaxing. We also stayed at Dwarika's Resort (same group) an hour's drive up in the hills. If you have one extra night and the time make the effort to stay there. Amazing views.

Dies ist ein mit viel Liebe und Sorgfalt gepflegtes Hotel im nepalesischen Stil, mit vielen verschiedenen Holzschnitzereien und Verzierungen. Jedes Zimmer ist individuell gestaltet, aber immer sehr großzügig und komfortabel. Der Service und das Essen sind ausgezeichnet.

After a 5 day trek in the Nepal countryside, Dwarika’s is a beautiful oasis within hectic Kathmandu.  The grounds are a series of intimate courtyards with lush vegetation and the rooms surround the courtyards like a wall, forming a compound. Once you step inside the hotel, you are transported to a beautiful Nepal.  We dined at Krishnarpan, the Nepali cuisine restaurant within the hotel, and the 6 course traditional dinner was excellent. Our room was spacious and well appointed.  I highly recommend Dwarika’s.

建物、内装、サービス、どれをとっても素晴らしいの一言です。カトマンズには世界遺産がたくさんありますが、こちらのホテルの方が保存状態がいいくらいでネパール様式やその文化をじっくり味わう事ができます。このホテルを作ったドゥワリカ氏に感謝したくなります。アジア圏内のクラシックホテルとしても三本の指に入るのではないでしょうか。ライブラリー、プール、バーもとても素晴らしいものでした。お泊まりになる際は早めのチェックインをおすすめします。レストランも文句なしに素晴らしいです！

One of best stays in over 150 hotels I have stayed in over 60 countries. They have excellent service which world class far superior to European standards. We stayed for 3 nights in executive suite room 311 which is 1350 sq ft. Everything in the room was perfect. Room service and quality of products TOP class. Resturants Toran was outstanding. They made almost anything we asked for. Yuna was so cheerful lady and had over 4 years of international experience in dubai. Uday and many others were so helpful. But never meet anyone like YUNA  outstanding service and cheerful lady. Spa we did three times and you should any of the special oil massages. Parvati , Chiron and nirajan were expectional. Spa is a must.Yoga my Wife attended and teacher was TOP class.ONLY negative would be spa which they say is open 9am to 9pm no one is their till 12’pm which I think management must improve .This is my longest review and I can write so many more things.Only place to stay in Kathmandu is dwarika. Also special thanks to Shailendra from dwarika tours for arranging all our trips. NEVER EXPERI3NCED SUCH GOOD SERVICE.

The hotel is a stark contrast to the hectic Kathmandu.You enter a lush quiet little neighborhood, with carved wooden buildings, everywhere with great care for details. The room was spacious and personally decorated. The bathroom kept lower class but worked ok. We had dinner at the Nepalese resutaurant, where you choose a set menu. Can highly recommend. Medium size was huge, with spicy, very tasty servings, and the Nepalese traditions explained along the way. The breakfast buffet is extensive, with an omelette chef. An annoying detail, however, was that bottled water was not included (but is in the room).There is a surprisingly large gym on the top floor of one of the buildings, well equipped with wooden floors. Treated myself at the spa and got the best massage ever by the therapist Shashi Nakarmi.

Such a calm oasis in the chaos of Kathmandu, a pleasure to enter each time.  We stayed twice in our trip and both suites were gorgeous, so beautifully designed and decorated though the open plan bathrooms only make them suitable for couples really, unless there are some which have different arrangements.  We ate at the three restaurants with slightly mixed results.  A pleasant surprise to find the hotel is only about 10 minutes from the airport (depending on traffic).  Very convenient.

I stay here on business trips and as a single female traveler, have had nothing but a positive experience. The staff is polite, the architecture gorgeous and the hotel smells like a spa through the day. Needless to say, I feel relaxed as soon as I step inside the hotel. The buffet spread is a little limited but healthy, nonetheless. They have a Japanese restaurant. Don’t try sharing the rooms though with a colleague since the bath tub is in the middle of the room and there’s literally no privacy. There’s a separate showering enclosure too, again without a door. The gym while basic is better maintained than most other 5-star hotel gyms in the city. After all the founding owner, Mr Dwarikadas is attributed to creating an awareness around fitness in Kathmandu. The hotel has a beautiful and clean swimming pool. Ideal spot to relax.

We had probelms with payment and I don’t manage to contact you, I wrote you a lot of emails but no answers. Please let me know how I can contact you. I hope you will answer as quick as possible. Thanks

こちらにはランチに伺いました。ホテル内の日本料理でしたが美味しかったです。食後も時間があったので中庭でのんびりしました。プールサイドも素敵でした。中庭、プールサイド、建物の中、色んなところでお茶できます。頻繁に民族衣装を着たホテルの人が 何かご用は？ みたいに歩いていました。外の喧騒は嘘のようなゆったりとしたホテルです。建物はネワール様式で豪華ながらもしっとりしています。ショップもありチトワンで犀を見た後だったので犀の置物を買いました。なかなか良いものが売っていました。カトマンドゥではアメリカのグループホテルに泊まっていたのですが個人的にはこちらの方が好みでしたが客室の使い勝手はわかりません。

We had no idea how amazing this place was until we checked in. It is visited by heads of states, royalty and from the second you leave hectic Katmandu and enter this place you quickly see how amazing this place is. Pristine grounds, amazing rooms, and a staff that is 5 stars. This place is paradise amongst the chaos of Katmandu. We have stayed at many hotels worldwide and this is the overall best experience thus far. Make this your splurge.

This is certainly the most beautiful and best hotel in Kathmandu. Also the most expensive...It is truly an oasis of charm, peacefulness and luxury, in the middle of a chaotic city. Actually with the different buildings, all in traditional styles of brickwork with woodcarvings, and the different gardens/courtyards, it looks like a small village. The lightings at night make it even more beautiful. The swimming pool area is especially charming and relaxing.The rooms are large and very nicely decorated, with extensive use of nepali fabrics.There are three restaurants but we only tried one. Food is good but expensive. And, as the hotel is located outside the city center (quite far from Thamel and Durbar square), it is not easy to really go out for dinner. That is one of the downsides of the Dwarika.Other downside, many rooms overlook the main courtyard; the view is quite pleasant but it can be at times very noisy until late at night and early in the morning; don't expect to sleep late in the morning !For that reason, despite all its true beauty, and the quality of service, which is excellent, I only give a 4 and not a 5 to the Dwarika.

This is how I felt during my stay here at Dwarika’s.. this was no ordinary hotel and therefore I do not think hotel criteria apply. It was not really individual aspect of the stay that be specifically identified-but just to confirm everything was five star..  a stunning spacious bedroom... I loved the bathroom it was just gorgeous and I loved the layout with a stunning marble bath in the middle.. I rarely take baths.. but this one was so inviting.. I ran one immediately. I loved the welcome detail in the room with fresh flowers lots of fresh exotic fruit.. particularly delicious cookies and a game of tiger hunt.. I wish I’d learnt to play.. all the food in the hotel restaurants was very good.. light lunch in the court yard.. fine dining in the evening and very impressive breakfast selection.. So to summarise my stay..I came away just feeling I’d been personally invited to a palace.. it just felt such an honour and a privilege.. the space was exquisite.. all the furniture and artefacts that Dwarika had collected over the years.. you felt the stories attached would be wild tales of adventure and intrigue... every nook and cranny had secrets and mystery..It was utter magic to have stayed here... the only piece missing was the mysterious prince...

Fantastic accommodation, fantastic staff and a really good food. An oasis of tranquility, cleanliness and excellent customer service. We've stayed there for 4 nights and every day was just perfect. Special thanks to the staff, from reception to the pool attendant and cleaning ladies, for their hard work and attention to detail. They provide a truly royal service in this pristine and magical property.

Our room was lovely with king bed, small sitting are and great window views of the court yard.  The staff is gracious and willing to make your stay outstanding.  Good food in the restaurants and great outdoor dining/drink area. Wonderfully quiet at night!

You walk into paradise; plain and simple. The quality of the restoration of this old world charm is exquisite. Don’t expect much from room although nicely appointed with amenities- it’s very simple. All bars and restaurants serve quality food. Try the Sherpa soup called Thukpa- I at  it for dinner every night. Service at a high level

Best hotel in Nepal - authentic arcitecture and food. Nice other guests and great amibience. Rooms are spacy and functional. Gym and yoga could be better and more modern for a five star. But still best place to stay in Nepal.

We booked a junior suite for one night in very short notice but surprisingly got upgraded to executive suite. We were very impressed by the super spacious beautiful room and terrace. Fully equipped with plenty of free drinking water supply, and with small things like wet tissue, hand sanitiser, sunscreen etc. Very considerate. We had dinner in the Continental restaurant outdoor. Delicious food and good wine. Staff are all friendly especially the lady in the restaurant. They offer morning yoga class in a beautiful yoga studio with good view over the garden. After class I stayed behind a while to have my own practice. No one came to bother. Love it! Since our flight depart at 11pm , after late check out we were offered another room to take shower and rest after we enjoyed the pool and spa. I totally agree with other reviews it’s an oasis in the hectic and duty Kathmandu. You won’t hear any noise from the streets outside even though it’s located on a busy road. It’s quite pricey compared to other same class hotels in the area but for the experience I would say worth it.

Stayed couple of nights. Excellent courtyard and architecture. Staff are polite and efficient. Rooms are old fashioned but have modern amenities.The courtyard is a lovely place to hang out.Food is good but wine is too expensive and encourages one to go dry!Do visit House of Treasure a boutique shop in the hotel with helpful Mr Narendra Shreshta bound to offer reasonable prices for good quality world famous Nepali mountain goat Cashmere

Our friendly guide is waiting for us outside the KTM airport and he brings us to this hotel which we would not expect after driving along the dusty streets and passing by those many ruined buildings (as a consequence of the devastating earthquake of 2015). A portal is opened by a security official and we enter a huge, open and green patio surrounded by a fully and lovely reconstructed palace or monastery like brick building full with the typical wooden windows and artwork. It reminds me of the Spanish Paradores Nacionales.We are heartily welcomed, get a refreshing towel and a delightful drink, the property is shown to us and are finally brought to our spacious room with wonderful views over the garden. A real oasis within such a vivid city...Excellent food, an inviting pool area and a special Nepalese restaurant to enjoy a 6 to 12 courses dinner with exquisite local and regional food. All staff members are most friendly and they all really want us to feel at home.Special gratitude goes to our local travel agent, Mr. Prabin Shakya, who really succeeded in making our stay here and our further travels in Nepal and Bhutan most relaxing and unforgettable.

This is one of the best Hotel's I've ever stayed in!  Absolutely worth it!  I've traveled the world and this place is magnificent!  It's good for couples and families.  The grounds are so beautiful.  So many places to sit and enjoy with tea or wine...the rooms are kept perfectly and authentic to the culture.

A wonderful property with extensive and very well maintained gardens and lit pathways to walk around. We enjoyed very much the huge, covered sitting area outside the main entrance with wood and leather armchairs and nice views to the gardens. It was an experience to sit there.

Pros:- Friendly staff- Spacious room- Great Nepalese restaurant in Khrisna- Close to the airport- Spacious and airy gymCons:- Bathroom shower curtain had spots, could have been cleaner- Bathroom smells like moth balls- Breakfast was so so

We went with my parents as a treat. We booked a 9 course meal at about $55 per head. The service was lovely, and the ambiance was nice. We were given our menus and a commemorative brick as a souvenir. The wine list was expensive and long, and would have been good to have had a sommelier explain what would go well with the meal, but our servers were not able to guide us. The meal took about 2 hours from start to finish. I'd been living in Nepal for 2 years and have eaten a lot of excellent Nepali food in good restaurants in the smallest of villages and towns across the country. The dinner here was nothing but average at best, nothing exciting and to be honest overpriced by about $50. The chicken was clearly of the broiler variety, no flavour at all. I've eaten many 'local' chickens in my time and was expecting this, but was sorely disappointed. As a 'dining experience' it was fun and my parents loved it. Would I return? Nope.

I had an unparalleled luxurious stay there. Everything from the staff turning down my bed, to my suite upgrade, to them providing me another room before my late flight (after check out). Thanks for such a wonderful stay! I will be back...

Qu'il est agréable de découvrir un bel hôtel qui ne vous donne pas l'impression d'y avoir déjà séjourné (sentiment fréquent quand on se retrouve dans des hôtels de chaînes, qui bien que très confortables n'échappent pas à une forme de standardisation de l'agencement et de la décoration)!Le Dwarika's est une petite merveille d'architecture: un ensemble de bâtiments principaux harmonieusement répartis autour d'une grande cour, au milieu de laquelle s'élèvement plusieurs bâtiments secondaires de moindre hauteur, scindant la cour en plusieurs courettes et patios. L'édifice est en briquette ocre, sobre et chaleureux, et on est tout de suite frappé par la richesse et la profusion des sculptures que l'on aperçoit sur l'ensemble des éléments en bois (châssis de fenêtres, poutres, portes etc.). L'hôtel a été conçu par un Népalais qui avait visiblement à cœur de promouvoir l'architecture traditionnelle népalaise, et qui a redonné vie à nombre d'éléments récupérés sur des bâtiments en ruine (portes, fenêtres, poutres sculptées, fenêtres linteaux en bois sculptés etc.) qui sans cela auraient été détruits. Les chambres sont spacieuses et confortables (quoiqu'un peu sombres à mon goût), la literie confortable (si on apprécie la fermeté du couchage, ce qui par chance est mon cas). Seul reproche, la plomberie semble un peu vétuste (bondes de lavabo fonctionnant mal, difficulté à trouver le bon réglage de température, bonde de baignoire impossible à ouvrir au moyen du système dont est pourtant équipée la baignoire etc.).Le service est impeccable, le buffet de petit déjeuner tout à fait convenable, le personnel très courtois.Cet hôtel n'est assurément pas le summum de ce que l'on peut trouver dans la catégorie à laquelle il appartient, mais il est en revanche tout à fait unique par son architecture et l'ambiance si particulière qui s'en dégage.

Non credevo ai miei occhi, quando sono entrato al Dwarika's di Kathmandu: un hotel di gran classe, in una città piuttosto disastrata, soprattutto dopo il sisma del 2015.Stanze spaziose, arredate in stile e con gusto, dove tutto è funzionale, ordine e pulizia perfetti. Piscina, ristoranti di gran classe, negozi: non manca nulla, ci si sente a proprio agio, servizio e cortesia adeguati al prezzo.

I had an amazing stay at Dwarika's - made me feel like a prince entering his palace after a long tourist day in the busy city, a real oasis of peace.The buildings are just amazing with these red bricks all over and very nice windows and other wooden ornaments.My room was just incredible... certainly the largest I ever had - huge bathroom, huge bed and bedroom, including a sofa area. a dream !Great staff. providing default-less service.Just PERFECT !

Ein wunderbares Hotel, man versinkt in eine Welt aus 1000&1 Nacht. Rundum stets überzeugender Service. Großzügige Zimmer und exzellentes Essen. Jedesmal wenn ich in Nepal bin ein Muss wenigstens eine Nacht dort zu verbringen.

We loved this hotel.  An oasis of calm from the hustle of Kathmandu streets.  Great historic building tastefully restored and turned into an excellent hotel.  Great staff and great food too!  We had a lovely very large courtyard facing room which was tastefully decorated and equipped with almost everything we could need including large TV with international channels.  Small mini-bar which could perhaps have been better stocked.  We loved both restaurants - the Krishnarpan was fun with personalised menus printed on local paper with our names.  Food and service both excellent. The regular Toran restaurant also served excellent food which we used on the evening we arrived. Staff were all friendly, smiling and professional and the transfer car from the airport was waiting on time and a short maybe 15 minute drive to the hotel.  If you are staying in Kathmandu and you want something with a local, authentic feel but also first class quality then this is for you.

Eines der schönsten Hotels dieser Welt. Wir hatten tolle 6Tage in Kathmandu, das Hotel ist eine Oase! Hotelpersonal absolut spitze, stets sehr freundlich! Sehr gutes Essen, wir haben uns sehr wohl gefühlt1

I loved this place. Not only because it is an Oasis in a very busy place but also because the place is decorated beautifully and authentic to the last corner, even stair cases and floors are a pleasure to be in. The rooms are large and light, clean and also beautifully decorated without being too cluttered. Outside they have beautiful flower arrangements and sitting areas. The restaurants are good but quite expensive. Hotel also has a lift which is amazing as we could take rooms higher up with my mum who had a sore knee. Altogether really recommend this place.

A most luxurious hotel, with lovely rooms and we have found the food to be very good, with very enjoyable Nepalese dishes. The staff are most friendly and helpful. We love the way that the Nepalese cultural heritage is being promoted.

We have stayed for 4 nights in total, and think this must be the best hotel in Kathmandu. The heritage rooms with their sunken baths are beautifully set out. Staff are polite friendly and helpful. Food in main restaurant is OK - we are trying the “ speciality “ restaurant tonight.We have been more than comfortable here and the buildings are a delight.

I had the distinct pleasure of spending two nights at this exceptional hotel while on a medical mission trip/site visit during my first trip to Nepal. The staff is friendly, welcoming and accommodating. We were in two different rooms, one in the main building and one across the courtyard and both were well appointed with divine linens, ample hot water, comfortable mattresses and room darkening window shades. From the moment you arrive, you feel shielded from the traffic, noise, dust and bustle of Kathmandu, which could leave even the most seasoned international traveler feeling a little overwhelmed. It's conveniently located within a 10 (or so) minutes drive to the airport but feels "world's away" from the outside world.The story of the founder's commitment to preserving the beautiful woodwork and historical Newari architecture is well documented but worth mentioning. The overall ambience of the place is magical. Friendly dogs roam the grounds and can be found napping in sunny patches in the courtyard. There are lovely spots to tuck up and enjoy a good book, a cup of tea and friendly conversation. Daily rooftop yoga classes are available each morning along with an abundant breakfast buffet. There's a spa, which I didn't have opportunity to visit, but the homemade shampoo, soap and conditioner are lovely and available for purchase.Dwarika's would rate on the top of my list for luxury accommodations in any of the many places I've traveled around the globe and I look forward to a return visit.

This hotel is very very special.  It is beautiful, the staff is very attentive and they provide you with everything you need or want.  Our room was very large and overlooked a beautiful blue pool with fountain features. We liked their restaurants, food and our time spent in the little Fusion bar.  I highly recommend this hotel.

This is a family run hotel and obviously the building of it has been a labour of love.  The architecture is simple stunning which lots of reclaimed items being used.  It offers an oasis of calm off a busy noisy street.  It also offers a good choice of restaurants including a Nepalese, Japanese and international.  The rooms are spacious and comfortable.  The staff are very friendly, helpful and caring.  Photos really do not do this place justice - it is quite unique and I feel lucky to have had the opportunity to stay there for three nights.

This place is magical.  It has immense character, charming staff, an organic vegetable farm supplying vegetables, and comfortable accommodation.  It has a feeling of uniqueness.  It appears ancient but the owner built this hotel using wonderful reclaimed carved wood pieces; and merged them perfectly.  The bar is wonderful.  You may meet incredible people here.  A world of uncanny coincidences and stories. I loved it!  Yes there are 5 star modern hotels nearby, but this beats the lot for a Khatmandu experience.

Wer sich im Rahmen seines Aufenthaltes in Nepal bzw. Kathmandu etwas besonderes gönnen will, ist in dieser in Anlehnung an die Paläste der Newar-Könige gebauten Hotelanlage mit seiner umfangreichen Sammlung an Artefakten aus dem 13. Jahrhundert richtig. Nach unscheinbarer Vorfahrt erwartet den Gast hinter den Mauern ein wahres Gefühlsbad mit allen erdenklichen Annehmlichkeiten. Aufmerksamer Service wird in diesem einmaligen Ambiente geradezu gelebt. Die ausnahmslos Suiten sind mit antiquarischen Mobiliar mit sehr viel Geschmack eingerichtet, ohne dass man auf den erwarteten Komfort verzichten muss. In mehreren Restaurants (traditionell nepalesisch, japanisch, international) werden selbst anspruchsvolle Gaumen zufrieden gestellt. Von uns getestet das „Krishnarpan” mit einer sechsgängigen Speisenfolge des Landes - eine klare Empfehlung!

We stayed at Dwarika's Hotel for two nights after a long flight and before trekking, and what a great decision that was.  As has been mentioned time and time again in other reviews, Dwarika's is such a peaceful, quiet and beautiful hotel, with unique traditional buildings and spacious surroundings.  We chose this hotel because it was so close to the airport, as well as all the excellent reviews.  It was lovely to be able to relax on a day bed around the pool for hours, being served refreshments and food in the beautiful grounds.  Food was very good.We will stay here again when we go back to Kathmandu, highly recommended!

Mr. Dwarika Das Shrestha (1925-1992) did an amazing job of renovating this luxury hotel just 15 minutes or so from the airport in Katmandu. We had no idea what to expect, but were blown away from the staff greeting at the entrance to our large and well appointed room. Spent a total of four nights there on two visits (interrupted by a quick side trip).

I found this hotel by searching to the internet, by see the rating and the pictures I said to my self that I have to try stay here. First, I got lunch here after city tour then I ask available room for today. Luckily, they have it. Since, we are 3 adults and 1 child I ask the best room for us. Again, they gave their best service to us by giving suite room, yeeah ! Overall, I think Dwarika is the best hotel in Kathmandu.

Traumhaft schönes Hotel mit fast mystisch anmutender Bauart und historischer Fassade. Schon allein wegen des Ambiente wäre das Dwarika's einen Besuch wert. Die Zimmer sind großzügig und liebevoll gestaltet.Der Charme des Hauses spiegelt sich auch in dem hervorragenden Service eines stets freundlichen und zuvorkommenden Personals wider. Die hoteleigenen Restaurants sind ausserdem unbedingt zu empfehlen. Das Essen ist ausgesprochen gut!Das Dwarika's ist perfekte Ort, um nach spannenden Erkundungstouren in Kathmandu zu entspannen. Wir haben unsere Zeit hier sehr genossen und wären am liebsten gleich geblieben!

Had an a amazing stay for new year's eve, specially by being upgraded to their Royal Suite, which was simply breathtaking! The room is spread out on 3 storeys, and everything with it exude luxury. The master bathroom is probably one of the biggest i've ever seen, and who doesn't need 10+ sitting areas?Dinner was a special new year's eve menu with a 5 course meal, and was impeccably prepared and served. Breakfast also had a nice buffet and a la carte selection.Don't be fooled by the dusty facade of the hotel on a busy noisy street, because inside you will find only the best in terms of service, and local heritage,

This is one of the nicest hotels I have ever stayed at. It’s so unique, from its heritage and story, to its design.. I loved everything about it. We had dinner and lunch and the food was amazing.. the spa is also worth a visit. Few 5 star hotels are not chains, this family run establishment is a must!

I have to say that this hotel was my favorite. It provided a visual pleasure and a luxurious element that was beyond expectation. Simply to wander the grounds, admire the architecture, was a treat in and of itself. The spa was tremendous. The scrub massage was the best I've ever had all over the world.The staff was wonderful, there but not overly present. I just loved this hotel. The proximity to the airport made it VERY useful as we tried to do the Everest Flyby  and it took two attempts. I recommend this hotel and the ONLY place to stay in Kathmandu.

Stayed at the hotel on a business visit. It is truly an oasis only a few minutes away from the international airport and off a busy road in the city. The Hotel is built in a traditional Nepalese style and the facilities are excellent. The service was very friendly and accommodating and overall a very positive experience. Keep it up!

This is a lovely hotel and fine quality place.    The owners and staff should be rightly proud of what they have created here.Room was good, service was good, ambiance in hotel grounds was good.   However, I wasn't entirely comfortable.    I felt something was missing.    I couldn't put my finger on it.I found the cost a bit high   ($335/night for a nice big room).    The wi-fi was good and the water was hot and the room clean and neat.    So what's the problem ?I found the 23% ++ service charge and tax a bit irritating.   It would be better to include these up front.     I thought the restaurant food was OK rather than fantastic.

Nice hotel, stayed for 5 nights. A little short of the usual 5 star standard, breakfast is not at par with the prices. Japanese restaurant is good. Room a little noisy from guests in the below restaurant/bar area

It is awesome.  The staff amazing.  Rham at the bar arranged a birthday celebration with every version of Happy Birthday ever recorded. The food is also very good.  The breakfast was a buffet plus you could order a large carte.  In Kathmandu, this is a must stay hotel!

So much of Kathmandu is crowded, unstructured, noisy, and, frankly, not very clean, that we were extraordinarily pleased to find this oasis of a property.  it is beautiful, with gardens, a small temple, exceptional food and restaurants, and a pleasant and friendly staff.  The rooms are large and interestingly decorated, as is the property itself, born from a desire by the owner to save many of the architectural treasures that were being destroyed as Kathmandu and Nepal grew.  One warning:  the air conditioning does not work very well - in one of our rooms, even though the thermostat was at its lowest, the coolest we could get the room was 77 degrees Fahrenheit - and the humidity was quite uncomfortable.  We came back for a day and were in the main building with central air, but it was still uncomfortably warm and humid.  I'm not sure anything can be done, but be aware of the issue.

This is a 5 star property and a place to stay at Katmandu. I travelled a lot and stayed at various 5 star hotels and resorts but found Dwarika Dhulikhel Resort very close to my heart due it willingness to preserve old architectural beauty. Excellent and very cooperative staff especially the chef Pramod. Spacious rooms, well maintained pool. The owners were very friendly and the resort provides excellent massages. The interaction with Ayurvedic Doctor is very interesting and educative to know about your few problems. Strongly recommend for family stay.

Stayed here after a trek and had a wonderful experience. By Nepal standards this idea very expensive hotel but is worth a splurge. Breakfast was included.  Wonderful rooms with ensure and separate bath and shower. On site restaurant is very good.

The hotel itself was really beautiful-both the interior and exterior .The staff were very attentive and friendly.The breakfast was just awesome,different  varieties  and options were available.One afternoon I spent the whole time by the pool side relaxing.It was just beautiful and peaceful.

Man betritt die großzügige Anlage durch ein schmales Tor und findet sich schlagartig in einer Ruheoase, mit perfektem Service und tollem Ambiente wieder. Die Zimmer sind einfach zum Wohlfühlen, ausgestattet mit allem was man sich wünscht. (wir hatten die Junior-Suite) Das Frühstück ist reichhaltig und lässt keine Wünsche übrig. Die Restaurants (wir waren am Pool, im Hauptrestaurant und im traditionellen Restaurant) bieten schmackhafte, frisch zubereitete Speisen zu einem ausgewogenen Preis-/Leistungsverhältnis und eine ansprechende Auswahl an internationalen Weinen. Die Lage in Flughafennähe (10 Minuten) ist ideal für einen kurzen Stop-Over. Wir kommen sicher wieder einmal.

This hotel is a peaceful and really nice place. The building is full of history with beautiful antiques.The stuff is so friendly and helpful. We enjoyed also the Japanese restaurant in Dwarika’s.It was not our last time in this hotel and in Nepal.

Grand entry and first class welcome. Room is huge and well appointed. Great attention to detail craftsmanship. Nice restaurant selection and all are very good. Lovely courtyard system. Glad we stayed here.  Could not have been more pleased.

This hotel has it all - beautiful buildings, very attentive staff, excellent food.  The collection of shops, the restaurant and lounge, the pool - the hotel is gorgeous and only adds to what will be a fantastic adventure in Nepal.  The only drawback is the location, somewhat far from the central shopping and sightseeing areas.  Otherwise, highly recommended!

Öncelikle söylemem gerekirse bu otelde konaklamadık. Sadece öğlen yemeği yiyip, oteli gezdik. Yemek yani momo standart bir tada sahipti,  çorbalar lezzetliydi. Dondurmalı elmalı pay da yemeğe değerdi. Masala çayının bir özelliği yoktu. Otel ise muhteşem görünüyordu. Nepal'in tarihine sahip çıkarcasına bütün antika objeler sade ve kaliteli bir sunumla ve işlevsel olarak sunulmuştu. Her şey inceden inceye konaklayanın güzel vakit geçirmesi için düzenlenmiş. Odalar çok geniş ve her türlü ihtiyaca cevap verir tarzda. Babalarının ölümünden sonra anne ve kızı oteli işletiyormuş, yaptıkları şey saygıya değer doğrusu.

Stunningly beautiful hotel obviously fashioned by the hands of an artist.  The rooms are spacious, beautiful and comfortable.  The service is friendly and on point.  Not a single negative thing to say.  Wish we didn't have to leave today.

Opening the front door to the hotel is literally like an amazing escape from the chaos that is traffic in Kathmandu. You enter the courtyard, which is a little piece of serenity, and all of a sudden the city is far away. The rooms are great, the food is even better, and the staff is amazing. The pictures on the hotel's website don't do it justice - it's much nicer in reality.

Dwarika's is a perfect hotel - spacious room, decorated with the beauty of a living museum, superb restaurants on site - we enjoyed the Nepalese traditional meal in a beautiful restaurant with impeccable service, as well as the superb Asian food, highest quality, warm friendly manager and staff. Perfect hospitality from always friendly, helpful, professional staff. Immaculately clean - just didn't want to leave.

Dwarika's is totally different from any other hotel we stayed at in KTM. An escape from the chaos and a perfect example of how a hotel in Nepal should be run-it gave us an amazing experience of the local culture and hospitality and the facilities, especially the pool, were stunning. The staff were extremely kind and helpful and the attention to detail in the rooms was very appreciated, which included Nepali teas, soaps and board games amongst others. The only thing is that the AC could have worked a little better. Their restaurant Krisnaparn served a delicious Nepali meal with up to 22 courses. We took the 9 course dinner and it was the best meal we had in Nepal hands down, with a personalised menu, rokshi and a gift at the end. Thank you to all at Dwarika's for a wonderful experience!

Es un oasis dentro del caos de la ciudad. El personal es de lo más servicial y agradable, las habitaciones son amplias y muy completas.Es un hotel bastante grande pero no da esa sensación porque te sientes muy bien en todo momento. El spa está genial y el trato como todo el personal ha sido exquisito.Ha sido una muy buena experiencia en general.

Hotel bueno, con muy buenas instalaciones. Los cuartos son grandes comodos asi como el baño que tiene tanto ducha como bañadera. Una pileta ideal para despues de un dia de recorrida por la ciudad. Variedad en masajes ya que ofrecen distintos tipos adapatos para todas las necesidades asi como tambien en cuanto a tiempos de duracion, desde 30 minutos a algunos de 75 o 120 minutos.Tiene 3 restaurantes: uno Japones, otro tipico Nepali (es mas formal en cuanto a como ir vestido), y uno internacional. Un lindo patio que ofrecen tanto para tomar algo a la tarde ya que tienen un bar y sino por la noche para comer. Para epocas de lluvias ofrecen paraguas en cada habitacion y tambien tienen un minibar con cafe, te sin cargo.  En general precio calidad muy bueno!

This is an oasis. Dwarika's commitment to preserving the heritage of Nepal not only is inspired. The rooms are stepped with history. One imagines they are in their very own palace environs. It is hard to leave the room - treat yourself to a suite and the memory will last a lifetime. The service is impressive. Enjoy a traditional Nepali meal - 6 course, 9 courses or if you can.... 22 courses! Six courses will be enough.

I had recently visited this hotel on my Nepal trip & was simply amazed by the ambiance. Beautiful cozy heritage hotel, a real gem in in the tiny city of Kathmandu. Though it is bit expensive being heritage, but worth spending. Personalize service, beautiful courtyard, spacious rooms, decor, nice restaurants, smiling staffs, everything will delight you. Hats off !

Company meeting in a superb quaint setting. A step back in history & in time to another World. Food is delightful and is all organic. Staff are very Proffesional. Rooms a superbly appointed. Highly recommended

having stayed at many hotels in Kathmandu, it was a blessing to stay somewhere, peaceful, and the internet worked (essential for business), and more importantly somewhere not affected by the load shedding ..

Luogo di tranquillità, le hall all'aperto e quelle riparate godono di comode poltrone e di buon servizio.Il ristorante - non abbiamo usufruito dell'hotel- è davvero superlativo.Servizio ottimo, piatti davvero particolari. Menù da 3, 6 o 9 portate.Occorre però dire all'atto della prenotazione quante portate si vogliono e indicare se veg o meno, nonché dare tutti i nominativi dei commensali perché vogliono regalare il menù personalizzato che poi personalizzato non è perché vengono indicati tutti i piatti, ossia nel mio vi erano menzionati anche quelli di carne allorquando poi in concreto mi hanno servito il menù veg. Poco male, è una loro mania. Lo dico solo per chi dovesse prenotare al telefono e impazzire con le domande che pongono.Il vino non è carissimo per essere qui.Da andare!!!!

I stayed 2 nights in Dwarika's and think it's the best hotel in Nepal, everything was perfect and remembrance of great old culture of Nepal, traditional, comfort and lovely. Thanks to very good manager and stuff, Super!

If you can't afford staying there, go experience a typical Nepalese dinner with 18 courses...or just have a beer and enjoy the beautiful garden.This hotel has been built by hand in the pure Newari tradition.

Beautiful boutique type hotel displaying typical architecture of Kathmandu with bricks and wood, heaviliy carved. Still it doesn't miss modern facilities and is well staffed by people who seem to genuinely care about your travel. Location is a bit odd, far from anything so one is mainly confined in after a day of sights.

Despite the recent earthquake, this place retained the classic old world feel of traditional Nepal.
