The design uses plentiful solid wood where you see wood and abundant brass where you see it and shows no obvious damage from the shakeup. The room’s seating area includes a raised padded platform for seating guests. Even the doors to then room greet you with the hand of peace. The large bathroom area is tiled, complete with separate tub and shower, full length mirror in the dressing area. The large room may complicate TV viewing as it is located some distance from the work desk as well as the bed. The hotel property is enormous to the point that you could gift, shop, eat dinner and play pool at the bar in three structures located on the property. Or just sit in the patio area and enjoy the day or evening.

Absolut top, schönstes Hotel von Kathmandu. Eine Insel der Ruhe inmitten einer "verrückten" Stadt. Sehr gutes Essen in tropischer Umgebung, einfach fantastisch. Genau das richtige nach einem anstrengenden Trekking in Nepal.

We were lucky enough to stay at this wonderful hotel which is in Kathmandu. The lobby and grounds are beautiful and exude the uniqueness of Nepalese design. Our room, a suite was huge and beautiful. Much of the furniture and many art pieces are museum like in their beauty and authenticity. The restaurant's food was delicious. The staff was exceptional. A great place to stay in Kathmandu!

O melhor da cidade não significa que seja um hotel cinco estrelas. A área do hotel é rústica mas bonita, tem lojinhas com artigos de qualidade, porém a estrutura está necessitando de reformas e atualizações. Os quartos são amplos mas muito simples inclusive nas roupas de cama, que por duas vezes solicitei troca devido estarem mal cheirosas. Os travesseiros são velhos e causam repulsa. Os funcionários são gentis mas precisei carregar eu mesma a minha bagagem por conta da demora no atendimento.  O restaurante tem padrão médio, com café da manhã apenas regular.

Magnificent boutique hotel!  The staff is extremely warm and welcoming.  The Junior suite was outstanding with full amenities, beautiful view and gorgeous decor.  The gardens, pool area and entire hotel was peaceful and relaxing!  The restaurants, food & service were excellent.  It is a very comfortable oasis, feeling like a home away from home!

Stayed in this hotel for a spring getaway. The hotel is easily accessible to the airport and the cab FROM the airport was 800N rupees. The hotel is huge and nicely appointed. The staff are friendly and very accommodating. They try to remember each and every guest and greet them by name. We stayed in room 309 and it had a nice view of the courtyard. Easy to get to the lobby either by the stairs or the elevator. Both the bed and the sofa were comfortable and very inviting to sleep. The turndown service was nice and they replenished the free water. The coffee press and loose tea was very nice, but troublesome if you are not used to it. For lunch try the Thali, its very delicious and filling. The breakfast was also excellent and gave a variety of local as well as international foods. Try the potato egg cup for breakfast.Taxis - if you want to go to Thamel, it usually cost 400 - 500 N rupee. DO NOT let them charge you 800N rupee even at night. You can either pay for the roundtrip but getting a taxi from Thamel is not difficult since its a big tourist area. This is also where lots of the restaurants are located if you don't want to eat at the hotel. Before boarding a taxi, agree/negotiate on the price or have them use the meter. Tipping - you can tip daily for the room cleaning but there is also a tip box: one for the front staff and a box for every restaurant on the grounds. The tips are usually pooled and divided but I always tip the room attendants separately. Tips are generally not necessary but appreciated.

I stayed here for a few nights. The room is beautiful and it was an oasis. Some of the staff are exceedingly friendly and provided great service. The senior staff at the reception can be more friendlier. The hotel in itself is an oasis and would recommend the hotel. However, I had issues with the sound proofing. I was on the 4th floor but I overhead every single conversation in the courtyard. One night it started raining and I got up because it was making a big noise on the roof. The mini bar is a bit expensive and the taxi pick-up was a bit of a rip-Off for such a short ride with other people. But overall, I would stay here again.

The historical feel and multiple interior courtyards create a really wonderful environment. As many reviewers have mentioned, it is quite nice to have a quiet escape from the noise and dust of Kathmandu.  A water project involving tearing up many streets has created a fairly unpleasant dust problem in the city.  This makes having the escape of Dwarika's even more important.  The hotel's inner courtyards give one the feeling of a small peaceful village.  We had considered staying at the Hyatt, which has more of a modern international hotel look, but are so glad we chose Dwarika's.  We enjoyed every aspect of the hotel -- particularly the environment, decor, and service.  The best food experience at the hotel was the outdoor bar-b-que, which is done every Friday.  So if you are there on a Friday, we would recommend this over other options.  In the evenings the courtyard lighting makes dining outside extra special.

Most relaxing peaceful hotel I've visited. Really enjoyed the architecture, Japanese restaurant, continental restaurant, and fitness center.  Restaurants are very reasonable, seem to be supplemented by the room rate.

Stayed on 3 occasions during our travels and each experience was excellent.  Staff are very helpful and the rooms are a pleasing mix of comfort and history.  Once you enter the front doors it is a different world from the street outside - flowers, birdsong and peace.  Good choice of food for lunch and dinner and great selection for the inclusive breakfast.  The Nepalese restaurant is an experience as a one off, more for the ceremony than the food.

No tengo duda de que si tuviera que volver a Katmandú, intentaría alojarme en este hotel. Pese a que is habitaciones pueden parecer un poco anticuadas, cenar en su patio, sentarse junto a su piscina o disfrutar de su restaurante  compensan con creces. Un oasis con encanto

Es un edificio absolutamente increible, piscinita para refrescarte y quitarte de encima todo ese polvo y polucion que te dejan las calles de la ciudad......habitaciones.....omg omg omg....quinientas veces.....trato fantastico....bar 24 horas....PERO NO TIENEN ACONDICIONADOR PARA EL PELO CHICAS.....solo lo comento ....!!!!solo pase dos noche, en una suit con vistas a la piscina....viendo los monos andar por las paredes del edificio......comiendo momos como loscos....desayuno genial para ser un bufet en un pais como ese....en definitiva solo dos dias que supieron a poco!!!

Amazing hotel, great break from the busy city. Room was huge and had everything needed and more. Loads of areas within the hotel to relax in. The staff had the perfect balance between great service and letting you relax. The bar by the pool was brilliant as was the Nepalese restaurant.

If you are looking to stay like royalty in Kathmandu, this is the best you will get. The rooms are palatial, the amenities are luxurious and the furnishing is plush. The breakfast too is good and the staff goes the extra distance to make you feel welcome. The concierge desk is great. There is outdoor seating for food as well as for business meetings. The hotel's location though is a bit off (not exactly in the middle of a business district). Worth every dollar.

It was my first time that I visited Kathmandu.  I was struggling between Hyatt and Dwarika; but having read all the positive comments in the reviews I have decided on Dwarika.  As many reviewers have said, it's really an oasia admist the very busy, dusty and chaotic Kathmandu.  This heritage hotel is very well mantained and managed.  Rooms are of a good size; the big plus about the room is a huge day bed where one can relax.There is much to pick on about this very well managed hotel where most of the staff is very friendly, accommodating and professional.  I wish they would have more restaurants for those guests, including myself, who dine in the hotel most of the time.  Stayed in the main building in a suite facing the courtyard which is very quite.  There are two new annex buildings in the hotel, I suppose rooms in these annex blocks are small, though I have not visited any of these rooms in the annex blocks.  I have seen the standard heritage room in the main building, even the Deluxe Heritage rooms are of a good size.  These rooms are better value for money as compared to a larger suite.

As I was planning my first trip to Nepal, a friend advised that Dwarika's was the place to stay in Kathmandu. It has a magical, almost mystical feel to it.  I recommend dinner at Krishnarpan.  Kathmandu is exciting, chaotic and exotic.  I would return just for the opportunity to stay at Dwarika's.

Etablissement magnifique !Decor soigné, dans les parties communes et dans les chambres. Etant en couple avec notre fils de 8 ans , nous avons été surclassés dans une Junior Suite: très grande salle de bain wc, douche, baignoire, penderie; chambre avec lit king size, salon, bureau et banquette-lit pour notre fils. La piscine est de taille moyen, un peu feaiche en avril; possibilité de déjeuner près de la piscine. L'hotel didpose d'un SPA, tarif correct, prévoir 4000 roupies pour un massage d'1h. Plusieurs restaurants: népalais, japonais ou international. Le népalais est excellent mais trop copieuxEn conclusion: établissement extraordinaire dans son architecture typiquement népalaise.

Having reclaimed and/or restored vintage woodworks and bricks incorporated into its construction, the hotel exudes an authentic historical charm, all the whilst offering the comfort and luxury of a five-star property. The location is ideal - less than ten minutes drive from the airport (necessitating utmost proximity, given the traffic in Kathmandu). The staff were excellent and the western food was reasonably delicious and not expensive. I would even go so far as to say, the hotel itself was one of my favorite parts of my Nepalese trip.

It was a real pleasure to get back to the hotel after spending a day visiting historic sites.  The amenities are nice. Beware of very slippery slippers which look beautiful but are dangerous to wear: one of our friends fall and damaged her wrist. The food is decent and the rooms are clean.

This is truly an amazing hotel.  The architecture, decor, greenery and staff really make one's stay unforgettable.  We stayed here 7 nights and truly enjoyed coming home to our room after seeing chaotic and strange Kathmandu during the day.  Our only comment and suggestion for improvement is in their all day dining restaurant.  The service could be improved (service staff could be more attentive and bus the tables more often) and the selection of their "international" food items can have more selections.  The Nepalese restaurant is great!!!   I highly recommend it!!

This hotel is an oasis of calm away from a noisy and dusty Kathmandu. The architecture is impressive and incorporates beautiful Nepali carved wood work and other Nepali artefacts.  The rooms are very spacious and beautifully decorated. The bathrooms are luxurious. The staff were very friendly and helpful. Breakfasts were delicious and the weather warm enough to sit outside under the trees. The swimming pool is lovely but was a little chilly!!

Ik kom jaarlijks verschillende malen in nepal en dit is zonder meer het beste hotel zowel qua setting als qua kamers. Een oog voor detail op elk vlak. Deze keer verbleven we in een prachtige juniorsuite. Gezellige bar.  Aangenaam zwembad. Oase van rust.

A friend suggested that I should spend my last night of a frenetic stay in Kathmandu and experience the wonders of this lovely hotel.It may not be perfect but its pretty close. In a dusty and bustling city you are struck by the exceptional architecture and the quiet and refined service of this oasis. As a solo traveller you are often given a dungeon in the basement with little or no view, not at Dwarika's, my room was enormous with all the extras, especially a fantastic view across the courtyard garden and a wonderful relaxing bathroom.Would I recommend the hotel to a friend, without a doubt I loved the place, its atmosphere and its friendly and attentive staff. Many thanks.

...welches wir je gesehen bzw. wo wir gewohnt haben...Eine wunderbare Erfahrung, die alles aber nicht günstig ist. Dieses Hotel muss man erfahren, erleben. Wenn wir wieder einmal in Nepal Kathmandu sein sollten, da gehen wir wieder hin! Top-Service, alles sehr professionell. Verschiedene Restaurants im Hotel. Alles gehobene Preisklasse. Empfehlung!

The restaurant in Dwarika serves a full Nepali dinner at $ 40 per head.  The six course meal of choicest Nepali food, served so well by caring staff.  A fabolous evening of two hours plus spent in the company of friends made it very enjoyable. It is worth spending an evening if you are foodie.

If you really want to experience the Niwari Culture of Nepal, I think this heritage hotel still preserves the best. As soon as you enter inside the compound from a busy traffic road, you completely feel peace and great difference.

typical newari style hotel,very beautiful and clean.all staffs are friendly and kind and smiley. this hotel is near from world heritage site called pasupatinath and boudhanath. airport also very near. very good inviroment. if you are visiting nepal then this place is best place to stay.

This is one of the great hotels. Superb architecture, remarkably quiet considering what is going on outside.  We had a fantastic room. Too many luxuries to list. Continental restaurant is very good with excellent breakfasts. Be wary of the Nepalese restaurant. 6 courses is more than enough and it is not cheap. The staff could not be more helpful and are happy to show you round and tell you the history. Two nights was not enough to do it justice.
部屋の大きさがかなり差があるが、概して広く、バスタブがはめ込み式など凝った内装で興味深い。部屋のコーヒーやお茶も数種類が茶葉で置いてあったり、アメニティもたくさんありおもてなし度は高い。ただ、値段の割に朝食が意外に品数少なく残念。一応オーダーメニューにあるエッグベネディクトはおいしかった。夕食は洋食、ネパール料理共に頂いたが、レベルは高いと思う。飲み物は高級ホテルだけにかなり高額。

We stayed at this hotel for seven nights and found it to be beautiful,peaceful,wonderful service and quite good food(the buffet breakfast was tremendous). The people at the hotel were fantastic and made our stay so memorable. Kathmandu is an extremely busy city and to have found a bit of tranquility in the hub bub was fantastic. They have a beautiful pool, spa,and fantastic areas in which to sit and read or just mediate. It truly was an oasis in which to come back to at the end of the day to unwind. Would stay there,again,without question.

Kathmandu is a surreal place, you're in complete poverty and then you enter this amazing hotel. It feels like you're on another planet. Great architecture and attention to detail. The design of the interior decor is amazing. We had a wonderful welcome. Drinks are expensive but luckily I wasn't paying. Good facilities. Breakfast was good.

When in Kathmandu there aren't many upscale hotels. The choice is limited and I am glad I stayed at Dwarika. The hotel itself is designed in a traditional Nepalese style and is beautiful.  It's well maintained property is also nice and serves as an oasis of peace and tranquillity from bustling Kathmandu. Service was beyond good and an example of it was: When we ordered room service (appetizer, main course and dessert) we were asked if we wanted it served by course! This service is rare for room service. The staff was fantastic with every employee being courteous and professional. Food was wonderful with both local cuisine and western food being of high quality. The best part of the hotel was the room and its huge terrace. From the terrace we saw beautiful temples and relaxed on the lounge chairs. The suite was huge and the best part was that it was not done in a cookie cutter chain hotel style. The furnishings and the art work were impressive. The bathroom was huge with a large tub and large shower area. The amenities were top notch with local hand made soaps. The suite featured a fully stocked bar (that was replenished) as well as  a large selection of daily snacks.The Dwarika is a world class hotel and I look forward to returning.

Just back from this hotel after being in Nepal for a week , all i can say is my whole experience from start to finish was excellent , staff all attentive and friendly , restaurant beautiful food compliment with good wine my room was a generous size perfectly clean and appointed to a high standard the love care and attention the owners have put into this place is amazing and must be experienced ....... if in Kathmandu spend at least one night !

We spent  three nights here - our room was lovely, light, with lots of space and a comfortable bed. We ate at the main restaurant, in the courtyard and the Japanese restaurant. The food was pretty good - lovely fresh produce from the farms and good coffee in the mornings. The bar is the original building is lovely with a fire at night and lots of musical memorabilia around the wall.I did the morning yoga class twice - great yoga master.The hotel organised a driver to take us to the historic area one morning - it was interesting seeing the damage the earthquake caused.Convenient for the airport,

We stayed at this hotel twice, a few days before Tibet and a few days after.  Rooms are spacious and both of ours were quite different.  A very interesting hotel using some architectural elements salvaged from buildings torn down or destroyed.  Desk is helpful and the onsite restaurant is very good.

Benché io sia andata, in più occasioni, diversi anni  fa allo Dwarika Hotel, non lo posso dimenticare ogni volta che penso a Katmandu. Tutto quello che ho potuto leggere nelle recensioni che mi hanno preceduta sono veritiere. L'architettura antica e tradizionale, l'accoglienza, i servizi, le camere, i giardini, la cucina, la piscina, ecc.. sono tutti ai massimi livelli. Potendoselo permettere è un hotel da privilegiare. Vero anche che, uscendo dall'Hotel, appariva in tutta la sua drammaticità la povertà della popolazione.

As soon as you step into this hotel from the hustle bustle of the street it sits on you step into what I term a refined version of Kathmandu, the air seems cleaner and the surroundings have the cleanliness and attention to detail you will struggle to find elsewhere in Kathmandu. When you step into the room, it's easy to see that plenty of attention to detail has gone into absolutely everything equivalent with service. The buffet breakfast has a variety of selection, maybe it missed the flavors of Nepal. Overall we would definitely stay here again the next time we visit Nepal.

Il Dwarika's Hotel è davvero bello,un recupero di architettura tradizionale nepalese di legni intagliati e scolpiti e di mattoni d'argilla rossa. L'interno è notevole, le camere ampie e coloniali, con tutti i confort e arredate con molto buon gusto.Stride il confronto con la povera e confusa accozzaglia di costruzioni che ci si è lasciati alle spalle al di là della porta, presidiata da grandi energumeni in abiti tra il folcloristico ed il tradizionale.La corte interna è un paradiso di vegetazione e armonia, il ristorante notevole. Ottimo sia l'anello brasato, sia la zuppa di cereali e legumi con alcuni profumi che non sono riuscito a distinguere.

Eski bir bina olan tesis tarihi dokuyu bozmadan otel olarak yenilenerek kullanima acilmis.Otelin avlusu ve mimari yapisi kendinizi bir tarihin icinde yolculuk yapmis hissini veriyor.odalar genis ve dokuya uygun olarak dosenmis.kahvalti ve aksam yemekleri basarili.otelin avlusu ve havuz kenari ozellikle aksamlari cok keyifli.genel olarak cok basarili.Farkli bir deneyim yasamak istiyorsaniz kesinlikle burda kalmalisiniz

This hotel is quite beautiful. Wonderfully decorated and furnished with original and replica Newari furniture and fittings. Excellent food, efficient, welcoming and friendly service and a quiet haven just minutes a way from the noise and bustle of the city.

Staying at the Dwarika’s Hotel was an absolute treat! There is no better use for the phrase “Urban Oasis” than to describe the comfort that the hotel provides from the hectically beautiful city just outside its hand carved wooden gates. The food was delicious; the rooms were spectacular, and the ambiance of the courtyard just serene. Never in my life have a seen a staff so dedicated to the craft of service; everyone from the cooks, to the waiters, turndown service, you name it, was extremely accommodating and friendly. In particular, our guide Rabin, showed us the city in an incredible and intimate fashion, taking us through all varieties of places from classic spots like Pashupatinath Temple, to Thamel, and of course Durbar Square, to lesser known streets and restaurants. Overall, I can’t say enough to try and allure people to this amazing hotel. Take my word and hurry to the Dwarika's Hotel in Kathmandu.

Stayed in this wonderful quaint hotel for 4 nights, January 2017.Much of the hotel rebuilt using antique window frames, decorative carved lintels, and other hand carved wooden pieces.  It is a world heritage site and deserves it.Service extraordinary!3 or 4 restaurants on site.I will visit again!!

Dwarikas Hotel is truly and delight to the senses in every way. It is an oasis in the middle of Kathmandu. The hotel is large with beautiful grounds. Reclaimed wood from old Nepali buildings were rescued by the Dwarikas and put to use in building this magnificent hotel. Service is excellent. Mrs. Dwarika makes sure everything is perfect!  Rooms are large and have tile floors. Our room had a large soaking tub. Food in  "Toran" was nicely presented and tasty. For a real treat and extraordinary dining experience have dinner in "Krishnarpan" their Nepali specialty restaurant.

We loved this. Booked directly with the hotel. Birthday treat and the hotel pulled out all the stops with a birthday cake and an upgrade. Staff were all lovely and restaurant choice great. Location is good for the airport and a taxi to town isnt that expensive. Really lovely and highly recommend.

We had three nights here and absolutely loved it. The place is so beautiful and atmospheric, with its gorgeous art, architectural fixtures and lovely gardens. The room was huge and very comfortable, again with lots of great architectural and decorative touches. The food at Dwarika's is also outstanding, especially the incredible six-course Nepalese meal at its speciality restaurant - an excellent meal and experience! The service is also very good - always friendly and efficient. Many thanks!

Just had 3 nights here and loved it, it is a very serene setting after the chaos of the traffic, pollution, sheer noise of what awaits outside the front doors of the hotel. Suites are huge and very comfotable. Bed was very large and firm. On a restaurant comment, all day menu in restaurant, standard,quite bland food,think sandwichs, wraps, fish & chips, chicken tikka masala!!Not really inspiring when in Nepal. Nepalese restaurant good but a lot of food, only went for 6 course menu, Not tasting  menu portions, these are quite big and would fail to see how any could have the 22 courses but there seemed to be a few up for it. The best we enjoyed was the Japanese restaurant where we enjoyed a really nice chicken  Teppanyki. The bar area was nice and the staff were delightful couldn't do enough for you. Very nice hotel would really recommend if you would like to find peace after a hard day touring Nepal

Great place to enjoy on your holidays, business, official, Nepal tour, museum, wood carvings, Nepali, continental, Japanese and all kinds of food and drinks, Day beds at swimming pool, Friday Barbeque.

Die Zimmer sind spitzenklasse. Wo draußen der Verkehr brodelt, kriegt man innen gar nichts davon mit. Die Zimmer liegen in den traumhaft ruhigen Innenhof, in dem man sich wie verwunschen vorkommt. Ein toller Schwimmingpool mit riesigen "Himmelbetten" drum herum lädt zum Relaxen ein. Ein wirklich tolles, gehobenes Hotel, das allen Ansprüchen gerecht wird. Wir kommen wieder nach Nepal und werden das Hotel sicher wieder buchen!!!

War während einer Trekking-Tour in diesem wunderschönen Haus zu Gast und war total begeistert! An manchen Ecken fühlt man sich wie in einem Museum und stöbert munter weiter, während man sich an anderen Ecken so wohl und aufgehoben fühlt, wie in einem romantischen Honeymoon-Urlaub. Toller Pool, welcher ein wenig verwunschen daher kommt, tolle Restaurants, welche wirklich den Gaumen verwöhnen und die Zimmer sind einfach famos!Gerne wieder :)

We spent a few nights at this most wonderful hotel before and after a trek to Annapurna base camp during Christmas a few years back (2013). It was an outstanding hotel in all respects. We had dinner at all of the hotel restaurants. They were all excellent!

Stayed for 1 night at the start of our Everest Base Camp trek and 2 nights on our return. What an amazing way to start and end a holiday. From the lovely greeting on arrival, to the check in process everything was swift and efficient. Rooms were really lovely. Excellent beds and pillows.Breakfast buffet was extensive and very good quality. Had dinner and again food was excellent.If your going to Kathmandu I would highly recommend this hotel. Absolutely amazing.

Beautiful place that has amazing rooms. It calls itself the place where the old wooden ornaments are left and the aesthetics are wonderful. But the sleeping experience isn't that great as rooms don't have proper temperature control.

Das Hotel ist ein traumhafter Rückzugsort in einer doch recht hektischen Stadt.Die Familie Dwarikas hat hier einen Ort geschaffen, der jedem der an der Geschichte und Handwerkskunst der Newari interessiert ist viel zu entdecken gibt.Das Hotel ist sehr geschmackvoll eingerichtet und bietet durch die vielen Innenhöfe, in denen die Vögel allmorgendlich und abendlich für ein Konzert sorgen, immer neue Ausblicke auf die faszinierende Architektur.Das Personal ist angemessen freundlich und hilfsbereit.Die japanische, nepalesische und kontinentale Küche sollten für jeden Geschmack etwas bereit halten.Übrigens Kathmandu, Bhaktapur und Patan sind zwar stark von dem Erdbeben betroffen, aber die vielen intakten, wie auch die beschädigten Sehenswürdigkeiten sind so einzigartig, dass eine Nepalreise jedem zu empfehlen ist.

I had such a wonderful stay here, even though it was for one night, I would have loved to have stayed for longer. I will definitely come back here in the future.I was collected from the airport with no bother at all, it was a very quick 10 minute drive from the airport, which is great when you have been flying all day.The hotel and the grounds were stunning. The hotel room was beautiful and extremely well furnished, it was extremely clean and comfortable. I ate dinner and breakfast at the hotel which was excellent.The staff were extremely friendly and helpful.

A beautiful hotel that feels a world away from the chaos and noise of the city. The whole place is a tribute to the craftsmanship of Nepal's woodcarvers, and the rooms are authentically decorated in tasteful and unassuming style. A variety of restaurants and bars, food is great, although not exactly cheap. Pool is a welcome respite from the heat and dust after a day sightseeing. Service is attentive and the staff are friendly and welcoming. A short taxi ride from Boudhanath, right around the corner from Pashupatinath and only 15 minutes from Tribuvan International airport, so very we'll situated

We stayed here for two nights as everyone we knew recommended this hotel as an experience not to be missed.  It is indeed a wonderful choice, definitely a place to try at least once and certainly for special occasions.  Location wise not centrally however, there's not much around it.  Very close to the airport, and not too far from one of the major sights, the Pashupati Nath temple.  You could walk to shopping and restaurants in Tamel (we did and it took about 40 minutes) but given the pollution and dust it's while interesting, not particularly pleasant.  Much easier to just get cabs which were abundant and safe for no more than $5.About the hotel itself, it's got great architecture with ornate wood carvings and beautiful courtyards. Lots of public space and the free wifi is fast.  Guest rooms are scattered in several buildings on the extensive grounds and all have elevators. We had room 301 in the main building where the front desk is and it's the best room we had on this trip.  It's at one end of the building and spacious with windows on three sides with good view, exquisitely furnished, firm and comfortable oversized king bed, large day bed and desk, style is traditional and exotic.  Huge bathroom with shower and long tub, black tiles. So many trees outside that in the mornings and evenings all you hear is the sound of birds chirping.  This is the kind of room that gives you no incentive to ever go outside.  Wish I could have stayed there for a week but that would have required a much larger budget because the one drawback of this hotel is it's not inexpensive.There are 3 restaurants, Nepali, Japanese and western.  We tried breakfast and dinner at the western one.  Breakfast is buffet (mostly for people who booked rooms with included breakfast which we didn't) but I found the a la carte menu to be preferable with fresh pastries, perfectly cooked eggs and super delicious ham.  And be sure to eat outside in the courtyard under the trees weather permitting, it's so relaxing.  The dinner menu has plenty of choices too and the prices are quite reasonable.Service is good, although you have to be proactive - I found the staff don't volunteer much information but if you have questions they are all there to help.  A note about wall outlets - in our room they came in all shapes, three squares, three rounds, but there were also couple of universal adapters which fit all plugs including the 2 flat American style.

Bellissima struttura in arte newari con personale estremamente gentile. Peccato sia un po troppo distante dal centro. Ho soggiornato con amici in occasione di un viaggio. Dispone di due ottimi ristoranti dove gustare specialità nepalesi. Lo consiglio vivamente.

Dwarika's is a peaceful oasis in the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu. The staff are friendly and made us feel very welcome. The rooms are beautifully in keeping with the Nepalese design. Time spent by the pool enjoying the peace and quiet while drinking ice coffee is the perfect get away from the hot, polluted sights of the city. If you are getting a taxi do not get it from the hotel, walk 2 minutes to the end of the road and hail one down as it will be half the price.

Seldom have I visited a hotel that is so perfect a haven yet at the same time so clearly representative of the pride of the country.This hotel ranks in my mind alongside the great hotels of the world. Not for it's endless facilities (which are wonderful) but for the staff for whom nothing is too much and everything is offered with a smile.And this is not to mention Dwarika's most well known feature - it's priceless architecture and historical significance. I can heartily recommend every restaurant but more than anything please, I entreat you, to take the time to visit Fusion and experience the excellent team there - especially Ram, Sabin and Sumit who could not have made our whole group feel more welcome.Beyond first class...

We stayed two nights in Dwarika's at the end of a walking holiday. It's just a superb place to stay. The highlight is the wonderful wood carving on all the buildings. The cultural heritage of Nepal is on show everywhere at this lovely hotel. The hotel is a bit of a way from the tourist places but we enjoyed walking through Dilli Bazaar to get to the tourist area. You can cope with the walking if you've got this haven of peace to come back to!

The hotel is a great haven after the hassle of the city traffic and it a tribute to nepal's cultural heritage. Rooms are spacious and well appointed and bathrooms are quite spacious. the hotel's furniture is made out of antiques collected over the years and a great deal of thought has gone into the detail. The rooms could do with a modern TV in this day and age and the only snag is that the positioning of the TV does not allow you to watch it comfortably from the bed as the bed poster comes in the middle of the tv.  Minibar could have more soft drinks and juices and I felt there was too much alcohol in the mini bar.  Staff are more extremely friendly and always ready to serve -  nothing is a problem.  Bfast is ok possible not up to five star luxury but in general good.   Food is ok

I have offices in Detroit and Kathmandu so my staff and I make frequent trips for business and sometimes tourism. After the noise and bustle of Kathmandu, there is nothing like the peace and beauty of Dwarikas. The rooms are beautiful and well appointed. The food and drink options are authentic and fairly priced given the level of luxury. Service is always superb. You can choose much lower priced accommodations in the Kathmandu valley but Dwarikas commitment to Nepal's cultural heritage, supporting local Newari artisans, hiring within the community, and a powerful commitment to quality and service make it an easy choice and well worth the premium price.

This hotel is a great place to stay after visiting the sites of the city. The rooms are spacious and luxurious, the bed linen can be chosen from a menu. Large bathrooms help with good quality toiletries. Food is very good in the restaurants and try the Nepalese taster meal in the Nepalese restaurant  . Staff very helpful throughout. We were stuck there for a full morning due to our agents error but it was pleasant sitting by the pool listening to the sounds outside.

I'm a bit torn in this review. While there are so many things I loved about the property and was more than happy to contribute to the economy of Kathmandu, I'm not entirely certain the suite delivers the most value for money. Certainly, in a backpacker city such as KTM, there are plenty of more affordable options, but none would offer this level of quality or luxury. If the rooms were priced 15-20% lower, I would give Dwarika's five stars, no question. For USD400 there are a lot of nice rooms you can stay in the world.  Overall, I would stay here again (mainly for the service, ambiance, and location), but I don't think the price is justified here.

After a nailbiting taxi ride from the airport, only about 15 mins away, Dwarika's is an oasis of calm, luxury and service in contrast to the hubbub of Kathmandu. As soon as you enter you will be welcomed by attentive staff, a cold towel and a refreshing home made chilled fruit drink, and it only gets better. The staff could not be more helpful, making phone calls, hailing taxis and fixing fares. There are 3 restaurants to choose from, didn't get to the Japanese, but the other two are great with the 6 course menu in the traditional Nepalese restaurant a truely memorable feast. Go for 9 course if you dare. Rooms are spacious,well equipped with a bath to soak stiff legs after 2 weeks of trekking and lukewarm showers,

My visit to Nepal (2011) was a trip of a lifetime and my stay at the Dwarika Hotel was worth every penny. It is such a peaceful place to come to after exploring the city. The staff and service were second to none. I hope to return to Nepal and if I do, I would not stay anywhere else. You will not regret staying here.

Best hotel of Kathmandu with so beautiful ambiance. Lots of verities in breakfast with good taste. Nice service so beautiful room with enough space. I would like to stay again there soon. Nice location of hotel. Nice staff with beautiful smile.

I must clear one thing that I didnt stay here or booked any room. We went to this hotel for a small family dinner and coffee. I learnt a lot about this hotel and the way it was built. Whole credit for the hotel's management, decoration, interior, exterior goes to the one and only Lady who has maintained it. It was her father's dream which she completed. Every piece of furniture used in this hotel is gathered from every part of Nepal and are antique in their own way as they got very rare Nepalese wooden carvings on them. Every window , door, in house furniture or utensils are gathered and perfectly decorated within the interior of each building. You will get whole Nepal's architecture at once place.What else I say as everyone did say everything about this hotel but I must say this hotel holds such a big role in conserving Nepal's Heritage.

excelente seleccion de platillos nepalies muy bien atendidos. el menu tiene varios tiempos (aprox 11). es muy romantico y es un hotel fantastico. su ambientacion es imperdible. un oasis entre medio de la ciudad

Stayed here several times from 2010 to 2014.Have travelled quite extensively worldwide and Dwarika's is simply the most beautiful and the best hotel we have ever come across. An absolute oasis in the heart of Kathmandu and richly deserving the many plaudits it receives.

Wonderful hotel with great heritage.  If you're staying in Kathmandu, this is your place.  Incredibly clean with art abound.  Almost like staying withing a museum.  Excellent food but at international prices.  If you're looking for a beef burger (we live in India, so yes, we are always looking), they make a very good burger.

Este hotel es un lujo, y un lujo tiene su precio. Todo es perfecto en este establecimiento, la recepción es muy atractiva, las habitaciones son hermosas, en la nuestra había una ducha y una bañera abiertas, es decir sin puertas, todo muy bien pensado. Preciosamente bien decorado, muchas tallas en madera, la luz de las ventanas llega a todos los rincones de laz habitaciones. Los patios y la piscina son hermosísimos, los trabajos artesanales en madera son impresionantes. Muchas plantas y flores. Aparentemente, esta ha sido una fábrica hasta que fue convertida, los artesanos trabajan en otra parte de este establecimiento.  Todo es atractivo. El restaurante sirve el generoso desayuno bufet. Las comidas, en nuestro caso las cenas, han sido excelentes y la atención más que generosa y profesional. El hotel está en Katmandú, pero se necesita un taxi para ir al centro, por ejemplo Durbar Square.

I stayed  Dwarika's Hotel between 13th of July until 15th of July for 2 nights. It is like a typical Nepalise house and decorated with very traditional accessories that belongs to Nepal. I booked deluxe room and they upgrated me to suit room with same price. What l really liked about the hotel,it is only 10 minutes to the airport,great food,helpful and charming staff.  What l really did not like is that l booked my room by booking.com and l have chosen deluxe room but  they do not have any room which is included breakfast. So l have chosen the cheapest room without breakfast. When l arrived to the hotel,l had to paid for the breakfast. Booking.com or hotel does not give any rooms which price included breakfast. The quest has to pay for the breakfast.  This is very irritating and l really did not like it and. l have been traveling all over the world and l have never seen any hotels which do not have any rooms without breakfast included. I talked to the manager of the hotel and the centilmen told me" this is the mistake by booking.com, they should put an option a room with breakfast as well". I do not know that they will do it but l really did not like that but except that breakfast is really good.The another thing which l did not like it,there was a dead insect in my room when l checked in and l called housekeeping. They cleaned the room,they apologized for that but  It was not big deal that l believe to decide to stay in that hotel.Except the paying money for breakfast,lt is a great hotel. I was felt like that l was staying in a Nepalise house..Do not try SPA,it is really expensive.
加德满都古色古香的德瓦里卡酒店真实还原了15-17世纪的尼泊尔文化，经推荐尝试了尼泊尔正统的6道式晚餐，酒店内低调的奢华与美景，让人沉醉其中。

A friend made the trip arrangements for a small group of us, but neglected to tell us in advance that we would not want to move once we went through the door of the Dwarika's Hotel walled compound. In my dreams, I move there for the rest of my life and enjoy the sublime, intimate setting, the architecture, the food, the delightful staff and the unforgettable smell of the place. Yes, it's on the expensive side, but if you're able to afford one splurge during your travels to Nepal, I recommend that this be the one. I am not familiar with their resort facility, but if they've paid the same attention to detail and effortless, outstanding service, I'm sure it too is quite a treat.

We recently stayed at Dwarika’s at the tail end of our trek to Everest Base Camp. We had been stuck in Lukla airport for days and were elated to finally return to Kathmandu. From the moment we entered Dwarika’s, we knew we had made the right choice of hotel. From the moment we walked into the courtyard, the sounds of the bustling city just outside the hotel walls disappeared. I have no idea how, but it is very quiet inside Dwarika’s even though just outside the chaos of Kathmandu continues at all hours of the night. The grounds are sublimely kept and the staff extremely attentive, professional and courteous. The staff did everything in their power to make us comfortable during our stay, even ordering KFC to be delivered to our room when we arrived. We found the restaurants at Dwarika's to be very diverse (one traditional Nepali, one international and one Japanese) and the spa to be wonderful as well.This was the second luxury hotel we stayed at during our time in Kathmandu. I can assure you that the first hotel came nowhere close to the quality of Dwarika’s. Please do yourself a favor and stay here, I promise you will not regret it!

Um hotel construído com entalhes de madeira antiga extraída de edifícios tradicionais de Kathmandu, ganhou o prêmio Unesco de preservação do patrimônio cultural.Almoçamos no restaurante do hotel, com serviço a la carte, comida natural e muito saborosa. O apartamento é muito grande, tem carrinho de chá e nescafé.  Equipe do hotel muito gentil. Os proprietários têm um projeto de manutenção de campos de desabrigados do terremoto. A massagista é ótima e faz massagens  relaxante, profunda e alogamento. Hotel charmoso e confortável.

Dwarika is a fantastic get away from the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu.  The staff is incredibly professional and attentive and the rooms are beautiful.   I originally stayed one night but had an abysmal stay at a hotel in Thamel.  So I came back here where I'm guaranteed great service.   Everyone should stay here once.

It's a beautiful hotel, the rooms are a piece of art! Very good service and breakfast was okay. There is another branch for this hotel downtown not near the airport, they say view is beautiful..try booking their instead but even if u booked in this branch it's beautiful. Enjoy!

La amabilidad de su personal, la belleza del lugar, la relevancia de la cultura, arte y costumbres de Nepal tratadas con el mas delicado refinamiento. Tanto las habitaciones como sus varios restaurantes, biblioteca, salones y jardines están decorados  enteramente por antigüedades y artesanía Nepali lo que nos permitió conocer mas de su cultura  y herencia.

This a special hotel built by a family who wished to preserve the ancient arts of Nepal.It is crafted in original wood with ancient antiques in the rooms,foyers and common rooms.Friendly staff with a 5 star restaurant and bar this is as good as it gets.

After traveling and hiking through Nepal and Bhutan we wanted to spend the last days of our trip in a relaxing and laid back way. The Dwarika's hotel was the right place to do so. This luxurious hotel offers a nice ambient. The entire  setup is marvelous. Everything is clean, well maintained and quiet. There is no huge garden or park but still there are plenty of plants and trees that make the hotel property worth wander around.The rooms are adequately big and you can either hang out or read in your room or outside on the patio. Our room had a bath tube that was embedded in the floor which was slightly strange. The room was equipped with a piece of a traditional nepalese board game: "Baag Chal" where a Tiger has to catch goats. It was actually fun to play.The breakfast was great with plenty of food options - by far the most we have seen in Nepal. One night we had a several courses dinner of traditional nepalese cuisine which was not impressive at all. The taste was boring. Our package included a massage which was not outstanding but above average. Overall we honestly enjoyed staying at the Dwarika's hotel a lot. It is a truly wonderful and miraculous place.

Pricey but what an experience! There's a lot of history and a bit of magic in this amazing hotel, the architecture alone is worth the price. I had the best Ayurvedic Spa experience ever, with Shoshi, who is from a long line of therapists in her family. The restaurants serve beautiful authentic Nepalese dishes or western food sourced from several organic farms. Their aim is to retain & preserve the handicrafts and architecture of Nepal, and they contribute to Nepalese welfare and society.

Musu musu=smiley, perfect to describe Dwarikas! Walk through the carved wooden door, and leave the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu behind and enter a tranquil courtyard taking you back in time.Maaz welcomes you through the door with impeccable English (he studied in Sheffield!), and Prakesh, Alpha and Buddha will look after you in the bar and restaurants. The traditional Nepalese restaurant run by Pramod is not to be missed and for those wanting a change, the Japanese food is scrummy. All the food is organic and home grown. The family run hotel is built using old bricks and carvings that have been saved from the city preserving tradition and culture. Steeped in history, it's truly magical.

i know about Dawrika hotel from my friends.one year before when they travel Nepal they had great stay at this hotel also knew form side of this hotel through internet.then we are there at Dawrika hotel.if anyone want to go Nepal i always suggest to stay at this hotel.thank you for all your kind and great stay at this hotel..all of you hotel family.

I travel often and stay in many hotels - this is one of the nicest hotels I have ever stayed in. It is definitely on the pricey side, but thankfully I used hotel points to get it at a discounted rate. My room was huge and everything down to the small details was exquisite. In such a busy city, I couldn't have been happier to come back to this hotel which was so quiet and peaceful.

Más allá de la calidad de instalaciones, servicio y comida, se trata de un proyecto que incluye la construcción con restos de edificios históricos, gestión sostenible y acción social. Todos los muebles fabricados in-situ. La dueña del hotel es la Cónsul honoraria de España. Una mujer muy interesante, líder del proyecto con una personalidad arrolladora.

Dwarika's  is a massive  authentic Nepalese compound  with everything--great restaurants, spa, excellent Western style breakfast--the help is unbelievable and friendly--great help for sightseeing and also negotiates taxi fares before the trip, which is a must in Katmandu. Also lets you know what you should negotiate for the return trip.And every taxi driver  knows the Dwairka's as the destination-really a help .-A better more rewarding stay than the Plaza Athenee in Paris

Dwarika's Kathmandu probably The best Hotel I have stayed any where else in the world great rooms beautiful bathroom mixture of amazing Nepalese Furnishings , beautiful little yard & the poll looks impressive with stone crafted running water fountains I would say if you don't have enough time visiting Patan/Bhaktapur go stay at Dwarika's you will fairly see almost what those sites has to offer Magical living museum would love to go again & Stay here .

Zum wiederholten Mal war ich in diesem einmaligen Hotel, eine Oase in Kathmandu. Das mit viel Liebe zum Detail errichtete Hotel spiegelt die Geschichte und Kultur des Landes wider. Großzügige Zimmer, perfekter Service auf westlichem Niveau und eine kulinarisch ausgewogene Küche mit Produkten aus eigenem Anbau runden den Aufenthalt perfekt ab. Ein Ort, an dem man sich wunderbar erholen kann, verbunden mit vielen Besichtigungshighlights in unmittelbarer Nähe.

Que se puede decir de un palacio restaurado al detalle y con mimo exquisito?? Impresionante arquitectura, habitaciones de ensueño, patios maravillosos.... Eso sí, Hotel 5*... Posiblemente el mejor hotel de Katmandu y a por eso, a partir de 200€ la habitación

The very best Hotel in the whole Asia!! Peacefull atmosphere, excellent design & services. For single travellers and for families. A very short distance away from Kathmandu`s airport. Very nice entertainment.

Ho soggiornato in questo hotel solo per una notte e posso davvero dire che è stata un'esperienza indimenticabile.Il servizio superlativo, pulitissimo e super super rilassante, entrati nel bellissimo giardino sembra di essere in paradiso.Raccomandatissimo anche se è l'hotel più caro di KTM ma per quello che offre ne vale proprio la pena.

Dit is een van de beste hotels van Kathmandu. Van bij de aankomst krijg je de volledige attentie (welkomsdrankje, sjaaltje) en begeleiding naar de kamer, waar alle faciliteiten uitgelegd worden.De kamers zijn zeer ruim en traditioneel ingericht, maar met alle comfort. Het ontbijt is ronduit schitterend en het internationale restaurant biedt een ruime keuze aan redelijke prijzen. Het traditioneel Nepalees restaurant (reserveren noodzakelijk) biedt een keuze van menu's bestaande uit Nepalese traditionals die je op de traditionele wijze moet eten. En ook hier is de uiteindelijke rekening redelijk.Het hotel biedt ook een wellness aan.Het hele hotel is tegelijkertijd een soort museum van traditionele Nepalese kunst, voornamelijk van houtsnijwerk. Je vindt het overal, dus een verkenningstocht door de tuinen is een aanrader.

We enjoyed staying at Dwarikas, its distinctive Newari architecture and the charm of its inner gardens make you feel you are really in a far away country full of history and culture. The service is just top notch, the breakfasts are lavish, the swimming pool refreshing after a long day visiting temples and ancient squares. We reccomend staying in this kind of boutique hotels (for Pokhara choice see our other review on Temple Tree) because it gives you a feeling of the place and the culture even when staying indoor. Well done

Cet hôtel est vraiment exceptionnel. Dans un pur style népalais le décor est grandiose. L'accueil est du même ordre . Le restaurant népalais est remarquable et les plats son typiques. Assurément le meilleur hôtel de Katmandou.

There's no question that the beauty of the hotel's grounds and architecture live up to its reputation but it's the service and hotel management that places Dwarika's among the world's elite hotels. The staff couldn't have been more friendly and helpful in ensuring a wonderful stay. In a city as chaotic as Kathmandu, there is nothing quite like retreating back to this oasis after a long day of exploring the region. Thank you to our friends at Dwarika's for making our stay so memorable! We hope to see you all again soon!

What a gorgeous heritage hotel in the middle of Kathmandu! Located at one of the busiest areas of the city... Suddenly you see the wall reading Dwarika's! And you are left guessing...Oh! Is this gonna be what I was thinking in this super busy &crowded area of Kathmandu! The moment you go to the other side of the wall.. It's a different world altogether & u go Wow!!! :)Such amazingly preserved heritage! The hotel has been done over the years in bits & parts! The reception, the rooms, the lobby, the corridors, the pool area, the coffee shop, the restaurant, the library, the gift shop...everything has been done up traditionally! This is the most charming heritage hotel I have stayed at!It's the so eye soothing & lovely! Interiors have been done very tastefully! Each & every artefact has been well chosen & well placed! :) The staff is dressed in Nepalese attire & welcome you traditionally again with a Tibetan sash! :)We had lunch at one of their restaurants called Toran which serves in their courtyard too..which is a peaceful place to eat..with birds chirping & plants swinging! The food was really gud & we did order quite a variety & it was all yummy...from penne pesto to cottage cheese steak to traditional Nepalese Thali to biryani to potato wedges! :)It has a couple of dining options! It has an amazing spa menu which I didn't get a chance to try in a one night visit! But the hotel is definitely worth another visit & am not leaving the spa experience the next time I visit Dwarika's! ;)The junior suite room is beautifully done up too & is very spacious! When you enter...It has dual basins one side with luggage space & almirah's...and on the other side it has a bath, shower & wc!Our room had lovely courtyard views  & had a diwan apart from the bed with a study & beautifully placed artefacts!What a charmer this hotel is! Definitely a thumbs up!

Whilst the location may not be great, it emphasizes the feeling of the hotel being a retreat from the bustle and pollution of Kathmandu.The use of reclaimed materials is brilliant in creating the atmosphere of the hotel and rooms. The staff are very helpful and always did their best for us. The food was of high quality and they were happy to make alterations to the menu. Our stay made the break in our return from Bhutan a real pleasure rather than a necessary delay.

Midst the tragic effects of the earthquake, a visit on the 1st anniversary to present a cheque from my charity to rebuild a secondary school occasioned 3 nights stay at this immaculate place, full of character, respecting local traditions and materials, service consummate, breakfast relaxing and stylish; rooms spectacular, facilities luxurious.Everything that one could wish but totally individual and Nepalese

Wonderful stay at Dwarikas. The staff could not have made it any better. We had our first and last night there. On the last day it was a friends birthday and they went a bought a cake especially for him, making his day really special. Thank you

Ein 5-Sterne Haus aufgebaut aus alten Herrschaftshäusern. Wunderbares museales Dekor, aber trotzdem ein perfektes 5-Sterne-Haus. Grosse schöne Zimmer, aufmerksames Personal.Das Hotel ist sehr gut aber auch recht teuer. Den gleichen Top-Standard bekommt man in Kathmandu auch günstiger, wenn dann auch nicht im Museum. Ist aber eine Nacht allemal Wert.Das Hotel besitzt Top-Restaurants, aber auch diese recht teuer.

We were invited to dinner at this hotel on our last night in Kathmandu and I'm so pleased we got to experience it. It was absolutely beautiful. If you didn't know the area, I think it could easily be missed as it doesn't look like a typical hotel from the outside, but once inside, it's like an oasis away from the noise and the busy streets of Kathmandu. It was absolutely beautiful. The staff were friendly, professional and very attentive, nothing was too much trouble. The food was amazing and I can't recommend this hotel and restaurant enough, definitely worth a visit if you're in the area.

一个不足2米的大门，没有设想的门头，毫不起眼。就在你要感慨我天朝不可比拟的时候，入门，顿时豁然开朗，仿佛穿越。院子里宁静恬淡，听得到野鸽子拍打翅膀和莲花水池流水的声音，高大的杉树枝繁叶茂。高大这座建造于1950年的酒店采用尼泊尔传统红砖的建筑形式，房间内饰也是原汁原味的尼泊尔风格；家具和饰品几乎每件都是古董，自带故事：仿古的葫芦型窗把窗外的景色加上了镜框；洗涤用品是尼泊尔手工植物制作，质量上乘。房间面积奢侈，洗浴、洗手、如厕各自分区，方便使用，但均不设门而用布帘子与居住区分开，浴缸全开放。相对1500-2500的标间价格，个人认为，还是值得的，有条件的话就住上一晚吧！

Don't be fooled by the surrounding city. The Dwarika's is truly an enchanting location tucked away amongst the business of Kathmandu. One of the best decisions we made in Nepal was extending our stay at the Dwarika's. It was such a treat to stay here. It was classy, clean, and the service was fantastic. I have nothing negative to say about this place. I would go back to Nepal just to stay at this hotel.

Hands down this is the best hotel in Kathmandu. It has everything: great rooms, restaurants, pool and atmosphere. You'll notice the antique window and door frames which were originally in the owner's private collection. These are true antiques, lovingly saved and integrated into the hotel. Try the Japanese restaurant for lunch or dinner. The breakfast buffet in the main dining room is magnificent. The only downside is that it is relatively isolated. But with so many amenities, you'll hardly notice and when time comes to check out, it is quite close to the airport.

We spent 3 nights at Dwarika's Kathmandu hotel and could not have been more pleased. The architecture is beautiful - preservation of the historical Nepalese accents with well-maintained structures, and the large rooms very comfortable and beautifully appointed. Very attentive and accommodating staff - excellent. I highly recommend! Make sure to schedule a traditional Nepalese meal at the restaurant (Krishnarpan).

This must surely rank as one of the finest hotels in This part of the world. The service is first rate, the rooms are sensational and the food is equally impressive. A choice of three restaurants and a welcoming bar. Nothing has been left to chance. The creator, whose name bestows this hotel, would be proud of his legacy.

We stayed here one night after a long trek. It was such a treat after the very basic teahouses. The service is impeccable. They offer complimentary breakfast and free yoga from 7-8am. The rooms are amazing and even have huge soaking tubs. It is such an oasis after the crazy hectic streets of Kathmandu.

The location, well that is hard to say.  I was there fore business and was shuttled everywhere.  The city traffic is very distracting so when I arrived at the hotel and walked through the doors I could not believe how different the atmosphere was.  I felt immediately at peace. Everything was simply lovely, the grounds, the rooms, the dining areas and the people and the welcome fruit basket in my room.  Breakfast was delicious...the fresh fruit juices were my favorite.BTW the bathroom was AMAZING!Namaste.

Dwarika's is a great hotel in a very convenient location, with all the modern amenities you'd expect from a high-end luxury hotel; all while maintaining an authentic, traditional feel. All the staff were always friendly and helpful, especially Robinson, who picked me up from the airport, and was kind enough to point out some nearby tourist attractions, as well as helping me with any other inquiries I had. All in all, I had a great time in Nepal, which was greatly amplified by my time at Dwarika's.

Luxury hotel in Nepali style close to the  airport and temples .The founder of the hotel collected beautiful metal objects and carved wood of various Nepalese artists , with each built and decorated the hotel. The rooms are spacious,  equipped with all the amenities including water , fruits ,  coffee .and tea . The courtyard is an amazing  place  to eat,  drink and relax . You can choose between three restaurants , Nepali , Japanese or fusion food , all very good .The staff is one of the best in the world , specially Sujan .Enjoy the spa , the massages, include relaxation and body balance energy .

Dwarika's was my first taste of a high-end hotel after previously spending all my visits at the excellent Red Planet in Thamel (where I again returned after my stay here). Thamel is great, but I do feel it has a shelf-life, especially for short term visits to Kathmandu, when you want somewhere comfortable to relax before and after adventures elsewhere in the country.The location of Dwarika's almost determines this for you. This is a place to enjoy as a hotel, rather than a place to sleep in between full days out and about. Close to the airport, you can't really step out and be straight into Kathmandu, so you're encouraged to stay in the hotel and that definitely isnt a bad thing!I stayed in a Junior suite, which was vast! Lovely low cushion sitting area, wonderful bright windows looking out over the courtyard, huge bed, television and wonderful surround sound music system complete with Nepalese music to set the mood. The bathroom was enormous, dressing room, cloak room etc etc.In the courtyard there is an amazing spa, functional pool and three restaurants, all of which were incredible! I love Nepalese and Tibetan food, and you can get amazing dishes out in Thamel or anywhere for a few dollars, but the western and fine dining element is hard to crack, and Dwarika's do it brilliantly, including the best breakfast buffet I have ever seen (unlimited cheese!).One downside was the prices once you are there are quite steep. My laundry cost me £40, which was obscene, though it did come pressed, folded and wrapped in a lovely Dwarika's paper bag. The food was also quite expensive, particularly dinner.Overall I cannot recommend the hotel enough, it's mountains ahead of anything else in the city and really the only luxury option that can compete with other top hotels that I've been in in other parts of the world, so if you're used to Oberoi or Aman, then this is the answer.

My husband and I visited Kathmandu for a long weekend and a friend recommended the Dwarika's. What a perfect recommendation. The Dwarika's is like it's own little Oasis right in the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu. We were able to do a lot of sightseeing while here and we were both happy return to a tranquil retreat in the evenings. We came during a low tourist season so it felt like we had the place to ourselves. We strolled around the grounds which are BEAUTIFUL and spent every evening getting drinks at the bar by the fireplace. Friday nights the bar does a traditional Nepalese BBQ, and I highly recommend it. The food was delicious and the atmosphere superb. The daily breakfast we received complimentary was the best I've had at any hotel, lots of selection, and  super tasty. We didn't get to try to the on sight Japanese restaurant but we did try the Nepalese on sight restaurant and had a great time experiencing the authenticity of Nepalese dining. The hotel rooms were delightful and smelled amazing! The staff was attentive and kind. We arranged for a driver both days through the hotel concierge and were extremely happy with both drivers. The staff made us feel so welcome, and were always giving us helpful tips and advice on where to go and what to see. Overall we had an amazing weekend due largely in part to the wonderful Dwarika's Hotel and the amazing staff. Highly recommend visiting this hotel and dining at the on sight restaurants even if you don't stay over night.

The entire hotel is like a hidden gem once you enter through the doors.  Beautiful wood carvings, the decor, old and elegant.  Our room was beyond comfortable, we ate at  both restaurants and at the bar and everything was well prepared.  Service was impeccable.

The historic buildings with courtyard, is a very relaxing hotel with spacious rooms and very attentive staff. The main restaurant (serves breakfast, lunch and dinner) is very good. Asian restaurant I could do without.

Dwarikas hotel er gennemført, smukt og elegant. Arkitekturen er historisk og opført med sans for detaljen og med respekt for nepals stolte træskærer-håndværk. Her er hyggeligt, roligt men også lidt kedeligt og stift. Værelserne er smagfuldt indrettede og altsammen er balanceret fint mellem nepals stolte traditioner og moderne komfort. Det er absolut et must see - besøg værd når man er i Kathmandu.

Beautiful traditional nepalese decoration and architecture.Great food and very friendly service. It is definitly the best place to stay in Kathmandu. An oasis in this chaotic city.Thanks for a beautiful stay.

Se trata de un hotel antiguo (Heritage) que mantiene la construccion original. Se encuentra en una zona céntrica y ruidosa de Katmandu pero al ingresar desaparecen los ruidos y uno se encuentra en un lugar diferente, apacible y muy confortable. Respetando la arquitectura original. LAs habitaciones son muy comodas, los restaurantes ofrecen muy buenos y variados platos y el servicio es excelente

hotel in stile coloniale nel cuore di Kathmandu. Ho soggiornato un paio di notti in questo hotel ed e' stata un esperienza davvero affascinante. tutto molto curato , pulitissimo, caratteristico, ricco di atmosfera.

My fourth time at this wonderful architectural hotel in Kathmandu. Near to the airport and everything else that this fascinating city has to offer. Thankfully unharmed in the earthquake earlier this year but sadly the number of visitors are down. I highly recommend you stay here for delightful service, excellent culinary options and wonderful surroundings.

This is almost an 'oasis' to escape to in Kathmandu!  Perfect rooms (huge), in buildings enhanced by collected traditional timber or terracotta artefacts from elsewhere, with potted flowers and mature trees in the extensive courtyard gardens (and consequent delightful birds' chorus), an excellent range of restaurants (don't miss the breakfast yoghurt), and attentive and friendly staff.  The only disappointment was the chilliness of the swimming pool, though perhaps I hoped for too much in November!  You can spend a long time just wandering around the courtyards, absorbing the delightful atmosphere, the peace and quiet, and choosing where next to sit in the sun or shade.

Impeccable rooms, fabulous service, and a building that is practically a vacation spot on its own.  The traditional Nepali architecture is absolutely beautiful, the staff and amenities are great, and the rooms are huge, amazingly designed, and beyond comfortable.  Short cab ride to any spot you'd want to explore in/around Kathmandu.

.. Not to be missed - although admittedly this was before the earthquake. Fascinating wandering around the grounds.  Bedrooms were well appointed & pleasant.  Nice swimming pool area. Restaurants were okay.

When we arrived at Dwarikas hotel we were blown away! It was incredibly unique and beautiful. The website for the hotel when we initially booked was in need of an update (it has since been updated), so I didn't know if the hotel would be too - but no..it was simply perfect and exceeded every expectation!  It was shocking bc when you drive up on the street the outside is quite plain, and it's a very busy hectic area so initially you think 'oh the hotel is here??'. But then you walk in and it's simply stunning! The rooms we had for two different nights (one before and one after our Annapurna trekking) were both very large, clean, and had great attention to detail. The entire hotel grounds were an oasis within the city (similar to what other reviewers said), and provided a place to relax, unwind, and feel like you were getting a luxurious Nepali experience without the chaos of Kathmandu.  The service was top notch, with lots of staff around who were always ready and eager to help. They all spoke English very well and were quick to smile and assist in every way. We ate dinner at the Nepalese traditional restaurant (Krishnarpan)- a 6 course meal - and it was delicious! (So much delicious food!).  The main intercontinental restaurant was also very good, and the breakfast was a perfect selection of Eastern and Western Option. They served very strong coffee which I realize is quite hard to find in Nepal and Bhutan. Overall, a lovely stay and I hope to return again in the very near future.

It was an awesome experience staying in this hotel. I really enjoyed it. Staffs as really friendly and rooms are really clean and comfortable. Food also tastes brilliant. Everyone should definitely keep it in first choice.

This is easily one of the top 5 hotels I've ever stayed in, an oasis of peace and luxury just steps off the dusty, clogged streets of Kathmandu. The rooms are huge and themed with authentic Nepali luxury, yet modern and filled with every hotel perk you could ask for. The restaurants are wonderful. This is the place you MUST stay if you can, it's a great return to civilization after trekking the mountains or working in a relief camp. Be sure to wander around the premises and check out all the historic wood carvings that have been incorporated into the buildings.

My wife and I returned to this hotel by special request to our tour operator before setting off on another trek.As always, this World Heritage Site hotel was a haven of serenity in an otherwise bustling capital. Our very large room was exquisitely furnished, the service was impeccable and we had a delicious meal in the courtyard and a comprehensive buffet breakfast before our early morning departure on trek.This is a delightful and characterful hotel in an unexpected location and we cannot recommend it too highly.

This landmark is a must place to visit when in Katmandu, to discover its unique architecture and Nepali heritage; the staff is exceptional and makes you feel at home. It feels like returning to a soothing retreat after a busy day in the frenzy of the Nepali capital city. I highly recommend it to any visitor to Nepal!

The Dwarika's Hotel is an amazing place like no other in the world.  The focus on Nepali heritage in the hotel architecture and room design makes your stay an adventure in Nepal's past.  The staff are wonderfully friendly and attentive.  Three generations of the family that founded the hotel have made this place into an amazing oasis in the heart of Kathmandu.  Their commitment to Nepal is reflected in their generous support of Nepali villages impacted by the 2015 earthquake through the Dwarika's Foundation.

I could not say enough about how pleased we were to stay at this property. Centrally located in the busy streets of downtown Kathmandu and about 15 minutes away from the airport, the Dwarikas offers the peace and quiet we were looking for amidst a lush and spiritual ambience. The hotel is itself a monument to the Nepalese traditional architecture and design. We suddenly felt peace the minute we walked into the hotel, which was tastefully decorated. Unlike other big hotel chains, the Dwarikas cherishes its Newari tradition which was reflected through representation of wood carved buildings, artifacts and brick-paved courtyards. The hotel staff was polite and helpful. We were pleasantly surprised to get upgraded to a suite overlooking lovely courtyards and gardens. Room decor was filled with antique items and carefully collected. The amenities were very much thought out, with a box of plenty toiletries and adequate towel hooks. The fruit and nut baskets were accompanied with a complimentary bottle of wine to end our memorable BD trip to Nepal. Other highlights worth mentioning were a lovely pool, a spa (Try the Pansha Kosha Himalayan treatment!) and dinner at the Krishnarphan restaurant. Breakfast at its all-day dining restaurant was delicious and has an outdoor seating. However, the gym facilities could use an upgrade; some equipment as one of the treadmills didn't seem to be in operation. All in all, Nepal is such a beautiful country filled with nature, culture and lovely people. I'd encourage anyone who hasn't visited to come and experience, most importantly, support its tourism after the quake whether it be the trekking, soul-searching or simply sightseeing trips with the family. We plan to visit Nepal again early next year, and hopefully, look forward to coming back to this little gem. #visitnepal

After a long hike to Everest base camp and back, I booked a stay at Dwarinka's for some quality rest and relaxation before my long journey home. Lounging by the pool and good drinks from the Fusion bar were just what the doctor ordered.  The peaceful atmosphere was a welcome relief from the hustle and bustle of Thamel and the hectic streets of Kathmandu. Go and visit Rojin and Ram in the bar. They offer great conversation and terrific service!

Pour terminer notre voyage de 3 semaines nous avons séjourné 2 nuits dans un superbe hôtel, le Dwarika's.Un cadre unique et calme loin du tumulte de la rue. Des façades newari, une belle piscine et beaucoup de plantes.Nous avions une très belle et grande chambre très propre.Cet hôtel, même s'il était un peu cher, vaut la peine de s'y arrêter.

Absolut top, traumhaft gemacht und hervorragend renoviert. Essen top und authentisch. Preisniveau doch sehr hoch, aber einige Tage nach einem anstrengenden Trekking hier zu verbringen, lassen alle Schmerzen vergessen. Eine Oase der Ruhe und des Luxus.

A very beautiful and historical hotel, once you enter the hotel the atmosphere is totally changed from whatever condition to a totally, peaceful very beautiful garden. The bar and restaurant is very very good  and the service is excellent.I had coffee and lunch during my visit to Kathmandu recently and it is a real paradise in Kathmandu.

the ambiance of this hotel is very elegenat. Very help ful and friendly staffs and good food... This hotel is like our second home. We visit this very often.. The ancient look of the hotel say a lot about its cultural aspects. rooms are well decorated

It's totally safe and sustained no damage!! The Dwarika's Hotel is uniquely stunning and an experience that should not be missed--it is honestly worth every penny (and anywhere else, this hotel would easily be triple the price). I arrived exactly one week after the earthquake and as I entered the hotel, you would never know that there was any problems, let alone that an earthquake had taken place. Fortunately, this amazing example of Newari architecture withstood the quake and is undamaged. After only one day, almost all of the staff know me by name and have gone out of their way to make my stay wonderful. I sincerely cannot say enough about this magical hotel, it's elegant owner and it's kind and attentive staff. Aside from being a literal oasis in the middle of crazy Kathmandu, the hotel is environmentally sustainable, zero-waste and chemical free. Spend the extra money and stay here--you will always be grateful that you did.

What a beautiful,peaceful place!! Rich in cultural heritage and history. The warm and welcoming staff takes care of all your needs. Lunch in the courtyard is always a delightful experience, and having fresh mint tea brought to you while reading and relaxing in the library is good for the soul. The sumptuous beds--with hot water bottles, if needed!-coax you into restful sleep and sweet dreams. Looking forward to another visit.

C'est avec un goût exquis que le Dwarikas a été aménagé. Chaque détail a été minutieusement choisi et rien n'a été laissé au hasard. Les chambres sont de taille généreuse et le lit peut accueillir au moins 3 personnes! Le confort est en contraste avec la pauvreté de la ville. Le personnel est assez imbu de leur personne et de leur importance. Mais cet hôtel est un ilôt de paix au milieu du chaos de Kathmandou. Bien sûr, avec ce fatal tremblement de terre, c'est très délicat de vanter la beauté et le luxe d'unn tel lieu

We stayed at Dwaika’s in early April, leaving only ten days before the quake.  Our memories may not correspond to current reality.  But we couldn’t stay at a hotel as marvelous as Dwarika’s without proclaiming its excellence on Trip Advisor, even if some things may have changed.Dwarika’s doesn’t seem like a hotel.  It’s more like a small village, with an intricate, quirky layout.  The beauty of the architecture, the salvaged decorations, the shrines and artwork is breathtaking.  Majestic trees and flocks of birds soften the brick construction and create the feeling of being in a forest.Staff and service are extraordinary.  Not only is the staff huge, it’s also as friendly, helpful and professional as any we’ve encountered around the world. Amazingly, Dwaika’s is still family owned and operated.  The widow of Dwarika Das Shrestha, the hotel’s founder, lives in the complex and was visible everyday we were there.  There are even a couple of family dogs roaming the premises.We fervently hope Dwarika’s will soon be back to the way we remember it.

My husband and me did not stay in here, as our return flight was too late, so I choose this hotel for half day settle down and to enjoy a quality hotel. We moved from the garden restaurant to the fusion bar, the atmosphere in here is very warm and considerate especially Ram, Summit, and Namuna. Namuna gave us a little surprise after she learned that was my husband's birthday. I will highly recommend to come to here again as we will only this time to temp stay. We wish you and all your family all are safe and trust your great heart will shine through after this tragic earthquake hurt so much.

This hotel is  built of heritage materials - handmade bricks , carved wood etc and is of lovey design and impeccable taste . We could only get a room on one of the two nights we'd planned to stay , but it was a real treat . Staff are well edcated , speak great English and are happy to help with anythng you need to arrange.Very expensive by local standards, but good value by any western measure. Only regret we couldnt spend longer at the hotel to enjoy the pool and gardens as we were keen to explore the city .Its in walking distance of Pushpatinath world heritage site - though crossing the road to get there is a challenge

Ho soggiornato in questo meraviglioso hotel per due notti, ed è stata una esperienza meravigliosa.L'albergo è in stile tradizionale, e non è eccessivo definirlo "lussuoso".Fascino e charme non mancano ad ogni angolo del meraviglioso giardino - specialmente la sera - come nelle bellissime camere in stile.Si mangia bene, è pulitissimo, e il personale è cortese e pronto ad ogni richiesta, come raramente mi è capitato.Verrebbe da perdersi in questo sogno, e restarci a lungo...Raccomdandatissimo: uno degli alberghi più belli e ricchi di atmosfera in cui sono mai stato.

Das Hotel wurde von einem Architekten gebaut, der den alten Nepalesischen Stil mit Holzschnitzereien erhalten wollte. So wurden über Jahre alte Teile von Abbruchhäusern zusammengetragen und mit neuen nachgeschnitzten Teilen aus eigener Holzschnitzerei  ergänzt. Dadurch wohnt man in einem historisch nachgebautem Gebäude dass wesentlich gepflegter ist als all die Weltkulturerbestädte im Kathmandutal. Wie auch immer es ist hier zumindest im Innenhof nichts mit Taubenkot verkakkt. Wir bekamen zwei wirklich schöne große Erkerzimmer im 4. Stock; dadurch hatten wir auch Ausblick auf die umliegenden Hügel, wenn nicht der Smog den Blick verschleiert hatte. Leider sind die Fenster nur einfach verglast und mit 2 mm breiten Fugen, durch die man das allnächtliche Gurren der Tauben auf der Hotelaussenseite sowie den lauten und schrecklichen Verkehr die ganze Nacht hört. Das Taubengurren ist auch so niederfrequent, so dass Ohropax hier nicht hilft. Unbedingt Zimmer ohne Fenster zu Hotelaussenseite nehmen, wenn man ruhig schlafen möchte.Der Innenhof mir vielen Sitz-, und Liegemöglichkeiten lädt zum Entspannen ein. Das Frühstücksbuffet ist gut bestückt, der  zum Frühstück bestellte Cappuccino sehr gut, der Service nett und zuvorkommend auf vier Sterne Niveau bemüht. Wir durften draussen im Hof frühstücken.Die Getränke und Essen haben europäische Preise.Das "Badewannenwasser" ist olivgrün und lädt nicht gerade zum  entspannten Baden ein. Nehmen Sie lieber eine Dusche. Dann sieht man die Wasserfarbe nicht so und die Kacheln sind wahrscheinlich nicht ohne Grund schwarz.

On our trip to Bhutan we stayed for two nights in the Dwarikas Hotel and enjoyed it very much.
