After a view days traveling through Bhutan, we received an email from the Dwarikas with the information, that I have forgotten an amount of cash in the roomsafe of our room in Dwarikas. I was really surprised, because since than I did not realise, that the money was missing. Luckely we stayed in Dwarikas on our way back home again for one night. The manager of the hotel was very friendly and I get the whole sum back. No cent was missing. We would like to thank the management and the housekeeping for their reliabiliy and honesty.

We only stayed a few days at the beginning and end of a trekking holiday, culminating in reaching Everest Base Camp.Rooms were large and comfortable and the facilities in room were everything you needed. Staff were friendly and helpful, food choice was extensive and quality was great, also several restaurants to choose from, would happily stay here again!

Tipico albergo in stile coloniale nella città di Kathmandu, sembra di stare in una foresta pluviale con vegetazione che sembra presente all'interno delle stanze. Non molto vicino al centro ma comunque ben collegato. Più di un ristorante in Albergo ed in particolare uno dove ho avuto modo di mangiare tipica cucina Nepalese seduto quasi per terra e scalzo come vuole l'usanza. Personale attento ai bisogni degli ospiti. Stanza grande e pulita arredata con mobili in stile coloniale. Ricezione canali TV non adeguata.

We did not stay overnight at Dwarikas, as it is very expensive, but we were sent here to kill time between our flight from Pokhara and our homeward flight to the US via Dubai. Everyone was very friendly and we sat by the pool, had a shower, and ate dinner there. It looks as though lots of people do this, as long as you have a meal there no one seems to mind (and they will watch your luggage). Definitely an oasis in the middle of Kathmandu, and it's very close to the airport.

Clima e scenografia tipica del Nepal.Servizi eccezionali, stanze spaziose arredate alla perfezione in stile locale.Dislocazione rispetto al centro cittadino di Latmandu non delle migliori, ma patio, ristorante e launge di gran lunga tra i migliori mai visti. Merita piu' stelle.

Es un hotel muy hermoso, comodas y amplias habitaciones con muchas facilidades ,limpio nuestra habitacion muy silenciosa.la comida del hotel muy variada respecto al desayuno bufet con mucha comida occidental ausente de picante. El spa con unos masajes variados y muy bien hecho recomiendo el de los cuencos tibetanos por ser muy diferente a todos los q me  he realizado.la ubicacion es central facil para desplazarse.el personal siempre dispuesto a complacerte me gusto mucho

Precioso hotel museo en Khatmandu, personal muy amable y servicial.Miramos las almohadas y las hicimos canviar ya que solo estaban limpias por fuera.Por lo demas todo muy bien salvo que unos precios excesivos por la calidad de la comida y las bebidas.

Siamo stati in questo albergo solo per la cena caratteristica nepalese. Una bellissima cena di sei portare con cibi caratteristici locali. Per noi solo belli. Dopo cena abbiamo visitato le parti comuni dell'albergo che sono veramente un'opera d'arte con splendidi arredamenti. Se avremo l'occasione di tornare a Kathmandu soggiorneremo in questo splendido albergo.

We had beautiful fond memories in dwarika's hotel...staff are friendly, great food and feels like only last week but that was almost 6 years ago and still is one of my favourite place i've been to...up to now!!! i am looking forward to be back there again next month.

Dwarika's Hotel is an oasis of calm not far from the airport and centre of Kathmandu.  All the staff were so friendly and hospitable. Here for a conference, with many nationalities attending. 31 people enjoyed a 9-course Nepali meal in the restaurant on the night of 26 Jan. We had such a great time, with our guests enjoying a sing-along towards the end of our meal - apologies to the guests on the other side of the restaurant for the noise!!  The bedrooms were lovely, beds very comfortable.  The staff in Fusion were a great help in choosing great local food and drink.  Thanks too to the guys who arranged our early morning flight around the Mountains & the sightseeing tour afterwards. I hope I have the chance to visit again in the future

確かに伝統的でクラシックなホテルでした。部屋はJr.スイート。窓からは中庭が望め、バスタブの他にシャワーブース、トイレ別、ダブルシンク。キングサイズのベットの寝心地はよく、お湯の出もいいし、トイレの流れもいい。停電もなく、ハーブティーや紅茶類もそろっていました。水とウエルカムフルーツあり。アメニティーはシャンプー、ソープはあるがコンディショナーは無し。これはネパール中どこのホテルにもなかったです。主人が体調を崩して部屋で休んでいたせいか、ターンダウンやチョコなどのサービスには来ませんでした。日本では普通と思われるこれだけの快適性をネパールで受けることが大変だと言うのは理解できるので星5つつけましたが、それほど感動的ではありませんでした。1泊6万ちょっと。朝食込みときいていたのに、含まれていないと押し問答を繰り返し、結局仲介業者にクレームしてくれ、とのことで払ってきました。レストランは夕食はネパールの伝統的な料理をクリシュナルパンでフルコース。スローフードの自然食で、雰囲気は抜群ですが、味は又行きたいとは思わないレベル。私の舌が数々の調味料等に毒されてしまっている可能性はありますが、印象としては素材の味を大事にした素朴な味。朝食はビュッフェ。ネパールでは頑張っている部類だと思いますが、世界的ランキングから言えば、雰囲気も考慮してかろうじて上の下くらいの部類。口コミ評価が高かったので、ぜひ一度は留まりたい、と思ったが、もう気は済んだので、次はドゥワリカスリゾートかな。

Dwarika's is a welcome sanctuary within the somewhat chaotic Kathmandu.  The staff were lovely; the food fantastic (Mako's Japanese restaurant especially delicious); the rooms beautiful; and the atmosphere just outstanding.  Architecturally and aesthetically, the place is stunning.  I recommend Dwarika's highly.

Das Hotel liegt trotz zentraler Lage sehr ruhig. In der Näheren Umgebung  gibt es sehr viele Sehenswürdigkeiten. Wir hatte ein riesiges Doppelzimmer für 4 Nächte durch unseren Trekking Guide Thapaliya Bashudev gebucht und waren überwältigt wie schön das mitten in Kathmandu sein kann.Das Personal ist sehr freundlich, hilfsbereit aber nicht aufdringlich. Das Preis- Leistungsverhältnis ist super. Können wir nur weiterempfehlen.34

“De grands moments de plaisir”5 5 étoiles Avis publié: hier NOUVEAULe Dwarika est un vrai bonheur! Les bâtiments de construction moderne sont entièrement parés des très anciennes boiseries de culture Newar récupérées au cours de années par les propriétaires successifs, y compris la déco des chambres. C'est un havre de paix dans l'animation de Khatmandou. Les 2 restaurants sont excellents et le personnel y est très accueillant et professionnel.Nous avons passé d'abord 4 nuits en 2009 puis 8 en 2010 et, à moins que cela ait beaucoup changé depuis (j'en doute!) c'est le meilleur hôtel de la ville, si vous êtes attachés aux hôtels de charme et non aux hôtels internationaux sans aucune personnalité.Quant à, la propreté, c'était parfait; seul petit inconvénient en 2010, des coupures de courant parfois mais l'hôtel dispose de groupes électrogènes pour assurer l'essentiel pendant les coupures...dont il n'est pas responsable!

La struttura di questo albergo e' di per se un'opera d'arte a cui si aggiunge il gusto di un arredamento sobrio,elegante e decisamente nepalese.La junior suite e' di fatto grande come un appartamento, comoda,luminosa e molto silenziosa. La struttura vanta un bel patio, curato nei particolari, piscina, palestra e diversi ristoranti,cucina newari,internazionale e giapponese, con una buona scelta di piatti vegetariani.La colazione ,inclusa nel prezzo della camera ,e' al buffet, abbondante e varia.Il personale e' molto accogliente,premuroso e discreto. Vi potranno anche aiutare ad organizzare trekking con la loro agenzia di fiducia!Un'oasi nel caos di Kathmandu che vale sicuramente il prezzo!

As was previously mentioned, Kathmandu is a tumultuous mix of exotic sounds, sights, colors, and tastes for those of us visiting for the first time. The Dwarika offered an oasis to regroup before setting out for another day of exploring. Warm welcoming staff; very large, impeccably clean and beautifully appointed rooms; many choices on the menus; spacious courtyard lovingly groomed; an intimate library with two fireplaces to sit and read, play chess or just sip a glass of wine and unwind. Other pluses:A separate large shower area lined in black slate walls with excellent water pressure;A free-standing bathtub in an alcove;Double sinks, large closets;Beautiful Nepalese upholstery;Very spacious public areas;A detail: we spent Christmas there and plates of cookies and chocolate were out for guests in the reception area, library and rooms. At dinner on December 25th, we were greeted personally by (what I assumed) were family members of the owner and the children received Santa hats (with battery-powered flashing lights!) and chocolate. And back in the room? A box of handmade Nepalese soap! I can only agree with previous recent reviews - worth a trip to Kathmandu just for the hotel!

What can I say that hasn't been said ? It is a beautiful hotel with beautiful rooms. A fresh of breath in hectic Kathmandu. Close enough to Thamel ( half an hour) and you can find taxis at affordable prices. The staff is nice, food is good, clean rooms beautifully decorated. Stay here. You will not regret it. Prices are a bit high but still I would recommend it.

This is our favorite to finish a trek or climbing trip. After wallowing 4 weeks in dirt, dust, donkey droppings and the occasional cold water bucket shower, this place is like paradise. Level of service is tops, it is in a world class league and would compare favorably against any of the top chains. We love the architecture and the feel and fabric of the hotel, no cliches here that have been repeated by the big names on all 5 continents. The service is truly caring and friendly, e.g. our climbing boots were cleaned by the "floor butler" within an hour. Did I say lovely rooms. Food, ok it comes at a price - still reasonable by NYC standards - it's delicious and after weeks of Dhal Bhat a very welcome change. Try the Nepali restaurant, it's an experience well worth it - reviewed separately. This hotel will continue to be our go to place in Kathmandu

Nepal has won 2 Heritage Awards, one for the Bhaktapur Medieval city and the other is Dwarika’s Hotel. The location is right to the centre tourist area/cross to the Royal Palace. I really like the architecture, the garden and the exclusive Krishnarpan Restaurant. The restaurant serves traditional Nepali meals up to 22 variety. The ritual and steps of dining (before, during and after) was very interesting. Apparently, it took months to make a reservation for dinner here as the wait listed is quite long considering this restaurant is very exclusive. Apparently, famous people  and other important people form Nepal government and actress been here.The room are so spacious and luxuries, with antique hand-crafted furnitures individually designed and unique. The bed was big and with amazing details like the bed cover, hand printed curtains, traditional fabrics and accessories. It also has a private court-yard.The service was excellent from the bell boy, room service, swimming pool to the garden. Two nights here were definitley not enough.

This is the one of the most beautiful hotels I have ever stayed in for three main reasons: incredibly warm and genuinely friendly staff, a stately old building that has been lovingly restored with class and care, and a wonderful breakfast! When I asked the ground staff to give me a little privacy as I swam very early in the pool in the morning, they were only too happy to comply with my shy request!

Notre suite était mal insonorisée : l'immense fenêtre de la salle de bains donnait sur une cour intérieure très sonore, réservée au personnel . Nous entendions toutes leurs conversations de 6 heures du matin à plus de minuit, De plus, l'hôtel donne souvent dans l’événementiel ; les baies vitrées des suites sont alors aux premières loges lors des dîners organisés dans les jardins. Enfin bref, nous y avons très mal dormi pendant 2 nuits ; Le petit déjeuner est quelconque et ne correspond pas, tout comme l'insonorisation, à un hôtel de cette catégorie. Ainsi les fruits frais annoncés au breakfast sont de qualité moyenne, voire en boîte! (ananas). Dommage car l'établissement est superbe.

Dwarikas is our favourite hotel in the world.  All the staff are excellent especially Ram and his team in the bar who make us feel welcome and at home.  Service is at a high standard that is not commonly seen in Nepal. We highly recommend the hotel to stay, and fusion bar for a drink.

My husband and I stayed at the Dwarika's Hotel for a few nights and were extremely satisfied with the hotel and its complex. It is an oasis in the middle of a very overcrowded, noisy and polluted city, yet you walk into this hotel and feel like you have gone back in time. The restoration of the hotel and its wood carvings are phenomenal, the grounds are very attractive and peaceful. There are good restaurants in the hotel grounds to sample various types of food, as well as one that does diverse food from around the globe to suit everyone. We experienced them all either sat inside or outside. All of them were excellent, the food and portions were perfect in everyway. The staff are very attentive and friendly and couldn't do enough for you. Would definitely recommend and would revisit ourselves.

have stayed here several times and it's an oasis in Kathmandu. Great rooms, great service, wonderful spa treatments . Expensive but worth it. hotel gardens and pool are beautiful, lots of cools spots for cocktails, solid American breakfast and awesome special dinner.

From the moment we arrived at this wonderful hotel we were absolutely thrilled we had selected this hotel - worth the difference. We were only able to stay two nights but loved the charm. We had great service from all the staff we encountered at reception, the dining room, the bar, the little shops. The rooms were generous, clean, well maintained and everywhere great views of the lovely gardens, great architecture, hidden spots - all exuding charm. I definitely Ho to return.

From the Manager to the Doorman, everyone tries to ensure that each guest has the best of experieinces. Mrs. Shrestha has a great property and terrific staff. The restaurants are all super with great food and service. The spa is a very relaxing experience. The grounds are perfectly maintained. It may be chaotic outside the building in Kathmandu, but once you get into Dwarika's you enjoy peace and tranquility with no knowledge that outside the doors, taxis honk constently.If you go to Kathmandu this is the ONLY place to stay. It is a fantastc experience. Get room 102 if you can.  A sunken huge bathtub will await you.  We look forward to another stay.

I can not recommend this hotel more highly, the rooms are tastefully decorated and extremely clean but the best part our the people especially, Mr Ram at the Fusion and Mr Prashahant, Mr Jawad and Mr Ritsha.   The hotel is more expensive than most but with every dollar.   I also add Ms Mihima, the best I have meet in all more travels.   I know this reports sounds over the top but it is worth it and I can not recommend this hotel more highly.  Josh

Nepal'da harika bir deneyim yaşatacak bir otel.. Odaları çok büyük.. Her sey düşünülmüş.. Kendinizi rahat , huzurluk , mükemmel hissedebilceğiniz bir yer.. Bazen evinizde , bazen her sevdiğiniz bir köşede hissedebilirsiniz.. Her sey birbiriyle uyumlu. Muhteşem bir ergonomi, peyzaj ve uzak doğunun ahsağ işçiliğini göreceksiniz.

hotel fantastico: bellissima struttura e servizio eccellente sotto tutti gli aspetti. caro, ma all'altezza delle aspettative generate dal costo.ottima colazione, personale efficiente e la junior suite è un vero gioiello! buona scelta di ristoranti all'interno.

Wow.  This boutique hotel is absolutely stunning.  It's as if you're staying in a Newari palace.  Accommodations are spacious with every amenity you might need.  The staff is extremely friendly and helpful.  This is a peaceful, elegant oasis in the middle of the craziness of Kathmandu.  Considering that a cab ride to Durbar Square or Thamel is only $3-$5, we will definitely stay here every time we're in Kathmandu.

We stayed at this hotel while on a World Wide Quest Presidents tour of the country. Quiet tranquility in a city that is full of noise, dust and smells. Hotel staff particularly accommodating to travel groups looking for relief from long bus and train rides.

Charme, confort, hospitalité, parfaite rénovation du site, qualité haut de gamme du service et de la restauration, calme et tranquilité dans un écrin de verdure, superbe piscine...... bref, tout est est réuni pour  nous permettre un excellent et luxueux séjour, à KatmandouPetit bémol quand même : la wifi dans les chambres est payante. Seul l'accès à la salle informatique en sous-sol est gratuite.

We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at Dwarika Hotel.  Kathmandu is a bustling fantastic city, so much to see, somewhat a sensory overload, arriving at The Dwarika Hotel, was a wonderful surprise.  A real oasis!  The grounds are beautiful and pristine, the food is very good, the staff is so accomodating and the rooms are very large, clean and beautiful.  Sometimes there are power outages, but this happens all over Nepal, at the hotel they last a couple of minutes, kind of adds to the charm of the area.  Would definitely recommend.

An absolutely amazing place and experience. Located right in the middle of a hectic (yet beautiful city), this hotel offers peace, culture, tranquility, 5 star services, excellent dining and absolutely perfect hosts/owners who are at the hotel every day making sure everything is just right! The staff are absolutely amazing, and all of our experiences and expectations were more than met!!! Again, absolutely amazing and I highly recommend this hotel for business or pleasure.

We stayed here in late October 2014. This is a really tranquil place in the noise and dust of Kathmandu. For us it was a gentle step back into life back home in the developed world, after 3 weeks of trekking, white water rafting and other adventures in beautiful Nepal.The hotel design is like a palace, with 4 outside walls looking in on a courtyard, swimming pool and an unbelievable array of wood carvings, stonework and other character features. Near the pool is a small temple at which a bell is rung and a seashell blown at around 9am as an offering to the gods (Shiva I think). Perhaps it is also to serve as a wake up call to the guests who have only 1 more hour until breakfast is finished...Our room was magnificent (a junior suite) on the top floor of a new building in the middle of the courtyard (room 35). The bed was enormous (I am 6'4" and I could not feel the end) and very firm and comfortable. I would recommend the room to anyone, but it is not cheap (especially by Nepali standards).There are 3 restaurants in the hotel. Krishnarpan (upmarket Nepalese), Mako's (Japanese) and Toran ("International") which serves breakfast for guests and has a mixed menu. I have written a separate review of each as  they deserve special mention. In the centre of the peaceful courtyard in this hotel is a cool bar called Fusion, which is great for a beside the pool or indoors drink or snack.  All of these places are very recommendable. We did not visit the spa, which was very busy. Dwarika's is located on the ring road, so it is about 30 mins (Rs500) by taxi from Thamel, and there is little in walking distance. It is very close to the airport (15 minutes by car). The only criticism I have is that the reception staff were quite slow, and we were given only 24 hour internet logon details until the last day, when they gave as 3 day vouchers (which would have been easier from the start). Another tip for guests is that at the front door of our room there was a master switch for the lights, which if not switched on, made it impossible to switch on the lights.Overall, for a splurge at the end of a trip to Nepal, I would recommend Dwarika's Hotel very highly!

Enjoyed two recent stays here. Certainly, it is a relative oasis of calm, and with plenty of heritage character.The rooms we had looked alright but too often the lighting did not work on various appliances; there were too few towels; too few pillows. - actually ridiculous to provide only 2 pillows on a bed festooned with plenty of sham pillows, throws and other unnecessary decorative items; wi-fi is a bit of a chore too. But, all of these could be overcome provided one had the patience to work hard to address the flaws. So, we made things work but it took an effort.More seriously, sleep quality was poor as the air con system and room fan just do not cool the room sufficiently for folks like us who dislike too- warm bedrooms.The restaurants are quite satisfactory too.All in all the, a Very Good rating that can't be upgraded until the hotel makes life easier Gordon guests.

We loved this hotel. As soon as you walk into the lobby you shut out the hustle and bustle of the big city. The courtyard is large and peaceful. We had a large junior suite and loved all the amenities in the room. We ate at the traditional Nepalese restaurant and enjoyed the meal.

This is an absolute gem of a hotel.  Astonishing to step back in time, with the ancient construction materials, but combined with every luxury that you could possibly want.  It was a wonderful experience being there - a very unique and special place.

These people are running a flawless hotel operation, about as good as hotels get, inside a really magnificent compound of buildings bursting with restored and recaptured traditional Nepalese architectural elements. So the buildings might be more recently built, but there are columns, windows and the like which are much older than the structure itself, and which are all traditional Nepali wood architectural objects. The effect is stunning and it's a beautiful experience to stay in this magic environment which comes with such outstanding service.

Very warm welcoming with pleasant smile. Greetings offered and asked about when came across. Room was really nice and clean with lovely bed. I am fond of Nepalese cuisine and enjoyed the food. Furnishing and decors are so attractive. We loved it.

Great place! We had a GORGEOUS room with a huge bath and comfortable bed, and they did our laundry at a pretty reasonable price. The restaurants are very nice, people travel from all over for the traditional nepalese food. Hotel staff was excellent, and the courtyard and furnishings were really lovely.

I stayed in the Dwarikas hotel at the beginning and end of a Mount Everest trek. The hotel is amazing.The staff can not do enough for you and the food is great.Every where is spotless and clean.A beautiful smell of lemon grass is always in the air.The rooms are amazing and mine had the biggest bed Ive ever seen. All in all a fantastic hotel a nod experience.

Our guide told us before we got to the hotel that Dwarikas was the best hotel in Nepal. Having travelled around the world and stayed in amazing resorts, we found it rather funny and really didn't expect anything out of this world. How wrong were we! Once we last the small and rather dull entrance we were instantly amazed by what was in front of us. We were greeted by warm and smiling staff who made our 4 days/night stay a dream. The grounds are simple but full of history and culture. Every object seems to be at the right place. The deco is not as bling bling as most of the hotels we stayed at, it is rather simple and warm which was a much appreciated and welcomed change. The staff never missed to greet us with a heart felt 'namaste' every time we passed by them and they did whatever they could to make our stay as comfortable as possible. We stayed in the junior suite which was just amazing. If there is one thing we could fault was the slow internet connection but hey, we really didn't care that much. Breakfast is also a little too 'average' compared to the sublime food offered in the hotels restaurants - try the Nepalese food, it's one of the best you will find in Kathmandu. Icing in the cake, it's located only 5 minutes from the airport and you really can't hear the noisy streets from the room.

I stayed in Dwarika's hotel for two nights. Loved the atmosphere, amazing service and wonderful staff. My room was clean and spacious. The breakfast was great and the staff made sure I was taking care of. I had an exceptional experience at the spa with Manoj. Manoj is one of the best masseuse that I ever had anywhere in the world. I highly recommend him for massage.Also Mr. Shiraj in front office had a great personality, very people's person and went out of his way to assisting me.  Dwarika's hotel is the best hotel in Kathmandu.

After reading the previous reviews I was a little concerned whether Dwarika could be too much "museum like", which I personally don't like (have been in some hotels were time has stood still and that look more like museams than hotels, eg Illyria House in Pretoria, and the experience was terrible). For my relief, in Dwarika the old and new was in a perfect balance. The hotel looks beautiful, the rooms are great. the food is delicious and the service is fabulous! It has charm, it has style and it has modern ameneties. I have stayed in many luxury hotels around the world and some of them may have been even more luxurious than Dwarika. However, very few, if any, have been more enjoyable!

Dwarikas is definitely one of the best hotels I have ever stayed in. All the staff will go out of their way to assist you and the food is magnificent. Not to mention the amazing traditional architecture visible throughout the hotel.

This is an excellent choice when staying in the busy city of Kathmandu. The hotel offers 5 starts service, the rooms are clean. We have taken the Junior suite and it over looks the pool. Very nice scenery. That being said, I have once stayed at the Hyatt regency instead and I still think that is the number 1 Hotel in Kathmandu. Dwarika would probably be a close second.Negatives: 1} the breakfast of the hotel was way below average. the services of the restaurant and the room service quality are below average as well. 2} INTERNET is extremely slow

Dwarika's Hotel may just be the best thing in Kathmandu. In the chaos of the city, this place is a real haven. Somehow walking through into the courtyard the sound of the bustle outside disappears and you find yourself in a quiet, historical property. Much of the detail is antique - Mr Dwarika rescued cultural artefacts over the years and built them into the hotel. The rooms are gorgeous, although if you are travelling with friends the "romantic" bathrooms are a little on the open side - be prepared to look away. There is a nice pool and plenty of pool and courtyard tables with cafe and dining service. The food is not cheap - if that's what you're looking for, walk outside - but it's tasty and there's a good deal of variety. Splurge at least one night on the six-course feast. It is a fabulous introduction to Nepali cuisine and an experience in and of itself.

Wunderschönes im Stil der Kolonialzeit errichtetes Hotel!Meine Gruppe und ich wurden bestens bedient.Schöne grosszügige Zimmer die durch die geschmacksvolle Einrichtung sich von anderen Hotels abheben, Freundlicher Empfang und Sevice!

This hotel is not located in an extremely good street but create an extremely good place for foreign traveler to taste Nepal. Good garden, swimming pool, lobby and place for a cup of tea or a cigar, hehe! Hotel embodies traditional emperor culture. But a little bit old.

This hotel is a gem and should not be missed.  When Kathmandu was being torn down in lieu of modern buildings, the Dwarika family rescued and restored antique Newari windows, doors, chandeliers and everything else you can imagine.  This hotel has been built with all of these beautiful items and is a living museum of Kathmandu history.  The food is also terrific, along with the pool and the spa.

After two and half weeks of intensive travelling and sightseeing in Nepal and Bhutan, this was an excellent place to stay and rest before the long journey home. The room was magnificent and the whole hotel steeped in recent history. It is a very interesting story of how the hotel came about. It was a dream of a young man to save his heritage when he saw the old pillars and wooden windows being destroyed. They started with 2 rooms and now a wonderful peaceful hotel in the middle of a bustling city. Where possible they have kept to the Nepalise architecture but the bathrooms are modern and excellent.The owners do an amazing amount of work with the local communities and are involved in various educational charities. Met the Owners who are very humble and Mrs Ambica Dwarika is a very inspirational 85 year old LADY who  still works tirelessly with charities and the main runining of the hotel is left to her daughter and grandson. The staff were wonderful and  nothing was too much trouble. Lovely Spa too. Highly reccomend this jewel in the crown.

My boyfriend and I stayed here and could not have been happier.  The hotel was so beautiful, the staff was so lovely, and the food options were so great, we almost never left the grounds.  Our room was large, clean, and gorgeous, the architecture of the compound was old and amazing, and the facilities were perfect.  If you are looking for luxury in Kathmandu, this is really the only option.

Hotel de lujo con un servicio excelente, un oasis en Katmandu.Estuvimos tres noches en una habitación de cuento, espectacular, un junior suite. Las instalaciones y servicios son excepcionales, apetece quedarte todo el día en el hotel disfrutando de su tranquilidad. Absolutamente recomendable

Whenever Hubby and I go on vacation we look for places that are as much an experience as the trip themselves.   The Late Mr. Dwarika realized his countries history was literally being burned up as heating fuel...so he decided to save it...Nepal is known for the most beautiful wood  trim...intricately carved door and window frames, columns, rafters etc.  He has created a beautiful retreat within the city.  It is a little bit out of the center of town...close to the airport.The aesthetic beauty he created is complimented by the service provided the staff.  Being from Orlando they seem to subscribe to the eye contact, smile and hello (or Namaste) as they approach you.  However I think the biggest hit with the Hubby was the bed.  It was so comfortable and the XLarge King.  The bathroom was huge, with a great soaking tub.  All the soaps, shampoos and toiletries are eco friendly and the towels are fluffy.On your trip thru Nepal, its a must!

We spent about 4 days before and after trekking - absolute gem. The rooms are beautifully decorated - the entire property is gorgeous - authentic, yet modern, with a lot of history and culture. There are 3 restaurants on the property and I must say each has delicious items to offer. Despite the noise outside, we could not hear a single car honk inside. Amazing atmosphere. Staff is extremely polite and helpful. Will highly recommend and cannot wait to go back.

This is great hotel in Kathmandu as my experience. nice staff and excellent breakfast. hotel pool was nice. I like the hotel structure. it's a little away from city but  we had panty of time for  fun. if you would like to go main city you have to take  car from hotel. but night time quite expensive .room was great nice t.v channel . thank you for all your service. we will  come back next year.

Stepping through the door of the Dwarika's is like stepping through a magical portal.  On the outside there is cacaphonic din and hooting and tooting.  Once you step inside, it is quiet, with birds singing.Stepping through the door is also like stepping back in time, hundreds of years.  The entire property is built with salvaged wood carvings, hundreds of years old.The food in the restaurant that serves a multicourse Nepalese meal is wonderful.   The breakfast spread is more than adequate.There cannot possibly be a more romantic and comfortable place to stay in Kathmandu.The service is excellent, I should add.

A lovely hotel set behind walled court yards ensuring peace and privacy away from the noise and bustle of the town. The ambiance is lovely with a traditional and old fashion style but with all modern amenities. Lovely helpful staff good service and a fun pack of the owners dogs around during the day [very friendly]My only complaint was the swimming pool it was freezing,this needs heating the sitting area was very nice with drinks and snacks readily available.The restaurants were very good and the food excellent .This is the place to stay and still feel you are in Nepal

This is my second time back in Kathmandu , this hotel blew our minds away with it's remarkable journey in reconstruction and preservation efforts.  The hotel is situated in the city and very convenient to get to places.. we felt very safe there . We stayed at the Dwarika on 3 separate occasions for this trip.  Every time, the staff were professional and service was great! Rooms there are HUGE compared to a standard hotel but Im not sure if its because we booked a different category of rooms than the standard.  Our 2 rooms had 3 beds and lots of room to run walk around .  Huge walk in bathroom, we enjoyed wandering the courtyard of the hotel during our free time , just taking in the ambience and being transported to a different era. Hotel breakfast was a mix of some local cuisine and western fare with table service for tea and coffee.  Tap Water in Kathmandu is not safe and we stuck to bottled water even for when brushing our teeth.  Be careful of run off water from head to face .  Better be safe than sorry .. the last thing you want is a stomach issue on a wonderful adventure like this.

Sono stata due volte ospite del Dwarika's: il primo giorno del nostro tour in Nepal e l'ultimo giorno. La prima esperienza era stata molto deludente per cui avevo cercato di cancellare la prenotazione per la settimana successiva, ma non è stato possibile farlo per cui ci sono ritornata.L'hotel è indubbiamente stupendo, ricavato all'interno di un edificio in stile architettonico tradizionale completamente ristrutturato, ma la prima volta la stanza non era particolarmente bella, inoltre diverse cose non mi avevano assolutamente soddisfatta.La seconda volta invece abbiamo avuto un inaspettato quanto gradito upgrade gratuito della stanza ed è stata tutta un'altra cosa: tutte i difetti riscontrati la prima volta qui non c'erano, e devo anche dire che la stanza assegnataci va annoverata tra le più belle in cui ho mai alloggiato. La colazione è ottima e varia ed il personale gentilissimo.Il Nepal è un posto meraviglioso con una popolazione accogliente e fantastica! Come si vede dalla mappa dei miei viaggi ho girato parecchio ma qui ho lasciato un pezzo del mio cuore.

Su ubicación y en especial su arquitectura le convierten en un lugar francamente agradable , sus habitaciones tanto las que dan a la piscina y jardines como las superiores que dan al interior mantienen el sabor y el atractivo exclusivo , creando una atmosfera perfecta , que conjuga con su buen desayuno y no desmerece en absoluto su cocina, la lentitud de su personal contrasta con la pretensión de dar un buen servicio , que aun y así consiguen

The completely renovated Dwarika hotel in the heart of Kathmandu is an oasis of tranquility. The staff attentive. The hotel boutiques are also highly recommended, I bought some beautiful gem stones and pashminas from there. We stayed in a suite and it was beautifully decorated. All in all an experience we will never forget.

I stayed here twice en route to Bhutan in April and had a fantastic experience both times.  For each stay I had a great room, both spacious and beautifully decorated.  Stylish without being ostentatious.  The staff are all fantastic, from those on reception through to the restaurant staff and ladies cleaning the rooms.  Breakfast is delicious - a buffet with a great variety to choose from and freshly baked bread.  Food for dinner is also.  I recommend the Lamb Thali.  The pool area is lovely with plenty of comfortable places to relax and great pool-side service.Dwarika's is in my top ten of hotels I have stayed in.

If you are visiting Kathmandu, only place to stay is Dwarika. It is located very near to Pashupati nath Temple. Entrance: The outside part of the hotel looks very cramped, but as you enter the doors of Dwarika, it was blissful. Rooms: We stayed at the Junior suite (didnt remember the exact category), & my god that was one of the room i will never forget. Quite local in every sense. The room is huge almost 50 sq. mtr. All in all a very nicely maintained room. Taxi: Taxis standing outside always charge double, they will never go by meter. So it is better to walk 100 - 200 mtrs on the right of the hotel towards the red light & you will easily find a taxi much cheaper. Only Maruti 800 is what available in nepal as public taxi. Room Service & Housekeeping: Room service is quite good. They will go extra mile to please whatever you desire. Since we were pure Vegeterian, & were craving for Indian food they made what we asked for. Housekeeping personals were bang on. Restaurants: I loved the concept of their Nepali cuisine restaurant. They make you sit on low cusions followed by a set menu. Though i didnt liked the cuisine that much but the way they give you attention is spot on. You can eat as much as you want. The rice Liqueur i liked the most.Breakfast: You will get lot of choices in the Breakfast. They made allo parantha & curry on our request. though it was not what we usually eat at the indian restaurants but they tried their best. All in all if you are in Kathmandu & budget is not a problem then this is a place to stay at.

Very good and charming, liked the Nepalese restaurant. Service is not top, but decent enough. We tried the SPA, the Cocktail bar.We stayed twice. the first room was on the patio, so nice, but with no intimacy and basic. Second room was much better but with no view.

We have wanted to stay here for many years and given it's one of the best and most popular hotels in Kathmandu we booked almost 6mths ahead - even then it was luck a room became available for the dates we wanted.Upon approach from the airport (less than 10mins away so get a taxi as it'll cost just Rps600) the hotel is uninteresting and unimpressive. The small drive through drop off area does not prepare you for the sight you get as you walk behind the doors.This spectacular project then shows it's the colours as you walk into the lobby and through to the grounds. It has been gradually built and added to over the years using original window frames and structures from previous lost buildings so you get the impression that the entire hotel is very old eventhough it's not.As a result you get all the charm of a beautiful heritage building but all the mid cons as well. The newest addition was built in 2011 which I dare say is much more modern than the room we were in as ours was in the original first building but even so we were delighted.We were upgraded to the heritage suite which was huge. A massive long bedroom area with a bed that could sleep four! A sofa area with table, desk and office section, huge walk-in wardrobe and lovely big bathroom with two sinks, bath, separate toilet and showroom.  Tiled floors throughout keeping it cool and massive windows on almost all walls overlooking the courtyard.The room was really comfortable but I have to say we were a little annoyed by the noise the staff make in the mornings. In prep for breakfast and the general day they were often loud and annoying with moving tables and chairs around at 6/6:30am which woke us up each morning. Equally there's some sort of ritual at 9am where flutes are played loudly - to herald the new day no doubt - we were up most days really early but that would have been very annoying if we were jet lagged and forced to wake up at 9am whether we wanted to or not.The grounds are stunning. There's a lovely pool with about 15 sunbeds, a great spa and gym, huge bar with space indoors and tables looking out onto the pool area, there's garden spaces with sunbeds, loungers and chairs plus a library should you choose to borrow books and lounge around after dinner. They play heritage films there most nights for free explaining more about Nepal.The restaurants were superb too. There's a main western/European friendly restaurant where you can eat indoors or on the large outdoor terrace which is gorgeous. Lunch, dinner and breakfast is served here - we had breakfast every day and chose to sit outside which was lovely.There's also a traditional Nepalese restaurant which we tried one night having pre booked a spectacular 16 course banquet. I have to say it was stunning but don't eat all day in advance!!! The staff were super friendly and chatty which really made the evening  special.There's also a Japanese restaurant called Mako's which we ate in one night and having travelled to Japan a lot, can vouch for how authentic and gorgeous the food was that we had. So much so we had sushi every day at lunch as well when we were sat by the pool. The manager Mako is adorable and from Kyoto visiting home regularly to perfect her next years recipe book. Again a joy to chat to and she made the evening special.You can choose bar snacks and food from the bar too. In fact you an choose to sit anywhere in the hotel and order any good from any restaurant!On top of this there are three shops on site - a great gift and book shop rather hidden at the back, a clothing store and a jewellery store.You almost need not leave the hotel grounds at all. A lovely hotel and one we'd return to without question.

Il Nepal e' un posto molto difficile e Kathmandu lo è  ancora di più. Bisogna prepararsi fisicamente e psicologicamente a un viaggio da queste parti. Sicuramente il Dwarika ha contribuito ad alleviare le nostre sofferenze. E' l'unico hotel di livello occidentale, caratteristico, pulito e silenzioso. Unico difetto: lontano dal centro.

this hotel felt like a haven away from the noise, dirt and pollution of Kathmandu.Our room was lovely , large with views over to a privately owned temple. There is a pool and good choice of food.We found staff helpful and  breakfast was super with nice choice of fruits, yoghurt, rolls etcDownside drinks rather expensive but the ambience alone was worth it

Amazing hotel, rooms, location and very good food but the service could be better. The staff (particularly on reception) didn't seem very happy and weren't very welcoming. With improved service and a smile this would get 5 stars.

This hotel was a wonderful respite from the bustle of Kathmandu city.  It is very peaceful with lovely grounds and an excellent staff.  We stayed here at the beginning of our trip to Nepal and returned at the end of our 2 weeks travelling. It is a great beginning and end.  The rooms are large and beautifully maintained. The staff is incredible, they are there for your every need with out being obtrusive.  There are several restaurants to choose from as well as a great bar poolside.  They offer a delicious breakfast buffet with bread made on their premises and local cheeses.  First time I ever had Yak cheese!  Their spa offers numerous treatments and is a perfect way to end a long day touring.

We stayed here for 4 nights and felt as if we were in paradise.  The antiques and traditional design of the complex was fascinating to explore. Our room (#60)was huge, divinely appointed with a huge soaking tub and home-made soaps. Plush towels, gorgeous bathroom, niches illuminated and filled with interesting bricabrac.   We loved the yoga in the morning and felt that was actually one of the highlights of our 3 week trip! Dr. Yati Raj Bhattarai is incredible-- do not miss his class!  Great food at the restaurants AND we did the singing bowl therapy at the spa which was also amazing.   I hated to leave.

This is by far the best hotel we stayed at in Kathmandu. A boutique hotel in the true sense of the word, it represents a decadent and blissful oasis in the cacophany that can often be Kathmandu! The care taken to recreate traditional Nepalese architecture is impressive, including the addition of original features where possible. The staff are very friendly and the food is some of the best in Kathmandu.If there is a negative, and again it is difficult to find one, is its location outside of the main tourist hub of Thamel. But then it's about a 20 minute walk from Durbar Square, though this can prove quite an experience at night when the lights go out!  stay here is highly recommended for any trip to Kathmandu.

We stayed at Dwarika's for 2 nights, after a month long tour of the interior of Nepal.  For a month we lived with  the hardships of no electricity, no heat, cold showers, dirty water, etc, etc.  So arriving at Dwarikas was like a dream.  The clean sheets and soft beds alone were luxurious!The grounds are lovely, with fountains and old buildings.Highly recommended.

When the car pulled up to the hotel, I was a bit weary but the moment you enter through the old beautiful carved doors, you step into an urban oasis.  The architecture is beautiful and the courtyard is cozy and comfortable.  I had a room in one of the new buildings and it was bright, spacious but oddly shaped. I took the liberty of rearranging some furniture to make it more comfortable. The room was very clean, despite the dustiness of Kathmandu.All the meals I had in the hotel were superb and reasonably priced. The spa was also very good.There are a few domesticated dogs (very cute!) hanging out in the courtyard. They're extremely friendly but if you're afraid of dogs, this might not be the best hotel for you.

Stayed at the Dwarika having trekked to Everest Base Camp - just what we needed - luxury without being overly ostentatious. Perfect combination of pure comfort, selection of dining options and attentive staff.Would loved to have stayed for longer in our junior suite - an oasis amidst the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu!Thank you for a wonderful stay - will be back!

Wonderful hotel with lots of character. So much better than staying in an impersonal chain hotel. It was a pleasure to explore. The only drawback was that the alcove outside our room was an ideal place for the pigeons early in the morning, as there was only a thin material on the window area to the alcove this proved a little noisy.Nice touch was the chocolates received each evening. We had a huge bathroom & was well appointed.

I stayed at the Dwarikas for one week. The hotel is in a great spot, and the staff could not be nicer. They have many different restaurants and on Friday night they have a BBQ, which should not be missed. Thanks to Dwarikas I had a great stay in Kathmandu.

Dwarika's Village is one of those very special places you'll look back fondly as  one of the more unique, authentic, and visually stunning accommodations you've stayed at during your travels. It's clearly a labor of love, incorporating Nepalese architecture, lots of brick, many antiques, stunning carved windows everywhere, a lovely pool (closed for remodeling during our stay), good exercise room, very nice spa (superb one hour massage for about $40 - terrific!), a separate, attractive bar and a wonderful restaurant serving reasonably good fare and a few standout dishes. There was also a Japanese restaurant on property, of which we did not partake. Fountains and lotus water treatments abound (one was apparently dedicated by Prince Charles during a 1998 visit to Nepal), there are a half-dozen lovely shops, and a good number of outdoor tables, lounge beds and lounge chairs. Dwarika's rooms are large, rectangular, with dark wood floors, carved wood furniture, a very comfy King Bed and flat screen tv. With lots of wood and carved trim on the windows, it's a bit dark on a cloudy day, but there are many windows and with all curtains pulled back, it's quite light and airy when the sun is shining. There's an entry area with armoire and window seat, a two sink bathroom, decent sized shower with great hot water pressure and small WC. The bedroom end of the large room included a good sized desk. We were asked to pay for wifi, but comped a second password so we could both access simultaneously.Service was simply impeccable. The staff was well-trained, very friendly and very competent. One word of caution. This is a "village" so there are people and voices in the courtyards below the rooms. Our room was near the front of the property, above some of the outdoor dining tables and near the bar, and proved to be a bit noisy in the mid-evening, but quieted by 10:30, which was not a problem for us.One minor annoyance. We asked for a later checkout (since we departing Nepal at 7 pm to begin the long trip home) and were told we'd have to pay one-half the daily rate for the three hours between 11am and 2 pm, but for that, they'd let us stay until 4 pm. Given they were far from full, we found that (and the wifi fees) a bit chintzy.Should we return to Kathmandu, we'll be staying at Dwarika's again.

Dwarika has sprinted to one of my top five hotels in the world. Amazing decor and layout,littered with Nepalese antiques, but also ensuring international five star comfort. The staff are kind, intelligent, fluent in English, and anticipate needs. It's a bit out of town. But taxis are so cheap, for this sort of experience who cares. I can't imagine anyone not enjoying a stay here.

We stayed at Dwarika after a 20 day trek to Kanjing Ri and Goyko - Goyko Ri. This is our second time at the Hotel. It is quite simply stunning. Excellent service. High quality furnishings. Think of what an oasis would be like - Dwarika is it. Do yourself a favour and stay. In all our travels - this is the best hotel we have ever stayed in and evokes old world service standards that are long gone in most other hotels. The outdoor sun beds are just a wonderful place to read a book. Highly, highly recommended.

Loved the Nepalese decor with a touch of modern flair! The restaurant food was average (not fresh) but inexpensive. The service was also good but I'm a stickler for attention to detail. I had to call twice to have them remove my in dining tray. In general, staff was very friendly and super accommodating. We had a junior suite overlooking the courtyard which was spacious and clean. The bed was comfortable and the overall the amenities were good. I would probably say this is on the high end of a 4 star property rather than 5 but overall an Excellent choice while in Kathmandu!Better food and more attention to detail would ensure it to be in the running of a good 5 star hotel!

3 Tage Eintritt in die märchenhafte Seite von Nepal. Dwarika's ist ein ganz besonderes Hotel, das einen einlädt, auf sehr luxuriöse Art in eine andere Welt zu reisen. Sehr nette Mitarbeiter, besonders die Damen am Empfang und im Service, soviel Herzlichkeit und Liebevolles; die Herren Mitarbeiter wissen zum Teil noch nicht genau, was sich der Gast in dieser Hotelklasse vorstellt: trotzdem macht es dem Service keinen Abbruch ,da diese Menschen Teil eines unglaublich einfachen, anderen Lebensstiles sind. Die Zimmer sind ein Traum; mit kostbaren antiken Möbeln und tollen Stoffen ausgestattet, wie das ganze Hotel, und doch fast stylisch, gemütlich und sehr geschmackvoll eingerichtet. Alles im Zimmer hat bestens funktioniert. Das Essen war landestypisch und gut, besonders das healthy food. im Spa war es sehr kalt, die Mitarbeiter dort sehr bemüht, aber sie konnten sich nicht wirklich einfühlen. Der ruhige Innenhof, die nette Bar, der schön integrierte Pool (wenn auch jetzt im Februar noch etwas kühl zum Baden und nicht beheizt), der fast verwunschene Innenhof zum Relaxen nach der wilden Stadt draußen: wir haben den Aufenthalt im Dwarika's rundum sehr, sehr genossen. Flughafennähe natürlich sehr angenehm, nachts hört man den Lärm der Straße nicht. Einzig empfanden wir die "europäischen" Zimmerpreise trotz des wirklichen 5-Sterne-Standards für nepalesische Verhältnisse nicht angemessen. Hyatt kostet die Hälfte und ist auch ein 5 Sterne Hotel im landestypischen Stil mit einer tollen Anlage. Wir würden neben dem Hyatt Regency das Dwarika's unbedingt wieder wählen.

Acredito que este hotel deveria ser considerado um atraçao turistica. Ele foi transformado em hotel, inicialmente era residencia. Porem, cada construçao, mantem todos os detalhes da arquitetura Nepalense. Apresenta um restaurante típico do Nepal que vale o jantar.

The hotel is only a few kilometres from the airport and thus, easy to get to. The hotel is easily recognisable and on the main road. Staff were welcoming from the moment I was met at the airport to the time, I left 11 days later. The room I had on the 5th floor was quiet and had a lobby where snacks, and even meals, would be served. The coffee shop in the GF lobby was a good idea, with snacks, mostly pastries but also some salties. Sit back, relax sip cappuchino eat an apple pie, watch Nepal go by and  check out the world on a laptop. They arrange a good taxi service to go into the centre of town, and visit the pilgrimage and tourism places in Kathmandu and in the vicinity. Excellent value for money hotel.

The Everest Hotel in my opinion is the grande dame of hotels in Nepal, and after its recent renovation, is a class above itself and ready to serve for the next few decades! The hotel has an openness and spaciousness about itself and has perhaps the warmest and friendliest staff. They are very welcoming, very knowledgeable and very helpful. The recently renovated rooms are modern yet warm and inviting and the restaurants at the hotel offer some of the best cuisine in Kathmandu. The hotel was priced well and offered great value given the proximity to the city centre, airport, Thamel etc. I will no doubt stay here again and believe it is a great hotel for both personal and business-travellers alike.Well done to all the staff for making my stay at the Everest Hotel my home away from home.

Let's just say from the airport pickup till dropping us back everything was perfectly done by the hotel.As you walk into your room you can see that it's well maintained and cleaned with a personalized welcome note from the general manager himself which makes you feel very special. Room service and housekeeping is quick in fulfilling your requirements.Their rooftop bar is just the perfect place to celebrate the mejestic view of Kathmandu with beautiful cocktails it offers.Restaurant is fabulous, one must try their Tibetan hotpot.Thank you team Everest hotel for making our stay so memorable, will visit soon!

The Everest Hotel, just remember this name for the best 5 Star Luxury Hotel in Kathmandu Nepal. Stepping through the lobby, I was immediately struck by the beautiful and friendly reception area. Light, airy, and very spacious...very welcoming atmosphere. Every staff member I encountered, from the valet to the check-into the cleaning staff was very professional, delightful, and eager to help! The Café restaurant is superb, serving culinary delights and ample dining options (p.s. – please wake up every morning for their breakfast spread). If you’re a business traveler or living in Kathmandu, The Bugles Bar is worth visiting, an epitome of old school and formal. I’ve enjoyed many a cocktail with friends, where you enjoy panoramic and breathtaking views of KTM city at night. Rooms are exceptional and have a great ambiance, with terrific service and cleanliness. And oh yes! - Location Location Location – the hotel is at the center of the city and only a few kilometers away from the airport. Easy access in and out of the city to visit Kathmandu’s heritage sites and other attractions from the Hotel is convenient. This is a beautiful hotel and one of the largest properties in Kathmandu, including a host of facilities and ballrooms for conferencing and private meetings.The best stay ever and I have no hesitation in recommending this hotel for guests considering visiting Kathmandu. Please stay at the Everest Hotel – a real example of Excellent Hospitality. Will be back to this place soon..!!!

Kathmandu is one of those destinations where you want the convenience of a clean, comfortable hotel with all the modern amenities and choice of restaurants . The Everest has all of that. Enjoyed the stay and was even able to get around with a local tour guide and pick up some souveniers . Hotel pick up and drop off service is the way to go if you're flying in to Tribhuvan International Airport. Great hotel overall with fair room rates, would go back again.

Memorable stay. Extremely helpful and courteous staff.The hotel is conveniently located while the airport is just 10-15 minutes away. Loved the retro feel of the room I stayed in (especially the black switches on the brass plate and the phone in the bathroom!).

The hotel has come back with a wonderful ambience. The hygiene of the hotel is highly maintained. One can  feel the pureness of the hotel as soon as you enter the lobby. The floors are sparkling clean and the lobby is well designed. The new restaurant The Cafe is amazing. The menu is best value for money. Its the most advantageous combination of cost, quality and sustainability to meet customers requirements.

I came to Nepal Kathmandu for a short-term yoga study abroad.I stayed at this hotel by myself for almost a month.Front office executive SUMITRA WAGLE,The cafe staff, doormen, housekeepers, people who water the flowers,All the staff greeted me with a smile every day,He was very kind, caring, and treated me like a family member or friend.So I was able to spend my time with a lot of confidence and peace of mind.Facilities include a pool, gym and bar.And the decoration of the hotel is like a museum✨The breakfast buffet has a large number of items and is very delicious.There are a hospital and a bank in front of the hotel, and the location requirements are also good.Various events were held every day.It's a little different from Japanese hotels, but it's a very nice ✨👏 hotel.I feel very lonely after returning to Japan and not being able to meet his staff.Also, when he comes to Kathmandu, Nepal, he would like to use this hotel.Thank you for all the happy and fun memories 🍀✨

I stayed for 5 nights at The Everest Hotel. The rooms are very specious and clean. The service is excellent and employees are very polite. Front office team Ms Sumitra, Pratima, Shristi including bell desk and housekeeping team are always at your service. i will be definelty back to this hotel.Thank you entire team for making me feel like my home.

Worst Hotel ever.....We stayed 2 nights there, our experience is very very bad. Especially housekeeping we call hundred of times nobody ever pick up calls same as front desk and room service at night we called so many times but call was never recieved..... Both of the Guest lifts were stoped at day time for service work so we have to wait more than 15 minutes in the lobby....water was yellow and smelly, flush was not working. worst hotel and worst services ever, i will never recommed this hotel to anyone and i will never coming back to this hotel again.

Beautiful hotel! We have visited this hotel twice coming and going in and out of Nepal. The staff are extremely hospitable and accommodating from arranging airport shuttle to room accommodations and even special luggage requests on our behalf. I very much recommend this hotel, particularly for those in transit to and from Tribhuvhan airport as it is also in close proximity. Also, very grateful to Radhika and the restaurant staff for a delicious breakfast buffet!

I had the pleasure of staying at the Everest Hotel in December 2019 during my visit to Kathmandu.The hotel has been completed renovated and refurbished and I must say it looks fabulous. The new facade has a very fresh, warm and welcoming appeal. The Hotel Lobby is pristine and inviting. The check in process was smooth and extremely hospitable. Special mention must be made about the cleanliness of the hotel, it was impeccable. The newly refurbished rooms were very comfortable ,luxurious and catered to all the amenities. Dining options are many and I especially liked the new coffee shop with a wide choice of local and international cuisine. Do not miss the opportunity to have a drink and take in the view for a relaxing evening at the plush Bugles and Tigers Bar.

Our stay at The Everest Hotel was most enjoyable.  We stayed for four days to meet with friends and to experience Kathmandu.  From greeting at the door, to check in, to room cleaning and laundry service, it was kind and professional. Rooms and beds were so clean and comfy, every meal was great with impeccable, professional service.  Our dining experience in The Cafe Restaraunt each day was so nice and personalized by Pramod Thapa, the food and beverage executive.  He and his staff provided excellent food and service.  Even down to how we like our coffee each morning . Very nice experience.  This hotel made our first trip to Nepal memorable. We will certainly be back!  Riley and Debra SheltonUSA

Nice hotel with courteous & helpful staff. Close to the airport. Neat and clean rooms & bed linens.  Issue faced with some ac noise in the room was addressed immediately by senior staff by changing rooms.

The restaurant (The Cafe) staff displayed excellent hospitality and warmth, The team comprising Ms Radhika, Yashoda and chef Alina were always there to make the dining experience an awesome one. The room service was also equally good however during our say at the hotel for four nights; experienced switching off Central AC, post midnight apparently for cost cutting; which leads to severe discomfort, specially when you are tired after a long day trip. Additionally, the replenishment of tea / coffee / water bottles etc in the room were painfully delayed; in spite of the reminders to house keeping and front office tele extensions. The overall experience i s good, however the hotel management to look in to these grey areas for better clientele and footfalls,

I was in the Everest hotel on the 31st night. The arrangements were perfect and the hospitality was really warm. The price of the ticket was best value of money. The limited flow of the premium liquors was the best attraction. The live counters with bon fire in the poolside was a perfect match. The night was really happening. Congratulations for a magnificent come back.

Stayed here 3 seperate times in April- May 2023.  Great Hotel rooms good. All staff are wonderful, helpful and welcoming. The Cafe staff are amazing. So professional and so friendly. Really make your stay lovely. Food is great. Front desk, security and doorman always welcoming and helpful - calling taxi’s, giving advice, answering questions, checking how your day is going.  Hotel has many wonderful restaurants nearby and is only a short taxi ride to Thamel and places of interest.

Place to enjoy lunch / dinner with family in a cozy environment and best in class service. Multiple options available in Menu and the food is delicious.Staff is courteous and always welcoming . No matter how stressed you are , once u reach here they will make sure that you are well taken care off

Checking into Everest Hotel was a breath of fresh air after experiencing other hotels prior. The customer service is beyond amazing. My favorite was having breakfast every morning seeing Radhika’s smile and service. I gave it a 4 star just because our tub had a Little bit of issue that they did try to resolve. Will definitely come back.

The hotel is a great hotel, clean, quiet, comfortable. The staff though made my experience though. Check in, doorman, valet, host were attentive, accommodating, smiling and genuinely warm. My best experience was t The Cape Restaurant, Promad Thapa the Maître d', he knew my favorite order, drink, seat. I felt like a king. Food was on point and accommodated special requests. The Best.

The location was convenient to the airport.  However there was a teacher protest right in front of the hotel so the taxi could not drop us at the door.   Staff was very friendly and made us feel right at home.  The room was nice, but I wouldn't say it was 5 star.  Could hear a bit of street noise from the room.    The location is close to the government building, but not much close by for tourist sites (that we could find).  We did walk the neighbor hood and felt perfectly safe, even though we were the only tourists we saw.  For someone new to this culture the neighborhood was very interesting to walk through.  The restaurant was big and empty when we ate there.  Food was a bit pricey for Nepal standards but it was very tasty.  No complaints about the hotel but would try somewhere different next time.

The Everest hotel is a nice hotel with very friendly and helpful staff, neat rooms with good beds, very good housekeeping and nice food. Staff respond immediately to your questions and concerns. The gym has two running devices and several weight devices to keep your body in shape while traveling abroad. The hotel has just been renovated after the earthquake damage. So in general I can recommend it to everyone who likes comfort but above all a warm welcome and great hospitality.

The cuisine at this establishment is amazing, with the culinary team readily accommodating specific requests for customized dishes. However, the hotel room experience could be enhanced, as we were not entirely impressed by the ambient odor. I would like to extend a special commendation to two members of the hotel staff - Himal and Radika. Himal's assistance has been invaluable; he has consistently responded to our needs with a friendly, respectful, and helpful demeanor. Radika has also demonstrated exemplary manners and kindness in her interactions with us. The overall level of service provided by the hotel is commendable.

The staff at this hotel are exceptional. The food at the restaurants was of a high standard. The rooms while satisfactory are a little dated and small things affected our stay, such as lack of all day hot water and slight leaks in the bathroom.

The Everest hotel is advantageously positioned in the centre of Kathmandu. Either corporate or leisure traveller, it’s an ideal destination next to the airport and the historical town centre. Everest hotel is my first choice when visiting Kathmandu serving either as a professional base or an enjoyable city break.It’s a family hotel of international standards and services reflecting a longstanding family tradition in hospitality. The rooms are comfortable and luxurious including many more five-star facilities. The management and the personnel  strived to make every moment of my stay unique, memorable and exciting.Should definitely recommend it to everyone visiting Kathmandu and look forward to visiting again.

The Everest Hotel has exceptional staff who are professional, polite and very helpful in addressing all of our needs. At the restaurant, Ms. Radhika provided us with exceptional service. The hotel is located close to the airport and we were able to reach all the attractions within 15 minute ride.

It is very convenient for a business traveller like me. Everything is just right as one expects things to be.What I like the best about is the team at the breakfast lounge makes you feel at home. They remember your preference of food and beverage, your favourite seat at the breakfast place. Also they are always around for making sure you get what you want.I travel mostly on business needs and don't have much free time at the hotels, but these few minutes at breakfast makes my day.

The Everest Hotel gave us far more than we expected. We were glad to stay three nights. The room was clean and comfortable and ready hours before check-in at no extra cost. The penthouse bar, tended by Ganesh, Bugles & Tigers, is a classic Bristish officer-style retreat with a stunning view of the sprawling city. Read about the heroism and history of the Gurka forces while you are there. The basement fitness center maintained by Suman is complete and comfortable. The restaurant , directed by Ankhir Pandey, was full of delicious local options as well as Western European mainstays. Finally, this hotel was  built in 1982 and withstood the 8.3 earthquake. We would definitely, gladly return.

Nice food and ambience and Himal was brilliant along with the entire staff. The room, the view and the connectivity as well. The facilities and amenities provided here is brilliant. It is the place to stay in Kathmandu as it is well connected with commercial places and offer services as well

We had a wonderful experience staying at the Everest Hotel. Got the level of service that we had wished for, and especially appreciate Radhika's hosiptality delivery that made us feel being at home.The morning breakfast serving staff are truly professional and always ready to assist.

It was a nice experience staying in Hotel Everest in Kathmandu. Service and ambience was great!Near by markets and easy access to other important tourist places makes it even more attractive.Radhika and Himal were very helpful at the breakfast counter and we felt being at home with their gestures. Highly recommended!

food was amazing, like the manager of the restaurant Rajiv. Good place to go and not very expensive. Room service was amazing too, like the swimming pool and healf club. The food is free buffet you can eat a lot

Amazing service and the food is Yumulicious. The head chef Vijay has a great taste for culinary cuisine and makes an effort out of the way to make sure the guests are happy. A big Thank you shout out to him for the Pani Puri:) also a thank you shout out to Radhika, Himal and Vijaya for an exceptional service. Would highly recommend this hotel for your stay. Our little one enjoyed the food a lot too. Gym is great too.

Everything was super good. Special food was yummy 🤤Room was silent, no noise, good view form room as well as from top 😍 Thank you for the good hospitality. Really appreciated 🫡See you next time as well.

Every one on staff is very welcoming, polite and knows the hospitality starting from  security guard standing at the main gate to folks in lobby to Front desk to house keeping and of course restaurant.  Loved the mixed paratha with tasty pickles in the morning breakfast. Radhika and her crew including but not limited to Sushan and Yashosha made sure I am well fed. A very professional crew all around !! God bless them. Har Har Mahadev!!

The best place to stay when in Kathmandu! Top class service, great food at the cafe, bar serves some really good cocktails and the view from there is just amazing.Highly recommended...must stay here when in k-town

Manager Mr. Umesh ji and his team took very good care of us during our stay in The Everest Hotel. They also advised and guided us very well regarding stays in other places like Pokhara. Regarding our specific diet this was also not a problem at all. The Chefs did their utmost best, and succeeded, to provide us with the best food according to our diet. More than anything they gave us the feeling of being a respected family member. Thanks again for everything!

What a fantastic hotel in a not so great city (lots of rubbish and pollution 😪).Staff were great, restaurant perfect, rooms very comfortable.There's a great view of the city from the hotel rooftop which can be organised if there is somebody working up there.The Tiger and Bugles bar is a great spot to catch-up and if you're lucky enough you might see a wedding being conducted in the adjoining function rooms.Parliament House is just a short walk from the hotel, but be prepared for lots of traffic.Our front of the hotel you'll find the barricades and wire set up for the frequent demonstrations that seem to happen.If in Kathmandu, I would highly recommend a stay in the Everest Hotel.

Radhika and Sushan were friendly, efficient and a joy to be served by. Small details like remembering our names and coffees were greatly appreciated. They made us feel very welcome in Nepal and were extremely helpful. We wish them all the best in the future.

Best in Nepal’s Capital and near the National Parliament.Good service and nice people.The rooms are big and very confortable.Complimentary newspapers at the reception Exquisite Buffet for 20% less at the Coffe Shop for in-house guests.They serve REAL coffe.

While staying in the everest hotel for 3 days my stay was comfortable and thoroughly enjoyed the hospitality of the staff. Staff is well behaved and serves you with warmth. Anu need special mention, from the start i entered in the hotel she welcome me with beautiful smile, everytime i see her she is smiling and come to talk with us very attentive and friendly. In my next visit it will be pleasure to meet her again.

We stayed in the Everest Hotel, Kathmandu. The hotel was elegant, with pleasant staff. The food was excellent. The front desk clerks and the cafe staff were very helpful and courteous. The bar tender, Mr Ganesh, was very friendly and made excellent drinks explaining the story behind each of the classical drinks of Nepal. The rooms were spacious with good amenities. It was less expensive and a great place to stay. We will stay here again and recommend to anyone visiting Kathmandu.

Santina highly recommended the Gyakok for dinner. This meal arrived in sizzling hotpot. It was visually mesmerising, delicious and a lot of fun to eat. This is a traditional Tibetan meal and a must to try as part of your Nepalese travels. Our meal was cooked by Chef Shiva Ram and served by Jagdish. The hospitality of this restaurant is world class.

Excellent ambiance, excellent staff specially Mr. Rakesh (Chef), Mr. Himal Mr. Subrana and Mr. Deepak. I would also thanks all the other staff. It is pleasure to stay here. We will surely come again to The Everest Hotel and we also recommend other to stay and take world class stay experience

Wonderful Experience at always. We visit Nepal 2 times every year and Everest has always been warm and welcoming. Good rooms, great food - especially indian, chinese and italian. An amazing breakfast spread especially for indians to feel at home. The Restaurant Staff has been especially accommodating and friendly especially Radhika, Abhinash, Sushan who have ensured our stay was comfortable.

I stayed in The Everest Hotel , Kathmandu from 31/8 till 3/9. My experience at property was not pleasant. The hotel did not have the standards of a 5 star. The toilet was not clean and had stains. The drainage was clogged and had to be called in for removing the block. The linen (blanket) had stains  that was covered with white sheets. Swimming pool was not operational. Water leakage from the AC panel resulting in drenching of my cloths to be used. They did not even had the courtesy to get these washed . The only thing I can say ok was the buffet breakfast. Just OK. Do not expect the standards of a five star and at the rate charged 4 star facility will be a better option in  Kathmandu

I am a guest of yours. I am very happy here. I sing highly of your service. Hotel is clean and tidy! Foods were well presented and tasted good ! Most import reason is hotel staff are friendly and courteous, and went out their way to make guests to feel at ease!

Dear Everest Hotel Team,A very warm greetings and namaste I would like to thanks  all the team of Everest hotel for providing wonderful hospitality and services during our event special thanks to Hemant sir, umesh sir, rajiv sir,Prasanna sir, sumitra mam, all the front office team and food and beverage department .I will surely visit again .Thank you once again.Best regards,Sabin LamichhaneNTSNFounder/ President

Overall the service was perfect including hospitality. Breakfast service was excellent and staff were found so much polite and professional. Few staffs such as Yashoda and Himal are the most professional that we met during our stay. If possible, please try to take care and respect the visitors not only customers.

Our stay was good...... we stayed 2 nights there  one night we booked suite room and next night was club room so we request ms. anu from lobby to upgrade second night to suite, so kind of her she upgraded us to suite. She is very attentive and cheerful. Food were also good and hotel location is pretty close to city center. Overall we enjoy our stay...

I had a wonderful stay at the Everest Hotel as it feels like an oasis in this bustling city.  Especially the very friendly and competent staff at the reception made my stay very pleasant.  From the friendly welcome, the well-kept room, a restaurant recommendation of the charming Usmita and the friendly farewell, my stay was very pleasant.  I would love to come back.

The food was awesome,The staff(Himal) recommended an omelette and the cheese omelette was delicious. He is friendly and nice. If I come back to Nepal again, I will visit here again. If anyone visits Nepal, I recommend The Everest Hotel Thank uuuuu

I believe,it's the staffs,hospitality and cleanliness that makes hotel stay more pleasure.loved spotless cleanliness n hospitality. As I have mentioned before also,the location is the heart of hotel and it is located in the heart of city.I truly recommend hotel everest for business or family trip,if it is to kathmandu.All the amenities n facilities here is the best value for money.

My stay at The Everest Hotel, Kathmandu was excellent and comfortable. The breakfast spread is excellent and so are the staff at the hotel. Chef Rock star - Rakesh’s food preparations and services is delicious. He has always provided with the best of food during my entire stay.Chef Chinta Mani’s preparation of food was amazing. He has always been very kind to provide the best of meals. Radhika’s services during breakfast buffet was excellent. She is extremely kind and caters to the guest’s preferences and needs. Yashodha services were excellent too. Varsha, Kristi and Vikram at The Reception were extremely professional and ensured a smooth and comfortable check in services and stay. The Night Manager Siroj was professional and very efficient. Ensured the best of services. Thank you to all! - Kabir Lal

Our stay was great I had a comfortable stay in my entire stay. The front desk was very welcoming Barsha, Abhishek & Akit were excellent. I loved the service of Radhika and Himal they were friendly and served me amazing food along with great hospitality. Ms. Menuka did my wife’s birthday decoration so well. I really recommend this hotel.Thanks You all of you for making my wonderful stay.

Excellent and very fast services. Whatever you request you get on time. Food is very tasty. We enjoyed our stay at Everest hotel.  The breakfast is also very tasty. You will enjoy Indian taste here. The hotel is very nice and clean. The front office staff Sumitra and Barsha are always there to listen and help.
Amazing food and amazing service. Had a great lunch meeting. Radhika and Sushant treated us really well and made sure that we had everything we needed. Also served us food every now and then.

The staff is amazing especially Radhika and Subarna. The rooms are getting old… however still comfortable and you get what you need.Resturant is amazing, Chinese food is the best I have had in Kathmandu (also Halal) Location is amazing and can branch out anywhere.Keep up the good work.

Everest Hotel is always my preference hotel in Kathmandu, after gone through the renovation. It is really nice to be back there with the staff from door man, porter and receptionist still remember me. It's like a home away from home. The receptionist Lalana is excellent whilw supervisor Sumitra and few front office staffs are superb including the Front Office Manager Mr. Umesh Shrestha. Looking forward to be back again, good luck.
