Kathmandu roads are in horrible condition and that is an understatement .  The taxi ride to get to Gorkarna Forest Resort is enough to rearrange your entire spine. It is up and down through deep holes and over unbelievable bumps. Every time you want to go sightseeing in Kathmandu, you have to endure the unbelievably unpleasant taxi ride all because of the road conditions. It is only because of Kathmandu’s road conditions that I would advise against staying at Gorkarna Forest Resort.

Had a meal at the restaurant. Mutton curry was too salty but the meat was very tender. Mushroom curry was great. Service in general was great. Aruna was very customer-oriented and Pradeep is trying to be joyful in the beginning though was later missing in actions. That would have a four stars from me. Here is the reason why it is two stars.Our kids went on to do horse-riding. I was hoping to use a drone to capture it. The hotel staffs were trying to tell me that it is not allowed so I asked for the rules and how to apply for permit. They have asked me to wait for the security manager to explain. When I saw someone come out from office I repeated my question where the rules and how to apply. The staff who came out is Divas Shrestha. After explaining my questions he doesn’t seem to understand and just bluntly asked me with a smug if I want him to call the police. To that I asked if he is threatening me. So his team found the website for me and upon reading it I pointed at the link for the permit form to request for printing, he replied this is beyond the hotel service. Eventually I printed myself. I thought it was hard to blame if he is the security manager. To my surprise his name card says front desk manager. For a hotel of such great facilities and all, it is important to train the managers before asking them to handle bigger tasks. In fact I thought his staffs at least handled it with a smile.

It was a beautiful stay there because of its huge space. Swimming pool was indoor. The golf course was huge which is the biggest asset of the place. I loved the restaurant space where we could hear live music ( Classical ). Because its a forest resort  expects monkeys roaming around , and at some point there is a possibility that they snatch your food if you are having your food outdoors. Overall beautiful place although commuting to the place can be a little challenge as the roads to the way are not great.

The two standout features here are the staff and the physical environment. It is well named because it is truly a forest retreat away from the intensity of much of Kathmandu. They also have a good golf course which I played with some rented clubs. For any golfers coming to Kathmandu as a jumping off point to hike if you can I would suggest to add a day and come play the golf course. My room was comfortable. Good bed and the room was very clean. Two staff to note are Bandana Khadka who greeted me at reception and showed me around and Dolma Sherpa who was working in the dining services area and was very good to talk with and attentive. I would stay here again.

So we were a large group of 41/42 people and had 15 rooms... I must say this was an extremely average and over hyped place... Servife was extremely bad , I have never ever seen anyone ever presenting a bill before serving food!! The buffet would always get over before the end time... The quality of food absolutely terrible and and sometimes not even cooked properly!! The staff here is trained to say no for everything... if you ask for something as simple as a glass of water or green chilli in the restaurants they will minimum 15-20 min and that too after many reminders... They want to only charge charge and charge.... even the use of Jacuzzi for residents is Rs.1000.00 per 15-20 min!!!

As far as accommodations in Nepal go, this has got to be one of the best—even though it primarily caters to the US and European crowds. One advantage it has compared to the Yak and Yeti, is that Gokarna is situated on a golf course, high above the polluted and bustling city of Kathmandu. Plus, there are hiking trails beyond the golf course that meander through a heavily forested area, where deer and birds are plentiful. The staff is charming and all of them greet you with a beautiful smile and Namaste. There is an attached spa with steam and sauna—making it the perfect place to unwind after trekking. And— the food overall was very good, including the gigantic breakfast buffet with a “made to order”omelet bar to boot.  The rooms are quiet and huge—beautifully appointed with Nepalese and Tibetan antiques and art.  My husband and I spent two very relaxing nights there before our trek and two more with our pals before heading home to the US. We found it incredibly convenient to leave our extra clothes and belongings safely at Gokarna while we were trekking. We would happily return.

The hotel is dated, the staff jaded, and the food inedible.  Highly suggest the staff (and / or the management) go and visit some decent properties in locations similar to what they have.  The property itself is a gem, sadly everything else falls terribly short.The one bright spot (beside nature):  the internet connectivity = it was excellent pretty much everywhere.

Gokarna is a welcome reprieve from the bustle of Kathmandu. A tranquil ambience sets your mind and body at rest.The golf course is wonderful - be prepared for lots of 3 putts as the greens are very slow.

The Gokarna is what we wish all hotels could be. It is an oasis of clean air, cuckoo birds, monkeys, stags and jungle. Everything that Kathmandu is not. The staff is outstanding- universally. Outgoing, anxious to help in any way. Rojin is an exceptional manager. His team is incredible.  Norbu Sherpa, Doreen, Sabeena, absolutely everyone on the staff genuinely is there to help and wants you to be completely happy. The restaurant staff, spa personnel, golf staff, cleaning and security staff are all committed to serving their clients in the best way that they can.The rooms are spacious, immaculate, and well supplied. There are two restaurants each of which are great. The one in the hotel recently got an Indian trained cook and the Indian food was a real standout. The golf course Chinese and Thai restaurant rivals the top tier found stateside.The facilities are broad. The spa offers excellent services, the pool steam room and sauna are awesome. I'm not a golfer but did play and it is not to be missed. What a course. The caddies were professional and found nearly all my balls, no matter how far I sent them into the jungle.My only complaint- the badminton court was eliminated since my last visit.I love this place of tranquillity. No better way to recover from the real world realities of Kathmandu.

I had rated this place 4 star previously. With the same hope i had again booked this resort at higher rate than usual. But i am highly disappointed by its service this time. 1)we were at the resort at around 12pm. We asked for early check in and staff told us that rooms were not ready and will call us once they were ready. We went to roam around but never got that call. Then we went to reception on our own presuming rooms were ready.2)A/c in our room was not working. We informed the reception about this 6 times. Every time they said they were looking into it but they never called us back. At around 6 pm and in our 7th call, we demanded for repair of a/c or change of room, They told us that a/c couldn't be repaired and asked us to change the room. Saying hotel is full pack, they provided us room in the next building which was not at all delux room we had booked for. 3)After that i lost my cool on the reception and  then they decided to give us the better room and offered us junior suite room, which was nice but still did not have bathtub.4)In the suite room, there was problem with hot water supply...water went off while i was taking a shower and had to call to reception again for that!!!5)We wanted to order our dinner from the restaurant but the menu was very limited and price was hiked. So we had to change our meal plan on the last moment because of unavailability of our choice of food.Overall i am very disappointed with the degradation of service than before. In my last review i had written about non availability of masala tea which they had listen to and was available this time. But service quality, value of money and staff friendliness/helpfulness has very much declined.

Gokarna forest resort has beautiful rooms with plenty of space for leisurely lying about, a large television and superb bathroom. Whilst the room itself is above average, and the food from durbar restaurant delicious, the other aspects of the hotel's service are not as outstanding. To walk through the forest trails a guide must be hired, unless you have spa vouchers the treatments are very expensive and the presence of army officers around the reception area and the grounds has the effect of making one feel less - rather than more - safe. The greatest drawback of the resort apart from the cost of extras such as food and spa treatments is being unable to walk freely. This is promoted as a "forest resort", but guests cannot experience the full forest experience one expects.

we stayed at the Gorkana Forest Resort for 4 nights in November after trekking in the Everest region and it was a welcome quiet resort to relax. Hidden on a hill top in a forest above the noisy, dusty, hustle and bustle of Kathmandu. Our room (229) was plenty big enough for all our luggage with a large bathroom. The resort was very clean and offered  2 good restaurants and a lovely bar. The Bar and restaurants all had a wide variety of fresh meals and the bar makes a very good Espresso Martini! Service by all staff was excellent and all staff were always attentive and very keen to help in any way they could and always with a fresh smile.The bathroom was clean however the shower fittings were showing a few signs of age. We would not hesitate to stay here again when and if we return to Kathmandu.

Spent three nights at Gokarna Forest Resort after a gruelling trek through the Annapurna ranges and it was a wonderful experience.Rooms are large - we had the bonus of a balcony, the beds very comfortable, the bathroom was well appointed, clean and very western (a huge plus after staying in mountain guesthouses for the past 5 nights). The staff extremely friendly and helpful.Room service was quick, delicious and incredibly cheap.My only complaint is they lack variation in menus, as both restaurants had the same food, which was slightly annoying as the menu isn't huge.

resort is nice , away from city, good hospitalty , staff is extremely nice specially women staff , restaurant is average menu options are  extremely limited ,normally i expect a lot of variety in a 5 star , pool water is not temperature controlled ,rooms in the main building are good, overall it was average experience  staying at gokarna

I was there to conduct a team building program for a team of 25 people and was amazed with the friendly staff they have at their resort. Very helpful and friendly. I would definitely recommend this resort to everyone.

This is a very nice resort and I have stayed here several times, but this time there was a new twist --mountain bikes for rent.   So I and a friend rented two of them.  Now, where to ride?  There are no extensive roads or trails within the resort.  The longest stretch of road is less than 1km coming in from the entrance and it is rather steep.  So we asked where to go.  We were told that although the main road is busy if we turn right outside of the resort there was less traffic.So off we went.  The first short stretch outside of the resort (also less than 1 km)is ok, graveled and pave with almost no traffic.  But once we hit the main road it was a nightmare.  Busses, heavy-laden trucks, motor bikes, potholes, piles of sand, cows all going both ways or no way.  Besides, the dust and diesel exhaust was so thick that it was hard to breathe.But that was only the half of it.  On the first hill, my friend went zipping past me at a frightening speed --- the back brake on his bike was not working.  Later it turned out that the seat would also not stay up and that the gears were also not working properly.After less than ten minutes we realized that what we were doing was both very unpleasant and very unsafe.  We walked the bikes most of the way back to the hotel and informed the manager on duty what had happened.  We also suggested that they suspend rental of the bikes.As usual in these cases the response was "Yes sir, we will consider that and mention to our management".  The next morning the bikes were still there and the rental signs were still up. In my view, this was clearly irresponsible.   Given our experience the rentals should have been immediately suspended.Besides that, as I said.  It is one of the nicest places to stay in Kathmandu --JUST DO NOT RENT THE MOUTAIN BIKES

Gokarna forest resort is not just another resort, it's an amazing resort situated just about 20-30 minutes ride from Kathmandu city. Very peaceful environment and away from cities hustle and bustle. This resort offers many activities for kids and adults too. And one and only resort in Nepal (I think) offering huge golf course..and driving range for kids too..service is nice..it never fails to welcome us back..if you are around Kathmandu city this place is a must stay if you want to skip the hustle hustle life of KTM City and you will not regret it!

We stayed twice at this hotel. The first room was large, but had not been updated. The second room was on the second floor in the main complex and was lovely. Wifi was iffy at best. Food was good - all buffet.

Gokarna resort is located in such a peaceful location where you can hear birds singing and monkey playing around. If you are looking for natural plus quite stay little outside the kathmandu then this might be your perfect choice. Food is outstanding specially thai and Chinese restaurant serves great food plus the view is breath taking. Very friendly staffs in all the departments but specifically the lady at Durbar restaurant during breakfast hour ms. thering and reception incharge Ms. Tashi  were outstanding and provide excellent service during our stay. Stayed only one night but it was truly memorable.Highly recommended resort. Thank you  and Namastey Samuel

Mixing business with pleasure,me and my wife, we both chose to stay in this place for its seclusion and sprawling green environment.Though initially until arrival we were not informed about the change of our desired accommodation booked,we would like to extend our kudos to the hotel staff and especially Tashi who took immense care in ensuring that the alternate arrangement was as per our likings.All of the hotel staff incl. security personnel were very courteous who never failed to greet us without a smile.After a strenuous travel and meetings,we both tried the spa which turned out to be one of the best till date and is highly recommended.The Thai Restaurant with the sprawling green golf course at its background was a delight.The rooms are aesthetically decorated and compliments the surroundings.We were so impressed that we had to cut short our visit to other places in Nepal to come back once before we leave Nepal.A fall back place for us in Nepal for sure and is hugely recommended.

A place which talks about beauty and luxury, a place which makes you feel like home - Gokarna Forest Resort! Been a traveller and have stayed in the best of hotel chains across the world , I would not hesitate to say that this Resort is the best one so far and shall always remain forever young in my heart. No doubt its a very beautiful property with all the modern amenities but what makes it precious is the people working for this resort. All the 5 stars offers luxury but Gokarna stands out because it makes you feel like home . Each and every one out there ensures to cater to make you feel comfortable- right from the front desk to the housekeeping ,one is greeted with warmth and smile. I would really like to thank each one of them specially Tashi & Deepika and there was another lady whose name I couldnt remember. Tashi - how much I appreciate for everything you did ,you left no stone unturned.Deepika with her smile ever willing to assist. Can never forget you Tashi!Everything was taken care and I had the best time of my life. The spa is brilliant must say . I wouldn’t hesitate to say that it is excellent and I liked it more than Anantara signature spa which I took last month in Dubai in Anantara spa &resort. The thai restaurant overlooking the golf course is so serene and food was good too. Don’t forget to try out the Nepali thali in their main restaurant .However couldn’t do the forest walk for it was raining in Nepal that time but it too should be great.All in all I would say, my heart goes out for this resort.

My first business visit to Nepal and it was certainly a pleasant experience and the one that I will remember always. Warm greetings from staffs each time they pass by you. The peaceful area away from the hustle and bustle of the city. It made it look like Gokarna was a place far away from the city, up in the mountains but in actual fact, it is just 10-15mins away from Thamel Street.Worried about the condition of the hotel at first but however, upon reaching the hotel we found it was safe and very much functional. It made us forget about our tiredness from the flight and coming back to Gokarna every evening after business dealings was the highlight of my day. Gorkarna will always be MY CHOICE of hotel whenever i'm in Kathmandu!

Excellent base for 8 day business trip to Kathmandu. It is on the outskirts of town so that's a half hour to the centre by hotel car or taxi (recommend hotel car service which is worth the only slightly more expensive rate, and for 350 rupees/hr they will wait in town). Hotel shuttle is only once a day in each direction and only to Thamel. But Kathmandu is noisy polluted with a lot of traffic and at the end of a long business day it was wonderful to return to Gokarna. Gokarna is perched on a forested hill at the edge of town. Staff excellent, every one, no exception. Lasta at reception was particularly helpful as were her colleagues. Their driver Arjun was wonderful! as I had to spend a day in Sindhupalchok and the hotel arranged a 4WD and Arjun skilfully navigated the hectic traffic and damaged roads without any fuss. He had worked 11 years with the hotel. Dining was a pleasure, loved the Thali. The bar and restaurant staff were great. So agreeable and helpful. Never got to use the spa or yoga class. Another day. Given it was postquake, the internet service was very good and I didn't notice any power cuts, where as at meetings in town hotels they were regular. I stayed in room 363 in very solid building only 5 years old overlooking forest. Very solidly built low rise resort. Felt two aftershocks there and was no problem. Monkeys in the morning with their babies were a delight to watch from my room and in the garden. Beautiful mature trees and well tended gardens. I felt very fortunate to escape here at the end of each day.

My wife and I stayed at Gokarna Forest Resort prior to our Mt. Everest Basecamp Trek and after. We were extremely pleased with the location, on the outskirts of Katmandu, and amenities, restaurants, food, lounge, even golf, that the resort offered. Being a forest resort we were able to experience the monkeys and deer that live on the property. We have only positive comments for the wonderful, caring staff, everyone from the management to the service staff. On our return stay to Gokarna after experiencing the earthquake on Mt. Everest we were relieved to see the same friendly, kind employees who we know had suffered personally. We were staying in beautiful, comfortable, safe accommodations and many of the employees were living in tents due to the destruction in Katmandu and you would never know it by the care and compassion that we were shown. Words cannot express how grateful we are to one employee in particular, Tashi. With all of the confusion with the airlines and flights after the earthquake, Tashi went above and beyond in helping us secure our flights back home to Canada. We would highly recommend Gokarna Forest Resort to anyone looking for accommodations in Katmandu.

It was our nepal visit after 6 years. Couldnt  be any thing better then this hotel to start our vaction. Excellent location away from kathmandu city good food good service.....  friendly staff Going back for sure :)

Gokarna Forest Resort exceeded all our expectations. Arriving with family including ages from 6 to 70, our needs were varied and all catered for very well. Daily early morning yoga classes, complimentary for guests, eased us into the right frame of mind to experience Nepal as it should be. The guided forest walk, even the 1 hour option, took us high up into the tranquillity of the forest trails - we saw birds, monkeys and several families of deer – magical. The spa was lovely – the signature Himalayan massage more relaxing than anything experienced in luxury hotels of Dubai or Thailand. Indoor swimming pool was relaxing but décor a little tired and the changing rooms could have been cleaner. Pony/horse rides available for kids and adults based out of the hotel’s stable a few km away, which come to the hotel to collect their riders.All of the staff: reception, bell boys, even the security guys around the resort (who carry catapults to deter monkeys from coming too close) are super friendly without being fawning. Lasta and Abha in particular ensured our comfort, and Ranita in Durbar restaurant made us, and especially our daughter, feel very welcome. Highly recommend the atmospheric Hunter’s Lodge restaurant and Nepalese tasting menu for at least one night in any stay. A cake was organised for a birthday celebration, a much appreciated touch. The hotel bar is well stocked and comfortable with obliging staff and a pool table.On the day of an unexpected national strike, we expected everything to be more chaotic, but with very little notice the staff did everything to ensure that we were happy and busy, organising a special ‘green number plate’ taxi to take us on an excursion out of town – in this vehicle we were not bothered by anyone. A free shuttle to Thamel in the city was useful on one day, and Lasta organised private excursions to Nagarkot, Bhaktapur and the temples around the city, and gave knowledgable recommendations for a first time taster of Kathmandu’s many splendours.The place has a unique character that you just don’t find in international hotels, mostly down to the people, but also the solid architecture and fittings, and quirky touches (large brick built bath tub in some rooms). Note - rooms on the 1st and 2nd floors of the main building are only accessible by the elegant stairway. Bills itself as an eco resort, and the bathroom flush certainly seemed determined to save as much water as it could (!), although the shower water pressure more than made up for it.It’s charming, pretty, and convenient enough to visit the city, but far enough away to breathe fresh air.

I played this Nov 2005 when I climbed to base camp for my 60 th birthday . While I wouldn't say the course was great it was interesting and probably much improved now . Don't think the hotel was built then but it's set in a lovely country setting . anything would beat the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu .

Absolutely love this place!  Staff is amazing--they do everything they can to accomodate and please their guests.  I have no idea how, but when we checked in we were greeted by name!  Gokarna is all about service.  3 restaurants all extremely reasonably priced and 24 hour room service will meet all tastes--extensive breakfast buffet with the best omelet station, terrific Thai and Chinese restaurant as well as Nepali and Indian food.  Plenty of Western options for those who need it, both veg and non-veg options.  Rooms are moderns, spotless, with upgraded granite baths with plenty of hot water and gym quality water pressure, flat screen tv, plenty of outlets that accept multiple plug types.  They have free transport into Thamel, a short drive away.  Resort is located just outside Kathmandu, but feels a million miles away from the noise and the hustle and bustle of the city as it is located next to Gokarna Forest with a reknowned golf course complete with plenty of deer and monkeys.  Grounds are expansive and lovely and they offer a variety of forest/cultural walks as well as personalized day tours.  It is wonderful to spend the day sightseeing and then come back to great food, peace and quiet--no barking dogs or honking horns to keep you up at night.  Just keep the windows closed so you don't have unexpected monkey guests entering your room.  I would not stay anywhere else in Kathmandu.  I truly felt pampered and cared for.  Most important, I did not worry about my 16 year old son wandering around the resort alone.  Even after I left Kathmandu for Bhutan, I received an email from the night manager wishing me a good trip and thanking me for staying with them.  Great value for the price--you won't be disappointed.

We spent 4 nights here after trekking. It was great to just relax in very comfortable temperatures in the grounds. Lovely spacious room from which we watched the monkeys play. The food was delicious and varied. We ate in the main bar, Durbar restaurant and in the Clubhouse restaurant. Breakfasts catered for all tastes and service was exemplary. In fact all staff from the cleaners to the manager were very friendly and had time for us. They even assisted me to use the internet when I needed it to solve a problem with my suitcase! Generally the free internet was slow when everyone else was using it. Lasta particularly attended to our every need. The yoga sessions were very interesting and inclusive but it was a shame the teacher arrived so late on the third occasion that I had to miss that class. The swimming pool was a reasonable size for a hotel and very clean. Plenty of clean water offered to drink. We enjoyed the Forest walk led by the charming Bekass (Spelling?) who took us through to the old village of Gokarner, where there were no other tourists, to view the temples.  The shuttle service took us into and collected us from Kathmandu very efficiently in about 30 minutes. An excellent  stay.

A true oasis with extremely friendly and helpfull stuff especially after visiting the sights of KTM.  Great location, beautiful spacious room - the monkey warnings should be taken serious - . We had great service during dinner at the club house, very few people find the way in the evening, therefore we had two perfect private dinners. Service at the bar was not always as prompt as we wished our drinks to arrive but with free WiFi. There is a  free shuttle bus to Tamel

Beautiful Nepalese styled resort and grounds.  Harmony Spa was fabulous.  Food and Service was great, especially Ranita who really took great care of us.  Lots of activites on property, but also lots of areas to just relex.  Front Desk and Concierges were so friendly and helpful in making sure we were enjoying ourselves and making arrangements...especially Abha and Lasta.  Thanks so much, we truly enjoyed our stay!

I stayed there for a night. Very nice staff and service. Rooms are good and spacious. The best part about this place, is that it is away from the hustle bustle of the chaotic city. Always request for a room in the main building if you don't prefer walking a lot, specially during the nightBeing a nature lover and a wildlife photographer, i went for morning forest walk. The forest is beautiful. Don't expect animals. We hardly had any sightings. The forest walk has to be done for the morning experience in the misty woods and to be one with nature. Posting some of the pictures i took during the morning walk.For more pictures,  https://www.facebook.com/SashidharVempalaPhotography

Looking forward to a stay at this peaceful resort away from the bustle of Kathmandu but disappointed with the room in a block 10 minutes walk from the main Hotel, not ideal for returning in the dark. The room was not at all like those pictured on the website, would advise requesting a room in the main Hotel. Buffet meals OK, nothing special & staff not over pleasant. Overall very disappointing.

We were put up at Gokarna for 3 days for a conference. The resort is a little away from the city but is self sufficient. Has a golf course, a trek, can rent mountain bikes and bike in the property, spa, indoor pool etc. The service was exceptional! Very friendly receptionists and everyone there were very professional and made our stay very memorable. The food is of exceptional quality as well. Every meal tasted delicious. They also have a BBQ night on Fridays.Even when they resort did not have a car to ferry us to the city, they arranged for a cab, negotiated the rates down on our behalf, without us asking them.I want to especially thanks Ms. Abha who helped us with whatever we needed....thanks.Positives: Staff, rooms, resort estate, food qualityNegatives: far form the city, so getting transport needs planning.

We arrived by Taxi (about $7) from Thamel in Kathmandu and It was like coming from the ridiculous to the sublime. The resort is beautiful, with tasteful decor all over, and every detail (almost) is perfect. The rooms are spacious and well decorated and appointed. We were warned to keep windows locked because of the possibility of monkeys entering and attacking the mini-bar. We looked out to see deep grazing. A tour of the property showed us the lovely and charming older building, the well-appointed spa, a children's playground, and a beautiful golf course. Also a choice of restaurants with varied menus. After a nice lunch outside near the bar, we went for a guided forest walk. We saw numerous deer and monkeys, and enjoyed the calm. When we arrived back at our room, we opened the door to find it had been ransacked by a monkey, who was sitting in the open window chewing on some of the food we used to have. The room was a mess, but other than food nothing had been ruined. The mini bar was also ransacked! The housekeeping staff was there in seconds, and they cleaned up the room quickly. We were offered, and decided to switch to a different room. A suggestion that when the staff escorts the guest to the room, they check the windows. The housekeeping staff should do the same when they finish service. We assumed they did - we had never touched the windows.We ate dinner at the bar, then realized the menu would be the same at the restaurant next to it. Service was slow but we were in no hurry. It was very comfortable. We also made use of the business center to print some documents. Wifi was available only in the bar but worked well there. Throughout our stay the staff went above and beyond to make us comfortable and well accommodated. There is a shuttle once a day each way back into town, but a taxi is not too expensive.

We spent three nights at this hotel in October 2014 before flying to Pokhara for a trekking trip and an additional night on November 6th upon our return trip from Pokhara.  The setting is quite and the grounds are lovely, and we enjoyed nice rooms on both occasions.  The rooms, though decorated nicely, are dark - there are many lights, but they don't provide sufficient light for reading.  Also, there isn't an outlet for a curling iron in the bathroom - I used the outlet at the mini-bar for mine.  Hotel staff were very friendly.The hotel lobbies and halls are decorated beautifully with nice furniture and art pieces.  Especially nice are the floral petal arrangements floating in water - just beautiful.  We ate in the bar on the first night, and the service was so slow, that we vowed to never eat in the bar again!  Breakfast was very good, and on nice days was served outside, which was very pleasant.

The hotel is clean, quiet and situated very conveniently for any experience in Kathmandu. The rooms are comfortable, and very well looked after. The food offered in any of the outlets is freshly prepared and beautifully presented. In the main building musicians play most evenings, and the standard of playing is very high. But the main strength of the hotel is the care and helpfulness of the staff. Nothing is too much trouble. They will organise outings, suggest places to visit, or just give talk to you and give you information you might need. I would definitely recommend staying here.

The hotel is the best one comparing with the Nepal capital hotels according to place, view, room size, staff, food and activity.  I'm advising people to try the forest tour to see jangle live and monkeys.  In this hotel you feel like you are living in a image not real.

The location of this hotel was a nice break from the Kathmandu chaos. They have good services with net & clean room, housekeeping did a great job cleaning my room every day.  I'll have to say that the best quality of this hotel was the customer service. Every employee was extremely helpful and very courteous.

We stayed there for one night in June 2014. We had booked 4 rooms. Reached late in the evening. The bell boy left our luggage outside of the rooms and went. Rooms having central air conditioning were noisy and the other rooms had too many problems to start naming. One of our rooms was spectacular with a brand new air conditioner and no issues at all. Toilets were spacious and modern.  Breakfast spread was good. Room service dinner was very average. Don’t expect 24 hour service. Only visit if you are a golfer because that is the main charm of this place. The property is very far from any public transportation so you need to have your own vehicle. It is not advisable for tourists to Kathmandu, more of a weekend getaway for the locals in Kathmandu. Staff in the morning time were a complete contrast than night and very helpful. Overall the place is nice if you are there for the right reasons

I had gone there for a night away from the hustle of Kathmandu. I got the bookings after a lot of persuasion. Bang!!!  When I landed there, I found out that it was full because of a wedding reception being held there. They didn't care to inform me of the same at the time of booking. And then they give me a room on the lawn where the reception was being held so as to make sure that I don't miss the noise of Kathmandu city. Atleast they could have given the room away from the site. One of the wedding guests could have stayed there. The TV cable was not working, the telephone line was not working. And despite my complaints nothing was taken care of as everyone seemed to be busy with the wedding reception. But ya the property was good. I'm sure if I land up there on some other day they might be able to serve me better. Guys make sure to find out the occupancy before you check in.

Kathmandu is a wonderful, chaotic, crazy, polluted city. And we really loved it!  We were looking for a hotel at the end of our trip that we could play golf and be away from the pollution. Unfortunately, GoKarna is still in the pollution. GoKarna is great from the moment you arrive.  The employees are well trained and speak great English. The hotel appearance is very nice and luxurious for Nepal standards. Our room was not ready when we arrived, so we went to the hotel bar to enjoy some snacks.  The food is fantastic on property. We enjoyed mocktails and some Nepalese cuisine.  The breakfast also received 5 stars for us. Once our room was ready, we were a little disappointed.  The room is very large, but they are old and desperate for renovation.  The best part of the room is the window area to view the monkeys.  I heard the rooms near the main lodge have wood floors and are a little more modern.  The rooms in the hunters lodge had the worst pillows we've ever slept on.  They were so puffy that I felt more comfortable rolling up the towels and sleeping on those.  Not having a comfortable night sleep is very high in my 3 star review. I could deal with the not so modern room, if the bedding were more comfortable.  Also, like most places in Nepal, the electricity goes out while they are booting up the hotel generator.We also played golf. It was a lovely course, full of monkeys and wildlife.  It is a real shame that the pollution problem of the city affects the experience.  I would rate the golf course quite high, if I felt I could breathe better.  I even enjoyed the local caddies, which I often do not.  The landscape of the forest is spectacular. Lastly, it is important to note the hotel is located a good distance away from town.  They have a great (free) shuttle service that takes you to and from Thamel.  However, if you want to go anywhere else the hotel car is 1600.  Otherwise, you will wait 30-45 minutes for a local taxi to arrive.  In my opinion, the hotel is good if you would like to be isolated from everything else around you or if you are enjoying a Nepalese golf vacation. (But bring your own pillow) If you want to enjoy the surrounding areas, prepare to pay a good amount in taxi fare.

best resort seen still now, very impressive, spacious, exciting and always something more to know.place is out of city which is the only concern but overall experience for self and family is very satisfying. best golf course and helpful staff. lot to explore and good food

We stayed there for a weekend, two couples and one infant. The location is really nice, immersed in lush green and mature forest, perfect for walks. There is also the golf course for those into the sport. Overall the experience was nice thanks to the location, room quality and very friendly and competent front desk staff. Our downside is that the two restaurants have much way to go to be at any level of quality service especially when considering the premium they charge.We ate at the club restaurant and it took more than 45 minutes for 3 simple tuna baguettes and one paneer. Mind you, there were at most 3 tables so this is not because of coming at a busy time. We then had dinner at the main restaurant and here it was really bad, the food was tasteless, hygiene left much to be desired and the service was extremely slow and poor. A normal meal for 4 set us back over 11,000 NPR, which is a steal in any restaurant in Kathmandu.On the positive side, when i reported the dissatisfaction to the front desk, they were very engaged, took notes while being apologetic and promising to take the issue up with management. All in all, the place is great but they must really address the restaurant aspect as it is otherwise a shame for such a nice place as the price/quality ratio is simply not there.

I was there for one day conference in Kasturi Hall which was very delightful. The view from the Hall was amazing.The location of the resort is very charming. The hospitality of the resort is very good. People are very helpful and friendly. We didn't played the golf but we enjoyed watching others playing. At last, the internet service was quiet impressive though the resort is very far from the valley. We enjoyed a lot and planning to spend a night with my friends.

Overall great stay.Great food and drink selection. Room were huge in size and comfortable.We tried horseback riding, which was ok. Nice fireplace in the bar, very cosy to sit in the evening. We liked :)

The Gokarna resort is situated on a hill among a verdant forest on the outskirts of Kathmandu.The tranquility is second to none, and troops of monkeys and herds of Samba deer roam the grounds  of the hotel willy-nilly. There is also a golf course as part of the property. the staff from top to bottom were very friendly and courteous. The rooms were spacious and despite its age well appointed. The food was of a very decent standard, and all in all the whole 3 day experience was very enjoyable.

Used the resort for a very short stay (2 days).  Use the Darbar and Hunters Lodge for dinner.  Excellent food.  Breakfast was standard fare.  Used the car service if the hotel for local travel, and it was excellent.  Recommend this place heartily !

We stayed at Gokarna for 2 nights, everything was really good, the room was comfortable and clean, the staff were very helpfull and the service was good, meals were top class with a wide variety of choice, breakfast buffet was also excellent, we really enjoyed our stay here and can highly recommend Gokarna Forest Resort

To stay here at the end of a long trek was absolutely perfect.Excellent service, quality all round! The grounds of the resort were picturesque with a golf course and a forest/ jungle at your doorstep.

Excellent property Delicious food Great hospitality shown by the staffIcing on the cake was golf club and spa. Really want to call-out Ishov and Rajendra for the great experience we had during our stay.

WORST HOSPITALITY EVER!We chose this place to celebrate our Valentine’s day and were planning to stay for a couple of days but on our first night there, the toilet fell apart when I sat on it because the hotel is so outdated and needs to work on a lot of updates.I have multiple cuts on my feet, my thighs and my butt.We called the hotel staffs to bring the first aid kit and to explain what had happened.The staffs came in and out a couple of times but  did not bother to bring in the first aid kit.The staffs were worried about the broken toilet more than the fact that their customer was injured and bleeding. After making few more calls, they finally sent us a first aid kit and none of the staffs were qualified to clean up my wounds. They brought in the first aid kit and just left.The toilet had broken and i had to pee but the staffs were not prepared for a situation like this so they kept on discussing god knows what instead of moving us to another room immediately. They were not even sorry about what had happened but instead they kept on insisting that their supervisor makes a strict inspection before a guest comes in, and that the toilet was fine before we moved in and that their supervisor had checked the toilet seats before we moved in.This accident could have been taken as an accident and we could have stayed there as planned but the hospitality we received was not acceptable. They don’t care about the customers.The hotel staffs did not offer us to move us to a different room till and hour or so, they were all panicking and moving in circles. We had to ask them to move us to a different room ourselves because i had to pee so bad, they finally took us to a different room but the room they moved us in was a twin bed room, then we had another discussion to move us to another one.I was so upset about all that had happened they did not bother to even compensate for it so we left and i am still injured. We had plans for the stay and to spend some good time away from the city but it turned out to be a disaster. I will forever be scarred for this.Definitely the worst hospitality we’ve ever received and i am sure that nothing can beat this.We paid 15,000 for the room and 22,000+ for the food, DEFINITELY NOT WORTH.
ツアーで行ったためホテルには夜中にチェックインし翌朝６時に出発し朝食はお弁当持参だった。部屋も広く清潔感もありスタッフも感じがよく、ユックリとホテルの良さを味あいたかったが残絵だった。

As a property Gokarna Forest is a wonderful property, but it needs some improvements as the Mattress over the Bed are of Spring and are very old, very difficult to lie down whole night with spring Mattress as the centre part of the Mattress goes down whereas sides are up!!! As far as food in concerned for the breakfast Darbar Restaurant is fantastic, where as in the Farm Restaurant in spite of our orders of the food 3 hours before dinner the food turned out to be very messy. to add on the experience of the SPA it is not to the mark of international standard, we felt that it was not a massage but they were fighting with our body and applied as much pressure they have in their body, not at all appreciated and we rate them as very POOR.

In need of a make over. Looks like the hotel has not been updated since it opened. The breakfast is terrible and the hotel is in need of a clean. The bedding was disgusting, grey, old and didn't fit the lumpy mattress. It is over priced. We had better food and bedding in some of the tea houses in the mountains.On a positivenote, the bar is pleasant and the massage was good. The hotel reception staff were helpful.This should be a 3 star hotel and lower it's prices.

As part of a trek with Yeti Mountain Homes, my husband and I spent a total of three nights at Gokarna Forest Resort, one before beginning our Everest View Trek and two nights at the end of the trek. We were very happy with our room and delighted with the choice and quality of the a La carte menu included in our package. The location of the resort, away from the hustle and pollution of Kathmandu yet close enough to easily access for day trips is ideal. The hotel grounds are indeed a relaxing oasis. However, the best thing about Gokarna is probably it's staff, who cannot do enough for their guests. We really enjoyed our stay.

Comparing to price service was very uncomfortable breakfast of 5 star hotel was so funny. Bed was so small old furniture... Awkward behavior for nepalese. So many activities in websites but nothing available at same time. Receptionist lady was so amazing when we said we want two rooms, lady questioned us do you know the price of room i felt so weird.

Enjoyed our two nights here. The staff are friendly and helpful and the room was beautiful. The food is good and breakfast on the terrace in the clean fresh air was delightful. A member of staff shoos any straying monkeys off, and whilst we were there we did not see any at all despite being warned about the problem.The grounds are quite and peaceful.The building is atmospheric with beautiful furnishings and photos of the Himalayas.

maybe the best place in kathmandu with regard to being away from the dirt and grid of downtown. the half hour longer drive from the airport is well worth it.the rooms are clean, the service is friendly (despite sometimes language frustration creeps in..)bfast is excellent with i wide spread. dinner at both places are excellent.wifi works and there is even a foldcourse streifght out of the door.only the gym is dated and stuffy.

This family-friendly resort is among the best places I have ever stayed in and visited in my life, it's so nice to live between deers, horses, monkeys, birds, in the resort located out of Kathmandu on a Golf course surrounded by forests, people can live there for more than a week not going out of the Resort with no bored Management is doing its best to make guests happy and always asking guests for any room of developments or improvements which I really appreciate in the horse riding, covered swimming pool, SPA, Golf course, chasing deers on Golf car and many many activities are really amazing, I and my family definitely will go back I need to learn so,      Pashupati get ready 😁

Sadly after 10 days in heaven in Nepal I’ve finished my trip in a 3 nights stay at Gokarna Forest Resort, after I’ve been recommended thats its one of the best hotels in Kathmandu. Ive booked the tower suite (one of their best premium suites). From outside the hotels needs serious renovation, old stairs, smelly carpets.... the suite wasn’t that bad, though its hard to reach, very firm mattress, no bathtub... but the service was so bad. On the first day, there was no hot water to shower and it took them almost half way to fix it. The second day there was no water at all 😂😂😂 and it actually took them half day to fix the pipes. On the third day the room service kept me waiting for clean towels and for water bottles till afternoon (and thats of course after giving them my one hundredth call) and on the last two days my TV signal went off 😂😂. The best experience actually are the monkey who keeps you awake at night because either they’re fighting on the tin rooftop or because they’re plotting how to get in the room..Ok, back to our loveliest stay, every restaurant lack hygiene, every cup and every plate has prints and old food remained on it. To find a diet Pepsi there is like digging for oil.For breakfast no food varieties, and the pastries are very dull. Every time we wanted to book an activity there (cart ride, horse back riding...) it wont work out for i dunno reasons, and it always end up by recommending me to go for a forest walk though they are leaches.And the funniest part they keep asking you how was ur stay, and when i answer them not that good, their answers was ohhhh did you report it?!

I had taken ill just before getting to Nepal and after looking on Tripadvisor decided on this hotel instead of the one in the centre of town For us it was a perfect decision the hotel is quiet the air is much cleaner than in town. Service and staff were all wonderful. After our trip to Pokhara we chose to stay here again on our return. If there might be a downside it would be traveling to the tourist sights as the roads are really terrible In my opinion this was not a problem Should we return to Katmandu this would be our hotel of choice

After our trek to Base Camp my daughter and I had three nights here and it was the perfect place for good food and pampering. The massages were the best we’ve ever had and every member of staff was attentive and helpful

It was the service levels and the warmth of the people that wins you over... coupled with the fact that it is an awesome property and the weather was great. We had a conference of over a 100 people but the way the hotel managed each of the guests, it was really a case study for hospitality industry... great show team.

Good food and ambience, clean rooms and courteous staff. The place has a driving grange for those not fully committed to golf. Other activities include jungle walk and horse back riding. Be Careful of monkeys and deers though :-)

A quiet, forested resort just outside of Kathmandu. Offers excellent food, indoor pool and spa, golf, and plenty of trails to take walks through nature. They even offer a guided 2 hour nature walk for $10.00

Have just enjoyed a most enjoyable stay at the Gokarna Forest Resort. It truly is an oasis amidst the bustle and busy-ness of Kathmandu. The staff - from the Front desk to the drivers, from the waiters to the cleaners, were unfailingly polite and professional.It is a 45-60 minute drive from the more popular Thamel area (over bad roads) but it was worth the commute.The amenities- walks through the forest, yoga, heated swimming pool and excellent spa made me regret not extending my stay.The wifi was at times erratic but mostly worked fine.Suggestions:1. Ask for a room that faces outside and not the courtyard if possible.2. The Front Desk very helpfully can arrange a Mountain Flight  (including transfer to and from the airport) which you only pay for after the flight.This was a tough week for this remarkable establishment as its owner was killed in a helicopter crash on 21 February. Despite this, the staff made us feel welcome and very comfotable.Highly recommended.

I loved my experience in Gokarna Forest Resort, a beautiful historical building on the outskirts of the bustling city of Kathmandu.  This was my first trip to Nepal and I wasn't too sure what to expect.  Lucky for me the staff here are so friendly and welcoming, especially as I embarrassingly didn't even know how to say "hello" in Nepali before I arrived.  Its "namaste" in case you're wondering ;)  While everyone I met was absolutely lovely, very professional and kind, I was especially well cared for by Kieran every day in the restaurant, and by Asha, the highly skilled massage therapist in the spa.  My journey to Kathmandu was for a work conference, and as I had not been well before I arrived I was taking things very easy.  The spa treatments helped enormously.  I felt so lucky to swim every day in the beautiful pool area, and enjoyed the food I ate, especially the delicious momo! The hotel arranged for me to have a driver to pick me up from the airport and then later to run errands in the city and to do some sightseeing.  As a woman traveling alone I was very grateful for this extra service, it just made things easier and I felt very safe (taking usual precautions of course, like any big city). The bed was very comfortable, nice sheets and everything was very clean, housekeeping are on the ball for sure.  I appreciate the efforts made to preserve water and to use ecologically friendly products in the bathroom, this is important to me and I am pleased to see hotels taking this seriously.  The only things that weren't perfect - and truly, they weren't an issue that detracted from my enjoyment during the stay - was that the TV volume was tricky to control (no big deal as I wasn't intending to watch anything really) and the mini bar fridge wasn't super cold.  Tiny details in an otherwise wonderfully relaxing week.Overall I had a brilliant stay and am looking forward to being able to return, hopefully for the 2020 celebrations...

We stayed at Gokarna for one night late October as part of a Luxury Escapes tour. We also stayed for most of the following day for which we payed US$100 for the privilege. On arrival we were upgraded to one of the resorts Tower suites. The suite was nice and huge, you walked up to the top floor and access to the suite was up a spiral staircase tucked away into one of the corners. Surprisingly the view wasn’t great from the suite as the walls rise slightly outside the windows and it’s not easy to see over them. We had 3 doors leading outside, 1 led onto the roof but was locked. The other 2 led onto the ledge (balcony) running along the windows but it wasn’t easy to get through the door and up onto this ledge and not attractive anyway as it was covered in Pigeon Poo. On 2 occasions we had large Monkeys come & look into the room, disappearing quickly when they saw us. One could only imagine what would happen if you left a balcony door open, the signs are not there for fun! We found the suite very comfortable and to be in excellent condition. The bathroom was huge & the step down tiled shower was more a large bath or even pool, it was enormous. The resort is old but it has been maintained well. We ate Dinner in the Restaurant, it was a buffet which we found to be varied and tasty. However, breakfast the following morning was not up to the same standard and we struggled even finding something to eat from it. It was very busy and somewhat resembling a feeding time at the zoo scenario. We noticed strong cooking smells in the restaurant & afterwards you clothes just reeked of the smell. I wondered if their range hood filters needed cleaning, the strong Smokey smell was not nice. The following day we ambled on down the hill to the golf clubhouse and found it very pleasant down there. We ate both lunch & Dinner at the clubhouse, with the Dinner it was lovely to watch the Deer & Monkeys playing on the greens just before sunset. Currently the road from the city & airport is under reconstruction and extremely bumpy & dusty. If you stay here you will have to factor the time taken to drive this road with any excursions you do, it is a terrible road. We enjoyed our stay here but probably wouldn’t return.

All of us really enjoyed our stay there, the whole ambiance and amenities makes the overnight stay  a nice gateway for families. The indoor swimming pool and the Jacuzzi was the highlight of our stay. The breakfast buffet is a nice spread with lots of choice and options. The staffs are nice and very friendly and overall we had a really comfortable and relaxing stay at the resort.

If you like The Four Seasons, you will like this place and deals are quite good in off season.Though a little dated in some areas, this added a feel of old world charm that I really appreciated.Got a nicer suite and it was large with beautiful local furniture and decor.Service is top notch, breakfast is good, large bathroom, fresh fruits and chocolates delivered upon arrival...basically I felt like a princess in a great novel.The grounds are gorgeous and my private roof top patio had some Monkeys visit. Don't feed them or leave the windows open!!! I just enjoyed them from within my room.Now I will recommend they invest in pillow top mattresses, at least for the large suites. Bed is really firm.Other than that I highly recommend getting the nicer suites, especially on your last day or two in town. I will be staying here again for sure!

Nice staff.. good food.. had to experience a/c breakdown after dinner.. staff courteous to bring extra blanket and the heater telling that it should keep us warm which it did not..No toiletries like shaving kit and toothbrushes...Water in bathroom flowing like the tank was never cleaned..Sore eyes after swimming ( may be its just me)..other than that it was a good stay!!

We were a group of 10 who were concluding a 7 day trekking experience. This property was to be the luxury experience before departure back to Australia. There is a sense of calm emanating from the property and its immmediate surrounds. In its previous history as a royal hunting lodge it certainly exudes a sense of privilege. There is a highly acclaimed golf course which guests of the resort have access to at reduced rates. The swimming pool and spa were very good and during our stay it felt as though it was ours. The rooms were spacious and well appointed. The lounge/ bar was well presented and very comfortable. The restaurant options were limited to two venues and the food experience seemed to be hit or miss. Whilst the a'la carte menu during our stay could not provide all the menu options. My main dish was excellent but others in our group,complained of their hot dishes being cold.A tip is to book a table in the bar/ lounge rather than the restaurant room as there is so much more atmosphere. The wine list is good but expensive. The service was first rate. One issue that our group thought needed to be rethought by the resort administration was the excessive charge of $10 us pp to have a guided walk around the golf course / grounds. This plainly a money grabbing exercise as the guides themselves relied on receiving a tip from clients. There are animals roaming the resort so there is justification to charge something however what is being charged is excessive given the low labour costs in Nepal. Breakfast was as you would expect from a resort hotel.

We had a great 4 day stay at the huge but beautiful Gokarna Forest Resort. The staff really does everything to make you feel comfortable and to assist with any request you have. The spa, golf and forest have everything to keep you busy for a couple of days. The restaurant is okay though we were happy to have eaten out in Kathmandu one night (a taxi is about 1000-1500rupis one way and takes about 30 minutes to reach Thamel, given the bad road conditions). The resort provides a free shuttle service at 9 and 11 to Kathmandu and back at 3pm.

Kathmandu is a crowded, noisy, dusty, chaotic city.  This hotel, in a peaceful, forested part of the city, is a very pleasant respite from the crowds and the traffic.  The rooms are very nice, the food is quite good, and he staff is capable, friendly and anxious to make your stay as pleasant as possible.  The hotel also has one of the few golf courses in Nepal. If you are looking for a lovely, affordable hotel that is removed from the frenetic pace of the city, this is it.

Great place to escape from the chaotic Kathmandu. Five star treatement bij all the staff, but the hotel itself is 3,5 stars at best. It’s overrated in case of room quality, clean and spacious but a bit out of date. Also the restaurant could use a make over. Reasonable food but overpriced, great service. Good breakfast, but not up to expectation. Quite good swimmingpool with sauna and bubble bath ( man and women apart). Beautiful golfcourse. Free shuttle service to Kathmandu ( once a day). If Thamel is to hectic for you I would advice this resort, but it’s a bit boring and surely needs an upgrade

Hi,  I stayed here last week for nights after spending 14 days on a trek to Everest Base Camp.  The resort was booked for us by the Himalayian Social Journey and it was amazing. Pros/ The welcome we received from the wonderful staff at reception,  who explained everything about the resort. Our room (123) was beautiful,  like an old colonial bedroom with all the modcons. We loved having the monkeys,  rabbits and the baby deer at our backdoor. The restaurant food was very good.  Well cooked and presented excellent. The prices for food and drinks are very reasonable for the quality and service. The Thai /Chinese restaurant was also great and service was top notch. Swimming pool etc was beautiful,  well kept with happy staff. The golf driving range was in top condition and very cheap to hit some balls. The Golf Course is amazing. I was going to play but I  damage my ribs on the way to Everest Base Camp.  I love golf and I will return here soon to have game.  It looked superb and in top condition. Cons / nothing.  It was just wonderful after spending 14 treking to Everest Base Camp and back. I would highly recommend this resort to anyone who goes to Kathmandu. It is a 45 minute taxi ride to the busy centre of Kathmandu but it so peaceful to stay at the Gokarna Forest Resort. A very happy couple. Scott and Hilary (Scottish)  living on the Gold Coast Australia

I have found this property more over than my expectation, very good for meeting and workshop. service and facilities are excellent. location is so beautiful and every facilities are comfortably managed during my visit. Staff are very friendly where es i had meet with Chef Sous Mr. Damodar Acharya and found him very friendly, dedicated and always ready for best service to customer. Wish for more progress to the entire team.

Disclaimer to start: this hotel was chosen for us as part of a tour we took.  Now, my review of Gokarna Forest Resort. This is not the place to be if you think you are heading out the door to shop.   Set at the edge of town, the setting is lush and green, peaceful and quiet providing a refuge from the dust and crowds of Kathmandu.  However, we were given a horrible room. Not knowing this from the start, we assumed this is what the entire lodge had.  The room was OK until you saw the others.  Additionally, we had a major plumbing problem that took the entire stay of three nights to get fixed and I'm not sure it was fixed, just time for us to move on. We had the pleasure of staying our last night back at this resort and had the good fortune to get a typical room which we found spacious and clean, modern and well planned.  Breakfast buffet was very good, better than average.  Dinners in restaurant were also very good. Staff was kind and professional. My husband had a massage which was very good.  The spa and pool were top notch.

Exceeded my expectations. Had to attend a conference in the city, but decided to stay here. It is worth the pain of going through grueling traffic conditions into the city just so that you can come back to this resort to unwind. In the midst of a beautiful forest reserve. Wake up to deer, rabbits and monkeys frequenting your backyard. Amazing amenities and will be back again.

This hotel exceeded our expectations.  It had everything!Staff....  excellentAmenities....  excellentFood.....  excellent.The only down side was the "dancing roads" to get into town. That wasn't the hotels fault.

Nestled in a forest but still close to the city, this resort with impressive Golf course is a delight to stay. The approach road from Katmandu airport however is bad ( it is under construction and hope current state of raod is temporary).  The Bar, Restaurants and Spa are of high standard.  Rooms and cottages are spacious and service is pretty good.  The Sue Chef takes lot of interest and talks to guests to meet any special need and is well experienced.  On some issue I wanted to talk to the GM but staff could not get him, I wonder what happens in case of emergency! the Golf course green fee is high even from international standard (Green Fee is about US$70).

A very surprising place in the valley. Beautiful interiors of the rooms and also the entire hotel. Lights and furniture were just perfect. Spacious bathroom complimented the rooms. Just next to the room was a courtyard where we could relax early in the morning. Food was great. Refreshing location. Just a perfect place to relax. Looking forward to next visit.

Beautiful Hotel with excellent location, clean and comfortable. I love the food, serene beauty of the place, the pool and gym and the golf course. Would definitely recommend this hotel to everybody! It's a true sample of excellent hospitality. Thank you again for the quality service.

Great  resort next to an excellent 18 hole golf course, rooms well equipped in a true Nepalese style, comfortable beds, tea and coffee facilities, good spa, excellent choice of 2 restaurants, friendly and competent staff, worth a stay

We stayed for 1 night as we had to return home the next day. We enjoyed most swimming. It helps that there is an indoor heated pool so our swimming would not be affected by the rainy season. The spa is great.

It was truly an amazing experience staying at Gokarna Forest resort with my family. As we reached the resort; the concierge were just there to welcome that made us feel special. We could immediately connect ourselves with the calm and soothing atmosphere around. We stayed in a room on the first level facing the courtyard, which was large with an extra bed already setup for our son. The room was meticulously designed to the aesthetics that best suited the character of the resort. The buffet dinner served at the Durbar Restaurant was delicious and the staff in the restaurant were courteous and we felt welcomed to be greeted by our names.We enjoyed the nature walk around the resort and our daughter enjoyed the children playground, while our son kept himself occupied at the pool.Thank you very much Gokarna Forest Resort team for keeping up with providing great value to your guests. This was truly a memorable and rejuvenating experience overall.

Set amidst lush green forests and a beautifully maintained golf course, this resort offers plenty of options to walk around. There is a great massage centre offering the most relaxing massages. It also has a little temple on campus with morning and evening prayers .... great opportunity to soak in the traditional Hindu rituals in a serene atmosphere.

Beautiful location.  Great service.  Good food.  Lots of choices for breakfast.  Located in a forest reserve.  Unfortunately, the roads to it are rough; but they are being rebuilt, so should improve.  If you want to be in the middle of the city, it isn't for you.  They do have a shuttle to town every day, though.The staff is super friendly and helpful.  Namaste!

Kathmandu has a real PR problem regarding cleanliness and pollution, but this place makes you feel its an oasis, even though its pretty close to the main city sites.Food was great, main restaurant was western, Indian & Nepalese, but the real gem for me was the Thai / Chinese golf clubhouse - which as a guest you have access. Please go to this early in your stay and have a look. The clubhouse overlooks the golf course and really is idyllic. There are a lot of steps / long climb down and what seems an even longer climb back up later on, but don't be put off. Spa was good, and the indoor pool was a bonus.Sauna and steam room are available.Gift shop appeared to stock an ivory piece, which is really disappointing. Inevitably prices here are beyond what you would pay in Thamel, my reference point here was the kukri's.Staff were really helpful and very pleasant. if you are booking any activities within the grounds make sure you fully understand what you are booking. The forest is available but maximum the forest only walk, must be guided, is 1 hour tops. All other walks will encounter villages etc. which is when you will see how close you really are to the noise and dust of the city.Definitely consider Gokarna if you go to Kathmandu.

We stayed three nights at the resort after trekking in the Himalayas.  We enjoyed the spa facility and the food was excellent.  The room was a very generous size and comfy.  The staff were very attentive and helpful.  We went horse-riding and enjoyed views of the golf course during our walks.  We felt completely rejuvenated.

Great place for a golfing holiday   The course is in good shape and challenging for club golfers. Try and get a good caddy and book him for all the rounds you play. The food on the golf deck is very good. Service is warm, hospitable and everyone goes out of their way to be helpful. There aren’t too many golf carts so be prepared to walk the hilly terrain - it’s really not that difficult. We will be back.

We stayed at the resort in March for, unfortunately,  only a couple of days. This was a heavenly oasis of peace away from dust and pollution of Kathmandu and its bumpy roads. Spacious rooms, great spa, gardens and golf course, good food, exceptional staff. Highly recommended.

Stayed at Gokarna Resort after trekking to Everest Base Camp in March 2018. An oasis in Kathmandu. The locale, accommodation and staff were absolutely first rate!!. Attentive and professional service, a good selection of food, well prepared and served and beautiful surrounding capped off this property.  The concierge in particular was extremely helpful.   A great place to get some TLC after base camp walk. Most highly recommend  this property.

Lindo hotel, excelente atención de personal recepción y especialmente la gente del restaurante. EL hotel tiene una decoración muy natural , habitaciones espaciosas y limpias, sus jardines son hermosos e invitan a relajarse después del día de visitas. la piscina interna, temperada con un SPA completo donde destacan sus masajes. Ojo, no cuenta con ascensores y en los pasillos es fácil ver personas extraviadas preguntando por la Recepción.

Gokarna is definitely a nice place if you want to just relax during the cold season: the rooms are nice, there is hot water in the shower, the sauna is ok and the swimming pool fun, even though a bit cold and moldy (and for some reason children, who love it the most, are not allowed). However, if you want to have a more active holiday, and you do not play golf, it is a bit boring since you are not allowed to go on your own for forest walks or roam around the (golf) fields (if you dont play golf). Maybe more suitable for romantic travel than for family travel.

My a day stay at this hotel has been very awesome. Got complimentry welcome and greet. I stayed in delux double bedroom, was very good at its price.  Everything inside is very beautiful and has everything you wished for. You even have restuarent of your choice and foods. I bet if you are in holiday and looking for place to stay, go for this hotel.

I stayed three nights with my family at Gokarna. It’s a beautiful hotel, with very spacious, gorgeously appointed rooms, and lovely grounds. Though you feel like you’re away from the chaos of Kathmandu, it’s within reach if you should want to visit the city or get to the airport. The food at this hotel is top notch. We ate in both restaurants (in the main hotel and in the club house down by the golf course) as well as in the bar, and our meals were excellent—better than those at the Kathmandu Hyatt Regency. We enjoyed the pool. We did yoga on the roof with a teacher at dawn. We had massages (which were good) and facials (which were not so good—they basically spent an hour rubbing lotion into our faces, though the menu promised “steam and extractions.”). We enjoyed the sauna in the dressing area. We also did a 2-hour guided hike, which was great. I’d made inquiries about us going hiking on the grounds without a guide, but the hotel staff told me that was forbidden for some reason that’s not clear to me, so we had to hire the guide. He wasn’t very talkative, but he led us in a loop that we enjoyed (and it was also a good workout). I highly recommend this place! Gokarna is charm and authenticity. It’s a lovely spot and the staff were great. Also, the monkeys! We loved watching them.

This resort is tucked away and with the roads it is not the easiest to get to.  However, once you arrive the place is very nice.  The rooms are large and spacious, they bathroom is huge and the shower is massive.  WiFi was dependable and usually fast.  The restaurant served good quality food and the bar, while a little over priced, was comfortable and the staff friendly. Speaking of the staff, they were friendly and helpful.  The grounds are well maintained.  Be aware of the "monkey thunder" where the monkeys will occasionally run across the rooftops and are quite loud about it.  Be sure not to leave your patio door open or the monkeys might pay you an unwanted visit.Shopping is available on site but are a bit over priced, as you would expect from any shop in a hotel.

The lovely receptionists organised a horse ride for me on the property, even though I wasn't staying at the resort. They were so helpful and the instructor was great as well. Beautiful horse and well maintained equipment. A lovely little ride through the surrounding forest, including trotting. Thank you so much for a lovely experience.

My family, partner and I stayed here for 2 nights after a 12 day trek to Everest base camp and back so you can imagine how stoked i was to stay in an amazing place like this. The rooms were unbelievable, the food was delicious and the staff were so friendly and always greeted you with a smile. There are cute monkeys and deer walking around the resort, a great golf course and a pool. I never wanted to leave. If you decide to stay here, check out the day spa, there are great massages at an affordable price. Will definitely stay here again if i ever decide to do a trek in Nepal again. Thank you!

After completing trekking this was the perfect place to rest and relax away from  the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu.  The resort and grounds are huge. We had a lovely room and an enjoyable stay, food was also good, staff very helpful, no complaints.

Nothing to do, pool is indoor and swim up bar hasn’t been used for years. Tried to do Paintballing and they couldn’t organise for the 2 days I was there. They lie and say things are included and they aren’t. Didn’t get dinner 2 nights like promised.

Stayed here after a long trek as a post hike wind down, and it partially achieved its goal. The rooms are nice enough, with a great pool, spa/sauna and other facilities.Breakfast is good, with reasonably fast (included) broadband, and service / food is pretty well priced as well. The surrounds are fantastic and relaxing, but if you try to spend more than two days here, you'll likely go stir crazy.The big problem is the location, and the road to get out to the hotel. Simply put, it is 45min of jerking and jumping around in the back of whatever vehicle your being transported in. Several people got car sick, and if you have a bad back / neck, you may receive several unexpected adjustments. Whilst this is to a reasonable extent outside of their control, the location is completely out of Kathmandu, and trying to do any tours or otherwise is a harrowing two way trip.To get a five star recommendation, only minor tweaks are needed, namely improvements to the luggage collection / check in processes, and some of the finishes need touching up.All in all, a good experience, but reconsider if you want to actually see Kathmandu

Just a few Kms away from the crowded Ktm valley, and close to the world heritage historic buddhist temple "boudhnath stupa", Gokarna Foresr Resort is a perfect place to relax.We got a reasonable rate for a night's stay (70 $ for couple due to festival offer), including breakfast, spa and swimming.The hospitality was world class, not to mention each and every staff who greeted us so humbly, every time we passed through. This should a great culture and professionalism they had built over time.The location at the restaurant besides the golf course was beautiful and the nepalese instrumental live show also was good.Only demerit was the food we ordered. The break fast was good. I heard that bar b que is also good, which they serve every saturday. So, I presume that they have good food during buffet, but when you order separate items, then it was not that good.I hope they consider this, to make Gokarna Forest Resort close to perfect.I will certainly plan to be there on my next vacation.Thank you.

Thanks a lot for receiving us like family! We have made your hotel as our go to for long breaks from work. It feels like home, as the staff always accommodate our request for packed breakfast so we can play golf.  🏌🏼🏌️‍♀️ early and also late checkout. Maybe you could allow more gadgets for your wifi?Happy Dashain 😉😊😇Leah and Volker Steigerwald

Best place to spend with family.i love the tummy full yummy buffet breakfast.Harmony spa is one of my favourite at this resort.My kid always gets excited to stay here.i will be soon celeberating my dashain vacation over there.Special thanks to Ayush Pradhan and Dikshya Thakuri.

Welcome end to our trekking holiday. Beautiful hotel set in manicured lawns, gardens and golf course. Service excellent, choice of food and drink extensive, rooms large and clean, staff friendly and helpful. Then the peace and tranqility is perfectly complimented by an amazing array of spa treatments, indoor pool, hot tubs, sauna and steam room. Perfect place to retreat from the hustle of Katmandu or rest up after a trek. My friends and I thoroughly enjoyed this little oasis.

This hotel was so luxurious and just the thing for after a trek I the Himalayas. Couldn't fault anything. Food delicious especially the dinner buffet! The beds were comfy and spa a great place to relax and unwind

Gokarna was wonderful!! The service, the rooms, the spa, the food - everything was great! Was there for 36 hour stopover after doing an Everest Base Camp trek and it was the perfect luxury unwind. Do yourself a favour.

This is a beautiful resort in the middle of the Gokarna Forest with lots of open spaces and green areas. The food is delicious, the barbecue in the club house was good. However, the cost is little high but we all know quality comes with cost! What I did not like is the toilet and bathroom, the commode is little high and it will be difficult for children and short people to use it, the wall of the bathtub is also very high and I almost injured myself while stepping into it. You have to be careful with the arrogant monkeys around the resort and he road on the way to resort is very bad.

The place is infested w monkeys, and the staff isn't much help. The food is oily n average. Location for people in transit is unfavourable as it took us two hours plus to get to the airport. However, Kumari in the main restaurant is an excellent hostess. Rooms are clean.

After travelling for 2 weeks in and around Nepal and Tibet, our last night was here at Gokarna Forest Resort and WOW, we only wished we had more than one night here.Our greeting from the staff was exemplary you're made feel like a VIP right from the beginning with pleasant smiles, warm soft voices and all very professional, a unique refreshing experience.
