Our host Rishma Lama gave us a complete description of the facilities and the entitlements of our stay and even called our room in the later afternoon to make sure all was satisfactory and that we were happy.Although the facilities are quite modern the building itself dates back to a more elegant time and its not hard to imagine yourself taking part in a black tie dinner or tea party here.Our room and bathroom was large, we enjoyed a soak in the bath after our very relaxing complimentary massage, just what was needed after sleeping on many very hard beds with very flat uncomfortable pillows.The bed was large too, pillows soft, the softest we had experienced in the previous 2 weeks hence we managed to sleep restfully and soundly for 10 hrs straight. The environment is very peaceful and relaxing and watching the monkeys can be quite entertaining.The buffet breakfast and dinner offered a wide selection of traditional and western foods mains, salads, desserts/pastry's all top quality and very tasty, no one leaves hungry.The Waiters, all Staff and Security (who would salute guests) were all so polite and cheerful, everyone willing to go above and beyond, so your stay was something special to be remembered.Whatever you decide to do in Nepal treat yourself to a stay at Gokarna for more than one night, you won't be disappointed.Thank you Gokarna keep doing it right!

Our travel agency booked us at Gokarna Forest Resort for a wind down after our 5-day mountain trek.   The check-in was effortless (well, after all the usual rituals, of course).   The receptionists were very professional and pleasant.  Also, the lobby guy was very nice.   I was looking for my room after checking in and one of the hostesses walked me there.  We had a wonderful dinner and the breakfast buffet is great...so many dishes to choose from.   All the dining room staff were ever ready to help and serve.Housekeeping and the bell hops were very quick to respond when needed.   And the rooms!   Need I mention the rooms?   They are very roomy and beautiful, it feels like home away from home.   Just make sure you don't open your windows, or you'll find some uninvited company (monkeys).The grounds are very well kept and you can't miss the beautiful plants that abound.We liked Gokarna so much that after we've checked out for another excursion, we decided to go back there instead of the previously booked hotel and stayed for 3 more days until it was time to leave Nepal. Although all the staff were wonderful,  Dikhsya Thakuri, especially, was so accommodating and made extra effort to make us feel comfortable and feel at home.   Her face is the one I see whenever I think of this place.   She would be a great face and ambassador for Gokarna.   Look her up when you visit.

We stayed at this lovely property at the beginning of May 2017. We were give a Club Room which had a huge comfortable bed, a sitting area, tv, mini bar, tea/coffee making facilities, a safe and a wonderful bathroom with a large powerful shower and a separate bath tub. It was an exceptionally comfortable room. The staff were very welcoming and could not do more to please us. This included the reception staff, bar staff, main restaurant staff and the staff from the Club House restaurant over- looking the golf course. The food at both restaurants was very good and well presented and breakfast was also very good and catered for everyone's taste. For wine lovers there is also an extensive wine selection. I would recommend enjoying a sun down drink at the Club House restaurant as the golf course is beautiful and it is lovely to watch the spotted deer come out and graze. This venue is also prefect for a leisurely lunch, during the evenings though it seemed a little quiet. We also did a short walk around the golf course and forest which was very pretty and we saw a couple of temples in the forest and the guide was really nice.We would recommend this property to everyone looking to be away from the busy city with its heavy air pollution, and will definitely stay there again on our next visit to Kathmandu.

We've arrived late around 4pm but still the room wasn't ready. But, they did gave us a late check out at 3pm as we've requested. The room is big and beautiful. The staff were very helpful. The food selection is great and tasty. Getting there was quite a trip with the roads under construction. So be prepared for a bumpy ones. While you're there, head to the spa for a massage. The masseuse are good. Really good! The resort is attached to a golf course if you keen to play. Overall it was a very quiet and relaxing stay.

What shall I say? Right from entering the premises and seeing the beautiful facade, we were in love.The check in process was quite seamless that we felt we were sleep walked through the entire process. The windows opened to the lush green outside and the room was cozy. What we needed at the end of a long journey to Nepal.Food is amazing and the staff are so polite and well mannered that every movement looked like a step from a slow dance form. The lawns were pretty with people playing Golf, I guess!Stayed only for two days since we were in transit for the Himalayas. But definitely will stay again.

We stayed there twice during a 17 day trip to Nepal...two nights at the start of our trip and one at the end.  We could have stayed there a week and would have wanted to stay longer.  They have a really great breakfast with a very good chef...excellent and attentive table staff with one named Manish in particular.  No problem with the water or food in any way.  Bottled water in the rooms though.  The rooms were very well appointed, clean and comfortable.  We stayed there in March and April of 2017.The resort has hiking trails, and a fantastic golf club dinning experience.  Easy walk from the hotel, and on the same property.  The Resort's elevation is above the current "dust" of Kathmandu (construction of roads) and on a clear day, you can see mountains.  Can't recommend the staff and resort any higher..we hope to stay there again.

I played my first round of golf at Gokarna Club in Kathmandu, Nepal in October 2014. This Golf Club is part of Gokarna Forest Resort. My older brother, KNS, lives in Kathmandu, who is member at this club.  So when I was visiting Nepal, he brought me to play one round of golf there. When I saw this course first time, I was kind of surprised and happy to see this beautiful golf course in Katmandu. The clubhouse was on top of the hilly area in between Hole #1 and Hole #18. Across from the clubhouse, I could see a fairly large nice putting green area. From the green, we could see a very nice view especially toward the 18th hole!I played golf with my brother and two of his friends. Four of us were playing and each had our own caddie. I never had my own caddie before.  When we play golf in the States, we usually have carts or sometimes we just like to walk for good cardio exercise.  My caddie was a very nice young man, very polite and gave me some good advice especially I was playing in this course the first time. I had good chat with him and I also took a picture with him.  The course was mostly surrounded by wood as well as they had some open areas, we could see herd of deer crossing in the middle of the fairways, and we also saw monkeys here and there in the golf course. I was not just enjoying walking and playing golf with my brother - but I was also very much enjoying the green golf course as well as animals - it was kind of an adventure and such a good experience!  The course was in little higher in elevation, so it reminded me of playing golf in Vermont. After the game, we had a nice lunch at the clubhouse restaurant. The food and service were great. After our lunch, I went outside again just to take a look at nice scenic view and I took some pictures.Couple of weeks later, I even received an email from the Gokarna Forest Resort where they asked me whether I had enjoyed the round of golf and good time there.  A very nice customer service approach, and of course I replied their email and said I enjoyed my golf round and I was very happy with the service as well.I also played another round of golf in 2016 with my brother there.  Every time I visit Nepal, it seems playing one round of golf with my brother at his club is going to be a tradition now - thanks to my brother KNS for taking me at this beautiful resort/golf course!

This hotel would not have been my first choice because it is a taxi ride from the city. However, I discovered that staying outside Kathmandu is not necessarily a bad thing. It's a $6 taxi ride to town and aside from the awful wifi reception at the hotel, everything was fine. After being in the crowded city, it was nice to be in a place with trails and green space. The room was large and had a sliding glass door to the outside where I could see an occasional deer or monkey. There are free outdoor yoga classes in the morning and the breakfast buffet has a variety of foods.

I really enjoyed my time in the hotel. Service was perfect. People were friendly and helpful, but not overwhelmingly so. Spacious rooms. The Spa center Is not big, but worth it (Himalayan massage is highly recommended). And the loveliest bit, considering the air pollution in Kathmandu is that this is one of the places you could breath.

Me and my husband were at the Gokarna resort in February for a wedding. Its a lovely property. A little away from the town so is very peaceful and serene. It has a beautiful golf course made by the David Mclaykidd. I am not a golfer but my husband is and he had two enjoyable rounds there. All the rooms are big and have nice views. The junior suite though very big is kinda dark and cold. We changed our room from there to a deluxe room which was comfortable and bright.The only thing that i would say was not upto the mark was that there was no turn down service. So if u had tea coffee in the room in the evening the dirty cups would be there in the room and you would need to wash them . yourself for the morning. Also the hot water pressure was rather low in our room and in the mornings at times there would be no flow. We had to call the housekeeping who did come promptly to look into the problem.

Apart from having lots of resorts and hotels in Kathmandu, Gokarna Forest Resort got its unique nature friendly resort with best in all. Having very nice rooms, ample area to walk and go around, nice foods and ofcourse spa and swimming areas are best on it. All Golf lovers will never miss this place as it has got huge space for this. I loved every moment while in our stay and if got chance would like to visit again and also recommend to others as well.

Relaxing forested retreat relatively close to Kathmandu (of course depending on traffic). Perfect opportunity to relax and have some spa treatments after trekking! The staff were all very welcoming and hospitable! Also the wifi works well!Only issues are that it's not centrally located and is a popular venue for weddings so it's very noisy with party guests. Also we had pre-booked transport (as part of a tour) back to central Thamel in Kathmandu and they organised a dodgy unregistered 'taxi-driver', who didn't know the next hotel's location nor understand English.Recommended for a short stay.

We traveled for two weeks in Nepal with 3 overnight stays at this hotel on 3 separate nights in three different rooms. All three rooms were very restful large rooms, nice bathrooms, great staff, good food. The every morning breakfast has incredible variety. A tip-- ask for pressed coffee if you don't like instant Nescafe. Also have a drink and/or meal outside on the terrace by the bar.

Gokarna is a peaceful retreat on a forested ridge. Rooms are large, well appointed and clean. The resort has a golf course, full service spa, restaurants and bar (including a fireplace) and the best gift shop too!The entire staff is professional, friendly and most helpful. You are always greeted with a soft-spoken, "Namaste".We cannot emphasize enough how much we love Gokarna. It is simply one of our favorite places to stay in the world!

We spent two nights in the calmness of a surrounding forest and golf course almost in the heart of Kathmandu, just a few hundred metres away.This is a first class resort with the amenities of a golf course, with views of ice capped peaks along the fairways, surrounded by forest populated with herds of deer and monkeys.  Hard to believe the proximity to chaotic Kathmandu.  Add a spa with heated pool, Jacuzzi, steam room and Turkish bath leading to massages.  All done tastefully and with minimum fuss.Meals are hard to fault with extensive buffet breakfast, excellent dishes at golf 19th hole and full on restaurants if required.  Rooms are spacious and well appointed.This was a welcome retreat having just completed an arduous trek to Everest Base Camp.  The staff could not have been more helpful.

Beautiful resort, spacious and nice room, big bathroom. Breakfast buffet with a variety of dishes and wonderful service. I had a very relaxing stay. Located around 40 minutes from the city, but that is not a problem at all. They have many activities organized.

Nice hotel and a good reprieve from the dusty noisy city. Food was good. If you have time, the forest walk is worthwhile. The grounds are beautiful. Lots of monkeys!The massage was reasonably priced and good. The bathrooms are modern and clean. Staff was very pleasant.

This place could be amazing but feels somewhat mismanaged. Things feel dirty and some repairs are in order. Breakfast was a disappointment with only instant coffee. The spa had a bad smell and dirtiness of the hotel itself continued. Dinner options are very limited and the place is very far from town if you need a change from the food.We had high expectations since we paid for a junior suite and were left disappointed. There are nicer places in town to stay in. This place is good if you are interested in golf, I guess.

Great place to be..Superb hospitality...Such a nice food and a good environment.Staffs are really nice and polite with always nice smile in their face...DEEPIKA SHRESTHA and RISHMA LAMA from the reception were fantastic..Many thanks to them...

We stayed at the hotel with an organized tour.  The hotel is on the outskirts of Kathmandu so it is very quiet, green and has wild monkeys that roam the grounds.  The hotel is nice but don't expect a five star as you would in the US.  You have to adjust your expectations.  Compared to the other hotels we stayed at in Nepal it was one of the best, but the rooms were not spotless.  The food was just ok.  The staff and the Nepalese people as a whole were just delightful.  They offer wonderful massages at the spa that you shouldn't miss.  If I went back to Kathmandu I would stay at this hotel again.

Gokarna Forest Resort has beautiful and peaceful enviroment. The rooms are very comfortable to stay. The view from resort is such a beautiful. There are many facililites too such as golf, swimming pool and many more facilities to enjoy. Ya its a beautiful place to visit and enjoy the facilities around here.

We stayed at this breathtaking resort for our honeymoon. The location is secluded in the forests outside Kathmandu and boasts the only 18 hole golf resort in Nepal. The staff are the friendliest I have ever known and the rooms were spacious.

We stayed two nights at this lovely resort. Our warm welcome on arrival was an indication of the friendly staff at Gokarna. The room was excellent with a great view and huge bathroom. The food service was first class. We soothed our senses at the Harmony Spa which we highly recommend. Definitely put this resort on the top of your list when coming to visit Kathmandu! Karen and Deborah - Australia

Excellent Property, very courteous staff always willing to help with a smile on their face. Food is excellent, WiFi good, has a golf course, spa. Rooms are spacious and modern. Bathroom had a big square tub as well.

Stayed for 3 nights post Everest Base camp trek. Building : needs a small bit of work interior wise , can tell its a bit old (90's feel). Staff: Excellent and probably the best thing about the place . Helpful to the end , amiable and genuinely nice people throughout. Amenities: Pool , average at best , cold , dark and appears old . Changing area is nice , but again it needs something (maybe just to be painted or better kept). Gym : old machines could be upgraded , but sufficient as a hotel gym I guess . Bar : great pool table , food is nice , good place to chill it . Breakfast buffet is good . Golf course : it's a nice course , hilly and long , but again just needs to be kept a bit better , the range is the same , everything needs a lick of paint . Room: stayed in a suite , bed was very comfortable, the room was very spacious and comfortable , good tv channel selection , mini bar is pretty useless and decrepit. 2 balconies : monkeys knocking around , was loving it ! The bathroom , the shower was amazing ! General : this hotel I'd say was beautiful a decade ago , it just needs a bit of a look at from an interior design perspective. I stand by the 4/5 , the staff were fantastic , the place just has a nice vibe , it was very easy to relax in and just stroll around. The wildlife milling around had me interested all the time . I would go back .

We had a great time at Gokarna last week. The staff were friendly and extremely supportive. The Jungle walk was very nice though it could have been a bit longer. The food at the Thai / Chinese restaurant besides the Golf course was very tasty. The Golf Course by itself was beautiful and the best I have seen so far. Special thanks to Tashi Dolma at the front office.

After staying in the heart of Kathmandu to visit friends and places, it was great to step away from the city environment - but not too far - and be surrounded by greenery. The rooms, the staff and the garden were amazing. I suggest asking about forest walks, horseback riding, and bird watching as soon as you arrive. If a large group or event occurs while you are there, it might not be possible to take full benefit of the surrounding area. Also: don't forget your swimsuit for the pool and Jacuzzi.

We stayed at the Hyatt when first arriving in Kathmandu and on our return from Chitwan we are staying at the Gokarna. When returning from Bhutan we will stay here again.  Hopefully things improve.  The Hyatt and the Gokarna should not be rated as both 5 stars. The Gokarna is at best a 4 star. The A/C isn't working.  We have  had to remind and remind and remind for all requests. Asked for a quiet room and were put at the road- basically the noisiest location.  To be fair, when requested we were moved. Everyone is very nice and friendly but the place is tired and has none of the appointments or service standards of the Hyatt or a 5*Wifi is extra, there are no face towels, no bath mat, no robes and the room is just worn. There was mildew in the shower and the shower leaked. Our room was tired to say the least. Since it had been rated as the Hyatt as a 5* we expected something comparable. It is not. Not even close. Hopefully in a few days when we come back we will have a better room and overall experience.  A Canadian couple

All rooms were well maintained, The staff was extremely polite and shown the best servitude ever I saw. The WiFi is free on the first day of stay and the remaining days are payable, this is very unprofessional in comparison to the other hotel standards. Overall the say was memorable and fantastic.

The moment I step out of the Taxi I wish I had booked longer and knew that it was literally only 15min from Kathmandu.Honestly, if this is what Heaven looks like, I dont mind dying.Its breathtakingly beautifull.We were made to feel like special guests and VIPs the whole 3 days of our stay.1. The room was so spacious, quiet and had HUGE windows overlooking the forest. Room 166. Even had a table and chairs outside our room if u want to sit outside and eat.The toiletries they.provide is well thought out. Shaving cream and shavers (I know I have forgotten mine more than once) toothbrushes and toothpaste, and conditioner..something not every hotel thinks of giving you.We made use of their laundry service, our clothes came back so beautifully ironed I didnt want 2 pack it back into the suitcases.2. The staff were the most caring people Ive ever met at a Hotel. We stayed in a few hotels calling themselves 5 star even here in Dubai, but this hotel's service is 5 star.3. They cater to your every need.My husband fell ill shortly after we arrived. He was really sick with a fever.They were so worried and caring. They got the dr out. They kept asking about his condition. When I went out for a walk they had sent a platter of fruit (cut up so that he doesnt have to) to our room, knowing he havent eaten anything.Tashi, (guest services) got us some medicine for him on the 1st night without having to ask her.I was never made ti feel alone even if I had to sit alone in the restaurant or bar, the staff, especially the a la carte restaurant staff- from the waitresses to the chef, came to talk to me and enquire about my husband.Even the porters.There is an Ala Carte restaurant and there is an Asian restaurant and then the 8848mnt bar and restaurant.I loved that the Asian restaurant is on the golf course and suurounded by trees.The spa was so relaxing. I took a spa package that included a Mani and pedi, a Himmalayan massage (wow) a deep cleanse facial and a meal. (NpR 9000)There is a sauna, steamroom and jacuzzi you can use for free. The last night of our stay I was sitting alone at the Mnt 8848 bar (named after Everest) and received a complimentary dish from the Chef.On a Friday and Saturday thet have a band playing on the grounds.I was sad to leave, but I will ensure to come again and stay longer.You dont know that there is power cuts, as they have sufficient generators it seems. When the lights went out it was for a few seconds and then came back on.There truly is nit 1 bad thing I can day of this little paradise.I asked to visit an orphanage and Tashi made it happen, she even accompanied me to the orphanage.Nepalse people are truly Ambassadors for the Human Spirit.

The perfect choice for your stay in Kathmandu. This resort was our welcomed respite after a full day of sightseeing and shopping.  Our room was spacious with a large comfortable bed.  The shower was wonderful!  Plenty of hot water too.The menu in the restaurant included some typical American foods along with tasty Nepal foods to choose from.  Breakfast is an American type brunch along with local cuisine. Free WiFi is available but usually only found in common areas and not in the rooms. A wedding was taking place one day.  What a beautiful celebration.  The bride was so friendly and happy to take a picture with me and allowed me to take pictures of her and her family. There is a gift shop on the premises with a wide variety of gifts. Cashmere and Pashmina is reasonably priced also. So for last minute gifts or if you forgot to pick up something in town, the gift shop is there for you.  There is a spa on the premises that offers a variety of services. I opted for the 60 min massage.  Wonderful.

I have visited this place twice in last 6 month and it was great stay both of the time. Room was big and clean and in my 2nd visit i booked the room with balcony and bath-tub and this room was way better than of my 1st one (Photo attached). Breakfast was lavish with many options but tea/coffee was below average (Please provide nice coffee/masala tea). Dinner was not was per my expectation. To be precise, Nepali food was not as good as western food and menu was limited. They had temperature controlled swimming pool and we could use Sauna/Jacuzzi anytime. Staffs were also nice and humble.  Hotel needs to work on list of Don't like don't step on grass/don't dip ur feet in the swimming pool, etc. Overall great experience!

A tranquil getaway which is close enough to Kathmandu to get to but far enough to avoid the hubbub and frenetic activity of the city.  The grounds, golf course and forest surroundings are scenic and very pleasant to walk around.  The Nepali people are incredibly hospitable anyway, and almost despite the hotel going for a more professional level of service, it is easy to just love the staff here.  Only point for improvement is that some information on our online booking was not captured before our arrival.  Minor point - very quickly remedied.

Gokarna is a wonderful place to stay! And only 30 minutes away from all the chaos in Kathmandu/Thamel. It is a beautiful forest type resort. With nature walks, fabulous horseback riding through the hills and local communities, golf course, incredible spa services. The entire staff was incredible and went above and beyond all expectations! The rooms were warm, clean, spacious and everything worked! If you are ever in Kathmandu, or close by, I highly recommend staying here!

This hotel is far from town on over 400 acres of forest.  The space is lovely with gardens, green space, outdoor seating for relaxing or eating, and even a golf course.  Rooms are spread out so you get the feeling of space.  The staff is well trained in every area.  The gift shop in the hotel is a super place to shop with good prices.  The rooms were very large and well designed and appointed.  The bathroom is enormous with a large tub/shower and lovely towels.  The restaurant was very good even during the fuel crisis.  The hotel has fabulous art everywhere so be sure to notice.  An art tour should be available,  Wifi is only available in the bar area, a surprise.  This is a lovely place to stay.

We went to stay after a year of our wedding here and it was again really amazing experience. The friendly staff and Managers were very welcoming as usual and well trained and well behaved. We had a lovely time seeing everyone and everyone remembered us. They were not serving the full menu because of the fuel crisis but it was understandable. The golf course has been maintained in excellent standard.

An excellent resort in a beautiful setting near the city... Staff at the hotel were very good and efficient. The resort is certainly better than any other resorts near Kathmandu. Special thanks to Mr. D Sherpa...

I cannot say enough about this resort. Very modern inside with a look of old Nepal on the outside. This classy resort and golf course is something you would not expect in Nepal and a wonderful surprise.The staff are super friendly, tending to all your needs. The food is amazing, considering this is a period of fuel crisis, you would never know it.The rooms are clean and well maintained, beds are very comfortable with an ambiance of modernity.The golf course is amazing...even with all the monkeys and the deer running around, it does not take away from the game. I will come back for sure!!

I stayed in Gokarna Forest Resort with my wife and two children for one week. The resort is set in a beautiful forest only 20 minutes from the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu! It includes first class facilities including the golf course and the spa. There are good choices of quality food in three different restaurants and the food price is very reasonable. My son was highly allergic and the kind chef made a special dish for him every day. The hotel didn’t even charge us for that food. You can only find this in Gokarna Forest Resort!  The hotel transport service was also very good and not costly. The most important of all were the friendly and helpful staff. They did everything in their power to make us happy and comfortable. The stars of the show were Tashi and Lasta at front desk and Tshering in the restaurant.I highly recommend this hotel. It is value for money!

A weekend work retreat took me to this resort, and it was a nice escape. Rooms are LARGE and tastefully decorated. Nepalese handicrafts and photos throughout the hotel are a nice touch. The spa/ massage was excellent, though a touch over priced by other hotel/Kathmandu standards. The Saturday bbq was fantastic and well worth the additional charge. The staff were fantastic. For a special treat book into one of the two tower suits - gorgeous. On the downside, the room smelt a little damp, but once I opened the door and let in some fresh air this was ok. The hotel is very very busy and so it wasn't possible to check in until the afternoon even though we had an early morning arrival. The large numbers of people using the pool, left the cleanliness off the pool a bit questionable. The only free wifi is In the bar.

This hotel is amazing. The hotel and grounds are world class. Green and peaceful, very relaxing. Beautiful.  Well kept. But most amazing is the staff and the service. Truly world class.  We were volunteering in Kathmandu for almost 2 weeks following the earthquake. The staff greeted us by name everywhere time we came and went. Fantastic to feel at home when so far away. The food was fantastic, Nepali classics and western food as good as it gets. I even had a great grilled cheese one day!  The quake did not seem to effect the hotel and it definitely felt safe and sturdy. If you need a beautiful place to stay in Kathmandu, go to Gokarna. You will be very pleased!

The property is a bit outside of Kathmandu city, and it is the perfect location. On the former hunting grounds of the King, it is a very relaxing setting and a great location for game spotting, playing a round of golf or do some easy hiking. A spa is on the hotel property as is a pool, so perfect possibilities to refresh, relax and rejuvenate.

My wife and I had some business in Kathmandu giving the situation and all the devastation from the recent earthquake we are very pleased with our decision to stay at Gokarna. This is not our first visit the Nepal and we found that the hustle and bustle of downtown Kathmandu was too distracting when trying to relax. Our first visit we headed up to a hill station which was very nice with amazing views of the mountains however the drive was long and the roads were a bit sketchy. Gokarna is minutes from the airport and allows you to still enjoy what Kathmandu has to offer with the hill station feeling.STAFF - extremely helpful, knowledgable, and pleasant you would not even know that outside their lives could be completely in a state  disaster outside of their work.ROOMS- They are very clean spacious with great views of the courtyard. The rooms have all the amenities that you could ask for however please remember this is Nepal and the power sometimes goes out briefly not more than 30 sec during my 3 night stay.Golf Course- Very well maintained with a challenging layout. The greens are well kept and placed to challenge most golfers with a double digit handicap, the fairways are tight forcing you to play a conservative style or risk loosing a few balls in the water hazards. There is plenty of wild life roaming around (monkey's, deer and birds). Once again courteous and knowledgable staff in the club house and they have everything that you may have forgotten club rental, balls shirts, tees, hats, sun screen, gloves and much more. Spa- The spas is very professionally operated clean and well maintained. There is a nice variety spa choices for both men and women I had a after golf massage which I must admit was very relaxing and stretched out my sore muscles after playing two rounds in three days lol.There are other amenities here that I never got the chance to explore like hiking, horseback riding, mountain biking. Shopping is available for the last minute gift that you forgot to pick up.The bar is well stocked and is decorated very nicely with local Nepalese live entertainment in the evening.The scenery is simply peaceful and relaxing with wild life roaming around mowing the grass (deer) monkeys climbing on the buildings with security attempting to chase them off (makes for great entertainment after a few cold pints)We will definitely stay here whenever we visit Kathmandu I highly recommend this beautiful oasis amongst the chaos of the city.

My husband and I stayed at Gokarna Forest Resort in Kathmandu for 1 week at the beginning of April and 1 week at the end of April including the day of earthquake and 5 days after it.Gokarna is a gorgeous hotel located on the outskirts of Kathmandu in a beautiful lush forest.Our first week was truly relaxing holiday, room was spacious, comfortable and very quiet and we sure enjoyed beeing spoiled by all of the wonderful Staff. Our second week started with an earthquake. We do not have enough words to express our gratitude for the genuine care and concern we were shown during that time.The Staff and Management worked very hard , some of them staying for 36 hrs to provide everything needed. Special thanks to Ranita, Abha, Tachi, Laksa, Tcheering, Krishna, Sugarshan, Rama, and the rest of staff the names are not mentioned but they  were equally important. Your attitude , hard work and moral will always be an inspiration.We are looking forward seeing all of you again in a future

Nous étions à Kathmandou le jour du séisme. Nous tenons à remercier vivement toute l'équipe du Gokarna et son manager qui ont fait preuve d'un grand professionnalisme.Nous n'oublierons jamais leur accueil chaleureux, leur disponibilité , leur souci de notre bien être alors qu'ils n'avaient aucune nouvelle de leurs proches. Encore merci !

I enjoyed my stay here for 4 nights.  The place is quite serene,  surrounded by lush, jungle like garden.  Love the many monkeys that roamed the estate.  The interior is beautifully decorated.  Lots of Buddha statues.  Lovely water containers topped with colorful flower petals everywhere.  The rooms were spacious and elegant with comfortable beds. The Nepalese/Indian food from 8848 MT. BAR & Patio was well prepared, normally salty for my taste but if i asked for low salt then they came out perfect.  Buffet breakfast has many selections but genenally ok, not great.  Good service from staff.  Enjoy the morning yoga.  Great to have the daily shuttle to downtown Kathmandu with stops along the way. The only minor gripe that i had was the flushing of the toilet.  It took me several tries and sometimes it just didn't work,  it happened in one of the rooms i stayed in.  I told them about this but seemed like there was nothing they could do.

Excellent and friendly hotel willing to help and accom date. Excellent she peaceful location out of the busy city. Only one code per wifi so a bit tricky when you have to devicesBut a lovely and friendly resort

An excellent retreat from the hussle and bussle of Katmandu.  Clean, spacious rooms. Very peaceful (unless there happens to be a Napelese wedding taking place on the lawn!).  Staff very friendly with good intentions. A litle short on things to do - and everything is charged as an extra.

Wonderful resort right in the middle of jungle and on top of the hill.A golf course is added advantage.Only problem is it might gets boring after 2/3 nights of stay. If you are an activity seeker like bird-watcher, safari, hiking then this may not be the place. But one night or two nights stay will give you enough fuel for your daily life ahead. Restaurants are so so. Not very delicious as they supposed to be. We find Gaya in the kathmandu downtown is much more delicious option.Breakfast items are plenty. Not very heavy though. Just usual stuff.Service is superb.Ambience and interior of the resort are so calm and peaceful. That's the main reason we have stayed in this resort for three times now.Very expensive also :)

Gokarna Forest is about half an hour away from the airport and we were collected. As we had planned to stay in central Kathmandu for the rest of our holiday, the hotel kindly transferred us at no extra charge. Central Kathmandu is exciting, busy and bustling and for us this was a perfect foil. giving us the best of both worlds.Taking breakfast on the terrace of the new club house overlooking the beautiful golf course was a lovely way to start the morning. Very friendly staff .  Very relaxing massage in the spa. Totally different holiday for us

We stayed here as part of a 16-person tour group and were treated very well. I especially want to say that the staff was very courteous, efficient and friendly, including the security force men outside; I think they were there more to ward off the monkeys than anything else ;-). Food was excellent, if a little heavy on Chinese fare. Lots of facilities here--spa, golf course, etc.--but these didn't take away from the feeling of being in the forest with its spotted deer (and monkeys!). It's just close enough to Kathmandu proper that you don't feel isolated, yet far enough to escape the hustle and bustle; a taxi ride from town one evening cost us approximately 8 USD. There is a village nearby that you can walk to without strain and forest trails to take. Overall, a restful, clean and beautiful place.

This place is a complete contrast to downtown Kathmandu. Rooms are spacious some with stunning views of the surrrounding Himalaya's! The bath in my room was big enough for a race horse if you happen to have one with you.  Indoor pool is great (race horse exercise) golf course looked excellent (if your horse likes golf) We hired mountain bikes and explored the local towns (you could ride your horse) I was here on business but would pay to go back.

Having stayed at this resort a couple of times this time it was cold during the evenings and mornings but during the day the weather was perfect. Walked down to the Clubhouse on the 18th hole and enjoyed the sunshine and a few beers. The hotel accomadates every class of tourist and is great for the area. Bar food was good and the breakfast was good for the area.

This is primarily a beautiful Gleneagle designed 18 hole golf resort near Kathmandu.Earlier the approach road was pathetic but things have improved.The final climb to the hilltop resort is through a lovely winding road through forests.If you are lucky you will notice deers,both spotted and deer,in the premises specially in the greens in the evening or early morning.There is a nice driving range.The climb down to the club house is through a fleet of steps through scenic beauty.The first view of the golf course is heavenly.The food at the club house is average.The golf course specially the greens are top class.Some of the tees are located atop small hills.Overall a 18 hole game is good exercise for the body and soul.The nearby resort with loud music specially on weekends is a poor distraction.The stay in the resort rooms is very comfortable.The bar and restaurants are adequate.There is provision for yoga and you can also do a nature walk with guides.The Hunter lodge has been turned to a restaurant serving Nepali food.Overall an excellent resort and an escape of the madness of Kathmandu.The architecture is very quaint Nepali and impressive.Ideally you should have your own vehicle to be at this resort as communication otherwise can be tricky.Disclaimet:This review is mainly as a golf club member though I have stayed at the resort in the past.

The Resort is really peaceful and comfortable. I was very pleased and happy with the customer service. Specially Abha was really sweet and her hospitality was great. I would highly recommend this resort.

Me and my family just checked out on 9th Jan 2015. This is the place whre you can check in but do not feel to check out.Staff hospitiality wore supper , very help full . out door activities are great. It is the place where you feel you are at the lap of luxury.Food is great. only thing i found lack of room amenities whre they need to look in to.I recomand GOKARNA to family looking for holiday and those looking for peace place.We are difinately coming back to Gokarna on our next visit.KARMA Namgay MERCURY BHUTAN TOURS AND TRAVEL.

This resort is really beautiful n peaceful. .. and magnificent greenery ... always love to be here...  morning walk around the jungle gives you more energy to start up the day... food are also very delicious. .

Location and the property:Gokarna Forest Resort (GFR) is situated inside the beautiful Gokarna reserve. Though it’s around 10 kms from the main Kathmandu city, however it seems like a different world in itself. Spread within the 470 acres of the ancient Gokarna Forest, the resort is surrounded by majestic Himalayas which offer an interesting backdrop.Formally Le Meridian, this property was historically the private royal hunting ground of the erstwhile Kings of Nepal, and is given out on lease for 25 years on rotational basis to several hospitality players (as informed by the hotel staff). Though the lobby area and the main complex of the resort is a blend of Malla and Rana period architecture and the decor is done by the owners themselves; but lately a French flavour has been added to it. Honestly, the traditional artwork is pretty nice, the carvings and few pieces are beautiful but the blend of French hasn’t worked that well. I was informed by the hotel staff that the resort might go for a theme change soon.The rooms at the GFR are quite big as compared to other hotels/ resorts in Nepal and are of high quality.  Our room had interior décor based on classical Nepali culture, while my friends got to stay room that had golf course view.Staff members are friendly and warm but all of them have a heavy American accent, not sure if they are trained to speak like that. Their room service is good and the staff definitely tries to help you as much as they can.   Access to Sauna, Jacuzzi, Gymnasium, Swimming pool and morning yoga are complementary for all guests. The indoor pool is heated and cozy so you should carry a costume no matter which month you visit GFR. Also, incase you have forgotten then the costumes at the spa shop are not expensive. For females it costs around 750 NPR and for men its around 600 NPR.Activities:The Gokarna  Forest Resort is very popular for its golf course and attracts lot of tourists who are Golf enthusiasts. Spread over 140 acres at 4,550 ft above sea level, the 6,755 yard par 72 course, it has an 18 hole course  which is a delight for recreational golfers and is one of the congenial highlights of the stay in the region. The greenery, serenity and the majestic settings are overwhelming. You could sight a spotted deer, a barking deer or monkeys who wander freely in the vicinity. Cost - 300 NPR for accessing golf greens and 200 NPR golf club charges.Cart Tour Escorted golf cart tour is one of the most popular activities at Gokarna Forest Resort, the resort provides environmental friendly carts (electric and solar) which takes guests right across the golf courses. If you want to experience freshness and greenery then this tour is recommended.  Some facts:-	The cost per tour (which has two guests) is 1600 NPR + taxes. However, the tour is nice but I felt it was little overpriced for the experience it offered. -	Weekends are comparatively busy for the carts. The cart that took us didn’t have sufficient battery as it was not charged so we had to walk some distance. This should have been taken care off.The other activities offered by the resort include: Forest walk, Bird watching, Cycling and Horse riding. Cost per activity ranges from 600 NPR to 2000 NPR (inclusive of taxes)Restaurants:GRF has four restaurants: The Hunter’s Lodge Restaurant, Durbar Restaurant, Club House Restaurant and the 8848 mt bar. I have reviewed the Club House Restaurant and the 8848 mt bar separately.We had breakfast at the Durbar Restaurant which I found was really bad. Infact the tea was also not upto the mark.GFR is close to the Bodha, so from the airport you can definitely visit Bodha and then check in at the resort because once you reach GFR you would not want to step out of this place. If you are looking for a peaceful, relaxed and luxury holiday, Gokarna Forest Resort is the place to be.

Jeg var kun på hotellet i et døgn, da vores fly blev aflyst grundet en meget tæt tåge. Fin mad og service. Meget flot værelse. Det som jeg bedst kunne lide var den lille skov, hvor jeg gik rundt et par timer og betragtede de sjove og skønne aber.

Set in the former royal hunting forest, this is a comfortable, quiet resort that includes a golf course.  Staff are friendly and attentive. Because we stayed for a night or two on three different stages of this visit to Nepal, we were always remembered when we walked in, paperwork was minimized and we sampled three different types of rooms. The rooms are large and comfortable but there is no lift so some are up two flights of stairs.  Other rooms are in small buildings near the main building and are reached by paved walkways.  These feel more "intimate" but are not well soundproofed. The rooms are well heated (and air conditioned).  The bathrooms are large with showers set in very large tiled "tubs".  WiFi is available without charge in the bar and lounge but requires a fee for use in the rooms.  Some sleeping room near the bar have access to the bar's WiFi.  Food is available in the bar, the restaurant and at the golf clubhouse which is down a long ramp and/or stairs.  Food includes Nepalese, Tibetan, Thai, Indian, Chinese and continental.  The breakfast buffet has a wide variety of food and an omelet station. The resort is several km from the city and from the airport so it can take half an hour or more to reach either.  This produces a very different experience (quiet and away from the hustle and bustle of the city) than staying in a city hotel. Walks in the surrounding forest are available with required guides and monkeys, spotted deer and several species of birds can be seen. The resort has a free daily shuttle into the city.

As we were in search of a peaceful, quiet and sort of a secluded hotel not too far from town, I think we made the right choice. It seems incredible that a few minutes away from what can be described as a filthy, unhealthy city you suddenly find yourself in a beautiful yet authentic, rustic hotel in the middle of a forest. This is such a serene place where hotel staff in their vast majority are genuinely friendly and helpful. As a lot of people have already mentioned, the rooms are quite spacious. Ours included a large balcony which comes in handy when you want to sip a cup of coffee or a beer.In terms of entertainment and activities within the resort, unless you are a keen golf player, there is not much to do but the lovely forest walks. The problem is that you can't go on your own and you must be accompanied by a guide and pay the equivalent of 10 dollars for one hour. When I voiced my frustration about having to pay for a walk I was explained that the property belongs to the government of Nepal and is leased to the hotel for a couple of decades. One of the most pleasant areas of the hotel for us was the 8848m bar where live Nepali music is regularly played in the evenings. We thought the food was not amazing and lacked diversity. We stayed in the hotel for ten days and given the fact that there is no decent restaurant anywhere nearby the hotel, you have not much choice but to order food to be brought to your room. By the end of our stay we got a bit tired of it. There is quite a big gym above the spa and the pool and the direct view on the forest is a plus. However, the equipment is old and some of it is not in good working condition.But overall we loved our stay at Gokarna and would definitely recommend it.

I have only good things to say about my stay at the Gokarna - four days of peaceful surroundings - amidst the chaotic environment of Kathmandu.  I had great service the entire time, friendly and very professional staff.   Played golf at the course and was pleasantly surprised at what a great layout it has.  The 6 course dinner at the Hunter Lodge was an unexpected find as well.  Tashi, Abha and the Hunter Lodge staff are to be commended.

Gokarna Forest Resort is wonderful.  It is a very relaxing resort with wonderful and kind staff, food and amenities.  If I go back to Kathmandu, I will definitely stay there.  I highly recommend this resort!

Definite go to place if you would like some peace and quiet around Kathmandu. The resort is located in the midst of a forest and has a lovely golf course. The food is quite good and the resort has 3 different restaurants which serve different cuisines. All the resort staff are extremely friendly and welcoming! Tashi dolma is a rock star!

This is truly a beautiful property.  Spent three days at this resort and cant wait to go back.  It may be the best kept secret in Kathmandu.  If you are looking for a unique property where you can relax, surrounded by forested hills and wildlife, yet be just a short taxi ride to any of the popular attractions in the city, this is the place to stay. First class golf course. Great courtyard where you can sit outside and enjoy a cocktail or a meal.  The staff was friendly and professional and catered to our every need. Lasta (guest relations) recommended some great restaurants and clearly went out of her way to make sure we were enjoying our time in Kathmandu.  Check this resort out.  You will be glad you did.

My wife and I stayed at Gokarna Forest Resort 4 days in October 2014.We enjoyed every minute!The staff was very service minded and friendly. The resort is nice and quiet, rooms where good (despite a little trouble with hot water..), and the forest guards kept the monkeys away from the outdoor breakfast!We enjoyed playing golf: The course is good and it is beautifully located in the forest with the Himalaya in the background. Fairways a bit rough, but this is compensated for by the animals (not least the monkeys) adding to the experience.The last golfing was also accompanied by a few buddist munks visiting the area. All very exotic.Can also recommend a day tour in Kathmandu to visit selected places and temples.

A far-from-the-crowds getaway that lets you check out Kathmandu city when you want, Gokarna is a great way to visit Nepal. It scored on cabin-style rooms, restaurants and above all on service, warmth & hospitality. We used Gokarna as a base while we explored temples, monasteries, shopping in & around Kathmandu. Whether we were headed back after a hectic day or just lounging at Gokarna through the day, we found it an ideal way to relax.

This hotel is located just outside of Kathmandu, some half an hour drive, by the forest that goes by the same name. The hotel is a proper five star property, with beautiful grounds, well appointed rooms and a indoor swimming pool and a really nice spa. Service is very good, professional and warm, only food a la carte could be better. Otherwise a very good place for a relaxing holiday by the forest.

I just returned from my 5th stay in the past 4 years at the Gokarna. Yes, as most reviews suggest, this is a beautiful, peaceful location which is conveniently close to the city, but far enough away to seem like a different world. However, the real attraction of this resort is the staff. I have visited 50 countries around the world and no hotel or resort tops the Gokarna. They are genuinely concerned about their guests and go out of their way to help with your in-house needs as well as touring around the city. My 6th stay is only a few months away!

My husband (Jose Ortiz) and I (Stephen Parelli) stayed two weeks in August of 2014.  It was a time share exchange.  This was our second time to stay at this resort.  Our August 2014 visit was perfect.  The service was excellent:  when we asked for much need extra padding for the beds, they provided.  (Beds are way too hard, but that seems to be the way it is in this part of the world.)

Gokarna Forest Resort is nothing like I have experienced before. A real retreat for me and a natural resort for my son. You encounter with monkeys and deers especially at night, take a jungle walk in the forest and feel rejuvenated.The hotel is far from hustle and bustle of the city, you feel quietness and full of serenity in the jungle. Hotel has a shuttle service at 10:30 in the morning to the place close to Thamel, and back to hotel at 16:30 which is quite convenient. Hotel has 18 hole golf course which is the biggest in Nepal, and in the top ten in Asia. You woud not like to stay in the city center otherwise you must, because of traffic and all the noise you exposed to.Personnel at the hotel was so friendly and helpful, they become part of my family since we spent six days with my son. Especially Ms Lasta at the front door, she took care of us every day in every occasion, and young trainee Mr Sabine at the Hunters Lodge, he was a superb waiter attended all night and explained every dish we had. The hotel has several restaurants, I strongly recommend the Hunters Lodge, which is quite old, older than 120 years. You have to make a reservation in the afternoon before you go there for dinner. They serve Nepali dishes there, and they explain every dish, the history and the ingredients. When you go out after your dinner do not surprise to see the monkey family waiting outside.This is just a gift of the resort.The other alternative for dinner is Golf Course Restaurant, it is nearby the golf course, they serve Thai and Chinese food with the view of the beautiful green.If you are interested in spa, there is a perfect spa. I have experienced multiple spas before this spa has a very good atmosphere and the massage you taket is perfect.So this is the place you would like to stay in Kathmandu, does not matter if you are going to stay one night or a week.

Very nice and beautiful location close to the airport and a way from hustle and bustle of khathmandu city, amazing oasis between greenery mountain, best place for complete peaceful and great relaxation experience, BF was great but no much options for dinner or lunch, WiFi is not available in all areas, staff are very friendly and helpful, overall it's amazing place to stay in Kathmandu a way from city headache.

Genuinely exciting to be given an enormous wood-floored room with a clean, well-fitted bathroom and spacious grounds. The dining area is a bit pokey and breakfast is actually cramped, but the forest trees in the grounds are lovely. In the evening there are deer, and monkeys are always about. Has the feel of an old British Club, if you know what I mean.

We reached Gokarna on the last day of our trip, being located 10 -20 min from thamel. The staff were very friendly and helpful, we actually got the best customer service in Nepal. I would really recommend Gokarna for at least 2 days of your stay in Nepal, as you can do many activities like golf, spa, yoga, horse riding, forest walks. Rooms are clean, food is great and you have many options. Best value to money hotel in Khatmandu.

My visit to this beautiful and peaceful oasis just minutes from the airport and the Thamel shopping area was absolutely the highlight of my trip to Nepal. I spent the last couple of nights at this resort and cannot compliment the staff enough. The food was delicious and the decor delightful. The barking deer and monkeys were an added bonus as was the spacious room with massive "Bali-style" bathroom ensuite. I would HIGHLY recommend staying at this gem.

We were in India for two weeks prior to going to Kathmandu, and getting to the quiet luxury of Gokarna Forest was like being in a different world.  We had considered canceling and staying somewhere in Kathmandu closer to the action, but after a couple of minutes that idea was history.  You'll get all the city you need via the free shuttle and cab trips. They offer a car service to town which, although it's slightly more expensive than a regular cab, you don't have to haggle and you know you'll get a safe ride in a clean car. Like most high end hotels,a Gokarna charges extra for wifi in the rooms as well as other little things.  All told though, such incidentals were less than we would have racked up on a similar stay at a US hotel.

my first visit to Gokarna Forest Resort was back in 2004 or 2005 for my Musical Concert there, since then i've visited the place often whenever i have the time & opertunity , This Resort has been one of our Family's favorite and best place to go and have a nice short break , Great Hospitality , very Well managed clean and spacious rooms and also the bathrooms , staffs are well speaking , Greeting and caring , Foods are Awesome ... me and my boy Norvin we get up early morning then others in our family members , then we have a little walk there along side the trees then we go have the breakfast which is always very Delightful and with so many varieties, for Us ... every visit to Gokarna Forest Resort ... we have something new and Sweet memory to remember and cherish :D Good Luck and all The best Wishes Gokarna Resort family :D

I was there with my family for three night . The stay was good . They have good services with net & clean room.  One lack for this resort is  no space for driver although with good parking. Rest everything's is good there . ...........,,,,,,,,,,,,

After spending 2 weeks travelling around Nepal this was a wonderful way to rejuvenate and have a little luxury before heading home. Set in beautiful scenic forest setting, the birds were a wonderful change to the hectic sound of cars in Kathmandu. The staff are welcoming and friendly, the rooms are spacious and spotless. Buffet breakfast was excellent with a wide variety of Nepalese and European choices. Three restaurants all reasonably priced give you a great choice to dine. This resort is about 30 minutes taxi drive from Thamel, the tourist area of Kathmandu. I have visited Nepal several times as this place is by far the best luxury resort I have stayed at. My only issue was charging for wi fi. This is the only hotel/ resort I stayed at that charged for wi if and it is very annoying. This should be available for free seeing the standard rooms were over $100.00

I was a looking for a quick getaway from Kathmandu City, as I was not in the mood to undertake a long bus journey. Gokarna Forest Resort was a great choice as it is around 45-75 minutes away from the Kathmandu / Lalitpur (depending on where you start off from). Rooms: We stayed in a Deluxe room that was quite spacious with a big verandah. Very clean and well maintained: this is the most important part of any hotel for me. Service: The staff was very helpful and friendly. Food & Beverages: The Breakfast was quite a spread and suitable for vegetarians too. I normally struggle finding a good vegetarian (no egg) spread at restaurants. Multiple restaurants offer you a choice of cuisines to choose from. We ate a Tibetan Dish (see photo) at the Clubhouse on the first night, which was fantastic. A big boat of steaming hot vegetables in a soup  with some rice on the side. The supply of soup and vegetables was unlimited but minimum order had to be place for two. To do: The indoor swimming pool is great as it meant come rain or sun shine, you could enjoy your swim. I did not use any of the Spa services there, but a friend who did, found it excellent. They recommend a forest walk only with a guide. I did not go for a guided forest walk, but walked around the golf course for a while. There are a lot of monkeys around and deer can be spotted on the golf course in the evenings, I heard. The gift shop in the resort is also quite good and rates are comparable to the shops in Kathmandu. Products are not outrageously overpriced as often is the case. Rates: The rooms are obviously quite expensive but I believe the rates for locals vs foreign tourists can vary, so do ask for discounts or let them know if you are with a local or South Asian and if they can offer reduced rates. I availed the discounted rates. If you have the money and are willing to splurge it is a great getaway from the crowded Kathmandu.

Gokarna is a beautiful hotel in the spectacular setting of the royal forest surrounded by a golf course. A wonderful retreat from the bustling streets of downtown Kathmandu. The staff at the hotel were lovely, very helpful with organising trips and we enjoyed our time in Napal all the more.

Stayed here as part of an OAT Tour of Nepal. The rooms were great - comfortable, spacious, clean. I was there in February and the temperature inside and out was great. Breakfast buffet, lots of options - serving more than one culture and it's all delicious. Dinner in the hotel - not only delicious, but inexpensive too. There was a wedding booked there when we arrived - the place was decked out with flowers, and other wedding decor. Big celebration that we were welcomed to join. Huge event. And despite the joviality, the music and crowd - our room was quiet. Staff is fantastic, super helpful. You can change some dollars at the desk. The gift shop has a little bit of all the major souvenirs. So if you missed getting something along the way, you can most likely find it here. Prices as reasonable. The grounds are lovely, forested jungle-y area. Didn't use the pool. Did use the massage service - in the Pool building. Nice set up with locker for your stuff. I had a short time frame - just did foot massage. Similar to another I had elsewhere in Nepal - and I have to say, it's a 'hard' massage, not a warm and fuzzy. Overall the stay at this hotel was really nice!

We have been 4 days in Gokarna forest resort, mainly to play the golf. Hotel:Hotel is nice, all the employees are very well trained, polite and helpful.  Room was confortable, clean, well maintnaned. There are some permanent troubles with electricity in Nepal, but we dont blame the hotel for it. What is quite weird, when you pay the wi-fi room connection you can connect only one device. We never got the same experience anywhere in the word. Once you pay for the room connection you should be able to connect any device, or more devices, more then one. Then there is also free wifi in the hotel's bar, that 's sympa but some people dont like to spend the hours in the bar...   One night we didnt sleep so well because there was any event with the loud music till the late night... That was not very nice.Restaurant in the hotel has a good offer of food, the same the golf-club restaurant. We didnt like too much the Nepali restaurant, the food was not very good, then there was no ambiance...music parexample, then the serving waiter was standing all time next to our table when we were eating, that was little weird, but this restaurant was the only disappointment. The breakfest bufee is big and tasty and varied.There is a interior swimm-pool and spa but I cant comment it as we had no time to use it.Golf course:The golf course of Gokarna is magic. We played golf in a beautiful forest with monkeys, deers... It was really relaxing. We really enjoyed it.Visiting: we did also some visiting of the city, there are nice places to see. We took a hotel's car with the driver. The driver stayed all the time with us, he was very helpful and attentive. So we wanted him also for the next day 's visits, then the next day he came... how to say that?.. he didnt take a shower probably then he surely didnt change his clothes. We were not able to breath in the car. This is a little detail what the hotel should improve. But he was very nice and helpful as I said, so we somehow survived it.Generaly if someone asked me if I'd come again to Gokarna I'd answer yes. it is not 100% peerfect but it is not that bad neither.

Tolle Anlage am Rande Kathmandus, vom gewaltigen Staub der Stadt bekommt man nichts mit. 3 Restaurant mit 3 verschiedenen Küchen. Direkt an einem Golfplatz gelegen, der zum Hotel gehört. Das Personal ist supernett, wenn auch manchmal ein bisschen planlos. :)

A group of 4 of us stayed here from the 24-27th March. After much deliberation, we were glad we picked this hotel. The huge property is located on a hillside, quiet and away from the dusty roads of Kathmandu. At reception, we were greeted by friendly staff whom were always helpful and attended to all our request promptly. The room were comfortable, spacious and our friends, had a view of deers outside the window. Unfortunately, wifi is not available in the rooms but only at the bar Dunbar. Food at the bar with the exception of Indian selection can be given a pass. Breakfast is reasonable but could be improved. We didn't get a chance to eat anywhere else on the property.We visited the golf course on a buggy ride which you need to pay for, like most tservices in the hotel.The spa is definitely worth a visit. We met Lasta, the PR exec of the hotel, whom took the effort to organise a surprise birthday cake for my other half on the morning of his birthday which truly was a gesture much appreciated and made the trip all the more pleasant.I would recommend this hotel most definitely.

We stayed here in March 2014 just for two nights while we explored Kathmandu valley.We liked the pictures on the walls of the hotel from all over the Himalayan region and enjoyable music that sounded through the halls of the hotel. Our room was clean and spacious and the bathroom was modern. The resort is in a great location with the friendly and welcoming staff and the restaurant had a very nice breakfast buffet.

A wonderful resort that is just outside the city. Far enough to experience peace and quit but close enough to get into town for a days outing. The resort in located in a forest sanctuary and it feels like you are in nature but have all the aminaties you could ask for from great spacious rooms to a wonderful spa offering various treatments. There is also a heated indoor pool. If you are into golf it has one of the most beautiful courses in the region. Great for a romantic couple get away and also enjoyable for families. Highly recommended.

We enjoyed our stay here. It was quiet clean and the staff very helpful. The use of the pool and yoga was appreciated. The golf course looked inviting. The buffet breaky was fresh and substantial. I would recommend Gokarna for those requiring a few quiet days.

We stayed here as part of our tour to India and Nepal. It is a little out of town but worth driving to because it is so lovely. We had a large king room with a patio overlooking the gardens. The hotel has a great spa with extremely affordable massages. I recommend the hot stone massage! The food was good although I thought the breakfast needed a little work. There is an indoor pool attached to the spa in case of bad weather. The hotel offers free early morning yoga classes and there is a lovely little temple on the grounds where visitor participation is encouraged. This is really a special place to stay.

A near gateway from the city . For a short trip in a hectic lifestyle would recommend it very much. Forest walk felt like we  were out of the valley. All in all a great experience!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Staffs were very pleasant as well.......... <3 <3

It was really great experience, we had amazing experience and loved the service. From the starting we had smooth check in by guest relation her name was sabeena theeng and from the marketing too. Her name was kamala. They made our experience best. We will be coming agian.

It was overall good experience.One suggestion is that since we r veg people so if one can provide separate veg kitchen with separate utensils it will add to the flavour for all veg people, gym is not upgraded need an upgraded gym and rest people staff were very good and kind.Thanks

We stayed at the Gokarna after 12 days of trekking in not too comfortable accommodation, getting here was a bit of a dream, tranquility, relaxation (pool and spa, the latter for a fee), nice and clean rooms, fairly good restaurant.I also played golf, the course isn't wonderful but it's maintained quite well, the greens are a bit slow, with equipment and ball rental I spent around €110 to play, let's say that €80 would have been a fairer price.:.Overall though, great experience, keep going.

My son and I planned an impromptu trip to Nepal late July, before he headed off to college. We just had 6 days including travel to and from the US, so I was keen on finding a place we could enjoy and to plan activities for all the days we were in Nepal. We both searched for options and independently picked Gorkana.  I was unable to complete my booking online (it was a temporary glitch I later learned) so I called the hotel. My one-of-kind vacation started right there!  The lady who took my call (Niymaya) patiently worked with me to get my selections, charged my card for the required one day and confirmed my booking for 6 days. She then took my WhatsApp contact info and shortly sent me a copy the charge to my card. Eager to plan trips while I was in Nepal, I asked her to connect me with someone who could help. To my delight, I was then connected to another fabulous member of the Gokarna staff (Sumita)!  For the next couple of days, she worked with me back and forth on WhatsApp and helped me plan numerous trips. This included booking a flight to see the Himalayas and flight plus a day’s hotel reservation to Chitwan. Our planning ended with her wishing me before we boarded our flights for Nepal. On arrival, we were met by our driver, who held my son’s name on the placard, just as I had requested!  We then arrived at the hotel and were greeted by the hotel staff, including Sumita and Nirmaya - it was fantastic to meet these two ladies who had helped me so much before I even arrived in the country!  We loved our stay at the Gokarna resort!  We took advantage of the sumptuous meals and spa, and had a really good balance of rest and activity. The day and other trips Sumita helped us plan gave us a glimpse of Kathmandu. The resort is a lush green paradise.  Out room was comfortable and luxurious and we were delighted to see deer from our room! This trip was special because Sumita, Nirmaya and the staff of Gokarna made me feel like I was their only guest despite me planning the trip at short notice!  And, despite there being other guests, including a large party from a corporate. My only advice to anyone considering Gokarna will be (1) Go ahead, book your stay there! (2) If you are unable to climb stairs, ask for a room on the ground floor as there are no elevators. I hope you enjoy Nepal and Gokarna as much as we did - and I hope the resort recognizes their wonderful staff for being such solid brand ambassadors!

We spent 3 days at Gokarna after trekking ebc. I chose this property because of its unique, beautiful grounds. It delivered!  We did the 4 hour forest, temple walk with a few leeches around and the bird watching tour with Nepal bird watching and trekking (within the property). We saw an amazing range of wildlife: 2Species of deer (spotted and barking) 2 martens, 2 jackals chasing deer on the golf course! Birds and monkeys are everywhere! We saw about 20 to 30 species of birds. I loved every minute of my stay there.The breakfast buffet is excellent and changes every day. The food at the main restaurant is excellent as well. The golf course restaurant is a wonderful place at night to see the deer and monkeys. Staff is very polite and friendly. Room was spacious, pretty and well stocked. I will come back in a heartbeat. We also stayed in an airbnb in Kathmandu, but next time I will go directly to Gokarna!

The Gokarna Forest resort is an excellent property with clean, big and comfortable rooms. The setting in a serene forest environment offers clean fresh air and quietness to unwind after a hard day at work.But the real beauty of this place lies with their staff. Genuine desire to see that you are enjoying your stay by offering to address all your needs.From Ms Sumita at Check in to Mr Rajendra Karki at the restaurant as well as Mr Bibek Shrestha and Ms Lhakpa, all offer service with warmth and genuine smiles.I requested a table at the restaurant, it was arranged for me immediately and I mention to Mr Bibek that I would like to have same table every evening. He was on off day on my second night in the hotel but called from his house to inform the restaurant manager of my request and to ensure that the table would be reserved for me. That level of commitment to service was excellent and very rare these days.I would like to extend my warm and sincere gratitude to all the staff.Had a pleasant stay made even more pleasant by the staff attention.

I,ve been to Gokarna Resort for a week in May,  I went with my boyfriend, and we both loved the place. The staff is amazing, supportive, attentive, friendly, we loved Nema and Shiva at the reception desk so much.The facilities are very great, the rooms are very comfortable, loved the traditional and elegant nepali furnitures and decorations. There is plenty of activities to do at the resort, The Spa is really good, and you can even go for a forest walk with rental bikes.Is located in a forest, full of birds, an beautiful trees, but really close to Kathmandu, in taxi is just 10 min.We defenetly enjoyed the calmess after a busy day walking around Kathmandu

Stayed in Gokarna Forest Resort recently. It's a quiet oasis, which is a contrast since the public road to Gokarna is not in good condition & dusty.The resort has a golf course (which seems quiet popular), spa and temperature controlled indoor pool (which also seems popular with families).The hotel rooms itself are alright, they're getting quite tired & old. Just be aware that the oasis also means everything is contained within the resort & you can't easily walk out to find restaurants or check out the surrounding area.But overall, I enjoyed my stay at the resort.

You can find tranquility and peace in Kathmandu, a city where mostly we encouter crowd, unorganized traffic and bad air quality, garbage, etc. A morning walk in the lust forest, passing through beautiful golf club, and good food, neat, clean and luxurious rooms are amazing experiences, while you are working on some important strategic work.

The resort is excellent. Service is impeccable. The staff helped us through everything. Food is also very good. The chef curated an amazing menu for our event. Overall the experience was great. Will definitely recommend.

1)A bit over priced for the quality of room & buffet ! 2) The toilet flush in room 321 for some reason was not working properly 3) The swimming pool was dirty and the pool  area overall definitely needs some maintenance work .

Perfect place for getaway, the view from my room was beautiful though the buffet dinner was not really good. Loved the indoor swimming pool, love everything about the hotel but the front desk staffs were not rly professional( lil rude) in my opinion

Poor hygiene...showing its age...maintenance is shoddy....was provided a room in the clubhouse...toilets dirty n filthy....no water in the shower....had to change rooms at 11pm night....these things should have been checked n done with before the new check in...This hotel doesn't come cheap...definitely an expensive hotel...wouldn't want to come back here again and wouldn't recommend to anyone else...with the shoddy service...

1. Booked the rooms as quoted and paid 50% advance even when the sales said we can pay at departure. Was implied by the reception people that the full payment was to be done in a condescending tone.2. No toiletries except shampoo and soaps.3. Major issue was the ridiculously priced food which lacked seasonings in all items. Tasted like some amateur cook made them. But the price???4. 600 rs ++ per 30 ml Jameson  (the cheapest drink there) served in chipped glass.5. Swimming pool not heated due to Covid-19. Why to even open the pool?6. Security guard at the clubhouse: looked and acted scary. Someone went a little farther in the grass and he shouted " oh baini, oh baini". Are they oriented that they are not the police officers?7. COVID-19 precautions: even the shoes were sanitized when checking in, but the breakfast buffet was served in the closed hall of Durbar restaurant. 8. Most of the staff treated us in a patronizing manner. Because we are soft spoken, easy going and Nepali maybe? First time ever experiencing this "Nepali bhayera hepeko" feeling by fellow Nepalese. Seen this place in its highs too and the everything was way much better. The bar and restaurant staff were very nice. The deer were nice. Monkeys were funny. Highly recommended to go only in tourist season when there are a LOT of foreigners.

Es war eine sehr schöne Zeit, entspannend und aufregend zugleich, neues in angenehmer Atmosphäre. Das Personal ist sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit und auch die Massage ist sehr schön. Essen ist sehr lecker und abwechselungsreich und das Gelände ist sehr schön. MIr fiel es schwer, dass ich nicht auf eigenen Wegen auch mal gut laufen konnte, da es an den meisten Stellen verboten war zu laufen. (oder Radfahren, hätte ich mich allerdings nicht getraut).Aber es sind problemlose fortbewegungsmöglichkeiten vorhanden, und man wird auch super dabei unterstützt. Danke

very pleasant stay and friendly environment...cosy rooms as we travelled with our two kids ! Had a very wonderful stay...imdoor swimming pool with many facilities...touring on Golf court was extra bonus for kids...have to visit once if you are in kathmandu !!! Close to Nature !

We were on holiday from India. We had a lovely time in peaceful surroundings and with friendly hospitable staff. It was good access to the main city too, so we were able to both site see and relax in same trip.

The hotel has beautiful views which is away from the crowd and chaos of the city. The landscape is very beautiful. It has beautiful rooms with great service quality. The staffs here are very professional and friendly.

We spend a week in this wonderful place. Everything was perfect. Stuff is so helpful and friendly! They made our vacation easy and enjoyable. They help us to organize all trips and transfers so we didn’t need to worry about anything. Horse riding, beautiful Forrest. Look forward to come back again. Thank you.🙏

Really lovely hotel in large grounds, with a splendid golf course and spa facility. We had a very large room, and even though there was a wedding party at the hotel it was very quiet. Lovely service in the restaurant, and we enjoyed an excellent massage in the spa. The location is several kilometers out from the centre of Kathmandu, so not perfect for exploring the city on foot, but as a peaceful retreat in fresh air just out of the mayhem of Kathmandu it is perfect.

Very nice hotel or resort, I would love to say. But pretty much far from the airport. Very peace and greenery. Perfect spot for relaxing away from busy noisy city. Restaurants also very nice and highly decorated. We will visit again.

Hard to believe that tranquility exists in Kathmandu but it does. The hotel staff are friendly, accommodating and only wish for you to have a happy stay. I can’t speak more highly of the reception and restaurant staff. Thank you for making our stay so easy, comfortable and peaceful.Rooms are a little dated but very clean and huge. To be honest the beds are in need of replacing with big, soft and comfortable mattresses. USB ports next to the bed would be handy or at least an international power point.The restaurant had a good buffet for breakfast and the local vegetarian thali for lunch was very delicious. Staff are friendly, coffee can take a while to be delivered but what else is there to do in a forest resort?The hotel grounds are beautiful, green, lush and natural forest. We had a guided forest walk and it was a great way to spend a few hours... it’s said there’s a leopard living in the woods but we didn’t see one on this day. In fact a golfer stopped us and said he saw one the day before.I couldn’t imagine staying anywhere else in Kathmandu.
