Personally I would rather be rained on outside than be inside and in danger of the building collapsing (which is possible). And those who complained that Hyatt wasn't there to provide shelter for locals and others were not even there! I witnessed a local guide asking Hyatt staff for alcohol, and Hyatt staff refused. And rightly so! So Sinead and Team, thanks for your assistance and patience and perseverance. There's no where in kathmandu that will provide breakfast, lunch and dinner, water, and blankets during the earthquake. It's the most comfortable place and safest place to be!

The presidential suite is fantastic . The direct  view of the stupa is a novelty. The club access is nice, but the club facilities itself are very basic and the canapes in the happy hour r pathetic. Drinks r good. The Rox cafe is not too great. The landscaping of this property is fantastic and an early morning jog at the internal track is a blessing in this city. We stayed for 4 nights in kathmandu and it was only possible in this hotel, any other hotel in this city and I'd go crazy !

I am with my family for a vacation and booked this property by just trusting the name but it's shocking that even after bearing the brand the rooms are in a mess. I would rate the cleanliness of the rooms in negative (even encountered reptiles in room). The check-in was delayed for reasons best known to the hotel. Bathrooms fittings are really worn out.... it's a task to adjust the water temperature as the taps  need to be operated by strong hands.It claims to be a 5* property but I would definitely not rate it above 3* ( even though I have stayed at much cleaner rooms of 3* properties).Would suggest management to intervene immediately so that the brand name as well was the reputation of all stakeholders be kept.

It is difficult to add anything to the two recent reviews 'The True Response...' and 'Kathmandu Earthquake Experience...' that sum up the amazing care and concern shown by every member of staff during the recent earthquake under the superb leadership of Sinead O'Reilly Hennell, the general manager.  They continued to provide meals, free phone calls, bedding, guidance and moral support in the most devastating circumstances and we shall be eternally grateful.  This was also extended to local people and tourists from other accommodation without any questions asked.  Mrs. O'Reilly's PA even phoned when we had arrived home in the UK to see how we all were.  I was pleased to hear from her that the hotel has been declared safe and bookings are coming in.  They are much deserved and I would not hesitate in staying at the hotel again.  Thank you to all at the Hyatt Regency Kathmandu - our hearts are with you as you continue to work under such tragic circumstances.

Stayed 3 nights , 2 before trip to jungle and 1 on return. Marvelous 5 star luxury , a great treat , as was the whole of Nepal after experiences in India.On 1st stay we were a little unwell( after India) so whilst being able to appreciate breakfast missed out on evening food.On return we were able to give the buffet a caning, and were very impressed. 2000 nrs plus taxes pp, well worth it, high quality and wide variety. Try the Himalayan French cheese.A really top hotel.great views of Stupa, city , mountains and airport.

We stayed here for 2 nights at the end of our NEPAL trip.On check in we requested for a higher floor room with a view. We also inquired at the reception if buffet lunch is served as we were very hungry - We were informed there is no buffet lunch and the hotel is over booked. Hence they have upgraded us and would be giving us a room on the same level as reception. We were given the room keys and had to find our way to our room. When we entered the room it was at the ground floor with no view, dirty bed, hair over the pillow, soiled head board. We were given the basic room and the front desk had lied to us about an upgraded room. We have stayed in Hyatt before in many other countries and are aware of the different rooms offered by Hyatt. As we were hungry we called the restaurant to order lunch and requested them to  keep it ready. We went down to the restaurant to have lunch - to our surprise there was a buffet lunch being served. When we checked with the chef he said Hyatt has buffet breakfast, lunch and dinner served every day. We headed back to the reception and requested for change of room. To our surprise the desk staff called the guest services desk and asked if they had cleaned the room. As if we were lying about the uncleaned room.  This was getting too irritating for us and we asked for the general manager or duty manager to whom we could log our compliant. The front desk informed us Duty manager would only come by 6pm for night shift and the general manager is too busy and cannot be reached. Really disappointed we resigned to our fate and wasted 400 USD for two nights stay on an old, badly managed, under trained staff hotel. Positives - Excellent bathroom, Good swimming pool, great staff in the cafe and restaurant.

This Hyatt Regency is located in a lovely palace in Bouddha, about 5km from Kathmandu's centre. Here, the air is clean and there is the special energy of Bouddha's stupa which visible from the top floor. Unfortunately, due to the earthquake, it is still damaged, but it us still special. Lovely rooms, very clean. The pool looks great, but I did not try it. Breakfast is probavly the best I every had, abd I had quite a few. TIP: When going to the stupa, use the gate the back of the garden. A security guard will let you out and back in when you show your room card.

We had an excellent stay at the Hyatt Regency for 2 nights with wonderful service and staff. We were about to leave when the earthquake struck. The staff were simply fabulous and welcomed everybody as their guest, whether they were staying their or not. They provided food, water and bedding for all, and also welcomed the local people in. The following day we had to leave in a hurry for the airport and a car was immediately made available for us, even though we were no longer staying there. We cannot praise the management and staff highly enough - even though they were suffering themselves, they put everybody else first. We send them all our best wishes. and are thinking of them at this time.

I'm the manager of a Guest House ( Ti-se Guest House ) right next to Hyatt Regency . In recent times there  has  been a lot of criticism about hyatt not allowing local people to use their property during the earth quake . I'm here to let people know that this is TOTALLY  NOT TRUE !! I've stayed with many of my guests and 100 of other local people at Hyatt ground for the past few days and I saw other hundreds on the  other end and there are people still staying there . Evryone despite rich or poor were allowed to stay. During earthquake the  management not only allowed to us to stay but  also distributed drinking water everyday and  let them use their rest room too . One day they even distributed  snacks to Evryone . Also from professional view ,Unfortunately, the Hyatt is a business and giving people shelter won't be a temporary solution. So Thank you Hyatt once again on behalf of Evryone from Shedra student to my guests and staffs to local people . Everyone here are so thankful for your kind hospitality ( FYKI most of people at our end are poor ). Very very professional !!! #recommended

I stayed in the Hyatt Regency duirng the earthquake in April 2015 and just returned back home. I would like to use this platform here to say thank you to Sinead O’Reilly-Henell, the GM of the Hotel and to her entire team. It was amazing how smooth the entire team was organised and how well the information flow was working. We all spend the night after the big earthquake in the hotel lobby and the tennis court and were provided with water and food and the entire team was supporting as good as possible under the circumstances! Once again a very big thank you to Sinead O’Reilly-Henell and her team!

The architecture of this hotel is very nice, as other Hyatt hotel chain buildings. We stayed at Club room floor and the room is clean although it needs a lot of make up over (small things). Lovely breakfast, good selection on canapé and drinks at Club Lounge. But Hyatt service is top notch! Would stay in this hotel again when we are back to Nepal!

The hotel is located close to some sightseeing as well as shopping (a mall is nearby) also the airport is easily reached.Room was a bit old, however clean and comfortable. Had the dinner buffet, nothing to complain about, however also not the best food I had in Nepal. Extra services are much more expensive than in other hotels in the area, the beer was pretty expensive, and I also made a few phone calls that turned out to be very expensive.

The Hyatt Regency is a stately building in a very smoggy place.  The hotel itself overlooks the city, which is covered in gray dust.  The rooms are quiet and reasonably large.  The breakfast is substantial and full of local foods, many of which were very tasty, even for a westerner.  I don't believe this hotel is up to the normal Hyatt Regency standards, at least not the ones I am used to in Asia, Europe, and the USA.

I've reviewed many hotels, but never critically before. We had stayed here a few days before, had several issues,here's just a few:, a double bed when twins were clearly requested, a single towel and bathrobe in a several rooms with double occupancy - we had to wait literally hours for room service to respond. Beetles (my friend was adamant it was a cockroach in her room) scuttling about. All was promised to be sorted by our next visit. It was far worse.First we waited well over hour wait to get into a room - again only one towel and robe between two people. We could hardly hear ourselves speak because there was a party with amplified sound right outside the window. We'd been up since 5am and simply wanted to relax in peace around the pool. That was not available, because all the grounds had been taken over by the party. So we were stuck in the noisy rooms. Our rep was assured the row outside would stop at 11pm. Which it did. BUT No one mentioned to him that a disco would then start up inside at 11.30pm, close by our rooms and run until 3am. So we got no sleep. Several of us rang to complain - the noise got worse. We had been given wine and chocolates to make up for our complaints from our first stay...we would have preferred a room where we could relax, have a bath without waiting so long for a robe the water went cold, use the garden to sit around the pool and simply be allowed to SLEEP from midnight.  I know hotel have large functions but Why book guests who have nothing to do with those functions, in rooms literally feet away?Its a lovely hotel, very impressive building and decor, friendly staff but I'd never stay there again - far too disorganised.

I cant believe I just stayed 3 nights and felt it was forever. I got sick from the food, the rooms are terrible...seriously this is consider a 5 star? From where!? Next to our room was some businessman staying which love shouting at night and even invited to their room more than 2 people...we called 2 consecutive days several times to the concierge and they "send security" to tell them to lower the voice, tv, everything...ofcourse the result was the same they continue with the screaming and even slaming doors. Again we continue calling conciergr and not also us but the room in front of us was also pretty upset and instead of calling real security for disturbance of peace they told us at 3 in the morning that we should change our room. Oh yes I forgot we had to get up at 5 in the morning both days for touring...so we sleep 2 hours. Thank you horrible hotel...we are never ever coming back and we dont recomend the hotel at all! Terrible, unclean rooms, tv of the 80s, everything smells bad...I had to use disinfectant spray on everything.

Before I arrived to this hotel, I wrote to Mr Prabin Shrestha about my request and requirement. All arrangement was made accordingly.But there were some misunderstanding between myself and the Club Floor staff. The staff were very apologetic and service recovery is fast.Please extend my compliment to them.CheersLyn Lyn

Had visited Kathmandu in 2001 and loved the city. Back then it was scenic , very clean and picturesque. The entire city is dug up and dirty.                                   When we arrived the people at the gate just looked at us not wanting to help us unload our luggage and just gazed in grief! Person by the name of Avinash or something . The  club rooms were not ready even at 2 pm . The rooms are pathetic , the slippery wooden flooring , high ceilings without any aesthetics, antique bathroom where you have to use strength to flush .   The Empty swimming pool( without water).  and shabby gardens . On day 2 , the room was not even cleant. Something unheard of in a 5 star hotel. The only saving grace were the few people . The club room staff especially the bespectacled last Chef and some other staff . Sita & Birat at the coffee shop were always helpful. The staff at the breakfast were very helpful.  Hyatt should review the property and maybe defranchise itself as it will create a dent in their brand value.

This hotel has very slow Wi-Fi service.  At first I thought that this being a third world country, this is the best one can expect in this part of the world, until I found out that even the coffee shops around town provide faster internet service than this hotel.   As I look at past reviews of this hotel, I notice that for a long time now many other people have complained about the internet service at this hotel, and, after a prefatory apology, management has always responded by saying that they are in the "process of upgrading" and presumably this problem will be taken care of then.  Well management has been telling us for a long time now that they are in the "process of upgrading."  By now such a response becomes meaningless and sounds disingenuous.  You would think that by now, with all these customer complaints, the Wi-Fi would have long been updated if management is serious about fixing the problem.  It should not take more than 4 to 8 weeks to fix the Wi-Fi problem, certainly not years.  So what is the hold up?The hotel room we stayed in is tired looking and in need for serious redecorating.  I noticed that this too has been one of the top customer complaints about this hotel for quite a while.  And you guessed it, for many years now management's response is that we are in the "process of upgrading."  I say, enough of that excuse.Notwithstanding the 37 acres of gardens at this property, I would expect a lot better for the US$ 180 per night I paid to stay here.  This hotel is not living up to its brand name, and management's drone response to customer complaints is completely unacceptable.I wish I would checked the reviews before deciding to stay at this hotel.

We spent 4 nights at this hotel 2 nights at a time with 4 days in between and what a difference.   We were shown to our lovely stupa view room on our first two days and we were very pleased.  However 4 days later things had changed when we arrived for our next 2 nights to be shown to a standard room which frankly had seen better days.  We informed them that we had booked and paid for an upgraded stupa room but they did not believe us and it lead to a rather unpleasant conversation with the reservations manager.  They eventually put us in a stupa room with twin beds even though we wanted a king and a very leaky shower but just to shut us up .  My husband then contacted our UK travel agent who confirmed that an upgraded room with stupa view had been booked and paid for.  We told them this and also our paperwork confirming this and they said we could use the lounge on 6th floor...big deal!  Wouldn't recommend this hotel as did not like the inference that we were liars just trying to get a free upgrade!

The Hyatt Regency in Kathmandu is a beautiful place to stay under normal circumstances.  Sitting in lush gardens it is an oasis in this busy city.  Very nice rooms, overall design and great staff service are a treat.  Having stayed there during the big 7.9 earthquake, however, showed me the true skill of the hotel's management and the dedication of its staff.  When this major disaster hit and continued for days, there was probably no safer and well organized place in town and the staff made us feel cared for and safe.  Absolutely amazing,

I am still in shock from the horrible tragedy. But thank god for the Hyatt and their incredibly generous staff. I was given safe shelter, food and water. I offered to pay, but payment was refused. I was told that this was the least the Hyatt could do. Thank you, thank you so much you made the impossible bearable.

My parents and I stayed at the Hyatt Regency, Kathmandu, both times we were in Nepal and enjoyed it profusely. The hotel is right behind the Boudhanath stupa (choose to get a room with that view if you can), which essentially offers you a view of the city and mountains behind the stupa! Gorgeous! Rooms were large and clean and amply supplied with whatever you might need for your stay. The staff was really fantastic. You are certain to be greeted with a cheerful 'Namaste' all through the day and quickly offered any assistance if you ask. The food options offered at the hotels restaurants cater to all your needs; I especially liked the Regency Club lounge which offers a nice view of the city while you sip on a hot cup of delicious tea. The pools and gym are also extremely well maintained. The grounds of the hotel are perfect for a nice jog or walk any time of day. I'd just suggest grabbing the torch provided in your room if you take a stroll in the night.  The location of the hotel helps its cause. It's quiet and away from any city noises, including any party going on in the concert ground next door. Talk to the concierge or front desk staff to arrange for transport any where in the city, airport, or the travel desk to arrange for a day's trip to a place of your choosing. The cherry topping of our time there was an upgrade to the Presidential Suite on the final night of our stay. Absolutely lovely, with our own private balconies and kitchen, large living room and personal sauna in the bath area! I would definitely recommend staying at Hyatt any time you visit. It's almost like staying in a palace resort!

Arrived on a tour after the grime ( and worse )in India and were blown away by this marvelous hotel.One of the best we have stayed at anywhere in the world. Reception area is beautiful, as is terrace bar and pool. Gardens are even better . Our room was atmospheric, furnished in dark woods , bed was huge and all facilities present. We had a view of Stupa,which is only 10 mins walk through gardens ( yes you can go out, hassle free inNepal!)There is supermarket and pharmacy across road at end of front drive.Breakfast was high quality, wide choice served in lovely restaurant.Evening buffet was ok but intending to try a la carte when we return at end of tour .Wi-fi is free everywhere, but slow in the evenings, prices are quite high for food and drink but in a true 5 star we didn,t mind.Highly recommended.

I stayed here almost 10 years back when it was a newly built and enjoyed. I came back here because of that only but disappointed. Old rooms and almost all the things are faded out. Value for money absolutely zero. Needs renovations urgently. Otherwise all very nice.

L’albergo più rumoroso della vacanza. Lontano da tutto tranne che da Bodhnath che è’ a 10 min a piedi.Arrivata ore 3 ( di notte) non c’era la camera comunicante- disponibile solo il gg seguente, non sanno niente sui ristoranti nei dintorni e sulle festività, ma la cosa più terrificante sono le pareti di 2 cm Brutti e vecchi anche i bagni.Buona la colazione.

Still one of the better hotels in Kathmandu despite it being dated and in need of some refurbishment (which I understand they are undertaking now). The interior of the hotel is charming and aesthetically pleasing. However it is only near to 1 attraction out of the many UNESCO heritage sites + popular eateries in Kathmandu, so do take note that it isn't very conveniently located as it can take a while to get to the city center with traffic jams.

I stayed at Hyatt Regency Kathmandu over the past weekend, and I think it was likely the worst Hyatt stay ever from the beginning (I am a globalist and go to a lot of Hyatt properties).Prior to arriving at the hotel, I asked the guest service via email whether they can send me a list of great Nepalese restaurants (I was the first time visitor to the country). I got an email back saying, "You can visit Thamel for different varieties of restaurant” and no list was provided. Then I did my own research and asked the hotel staff to book a restaurant for me.The staff got back “For booking the restaurant, I consulted with my colleague here and they advised it will be better if you book the restaurant directly on your own."Seriously?! I cannot believe that the "colleague" told not to help book my dinner reservation request... This is a five star property!I then sent this email chain to the front desk team suggesting that their guest relation team needs to do a better job but no reply was sent.The room was very cold as well. The heating system did not work. When I asked for help, the guest service simply brought me a half broken heater that made a disturbing noise that woke me up a few times overnight.Overall, this was a bad stay.

We stayed here on 2 different nights during our Nepal tour.  The first time we had a room facing the front of the hotel.  It was a nice view of the gardens, but nothing special.  The second time we had a room facing the stupa, which was pretty spectacular.The food at the breakfast buffet and dinner buffet was great.  Always a nice selection and I enjoyed my omelet each morning.The location is great.  It is a short walk to the stupa if you go out the back way and a short walk to a supermarket if you go out the front way.  Crossing the busy street going to the supermarket it interesting if you aren't a local, but we finally made it.We had room service for lunch one day.  We each ordered a sandwich, but one sandwich is probably large enough for 2 people, plus they included fries with it.Since we didn't spend multiple days in a row there we can't say how the maid service was.  The workers we did interact with were always very helpful and courteous.

An oasis in a delightful, jumble of a city. The architecture is increadible, yet the rooms more down to earth. The food was delicious, had hoped to use the sprawling pool area but ran out of time. We Highly recommend this hotel as probably the very best is the city.

This Hotel is in a poor state. I have spent  a few nights here. The pool is very nice and the location very handy to the Boudhna Stupa. The hotel rooms and the restaurant furniture is in a very sad state. Even the staff in the restaurant is dressed in stained suits and uniforms. Th food was good and not to pricy. The free internet very slow.

I attended a week-long conference in Kathmandu (KMU) in March 2018 and was so happy to be able to retreat back to the Hyatt each evening. Indeed, the hotel is not in downtown KMU, but it is absolutely a quiet sanctuary set back on 37 acres of landscaped gardens. Further, it's only a five-minute walk to the UNESCO heritage sites Bouddhanath Stupa and Pashupatinath Temple, two of the most venerated Buddhist sties in KMU; it was wonderful that when I had free time I could simply walk to these sites and soak in the spiritual history of Nepal for hours at a time (plus wonderful local restaurants....Shambhala Cafe being my favorite....and local handicraft shopping). I try to stay in Hyatts whenever I travel but I was also attracted to the Dwarika hotel because of its stunning architecture and interiors, however the Hyatt is also a beautiful property but at least half the price of the Dwarika (thus, the perfect combination was to stay at the Hyatt and go for a meal in the lobby of the Dwarika as it's the lobby that is the beautiful part of the hotel and the rooms nothing special or worth the higher cost).In terms of the actual property, the overall ambience reminds me more of a Grand Hyatt than a Hyatt Regency. The outdoor facade and indoor lobby combine Nepalese and colonial wooden features which are beautiful and restful. Live Nepalese music welcomes you along with excellent staff at the front desk. I stayed on the Regency Club floor. The rooms are spacious and as others have noted, rather dated at this point but still comfortable and sufficiently refined. The Regency Club was superlative (as good as most Grand Hyatts thoughout Asia). The Club (and my room) had a direct view of the Stupa. The wines were of high quality as was the food (and ample enough for an entire meal). The Club price includes breakfast which is served in the main dining room (the offerings are vast and multi-ethinic....huge selection and freshly prepared). I used the gym daily (small but decent) and the weather was warm enough during the day to rest by the large pool and swim. There is a running path within the grounds which is so convenient as otherwise no way one can run on the dusty and chaotic streets of KMU. Overall, it was simply a wonderful stay and when I was finished attending the conference each day it was such a pleasure to return to the quiet and relaxing atmosphere at the Hyatt. I definitely felt pampered and will stay there on future trips as well as recommend the hotel to others.

I was there on a business trip and the service from the staff was fantastic and I felt like an honoured guest especially by Chef Arun and the rest of the staff in the Cafe. It has a good gym, you can walk or jog around the grounds or explore the surrounding Boudha stupa that is a 5 minute walk away. Other than that you are quite isolated from the downtown areas but they do run a shuttle bus into the city.

Overall poor and run down condition and furniture in rooms were run down and poorly maintained. Leaking walls and peeling wooden floors. Poor heating in room with smell. Carpets on corridors were dirty and run down. Similar breakfast everyday, no changes ..

We would strongly recommend this hotel, the attention to detail by the staff and management is second to none. The quality of the food and accommodation is to such a high class. Its a quite peaceful oasis in the middle of a bustling city. Close to the Airport and a lot of other amenities in walking distance.

Firstly I requested to check in at 11 AM, but it was not fulfilled by the lady met at reception, she just showed the club lounge and said sit here. She was offering me lower category room ie. HYAT king room, but I rejected to take as I had booked hyatt club room by paying 1 1/2 Amount of HYAT king room. But I requested that lady to please give me any room that time for few hours as I was With my old mother, but she rejected my request, it's not our hotel policy to give room before and then to give your booked  on day, and then shift to your booked category room.      After waiting an hour in lobby I again gone to her, but with same reply from her. At 12:30 PM I requested to Mr. Bipash and tell that I am with my old mom and waiting since 2 hours, he immediately given hyatt king room that time for rest and also give the best pool view club room on 2 Pm. I see that lady has falsed to me.      Again once incident happen, which is not expected from hyatt when we were allotted room, housekeeping staff without knocking, opened our Room with master key and enter our Room, and we were sleeping on bed. I immediately snatch his master key and said to call duty manager.   Duty manager has come and in just compensating this incident with dinner.   All over after paying 15000 inr Approx per day for club room I was not satisfied with this HYAT category Hotel. As it is mixed experience of staff, As some staff are happy to help and some did not bother you on. Housekeeping staff is poor and not maintained.    Club lounge staff is nice. But again nothing to have full day in club lounge, just tea coffee soft drinks and biscuits. In evening of cocktail hours, there was of cheap cold snacks, when I complained to staff , they told that we serve cold snacks only and didn't bother to serve hot snacks.   In restaurant also dinner buffet was lack of variety as also in breakfast.     In despite I would never come back with this huge price to hyatt REGENCY hotel.     I TRULLY SAY IT IS TRUE THAT LAST GUEST IS ALSO RIGHT WITH IS REVIEW ON TRIP ADVISOR AS I ALSO FACED SAME ISSUE AT BREAKFAST TIME

This was my third and last visit to Hyatt Kathmandu. Over the years things have gone bad here. Staff seems tired and unhappy. Facilities such as key card access doors are not working. Worst of all we were awaken 5:30 am by someone entering the room with an access card and quickly disappearing. I called reception immediately but never got an explanation or follow up from the staff despite being promised so. Then again 6:30 am delivery of two bottles of water we never asked for. On check out reception had nothing to say other than must have been a mistake. Thus double lock your door if you plan to stay here. Wifi is slow. Food service at the Cafe is just okay but not what you would expect from Hyatt Regency. This hotel is also popular for weddings and events that you might like or not. What's left of the old glory days is the surrounding green garden, in contrast to the dusty, busy Kathmandu roads. But I've had enough of this dump and will on my next visit head to the new Marriott that just opened in Kathmandu.

Pricey? definitely! Room is homey, bed and pillows are heaven sent to a weary traveller. Desk and chair was so comforting i actually  finished a lot of work.  Breakfast is fantastic and the lawn is the best in the city.  Well worth it when you are on business.

Excellent f &  b service. But thats where it ends. No smile at getting out of car and passing concierge n reception. At check in room was filthy despite the hotel being aware of our arrival time etc 6 mths in advance.  during checkin we were not told of the facilities of the hotel, we had to go to our room, thought there may be info in the compendium but guess what there was none in the room so we ended up going back to reception to find out. Every night since then the ac has not been working. We have not been sleeping well at all because of the heat in the room.  There was an ill-mannered wedding group on our 1st 2 nights who would create extreme noise pollution after midnight. We called reception many times to no avail.  The 3rd dwy we thought of catching up on some sleep but guess what, they thought it was ok to scream talk directly ourside our room. My sister went to reception to let them know about the noise. The best she was told was, they were checking out so the noise would stop. It didnt thoufh until 3 hours later.It seemed we were less important, but excuse me we were paying guests not staying for free. A few staff who highly deserve a hystar mention are rupesh in reception, sajan and nabin in housekeeping, narayan, ashish, ranjita, raju, sanjee, rabin, nigam, reshmi  and the chefs at the cafe, and annie in reservations. The other reception staff and concierge are not noteworthy.  As  we were only given good service  at the cafe, thats where we spent most of  our time.  Being hyatt, an american brand you should be aware of how to design a disabled room's bathroom. Ours was not at all disable friendly. I could have slipped a few times in the 6 days.  Hopefully when refurbing the rooms this is desperately looked into. Also providing good customer service should start from the door, not after we have put in a complaint on the first day.  We did not require consolation service. We just wanted the hyatt regency service from the get go. Would not recommend the hotel to anybody for the future. Thank you for nothing HR kathmandu

This was used to be the best hotel in Kathmandu to stay but recently with the change of top management the quality of service at hotel has gone down (real sad) Building of hotel is really beautiful and majestic. This hotel used to take care of their long time customers pretty well but during this stay I did not experience that usual hospitality. The major problem is room temperature during winter months. It is not very cold in Kathmandu but central air conditioning system has only one setting per weather so in winter rooms are too hot to sleep as hot air is being blown by the system. Windows can be opened but there are hundreds of pigeons sitting outside and make loud noises. Rooms have wooden floors and are not cleaned properly. There are stains all over the floor. With little care by management this hotel can be top Kathmandu hotel again.

カトマンズの中心部からは少し離れた高台に建つ、伝統建築を取り入れたまるで宮殿のようなホテルです。世界遺産のボダナートから程近く、敷地に隣接する美術館をショートカットすれば歩いて6～7分ほど。空港からも渋滞がなければ車で20分ほどで、送迎バスも運行されています（有料）。中心部へも降車専用のシャトルバスが運行していますが、戻ってくるにはタクシーが必須なので注意が必要です。渋滞が激しく、整備が行き届いていない大通りの土煙や排気ガスが嘘のように、ホテルの広い敷地に一歩足を踏みいれると驚くほど静か。食事もスパのトリートメントも手頃で利用しやすく、プールサイドや庭を散策して一日のんびりと過ごせます。クラブフロアのゲストは空港シャトルバスが無料で利用できるのも嬉しいところ。

Stayed in Room 508 for a night, on business. It was a welcome harbor - filled with Kathmandu charm -  from the cacophony of the City.The lobby is spacious and and the staff were o hand to welcome us with the traditional silk scarf. Nice touch. Check-in was reasonably quick and with just the right amount of pleasantries. I was then escorted to my room.At first instance the room looked tired. But the upkeep was good. Good sized room, king bed, writing desk, huge flat screen tv with reasonable selection of channels, more than adequate closet space and mini-bar. Clean, working aircon, lighting a tad dark. Good sized bathroom, separate tub and shower. Adequate amenities. Good water pressure.Fair Breakfast buffet spread. Quality of food is okay but have had better. Staff is attentive. Airy and well lit coffee shop.The gym was reasonably equipped though the machines were old. No tv monitors on the tread mill and elliptical machines. Helpful staff.Be prepared for intermittent power failures though it kicks back in quickly. I almost got trapped in the elevator but was glad I stepped out in time.Check out was quick and efficient. The staff even helped reinstate my Hyatt Passport account.  It was a pleasant stay.
２泊しましたが、以前宿泊したYAK&YETIとは比べ物にならないくらい良かったです。朝昼夜ともホテルで食事しましたが、質、品数、味とも最高です。またスタッフのサービスもよいです。清潔感は日本並み。プールやジャグジーの水もきれいで、楽しめました。シャワールームと浴槽が別で広々しています。

I have been staying at this property for many years and this time it felt in need of refurbishment ... I stayed in the Regency club and the room was on the 5th floor ( not 6the where the lounge is. The parquet floor was buckling, the towels were thin the beds and pillows not terribly comfortable. I was surprised that there was no evening turn down service and only one bathrobe in a twin room. No face cloths until I requested them either. The dress code for the executive or Regency Club Lounge seems to have slipped: singlet and workout shorts???😳And small children and babies being Brest fed???The pool and garden are still beautiful as is the lobby. Ask for a high floor room with stupa view ( although this is being rebuilt at the moment)

I have only just returned from Nepal, and wish to say that the HyattRegency Kathmandu, where I stayed for 2 nights, was one of thehighlights of my Nepal experience!   From the moment one enters the hotel, you are made to feel special!The Lobby staff, in particular the very handsome and elegant Julian,made my stay very special .. I would like to thank him for catering tomy needs and, again, making me feel special.The restaurant food, the ambiance, the lovely room, the atmosphere ..this hotel provides everything!I thoroughly recommend, while in Kathmandu, to stay in this lovely place,with it's manicured garden, tranquil atmosphere ... you need this afterthe noise, and bustle of the outside city.Best wishes to all who took care of me ... a single female.

We stayed in the Hyatt Regency in June 2015 (post earthquake).  The staff and facility was outstanding. I felt secure that if there were aftershocks, I would be taken care of (I did not experience any aftershocks)--there was even a flashlight in my room.  I recommend this facility highly for its comfort and excellance.

located a bit away from tourist Thamel, you can walk out the back gate to Bouddanath in a few minutes. The common rooms are spacious with a twist of Traditional but the entrance looks like large pond without the water.Service was great, but ned a taxi to go anywhere. Rooms were fine, typical of a 5 star hotel in a developing country. It's expensive for Nepal.Lacks the true local charm of Dwarikas, which is my 1st choice

Even though it's a Hyatt, never think that you will find the same standards. A serious renovation is needed to improve physical standards of the property. Also staff should be trained in order to reach the service quality of a 5 star hotel.

Excelente ponto de partida e de retorno para as trilhas do Himalaia. Nada como um hotel muito confortável, atendentes muito atenciosos, limpeza, comida boa, ótima localização. E voltar para uma cama confortável, um banheiro amplo e com muita água é uma benção para quem andou pelas trilhas, por melhores que sejam os guias e equipes de apoio.

My friend was an outsider staying at Hyatt without any local number.I called Hyatt at around 6pm just to know if she was in the Hotel and got a taxi to come till Thamel.To my surprise i got a very bad response from the reception.He was one rude man iv ever spoken to.I always hated the location and it added more with this kind of behavior.Think twice before you want to book a room in here.They might not live upto your expectation.The name is big but the service is poor which is important for the travelers.They would want a better service after they pay so much.They are less systematic as well.

I unfortunately had to stay at this hotel on my way back to Canada, and what a total nightmare.I was guaranteed a price of $178 when i booked, and upon check-out the rate changed to $200!!I had to then provide "proof" to the gal at the front desk that this was the original rate i had booked at.  After 10 phone calls to their reservation dept, 20mins, and my complete disgust at their lack of professionalism i was 'allowed' to check out.I will never stay here again and would not recommend this hotel.Internet charges are on top of the cost of stay here…for $200/night, there are far better rated hotels that offer comp wi-fi and breakfast and service versus this placeThe Royal Penguin in Thamel is far better!!Rooms are old, not in very good condition, beds are old and lumpy.  And the bathrooms lack any maintenance at all.Only benefit of this hotel is that its close to the airport.

This hotel was absolutely amazing.  The staff were first rate and made sure you were taken care of.  The grounds of the hotel are beautiful and well kept.  The architecture of the hotel is fabulous and has a flair for the Nepalese culture.  It is well situated by the Stuppa which is a 5 minute walk from the hotel through the back gate.  The gate has a security guard and there is a bell to ring to be let back in.  The hotel has a shuttle service to all the major tourist areas from the hotel which is free.  The food at the hotel is first rate and varies each day.  I recommend getting a Stuppa view room which is well worth it.  The size of the rooms and the decor is great.  It is very easy to arrange tours also as you can do it right on site.  The pool and the grounds are a great oasis of tranquility that makes you feel so relaxed.  The only complaint I have is that they charge for internet access which I would have liked to have had included in this day and age.  A definite return destination for me.

ホテル内にあれだけの警備員が見回りしているハイヤットに始めて来ました。一般ピープルの私にはちょっと自分が要人になった様で楽しかったですが。。笑現地人の人からはとても高い宿泊費のようなので（といっても1万五千円くらい)ロビーにはやはり現地のお偉方さんが打ち合わせなどしてました。ロビー前のスペースがむっちゃくちゃかっこいいです！お部屋も広いです。私はホテルのアイスティーがとても気に入りました！タイとかもそうですがライムをかなり入れてあまーい感じ。ただ私が行った2014年４月現在、空港からホテルのほうに行く道を拡張工事していて砂煙が凄いです。かなりビックリすると思うのでマスクか口を覆えるものは必須です。

This hotel is in a very good location, a short walk from the Boudhanath Stupa and whilst very close to the hustle and bustle of the city it is set back in an enormous garden making it a tranquil heaven amidst the chaos of Kathmandu! The other main attractions in the city are a bit further afield, but as the taxis are very inexpensive it isn't a problem.Our check in at the club was smooth and we were taken to our Club Deluxe King room. The bedroom was spacious, the bathroom very big and both had doors to a huge terrace with superb views of the Boudhanath Stupa; In fact we could see the Stupa from both our bed and the bath! The rain shower was very powerful; the air conditioning system very effective and our room was kept very clean throughout our stay. The Wi-Fi was included in the rate and seemed to be just fine.The food served at evening hors d'oeuvres was fresh, varied and had enough choice for vegetarians, their orange juice was also very fresh and the Staff at the Club were very attentive. The breakfast buffet was very good, offering a wide variety of freshly baked breads, pastries, fruit, juices, cold meats, cheeses and much more. We can’t fault the variety and food quality served at this hotel.The Staff at the Club and throughout the hotel were very friendly, efficient and always willing to help, they always delivered their service with a smile! We would definitely recommend this hotel.

My wife and I recently stayed in this Hotel for three nights. On arrival we could not enter the hotel by the main door as it was being refurbished. As we checked in nothing was said about any works going on and we had not been advised of anything when making the booking or prior to our arrival. We also noticed that the bar balcony was off limits as it was being painted, but didn't think much of it. The room looked a little tired, but we managed to get a decent nights sleep on the first night. On the second day they were painting the main reception area and that evening/night it sounded like furniture was being moved around in the room above ours. I managed to get some sleep, but my wife was kept awake most of the night. The next day we decided to relax by the pool in the afternoon to try and recharge our batteries, but no sooner had we got onto the sunloungers, the pool was closed, a chemical cleaning pump was set up not 10 feet from where we were sitting, and in addition they started jet washing the façade of the building (hanging on ropes with a Karcher!). It was rather noisy and not conducive to relaxation so we retired to our room for some peace and quiet. We had a very early start the next day so on returning to the room after dinner we wanted to get to bed at a decent time (10pm). However, the furniture movement, regular toilet flushing, banging and crashing fired up again and went on for over an hour at which point I tried to call the manager and this is when we found out the phone in our room didn't work. I went down to the front desk and that is when the manager explained the hotel was being refurbished, that the work crews were occupying the rooms above ours and were refurbishing them too whilst they were staying in them!! I have no idea how many were staying in each room or what they were doing, but the manager told them to be quite, but 30 minutes later it kicked off again and went on all night. Needless to say we got little sleep. One of the worst hotel experiences ever. They did refund our money in the end, but be warned, their policy is clearly not to advise customers of what could be going on during their stay, and the managers comment that "this refurbishment is being done to make your stay better" was unbelievable.

Decor with atmosphere, friendly and polite staff, breakfast not bad but would be better with more international choices, eg other Asian choices other than Indian and Nepalis, perhaps Japanese or chinese choices for guests with a longer stay? Food clean and fresh. Don't understand why some got sick. Perhaps from outside the hotel?Nice live native music every night in lobby from very early (6pm.) till late.Convenient free shuttle to town. Nice and exclusive to be a little away from dusty, crowded and crazy traffic. Close to major historic sites.Walls too thin, can even hear the newspaper delivery every morning at around 6am. Sauna too crowded (men's, women's: not tried). Outdoor whirlpool: a walk outdoor from changing room, can be cold in winter). Compared to other Hyatt: would be nice if tooth brushes/paste are provided without asking.Wifi in many coffee shops in town are free so in this hotel, it would seem more friendly to guests if it was also free.

Thank you to the Regency Club and specially to Rijesh for his  kindness of heart and his diligent attention to meet our needs and requests. We love the Regency Club’s coziness and the abundance of delicious food served around 5.30pm. A peaceful oasis to relax into💗🙏🏻Namaste

experience was exceptional and  making it a perfect spot for relaxed evening. The decor is vintage with a touch of elegance, creating a welcoming ambiance.The staff at Nirman were incredibly attentive and friendly. From the moment we walked in, we were greeted with warm smiles and prompt service. Our server was knowledgeable about the menu and provided excellent recommendations tailored to our tastes.Thank you  Nirman will definitely back again.

The drink was so delicious, refreshing and aromatic  and well presented and the food was mind-blowing , fresh I will recommend a regency club sandwich to others and The service was second to none and our main  server nirman in white t-shirt and his team was so accommodating and friendly

We had visited the Hyatt regency Casino on 29.09.23 with my friends. While playing blackjack, the dealer made a mistake due to which they lost the game. But the manager overturned the mistake and took the game. All the players at the table protested, but the management behave very unprofessionally. All the players decided to walk out in protest, and the managers was unmoved. I have visited all the major casinos everywhere and no where could the management be so casual about game rules. Casinos run on fair play and when the management can behave in such way, it amounts to cheating by the casino.Hope this mistake is not repeated with other customers, because we won't be visiting any of their casinos again.

Good and large property and very  good staff. All staff were very attentive from check in to check out and during the stay as well. Would definitely like to recommend to visit this hotel hyatt regency Kathmandu

Hyatt Regency, Kathmandu is beautiful property. The staff is very friendly and helpful. The rooms are specious with amazing view. The hotel is  suitable for both business visits and leisure. I highly recommend the Hyatt Regency for your stay in Kathmandu.

Cet hôtel est superbe, luxe et calme au milieu d’un grand parc au cœur de la ville. A deux pas de la fameuse Stupa. Idéal pour se remettre de la turbulence de la ville.Nous y étions en convention, superbe organisation, repas délicieux, service impeccable.Les chambres sont spacieuses et confortables. Le wifi est gratuit. Les restaurants sont délicieux, j’ai particulièrement à dire le buffet du petit-déjeuner, pain croustillant, fromage de Yak et lassi savoureux.Il est un peu loin de Thamel, mais idéal pour visiter ce quartier de Kathmandu.Il y a une énorme piscine, mais il faisait encore frais en mars pour tenter un bain.

4-5 defa kaldım bu otelde. Az çok gözlem imkanım oldu. İlk önce Katmandu şartları açısından bakıldığı zaman, çok ama çok iyi. Kendi içlerinde steril bir dünya yaratmışlar, dışarıya göre oldukça temiz denilebilir. Otelin girişi o mistik havayı size yansıtıyor zaten. Fiyatları için çok emin değilim, şirketimizin bizim için ayarladığı otel, ama bildiğim kadarıyla pahalı bir otel. Resepsiyon hizmetleri hızlı sayılır, otelin içerisinde atm var, ama yaklaşık 500 Nepal Rupi’si komisyon alıyorlar dikkatinize. Otel yapısı itibariyle modern değil, eski bir yapı ama yanlış hatırlamıyorsam 2016 ya da 2017 de olan büyük depremi atlattı. Arka tarafında yürüyüş yerleri ve büyük bir bahçesi var. Bu arada arkadaki yoldan, Bodha Stupa’ya hemen 10 dakikada yürüyerek varıyorsunuz. Aslında merkezi bir konumda sayılır, ama malum, Katmandu’nun olmayan yolları ve keşmekeş içerisindeki trafiğiyle istediğiniz her yere hemen ulaşamıyorsunuz. Daha iki gün önce geldim sanki renovasyon vardı, tam emin değilim, ama odalar artık eskimiş. Yataklar rahatsız, internet geliştirilmeli. Bazı odalarda sadece sayfa açabiliyorsunuz. Odalarda gerçekten ısınma problemi var. Klimayı sıcakta açmanıza rağmen, buz gibi olabiliyor. Yemekleri başarılı tipik hint mutfağı, kahvaltıda çeşit bol. Fast food yiyecekler de güzel ve leziz. Rox restaurant çok iyi diyebilirim. ‘Katmandu’nun en fazla tercih edilen otellerinden birisi’ olmanın kaymağını fazlaca yemişler, artık yenilenmeleri lazım. Ama yine de Katmandu için çok iyi bir seçenek. Bu arada, asansör 3. Katta oluyor rezervasyonda, kahvaltı salonu 1. Katta ve kahvaltı ve yemek saatlerinde bütün odayı ve koridoru yemek kokuları kaplıyor. Bilginize.

Built in typical Nepali palace architecture...beautiful lobby...great gemstone shops...wonderful staff...walking distance from Pashupatinath temple...good Indian and continental cuisine...great breakfast buffet

The hotel is very highly priced compared to luxury you find in other Haytt group of Hotels. The hotel do not keep sufficient toiletries in the bathroom and you have to ask housekeeping every time to send the very basic things like Shaking Kit. The Shaving Kit quality they provided me after asking for the same is of extremely poor quality. The maintenance / housekeeping is also poor , Electric cattle was not working, later they replaced it.The remote of TV was non - functional , later on calling the service staff, they replaced the battery. The blower stopped functioning, again I have to call them to rectify it.However the hotel provides a very good morning breakfast with lot of options. The food quality and taste is awesome, I had dinner and it was sumptuous.

Ich habe mich im Hyatt sehr wohl gefühlt. Hotel ist umgeben von riesiger Park Anlage mit schoenem Pool. Schon daher fuehlt man sich wie in einer Oase in der stinkenden Stadt voller Luftverschmutzung und Laerm. Ins Zentrum faehrt man mit den preiswerten Taxen ca 20 Min.Durch einen Hinterausgang am Pool kann man zur Bodnath Stupa in wenigen min gehen, sehr sehenswert insb zum Sonnenuntergang mit Tausenden Pilgern.Das Zimmer war grosszuegig, die Klimaanlage schaffte es aber nicht immer fuer eine angenehme Beheizung zu sorgen, es waren ca 4 Grad nachts draussen. Auch das Marmorbad war grosszuegig und gepflegt. Sehr gut war das Essen im Buffetrestaurant mit vielen einheimischen Gerichten. Das Personal war stets sehr zuvorkommend. Der Healthclub mit Sauna koennte eine Renovierung vertragen, ist in die Jahre gekommen. Er ist getrennt fuer Frauen und Maenner.Die Bar des Hotels koennte auch eine Änderung gebrauchen. Sie ist sehr dunkel, schön ein paar Kerzen koennten das Ambiente aufwerten. Die Lobbybar wird derzeit umgebaut und ist danach sicherlich eine gute Alternative. Ich wuerde das Hotel erneut wählen und habe mich wohl gefühlt.

Das Hyatt Regency hat eine sehr gute Lage insbesondere wenn man in Boudnath übernachten will. Vom Hotel hat man direkten Blick auf die Stupa. Wir waren zum zweiten Mal im Hotel. Der Empfang war gut und wir konnten von einer Suite auf ein Stupa-View-Zimmer wechseln. Diese sind nicht nur groß sondern auch mit sagenhaftem Blick direkt auf die Stupa. Zimmer war sauber und auch das Bad angenehm mit separater Dusche. Generell ist es Hyatt-Qualität, aber man merkt auch weiterhin ein paar Abnutzungsspuren. Das Frühstück war mit sehr großer Auswahl und guter Qualität sowohl westliche als auch nepalesische/indische Speisen. Der Pool-Bereich ist sehr schön und auch als kleine Oase in der Stadt entspannend. Der Spa-Bereich war auch schön, die Funktionsfähigkeit des Dampfbads etwas eingeschränkt, aber die Massage auch sehr gut. In Summe ein sehr schönes Hotel in Boudnath und sicher eines der besten in Kathmandu.

The hotel and grounds are very impressive and lovely.  Nice room, especially the big bathroom.  The buffets in the main restaurant were great and reasonably priced too.  The grounds and gardens are especially pretty.  I enjoyed the once a day free shuttle to the Thamel area.  The staff were all as friendly and as helpful as can be.  The rooms didn't  have heat in December,  and it might be cold for some,  but they promptly brought extra blankets and a small portable room heater.  The wood in my room was slightly worn, and the bed comfort was acceptable/good.

After being away from family for more than a month and half, I took my family to Hyatt Hotel one night stay as a treat.  The Hotel's architecture seemed nice and blending quite with Nepalese arts and architecture and values.  The place being in the middle of the city offered a quiet and peaceful environment.  Boudhanath Stupa (the world heritage Buddhist Stupa) was at walking distance and even much shorter from the back gate. The food was good although I expected to be better.The best thing about this hotel are it is very near the city center and quite close to airport and golf clubs.

Spacious and comfortable hotel with large hotel room, friendly and helpful staffs in all areas. You can enjoy yourself with swimming pool, gym room and spa services. No worries if you cannot eat outside, hotel has two big restaurants and one small cafe that can feed your stomach. I must say food in Rox restaurant is really nice, especially after a long day for business meetings. I will recommend anyone to stay with Hyatt in Kathmandu

we had a wonderful stay. enjoyed the gym, spa & club lounge. Had good time at the rox bar excellent bartender. Room service was also great. The property ground is so beautiful & my son had a blast playing at the playground with slides, swings & see-saw. the water at the kids pool was colder than expected so we skipped it. I've stayed here numerous times over the years & its always a gem of a place and so peaceful. this time only little let down was that we had booked 2 club level rooms for better views but we were placed on 5th floor one floor below the regency club lounge floor(6th fllor). not a big issue. lastly i had an interaction with club lounge staff (shalima) during checkout, she could use more smile & better attitude so we the guests would feel more welcomed.

Ambience of hotel was quite good and all over staff of hotel was not bell behaved and not friendly at all . Breakfast of hotel was not so good ,small insects were there in the dry fruits but none paid attention to that thing after complaining also . very poor experience at the hotel. staff of the hotel only pa attention to the people of other countries and not to Indians at all. Dint expected this much poor experience . rooms were also not so spacious.

May be the best option of Kathmandu. We stayed here for two days. Was an excellent stay. Rooms very big in size, but requires some renovations. Very simple decor, so, requires to update it. But, bathroom is definitely very good. Quality of bed linen and bath towels very good. Lobby area is also excellent, decorated in Nepalese style. Very big property. Good restaurant serves all types of delicious food. Staff very courteous. Overall our stay at Hyatt was excellent.

The primary reason I am writing this feedback is to commend the amazing staff that makes this hotel great. But first, the hotel itself is just as amazing. We chose this hotel after our trekking trip. It was the best decision ever after spending many nights in teahouses. Right from the start, you enter a gated area in Boudha and you drive up this long driveway to the hotel entrance. The hotel is set inside ~30 acres of property so you don't get the dust and noise (like Thamel). Boudha also has great shopping and better prices in my opinion, and this hotel is situated close to everything. The room we got were much more spacious than expected and for the price, it was a steal! Every amenity imaginable is there and the restaurants were all great. What makes great hotel even greater or great to begin with is the staff. The staff at this hotel is just that! Right from the start when we arrive without a reservation we spoke to Nima at the front desk to make our reservations. She accomodated every possible need and was able to get us the room we wanted (needed after our trek) even with almost full occupancy. She truly was a savior and we called her that! We also had an unexpected delay to our departure from Nepal due to the Chinese President visiting. This caused us to extend our stay for a day, again without any reservation, and Nima accommodated us right away. We ate alot at the hotel, which has great food, and wanted to also call out Rajendra and Deelip who I believe are the chefs. There was also the wait staff Deelip, Sanjeev, Sangita, Binu, Amrit and Nirman at the pool. I am sure I am missing others not because they were not good but I didn't have the pleasure to meet all of them. ALL the staff made us feel like home. They always made sure we had our food and drinks on time. They also made sure to follow up on the food and solicited our thoughts on the food. They felt like family to me from the first time I met them and while I stayed at a hotel I felt like I ate at home, at a family home. I will absolutely return to this hotel and if you have a chance to go here, you should. I would go here just for the staff who made me feel like home. But the hotel itself is amazing.

Pase dos noches en este hotel,esta muy bien , el personal muy amable se esfuerzan para que estes bien, el buffete del desayuno correcto incluso te hacen tortilla,huevos i algo de carne al momento, buen hotel

This is the grande dame of Kathmandu hotels: good location, big rooms with high ceiling, great pool and running track, tennis court and very good restaurant in particular for breakfast. I enjoyed the executive lounge where the very professional and kind Tscwang, Salina, Samitshya and Asmita made my stay quite pleasant. I suggest to add some more pool umbrellas and to renovate the gym and sauna area which are a bit tired. The hotel keep the promise of its high standard.

The hotel is surrounded by a nice garden and well maintained, very close to the Stupa Baudhanath!The room was ok, with a nice view of the Stupa.To be honest , I didn’t like the breakfast ...not that many options and quality not ok, compare to the lunch that I really liked!The big issue is the ventilation system of the restaurant...after your meal, you need to change your shirt, if you don’t want to smell of food for the rest of the day....Few things to improve in order to make this hotel a great place .

Spent three days at this hotel which is only a short walk away from the Stuppa, The room was large and well equipped. Service was excellent and the Club lounge was great in the evenings.The grounds and pool are wonderful, Breakfast was a little too Nepalese for my taste.

Hyatt Regency is perhaps the best property in Kathmandu today. The rooms with Stupa view are very nice. The attached Casino Pride is definitely an added attraction.The lobby with miniature temple decor is stunning. Hyatt has sprawling lawns and nice walkways. The spa is also quite good. The Italian restaurant serves excellent food & drinks.A special mention must go the courteous staff as well. We were specially handled very efficiently and smilingly by Sujita at the reception. A comfortable stay in every which way!

This is the absolute best place to stay in Kathmandu. Beautiful heritage moments and peaceful clean rooms. The gardens are spectacular and the food is delicious! Do not miss out on that amazing breakfast buffet. The service was outstanding and truly made me feel welcome and cared for. They surprised me with beautiful wildflowers in my room and were available to help me navigate the wild and wonderful Kathmandu. I will be returning and definitely staying at my new home at the Hyatt. Also- make sure to splurge on the rooms facing the stupa- there is nothing more beautiful than waking up to the golden glow of the eyes of this spiritual Mecca!

THis hotel is a gem with staff helping us like we were long lost family and our welcome home. We salute all staff from the front driveway people to the hotel check-in and concierge/travel agent. They really help you out with your questions and take the time to care.  The laundry team really helped me out on two occasions. The F&B Service helped us eat a wide variety tasty breakfast; I would like to especially thank Binu, Puja, and Amrit there in the F & B Service. Thank you. The tennis facility is excellent with staff there to help out. I never had a ball recovery service until I went there. The hotel gym staff were helpful for us to orient how to rent raquets and proceed. The hotel rooms are very quiet with thick walls to ensure quiet.  When I booked a second visit for my last night, they appropriately gave me the quietest room I have ever seen and heard. Someone said that this five-star is the closest one to the airport. Traffic in Katmandu is intense gridlock during rush hour so this tip helped us. When we left Nepal, we left at late night -- no traffic -- and the taxi to the airport was only ten minutes.

This is my third visit to Hyatt Regency Kathmandu, I am always been treated as a value customer and a loyal member. The hotel takes my feedback positively and I see improvement almost immediatelyKudus goes to Salina, Pumu, Rabison and Ashmida at the Club Lounge. They had assigned the room I want it to be and they also put my request in my profile. My rooms are ready upon our arrival and staff are always happy to serve.I also wish to thank Mr Pravin Shrestha for making the reservation for me. I will definitely return again.Thanks and please keep up the good work. I am so delighted to be here again.Regards,Lyn Lyn PEH Swo Keaw

This is the second time I’ve stayed at this hotel ... and once again it’s been wonderful ... mostly due to the fact that our Boudhanath stupa facing room provides the best view in the world! Thank you to Promiksha at the hotel for arranging this room for us - we loved it. The staff across the hotel are professional, helpful and never too busy to support guests’ needs. Thank you all.

Excellent location with professional staff to cater your needs and provide best service in terms of value for money. I would recommend to stay when on a trip with family . Good food and we'll connected to the city .

Very nice hotel! The pool is very nice and service there is excellent.Such a delightful experience. We were greeted with so much elegance. Well thought out rooms, I would like to thanks entire staff for their efforts to make our stay comfortable

I have visited all the available 5 star hotels in Kathmandu and none of them compare to this one. Little far from the city Center but close to the airport. Food is excellent, rooms are large and comfortable. The pool is large and beautiful. I also enjoyed the spa services and would highly recommend the same.

I went there for meetings but when I ask for the WiFi receptionist told me that they will not allow to use WiFi for outside people. Nowadays in Nepal everyone can get WiFi everywhere but in this 5 star hotel you cannot use WiFi this is really strange😂

De verdad, pedazo de hotel.Enorme, habitación buenas, piscina, cuando yo estuve, era enorme.Debo decir antes que nada que estuve en 2006.Comidas genial, personal amable.Y en general el hotel perfecto, limpieza de las habitaciones bien, del hotel en general perfecto, no tengo ningún pero ni nada.No disfruté mucho del hotel y las instalaciones, llegaba para dormir prácticamente, pero es que aquello tiene muchas cosas por ver y no te da tiempo de disfrutar del hotel, Katmandú es increíble.Además, da gusto llegar a un buen hotel, como éste, después de estar de visita por allí y poder encontarte con una buena habitación y restaurante.Si vuelvo allí, volveré a éste hotel.

A entrada e recepção do hotel são lindos. Porém chegamos as 16:30 e nosso quarto ainda não estava pronto, fizeram uma confusão com as chaves.Os quartos são espaçosos, porém muito antigo. Cheira mofo. Nosso banheiro não descia água, ficou um nojo o banheiro, pois alagou inteiroCafé da manhã e restaurantes razoável.A vista do club lounge eh bem bonitaPiscina bacana. Porém não me hospedaria novamente, serviço muito fraco.

Saya tinggal di hyatt untuk urusan bisnis pada Juni 2019. Hanya 20-30 menit dari bandara dan hotel ini bagus untuk mengatur transportasi di Kathmandu. Kolam sangat besar. Saya sakit setelah makan di sini jadi hati-hati.

hotel perfectamente ubicado, cerca del aeropuerto, a dos minutos andando de la mayor estupa de nepal, a 20 minutos andando del crematorio, justo en frente tienes un supermercado con todo lo que necesitas, un placer la estancia y el lugar.

Its a combination of excellent exterior / interior alongwith luxury rooms . Staff is very courteous . Nice food and great spread in breakfast for veg and non veg both . Pool and walking track is perfect . Lobby area and entrance is a place to click lot of pics

This hotel was exceptional!  The rooms were large, comfortable, and well furnished!  A large soaking bathtub was so nice after a long day of touring!  The mini-bar was astonishingly inexpensive as I discovered after a day of Delhi-Belly necessitated staying in the room.  The grounds are lavish and well tended with plenty of grass, roses, and a huge swimming pool/spa area.  The lobby was interesting and all the staff were attentive and welcoming.  The location could not be better as a short walk out the back gate (attended by a security person) leads to the incredible Boudhanath, the world's largest stupa.  Here in the center is the Stupa surrounded by brass prayer rollers and shops where no one is harassed so you can look at your leisure!  Monks of all ages are walking the area which is accomplished in a clockwise direction where everyone is welcome to walk the path of happiness and contemplation!  Fantastic feel and upbeat energy that must be experienced to fully comprehend!  Goodwill personified in a truly magical place.

Entering this oasis in the Kathmandu dust and chaos was a welcomed relief.Quiet, spacious and a little western was great.  A great mix.Nirman at the pool bar makes a great caprioska, and Milan at the Rox restaurant looked after us beautifully twice.

Superb resort near to airport. Ambience is very pleasant and the service is excellent. Food options are many by way of different restaurants and quality is excellent. Swimming pool is nicely located. Staff is serving guests with pleasant smiles and enthusiastic attitude. Best choice for a great stay in Nepal capital.

I used my points to book a club floor room the nights before and after my Bhutan tour.  I was not disappointed.  The hotel is excellent with plenty to do.  The food buffets over a wide variety of choices and I came out satisfied each time.  Menu service at lunch both times was a bit too slow.Room furnishings on the club floor were satisfactory.  Room was a great size with high ceilings.  Club floor perks include airport transfers as well as a delightful late afternoon layout in the lounge.Spa is professional and I services were above average. Well worth what I paid for a hotel of this calibre.

Un hotel increíble, cómodo, con un servicio de primera, personal muy amable y su restaurante con muy buena comida y variedad de opciones. Definitivamente la mejor opción en Kathmandu.Lo recomendaría sin dudas

We recently had a comfortable and very good stay in the hotel. It is a fabulous property with very nice lobby, good gardens and very good swimming pool and outdoor area. Our club room was spacious and had very good views of the Stupa. Club lounge is very good with exceptional service. Mr. Robinson, Mr. Kushal were there to help us with all the needs and information including suggestions for food and helping with reservations. All other team members in the lounge were very hospitable and caring.Making room reservation on the hotel website was a nightmare. Most information on the website related to rooms and inclusions was factually incorrect, confusing, misleading, and casual. When I sent e-mails to make enquiries about some of these confusions the communication from the guest service staff was disappointing, unprofessional, and useless. Keeping all the ambiguities as they were I still made my reservations on the hotel website but hotel can audit its website to remove some of these irritants. Staff dealing with guest communication also needs training.Hotel has two restaurants - The Cafe and The Rox. Both were very good and food and service was of high standards. Concierge desk has some very good staff and they were very helpful. Travel Desk in the hotel was unprofessional and useless. They have fixed packages for which the rates are exorbitant and worthless. They don't have any flexibility to provide cars to guests for flexible use in the city or to use it for a few hours. One can only take a car for the rigid packages as designed by them and that too at very high rates. Never seen such travel desk in a 5-star hotel anywhere in the world. Hotel will loose its reputation if they allow such Travel Desks and such policies in the hotel.This hotel is little away from the main city area and is near to airport. Roads outside are very dusty with lot of traffic and poor infrastructure. But once you step inside the hotel property it is an oasis.

It is a great hotel with a nice ambience around. The food was great too. Overall cleanliness and value for money are great. There is a nice jogging track surrounded by trees which were great. The only thing I didn't like is the bathroom. Being in Asia and especially Nepal, a Shattaf (bidet spray) is essential. I am sure every Indian and Nepali guest will have the same comment. On top of that, there was only one toilet roll kept. There is no comfortable hook to hang clothes and towel, close to the shower while taking a bath. The shower is at an angle wider than required and is not adjustable to be as vertical as required.

One of the many things that this hotel does right is realize that the main interaction that the guests will have is with the restaurant staff and the people I saw every morning, Manager Suman and his wonderful staff, including Reshmi and Pemba, made my stay here so memorable in every way.  The grounds are lovely and the rooms spacious, beautiful and well-maintained.  Also, it's nice to be slightly outside of the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu - this place is a terrific retreat from the City - but it's also convenient as well.  Love this hotel and looking forward to returning one day!

The Hyatt is located in one corner of the city. it is very close to the airport - about 10 to 15 minutes from the airport and about 15 to 20 minutes to Thamel (30 minutes in heavy traffice). the taxi fare from hotel to THamel is approx 600 Nepali and about the same to the airport. It is located about 5 min from Boudhanath and about 10 min from Pasupathinath. Very convenient location for everest flight early in the morning. getting a taxi is not an issue at all in Kathmandu but a bit of jovial but focused bargaining on the fare is a must.It is a big property with a casino on site. from some of the rooms (towards the swimming pool and higher floors) one can see the Boudhanath Stupa. the breakfast spread is good but can do with a bit of variety. the italian restaurant is decent. the lobby is beautiful and there is a nice bar / tea joint just behind it with a good balcony overlooking the pool for seating. the staff in the hotel are very nice. the exchange rate is decent.overall a very good hotel for a short stay and making it your kathmandu base.

We stayed here for a total of four nights. The hotel itself is modern and clean, but the staff really need to up their game... - When we checked in the first question from the front desk (before we had even identified ourselves!) was what time we would be leaving on the day we depart. It was very off putting and odd. - At check in a bell hop took our bags and we were told he would take them to our room straightaway. An hour and a half later he still had not arrived. We had to call the front desk three times over the course of the next 45 minutes to get our bags. - When we checked in our room was dirty. Someone else’s garbage in the bin, toiletries opened and used by someone else, and someone else’s pee in the toilet!! The front desk had Housekeeping come (we were still waiting for our bags anyway!) but it was unpleasant. - At breakfast it was impossible to get coffee. You could ask three separate staff members and still not get it. Disappointing.

Amazing property with great hospitality and nice food. Had a pleasant stay here on my parent’s 50th anniversary and it was a real delight except for the the last day when it took the staff at the reception too long to finish our billing which eventually ended in we missing our flight way back to home.though the hotel offered us to stay with them on complimentary basis but we had to pay huge penalties to book our self again the tickets of the the return flight. Anyways the hotel rooms are bit outdated now and needs some updating.

Nel complesso tutto molto bene.L'hotel è accogliente ed il personale super efficiente. La camera silenziosa e pulita.Solo qualche sfumatura negativa; le tende un po logore e sporche, forse sarebbe il caso di sostituirle o lavarle, in relazione all'elevato standard dell'hotel.  Poche prese di corrente disponibili; si deve staccare dove possibile una lampada per poter ricaricare PC e telefono.

A group of us stayed here for 3 nights this month.  We had all upgraded to the Club floor for the benefits of breakfast, evening reception, and free transportation, and it was well worth the upgrade!The evening reception had a wide variety of food choices, so much so that we ended up eating dinner at the restaurant only one of the evenings.The rooms were well equipped, and the shower had great water pressure.  I also appreciated that the hair dryer was plugged in through the drawer in the vanity, so I actually could dry my hair and use a mirror.  After many days on the road, I was tired of seeing the bathroom outlets read "shavers only"!The hotel is an oasis from the dusty roads of Kathmandu.  The entrance and lobby areas are beautiful!

1. If there is a another option choose that over Hyatt 2. Poor condition of the rooms, corridors 3. The electric plugs in the room are inaccessible and has only Nepalese options, considering this hotel caters to international guests a simple change of plugs should be done.4. Food quality has gone down since my last stay 5. Outside area of the hotel is pathetic-unkept 6. And overly priced rooms.

Stayed in the presidential suite and hosted our corporate Christmas party in the suite for 13 guests and this hotel pulled out all the stops and made the stay and party one we will always remember.  The room was amazing with views of the pool, Buddhist stoupa, and the Himalayas.  They also decorated everything for Christmas and we had such a wonderful time and their staff went above and beyond with every detail to make sure out time there was a pleasant one.

We stayed here from the Christmas eve till the year-end. This is undoubtedly one of the best hyatt properties I have been. right from our pick up from the airport to our check in , the lounge access etc were so synchronized, we felt like we were VIP. We had 2 club rooms on the 6th floor - I will surely go back to this hotel with my family. Special thanks to Varun, Salina, Navina and Akansha. They were the best.

Pessimo hotel, sporco e trasandato.10 minuti per il check in, camere puzzolenti di fumo misto deodorante bagni con macchie di muffa e rubinetteria che perde.Ambiente trasandato e maleodorante, esterni trascurati, servizi inesistenti: uno Hyatt?Sì nel prezzo.Evitare!!!!

Stayed here for 3 nights and had a wonderful time. Prathima from Travel Desk was excellent in helping us narrow down must see since we had limited days and helped us patiently with travel reservations. Overall staff at the restaurant and front desk were also extremely courteous. Rooms are clean and spacious. Food is great ! On the pricey end compared to other hotels but will definitely recommend for families looking for a great place.

The rooms and facade are old and tired.  Frontdesk wasn’t exactly friendly or welcoming, and the food (both Western and local cuisine) was mediocre and often too salty.  Location was its only saving grace, within 30 minutes of the airport and walking distance from Boudanath Stupa.

Very Low quality.NO good interior and very high prices.Rude behavior and insulting attitude is what you get there.No socialiable Hotel.SARAF & MITTAL management is one of the worst.NO RESPECT for Client.Putting their ego and BIG name is what they offer.

stayed just for 2 days as a business trip. couldn't get much time to explore the whole hotel. overall experience was great. staff was cooperative, rooms are good, excellent breakfast. will come back again

I had an accident and was hospitalized: this was not only the best hospital to recuperate; but also the BEST hotel for any visit to Kathmandu! Thank you Asha & Prebin; and especially Kushal for the great service during my stay.Ricardo

We booked through booking.com and compared to tripadvisor there is a big gap in review score 4,5 vs booking 8.2. We found the hotel is not really up to 5 stars. The rooms are nice design and feature a well equiped bathroom with amenities. However the cleaning is really lacking, the furniture is dated (and damaged) and the rooms smell is unpleasant. The beds are comfortable. The hotel has a quiet location but if youre unlucky you might have loud drunken indian neighbours... The food was fine, rather spicy as one can expect in  Nepal, not so much western food. Staff was friendly and helpful. Pool looks nice, 10 min walk from the Stupa as well. We used the airport shuttle which is convenient also (9usd/pers). For the high price you pay to stay here (one of most expensive in Kathmandu) I would expect a much better value for money. A lot of work to be done to the rooms and the airconditioning system.

We got charged someone else’s bill from restaurant and the manager said that it has to be paid by someone so apparently we are the ones paying it. Very unprofessional. will not be back.Make sure you check your bills !

Kathmandu is a tough city, not a city that is easy to walk thru, and as a traveler you’ll appreciate a reprieve from the congestion and dust. The Hyatt Regency has enough property and surrounding manicured gardens to give you a break from the mayhem of cars and motorcycles roaming the streets unfettered by traffic lights, control signs, or even typical traffic laws. The added perk is its’ proximity to the Boudhanath Stupa which you can walk to via a back lane that is lined by authentic shops catering to Buddhists monks in need of robes, religious objects, or just a haircut. The walk way around the stupa is worth a visit and a revisit to watch pilgrims doing their rounds, to see monks chanting, window shopping for souvenirs, or to have a few reliable meals.
