The Hyatt is close to the airport and that is a real perk considering what the traffic is like. Rooms on the fourth floor (435-450) have a view of the stupa.

Hyatt Regency Kathmandu is a beautiful hotel, very near Boudha Stupa. The lobby area is spacious with a very calming and beautiful atmosphere due to the Nepalese temple style decoration. Every evening there are musicians who play very lovely Nepalese mountain music (flute, Sarangi, tabla) which creates a very serene atmosphere. Our room was very comfortable, spacious and beautifully decorated with a view of Boudha Stupa; very comfortable bed. It was a pleasure to come to come back to the hotel and the room after a busy day out - the moment we entered the room we could smell the sandalwood aroma. The hotel has a big garden with a jogging trail. The outside swimming pool area is lovely - surrounded by trees and a glimpse of the Himalayas at the distance.  Staff were very helpful and courteous. the only `complaint' we had about the hotel was that the food was overpriced! Overall a very lovely fantastic hotel - would love to come back again.

We stayed for 2 nights in Hyatt. The hotel is big, entrance, lobby, swimming pool, walking areas everything is beautiful in this room. We stayed in room 567 it had a swimming pool view, room was big and spacious.Hotel is situated 15-20 mins drive from the airport. It has a casino attached to it, which makes it a gamers paradise.Service was good, fast and efficient, we never had to wait long for and demand to be fulfilled. Breakfast spread is not very big but not small too as well, some may find it limited in choice but it was delicious.Overall a very good experience and when in Kathmandu I would like to stay here.

The high prices appear to be a reflection of the expenses of maintaining the huge premises of the property and not the service, furniture or fittings. Suffice to say, no where close to what one would expect from a Hyatt. We were disappointed. Had planned to stay for 4 nights - left after 1. Certainly not for those who don’t have a lot of money to spend.

Excellent hotel to stay.  This hotel has new management under Mr. Rajesh which has brought the cleanliness of hotel, services of staff and quality of food to its best.  I have been staying at this hotel since last 12 years and hotel was at its best during my recent stay.  My special thanks go to Nima and Robinson at club lounge and Bindu and Dipak at breakfast restaurant.

This is the most impressive, biggest hotel property in Kathmandu. The Buddhist style decors, perticularly in the lobby and executive lounge, are very impressive. Staff provided very good services. Breakfast has a good variety of choices. The three pools provide great relaxation and enjoyment, as well as the spa. A wonderful, beautiful, huge garden for a leisurely walk or jog.

I stayed on the club level, 6th floor with views of the Stupa.  The staff at the Hyatt make this hotel fantastic, I found the rooms to be very clean with updated bathrooms.  The location is great being within an easy walk to the Stupa and that area of restaurants and shops.  The grounds around the hotel are an oasis from the city and the pool is very clean. This was my first trip to Kathmandu and I found the hotel to be ideal.

Overall experience is not good at all,rooms are not up to the mark does not fit as Hyatt properties , swimming pool is good ,staff was not very courteous so overall experience was bad what they charged was not at all worth it

We stayed for two days at the end of our time in Nepal to unwind and relax. Everywhere you turn there is beauty, from the magnificent entry way featuring traditional Newari architecture to the musicians played Nepali music in lobby in the evening to the artwork located throughout the hotel . The gardens offered a quiet place to stroll amidst the trees, a most welcome retreat from the noise and chaos of city streets. Staff was friendly and our concierge on the 6th floor, Mina, went out of her way to make us feel welcome and to ensure that all of our needs were taken care of. The spa also offers a wonderful hot stones couples massage.

this large resort was a haven within this busy city; very relaxing lobby, grounds and room; the club floor drinks and food was definitely an added bonus; location - walking distance to the Buddha - made this an ideal location

The hotel facilities are well maintained (although it’s a bit outdated), the food is pretty good, swimming pools are beautiful even if the water in the biggest one is really cold - I could enjoy only the small whirlpool with warm water. The main negative point for me was unfriendly staff in particular in the front desk - unwelcoming, unfriendly and not able to provide with the necessary information. Could be better for a 5 stars hotel!

Security deposit of NPR 100,000 during check in and after 48 hrs of check out amount not reversed or credited in my account. Unbelievable that Hyatt is begging for security deposit and unable to reverse the same even after 48 hrs

This is a nice hotel - a bit old and some aspects need renovation (e.g. elevators) but overall very comfortable and with friendly staff. The breakfast buffet is very good with lots of variety. Transport congestion in Kathmandu is a fact of life and this can influence which hotel one selects.

I've stayed here twice and it's a lovely way to end a holiday of too many hours travelling by road in a van!!! Nepal is so beautiful and this hotel is far reach from what is outside it's doctors but it is wonderful to see the service and food from this country in such a luxurious hotel. They provide great jobs and training for their employees. We stayed in one of the suites and it was fantastic. Excellent service

We spent nights at this Hyatt three times during a tour of Nepal and Bhutan and enjoyed each visit. The location is convenient to the airport and the hilltop siting and large surrounding grounds are a nice escape from the bustle of the city.Our rooms were all good, though a little dated. A great foam top mattress would have been a real addition. However, the staff was uniformly friendly, the breakfast buffet was very good, the pool area was terrific and we really enjoyed the short walk to the massive Boudhanath stupa and the shops and restaurants which surround it.We enjoyed our stay and would go back.

This hotel, about 2 miles from the airport is a gorgeous and beautiful property. Unfortunately it is far from the center of the city and all the action of Thamel and Durbar Square. The traffic is really bad and so it takes forever to get to the sites in Kathmandu except for Boudhanath Stupa (which is a 15 minute walk) and Pashupatinath temple which is less than a mile away.The hotel is new, well maintained, has extensive grounds, friendly staff, an excellent restaurant and good bar.

This was my fifth stay at the Hyatt Regency.It was really value for money to stay here.Everything works well.Excellent breakfast.Concierge made an outstanding job.The Regency Lounge is good.I hope to come back soon.

I stayed here last summer as a treat for my birthday, while I was living in Boudha and attending summer school. I also used the pool and spa facilities a few times during the summer, which you can do if you purchase a day pass. The apartment that I rented for the summer was steps away from the Hyatt back gate so it was convenient for me to visit often. All the staff I had dealings with were amazing, warm and friendly, and I want to especially thank the spa staff including Ashok, as well as the amazing kitchen staff. I have celiac disease and cannot eat any gluten, not even any cross contamination because it makes me extremely ill. I explained this to my server on my first evening and he provided me with a gluten free menu. The sous chef came to my table to personally ensure that he understood my needs and reassure me that precautions would be observed in the preparation of my meals. I even got baskets of baked in house, gluten free bread with every meal. All of my meals were delicious, the espresso was great, I enjoyed some nice wines with meals and all the servers were friendly and attentive. My standard room was clean and well appointed. The bed was so comfortable and made up with crisp linens.The ac worked great and the water pressure was awesome. The extra large bathtub was divine and such a treat. (my summer rental apartment only had a shower) The grounds are lovely and well maintained and the pool refreshing. There are plenty of lounge chairs, some hammocks and bean bag chairs around the pool. There was a large, private party by the pool on the Saturday with a dj playing loud music but I didn't mind at all. It was fun to see the families enjoying their celebration and I spoke to some of them. They were very nice. The pool is large and clean. There is also a small wading pool for wee ones and a hot tub. The poolside bar menu was great and the pool staff friendly and attentive.The lobby is really amazingly beautiful with miniature stupas. There is always fresh, fruit infused water in the lobby area. I took afternoon tea in the upper lobby area which overlooks the patio and pool. It was quite nice and peaceful and they have a great selection of teas. There is also a casino but I did not visit.I treated myself to a day spa retreat on the Saturday. The Oasis is in the lower level, accessible by lift/elevator. It truly was an oasis. I enjoyed a hot stone massage and a pedicure. The ladies locker area has a steam room, dry sauna and jacuzzi with nice, powerful jets. There are showers and all the dressing table amenities are provided. Even if I hadn't been a weekend guest, the day spa package includes use of the pool and facilities until dusk. The spa attendants and the ladies in the beauty parlour were friendly and attentive. During my three month stay in Boudha, I returned to the spa multiple times for assorted services and had a great experience every visit.It's also worth mentioning that the wifi was great. I watched a movie on Netflix in my room, with my laptop one evening with no trouble.If you are interested in seeing the Boudhanath Stupa or going to Pashupati, the Hyatt is a great place to stay. You can walk to the stupa and it's a short taxi ride to Pashupati or even Thamel for shopping.Many thanks to all the staff for providing me with all I needed to enjoy a fantastic, birthday weekend away!

The Hyatt Regency vastly exceeded my expectations and is surely one of the best Category 1 properties in the Hyatt portfolio.The rooms look slightly spartan and bare on the website but I found my Club King to be very comfortable and great value. The property itself is stunning and well-maintained, with great views of the city and nearby Bodanath stupa from the club.The lobby decor was awesome and the breakfast buffet up there with large international hotel standards. The staff are all genuinely friendly and helpful and do their utmost to make you feel welcome in their country. They’re clearly proud of their property (and rightfully so) and this reflects as a great guest experience. Special thanks to Lopsang in the club for attentive and proactive service.Definitely recommend this property.

I stayed for 3 nights and this is my fifth visit to the same hotel ,yearly once,I notice recently that this 5 star hotel is in need of renovation specially rooms i.e. Mattress ,side table , but my general comments it's one of the best in Kathmandu , not a lot a variety in menu same menu from 5 years , hotel is near the airport but far from city center

The Hyatt is Hyatt everywhere, but in Nepal I won't recommend to stay there. First you don't feel the country, second is quite far from the centre. The room was really dated, so I don't really think it worth the money. From the other hand the Stupa is walking distance, and during warm season you can enjoy beautiful property and swimming pool

Overall a good experience. Friendly staff. Spacious rooms. Got our-selves upgrade to their Club room at 6th Floor. Got complimentary food and drinks at their club lounge for 2 hrs. ( 5:30pm to 7:30pm) along with free airport pick-up and drop. The attached casino is great plus for this property. Casino allows kids as well in the playing area. You get complimentary food and drinks on the playing table as well as there is also a complimentary lunch & dinner buffet spread available in the basement of the casino. Pool is big, also they have good SPA services. Gym & Jacuzi is also available. The only negative side is the free Wifi Internet Speed and the buffet spread of breakfast is not that great. We stayed for 4 days and the menu was almost the same everyday with not too much of taste in it.

This is a beautiful hotel set in very nice grounds. It is however slightly showing its age. The hotel needs more detail attention to maintenance. An example is the inside handle of my bathroom door, which fell off - clearly having been poorly refixed in the past. Also corrosion round sink taps and one tablelamp not working. Just details but, like the badly chipped/scraped tables in the all-day dining, all could be resolved with simple attention.  Nevertheless, the hotel ambience is exceedingly pleasant and the staff are friendly.

The hotel is an oasis of luxury in a sea of dust and confusion.....Kathmandu city is a bit of a mess at the moment.But you forget everything outside the walls of the hotel when you are there.Excellt rooms ,food and service..Friendly staff and good access to some good shopping areas and restaurants.

ネパール行きの全行程11日のなかで、最初の３日はここで過ごしました。カドマンズの空港から近いこと、日頃欧米型の生活に慣れていること、到着後に身体を整えたいこと、そんな理由で安心のハイアットグループにしました。施設、食事、ホスピタリティ全てにおいて、よく出来たホテルです。お部屋も十分に綺麗で広く、窓からの眺めも素晴らしいです。中心部からは少し離れていますが、カドマンズでは徒歩で移動することはまずなく、タクシーを多用するので、不便さは感じないと思います。宿泊料は、日本から行く私の感覚では「リーゾナブル」とは言え、現地の物価や賃金からしたら、ありえないほど高価です。工場で働く女性従業員の月給より、1泊は高い(汗)。３日間の滞在で、朝食も満足、施設も満足、室内もバスルームも、眺めも、とても良かったですが…唯一、ホテルの無料Wi-Fiの接続が悪かったこと…がストレスでした。何かを取れば、何かを捨てることにはなるのが常でしょうが…ビジネス目的で連絡を密にしないもいけない場合にはこれは重要かも知れません。チェックアウト時に少々強めに言ってきたので(笑)もしかしたら改善されているかも知れませんが…いずれにしても、次回またこの国に来たら…最初はまたここに泊まっていちど心身リセットしたいな、と思います。ゴルフ場も近いので、その目的の方にも良いでしょう。

A highlight on our guided tour of the sub-continent, the Hyatt Regency in Kathmandu was an oasis of luxury with great service, food and views of the mountains surrounding Kathmandu - highly recommended.

This is my 2nd trip to Nepal and I have to say that this place is an oasis for any traveler. The hotel anticipates your needs and knows what every type of traveler wants. It has every amenity that you could possibly need in a developing country. The staff is amazing and the food is incredible.

Its well connected to the local attractions.  This hotel needs a lot of improvements when it comes to the rooms, interiors, service, attentiveness and staff awareness of the services in their own property.

Rooms were large, need a little bit upgrading, the bed was creaky, suggest you remove the card in the room giving a number and email address for any service issues, as i did complain about an issue at the CAFE, however I did get a call at end of the day around 2039h, I told the lady concerned was busy with overseas call on my mobile to call back after 5 minutes, never heard from her ever again.Overall property is good, needs little upgrading, it was much better than the Crown Plaza I stayed last year, however service levels poor,I visited The Cafe only once, decided never to visit it again as basic black tea was not served, after asking twice, this is standard at property like Hyatt Regency, not sure what to expect from others.

We arrived on a rainy day in the valley , and despite giving multiple reminders of our flight arrival time , there was no person / placard of the Hyatt Regency to be seen. Made a few calls to the hotel , but nobody picked up. Then tried contacting the 'airport representative' , only to be told he's on leave. As the airport police did not let anyone stand near the exit , we were left drenched in the rain for a good 20 minutes. Finally the hotel did pick up my call , but by then the car had arrived , thanks to a few helpful guys ( from other hotels ) who knew our driver.As we had booked the Club Rooms , we were checked in at the Regency Club Lounge  , by the very courteous Ms. Nitya. We had placed a request for rooms with the 'Stupa' view , but surprisingly , "they had no such room left on the 6th floor" i.e. the Club Lounge floor , which was disappointing considering that we had asked for it well in advance. Thus , while they upgraded one of the rooms to the 7th floor in their Club 'Deluxe' category ( which has nothing different apart from a balcony ) the other room was assigned on the 5th floor , which made movement between the two rooms quite hectic.The rooms are nice , but there is an acute shortage of power points , and even those require adapters to be used. The bathrooms are quite big , but the showers have a dysfunctional temperature control , with hot water taking almost 5 minutes to come at the start , and then stopping intermittently , a phenomenon one does not expect in a Hyatt.The Regency Club Lounge is spacious , with a friendly & courteous staff , but service can be painfully slow even for a cup of tea/coffee. Unlike club lounges across the globe , where you have cookies,fruits,etc. available throughout the day , this doesn't seem to be the norm here. I was quite surprised to learn that they don't have the concept of 'Afternoon Tea' , which precedes the evening round of 'Happy Hours' everywhere. Coming to the latter , while the variety of alcohol might be satisfactory , a teetotaller like me has to settle with just 2 options - Coke or Gingerale. On our first day , the canapés/snacks were being frequently replenished , but it was the complete opposite on day 2 , with empty plates ( for some items ) seen just half an hour into the Happy Hours , right till the end.Breakfast at the main restaurant is utter chaos , with staff trying their level best to streamline the process , but to no avail. The Indian selections are not impressive and are presented poorly. The 'Juice Corner' is sloppy , and no matter what fruit / vegetable you choose , they use the same jug again & again resulting in a messy concoction every time.The Hyatt Regency Kathmandu unfortunately has a long way to go in my opinion. I would easily get much better service & hospitality , at this price , anywhere across Asia.

beautiful but oldBoudhanath Stupa view from the window was amazing!!Breakfast not delicious, salad not freshAll staff was nice and excellent servicePs. I like welcome drink a lot (Rose tea)      Casino beside hotel for your relax after enjoy city

I designed a 15-day customized 5-star tour of the Himalayas (Nepal-Tibet-Bhutan).  We were a group of 10 friends.  Our first stop was Kathmandu and we stayed 4 nights at the Hyatt Regency.  I had a very comfortable & enjoyable stay there.The grounds were beautifully kept, well-manicured & clean.  The entrance & lobby were impressive.  The pool in the back looks nice & inviting.Check-In & Check Out -- fast & efficient with friendly serviceBellhop service -- very goodLocation -- close to Boudhanath Stupa.  There's nothing outside the hotel worth walking to.  The hotel property is gated from the craziness outside.Room -- Clean, comfortable, good size, has coffee maker, free wifi, safe, air conditioned,  iron & ironing board & robes.Bathroom -- spacious with shower, tub, single sink & hair dryer. Cleaning staff -- does a good jobRestaurants -- the buffet breakfast at The Cafe has plenty of selection.  Dinner at Rox was OK.  Service in both restaurants were good.This was a very good choice in Kathmandu.  We also stayed at Dwarika's for a couple of nights while we traversed in the other Himalayan countries (Tibet & Bhutan).  I prefer the Hyatt over Dwarika's.  Next time I'm in Kathmandu, I'll stay again at the Hyatt.

Excellent location between airport and city center - a very short walk to the main stupa of Kathmandu. Great for relaxing after a days sightseeing or a weeks trekking in Nepal. Nice swimming pool and spa facilities. Free shuttle bus to the city center.

Un hotel genial en todos los aspectos, lo mejor la comida y el personal. La ubicación aunque no está en pleno centro es ideal para descansar y tiene alrededor todo tipo de servicios. Muy recomendable.

My family and I (3 kids ages 11, 9, 7) went to Kathmandu for 3 days and then to Bhutan for 6. While in Kathmandu, we stayed at the Hyatt. The hotel is beautiful with a walking trail in the back.  The jewellery stores just inside the lobby carried nice gems and the staff in these stores seemed genuine. I went home with a pair of old diamond earrings for a fair price. The pool is not heated, or at least doesn't seem to be heated. And was too cold to swim for my kids in early April. While the streets in Kathmandu are dusty and busy and hectic, as soon as we entered the gates to the hotel, I recall telling my kids, we are in total bliss, instantly. We booked 2 rooms, and the facilities in the rooms were a bit dated (blow dryer is old, phones were filthy dirty when I used a sanitizing wipe on it, only one outlet for charging all my electronics). The restaurant was good and had a nice selection of food from the a la carte. My kids don't eat spicy food and were able to order food (they loved the daal makni and the naan bread was yummy). We found the a la carte menu was perfect for us, rather than the buffet, which we didn't really eat much of, when we used it.

Do not normally opt for 5 star hotels but arrangements were made by a friend.  Trip to Hyatt from airport through Kathmandu traffic was an adventure but upon entering the hotel, the beautiful grounds and lobby were stunning, greeted by three sitting musicians playing raga.  Service was excellent, dining buffet was wonderful and room very comfortable.  Out the back gate, past the Taragon art museum, turn left and just a few blocks to Boudhanath Stupa, fully restored, and a great introduction to Buddhist culture.  Highlight was the lavish Hindu wedding ceremony with 700 guests my last night.
ホテル構え、お部屋も立派でした。部屋の温度、ベッド、ソファ、バスタブなどどれも心地よかったです。朝食の味や種類がお国柄のせいか物足りなかったかも、、

Over the last 5 years, I have stayed in a number of hotels in Kathmandu. The Hyatt Regency is hands down my favorite place to stay. The facilities are complemented by spacious green area around the hotel and the off-road path to Bouddhnath connects to cultural learning and shopping.

A very enjoyable stay before and after the Everest Base Camp trek ( after the tea houses in the mountains it looked even more attractive!). This majestic hotel is not far from the airport and close to the magnificent Budanath Stupa. Taxis are available and very cheap. The staff was kind especially at "The Café" were they did their ultimate best to please us. Their Nepalese specialties are delicious and we loved their momos. The room & bathrooms are very clean, light, spacious and comfortable. The room service is impeccable. There is a supermarket and several convenient ATMs in front of the hotel.. A much appreciated oasis of serenity in the hubbub of Kathmandu.

Definitivamente la mejor opcion de alojamiento en Kathmandu. Por que lo digo; primero, la ubicacion ( Zona de la estupa Boudanath), es una zona tranquila, el edificio esta rodeado de una gran area verde que separa la estructura del bullicio de la calle. La vista que tuvimos desde nuestra habiatacion hacia la estupa son inolvidables. Segundo, a pesar de no ser un edificio nuevo, toda la estructura se mantiene en muy buen estado y mantenimiento. Desde la entrada encontraras en el lobby un lugar apacible y espectacular. El personal de recepcion siempe amable y cordial. Se me ofrecio un paquete de up-grade el cual tome y se nos coloco en el piso 6. Disfrutamos del excepcional servicio del lounge, que ofrece alimentos y bebidas gratuitas en la mañana y tarde-noche, ademas de las mejores vistas desde la habitacion.Las habitaciones muy amplias, asi como el baño, por mucho mas amplias que el promedio de las habitaciones en Asia. Pisos y muebleria de madera, hacen muy calido el ambiente.En cuanto a Alimentos y Bebidas, el desayuno buffet en " El Cafe" tiene un buen numero de opciones con estaciones asiatica, caliente, frutas, cereales, huevos, panaderia y quesos. No es el mejor buffet al que he asistido pero para un occidental sera mas que suficiente.No pierdan la oportunidad de disfrutar de la alberca y tomar el almuerzo en el BBQ.El hotel tiene un camino a traves del cual puedes caminar a la estupa de Boudanath sin necesidad de usar carro, eso es muy valioso, diario lo usamos.Contratamos por email el servicio de transfer desde el aeropuerto, un taxi es mucho mas barato, pero quienes quieren sentir la seguridad de ser esperados por alguien tomen la opcion, el personal es muy amable.Lo que tengo que resaltar como lo mejor dle hotel, es su gente. Cordiales y siempre alertas a las necesidades, en recepcion, las 3 veces que fui, la chica que me atendio siempre recordo mi nombre y numero de habitacion.

The location is good, the rooms are nice and the food is great!  That being said when you have terrible customer service it just cancels out all the good.  From the moment I checked in they tried to stick me in a single bed room even though I paid for a king superior room. I attempted to exchange money at front desk a 100 bill had a micro tear and they would not accept it. The staff are rude and overly suspicious. Do yourself a favour and stay at the Annapurna hotel in Kathmandu. Much better service. I was disappointed as I stay in Hyatt all over the world and this is by far one of the worse customer service experiences.

Excellent hotel - staff very welcoming, great breakfast, choice of restaurants for dinner, good location for airport and for visiting sites in Kathmandu valley. Hotel is set back in own grounds away from the main road, creating a peaceful relaxing environment which was very welcome after long journeys and touring days. Nice pool though didn't get much time to use it. Some previous reviews seemed to say that this was not up to the normal 'Hyatt' standard - I would disagree and thoroughly recommend this hotel. Tip - had a room described as 'Stupa view' - the view itself is not worth paying extra for as the Stupa is only partially visible across the skyline of buildings, though the higher standard of room may still be worth it depending on the cost.

After having climbed to Base Camp Everest or trekked to the Laya hill people of Bhutan on the Tibetan border, this hotel is a MUST to unwind, sleep, eat, and be utterly pampered before your return to the West.

Not sure if I would stay again for the price I paid. Not value for money. Staff need to interact more at times. Location is fantastic and very close to city as well as the airport. Carpets are dated and walls need good paint.

Stayed here a night in October. Very impressed by the look and feel of the place. Large rooms and bathroom. Nice pool and spa area. Room service breakfast was excellent. Overall grounds was large with many gardens. Close to airport and shuttle provided if guests want to venture further into the city.

Beginning from my checkin until my check out I got a superb respect and service from all the hotel staff members.From breakfast to dinner I really enjoyed a lot with the delicious foods and restaurant friendly staffs and my salute goes to the great chef's who prepared that great food , and I'm really sorry that I can't remember their names. Location of this hotel blown my mind, I was able to see one of the world cultural heritage  boudha stupa nearby. Lastly, the people I met, and the people around was really very helpful , cooperative . I hope to see this hotel and staffs again in the future .

I have been to this place so many times but writing something for this gem today. Though I live in Kathmandu but my second home that is Hyatt regency is so luring that I can't stop myself being pulled by this property. No words are enough to describe this gem you should let your heart mind and senses to feel it. Amazing Nepali hospitality with overwhelming staffs are there to make your stay so wonderful that you will have memories to cherish in your life. Cheers guys see you soon and remain wonderful.

Esse hotel é inesquecível! Com vista perpétua para o centro de Kathmandu, ficamos num quarto com stupa view. Palaciano, instalações suntuosas é muito conservadas. Recepção impecável, quarto muito espaçoso e decorado na medida. Piscina linda e espaçosa. Nela tem um restaurante onde se serve churrasco feito na hora. Café da manhã farto, completo. Vários bares e espaços para ficar à vontade, contemplando a vista para Kathmandu. Perto do centro, fomos a pé para muitos pontos turísticos da cidade. O povo nepalês é simpático, sempre disposto a ajudar. Recomendo!

Check in:I stayed at this HR as a Diamond Guest of Honour. So I asked if check in lady knew what benefits are for me and the lady just kept saying yes. I told her I wanted a late check out at 2pm but instead of a yes, she asked my flight departure time. And said oh you fly out at 4, you need to check out at 1!! I fly at least once a week and I am pretty sure what time I need to be at the airport. But I am sure that was just a way to get their room back sooner. I spent 150 nights at hotels last year, and this is the first time I had a check in staff saying no to my late check out request.After she gave me the room key, I asked about lounge access but she told me no lounge for me. I then asked her to look up the diamond benefits and find out the new benefit. She didn't take any actions. She must thought I was stupid asking for room upgrade, late check out, then now lounge access.Luckily another staff at the reception did look it up after I explained to him again. I then waited at the lounge and he came to me and apologised. He explained that was a new benefits and he had never heard of it. (New = 9 months ago) Well at least, he recognised it. He also offered a club room but with 30 mins wait. I declined because the check in process took 30 mins already. I later went to the room and it was right next to the lifts. so I called reception that I will move to the club room.Room-Room itself is a bit dated, but large  enough. View is not bad. The bed is not very comfortable- thin/hard mattress. Club lounge-Not bad for Nepal! It's all self serving and staff were friendly. Not much food for happy hours but as this is only a cat 1 Hyatt I can't complain about the 2 hours all I can drink gin and tonic! Breakfast-I enjoyed it, the breakfast selection is pretty good. Egg station, Indian station...Overall I enjoyed my stay. I wish check in staff can be a bit more humble. If they don't know something, they should look up the T&C first. And they hotel also need to address some problems with the bellboys. They really annoyed me.I asked them about hiring a guide and taxi, everyone there told me a different price and one staff even told me he runs a travel agency and wanted to give me a discount for any travel arrangement. I told him I know a local and not interested he still kept going on about it saying he wanted to help a new friend while he was walking me to the ATM. I am sure they take commission from taxi as well. I recommend you just walk out to the main road and talk to the taxi driver yourself. I took a taxi to the city centre and airport for both 500R. Hotel bellboys said it would cost 1000R+ if I order a taxi from them. There are usually more than 10 taxi waiting outside on Buddha road. They try to get you to order in advanced so they can talk to the drivers about how much they can make from you. They are all about making money there, so be careful!

カトマンズの中心部からよりトリブバン国際空港からの方が近い位置にあるハイアット・リージェンシー。「地球の歩き方」のホテル紹介でも最初に登場するほどにさすがのクオリティと言える。スイートルームはそれほど個性的ではないが、部屋そのものよりこのホテル全体の広さに圧倒される。建物そのものが工芸品のようですらある。停電が多いのはカトマンズにおいて仕方のないことであり、本ホテルでも例外ではない。一日に 3〜4 回は数秒の停電があると思った方が良い。気をつけるべきは空調である。空調は停電の後、設定がリセットされるのか温度設定が反映されない感がある。空調を一度 OFF にしてから再度 ON にすると直った気がするが確実な情報ではない。歩いて 500 m ほどの距離にネパール最大の尖塔を抱くボダナートがあるので気軽にカトマンズ観光を楽しむことができる。その一方、隣接する Tara Goan Park では 2015 年のネパール地震により家屋を失った人々が暮らすテントサイトがある。何ができるというわけでもないのだが、せめて被災した方々の今後の多幸を祈らずにはいられない。一点、ホテルの難点を述べるなら朝食が提供されるカフェで毎回着席時にコーヒーかお茶かを尋ねられるのだが、答えても「一度も」それらが提供されたことがなかった点である。食べ終わった後ぐらいに給仕がやってきて同じ質問を繰り返す。給仕には罪はないのだが、ついつい感情を害して「さっきも言ったけど」と言ってしまう自分は器が小さい。

It is a beautiful resort in Kathmandu. We spent our entire 4 day holiday not wanting to step out of the property. It is so green, well maintained and beautiful- you could actually feel the difference in pollution levels once you enter Hyatt regency in Kathmandu from outside the hotel. They have a casino inside the property which was pretty amazing too. Rooms are good in size and well maintained.

The first thing striking about the place is this property not a typical Hyatt one. Its not one of the high rise buildings, refreshingly it has more lung space !! I love the location of their restaurants within the property, very pleasant. Its located in a very short distance from the airport, its very close to most of the attractions around Kathmandu.Must add the only casino in Nepal is located in the same property perimeter.

I go to Nepal every year for work and always stay at this property. The public areas are magnificent! The lobby, the gardens, the pool, all beautiful and well kept. I am not giving this 5 stars because the rooms are not quite there. They have not been updated in years. I have also had problems with showers draining water.The food is great.  The breakfast buffet is one of the best I have seen!  The staff is friendly. It's a bit of a hike to get to some rooms since the hotel is so large. You may want to ask where you room is when checking in if that could be an issue.

This is the 3rd time I have been in this hotel in the course of the last 5 years.  Short staying always 2-3 days nothing more nothing less. I was expecting somewhat as the recent 2015 earthquake that hit Nepal might have impacted either part or majority of the structure/s. The hotel, the structure & the totality of it all seemed "unchanged". Not sure if it is good or bad - The room is still the same, the fixtures old, bed a bit hard (same as I remembered), the decors - exquisitely nostalgic. It seems that you don't get to care about how old or how limited some of the services are - you get lost in the culture of Nepal. Ever present in and around the hotel. The gym small, cramped with 5 people. The pool is big - good for avid swimmers (bring a body glove - water is normally cold)The only thing I don't see eye to eye with this hotel is the breakfast buffet; there is limited variety and in all my 3 days - food was the same. Overall the service is average, 3 out of 5 Stars. I would have expected at least that they have my name in their database of frequently staying customers but was not recognized, specially that this is a Hyatt. In other hotels they would see if I have stayed in their hotel before and they would recognize the name and provide some sort of acknowledgment - I guess I was expecting too much.Request for room facing the pool. Nonetheless it is always exciting to be visiting Nepal.

Hotel is great, it has a really nice interior and it is in a great location. But i was really dissapointed with my room especially when it's a five star hotel. The room seriously needs the renovation also bed sheets found a hole in them also the bathroom wasn't clean properly it had a water spots all over the shower room door. The wifi was very poor as well. Also the pool benches are really dirty i don't understand when they say five star hotel we expect clean and outstanding result. I was really disappointed even though i love the interior decoration of the hotel.

They Hyatt Regency Kathmandu provides a clean, safe, comfortable and beautiful oasis to the hustle, bustle, and noise of Kathmandu. Reliable hot water, power and internet connection, good food and and excellent, responsive staff make recharging in the evenings a valuable part of any stay in Kathmandu.

Very courteous and helpful staff. The food is really good and its served with generous portion of smile which adds and stay along with u. The hotel has quaint feel to it. The spa is a must try. One can enjoy lazy noons by the pool with mountain views.

Good location, very close to Budhanath Stupa. Nice pool, big and beautiful garden, good facilities, very kind and helpful staff. The hotel survived the devastating earthquake with minor cracks and is safe in that aspect. I really enjoyed my stay. Only con is; rooms need renovation.

I stayed here for two nights and could not complain anything. They provide excellent services. The room is super. The hotel is walking distance to Bodanath Supta. They serve the best breakfast included with your room.

I stayed in this hotel overnight on July 4, 2015 (post earth quake) as part of the Press Club of India delegation on the invitation of Nepal Tourism. Close to airport and City Centre, it's a lovely hotel with gr8 ambience. It's a rare experience to see stupas in the hotel lobby that provide a sense of serenity. The best thing about this hotel is its great architecture and nicely landscaped lawns/gardens which add to the grandeur of the hotel.It's so refreshing to have a morning/evening walk in the lavish, well- manicured green  lawns spread over 37- acre property that offers resort like experience. I had a pool facing room with a beautiful view of Boudha Stupa which is at a walking distance. This luxury hotel lives up to its reputation of Kathmandu's number one hotel in terms of amenities ,service standards, safety & security. In all, I had a short, sweet & memorable stay here.

My husband I were trying to decide between Dwarikas and the Hyatt for a weekend 'retreat' - my husband lives and works in Kathmandu. Ultimately, our choice boiled down to price - the Hyatt is significantly less expensive and was willing to offer a special package (probably due to lower occupancy following the earthquake) whereas there was little flexibility with Dwarikas. But I am doing a comparison of the two hotels in case there are others not familiar with either hotel who might wonder if Dwarikas is worth the extra...I like the location of the Hyatt near to Boudhanath stupa and reasonably near the airport. The Hyatt sits on a large expansive compound which is very unusual in the crowded city of Kathmadu. In this large compound there is a wonderful pool area and grass expanses with lots of trees and plants. In contrast, Dwarikas is much more compact - there is a courtyard which is very attractive but the pool area, bar, restaurants and little shop areas are all close together in this centre area. They both have good restaurants - we have eaten at both places. Good choices of western and eastern cuisine and good service. One person will tell you the food is better at Hyatt; another will say Dwarikas. One thing I can't compare are the rooms having never spent an overnight at Dwarikas. I'd give the bedroom 4 stars and the bathroom 5 stars. The bedroom was comfortable and nicely decorated but lacked some special touches. (contrast the bathroom which had a bathtub - large walk in glass tiled shower and very attractive granite vanity area.) The TV has only 4 english speaking channels and some are there one hour, gone the next. And there is a kettle for tea but no coffee maker - just a packet of instant coffee as a nod to the coffee drinking guests. Service  was very good all round - room service came quickly and order was correct. We did try the spa and had treatments there - found the treatment rooms lovely - soft lighting and music and therapists very professional and courteous but the changing rooms are in need of updates. A little 'cruddy' in the showers and steam room and the overall changing area more like a Y gym back home than a luxury hotel. Will mention there are many tents on the perimeter of the property now as homeless local people are camped out -- kudos to the hotel for working to help their neighbours. But oddly the hotel explained they had taken over the a/c units since the earthquake so the rooms are not individually controlled and we would have definitely liked them about 10 deg cooler!

You'd think they'd want to keep my business after the damage sustained in the earthquake but they'd rather rip off customers.Good points, hotel is spacious, very few people, large welcoming lobby, big bedrooms, big bathrooms, tastefully  decorated.Bad points, lots of crack filing, sanding & painting going in. Bottled water in room is not fresh but refilled and then cellophane sealed, makes you wonder whether wine & spirits are too. Most annoying is the price on the menu is not the price on the bill they bring, for instance bottle of water at bar is 200rupees but 248rupees on bill. So I'd rather spend money elsewhere locally where it will go more directly to the local people.

I would like to congratulate Mrs. Sinead O’Reilly-Henell, the GM of the Hayatt-Kathmandu  and her entire winning team for the great job done during the recent Earthquake experience! The whole "crew" did an amazing work under very demanding conditions with ambition to safety, safety and safety! The emergency response plan worked to a good level and every resident has been evacuated. It was an unforgettable experience since the first earthquake wave (of 7.9 Richter scale) has  been expirienced inside my room! Once again a very big thanks you to Sinead and your hard working team... Very Best Regards. Capt. Georgios Kattidenios

We checked in on the evening of 27th December. We were convinced to take the upgrade to the 6th floor (the regency club lounge). The extras included unlimited internet and canopes and drinks from 6-8pm, breakfast, and pick-up and drop from the airport. If you were to add these perks individually, they would add to more than the upgraded amount. We were greeted with a delicious cake in our room.We were given room number 639. The room looked very basic. Definitely not like hyatts in other parts of the world. However, according to nepal standards, this is one of the best. While it is quite basic, it was a very comfortable stay, and the staff made sure of that. Room 639 has a direct view of the stupa. It is indeed nice to see, however that was just the first day. The next few days were a bit foggy to see. The bed was comfortable. On the first night, we wanted to sleep early due to the long lady of travelling to kathmandu, however we were kept awake by barking dogs. The hyatt is a huge closed off property. They should have made sure that the dogs are kept off. The 6th floor is the second highest floor. So i'd suggest the higher the floor, the lesser the barking noise. The other problem was that because the regency club floor (6th floor) has a huge seating area, guests would congregate there till late night, and the doors aren't soundproof. So you are kept awake by their voices. Our room was cleaned twice a day. The bathroom has a nice walk-in shower. The water is always hot, and the pressure of the water was great. The toilet doesn't have a bidet. The glass of the walk-in shower was not cleaned thoroughly even on the first day when moving in. It seems that the previous guest showered, and they didn't bother to clean the glass. The canopes and drinks from 6-8 are definitely worth it. Great plus. The breakfast had a good spread of indian, and continental. Eggs are made to order. Pancakes and waffles are available too. The proximity of the hotel is very close to both airports. There is a free shuttle to thamel 5-6 times a day. Make sure to use that if you wish to go for shopping, or where the main restaurants are. The wifi was fast and reliable. Nepal is known to suffer from power outages. Hyatt has taken care of this problem. I believe it has its own generator.

You drive past manicured gardens into the the porch of the hotel. Very imposing , beautiful Nepali architecture, a pond in the centre and beautiful brass doors leading you into the main lobby and reception area. We go up to our floor which turns out to a no smoking floor when we had asked for , and had been confirmed by the hotel that we would get one. We go down back to the check in man, he says ' oh yes you wanted smoking, but if you want it we can't give it to you now you have sit and wait', we ask why ? The hotel is not full it's just one room? Never heard that one before at a hotel of this level.Checked out mid-booking and moved to a friendlier property. Never going close to this property again. In facf, after this horrible experience, staying away from all Hyatt hotels in future.

The spa is EXTREMELY UNHYGIENIC!I witnessed a woman sit on the ledge of the jacuzzi and shave her legs; after she was done, she threw all of her shavings into the jacuzzi. When I approached a staff member about this experience, the attendant told me that the woman was a long-time member. Although the Hyatt was apologetic, I did not get the feeling that they would speak to the woman; it didn't seem like a big deal. IT'S A HUGE DEAL WHEN SOMEONE THROWS THEIR BODILY SHAVINGS ALONG WITH FOAM INTO A SHARED JACUZZI! I am writing this review in the hopes that someone will speak to that regular. No one should have to sit in someone else's grime.

Frühstück nicht inbegriffen obwohl bei Booking.com so gebucht wurde! Das Hotel verlangte von mir, dass das Frühstück bezahlt werden muss. Das hat meine gute Laune verdorben. Das Frühstück Atmosphäre war laut.

I stayed in Hyatt for two nights with my 5-year-old daughter to attend a business event, and we both got ill the first night after breathing the terrible air inside the room. I had noticed that the heating system was too noisy but recognized only later that their air filtration system was faulty. I developed severe headache within hours of staying in the room and high fever and lost voice cord by midnight. The next day I flung the window open and let the chilling Kathmandu air come in, which is when we both began to feel better, ironically.I later learned that several other people who'd stayed in Hyatt for the same event, had fallen ill too. Especially as we are considering corona virus threats, it was very irresponsible of this so-called five-star hotel to be so careless about its air filtration system. Other "minor" glitches: We'd checked in late in the night and it took three rounds for their service staff to programme their entry cards correctly so we could enter the room.... The room phone was broken which they never bothered to fix... Their spa timings were written incorrectly in the room-book so I could not use the steam room when I turned up with unbearable sore throat and high fever (and lost voice cord) and the pressure of a public speaking engagement the next day.It's one of those glitzy but third-class hotels which does enjoy amazing location and infrastructure but showed absolutely no interest in individual clients. Won't recommend this to anyone.

The best location in Kathmandu, u can see whole area around from this height, have very nice poolside, casino to enjoy trying luck.., swimming pool is really nice, buffet breakfast have variety of dishes..

Everything was very old. The breakfast was very limited. The service is poor. One very positive thing however is that they said all the food was halal which is great since Kathmandu does not have many halal options.

The hyatt pool and grounds is one of the great treats of Kathmandu.  A real oasis.  Now if only the pool was heated in the colder months....................Meanwhile a heads up to all the staff at the pool who are wonderful - beautifully trained and incredibly helpful - and a big thanks especially to Nirman the head barman who is always a great help.

We stayed twice at this hotel during our trip through Nepal, Bhutan, and Tibet.  Beautiful, quiet resort in the heart of chaotic and noisy Kathmandu. Spacious rooms with great views. Wonderfull grounds, great pool to relax at. The very helpful and courteous staff. Excellent food at hotel restaurants.

The Hyatt Regency Kathmandu is a traditionally decorated luxury hotel located in Boudha district of Kathmandu. The garden is lovely and peaceful, particularly at night as the soft lights illuminate the grounds. The Hyatt truly is a peaceful oasis in the midst of the chaotic Kathmandu and one wakes up in the morning by the melody of beautiful birds. The location is also terrific - quite close to the airport and within an easy (10-15 min) walking distance to the Boudhanath Stupa. We spent 10 nights (three separate stays) at the Hyatt in club rooms facing Boudhanath which offer wonderful views of the famous landmark in the city. The room is very clean, spacious, and comfortable. The restaurant cooks authentic and tasty Indian dishes once the chef understands your taste and preferences. Everything is freshly cooked and service is excellent. Restaurant ambience desires some improvement. In the evenings, local musician play music in the lobby area which is extremely enjoyable and relaxing. What makes our Hyatt stay specially enjoyable is its exceptional service oriented culture. At club lounge, staff members ( Kushal, Salina, Samikshya, etc.) are truly dedicated to delivering their guests with best-in-class service and hospitality.  Every day we were treated with freshly cooked ginger/honey tea on demand and enjoyable evening happy hour. Excellent breakfast and spa facility at hotel. Highly recommended to all travelers.

Pls keep up the level of service and the food quality. The staff were excellent.The well cooked and specially prepared vegetarian food with onion and garlic for some and without onion and garlic for some made our stay very comfortable.

Nous avons sejourné deux nuits au Hyatt.Les chambres sont spacieuses et confortable , un peu vieillot mais fonctionnel La piscine est magnifique mais très froide à cette période Le petit déjeuné’ est varié et de qualité le service est au top ! L’avàntage de cette hôtel est la proximité de la stupa de bodnat ( 9 mn à pieds) et pas très loin de pashupathinat Dans l’ensemble très satisfait d’y avoir Sejourné je recommande

When you drive from airport to Hyatt Regency in Kathmandu you realize how quied is this hotel and sourandings. Nice and big rooms, may be should be restaured as Hotel is propably from 80’s. Nice terraces and big outdoor pool. Breakast and lunch buffet at a affordable prices for western visitors. On my next visit to Kathmandu will come back.

I have stayed at the Hyatt Regency Kathmandu on a regular basis over the last 12 months for a combination of business and leisure. It is a fantastic hotel, in a wonderful location (walking distance to Boudanath Stupa down some fascinating alleyways) and only 15-20 minutes from the airport (traffic permitting!).The building itself is elegantly constructed to reflect local Newari architectural traditions, so despite being large, it is not simply another concrete international hotel and you have the feeling inside of entering an old palace, rather than a modern hotel. The pool is lovely in the summer but it is not heated in the winter (which is a shame and I think this would be one thing they could do to improve it). The spa (hot tub, steam room and sauna) is good and never busy in the evenings. The rooms are large and well appointed, with large bathrooms.The staff really help make the hotel. Despite being a large hotel, I am recognised and greeted by name by the staff who remember the small details and ask after my family. A particular mention should go to Salina, Kushal and Samshyka on the 6th Floor who are always so accommodating. Thank you to them for their ongoing attention to detail and service. The rest of staff (including the waiters in the restaurant, spa attendants etc) have all been brilliant.I hope to return to the Hyatt in KTM again soon and would highly recommend this hotel to friends and family.

The site, the surroundings, the ambience were all wonderful. In essence the hotel reflect the especial place we were visiting- Kathmandu. Once the arrival is made, we enjoyed wonderful service and great meals.

Loved our stay at Kathmandu Hyatt!!  We were greeted by very friendly staff, and a long peaceful entry way surrounded by water on both sides, with quiet fountains.  The hotel lobby continued to please all the senses.  Our rooms were large, well appointed, and quiet.  The breakfast buffet was fabulous with so many selections from many different cultures.

The hotel is 19 years old but the condition was good and looked new.  Well maintained.  Staff were friendly and kind.  Excellent choices at breakfast buffet.  It was nice to see some local foods as well.  Also they provide two shuttle bus services a day to the city center.

We stayed one night on the way back from our Week long trip. It was a great resort. We needed it after a week. The property was absolutely great. The staff went above and beyond to take care of us. The hospitality was awesome. From the moment we checked in till we checked out they were awesome. The manager was extremely helpful in giving us a late check out. The bar tender Nirmal was great, he made these awesome cocktails. They were great. Overall the trip was great. Wish we could have stayed longer. Will surely stay when i am back.

Today security guard  stop and beat  me   if they cannot Mange crowed how they became 5 star hotel I complain to duty manger  he is not talking  and it is so bad  so pleas think before stay So we would like attend to matter to pleas be aware there was one Indai  security

Les chambres commencent à être un peu vieillottes, une rénovation serait nécessaire dans tout l’hôtel sinon le jardin et la piscine sont de beaux endroits, ne pas y aller le Dimanche trop de monde (enfants, etc)

it was an awesome stay at the Hayat regency, Kathmandu .....it was literally like resolving all your stress and getting boosted for a new start , and the staff was superbly amazing :D. THE ROOMS WERE FANTASTIC AND BEAUTIFUL the spacious rooms gave me more pleasure of the stay ;D

Beautiful receptionist Ms Aarati took exceptional care of me during my stay. Mr Kushal and Ms Salina looked after me very well in Regency Lounge. Greetings to super friendly and helpful Pumu and Samitchya in Regency Lounge. Restaurant manager Mr Suman is absolutely amazing!!! and his restaurant staff Mr Dipak, Mr Samundra, Mr Rohit, Mr Amrit, Mr Badri, Mr Gopal, Ms Reshmi, Mr Bibek are so helpful and kind. Thanks for pineapples Rajendra!!! I love Ms Sushila's beautiful smile and delicious momos. Srijana’s flower arrangements in my room are second Thank you!!! Gardener ladies you are number one!!! Hi Rushna, thanks for nicely arranging my bathroom. Sujita and Sanu at front desk, thanks for your kindness and generosity. Let’s talk about amazing Rox Restaurant with the view of heaven and food for Gods. Hello lovely Meelan and Luna at Rox, how’s worlds best Norwegian Salmon and New Zealand Lamb Chops going? Scallops and woodfire pizza perfection !!! This hotel is so spacious and super comfortable !!! And has a friendly and patient General Manager called Rajesh Ramdas. If you go to Nepal, I recommend you stay here.

a truly exceptional hotel.: the staff are very helpful, professional and keen to meet the needs of the customers. the food was also of a very good standard.  I would recommend this hotel, I have stayed there previously and look forward to staying there again

Amazing hotel property with best Customer Service one can find. The Hyatt Regency Club Floor was second to none with fantastic employees and food and beverages. the Rose Iced Tea was delicious! The Regency Club experience should be priority for all guests. The small with the Buddist Temple with a five minute walk from hotel is a very nice experience of Nepal culture.

Everything was memorable , Cleanliness , Property is huge, Staff is very soft spoken & responsible. From Front desk to cleaning staff. It's very difficult to find negative things about this property..

We stayed here for 3 nights, the experience was refreshing.Kathmandu's assault on our senses was mitigated by the Hyatt Regency calm.  The hotel grounds include a vast swimming pool, 1.6k walking/jogging track and multiple other wonders.The rooms were clean, cool and well appointed;  internet fast and reliable, water pressure therapeutic,  bottled water available etc.The breakfast buffet was worth allocating an extra 15min of our morning and an evening drink on the balcony the perfect end to the day.

Hyatt Kathmandu offers a quiet getaway. The rooms are spacious & the service is on point. Tried the spa which was excellent. Loved how green & peaceful the entire hotel was.Definitely recommend it if you are looking to spoil yourself a little.

We spent 5 nights here and we were impressed with everything from the attention to detail, the service, the food and the facilities available. We used the tennis courts, there are three pools available and we also took the package with the lounge where there is a lovely cocktail hour with a great selection of food and beverages. What made our stay very special however was the staff at Hyatt. Everyone from Ashmita, Pumu, Robinson, Sanjeep and Salina in the lounge who ensured that we were well fed, transportation arranged and that any local questions were answered! From the breakfast service, Aman and Mamila who every day ensured that we were well taken cared off and they were such a pleasure to speak to. We left Hyatt with warm memories of the top class service and the great offer available. For three of our five nights we ended up eating in the hotel restaurant (which we hardly ever do) but the food was exceptional and the offer was priced much more reasonable than the “fine dining” restaurants we visited in Kathmandu. The spa is also excellent and with good prices for a hotel. I had two massages with Maya Prem who was amazing! Thank you to everyone at Hyatt for making our stay so memorable and we look forward to returning in the future!

This year we decided to go to the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra in the month of July and as first point of starting the trip was Nepal.We were booked at Hyatt Regency and had a fantastic stay both while going and returning.Excellent service, good food and always smiling staff, what else do you need on a trip?Will definitely recommend it and will love to visit again.

Travelling for business can be exhausting ... but this hotel has proved the perfect Oasis in a place of beautiful chaos. Stuck in monsoon weather ... Nirman at the bar kept me smiling with good tunes, the best margaritas and the perfect customer service. I have travelled the world and cannot fault this property - well done team! I will make this my second home from Australia.

Myself and my bunch friends are regular visitors of your cafe restaurant. We are also club oasis gym members since more than 15 years. We have been enjoying your buffet breakfast from day one and lunch n dinner occasionally. I am very impressed with warm hospitality from your staff Mr. Amrit, Rohit , Binu and Gopal. You have definitely won me as one of your permanent customers and I would love to recommend your restaurant to my acquaintances. Also , The atmosphere inside the restaurant was very soothing and relaxing. Beautiful interior and wonderful and accurately placed lighting system - neither too bright nor too dim make this place a perfect spot for celebrations. The taste of the food was just out of the world. Allow me to say that it is world classed.

I stayed here in August 2019 and found the food, drink, service and facilities to be first class. I could not fault anything.Whilst it is not cheap - (it is a 5 star hotel after all) - it is worth the money and an oasis from the hustle and bustle of the city outside the extensive grounds. It is in a very convenient location with the Stupa fairly close by.This would be where I stay should I return.Highly recommended.

Just stayed 5 nights and wish it could have been longer! The hotel is truly luxurious set in peaceful landscaped surroundings and offers comprehensive facilities .... breakfasts in the Cafe were wonderful and we were especially lucky to have a great team ( managed by Nima ) in the Club lounge who were super attentive / friendly....

From the moment we arrived, we were impressed with the service at the Hyatt Regency Kathmandu.The staff is extremely friendly, attentive and ready to help with whatever you may need.Our room was on the Club Level which I recommend. It was spacious and the bed was comfortable. The bathroom was clean and very nice. Only minor complaint was that the water temperature in the shower didn't stay consistent.The lounge was also a nice amenity to enjoy. From 5:30-7:30 there was a nice spread of small bites which could be enough to cover dinner. Appetizers included Western and traditional foods.Staff were eager to explain details about the food.Guest Service Officer Kushal was great to communicate with both before and during our stay. He also had a nice surprise waiting in our room for a special occasion! The hotel grounds are also really impressive. The pool area looked great but we didn't get to use it. Our kids (ages 7 and almost 3) enjoyed playing in the playground on the property.Overall, the Hyatt Regency Kathmandu is a great option if you want to get away from the busyness of the city.

We had a pleasant experience at the Hyatt hotel where we stayed from12 aug to 15 aug 2019. Amazing interior decor, cleanliness of property, a large and well maintained garden, very nice swimming pool which is close to 25m. Food and beverages on the pricey side, not much choice for breakfast but this will not prevent us from coming back

Very beautiful hotel, beautiful view from room, very nice swimming pool, the best part is the garden area the jogging tracks. The rooms are big & spacious. Not to forget the best staff ever, most of them are locals, very very courteous, soft spoken and always smiling. I don’t remember names, but Restaurant team at breakfast, the lobby Bar, housekeeping & front desk staff was very very good. Thanks to our chauffeur Mr. Thapa, he showed us around suggesting things we can do, caring about our comfort level. everything was just perfect and very very good, in one word “perfecto”

Hyatt Regency is the best hotel to stay in Katmandu. A delicious breakfast, warm service in a peaceful place. The hotel has nice restaurants, a wonderful swimming pool with a nice bar! Lobby is a must. A special note for the replicas of “stupas” and their history.

Got treatment as if you are a King or a queen.Ambiance is excellent.Interior is like private room of KingHuge bathroom with bath and shower facilityseparate closet with iron board and ironwater pressure and temperature execellent

What a lovely hotel in a lovely place. So friendly. The hotel is great with an excellent pool. The food is a particular highlight with the afternoon offerings of chaat a real treat. It’s a bit warm in the cafe for breakfast and if the sun is out it’s not comfortable outside either. But I’m scraping the barrel! Great hotel, great staff - will be back.

Location to the STUPA is just a 5-10 min walk for shopping and dining.  Very inexpensive Ti-Se massage spa located just outside the back gate.  STUPA restaurant, the ROADHOUSE CAFE has great pizza and many other menu items.

The Hyatt Regency is like a little Oasis in the middle of Kathmandu. Great staff, great service and a big property with a great swimming pool. The rooms are big quiet and comfortable. The breakfast buffet has a great variety of food. Top choice for Kathmandu

The Hyatt Regency has been in the news lately as it was closed for a week over a labour dispute. The good news it is now open again and the service and food at The Café is excellent. Can highly recommend The Café for its buffet breakfasts, and also for lunches and dinners, but the buffet breakfast is a really special treat for solo travellers and for groups. You do not need to be staying at the hotel to go to The Café for breakfast, lunch or dinner. On Saturdays and Sundays, The Café also has buffet lunch specials with swim in the large clean pool set in the spacious pretty garden which at ground level in front of The Café. It is a good idea to book or you can just turn up especially for the Breakfast Buffet. The Buffet includes healthy food, cereals, western foods, Indian foods, cheeses, bakery items and many other tasty fresh foods - and plenty of other indulgences. Enjoy!

I was very disappointed with our stay here, my experience of the front desk staff was surprising, they were rude to me while we resolving an issue around our stay. The room was clean, nice amenities but it’s a large hotel and many rooms font have a good view.The staff in both the restaurant and the upstairs lounge were amazing though! Warm, fun and friendly. The food was excellent and the service was great. I will not return to this hotel next visit to Kathmandu. It’s very pretentious when it doesn’t need to be.

Per the Hotel website homepage (as of 16 June, 2019):"At Hyatt it is our top priority to deliver the outstanding experience and service that our brands stand for. Unfortunately, Hyatt Regency Kathmandu is currently involved in an ongoing dispute with local trade unions. The hotel is working with all parties involved to resolve this dispute at the earliest possible opportunity, but until then the hotel will temporarily cease operations and will not accept any bookings. Guests and groups who have existing bookings will be contacted proactively and will be relocated to other hotels. We hope that the hotel will be able to resolve this issue promptly and continue to deliver the service that the Hyatt Regency brand stands for."I wast here to hang out with a friend in 2018 (winter) and I was not impressed. It felt uninviting, and the restaurant was overpriced for what you got (don't order the fish).

Classic Asian luxurity feeling.Some say it needs an upgrade but I love this classic Asian luxurity hotel. Large rooms with quality furniture and nicely decorated. Spacious bathroom with separate shower and bath. We arrived early but surprisingly we could already check in. We stayed on the club-floor and I believe it is definitely worth the extra money. Included is breakfast, evening Hords d'Oeuvres with alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages and all day tea and coffee and some non-alcoholic drinks. Also transfer to and from the airport is included for club-floor guest and access to spa and fitness.As  from pictures and other reviews you can tell this property is huge. Good-sized swimming pool, well maintained gardens and a casino on site. A perfect place to end or start your holiday in Nepal as it is close to the airport.However it gets busy in weekends as the hotel offers brunch and pool access passes with kids activities for locals and expats. The best thing I believe that makes this hotel special is the staff. The cleaner, waiters, receptionists, cooks, bell boy etc all seem to be proud to be part of this hotel. Everybody is so kind and caring and they genuinely are happy to do whatever it takes to make your stay enjoyable. I would recommend this hotel to anybody in a heartbeat.

Stayed in Club rooms facing Stupa, Excellent ambience & photogenic location within crowded Kathmandu, Superb quality of food, Easy accessibility to Casino, good & clean rooms, good service but not value for money.

Beautiful hotel very  with excellent surroundings and all amenities one would wish to have.Excellent personnel always willing to help - NAMASTE" - and help in everything we asked help for.Highly recommended

Property is very good. Staffs are excellent. Casino out here is pretty good you can try your luck. Will plan a visit again. Breakfast spread is also good. It is located close to pashupatinath temple. Will try to visit again if I get a chance.

To start with it is a huge property with lot of space to walk even inside the hotel amidst the greenaries. The pool is huge even though could not swim in short stay time. The hotel staff were courteous and helpful always. The club lounge was too good and the manager &staff  handling it was going extra mile to feel us comfortable.Will definitely stay next time too in this hotel. The only drawback I found was housekeeping was not keeping enough stuff like paste, shower cap, soaps in bath room . We felt it was miserly and every time we have to call and ask for things. While having breakfast the marriage crowd mixed with hotel guests and we felt noisy and cramped while having breakfast. Noise levels were very high. Marriage crowd should not be allowed to join the regular breakfast area. They shoud have separate room or place to have breakfast like how companies do during their meetings.  Otherwise the breakfast spread was good and great experience.

Had an excellent stay.Front desk team was very helpful. Hotel lobby and restaurants are well maintained. Quality of food is also very good. Location is also very nice. They do provide shuttle service from Hotel till the airport.

Thankyou so much for welcoming us to you house.The Hyatt regency  is just like being home; staff very friendly and helpful. Don’t walk past the travel desk, we found them to be a wealth of helpful knowledge.The rooms are massive, clean and quiet. The hotel restaurants have good food and offer great value.

The drive from the airport to the hotel is shear madness, thousands of cars and bikes all vying for the same piece of road so when you arrive at the hotel grounds there is a big sigh of relief to be away from the chaos outside. The hotel is architecturally beautiful inside and out. Reception area is spacious and staff are courteous and friendly. Our room was clean, quiet and comfortable. The Cafe, breakfast choices were plentiful and staff attentive. The Rox restaurant served good Italian food which made a nice change from spicy curries.The pool and grounds made a welcome retreat from the dusty city streets.

Had a great time staying here.  Perfect location.  Great staff.  Comfortable rooms.   Stayed here twice during our stay.    There’s a grocery store if you exit and turn right.  Staff gave us some free milk for our daughter when we checked in.

The Hyatt Regency provided excellent service at a great price.  I found my room on both occasions that I stayed there, to be nice and comfortable. Additionally, the breakfast buffet and their fine-dinning restaurant were both lovely decorated with delicious food to go with them. In the future, we will have more leaders going to Nepal and they will stay at the Hyatt Regency.

The hotel provided a very good stay experience. I booked a club level room which came with the standard club benefits including a very good evening cocktail hour with a self-serve bar and delicious regional foods and canapes.  The guest rooms were reflective of the Nepal culture but clean and comfortable, roomy but maybe a little sparse in feel (but that might be a reflection of the local culture). The bathrooms were clean and typical of the Hyatt Regency brand. The outdoor areas included a large pool and hot tub facilities that seemed to be very well maintained, and expansive lawns and gardens for strolling during the day. The proximity to a world-famous Buddhist stupa (which can be seen from Club level rooms) made it a great vacation experience. The hotel property is about four miles from central Kathmandu but the hotel operates a complimentary shuttle to those historic and shopping areas.  Overall, I felt that the staff and hotel delivered well on the Hyatt Regency experience.

Haya Regency Kathmandu, Nepal. Great property, but far from center of city and Government and tourist activities and with  heavy traffic, problematic for business. Staff very friendly and hospitality great. Special thanks to Aarati, Sabina, Promikshya and Ajay, for their  patience , support and hospitality.

Facilities were nice, location excellent (back gate opens onto Boudha area and is only a few minutes walk from the large Stupa) and staff were very friendly and professional.  Breakfast was excellent too.

Incredible beautiful hotel. My room was spectacular. Lack of outlets and a comfy bed, were constant irritants. Breakfast was great, but Club food was terrible. The staff were very kind and helpful. It’s far from Thanek, but close to the Boudhanath stoopa. It’s a good place to stay if you want to be a bit removed from the chaos of the city.

Venivamo da un tour in India, dove abbiamo soggiornato in bellissimi e confortevoli  hotels, ma questo di Kathmandu è stato veramente il top. Bella la struttura, una hall magnifica in stile templi, bello l'esterno, giardini, piscine. C'è anche la zona spa per farsi coccolare. Abbiamo provato ambedue i ristoranti presenti e ci siamo trovati molto bene, soprattutto in quello con menu orientato all'Italiana.

After the 2017 earthquake, all of Kathmandu is undergoing reconstruction. The hotel itself was in great shape and not appearing to have been damaged, from being a guest, but traveling to the airport or any tourist site as a disaster. The roads everywhere, simultaneously are being rebuilt, causing such a dust cloud and bumpingtraffic jams and delays getting anywhere. What would be 15 min was an hour.My karma...upon arrival the front desk staff I found cold in affect, almost as if they wanted to finish dealing with me to get back to their business. I was surprised by noescort to my room, something I found in all hotels in India. The a/c was broken in my first room, and after an attempt by the engineering staff, still wasn't repaired. Second room the a/c worked sufficiently to sleep comfortably but wasn't functioning properly. Reception responded to me as if I was inconveniencing them! But I must add: there is one outstanding front desk employee: Yashoda, to whom I found warmth and kindness and patience and friendliness. She needs to teach the entire front desk staff how to behave!The property is gorgeous, food very good. Don't plan on swimming in their gorgeous big pool, the water temp was icy.

I spent about 2 weeks traveling India and Nepal. All Hotels were to be 5 star, this one was the only one I considered 5 star. Tremendous service, good food, comfortable bed, quality tv , great bathroom ,etc .

Spent a couple of nights there in March. This is a large hotel with above average amenities including hot tub, pool and spa. Spa treatments were good. This really sums up the hotel, everything was good but not great and as such loses a little for the value persoective.

As I mentioned earlier it is is better to provide more charging stations near to the bed side area.  Food quality to be improved.  We had a Chicken Biriyani which was absolutely not good especially the quality of Rice used and the preparation.

Lovely hotel in spacious grounds away from the dust of Kathmandu. The hotel has 2 restaurants, a bar and pool bar serving food.  We ate at each of these and were very impressed with the quality of the food and the service provided The pool area is lovely with plenty of beds and for those wanting the facility there is a gym and a spa. I would recommend this hotel to anyone wanting a bit of down time in Nepal.  It is only 15 minutes to the airport which is a big bonus with the traffic in Kathmandu.

The Hyatt’s lush acreage is reason enough to stay here. In town but a world apart. As soon as you turn in the (well guarded) gates, you leave the dust, bustle, traffic, crowds, and hassles behind. Huge but still offers a terrific level of personal service. Buffets at breakfast and dinner offer a range of cuisines and choices. Rooms are spacious, well appointed, and comfortable. Pool, outdoor hot tub, spa, and jogging trail complete the picture.

My wife and I traveled to Kathmandu and stay at the Hyatt for a week. What a wonderful hotel! Beautiful lobby, restaurant, bar and pool. After reading fair reviews, I was expecting anything. I was wrong ! The staff is what makes to hotel and beauty of the hotel was WOW!! Next time in Kathmandu, please stay at the Hyatt. Also book a club room, it’s well worth it. A special thank you to Nima at Club Lounge - she really was a big help to us.

I'm kind of amazed by the low reviews of this place. I am super picky and I found it gorgeous. The pool area, lobby and grounds are very impressive. The breakfast room is pretty with outdoor optional seating and a view over the pool area, with a wide variety of options and the  breakfast food was above average. The Italian restaurant has a lovely candlelit atmosphere at dinner although the pizza was just so so, but then it's Nepal not Napoli. I didn't notice any cleanliness issues in the common areas or room and the staff was pleasant and helpful.I also like that the business center allowed you to just go in and use the computer whenever you wanted without needing staff assistance - a good learning for the ITC hotel chain in India.The rooms are a good size and the bathrooms are HUGE with a tub and modern shower and really good, hard water pressure. My only issue is that when it comes to decor and comfort, the rooms are hardly a match for the opulence of the lobby and other common areas. The room makes you feel like you're staying in a monastery. Very sparse with low beds and a thin mattress, no box spring. The beds were not horribly uncomfortable per se, but a place like this should have thick luxurious mattresses and great pillows, not make you feel like your're doing penance everytime you go to bed. The 'headboards' are literally a wooden bar over the bed that looks like a curtain rod with a fabric-covered cushion hanging from them, which of course can't be cleaned and is probabably covered in all matter of things a blue light would reveal. I tried not to think about it. Oh I lied one other issue is I frequently smelled cigarette smoke in the room and hallway leading to our room, unless that is just the general Nepal pollution smell? I couldn't tell but it was an unpleasant musty odor.If this place would just refurbish the rooms and deal with the musty smell I'd give it a 5 rating. The short 10 minute walk to the stupa out the back gate is a nice plus, just don't attempt it at night. If a hotel like this is only ranked 69 I'm dying to see what is ranked higher.

Great location, quiet and set back from the busy streets of Kathmandu. Five minutes walk to Boudhanath Stupa, wich is nice.But I think it's quite some time since this was a luxury hotel. The rooms a nice, but tired. Although clean, the bathrooms need some serious attention, as does the furniture in the restaurants. The staff is nice and helpful, but please, maintain this beautiful hotel before it's too late.

The Hyatt Regency is a 5-star hotel considered among the best hotels in Kathmandu. It sits on an immense property which if it was managed properly would be a lovely hotel. We were really surprised that the hotel does not seem to maintain cleanliness standards at all. There were simple things like the public areas and bathrooms which were dirty. Floors and carpets that could quickly be cleaned were left messy and unclean. The many gardens of the hotel have potential to look nice but instead have no well designed trees, grass or flowers.  It seems nothing is being done to make the property look nice or clean!The management team of Hyatt needs to pay some serious attention to hire some cleaners and landscapers. As many reviews have mentioned, hotel also needs to update its rooms as well. It's a shame this beautiful property is not being well maintained.

Still very imposing - the charm of the Hyatt has faded over time and looks a bit jaded. The interiors especially the rooms badly need a facelift.
