Aircondition in club room was turned down/shutdown making it uncomfortable between 11pm and 6am on day one. after repeated requests on day two, this was not done and night was comfortable. the condition of the hotel is very average maintainance. sofa in room was stained

This is a very big property with vast lawns. The building and other infrastructure is old and has started to show it's age now. But food is excellent. It's away from major tourist centre i.e  Thamel. However it's vey calm and peaceful.  Overall an excellent place to stay.

Considering the price, staff is not very friendly or hospitable, especially the higher up you go.  Kind of shabby, taking all into consideration.  A hotel of this caliber should at least have a gift/book shop where you can pick up a few treats, souvenirs and necessities.  All they really have is a high end jewelry store...Food is ok...

Really cool and luxurious hotel. The rooms are big and clean. It includes nice cafes and restuarants and they have a great spa. It's far from the famous Stupa with a walking distance of 5 minutes. And if you want to buy some Nepalese jewlry, there is a fabulous store within the hotel owned by a guy named Asim.

I visited the Hotel for two nights in June on a bed and breakfast basis. The distance from the airport is very good and takes only 15-20 minutes with light traffic.Check in at the hotel was okay as nobody else was waiting. This could be a delay as there are only two checking in stations.The rooms are adequate and reasonably sized. Breakfast buffet is reasonably extensive with a wide choice to choose from.The spa area and changing rooms are in dire need of refurbishing as they are quite grubby. In general the whole hotel needs money spending on it as it looks well worn. New hotels are due to open in Kathmandu next year so this hotel needs to lift its game.

I had my supper in the ROX Italian restaurant and ate lazagna, which was the last food i ate and got poisened due to that i took the bacteria from the beef on it. In the following 24 hours, i had diarrhoea and then i had fevers of 40 celcius degrees and taken to emergency and got given total 5 serums. In the next 2 days, i suffered from the serious tough abdomen aches and my fever continued between 38.5 and 40 C, I used many kind medicines the doctor prescriped and i was no able to go to my job for 1 week. Because I had intestine infection, BECAUSE I TRUSTED THIS ITALIAN RESTUARANT TO BE CLEAN .

A friend and I went for a late lunch, early afternoon tea to what we had been told was the best hotel in Kathmandu.  We both ordered a club sandwich - what a disappointment, entirely without taste!  The service was slack, at best, bordering on rude at times and very expensive!!!!!  The hotel itself, apart from the beautiful entry doors, was seriously lacking in any character, you could have been in Detroit or Bognor Regis.....

In my opinion Hotel like Hyatt should know guest prefernces  about thier choice o room they prefer to stay or food they prefer to eat . Not necessarily guest has to provide or remind at reception every time i check in to the hotel . I have been staying in Hyatt for last 8-9 years and have never seen any difference of service or even improvement in service so  not sure whether i can expect any further imrpovement ...

Large hotel with lush grounds.   Post-QK Kathmandu is overwhelming. The hotel was a welcome respite each evening after spending the days sightseeing.   Air pollution was an issue in KTM when we were there because of the heating oil & gas embargo from India.  We wore face masks and washed them out daily.   The club lounge staff (Nagina) was outstanding.  They knew I drank Diet Coke and one evening they ran out because of delivery delays (embargo).   But majically more appeared the next day.  The staff had gone to the local grocery store and bought more for me.  Unbelievably top service!   The dining staff and chef was aware of my wife's gluten-free dietary intolerance and went out of the way to accommodate.  The rooms could use an update.  Overall, this hotel is very nice

I spent 2 weeks traveling throughout China Tibet and Nepal  The Hyatt was by far the best hotel I stayed in during my trip The staff was excellent and very attentive. Wide choice of both western and Asian Cuisine and Good workout falculity

I have been to the Hyatt Regency in Kathmandu four different times and each time it gets better.   This past stay I was there for 9 days and it began to feel like a home away from home.   The staff made every attempt to make sure my stay was comfortable and enjoyable.   The grounds are impeccable and the design of the lobby area is gorgeous.  The pool area has three pools: a large pool for doing laps and relaxing, a pool for the small children and a hot-tub pool.   It can be very tempting to hang out by the pool all day long. The Hyatt is about a 5 - 15 minute walk (depending which way you go) from the Boudhanath Stupa, the most highly revered stupa in the Buddhist world.  Being close to Boudhanath was the main reason I originally chose the Hyatt.  What I found out is that one is very close to the airport, Paten and it is very easy to use a taxi to drive to many other local destinations in Kathmandu and the valley.The rooms are comfortable and are a nice size, unlike many of the hotels in Europe and the US.   The Regency Club room is well appointed and has a very nice happy hour for the end of each day.   I highly recommend the Hyatt Regency.   It is one of my most favorite hotels on this planet and I have been to many of the luxury hotels in Asia and Europe.   This hotel is calming, peaceful and it is in one of the most wonderful, interesting cities on this planet.

Ok, really.... This hotel no doubt has wonderful grounds for sure!  Rooms are dated and tired.  Air con is good, but it's centrally controlled, so the temp is not really adjustable.  I found it adequate, but still feels musty.  Dirty and old shower glass...tired everything, but ok.  Internet is very very slow, forget about the speed... less than 1mb on up and download! Pool is nice. Breakfast is good, but meat dishes are lacking.  Fresh juices and a simple variety of breads from donuts to fried bread, rice, processed meats and salty fish.  Service is good all around, but lacking slightly in some areas such as the restaurant and pool area.  Linens and towels seem old, but clean.  Lobby is wonderful though and hallways looking worn with wooden doors and creaky floors.
ロケーションとしては、タメル地区から遠く、観光には適していないかもしれませんが、その分静かに過ごせるし、なんといっても普通にホテルライフを楽しめました。お湯も普通に出るし、何一つ不自由がありませんでした。なかなか来れるところではありませんが、機会があったらまた宿泊したいです。

Pros:- rooms are up to the usual Western 4* standard, which is not a given in Kathmandu (e.g. also stayed in Yak & Yeti which feels a lot more dated and used up)- I really liked the architectual style, it seems like they made an effort not to make it look like just another business hotel- food in the restaurant was pretty good and reasonably priced- the grounds are not huge but they are nice- good outdoor pool + jacuzzi- good serviceCons:- next to the hotel, there is a small "tent city" for victims of the earth quake who lost their houses. we didn't have any issues at all, but it is a bit sad to see people so deprived next to a 4* hotel (though it's a good thing that these people have not been moved away to be forgotten somewhere out of sight I guess)- location is not right in the middle of town, but it's a short cab ride away to the center. However, quite close to the Buddha Stupa (one of the key tourist attractions)

The uncleanliness, inattention to detail, and dishonesty of the Nepali culture is rubbing off on the Kathmandu Hyatt. We had a terrible experience. Service was bad, food was bad, hotel smelled badly, and room was not clean. There were stains on the bed and on the chair. The shower drain was clogged and water would flood the bathroom during a very short shower. It was not a five-star hotel experience at all.

Great resort type hotel but needs hotel staff improvement.  The staff do not greet their hotel guests and pool side food took awhile to arrive.    I traveled solo to Kathmandu to relax.  I was having a relaxing dinner and all of the sudden, a dozen of businessman marched in and were having a very loud business meeting.  After watching the meeting, I couldn't finish my meal and was very stressed out . Hyatt should of accommodated these people in a private room a removable partition walls/doors.

What more than coming home, had nice nyt partying with friends after a long stay abroad. Was good catch up with friends in december and always polite service in hyatt makes me go back again and again. I miss nepal hyatt even if i am abroad as it is home its big and great value for money!! Thoroughly recommended and cant wait to be back soon

I would stay here again, I understand it's the best hotel in Kathmandu (at least for business).  But it's an average "best".  Older furnishings, low beds (fashionable, culturally relevant, but for people who are older, with bad backs, maybe a little hard to lift off from, lol).  No clock by the bedside, a certain aged dowdiness (but not in a heritage kind of way...).  Staff v. friendly & generally competent.  I found the b'fast buffet pleasant but somewhat limited.  I think most people would be happy here, it has a lot to recommend it, but it's not the type of hotel I would look forward to returning to...but would because there seem to be no better alternatives.

On a short visit to Nepal arranged by Google Treks I stayed at the Hyatt - and was amazed by the scale and quality of the hotel.  The rooms I stayed in (the '11s and the '13s) were quiet, even though they were on the airport side, because of the size of the hotel grounds, which are enormous.  For meals the patio is nice in the cool of the morning and the evening.  Explore the grounds - I saw mongoose.

Place was just a art of people out there..  The place was of Nepal culture and the way customers were treated was to appreciate for.  The environment was really clean and beautiful.  People was outstanding and services was lovely

I doubt you could find a better hotel in Kathmandu than the Hyatt Regency.  It was a great value and provided an oasis to the hustle and bustle of the rest of the city.  It has an incredible pool and would appeal to both families and single travelers.  Te business lounge provided a nice place to relax and chat with fellow travelers.

Everytime I visit Hyatt its kinda nostalgic. Reminds me of my childhood days when i used to come for the food festival with my family and weekend brunch and a dip in the beautiful pool. Hyatt Regeny never fails to impress me,

It is huge and nice building.We booked 3 Deluxe Club Rooms for 3 nights. Rooms are large but a bit dated. anyway if you think about conditions in Nepal, this is great hotel. We could check in 6th floor in lounge and also between 17:30 and 19:30 happy hours in the lounge. Instead booking a regular room with breakfast, better book club room which is already includes breakfast.No electric or water cut down. Staff is very polite. Even we got an offer for airport transfer from hotel and confirmed the fees, they made both side transfers complimentary. Restaurants are fine. I strongly recommend to stay in Hyatt Regency Kathmandu.

Hyatt regency is spread in a very huge area. The building is inspired by traditional Nepali architecture  but quite modern. The room was good with a small balcony to enjoy the sun. It was neat and clean and had required amenities.  Though it lacked sound proof The sound from adjoining room could be heard.  The bathroom was larger than so many I have seen in Nepal and abroad. There was separate shower cubical too besides bath tub. Hot water available all the time. Breakfast was good, wifi , airport transfer and spa was given complimentary.  24 hours electricity even there was huge load shedding in Kathmandu. hotel lobby was very impressive.The ground and garden was lovely and well maintained. Highly recommend it.

One of the best hotels ever stayed. Outside park view. Food. Rooms and lobby area simply makes me feel awesome about the place. Staff is helpful too. I would love to visit more and more. No place like nepal!

Went to Katmandu on official trip. What a trip it has turned out to be when u get to stay in hyatt. Hotel structure, ambience, staff and a view from the room picture perfect. Had a wonderful stay and enjoyed every but of it. Truly spectacular. Keep it up

The rooms are everything you would expect from Hyatt clean comfortable bed nice décor. The lobby area leads to a beautiful garden and water features with fountains and a relaxed atmosphere.  Pool area is very nice for the Himalayas !The breakfast is a spectacular experience and for me worth everything after being in the mountains. Location is a little out of town which is an inconvenience but the environment is clean and a sanctuary away from the dust and hustle and bustle of Kathmandu life. Personal favourite on multiple trips. There are usually some really good offers on line and I have paid as little as $120 a night. Worth comparing.

Being from aviation background I get to see a lot of properties but this one is my favourite by far . Peaceful ,elegant and classic in every manner. Has a casino too if you wish to try your luck. Perfect in every sense. I had stayed here in 2014 Jan as well when I had gone for my wedding anniversary and had real good time.

Very nice property on extensive grounds. Hotel was quiet with good amenities. Enjoyed the restaurant was well as it sever local flavors in a buffet style, very convenient with good serve, would recommend this property

Slightly dated building but with its own charmPros : Near airport Jogging / walking track Spacious compound, not much of noiseBoudhnath stupa nearby - good for a evening walk through the back gate excellent spa - sensational hot stone massage Decent food - with good choice & reasonable price Cons weak internet / very slow Outside the main gate is not a great place to walkoverall decent stay but do not compare with other Hyatt across the region, this is bit different

I had thought about going to another hotel for a change. I am glad I didn't.  The service and standards are high here and they never change from this. I was here a year ago and loved every minute of my stay. I am glad to say that I loved this stay too.

I have stayed at this beautiful property for about a week over a year ago.  Even though I had my choice to stay at the Radisson,  the Soaltee Crown Plaza or the Hyatt Regency, I chose to stay the Hyatt and it didn't  disappoint me. This time I was going to stay in Nepal for only about 10 days but my son started feeling sick in India (visit) and I changed my flight itinerary & returned to Nepal sooner to start staying at the Hyatt.After the first day of my stay at the Hyatt KTM, I felt bit disappointed for things like the pool being closed, the lawn having no green grass for my son to play, the free shuttle rides to Thamel no longer being offered.Some of the staffs were not so welcoming to us like they were before. I thought about canceling my remaining stays at the Hyatt  to try the Radisson or the Crown Plaza but thanI was fortunate enough to get a chance to meet & sit down with Mr. Vijay Karki the next day.He was very professional, a good leader and he assured us an enjoyable stay.We did enjoy our 2 week long stay at this property. The staffs treated us nice and I have few names I want to mention here who really were so nice to us and so caring to my young son. The first in the list is Mr.Vijay Karki who is the director of the rooms of this property. I want to thank Executive Chef Mr. Arun Prasad for the delicious  morning breakfast buffet every morning at the Cafe and for being so nice to my young child. Thank you Arun for the delicious rice & dhaal you made for my toddler. The breakfast menus, wide range of options and the tastes have NEVER disappointed me and my wife. I believe he is a great asset to the Hyatt Regency hotel in KTM.I also want to thank Mrs. Sunita Basnet -cafeMrs. Nirjala and Sujita at the Regency Club lounge.I want to give a shout out to all those names who really made us feel at home.This is a true  5 *****  star property and you really do get what you pay for.It is a fantastic hotel with  dedicated leaders & staffs. . I saw the GM at the Lounge and had a chance to say Hi to her.I hope to return to this property in near future

There are few 5 star hotels, we did not see the other ones, but were very happy with our stay. Location is good, there are restaurants and shopping nears Stupa. 10 minute walk to Boudhanath stupa, can be easily reached through an exit at the back of the hotel. Large, pleasant and spacious rooms. Somewhat dated but fantastic for Nepal standards, mostly now that the country has suffered economically after the earthquake. The restaurant on the first floor, The Cafe, served delicious food, both western and Nepali/Indian, with great service in a pleasant ambiance.

A very well run property near the Stupa. Staff great hotel big with lots of facilities but only 40 % occupancy so at times felt a bit desolate. You should try it - you will enjoy. The pool was empty but the weather too cold to swim - go in the warmer time if you want to swim, This did not affect our holiday,

After doing a hike to ebc we wanted something luxurious and to treat ourselves and it's exactly what we got. The property is huge with security it's like a suburb on its own.. The hotel itself is 5 star as is the staff.. It has everything from pools bars restaurants which are good quality and not over the top expensive a casino and shops. You can get closer hotels to Kathmandu it took us about 10-15 mins to get into Kathmandu where we needed to go that's a small price to play for the quality

Stayed at Hyatt Regency during the last visit to Kathmandu and I must say this is a fantastic property. Have stayed in some other five star hotels in Kathmandu as well but they are now a bit old and not very well maintained. However this was excellent. Huge property with nice views. The lobby is huge and had live music playing when we checked in. Rooms were very spacious too with huge bathroom. Rooms have everything you need.Hotel has some nice restaurants. The hotel has a casino as well and the crowd  was pretty good.Overall i think the best property to stay in Kathmandu.

It was a grand building located near to the Kathmandu Airport. Staying in the resort make you to have a luxurious feeling. They have good restaurants. We went hiking in Nepal and it gave us a cozy environment for us to recover from the tiring trip. Even the room service was reasonably charged with good quality.

This is a hidden gem within walking distance to a large pagoda where you can spin the prayer wheels, great local shopping and site seeing. I never felt unsafe while walking around the city.  The hotel sits on several acres and the grounds are beautiful.  Bring a bathing suit as they have a large pool.  The hotel has great food and the rooms are kept cold and are very nice and clean.

I do have to remind myself that this Hotel is located in Kathmandu. A city that is still crumbling from the last Earthquake and all the previous ones as well. As such the Hotel provides excellent 5 Star Service. However, the Property is need in for some Room Upgrades as even the Club Level Rooms look tired. It is a short distance from the Airport which is very convenient when arriving and departing. The food is also delicious. The city is filled with dirt and smog. So it's hard to escape the dust and smell unless you retire to your Room. Not my favorite Hyatt!

I was really surprised to see such an awesome hotel in Kathmandu. anybody travelling to Kathmandu must not miss staying here. the food is good and not very expensive. the lounge area is well made and they have a nice bar where they serve some stone fire pizzas :)

probably the best character Hyatt in the world...probably the best hospitality you can ask for...we love the jacuzzi and the pool..the breakfast is amazing! afternoon tea overlooking the stupa..monks welcome and roaming around give such an amazing aura

We stayed one two occasion for a number of nights at the Hyatt Regency Hotel on two occasions for a number of nights during a tour of Nepal with Riviera Travel. This review is probably going to be a short one as there is little to fault the hotel.The grounds are beautifully maintained, the location is excellent for experiencing the city, all the staff are incredibly helpful, the restaurant was very good, the wines are also really good, the room spacious and though slightly old very nice, the pool area is spectacular, the breakfast/restaurant outside seating (overlooking the pool) is a super place to eat.In the large entrance foyer there was a 3 piece Nepalese band playing soothing traditional music which adds wonderfully to the atmosphere. We were B&B on our visit and usually ate from the buffet in the evening although there is an a-la-carte option. The buffet had so many dishes to offer it suited all of us well.Just across the road from the hotel entrance is a large (by Nepalese standards) department store which sells nearly everything, manly Chinese imported goods I think so rather like all the £1 shops in the world rolled into one – but handy for a few things you might needs.I would add a note of realism in that when you pass the security guards on the entrance gate and walk up the well-manicured gardens for about 300 metres to the hotel it is a world away from the lively/bustling street out with the manic buses/tut-tuts/motorbikes etc. all of which makes Kathmandu such a wonderful place to visit. So speaking as a slightly soft westerner a snack or cocktail by the beautiful pool after a day’s wandering around the city is wonderful (sorry about that).As a thing to do – there are many very poor charity schools which if you ask you may get the chance to visit and make a small $ donation, we went and wish that we had gone to the £1 shop in the UK beforehand and bought several packs of simple lead pencils (not colour) as the children have so little. Give it a go if you can, it’s well worth it.

I stayed here as part of a package holiday to Nepal and have to say this hotel is really really something else! It has a calm atmosphere from the entrance to the restaurant and the staff are very attentive. The rooms are beautiful very spacious and clean. The restaurant downstairs has a great variety even though there were shortages of food in Nepal while I was there due to the blockade by the Indian government. Lunch on the terrace was lovely too and the breakfasts were tasty and varied. I would definitely recommend this hotel and would love to return one dat.

The spa experience with Ram Kumari was exceptional. She was a delight: very experienced, polite, outstandingly competent, almost a spiritual body scrub. Ram was delightful. I enjoyed every moment and highly recommend. The whole thing also represented outstanding value for money. I highly recommend. Julie Cutts

Will 100% NOT being staying at the Hyatt in Kathmandu again. Upon checking out I was presented with a €200 bill for a small bag of laundry. When paying I presumed it was €20 and paid the bill in a bit of a rush checking out. After looking at my online banking, I now realise it was €200 and am absolutely disgusted. There is no mistake here - this is just what they charge which is completely absurd. This teamed with the fact that the staff and hotel seemed to overlook the 21 of us that brought our business back for the 3rd/4th year in a row makes returning not an option. They attempted to charge us all for breakfast on the day of checkout and had and all round lack of care for anything other than money, which is really unfortunate for a 5 star hotel. Next year our business will have to be brought elsewhere.

It is an average hotel with good exteriors but very poor interiors and fittings. The rooms are in desperate need of an upgrade and so is the spa. The wooden doors in the spa could do with changes as they are literally broken. The service was good at the reception but very slow at the restaurants. They did not have more than half the things on their menu. Overall, parts of it were better than expected and bits that could do with a major overhaul.

Was not impress with my stay this time.  This is my 6th time in Kathmandu and I had always stayed at the Hyatt.  Not sure if they had changed managements?  Things don't feel the same.  Service level is down and the rooms are getting old.  The king size bed was lumpy.  Key cards not working well and to my surprise when filthy water came out of the bath tub.  I was brushed off when I brought it up with management - they say they were servicing the water pipes and to run the water longer to clear it.  It was disgusting - and should not occur in a 5 star hotel even in Kathmandu.

Want to experience a wonderful Nepal experience while having the important conveniences to do emails and Skype on the go with steady electricity.  Splurge a bit and go to the Regency club level so you can enjoy great views of the 6th floor of the world famous stupa and a 5;30- 7:30 free happy hour + free breakfast. Room Tip: Go for a room to the left side of the hotel so you get more neighborhood views.  The 6th floor is best.  Spa Tip: Excellent spa service including wonderful massage experience with Ramikumari.  She is one of my top 10 massages I have had in my life.   The spa sauna and  steam work really well and while not overly ornate it is right in keeping with the Nepalese style.   Ask for a mid day discount rate around lunch time so the price is so great you can afford to do more than 1 treatment if you wish.

This hotel had minimal damage during the earthquake.  Rooms beautifully appointed but getting a little worn looking, breakfast is fabulous, grounds are beautiful.  Staff is wonderful, helpful and pleasant. Location is great with a short walk to Boudhanath Stupa.

Estuve tres días. Me impresionaron favorablemente: la arquitectura del hotel, su parque,  la seguridad sin controles agresivos ni invasivos. Nadie puede transitar por los pasillos del hotel sin abrir las puertas a los mismos con la tarjeta de la habitación. Es destacable el excelente el trato de todo el  personal. Pero lo mejor es  la comida. El sabor de los platos que comí la última noche - no era buffet y pedí cosas sencillas - fue excepcional. Realmente felicito al chef y su equipo!

Close to the airport, designed with Kathmandu in mind and a short walk down to the most holy Boudha Stoupa, the Hyatt Regency Kathmandu offers a respite from the hectic city. Public areas and restaurants very nice. Guestrooms need renovation.

This is a great place to stay in Kathmandu. The hotel itself is very complete. Food is great, especially breakfast. The room I had had a sublime garden view, was big, and always very clean. The hotel is within a large domain that contrasts with the city's cramped and crowded environment. You don't have to go outside for your jogging. The location is also good, with a temple right across the street. Cabs are always available, and for $3 to $4 and 20 minutes or so you'll be downtown. Airport is also very close.I've stayed there for a week. Staff were always helpful and extremely nice. I haven't tried it, but colleagues told me massages were great, and not expensive.

This hotel has been consistently good over the  years.  I love the location with its amazing views of the Baudha.  it has a nice leisurely feel to it which is quiet relaxing.  the club rooms are worth the extra spend.

No doubt that this hotel needs to be refurbished, yet the overall experience was good and the staff really friendly wherever you are or ask for.Food was better than I expected but definitely not exquisite and doesn't always match how it's described on the menu.Haven't visited any other hotels in Kathmandu but this one is a safe bet.

Fantastic service and space around the outside hotel facilities. The staff was very friendly and everything is extremely well functioning. We stayed with 2 kids and even though this might not be a family hotel it is hotel where kids are welcome and you can have a great stay

Located just 6 Kms from the airport  and 2.5 Kms from the Pashupatinath Temple is in the heart of Kathmandu city . An 29 acres resort with manicured gardens and lawns it simply blows you away with its serenity & tranquillity. Lovely Nepalese architecture adds to the beauty of the hotel . Very comfortable and spacious rooms , courteous and efficient staff made my stay very enjoyable . Food was great .Overall a great experience .

Beautiful hotel and exquisite grounds. A bit far from Thamel and other visitor attractions in Kathmandu. Good service and great food. Close to Boudhanath Stupa and restaurants in that area. Tennis courts are an added positive.

Estuvimos a finales del pasado mes de marzo y la experiencia fue buenisima. El trato exquisito y las habitaciones grandes y limpias. Tanto en recepción como el resto del personal siempre dispuestos a ayudar. Por supuesto todos los dias el agua de regalo en la habitación. El restaurante expectacular, siempre tratando de agradar y de complacer a los clientes. Despues de los ultimos acontecimientos en Nepal no se si habran tenido algun problema, pero yo lo recomendaria sin dudar.

Upon entering exiting Kathmandu Tribhuvan airport, we were greeted by two men who we had arranged with the hotel, to bring us to the hotel. We were graciously greeted at check in and were offered a complimentary upgrade with our Hyatt passport. This card also gave us access to the lounge on the top floor, which offered drinks and small canapés during certain hours. The rooms were large and incorporated local designs whilst still offering the modern conveniences that one would expect from an international luxury hotel. Our room also offered views of the world famous Boudhanath Stupa through the wall to wall, floor to ceiling windows. The gardens were meticulously maintained, and offered an insight on all of the endemic plantings that Nepal has to offer. One sector of this otherwise spectacular hotel that I feel could use improvement are the food services. Though the hotel offered many well prepared, and flavorful local and Indian dishes, there were not many meals that appeal to the Western pallet. In all, this hotel offers Kathmandu's best large accomodations.

My stay was very brief so it is hard to comment on everything you could experience. The atmosphere is phenomenal, a bit old world feel with the wood throughout the facility and lots of stone.  I awoke early and the staff provided coffee out on the upper patio so I could watch the sunrise. Wish I could have had more time and plan to come back in the near future.

My wife and I spent our anniversary here. We really enjoyed our stay here. We spent the night before leaving and the night after returning from a trek to Lukla/Namche Bazaar. The rooms are huge and comfortable and the hotel property is very beautiful. We really enjoyed the pool and it was very relaxing after trekking for so many days. The service was amazing and the hotel is close to a lot of major sights. I would recommend staying here to anyone visiting Kathmandu.

Having just returned home from an extended holiday abroad, I finally have time to sit down and not only write this review, but thank the staff of this hotel.Arriving on Friday, 24APR15, we only had two days in Kathmandu, a place I hadn't visited previously.  The hotel staff was waiting at the arrivals area to drive us to the hotel for our short stay.  A grand hotel, this property definitely sticks out as one of the larger properties in the city.  Check-in was quick and efficient.  Our room on the 4th floor was nice, had a comfortable bed, working air conditioning, and plenty of room to relax.  We were also granted access to the 6th floor lounge due to the Hyatt Gold Passport Platinum status.  The property sits on several hectares or land with well manicured surroundings.  Inside, the property is also well maintained and clean.  The lounge on the 6th floor offered PM cocktails the night we arrived and small bites to enjoy.  The food and drink was limited, but very adequate.  Staff was also very helpful with suggestions on places to visit and hotel shuttle (free) drop off locations/times.Breakfast in The Cafe the next morning was also impressive.  Chef stations preparing eggs and pancakes.  Plenty of other food to choose from including fruits, cereals, fresh baked breads and many local items.  You will not start your day starving.11:56am on 25APR15 - The earth decides to make a pretty significant shift beneath the region.  We were clear across the city at the time of the earthquake and took several hours to walk back to the Hyatt, helping along the way in any way we could.  Upon arrival, the hotel staff, guests and many others were camped out on the lawn awaiting a structural engineer to come assess the building's integrity.Food, water and juices were available to all those camped out on the lawn.  As the evening approached, the GM, made several announcements and directed guests to move from the lawn to the lobby and await further instructions.  We were fed dinner, provided water and camped out in the lobby.  The scene was unreal, but a safer location than guest rooms at the time.  The hotel had power due to their own generator, while much of the city looked dark.  Aftershocks rocked the area several times throughout the evening.Luxury hotels have emergency plans in place.  This hotel, under the direction and guidance of GM Sinead O’Reilly-Henell, did everything in their power to help.  She remained very calm throughout the evening and into the next morning.  Her staff did the same.  This shows a great deal of strength to do what they did during the time of crisis.  Many stayed on hand throughout the whole evening without any sleep.With the assistance from the hotel staff, we were lucky enough to make our flight out the next morning on Druk Air. I have worked in the luxury hotel business for many years and I would be honored and proud to work for a woman like Sinead.  Many thanks and praise to her and the staff.

It's my sixth stay at this hotel in the Kathmandu area. The hotel is about 15 min walk to the Boudanath stupa. If you stay in a "stupa view" room then you would see it from afar, giving you a serene and peaceful feeling at night when it's lit up! Room begin to show wear and tear even though hotel has done its best to keep it in the best condition it can. I think it's about time they need to do some renovation. The service offered by its staffs are still the best you can find in Kathmandu! Breakfast was pretty good with many choices of Western, Asian and Nepali cuisines. Room rates are getting pretty expensive compared with other five star hotels in the area.

We were there on the day of earth quake and the staff and the whole team rendered very good support to the guests.It was a nightmare but we are able to reach safe and sound back to Delhi.Other wise also food was and services were good.There was only one small problem that was the key to the room would not work in one go , you need to swipe it many times to get in the room

O Hotel tem uma arquitetura linda, que acompanha os templos e palácios da Cidade, tem a vantagem de ficar perto do aeroporto e o quarto é amplo, confortável em um espaço que lembra um parque.o barulho da rua não chega ao hotel, mas tem um supermercado muito bom a poucos metros da entrada.O restaurante oferece uma comida bastante variada, com muitas opções vegetarianas e o café da manhã é um deleite.

O Hotel é bom. ouvimos falar que é o melhor da cidade, mas quanto a isso não tenho como opinar porque não conheci os outros. A arquitetura dele é incrível, muito bonita e detalhada, remetendo aos principais templos e pontos turísticos da cidade. O atendimento é muito bom, todos os funcionários atenciosos, simpáticos e tentam ajudar ao máximo quando possível, a exceção fica por conta dos funcionários da recepção que não conseguem ter o mesmo carisma e atenção dos demais, infelizmente. Os quartos são amplos e confortáveis, contudo um pouco antigos e mereciam uma reforma para deixa-los um pouco mais modernos e confortáveis. Mas no geral com certeza é um bom custo x benefício.

We spent one night here and were very pleased with the stay. The location near the Boudinath Stupa is amazing and the management staff were all very attentive. I couldn't give the place 5 stars as the rooms lacked charm (like dwarikas hotel) and were showing a bit of wear and tear. The sound proofing wasn't very good either as you could even hear your neighbors sneeze and cough. That being said the value for money is great and you will get to relax! A solid 4 star rating!

Peaceful, tranquil escape right in the middle of the city. I could feel the serenity the moment the vehicle turned into the compound. It felt like I was entering a palace with well-manicured gardens and attentive staff. The service was impeccable and the hotel was within walking distance from Boudhanath. We had a pleasant surprise when we returned to our room after dinner to see a birthday cake on the table. It was my friend's birthday that day! This really made our experience in Nepal all the more memorable. I am truly impressed!

Firstly I am a hyatt gold passport and this property is amazing value at 5000 points !!   Great location at bodhi Nath good selection of restaurants and ideally located for international airport Price is usually in the 150 range and great value especially when arriving or departing Nepal

the Sunday brunch is wonderful at basment restaurant. plenty of buffet option food and veeeeery delicious @ nrs 2000. start from 12noon. or menu option also available. and swimming is complimentry on Sunday brunch package. LOVELY

very nice place, one of the largest hotel properties i have seen anywhere in the world, courteous staff, Facilities were great. The Stupa is walkable from behind the hotel but this walk is not recommended after dark.

Beautiful landscaped property away from the noise of the city.   Private road leading up to the hotel.   No street noise at all.   Room and property were wonderful.   Live traditional music from a trio/quartet every nite in the lobby.   10 minute walk, 510m, on well marked route to the Great Boudha Stupa where you can also find a number of good restaurants.   If you go there at nite, bring a flashlight.   The route is not lit at all.   Noise is not an issue on either side of the hotel.  Left rear rooms have a better view - swimming pool, gardens, and the Stupa.  Not too much to see from front rooms.  We had a breakfast and a dinner here.  Both were quite good.   Highly recommend this hotel.

I stayed here for 3 nights in the club room. I was deciding between this and the dwarikas, but the rate I was getting on the club room swung it for me, and it didn't disappoint. I utilized the bus service which was only $9 and was almost like a private car , had a chap waiting for me with hyatt sign and a mini van to myself at the airport. I had lots of trouble with my luggage as they told me it would be on a later flight, but honestly the hotel took care of the whole ordeal, which was so comforting.I loved the VIP check in on the club floor and they even gave me a beautiful Stupa view room. The room was large, pool delightful and the restaurants were great too.It's set in such nice grounds, lovely and fresh, with old artifacts around the property and only 10 mins walk from the largest stupa in Nepal.Breakfast was a delight as were the 5-7 happy hour treats on the club floor.Only weakness would be the bathrooms could do with an upgrade and the concierge wasn't great on restaurant recommendations, but these are just minor.Highly recommend this , think it was great value and def worth going for the club floor.

This was my second visit after having stayed at Holiday inn I was looking for a more central location and closer to the airport. I am happy that I chose this property. The lobby of this hotel has replica of squares of a city. Awesome, coupled with live traditional music.. It is so serene that I spent 30 mins listening to the music and absorbing the positivity. The rooms are clean and upto mark as expected with the brand. However, I feel the bathrooms need up gradation and have more water saving equipment . The bar, lounge , restaurant all upto mark. I look forward to taking my family to this property .

Because of our occupation we stay at hotels all over the world, this is one of them, it has been longer, we were supposed to stay just two days but have been staying for a longer time, just would like to say, very nice and clean for the circumstances in Nepal, for staff they try to help you all the time, very good options for breakfast, but it was very big problem for us to find a smoking room, on the other hand wi-fi is very poor. Anyway very good for this area, there is also one temple very close, you could reach very easily and not far from "Thamel"

I was there about a month ago on an organised tour and this hotel was one of the best we stayed at.  I was actually not very well and the waiter noticed I hadn't finished my soup and asked if everything was all right.  When I told him I wasn't well he insisted I chose something different, some plain rice for example, and offered to have it sent to my room.  You couldn't ask for better/kinder service than that!  All the staff was helpful and friendly, the rooms first class and the food very good.

Superb hotel...great service outstanding food. The hotel was an pleasure so stay in in.The rooms were jaded and looked their age, and could do with an upgrade. They made up for it by providing great service, food and a smile.

Совершенно райское место.Восточное-азиатский колорит интерьеров в сочетании с дружелюбием персонала настраивают на тёплую и безопасную волну комфортного отдыха.Место - куда хочется вернуться.Особенно после недельной поездки по стране.

Estuvimos en Enero 2015 para nuestra luna de miel. Altamente recomendable por los servicios, instalaciones, los bonitos parajes que lo rodean y las vistas de la estupa de Boudhnath al atardecer. Cada tarde amenizaban la velada unos músicos nepalíes en el hall. La verdad es que parecía un oasis en medio del ajetreo del tráfico de la capital. Hotel muy recomendable

Un Oasis dentro del area, Hotel con unas instalaciones soberbias y lugar ideal para relajarse despues de el ajetreo diario, en un area tranquila y apacible, con muy buen restaurant y vistas agradables, vale realmente la pena, la atencion y confort de Hyatt se siente.el desayuno y cena buffet muy completo en todos sentidos, con la ventaja en el caso nuestro de poder escojer lo que comes ya que el tipo de cocina es diferente alo que estabamos acostumbrados

Given the paucity of good hotels in Kathmandu The Hyatt is a good option. The facilities are great and the service quiet good. The downside is that the hotel is located on the outskirts if the city hence away from the business district. The surrounding areas a quiet noisy hence sleeping at night is a problem.

Stayed in this lovely property during my first visit to Nepal for 5 Nights in November.The view from the room overlooking the mountains & lawn feels good still in my memory.The housekeeping department cleans the room on a daily basis and they are very friendly & they always greet us with a smile.The room was very comfortable in every way and had a good nap on arrival.Every meal served in the restaurant on the Ground Floor is good & tasty and I am sure they have one of their best chefs on earth.Climate is pretty chill in the evenings and we are sitting near the Pool Side.The hot starters along with Coffee & French fries are still in my memories, as my other colleagues are busy with their own drinks.I am an early bird and when I went for my early morning walking within the Hyatt property, I am amazed to note that the way the maintained such a huge property. Good work done by the Gardner's who take care of all the flowers and plants inside this property.You can easily reach most of the tourist attractions from this Hotel.I have visited Kathmandu many times after my first visit and stayed in almost all the hotels in the valley and I am sure Hyatt is the best and you are rest assured with their services.

搭乗予定の飛行機がフライトキャンセルとなり、航空会社の手配で利用することになりました。カトマンズでは色々なホテルを利用しましたが、間違いなく最上位のホテルの一つと思います。セキュリティーは万全で警備員も沢山いますが、エレベーターホールから客室エリアに入るためのドアがカードキーが無ければ開錠しないのですが、そのドアが開放されていることがあり、あまり意味が無い感じがしました。一番グレードの低い部屋でも十分な広さと高級感がありますが、窓枠には鳩が結構とまっており、少し興ざめしました。バックアップはされるのですが、停電もしばしばあります。テレビは日本の番組が一つだけありました。周囲から隔絶された感じのホテルですので、歩いて近くのレストランとか、ちょっと買い物しにいくというのは不便だと思いますが、喧騒とは無縁の落ち着けるホテルです。ロビーではネパール音楽の生演奏も楽しめます。

Visited here in January, and stayed for 4 nights from 24th to 28th Jan. It is an old property and looks old too. Not as well kept as one would expect Hyatt to be. The carpets in the room were soiled and the bed broken (Room#408). The service, room service to be precise, is one of the most un-prompt of any hotel I have been in a long time. There was a instance when the staff even forgot that I had asked for water and I had to go down to get it. No problem doing it, but then what is the fun of being in a place and paying so much when the basic facility of room service is non-existent.The buffet breakfast and lunch was good and the chef did a fabulous job. The service at the restaurant was good and having breakfast in the sun near the pool was surreal. Loved it.The property is located very near to Pashupatinath temple (NPR 250 in taxi and 10 in bus, your choice) and other places of interest like Thamel, foreign ministry office and other temples. Overall, a good stay.

O Hyatt Regency Kathmandu é um verdadeiro oásis em meio ao caos urbano de Catmandu. Trata-se de uma propriedade enorme e muito bem arquitetada, próximo ao aeroporto, em meio a jardins muito bem cuidados. O hotel tem um saguão muito bonito, com muitas obras de arte e, ao final da tarde, músicos nepaleses ficam tocando na área. Os quartos são simples - não suntuosos - mas muito limpos, aconchegantes, confortáveis. De um dos portões do hotel, pode-se ir a pé a uma das estupas mais importantes do mundo budista. E vale a caminhada. Mesmo sendo das opções mais caras da cidade, acredito que vale muito pelos serviços e por se tratar de hotel muito agradável.
建物も昔の建物を再現してネパールのホテルって感じで、作られておりとても素敵です。 ロビーも広くゆったりしています。お部屋も広く清潔です。お茶セット、ガウンもあり、お風呂も熱いお湯が出て、以外でした。敷地も広く､ゆっくりと庭を楽しみながら散歩できます。警備員も多く安心して滞在できます。
親切なスタッフに迎えられ、快適なひとときを過ごすことが出来ました。街の中心部へのシャトルバスや、空港へ送っていただけるバスもあり、とても助かりました。部屋からはボダナートと日の出を見ることができ、カトマンズにいることを実感できました。ルームサービスの朝食も美味しくいただき、大満足です。

The best choice to sleep in Kathmandu is this property. Located 15 mins away from the airport , this gigantic hotel property has a lot to offer. The staff is very kind and dedicated to the guests. The rooms are good and comfortable. The hotel has a nice pool area which is under maintenance right now. You can also enjoy the jogging track to walk around the hotel park as it is so big. My recommendation for the Hyatt is to enlarge the jogging track as I saw there's much more to walk around but it is not accesible. The hotel is also 5 mins walking from the bouddah pagoda so don't miss it!.

Отель Hyatt Regency в Непале, город Kathmandu - исключительное место! Прекрасный дизайн, просторные номера, хорошее обслуживание и вкусная кухня! Очень чистая территория, несмотря на то, что Катманду очень грязный город, попадая на территорию отеля как-будто  попадаешь в другой мир.   Очень понравился отель! Модно рекомендовать самым требовательным путешественникам.

I had booked three rooms at the Hyatt Kathmandu (Dec 24-28). Given that it's a Hyatt, I assumed (in hindsight, wrongly so) that the quality would be the same as I am accustomed to when I travel around the world. However, I was extremely disappointed with the hotel for a number of reasons:1) the property and the rooms are outdated.2) the heating units were not working and were either too hot or not working. We had to call maintenance a couple of times who tried to fix it. 3) In one of our buffet dinners (on Dec 25), I found a baby cockroach around one of the buffet tables. I pointed it out to one of the managers who grabbed it and threw it out.4) The bathroom sink did not dispense hot water. I had to call the front desk and manager and it got fixed for one day and then didn't work the next day onwards.5) the bathroom had several white/beige stains on the floor. I have taken pictures of this.6) The bathroom shower flooded and there was 3-4 inches of water on the floor after taking each shower. I notified the front desk who sent maintenance to fix it but to no avail. I asked several times to speak to the general manager but no one ever got back to me (The asst manager called me a couple of times but she couldn't offer anything and didn't really have the customer service skills).  That said, the best part of the hotel was the breakfast buffet. I had to call the hotel and get that added on my rate.Overall, we were (all 7 of us) very dissatisfied with the Hyatt Kathmandu, Hope the management team takes notice of these issues and fixes it asap, as it will likely affect the overall brand at some point.

Lovely hotel! A quiet setting in crazy Kathmandu. The grounds are well maintained and have many gardens. There is even a running trail within the hotel grounds.  Great breskfast buffet. Good location from which to see many of the sights of Kathmandu.  Walk to the Boudda stupa.

We stayed at the Hyatt Regency on two seperate occassions - both before and after our trek to Everest Base Camp - and each time was WONDERFUL.The ground of the hotel are immaculately maintained and are far larger than I could have imagined. In comparison to the noise and chaos of the streets of Kathmandu, this place is truly an oasis. The hotel itself is large and grand and the feeling of luxury greets you as soon as you step out of the car. The staff are professional, courteous and always willing to go the extra mile. Special mention to Shekhar - he went out of his way to ensure we had a magical stay (the chocolates were delicious!)The facilities of the Hyatt Regency are the best on offer. The Club Lounge, the dining and the spa are all worthy of mention. The rooms are spacious, clean and ever so comfortable. After our trek, we REALLY appreciated the strong water pressure in the shower and super deep baths ! If you are looking for 5-star in Kathmandu, look no further than the Hyatt Regency.

This is a beautiful hotel. The long sweeping drive way teases you as to what to expect. There are gardens all around and they are well loved and cared for. I was greeted with a friendly smile at reception and check in was smooth and efficient. The lobby has a large area for seating, large cushions for you to relax upon whilst you wait for you friends. The rooms have an extra bit of security as you cannot access the corridors without a pass key. Excellent for the single traveller.My room was clean and well appointed. A very large comfortable bed with crisp white sheets awaits the tired traveller. A modern TV with a multitude of channels and a desk from which to work from. The room could be bright with light or you can adjust it to give soft undertones.The bathroom, wow, it was as big as the bedroom. A large walk in shower to wash away the dust from the day. A full size bath to relax the ache and pains. Complimentary products were of good quality and plentiful. The rooms were quiet. Breakfast and dinner were great and would satisfy the fussiest of eaters. WiFi is not free.I used the hotel’s taxi which was efficient and clean.There is a swimming pool it looked beautiful and inviting.

Staff were very friendly and helpful when arranging outside tours.A few small gripes though that for the price of our room I found hair in the shower when we first arrived, so it had not been cleaned properly, and also the hair dryer in our room was not working.  I mentioned the hairdryer to a lady in reception the following morning but did not make a fuss.  We were out all day and got back late and sadly the next morning the hairdryer still did not work.Breakfast was very good quality and the location so close to the stoopa out the rear gate was super convenient.I find that after paying around $190 USD for a room you should not then be asked to pay another $10 a day for wifi when you can go to local restaurants and cafes and have it for free.We moved out for our last night and stayed somewhere else which although less luxurious, was much better value for money.

Vaste chambre club (peut être un peu impersonnelle) au 6e avec vue sur le parc et et stupa de Bodnath. Dîner et petit déjeuner délicieux. Personnel souriant et serviables.Par une petite porte au fond du parc, on peut se rendre très facilement à pied au stupa de Bodnath. C'est très agréable.vraiment un bon souvenir. A recommander.

Booked 2 rooms, a regular room and a club room. Upon check in, the front desk staff doesn't seem to be knowledgeable. And it seems that he used a different tone when talking to my boyfriend who is a local. The regular room and the club room is similar, nothing different at all. It only differs on the room benefits and wifi. Only club rooms have free wifi which can only connect 1 device. The breakfast at the club floor has nothing in it. But the evening cocktails has good food selections. Decent room size, huge bathroom but no bidet, air conditioning doesn't seem to work well, staffs are nice, the surroundings of the hotel is so beautiful and is more of a resort type. The only thing that annoyed me so much is the room key. You would need to swipe it a couple of times before the light turning green. Comparing this property to other Hyatt hotels, the rooms seem to be a little bit outdated. We ordered for room service and the fish and chips is really good, however, the pasta is really bland. Overall, it was a good stay. I just hope that next time the wifi should be complimentary since other hotels offer it for free.

My friend and I absolutely loved this hotel! Pros:• Luxurious and beautiful estate from the grand lobby, comfortable rooms, to the grand back garden area. Felt like a resort more than a hotel. • Very comfortable beds with clean sheets• Only a 5 min drive or 10-15 min walk to the main Stupa • Amazing breakfast buffet - and myriad of delicious choices from local cheeses (Himalayan French and Yak Cheeses, huge fruit and cereal tables, yoghurts, and pancake/waffle and egg stations. • Although the WiFi was chargeable- it was super fast and reliable! Cons:• No free WiFi- for such a nice and pricey hotel this should at least be included• Our room’s card and card machine were not working very well, we had to swipe each card at least 4 times before it turned green.

Nov 14, 2 stays, 3 nights in all.  Attractive design style reflecting traditional architecture of the region.   Excellent high specification facilities with largely well maintained and attractive grounds, gardens and pool.  Children's play area unkempt and overgrown, perhaps as out of season. Excellent breakfast and dinner buffets, with good variety of dishes and multiple courses.  Courteous, very helpful and friendly staff.Only significant flaw, an environmental issue.   Must be one of the biggest feral pigeon roosts on the Planet.   Vast areas of ledges on the outside of the building covered in pigeon droppings and  squabbling pigeons, especially as dusk approaches.  Aircon was fine and there was no need to open the bedroom windows.  Bedroom windows on the bedroom occupied on 3rd night very dirty and strike marked.    Pigeons are a cultural issue - Kama related - and not yet recognised in the whole Region as a potential "health hazard to humans".

Spent one night here two days ago to get cleaned up after 28 days camping trek round Kangchenjunga.Good points: huge clean bathroom, masses of hot HOT water!; quiet and secure locationNeeds improvement: staff attention at lunch by pool was very slow; breakfast croissants slightly stale, coffee somewhat weak, buffet lacked smoked fish; no soap in ladies toilet by restaurant (two days in a row)Seemed to lack much atmosphere - despite the awesome location so close to Boudhanath.I think I'm looking forward to more camping again!

We went during the peak season just before Dashain festival. Family trip with my 8 year old son. The hotel is located next to Boudhanath which is a leisurely walk from the place. Also opposite to the hotel is a mall from where amenities can be picked up. Hotel itself had an excellent buffet breakfast and two ery good dining options inside. Rooms are very good with top class amenities.

I stayed here in Nov. 2014 and loved it.  This is indeed a gem set in a large 40 acre or so walled area that provides a very quiet and secluded setting, yet only moments from the heart of chaotic and hectic Kathmandu.  It is a fairly short walk to the Boudhanath Stupa which I could see from my excellent room.  The hotel is a built like a palace on beautifully landscaped grounds with a lobby unlike any I've seen.  After a hectic day, I thoroughly enjoyed just walking around the property and finishing at the pool which is beautiful and serene - see my picture attached.  I had a deluxe room, which was huge with a great view of the Stupa and pool.  The restaurant was excellent with one of the best breakfast buffets I've experienced in a long while.  I also loved both bars - expecially the Rox Bar which was beautiful and huge.  I'm not sure why some reviewers found this hotel sub par to Hyatt standards.  I've stayed in Hyatt's everywhere, and find this hotel on par with any.  The staff was incredibly friendly and helpful and offered a cheery "Namaste".  They also exchange US Dollars at the front desk which eliminated the need to use ATM's for me.  I honestly can think of no negatives.  I highly recommend a stay here and you will be glad you did.

I love to travel and have been fortunate to do quite a bit in SE Asia.  This was my first time to Kathmandu and I'm so glad I chose the Hyatt Regency for my week stay.If you are someone who likes to travel in comfort and would like a Hyatt standard, I would strongly recommend this hotel.  Beautiful grounds and facilities.LOCATION:  Great location, that is away from the busyness of the city.  Although it conveniently located to the airport, major roads and Boudanath, it is really quiet and peaceful.  The only noise I heard at night was some dog barking non-stop, but that was nothing to do with the hotel.SERVICE:  Up to par with the Grand Hyatt standard.  I found that the Executive Lounge staff to be extremely helpful and friendly.  They took care of my requests, make recommendations and provided a lot of helpful information.ROOMS:  The 6th floor Executive Lounge rooms were great.  Ask for a Stupa facing view, as it is worth it.  The room is spacious, very clean, great A/C, with good amenities.  If you have a power adapter, I would suggest bringing one/few.  You can get them from the hotel (as I did), but many of them were broken or had loose connections.  I had to go through about 6 adapters before I found one that worked.  It is nice that the hotel has a sufficient and responsive back up generator.  In Nepal, power can go out for up to 12 hours a day.  At the Grand Hyatt, you will not notice this, as a power outage will last a few seconds before the generator kicks in.  The only issue I had with my room was the shower head.  The water flow was really back, but maintenance was quick to fix it.  Wifi was good - not great, as it was slow at times, but to be expected in NepalEXECUTIVE LOUNGE:  I would recommend getting a Club room.  It was nice to have beverages available all day and they did a great job with canapes during the evening.  Free wine/beer/drinks and well prepared appetizers.  They also do breakfast, but I chose to go down to the main restaurant.FOOD:  The buffet breakfast was great - good selection, quality foods, and wonderful service.  The only negative would be that when I dined outside, there was always someone smoking, which ruined the ambiance and quality of my experience.  I would suggest to the hotel that they have one side of the outdoor seating for smokers and one side for non-smokers.  That way everyone could be accommodated and enjoy their meal.I do have to commend that egg chef.  On many occasions at other 5 star Asian hotels, the buffet breakfasts are amazing, but they never get the eggs right.  The Grand Hyatt Kathmandu did a great job and had a good system - one individual (speaks perfect English) takes your order at the station and writes down the details on a check list.  He ensures that the order is cooked properly and then delivers to your table.  Great job!SITES:  If you walk out on level 1 behind the pool, the guard will unlock the back gate and you can turn left and follow that road to Boudanath.  It is maybe a 7-10 min, very easy walk.  I felt safe walking there on my own early in the morning or late at night.I also walked to Pashipatinath.  It is a bit farther (30 min), but got great directions from the hotel.  You only need to turn off the main road once.  The walk is very dusty, so make sure to take a scarf or something to cover your nose/mouth.The hotel has a free shuttle available for drop off about 6 times a day down to Thamel area, so I would recommend that and take a taxi back.I would highly recommend this hotel, especially for those who are accustomed to a high quality, Grand Hyatt product/service.  I used this as my little sanctuary after venturing out to see the wonderful sighs and people of Nepal.
広い敷地で、散歩にはいいです。セキュリティもしっかりしていて安心できました。食事はカレーが美味しかった。快適に過ごせました。スタッフの対応も問題ありませんでした。

I spent a total of 4 nigthts at this hotel at the start and end of a trekking trip with friends in the Langtang valley and we were very satisfied. The hotel grounds are beautifull and the size of the garden provides isolation and calm from the hutle and bustle of Kahmandu.The rooms are large, comfortable and tastefully decorated. The staff was very friendly and spared no effort in making our stay pleasant. The food was very good at both the main and Rox restaurants. I had two very relaxing massages at the spa which provided muc needed relief after 10 days of roughing it on the hiking trails.Having looked at some other hotels aroound the city, I doubt one can find better accomodation in Kathmandu and I will certainly return to the Hyatt on my next visit.

Hotel antigo de quartos amplos, alguns com direito à vista para o Boudhanath Stupa, o maior templo budista de Kathmandu, a poucos metros de distância. Piscina convidativa, serviço atencioso, boas instalações comuns, ótimo restaurante (sistema de bufê para as refeições principais). Destaque para o café da manhã, que é excelente. Bom spa e uma sala de ginástica bem montada. Contratamos também um tour por Kathmandu e arredores diretamente com a agência do hotel e tudo transcorreu muito bem. Ótima relação custo-benefício, com diárias baratas se comparadas a outros hotéis da rede.

Hidden behind a walled compound this hotel offers remarkable comfort and excellent service. Arriving weary after a trek and for a special anniversary celebration, the staff were welcoming and friendly. We were surprised with chocolates and a cake on arrival. It was worth paying a little extra to utilise the Hyatt Club as drinks and snacks were available and the food provided during  happy hour was delicious. The pool and surrounding grounds are grand and spacious. Breakfast was a feast though can get hectic at peak times. My only disappointment ( and I don't want to sound spoilt) was that the nail polish choices when having a pedicure was extremely limited and the polish did not seem to be of a high standard. Overall it was a wonderful stay that added to our wonderful trekking experience.

Stayed here on business for 4 days. I found the hotel to be well run, with gracious staff, and an excellent breakfast service.  Peaceful, quiet grounds located near the Boudhanath Stupa, the largest Tibetan Buddhist Temple in Nepal which is definitely worth seeing. Also boasts some shopping the the area surrounding the temple. Small downside is that it is located a bit away from downtown Kathmandu. However the Hyatt has a free shuttle to the Thamel and a cab ride back is not expensive, although some drivers are reluctant to take you that far after 8pm and you will have to haggle a bit.  There is an outdoor jogging track on the premises, a nice swimming pool and a fitness center.  Wireless service was reliable. I would stay there again.

The hotel definitely does not stand to its name.The staff seems to be too mismanaged or unorganized.I had done an advance payment for my guest and booked a room for them.The hotel did not acknowledge the confirmation no. which was issued by them.Sadly, the staff too some 45 minutes to fetch the refernce of the booking which was made.The reception staff was totally lost and unaware of hospitality and welcoming the guest.Hyatt should definitel start recruiting more professional and friendly staff at Kathmandu.

La llegada al Hotel Hyatt de Kathmandu, después de haber pasado 15 días en India, es una experiencia relajante, recomendable a todos los que deseen terminar sus vacaciones en un lugar bonito y  tranquilo que ofrece todas las prestaciones deseables en un hotel de 5 estrellas.Las habitaciones son grandes, con un inmenso cuarto de baño. La nuestra daba al jardín en un ala del edificio por lo que gozamos de un sueño reparador.Se puede pasear por los caminos, bañarse en  la piscina o simplemente sentarse en una de las mesas de las diferentes terrazas para  disfrutar de la vista y del silencio.Un gran lobby con toque nepalíes nos acoge. Al fondo, una cafetería con sillones que invitan al descanso. En ella sirven bocadillos y bebidas; con la consumición hay wifi gratis durante una hora. En la planta baja se encuentra  un restaurante que ofrece un buffet libre de calidad y unos desayunos muy correctos. En su otro restaurante, a la entrada del edificio principal se pueden comer buenas pizzas y algunos platos continentales (allí también wifi gratuito).El precio es caro para el país  pero correcto atendiendo a la categoría del establecimiento.El servicio es amable y profesional, aunque en ocasiones falla en el arreglo de las habitaciones. Algún día a primera hora de la tarde estaban todavía las camas y la limpieza por hacer.Resumiendo: Un magnífico hotel que no dudaría en recomendar

Hem yaz hemde kış kalınabilir .Güzel açık bir havuzu var .Mutfak harika .Odalar temiz ve harika .Şehir merkezinde olduğunda ulaşım için iyi .WİFİ var yalnız ücretli .Bu kadar artı içinde ücretli wifi can sıkıcı.

Stayed for a night before trekking upto annapurna. Had high expectations that it would be relaxing.I have sensitivities to smoke and requested for a non smoking room. But ofcourse getting into the room, there was a strong cigarette smoke smell. Everywhere, it seeps into the curtains and pillows. So they changed the room for us to the non smoking floor. Guess what ? It smelled of smoke even more. People smoke in the non smoking rooms, they declared. And if we would like to pay more, they can upgrade us to the executive floor !Considering it was just one night, we just stayed where we are. And ofcourse, a five star hotel did not include the wifi service in the room. 15$ more a day for wifi.

I would typically call a hotel like this a bit mediocre, but as the title says, well.. In fairness it is probably the single best hotel in the city. For a country with some of the most abject poverty in the world and virtually no actual infrastructure, the Hyatt here is superb. The lobby is delightfully decorated with classical Nepalese temples and a lovely ambiance. The pool, spa and gardens are easily the best. The staff at the pool are wonderfully friendly and attentive. The way the hotel designed the the gardens to go for walks is an amazing juxtaposition to the squalor and chaos of the city that is only feet away. It's superb! Now for the rooms, there is a lot left to be desired. The beds are rather uncomfortable and nothing that could be called remarkably cozy. Not awful, but hey, they could invest in much better beds and spruce up the rooms,along with many of the public areas. Yes, the hotel has a considerably tired and weary look and feel to it. Having said that, if you will be in the capital for any reason for any amount of time, please do stay here. Don't expect Four Seasons or Mandarin type accomadations, but for what the Nepalese government and economy has to offer, it is actually sort of perfect. Go for it but remember my cautions.

Hyatt Regency, Katmandu'da bir vaha. Katmandu'nun en iyi mimari ve peyzajına sahip modern yapısı. Otel Nepal ve Hint Mimarisine ait öğeler kullanılarak yapılmış. Ana yapılar ve detaylar hep geleneksel. Lobisi, odaları çok tarz. Otel içerisinde bir müze bulunması gibi özel bir durum var. Banyolar çok geniş. Küvet ve duş ayrı. İnternet ücretli. Yemekler üst kalite. Günlere ayrı yöresel yemekler sunuluyor. Havuz ve barı bir tatil köyünü aratmayacak kadar iyi. Olumsuz söyleyecek bir şeyle karşılaşmadım. Otel Katmandu için bir artı değer.

We got an upgrade to the high floor and can view the Stupa from our room. The hotel compound is huge and it will be some walking from its main entrance until we reach lobby. This huge compound provide additional benefit - away from the noisy and dusty Kathmandu city. It is peaceful and silent here, we are completely isolated from Kathmandu noise. The art inside the hotel mimic ancient Kathmandu decor, the carving, the statue, definitely ensure it is unmistakably Kathmandu. A wonderful place to stay.  https://vinshengloh.exposure.co/chinese-new-year-nepal

On arriving at the Hyatt we were warmly welcomed and invited to an upgrade.  Although it was an extra cost, both my wife and I felt that this was sincerely offered and decided to go with it.  It was a time to integrate all we had experienced since arriving in Nepal.Boy are we glad.  from the room looking over the Boudhanath, the spa facilities, sumptuous breakfast and wonderful poolside it is more than we could have hoped for.However this was just a bit of the experience that made it was wonderful.  Each evening there was the evening happy hour on the 6th floor.  The food, beverages are incredible.But again that is just the small part.  the defining moment is the staff.  Their complete attention to detail and being of service truly humbled me, in a way of upliftment.The first evening being my birthday a cake arrived unexpected, and each evening we were so looked after.  in particular Denish and Bhishma (from the 6th floor) exemplified all that the Hyatt has come to mean to us.An Oasis for the heart.  A place which we will warmly remember.  a place that rested and nourished our bodies and soul, as we prepare for the next part of our journey with our friends in Bhaktapur.Thank you for touching all that is good within us and we hope those we met in some way remember us as fondly as we will them.

Stayed at this hotel before and after 10 days working in Chitwan, very quiet, very calm in the middle of noisy and dusty Kathmandu.  Breastfast was great with plenty choices and included in the price.  Lunch and dinner also were decent with variety of foods.  Services were also very good especially at the restaurants and bar.  It was such a treat to return for the stay after a long week working in Chitwan, the spacious bathroom was such a nice luxury, will highly recommend the Hyatt for a nice stay after working or after a long trek.

The hotel is a lush, green retreat from a dusty, chaotic city.  I looked forward to going back to the hotel every day after sightseeing. From the back gate, it is only a 10 to 15 minute walk to Bouddanath.The hotel was probably built in the 80s, but well-maintained. The lobby is amazing and the rooms clean and comfortable.  The compound is green and nicely manicured. The pool is a godsend and the small but well-equipped gym, the icing on the cake.  I cannot imagine not having the pool after a day outside under the hot sun.We had meals at The Cafe and Rox Restaurant and the food was very good.  All staff in the hotel, from reception to the restaurants, were excellent.  They were always polite and welcoming.  Biyunath ( I hope I spelt her name correctly), who welcomed us at the Front Desk, also dropped by occasionally to ask if our stay was comfortable.  What an exemplary staff member! We asked for the hotel limousine to take us to the airport and instead of just sending a driver, they arranged for another staff member to sit in with us too.  5-Star service all the way!The only part I found a bit unnerving was the large number of security personnel in the hotel.  At the entrance to the compound, there were at least a dozen security officers in army-like uniform.  Once you get in, there are a few more security personnel walking the grounds.  I'm not sure why security was so tight and wasn't sure if I should feel protected or targeted.

Probably you don't have to expect too much in Kathmandu, however I do expect better from Hyatt.The Hotel is quite old. The room is large but outdated. The TV channel choice is really poor and mostly there are indian programs. The shower handle is old and it's fixed to the wall, not comfortable. The internet signal was very low and cannot even stream properly from youtube. Again, maybe this is good enough for Nepal but I want to express my experience. The swimming pool is very nice, as well as the a la carte food at the restaurant. I had a very good and tender beef.The breakfast is good at the main breakfast area but poor at the club lounge. The coffee is really the worst part. It is undrinkable and the cappuccino was prepared very badly. The milk stinks.If you need a good coffee, better to go to the city center. The location is really close to the airport and the staff is really friendly and helpful.

It used to be that the Yak & Yeti was as good as it gets in Kathmandu.  Compared to sleeping in tents on a glacier at Everest Base Camp, it was good enough.  Then came the Hyatt Regency, and that raised the game considerably.  First of all, it's beautiful and well-serviced.  It's not in the heart of a shopping district like the Y&Y, but nonetheless is in close proximity to a Buddhist shrine and local shopping, and there are taxis everywhere to take you where you want to go.  If I ever return, I'll definitely stay here.

Room: The room was very clean, if a bit standard.  The bed was comfortable, and the bathroom had a separate shower and tub.  Honestly, not much to speak of, but nice and comfortable.Of note too, was the hotel pool(s).  Relaxing in the pool (hot tub or the normal pool), after a long day of exploring the streets of Kathmandu is a real treat.Location: I found the location quite good, but it may depend upon your interests or itinerary.  It is only a few minutes walk from the excellent Boudhanath stupa; in between, there are many shops and restaurants (and money changers, with better rates than those in Durbar Square or Thamel areas).  Across the street is a handy grocery store (which is attached to a complex with a stores selling all manner of fake clothes and bootleg CDs / DVDs).Service: The front desk and room service (which was good and relatively cheap) agents were routinely excellent.  The hotel offers a free shuttle service into town (not to or from the airport, however), which was extremely handy for tourists.Value:  For 5K Hyatt points per night, this hotel was a very good value.

This place is the only part of Kathmandu where you could roam around without a face mask.A beautiful building with all expected amenities and good food and that to in heart of city.This is one of the clearly visible spaces from flight, so you could easily guess it's decent size.Staff is really supportive. I find this place as one good reason to visit Kathmandu again.

I wished there was a way to give this hotel a rating of 4 and a half out of 5! I stayed here with my girlfriend for a weekend getaway of lazing by the pool and walking around the stupa. The check-in was not as smooth as could have been. But, luckily for us a young lady called Bidhya was there to save the day, she was very good at satisfying our requirements and after about 45 minutes we were finally in our room with our luggage. The quality of sleep here is almost excellent, shame about the thousands of pigeons that flock here every single evening. Even though they do stop cooeing towards 9 - 10pm. But, the mess they leave behind! The breakfast is very good and there is a good mix of food to satisfy most palettes. The knock by house keeping on our door at 9.30 am  was very annoying, asking us if they could clean our room!!! Never have i experienced that in a '5' star hotel, this is Nepal after all!! I shouted no from inside the room and they eventually came to make the bed later that afternoon. The pool facilities are excellent and it is a day well spent if thats what you like. Even though some of the prices are somewhat steep for what you get.... All in all a great stay and will be back in the future for a swim and maybe even an overnight stay. Highly recommended hotel in Kathmandu!

We stayed at the Hyatt for 3 nights  and totally enjoyed the stay.the rooms were very comfortable ,good service with pleasing manners.Wevisited the Pashupati temple besided the market place.It is ideal for shopping of Pasmina shawls,sweaters .

Stayed here with family. While we went for the casino, unfortunately all casinos were shut at that time.  Positives - - Huge property - more like a resort - with tennis courts, gym and a big swimming pool (including a very small heated pool)- Very well maintained gardens and friendly staff- Breakfast spread is also quite good- Great price for a 5 star- They serve sisha on a terrace with a view of the mountainsNegatives- While located close to the airport, it about 30 mins from the city center - Rooms were slightly worn down due to usage

La verdad que impresiona el edificio, la entrada al hotel después de las barreras de seguridad y el hall. Elservicio excelente y las habitaciones amplias y con vistas muy buenas. Nos hemos hospedado en tres habitaciones distintas por los traslados a Buthan y todas igual de buenas. El desayuno en el hotel mágnifico. Todo muy bueno. Sólo una pega que con lo que cuesta el hotel la wifi no sea gratis. De todas maneras aconsejable.

The Hyatt Regency in Kathmandu is typical of high-end hotels in crowded cities in Southwest Asia.  The hotel is located in a green oasis in the center of otherwise urban area.  I found the gym adequate and the bar above average.  Numerous restaurant options, a spa, and tight security make this hotel an easy choice for business travelers.  The rooms are spacious and clean, if a little dated.This hotel compares unfavorably to other hotels in the region I've stayed at recently, most notably the Radisson Bleu in Dhaka.

This hotel is beautiful and is extremely well appointed. It has it's own private grounds which are like an oasis from the hustle, bustle, smell and dirt, that is Kathmandu. It has great restaurants and bars and the executive level lounge is outstanding.  Food was always plentiful. The staff constantly strived to please.Unfortunately many of the people at our conference became ill and we then discovered that the seals were broken on the water bottles, leaving them suspect for being refilled with local water.
