The Malla Hotel is well-located, being 30min (or less!) from the airport and walking distance from various attractions. I particularly appreciated the attentive service from the staff at the health club. It's not set up as a health resort, of course, but having yoga and aryuveda treatments available on top of the gym and pool helped me to make the business trip more comfortable. The rooms are a little dated, but all the necessary are there.

Very kind hospitality. Very accommodating. Nice to have the option to get coffee to order included in breakfast as well as breakfast to go for the morning we had to leave before breakfast opened. It was also a pretty quick trip to and from the airport.

The service and food are quite good. The staff are very humble and cooperative. The other facilities invluding playing Table Tenis, gym, spa are added advantages with complementary packages. Specially the food is very delicious. Good place to be with family.

We had a fabulous afternoon/evening dinner at the hotel, outside in the courtyard with its beautiful rose garden ambiance. The food was first-rate, delicious, with perfect portions. Service was over-the-top special— Subina made things flow so smoothly while a large wedding and other guests were also served. A very enjoyable evening, and we will certainly be back.

This was my first hotel stay in Nepal during an introductory tour. I stayed initially for 2 nights and the staff were amazing and friendly whilst the rooms were clean and spacious. There is a pool and spa (spa treatments here were best we had on trip). We only had breakfast and drinks in the hotel - both were delivered with smiles in a relaxed and beau environment.

Food was well served and prepared, the service was with much care and love !! You should definitely consider Malla Hotel and bring your friends and family if the rate of the hotel is appropriate for your budget. They even gave us a surprise for our honeymoon with a cake and our queen size bed decorated by roses and artisan towels!!

I stayed at the Malla Hotel as part of a group tour. The rooms were clean and spacious with two large bottles of water and a fruit basket in the room. Breakfast was plentiful with a good variety of foods. The hotel does have a pool. It was very clean but I did not try it so cannot comment on warmth. The location was great with easy walking to shopping, atms and restaurants. I would stay here again

I had the most WONDERFUL STAY of my life at Malla Hotel. I was left feeling incredibly well looked after by Shambhu and Jeevan at the restaurant!!  We had a wonderful conversation where I learnt so much about the history of the hotel and Shambhu and Jeevan were so professional and told me wonderful stories of the mountains and culture!!

The Hotel is maintained really with its good environment. The staffs are really friendly and they rendered an excellent service. They are so helpful. The rooms are clean and daily it was cleaned. Enjoyed the tasty food. Specially the receptionist (I think), Ajina helped a lot in the need of investigations and suggestions about the places in Nepal. I felt grateful.

Great location with exceptional service by all the staff.No.1 place to stay in Kathmandu …………..Good selection for breakfast and Nice seating areas in and outside hotel…………..Many restaurants located close to hotel Garden of dreams just around the corner

Front of office Shenaz and Bawana were amazing well trained in handling crisis and assuaring the guest safety & security. Was a remarkable experience. Wish them a successful career. Suraz i a trainee at the front desk in on the correct track to mention

The entire staff team was so kind and supporting. I would specifically thank the following staff members, Riya Shakya and Akriti for their excellent customer service support whenever requested.It was indeed a beautiful experience staying at the Malla Hotel. Thanks.

Its was great to observed the service of malla hotel. The dinner was western ,friends does not like but i like it. Hope according to maxi. Costumer nepalese its better suggestion to put indian or nepali dish. BBQ was not so satisfaction as need to wait along and some buffet were empty. Please need to monitor on that issue. Other thing is great.Hope to get back soon.

Kathmandu is a busy city and Malla Hotel is a great spot to get away from the chaos. This is certainly where I would stay again if I was in the area. Very nice staff, enjoyable breakfast, and nice shared spaces such as the garden, pool, and bar.

Lovely hotel with great green spaces and pool. The rooms were very comfortable, with a separate tub in the bathroom. The staff were very attentive and friendly, especially Agira who helped us book a taxi. Would stay here again if I returned to Nepal and would recommend to a friend!

We stayed three nights at The Malla and it was great!  Check in was super fast and easy. Rajita was soo helpful and pleasant!Rooms are large and very clean. We had breakfast every morning and they had a nice selection at the buffet plus omelets, etc.  Location is great for walking to all kinds of shops, etc.Totally recommend The Malla!

Thanks Mr.Upendra Nepali and his team...............................i was visiting at The Malla Hotel,i meet again Mr.Upendra Nepali,as i had already expereinced his serivce,this time again i got a chance to to meet him an get his service,he is very friendly,all the smiles,and very generous to support the customers.service was excelelnt,food were really good.though he is a manager,he does everything to support the guest,coffee were really good and best.thanks again to Mr.Upendra Nepalinext time i come back to Neapal,i will surely stay the Malla Hotel,really a great hotel.

Really enjoyed the property, very comfortable stay. The staff is really very helpful. Big shoutout to Madam Saru from the management team for helping us and guiding us throughout. Best part is that it is close to Thamel market area and we get better connectivity. 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟

Quite excellent more specifically the BBQ, the buffet dinner and buffet breakfast. All was elegant and of high quality. Swimming pool benefit and foot massage were great. Room and amenities was also very good. Only feedback is to provide extra bed to child as I paid extra for that. I rate 9.5 out of 10.

Excellent from the first moment I arrived.  Staff were exceptionally friendly, professional and customer focussed.  My room was spacious and very comfortable with everything I needed.  A wonderful stay in an interesting city in Nepal - a beautiful country with beautiful people.  THANKYOU

Close to Thamel. Clean and neat nice room, building is nice.  Easy to park so good for pick up.Can stay calm cozy quiet.  Nice staffs, beautiful garden. Recommend! Small shop nearby and lots of place to eat.Spa was also nice.

I'm stay few time in this hotel,hotel  location is nearby Thamel street convenient for shopping and meeting with friends.Room is clean, value for money, staf is friendly and helpful. Have a nice garden for breakfast, room facilities is good

Well appointed hotel in a great location- walking distance from the bustling  Thamel area- Darbar Square, Palace Museum, Garden of Dreams etc. Attentive and helpful staff.  They have a small gym and a pool. The garden is well tended and makes for a nice seating.  There is also a hotel bar that is well equipped.

Great hospitality and good breakfast and room was very comfortable. The garden makes the overall ambiance very fresh and nice! Shout out to Subina, very friendly and helpful hotel staff :) hope to see you again in the future. Making our Kathmandu experience better!

I'm very satisfied with the service. The food was also delicious. Great Masala tea. Perfect localisations in the centre of Thamel, tourist district of Kathmandu. Hope to visit this hotel next time in Kathmandu!

this hotel is one of the most beautiful hotel ,as we had stayed .it's garden,is so precious,pool is so beautiful with garden,with spa,and beauty parlor within the pool .rooms are cleaned and and well maintained ,by the house keeping staffs.all the service staffs are so friendly,caring and welcoming.thanks for Mr.Upendra and his team ,for providing such a memorable stay at the Malla Hotel.service staffs are willing to provide us anything this is possible ,be it in rooms,or in the garden,Malina she is a good host,as we experienced ,over all really wonderful experience for us during our stay,thanks to all the staffs of the hotel.every one most visit to the hotel.

We have so excitement to live in Hotel Malla, specially hospitality of Swastika, Suroj, Riya, Chandra, the receptionist. We enjoyed too much foods. Thank you so much Hotel Malla othoraty to collaborate these amazing people to serve us. A lot of loves for you. 💝💖

Very good nice hotel. Very good employee.  Nice hospitality.  Good garden.  Swimming pool.  Front desk sfatff and guest relations officer are good.  Very good location closed to Thamel and Narayanhiti historical palace.

Great hotel! Friendly staff. Nice amenities. Make sure to take advantage  of the complementary foot massage. The pool is very relaxing. Beds are very comfortable. Nice break from the busyness of Kathmandu.

Beautiful hotel and excellent service, especially at the front desk. Pradip and Madhur were so helpful and always ready to accommodate our requests. The rooms are clean, spacious and the pool area is tranquil and relaxing. Would definitely stay here again.

Really nice place with very nice people we really enjoyed out time here. The reception lady  Miss Rajita and Suroj   were really nice and help us with all the thinks we wanted to do.We recomend this place 100%

Staying in this hotel was one awesome experience, the architecture, Services, and food is so so so good.Thou the hotel is getting new face lift, none of the In house guest got disturbed, I wonder how they do that.I will be back again soon.

Environment is peace and beautiful as well as well neat .Rooms services are better . But need improved in bathroom, and outer entrance surface..lobby area is so good.gardening is nice.lift has some noise problems.at the summary hotel is perfect in every aspect.

It's quite a great experience staying at Malla Hotel. The friendly and amicable behaviour of Rajita shrestha, Monika & Ajina have been very impressive. The room service has also been pretty satisfactory. I will definitely recommend guests to stay here.

It was great stay at the Malla Hotel. Wonderful staffs, great services, poolside very good, spa service was fantastic, food and drinks, cocktails were really nice, good. receptionist was really nice and did a good job on our arrivals.Waiter and Waitress did a wonderful service too us.they often came a spoke to us.Subina and Mr. Upendra did a good service to us. they kept asking if we need anything more, with a good smile.thank you, Mr. Upendra, for a great hospitality during our stay.we will definitely come back again.

Subina served me in the garden and she was so lovely! Service was excellent, and the ambiance perfect. I had a nice tea with music and I really enjoyed my experience - can’t wait to come back. I would recommend an Al fresco experience in the garden.

It was a pleasant stay here at malla hotel. Front office team was way to flexiable and co-operative. I would like to thank all the hotel staff and managing team for providing us a beautiful stay! Special thanks to ms monika and mr suroj and whole front office team.

The hotel is very beautiful , i like garden  very much . All the staff are friendly . Especially thank u Ms. Rajita for awesome servives and provided information  about tourists area .we like to recommend this hotel  to our relatives and friends 🧡  we enjoy  our stay . Thank you.

The entire complex is clean, staff are courteous, food is freer and wifi is ok. Will recommend to friends and colleagues. Will be back again. Everything is great except this trip advisor review forcing me to write 200 characters

I had a great time during my stay at The Malla Hotel. Ms. Rajita Shrestha from reception was wonderful. She was very friendly, helpful and welcoming. Room was spacious and hotel property has a big garden in middle of bustling Kathmandu.

things are excellent i love the way they treat us .the hospitality was memorable. i like the pleasant and cozy environment the the hotel provided. its serene and wonderful experience in these three days of stay. the way they teat us is like a homely environment. and the all staff were welcomng and supportive. the food ia great and the pool area is so fascinating. the service withe the people who helped was memorable.

Ajina monika pradip best service provide by them ...prompt service.. all staff are cooperate  .Food and  the customer  was amazing. I most say the  front office staffs are amazing.  I would recommend hotel to everyone. Really appreciated all the services provided by hotel.

Very comfortable hotel with great amenities. Relaxing foot massage by the pool and great morning yoga class. Breakfast is delicious. Staff is friendly and accommodating. Nice hotel to stay at after trekking.

The malla hotel has the excellent  service  from room to food  and spa. I had good welcoming  and nice spa at wellness.  I specially  thanks to Mr Madhur, Tufan and Ms Shahnez for grat welcoming.  I recommend  everyone  to visit.

Very beautiful hotel with good ambiance and staff. Good is really good and awesome. My special thanks to Rajita and Swastika for making the stay beautiful. Such nice staff with so beautiful and warm welcoming behaviour. It's worth staying here everytime.

Beautiful hotel. Very clean. Comfortable beds. Good food. The staff was very helpful and welcoming.  I took a yoga class in the spa that was first rate!  My only issue was that the toilet did not always completely flush, which overall was just a minor irritation.

Excellent hotel, nice grounds. Close to all the little touristy shops etc in Thamel. Beds were comfortable. Workers were really pleasant. Food in restaurant was good. Breakfast buffet is okay, but worth getting.

The Malla Hotel is named after the Malla Kings of Nepal. It is an Old hotel. We stayed in Room number 514 for two nights and 208 for one night. 514 was better than 208. The furniture and toilet fittings were old. For a 4 star hotel they do not have exhaust fans in the toilets, No tea making facilities in the room and no FREE Wifi (you have to pay to obtain password for on an hourly basis). You will only get complementary water on the first day and after that you will be required to pay.For a country with cool climate most of the year they do not have heating facilities but on the second day without request they provided an electrical heater but the trip started to go off due to high capacity (the hotel was on generate during time as there was power cut). Pool and SPA - They have a nice pool and Spa facilities. The Hotel provides you with a wide range of TV channels including STAR channels. The staffs are friendly and polite. If you rise complain they will address it immediately with the available resources. Toilets were equipped with average bathtubs. Food - We had 2 Dinners and three breakfasts, was very good specially the vegetarian food and the Masala Tea. Breakfast will cost around USD 8-12 and Dinner USD 18-20. Location – It is situated about 15-20 minutes drive from the airport and situated near Thamel (prominent shopping area).After seeing the reviews on TripAdvisor we requested our travel agent Eco Trek to change the hotel but the alternative they proposed was even worse than Malla so we fixed Malla.

We stayed at the Malla at the beginning and end of our trekking trip to EBC. While the reports are mixed, it was good to arrive after over 24 hours of travel to a reasonably sized room, with a decent en-suite (with a very powerful shower)  and a large comfortable bed. While the decor is a bit tired, remember that you're in Nepal and by the standards of the country, it is a more than adequate place to stay.The breakfasts were good, as was the one lunch that we had there. The dinners were also acceptable, both in terms of the quality and quantity of the foodThe staff, and it is a very well staffed hotel, were courteous, friendly and helpful.The gardens were a wonderfully peaceful place to while away a few hours, especially after the hustle, bustle, noise and fumes of Thamel.In summary, it is difficult to be too critical of the Malla and I do think that some other reviewers perhaps judge it too harshly.I would be happy enough to stay there in the event of returning to Kathmandu and indeed after two weeks walking in the Khumbu, we were delighted to get back to the hotel, the luxury of which we truly appreciated. I have only one significant complaint - the price of a pot of tea for two - over £3 (sterling equivalent) was unduly steep.

Our company recently went on a trip to Nepal and the 14 of us stayed at Malla hotel, in Thamel.  We spent 3 nights there, and whilst it was comfortable I felt the price was a bit high for what you get.  Thankfully it was clean and the breakfast was pleasant, but it's fairly dated and could use a few small improvements.  The best thing about the hotel is the location, it's very easy to walk into Thamel which is the more touristy area with many nice restaurants and shopping opportunities.  It's also across the road from The Ship restaurant which offers free wifi, delicious Momo's and very friendly service.

Malla Hotel hasn't forgotten its heyday in the 60s. It's warmly preserved across the Hotel, with aged furniture and utilities, slow and unresponsive staff etc. All of this would have been bearable if Malla Hotel had woken up, smelt the coffee and realised that its nowhere close to being a 3-star hotel, let alone a self-proclaimed 5-star hotel. The prices it charges are still based on 5-star land, with a ludicrous NPR200 for a Coke to NPR 180 PER HOUR for WiFi. The latter is mind-boggling honestly. Stay far away from this hotel if you can. The only redeeming feature it has is a very nice garden, which is a soothing change from the warren that is Thamel next door.

5***** hotel? This has to be a joke...... Stay away.... Lots of better hotels in Kathmandu When I think about this hotel I see one thing "Too many chiefs and not enough Indians. I have never seen so many managers as in this hotel. But one of the managers will take his responsibility. Each one of the managers said the other one should have done it. I send about 30 emails to this hotel to ask for a peaceful room (because our son died a few month ago from cancer) I didn't receive an answer to anyone of the mails. Our travel agent booked us anyway in This hotel and told us it was a very good 5***** hotel. We got a room on the 4th floor a deluxe room (which we paid for) . The room had a king size bed (which was very good and clean) The Pc did not work. Mini bar did not work. The central air conditioning was set at 24° ,with was way to warm. The bad room was not big and the door to get into it was only 0,60cm wide . The room had a view on the garden with was really nice.(The thing that we did not know was that on this side they were going to have a New year party for everyone from outside the hotel.) The other rooms on the side from the swimming pool were the same rooms but did not have the noise from the party.( I know because my wife went and slept in the lobby on the fourth floor on the side of the swimming pool. (I finally got to sleep around 2.30. The breakfast was in buffet and was very poor (2 water fruit juices) ,one kind of bread,one kind of fresh fruit ,eggs, I didn't see any Bacon..We had to keep asking for coffeeThe buffet for diner was also very poor. We did eat two times diner a la carte which was good. It hotel has a nice reception ( too bad a about the many managers that did not help) 4th and 5th floors are nice. The rest from it hotel is dirty. A Swimming pool that is dirty and outdate. Garden furniture that is falling apart. See Pictures So if this is a 5***** hotel ??I think it should be among the 10 worst 5 ***** hotels in the world

Stayed here before and after our epic trip to Everest Base Camp last November. On the way there it was to prepare our selves and do a bit of sight seeing, in fact we saw David Beckham! On the way back it was the scene of a first bath in 3 weeks!Kathmandu is an amazing city, the Malla is sort of colonial style meets slightly neglected but OK. Having said that, they are really up against it, its a very poor city with many limitations that we just cant imagine in GB. After all you go the Nepal for the mountains not the hotels!. Hotel staff and Nepalese people always very friendly.

This hotel could be really good with a bit of care and attention to basic maintenance, a lick of paint and staff trained and supervised to housekeep to a high standard.Staff generally good and quite attentive. Tried to buy a coffee in the Terrace Coffee Bar but it was obviously too difficult for the young man busy on a telephone, so I wandered elsewhere. We enjoyed our meals having been out in the countryside for some days.The gardens are lovely, it is quiet, property has an outdoor pool and a spa and sauna. Would go back if it was spruced up. We were in 406.

We stayed in 3 different rooms over 3 weeks, 227, 311 and 315, whilst using it as a base in Katmandu. It reminds me of an old colonial hotel that has seen better days, it is in an excellent postion, close to the Thamal district, the Palace and various other attractions which can be reached by suzuki taxi for around 3-500 rupees. We were there with Community Action Treks, so didn't have a breakdown of prices, but the location does enable you to get away from the noise and dust of katmandu. The rooms we had all had hard floors, were clean and looked as if they had been updated fairly recently. My only gripe was that the pillows are hard. The showers in all rooms were powerful with plenty of hot water. Yes the bathrooms are dated, and we had a mix of towel combinations on our various visits, but the staff were very helpful, friendly and looked after us really well. Breakfast was buffet style with eggs cooked at the buffet to your requirements. We had no preconceived ideas so weren't let down. We used the spa and had a massage after the trek, which were both reasonable.

We stayed at the Malla Hotel before and after our trek to Upper Dolpo.  It was well located with easy walking access to shops and restaurants.The hotel lobby had been remodeled and was nice and fresh.  The ground are beautiful and a wonderful place to sit and escape the hectic streets of Kathmandu.The pool is also lovely.I know that they are working to remodel the rooms.  We were there in September and the rooms we stayed in could definitely use a bit of paint and updating.Everything was very clean and the staff was very responsive.We left our extra luggage there and then picked it up when we returned for our post trip stay.If they update the rooms as they have updated the lobby and common areas it would get an excellent rating.

Our flight was cancelled so we were put up in this hotel. The Hotel was significantly better than the hotels/ tea houses we had been staying in. It was super clean and the food was great.Unfortunately we didn't have swim wear with us- as my friend and I were really keen to swim- when you've spent the best part of 7 hrs sat on a plane not moving, and nearlt 12hrs at a stressful airport this would have been great. The Staff were very sympathetic and gave us a lot more information than we had received from our airline. A buffet dinner had been put on for us- there was a wide variety of very fresh food both veggie and meat options- super tasty and the staff couldn't have been more helpful.Each room had it's own wifi router, so the wifi is very fast. There was sky TV, we did have a problem getting the TV to work, but were sent a engineer to sort it out.Overall we were really impressed with how well we were looked after, despite having no info from the airline.

Excellent staff and accommodation in this high quality hotel within 30 - 40 minutes walk of Durbar Square.The food was very good and reasonably priced, and it was nice to return to the hotel and relax in the gardens.We were kindly allowed to retain a room beyond checkout for our luggage and a pre-flight shower

Für Kathmandu natürlich schon gehobenes Niveau; man bemüht sich zumindest. Der weitläufige Park/Garten und der Barbereich sind auch ok, schon bei den Zimmern merkt man aber dann, dass dies zwar gehobener Standard sein soll, es aber gemessen an europäischen Standards nicht ist. Ich schreibe dies nur, weil die Preise sehr wohl europäisches Niveau haben. Das Hotel ist richtig teuer! Trotzdem: Was soll's, man ist halt in Nepal. WLAN ist in vielen kleinen Restaurants und Kneipen in Kathmandu kostenlos, in diesem Hotel ist es zeitlich beschränkt und kostet Geld, klar, gehobener Standard halt ;) Die Angestellten sind sehr freundlich, aber natürlich im Grunde alles sehr oberflächlich. Insbesondere im Frühstücksraum wirkt es oft nicht wirklich organisiert, obwohl da oft viele Leute mit schicken Uniformen herumstehen.

I was moved from another property to this hotel as an upgrade. The room and bed were comfortable but I got the impression that I was a nuisance rather than a guest. They do seem to be stuck in the past when service was not expected to be high! I agree very much with another review that notes that there are too many managers and not enough workers!

I stayed only for one night. The room was ok and the amenities were good. I needed to change some UAE Dirhams in the evening but they said it will be possible only the next morning. The next morning a manager type in reception refused to change UAE currency. I had to scramble in a taxi to find a money changer that was open that early in the morning. Accurate information is a must, specially to overseas visitors.

This felt like a hotel in old worlde Britsh Raj days, very grandly decorated! We stayed in this hotel with my family, my husband and I in one room, and my teenage boys in an adjacent room. The rooms were comfortable though dated and in need of maintenance, but I suspect luxurious for this part of the world.We had breakfast every day (included  in the package) and the staff knew our regular breakfast orders every morning! We had dinner twice in the restaurant, the a la cart is much better than the buffet which was a little average. The staff are super friendly and eager to assist and were never far away to refill your tea or bring you more bread or open the door for you with a salute! Lovely cocktail bar overlooking superb and well kept gardens. A welcome respite from the hustle and bustle and hurley burley of Kathmandu street life just outside the door!

Really kind and considerate staff. Kerma, Suraj and many others were so helpful and friendly. The hotel is clean and updated, the food is good, but the standout staff really  make the stay special. The only thing I wished for was the ability to buy small snacks or convenience items like pretzels, juice, paracetamol etc at the front desk - would be nice to have.

I am very satisfied with the stay whenever I come here I will advise my friends that this hotel is best and Shehnaz sheikh in the reception was amazing to assist us about any problem amazing hotel good ambience and breakfast and rooms

The service was excellent, the behavior of employees particularly Shenaz Sheikh. They responded in all our questions and support during our stayed. The breakfast was awesome and the environment was excellent.

Otel güzel çalışanları çok zarif girer girmez boynuma hediye fularlar taktilar yorgunum diye odamı hemen hazırladılar .. odaları temiz güzel geniş geniş bir bahçeye bakıyor.. düğüne bile katıldım :) hiç bir sorun yaşamadım güvenliGüzel bir otel ..

Coming from some very simple hotels in China and Tibet, the Malla felt like a luxurious place with its large rooms and lobby, and its nice garden with pool and available massage services. Premises were clean, beds were comfortable, staff was super helpful, TV had many international channels, and breakfast was varied and plentiful. Its situation is great, on the rim of the Thamel old quarter, with its many shops and restaurants, and also pretty close to Durbar square. Definitely a good choice.

Estuvimos 4 noches. Hotel a 5 min de la zona de tiendas de Thamel! El hotel nos gusto! Buen servicio, habitaciones amplias y limpias con vistas a un precioso jardín! Los desayunos estaban muy bien! Recomendable!

Thoroughly enjoyed my 5 nights stay. Some say the hotel is a bit tired,  but has everything you could require, is clean, comfortable with a lovely garden to enjoy a pre dinner drink whilst watching the fruit bats overhead. Excellently located to explore Thamel bazaar and Durbar Square with it's temples. Would certainly recommend this hotel. Friendly, efficient staff.

Good hotel, like the Shangri La a little better as it has a pool.  It is a little bit sterile and the rooms are a bit cold but overall a nice hotel.  I would stay here again.  I would choose the Hilton over it tho adn even the Shangri La

Rooms are pathetic, Services of hotel is too bad. Food menu is not as per the standers.  Food quality and taste is pathetic. Staying in "Malla hotel" is waste of money  and time. Ambiance is so bad. Not suggestible to stay.

Do not waste your money here as with the price (at least 100 euros for a night) you really get nothing. The furniture in the rooms looks ancient and not welcoming at all.There was trouble to get warm water in the shower, heating was working properly though.The big garden area was quite nice but pool was ice-cold. I liked the breakfast, especially the yoghurt made of yak milk was lovely. This hotel is stayable for a few nights but maybe with a price of 50 euros, not 150 for a night.

A well situated hotel in the city. Staff were very friendly and helpful and they really did try to make our stay as pleasant as possible. Dinner was really excellent, on all three evenings we stayed....its also worth noting they have a really good western/European choice, and not just the usual curry! Desserts were lovely too. Our only slight criticisms were that breakfast doesn't match up the dinner, there is a cockerel that likes to have a bit of a crow in the morning, the wfi although it is free, is pretty slow. The Manager of our tour (Saga) did kindly print our return flight boarding passes on the hotel printer though.

We were booked to stay here for 2 nights at the start of our Nepal night and then again at the end. Having read the earlier reviews, I was a bit concerned about what we might find. However the hotel and the rooms were nice.  Staff were friendly. We had breakfast which was good. I agree that the hotel could do with a lick of paint to tidy it up in a couple of places but we were perfectly satisfied with our stay. And the hotel kindly stored a case for us when we were off in our travels.

My heart sunk at the thought of staying here once again.. having spent the first night in Kathmandu in a Patan heritage house with a delightful host, great food and comfort, I was less than impressed to note the poor standards  that are prevailing  at the Malla  since last year. The room.....torn sheet on one bed, not very clean all round with the bathroom downright grubby..the shaving mirror hadn't been wiped since time began, the door had food slopped up it and not cleaned off....no hot water except buckets brought up as and when....we are all aware of fuel shortages in Nepal but after a week of trekking staying at lodges WITH hot water I really do wonder at the management of this  so called hotel...it reeks of mismanagement  and decay....my suggestion would be to avoid like the plague !!Saga uses this place , which in itself is amazing ..they obviously don't check properties any more

Stayed here with our Saga tour at beginning and end of our tour in Napel, it's quite a way from most attractions. It's also a very rundown hotel, rooms all need a revamp and to service in the bar and restraunt was very slow, I ordered a noodle dish and it took over an hour to be cooked ,not very tasty either. Would not want to stay here again.

Excelente hotel, buena ubicación, la zona no es muy linda pero seguramente debido a los terremotos que han azotado a la ciudad. El hotel tiene de todo!, piscina, un area recreativa con mesa de ping pong y sala de musculación y ademas un espacio verde muy lindo. Recomendable 100%

I am impressed by the way they serve. They have quality and prompt service. The taste of the food were too good. The location is also in the suitable area. It is just a few minutes away from Thamel and near to the Narayanhiti Museum.

The lobby appears inviting, with comfortable seating and current newspapers. Large sitting room is behind the lobby. I stayed in Room 507 on the top floor. There was an old king bed. All furnishings are old and quite worn. The baseboards are dirty. The carpet is worn and badly stained, making one wonder how long it has been since they were truly cleaned. Refrigerator was empty, except that it was filled with mold spots. Finally, the AC did not work. The staff service is friendly, but not flexible or well prepared. I had Internet connectivity issues which even the manager was not able to resolve. There is a breakfast buffet but you can order custom omelets. The food was not exceptional. I would suggest you consider alternate lodging. I do have to say that the Malla is located within 5 minutes of Thamel shopping district, so that is a plus.

The location of the hotel is great near the Thamel district and the entrance and common parts are good, but the bedrooms are very tired and tarnished, the bathroom was dingy and the plumbing was in a poor state of repair the service staff were friendly but the dining room staff were miserable and also tired looking. The breakfast was so bad Luke warm and soggy that even though we had paid for it we went out to a local cafe. It appears to want to be up there with the big boys but fails miserably. Tried to book another hotel for our last night but couldn't find a room - says it all.paid wifi was poor.

I am a British Nepalese, own a business in England.  This time the purpose of the trip to my birth place Nepal was Climbing Mt Makalu and Mt Amadablam. Before and after the Expedition I had some spare time in Kathmandu. During this period, I mostly stayed at Yak & Yeti, and Annapurna which both were amazing. Due to unavailability at Yak and Yeti  and Annapurna I moved to Hotel Malla. I checked with my British passport and it was okay. Ho soggiornato con un gruppo in questo hotel ad inizio Settembre 2014. Hotel grande, per niente tipico. Camere abbastanza spaziose, letti comodi con alcuni confort (clima, tv, asciugacapelli). Nella prima camera che ci avevano assegnato non funzionava nulla (luci, clima rotto ecc.). Le finestre non si possono aprire dall'interno se non con una chiave che non viene fornita. Ci hanno sostituito la stanza e spostato nell'ultima camera in fondo al corridoio all'ultimo piano dove soggiornavano numerosi indiani, noti per la maleducazione e per niente rispettosi degli altri (si alzavano presto ed iniziavano a parare ed urlare nel corridoio, più di una volta sono venuti a bussare alla nostra porta ad orari improponibili). Pochi servizi in questo hotel (wi-fi a pagamento: viene fornito un codice, che a volte non funziona, che permette di collegarsi per un tempo massimo e se lasciate acceso il wi-fi sul telefono, nonostante non vi stiate collegando, il tempo scade). Avevamo il servizio di bed and breakfast per cui abbiamo usufruito solo della colazione: poca scelta, cibi internazionali scadenti. Unica nota positiva: buona posizione dell'hotel.

We stayed here on three different occations,  in three different rooms,  for a total of five days during our 34 day tour..The lobby and public rooms of the  hotel are really nice,  you think you are checking into a five star hotel, and the grounds are outstanding, we loved looking onto the garden from our rooms. Other than the front desk, the staff was very friendly and helpful. We had issues trying to get bottled water, and getting things fixed in the rooms. They  just yessed us then did nothing.   The breakfast buffet  was consistantly excellent, they even opened it up at 5;00 AM  on our last day,  with most of the regular food available, because we had to leave early to the airport. The first night we had a buffet dinner, which was very good.The court yard restaurant we thought was way over priced for lunch and had a very limited uninteresting menu. All three rooms had a small mini bar type  refrigerator. In two rooms they even gave use separate keys to the minibars.  None  of the refrigerator worked, and were full of mold. I don't understand why they just did not remove the broken refrigerators rather than leaving them in the rooms, causing the rooms to smell like mold. In two of the three rooms the air conditioners did not work. They made noise as if they were doing something but the rooms were very hot even with them turned on to low setting. We had to open the windows at night, which caused an other problem.  They have cages full of roosters and other  birds in the garden. The roosters started to crow around 4:00 in the morning and continued until sun rise. It is beyond me why they even have noisy roosters on their grounds.Our second room which was on the first floor facing the garden had no window latch, which means  that there was no way to secure the window closed and keep intruders from just climbing in the window. When we checked  in,  the window had blow open by the wind and there were lots of bird feathers in the room.They only provide bottled water on the first day, after that you have to buy it from the bar. The hotel's tap water is undrinkable which is the norm for this part of the world(except Tibet). Water both hot and cold came out of the taps  a yellow/brown color.Rooms had old tube TVs with a few English channels. Rooms are smallish and kind of dumpy with out dated furnishing. All three rooms smelled moldy. Our second rooms sink stopper did not work and it was difficult to control the shower. The third rooms shower did not work properly and was impossible to control.  There was adequate hot water though. Thamel district which has  lots of stores and restaurants is a short walk away  but the road outside the hotel is really in poor condition (not the hotels fault, it is typical through out Kathmandu). We had to walk through mud patches(my wife fell in the mud) sharing the road with crowds  of motor cycles and cars. It is very difficult to get across the main street due to all the traffic.   At night there are no street lights, so bring a flash light.I would not recommend this hotel.

Imagine planning a corporate event for your company at a 5-star hotel, only to have the in-house guests waltz in share your space, snacks, dinner, live BBQ and the drinks you bought at your expense. That's exactly what happened to me at The Malla hotel last Friday.*I had booked the entire garden side banquet hall for our event, but the hotel staff did nothing to stop the in-house guests from entering. They helped themselves to the food and drinks, and even started using the live BBQ counter and snacks counter. When first confronted they denied it completely and only when I showed them the photos they apologized and covered up saying they “forgot to inform” us and it’s a Friday ritual.*The snacks weren't enough for our guests, and the in-house guests took over the food counters. Instead of stopping them since we were on a schedule they had no restrictions. Even at dinner we had THE SAME DINNER BUFFET as the rest of the guests at the hotel. With no space to sit they finally arranged to move the buffet to our “private” space while the in house guests lounged in the dinner space that we had paid for.*The staff were poorly trained and unhappy, and the management didn't seem to care about the problems. From the beginning all the staff at the junior level were decent but at the mid level they were out dated untrained and plain unhappy and that portrayed in their service. The management at the highest level were well trained to smile and apologized when I complained but they seemed to have no remorse for the way they hosted our event.*It was the worst experience I have ever had at a hotel. I would give it 0 stars if I could.

I was on the 4th floor overlooking the rather splendid gardens which are a joy to sit out in. My room had a huge double bed, brilliantly clean with all the amenities you would hope for. The housekeeping team are very efficient and friendly ladies who always have a smile and warm greeting in the morning.Downstairs the front desk and reception team are very willing and helpful and a special shout out to the guest services lady Shristi who went beyond the call of duty by taking me to find a local florist to have bouquets made up for some friends I was meeting. Shristi found me a shop, stayed with me to translate my requirements and then went back to pick them up and deliver back to me in time for the evening- top class service and attention to guest needs, thanks so much Shristi- you’re the best!Also must mention the excellent spa where I had a top class massage in a wonderful relaxing environment- maybe one of the best I have enjoyed. Breakfast I served buffet style and there’s a huge offering to enjoy from Nepali and Indian dishes to western expectations too- great service from the team there too. All things considered this is a terrific hotel at reasonable prices in a terrific location, central to the city and a two minute walk to get into the tourist area of Thamel.  Staff are great, lovely environment, did I mention the bar? Yes terrific too!

It was a great experience great services polite staff loved being here. The hotel was absolutely clean … expresss room service …smooth check in  at hotel … Garden and sit out is very good and green!  Food as expected was great at the hotel and coffee shop too is good

The rooms were clean and the staff would attend to the little issues we had during our stay.The food was good too.The location of the hotel is a big plus point. It is very close to the Thamel market where souvenirs and handicrafts are abundant. There are also many good restaurants close by - at walking distance.The hotel arranges for taxis for tourists too.It is a good choice to stay in Kathmandu.

Cette hotel est très bien situe juste à côté de l entre dans thamel le quartier touristique. Les chambres sont corrects mais mérite un peu de rénovation de plus une odeur de moisi désagréable. À note un très beau jardin bien calme qui contraste agréablement avec katmandou.

We stayed 4 nights in the Malla.  The staff were amazingly helpful and served a fresh drink on arrival.  The location is brilliant as you can walk centrally.  The rooms were clean and tidy, very quiet. The pool was lovely to use and relax by too.

Great newly painted hotel with fresh cold drink on arrival. Good location , close to restaurants but good service also in the hotel dining. Nice size rooms and good views from rooms on both side of hotel. One is pool and garden ,other is a beautiful garden and if you look carefully you see some animals. Coffee and tea in room , hair drier bit old but works well, warm shower , good facilities available. Staff are welcoming and very helpful. Free WiFi works well.

We stayed in this hotel for 2 nights. The lobby area was fine, but the bedroom was tired and definitely needed refurbishment.  The paintwork needed freshening up, as some was peeling.  The furniture is cheap and the windows and doors don't fit properly.  We certainly appreciate that Kathmandu was hit hard by the 2015 earthquake, but our bedroom window had a large open gap, when it was fully closed.  Surely something like that should have been fixed 4 years on. There is no safe in the room, only a safety deposit box at reception.  You only get 2 hours of free WiFi in your room, but it's free in the lobby.  The staff were attentive, especially in the restaurant and they made an effort to provide a good choice of food for both breakfast and dinner. It's redeemed by its convenient location for getting into the old town and its attentive staff. However, overall, for the price charged, we would have expected a higher standard in the rooms.

The hotel is a short walk from the Thamel shopping area and restaurants (though you have to put up with Kathmandu's pollution and dust). It's also close to the Garden of Dreams which is well worth a visit for a bit of relaxation. The hotel has a big garden, with birds and squirrels; the rooms have good facilities, the food is good and the staff helpful. Our major criticism is that the wi-fi was unpredictable - the staff couldn't always get it to work, and we were continually having to log in again.

As we were called for the entertainment purpose at the wedding we were there in the Hall room of the Hotel. We were not praised at all for the work on any aspects. The food served were also very limited and the service was not good. While we were taking our dinner the some food items have been finished already.

We spent two nights here en route to a safari venue and a return visit for one night awaiting return flight to Delhi/UK.  Although not the smartest hotel on our tour it was homely and small.  The staff were helpful and the food was rather good, especially breakfast which was mostly cooked to order.  There was a good selection at dinner with options of English dishes.  There was a kettle in our room but we were unable to obtain any coffee, only t-bags were offered.  The grounds were especially nice, very well kept and much like an oasis of quiet in the middle of a busy, noisy city.  The room was adequate and as I have stated not the smartest but clean, quiet and comfortable.  If I were to return to Kathmandu I would happily stay here again.

Initial impression of the hotel entrance and staff in traditional dress was impressive and the grounds are lovely.  The room allocated to us was a health hazard with stained bed linen, thick dust and dirt on the carpet & skirting boards, paint and rotting woodwork on the windows, dirty/broken furniture and non-working fridge.  It was not fit for use.  The second room was cleaner and habitable but the rooms need investment.  Breakfast and dinner were good, and the staff were polite. WiFi was free in reception, but chargeable in bedrooms.  It is close to a local market and ideal for shopping.  I would not stay there again.

Initially the entrance area was good and the gardens were good, but the rooms seemed faded.  Breakfast and dinner were good, and the staff were all excellent.The rooms seemed a bit small and in need of an upgrade, but we found it all grew on us.  We stayed here twice, with rooms overlooking the garden on one occasion and the pool on the other, and they were quiet with no noise heard from other rooms or from the roads.The bathroom was on the small side, but with plenty of hot water.  WiFi was free in reception, but chargeable in bedrooms.  TV did not have any U.K. news channel, but this was true of all hotels we used in Nepal.We would stay here again.

We stayed at the Malla Hotel as we were transitting through Kathmandu to and from a trip to Bhutan.  The hotel was satisfactory for a one night stop off enroute.The hotel is located in a good location on the edge of the Thamel area, close to restaurants and shops.  Durbar Square is a 30 minute walk away, although they were resurfacing some of the streets and those streets were not easy to walk down due to liquid tar (Oct 17).  The reception, bar, lounge and dining room were of a good standard.  There was also another area where we ate breakfast and dinner (like a conference room) which was not nearly as nice as the dining room where we had breakfast on our return trip to Kathmandu.  The gardens were nice and had a bird cage with some lovely coloured birds.  The pool area was clean and tidy, although we didn't use the pool.The rooms themselves were ok without being anything special, the outbound stay the room was better than the room we had on the way back.

This hotel's rooms are pathetic, services are bad, food is not at all eatable, this is a proxy 5-star hotel. Its an old property and have never been refurbished. Service and food is also good. There is a shop in hotel which sells souvenirs and dresses. Lobby is nice. Beds in room are cozy and it has option for both hot and cold air. Lawn of the hotel is nicely maintained. There is swimming pool and saloon in hotel. Both veg and non veg foods are served.

I did not enjoy my stay at this hotel.I am sure when this hotel first opened many years ago it was beautiful.  This hotel is in desperate need of renovation.  The lobby is very dingy and the lighting is very poor.  The rooms in my opinion are so outdated.  The carpet smelled the furniture was old and the lighting was so poor I was tripping over my shoes.  I believe the amber light bulbs were probably 15 watts.  I felt so depressed in this hotel I asked the travel company to change my hotel I wouldn't stay there another night.  I will say the staff was very nice but totally limited to what they could do.  It seems that hotel has not cash flow.  A lamp did not work they sent someone up to look at it. Para quienes conocen Katmandú, el Malla es un hotel correcto, de los mejores dentro de la franja de los "buenos hoteles" que ofrece la ciudad (apenas superado por un par), por lo que es un error compararlo con hoteles 4/5 estrellas europeos (sólo es justo si se lo hace con otros hoteles locales).
