Having not visited Kathmandu for over 10 years, it was a great relief and pleasure to see the Raddison maintaining such a high standard. Excellent reception, clean and tidy rooms, and polite staff. The new building and especially roof top bar a great addition. Good to see so many cheerful and positive staff.

This is just a a word about the pool and the gym.The pool in late November is open. The water is dang cold (+16) but the patio by the pool is still warm enough for chilling in your swimming shorts.  It will also be find in December I'm sure. Daytime heat is a bit over 20 degrees and it feels warm. There are decent covers for the lounge chairs and the towels are solid too.The gym is alright. A solid 5/10. IT costs about 20 USD for one time use or 200 USD for a month. It has nearly everything you need and is run down as the rest of the reviews suggest. The cardio machines face some TVS (some English channels if you can swindle the locals) are mediocre and they're essentially overlooking the pool while all the other gym facilities are two stories lower. Odd but it's adaptable. The sauna, steamroom and jacuzzi are a fair 2/10 and rather appalling frankly. The steamroom is overly intense (zero visibility) and the sauna is dark (freaaaaakay). The hot tub is bubbling and hot but not at all tempting especially if you have any open cut as it's an incubator for diseases I'm sure. Everything else is like it's been trapped in the 70s and barely kept up. But hey, it's a gym and a pool in Kathmandu so that's rightfully worthy for some acclaim. Live the DReam!!!

We stayed here before and after a trekking trip. It was wonderfully comfortable. The spa is pricey but was wonderful. Staff are very helpful. The food was really good. We had a wonderful stay. It is also very close to Thamel .

Stayed here for three nights at the end of a trekking trip.  Recommended by a friend who used to live in Nepal.  Can't say check in was anything to write home about - waited forever for the two front desk ladies to even acknowledge that I was standing in front of them, as they were seemingly buried in whatever paperwork that was consuming their attention. In the end I had to wake them up by saying, is this the right place to check in?  As it turned out, it wasn't, and the staff who discovered that seemed relieved that she didn't need to check me in after all.  The Radisson has two buildings across a narrow street from each other, and I was informed that I'd been upgraded to a "premiere" room, which is in the annex building.  At least we didn't have to lug our luggage across, but were assured that once we were done with checking in luggage would be delivered.At the Annex front desk, we were greeted warmly and promptly checked in. Still not sure what was with the attitude of the staff at the main building but from then on everything worked pretty much smoothly and we had a very nice stay. Saw some mention on TA about renovated rooms vs unrenovated ones so I guess this must be the newer building.  The room we had was on the 2nd floor (257) looking at the main building.  Room's not huge but adequate sized and updated (lots of glass and mirrors) as can be expected from an international class business hotel. Oversized king bed is comfortable with quality bedding. Floor is wood with area rugs.  Wall outlets come in every shape and form imaginable so no worries about adapters.  Good wifi. The bathroom is see through design with glass walls, common in many newer hotels in Asia.  Not sure if all the rooms are like this but it's a fun feature only if you are alone or sharing with someone you know well, no point in having a glass walled shower if you have to keep the blinds lowered!Overall, I preferred our building as it's smaller and quieter, with a lot of open and comfortable public space. There is only one restaurant in this building serving buffet breakfast mainly for people who have breakfast included in their rooms.  We also ate in the main coffee shop for breakfast and dinner - buffets as well but a la carte available for dinner, plus you can always get a partial buffet of salad or dessert only. The dinner buffet is a good deal however, with a lot of selections including many Nepali dishes.  We also tried room service breakfast one day which is the best option and most reasonable if you just want an "American Breakfast", a category only offered for room service.Location wise, while not right in the center of Tamel, it's not far - about a 20 minute walk.  The narrow street in between the two Radisson buildings is lined with souvenir shops, restaurants, as well as a grocery store with plenty of items catering to western taste - I tried to find a particular local type of cookie and couldn't find it there but they have things like digestives biscuits.  A bit further on the main street leading to Tamel there is also a bakery and a small tea shop with very nicely decorated boxes of tea at reasonable  prices.

I came with my Wife and  Stayed here as all places near by and had Lovely Time .It was Calm and Quiet ..Food is also Nice and Tasty .Rooms are Neat and clean .If You are getting Bored..Better to go to Casino and Enjoy your Time .Shops are just outside Hotel and you can do shopping.Once you come to Kathmandu ..You can Visit This Hotel

I stayed here with my husband. The moment we were picked from the airport, positive vibes started coming in my mind. The moment we reached the hotel, it is so beautiful. The staff is extremely good and generous. Rooms are well maintained and decorated. Food is also good.

My wife and I just spent four days here. It's quite impressive to look at and very large,consisting of several buildings. The staff were split into two catorgaries. Those who were polite and helpful and those that weren't interested. We experienced both, but luckily none effected the stay. Cleanliness was a bit lacking and this was a concern. Overall, by Kathmandu standards, it was ok, but could have been better for an international hotel. WE used the Tibet hotel next door most of the time, where staff where staff were more professional, the hotel was cleaner and the facilities better suited. Cheaper also. Would definitely use the Tibet ne t time, but don't let that put you off the Raddison. It's adequate.

Firstly let me say that i am a club carlson member and have been frequently with Radisson in other countriesI was quite surprised with Radisson Kathmandu's service quality1. Good location 4/52. Hospitality : the personnel at the reception are so paranoid. As soon as the customer asks for some service, they first quote a charges for the service like it is a deal in a shop. This is quite a substandard approach3. Internet is 512kbps but it took over 45 mins to download a file of 3.7mb. for a 5 star business hotel 512 kbps is an insult. 4. Business Centre acknowledged bad internet but insists on customer to pay per 15 mins use. Again business centre internet is pathetic. 5. The room provided is in the premium building next to a noisy bar with lots of noise ans loud music the whole night. The windows are also not sound proof. 6. Ask for help about directions or places to visit and the reception does not help. They direct you to the taxi stand outside . 7. The food at the coffee shop is average. The cold coffee served had residue of bitter coffee powder. 8. The bed mattress was hard. The hotel provided hard coir mattress with no custioning. Seemed like sleeping on hard floor. The building may be equipped with all advanced features but if the hospitality staff is not upto standards, the very experience is average.

Rooms, Food, People, Location were very good. Though the hotel is a bit old fashioned. The central location was important because traffic in Kathmandu is very poor. One of the lifts were not working so took lot of time to reach the room.

hotel is old and needs refurbishment. Rooms are shabby, one lift does not work. Stewards at coffee shop needs to be trained. staff behavior is good and courteous. Location of the hotel is central and convenient. Has a decent casino attached.

Stayed at Raddison Kathmandu for official visit. Initially we were given room in original building but everything was very inconvenient (ironing plug was loose, water in bathroom was yellow). On request they sent staff immediately to look at the problem. Later we were moved to newer building of the hotel, which was amazing and everything was clean and new. I used their spa for reflexology and spine massage and it was one of the best massage I ever had. Spa staff knew what she was doing and she didn't look at the time. Spa is highly recommended!! Breakfast was ok. Otherwise it was good stay. We had dinner at Annapurna restaurant which was SO DELICIOUS and to add great music.

Well located hotel ESP for business traveller .....Gud service and Gud breakfast buffet .Rooms and bathrooms need to change with time .....Beautiful new spa.Staff Gud and courteous .Recommend for business travelers who want to be in the centre .Worth its price ....

Booked two rooms for my family and niece by Booking.com with US$ 540 from 9-12 September.Called the Hotel just to realise that we have to pay for the breakfast.What's this Radisson ?Are you crazy ?How do you expect people to react to your attitude ?One Standard Double Room @ US$ 95 per night at Kathmandu without breakfast.Insane.

Good ambiance, friendly staff. The hotel is placed in the heart of the city of Kathmandu. It is very near to Pashupatinath temple and one can also enjoy the night life of the city and can do the shopping in the near by local markets. Stay is absolutely refreshing and value for money....

Very nice and accommodating hotel staff. Clean and meets the criteria for all US standards. But the hospitality surpasses all of US standards. Was very pleased at the service and quality of food too..

The staff service from check in to check out was impeccable.  Unwaveringly friendly and welcoming throughout my stay.  The room was spacious and well maintained.  I checked out after a couple of days for travel outside the city and realized I left my running shoes in the room.  Checked back in a week later and they had my shoes up to my new room within 10 minutes.  Really extraordinary!

1) A rusty nail protruding from a chair in the breakfast cafe scratched my leg exposing me to the risk of tetanus 2) The TV didn't work for 2 days.  Repairman disappeared as soon as I went out and had to be called back 3) The hotel staff assisted a taxi driver to overcharge me 500 rupees to the city centre - standard price is 200 4) The windows in the guest room (659) are not sealed properly.  When it rained my room was flooded and the carpet soaked.

Property is old and the rooms are not well maintained. Needs major upgrade and the service team needs major orientation in providing superior service. Foul odour, equipment and fittings didn't work to name some of the problems faced. Thank god it was only one night's stay enroute to Pokhara!

Booked to stay with them and cancelled my room during the permitted cancellation period. They promised to refund my payment but never did. AVOID!!!I had numerous emails from them all promising to pay, but it has been over a year now so I've given up any hope.

I'm usually pretty forgiving of hotels and travel extensively for work in this region but on my recent stay at the Radisson myself and my colleagues had a bad experience on all fronts. The wifi hardly worked anywhere in either of the buildings, extremely frustrating for a work trip. Aside from the breakfast which is fine, food in the restaurants and room service was pretty awful, not fresh and very over priced (and a couple of times room service dishes came with only half the ingredients listed on the menu or key ingredients missing). I was also unimpressed that additional items were added to my bill that I had to ask to have removed. Some colleagues didn't have hot water in their showers. Staff were friendly, but very disorganised and not particularly helpful. Basic requests would take up to an hour to hear back about. Lastly the gym is chaotic and not clean or well maintained. Very unimpressed with this hotel especially considering the price. Other than the location I can't say there is any silver lining to this hotel. Will not be staying here again.

Had to spend a night at Radisson as our Jet flight to Delhi was called off. Wonderful experience as rooms were good, bed was comfortable, all modern amenities provided, free internet and staff was very helpful in spite of having too much rush to handle. The food was excellent, great variety, very nicely served, innovative at dinner and breakfast.

The Radisson is a comfortable hotel in an excellent, quiet location convenient for business or exploring the city. The main part of the hotel seems to get huge busloads of tourists, but I stayed in the newer wing, which is a separate building. I am not sure how new it is actually, as it shows some age itself, but it is quiet and very comfortable. I slept well. The breakfast buffet is enormous, with vast offerings for any palate. The wifi is good but not exceptional. The city has frequent power outages, so expect some gaps in electricity until the generators come online -- this is in no way unique to the Radisson! The fitness center is very nice with plenty of equipment. It also must be said that the Executive Lounge service is truly exceptional. Pramesh is amazingly client focused, remembers guest names and preferences, and is a delight every day.  I had a wonderful stay and look forward to returning.

Hotel lujoso ( pero sin excesos ) en Kathmandú. Muchos extranjeros se alojan en el mismo, ya sea por negocios (la minoría), o por turismo.Subiendo y bajando por los ascensores, te puedes encontrar con gente con la nariz más roja de lo normal, alguno te explica que acaba de llegar de subir  - o intentar subir - el Everest.Desayunos muy consistentes y variados, adaptados a todos los gustos y culturas que allí conviven.Servicio muy amable y atento, dispuesto a solucionar cualquier problema que tengas. Realmente es una buena opción como punto de partida y regreso de cualquier trekking en  Nepal, o simplemente para hacer turismo.

We spent four nights with our seven year-old son and it could not have been more satisfactory --- It's in a very good location to walk to Thamel, convenient to the airport, there's an  attentive staff, an easy restaurant with a variety of good foods (Nepali and not), and the whole place is very clean.

The worst Radisson property or star hotel I have ever stayed in. In the supposedly premium rooms, I enter to see the shower remains of the previous guest still lying around. Hair in the shower area and other telltale signs that the room has not been cleaned but only spruced up. Pic attached.Beware, the towels do not seem washed or cleaned even after requests. Saw small black marks on bath towels.But the breakfast restaurant area takes the cake. I asked for a Dosa, which would take 5-7 minutes and I am left waiting for half hour while other guests are being served. I then ask the restaurant manager for my unimportant request and he goes looking for the chef. Suddenly, he discovers the chef, Nabin, taking a leisurely stroll in the restaurant. The chef had outsourced the task to someone else, who in turn has gone missing too!What I realised at the end of the stay is that the staff is very very poorly trained and extremely insensitive. They do not have the first clue of how to resolve guest complaints and assume that denial is the best manner.Terrible hotel and service, regret that I stayed at Radisson Kathmandu.

I travel to Kathmandu once in every 2 - 3 months. This was my first time in this hotel. The hotel is very conveniently located. Huge property. One case spend some time in the Casino which is also there in this hotel. The staffs are very courteous and professional which you expect from a Radisson branded property. But, the hotel needs serious renovation. Specially the toilets. I was staying in the old wing.

When we visited Kathmandu with a packaged group tour and this hotel was perfect for our visit. It was located just a short walk off the main street and was surrounded with small shops and restaurants. Our room was clean and spacious. The breakfast buffet had a large selection.

I chose this hotel based on college recommendation and I do not regret it. Although it must be an old hotel - built with a large lobby and reception the rooms are still incredibly well maintained and overall are very comfortable. I regret that air conditioning does not work entirely well - although setting to low values the room was still a bit too warm inside. There is a huge lcd tv set in front of the bed and I have a nice working desk and a sofa with coffee table. There is a kettle and set of coffee/tea (black&green) and two regular size cups (not like some other places where you can barely sink the tea-bag in the water). There is also a minibar. Bathroom is small but all the essentials are there - hairdryer, toiletries, tissues and full set of washing gels, shampoo and body lotion. There is also a rather big tub so you can easily relax after a long day in Kathmandu. Breakfasts are ok - 4/5 - one point deducted for missing flesh vegetables. There is an egg station, some sausages and meet, cheeses, cereals, some noodles, fruits and pastries. Good tea and nice service. I had dinner in the lobby restaurant twice - once a curry and club sandwich the second time. Quality is all right and prices not too drastic but I do suggest to walk around - there are some nice restaurants that provide good quality (or better) and are usually cheaper. There is a gym on the top floor - nicely maintained with many machines and weights to train with. There are people coming from outside of hotel so it must be one of the better in the neighbourhood. There is also an outdoor swimming pool but it's not warm enough outside to try it in mid Feb.During my stay one of the elevators was broken and all the guests had to use single 6 person lift to go up/down. Worth mentioning – it’s not a fast lift so there is a bit of waiting. Cleanliness – excellentI would chose it again.

I know it is a difficult time for Nepal's tourism industry. This is a hotel nicely located and its staff are efficient and friendly. Breakfast was of high quality. But the rooms badly need refurbishment as the condition and style of furniture and bathroom furnishing is very outdated. For example the hair dryer mounted on the wall is the "vacuum cleaner" type which was common in 1980s and it takes long for your hair to be dried. Wardrobe is very old with many marks of wear and tear. Gym was of very low quality with old equipment which makes many noises. Some of the equipment was not even in working conditions.

Stayed here for one week on business trip. First time visiting Kathmandu. This hotel offered many conveniences. Like airport pick up, with no additional fee, how convenient could that be, not to mention cheap? The location is also strategic. In front of hotel you can find many souvenir shops. If you want to look for many other options, you can walk for around 10-15 minutes to Thamel. They have grocery store just around the corner if you need to buy water, biscuits, or fruits. The room itself fills out my expectation. Clean. Only minus is you can hear next door sounds/voices. The breakfast option is plenty from international to local. I had great stay and would wanna come back.

The Stay at Hotel was very good right from check in time till check out time. Quality of food was very good.  Warmthness from team is very nice, located in main city of Kathmandu and good places to visit near by.  Market area is nor far away and lot of options for food and shopping

Ich war jetzt schon 3 mal hier, immer mehrere Wochen. Schöne Zimmer, guter, aufmerksamer Service. Gym auf 2 Etagen. Schwimmbad auf der Dachterasse, im Winter leider geschlossen. Ausgezeichnetes Frühstücksbuffet. Abends Büffet, oder a la Carte.

I haven’t been back here since the earthquake but all is well and people should know that it’s safe to start coming back. They need your tourism and to fill the extension block across the road that seems to be in mothballs.As always the staff were most helpful. My case arrived smashed and I needed some help to liaise with the local Turkish Airlines office to sort compensation and the front desk staff were more than happy to help me out.If there is an adverse comment it is that the food wasn’t quite as delicious as usual and the number of local dishes seems to have been replaced by Chinese-type recipes. But still tasty fayre.

En una ciudad como Katmandu probablemente debe ser el hotel mas lujoso que existe en la misma.extremadamente cordiales sus empleados,buena calidad de las camas y de la restauracion.habia limitaciones en el horario de agua caliente debido al problema actual de limitacion de gas y gasolina pero no constituyo ningun problema

The location of the hotel (in terms of work) was perfect as was the comfort and warmth of the rooms, and the friendliness of the staff. The breakfast offers everything imaginable and the availability of the fitness centre from 6am was wonderful.

I was satisfied with the hotel facility and the services and really want to revisit the hotel in the near future. Thank you for the hospitality and kindness.Of course i recommend this hotel to my friend those traveling to Kathmandu

This hotel is very well located near to the tourist center of Thamil in Kathmandu and to other interesting local shops.  You can obtain anything that you need quite nearby to the hotel.  Rooms are comfortable, staff is friendly and the food is good.    When I stayed the country was suffering from a fuel embargo so there was insufficient heating and hot water but the hotel cannot be blamed for this.

It was a good  comfortable stay.. rooms and the food was marvelous...vegetarian to non veg it was complete. I enjoyed their food. Staffs were helpful and humble..the rooms and toilet were clean n tidy..free wifi avaible. Easy taxi catch up in front of t hotel n surrounded with shops to shop..overall excellent.

I had visited Kathmandu on work before the earthquake and had put up at the Radisson.The hotel is very comfortable-- i ate most of my meals at the hotel and the food was nice. Breakfast was vey good.The street leading to the hotel is lively and good for picking souvenirs. There is a well equipped grocery store on the street as well.I would definitely stay here again-- pity the trip was too short.

If you have time in Kathmandu you MUST go to the Tranquility Spa in cave of Hotel Radisson. I was there two times and it was wonderful ecperience. I have got excellent haircut by very friendly hairdresser and a unforgetable feet massage by a very special friend of mine. I felt really like in heaven. Totally different to this noisy and dusty city of Kathmandu. And the prices so low for european people so go there. You never will regret.

The newly constructed building is still ok, the food and service is very average, have constant wifi issues, the saloon and spa was very average.They need to improve a lot VS what they charge. But knowing KTM that's not a bad option provided ypu get good rates.

Radisson Hotel is located near to key tourist spots like Darbar Marg and Thamel. Hotel provides good services and food however bathrooms badly need renovation as products were not working upto the expectation.

The hotel service is good.  up to my expectation.  nice environment, and good for business trip.  room housekeeping in order.  Breakfast buffer is acceptable, but need to improve.  Lobby waiting hall is good.  friendly staff.  out side the hotel have many gift shop, and food store.  good location.

Overall nice stay..  located In the heart of the city.. !! everything is pretty close from Hotel. Room was neat, comfortable. Recommended for everybody. Food was great.. had lots of Indian touch which suited me most.

Rooms are good, services provided are value for money except food. Your spa is also good and value for money. Food is not upto the mark. I'm a vegetarian but got up half filled when I tried your buffet dinner on 19th evening. Cream pasta without cream, noodles without any flavour and taste, bottle gourd veg half cooked, Idli were also sticky, etc. On 20th I had opt to have egg and veg sandwich only. I really need to bring ready cook packets, if at all I choose to stay with you.

Excellent facilities and very comfortable rooms. The people are very good, polite and respond very good to customer's need. I would recommend this hotel to every Indian. The only hitch is that the room tariff is a bit high. The nearby souvenir shops and the local market is also good and with a bit of cajoling you get a good price for most of the items. The conduct of the business meeting/conference was also excellent and the major international conference of the Nepal Seed Congress went on very smoothly and successfully with no hassles at all. Excellent work by the hotel management. If the hotel management looks into the price/tariff issue the customers from India will increase. The pickup and drop facility by the hotel is good, but I would have preferred a smaller vehicle than the minibus as that would reduce the waiting time for the early arrived customers.

My stay was for a week and overall I was happy to have stayed at this hotel. Hotel staff is very helpful and always ready to help an extra mile than expected from them. The hotel has two buildings, the new one is much better infrastructure wise but the WiFi is much better in old building. I ended up asking for a LAN cable as my VPN was going mad due to the frequent WiFi outage. There is no electricity backup on the internet, i.e. when light goes off, the internet goes off as well which is a bit irritating when someone is on voip calls/meetings.

The hotel is good base to rest before and after the trekking. The spa salon will provide you the good service for the preparation and after the resting of the trek. Around the hotel can find everything. The city region Thamel is just 10 minutes with a taxi or even 20 minutes with a walk. The food is very tasty and the hotel staff is friendly and kind.

I enjoyed my stay at the Radisson in Kathmandu, thought the property is not what attracted me, the staff did. They were friendly, courteous and considerate. The location is also noteworthy, only 20 rupees from Thamal, the touristy, downtown area.

Perhaps it is not easy to find a great hotel at Kathmandu, so expectations are also low. This hotel has a potential to be a great hotel provided the management is more pro-active in managing the place. I still find this hotel very convenient, but often think of looking for an alternate place to go in my next trip. There are few things which hotel can easily improve upon but they dont! One is their lifts. Almost always I find one of the two front lifts have some problem. Second is their in-room wifi. I have to collect a coupon with a number on it to log to wifi from your room. And every time the laptop goes to sleep mode, I have to re-login. And if I have a laptop, a mobile and an ipad, I need three different coupons, and these are not inter-changable. Recently I was firmly refused by the frontdesk staff for more than two coupons. And wifi speed is not good.Third thing that I dont like is, the hotel often rents out the open-air space in their grond floor. This is the only and a pleasurable place to go and relax, but very often you find it blocked because a dinner party is being hosted. I need a place to unwind and that is the only place that they have.Fourth is their travel-desk service. Simply not good. The vehicles are not comfortable at all, but even worse is their service standard. I was waiting for their pickup car at the airport, and then had to take a taxi to come to hotel. The reception staff was unapologetic and explained to me that the driver was a 'bit late', not a great deal to them!!But the good things about this hotel is its location. The lounge and rooms are good. But the most i like is their door men, always very welcoming with a hearty smile.

nice stay will have again to stay there if the matter i tell you will be done fullfill.hope you can understand the matter regarding points i have spend there and about the services,there was no swimming pool you must clear that first

Good service, great location. Moved to this hotel because of its proximity to Thamel and other areas of interest in Kathmandu. It is surrounded by good restaurants, facilities like tailors, shops, and live music venues.

The hotel has pathetic internet services, the rooms have not been maintained for ages... the taps and shower etc are not in working condition. Food is average. While having breakfast, i realized the milk in the tetrapack was expired by 2 months... the staff acknowledged and when I asked them the reason... no answer.

I have stayed here for about once every month from April 2012 to September 2013. It became my 2nd home. I felt safe & secure here.The staff was very polite , courteous & eversmiling. Though its situated in the middle of residential area it has its own charm.

Hotel is surrounded in a residential area - not much space surrounding the exterior part of the hotel to enjoy.  Check in and check out was fine and efficient.  Staff were overall courteous and carried out their duties efficiently.  Rooms are outdated and overdue for renovation. There was no international adapter in the room.  Had to made a few calls before a staff bring it to the room.  Fitness center needs upgrade, like outdated TV.  Staff needed to be stationed in sauna area to clean and maintain. Pool water was completely empty due to quake, but there was no public sign at all to advice guests about the situation.

The Kathmandu Radisson is worth it. The service, the room, the food - all were good. The hotel is situated within an easy walk of the shops and restaurants of the Thamel tourist location. My experience was really enjoyable and I gladly recommend the Radisson.

Wonderful Hotel close to the heart of Kathmandu. Easy auto-rickshaw / cab ride to the King's Palace / Kings Way - Darbar Marg. Hotel is clean and comfortable. The Restaurant has great food + very reasonably priced. The breakfast buffet is quite amazing. The spa is nice too (I tried their deep tissue massage). The cold (iced) coffee with ice-cream at the restaurant was my favorite.

The rooms in the annexe (the newer building) are much nicer and newer than those in the main building - with proper double beds, rather than two singles pushed together.  Bathrooms are also more modern in the new building.  New building rooms sometimes have a weighing scale too - handy if you need to make sure that you bags are under a certain weight!It's quaint to start with that the door staff greet you with Namaste each time you walk through, but if you're coming and going a lot it becomes something of a game to get through before they say anything.The restaurant staff in the main building at breakfast (for each of the three breakfasts we had there) were indifferent, hard to get hold of - you're going to want to get your coffee before you get sat down, otherwise it might not arrive until after you've finished your breakfast.  All apart from the egg guy - he's magnificent, you'll want order eggs (in any format) just to see his mastery.Its a nice hotel, but I wouldn't say 5 star.

We consider ourselves extremely fortunate to have chosen Kathmandu Radisson for our stay during our vacation.  We were hit by the earthquake the very next day after we arrived.  The Manager was at the hotel within no time.  She mobilized the staff to make sure all the guests who were at the assembly point had water, blankets and food.  The staff also arranged dinner and breakfast the next day for weary guests who slept in the parking lot on carpets, comforters and pillows supplied by the hotel.  I can't thank the staff enough for taking such good care of us.  We pray for the safety of you and your families and a speedy recovery.

I was at this Hotel for 4 days in mid April 2015.  The Hotel needs a major renovation.  I was on the 6th floor which has been mentioned in other posts where services are spotty.  The room was small, very hot, but clean.  The staff was friendly.  I did not know about the "new section" of the Hotel and ate in the regular restaurant which has very limited choices.  If I knew about the other restaurants I might have had a better experience.  If you want a average hotel that is just ok stay here.  There is nothing to brag about. Not a five star hotel.

An excellent stay, everything was perfect, the room was clean, the bathroom clean and easily accessible, the bed was fine.  Breakfast was excellent and also lunch.  The staff were the best always pleasant and eager to help.

We stayed two nights at this hotel, the location is wonderful, however the hotel is nothing special. The breakfast buffet is lovely, and very abundant, the location of the hotel is good too. If you are just transitting through the city, it is a nice resting spot.

Was booked at the hotel on an assignment and as the meeting was in the same hotel. Surroundings real "tourist" and no genuine local environment; taxi drivers in cahoots with the hotel have a surcharge. Walk to the main road and you will pay less (although metred, no taxi does it by meter). However sufficient money changers for competition so rates for foreign currency better as you step outside the hotel.Rooms OK but dated. Cleaned regularly with polite reminders if you accidentally left "Do Not Disturb" sign on. Breakfast good spread but could do with more local food. The really major problems - technology. The TV reception suddenly became poor - technician came and identified it as a "floor" (6th floor) problem and said it will be fixed. Not so for 36 hours. Check with reception "We will send a technician to the room" completely unaware that it was a floor problem. Automatic "reception speak" without checking and fob off customer. That was only the minor part in Technology.The wifi was beyond atrocious - password to be renewed every 24 hours and very haphazard. Seems unable to give one password for length of stay. System does not log you in repeatedly - call reception "It is broken we are fixing it" - no attempt for webpage to say "Problem" - just frustrate customer with repeated failed log ins. Whose problem - not ours, Internet Provider (but we deal with hotel and not internet provider). Any refunds for non-working Wifi (No, we dont provide refunds). Other Radissons do - No we dont.Finally, went to Business Center with laptop to get good wifi and work - failed there too and fled to office to work. No, it is not Kathmandu internet as the Coffee Shops down the street have much faster wifi, So in conclusion, dont go there unless it is to eat and sleep.One good point - they will offer you a voucher for a free coffee at the (Radisson?) Airport Lounge on checkout. Take it as on that day it was "Oasis of Calm" at the lounge with good wifi using the same hotel password (!). Got a lot of work done as went to the airport early.

Interesting to read some of the mixed reviews at times for the Radisson at Kathmandu, but what I can say is that I never experienced any patchy service in the lease during my four day stay in the new wing of the hotel and the hotel was very comfortable and clean.Firstly, the Radisson website does not seem to make it very clear that a new wing was completed about a year ago.  Well actually the new wing is not attached to the original hotel, but sits across the entrance drive from it, and is effectively a standalone hotel with its own reception, bars and restaurants.  Accordingly, when I have looked at some of the photographs other guests have posted, there is perhaps a distinct difference between the original and "new wing", with a more modern look and clearly less time to become "used" as they say.The room I stayed in was very comfortable with a large LCD T.V (with a few English news channels available BBC, CNN etc).  The bathroom had a great walk in shower (no bath though) with good pressure and either overhead sprinkler or hand held option.  I had a slight problem with the TV control (flat batteries), which was quickly resolved by house keeping.  There was a room safe and decent storage.  The view was a little drab though, looking out onto part of the original hotel and local buildings, but I did not come for the room view so to speak.We ate once in the original hotel and then in the new wing restaurant the remainder of the time.  All was very enjoyable, with a pleasant choice of curries to choose from, as well as other more traditional European selections.  In the restaurant in the new wing on the 3rd floor, you could watch the staff prepare the food and the place was spotlessly clean.  The breakfast was the usual buffet affair, with a reasonable, if not extensive, choice of cold and hot food.  You also had an outdoor seating area with balcony.  There was also another outside restaurant/bar (on forth floor as I recall).The bar in the new wing is relatively small and compact, whereas a walk through the original hotel feels very much busier and noisier, so in some cases you can have the best of both worlds.  The original hotel also has a casino if you are into that and a few shops.  There are also a fee local shops adjacent to the road that runs to the hotels.There is free Wi-Fi, with a voucher system provided by a reception.  This was a bit of a pain as you had to visit them every day to pick up a new voucher code as they kept expiring.  It would be easier to provide a general password that changed say once per week as its a pain when you have multiple devices on a business trip.The staff come in for a special comment, as we were met by nothing but a smile and they were all very attentive and friendly; I always make a point of striking up a rapport with staff as its surprising what a smile back can do for improved service.The hotel also offers a free airport pickup and drop-off service so long as you pre-book it.   The drive took about 20 to 30 minutes.Overall, an enjoyable stay and would have no hesitation in returning, but would make sure its in the "new wing".

Es un hotel muy acogedor, con un excelente servicio de todo su personal, con buena ubicacion. El restaurante es muy bueno a un precio justo. Un buen alojamiento, de buen nivel, en un bellisimo lugar, lo recomendaria a quien decida viajar allí.

On the whole, I've been very unimpressed by Radissons in other parts of the world.  Generally, their staff lacks training and in this case, friendliness!!  I hold American name brands by American standards and this Radisson fell short.  Unfortunately, this was part of a tour package and our first choice of hotel (Hyatt) was fully booked, so we had to settle for the Radisson.  Upon reading other reviews, it seemed that the newer building was superior to the older building, so I requested a room in the newer one.  Upon check in, I was repeatedly told that 'even though my booking was ONLY for a standard room,' I was incredibly 'lucky' to have been upgraded to the new building.  While I appreciate the upgrade, I'm not exactly sure why they felt the need to tell me 4 times.  It was a classless.The room itself was dingy, the curtains were dusty and the furnishing were very drab.  It smelled and looked much like your grandparents' 100yr old, unchanged house.  The shower was nice as it had a rainfall shower head and the water pressure was decent.  The toiletries were obviously used several times and they came in stained yellow boxes.  The 'high-speed' internet was slower than a dial-up connection, but most of Nepal is like this.  We ordered drinks at the 4th floor terrace bar and were thrilled at the prices (only $6) for a gin martini.  When the drinks came out, the glasses were truly laughable - they looked like martini glasses for children and could fit little more than 3 thimble fulls of drink.  The staff had no idea what a 'twist' was, or the difference between dry, dirty etc etc.  I don't blame the staff, I blame the training.  If you're going to list a drink in your menu, you had better train your staff to learn how to make it.  Some of the staff were wonderful and super friendly, but I would say half were not.  Smiles were returned with completely blank stares/glares.  Breakfast was fine.  I've learned my lesson.  Never stay at a Radisson again.

Great location for exploring Kathmamdu. Within walking distance of main areas and good taxi pickups. Restaurant closed for refurb so we ate in the nearing Yeti Bar most nights,after a disappointing burger the first night at the roof top bistro in the new building.Rooms are clean, just a little jaded, but given the battles they have with power load balancing and generators it's to be expected really. Our room was next to the generator so each night it kicked in and wope us up!Breakfasts very cosmopolitan, omlettes made to order and very nice.

We spent 4 nights in feb , and was in the business class room. The rooms were clean n lovely but the food served in the business lounge was disappointing . It had limited variety .and he food was cold . We had breakfast in the coffee shop n the choice was limited , there were not staff in relation to customer and service was slow . There werenot enough tables for the guests as it was packed with people who attended a conference there . Overall it was an Ok experience

I have been a regular visitor to Radisson Kathmandu. My recent visit as well at Radisson was as enjoyable as ever.  The staff were courteous and friendly. Rooms are of decent size and good beds.  Overall a great experience. Would recommend to one and all.

The beds are too narrow. There are pigeons perched by the window at night, and once day breaks and you peek through the window you can see pigeon crap all over the window base outside (which they claim they clean only ONCE a week). The food in their restaurant is mediocre for my taste, but there's an Olive Garden just adjacent to it. Their internet is absolutely horrendous, it claims to be 512 kbps but you can barely connect at all. They can issue you a PIN code for it, and it's for ONE device only, PER DAY, which is entirely irrelevant because you can't connect or utilize it at all, so I didn't bother trying out the paid "breakneck speed" internet. Also, they use the new technology touch-keycards on their locks (tap on the door lock to open instead of inserting the card and pulling it out), which are VERY SENSITIVE. If you happen to have your keycards with your celfones in the same pocket, they will malfunction and you can't open the door to your room, so you'll have to go back to the front desk to have it re-activated again, which is extremely annoying.However, I'm giving this hotel 3 stars average just because the staff is friendly and very accommodating, especially the concierge and front desk people. You will be frequently greeted with a Namaste from the housekeeping people you encounter with vibrant smiles. So at least my atmosphere is friendly and they deserve credit for it.I would not recommend this hotel for tours, but perhaps only if you're spending one night in Katmandu on a business trip or so.

The beds are very narrow and uncomfortable. The bathrooms have see thru glass with flimsy curtains. Not suitable for double occupancy if you are not a couple. The housekeeping is very poor. The reception staff are untrained and lack basic knowledge of courtesy and etiquette. It seems that the staff are not being trained on a regular basis.The restaurant which serves breakfast is of very low standards. The temperature of the hot food on the counter are not maintained at the required temperature. The food temperature is below the danger level and when you complain to the staff they just take it away from the counter, re heat it and bring it back. This is totally against the Food Safety requirements. Again it is very apparent that the staff are not aware of basic food hygiene requirements because of lack of training. Service is also very slow. If you go for breakfast about 30 minutes before closing then you hardly find anything in the food counter. You literally have to scrape the dish. Would never recommend this property as a 4 star. Probably 2 or 2.5 star

From the moment I checked in, to the moment I checked out, I was disappointed. I was on business for one night, while my booking was made certain things were promised which were then reneged on.I had asked for my frequent flyer airline details to be upgraded, these were not, I had asked to not bill my credit card, but this was done!I would not stay here again and neither would I recommend this hotel to any one.For the price they charge, there is no value for money.

Good: Bed,  internet , Rooms in new building onlyCan be improved : long list...Bathroom should have HOT water all the timeRooms walls needs to be sound proof else should have sound control for TV.ppl need ac..so do not keep centralized heater on..Please serve breakfast atleast warm in new building Breakfast spread is good but taste is not good.Old building rooms on 3rd fl ( this is what I saw ) definately needs extra lights inside.Please offer complimentary airport pick up and drop..hotels smaller than you are offering...

We stayed here but honestly I preferred the Hyatt. The bathroom was not as clean as I expected and the service was poor. The buffet breakfast was big but not tastyThe location is good because is close to a lot of shopping places

Wir waren auf dem Rückweg von Pokhara, da der Anschlussflug sehr früh am nächsten Tag ging, haben wir eine Nacht im Radisson Kathmandu verbracht. Bei der Ankunft fragte uns der Taxifahrer in welchem Gebäudeteil wir unser Zimmer gebucht haben. Wir konnten nur sagen, wir haben ein Standardzimmer gebucht. Beim Einchecken im älteren Gebäude wurde uns mitgeteilt, dass wir ein Premium Room upgegradet werden.  Das war sehr freundlich, wir waren nur für eine Nacht hier. Also sind wir zu dem neueren Gebäude gegenüber gegangen. Unser Gepäck wurde schon auf das Zimmer gebracht. Diese war im vierten Stock und sehr groß. Glücklicherweise kein Teppich am Boden. Das Badezimmer sehr angenehm, mit Regendusche. Die Corner Bar, ein separates Gebäude gegenüber, war am Neujahrsabend nicht wirklich frequentiert. Die Cocktails waren lecker und die Atmosphäre angenehm.

L'hotel è composto di due parti, Una più vecchia e una più nuova. Io sono stato 3 volte in quella vecchia e le camere sono un pò datate e anche la pulizia della polvere è un pò limitata. Nel complesso è comunque confortevole. La colazione è eccellente e abbondante. La wireless gratuita non è molto veloce quando è sovraccarica di clienti.

Gut gelegenes Hotel in einer ruhigen Seitenstrasse, darauf achten, dass man zum Hauptbau  schaut, sonst etrwas laut, aber die anderen grossen Hotels sind fast alle an Hauptstrassen. Service, Sauberkeit alles ok für so ein Land

My wife and I got stuck by an airline who "cancelled" our flight even thought it still went to Guangzhou.  In any case they put us up and about 50 other guests at the Radisson in Kathmandu.  The rooms were just ok.  Shower had a dead bug in it (it is Nepal) and sheets looked clean but had an iron burn on them (at least I hope it was an iron burn).  I slept in my clothes just in case.We tried to get a drink, but the hotel lounge is outside across the parking lot and was way to smokey.  Open smoking in the bar - so we left and went to the "olive garden". the onsite Mediterranean restaurant.  They were open but nobody was eating.  We looked at the wine list, but to be honest 5+ times mark up compared to US seemed too pricey.  Mini bar in room is a good choice.Staff was efficient and buffet breakfast was plentiful but nothing special.  Internet worked, but slow.  I'd recommend the Hyatt Regency instead if you can afford it.

my stay was very excellent, had no problems and staff was very friendly and professional.  the room looked as if it has been remodeled.  the food was good and centrally located to areas in which i wanted to visit.

We stayed there only for one night because our plane left early in the morning, so this review is only a snapshot and might not be generally valid: our arrival offered a little surprise: after booking a Superior Room (in the old wing) we were upgraded to a Deluxe Room (in the new wing). Looking back this was maybe the worst thing that could happen to us. The room was large and clean with minor deficiencies (only one wine glass - the second was missing, no hotel slippers etc.). BUT: before going to bed I switched the air conditioning off. After about 45 min the room filled with a strong odor from combustion or diesel. The odor didn’t disappear even after restarting the ac and stayed approx. until 4 am. We didn’t complain because we were tired and needed our sleep but the next day all our clothes and luggage smelt like we had spent the night at a filling station.There is a nice bar (The Corner Bar) nearby with a tiny selection of cocktails – when we stayed there on New Year's Day it was complete empty The hotel is near to Thamel (within walking distance) and some other small restaurants nearby (we choose a fancy Vietnamese Restaurant approx. 500 m up the main road)

stayed at the radisson for 3 days. The positives are the room size, professional check in staff, good breakfast, nice spa, free airport transfers and above all, Krishna, who welcomes you at the door when you walk in, with a genuine and enthusiastic smile. The wi fi works well, though u need a separate code for very device, and need to change it after 24 hours. The housekeeping staff needs some improvement....they knocked at 8.15 am one day to do up the room, even as the kids were asleep. Also the shower taps are far too low...if u have to turn on or off a tap, you have to bend really low. Overall I enjoyed my stay at the hotel. Wish there were other facilities also like a TT table or a pool table. The property has no grounds really, but they try and make your stay as comfortable as possible.

I have  visited Kathmandu on numerous occasions and recently was there last week. As usual, I put up at the Radisson, Kathmandu. The hotel provides free airport pick-up and drop which is part of the package.The guards at the doors offer you a very warm welcome. Once at the reception, the staff there is very friendly and will provide you with your free wi-fi coupon, breakfast coupons and room keys. A person will guide you to your room. The rooms are spic and pretty good. A 32 inch LCD on the wall provides for many channels. The toilets are clean and the room is cleaned twice a day. Complimentary 2 bottles of mineral water, tea, coffee maker at the room are available. The breakfast in the mornings has a nice spread consisting of continental food, Indian foods, eggs, breads, cereals, bacon, sausages etc.There is a fitness center at the hotel on the 4th floor. There is also a new wing which has modern newer rooms but I personally like the old wing as this is more cosy and homely.A swimming pool is there for in-house guests at the terrace. The pool is well maintained. In all, you will have a great experience here especially because the staff are well trained and very warm. I love the Radisson at Kathmandu. A definite recommendation from my end.

Prepare for bad room service especially cleaning, long waits for food ordered, grumpy dining and an unpleasant vibe all around. Definitely not worth the price they charge to stay there. Spa services are good, however the times of fitness center, pool and dining are only available until 11pm, so if you would like to have a nice relaxed time after a very long day, it won't be possible.

This place was absolutely beautiful, but like most other places they were much over priced! The Radisson is on a big lot off the main road. The whole place is very aesthetically pleasing and the guys working there are helpful, kind, and sweet. The included breakfast was good and was consumed around a common table, that made i want to stay more

Overall experience is ok. Internet connection is not as speed as they say.. House keeping staffs were friendly and polite Fun café food..ok ok Break fast spread.. not at Radission level Location wise is comfortable for my business

I had a fantastic experience at the Radisson, Lazimpat, Kathmandu, Nepal.  I was in the new building or VIP wing(?). The staff were so incredibly nice.  I was there for a wedding and needed to put on a saree. Needless to say, I was not adept at this.  I had two very helpful hotel employees who's names now escape me :-(, with these tasks.  I was pleasantly surprised that everyone was so incredibly nice about this and helpful.  I see the other reviews about the internet and yes, it was pretty shotty, but Kathmandu has rolling blackouts, so you just have to deal with that.  Luckily the hotels have generators which most locals do not, so it comes back on in less than a min.  The internet is also very expensive in the country so the passwords change all of the time.  However, it was very easy to just call the reception and have the password updated to me.  The air was also a bit of an issue, but nothing that was too terrible.  They change the air from hot to cold or vice versa and that's the only air you get.  But as with the wifi, once I called someone came and updated it for me, so there was no heat just blowing air. The room is gorgeous and fantastic bathroom.  There was a weird view of the parking lot with stray dogs (!) but it is Kathmandu and not Paris so do keep that in mind.  I had breakfast in my room each morning and was very pleased with the food (American and Nepali) and the service.  I had my laundry done and received it the next day, clean and pressed, which was awesome since I had been traveling already ALOT.  Overall I really enjoyed this hotel, perhaps the location is not prime and the internet shotty, but the service really makes up for it all.

One of the best hotels around, cozy, comfortable, romantic and excellent service. From the security staff to the staff behind the reception, concierge, in the restaurants are very helpful and there Corner bar is a great place to spend the evenings

The old building and rooms are not maintained in good conditions.All the interiors in room and wash room are of poor quality.No water for some time and when supply restored it was water with rust.Food quality average.

Stayed on 6th floor of 'new building' for 4 nights early December 2014. Agree totally with other comments here. Staff are very welcoming and helpful, but rooms have lots of issues. Wardrobe doors jamming which keeps light on all night,horrible mold on the blinds inside bathroom, terrible wifi that kicks you off every 5 minutes and is pegged at 512kbs when you can connect. No hot water in bathroom sink for first two days. Gave up complaining to staff and got under sink to find stop cock turned off ? Rooms have a surprisingly wide range of TV channels but the picture & sound quality is so poor that many are almost un-watchable. However the really disappointing aspect was the total lack of Air conditioning. Outside temperatures were around 24 - 26 deg C. Room was at least this temperature. Staff advised that the aircon had been switched off due to the season and nothing could be done to rectify it. Their only solution was to open the windows. Dogs barking outside at night and high levels of pollution made this a pretty unattractive option. Putting this all in perspective, rate was only around USD100 per night, so could be considered getting what you pay for ?

I recently stayed at this hotel on a business trip (the new wing). On arrival I and other colleagues were welcomed with a drink - guava juice, I think. The check-in was quick and efficient, and the front office staff were very friendly and professional. I was given my key, and - a highly surprising element - a one-day Wi-Fi ticket. Overall, I think this hotel fulfills its purpose, is clean, and convenient, but for the rest of it - I'll break this review down to make it easier to read.Room: The room is spacious, with nice bedsheets and a couple of types of pillows - the softer and harder kind. There is a table, a couple of mirrors, tv (with no international channels), a comfy armchair with an ottoman for lounging. All your basic hotel stuff. Nothing luxurious, but suited me fine. The mattress on the bed is hard, but quite comfy. No luxury like at a Conrad or Hilton, but very nice to sleep on nonetheless. As I sat on the bed attempting to talk to my family and let them know I was there safely, something flew past me and landed on the floor, scurrying away. A lizard. I'm a crazy person who thinks lizards can and will, under certain circumstances, kill you in the night... so that freaked me out. However, ceiling lizard didn't reappear for the rest of my trip... wonder what he was eating this whole time, hiding under my bed like that.The bathroom has no bathtub, but that's fine, as few people take baths, I suppose... still, I was a little disappointed, as I really wanted a bath after my long travel. Settled for a shower. My room, for some reason, had busted shower controls, and I was unsuccessful in making my rain shower stop. I ended up wasting a lot of water, because both the shower head and the rain shower were working at the same time. The shower door didn't hold all the water in the shower, and the threshhold was too small, so there was water in the bathroom after every shower. There is a normal enough hair dryer, and all the shampoo/lotion/other stuff you'd expect. Overall a nice bathroom, if they make sure the rain shower and the shower head work as expected.Wi-Fi: the Wi-Fi there is horrid. The very basic of applications, like chat applications, refused to work. I tried Skyping with my family, and completely failed. Forget video chat, even voice chat wasn't possible! Added to that, you have to get that stupid Wi-Fi ticket every day! It was a pain. However, as I later found out, you could ask the front desk staff to extend your ticket, and they'd do it for a certain number of days. But they don't tell you that up front. You have to either be driven crazy by the every day tickets, and ask them yourself, or have someone smarter than me tell you that up front. Restaurant: for the first couple of meals, I ate at the 3rd floor restaurant. The breakfast spread is quite sufficient - there is a number of Nepali dishes, 2-3 types of sausages, boiled eggs (and you can ask them for scrambled or an omelette), a good selection of breads, some local cheese, cereal, jams, etc. Bottomless coffee (thank heavens for coffee...), and juices. But don't go there for lunch or dinner. The menu choices are few, and are NOT good. I had a chicken curry the first time, and some pasta the second... the curry was bland, and lacked flavor. The pasta was horrifically greasy, oil was floating on the bottom, it was disgusting honestly. The very friendly staff was worried I didn't like it, and even went to the kitchen to ask why my pasta had so much oil, and she was told that it's due to the pesto. Well, maybe this was my error in ordering it in the first place, but... pesto shouldn't separate like that, In my opinion, and there shouldn't be 5 tablespoons of oil on the bottom of my pasta. Ever. Maybe i'm just picky. And i thought that the price was NOT equal to the quality.Random: I am a person that gets cold easily, and I like to turn the heat on sometimes. On trying to turn the heat on in the room, I found out that it only worked in "humid" and "cold" settings (as indicated by the little water droplet and the snowflake on the LCD). I called the front desk to inquire how i could turn the heat on, and was told the most ridiculous of things - that as the hotel was on central heating, I COULDN'T HAVE HEAT until ALL THE ROOMS WANTED HEAT. Seriously? I had to demand that they bring me a heater, which they immediately did, so it was of some help. But come on! I know it's not the middle of winter or anything, but this is an international hotel chain and I should be able to change the temperature of my own room without having to wait for everyone else to have the same reaction to surrounding temperatures as my own body! That was completely unacceptable. On the day of checking out, I discovered by accident that the door to my room wasn't locking. AT ALL. As in, I'd been living in a room with a door that was permanently open. It closed, but if you just pushed it, it opened again. I usually use the latch at night, but during the day, when I was out of the room, it was completely open. In my opinion, this was completely unacceptable, and the room and the LOCK on the room should have been checked by the hotel to make sure that everything worked as it should. I was very upset at having found this out.The sound isolation isn't too good. I had some noisy guys staying in the room next to me, and I could hear them TALKING, I could hear their TV, everything... forget it if anyone was walking down the hall talking, it was like they were in my room. All in all, I might stay at this hotel again if i want a more or less convenient location, but I would not recommend it if there's another choice. 2 years ago I stayed at the Dwarika Hotel, and I found the rooms, hotel itself, the food, everything - MUCH nicer.

Arrival 3/5. After 5 nights in lovely and peaceful Pokhara, Kathmandu was bit of a shock - really busy and dusty. A NR750 (£5) cab ride from the KTM Domestic Terminal. Check in was efficient, if a bit impersonal (well it is a Raddison). Room 4/5. We were in room 612 on the 6th floor. A typical corporate room. Quite small, but well appointed. 2 single beds with quality linen. Large flat tv. In-room safe. Mini bar, desk, tea/coffee & phone. No balcony. Views across bustling Kathmandu to the mountains beyond. Plenty of storage. Not many power sockets for charging phones etc, but there were both round 2 pin and UK 3 pin sockets.Bathroom 3/5. Small, but again well appointed. Full size bath with shower above. Hair dryer. Plenty of toiletries and nice towels. Good mirrors. Power socket. Our main problem was that the floor flooded with every shower. The bath was slightly tilted and the water ran onto the floor every time. We eventually made a towel dam to stem the flood. We should have moved rooms, but didn't bother as we were only here for a few nights.Staff - 4/5. Generally very good.Location 3/5. You could be anywhere in Kathmandu, but there are some shops and a good supermarket nearby.Food 4/5. Breakfast - a nice selection of hot food. Egg cooking station. Good omlettes and some fine fish. Some cereals, fruits & yogurt. Dinner - 3 restaurants. An a la carte in the main lobby, with a buffet and an a la carte restaurant in a separate building. The two that we tried were fine, if a bit pricey.Value n/a. We were part of a tour, so we did not know the hotel cost.Overall 4/5. 3.5/5 really. It's a typical business hotel. Slick and efficient, though with little character.

Stanze business ottime con buona pulizia e ampissime. Molto confortevoli. Servizio buono, buono anche il servizio colazione. É possibile usufruire della spa dell hoteladiacente: i prezzi sono convenienti e il servizio di buon livello. Personale di servizio disponibile e competente, soprattutto il ragazzo addetto alla lounge del primo piano. Consigliatissimo

We stayed twice at the beginning and end of a tour to Nepal.  The rooms are a good size and the beds are quite firm but we slept well.  There is a large wardrobe with safe, tea/coffee making facilities, a large flat-screen TV (did not watch), decent aircon and a good shower with toiletries provided.  The breakfast buffet has a good selection but there can be a long queue for eggs which are cooked to order.  One black mark though - breakfast starts at 0630 and when we arrived at 0645 for an early departure, some of the hot dishes were already running out; plenty of staff but not much organisation to make sure all dishes and butter, etc were topped up immediately.  Staff generally were friendly and approachable, especially the doormen who were always polite and smiling.

This is a good hotel in an excellent position for accessing the airport and Thamel. Not much to do around the hotel but enough. Swimming pool is ok and affords a view over Kathmandu. Generally the service was fine but slow and pretty good for Nepal.

Spacious and nice room in the new building. Friendly staff around but quite unhelpful and tough speaking staff at the front desk. Breakfast tastes good but similar choices for my four days experience. It was located at 15 minutes walking distance from Thamel area and it may cost 150 to 250 NPR, if you grab a cab. The environment is peaceful and you can find small shops around hotel. The dining experience was not that perfect but there are some restaurants around. A nearby mini mart would be a perfect place to buy snacks and drinks. Money changers around with reasonable rate. If you ask me 'cost for value', I will say 'depends on you'.

My friend and I stayed here for five days after a trek in the Annapurna region. The hotel is a great place to relax and I highly recommend the day spa for some relaxation and pampering to feel human again. The food on offer is terrific - pretty much anything you want is available. The staff are delightful and deliver a high quality service.

I have stayed here on numerous occasions on work and I have to admit that this hotel is extremely nice from all aspects.The staff is real warm and courteous and eager to help. The rooms are well appointed and comfortable. The location is rather in a domestic colony so the surroundings are not that impressive. Leaving that the Cafe Shop, the poolside bar, the other eateries at the hotel serve good food. Service in the room is great and elsewhere.I can easily recommend this hotel to all visitors from across the globe. You will feel safe here and at home.

It is a little strange when you go to the Radisson in Kathmandu. It has two separate buildings! The one I stayed n was comfortable but definitely dated and if I wanted a bar or to eat I needed to cross the small road and go to the 'newer' building across the road. That had a nice roof terrace bar with views to the hills and decent food. The newly opened spa in the basement was clearly suffering from some opening teething problems (always a bit worrying when the foot spa they give you is linked to an extension lead with live wires and no plug) but the manicure and pedicure was excellent- unbelievably thorough. Good service from all the staff.

The wifi is not good at all especially in the 6th floor The food is average but good comparing to Kathmandu food quality.  The staff were nice and helped us in all requests but they need more training in the customer service   The location is good

Horrible value for the outrageous rates.  Food was bismal.  No hot water.  Non-functioning toilets.  Staff non-responsive.  Internet was extremely slow and 'codes' the hotel staff gave didn't work half the time, so had to call the front desk numerous times for working codes.  Wouldn't stay again.

I stayed in a club room in the old wing and have to admit it is terrible. The rooms really need a makeover. The carpets in the old wing of the hotel stink and it generally looks really dingy. What was really annoying despite asking the hotel staff numerously to give us the best room they recommended the club room with is  really dated. Luckily I managed to move to the new wing after 1 night and the rooms there are much better. Not impressed by the service offers by the reservation team. The hotel needs to have a quick makeover if they want to still service the Raddison brand.

Buena ubicación y excelente trato por el personal. El baño era mejorable. El transfer del aeropuerto al hotel funcionó estupendamente. Nos hubiese gustado que nos informaran que la piscina no se hallaba en el mismo edificio en el que nos alojabamos

The hotel is spread in two buildings which is uncomfortable as the swimming pool is located in the main building. The driver came to pick me up and we nearly lost each other for the same reason. The room is cosy and overall comfortable. Good shower. TV set is huge with lots of channels but didn't show US Open so I was disappointed. The wifi arrangement was akward when you have to get new password every 24 hours. Very inconvenient. Lastly, the breakfast was very average. The good point in its favour was that the egg station was located behind the counter so this was one hotel where you don't get all smelly after breakfast.

Just stayed here for 3 nights on business, overall experience was average. The location is slightly away from Durbar Marg, the service is average and the food in the coffee shop much below average. Moreover, the options in the menu and the breakfast buffet are also very limited. The service needs to improve as well.

Over all very good hotel. Airport to and fro transfers are very convenient provided by hotel. Excellent Breakfast spread, good fresh rooms but only in new wing. Friendly and courteous staff.  Good pool and health club

This property is one of the better hotels in Kathmandu but it has to live up to the name. Areas that need improvement are the following:- The rooms in the hotel are have aged and are in need of some refurbishing.- The bathroom fittings need to be replaced (they are falling off!)- The fitness centre can use some facelift and a few new machines- The electricity backup and hence the internet connectivity can be enhancedThe good points:- The staff is most polite and helpful- The food spread is good and tasteful.All in all this is an average hotel and does not measure up against the costs it charges.

Service was excellent, room adequate, ambiance --could be anywhere.  so had no feeling that i was in Nepal, too little local color.  was US chain transplanted. there was disco next door so was noisy.  excellent location.

I was really looking forward to this stay,but next time I won't stay here again.Why?Check-in: not the best check-In ever, wrong information, not referring to the travel desk in old building, ect Breakfast: poor quality and hot dishes were cold. Dinner buffet: Again poor quality and some warm food was really cold. Room: upgraded to the new 2nd building however:- no double glass at the window  very noisy since we had street view.- bathroom: not very clean and fungi in the room :(- unpleasant smell in the roomThe hotel is known at the market for the weddings and parties. So every day and night we had parties and noise ,loud music.  I would advise the guest upon check-in about those events.  I'm not the person to complain but this was unacceptable. Staying in downtown Kathmandu ie Thamel can be intimidating experience. As a regular vistor, I would advise against it. A good option is the Radisson in the Lazimpat area. We have stayed in this hotel several times over recent years as it is the start and end point for World Expeditions trips and treks. It always makes me feel comfortable and happy to return to this lovely hotel. The staff are exceptional, very kind and obliging. The trekking company booked a twin room for us but the reception staff managed to get us a double room which was our preference. Rooms: The rooms are well appointed, spotless, and very comfortable - lovely hot water in the shower without fail. Wifi can be a little slow but most of the time was fine for us. One suggestion for the hotel is to have limitless filtered drinking water for guests - guests are given two bottles a day but this is not enough and generates a lot of plastic waste. Dining: Breakfast buffet is amazing! There is so much choice which is a little overwhelming after a trek. They do omelettes and eggs cooked to order, and used to do masala dosa to order although on our last visit, this was not advertised. Coffee is percolated coffee unless you pay extra but very nice and bottomless. The TFC restaurant is also a great option for lunch or dinner - prices are reasonable (lunch for two with non-alcoholic drinks cost us 2600 Rs) and the food is very tasty. Location:On my first visit, I thought the location was a bit of a limitation, but now I think it is really ideal. It is a 10-15 minute walk from Thamel along Lazimpat, and just so much quieter than Thamel. The area has lots of embassies, so there are a range of restaurants and cafes around. The street in front of the hotel has a well stocked supermarket, money exchange, laundry service, gift shops and trekking gear shops and there are ATMs nearby. There are some very cool shops on Lazimpat if you walk in the north direction (away from Thamel). It is also a short walk to Durbar Marg, which was really handy as they have a NCell office (for my local SIM) as well as banks and airline offices. There are many shops and fast food restaurants on Durbar Marg. Our usual preference is small boutique hotels rather than large international chains but there is something very reliable about Kathmandu Radisson and we have enjoyed our stay here every time. It is expensive compared to guesthouses but in the normal range for a 5 star hotel. We had a very average experience in a Thamel hotel that cost USD 100 per night before transferring to the Radisson and I was wishing I paid a little more for the Radisson - you get what you pay for! Happily recommend this hotel to friends and family, and would definitely stay here again.

首都にあるのでリゾート施設はないが、客室はきれいで満足いくものでした。小さなことですが、各プラグ対応のマルチタップがあり変換プラグなしに日本のものが4口あったのは便利でした。

A good place to stay especially with family and for business purposes as well. The location and view from the hotel is excellent. The hotel and it's it's cleanliness are well maintained. Only thing required is to improve the variety of meals for vegetarians.

Clean and excellent service from Radisson in KsthKathm - well done. No issues encountered during 7 nights stay. Staff were friendly, polite and respectful through out the stay. An exemplar service offered.

Beautiful rooms, and the staff was very attentive to our needs and comfort. Was given an amazing surprise of a birthday cake in my room...so thoughtful, and it definitely left me smiling! :) Highly recommended!!

The hotel is a nice place to stay in Kathmandu with friendly staff. The Olive Garden on the ground floor serves a nice pizza. The business class offers a happy hour served by very attentive and friendly staff. Also, the food at the breakfast and happy hour is great.

Accueil parfait sur l'ensemble de mon séjour. De plus, le personnel de l'hôtel a été très prévenant et m'a beaucoup aidé dans les démarches administratives après la perte de mon passeport. Un très grand merci.

Noisy. Good bed. Standard international atmosphere, nothing special. Used the spa they tried to charge me more than what was advertised online. Food ok but also overpriced. Good location to access Thamel

This is a well run hotel.  The breakfast  buffet was great.  Thamel was within walking distance or 300 rubles by taxi.  There are a few tourist shops nearby, a grocery store and a Dal baht place.  The place felt safe.
#NAME?

We stayed for three days during our trip,the tour of Nepal. Modern, clean,luxurious in the heart of Kathmandu. The stuff was really friendly and always with a smile on their face. Breakfast and dinner were excellent too, with a great variety of local and western selection. Of course I  can recommend this hotel.

This hotel was friendly and inviting.  The spa was nice and the prices were great.  The food was interesting and plentiful and the bar prices were also fair.  It was nice to have access to a swimming pool, and there was a changing room and plenty of lounge chairs.

Rooms in the old wing are finally upgraded. Good experience.  However, air ventilation needs improvement.Weather was perfect. Wish the windows could be opened to let fresh air enter the room.Buffet Breakfast was good with many choices. Idlis are there everyday bit boring and need to improve. Wished Vada is added on some days. Omelette are really fresh and customized to taste of the guests. Fruit quality this time was just OK. Papaya was not well ripened.Pasta options are great too in Lunch with many types of sweets. Fruits options were not as much on some days. These days people want more fruits and salads. Please add more of these.

Hotel, rooms and staff were excellent.No complains.Try avoiding ordering Chicken Dishes at the TFC Restaurant, as the Chef doesnt know how to cook chicken.He couldnt prepare a Chicken dish even after 2 attempts. Finally, I ended up ordering a vegetarian dish, as I didnt want to take any more risks with their meat cooking.

I stayed at Radisson for almost a week and feel like home: the room is large and clean, staff is friendly, location is at the heart of the city, breakfast is wonderful. Just very very short time, internet was in an unknown issue but it is not worth to count.Will come back, no doubt!

โรงแรมมีสองอาคาร ได้พักในส่วนอาคารใหม่ ห้องพักไม่ค่อยกว้าง ความสะอาดดี สิ่งอำนวยความสะดวกพอเพียง ทำเลค่อนข้างดี ไม่ไกลจาก thamel หน้าปากซอยมีร้านขายของ และร้านอาหารอยู่บ้าง อาหารเช้ายังไม่ค่อยถูกปาก พนักงานยิ้มแย้มดี

I have stayed in many different hotels in Kathmandu and the Radisson remains my favorite overall. The staff are excellent, the hotel is clean, the pool is in a excluded location and great for swimming, the breakfast buffet is exceptionally yummy. I also like the location better than Durbar Marg, Thamel, and Kupandole… A great place to stay.

We really appreciate the dedicated team who help us for the organisation of our EU conference.Radisson Hotel is perfectly located and offers nice facilities and delicious breakfast .I would come back for private Kathmandou visit

I always love staying at this hotel when I travel to Kathmandu for work. The location is great (super walkable to Thamel and other good restaurants). The staff are always friendly, saying hello when I return at the end of the day. The room is very comfortable, so comfortable that I fell asleep at 6pm everynight for the first week due to jet lag. If any of my work colleagues need a recommendation I always recommend they stay at the Radisson.

Location, room cleaness, and breakfast service was good.  Hope to expand the facility of bar for the spending night time of guests.  One thing I ask is for guest check out, have a time a little more and check something missed by guest is much better. Actuall I left my skin cosmetic in the room and if possible, I want to receive it.

Situated almost at the heart of city, this one provides a calm and quiet stay. Slightly off the main road, identification may be slightly tricky.Very spacious lobby and reception welcomes you at the hotel. Rooms are spacious. Room numbering is slightly tricky as even numbers and odd numbers are kept on both sides of the way. Facilities include loaded bar, TV , toiletries and a high speed free wi-fi. The morning buffet have a large variety of indian dishes but in a local taste.Overall rating for the fare being paid is 8.6/10

Hôtel calme, bien placé dans un quartier très vivant, commerçant en plein centre de Kathmandu. Dans le tumulte de la ville au fond d’une impasse vous trouverez un jardin calme avec ses chants d’oiseaux et la plénitude nécessaire après une journée de visites ou de déambulations dans les rues du quartier des bazars où ce trouve l’hôtel.
