The sunset view from the helipad is really peaceful and the panoramic view on the Himalayas seems breathtaking from the resort, nevertheless we didn't get a chance to admire due to a very cloudy sky our entire stay. They do propose several activities to enjoy but being exhausted from all the walking and hiking, we just booked a massage at their spa and it was divine, the best we've had in Nepal.

The hospitality was exceptional, with incredibly friendly staff who provided top-notch customer service.The food was fantastic, and overall, our experience was truly memorable. We're grateful to the staff who went the extra mile to ensure our stay was unforgettable.

Beautiful. Fantastic. Amazing staff. One of the best experiences of my life. The location is spectacular. The buildings are so well thought out. The facilities are great. The food and bar were wonderful. This is how great Nepal is. Thank you.

My stay at The Terraces was just what I needed after trekking in the Himalayas. The staff was very welcoming and friendly. The atmosphere was relaxing and calming, and the food was supreme. I went for the Sound Healing session which was super nice. Highly recommend for anyone in need of a break from the hustle and bustle of everyday life.

The best hill station resort we have ever been to.beautiful view excellent chef Mr dipak mishra along with him team provided super food .thanks for the special arrangements made for our special day. Mr Suman the gm was a super host with excellent hospitality.highly recommend
Everything is just great about this place. Me and my wife had a lot of fun.Great view , friendly staff , best food and a wonderful stay. 5/5
Hospitality was great, staff were amazing. Food is just delicious, yummy. A great place to be with family, friends and business colleagues.

The hotel is set in a beautiful location, amazing attentive staff, the infinity pool looking over the Kathmandu skyline (sadly it was very hazy so we didn’t see the mountains) Food selection was great and very tasty, perfect stay if you’re looking to switch off from life

Our stay was very relaxing and enjoyable.....The staff were all very friendly and helpful....Top notch hospitality and facilities...The rooms were clean and the private balcony was wonderful with a stunning view of the city lights at night...The food was also good...Highly recommended!

We stayed 5 nights and was wonderful all employees was wonderful helpful polite fast, Binod of them .Good facilities yoga sound hilling spa meditation massage is really nice for the person that like to stay only here to relax as is not for going to the center and coming back but is nice place

Everything was so nice- the staff, the amenities, and the rooms. You get the royal treatment here and everyone really goes above and beyond. The hotel itself has an amazing view from anywhere you stand. I have never had such a great experience.

we had an amazing experience, the food was delicious, overall we enjoyed it :)Atmosphere was serene with the nearby nature, couldn't have been than this for the weekend getaway! we hope to come back  and stay for longer time and do some fun hiking or biking.

From the moment we stepped through the magnificent doors to The Terraces we had a most wonderful experience. The staff are just fantastic everywhere and share in the appreciation of the mountain views. As you walk around the hotel the views are breathtaking and sunrise is very special. Sundowners on the helipad was a lovely first evening. The beds are super comfy and the shower's lovely and warm. Food is outstanding and beautifully fresh. The inhouse made winter infusion spirits were a great accompaniment to the hot tub in the afternoons. John was very attentive at the pool and in the restaurant and Rabin is so friendly and helpful, enjoying the morning views. Tenzing is an enthusiastic and passionate leader and shares his love of the space with guests. We would thoroughly recommend this place for a relaxing serene break.

Rabin makes me fell so relax and nice that i truly wanna praise him for the best serves provided by him. I believe with him your hotel will be better.The cooking class is good too，my wife and i all take hiking class and yoga class，which really filled with culture

We had a wonderful time at this beautiful and peaceful resort. All of the staff were so helpful in coordinating our experiences, the views were amazing, and the food is top-notch. Shout out to Rabin for making our time in Kathmandu so special!

Absolutely superb in every way. Was a great place to have a conference with every request acted on quickly with enthusiasm. Couldn't recommend it more highly. From the hiking, to the super-chef to the outstanding manager - we were impressed at every turn.

Excellent service from arrival to departure. Staff is very professional, friendly and helpful.  Love this place. We loved every minute and will definitely go back thanks..……………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………..

Tremendously happy with the service. Staff is very helpful and attentive, and ensured that our stay was as relaxing and enjoyable as possible. There are also some lovely utilities, of which I would strongly recommend participating.

Stayed at the Terraces for 3 nights with my family and it was a very memorable stay. The resort itself was beautiful, with stunning views of the Himalayan range and Kathmandu valley. The service was the best I'd ever received at a resort. The food was delicious and nourishing. Some highlights from our short stay below:- The rooms were very comfortable and well heated (temperatures went down to 6 degrees Celsius/42 degrees Fahrenheit). The beds were very comfortable to sleep in (we all had uninterrupted sleep after a long day), the mini bar was complimentary (had beer, soft drinks and snacks), the bathroom amenities were great, and the terrace (each room comes with one) was quite large with outdoor seating and breathtaking views of the mountain peaks and the valley. Also, every evening the resort arranges a sunset viewing 'ceremony' up on the helipad (5 mins walk from the resort) where they served us hot drinks and delicious snacks. The sunset views were indescribable (see photos).- The resort grounds were also beautiful, with plenty of spaces to sit outside and enjoy some masala tea, or get warm by an outdoor fire. We did yoga twice at the beautifully located yoga pavilion. Our instructor - Adarsh - was excellent. We also used the spa for massages and sauna - all excellent experiences.- The staff were incredible and anticipated all our needs. They were very polite and helpful, and even accommodated special requests like bringing over a giant heat lamp to our terrace so we could hang out comfortably during the chilly evenings. Special shout out to the following staff: Mensura - who was finishing up here internship - who was very kind and helpful. When one of our family members hurt themselves during a hike earlier in the day, Mensura assisted them when we went up to the helipad to watch the sunset, and even wrapped up their ankle with a bandage!Other staff who were extremely helpful - Nishan, Binod, Sujan, Tulku. Also special shoutout to the person at the front desk (forgetting his name) who drove our injured family member back to the resort from the helipad on the ATV.We also had a chance to chat with the resort owner and General Manager who were both lovely.- Food: The food was delicious. The buffet breakfast spread included both continental/western and Nepali cuisine, and we particularly enjoyed the chole bhature. For lunch and dinner, the food items were also delicious, particularly the momos and the chicken thalis (which we tried twice during our trip). The head chef was also very friendly and engaging, and cooked trout for us for dinner one night and also prepared delicious local snacks for us to eat up on the hilltop.We will definitely visit again!

Perched on top of a mountain overlooking the three ancient cities of Nepal with spectacular 180 views of the Himalayan range, this has to be one of the top resortsIn the world. Everything is wonderful - from the moment you arrive  (after a bit of a bumpy ride towards the end of the hour long drive from Kathmandu - highly recommend the property transfers) you are nestled in a calm oasis of tranquility with luxurious rooms, facilities and amenities. The staff are all very hardworking and ever ready to go over and beyond to meet guest requirements. The seasoned Executive chef, Deepak Mishra, carves out culinary delight after delight and the custom made food is super delicious with top notch ingredients. The spa provides excellent massages with professional therapists. Yoga is provided by Yogi Adesh, who is a master in his trade and energizes the start to the day. There are variety of activities and organized hikes topping it up with the dramatic sunset on the helipad area with super selection of snacks and drinks every evening. Terraces resort is the perfect place to unwind and connect with nature.

Experience was awesome. Great view of the mountain range from the resort as well as from the room. Super clean room and the service were also nice. The resort is a quiet and a peaceful place for a quick getaway.

The Terraces offers spectacular views of the Himalayan range and all three historical cities of Nepal in the valley below. We loved its elegant blend of minimalistic and traditional interiors with exceptionally relaxing ambience be it in the spacious rooms with scenic balcony or just strolling through the serene nature surroundings. My mother and I felt totally pampered by the most welcoming, friendly, gracious, and professional staff members who made us feel so comfortable every minute of our stay at The Terraces. Morning bird-watching, outdoor yoga, a guided hike in the neighboring hills or happy hour watching stunning sunsets, rekindling childhood memories by flying kites (during Dasain), and after-dinner fun games for guests made our stay extra special and memorable. I highly recommend spending at least two nights at The Terraces next time you’re in Nepal - it’s a hidden paradise waiting for you just an hour outside the bustling city of Kathmandu - with a wonderful crew eager to give you a spectacular stay all year round but especially during the holiday season with their special holiday packages. It’s one of the best getaways so close to KTM. Namaste, Happy Holidays and Thank You to everyone at The Terraces - till our next visit! Happy Holidays to all reading this post!

Had an excellent Ayurvedic massage session with Malina and Sapana. We have had massages around the world but these two ladies put them to shame. Excellent view of the himalayas and the surrounding terrains.

Great escape from the hustle and bustle of the city life.Peaceful and calm environment with lovely great hospitality.If you are looking to come during the winters I would suggest to bring in warm clothes.

Exceptional service, comfortable and modern rooms, fantastic dining and drinks menus, multiple locations and facilities throughout the resort to unwind and relax. We could not have asked for a better stay - thank you!

Everything was so nice 😍😍😍Rooms were very clean 💖💖Staff were all very friendly 💖💖💖Food was very good 🍕🍟🍔🥬🍅🍑🫛🥥Also the drinks🍷🥂🍺🍷🥂🍻Spa very efficient 🌺🌺🌺Only missing a small supermarket or gift shopThanks to everyone in this magnificent place

Very cool place..lovely ambience..esp best time to visit is start of the summers before rainy season..very warm and hospitable staffs and managers..just need a improved roads this place will have fotfall like anything..

This place has my heart. The peacefulness and the mesmerizing view from it is mindblowing. I liked how everyone was friendly and attentive. Spa was amazing!! I will absolutely visit this place once again with my family.

We had a wonderfull stay at The Terraces. The infrastructure is top, the views are amazing, the team spoiles you, and the food is great. But above all the staff makes you feel at home. This was a stay that I will always remember.

So many little extras in this package. Enjoyed everything. Sunset, quiz, bingo.But as well as that everything else was great:comfortable, really tasty food and great selection of vegetarian options. Nice hot water in the super, great jacuzzi and steam room. Pool looked good but I'm not brave enough to get in at this time of year!!I will just have to come again in warmer season 😊Thankyou for a great stay
We had a very good and relaxing 2 night 3 days at The Terraces. We will most definitely come back again. Everything was very good and the best part was the resort people. Very nice, very helpful 👍😁❤️

Great hospitatility! Managing director was humble, individually greeting the guest, budding goodbye and the overall staff were super! They made our stay very comfortable! Not to forget the maginificinet view!  LLoved every bit of stay.

The place and the view is amazing…And so is the food…Had variety of Salad and dessert all were amazing Special thanks to the Chef who attended us personally…The rooms are comfortable and spacious The staffs are very welcoming

What a sublimely awesome experience👏👏This place is something else! amazing design, fantastic staff, and a truly luxurious 7 star experience overlooking Kathmandu…well done to the owners in their vision and their General Manager on the quality service and guest engagement- will certainly be back when next I. Kathmandu👍

Went with my dad and created many wonderful memories. Chef Deepak was incredibly hospitable to us. We inquired whether there were any cooking classes we could do to learn how to prepare traditional Nepalese cuisine. Chef Deepak, together with the resorts’ management team and staff organised an amazing cooking lesson by the poolside where we were taught how to make Momo and Bara which are Nepalese dumplings and pancakes. This was such a wonderful experience given to my dad and I which we will cherish for a long time. Our yoga instructor Aadesh is an incredible spiritual teacher. Trust me, he’s really good. Super wide and down to earth. Ask for him if you intend to do yoga sessions in the morning.We also went for trekking and mountain biking with Rajendra. He bought me water and drinks along the way because I had not brought any. We visited the villages around the resort, went to a trout farm and even played some board games at a local shop. Wonderful experience.The view here at the terraces is always magnificent. The best time to come is closer to the end of the year, around late September or early October. This is when the fog clears up and the view of the mountains will be extremely clear.Food: Chef Deepak Yoga: AadeshTrekking: Rajendra

Excellent rooms and great customer service. The bed was very comfortable and the views of Kathmandu and surrounding districts are breathtaking. My team and I had a retreat there for a weekend and the service was great.

Loved the location and the view!! We spent so much time on outside patio (terraces) , and cabana by the pool. Cabanas were available all the times, even on Friday night!!! Foods were amazing!! Free minibar was a plus!! Kids loved the pool and jacquizzi and so did we!!I wish the roads were better but it is not Resort’s  fault!!!

The Terraces Resort exceeded my expectations! I thoroughly enjoyed my stay with my family and young nieces. The rooms are so warm and inviting. We experienced good sleep throughout. The staff are all so friendly and super attentive. The hospitality and service is beyond excellent... much better than any other resort experience I've had in other 5 star establishments in Nepal. The pool was exceptionally clean and soothing to the senses. A serene oasis, away from Kathmandu's and life's everyday chaos. The cuisine was also delicious with a multitude of options. I highly recommend this resort and certainly look forward to more relaxing getaways at The Terraces.

Great hospitality 🥂 amazing experience We came with our American cousins. We are satisfied with the service and want to visit again. Roads are very scary though. We almost thought we can’t make it to the resort.

Such a beautiful and well kept property. Adheres to international standards. Suman was beyond excellent in his welcome and service ... the food was delightful. Each and every dish had a unique flavor. And never known the buffet to have every dish tasty. Lovely simplistic architect too. Thank you to the staff for making it so lovely ..great team effort under fantastic guidance

A single word can be 'wow'. What's a beautiful experience. It's only 1 hour from kathmandu Airport. As soon as you enter, a feeling comes of serene atmosphere. Absolutely no pollution and so calm and peaceful.  It feels like a piece of heaven. Service is superb and staff is very friendly.

One of the best resort i have ever stayed. Staff were super nice and there were lot of activities to do.room were comfortable and spacious. All utilities were available. View and swimming pool was exceptional. All staff wete friendly.

The view was stunning, there is a viewpoint uphill where the resort provides complimentary snacks and drinks, the place is awesome. We enjoyed the sunset from our huge balcony. There is a good sauna and steam bath, a jacuzzi, and a billiard. There is a possibility of using mountain bikes but the ride would be tough. So we preferred to go trekking which was so enjoyable. You can also rent ATVs and go around. There was a variety of food in the restaurant. The staff are super nice and helpful. The distance to the hotel is not long from the city, yet it is off-road. So, it is rough. Transportation is provided by the hotel, yet it is overpriced.

What an experience in such short distance from Valley! Well trained staff, ambience and variety of food options will definitely make me visit here again. Specially the heilpad side is MAGIC for sunset.

Un endroit hors du monde, unique , rare , élégant.. un privilège rare qui fait du bien à l esprit et au corpsL élégance , le raffinement, la simplicité.. avec tellement de générosité et d empathieDu service au top Une restauration délicieuse De magnifiques chambres Des soins appropriés

Had an awesome weekend. Sundown sunset ❤️View point❤️ Koya fish ❤️ Spa time❤️ Cycling❤️ The View❤️Room and the views ❤️ Yoga Point❤️Food- KungPao Fish is a must try for dinner..  Breakfast with the view  in the morning is🔥🔥🔥Love the vibe & the serene ambiance..

The staff went above and beyond to make our stay spectacular. The facilities are fabulous and we enjoyed our reunion trip so much at this wonderful resortThe food was five star - and we experienced hiking, bike riding, yoga , sound healings all arranged by the wonderful Tram at The Terraces

Great view from the hotel with nice room with good facilities.Very comfortable and cosy room. Clean. Staff very prompt and hospitable. The food was excellent,including buffet. Had a great time during the stay.

Very nice place with excellent hospitality, sunset trip, morning hike are a must do! Great dinner and breakfast buffet! The drive from Lubhu to Lakure bhanjyang is very scary, uphill drive! Call resort ahead of time for directions! Servers, attendants everyone is very polite and goes above and beyond for everything

Fantastic hospitality, fantastic staffs, fantastic view with very comfortable rooms so would love to visit again but pets should be allow very soon because I can’t go out without my pet.  Hope they will allow pet soon so that I can enjoy with our whole families

Great experience! Amazing views and atmosphere! Weather was perfect! Hospitality wonderful! Steam and sauna could be better. Yoga teacher was excellent. Sundowner was a good experience. Hiking wad good too.

The snacks in the room were all free and they gave us a note and everything was good everything was clean and they always had hot water I. The sink and shower the food was great and really nice dessert the view was good too

Amazing asthetics. Brilliant staff and service. Most comfortable bedding. Great food. Can’t fault anything.  Highly recommend a stay here! However summer months are probably more preferable as we went in December and sadly the clouds blocked the Himalayas view.

Everything is super nice here. Highly recommended. Be reminded to have enough clothing here. Its coldEnjoying every second of the majestic himalayan mountain range. 8 out 10 highest mountain in the world are here

Die Aussicht auf das Kathmandu Tal ist atemberaubend, in dieser Hinsicht das beste, was ich während meinen vielen Nepal Reisen gesehen habe. Das Resort ist sehr schön, die Zimmer sind ok, aber auch nicht mehr, wenn man den enorm (!) hohen Preis in Betracht zieht. Die Zimmer haben, nicht wie im Angebot steht, alle Aussicht auf das Tal oder die Berge. Meinerseits habe ich ein Deluxe King Size Zimmer gebucht (zweithöchste Preisklasse), und ein anderes Zimmer bekommen mit Aussicht auf... Bäume. Service ist ok, aber nicht überragend.

Excellent service, nice view and kind staffs.Would be convenient if bathrobes were available in every rooms tho not just spa!Everything else was good Would recommend people to come here and enjoyyyyyyy

Had a few days and wanted to explore a new property and it was worth the time - great views of the mountains and the city Would recommend it for a quick getaway from KathmanduGood place for singles, couples and family

We stayed at this hotel for about 15 days. The employees were extremely friendly. Like to mention one particular employee who works in different department but musty we see her in the breakfast time. Her name is Komal .She went beyond her duty to help us. Other were also very helpful. The hotel is kept in good standard. Only suggestion I have is to upgrade on the breakfast menu and smoke free rooms need to smoke free. We had to call for help because we were smiling smoke Oder at middle of night. Over all we had nice stay.

Excellent location to visit Kathmandu. The hotel is supposed to be a 5 star hotel but it needs a lot of refurbishing. However, it has so many positive aspects apart from its location. The staff is friendly.Heritage rooms are nicely decorated in Nepali styleThe room is very comfortable, specially with space to put all your luggage.Highly recommended to ask for a garden view.Breakfast was really excellent. Great variety and you could ask for different options that they would cook for you. Great opportunity to taste local and Indian food as well.Bathroom amenities included even toothbrush and toothpaste apart from the usual.We enjoyed our stay.

We were located in the older section for this visit, but the room standard was good with comfortable beds and good shower/bath - the 2 main requirements of a room. The hotel was undergoing some small renovation which did not impact the stay and the front of desk staff were helpful and attentive. The stand-out for us was the Chimney restaurant where, suspecting most people only stay 1 night in transit by staying 3 nights we lost became part of the family, with offers of food samples and extra Nepali marsala tea gratefully accepted. In addition whilst my wife wanted to keep things quiet the hotel checked her passport as her birthday fell on our last night resulting in a Birthday cake arriving unexpectedly...so for us a great 3 days with nice attention and service.

We had a regional conference for Asia & pacific here during November in this hotel. The hotel looks very grandeur and impressive with a beautiful garden and pool. AND all the good things for the hotel ended there. The management and staffs all were such un-professionals that we wondered how could a five-star hotel be like this!! We were around 600 people all together for 3 days; 120 rooms were booked at this hotel but except airport transfer no other service could be felt satisfactory. If I write this list can go on and on....In short Never trust this hotel.We have officially decided not to choose this hotel for any event or accommodation for  our guests.... neither we recommend for any one coming to  Nepal

We would give this hotel a five star review if it wasn’t for the Spa.Avoid the spa at all cost. Underrated massage ( very noisy ) and not professional with high prices. The locals ( not guests ) also use this spa and therefore no privacy and very noisy. Massages are supposed to be quiet and relaxing.Food is excellent. A visit to “ The Chimney “ restaurant is a must.

We stayed at the Yak & Yeti after completing the EBC Trek, and it was such a nice luxurious experience after the accommodations we had been staying in on the trek. This hotel was included as part of our "luxury" EBC Trek itinerary. Room: We had a huge room complete with a living room (multiple couches, working desk, two TVs) as well as a bedroom with a king-sized bed. There was a walk-through closet to to a nice bathroom with a super hot shower. The provided robes & slippers were comfy. We were sick after the trek, and this room was so nice to stay in. Food: We didn't try the restaurants (we were sick and didn't want to put on non-pajamas) but had room service multiple times. The food was only okay but came with a hefty price tag. The restaurants might have better food. Other: There are beautiful shops on the main floor of the lobby with all kinds of lovely jewelry and other souvenirs. The grounds have a tennis court, pool, and a beautiful walking garden. It's a slice of beauty in the craziness of Kathmandu. Internet was great.

Loved the pool view from our room ..was a bit cold so didnt enjoy the pool though.Well maintained hotel with exceptional service.The restaurant experience in the restaurant the chimney was very pleasant. We had the chicken satay as starter and later a risotto and pasta with white sauce. The service was formidable and sitting outside on the terrace in the hotel garden was very calming after a long day of walking around.Would love to go back and visit it for sure.

Stayed with Yak & Yati last weekend (10-13 Dec 22) for a family weekend Trip. The visit was really made memorable primarily because we decided to stay at Hotel Yak & Yati. It just happened that I emailed to hotel enquiring about the availability and the best rates and Mr. Rabinson responded promptly over email and subsequently spoke with me and made me absolutely comfortable. Once we checked in Hotel, he ensured that our stay was comfortable through out. The Hotel is centrally located, wonderfully connected, staff is very good and helpful. All that you need. Hotel Yak & Yati made our trip absolutely memorable.

In the center of Kathmandu close to all possible services and shops, very spacious room with gorgeous view on the internal garden with pond swimming pool and colorful flowers. Nevertheless the most pleasant aspect is when you go the the restaurant named "Spicy Room". The re the food , indy style, is excellent specially when served by two beautiful and extremely gentle maids: ANISHA and ANITA to whom I want to convey my most grateful thanks.

The Hotel is Cousy, well organized, clean and the staff extremely helpful and kind. Plus  the Internet connection is very good never let's you down, like it happened  to me in more pretentious 5stars in Kathmandu.The restaurant Spice room, cooks good Indian food, it is quiet and never noisy, and all the staff and the waiters are among the nicest I interacted in my many missions worldwide. In particularly Anisha, one the waitresses, goes the extra mile to make the client feel at ease and happy, advising about choices and offering quick services, always present  without imposing, fantastic service. For this reasons I dined at the Spice room during 3 consecutive nights. I would advise the Y&Y to anyone.

Amazing hospitality and great service. Historic and one of the most beautiful hotels I have been to. The varieties in sizes and beautiful interiors of the halls gives you plenty options for your event. Also, the staffs went out of the way to fulfill our smallest of the requirements till the end which made our event wonderful and enjoyable. I am so glad that I chose Hotel Yak and Yeti for my big day. Absolutely loved the  setups in the crystal hall and the garden. My whole family and friends are looking forward to do another event there very soon.

I was initially given a room at the heritage wing. There was a garden party that night that went on and on. I had to call to complain many times. I mean - who allows a garden party at midnight when you have paying guests who are trying to sleep, right? And I'm talking loud music.They shifted me to another room at 1130 pm. See? They do try to be accommodating. They even gave me free breakfast for the rest of my stay. But why do you allow parties to go on past 10 pm in the first place? Don't you have ground rules?

We found the reception staff very “offhand” and unwelcoming. This is the first hotel we have visited on this trip that we were not offered a welcome drink, and this is the most expensive we have stayed at. The bar staff and waiting staff were lovely and friendly. We were told to leave our luggage in the lobby and it would be taken to our room, but after some time of waiting we had to chase it up before it was delivered. The room was very basic, the bathroom door should swing the other way as it makes getting out the bathroom difficult especially in the night in the dark! Suffice to say we are just glad it was just 1 night!

The property is old though the facade and interiors have been modernised. You can still see remnants of old Nepal from a bygone era of the Rana family, the Prime Ministers to the King. The property is central but tucked away in a bylane away from the main road the Durbar Marg leading to the Royal Palace which is also a museum. The facilities are good at the property. The staff are helpful at the reception desk but room service is not up to the mark. This could be because there seem to be many rooms to service on each floor. There are 3 restaurants and Chimney dishes out great continental food with seating outdoors as well. Spice does good Indian food and also serves as the breakfast buffet. The pool and tennis courts are an excellent addition to the property. There is a Spa in the basement where the Gym is also located. There was some renovation work being done in the garden where I think a little pond is being built. The shopping arcade is a bit pricey and you can get stuff cheaper outside in Thamel but there is no doubt as to the quality in the arcade. All in all not a bad place stay if you are into history and like airy spaces as compared to the modern niche hotels also around.

we stayed at yak &yeti with elderly parents. the facilities were awesome. the staff was so helpful and made extra effort to helping my mobility challenged parents feel welcomed.Chabbas and Swostika in the spice room restaurant would take extra care to ensure the food was not overly spicy. muskan  at front desk made sure that there was an extra step stool to help these elderly people step into the van. Such wonderful hospitality!

The hotel is an oasis. The staff is lovely and professional. The restaurants serve great food and the bar is just perfect to relax. The garden is beautiful. You get what you pay, we decided to stay in the heritage rooms. We actually booked a lower category for a lower rate - the rooms are fine, but we thought to pay some extra money and we got a perfect room. If you want to save money, you can take a normal room as you can enjoy all the other facilities of the hotel, but keep in mind you get what you pay. We will come back and stay again in the heritage rooms. Try to get garden view room.

Went to dinner at Spice Room  for some Indian food. The ambience was great, the food was delicious (and the servings were generous, we were so full by the end). The dining staff was really friendly and attentive, special shout out to Pratima Basnet, she was sweet and served us very well. Will visit again, soon

Kathmandu is a busy, crazy place and is sadly quite a dirty and hazardous city to walk around. The Hotel Yak and Yeti is located in the heart of all the craziness, but it occupies a location off the main streets, in a large walled garden away for the traffic and crowds. This is where the rich natives come to conduct their weddings and other celebrations, and is viewed locally as the poshest hotel in the city, largely due to the large, ornamental garden, ideal for such events. My friend and I were there for 3 days only, to take a helicopter flight to Mt. Everest Basecamp and we chose the hotel because of its links to many Mt. Everest expeditions, as well as the unique name and decent reviews. We heard that many of the guests there are either on their way to Everest or on their way back, so we expected there would be some good conversations to be had in the bar. Plus, the hotel is close to the Thamel area, which is where the main market is located where you can find most things you might need for a mountain trip. I have given this hotel 5/5, due to the fact that it is an oasis of calm and cleanliness, compared to what you’ll find outside of the gates. To give further context, it would probably be classed as a 3 or 4 star hotel in other, more developed countries. If I returned to Kathmandu I would consider this hotel again but would also consider the Marriott Hotel and the Aloft Hotel too, as both are new and well situated.

Perhaps this hotel was once a luxury hotel, but I think it's best days are behind them. A mixture of good and not so goodPros:Attentive and friendly staffBreakfast selection was decentChimney restaurant was greatGym had decent equipmentCentral Location in KathmanduCons:Internet was not good and kept dropping outHot water did not work for a full dayLights on the smoke detector in my room were incredibly bright - flashed green every 5 seconds and lit up the room, I therefore found it difficult to sleep (bring an eyemask!)Hotel windows are a resting place for hundreds of pigeons. They don't disturb you at all but ruins the aesthetic somewhatSummary: A decent comfortable stay, but may look elsewhere when next in Kathmandu

My wife and I were on a tour and had been assigned to a room on the fourth floor. We soon discovered that the heating did not work and since we were going to be there for 3 nights I found this unacceptable. I contacted the front desk and was told someone would come up to assist us. When the staff person showed up,  he only had a portable heater that he plugged in. It was loud, and unacceptable. When I  explained this to him, he went back and got me another portable heater which was quieter but provided no heat. By now I had enough.  I am paying good money for this room and am receiving terrible quality in return. I went downstairs to the reception desk and spoke  to receptionist Any. She clearly understood my concern. She immediately suggested changing room. She went upstairs to the 6th floor with me to inspect another room, and made sure it was to my liking,  with appropriate heating.  I approved of the change, we went back downstairs to finalize everything.  Thanks to her assistance,  my stay at Yak and Yeti was very comfortable and I  am thankful to all the staff there who made our stay very enjoyable.

I checked-in in the hotel on 26.11.2022 in Room No-365.The hotel has nowhere mentioned on the internet that the CASINO IS NOT OPEN, this is really disappointing. Further, as per the hotel staff they've upgraded my hotel from Deluxe to Heritage Deluxe category. However, when I compared both the rooms there was no difference at all in size as well as the interior of the rooms.Further, the interiors of the rooms are very old and is not all value for the money charged by the hotel. The photos of the rooms posted on hotels website are different from the realty.

Historic hotel in great location.  The original part was been the go-to place for climbers and trekkers, now there is a newer large, modern convention center as well.  The old part is very mid-century.  The staff was super helpful and attentive. The hotel is very clean and the grounds were nicely kept.  We stored our luggage while we trekked for a week and were very grateful to have a late check out, for a fee, so that we could shower before our evening flight.  The hotel is within walking distance to Thamel, the Garden of Dreams, and the old palace museum.  There are many good shops and restaurants within walking distance as well.

My wife and I thoroughly enjoyed our stay at Yak & Yeti in our recent trip (February and March 2020) to Nepal. The hotel was a base for us travelling around Nepal and to Bhutan.Yak & Yeti is truly a 5-star hotel in a grand setting and situated in the heart of the city. It is close to many landmarks for sightseeing, including many World Heritage sites. Customer centricity is the very essence of the attractiveness and success of this hotel. This is a simple truth, and yet it is extremely difficult to put into practice. Yak & Yeti has proven to be a winner among all the 5-star hotels we stayed in Nepal and in many hotels of similar standing around the world. We travel a lot.Internet connectivity in hotels in Nepal is relatively poor (average or poor or weak). This was no exception in Yak & Yeti. But the hotel really made effort to get it right. What was good about their outstanding customer services was that they kept the communication active until the problem was finally resolved. Staff always interacted with us in a friendly, helpful and positive way. Their smiles made a difference to our positive feeling about the hotel (smile doesn’t cost money!).  Good customer service means meeting expectations – but excellent customer service means exceeding them. I rated Yak & Yeti as excellent not just for its magnificent buildings (part of the build used to be a Royal Palace) and beautiful surrounding, but also for its customer service.I strongly recommend this hotel.Dr Danny Lam (or known as Mr Kit to the hotel)

I'm sorry to say that my experience at this hotel was an absolute nightmare. Not only was there construction going on late into the night on a Sunday, but the sound of crows outside made it impossible to get any rest. Despite my complaints, the management did nothing to address the situation, leaving me feeling frustrated and helpless.I would strongly advise anyone considering staying at this hotel to think twice. The lack of consideration for guests' comfort and the inability to provide a peaceful and restful environment are completely unacceptable. There are plenty of other options in the area, and I would highly recommend looking elsewhere if you want to avoid a similarly unpleasant experience.In short, this hotel is a disaster and not worth the money. If you value your sanity and want to have a good night's sleep, I suggest you steer clear of this place

Dinner at spice room was very enjoying and delicious specially services of Anisha, it is really excellent and quite satisfied with her services. Enjoyed a lot.i will like to avail such opportunities again and again. I will like to have same with my family and friends.

The services are excellent.  The staff in the dining room called Spice Room is very welcoming, friendly,  warm and family like. The tram is led by Salikram who is very caring to provide best of what you need during breakfast and dinner. The reception desk staff is very cooperative especially Manish, an always smiling face. They immediately address your requirements and come to help wherever needed.

We stayed for 10 days, and had a great experience.   Our days often would start and end with Artuta in the morning and Muskan in the evening.   As Guest Relations Officers they both earned special mention, in particular because one of our family members was in a wheelchair and required extra accommodations.   They were consistently attentive to our needs and experiences, ensuring we had accessible access throughout the hotel, restaurant and spa experiences, as well as excursions and related travel.   This guest experience was amplified by the rest of the staff at the front desk, the Spice Room restaurant and bar, and the Chimney restaurant.   The front door staff were always attentive with door assistance and enabling a ramp every time we entered and exited the hotel.   The friendliness was genuine, natural and consistent.   The rooms were clean and complied with our needs for disabled access.   The garden and surrounding buildings were lovely, and overall this hotel served as a great experience and base camp for our stay in Kathmandu.

The place has a very charming and old school vibe. The hotel is large and has a wonderfully landscaped garden , pool and pond Rooms are comfortable though not very large Despite the age of the property it’s impeccable on cleanliness and maintenance .It’s also very kid friendly due to the open space and activities What was a complete winner was the food especially breakfast. Had the most terrific omelettes , baked goods and Dosa which was as good as having it at my hometown in South India.

This "Grand Old Lady of Kathmandu Hotels" is a great place to stay at the beginning/end of a trip to Nepal. It's very comfortable, full of character and history and the garden and greenery provide tranquility in the midst of the bustling city. The staff are very helpful and welcoming; special thanks and commendations to Srijana in the Spice Room for friendly professionalism, outstanding service, smiling welcome, attention to detail and eager willingness to help with every request!

We had an evening meal in the Chimney restaurant after two weeks trekking and it was great!Lovely atmosphere, warm real fire. Waiter, Prabhat,  very friendly and professional and food was really tasty, big portions with lovely extras provided as complimentary. Would definitely recommend.

I arrived here at night and was super tired but the hotel reception staff was extremely gracious in receiving us. Had am awesome and punctual car pick us up, gave the best services.The food here is beyond delicious and so is the ambience of the place. It's a former palace and it shows.Overall the hospitality and services provided were exceptional and would recommend it to anybody visiting Khatmandu.

The central location of the hotel enables one to reach several tourist attractions easily, even on foot. The ambience is aesthetic and the rooms spacious and comfortable. Good service by housekeeping staff. Helpful front desk. The morning breakfast has a good spread however, inclusion of some traditional Nepali dishes will be appreciated. Ball room good for conference.

Excellent experience rooms size is nice ,cleanliness is good,comfortable mattress. Courticious staff.We ate dinner twice the quality of food was excellent. The service was very good especially Ms ashina & Ms pratima was excellent very polite. The chef mandeep was very attentive, he tried and almost prepared food according to our test.Overall awesome experience.

Location: Centrally located. 10 mins from most places. Hotel : Clean and big. Traditional style of setup. Nice. They are building new blocks. If you have time to spend in the property then you will enjoy. For a day or two you cannot enjoy the property.Food : This is the lowest point of the hotel. They need to improve their spread and quality of fruits and desserts. It will be good if they have one more restaurant.Staff: Very Friendly and nice. But the systems are slow. They need to upgrade. Even with prior booking they did not have room ready at 3pm. This is largely occupied by tourists who are booked through the travel agent. The staff have to ensure that game room is seen, spa is utilized etc., The atrium is good as well, but not projected well enough, we went and saw it on the last day. While someone is checking in, it is good to show and tell them the features and what is available in the hotel.Rooms: Clean rooms. But there is no tap or shower head. Only Hand shower. TV: Only local channels. Not much there.

A large hotel in Kathmandu. It is supposed to be 5*, but I am afraid does not come up to 5* standard. 4* at best. Yes it has the facilities, but everything is a bit old and tired. Our room was large and had everything you need, but dated, especially the bathroom. We had a suite and you do not expect a shower above the bath. Wi-Fi is free but a bit slow. Free water. Lots of power cuts and a generator cuts in and out so each power cut only lasts about a minute. Staff are very friendly and good. Outdoor swimming pool and area look nice, but too cold in January! Breakfast buffet is poor for a 5* hotel, very little fruit and just not 5*. Chimney restaurant is very good.

Since I was travelling with my family for a 5 days Kathmandu trip, I spent time in finding the right hotel for us looking at comfort, location and service. After going to most of the hotels in this category, chose to stay with Yak and Yeti. A big credit for this goes to Mr. Robinson who looks after sales and helped me with the best offers. He also was kind enough to sort out all our queries and got us good offers at another Casino. It was moms birthday on the day of arrival and he surprised us with a cake. Thank you Robinson! As regards to the hotel, the newly furnished rooms have the local Nepalese design and yet all the luxury of a 5 star. Our rooms faced the swimming pool and garden area. It’s a wide spread property surrounded by greenery. The cherry on the cake is the location. It’s bang in the middle of the city and access to markets, durbar square is a matter of few minutes. I am glad we chose this hotel and would love to stay with them again.

The restaurant staff are very friendly, especially Sujan.  He makes you feel at home and gives excellent suggestion of food.  The chef is also excellent who makes sure that the quantity and quality is to the level!  I would surely recommend anyone visiting Nepal to stay at Yak and Yeti as well as enjoy the food at their restaurant with friendly staff

We experienced heavy dust in our room which we noticed in the morning only. The whole night we were coughing without understanding the fact that this was due to the polluted air in our room. The room was polluted with the dust coming out of the airconditioner in the room. We have stayed in this hotel several times in the past also due to its good location but this time our stay in Yak and Yeti Kathmandu can be categorically marked as a 'Life Threatening Experience' for us. People with asthamatic problems must be careful.

Dropped by the Chimney for drinks after a day of sightseeing round Kathmandu. A great evening, with lots of tasty snacks a welcome extra with our cocktails. The hot rum toddy and Boris's delicious borscht really warmed us up in the January chill, and the blazing logs on the fire were lovely. Special mention for the charming Santosh, who gave us a fascinating mini tour of the older rooms, with lots of historical background. Heartily reccomended!

Found the property really great.Great location, situated in the heart of the city Darbar Marg.Staff is really helpful & courteous specially Ms.Komal in the spice room always ready to help.Fabulous property.

We have a very nice dinning experience at Yak & Yeti. They serve delicious and mouth watering cuisine. We are also very much delighted with the service of Mr. Satish Basnet who took good care of us during dinning. He truly reflects 5 star service. Overall we really had excellent experince here.

Just tried to check in my group at the Yak and Yeti. Queues at reception - no hospitality, no welcome drink, one luggage boy on duty so had to bring own luggage in, no lobby manager in sight, laughed at by the receptionist when I complained. Usually put our groups at the Royal Singi hotel where we are met with a smile , sat down and given a welcome drink. Much more professional. This was one of our premium groups - doesn't leave a good impression.

We had the opportunity to stay in Nepal’s finest hotel, Yak & Yeti, A peaceful, luxurious sanctuary in the middle of the bustling capital city! Yak & Yeti is a five-star luxury hotel located in the heart of Kathmandu, Nepal and is one of the most prestigious hotels in the country that has hosted many celebrities and dignitaries over the years.The hotel is located in Durbar Marg, a popular tourist area with many shops, restaurants, and historical sites. It is also within walking distance of many of Kathmandu's major attractions.They also have a variety of facilities and amenities, including a restaurant, bar, spa, tennis court, convention hall, jewellery shops, swimming pool, and fitness centre. The restaurant serves a variety of cuisines, including Nepali, Indian, Chinese, and Continental. The spa offers a variety of treatments, including massages, facials etc. The swimming pool is heated and is located outdoors. The fitness centre is equipped with great types of equipment.The Chimney is one of the first fine-dine restaurants in Nepal situated inside this Hotel.They have Lal Durbar Palace which is one of the grandest convention centers in Kathmandu.Their breakfast buffet was very good and both of us enjoyed their food, they offer a lot of varieties, and I must say most of the items were very good! We totally enjoyed our stay here!

We have visited to the spice room of hotel  yak and yeti . The food and gesture by the satish banset ji was good . The  restaurant serves pure Indian taste food and the restaurant has peaceful environment and good ambience .

Once upon a time this hotel was a great choice for individuals, but now it seems to focus on corporate events and weddings.  We booked unknowingly in wedding season and on 3 of the 5 days we were there the whole or part of the garden was set aside for weddings and unusable for other visitors.  On 1 day the whole garden was unavailable, and loud drumming went on from around 11am to 6pm.  However the location is great, the food is excellent, and the staff are lovely, so OK if , and only if, you want to be out and about all day.

A fantastic hotel, really nice meal in Spice Room with great service. Anisha was very helpful with describing dishes and recommending what she would order. Great service, would definitely eat at that restaurant again! Thank you Anisha!

A great place to start or complete any trip to NepalThe staff are friendly and exceptionally helpful, and the breakfast historicCentrally placed and full of character. The rooms at present are fine, but would welcome the coming renovationBut it is an institution. Bravo

We were at Spice Room. Mr. Satish Basnet was the best server one could get. Very reasonable price with excellent customer with excellent delights. Price was cherry on the top, very reasonable price compared to many local restaurants.

It was my first visit at Kathmandu I  had a great experience staying here.lobby was beautifully maintained.room was so clean and maintained. Breakfast was wide, staffs were so much professional, I would like to mention the names of some staffs who are really good Manager hari at breakfast room is very much accommodating, sonika, Pralad, kishor , swastika are very friendly. Kritika in reception is so much helpful. I definitely recomm this place if you want to spend holiday at Kathmandu.

Great location, lovely facilities and wonderful staff. We stayed here before and after our 14 day trek of the Annapurna Circuit. It was a wonderful experience, staff were very helpful, we were able to leave our bags at the hotel and only brought what was needed for the trek. On our return we were welcomed back and we spend another 2 nights  which helped us to recover. When our flights were cancelled due to the flooding in Dubai, the hotel arranged another hotel for us as they were fully booked. We would really recommend the Yak and Yeti as a peaceful place to stay. Breakfast was great too!

An oasis in the city! This hotel's prime location near attractions and the area of Thamel, coupled with staff's warmth and efficiency, makes it a gem. The serene park with vibrant flowers adds an enchanting touch to a tranquil stay. Highly recommend for a rejuvenating experience!"

This hotel in Kathmandu is one of the worst I've experienced. The reservation staff and sales manager were extremely rude. The guest check-out time is midnight, which is inconvenient. During payment, they used inappropriate language, which was unacceptable. Our guest was also dissatisfied with their stay. I strongly recommend choosing another option and avoiding this hotel.

At the lounge, Mr Kesan made excellent cocktails !🍸 especially the whisky sour and negroni. He served freshly made snacks from lotus seeds. The ambiences is really warm and welcoming. Everyone should check out Lounge 77…………………………………….

We find this hotel quite expensive while booking it but the experience was nice and they had a great decor and they have an in house casino too.made the trip a very good one . They have the casino royale and you can get free chips in the package also Had a great time

One of the most courteous staff I have met. The food was amazing, and the ambience is just mind blowing. It houses one of the oldest copper chimneys, and a continental restaurant started by a Russian Chef. Overall loved every bit of it.

The hotel is great. Situated in the center of Kathmandu, with beautiful gardens, nice swimming pool, tennis court and a great staff that will take excellent care of you. We stayed twice: at the beginning of our trek to EBC and after the trek. The first time we had an older room with a worse view but when we came back we had a lovely spacious room with great views of the garden. The staff are all great and we also enjoyed eating at both of their Restaurants. If we come back to Kathmandu we would be definetly stay again at the Yak & Yeti. Thank you.

Hotel yak &yeti is an amazing oldest hotel.  It was amazing experience while staying there thanks to the wonderful staff, especially sandeepa From the moment we arrive, she greeted us with a warm smile and was incredibly attentive throughout our stay . I highly recommend this hotel for good experience looking forward to returning soon . Thank you

Just spent a great couple of days here. A lovely oasis in the heart of the city.Lovely quiet grounds with ducks and a cranky goose. Shame the pool was drained.Hotel and grounds were spotless as you'd expect. All staff were very attentive. Special mention to Prabhat, Suraj, Prakash, Anjuli and Lekhnath at the Chimney Restaurant where we ate both nights. Favourites were the catfish and baked Alaska (both a first for me) and the small complimentary starters.Also to the waitress serving at breakfast both days who remembered our hot drinks order for the second day so Americanos waiting when we returned from the buffet!

Small, tiny rooms  what they call as Heritage deluxe, can be claustrophobic for some. Clean hotel, service was better at restaurants compared to front desk. Breakfast spread was good with nice flavors. The other restaurant Chimney was just ok with very limited food options.

We stayed here either side of our EBC trek and loved it. The rooms are so nice and the gardens are beautiful. It truly is a retreat from the busyness of Kathmandu. But also handy to shops, including walkable to Thamel. Only niggle was that they quoted USD 30 for an airport pickup, which seems excessive, and a couple of times I was ignored in favor of my husband (eg putting his bag in the car but not mine). But overall the staff were super-nice and provided great service. We appreciated an early check in after our trek. The breakfast was delicious with a great selection. We went to the Chimney restaurant for a birthday dinner and the food and service there were excellent. Highly recommend Y&Y.

One of my favourite hotel in kathmandu. It is really beautiful and centrally located. I  Visited to meet my clients who came from India, I had my drinks at Bar and  dinner at spice room, dahi ka kabab was supper delicious. all the staffs were so much courteous special thanks to manager Hari  jacissa sujan and all team. This hotel can be a best option if you want comfort at downtown.

We ended our trip in Nepal here at Yak & Yeti, and it was a marvellous stay. The hotel is stunning and a welcome sanctuary in hectic Kathmandu. We celebrated our wedding anniversary at The Chimney and its amazing staff arranged an unforgettable plated 4-course dinner on pretty short notice. We were attended by Syaron Lama, and Rabi. Chef Rabindra and Chef Jitendra prepared exquisite dishes. The meal ended with a spectacular dessert aptly named Sagarmāthā. Every detail was taken care of and they were friendly, patient and caring (we got a lovely card too). Highly recommend both the hotel and the restaurant!  Not to be missed.

I had a wonderful visit to Hotel yak and yeti. The care and a warm welcome  received from was exceptional. They listened attentively to my concern with positive results was highly appreciated. The entire team at the hotel displayed a high level of professionalism and made me feel comfortable throughout my visit. Special thank to MR. Humnath Acharya for making the stay more memorable and comfortable.

This is my third visit in Kathmandu and in Yak and Yeti hotel, I’m having a long stay for affairs and I can tell that all personnel are very kind and helpful. Since the room cleaning very carefully done by Binita. Shailandra and service room by Rajesh and Vola… in the spice room kind and dedicated service  by Sonika, Srijana, Serina, Alina, Shreeya, Srijana, Kisher and Anish-chef have no price when we are far from home.. to finish to thank Monica who manage the hotel making it a special place for all their guests… highly recommended!!

Front desk Binaya / Sapana are very cooperative * * * * *. Good is good . Good property * * * * *  in ktm valley centrally located. It’s lobby is good and for meeting with guest and well service during metting . You fell personal meeting aera in hotel lobby . * * * * *. Food room service is properly with some extra chutni , papad abs salad that’s I love service of Yak n yeti .

I went to Kathmandu for a trekking adventure to Base Camp Everest but sadly had to leave early on due to unexpected circumstances.  Thank goodness for the Yak and Yeti, a wonderfully warm and comfortable environment.  Excellent staff all around including lobby front desk, breakfast dining area with an amazing chef who made the ultimate daily omelette for me.  Every housekeeper on staff was incredibly kind, and the bar/lounge area was a lovely retreat staffed with very gentle and respectful good souls.  The spa area was soothing and inviting as well … fabulous massage !!  I have nothing other than high praise for this gem of a hotel in the bustling and vibrant city of Kathmandu.

Everything about this hotel.is amazing. The interiors gives you the vibes of a temple. All the requests were dealt promptly. Staff were super helpful and out of them there is this staff(Bhola) he has been a superstar, he was the 1st one to greet us and assisted us by bringing our bags inside the hotel, he was adhering the covid protocols by wearing mask but u can see a person smiling if he smiles from heart, he really sets the tune for the check in and check in to check out were so smooth and whil leaving as well Bhola helped us with our bags and greeted us wished us safe journey. He along with other staffs made sure our stay in ktm although for a day was eventful. Thanks and congrats to yak n yeti hotel for bringing  out best in ur staffs and i can say it for cent precent that Bhola is an asset for this beautiful hotel. Many thanks once again and cya again in my future stays.

Had a very pleasant stay at the Hotel Yak and Yeti in Kathmandu. The facade and interiors of the hotel are very beautiful; the rooms, conference venues, and amenities are also well maintained. Most of all, all of the staff I encountered in my brief stay - from the reception, bellhop, servers/waitstaff, to housekeeping - were so friendly, warm, and helpful.

Great location close to market and restaurants. Hotel staff was very friendly and helpful. Conference facility was also very good. Very good food quality and it is a certified halal hotel. Hotel manager and other staff was always available to help and support.

We had the most incredible stay at the Yak and Yeti. The customer service from the staff there is world-class in all elements of the hotel- management, front desk, bell staff, guards, restaurant workers, and room cleaning service staff. Everyone is incredibly friendly and polite. Notable standout staff were Kamal in the Chimney Restaurant, Kiran the Restaurant Manager who put on a stunning evening of surprises for our anniversary meal, Salikram and Swostika who were exemplary in their breakfast service, and others include Santosh, Joshef, and Numa. The hotel itself was immaculate and everything was of the highest standard. The rooms were so beautiful and so were the hotel grounds. We were made to feel so special as guests here. We loved the hotel so much we actually cancelled one of our other planned hotels, and returned to the Yak and Yeti at the end of our stay in Nepal. The hotel is absolutely faultless. Thank you for everything!

Good kitchen that adopts meals according to your wishes - tasty from meat to veg.Surrounding nicely decorated in wood and copper.Waitress Anisha intelligent and friendly - providing an atmosphere you'll like to stay longer and more often.

My experience in yak and yeti was overall good. I enjoyed the food and even more the service. Our waiter for the day was Satish. He served us very well and was very respectful. If you ever decide to dine in yak and yeti I highly recommend him.

Myself & my wife stayed at Yak & Yeti during May & June 2023 for 7 days during our 19 Day travel to Nepal. This is one of the best 5 star Hotels in  Kathmandu Nepal. The Customer service & Food was excellent and also the rooms were well maintained & clean. Most importantly all staff were well behaved and courtoeus. We make a speacial mention of Dinesh -Manager Food & Beverages and also Rajesh & Bhola  for their kindness and hospitality.

I'm staying in this right now in room 434 while writing the review. Property is definitely 5 star however level of service is not more than zero star. Extremely pathetic. While there are numerous things i can talk about that i experienced in last 24 hours, however the biggest one is AC being locked at 23degree in this summer month. I had been following up from last 9 hours now for reducing the temperature as my family of 3 could not sleep at all yesterday night due to the heat. As of now the response received is not proper. First of all, no one attended for initial 3 hours, then once someone came, he went back saying he will inform the engineer. No one again came for next 3 hours. Now, a guy popped up to inform, that ac temperature is locked at 22-23 degree and they can't change it. A manager now offered to instal and extra FAN in the room, shabby !! You pay 20k for this level of service. I'm speechless and don't know whom to talk to. This is waste of my holidays, money and time in setting up things at a so called the best hotel of Nepal

Really relaxing place with lots of courtesy on offer besides great food at Spice Room where the staff is at it toes to serve the most mouth watering cuisines. Had a littel interaction with the Chef Mandeep from whom I could discover that its love that they add in their dishes. Special mention needs to be made of Mr Binod, Saksham, Dewan, Sujan, Jesicca and Nirzala for their outstanding courteous service and always ready to help gesture.

Centrally located hotel Yak & Yeti has been my home away from home for past several years. I find this place very convenient and comfortable.  I am quite impressed with the excellent service I have received from hotel staffs each time I stay at this hotel.  A special thanks goes to Sonika, Swastika, Naresh, Salikram, Pralad, Charas over at Spice Room and Kritika, Manish, Manager Ajay sir and many others over at the Reception.  I would recommend this hotel to all travellers who are looking for convenience and great hospitality while visiting Kathmandu, Nepal.  Best, Raju Shrestha, OAO Investment, LLC, Dubai

It's a great place here! The entire staff  (Santosh , Prabhat, Numa, Melina, Saurav and Rikesh) were friendly and they made us feel comfortable whereas Santosh ji narrated the historic background of the hotel very nicely. The atmosphere there was comfy and calm.  You can tell they are passionate and that the satisfaction of their consumers is their top priority. The food is likewise very good, and it is completely worth paying for it.  The best restaurant in the city with a noteworthy historical background.

This hotel used to be a palace and has definitely preserved its glamorous. I love the woodwork in the room and throughout the property. There are lots of birds on the property and they come and sit on your window for hours. The staff and management go above and beyond to make your stay memorable. I highly recommend trying the breakfast. It includes items from the Nepali cuisine. The pool was not heated, but ok for 15 minutes. I will consider this hotel again when I come back to Kathmandu, Nepal.

We stayed here 3 nights in the beginning of our tour then about a week later went back for two nights.the first time I think we were all upgraded to suites, very nice. Second time we were put in standard rooms. Several in our group, including us, had to call reception due to missing hand towels and bath mats. It took a while for them to be brought to the room. The standard rooms are definitely not as nice and much smaller. Restaurant staff were wonderful and the breakfast buffets were varied and delicious. Good location to walk to shops and restaurants.

The Yak and Yeti is a classic hotel near the Royal Place Museum. The garden with a swimming pool is a real treat in Kathmandu. Having greenery is a welcome respite from the dust of the city. Over the years I have stayed at the Yak and Yeti  - what makes this placer exceptional are the people that are part of the hotel, The morning breakfast offers cuisine that appeals to all. Monica (GM) and her team are here to help.Special shout out to Kishor, Sonika, Charas and Srijana at the Spice Room.  Thank you!

Had a wonderful experience at the hotel, the staff was very polite and hospitable. The ambience and food was excellent. They had beautiful lawns and a pond with cute ducks. The woodwork, antiques and architecture was also fantastic. They had Tennis and Swimming, however indoor games such as Table Tennis and Snooker would make it even better (they did have chess though). A big thank you to Monika and Deepa for making our stay incredible, and also to Hari and Prakash who were extremely hospitable and polite. I wanted to write about my Yak and Yeti experience 26th-28th April 2015. The earthquake hit Nepal on the 25th April and I was out of Kathmandu. I managed to get to the city on Sunday 26th and fortunately was already booked into the hotel for the week. Upon arrival it was obvious that hotel manager Philippe Belhay and his team had been working tirelessly to ensure that their guests where as safe and as comfortable as possible after the earthquake. Immediately I was booked in I was informed that due to aftershocks and a possible second major quake it was advised that guests sleep in the garden. We were provided with shelter and bedding and amazingly a full buffet dinner was served. Later on a thunderstorm hit and we had to make our way into the lobby. It was a long and nervous night but throughout Mr Belhay was present and his staff did all they could to keep us calm and comfortable. It was the same story for the following two days.If the test of a hotel is does it deliver in a crisis ? If the test of the staff is do they care for the customer when it is most difficult? And if the test of the management is whether their stated values are reflected across the institution; this hotel is a five star gem.Thank you Yak and Yeti. That I came through that week in decent shape is due to the courage, commitment, dignity and respect that are the hallmark of Philippe Belhay and his team.

We’ve had a mixed experience. The hotel iteself is pleasant, but definitely not a 5 star as it is advertised. First, the good things. Decent buffet breakfast, reasonable prices for lunch and dinner. Most of the staff is pleasant and welcoming. The rooms vary, but overall - of a decent quality. Confortable bed. Complimentary bottled water and tea making facilities in the room. Now, the not-so-good things. You have to pay for the WiFi, and it isn’t particularly fast. The 4G you can get from NCell is faster. The water in the tap is yellowish in colour. The lifts are antiquated and sometimes temperamental. And now - the really ugly stuff, and why I gave this hotel only 1 star. Some of our trek clothes gone missing from the suitcase, which was cling-film wrapped and only opened in the hotel to be put into the duffel bags.  We discovered it after we left for the trek. The management denied any responsibility and tried to give us a number of excuses, starting from the suggestion that our stuff was stolen at the airport from the cling-film-wrapped bag to saying that we should have counted things we had in the suitcase after we left the suitcase in the hotel room and went to dinner.  In addition, there was an attempted break into the iPad - to the point that it was deactivated. The management suggested that this may have happened when “the staff was cleaning.” Bear in mind - the iPad deactivates if the password was entered incorrectly at least 10 times. Additional point - according to CCTV - the staff was in the room for less than 2 minutes - and in this time, apparently, managed to clean the room and to turn down the beds. The printouts of the room access had inconsistencies and were reprinted the next day when we asked to lodge the complaint with the police. The CCTV has time discrepancies with the room access system, which management had no explanation for. They told us we “should ignore the discrepancies, because they are not important”. They went as far as to threaten us, in case we diced to publish our experience in the review, and were very upset when we explained that our conversation is being recorded and will be available to the police. All in all - I will never recommend this hotel to anyone for a number of reasons: first, because of the disappearance of the clothes, and second, because of the inconsistency between CCTV and room access systems - no one can feel secure, if the security system in the hotel may be tampered with and the management prefers to ignore the problem instead of addressing it. What’s more - this hotel is an embarrassment for the otherwise wonderful Nepalese hospitality and undermines all efforts that other people put in to make Nepal attractive to the foreigners.

That is just wrong!And then there was the Nirvana Spa!!!  Seriously!!!  That was closer to Hades than Nirvana!  The ridiculous coupon system in place before your massage, should have given my husband and I the heads up!  You book your massage, you go to main reception and collect a voucher, which is all hand written out, then you go to the "spa" reception and hand this over, you are then given a locker key and so your road to hell begins!Into the ladies changing room to undress under the very watchful eye of the female "therapist".  I was told to keep my bra and knickers on (I understand the latter, but the former seemed unusual).She then ushered me into a room off the locker area and told me to get onto the couch.  There were two doors into this room - I soon found out the other door led to the men's locker room, as the men in the changing room seemed to be having a farting competition!  Nice!The room itself was windowless, hot and stuffy with no air condition, just a fan.  The couch was rock hard and had no face hole!  No questions were asked about what I wanted or any medical issues, she just started trying to crack my spine - NOT GOOD!  I instantly asked her to stop!  She's not a chiropractor or an osteopath!  Anyone with any massage training knows you DO NOT do this!!!  Then she got the oil, I had repeatedly said at this point "no oil" but still she tried to get oil on me, after 15 minutes of her fumbling around on my back and arms I called a stop to the "massage", I could have had a better massage letting one of the stray street dogs walk on my back!She called in a 2nd "therapist", he started work on me.  He did the same as the woman, and tried to pop my spine - I asked him to stop!  He carried on!  I turned side ways and insisted he stop, he got the oil - I said no!  It was like Ground Hog day, but with a man instead of a woman.  Then he did his coup de grace and used his full force on my left elbow to pop it.  I nearly thumped him!  The pain shot down my arm and I stopped the massage.  What should have been a 90 minute, oil free Shiatsu massage ended up as a 45 minute torture which has left me with an acute case of Tennis elbow in my left arm!These people were BADLY trained, if at all, they had NO idea what they were doing and as I said to the duty manager, after I had calmed down, they were utterly DANGEROUS!  If this is their idea of a spa, they need to go and look at some others - this place is NOT fit for purpose!  IT SHOULD BE CLOSED DOWN!!!

The hotel is very good and conveniently located, just 10 mins walk to Thamel. The garden is very nice and well maintained so is the swimming pool. The restaurant offers wide range of multi cuisine buffet. Staff is very courteous. The only negative point is wifi is chargeable.

Stayed one night on a business trip. Very nice garden. Pool unheated but 22°C (enough for me) (April). Extensive facilities. Within walking distance of main street, quiet location. Curtains do not darken completely. Free airport shuttle. And all that at a very reasonable rate (check out the price on their website for last minute promotions)

With the airport closed due to a Turkish Airline accident which blocked the runway for four days, my wife and I needed a place to stay.  Rajan Tuladhar, our local agent for Icon India Tours, immediately arranged for two nights at the Yak & Yeti.  Our short stay was so peaceful that my wife and I decided to tour the world in similar hotels during our next life.     The airport was closed until further notice, our connecting flight from Delhi to JFK was history, Rajan and I were waiting in line at the Air India Office in Katmandu for six hours, the power went off at 1800 hours and everyone went home until Sunday morning and I needed a drink.  Rajan and I returned to the Yak & Yeti to cool our jets (sic) and reassure my wife that we would leave Katmandu sometime in the future.     Service, hospitality,food quality and surroundings were just what my wife and I needed.  Our emergency stay was a delight and two days later Air India delivered us from the heights of Katmandu to the plains of Delhi.

Stayed here for 2 nights. Its fairly close to the airport and also to the tourist attractions, The hotel has an old world charm & some of the bathroom fittings remind you further. Staff were polite and courteous. The travel desk was very helpful

A very solid stay, nice grounds, decent workout facility, good location.  Very reliable service and care from the staff.  Well organized system for assisting transport to and from the airports.On site casino but more importantly nice historical displays.  On site gourmet Russian (yes, RUSSIAN!) restaurant was a highlight - probably the best Borscht I have ever had!

Beware!  This hotel lies beyond belief.  I had inquired about the hotel's policy on guests.  They informed me that local Nepalese are not allowed in stay in rooms with foreigners, when asked if it was the hotel's policy or the governments they said the governments.  They lie.  There is no such policy.  I continually questioned them and asked for proof, they refused and still informed me of the same thing, that it is illegal for local citizens, ESPECIALLY WOMEN to stay with foreigners in Nepal. It is a complete lie.  There is no such rule or policy in Nepal.    They refused to site specific government information about it.I believe that this hotel just does not want locals to stay with guests, period.  That maybe there own policy, but lying about it makes them look stupid and pathetic.  I refused to stay at this hotel because of my email exchange with them.  This hotel is ridiculous, lies to customers and is discriminatory towards foreigners.    STAY FAR AWAY!  I am quite sure if they reply to my review that either they will deny such things from happening, I have email proof, or they will say that indeed it is government policy, but still provide either fake reports or no information regarding it just as they did to me.    I have no reason to exaggerate the truth, I was very interested in staying here until I received constant lies from them.   Again, avoid!   Stay in Thamel instead. Save your money.

This was by far one of the worst “five star” hotel experiences I ever had.  Every single (and I mean EVERY) aspect of our stay was problematic, frustrating, and upsetting. Our experience was SO bad it almost seemed funny for a while, but when you are paying hundreds of a night for your destination wedding, it is not funny... It was in fact so bad that we ended up leaving several days early, and had to scramble to make other plans. I booked a weeklong stay at Yak and Yeti for my wedding for myself, my now husband, and our friends who were traveling for the event.  When booking the rooms I put all the details in our reservation (such as requests for a wedding dinner, a wedding cake with the dinner, when I was arriving at the hotel from another destination in Nepal, when our friends were flying in and should be picked up, that our room and the guests rooms be close to each other, that we requested smoking rooms, etc). Being a thorough and organized person, I also emailed the information again to Yak and Yeti three days before our arrival to make sure that everything was all set. Despite all my attempts to make sure everything was set, the problems begun as soon as my now husband and I arrived. I’ve listed out the myriad of problems below in chronological order:1) When my (now) husband and I arrived, the check in person seemed to have lost all records of the rooms I had booked for our friends (who were arriving later that evening).  They seemed to be struggling to decide where to put their room. They had none of our friend’s flight information even though I had sent it to the hotel twice. They seemed unsure of who was picking our friends. They assured us they would sort everything out, and sent us up to our room. 2) When we went up to our room we asked the bellhop if our room was smoking (it obviously wasn’t, and we had requested a smoking room).  He said it wasn’t, and that he would run downstairs and get us a key to another room. When he returned, we grabbed all our stuff and followed him to another room, which was obviously non-smoking. We asked him again “is this a smoking room? We booked a smoking room”. He again told us to wait while he ran downstairs to find us a new room. The cycle kept going: we kept dragging our luggage all over the hotel to arrive at rooms that were obviously not smoking…. By the fifth relocation we finally got it right.
