Already nervous about the confusion, we ran downstairs to the front desk to check and see if our guest’s rooms were found, and understood to be smoking rooms as well.3) When we arrived back to our room (only ten minutes later max), we found our wedding cake… Sitting there… On the desk… It was Monday… Our wedding was scheduled for Friday…I started laughing because it was just so effed up. I never really had any “bridezilla” moments, but my wedding cake just showing up five days early threw me for a serious loop. I sat there staring at it for a while. I was confused mostly with a hint of anger. Who delivers a wedding cake five days early? Why would it be delivered to our room? Why wouldn’t it be served with dinner? How did this even happen? I decided I couldn’t deal with this situation that night, and decided to wait till the next morning to talk to the staff about it. (They all seemed very confused why it was an issue that our wedding cake arrived five days early when I did talk to them)Our friends arrived, and though there was slight confusion getting them checked in, we thought the worse was over, until:4) When we woke up the next morning, we found A TOENAIL IN OUR BED. It was clearly from the big toe. One perfectly cut yellow toenail. It was definitely not ours. We didn’t even have nail clippers on our trip. I don’t know if the bed was just dirty and unchanged, or it had somehow made it through the wash and dry cycle clinging to our sheets. But it was disgusting and gave me serious heebie-jeebies. Who knows what other body parts of other people where clinging to our bed. 5) From afar, the view of the grounds and pool were absolutely beautiful, but every time we tried to use them there were also issues. A few times we tried to use the pool and it was too dirty. There were feathers from the local geese, leaves, and actual TRASH (like used and empty water bottles) floating around in it. I asked a grounds person one day if he could clean it for us, and his response made it clear that he was not happy I asked…. While we saw other people receiving poolside service, we always had to go inside while dripping wet to find a server. Maybe we just had bad luck, or maybe they just labeled us problem customers, but we had to work to get any level of service… Odd at a “five star” hotel. 6) I booked a pedicure at the onsite spa. It was literally the worst pedicure I’ve ever gotten. The nail technician was rude, a friend sat next to her the whole time talking about me, and giggling at how large my feet were. The facilities were horrible, they were using old buckets that did not look clean to soak feet in. The chair I was seated in was broken, much of the stuffing was removed, and the seat springs missing. Because of the way I had to sit in the seat, all the weight was placed on my tailbone. This was OK for the first bit of time, but the pedicure took SO LONG (probably because the technician kept stopping to talk to her friend). During the hour the pedicure took, all that was achieved was my tails cut, cuticles pushed back, and lotion applied to my legs and feet. She didn’t even rasp my heels. By the time she was ready to paint (I had to bring my own nail polish color), I could not take the pain from sitting on my tailbone anymore and told her to just leave it without polish. I paid the $28USD (the same price I would pay in the US and would have gotten a better service), went back to my room, and just painted the nails myself.  7) The guest service desk was not very helpful. Though they said they opened at 7AM, it was often not staffed until up to an hour later. We tried renting a few cars through them, and their price was literally 3 or 4 times the price that every other hotel in the area had gotten us. At other hotels we stayed at during our trip a nice vehicle that would fit the four of us would cost $40, through Yak and Yeti the same car costed $150 for the same amount of time. 8) The two times I ordered room service my order was incorrect. The first time I ordered a pastry dessert that was served with ice cream and a chocolate sauce. Instead, I got bright pink strawberry ice cream topped with chopped pistachios. When I called back to see if there had been a room mix up, they kept telling me that was the dish I ordered. After insisting that it wasn’t what was listed on the menu, they came up to my room, read the menu, and finally believed me. A few evenings later I was too exhausted to go out to dinner with my friends, and stayed back at the hotel and ordered dinner through room service. The order, again, was off from the menu description. I will say though, that the room service manager brought the dinner himself, and gave it too me for free as an apology for the mix up on the previous order. I appreciated that, and it was completely unexpected. It was the most anyone at Yak and Yeti seemed to care about any issues. 9) The Piano Lounge Bar was nice, though the service was slow and hit-or-miss. Some evenings we would go down for some cocktails, and the wait staff would be missing… Or just staring at us from the other side of the room. Almost every time we needed to order we had to get up and go find someone. Which, while not a huge deal, was annoying.   We tried bringing up our experiences to a few managers because we were getting increasingly frustrated as problems kept accumulating. While each manager seemed sympathetic, it also seemed clear that there were no steps they were going to take to try and make sure that our experience moving forward would be smoother. In fact, I got the distinct impression the managers from the different departments (ie. Room Service, House Keeping, Lounge, etc) didn’t communicate with each other. Because of the lack of communication, I don’t think it dawned on anyone just how bad our entire experience was. Frustrated, I paid the bill for everyone, took my guests, left 3 days early, and went to another hotel (Club Himalaya) that was 100% better in every single aspect. Yak and Yeti made me feel unimportant, unappreciated, unwelcome, and not well cared for. Especially since we were staying there for our wedding it was a disheartening experience. I would strongly recommend against anyone ever staying here.

I would like to sincerely thank the Management especially, Phillippe, Bharat and Krishna and of course the hard working staff at the Yak and Yeti Hotel Kathmandu. I have stayed at this hotel on my many visits to Nepal but did not expect to be there when the most severe of Earthquakes hit Nepal on the 25th April 2015.  The staff went out of their way to make everyone feel calm, safe and welcome, even though they themselves were concerned for loved ones, had homes destroyed. Thank you you are strong hard working people who will rise above this disaster.

We were very pleased to have chosen to stay at Yak & Yeti for three weeks holiday in Kathmandu.The location is ideal being at the heart of tourist hub of Kathmandu yet away from the crowd and pollution. Our room was excellent with a nice view of the beautiful garden with jugging path and swimming pool. We really enjoyed the morning walks.The best aspect of the hotel is that all the staff are very well trained and all of them greeted with wide smiles each time you pass by.and offered help for anything. Most of the staff seemed to have been working for long many years indicating that the Hotel is served by happy staff.The Chimney Restaurant is an experience which should not be missed.So looking forward to stay during next holiday.

Visited Kathmandu with a pre booked stay with parents and kids.lack of professionalism was noticed right upon arrival at airport.no body was there to pick up leaving us stranded for about an hour.this was despite the fact that the reservations had been contacted even a day before to update and cross check flight details.took about an hour to chek in .rooms are literally disappointing.smell of carpet dampens the feel of the 5 star.hotel is heavily occupied.request for upgrades was declined.food is good.nice jogging track and good club with spa facilities.adjoining casino is nice.no proper concierge however the lady on duty at guest services on 27 March was extremely help ful.house keeping has to be asked for everything unlike usual five stars. Overall not suited for someone looking for luxurious stay.ok for a business trip.wont recommend for a family stay if someone is prying for luxury.rooms are a real put off and give feel of hotels that existed 15 years back.

I have stopped at this hotel a number of times and always been happy. It is centrally located and you are protected from Nepal electricity load shedding as the Hotel has its own generator. They have also recently upgraded WiFi facilities.When I arrived without a booking when TIA closed unexpectedly due to Turkish Airline plane problem the staff were just superb. I was allowed free WiFi whilst I waited for updated news then a room was available with no problem. All the time the staff were attentive and helpful in a stressful time. I cannot praise them too highly - thank you Y+Y

We wanted to stay outside of Thamel but still close enough, so we chose this place.It's only 15 minutes walk to Thamel.It offers very peaceful grounds, great restaurant ( try the buffet) nice and clean room. Loved the garden . The wi-if cost extra and doesn't work that great. The staff is nice and polite.Had a good and peaceful stay here.Recommended!

We have stayed there for two  Nights but the location of this hotel itself is very conjusted between city with no good view from inside. There was no powerbackup and  pool area was very small.Please go through properly about it before booking.

Kathmandu is a fascinating place, but it is nice to come back to an elegant hotel at the end of the day. We found good food and comfortable rooms. We were beginning a month long trek in Nepal, and the hotel was a nice jumping off point.

With a terrific staff of friendly and considerate Nepalese, plus a garden and historical palace setting, the Yak & Yeti Hotel is the only place to stay in Kathmandu. Location is central and the huge garden a bonus of utter relaxation. We know this because we've been staying there annually for several years.

Stayed there when I was in Kathmandu this Nov. Nice quite place. Rooms are quite spacious. A bit old but very comfortable. Must try their the lobby bar. Service is friendly & very accommodating. Would definitely stay again when in Kathmandu.

I have been traveling to Nepal for over 20 years.  There are two luxury hotels in the game and I have stayed at Both.  The Hyatt and Dwarikas.  The Hyatt is in the boonies 30 minutes outside of Thamel (Main Kathmandu town), Dwarikas is good for first timers but vastly overpriced for what is delivered and location also...not great.  I am a walker and LOCATION is key to me, I don't like having to sit in terrible Kathmandu traffic to get anywhere and these hotels force that due to location.  I like being independent when I travel.The Yak and the Yeti is one of the historic grand dammes of Nepal....One of the oldest hotels on a giant plot of land with a beautiful swimming pool and garden.  LOCATION is PERFECT.....you are not a prisoner to this hotel.  You can walk into Thamel in 10 minutes and there are 50+ restaurants at least, within walking distance.  All sights are close as well and the ability to walk puts this hotel two steps above the others.  Unfortunately, over time the rooms at the Yak and Yeti have become run down.  However they have just opened a Newly Renovated wing that puts them back on the map!  The new heritage deluxe rooms are beautifully done with old wood, individual climate controls and beautiful rain shower, showers in stone.  The new rooms are (For Nepal)  Lovely and I would highly recommend staying in these.  The beds are new...so not sagging....the sheets are actually quite good and the pillows were clean and not smelly.  Keep in mind that Kathmandu attracts lots of dirty backpackers.....and Hygiene is not always their priority while hiking to basecamp....So to find an oasis like the Yak and Yeti is with newly renovated rooms is much appreciated.  All plugs and outlets worked, they have a back up generator so power outages are infrequent (Often in Nepali cheaper hotels) and our Internet connection was excellent at the best speeds I have seen yet.  The rooms were clean and efficient with lots of luggage space.  I would only book the New Heritage deluxe rooms.  But alas, I am fussy.  Service was excellent.  My reservations experience was easy and efficient with no errors as I was booking 4 rooms for my friends.  The day before we arrived we were notified that our airport transfer was going to be problematic as due to an upcoming Asian Summit, vans were not allowed in front of the airport for security reasons.  The hotel said they would meet us with some helpers to carry our luggage to the holding area.  Upon arrival, The Yak and Yeti had "facilitated" the van onto property and they picked us up easily on time with no fuss.  The service at this hotel was EXCELLENT.  Everyone smiled and tried to help us with whatever we needed.  Most employees here are long term employees and I think that is good as it shows the hotel treats their staff well.  Food for breakfast was 4 stars, very good service and they are catering for American/Chinese/Indian food....My friends loved it.  I ordered fresh scrambled eggs every day cooked in butter not oil....and there was no extra charge and they were hot and delicious.  We had drinks in the lounge and they ran out of our wine and didn't tell us they had substituted another bottle, but overall everyone across the board at this hotel tried to be as helpful as possible.  Between the renovated rooms and the location of this hotel, the Yak and Yeti is my current go to in Kathmandu.  It is a great balance between luxury and function and I look forward already to my next stay.    Enjoy Kathmandu Valley.

The hotel is very cozy and comfortable, the food is so delicious and room services very quick. All amenities available in the room no issues faced with WiFi so far . The staff very polite and helpful.

Very poor malabar prawn fettuccine cooked by complete amateur, drowning in sauce with only the taste of chilli and virtually inedible prawns, dry and hardened! Momos were OK, but will give the Chimney a miss in future!

On the whole, hotel was pleasant. Room was dated but well-decorated. Location was not the best but still reasonable. Food was edible. What really got me though was constantly being ripped off by the hotel on transport charges. It's as if they run some kind of junket with the taxi drivers on location. This was hardly an isolated incident. Here are some examples: 1. We were charged $30 for an airport drop off - at this price you would think you at least got a sedan with air-con. Nope. As comparison, we hired a driver to take us to the airport, wait for us and drive us back to the hotel for our everest flight - 2,000 rupees (i.e., <$20) and with a proper sedan with ac.2. We took a taxi from the hotel to the Boudanouth stupa - hotel insisted it would cost 800 rupees which was what we paid. Taxi back, flagged on the street - 500 rupees. And almost certainly already an overcharged tourist price. 3. We took a taxi from the hotel to a restaurant nearby (no more than 10 min drive). Hotel insisted it would be 1000 rupees for one-way 2500 rupees for a standby. In one of those no-ac taxis. Even after we expressed unhappiness at the price, and after a lot of bargaining - finally got it down to 700 rupees. The final price when the restaurant called us a taxi home? 400 rupees. I have no problems paying for quality service. The problem is staff clearly prized their unethical taxi drivers (who sit around the exit all day waiting for idiot tourists) instead of the well-being of their guests. Also i would have a lot less of an issue with this practice if there were slightly more luxurious cars. Let's just say driving down the dusty streets of Kathmandu in a dirty open-air taxi, having paid 2x of market rate is NOT my idea of good hotel service.

I ordered for the Yak and Yeti club sandwich sadly to my expectations with what I came it didn’t go well. The sandwich was icy cold tasted only ice the presentation was bad and the fries looked bad as well. To my disappointment when I requested to change it to the server they said 80% had been consumed! And they tried to offer me a coffee rebate to cover up! I am disappointed badly being a 5 star hotel such poor customer service!

Really enjoyed the amenities and the staff is all so kind and service oriented - very centrally located and convenient for dining, shopping and tours. Beautiful gardens and relaxing lounge as well as a wide variety of food options - the best hotel service I have encountered anywhere!

Very well located near main street in Katmandu, shopping and restaurants all around, staff is very kind. WiFi should be complimmentary, the furniture looks old. For breakfast ther is buffet, for lunch or dinner there is also buffet or other preparations.

I stayed at Hotel Yak & Yeti for a business trip. The hotel location is safe and secure, and very close to many main attractions. The breakfast buffet was okay. The room was clean and comfortable. There are a couple of reasons I gave this hotel 3 stars. First, I was disappointed with the customer service. I had made my purchase from Expedia, and the hotel had received my confirmation through another email link. I had to ask them to honor the free breakfast that was included with my deal. The staff stated I booked through a different website, but I had my confirmation email with me. I also felt the desk and door staff were not helpful about booking taxi service. As a foreigner, you will be ripped off in Nepal, and taxi drivers do not speak English very well. I would have appreciated a little more assistance. Lastly, while the room was clean, I think they could put more water in the room for the price I paid. I would stay here for business, but I would welcome other hotels for personal travel.

The yak and yeti Hotel is a sanctuary in the hustle and bustle that is Kathmandu.It has a modern feel yet the service is old fashioned . Mind you it is not cheap ,but the attention to detail is comforting.We only spent a few nights there ,one being my birthday and a surprise cake was delivered to the room.The buffet restaurant is a bit noisy but the room service menu is comprehensive.

i have never had such a pathetic experince ever. i have been to some finest and shady hotels, but never felt the need to bad mouth any homeland i am not too good with words. But the staff of this hotel leaves no stone unturned to put you off. The staff is not well trained and have extremely bad attitude. Booked this property for our stay over the new years weekend and location of this property did not disappoint. But nothing apart from location seemed to work for us. The staff is rude and outrightly refuses to provide with the basic/ extremely necessary things like boiling/ sterilising the bottles for kids. Waiters act as if i have asked them for money while i have just asked for tea while having breakfast. room service is poor. our rooms were not cleaned properly whenever asked for. food was bad. All in all i would say just spare yourself some bad time and money and not book this hotel.

I stayed here in the Spring as part of a group; two visits of several days each  before and after a trip to Everest. My reason for hesitancy in staying here was partly because of any hangover from the 2015 earthquake and partly some of the reviews I read before going. Overall I would say this is a very good choice in Kathmandu and I would stay here again - It's certainly an oasis in the middle of a dusty, noisy hubbub.. It does give off a sort of (post) colonial air with things like reserved parking near the front door for UN vehicles. There seem to be quite a lot of functions (conferences) and meetings. Note some of these include outdoor entertainment or dinners (they didn't go on late into the evening when I was there but they can fill up large parts of the gardens).  Some of the reviews around  Winter or Spring mentioned it needed decorating and there were heating and or cooling problems. I thought the decor was fine in the rooms where I stayed.Yes maybe they could be updated a little (this is not a contemporary glass palace) but much better than I feared and way better than many "world class" international hotels . I did have a heating / cooling  issue on my first visit but maintenance came to the room and fixed the problem very quickly. The room was a good size (lets say traditionally decorated in a western fashion) and the bathroom also very good. TV etc worked fine and there was a coffee maker in the room. I'd read somewhere that the Internet was expensive ($40 day??). In fact it's $10 day and the speed, signal were fine - so the value was not bad as far as I was concerned. You may find some deals with it included. I think they exist but not when I was there.  Again some reviews mentioned the breakfast buffet was a little static in terms of offering. To be honest I'm not sure what else you could offer since it is a pretty huge selection (but yes it is basically the same selection each day). There are many western items such as home made cakes and pastries, eggs, potatoes etc and the most wonderful home made bread.    There is a crepe station where you can get them made to order. I believe you can order eggs as you like them, though I did not do this. The buffet includes Asian (Indian) food, Chinese and Middle Eastern, everyday. One thing I will say is coming from across the other side of the world and needing a caffeine fix at odd hours,  they do have great coffee. Strong and certainly beats Starbucks - or I thought so anyway. The restaurant has great views of the gardens by the way. Sit near the windows if you can. Note some of the room rates include breakfast. Definitely worth taking advantage of this.The public areas of the hotel are fine (lots of sofas and chairs in different areas as well as a bar) and all the staff (including in the restaurant) were very responsive on the whole. On thing I will mention is that the hotel provides bottled water in the room every day - to bottles. I don't think you can drink tap water anywhere in Nepal and if you are traveling through the countryside (Climbing or Trekking??) where there is little to no medical support then health is so important - start as you mean to carry on and be manic about protecting yourself. The reason I mention this is that you need to use bottled water for teeth etc not just drinking. So you may well find 2 bottles a day is not enough if you are keeping hydrated. I personally feel the hotel  needs to allow more than 2 bottles a day without having to purchase the extras - that can get (relatively) expensive.The hotel grounds are large and (depending on the time of year) green and full of flowers. There is quite a large pool and again some of the reviews I read said it was empty. I do think the availability of facilities probably cycles with the (tourist) seasons.Just outside the hotel gates are some shops selling T shirts, clothing, etc as well as money changers. Thamel is about 20 minutes walk away - have a great death defying time crossing the roads on the way !!  If you cross at the junctions, the traffic does seem to avoid you but it is exciting......

It is a hopeless property, we had to wait for 4 hours on our arrival to get a room, the rooms have very few lights, only one mobile charging point, bathroom door doesnt lock , old bath fittings, food is below average, room service takes 1 hr to get stuff you ask. Casino is very old and dingy, airconditioner doesnt work there, service in the casino is very bad , you have to ask atleast 10 times for a glass of coke. Overall a very bad experience, will never come back again in Yak and Yeti.Advice to all -stay in Crowne Plaza or Shangrila when you are in kathmandu,both are in same price range and best of service and experience.

Had a one night stay at this rather grand looking hotel, stayed in a heritage room which was comfortable and clean.Strange smell of cooking on the fourth floor corridor was very odd like walking into a kitchen.The staff and welcome were great but it did feel chaotic as it seems to cater much better for groups and we did have this feeling that we may have been in the way.The room worked fine but had single glazing (not as described) and there was lots of outside noise and when the music played the glass rattled in the frame.We should have been advised there was an outside event on before finding it for ourselves, this made it impossible to use the swimming pool, in addition the 7am wake up dismantling the stage the next morning was annoying.Service was slow in the bar at first until finally somebody must have decided we needed to pay for using the seats and we got our drinks.Worst of all was the non working a/c, whilst it blew ambient air there was no chill about it, and I complained and then I opened the windows, then at around 3am when I still had no working a/c I send the reservations manager an email and so far no reply. So in the end a terrible sleep followed by a chaotic scene for breakfast, and at check out they could not wait to get rid of us even calling at 9am to find out why we had not checked out.I liked the look of this place and did some of what was described but it's not on the list for a return visit.

I was in Kathmandu when the April 2015 earthquake hit. The hotel manager showed EXCELLENT leadership to make sure that his guests were safe, reassured, and well fed in the aftermath of the earthquake. Both he, and his staff, went way beyond what was necessary, to ensure the safety and comfort of the hotel guests, especially at a time what the situation outside was quite chaotic. I have stayed twice at the hotel, and will return whenever I am back in Kathmandu.

I am grateful I got to see Kathmandu and this grand hotel before the quake. Place was lovely, with different rooms for different experiences.  Did some walkabouting and twas a great base for all my explorations. I sure hope to come back soon.

After reading some negative reviews on tripadvisor, we changed our original reservations of 3 nights to 1 nite at Yak and Yeti.  The other hotel we stayed at for two nights was Hotel Dwarika.  Our one night stay at the shangri-la executive level was very pleasant.  As another reviewer said this is the best option for this hotel.  The extras of breakfast, wine and afternoon snacks were excellent and our private concierge on the floor made it a very very nice stay.  On top of all these positives, we had free strong wifi. I would definitely stay here again.

This hotel was a haven after we had been sleeping rough following the earthquake. The U.S. Airforce guys informed us that after the Hyatt and Raddison the hotel was the 3rd safest.. So we were thrilled to hear this! The room was clean and tidy, I wouldn't say 5star compared to UK hotels but a good 3+/4, the buffet was expensive and the drinks but it was fantastic food and the staff were great! The grounds were also very beautiful! However all said the only disappointment we faced was my colleague Donya having £700 stolen out of her handbag. We informed the mangers, who then proceeded to search our room, and then try and convince us as if we were naive children, that we could of spent the money???? Now we had a room filled with aid and toys which we had brought in the UK and nepal out of sponsor money , we tried explaining and even showed receipts to show they had all been brought on card? Jesus! We are women in our 30s and were made to feel like we were lying! Basically out safe had been broken, so my friend made the mistake of thinking her money would be safe hidden in her handbag in the wardrobe. Following this the helpful manager (head of security) said we didn't need to involve the police he would start an investigation. This produced nothing but only to show who had been in the room, on one day in a 45 minute gap .. After housekeeping, someone had entered our room 3 times??? We had no mini bar etc so when we questioned this and why they had gone in so much we were shrugged off! In addition to this, a guy from housekeeping turned up un-announced and knocked without saying a word... Now the housekeeping maid had already been to the room 30 minutes before, when my friend opened the door, he and a friend stood there asking if she was 'ok' ? As she answered the door she saw coincidently a bug, so she asked these two guys to remove a bug, they then vanished!!! When we asked about these guys, the manager told us they were pest control and we had called them????? Bizzare!!! Because the bug was only spotted when my friend got up to answer the door to them, we hadn't called anyone or prompted any visit!!!  We had to chase for constantly for updates nobody ever came to us, we also contacted and informed the British embassy. Upon check out no apology or even mention of it, and we left two weeks ago, and still no contact! They have literally brushed it under the carpet! Quite rude. It saddened me that this hotel ramped the prices up on booking.com and also totally denied and ignored the fact we had £700 stolen from our room.. Very sad, especially when we were there on our own, offering free volunteer support to its country and working with their children.

I was at Yak&Yeti hotel last Tueday and Wednesday nights.On Tueday, as you might know, there was a 7,4 earthquake during day time and we had a 5.6 in the middle of the night ...The staff has been very nice, bringing blankets for those who wanted to stay sleeping in the garden.Generally speaking, I have the feeling that this construction is rather strong and safe.

We flew from Kathmandu to Pokhara then spent some time trekking  and taking a flight across Everest. To save money we took a bus back from Pokhara to Kathmandu. Least said about that the better. Quite unnerving  However we used the savings to have two nights in the Yak and Yeti.   Very sumptuous.  Great barbers for a decent shave. Good food  all in all a really good place to stay. Much impressed by some of the wedding ceremonies that took place.  The Yeti footprint is a must see. If you can go there. go there  a really lovely place

We entered the Hotel at 5pm after the the severe Natural disaster. The Hotel lead by its General Manager, Philippe Belhay did a wonderful job of its Hotel inmates.Philippe would address all and update the forecast of quakes and assured us that the Hotel is strong enough. An assurance of this kind provides assurance to one and all and ensures that concerns are addressed.The Hotel took care to give us Water, Breakfast,Lunch and Dinner which was par excellence considering that the world outside the Hotel was that ALL restaurants and shops were closed.We felt very safe in the Hotel institute of repeated EARTHQUAKES over the next 48 Hours.Sense of ownership and Passion for the job was Very High among the staff and customer satisfaction focus was utmost.

This was my third stay at the Yak and Yeti and have to say I discovered another important reason that the Yak should be your hotel of choice in Kathmandu.  Yes, it is a comfortable hotel with a lovely garden that is quite a haven in the centre of busy Kathmandu and cleanliness is an important priority here so just a pleasure to come into your room at night.  Staff are always ready to assist.But being there during the earthquake convinced me it is THE place to stay.  The building was built by a Japanese firm with the spring construction system that offers protection in earthquakes.  A 7.9 on the Richter scale  only produced very minor damage - nothing in my room.  However, it was the response from Hotel Manager, Philippe Belhay and his terrific staff that deserves recognition.  He made an extraordinary effort to keep the hotel guests constantly informed of the situation and provided advice to ensure our safety.  And his Nepali staff were equally stellar.  Here they had families and homes affected by the quake and they were constantly asking us if we were "okay" or need anything.  An outstanding performance.

Cannot really fault the Yak & Yeti as a safe, good quality hotel, guaranteed to deliver what you would expect for the price. What it lacks is any emotional or visual connection with Nepal / Kathmandu. Staff were efficient, but could have come from any mass global hotel chain....In summary good business hotel, excellent gardens, but leaves you a bit cold!

- Humongous hotel compared to others in Kathmandu.- Stayed in another supposedly 4 stars hotel and moved the other day to this one.- Check-in took less than 5 minutes- Spacious room with effective air conditioner.- Very quite to relax. - Big beds with very comfortable mattress, pillows and covers.- Bathroom was well equipped; nothing major missing. For those who like to use water for toilet cleaning; a toilet nozzle is in place.- lobby is very spacious with many seating areas.- Service within the hotel is not open 24/7; everything is dark early morning.- Spacious outdoor area with greens and a swimming pool ( dirty too swim in but you can still enjoy the shezlong, drinks, etc.- Nothing spectacular about the breakfast and dinner buffet, but surely gets the job done with satisfaction. But don't expect like full cheese bar or the perfection of your choice of eggs.- Room service was acceptable.- Different regions have different standards for hotels; so comparing it with Middle East or East Asia (Thailand, S. Korea); the standards are lower.- Throughout my stay, apparently they had a guest who is accustomed to book the very room I was in. That didn't bother me much to move around, however, took us 3 rooms to find a decent room without a stinky odor and a proper air conditioner. So watch out and ensure you get a room without the hassle.- Required 2 visits to fix the light strip running by the wall; which wasn't very convenient, but was resolved.- Booked an express laundry; which apparently never arrived on-time and they close at night. Took Danish (from the reception and if I remember his name correctly; hope I do) at least 2 hours to allocate it. Appreciate his efforts a lot.- Provided free comfortable transportation back to the airport.Conclusion:Room & sleep quality: 9/10Service: 7/10; even though staff is very friendly, but they are not very well prepared by management.Buffet: 7/10Facilities: 7/10Would I book it on my next trip: Most likely yes.Price: A bit more expensive to the quality seen.

This landmark Kathmandu hotel, which has an old-world charm about it, is centrally located, close to the main shopping street and the bargain bazaar district of Thamel. It has beautiful red-bricked buildings and a lovely garden with an elevated pavilion and a swimming pool. The lobby has a quaint rotunda-like waiting lounge where guests can sit and chat. The rooms are reasonably spacious and comfortable with a useful window  ledge where you can conveniently place your travel stuff, The breakfast buffet does not have a wide variety but is reasonably good. There is a small casino next to the hotel. To gain entry is cumbersome as you have to provide passport details. Once you are inside you will  be disappointed to find a somewhat primitive operation consisting of a handful of roulette tables and betting machines. The air is heavy with cigarette smoke.  There are quite a number of shops in the laneways around the hotel but prices are nowhere as competitive as Thamel which is about a 20 minute walk away. Be careful when walking at night in the laneways leading to the hotel as some sections do not have street lighting. Overall we had a pleasant stay.

stayed here for 3 nights. beautiful gardens and ideal for hotel guests to do some exercise - brisk walk in the mornings...rooms are nice... and quite spacious....only thing is Wi-Fi.... keeps disconnecting....also, airport pickup and drop off.... hotel has only one mini-bus.... had to wait an hour plus to get a pick up from airport to hotel.... disappointed.... making you wait...I would go back to this hotel again... improve the

Yak&Yeti is an up-market hotel back to back with the former Royal Palace which is now a posh conference center. There is something majestic about the whole place: lobby, reception, guest rooms, restaurants and garden. Staff are courteous and genuinily helpful for solving all types of problems and arranging tours (e.g to Bhaktapur)--but probably this place will give you no problems of its own. Breakfasts, lunches and dinners are delicious and  their buffets varied, Lamb curry is a must. The ambiance is welcoming for body and soul. The hotel provides airport shuttle service which takes you to your destination as fast as local traffic circumstances allow, i.e. sometimes rather slow. We enjoyed our stay at the Yak&Yeti and the shops and small businesses in the nearby neighborhood just outside the guarded gate. This is a comfortable sanctuary in the middle of Kathmandu, standing out in a city of numerous challenges and mental rewards and a point of departure for explorations in Nepal.

Very good property , one of the best in KTM. We stayed here for 3 nights and was a confortable stay but Staff is too professional with no personel touch with customers. The quality of buffet is very good but A La carte menu is just useless no variety in A La carte. However the backyard of hotel, is good as well the Spas and other location are nice but the Casino is pathetic people , pathetic condition and pathetic outputs by machine all are set with low payouts.

Lovely hotel within easy reach of the sights of Kathmandu. We were upgraded as the first room we were allocated was in need of some restoration. The second stay we were in a room at the front on the 4th Floor. After a long road journey from Chitwan we needed to sleep. There was heavy noise from a generater. After complaining we were move to a room overt he gardens. Much better. Food was very good. With a large selection. Probably the best on our tour. Staff were efficient and helpful. Hotel General Manager, Phileppe took time out to visit our table and chat.  Recommend this hotel.

This place is one of the top choices in Kathmandu. I enjoyed my stay here and found nothing lacking (except the free wi-fi was very frustratingly spotty). Puzzled by some of the reviews. I did not find this place to be resting on its laurels at all, on the contrary, everybody was very friendly and helpful and the facility has just about all the Kathmandu/Nepal traveler could want in a hotel.

We stayed at Yak & Yeti during our first trip to Nepal and Kathmandu. This does not offer a 5-star experience, but the location and good service makes up for it!The hotel is located on the Durbar Marg though the entrance is a bit inside and a short walk from Durbar Marg. It took us about ~15-20mins drive from the airport. Thamel is also closeby.The rooms are really dated and unimpressive. But everything in the room was functional so no complaints there. We had a deluxe room with no view to speak of. The windows were overlooking neighbouring private residences. The room was quite large and spacious.Where I would score them high is on their satisfactory service. Our arrival flight was delayed and I was really concerned about not finding a transport landing late in the night in a new city. I was pleasantly surprised that the hotel airport pickup was patiently waiting for us despite 4-5 hours of delay from the scheduled time. The in-room service was also very good. We ordered breakfast and dinner in the room and everything came right on time.The concierge was helpful in arranging our day tours. This is probably the best that you can expect in this city, but they will definitely score higher if they can beef up the rooms a bit! I may decide to explore another hotel next time.

We spent 5 days at this lovely oasis in the middle of the chaotic Katmandu. The service could be a little better and the spa is overpriced for a not very good fully clothed massage.The room was nice and well serviced during our stay. It is worth booking a club room and making use of the happy hour.

I stayed Yak&Yeti 6 days  during my business visit. The most important thing  for me in the hotel was, that it has  good internet connections, peaceful night sleep and  room available soon after my  night flight. Those things are very important  during business visits, but what  I enjoyed most was kind room service.  Everything was clean and even several times a day  I was asked if everything is Ok, do I have laundry, remote batteries were changed  rapidly etc.  I was even asked if I want room service to make my night bed, lights and curtains!  It was luxury after a hard day! And a smiling guard opening the door every time when going out: Namaste!

When i visited nepal, we stayed at the yak and yeti hotel and the breakfast is just awesome, i had very much fun in the swimming pool with my siblings and the beds are so comfortable...loved the experience

We stayed in the Yak and Yeti upon our arrival into Kathmandu, and it is a wonderful way to become acclimated to the hustle and bustle, the chaos, and the other-worldliness of Kathmandu.  The hotel is very well-equipped by any standards whether Western, or Nepali standards.  Most importantly the staff is highly professional and welcoming which ensures that you will have the best stay possible.  Or particular note is the delightful concierge, Manisha, who we found to be exceptionally charming, knowledgeable and helpful.  She helped ensure that we would have the best time possible, and make the most use of our limited time in the City.  To us, she was the face of Yak and Yeti, and made a wonderful impression of our entire experience at the hotel.In summation, I highly recommend a stay at the Yak and Yeti to get the most out your visit to Kathmandu, and to acclimate yourself to the adventure of Nepal!

I found the service at Yak and Yeti excellent. The staff was generally warm , friendly and attentive. No request was beyond them. There was always a friendly smile and greeting from all the staff, from housekeepers to front office staff to bell hops . I highly recommend this hotel.

Amazing place. Started with a big smile when we entered the hotel. I with my other 5 friends booked 3 rooms at the beginning and end of our trip to Nepal for a couple of days.Nice and big rooms with a nice view to the swimming pool. Breakfast is great especially the mango juice. It's fresh. They do provide Halal food as well.Swimming pool is quiet and clean. Ducks are playing near the pool. Internet is available free only in the lobby. We talked to the General Manager Mr. Philip and he offered us a free access to the rooms as well. The hotel is few minutes far from the main shopping area in Kathmandu. Spa and money exchange are one step out of the hotel.Frankly I can say that Yak and Yeti is the best hotel I visited in Nepal. If I do visit Nepal again, definitely I will stay at Yak and Yeti.

I've been staying at the Yak and Yeti for one or two nights a year on business for many years. It has always struck me as having a great deal of potential but needing a lick of paint and a bit of tlc generally. My most recent visit was after an absence of a few years and I noticed several improvements. I stayed in a heritage room which despite being cheaper was a big improvement on the shangri la club room that I usually stay in. More modern and fresh looking but still retaining some traditional Nepali charm. A comfortable bed too. The food as always was good, although I always eat from the Indian selection so I can't comment on the western style food. And the public areas including the swimming pool and gardens seemed much cleaner and improved. The hotel itself has many interesting nooks and crannies including an indoor shopping boulevard selling local souvenirs and at the end of it is are the conference rooms with a magnificent staircase and pictures of Nepali life over the last one hundred years. Well worth spending an hour wandering around. My only complaint is that the cleaning in the rooms is not up to western four or five star standards. Not enough to put me off but some areas need a bit more attention from cleaning staff which other than training wouldn't cost the hotel any extra to do. Cleaning behind the beds and in wardrobes and cleaning of a/c vents for example. Overall though a big improvement and I shall definitely continue staying here despite there being increased competition from other hotels in Nepal. Hope to see more improvements next time I visit.

I was the most confused soul to book the hotel in Kathmandu since it was my first visit and read various mixed reviews about all the five star properties. Booked my hotel at 2 AM in the night and had to catch the fight at 1(afternoon) the next day. Narrowed the decision to 2 hotels - Annapurna and Yak and Yeti and thankfully chose the latter. As my trip went by I kept loving my decision. Check-in was very quick with the smiling front office staff who upgraded us to a suite, which was a lovely welcome to us. The suite was spic and span and overlooked the lawns and the pool. Wi-fi worked fine and is free with the room tariff (it just works on one device though). I misplaced my password and the business centre kindly helped me with the same.The Best Bit - was the casino - Casino Royale - surely not the bond's casino royale but still kept the charm of the name. Filled with people me and my friend had a splendid time playing Black Jack and Little Kitty , not to forget the countless coins I lost and countless my friend won. Some of the dancers were really pretty and danced amazingly on bollywood numbers :)The buffet was average not expanse but enough and hot. I will not say it was bad but would like to mention that croissants and tea were really nice.The location of the hotel is at the right spot Durbar road and very close to Thamel. I was happy to be back on Dubar road after having bought variety of tea from Thamel and eating dimsums.My entire weekend was spent wonderfully and the main reason was my hotel. I went to Casino Anna but was totally disappointed by the people in there and the layout. The staff and the manager at casino royale also always recognised the guests and gave us good welcome whenever we were at the casino. Made friends there who moved to Yak and Yeti on our recommendation from Hyatt.Well whenever I go back again , I will book it once again on the hotels website. The only drawback or feedback would be for the hotel to offer some counters for the casino to resident guests .. Thanks

stayed from 16th to 19th jan 2014nice stay good staffbreakfast was not  up to the mark as daily the menu was same my family got bored to eat the same breakfastbut overall experience was good looking for staying again

Nice hotel which is about 10 minutes walk to major tourist attractions and very helpful and friendly staff. Only issue was the breakfast which did not have much options of local variety of dishes which tourist would be expecting. Mainly continental and south Indian dishes.

The Hotel is very old now. More than 45 years old!! It badly needs renovation as the rooms are old and run down. Though it’s a very nice styled place and the foods not bad and the service is good and location too is good , the place need modernisation.

We were booked at the Yak/Yeti as part of the upgrade package to 5 star hotels during our Everest Base Camp Trek tour.  We were disappointed at the quality of the hotel rooms.  The bathroom door and cabinet doors in our rooms were old, run down and dilapidated, definitely not worthy of a 5 star hotel, more like a 2-3 star hotel.  Wifi is not free and cost $7.50 usd/day.  Overall experience was mediocre.

We stayed in Yak&Yeti hotel from 8th of Nov till 10th, first we tried with reception to get a room with toilet hand sprayer but unfortunately they have 2 buildings, one old building without this option in the toilet and another building with this option. The receptionist which was wearing traditional uniform for Nipal people responded to our request that there aren't available rooms. She took very long time to accommodate us.The room was very old in decor and furniture.Although the provided shaving blade was kept in small box but unfortunately it was used one ( I found hair on the blades), imagine if I didn't note and use it!!!??I informed the receptionist same day to consider such hygienic problems with their housekeeping.We requested to change the rooms to the new building which equipped with toilets hand sprayers and actually the reception applied our request.The room in the new building is totally different, it's decor and furniture are new and the rooms look better.The view from the room was on the pool and the hotel garden which is huge and looks well arranged.The breakfast was good and there were many varieties.We got our dinner 3 times in the main restaurant in the hotel which was good and actually we looked for vegetables items and shrimp items as we were afraid from unavailability of HALAL food which was not mentioned in the menu. The service team was amazing and their care about their guests was observed.Check out was so quickly and better than the check in.

We spent two nights in the hotel. We had very high expectations having read and heard a lot. It is a good property right in the center of the city with good ground, greenery, etc. but alas the rooms are tired-looking and needs lots of upkeep. The bathroom and main door are chipped, mattress not very comfortable and horror, there was roach in the bathroom!!Breakfast spread is excellent but the restaurant has a very limited choices for vegetarians!! Well, if you do not go with a very high expectation, you would enjoy.

2 British ladies travelling together for Tihar. Lovely oasis in middle of chaotic Kathmandu. Did not feel need to complain of feedback about any issues there and then however would like to comment for improvement reasons.I would suggest 3 star by European standards so rather pricey / difficult to book local excursion is bus ticket to Bandipur.....much easier doing it on 'high street' / pricey and not nice wine by UK standards (its imported) / bar shuts prompt at 23.00 so no night caps (missing an opportunity?) / pool wasnt well designed ie low water and tiles looked dirty so not eay to get into, just ladders and pool coffee service was hit and miss / breakfast room was long walk but I belived was moved closer during our visit (we werent impressed with food anyway so went out).

Two sides to hotel, think of it as “classic” vs “new”.  I prefer classic side when arriving to go out on trek, with each room having a “gear sorting bench”.  And then the “modern” side when returning from trek, where the hot shower force is 2nd to none in the world (can peel your skin off if you ket it 😊)

Housekeeping was good and attended to a small complaint immediately. The restaurant Chimney is very good. Momos fantastic!! Though the check in on 23 was a bit delayed, the staff were very friendly and the overall experience was good. Location is great. The property has rich heritage value!!

YNY provides the old school charm of living in a heritage like hotel. The rooms are fairly luxurious and the deco is gorgeous. One downside is that the hotel staff can be a little unattentive, having opened my hotel door at 9am one morning for housekeeping (whilst i was getting out of bed) and started vacuuming the common corridor at 8 am on a Sunday.

Honestly the staff is really perfect - the room are not the most of top - breakfast is poor quality - but all the staff do their best for make your staying as better they can.The place is really charming - too much pigeon for me …. but again garden is so beautiful

I stayed here for four nights in July with friends.  I loved the name of the hotel, and enjoyed my stay, too.The Yak and Yeti is probably one of the "Old School" hotels of Kathmandu--the service is very good, the restaurants were convenient with good food and lots of choices.  The hotel itself reminded me of something out of the golden days of the Raj in India--it's huge and in a style not seen much anymore. The building was added onto over the years, and retains its charm.  If you want an authentic Nepalese experience, stay here.

Found this hotel as best value for money with options of entertainment and nightlife in close vicinity. All night clubs and massage parlours in neighboring areas at walking distance. Good professional staff and nice ambience of hotel. Good for family stay.

This is an excellent hotel with a very nice garden/pool area and good restaurants. The rooms are very nice, although some will find wear and tear it is excellent value by western standards. Just don't expect 5* rooms - more like good 4*. Good touches are biscuits/apple on arrival in the room and bottled water provided daily (useful for brushing teeth as well as re-hydrating). Good shampoo/shower gel and a big shower.The breakfast is a very nice buffet - with everything from noodles to curry and even baked beans. The two restaurants are also good - especially the buffet near the entrance.There were a couple of issues they could fix: mini-bar person knocking on the door around 9am, room service not waiting before opening the door to ask if everything is OK, phoning the room to discuss marketing, sitting next to you in the restaurant to "discuss the hotel"/marketing. A bit of staff training and the hotel would feel more professional. As I knew about the water shortages I left towels on the rail so they were not washed - but I suspect they are swapped anyway. A shopping tip is that there is a little street on the way out which has a good range of items at excellent prices.In summary this is easily 4.5/5 and an ideal place to stay in Kathmandu.

I just entered Nepal & have booked a business class shangrila suite with Yak & Yeti for 3 people. They offer complimentary pickup. But sent a indigo for 3 people that too broken car. We had to rent another car. When we reached the hotel there was no special welcome. Later the hotel staff also asked us to pay for the taxi. Poor service. Regretful decision. Will not advice. Bad first trip impression to nepal. Will post this on all websites.

This combined the interpretation of the Tibetan culture heritage area with the blue skies and big mountain views of the arid Himalayan rain shadow. Sort of like Grand Canyon meets the world's biggest mountains.Not only was the trip well planned and guided in a fast-changing region with great care taken of us, Local knowledge and connections resolved the problem without affecting the success of the trip. obviously enjoyed this area themselves and knew it thoroughly. There was hardly a question they couldn't answer.We would recommend this company highly.Bryn BeorseSeattle USA

Magnificent hotel, which has seen its best times. Big grounds,swimming pool which all needs a facelift now. Staff was very polite and courteous. Did their best to make our stay pleasant. Excellent location.

After trekking for 3 days and staying in some... interesting places, I was pleased to be at the Yak & Yeti for the final part of our stay in Kathmandu. The service during our stay was great at the staff could not do enough for us when needed. The hotel was clean and rooms were a great size. I confess that the plug sockets and wifi were an issue but not having wifi for a few days is not the end of the world for me being connected 24/7 was nice to switch off.Was a little disappointed with the pool not being cleaned and ready for use which would have been appreciated in the humidity and heat, however, was being cleaned the following day... although to late for our stay.I would recommend the Yak & Yeti for its location and service, and although yes, could do with an upgrade and little maintenance. Would go back again!

Let's not discuss things which is supposed to be in 5 star Hotel.I have not found anything extra or special from staff or hotel itself.But somethings nice I could see like mini lake for geeses and monument in the courtyard ( pics attached). That's all.The breakfast.One of the worst bakery I ever seen in all hotels around the world. Banana bread just for lough. 2 types of not ripe melons and watermelons. Dirty nuts. I asked the staff to wash them and make it dry: they asked why and they just  heated in microwave for 5 minutes and gave me back. I didn't want continue this and just gave them this nuts back.The swimming pool area.Absolutely impossible to lay done because of the flies. They are hundreds there and you can not relax.The room.Quite old furniture. No sockets next to the bed. Dirty toilet and bath. Mould in the corner next to the bath. No bathrob. Minimum towels, not meeting standard of 5 star hotels.Annoying service.Every day at 10 o'clock guy knocking to your room check you mini bar. Doesn't matter you are sleeping or not. Same in the evening. It's called "evening service, sir". They woke me up a lot of times with no reason.Parking bicycle. The metal Z installed in the parking area for bicycles fell down when I lean my bicycle against it. And the last is money, almost 200$ for nothing. The staff don't know how to treat customers at all.

We were expecting a 5 star hotel, but that is not what we got. We were not happy that our travel agent selected the Yak and Yeti, which we ended up calling the Yuk and Yeti. Apparently she has not been to to hotel in several years because it is no longer the classy place she described. The hotel has lovely grounds, that's where the complements end. There is no way this place deserves 5 stars - maybe 3 on a good day. It is dark, the furnishings are dated, they have a pigeon problem so the rooms facing the gardens may come with the noise of nesting/fighting pigeons (ours did). Many of the rooms have a terrible odor of smoke, which lingers in the hallways too. They have intermittent blackouts so the power goes out fairly regularly. The rooms are spartan. The service at the breakfast buffet was slow - I had to get up to chase down a waiter to get coffee (but the coffee was exceptionally good once I got it). The one bright spot os the concierges, who were terrific when we needed to get something from a pharmacy.I do not recommend this place. We had dinner at Dwarika's and loved that hotel - that truly is a 5 star property. You can do better than the Yuk and Yeti.

The Yak and Yeti is a little old but fairly well kept, not as grand as it looks in the photos but the rooms are okay and the restaurant seems clean and reasonable. Upon arrival there was a big fuss about Wifi and payment - the staff were not overly accommodating or friendly about their mistake. We also moved rooms due to heavy smoke smells coming through. Overall a fairly good stay, we had a driver take us around but still only a short walk from the main street. It is far enough away that you don't get too much of the noise and traffic which is a bonus.

Very confortable hotel, with a higher level than many others in KTM. Rooms are large and clean with a very nice view on the garden which is a nice place to walk and take some rest. Nice swimmig pool open when is warm. Hotel staff is very friendly, a very special thanks to the always smiling and kind girls Goma, Bindu, Sharmila, Sabita, Shanti, Ritu and to other hotel staff cleaning rooms. Breakfast is very good, restaurant food usually good even if not so much international. Very recommended hotel.

Our recent stay was very comfortable with large rooms. Check in was very fast and we were greeted warmly by Ms. Anu and Ms. Sabina. The hotel has an excellent bar and restaurant and its close proximity to the main shopping area makes this an attractive place to stay. The rooms and the hotel areas are kept clean and the exposed ground is watered down in the mornings to keep the dust down.

I have a fond liking for the buffet lunch at Yak and Yeti. The food spread and the dessert items are lavish. I always come here once a month. Started with a casual lunch and now it’s become a must.For lunch it’s Yak and Yeti buffet!!!

We stayed at the Yak & Yeti with 4 adult children (3rooms) after our EBC trek. We couldn’t be happier with our choice.(We stayed at a 3star in Thamel on the first night in Kathmandu which was cold with intermittent wifi, so can definitely compare favourably.)The property is well maintained in a heritage style. It’s warm with good lobby area sofas.The staff from doorman, porter, front office, housekeeping, waiters were all excellent and attentive.Breakfast was plentiful and delicious with a wide range for Asian and Anglo tastes.The rooms were very comfortable with good beds, great pillows and climate control (although a bit warm for our taste even with the heat off). The bathroom was in good condition with a very good shower with excellent water pressure.Wifi was good in the room and in the common areas.Walking distance to Thamel (10 mins) and restaurants and shops.I would highly recommend this hotel if you’re looking for 5 star comfort with atmosphere.

Room temperature in the room kept warm and nice when the outside is  6 degree c. Very helpful staff. Especially Miss Sabina.Money Exchange offered at the hotel is very fair compared to money change outside.Breakfast had limited variety compared to other 5 star hotel.Location is good . Not far from main road So, it relatively quite. Sue

My wife and I stayed for 2 nights at the hotel. The hotel is well located near to Thamel area. The hotel however is old and in desperate need of repair.  During our 2 night stay there was no hot water one morning, the lights were not working for a while and the toilet was always not flushing.   The staff were obliging in trying to fix it but it was a real inconvenience. Not a great stay

We stayed here for 3 nights in this out of the way hotel in quiet neighborhood. Not really close to restaurants and main part of town, but a quiet oasis in busy noisy city.  This is not a 5 star hotel but probably use to be 30 years ago.  We heard it was owned by. 89 year old man and his family who doesn’t want to spend money on renovations. The carpets in the rooms and lobby’s are old, stained and needed replacement years ago.  The furniture is also aging. The buffet breakfast was really good, but chimney restaurant was always empty since the food was average and the construction throughout dinner ruined the evening. The gym and spa were old with gym equipment rusting in a cramped hot room. The staff was nice and very accommodating and I would stay here again if they go through a significant renovation.  We did get a reasonable rate and they beat Expedia rate after I asked them to match.

This hotel is doing a great job in servicing visitors to KTM and every type of trekker you can imagine. It seems to be the "go-to" hotel of choice for trekkers from all over the world and, despite being very busy, seems to be upholding its standards. Accomodation is great; buffets are plentiful; and staff are very pleasant. With all that traffic it is easy to spot areas that are need of refurbishment, but overall I'd strongly recommend it. A solid 4 star hotel.

I was supposed to spend a week here but fortunately only spent a night. My room was 407 and it looked onto a cinder block wall. To make matters worse I smelled smoke from the nearby buildings throughout the night. Yuck. As many other reviews have also noted the place is a bit run down. On the positive side, the staff are friendly, the grounds nice and the breakfast buffet good. The highlight was the Chimney Restaurant. They’ve recently changed the menu to “comfort food “ and I tried 3 different tapas and loved them. I’d give the restaurant 4-5 stars.

I was at the hotel in the early September from 08 to 13 I was very impressed with the great food , hospitality and gym there The gym instructor was awesome At restaurant , all the guests were provided special care. The staff was super friendly and caring. They would reach to your every need and will make sure you are best pampered while having mealI would specially like to acknowledge Ms Ruhisha Neopana Paudel for taking very good care of us. She was very professional and well mannered. At one instance when the ordered was confused , as an amend , she brought fresh all along to best extend Nepalis hospitality. I would like to wish her and the entire staff of the hotel all the very best :) I was very pleased with my stay there and hope to be there again and again

Stay almost three weeks here for a conference. The hotel is in a great location and is with waking distance of many shops and eateries. The historic nature of the hotel adds to its charm and it is a great place to stay. The best part about the hotel is its staff. What a wonderful and professional group of people. Always polite and willing to make your stay and experience the best possible. I cannot say enough about how well the staff treated everyone, and will almost 300 people attending for two weeks they had a big job on their hands. Thank you Yak & Yeti staff for all that you did for us. You made out time here truly memorable.

The hotel is very peaceful and quiet... very beautiful rooms too...It’s a beauty with quiet surroundings but lots of shopping areas too. Very clean place and food is delicious, hotel staffs very helpful and polite 👍👍

Looking at the pictures on the hotel's website you expect an imposing, luxury hotel. When you arrive you realize that the hotel has received minimum investment for decades and the result is disappointing. Instead of luxury you get maybe 4 stars by international standards. The carpet in the room, for example, should have been replaced decades ago, it has stains everywhere. You don't even want to walk around barefoot in your own room. We booked a massage in the spa and were also disappointed. The spa and fitness center seemed run down and the service was not great. While we enjoy having a massage after doing sightseeing, here we only tried once and never again. As this is the only hotel we visited in Nepal it is difficult to know if there is anything better in Kathmandu. However having spent weeks traveling in India this was a major disappointment and would not recommend it.

This property isn’t five stars but it met all of my needs during my stay in Kathmandu. Clean rooms and good service were key. The hotel has a nice little bar and a restaurant that offers mediocre options for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Still okay though.It is situated a medium walk to Thamel if you choose to explore shopping in this neighborhood.

5 stars is a stretch - some of it is a bit tired. It is however an oasis in Kathmandu with an excellent location, attentive staff, nice grounds and comfortable rooms. The breakfast rush can be a bit daunting given the limited space but otherwise the bar and restaurant facilities were fine. The Concierge and desk staff were very helpful and to be greeted with a salute that would rival the best  British Sgt Major upon return from each outing was a nice touch.We stayed both before and after trekking – appreciation naturally being greater upon the return (6 was on our mind at that time). We were well looked after on both stays.As an anecdote we stayed in this hotel 25 years ago in the original building with the Chimney restaurant. (those are the website pictures). It is difficult not to compare the ambiance and nostalgia of that hotel which is now sadly lost and replaced with something more modern. There was a charm to that hotel that is not present now. We await our next visit and completion of the chimney restaurant rebuilding to see if some of the old world is reignited.

Stayed at the hotel on three different occasions.  The lobby, lounge, concierge area, and restaurant are all very nice.  Nicely decorated, well maintained with very professional, friendly and helpful staff.  The garden, pool area, and grounds were beautiful.  The rooms are somewhat dated, but still very nice.  The beds are comfortable.  The room and bathrooms are clean.  The hotel is in an excellent location to explore Kathmandu. I would recommend if your looking for a place to stay in the heart of Kathmandu.

My stay in Yak & Yeti was in Feb 2018, for a conference being held in the same hotel. My room overlooked the spacious lawns that were used for lunch and socials. The room was smallish, but clean. There was a ledge by the window where one could sit and watch the lawns below. The toilet was neat although basic.Internet was fast by Nepal standards. The breakfast spread had local, Indian and continental fare, and was adquate without being lavish. The staff were very friendly.Overall, a good place, with a great location and well-deserved image of a modern property with traditional values.

I had booked a heritage room with queen sized bed couple months in advance but was given a modern room with two single beds when I checked in. They told me it's on a first-come-first-served basis so what's the point to book it in the first place? The power went out very frequently everyday and the wifi was highly unstable. Boiling hot water came out of both the cold and hot water taps and I couldn't wash my hair on the first day as the water was so hot! Someone told me to let the cold water tap run for 10 mins or so and finally I got cold water the second day but noticed the water was yellowish. Also, somebody was hanging underwears outside my window on my first day.

Stayed here and enjoyed our stay very much. Hotel is just like a top class palace. Rooms are beautiful and well maintained. Staff is too good and helpful in nature. Pool and greenery adds to it's value and beauty. Food is also good. Everything is on a walkable distance.

We stayed here at the suggestion of our tour operator before and after our trek in the Khumbu. It is a quiet refuge from the intensity of the city and is in a central location for sightseeing. The cons- the rooms are outdated, the bathrooms need renovation and the carpeting needs to be replaced. But the pros outweigh these problems. The twin room we had was spacious, the beds were very comfortable, the hot water was always available, the views into the courtyard were pleasant, the lobby area was quite nice and light filled with comfortable seating areas, the staff was friendly, courteous and helpful, the breakfast buffet was extensive and good quality. The hotel is a popular place for trek and tour operators to use as a city anchor and so it's a nice meeting spot for like minded travelers. Altogether it was a very good stay for 3 nights.

We stayed in a suite, lovely setup, spacious and gracious, on the Club Floor. Checkin was fast and professional and easy, and our rooms are beautiful. Our rates included breakfast, happy hour, and WiFi; WiFi speed was decent to excellent. Breakfast and happy hour were served in the Fourth Floor Club Lounge on the Club Floor. Both were a definite plus (included in the Club Floor rate) and the happy hour table was enough to make a dinner. The Club Concierge was fantastic and introduced me to a local scotch whiskey (Nepal is surprisingly wonderful for local beer and scotch and, I hear, a millet wine similar to sake, although we did not try it.) I took a picture of the whiskey for you. The Chimney Restaurant was closed for renovations, so can’t comment. The main restaurant was quite good; went twice and liked my meal so much I had the same thing the second time; the wait staff remembered us and our order, a sign of highest quality service. Centrally located in the main district. An ‘oasis’ from the hustle and bustle of modern Katmahndu, an exciting place, to be sure. It is a genuine resort, with beautiful tranquil grounds and highest quality service and facilities. Highly recommended. We loved it.

I spent two nights at the Yak & Yeti in October 2017. Overall, it was a good stay but not without some issues.Positives:-Airport pick-up and communication before my arrival was very good-Checking in was fast and good-Room was ok, not bad but not really 5 star quality. Especially for the prices they charge. It needs a refurb, the room, bathroom, new TV etc.-Location of the hotel is very good, central, taxi drivers knows the hotel which helps-Staff was generally good, helpful, polite-Breakfast options were reasonableNegatives:-As I said earlier, staff was generally good but there is one elder gentleman behind reception who talks to you without looking at you which is a bit strange/rude. The younger guys and girls were all good.-Like I said earlier, the room I was in, can do with a refurb, especially for the prices they charge-I had arranged and confirmed an airport drop-off but it turned out the relevant people who had to book the car weren't aware, so there was some minor delay.Like I said, all in all, a good stay and I would definitely consider staying here again if I were to return to Kathmandu.

What I liked:- Good location, access to shops, restaurants outside the hotel- Attached casino- Overral service- great breakfast that was included with many choices- internet speed was decent, not fastIssues:- room is equivalent to a 3-star in Europe/US comparison but great overral- the pictures you see online for grand staircase and hallways are of the casino not hotel, hotel is a bit simpler- very busy hotel as tourists are there for Tibet tripWhat I didnt like is a bit of deceiving I got at dinner time. One of their restaurants was under construction, we didnt need much food just something small but they had only dinner buffet. I asked for price and they said Rs 1800 per person.  So I expected Rs 3600 for 2 people.  Its self service buffet. No other service was provided by the restaurant to us. When the bill came, not only is there a VAT of 13% but service charge of 10%.  It made the bill close to Rs 5000 as a bottle water was also charged because we didnt water regards water.  This is deceiving. When someone asks you a price, you should quote with service charge included and mention VAT is added otherwise, you are lying. And I have never seen service charge added for self service.  You should quote 2214 per person not 1800 because you know your charges. This way we can decide whether to eat there or go outside. So hope everyone from this review now knows the real buffet charge.

Food was delicious but unfortunately breakfast menu repeated on 3rd day hotel location is good its nearby all happening places like darbar sqaure themel area which is famous for night life second 15 min run from airport

Pleasent location. Staff is courteous. Excellent restaurant in case you have time for a leisurely meal. Executive lounge provides a nice quiet location for meetings. Rooms are renovated and have hot water, which is not an automatic in nepal

Stayed at this hotel on eight occasions over the last four years for business. Consistently high standard and warm welcome on each occasion.  Food  and service in the restaurant excellent on all occasions.  Rooms are comfortable  and functional.  The hotel is centrally located with large 'manicured' grounds and outdoor swimming pool. Its decor is a more traditional Nepalese, rather than the corporate bland hotels of a similar 5 * standard. Overall, would highly recommend the Yak and Yeti Hotel for a real 'taste of Nepal'.

After trekking to EBC for 14 days, it was a luxury to spent a few days acclimatizing back to reality. The Hotel was clean, had western toilets and real food. Service was excellent as were the Mojito's in the afternoon. Grounds were well cared for with a small walking track. The Hotel was gated so only guests and transport vehicles in the direct area. The hotel was in the very heart of Kathmandu but you couldn't hear the noise of the busy streets from the Hotel. I would definitely recommend and would stay here again.

Outdoor garden and location was great!Disappoint with the quality of room!Things very ok type except the room!Very old fashioned! Need a renovation!I never felt I m in 5 star hotel!Cheated in the name of 5 star!

when searching for hotels in KTM, this hotel comes as top 5 or 10 hotels. Its a let down the hotel smells n has dated interiors. It's not a 5 star. Not worth the price.its ok to be ranked as 3 or max 4 star.The breakfast buffet does't have live stations, coffee machine.

I arrived at this hotel today after my friend stayed one night already. We were very excited as we have been to Kathmandu before and stayed at a lovely hotel but this time we wanted to be closer to the city so we chose this as it looked decent.We are so disappointed but unfortunately we are forced to stay here as all other better hotels are full on such short notice. The room was so dirty like nobody had cleaned in days or weeks, there was unknown hair in the bed and all over the floor as well as dust balls. We complained to the guest relations manager who tried to help and moved us to a new room, but even here - we moved the TV cabinet to get to the plugs and it so dirty. Our bed sheets have several holes and stains in it! The furniture and carpets are so old and used, the hotel really needs a refurbishment!! Honestly, for 30 dollars more you can stay at the Grand Hyatt and I recommend you do so because this hotel is not even worth 50 dollars.

The hotel looks absolutely stunning at dawn or dusk, especially the wing where the casino is. Big sprawling garden – it has it own jogging path (mindful of the geese). Spacious interiors clean and amentias like wifi satisfactory but lots of connecting corridors some of which can be a bit dark at times. Breakfast is a good spread, variety is there, I stayed for five days and never felt I was without a choice. Has a history with trekkers and climbers. In the lobby, I constantly met groups going in and out. There was in fact a board that said Base Camp…but it added to the ambience. Shops around the hotel expensive, but Thamel is quite close, I walked on several occasions, felt safe even around 12 mid-night. All in all value for  money, if you can afford it. The old charm in Kathmandu…bit on the steep side though

A nice spacious hotel in the tranquil surroundings of a garden with a pool. A quiet,  clean and safe place you need after bustling, dusty and noisy Kathmandu streets with a crazy traffic. The staff is very friendly and dedicated and the management excellent. The breakfast is abundant with Western and Asian choices, I tried both and they were really good! The only downside is the choice and quality of TV channels but that's probably not why you came to Nepal…..

I organised a large party on 10th March 2016 with international visitors. The function was held in a hall next to the beauty parlour and tennis court. The photo on the web site looked fantastic but the floor surface was uneven. Many guests tripped. So I had to arrange one of my guests to stand near that area permanently.The large garden next to the pool was rented out to an exhibition sponsored by the American Embassy with ugly looking tents. Hence we could not use the garden. The swimming pool was inoperative with small insects visible in the half full pool.The tennis courts were locked. Mind you this was one year after the earthquake.The health club was not used by any one. The ladies jacuzzi area was stinking of urine. In short there was nothing right. I had seen this property two years back. From then and now it is changed dramatically.
