The hotel is convenient located near Thamel. Facility wise it is quite comprehensive, with a very good jogging track and quiet environment.The room itself was a bit Worn Out and need renovation especially in the bathroom.Wi-Fi is not complimentary and breakfast choices are quite limited.

A fine hotel. Nice rooms. Good food. Good service etc. etc. etc. But, the real reason to stay here is the laundry! I save up my shirts just to have them done here to perfection. No ONE in Asia starches a man's shirt as well as the Yak and Yeti. Worth the trip!!

Conveniently located, with attentive staff and excellent facilities. The hotel is worth serious consideration, for a  relaxing break. The staff particularly give their utmost to supporting guest throughout their stay. Well worth recommending!

Despite the ongoing fuel shortage induced by a stroppy Indian government upset with some aspects of Nepal's new constitution, the Yak & Yeti continued to provide a great service. Food, rooms and service was 4-start on an international benchmark, but I've no doubt counts at or near the top of what's available here.WiFi speeds are decent during the night, but - like the rest of the country - pretty slow during the day. Short walk to the excellent Peace Gardens and Durbar Market.

Look, this hotel has so much potential it would be amazing to see investment into it.  I will summarise by saying the price they charge is not worth it.  After reading the reviews on here I was praying for a different experience but unfortunately not.  If I could get my hands on the Cleaning Team I would give them a lesson on how to properly clean a room.  My god it was terrible of what I could see, let alone what I couldn't see!!  Who in their right mind leaves an extremely visible shower door filthy and full of scum?

Great location and clean and well appointed rooms and loved the brickwork and polished wood interiors.Nice lawns and thankfully great weather made these perfect for a longish afternoon lazing over a beer. There was at the time of our visit a shortage of cooking gas and fuel in all of Nepal and menus over the country were limiting thier offerings due to this shortage.So had to request the manager for a plate of Pakoras (veg fritters) and once we bit into these they were great.

Reading some of the reviews, we weren't sure what to expect from the Yak and Yeti. People seem to love it, or find it middle-of-the-road, for a variety of reasons. It was the hotel's central location (and close to Thamel), as well as their very reasonable online pricing that sold us. When our taxi pulled up to the Yak and Yeti and we stepped inside, my husband and I were both impressed, especially given the nightly rate we paid, which we think was a real bargain. The staff was extremely friendly and accommodating. Our room was clean and the bed was comfortable. The breakfast buffet, which is included, was extensive. The concierge was fantastic. She gave us many tips and steered us in the right direction for shopping and site seeing. Everyone, from the front desk personnel to the doormen and bellmen, was gracious, helpful and so very kind. The decor is a bit old school, but the hotel is very clean and well -maintained. We loved the garden, too. All in all, we would recommend the Yak and Yeti. We've traveled and stayed around the world. We were comfortable, well-fed and felt safe at the Yak and Yeti.

Thanks to all the staff, had an amazing  stay, food for dinner and breakfast was delicious. Great selection on the buffet.  Thanks Deependra for looking after us. Rooms wear clean and comfortable,  central location , i loved the shuttle  service to and from the airport.  See you all again soon

I would recommend this hotel to any visitor to Kathmandu who could afford it, and right now, because of the ongoing series of crises afflicting Nepal, occupancy is extremely low and the online offers extremely good. For location, comfort, service and generally all of the amenities one expects from a 5-star hotel, the Y&Y is a very sure bet.

Its nice Hotel for Individual and For Family  and Business People!!! It Has Very Friendly Environment and With Nice staff and lots of Greenery Around with Swimming Pool!! Also You Have Shops Inside and Outside for shopping and The best part is You Have all Famous Places near which is Airport,pashupati Nath Temple,Durbar Square,Royal Kings Palce and Many More..Regarding Food its very nice and Staff are also Very Co-operative.Its clean and Love to Visit it Again and Again and Also Casino is just Adjacent to it for Killing your time.

It's really big. This hotel has a lot of carved woods in it and they're beautiful. Loved the garden! Too bad the pool was badly damaged because of the earthquake, still under renovation. Staffs were helpful and friendly. Walking distance to Thamel area. I don't mind staying here again :)

Hotel Yak and Yeti is the only hotel we know within 10 minutes walk of shopping areas in Thamel and Ason, with more than enough space to swing a yeti.  The grounds and nearby casino building are vast, expansive, and dramatic in the middle of a crowded city, reminding us of Kathmandu the way it used to be in a more regal era.    Pluses:- Big waiting room next to the lobby, function rooms and empty rooms on the ground floor; romantic gardens, paths, a hill surmounted by pavilion-covered Garuda kneeling with hands raised in namaskar, and an enclosed Buddha statue- We attended a delightful classical guitar concert in one of the hotel's function rooms- Staff with fluent English are experts at welcoming and good-bye-ing- Heritage Deluxe Queen package room with a view of the wide lawn, umbrella-tables, and garden is worth the premium. The ledge/seat by the window was very useful to us for packing and repacking suitcases. The room was bright, spacious, and friendly.  - We had read that breakfasts were not very good, but we found ourselves looking forward to them, especially the breakfast crepes, even during a period when very few goods were passing the border with India.  Perhaps eggs are too fresh because hard boiled eggs stick to the shell.- Wi-fi included in package was reasonably reliable given frequent power outages, but only two devices per room are allowed.- Attentive staff.  A family with loud children and an indifferent mother moved into the room next door, and the staff kindly moved us to another room (directly below the family's room, but their occasional tantrums were not at all bothersome from below). The staff froze our ice pack and retrieved it in good time before we left.  Minuses- Better to eat lunch and dinner out unless you want the large buffet dinner. During the border closing, the Chimney Restaurant was closed, and a la carte lunch and dinner at the hotel were mainly ham and cheese sandwiches with French fries.  We ate dinner at the closest restaurant to the hotel, The Old House, but we were not overjoyed with the food.- Homemakers may not be impressed with thoroughness of cleaning, especially of coffee spoons and utensils in the room and coffee shop, and the rooms give the impression that fabrics are overdue for vacuuming.- It's already an old hotel with small elevators. Overall we felt slightly inconvenienced and highly charmed.We feel ready to give up some small things for the location, space, and sense of former grandeur.  We recommend the Heritage Deluxe room and Hotel Yak and Yeti for its location and unique advantages.

Spent 2 nights here at the front end of a trekking vacation. It is a nice combination of historic and contemporary, with the original part of the building part of a former palace. The grounds were beautiful, although the pool was closed at the time due to earthquake damage. Service was very good, and the breakfast buffet was great. Highly recommend!

I have stayed in other hotels in Kathmandu before, but nothing really compares to this one. The grounds are expansive, with a large garden. You can even have your meals there, outdoors.The welcome wagon is really great: they bring out lemonade & a tray of chocolates. A hostess is there to personally greet you & inquire about any special needs.The rooms are quiet and quite good. I stayed in rooms of different categories at this hotel, and I would recommend the Heritage Suite with a view of the garden.The breakfast buffet offers a wide range of items, including traditional as well as continental cuisine. I would recommend lunch & dinner elsewhere though.The location is close to all your shopping needs. You can walk half a kilometer to the branded stores & good restaurants. You'll need a taxi if you want to go to Thamel (the main tourist shopping area, bargain items).Only criticism: the wifi inside the hotel grounds are chargeable at $10 (USD) per night. I travel extensively, and this is the first time I have encountered a hotel where the wifi is charged.

Hotel is nice and have a heritage decor. It is centrally located and very close to Thamel. Breakfast buffet is bad and over all quality of food is not as per expectations. Since its one of the expensive hotels in Nepal it does not meet the basic standards of service which other hotels provide

A hotel par excellence,with an authentic feel,right in the heart of Kathmandu.Located off Durbar marg,it is centrally located,but has that "old world" charm.Courteous staff.Lovely walking track with a nice pond at the back for morning exercise,together with a tennis court.Rooms are nice but lack some modern conveniences such as automatic switching off of light etc.All kinds of wine in the pub.A great address to call your corporate guests !

Stayed in the hotel only for a night on August 5th and was thoroughly satisfied. Nice room, fast wifi, great location and very nice staff.Breakfast was a let down but not bad enough to rate a star less. I will recommend it to those looking for a peaceful stay in the posh location in Nepal.

No complaints regarding hotel's food and beverage service. The price of the hotel was admirable. The behaviour of the staff of the hotel was also admirable. It was the hotel visit program organised by our college to learn about the services and facilities served by the star rated hotels and relation and behaviour towards the guests.

Had a very comfortable 3-nights stay last December. Quite an upscale establishment, but worth the price.Travelling from the airport to the hotel, the more you get near the Durbar Marg area, the more it starts to feel like you are leaving Kathmandu behind and entering a more "western" zone.Once entering hotel gates, felt secure and secluded from the usual scenes of Kathmandu. Those seeking a more authentic Nepali experience might see this as a negative, but those who want a relaxing time would feel great here.The staff were helpful and responsive (even though didn't get to have too much of an interaction with them). The buffet is quite good and offers a variety of choices. A morning jog or even a stroll on the walkway in the backyard is a relaxing way to warm up for the day ahead. Loved the ducks roaming freely. Skeptical about the Yeti footprint, but it's a great photo op and chance to brag to your friends back home.The rooms are clean and simple. Not too shiny, but not shabby either. Would've loved to have free WiFi in the room. If all the cafes in the country can offer free internet, so should they.Location of this hotel is a good reason to pick it for your stay. Although the hotel is like a 20min walk from Thamel, the place to be to get the true Kathmandu vibe, the alley leading up to the hotel has some good shops as well. There are also some great places to eat (offering both Nepali and Western cuisine) nearby if you want to skip the hotel food. Had momo in the afternoon and KFC at night, both just 5min away from the hotel. A woman sells great Nepali Parathas with eggs on the alley, if you're into street food.If budget is not an issue, would recommend this hotel to everyone

The enviroment of this hotel is really a dream, it is organized like bungalows in the forrest with a lot of vegetation and even monkeys! Great luxus in the rainforest :)It was the best hotel of our trip, and I we were also impressed of the great reception with chill-out furniture wher you can drink something or wait your guide and they have a nice & clean swimmingpool  with lot more services. We were really impressed. The hotel has like a conscious concept with the nature, the notebook, the natural soaps... nice.The taxis are super cheap and it is great to be in such an enviroment, with taxi takes 5 minutes to the city.

Right in the heart of Kathmandu down a little side street is the peace and tranquility of the Yak and Yeti. I had the pleasure of visiting for two days on business in early June, and life in the city was starting to return to normal following the horrific earthquake. The hotel building and grounds are grand and very well presented; the rooms starting to look a little tired but are comfortable and clean; the breakfast buffet is adequate; The Chimney restaurant is very nice. The thing that really made my stay is the quality of the service - the staff are extremely polite, efficient, and helpful without being overbearing. I will most certainly return on my next visit.

I stayed for more than two weeks and I am glad I picked the Yak and Yeti for my time in Kathmandu. The service was always great, the staff pleasant and helpful. The grounds with lake and outdoor seating a plus. There's even a 400 meter track for walking and running. I am someone who likes a good lobby area with plenty of places to sit and work - and the Yak and Yeti has plenty. There are also two restaurants, both very good. The morning breakfast bar is diverse and plentiful. And also important, there was great, consistent internet. In Kathmandu, you can't go wrong staying at the Yak and Yeti.

We stayed at the Yak & Yeti before and after an aborted trek to Everest Base Camp.  While we were on our trek, the April 25 earthquake struck Nepal, and therefore our experience was quite different than we intended.  However, the Yak & Yeti proved up to the challenge.  Despite staff obviously having concerns for their own families, friends, and homes, we felt well-cared for and comfortable in a very difficult situation.Our pre-quake experience was also excellent--the rooms are very comfortable, the buffet breakfast, lunch, and dinner were extensive and delicious, and the grounds are quiet and peaceful.We expect that the Yak & Yeti will be able to make any minor necessary repairs in short order; the quality of the staff suggests that if any hotel in Kathmandu is able to recover quickly, the Yak & Yeti will be the one to do it.

Checked in radission hotel on april 17th but i was so unhappy then the next day i immediatly checked out and then checked in hotel yak and yeti . Everything was as usual i was so surprised that i met Mr. Suyash of sales department who helped me in various ways to make my business trip sucessful. As i'm a Arabic guy and he fully have a knowledge of Arabic culture  and tradition. Once again thank you Mr.Suyash i have succeded in my business trip by your help with the outer contacts of yours. Keep up the good job Allah be blessed upon you. Sukran

well located if you want to be near the tourist chaos of Thamel. Rooms are more than adequate and service is good. Breakfast is very disappointing. Lots to choose from but standard could be higher- curdled yoghurt- in a Country with famous delicious yoghurt. Grounds are large and have good facilities. Not the charming oasis of the Dwarika, but good if your in the shop phase of you trip.

I have stayed here many times, and the food continues to be excellent. The rooms are big but they are sometime smelly, especially the bathroom, once the bathtub drain also clogged but the staff got it checked right away. It's location is fantastic, within few minutes of walking distance to all shopping and food. The garden is huge, pool is small, staff is good, bar is also nice. This being a popular hotel, there's always many guests, over all great place to stay

hotel is located in central kathmandu and is one of the best destination. the casino is a must visit and the overall stay is very comfortable. do book in advance for a stay and remember to take the full day kathmandu tour

This is a lovely hotel in a very poor country which lacks the basic infrastructure we westerners take for granted.  Pick up from the airport is a battle but nothing to what the locals get.  On arrival we were greeted by staff who dealt with our luggage and offered a cold drink and chocolates.  The desk staff are very competent, polite and speak English perfectly.  Our rooms were delightful and beautifully decorated though the cupboard space is not so good.  Our shower outlet overflowed but the next one outside the shower dealt with the water.  One day a man and woman asked to come in to wash the windows.  He scraped the ledge with a screw driver, she wiped the windows with a dry cloth.  They left after two minutes the windows just as dirty as when the came in!   We felt like fat indulgent westerners in a country where everything is done manually, by people who have no training and earn a pittance.  How could we complain.A strip of cute small shops lines the corridor to the conference centre.  Don't go near them.  You will be harangued for an hour to buy stuff you were never interested in.The staff all over this hotel were very polite and hard working and keen to please, the young bar staff with their limited English put up with all sorts of difficult western requests with humour and professionalism and a keenness to please.  Paper delivery was intermittent and when I asked "Staff Services" about my paper she rudely told me to go and read it in the business centre.  When I asked a very un-busy "Travel Services" woman about where I could do a cookery course she said she didn't know in a very uninterested way.  Go to the Tamal she suggested.  I found one on line.We ate most meals in the hotel as they were fantastic and offered great banquets and a la carte.  Plenty, delicious, and varied.  Chefs cook select dishes at most meals.  Waffles with real maple syrup, can you believe it! The coffee could be better, another western cry, but hey, this is Nepal!  They do fantastic masala tea everywhere.Another western complaint.....the air conditioning was not connected to the control.  Just open the window.Overall great comfortable, lovely staff, centrally located.....

I stayed two night in this property and I am happy about they stay. It's right int he heart of the city center. You can walk to most of the shopping areas and palace etc from here. Good Bed and rooms are great. Bit pricy. But good food and great staff. Great garden tooOnly flip side is Don't use their travel agent. We ended paying too much for the Everest flight.

Its a nice property with wonderful interior and a nice casino, A decent place to spend some time while you are back in evening. Although i did not found front desk staff that supportive (may by my expectations are high due to a lot of travel to many star rated properties) and were more busy in their personal care then guest care.Free wifi made my day. They should have increased bandwidth (good wifi but bandwidth is capped  to 1 mbps so you cant even run HD video's).Food was very good. this hotel  is right place in Kathmandu for business stays and wish hotel staff become more guest friendly.

going to Yak & Yeti is like coming back home after a long trip. everything is just the same, though i visited after almost 13 years. and thats' not always a bad thing. the staff is just as helpful and the food just as good. the bar is a regular meeting place just as before. being in the centre of town, the location is untouchable and almost everything one may need is just walking distance. i was sad at the condition of Kathmandu though. its a shadow of what it used to be !!

I am writing this in behalf of my guest who stayed in your hotel. They comment me the hotel was very beautiful, excellent service and mostly they like to thank suash of sales who was very helfful. H e helped them to book hotels in Denmark THANK YOU YAK AND YETI  and thank you suas. my guest will definetly come back again and again.

Easy walk from Tamil, great bar, wonderful staff, and comfortable rooms.  The old section is better-if you can book a suite on the club floor.  Very comfortable and happy hour is free!  (With additional snacks)  Its a great place to relax after returning from a himalayan adventure.

I have been to Kathmandu a few times before - and this stay provided a sanctuary away from busy Kathmandu (Oct 2014), and restorative stay between hiking in the Himalayan's or Chitwan National Park.The grounds at this hotel provide a oasis away from the hectic life just outside on the walls - very nicely kept - with extermely curtious and helpful staff. The rooms are similar to the other upscale hotels in this area, but the management, and staff really make the difference for an enjoyable stay in Kathmandu.I would definately recomend this to anyone staying in the area.

We stayed in December 2014. The heritage deluxe suites are great value for money - excellent view of the pool and the lawn, enough space for two people, amazing housekeeping and other services! While is kathmandu, do try this hotel. The location is added plus - very central with easy access to cabs. Will definitely return.

I guess it's one of the best they have in Kathmandu. So, gotta live with that. Room : old, sufficiently clean, spacious. The interior decorating isn't that appealing. But exterior building and lush garden are wonderful. We enjoyed morning walk around the garden very much. Breakfast : it gets boring pretty fast but compare to other KTM food, it's heavenly. Note : I stayed with my 1 yr old baby. So, I had to use wet wipes cleaning floor, corners, windows as well as any plane my little rascal could crawl / reach. If you clean it as well as I do, you will find that the room is much dirtier than it looks :(

i love the setting of the hotel in the middle of the business district .Not too far from the airport.We stayed last November 8 and 15 when we have #buildon and dubai cares journey in Nepal.So we stayed here  with the group,recieved a warm welcome with drinks and good ambiance in the lobby.Great dining restaurant serving more Succulent Asian food.Pillows so soft.,twin beds and a sharing bathroom in the suite.Beers needs to be served by the Room service ,only liqours and soft drinks in the mini bar.Surprisingly thebeers are so huge when it was delivered.Lovely pond view from the room.Hit the gym in the morning in thebasemen.Took a few walk outside wih good views  of trees ,and Buddhist attraction .Outside is a nice place to play tennis and running or jogging.The shops are open 7:30 in the morning ,but I found shop open at 7 and bought souvenir items before we departed the hotel.If you lost your room key ,they will charge you.Good thing to see the Hotel Manager introduced himself and went hus way to greet us in the arrival.I think he is great and he does speaks Arabic.Overall,this is a great place to stay in Nepal,remarkable and with distict.I saw huge groups like National Grographic stayed in the hotel.

I stayed at the Yak & Yeti two night in Nov. 2014 and loved it.  I had a deluxe room which was spacious, clean and very well appointed, with a great city view.  The location is perhaps the best of any luxury hotel in the city - walking distance to Durbar Square, the City Market, shops and several night spots.  It is easy to understand why the Yak & Yeki is considered "The Place" to stay while in Kathmandu.  It is a quiet gem in the chaotic and hectic Kathmandu.  The restaurant was exceptional with the best buffet lunch I had on the entire trip.  I only dined in one evening, but the food was also excellent and priced very reasonably.  The lounge bar was well stocked including three local beers - try all three (Kathmandu, Gorka and Everest).  The hotel staff were very friendly with a cheery "Namaste" at every turn.  Although I didn't partake, there is also a VERY NICE casino on property.  Another plus was they exchanged US Dollars to Rupees at the front desk.  I have only positive things to say and strongly recommend the hotel - you'll be very happy and glad you stayed here!

I wanted to have a cozy dinner with my friends and had choosen Chimney restaurant at the yak and yeti hotel. Before entering the guards seemed to be rude asking where did we wanted to go. After letting them know we wanted to go inside chimney restaurant they said it was shut down 10 days ago. We were surprised to know about it. Again asking to verify he went inside and came out shortly saying its open. Amazed! We went in. The place was warm and peaceful. We had a good time at the restaurant. Now returning back, I had parked my car at the basement. A guard rushed to me saying I had to be charged of the parking. It is known that if you are a guest in the hotel or have come from restaurants then parking charges shouldn't be taken. He was rude with his behaviour saying I came from outside. This for me was a bad customer experience and even though I had a good time at the restaurant,  I dont feel like entering the hotel because of the guard/s behaviour. I believe the management should seriously look upon it or otherwise they are going to loose customers like me!

I stayed for 3 nights in Yak and Yeti and was very satisfied and over all it was a great experience.The room was cosy,neat and clean.The staff was very co-operative to help you anything that you need.The food and particularly the breakfast was excellent.The location is central and so convenient.The only thing to suggest that the lighting was slightly dim and could be improved.Overall it is worth visiting at least once.I will strongly recommend this hotel to anybody visiting Nepal.

I had a conference at the hotel for a week and brought my wife and niece along with me. We had a wonderful time. The staff were very friendly and the food was great. The highlight, though, is the garden at the back of the hotel. It's a beautiful and relaxing spot in which to escape the dust and chaos of the streets of Kathmandu. I highly recommend the hotel for its quality and excellent central location.

After two years back at the Y&Y I landed myself in one of the newly refurbished rooms. Beautiful! The pigeons are still outside the windows, the bathroom needs a lift but again 'home away from home'. Greatest staff, great food, esp. if you like Indian. Cocktails are great too. Thank you Y&Y for being there after all these years. My first visit was in 1996.

This was my eighth trip to Nepal and my third stay at the Yak and Yeti. I have stayed here for the past three visits , having discovered the hotel through a fellow traveller.  This year I conducted an international workshop in June for 30 people, with 18 staying at the hotel , and just recently I conducted 4 separate workshops for the local financial sector.  I have found the staff very hospitable and efficient in organising the training rooms and looking after my needs. I used two different room sizes: the larger room allowed enough space for group exercises where movement was involved as well as having space for 30 people seated around round tables. A larger Whiteboard would be a welcomed addition . I made do with a small one, but hey I haven't found a hotel with a large whiteboard so far in Nepal, so they maybe hard to come by.  I like the fact that morning and afternoon teas are simple with tea, coffee and home made biscuits rather than too much food, which is so often the case in many hotels.  Catering for lunch was at the Sunrise Restaurant, which had an extensive range of buffet style food. There was local and western style food, which changed daily.  The home made yoghurt served at breakfast is a treat. The accommodation was very good; I had a traditional room facing the gardens. It was quiet, which is a very important quality I look for when travelling for business.  There are pigeons roasting outside the windows but I found as soon as it was dark they settled down and were quite. Staff were courteous and prompt . The room was a nice size and tastefully furnished. The best thing was the chocolate on arrival. I'm afraid I good not keep the plate for the whole week but devoured it on the first day. As far as location is concerned, the Yak and Yeti is a short walk to Thamel, the main tourist shopping area and not far from Durbar Square , the historic centre of a Kathmandu. I found it was a good location for my local workshop participants to get to as well when I had free time to do some shopping myself.

Hi, I've been at the hotel from 6th to 9th Sep 2014. Terrible stay, incongruent staff answers, the manager (at night) very impolite, facilities inadequate. Well, don't know if it is the standard for Nepal or not...First of all, I went to Nepal for business. I need a sim so suggested by a friend, I called the hotel from the airport to ask if they have an Ncell shop in their hotel. The answer on the phone was yes, we do, please come. When I arrived to the hotel, surprise surprise! no Ncell shop and the staff answer was: "I don't know whom you spoke on the phone, here we don't have any shop".Second thing, asked for wifi which at the time of booking, they said yes we have. I arrived there and second surprise, wifi not included and have to pay extra.Third, asked for airport transfer at the customer service of the hotel. And the reply was yes yes, we provide the transfer, and it is free. I asked again, should I book it now? No sorry now it is close, but because you leave tomorrow, you can come tonight at the concierge to ask for the service. I came back late night and went to the concierge, 10USD/person the cost of the transfer.Room, quite small and water in the bathroom was leaking! An horrible stay! And when I was a little bit furious with the services, and said I won't never ever return to your hotel again. The reply from the manager was: thank you!

It is been a very bad experience on this trip. Right from the airport which came 1.5 hours  late. When checked into the room the lights were not working. The techinicial came after 15 minutes. I am sitting in the dark. When checked with the front office, no proper explanatiom nor they say can allow me meet the GM. Very bad attitude from the front office. Totally a very terrible experience. Never expected from yak and yeti

My partner and I booked to stay at the hotel & were pleasantly surprised when we were picked up at the airport by the complimentary hotel shuttle. Our room was spacious. Breakfast was nice with lovely views of the garden and swans wondering about :) In room dining was good. The hotel also had a fitness centre. It was quite small but it gave us the opportunity to work out on holiday. What I most enjoyed about the hotel was the location - it was so convenient. Only a short walk from the high street & Thamel.

The Yak and Yeti is a very nice hotel when staying in Kathmandu – the staff is very accommodating, facilities are nice and comfortable and the rooms (we stayed in heritage section which have been updated) were very good with a comfortable bed, good-size bathroom w/shower and quite fast wifi.  The shower does take a long time (many of the guests were commenting on this) for hot water to arrive…we would let it run for 10-min before getting warm enough to get in.  The staff makes the hotel – there is no request they will not work hard to deliver on – and in fact, recommend corresponding via e-mail with the staff prior to arrival to set your accommodations and associated costs.  We did that, and the staff was prompt in replying and we negotiated a room rate that included airport transfers, breakfast buffet for two (good selection of foods), two large bottles of water per/day (you will need these) and a room in the heritage section.  The rooms have universal plugs, so we did not have to bring an adaptor for the rooms (and there are 5 of these plugs in the room for use).  (These work great for cell phone, iPad, computer chargers, etc which do not have polarized plugs.  But my wife had to use a 2-prong Europe adapter for her curling iron.)  There is a small gym (4 cardio and 6/8 weight machines) and also a spa that has a sauna/whirlpool and place to get a massage.  My spouse and some of our conference attendees when right outside the gate to a spa where they could get a massage at a lower price – all said it was very good.Kathmandu is a crowded, poor and extremely run-down city with very poor roads and power that only stays on for about 11-hours a day; so the hotel runs on generator power and also created a garden area for walking and relaxing from the noise of the city – the hotel has a nice garden area to either sit and walk…or swim in the pool.  We did not swim but saw some guests who did.Some Tips To Consider:  Tip:  Kathmandu is a very crowded and large city w/poor roads and very interesting drivers – so expect it and plan accordingly for what you plan to do – we had a transfer to/from the airport and worked very well.  We provided our arrival info to the airport and upon leaving the airport, looked across the street and saw a gentlemen holding a Yak and Yeti Hotel sign.  They took our luggage, loaded us in the car and within 20-min we were at the hotel.  Recommend the airport transfers.Tip:  If you need a VISA upon arrival – have $25 US cash/pp (they have a challenge making change) and also a passport picture.  Upon entering the immigration section go to the far end of the room and there is a bank booth (far end on right next to immigration booths) where you will pay for your VISA and get a receipt and then proceed to an immigration booth where you get your passport stamped.  Took us less than 10-minutes to do both and we had exact US cash.Tip:  My spouse did the Everest flight – was awesome and she booked it at the hotel Travel Desk – was $200US and was picked up at the hotel and taken to the airport for Buddha Air flight.  Was in the air for over an hour (left hotel at 5:45am and was back for breakfast by 8:00am) and got to see the entire range to include Everest.  Only 18 per flight and everyone gets a window seat and also opportunity to go up into the cockpit for pictures through the front window.Tip:  Everything is negotiable – everything so do not pay the first price offered.  For instance I watched four people negotiate 4 different rates for a taxi to the same location…..from 200 rupees to 500 rupees.  We even negotiated a lower price for a tour from the Hotel travel Desk.  So negotiate.  Tip:  Enjoy the people and the natural beauty of Nepal and get outside the city if you can – by air or car.  Do not let the challenges of the city (there are many) distract you from the beauty…..Tip:  We booked a tour w/guide and car to see the specific highlights (temples, palaces and artisan locations) of the city and did so via the Hotel Travel Desk for 6-hours.  (you can also book a three hour tour).  Cost was $120US for both of us and did not include the admissions into some of the locations -- which we paid separately and was approx $50US for both of us.  Was well worth it as our guide was extremely knowledgeable, spoke excellent English and bartered for us on things we wanted to buy.  When we completed a tour the car was right there – with a/c running – to take us on to the next place.  You can go see all these sights much cheaper by taking a taxi – but you will not get the education and understanding of what you are looking at.  So choose based upon your preference but would recommend the tour – we will not be back to Nepal so wanted to understand what we were seeing.  We left at 0900 and were back by 4pm.

This a nice hotel and the food is good. I like the garden very much. When I saw it first time from my room it was just a wow scenery. when I went down to see it was more beautiful. I fact I shared some pictures on FB and my friends thought I shared some pictures from some posters

Me and my wife stayed in this hotel for a day from July 26, 2014. The check in was very fast, with a tasty welcome drink. The room is comfortable, service is good, food is acceptable and house keeping effective. We enjoyed our stay there. It's central location close to Durbar square is an added advantage and one can just walk through in 5 min. Casino Royale's closure disappointed us, but no casino is operational for some reasons.

I spent 7 days at the Yak and Yeti in June this year. The hotel is in pretty good shape having been renovated recently. The staff is very friendly and service oriented, displaying a tipycal (and wonderful Nepali hospitality. My room was very large and comfortable (other than the pigeons roosting on my window sill :-). The hotel grounds are well maintained, and the pool seemed very attractive (I did not get to use it, as we were on a tight schedule). The A/c, at times seemed to struggle to maimntain  a cool temperature, but other than that, no majpr complaints. The bathrooms have a glassed shower stall, very con venient, but the management should pay attention to the fact that mineral deposits, after a while make the glass cloudy (I know that it is not dirt, but some other guests may feel differently). It is prettyu easy top take care of it, but les so, if one lets those deposits accumulate. The housekeeping staff was very nice and friendly. The lobby area was not property air-conditionned, but I understand atht due to the many electricity shortages, it must be difficult to manage that proeprly, even with generators. All in all, a good experience.Oh, BTW, breakfast quite nice also, especially the fruit and pastry sections.

The hotel is not 5 star, possibly 3 at best. There are attempts here and there to deliver 5-star service by housekeeping so kudos to that. I stayed here 20 nights on the club floor. The staff there Khin, Bhakta and Ram took very good care of me and colleagues. The masseur, Mukhti, also gave me the best shiatsu I've had in years. Comfortable bed. Food's just OK. Beyond these, the hotel's a bust. Dirty carpet. Room smelled like moldy (had to buy air freshener). Gym's lockers stunk and staff were gossiping loudly while I was getting a massage. Gym is basic with no ventilation. Bird poop on the windows. The curtains are dirty. Mediocre room. TERRIBLE internet (ask for a router in your room!), and a reception and guest services desk staffed by cold, apathetic personnel who all obviously need a refresher course on customer service.

I was spoiled at the 5 star hotels in India. The Yak and Yeti does not hold up in comparison. Rooms are adequate, mold in bathroom, soft floor under bathtub (leak?), and dingy carpets. However the beds are comfortable, service was excellent and the breakfast buffet was fantastic. The location was perfect - walking distance to Thamel and lots of excellent restaurants. They have a very large and pretty garden and pond area with outdoor seating which was enjoyed by us all.  I was in Nepal 3 weeks and this was definitely the oasis of comfort when we would return to Kathmandu from our expeditions.

Hotel Yak & Yeti has beautiful grounds, good buffet breakfast, generally helpful front desk personnel. However, the support staff needs to be culled - eliminated from the group. First the wifi policy: Each room has a passcode.  If you have an iPod and your spouse an iPhone they cannot be used at same time.  It is not just one at a time. One must go to a separate Internet website and log off each device before the other can be logged on. At check out the front desk was quite nice about there being 8 hour wait until departing for airport even offering that we use the exercise facilities if we wanted to shower.  However, "the Dragon lady" that runs the business office cut off wifi access. When I asked about it she glared at me and said "your time has expired".  The Hotel is a 5 Star hotel with too many no Star employees.

Even though the furnitures are a bit old, but my room is big, clean and very comfortable. Room service is excellent, the food is quite tasty, too. Good location, 10-15 minutes walk to Thamel. They have a nice yard where you can sit and eat outside on the lawn. The swimming pool looked a bit poor but well I had no time to try it. My only complaint was the massage therapist at their beauty center whom unashamedly asked for tip even though she was only giving me 40 minutes massage instead of one hour massage that I paid while managed to look sour the whole time. Some staff were nice some were unfriendly but I didn't care much. All in all, it's a good decision to stay there. Don't compare it with any other five star hotels in different part of the world. It's still too pricey, I'd ask for more from what I've paid but still I'd recommend it.

I am a Nepali but born and brought up in The US. This was my visit to Nepal for the first time ever with my sister. We decided to stay at Yak and Yeti as it was recommended to us by one of our friends. We even read the reviews to be more sure about it. Firstly, I found the hotel very beautiful as it was an old property of the Rana Regime. I had a good time talking a walk around Durbarmarg and Thamel area. Both the places are very nice for shopping as well as restaurants. As this was my first visit, it was very precious to me and this hotel will always remain in my memory .

Stayed here before our trek and after. The hotel stored our bags while we trekked with professionalism. Spotless property. Gorgeous shops in hotel lobby. Older architecture added to the charm. Friendly staff at desk and the bellmen - everyone greeting us and making sure our stay was top notch.

Don't trust this hotel. The staff is dishonest and even the duty manager is hand in glove. There is no authority to look into theft. As soon as we entered we lost our money. Your belonging are not safe at all. It goes missing in your absence.If you ask for cctv footage they will say that they can't show as per their protocol.I have requested many times to look into my matter no one gave a firm answer. Even after returning back I was waiting for their response but in vain .I personally request everyone please don't book this hotel its unsafe for tourist.

We checked in on May 18 2023 for 3 nights,  it took more than 35-40 minutes for check-in, and after check-in, persons were not available to deliver luggage in the room. Room AC was not cooling and informed reception to take care at night they informed AC is cooling now. But the whole night it was not cooling. From the bathroom, drainage water was coming into the room.We expect rooms shall be given to guests with prior checking and after complaining to their Senior manager Ms. Monika, Mr. Ajay, and Mr Govind feels this kind of situation is normal for them. We are shocked by the behavior of the hotel team.

Security Lapse at Yak & YetiDay 1:1. A/C didn't work all night. 2. Shower drain was clogged leading to water overflow. To make up for it we were offered their business suite. Night 2:1. At around 10:30 PM we were issued the keys. We walked in to check out the new room and saw a ladder and roof opening in the dressing area. (images attached) 2. While I was checking the room, my wife called the reception from the living area. A stranger walked into the room, without knocking or ringing the door bell. 3. She screamed in shock and I ran to the outer room, we were panicked.As a knee-jerk reaction we could have hit the stranger or anything else could have happened.Who would have been responsible?

Maybe 30 years ago this was a 5-star property, but I don’t think it has literally had a single update to the rooms for at least that long.  The rooms are TERRIBLE.  Two-star quality at the very most (maybe even one-star).  Honestly one of the worst hotel rooms I’ve ever stayed and started my time in Nepal off on the wrong foot.  Do not stay here if want anything better than a 2-star property.  My mind is still blown that they hold themselves out as a 5-star resort.

What an amazing place to stay 😁Very central to Kathmandu but has a sense of peace and calm and a buffer from the city hustle that was priceless 😊The hotel was clean and well run - the rooms where spotless and had everything you needed for a stayThe Chimney and The Spice room served delicious food night night after night and the room service food is highly recommended The staff were incredibly helpful when our luggage went missing thanks to the airline - they really went above and beyond trying to help us outWould definitely stay there again and would strongly recommend as a place to stay 👍

I don't know how this property is rated as 5star, basic services are not availableNo house keeping service available after 7pmNo amenities refill by HK during daily  room cleaning, you will get only when you will orderAll bath towels and hand towels are very very old and not cleaned properly, never get a clean towel during my 4nights stay even after asking, the reply was this is what we have. If you wish to useServices are very very slow, we order for tea, it came after 1hr and after that also the person was telling us to take 1cup tea and I will take back the tea potBreakfast is very limitedIf you are on medication or any special diet, even after making prior request, they don't give anythingI have asked for a hot fresh bhatura(puri) and the service staff asked me kindly go to kitchen and get it your self as it's self serviceNo bell boy available during check or check-outFront office staff was useless no assistance providedThe worst hotel I have ever stayed across the globe, will never suggest anyone to stay at this propertyI would like to thanks only 2person 1 Chef Mandy 2 I don't remember the name but he was very helpful and served us tea everyday, he is serving at this property from very long time, I have also mentioned his name to F&B Manager Uttam)

I had to stay at the hotel for five days compulsory quarantine. However, this hotel didn't meet my expectation. I was also concerned whether the hotel has properly implemented the covid safe measures.

Notwithstanding the thought situation in all other the world due to the COVID pandemic, I wish to remind that a very high standard which can characterise my stay in Kathmandu is the Yak & Yeti Hotel. Impeccable service under all aspects especially I appreciate the promptness a the gentle approach of the maids in the Spicy Room Restaurant with special regards to Anisha and Anita to who goes my most grateful "thank you".

We stayed here 4 nights as part of a 3 week trip to India and Nepal  It was truly lovely.  They have captured the soul of Nepalese style woodworking , but provide all of the modern amenities that travelers want.  The rooms are not particularly noteworthy, but the bed was very comfy and the bath was modern and nice.  The buffet breakfast was very nice each AM --a combination of traditional and western tastes. The BEST part of this place is the garden in back.  There is so little beauty for the tired traveler's soul in Kathmandu --that one is just drawn to this lovely oasis.  Beautiful lawn and flowers with a little Buddha temple up the hill.  While we enjoyed our very overpriced gin and tonics in the garden ($14 US each)  we were fortunate to watch about 10 local Buddhist monks wander into and around the gardens.  Obviously creating a photo shoot mania among the tourists in the gardens (see photos) , but it was enjoyable to watch them enjoy themselves with selfies and group photos.

WE HAD REALY GOOD TIME IN YOUR HOTEL. Comfortable lokation, cosy garden and room, lobby. Easy way to Thamel and many cafes. Breakfast already delicious  and abundant. Thank you for your hospitality. Best regards.

I stayed for 3 night with my best friends and we had a great time. The staff were unbelievably nice. The general manager was very helpful. The ambiance in the Chimney is soooooo cozy and the rooms are super nice. The food was excellent and so was the spa. The garden was extremely beautiful and very big. My friends daughter was having the time of her life. The hotel in general is great for family reunions and other gatherings. The ballrooms were super nice. They were all kept in such good condition. The hotel itself is so Historic and lovely. I will definitely come again with even more of my friends and also my family.

One of the worst five star hospitality till the date.I don’t recommend this hotel to anyone at all.Arrogant staffs and only money focused management.They served was uncooked and unhygienic food as well.Overall very sad and disappointed.

It has a grant entrance and the foyer is amazing does feel 5 star however that stop there as the rooms are not , its sub standard as bed and breakfast which does not feel like 5 star hotel. The view from the window was not appealing at all. In the sink the water did not go through the drain properly and the bathroom needs an update it looks so old but the breakfast in the premium hall was amazing had a lots of choices I throughly enjoyed. Overall it is a good experience but I think the price does not reflect on 5 star hotel standard its a bit over rated for that reason I will not be returning. It definitely needs an upgrade in the rooms. Please update all rooms.

I stayed for 3 nights and though the hotel was located in a nice area for waking around with a few shops and restaurants within a couple of mins easy walk. Hotel itself was old, rooms felt a bit basic and need some tlc. Windows let a lot of noise in (there was a wedding every night I was there which went on until late). Show was nice and bed was comfortable. Breakfast was a sorry, poor effort with most food being cold, nothing freshly cooked. The chimney restaurant was excellent and well worth a visit. Gym was small but good, outside pool was poor and the steam and jacuzzi in the men’s changing was good. Staff were helpful and the lobby bar was a comfortable place to work and have a meeting. Travel desk was vastly overpriced for tours etc. About 15 mins from the airport so location was very good.

I had opportunity to visit this magnificent Hotel embedded with great interior of palace and lush garden with swans and ducks during my visit to one of the largest conference taking place in Nepal at Yak & Yeti.During the rush of this conference, I had opportunity to meet Director of Sales - Pradeep & Front office Manager Anil, who walked me through the history of the Hotel. It was Jaw dropping to listen them in caring out day to day activities meeting event needs, satisfying clients requirements on last minute.I have seen smiles , humble hospitality from each and every staff of Yak-Yeti, I will never forget to moments shared on coffee at Piano Bar- where I met employee working for over 30 years behind same bar,  a humble hostess who offered me Momo (dumplings) as a courtesy.Above hospitality hotel offered comfortable luxurious bed and fluffy pillows to have a thought for the day.I cannot stop saying to every companion I meet, how much I would love to visit Yay & Yeti again for a Momo, Tea and a good company.

I have stayed at this hotel three times during a trip through Nepal.  The first time the room smelled something strange.  I complained and immediately moved the room.  All Hotel staff proved to be efficient and friendly.  Unfortunately, I cannot say the same about the culinary sector.  All dishes are extremely spicy and little varied.

Location of the hotel is good - near the airport and you can walk to shops. The room was very comfortable and quiet with a view of the garden at the back (only minor concern was not having separate controls for bedside lights in twin room). The staff (with the exception of some in the restaurant) were helpful and efficient.  But there is no free wifi and it's expensive - extraordinary for a "five star" hotel in 2019. The restaurants (Chimneys and breakfast room) were chaotic while we were there, the restaurant service slow with only a couple of dishes suitable for non-meat eaters (in India??), the breakfast area crowded, too small for the number of guests and limited in its offerings compared to other hotels we stayed in in India and Nepal. The restaurant staff did not understand what was involved in preparation of vegan food and we did not get food of a standard we expected. We did have serious concerns about how we were treated with regard to one particular meal and our concerns were listened to by the hotel manager, thanks to our local guide, and to some extent addressed, but we left with the view we would stay somewhere else on return to Kathmandu.

I was surprised that for such big 5 star luxury (as they call themselves) hotel breakfast is actually less than average quality and variety. Location is good. But what really surprised me is when I was charged 8 dollars per day for Internet with explanation -this is hotel policy, talk to our senior manager. We stayed in few 5 star hotels in Nepal And this was only one that  charged for internet (and terribly slow anyway). Considering how much you pay for a room, it’s shame and disrespect towards the clients. They should change their policy and management immediately.

The hotel seems to be quite disorganized. Firstly our visit got off to a bad start when the requested airport pickup did not materialize. No one was outside the hotel to help us with our luggage and I had to go in and look for someone for a few minutes who could help us. For dinner that night, we had to wait more than 45 minutes for food that eventually came out cold. The room service menu contains mistakes and is not clear at all, and despite that the staff kept insisting that the fault was with us.

Best place to relax and enjoy great food. Staff are friendly and has full filled all our demands. Mr. Ron and his team has never disappointed us but rather served more the what expect truly a 5 star service and food. Must visit again.

Good Old Hotel ; walking distance to Darbar Quare & Thamel+Great Location+Peaceful Atmosphere+ Private walking Track+Well kept property (though dated)Will stay again.- Breakfast Cost (Too high)- Airconditioning Controls

First of all thank you alot and much wishes to yak and yeti and all the entire team,for our grand partners meet of moneygram event  that was been held in crystal palace for two days.It could not had been successful with the team of yak and yeti thank you again and i wish to work further again grt doing business with u .and thank you for wonderful service that my clients enjoyed in their stay at yak and yeti .thank you susma ji ......

We visited from Delhi with mother’s and in-laws. We had 3 double rooms. Hotel is at a convenient spot. a short walk away is a busy market place.Staff were friendly and polite. Breakfast and dinner were average.It’s an old hotel so don’t expect new and glossy but hotel is clean. A couple of times the electricity went off in the hotel but they have generators. They have a small outdoor pool.Overall a pleasant experience apart from the fact that you have to pay extra for wifi.

I stayed there on two occasions during July. The first, longer one, was for business, and in this instance, I was given a room on the sixth floor with a garden view. The room was shabby, even the bedsheets looked and felt overused (there was a hole in one of them). The bed and the pillow were not comfortable, and I could swear that the floor has not been vacuumed, let alone mopped, in ages. The other stay was only for one night (I traveled around then returned to Kathmandu to catch my flight back home) and I was shocked to stay in an extremely nice and well maintained room, with an immaculately clean floor and bathroom, new and clean bedsheets and towels, and even a welcome plate of fruits and snacks. It was as if I was staying at a completely different hotel! It is important to stress that I paid exactly the same price per night for both stays. One more important point: make sure to check your payment and receipt against the number of nights you stayed. When I checked in, it was at 4am, after a 4 hour delay on my last flight and a trip of over 40 hours, yet, I told the receptionist that he had made a mistake in the number of nights, but he insisted that he had not. I doubted myself because I was tired. But when I returned home and was reviewing my travel expenses, I caught the mistake, and contacted the hotel over the phone and it turns out that I was right --I was charged for an extra night. To their credit, they immediately reimbursed me for the error.

Very Good place and good stay , friendly staff and people. Lake view was good with swans and ducks and scenery was good. Food was good. The Indian food was slightly overcooked and could have been less cooked but overall was enjoyable

Rooms were not updated and it was old washrooms. Bugs were crawling I have a video if you needed. Food quality was very poor I throw up after eating vegi sandwich. Araff and manager were nice but  food n room update is must

We started our anger from the airport when we saw a hopeless service of pickup ....hotel sent  local small accidented car and the  we hire a taxi from our own pocket ....staff says we sent a car. Shameless staff on this activity.

The hotel grounds are very beautiful and well kept, the same goes for the reception, shops and restaurants area; however, after you see the entrance your expectations about the rooms grow higher and you get quite disappointed when you see them. The rooms are in desperate need of maintenance. The carpets look quite old and the toilet has mold on the bathtub and shower curtains. Other than that the rooms are ok, the beds are very comfortable and they provide you with drinking water, tea, coffee and you can find a kettle, safe and a hair dryer. The service is outstanding; all the staff is super friendly, efficient and most of them speak very good english.

A beautiful hotel with gorgeous gardens and public spaces, comfortable rooms, and really nice service.  The location is great--walking distance to key places and centrally located, but it has space.  Part of it is an old palace, be sure to check out the old ball rooms.  With busy, dusty Kathmandu, it is wonderful to have the gardens and spaces with traditional carvings and decorations.  The rooms are very comfortable, and the breakfast was great.  Service was really nice, with a bow and namaste every time the front door opened.

i was there for a step of my honeymoon trip across nepal.we soujourned there for 4 nights.it was great and comfortable.the service was impeccable, the people friendly and professional.we had to leave a day early and, since they could not refund our money for the room, they offered us to stay in one of their very best suite.it was awfully kind (and unexpected) and pleasant.a place to go back to.definitely.

We have stayed in this hotel several times in the past but qw were very very disappointed this. Having said that the staff is extremely polite and hrlpful but this hotel hasn't been updated for over 25 years. There are molds in bath tub, dirty old rundown carpet which has very bad dampness smell. I have feeling owners don't really care anout it. It's location good and convenient that may be the reason they really don't care. Sales and reservation staff need to trained. They don't have substitute of milk like soy  milk even they don't have plain yogurt only sweetened one.  there are much more than that. But the staff at FOOD SERVICE are  very simple polite and helpful. There are better choices close by who are striving to serve better.

I have had the pleasure to stay in Hotel Yak & Yeti many times over the last thirty years and especially during the last four-five years the hotel has established itself as the prime hotel of Kathmandu especially in regards of the warm and friendly services provided by all of their staff which offers a unique ambience and sense of familiarity which is unusual at high end hotels.Every employee from bell boys, receptionists, restaurant & bar staff to the domestic service staff provides you with an impeccable service with a smile and a sense of pride over their work.The ongoing upgrades and restorations at the hotel I'm sure will further enhance the quality of this classic establishment and ensure it's continuous ambience for future guests.I warmly recommend Yak & Yeti for all visitors to Kathmandu that are looking for a real treat.Tommy Gustafsson

I really enjoy the experience during my stay and I wanted to express my gratitude to Anita for her caring and dedicated attention to my insistent requests for help at her office. I'm also very grateful to Aayusha and the rest of the staff for all their help and guidance!I wish you all to continue your work with such professionalism and joyGreetings Beatriz García Machado

The hotel staff are great, very friendly and helpful. Having said that, the restaurant staff seems to be a little cold, if not outright surly. The hotel is beautiful and in a great location and the grounds are beautiful. As other reviewers have said, it could use with some updating in areas.I was a little disappointed that they shut down the air conditioning to the entire hotel during certain seasons of the year. My room windows were facing the setting sun and it would have been nice to have the A/C, especially when there is a sign telling you not to open the windows.I would stay here again.

Stayed prior to a trek to Everest Base Camp.  Has a great restaurant and a bar. Easy walk to downtown areas of Kathmandu and other restaurants and shopping.   Has a variety of room types and views. Holds events and conferences as well, so often the garden area is busy.

Went to the Chimney Restaurant for a special anniversary dinner.  It was wonderful.  We were greeted at the door by a warm and friendly hostess.  The table was close to the fireside and elegantly set.  The whole atmosphere of the restaurant was great.  The food was excellent and properly served. The sauces were some of the best we have had in a long time.  The staff learned this was our 58th wedding anniversary and surprised us with a small decorated chocolate cake for dessert.   It was excellent and provided a great conclusion to a very special dinner.  Will recommend this restaurant to all our friends.

Stayed here for 7 days in very spacious and clean rooms. Lovely big gardens, pool and tennis court. Breakfast buffet was fantastic the manager Bindu always greeted us with a smile and made sure we were well looked after. Short walk to Thamel. We hope to return with our kids next time.

We stayed at this hotel for a total of   5 days three times on Oct 5-20. It is in a great location... not chaotic, nice place to walk around, very relaxing to just sit by the pool or walk to the Casino at night. We enjoyed the food and service at all their restaurants n the Spa. Rooms are clean and staff are very helpful and always smiling. Appreciate the daily complimentary bottles of water.My gratitude to Ms Sabina Maharjan , the beautiful guest relation person, who helped me  get into their Business Center beyond the office time and guided me in the computer. She returned for me to close the CenterWould stay at this place whenever I am in Kathmandu, Nepal and recommend it to friends and acquaintances.

Coming from Europe, this is the perfect hotel to start your trip in Nepal and you might as well spent some more days at the end of your stay in Nepal, just to spoil yourself a bit.Make sure to book a heritage room, not just a deluxe room since they still have carpet on the floors and are a bit old and dusty. So, where the experience in a deluxe room is certainly not worth 5 stars, the heritage rooms on the other hand are.Breakfast, lunch and dinner buffet is truly the best I had during my stay in Nepal because they serve a variety of cuisines (although I prefer Nepali chulo). The a la carte food is more then excellent too!The staff is very service minded and friendly, the deserve all credits! I would book this hotel again, for sure!

Stayed there and enjoyed a lot .staff is extremely polite and friendly.Love the casino and staff there .Rashmi,  I guess that’s the name of girl in chimney restaurant, she was outstanding .very polite ,and professional and good sense of humor as well .Overall very nice hotel and staff .strongly  Recommended.NAMASTE🙏🏻

I really enjoyed my stayed in Yak & Yeti. The location is very good near handicrafts store , restaurant and coffee shop. The rooms are bigger and very classics , the bed is very comfortable and the bathroom is very clean. The staff is amazing they are very helpful and always you feel welcoming .The buffet breakfast is spectacular with a lot of variety of hot and cold options, with a great variety of fruits and vegetarian food.I had dinner and is buffer also, so you have a lot if option of dishes.Absolutely recommend this hotel

Sabina made our family very welcome to the hotel. It is in a very quiet location and my 13 year old grand daughter could not get over the choice of food at this hotel. Thank you Sabina for making our stay so wonderful.

Nice hotel with friendly and helpful staff. Probly a little pricey for the dated features and pool but nice for a night or two of comfort before or after a trek. Room was nice and big but once again a little dated and older in style. Grounds of hotel were lovely and its positioned in a very central location to get around Kathmandu from.

Stayed at the hotel from 19-22nd August and then from 1st to 2nd Sept. Stay was part of Pilgrimage of Kailash Mansrovar. The hotel is perfectly equipped for such stays have all amenities like good restaurant cooks, sauna, walkway, swimming pool etc. Staff understand your needs and always ready to serve you better ( Nepalese Hospitality)

We booked a deluxe room, as we arrived, the toilet flush didn't work (it was repaired but never worked properly), bathroom wasn't clean. Old room, poor iluminated that was never renovated. I will never sell that as a 5 stars hotel.

There were plenty of good things about the hotel but the best was their breakfast menu. With a variety of food items from eggs, pasteries, salad, meat and even rice, you could easily call it a brunch. Just wonderful!

Hotel is good in terma of rooms and food. location of the hotel is near to main market that is the best park of hotel.hotel also have casino next to it where inhouse guest are free to enter.This hotel is old you can easily make out once in.

We booked a Junior suite for the start and finish of our journey and on our arrival were upgraded to the 7th Floor and on our return a Business suite on the 4th Floor. This second stay was much, much better than the original reservation, especially as the Business suite had ample square pin plug sockets.The suites were tastefully furnished, albeit that some of the furniture appeared faded and had small stains, toiletries were well provisioned and were complemented by clean soft fluffy towels. The bed was very comfortable and the mosquito netting gave it a honeymoon feel and there were no mosquitos. The staff were very polite, listened to the questions and provided answers, as well as providing all the information essential for WiFi. No problem changing money, leaving luggage whilst we went on the second leg of our journey and they provided transport to the airport. On the Saturday when we left, it took just 15 minutes from the hotel to the airport.The location is opposite a casino and has a wonderful lake with a fountain and geese, lots of colourful flowers and a "jogging track running around it, or you could do just a gentle walk and sit and contemplate life on the many benches, or at the seats with tables provided.For both stays we dined in the Club Shangri La, as the Chimney restaurant was closed, however the personalised service provided by Klim in the morning and Bhaktar in the afternoon/evening made our stay truly memorable. some cereals, fresh fruit, cakes, cold meats pastries, fruit juices were laid out and could be supplemented by ordering what you wanted and it always came back hot and of an ample portion. We had the same window seat looking out to the lake and the limited dining spaces took us away from the hustle and bustle of the dining room. Our last night was the eve of the 2075 Nepalese New Year and we had a fantastic 6 course meal that cost £16.00, which was certainly value for money.I tried the massage and think that they were a little too vigorous, as over two weeks later I cannot rectify a "trigger" thumb resulting from the yank applied. Should I have not been leaving the next day, a complaint would have been lodged.I would return here, despite the walk from the lift to our suite..

I stayed here and it was my first visit to Nepal. The gardens are very serene. The staff extremely helpful. Centrally located. The restaurant was very nice and view from the window made dining an experience. I recommend this hotel..

This hotel has a good location, in the middle of the city but with a quiet garden to stretch one's legs in the morning. Rooms are clean but need refurbishing. Great buffet breakfast to start a day. Pool area so-so. Nice staff.

Old pro things mature with age, so is the story of Yak and Yeti. The experience has been good,the facilities of the hotel are quite up-to-the mark. However, the floor carpet could have been less rugged I felt.

Third time at the Y&Y.  We stay here because it's convenient to people that we visit in Kathmandu.  This visit, the hotel was busy with a large group meeting.  Though advertised as a 5-star hotel, the accommodations in no way merit this rating.  The rooms are not well maintained.  We stayed in the newer section, yet the closets have a mildewed odor, and the carpets are not particularly clean.  Only two bath sized towels are doled out per day. It's worth having breakfast here!  Really great with fresh pastries and an array of cuisines.  The lounge has been the best respite for us after a busy and noisy day on the polluted streets of Kathmandu.  Good bar snacks to accompany a much needed gin and tonic.

I started out in a worn down room but once I had a mouse in my room they moved me to one of the newer, beautiful rooms. No discount but I did get a free dinner as an apology for 5 suited men coming to my room to try to catch the mouse. Which they didn’t! The pool is lovely. The grounds are pretty. You can do much better if you go to the other spas in town after a long trek.

Three takeaways from Yak and Yeti:1) Incredible food!2) Feels like being in a classic hotel from the 70-80s, it would not be hard to imagine  the conversations of legendary climbers and mountaineers in the hotel lobby. Very Nepali and warm.3) Hitesh Sharma may be the greatest concierge to ever live. I had a broken MacBook Pro that was quoted at hundreds of pounds to fix in the U.K. Hitesh got the laptop fixed for 70 US dollars while I was trekking the Annapurna circuit and did so will the greatest touch of true hospitality. Ask for him at reception, and he will sort out for sure!

Hotel is on the durbar Marg but not on the road you have to walk , the hotel is old style but food is average at the restaurant.Hotel from inside is average not what is expected from 5 star . Swimming pool is also average.

This hotel was a delight. The lobby was very spacious and clean. There was lots of natural light with plenty of windows. Our room was clean, spacious and pleasant.  The breakfast room was efficient with staff being very attentive and friendly.  Our bed was comfortable and the  overall feel was good.We walked to restaurants nearby and other nice shops thus the location was very convenient to all that we wanted..

The Yak and Yeti is said to be the only hotel in Kathmandu that can handle a large conference (we were 800+ pax). The facilities were good and the frequent power outages seemed to be rectified quickly, presumably with a back-up generator kicking in.The accommodations are a little outdated, but clean and serviceable. The conference facilities are majestic since they are housed in what was once a palace.The breakfast was quite good for Nepal and the conference lunches were exceptional. I ate room service once and was pleased with the food, although there are plenty of eating options (including KFC and Pizza Hut!) just a few minutes' walk away.One really odd thing was that I had hot water from both taps in the shower. That might be good in winter, but almost impossible to shower when the temperature is that high.The staff were good, but the high cost of these supposedly 5 star hotels doesn't reflect the quality you would get in South East Asia, for example. I have reviewed the Crowne Plaza in TripAdvisor and I think I'd prefer to stay here. I'm not sure the quality is better, but the location certainly is.If you are like me - a bit flexible and used to travel in Asia - I'm happy to go a little down market and pay nearly a quarter of the price for one of the many small hotels that aren't classed as 5 star.

I have stayed in the classic Yak&Yeti Hotel in Kathmandu ever since my first visits back in 1983 and seen various dinner buffets at their Sunrise Restaurant.Tonight I was utterly amazed, firstly the presentation of all the different foods & dishes was stunningly beautiful, well balanced and created a great urge in me to try all of it out,which I almost did!Cooked vegetables were “ a point” as it’s called in French, the pasta exactly al dente, the raw food miniature bowls with beatroot & onion, cous cous, hummus etc perfectly sized as first snacks!The Indian & Nepali main dishes like Yellow dhal, Paneer, Chicken curry and various others were deliciously perfected in every aspect!Finally the dessert table offered a variety of desserts from fresh fruits, blueberry mousse to chocolate cake!Finally the staff of the evening were as usual impeccably friendly and swift performing a very agreeable service which also elevated the gastronomic experience!To all of you who haven’t tried this buffet out, don’t miss it!!To the Head Chef and his whole team:  It was World Class tonight!Thank you so much,Tommy Gustafsson

This hotel is clean and safe, not exactly easy to come by in Kathmandu. This was recommended to me by my tour guide who highly recommended it. The grounds were well maintained and beautiful. The rooms had a lot of traditional nepalese character but were clean with good water pressure.The restaurant and bar downstairs were good to grab something quick before heading out on daily adventures.The concierge floor was particularly great for a quiet breakfast and evening snack/drink/tea break.

This hotel is a little bit out of date but still very charming. Our room had exposed brick and unique Nepalese detail. The food was amazing. And the staff were incredibly hospitable, helpful, and kind.

I stayed at the Yak & Yeti as part of a group tour both before and after our trip. I had friends who had stayed here before and they highly recommended it. I can only say how disappointed I was in this hotel. Had it not been for the group I was traveling with that had already paid for my room I would have checked out and gone somewhere else. First of all, the hotel was undergoing extensive renovations while I was there. There was a huge cover over the back half of the hotel and their main restaurant was closed. Our tour leader wanted to brief us outside in their garden area. It was an absolute comedy as hundreds of cackling crows sit along the trees and roofline and we couldn't hear a thing he was saying! We ended up eating in the only restaurant that was open which had an unremarkable buffet which was overpriced for the offerings.  The hotel itself is NOT centrally located, You have a mile hike through dusty crowded streets to get to Thamel.  There are no convenient laundry facilities near the hotel so I had to take all my hiking clothes to Thamel. On our return trip, they booked everyone on one floor and put me in a room on a completely different floor. The room was absolutely filthy dirty. The carpets could not have been cleaned in years. There was a sign on the door to the patio to not leave it open or rats would come into your room! I went back to the front desk and told them in all my travels around the world this was absolutely the worst room I had ever been given. They said they had no other room but I could check back. I told my guide if they didn't find me another room I was going to leave and pay for another hotel. Fortunately they did find me a room (oddly enough on the same floor as my tour so I'm not sure what happened there since it wasn't available earlier).  I also booked a massage. To get to their "spa" area you descend down a concrete set of stairs into a basement area. I was led into a sparsely decorated room with a fan blowing. The massage table didn't have a place to lay your head so my neck was killing me by the time it was over. The massage itself was nothing special. I have to say it was the worst spa experience I have ever had and I communicated that to my group so they could go elsewhere for that service.  I just left here shaking my head that people think this is such a great hotel.  Maybe it was 30 years ago but not anymore.

Room was superb. Me and my wife enjoyed our stay in this beautiful Hotel. The staff at the desk was very welcoming and they received us with open arms and our luggage was taken care off and was delivered to our room straightaway.  The view from the room was superb facing the swimming pool. The outisde garden was very neat and clean and the service was superb. The food was delicious.

Located centrally in the heart of kathmandu,is a heritage and one of the most oldest hotel in the vicinity.The rooms are good and the housekeeping is excellent.Special mention to the manager Mr.Jatin shrestha who is extremely professional and courteous.The hotel is well laid out and we had a fantastic stay.Will return in future.

The downsides were minimal, and the upsides were significant.  The only thing that really got under my skin was having to pay for wi-fi in this day and age.  In rural areas of Nepal, the wi-fi was strong and free, but not here.  Alas, my pet peeve.  Aside from that, the place was great. Let me give you a rundown as to my observations on this place:Location:  Can't beat it.  Shopping, restaurants, banks, ATM's, all within walking distance from the hotel.  It's only a short walk (3 to 5 minutes), to the Durbar Marg at which you'll find anything to eat your heart desires.  From KFC, to German Bakeries, to Italian, and lots of traditional local fare.  The hotel is situated far enough from the madding crowds that it's fairly quiet as well.  Like I said, great locale.  Rooms:  Fairly large, plenty of storage space, comfortable bed and bedding, room controlled thermostat, flat screen TV with cable and multiple language broadcasts of news and entertainment.  Plenty of lights and lighting, but you have to spend a little time figuring how it all turns on.  Not a big deal, but a little time consuming.  No bathrobes provided by hotel.  In room safe.Bathrooms:  Large, clean, plenty of towels, well lit.  Nice.  Wi-fi:  For wi-fi it's 7.50usd per day, or you can buy a coupon at the front desk and get two devices activated for 10usd per day.  Wi-fi is pretty strong in the bar, restaurant, lobby, and rooms we stayed in.   Annoying, but if you need wi-fi, it's there.Complimentary hotel breakfast:  Terrific.  Plenty of western and international dishes served buffet style.  Fresh baked goods, and good coffee.  Nice breakfast room with a view of the pool and grounds.  Pool:  Nice pool.
