Didn't get to try it out, but I wouldn't have minded hanging out there for a bit.  Stuck my hand in during a walk about, and it didn't seem to be heated.  Quite brisk.  Bar:  Right off of the lobby.  Well stocked, with plenty of seating.   Rather nice I thought.  Good bartender equals good drinks.  Hotel grounds:  Manicured landscaping and a large lawn area with tables and chairs, and a water feature.  We found it a nice place to hang for a bit with traveling companions and drink coffee.  Hotel service on the hotel grounds area was pretty good.  Monte Carlo Casino:  On the far side of the hotel.  Don't gamble, so I didn't check it out.  Seemed popular.  Noticed no noise from the casino whatsoever. Laundry:  We stayed at the hotel for a couple of days upon entering Nepal, and a couple of days before leaving.  After trekking around Nepal, we decided utilizing the laundry service was something that was definitely a justifiable expense.  They did a great job, for a very reasonable price, and got the laundry delivered to our room as promised, on time.Conference rooms:  Plenty of them it appeared.  Housekeeping:  Quite friendly, efficient, prompt.  Hotel front desk:  Check in time was average, check out was quite efficient. Hotel staff:  Quite pleasant and accommodating.  If traveling again through Kathmandu, I'd stay here again without reservation.

My family and I travelled from overseas to visit friends and family. I stayed at room 535, a Heritage room. It was the worst night. The room was heated at 28'C and the maintenance could not fix the AC.I was advised to keep the windows open to sleep. The room is extremely small. The TV controlled did not work. Wifi's not free and I mean who "PAYS" for wifi these days in a 5 star hotel.There were neither slippers nor wardrobe. Water flows everywhere from shower to the toilet keeping the toilet wet.I particularly requested for a very quiet room and the heritage room was facing the main road with taxis beeping, flashing lights and the loud drum/music on the New year's eve.Yak & Yeti Kathmandu should be degraded to 3 star or less. Apologies to costumers will not improve your review. The admin actually needs to work hard to upgrade the standards.

This hotel is like an oasis located off the busy street of Durbar Marg where there is alternative dining options within walking distance, and close by within 10-20 minutes’ drive to the main tourist sites of Kathmandu Durbar Square and Thamel shopping area. The small road leading in/out from the hotel to Durbar Marg is also a pleasant walk offering an array of gift/souvenir shops.Rooms are clean and comfortable despite being a little aged. Pretty decent WiFi, but can do with more power outlets at the writing table. The Sunrise Restaurant served a good mix of local and international breakfast suitable for our young family of 5. The hotel gardens next the poolside provides an enjoyable walk away from the busy streets.

The Yak & Yeti was a great place to stay. The location puts you near the palace, not far from Thamel and close to many eating establishments. You can tell this hotel has royal heritage and it is still pretty grand. With some updates this would return this building to it's glory days, however it could cause the price to get too expensive, so minor updates only.I booked a Heritage and was upgraded to a Jr Suite, which was excellent. The restaurants on property were good, many choices for breakfast, and dinner had a buffet and A-La carte menu. So if you are staying to prep for your trek, Thamel is 10-15 minute walk for last minute supplies, and maybe last upscale stay before your trek. My room came with round-trip airport shuttle service. The wifi only allowed 2 devices per room (at least my package), so you had to remember to disconnect a device at times. Room service, was fast and the food very tasty. The staff was kind, helpful and very pleasant  . If you have to stay over, remember you're in Nepal, barter for the price. The room keys need a magnetic and they make a great fridge magnets, the picture is great. I recommend this place. Just start price shopping early as the price moves around alot

Spectacular architecture and great location however cleanliness is way substandard, staff not as well trained as one would expect from a hotel of this quality, WiFi service available only as add-on and is extremely expensive, breakfast quality poor and many appliances and plug points are not working. Such beautiful infrastructure is wasted if there is a lack of maintenance and service.This hotel needs a huge and comprensive upgrade.

We stayed on two separate occasions in November for three nights each. On both, the staff was very professional and courteous. We paid about $150 per night for rooms and it was worth it. Nice rooms with plenty of hot water for showers. The toilets are quite nice to and after our trek this was much appreciated. The food is a bit on the expensive sides, particularly the buffet, but if you have just trekked and eaten countless fried rice dishes in tea houses, the buffet is just the thing.

This hotel is very well located in the city, most of the places a tourist will visit are relatively accessible. Even if the rooms are not that luxurious, they are clean and modestly decorated. Bathrooms need a bit of improvement on the wooden cabinets but the best thing is the restaurant. The lunch buffet is very good, with many local options as well as western style food aka "not spicy options". Breakfast are busy as many groups stay here but the efficient staff is always willing to help. Try the masala tea...great option. The pool is clean but very cold so don't think you will be swimming during your trip.

Not sure if this is rated 5 star but it only deserves 3 stars. It was probably a grand hotel at some time in the past. It is well located near shops and famous sites.We stayed twice in November. first time on floor 2 which was much better than than the ground floor. The second experience on floor one which is the ground floor was very disappointing. Room smells damp, carpet is filthy, there is only one bed side lamp, wifi has to be paid for, the air-con is totally inadequate [ far too hot and cannot be adjusted], there is no fridge or mini bar  and the bathroom needs an up grade [ towels look like they are 5 years old].  The breakfast area is over crowded. The offering was ordinary. for example fresh fruit consisted of two offerings. There is a swimming pool and tennis court. I swam in the freezing water.I think until a little money is spent on the infrastructure you should look for others but do it carefully for sadly there are few good hotels on offer.I will say the staff was pleasant and helpful.

We were Group of Friends who travelled to Kathmandu and Selected Yak n Yeti for our Stay.The Positive about the Hotel is its Location, it is Very Much Centrally Located and ease of Moving within the City is very good from the Hotel. Lots of Restaurants, Shopping are to be found near the Hotel.The Hotel gives you a typically Local Flavour inside the Hotel. Rooms are Spacious and Good with all Modern Amenities. Breakfast Served in the Restaurant was again a Good Mix of International Cuisine with a Good Service.The hotel is Spread out in a Big Area with Good sprawling Open Green Area to Walk aroundThe Problem is Overall Feel of the Hotel is Quiet Old. Normally i prefer to stay at the Hotel which is Quiet Buzzing, here at yak n yeti it was pretty dead and dark . You Get a Feeling as you stay in the hotel that it is dated and old. Wifi Services which you get a Complimentary now a days even in smallest of hotels, you have to pay here. Overall an Average Place to stay no fancy stuff

Visited for a conference on site. Rooms were good but facilities a little tired. For a conference the wifi was pretty ordinary. Conference rooms were very airless and no windows.Food not kept hot enough at Bain Maries in dinning room or for lunches in conference facilities. Stick to vegetarian or closely check out that the burners are still working on meat dishes. A good choice of foods at the buffet and also al acarté available.

This was a very pleasant surprise in Kathmandu The hotel is nice and elegant( a bit outdated, sure ) but super clean and comfortable with the best breakfast we had in Nepal, fast internet and very amiable and pleasant service For us it’s the top hotel in Nepal

Absolutely love Yak & Yeti, the staff always makes me feel at home.  The food is delicious and if you are vegetarian like me there are plenty of choices.  Rooms are moderate, but comfortable.  Best shower in the world - especially after a trek!  The rooms are like 2 star, but the service and rest of hotel feels like 5 star.  If you travel to Kathmandu you must stay here, it is a right of passage!

My wife and I stayed at this hotel as part of a Gate1/Discovery guided tour. We spent 5 nights in total in 3 separate visits during an 18 day tour. The hotel is very convenient for sightseeing in the Kathmandu area. The rooms are well equipped. The hotel facilities are good, i.e. the garden, bar and restaurant. We only had one a la carte meal, but that was excellent Indian style food. We had multiple breakfasts, which is provided buffet style. There is a good selection and it is high quality. The room has all the amenities, including reasonable WiFi, the beds are comfortable and the overall experience was good. The service was extremely good. We would recommend this hotel to all travelers.

A very nice hotel at the center of the city . Good rooms , good service and have a good massage center near the swimming pool .  Food is also good . The guest place is adjacent to a coffe shop and bar . It is 10 min walk from thamel which is the night life place .

I was happy to get a smoking room.  The room wasn't fancy, but was very serviceable.  Laundry got done promptly, as it was my last stop on an 8 country trip.  Service was excellent.  The breakfast buffet wasn't as great as I had seen in other places, but it was good enough.  The location is convenient.  The staff is excellent.

Very clean, well presented hotel. Excellent conference venue and very close to shops. Make sure you book the flight over Mt Everest which is offered by the tour desk. 4th floor Business Centre serves a lovely breakfast and has drinks after 5 pm.

The Yak & Yeti operates at an international standard that would put it comfortably in any major city in the world.  The staff is well trained, efficient and friendly.  The rooms are spacious and comfortable.  A fitness center, spa and pool are on premises.  A small casino is 100 m away.  The only drawback is limited dining facilities (main restaurant is closed for renovation).  Upper end of price/room for Kathmandu but a value if you are looking for 5 star accommodations in Kathmandu.

I thoroughly enjoyed my stay on the Club floor at the Yak and Yeti.  The room was very nice with amenities to make one's arrival special.  The staff service, hospitality, and kindness was above and beyond anything for which I could have hoped.  If on the Club floor, please greet my favorite staff member Bhakti (Raj Bharati)!  I have traveled to Nepal many times and stayed in many hotels.  This experience has encouraged me to splurge and make the Club floor at the Yak and Yeti my Nepal home away from home.

Very good, but it is getting wear-off, it requires renovation to become a luxury hotel. I think the quality price should be a bit better. The friendship and kindness of the staff, like in the whole Nepal, the best

Can't say enough about the property and the service.  All were 5 star quality.  Very comfortable room.  Central location.  Great breakfast buffet.  Internet service was mostly reliable, although not perfect.  It was better than anywhere else I stayed in Nepal.

The Yak & Yeti market themselves as a luxury hotel but the wing were I stayed was certainly not  luxury. Smell of mould in the corridor and carpets that look as they have seen better days. I had booked room and expressed that I wanted to use the free airport shuttle. Flight schedule was sent to hotel but no shuttle was there. In spite of two telephone calls to hotel no shuttle and hotel suggested I should take a taxi. I did and hotel refunded the taxi bill. The room was very dark but at least no bad smell as it had wooden floor. Breakfast restaurant is very small for such a big hotel. People at times had to wait for seats. Breakfast is ok but limited selection. Some local dishes, bread, jam ,cereals, some fruits, tea/coffee. The grounds of this hotel are nice for a hotel in this location. Swimming pool and green lawns. If you want to do shopping in the busy Thamel area this is just a bit more than 10 minutes walk from the hotel. I had issues with the reception and especially check out was not a pleasant experience.

Checked in with no problem, welcome drink was a nice touch. But $10 for nonexistent WiFi? Normally it’s free at every other property. Nickel and diming are not appreciated. Dinner served at hotel restaraunt (not the buffet) was of poor quality and lacked flavor. Room was really moldy/musty with damp carpets and used tissues found around the bed. Water consistently yellow from the shower and sink. Hallways smelled heavily of smoke.  Will never be returning

This was a trip for business and then also social.  The hotel worked brilliantly for the business event and then for the personal stay too.  The staff were completely wonderful, the hotel itself really comfortable.  The food was delicious and plentiful.  The location is very central and easy to get to from the airport.  I loved it!!

I can in 2017 for a week for my business and I decided due to my previous experience in Y&Y to come back in September and I was not disappointed. Perfect stay, so great thanks to Y&Y.I really l ove itBest.SdC

The rooms are comfortable, roomy, and quiet. The breakfast has a choice of several fresh veggies and healthy options. The staff is very friendly and helpful. The hotel is clean, in a good location. Internet is fast and reliable. Beautiful grounds and nice swimming pool. It's a great choice for business travel, has all you need.

Found the hotel reservations department to be most accommodating to meet my room budgetin offering a range of rates depending upon the room type.Many staff very friendly and service oriented, especially "Bandana" and "Gobel".Only negative was I found the costs a bit pricy for side excursions at the  travel agency located within the hotel.

During my three weeks holiday I tried quite many different hotels in Nepal and this was definitely the closest you can get to the luxury. Rooms and decoratorions were a bit outdated though but the staff was friendly, the backyard garden with the ducks was lovely, breakfast buffet was great and the location was superb. There is also a casino next to the hotel.The biggest minus comes from the pool that was ice-cold in January and impossible to swim even for a Finn used to freezing conditions :D

First things first. This is one of the best places to stay in Kathmandu. A proper hotel with travel desk, business centre and a very friendly front office staff. The restaurant is small but the food quality as well as taste is good. The drawbacks- the place desperately needs refurbishment. The rooms, although well decked up, needs to be repaired and modernised and so the bathrooms. The rooms also most definitely needs more power outlets.

Old and small rooms, sad staff, not so good food. It looks like remains of a once splendid hotel. The only plus was the location of the hotel. Amenities were surprisingly expensive. Pool was dirty with some sticky covering and dead insects.

The hotel building is fantastic, like a palace.  The garden and the pool area is also very nice.  The location of the hotel is also great and we walked to the Dubar Square in around 15 minutes.  We had a standard room.  The decoration of the room is a little bit old, but still clean and comfortable.  It's a pity that we don't have any view from our room but there's a kind of huge air conditioner outside the window.  Fortunately, I'm not a light sleeper, I still can sleep well with the noise outside the window.The breakfast is nice with western style but it's quite crowded in the dining room.  There's not enough waiter to clean the table and it took quite some time to wait for an available seat.  But it's still a nice choice in Kathmandu with clean and comfortable room.

Quiet location and friendly staff, good security, nice gardensThe rooms are ok, however food is relatively I am sure there are other hotels that are better value for money, depends what sort of budget you are on!

Yak & Yeti is a Well Located Centrally Located Hotel in the Heart of Kathmandu having spacious Sprawling Lawns and Lush Green Meadows with a Good Swimming Pool and well Decorated Rooms. It is value for Money.

Stopped here enroute to some work with the Nepalese military and loved the service, food, views, and central location. Spring for the concierge level and enjoy cocktail hour and conversation with the bellman always situated nearby. Beautiful place and great rooms albeit a bit weathered!

A warm and cosy hotel , well trained staff , I loved the Exterior and the Interiors ( very antique)could not use your facilities , but there is always a next time.You could say HOME AWAY FROM HOME.Neeed to improve the roads in Kathmandu , and the Airport needs lot of maintainence, bad toilets , no aircon ?

The hotel looks great on the outside and the garden is nice. But the rooms we got were dirty, smelly and otherwise totally unacceptable. The floors had black spots and the walls and mirrors were horrible. The bathroom had constant bad (sewage) smell. One of the 2 rooms didn't even have a fridge, while the other did! I complained and 3 different managers apologized nicely. It feels like the Yak and Yeti is tourist factory catering to large groups and conventions. After all the apologizing, they still sent me an email to get my opinion. I assume it was automatical but bad move. What did they expect, that I would lie?! It's a factory not a hotel, even in the services and restaurants, rough and cold.

We stayed for 4 days at this hotel as part of our Nepal trip, before and after traveling to Pokhara.Good pointsHotel is located just off the main durbar road.Good clean rooms with an excellent view facing the gardenExcellent breakfast and dinner buffetsGood servicePick up from airport and drop to airport every 1 hourExtremely beautiful garden with lots of birds in early morning and eveningsClean swimming poolGreat walking pathInternet was reasonably fast in the roomsNot so good pointsHotel is not value for moneyPick up forgot to pick us up from the domestic airport so we had to walk to international airport and wait for shuttle there.Health Club is not for people under 15 as one has to be in the nude so my 13 year old son who was looking forward to the Jacuzzi missed out on itWorth a stay at better/cheaper prices

Our Nepal local agent wasBook the hotel and they have good relationship. Last time also we had stayed this hotel only. When check out time they don't want leave us without payment local agent. Finally we paid direct them. The issue was was when they do such a booking from any one why don't do such a good policy and abarrasing the people?

Spent a couple of nights at the Yak & Yeti Hotel following a trip to Everest Base Camp.  This was a last minute change to our itinerary from what was supposed to be a couple of nights at the Gokarna Forest Retreat.  The one redeeming aspect of the change was that the Yak & Yeti was located in the heart of Kathmandu.The foyer entrance is very impressive, while the buffet lunch, and to a lesser extent, the buffet breakfast are a nice way to saviour the delights of fresh food again.I was a little disappointed in the room given this hotel was rated five star. The size of our twin share was on the small side while the fittings were dated somewhat, along with the worn floor coverings, especially in the corridor.  The external gardens could certainly do with a makeover as they were looking a tad tired.Could not fault the service staff as they were considerate and very pleasant throughout our stay.  Overall, I'd rate this hotel 3.5 to 4 star.

I had stayed in few other properties in Kathmandu valley but this time i chose Yak & Yeti due to location and ambience. Overall booking experience was smooth and pick up from the airport was prompt. The rooms very quite traditional but pleasant. I found the lighting in the rooms was very dull (yellow lights) and very minimum. Also finding the charging points for your phones/laptops was a task! i could find just two and one was not working! ( you definitely need more charging points in rooms for sure). The hotel has a very good bar and posh lobby which was usual hanging point for most of the tourists and guests! Used one of their banquets for my conference and overall experience was very very smooth (thanks to banquet manager Mr. Pran). would like to stay for some more days here and experience the leisure!

I saw in the city center some boutique hotel in a better condition the quality of the room are really not good and you have to pay to access to internet no WIFi free and it s available everywhere in the city even in small restaurant outside of the city .....

Beautiful, good, clean, comfortable, friendly, and with all the facilities one would expect from this class of hotel, including several restaurants, lovely garden, pool, etcWalking distance to world heritage site (just)

Excellent location with good food.Very good staff , I always stay at the Y & Y.Rooms are clean an found of this lovely property.Garden is very big and nice.I like this hotel its very close to Narani palace.

I chose the Yak and Yeti based on location and some photos I saw online.   It's a decent hotel but the rooms are not that nice.  The wifi was very slow also.  Breakfast wasn't that great but lunch seemed better.   Employees friendly and security guards always smiling.   The room was clean and it was quiet which are important to me.   Just expected a bit nicer furnishings.

Before I wrote this review, I reminded myself that I am in Nepal, not exactly a first world country. The facilities here are not comparable to a developed country.  The original wing of this hotel was built as a palace more than 100 years ago. The facade was kept and  the internal part of the building was restored as a hotel. The new wing was built about 40 years ago.This is a busy hotel which catered for mountain climbers, group tour as well as a conference participants. I came here for a conference and the conference rooms are situated within the hotel itself which made it very convenient. My hotel room was spotlessly clean. It has a wooden floor and is rather big. The room is decorated with wood carvings. Even the TV rack/desk has carvings which made the room homely. My room is very quiet which was great. The WiFi speed was reasonable. There is a big garden within the hotel premise where they is a short jogging/walking tract which is open 24 hours a day. I love the garden as I could go for a stroll in the morning and evening. It is a relaxing and tranquil garden with water features. The location of this hotel is very convenient. The airport is only about 20 minutes away when the traffic is good. It is also located about 5 minutes walk from the main street where the are many places for shopping, dining and drinking.In the hotel, breakfast and lunch buffet served mainly food with a Nepalese flavour. It will need some time for a tourist to get use to the taste. It will be great if room slippers are provided as the tiled toilet floor can be quite cold.

The first impression is the helpful, friendly staff that meet you and take care of you during your stay.  There is a lobby consigner ready with answers, recommendations, and great maps. The restaurant has both buffet and menu selections.  We ate there and thoroughly enjoyed our meals.  The bar area is very comfortable and well staffed.  Our room was comfortable, clean and well maintained.  The grounds are very well maintained and a nice place to sit.  It is also centrally located with a wide selection of shops right outside the gate. It was interesting that a hotel with such a great history and name had no memorabilia items to purchase with the hotel name.    We asked for a five star hotel.  Not sure  the Yak & Yeti is five stars, even for Katmandu.  But it is well worth staying at and we will stay there again if in Katmandu.

The Garden at the Yak and Yeti is beautiful!  Wonderful place to sit and ponder!  Lots of birds and flowers.  However, that is pretty much what you are paying for as the service of the front desk staff was rude and unhelpful.  The waitstaff at the restaurant who deliver outside were nice, but the "greeter" at the restaurant had the same rude attitude as the front desk staff. The doormen were friendly.  The breakfast buffet was of an average standard, but you can get better quality food by going out for breakfast.  The rooms are adequate, with dated bathrooms and interiors. The internet was also adequate if you were in the right place. You are paying top dollar for average rooms, a nice garden and bad service.  Although it says it's 5 star, it's actually more like a 3 star hotel. I've stayed in 5 star hotels in big cities around the world that were of a much higher standard and had wonderful service yet were cheaper than this place.  If you have to stay here, it's doable, just don't expect good, friendly, service or the quality and atmosphere implied by the photos on the hotel website.

If you stay in the renovated wing of the hotel it is satisfactory. Wood floors, decent space, updated bathrooms. However, if you get stuck in the non-renovated wing it is atrocious. Vents and drains filthy. Extremely beat up. Smelled moldy. Grounds are lovely and the buffet is quite extensive for both breakfast and dinner though the great emphasis is on Indian cuisine. Nice relaxing bar area.

After a long journey to the Everest base camp, arriving at this hotel is indeed a rewarding one. Our king size bedroom is a beauty. Don't forget to visit the swimming pool and take a walk in the garden. Absolutely stunning! The service is excellent without doubt. The staff were friendly and helpful. The casino is just next door if you're interested in trying your luck.

This was my second stay at the Yak and Yeti. I chose to return because I was so pleased after my first stay. It is a charming hotel with good to excellent service in a serene setting. Because I travel for business, it is especially helpful to return to my room after a long day of meetings in the busy city to a quiet atmosphere where the staff is helpful and attentive. I chose to book a club room on the fourth floor with access to the lovely lounge. This room type also includes breakfast (I was able to choose to have it served in my room or the lounge if I did not want to eat in the dining room, a nice benefit especially for someone traveling alone), and two free laundry items. The room was well appointed, fruit and chocolates delivered for a delicious snack. Room service was efficient and polite, and housekeeping did an excellent job of preparing my room each day.       Although some of the staff seem a little reserved with rather unsmiling demeanors, most stood out as accommodating. I especially want to mention the gentleman who oversaw the fourth floor lounge, I hope I  his name close to correct, Bhaktar. He is one of the reasons I wanted to return to the Yak and Yeti a second time. He was very friendly and tended to every detail. Although I know it is his job to do so, he makes the guests feel very welcome and very pampered. I was amazed that he remembered me after many months. Even though he was on duty in the evenings, he arranged for me to have an exceptionally well appointed breakfast in the lounge on the one day I was able to take time for breakfast. He is a valuable employee. I also want to mention the young woman at the front desk whose name I think was Sharmilla. She, too, was polite and personable, trying hard to meet all of my needs. When I arrived, I had a slight glitch with my room, and although she was confused about what I was asking, she stuck with me until we had it figured out. She was also helpful in arranging my travel needs when leaving.       The Yak and Yeti is close to many of my business meetings so I am able to walk, and it seems to be a very safe place. The area is good for shopping and restauarants, very close to Narayanhiti, the royal palace that is now a museum. It is easy to catch a cab to Swayambhunath and Pashupatinath, two very impressive and important temples for pilgrimages in Hindu and Buddhist faiths. I would, without question, choose the Yak and Yeti for my next trip to Nepal, and would recommend it high

A nice hotel hidden from the noisy & dusty  main street of Kathmandu but close enough to walk to Thamel shopping area. I like the old school ambience of the hotel with a garden and blooming jacaranda tree. Rooms and amenities need a serious upgrade though. Water tend to splash out of the shower as there are no curtain or door causing the toilet to be wet all the time. Overall a nice place to be if u want some quiet. But cheaper and modern hotels are coming up which will give YNY a run for their money.

I booked a Heritage Room outside of the group that I was traveling with.  From the sounds of their comparison, I'm glad I did.  The room was fine (nothing special). Mini bar was barely stocked and snacks were minimal.  There is no hotel gift shop where you can buy any snacks or toiletries to make your stay more comfortable. Water temperature in the hotel is "warm".  They tell you let the water run for a few minutes in order for it to heat up, but after 10 minutes I was over waiting. After trekking for 2 weeks I decided to get a massage. Do yourself a favor and go to "Seeing Hands Clinic" (voted #1 on TripAdvisor).  The hotel spa is not a spa (contrary to the lovely advertisements throughout the hotel"). It  is one little room in their workout area. They play loud rock music, the massage table has no neck cradle (so you're in worse shape when you leave) and the massage therapists are not professional at all.  Mine came out of the bathroom and straight into the massage room without even washing her hands!  I had to ask her to "please go and wash her hands"!   We dined at their 5 star restaurant "The Chimney" and that was another disappointment.  Service was ridiculously slow and we were left with empty glasses for over an hour.  I had to get up and find the manager THREE times to ask for water and service at our table.  They also messed up our order and my friend never received her main course. Rather then admit error and ask if she still wanted her meal, they didn't even acknowledge their error and left her with nothing while we all finished out meals (I shared mine with her) and then they ended up bringing her main course when everyone was finished.   Service out at the pool was just as disappointing.  No towels available at the pool stand (which was filthy) and when I asked for 6 towels (as I had friends coming), they brought 2....etc. etc.  It was just one thing after the other. If you asked any questions at the front desk, they just looked at one another as if they had no idea how to answer any question we posed.  I don't think they deserve to advertise as a five star property, the service was definitely lacking all around.

This is an amazing building set in lovely surroundings in central Kathmandu. It is an easy walk to many central sites in the city including Durbar Square and Thamel. The hotel occupies an old royal palace and is grand and stately inside. The décor is traditional with lots of wood carvings. I found the staff incredibly helpful. The restaurant serves buffet meals and a la carte with a strong emphasis on local dishes. I had my first taste of yak cheese.The rooms and spacious although a little shabby but clean and comfortable. I loved staying here and will certainly return on my next visit to Kathmandu.

The hotel sadly is a medium score for me. Booked a heritage room and they gave us a regular room. We complained and they had no availability so we agreed to move the next day. When we went to change they said they didn't have smoking rooms even though the booking stated it did. After much confusion we took the non smoking. Nothing was offered in compensation (except moving to a club room which was still a lower grade than the heritage) for having one of the 3 nights in a regular room despite paying a premium. The breakfast isn't good, rice and chilli chicken at 8am wasn't to my taste but there are alternatives like pastries if you need them. The travel agent girls were very nice and we took tours from them but the front seat and management seemed preoccupied with other things whenever questioned. Rooms are clean and the location is central but I wouldn't bother with this hotel if I was to return, sorry guys

Back here for the second time in 3 years.Unchanged.Old décor with great staff.Plumbing variable.Food fine but not overly exciting.Bar fair only.On average the Radisson probably a better choice tho its bar in not in the main bulding (unbelievably)

The Hotel has a very nice garden and that's it. My room had a big mouse in it. They caught it in the bathroom and then tried to kill it on spot with electrical shocks. Although I changed my room but, the new room also had plumbing issues in the bathroom.The breakfast is also pretty much the same on all days.

The location's very central and the grounds are special. Lovely garden and pool; food good — buffet dinner was v.good. Superb variety. The room was a little underwhelming... noting really beautiful except for the wooden carvings around door frames...they did make up for the rather uninspired rest of the room. Toiletries... nothing special. I'd have liked a hairdryer and an iron in the room. Didn't bother to get them from housekeeping (though undoubtedly could have). Overall, room less impressive than the service and look of the lobby and outside environment.

I was delighted to find such a nice hotel in Kathmandu. It's walking distance to Thamel. The Chimney resteraunt was excellent.  The gardens are beautiful and geese walk the property. The rooms open up with large picture windows.

Well after a very busy 7 days Helping at an Orphanage we decided to treat ourselves to a 5 star hotel. This is not 5 star. Its old and shabby. The pictures submitted are from a 5 star room. Its old and i would not give it 3 stars. Gutted and very tempted yo move hotels..I asked  for a quiet garden facing room with a bath. I got a beautiful view and quiet but rest awful. We have now been moved and i am facing a noisy reception area. Will be seeing manager in morning. ( No garden view)Just tried  buffet which was very good

The hotel rooms are spacious and comfortable with adequate storeage space for an extended stay. A colleague has been staying there for over four months with just a small change to his room provided by the hotel. The shower was good with towels changed every day of my visit. There was a TV, tea and coffee facility, stocked mini bar and wifi or cable connection to the Internet. The whole hotel is clean with good house keeping. There is an out door fresh water swimming pool, jogging track, fitness room and spa facilities. There are two restaurants plus snacks are available in the bar area and a good in room menu. The "Chimney Restauant" is a "must" visit if you have time in Kathmandu. The staff are absolutely magnificent and treat guests like royalty.

Spent a week in Yak & Yeti in Feb 2017. Good location, middle class hotel. Breakfast ok, and good service, as well as in bar. Rooms are clean and ok. But otherwise I have to admit there was nothing special in Yak & Yeti. Ok & average are the best words to describe my experience.

wifi need to pay even on room... no free wifi. free wifi only if you buy coffeee... location hotel is very exclusive. this hotel was visited by prince harry of England. reception not speak english well. AC room was very cold, we even asked their staff but they cant do anything. breakfast start very early 06.30 am...

I stayed at Yak & Yeti for almost 2 weeks and enjoyed it sincerely. Although I mostly dined out in the evening, except for one time, I ate breakfast every day, and I was impressed by the quality and variety of foods available. The staff was super friendly and very accommodating. I not once experience any complication during my stay. The rooms are well lit, large, clean and have all the amenities necessary. The decor is authentic and overall ambiance very pleasant.  It was central located, walking distance to the main street, in close proximity to dining and shopping. I would sincerely recommend this hotel.

We decided to have a minimum 7 days stay, but unfortunately has to change the mind by the end of second day. This is due to the rough attitude of the front office staff towards us. Even they are trying to make us foolish while we asked for an extra room for our guest by increasing the  price . The rooms are with very old furniture and fittings. The bathrooms are having old fittings and the water flowing is of yellowish in color. There is not even a shataff fitted in the toilet. The corridors are of with very old carpet which has lost its softness. The food for breakfast was little better. The room tariff is also high.

I had such high hopes for this property, but regardless of what other reviewers say about this property ( take a look at 1. Where the reviewers are from.  2. Look at the number of reviews they have made; that should give you a better evaluation of whose giving glowing comments).Let's start with the front desk host, who unfortunately did not have any personality.  Perhaps a class in greeting guests maybe helpful.   Secondly, don't believe the images that they have posted about the rooms, ours looked nothing like their website.  The fun then started as we came back from exploring the area, we found out that the hotel doesn't have its air conditioner on. When we called they said , sorry we have only central heat.  Well it was over 27 Celsius in the room, way too warm.  They advised us to come to the desk and would room change us.  We went to 3 similar rooms with all of the same problem.  On top of it we had asked for a non smoking room and when the desk manager advised us it was a non smoking room, he stated that some people smoke in the room.   Well that's not a response I would expect to get, fix the room or find us something else.   We stayed in the room, opened the windows and yet more smoke came from outside.  We endured the endless partying going on at nigh so we could get at least some air circulating.   Please note this hotel is more concerned with the events that are going on and could care less of about the level of noise going on.  It's a shame.Next day we went down to the pitiful breakfast buffet, really this is what you this an alleged five star property has for a buffet? Again shameful.  We went out for part of the day returned and just about to get in the elevator and the lobby looses power.   They said, oh it will be 10 seconds, not the case, we waited 10 minutes and still no power, so we asked where are the stairs? Was directed to another part of the hotel down a corridor to use another elevator.  Unfortunately we got to our room and still no power.  We decided to walk around Thamel, please don't waste your time and if you are able to cross the street without getting hit by a motorcycle consider yourself lucky. The huge closet they that state they have in the room, looks more like a locker from gym class another false statement that they make.  As I'm writing this review, the noise from the party is getting louder and we can't even sleep, the room is so warm.We can no longer stay in this property, so we will be checking out early. Spend some money on painting the walls in the rooms, placing a nightstand next to each side of the bed, clean the nasty drapes and make sure your housekeeping department refreshes the rooms, with at least one water bottle and tissue paper.   And I won't even discuss the flooding that happens in the bathroom shower to the entire bathroom floor.This hotel is a mess and my recommendation is to stay far away from the Yak and Yeti.  It's a disgrace to the name and if I could give zero stars I would.  You've been warned.

This hotel is an example of a great hotel!. We were recommended to stay here by a local friend and we are glad we did. To start with, the front desk staff were extremely friendly and helpful. Couple of times, they went out of their way to help us as we were travelling with kids. They had a good knowledge about the area and were very pleasant and professional. It was such a nice feeling to see wonderful people welcoming us after a long flight!! The rooms were cleand and had a good decor. The restaurants were beautiful and had a classy touch and ofcourse the food was amazing! The hotel is very near to the shopping area and other places of interest at Kathmandu. In a nutshell...we loved the hotel and its services and we are surely coming back.

So here we are in Kathmandu, for a documentary filming assignment.Back in India, when we were about to make our hotel reservations, we came across many newhotels and boutique hotels. Thankfully, my buddy who is familiar with Nepal and had stayed at Yak & Yeti Kathmandu, Nepal, recommended it highly. And we went ahead and booked it in good faith.And if you're heading for Kathmandu, and looking for some old-world charm and hospitality, I'd recommend that you stay there too. And I'll tell you why.First off, it doesn't feel like a hotel at all. Really friendly folks, these guys at the hotel. Right from the managers at the front desk down to the bell boys and house-keeping. None of the hosts wore plastic smiles - they were just friendly and simple. The gate man greeted us with a cheerful Nepali namastey everytime i went in or stepped out, even if it was ten times a day. I thought that was striking. If you're staying at a hotel for a few days, the greetings and smiles do get jaded and I don't blame them. But these nepali lads just don't give up! They did everything with great honesty. Every namastey was as shiny as a newly polished brass door handle! I enjoyed that.  Little wonder then that the world's finest armies come to Nepal to recruit these truthful men.Well, once you're past the door, it's a breeze.It was for us, at least.We made a specific request for certain kind of rooms and one of the senior managers Mr. Kuljeet Singh made it his business to ensure we got what we were looking for - two rooms overlooking the back garden!Not just that, without our asking, he kept the same rooms for us when we were returning fromour filming and we were delighted to check into the same rooms again. It was almost likecoming home to your own bed. Now if that's not personal attention to detail, I don't know what is. I met a lot of foreigners who were really having a good time.Though I was a little disappointed with one of my own countrymen (from India) who were impatient at the restaurant and behaved rather rudely with the polite staff. The "I paid so I'll be rude and fussy if I like----Deal-with-it" kind of attitude. The place was packed in November-December when I visited. One has to give the staff some time to look after all guests. Would like to thank you again Kuljeet, but I won't call - I'll come over to Yak & Yeti and thank you over a beer!Really appreciated the special arrangement of a reliable cab service that took my wife and I for a tour of the city and the Pashupatinath as well as Swayambhunath temples. I think we've stayed with your hotel 3-4 times already in 2016. Now we're hoping we get posted out again to this beautiful Himalayan country for another shoot and without doubt, we'll come back to good ol Yak n Yeti.Keep the dumplings ready:-)

For the price paid, I would have expected the ability to control my room temperature instead of relying on centralised air conditioning, more toiletries and better insulated room. On the plus side, the bed was comfortable and staff were friendly and helpful.

I have stayed in this property a few times. However I found the room allocated to me this time to be very basic for the price. Had difficulty in finding a plug socket to charge my phone and had to use the one for shavers in the bathroom. Needs renovation.

I stayed in Hotel for Marriage function of my friend's son. Good hotel , very clean , good food & BXF.But I have to go for Mountain flight at 6 AM, the FREE  BXF  start time was 6.30I demanded free cup of Tea at 5.15  with Temp. of 5 degree C ,but they refused & demanded charge for it.This is not good for such a great hotel. Balance - GOOD

I stayed here for around four days and found the place to have very friendly staff, was close to the main tourist area called Thamel and had great food that was all cooked fresh (even the bread) at the hotel if you ever go to the buffet meals. The only gripe of the place is that the rooms could be a bit better, the decor is dated and the carpet needs to be cleaned up a bit more.

We spent three nights at the Yak & Yeti at the end of December and enjoyed it thoroughly. We've stayed there a few times before and have always been happy to return. We had two excellent meals at the Chimney restaurant - a wonderful experience, especially on a cold evening. The staff are unfailingly helpful and the hotel gardens are pleasant for walking or jogging. I'd suggest guests ask for a room in the new wing overlooking the gardens.

We stayed at the hotel for 2 nights during a last minute trip to Kathmandu during the new year weekend. The reviews online seemed to suggest it was a great property and so we didn't mind paying a high tariff. When we reached the hotel, the facade and gardens appeared grand and very pretty. The check in process was also very smooth and front office personnel were very warm. The room was underwhelming and small. It seemed under furnished and very poorly lit. We checked at the reception and were told all rooms have similar lighting. The washroom too appeared very old and stained. The housekeeping could have been better (room cleanliness). We asked for fresh towels and extra cups on one of the days. Only after a reminder were we given a towel and instead of a fresh cup, a housekeeping lady picked up a cup we had already used, took it to the washroom and rinsed it with water and gave it back to us to use!The view from the room was great (overlooked a pond, beautiful garden and swans). The breakfast buffet was decent. The guys at the travel desk were also very helpful with suggestions. We also went to the casino in the hotel (Casino Royale) on one of the evenings. As with most other Nepal casinos, it was very small when compared to most international casinos. Very few tables, all tables with the same minimum betting limits, over crowded, poor customer service and average food. Overall would rate the experience as average.

Some of Kathmandu's five star hotels have legal casinos in their premises. But the casino establishments are owned and operated by third parties, and not by the five star hotels themselves. A unique feature of these casinos is that Nepal's citizens are not allowed to gamble here

Lovely hotel with helpful, friendly staff in a good central Kathmandu location. The garden is the finest feature, with its pool and trees. The breakfast are fabulous too. Local food is mostly excellent in the hotel and beyond. As is the Nepalese beer. Wine is best avoided. Let's just say it is not what it says on the label.

This hotel is very big and offered nice clean rooms with modern facilities and good internet options. Restaurant had good (though limited food at the time due to sanctions from India). Pool area was nice and had a nice eating/chilling out area outside which doesn't get to crazy or busy.

The best calm hotel in Kathmandu, away from hustle bustle. The hotel is so so beautiful well maintained and well planned. Full of greenery and very close to nature. Rooms are nice and staff is extra helping and sweet in nature. Always ready to help. Swimming pool adds to it's value.

I was looking forward to stay here. One morning i wake up..i had huge allergy because of their carpet/ moquettes. So it was a bad stay. Room furnitures were very much dated and tv aint workin well. Bath got yellow water but well its nepal. Its crowy lobby and bfast as well. Many manpower but not much motivated workers. Its has good size garden and good bed though. Hotel needs a lifting and new furnitures.

Great hotel,clean & spacious rooms , magnificent gardens where we enjoyed a lovely afternoon reception thank you Philippe Belhay for making our stay memorable Definitely look forward to visiting the Yak & Yeti again!

We are 2 couples stayed for 3 nights.Basiclly the hotel was ok but the last night there was a jazz concert in the hotel yard withe dreadfull loud noise that we could not stand.Although we asked several times to lower the music we were decieved time after time and the did nothing to help us and all the other guests.It is a scandal to organize such an outrageous event under the room windows.Make surethis will not happen to you in your stay in kathmandu.

I stayed there last week for 5 nights. The only advantage of that hotel is the location.When it comes to service and quality of food , Forget it... not even 3 stars hotel would ignore guests request the same way this hotel dealt with my " regular customer " requests. 3 hours to get iron board and iron machine (operator transfered me to housekeeping who doesn't understand english) . Internet don't even think about it ... super slow and constant disxonnection. 5 stars hotels give 2 access for the guest ? If we are couple, how can we manage ? We need to Purchase. WAWBreakfast way below average for a 5 stars hotel.Reception team Disaster.... there is no communication between guest relation team and the rest of the hotel.  I guess... as every time I have them for something , it was never organized! Extra room key ? Sorry we can't give you as we run out today due to group arrival ! Business center girls very helpful and always smiling. Big credit to the 2 ladies I met there .Housekeeping? Forget it ... there is no standard at all in cleaning and arranging the guests room... call for dental kit,  shampoo and shower,  wait 30 minutes and get half of what asked for ! Every time missing items... Blackout in the rooms is not well arranged as curtains are short so light come into the room not to mention the Crowl as if they are sitting in your room at 5 AM alarm... Overall, for 180 usd for the heritage room and such service is not value for money at all...Being a hotelier and very well traveled on business and leisure , I see that staff in this hotel are super relaxed and don't care to details ... beside their NO knowledge about the restaurants timings for example telephone operator doesn't know until what time breakfast and she had to connect me to the restaurant ?Extremely disappointed and never again to this hotel !!!

From arrival, the Yak & Yeti proved to be a great choice offering clean, comfortable rooms, varied tasty options in the morning and evening buffets, and gorgeous gardens which include a lovely path around the perimeter.  Certainly a place that one can truly recharge before further travel or trekking, or a day of serious shopping on the fun streets of Kathmandu.  If you need to be connected, the Wifi is excellent both in the room and throughout the hotel.  The staff are friendly and quick to accomodate special requests.  Many thanks indeed.

The Yak & Yeti bills itself as a 5 star hotel. I would say it's more of a 3 star, 3 1/2 if would be generous. I could see it being considered 5 stars in its' heyday but not today. With that said, they price was fair.  There were some nice things about the hotel and some issues that drove us nuts.  I would probably not stay here again except for the location which makes it very convenient. The rooms had plenty of power outlets for charging.Pros:- It's in the heart of the city and close to many shops/restaurants and is about 1 1/2 miles from the old part of the city. We walked most of the time we left the hotel.- The breakfast and lunch buffet were very good with a very large selection and a large variety of foods from traditional Nepalese to Asian to American- It does have some "rustic" charm- They have an in-house travel desk that arranged a good afternoon tour for us.- Bottled water is provided daily.Cons- They seem to host a lot of wedding receptions and parties. The first night was loud music (making it hard to sleep) until 10:30pm, the second night until 1am.  The 3rd night we got lucky and there was no party). They did offer another room at 12:30am when we complained but it was a smoking room....the smell was worse than the noise so we declined. - It's an older hotel with the issues that come with it:  One day the shower didn't drain well and had water all over the floor. One day the water was warm, not anywhere near hot (shower at 11am)

Transiting through Nepal on a trekking holiday in Bhutan requires at least a day on each end of your travel in Kathmandu.  How lovely it was to be greeted at the airport and whisked to this clean and comfortable hotel! Our group really appreciated the views from upgraded rooms, the late check-out, and the never-failing courtesy and helpfulness of the staff! I really enjoyed the spicy Indian food on the breakfast and evening buffets, and as I'm an early riser who enjoys a brisk walk, I took advantage of the walking path through the fragrant and nicely manicured garden! Thank you, Yak and Yeti, for the smooth transit!

This was my first stay at the Hotel Yak and Yeti - although I was familiar with Dwarika's hotel in Kathmandu.The Y and Y offers lovely rooms, an accessible  business center for those of us who don't travel with smart devices, and absolutely impeccable service in all areas.When I was left waiting in the lobby area for longer than I expected for a guest to arrive, I was approached by hotel staff to find out if they could do anything to assist me.My room in the "club wing" of the hotel included evening "happy hour" and a breakfast buffet on the 4th floor that was just as extensive and much calmer than that offered in the main coffee shop area.Greeting and check in, assistance with luggage, and a speedy checkout  - combined with beautiful grounds for roaming when not interested in venturing out sightseeing - were all part of what I would say was a perfect experience.

The hotel is charming and beautiful. The place is full of history and atmosphere. Very nice and helpful staff and service is in the high level. The location is great too. Black off is still there, though it is common for entire country and generator is there.  The restaurant disappointed us, despite the good service and noble interior. the food was literally awful and spoiled all impression of the place. No need to say that the prices were high, but we did not expect to have the worst dinner there!

Very nice Hotel will all amenitiesPros------ Good location in central city with market to buy local as well as branded stuff- Good buffet option for breakfast, lunch and dinner- Fine dining Chimney restaurant with European and Russian cuisine. They serve complementary starter and desert :)- Nice rooms with traditional decor , well lit- All facilities - Big hotel with good capacity- Friendly trained staffOverall very happy when I compare to Shangrilla in which I stayed last time. Of course price is to be considered :)

This is a partial heritage property and new wing. excellent location on Durbar Marg. Off street so quiet. Good pool and health club. Excellent service. Competitive prices and booking online best. WARNING. A frequent guest and know many other guests consistently get ill at the delicious but unsanitary breakfast buffet. Maybe water. certainly eggs. Buy a bottle of mineral with complimentary breakfast and avoid eggs. Otherwisedelicious and varied.

Stayed in the hotel after six years and the situation has not improved! The rooms, beds, food all need a serious overhaul. As it is one of the heritage hotel located in the prominent area and with the tourist inflow, they are somehow getting away with it. The property is huge but needs proper care and maintenance to meet at least 4 star level. The beds creek, aircon makes all sorts of noises and so does the plumbing. There is no clear distinction between  smoking and non-smoking rooms. Rooms have musty and lingering smoke smell which makes life hard for people who get triggered easily by mite and smoke allergens. The filteration system of the pool is not continuously on. The linens, towels have been overused and badly need replacements The breakfast spread is very average. Also observed recycling of food, which is rather common in all hotels. Complimentary WiFi is good and suffices the business requirements.

I travel to Kathmandu frequently and have been staying at the Yak and Yeti for years. I love this hotel and wouldn't stay anywhere else. It's in an excellent location where you can get to Thamel by walking 10 minutes, the rooms are great and the staff treat you well. They also have a great restaurant that carries a variety of foods from around the world, and if you really want to be pampered you can stay on the Shangri-La floor where you'll get individual service.

Room was very beautiful, clean, tidy and with a nice view inside the garden.Breakfasts - yummy! Variety of Nepali, Indian and European food. There is a great restaurant "The Chimney" with excellent cuisine.Staff - extremely polite and helpful! First I didn't like my room, as it had two twin beds, and I wanted a double bed. They immediately relocated me to the room of my dream - in the ancient Nepali style and with a big luxury bed!Thank you for making my stay incredible!

I must acknowledge Bhakta Raj Bharati's remarkable helping attitude towards the hotel guests. It may may me feel to stay in Yak&Yeti again in future. I will recommend other people to stay in this hotel.

I was in Nepal for some business trip with my business partner. By far, Yak and Yeti experience was the best. Centrally located, customer service was beyond I expected. Warm welcoming and friendly staff made my stay at Yak and Yeti, a memorable one. Their architectural setting was so amazing, I hired a local photographer for a photoshoot. Thank you Yak and Yeti. Will be back soon.

This giant of a hotel is a very aesthetic piece of architecture-a palace restored lovingly to house a casino and a large number of rooms. The corridors have a musty smell and the room did as well for a short while. The room had very fine woodwork everywhere, typical of Nepal. The staff were welcoming and friendly. The guest relations who were used to many foreigners staying there and wishing to explore the city, were helpful with recommendations, maps, tours etc. The breakfast buffet was a sumptuous spread and reflected the wide variety of travelers who pass through the portals of this hotel. There was a swimming pool which I did not try out. The gardens with a small walking path was impeccable. Overall an enjoyable stay.

The room was huge and very comfortable, the staff were very helpful. The pool was too cold but there are tennis courts. It feels like entering a scene from an Indiana Jones film - truly colonial and otherworldly. The highlight was the Russian restaurant which is set out in a circle, boasting some of the best food I have ever tasted.

Warm and friendly hotel- The staff are always willing to help with a smile- Stayed in a room with a beautiful view of the garden but could not keep the windows open due the stench of pigeon droppings - Well appointed and furnished rooms   with efficient and prompt house keeping .Wi fi is a bit of an issue and changing over from one device to another required hotel intevention unlike in most hotels The hotel is very well located about 15 mins form the airport and just off the darbar street The coffee shop has a well laid out buffet at all three meals and a cosy bar lounge is a good way to spend an evening though We spent a lot of the time in the garden and the service was excellent A well run efficient hotel Will be back next time

We stayed here during my travel conference. I was  not pleased with my room but hotel moved us to another room . During our stay , there were power outages and AC and heat was not workingHotel is quaint and located in a prime location within walking distance of major historical locationsthe breakfast is amazing.Chilli chicken at bar was my favouriteHotel has a great garden and is historical

We visited the hotel during the last few days of our holidays. We had a very nice room with a garden view, to be recommended! The service was very good, the pool was nice and cold and the garden a real quiet oasis in the busy Kathmandu. The location, just about 10 minutes by foot from Thamel, is very good. We had dinner in the Chimney once, although we were the only guests, they made us feel like a king and queen. Very kind staff, always greeting you and very helpful. The only thing we missed was a real bad either in the hotel or at the pool side, so you can see when cocktails are made and to have like a social point. One downside I would like to mention is the smoking in the lounge area, which is allowed. For us it was a reason to not have a drink there. However, we really enjoyed our stay and can warmly recommend you the hotel!

I sent laundry to be done by the hotel and was WAY overcharged. I asked staff to look into it, and Amar at the front desk said he did, but insisted the charge was correct. Basically I got charged dry cleaning prices for a bunch of regular laundry.Also, this hotel charges premiums on wifi, business center computer use, pretty much all extras. For $130 a night, a hotel in the US would include those for free. They attempt to market it as a "luxury" hotel but these are average rooms (mine looked like it hadn't been changed since the 70's) and definitely subpar service.

Quiet western hotel with all amenities, pleasant staff,  easily walkable to former royal palace, Thamel, Durbar, parks in heart of hurly burly Kathmandu.  Free wifi in bar but $9 per 24 hrs from room, albeit, not always reliable in three recent stays at this hotel.  Check air cond when arrive in room.  Ask immediately for other room if not fully functioning-- this was only downside faced at this luxury class hotel.

The people here are great and a serene outdoor garden area with pool enhance the appearance. The conference rooms are great and some are beautiful like a palace. The rooms are a bit dated with some carpet wear and stains. My bathroom tub and sink didn't drain well. Restaurants are good. There is smoking in piano bar and the Russian/French restaurant though thankfully people weren't puffing much the days I was there. The staff are so friendly and helpful along with the overall ambience I'd stay again.

Recently I was on a tour in Nepal and Bhutan and has the opportunity to stay at this property twice (2 nights and 1 night). The service is really good. Everyone is truly respectful, caring and genuine. The food is very good in the their main restaurant. The setting of the hotel is also nice, though I really didn't get to enjoy it as a result of being tired from the busy day. My first stay I had a single bed in a room. on the second floor. The HVAC is locked out, the temperature of the room and air quality were extremely poor. In fact so much so, I got sick and had problems breathing the second day of my tour there. The Bathroom had a shower with no door or curtain and the water spilled out. The amenities in the bathroom were also very limited. The second stay they upgraded me to their "club floor" and it was a much nicer room with none of the issues of the first stay except the rooms are carpeted which smell a little like smoke and the tub has a shower curtain the rubs the bottom of the tub. Just simple hygiene concerns. Overall, I would stay there again for the great service and good food. Internet is slow and priced at $10 USD per day.

Our VOSH (Volunteer Optometric Services to Humanity) team (10 people) spent one night at the Yak & Yeti.  Some of us were there in 1990... it was great to be back.  Rooms are exceptional... breakfast and lunch were wonderful.  Staff goes above and beyond to make your visit superior.

Situated in the heart of City, very convenient place. Nice rooms. very good facilities. Very Friendly Hotel staff. My stay at the hotel was excellent right from Aiport pickup. Buffet breakfast was really nice.

Pretty centrally located. I was pumped to stay here for a conference for my first visit to Kathmandu. It is centrally located. It's a 15 minute walk to Thame. The grounds are very peaceful. The staff is so friendly- they say Namaste and mean it! The rooms were nice. Complimentary bottled water. The breakfast buffet was #offthechain and had options from many different countries' typical breakfast fare. The conference rooms were great with good IT support as best I could tell ( I was just attending), however one day there was a wedding with a pretty loud band that played intermittently through the day- actually quite a nice distraction. I'd stay here again.

Terrible service. Managers blatantly lied and disregarded our complaints about ventilation units not working. We were initially booked for a deluxe heritage room but was given us the normal room. Heritage or not, it's definitely not worth the money.

I stayed at this hotel for two night prior to my expedition. I was a little bit disappointed, as I heard from friends how great this hotel will be. It really wasn't. My room was small and and very simple, not fancy. I just expected more, as the price I paid was five times more expensive than a hotel proposed by the mountaineering company that organized my expedition. I was nicely surprised by their breakfast - great choices for all travelers, including the local nepalese food. Wifi didn't work. Only in some places at their lobby I could get weak connection.

The hotel offered us its facilities to conduct a large conference involving 350+ people; the arrangements were excellent, support always provided, timely inputs, and help always at hand. Overall, excellent conference facility.

The hotel is in need of a complete remodel.  The rooms are very worn, wood cabinets, bathroom etc.  I stayed in the heritage section, overlooking the garden (?).  It was Feb. so no plants growing yet and the stream dried up. The wood railing out side my window was a pigeon roost so had an 'up front' view of their droppings. The food was below average.  Do not hesitate going to Nepal now.  There was also, an Indian embargo when I was there, over now, and it did not cause me any problems. However, you may want to rethink booking this hotel.

We had two stays at the Yak & Yeti and both were extremely pleasant. From friends who have a lot of knowledge on Nepal and our own research I don't think there are any hotels in Kathmandu that are true 5 star hotels or extremely luxurious etc. The Yak & Yetis' location is what is perfect - its centrally located and a very easy walk to Thamel markets, whilst also having some good restaurants in the surrounding streets, access to ATM's close by etc. And whilst being in such a central spot in such a busy bustling city like Kathmandu the hotel is so large and the grounds so extensive that the rooms are still very quiet. The rooms are quite basic but more then adequate. The beds are extremely comfortable & house keeping was always prompt and done to a good standard. We were there during the fuel restrictions so were on limited menu options & ate at the buffet most nights which was fine. There was a lovely maitre de there who would chat to us each night and remembered us after we returned from base camp and stayed the 2nd time. Whilst they were on meal restrictions they made it known that if we had any special requests to ask and they were more then willing to accommodate  The front desk staff are extremely helpful and accommodating with leaving bags& items there whilst you go off trekking.  I intend to return to Kathmandu in the future and will definitely stay here again

The buffet dinner was good. However the heating system in room was ineffective, did not work for me  and the house keeping service needs to be prompt as well. Wasn't a confortable stay. I was told it was due to fuel crisis in country that hotel is operating with limited resources therefore was not able to run generator. Maybe will be better in summers.

The hotel did not suffer from the earthquake of April 2015, if not minor aestetic damage. The rooms are a bit spartan, the service is very good, employees very kind. Wi-fi works well. Some problems with electricity, but they solve them with stanby aggregates. Keeping in mind the aftermats of the quake and the dire economic situation, these people deserve our congratulations!

The Yak and Yeti which is the finest in Katmandu. It is situated right in the heart of the city and conviniently located. Out room was very comfortable, double bed, and the rest of the works.. Nice outdoor swimming pool with a gym too. Food...

old furniture, great garden with only 3 tables so u need to be down on time to have a seat, not good organization in the hotel, they miss all the time something, too much expensive for this service. there are much better 5 stars hotels in Katmandu

Hotel is a good old place which kept the atmosphere of its origins. the hall is great looking, unchanged, and quite empty. but the floors are a bit aging and would need some refreshment . The spa downstairs was out of order when I went there and staff had not told me on the telephone when I called to enquire. But practically , the location is perfect central and easy reach for all activities and temples to be seen .

I have been coming as a guest to the Hotel Yak & Yeti for nearly thirty years. It has been providing consistent quality of service over all these years and survived the recent earthquakes without any obvious structural damage. It is well located near the former Royal Palace and the major tourist area of Thamel. The offices of the World Bank are in the same complex. Rooms and amenities are of high quality, with a choice of staying in a traditional or more modern wings. Breakfast, with a wide selection,  is served buffet style. The hotel has a very pleasant garden with access to tennis facilities and a swiming pool, which was empty.

For a westerner who does not want to deal with the noise, closeness, and energy that is Kathmandu, the Yak and Yeti is perfect. It is an oasis, complete with beautiful private gardens, in the heart of Kathmandu.The flip side is that, if you want to walk through the vibrant, noisy, energetic parts of Kathmandu, you will need to ask the doorman to get you a taxi. (However, the taxi is not that expensive, and quiet is so nice when one is jet lagged ....)

When in Npal, don't go hunting for a Hilton, or a Marriot, instead stay at the Yak and Yeti which is the finest in Katmandu. It is situated right in the heart of the city and conviniently located.Out room was very comfortable, double bed, and the rest of the works.. Nice outdoor swimming pool with a gym too. Food was really good . ASatff was polite and extremely helpful. All in all a really good experience.

typical asian welcome at the doorvery secure area with guards at the gate - not that it is necessary. Kathmandu is very safe. guards at gate keep out unnecessary peoplevery well english spoken reception staffvery nice surroundings at the back. very relaxing garden surroundings. breakfast alfresco was fantastic. but limited tables outsideinside restaurant is well set, cosy and comfortablethe lobby has much space for waiting and sitting area.the bar is also well set up but closes at 11 pm every night, bust room service is 24hrswifi is available but need to pay. valid for 24 hours then recharge at business countermy trip in November was surrounded by an embargo by India which severely limited supply of petrol, diesel, gas, medical supplies and other essential materials.hence this was only limited to kathmandu. any trip outside kathmandu depended on the cost and availability of fuel.The himalaya range is not visible from Kathmandu. One needs to travel about 50km out of the valley. I highly recommend visiting kathmandu and Nepal in general when the Indian Embargo is fully lifted.

This is a great hotel with well trained staff, polite and helpful. The environment is no doubt very good, you can walk around the gardens and the small lake, and it is close to the Thamel area (10 minutes walking or so). My room was quite nice and the right size, breakfast was also good and enough options. Will certainly choose it again if come back.

The hotel is an island of the things people coming from the western world need and much more so that it is really luxurous! Our stay for three days has been pleasant not only due to this stuff also due to the geograhical Location the the City. You can reach many of the touristic highlights by foot!

Tucked just off Durbar marg so a 10 minute walk to Thamel and 20 mins to Durbar Square. We only ate breakfast which was a normal large hotel buffet style. Food was good, especially as they were suffering from a national fuel shortage at the time. Nice garden, although pool being renovated currently (Oct 15). Room was fine, although the shower was slightly prone to flood as a strong shower but slow plug.

I spent the past weekend at Yak and Yeti. The reservation officer was great and let me book via the telephone, and was okay with us paying upon checkin. Upon on Check In, I got upgraded to a Club Room (minus the facilities). The Front Desk staff was amazing btw! I had a not so glorious view of a wall (room 405), but the bed and pillows more than made up for it! My room was however right across from the House Keeping utilities room, and I'm not too sure if that was the reason or not, but my room had an old, misty/mouldy smell to it. House keeping also needs major improvement- not the cleanest.I will definitely go back and stay here- it is close enough to Thamel and KTM Darbar Square without being smack in the middle of Thamel, and thus offering a little more privacy, the staff extremely friendly, it's absolutely beautifully decorated, and overall has the potential to be an amazing hotel! Would love to see improvements!

Had a short stay in Yak & Yeti. The hotel at its best maintained the electricity supply. This is a great hotel for business travel. The location is excellence and it is within walking distance to Thamel area. The hotel had a great garden, great for a short morning walk. During my stay, the hotel was full house. And the breakfast is sufficient for the guest with great varieties.

One of the best hotels I've ever experienced in terms of service.  Breakfast was very good (nice options), and the staff know you after Day 1.  Concierge service was excellent -- she knew everything about everything and really listened to what we wanted to do (and provided great suggestions).  Garden is beautiful -- nice jogging track around a little lake with ducks!  Short walk from Thamel (shopping and restaurant/bar mecca! A must do!)  And, there is a little supermarket only a few blocks away (if you want to buy snacks).  Only reason Y&Y doesn't rate a 5 is that the decor is a bit dated -- in the rainy season, the rooms smell a bit musty. But, definitely a good choice -- would stay here again!

I did not stay at the Yak & Yeti, but was there for 7 days for a Buddhist teaching, so this writing really belongs under attractions.The garden at the Yak & Yeti, as well as their terrific buffet is open to all.The garden is large, lovely, well landscaped and a welcome escape fromthe traffic  and pollution of Kathmandu and Themal.Give yourself a break and take advantage of this space.

We were group of 30 and stayed 3 nights at Yak & Yeti. We were given very good overall service. Buffet food was tasty and had large selection of choices. Just 10 min walk from Tamel, but the streets next to the hotel offers also large variation of shops. Katmandu's charm is unforgettable.

Last week Yak and Yeti Hotel was able to hold a function for more than 500 people for 7 days  with outstanding service and facilities.  We congratulate Yak and Yeti Hotel for being able to cater for so many people when Nepal is facing so many difficulties after the earthquakes and with the Nepal-India blockade. Fortunately Yak and Yeti Hotel was not damaged in the quakes and its magnificent old and new buildings looked splendid set away from busy roads with a beautiful back gardens. Friends staying there said the rooms and service were great.  To be able to cater for over 500 people each day for seven days is a tribute to Nepali hospitality. You can also go there for lunch or dinner in their delightful restaurant which has great buffets. Highly recommended as an oasis in the chaos of Kathmandu and as a venue for small or large functions.

(+) Room is big. The decoration is testy with craved wood. The hotel looks classic. I heard that it used to be palace. The elevator is also decorated with craved wood. The air condition shows temperature. There are many plug many places in the room so it is convenience. There are free wifi. I can connect two devices simultaneously. The location is good. We can find many shops nearby. I can walk to Thamel street from here easily. (-) There is only shower. The shower doesn't have door so the rest room becomes messy easily. There is not toothbrush. Internet is slow. Dinner inside has only buffet. Bar is quite expensive. The soda water is just water. The first night is quite noisy with loud music from somewhere.

If you arrive in Katmandu from the west, you struggle to accept this as 5 star hotel. The structure is nice (wooded carvings, large garden), but the service or cleanliness has no comparison with an Indian 5 star hotel. Breakfast is okish, no big deal, sweets are ok, but the fruits have no taste. If you arrive at y&y after a long trekking, well ....you end up appreciating the various luxuries of y&y that at the end may cost you a bit over €100.

We've been coming to this elegant and venerable Kathmandu hotel for many years.  But now, in the wake of the catastrophic earthquakes that wracked Nepal from April 25 through May, it is important to report that the Yak & Yeti was not damaged and that the level of service and staff competence is undiminished.  The accomodations, the quality of the restaurants, the lovely and spacious garden and grounds, the very central and convenient location, and the professionalism of the staff, make this a good choice.  As I write I am sitting in our room on the 4th floor after snacks in the Club Floor hospitality room with Mr. Bhakta raj Bahrati, a 19-year veteran of the staff, in attendance.We are at home.James A. Pearre

A fantastic historic hotel with great service and staff. Pricey, but a great place to relax after trekking or climbing. Lots of trips to begin and or end at the Yak & Yeti. Treat yourself to some Nepali style luxury. The sauna and steam bath are a bonus after some serious Himalayan travels.
