Went for a meeting and lunch over there. The hotel is big and fascinating. I had a perfect meeting with a perfect lunch (excellent service, tasty food, along with very soothing instrumental music). Although, I had to pay for WiFi (it's not free everywhere) but I don't mind it at all.

We stayed here in October/November, 2014, before the earthquake.  Facility is excellent, lovely garden area, nice pool, service was excellent, location in Kathmandu is excellent.  Kathmandu has multiple power outages daily, but can't blame that on the hotel.  We enjoyed the Y&Y when we arrived in Kathmandu, but it was even more appreciated after returning from the Khumbu region's more spartan tea houses.

Stayed with family, good location great view, but  hotels seems look old. Room was nice comfortable but renovation required. Food was average nothing great. Heard lot about this hotel, but didn't live up to the expectation. Staff badly required training.Good business hotel but badly required attention towards upgradation.

Stayed here for two nights after the earthquake. Seems like a lot of NGO and doctors have been making this place home. The hotel and grounds are beautiful, an oasis in the middle of the city. The staff is polite and efficient without being overbearing. The two restaurants are wonderful. Rooms could use a bit sprucing up, but the wifi is reliable and fast. Wouldn't hesitate to stay here again.

We had a booking at the Yak & Yeti for the nights of the 25th April (the day the earthquake struck) & 26th April.  As we were in Bardia when the quake struck we could not get our scheduled flight back to Kathmandu that evening, due to the closure of KTM airport. We ended up getting an overnight bus to KTM in the hope that the airport would reopen by the time we were due to leave Nepal on the 27th.  We were worried that, even though it was due to exceptional circumstances, the Yak & Yeti might not honour our booking as we had missed the first night, (You would like to think that any decent hotel would but, unfortunately, experience has taught us otherwise.)By the time we got to the hotel our nerves were frazzled from the overnight bus journey and things we saw on the way. Understandably, the hotel staff were also clearly on edge and absolutely shattered, as most of them had worked through the night to accommodate their guests. However, they welcomed us and assured us that we would not be charged for the first night (although that was not the case but we were not keen to argue over it). The staff did an outstanding job under very extreme circumstances and went over and above their remit.  Obviously they had worries of their own, but I witnessed one particularly rude, arrogant, egotistical customer unbelievably abuse a member of staff, who while upset, took it on the chin.  He is a better man than I.Having just read through some of the latest reviews of the Yak & Yeti I came across David R's. It seems that we were there together and I can confirm and support everything he wrote.  This hotel is absolutely worth going back to just for the professionalism alone.  Well done Yak & Yeti. You should stand proud. We truly hope that you can come through this terrible tragedy on a personal as well as a professional level.

We enjoyed our stay at the Yak and Yeti.  It is a bit upscale and not the type of place we normally stay.  I must admit it is a quiet place in the middle of a crazy Kathmandu.  When we first arrived we had just come back from trekking to Tengboche and the people were a bit much.  We went to our quiet room with a view of the gardens and quickly relaxed.The room was lovely and the garden area even better.  The breakfast buffet was amazing.The only negative is that we had to pay for wifi service.  This just doesn't seem to make sense for such a lovely place an with the cost.We left just before the earthquake and hope all is well.  If we had been there during the earthquake, I can't imagine a better place to be.

Stayed here from April 18-April 22, 2015 in room number 648. As in my usual style...Positives: 1) Super quick check-in and friendly staff at the reception2) The room was cozy and quiet. The bed (although the mattress was old looking), was very warm and comfortable and I slept very well on all nights.3) Quick room service and housekeeping service4) Well stocked mini bar5) Good view from the room and nice seating space near the window 6) Large, clean pool and beautiful garden cafe7) Located in Durbarmarg which is a good location, close to shopping streets, restaurants adnd Thamel8) Ample plug points for charging your laptop / cellhphone with one located right next to the bed. 9) Good gymnasium. Negatives:1) Wifi was chargeable (750 Nepali rupees for 24 hours)2) The room service menu had a small selection. Very few round-the-clock dishes and the taste wasn't that great3) Limited variety in the breakfast / lunch / dinner buffet spread. I also found the restaurant staff very slow and inefficient. I had to ask for water thrice and after not getting it, I had to go and fill it myself. 4) TV had a very small selection of channels.

Nice quiet place to stay and rest after an outdoor trip to see the Himalayas. Yak and Yeti are mythical creatures in Nepal, and they keep the legends alive for tourists. Tour oriented hotel.  Kid friendly hotel, and ok rooms. No frills, but value for money.

The hotel isn't a modern building but it is all the better for that. It has all the assets of the latest technology. The staff were professional, friendly and wanted to please. The restaurant had a wide variety of food, including appetising bowls of fresh fruit and delicious dessert delicacies. The rooms were spacious, clean well appointed. The gardens were a wonderfully peaceful area to sit in the shade before or after a day sightseeing.

Nice Welcome when we arrived. Stayed 4 days.  The room was clean.  The bed was great.  The shower was great with super hot water.  The breakfast buffet has good food that would please folks from all parts of the world.  One day we had breakfast to go and the packed food was very good (arranged it the night before). Ate supper also and it was good with great desserts!Easy walk to Thamel area.  Wifi was included with our reservation.  Would stay here again.Ask for a room overlooking the gardens.

I stayed at the Yak& Yeti about 16 days of my 5 week tour of south Asia. At the time of booking I almost knew nothing about this hotel other than it's somewhat humorous name. From the time I set foot in my room there the staff was kind efficient and above all professional. The Yak&Yeti is older by western standards but makes up for it with a 5 and one half star staff. The room comes with breakfast which by Nepali standards is good. The big plus is that the hotel is located in center of Katmandu in an upscale neighborhood surrounded by walls and security guards posted everywhere.  I have travel to 56 countries and usually stay at 5 star hotels and have to stay the Yak& Yeti staff is among the most professional of them all.

I really can not praise the service of this hotel enough. Our bags had not arrived and they provided us with toiletries , then drove my husband to the airport the next morning. Checked out then in again at the same rate after our flight to Pochara was cancelled !! We were then stranded in Kathmandu a week later due to airport closure, checked in again !! The staff could not have been more helpful in such a stressful situation . A big thank you to all at guest relations The beds are so comfortable and the hotel is really peaceful after the chaos of the city and airport . A big thank you to all at the Yak and Yeti , we look forward to staying with you again . Almost forgot the wine selection in the bar , the bar manager and staff were first class !!

First, please note this is NOT a five star hotel.  Not even close.  But, if you are traveling to Kathmandu - then I have to guess you are not truly expecting five star services.  The rooms are reasonably priced and the location in-town makes the Y&Y a good choice for a moderate hotel accommodation during your stay.  The staff at the hotel is very nice.  There is some tradition among many travelers that puts the Y&Y on the top of the list of hotels for Nepal, but I must say that I think that is a fading sentiment.  I did not find any specific charm or allure about this property, except that is close to the main part of town and you can walk outside of the hotel to look at the tourist shops.  The rooms are clean, modest and offer few amenities.  The rooms and bedding is similar to what you might find in an average Hampton Inn in the US - with a little touch of Nepal.  Beds are slightly firm, pillows synthetic, towels average, no hair dryer, no robes, etc.  Like all spots in Kathmandu, the hotel suffers power outages that recover within a few minutes.  There are a few areas in the hotel that are considered upgrades, like the Heritage rooms we selected or the executive floor, which I would encourage you to book.  Be aware that the noise in the halls comes directly into your room, so pick a more secluded area, if available.  Also, smoke poured into one of our rooms, even though the hotel insisted it did not allow smoking in the area we were assigned.  We asked for another room and they did politely move us. There is a garden and pool in the back of the hotel, so you might request that view... however, given the number of birds in the area - I would not actually make use of this area.   The restaurant on site does have an extensive menu, but not one person in our group enjoyed the food - so that is sort of limiting for this hotel in terms of recommendations.  Having stayed at both the Yak and Yeti and the Grand Hyatt Kathmandu, I would say the Y&Y has appeal as the in-town choice only - or if you have some sense of tradition about this hotel. I would opt for the Grand Hyatt over the Y&Y based on overall performance and especially given the far superior food choices at the Hyatt.

Very nice hotel with a great architecture and history. The old building used to be a palace. With a nick of history pictures along the way i enjoyed my stay there. Nepalist a bit funny when it comes to bookings through online. We booked for one standard room (King bed size) obviously it can fits 2. but we just put one guest. regardless how many guest we demand for king size bed anyways. they will charge extra fee per head.which never happens to any country ive been. Nepalist way I guess. so heads up when it comes to bookings online guys :) Other than that everything was alright. small bathroom. super comfy bed. delicious food. But the casino has been shut permanently.

I am not sure if I felt it was worth the money I paid; more than 180USD a day!Rooms are small and view that we had was very average. Decor is alright but the rest needs to be upgraded. At the reception, it is not nice to have a bad surprise on the room rent when it was confirmed very well several times just upon arrival. after clarification, the reception agreed that I was right. This is serious and bad! I say better watch out in this regard.housekeeping is absolutely bad.Breakfast spread was nice.Food from the restaurant was nice too.airport transfers are done in a shuttle which can be inconvenient.I also dint find their local travel agency(in the hotel)very genuine and efficient. Overall I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

Stayed here for a week while I was on a work trip in February 2010. Overall a satisfactory experience but the rooms need some renovating as they are quite old. The bathroom is not up to the standard of a 4/5 star hotel. The hotel is very close to restaurants and shops and about a 10 minute walk from Thamel. It also has a casino called Casino Royale :)

Statyed here just before and immediately after a 15-day trek in the Himalayas.The hotel is clean, well run & an absolute haven after the decent, but basic mountain tea houses.  Room service was terrific & the staff very friendly & helpful.I only had breakfast at the hotel & the range of foods on offer was sumptuous - especially liked the Indian breakfasts.The Spa lets the place down a little, even though it has a decent Jacuzzi, steam room and sauna.  The fit and finish is a little lacking & rather lets the hotel down a bit.  Perfectly serviceable and usable though!The lobby bar is a cool place to hangout & sink a few beers over delicious nibbles.Whilst it's a great hotel & I really enjoyed my stay, the hotel is not quite up to the best 5* service you can find elsewhere in Asia.  Nevertheless, it's a wonderful place to stay & extremely welcome after a long trek.

I stayed in the Yak and Yeti for the last week of November.  I've been visiting Nepal once or twice  a year for at least 25 years and for some reason had never previously stayed at this hotel - but I will return.  Everything was handled most professionally and the staff were helpful and went out of their way to ensure that I had everything I needed to enjoy my stay.  A couple of members of staff saw that I was struggling to put my sari (I was there for a wedding) on correctly and spent time redressing me.  The room I stayed in in the New Wing looked newly decorated and it certainly had a fantastic new bed, bedding and towels.   Lovely garden, good room service and excellent Wi-Fi.   The only area which I think needs looking at by the management is the coffee shop.  The first night I ordered a glass of wine and it arrived , despite reminders, as I was finishing my meal. Even the beer I ordered on the following night took 20 minutes to arrive at my table.   Also it does not look very professional when, at about 9 o'clock, the black jackets in the restaurant start queuing up with the guests at the buffet and sit down to have their meal in the restaurant.Aside form that a delightful hotel and I am looking forward to trying the spa on my next visit.

Stayed there for 3 nights this month, Oct 2014.  We took several rooms as we were a group visiting from Dubai.  Very nice hotel, good service, and perfect garden for morning coffee. We had a pleasant stay there, and the managemern, Philippe Belhay and team, was very friendly and hospitable.

Staff were very friendly and courteous. Room was recently renovated and bed very comfortable. Breakfast was good with some excellent Indian options. Nice quiet location, with rather nice restuarant across the manicured lawn. Free wifi for only one device, which seems a little unnecessary. All in all a pleasant hotel.

See the note on picking a good room first.  Beyond a slight issue with the room which we had switched after asking twice, the hotel grounds, foyer, restaurant, etc. are very nice.  The pool is a bit on the chilly side once you get out of the summer months, but it's nice to sit around and sip a cool drink.  The restaurant has a large and varied buffet breakfast and dinner (a definite plus).  This is a hotel for many trekkers first and last stays in Nepal, so you get to chat a lot with people about their activities.  There is a main street a short walk from the hotel with lots of small restaurants and shops.  Kathmandu is a very crowded (and unfortunately dirty) city, so it was nice to retreat to this clean oasis after a hectic day of visiting.

This is how our stay went:1. Arrive at hotel after 6 hrs journey from Pokhara and wait outside with our stuff for 15 minutes before a bell boy arrives. The gatekeeper is busy welcoming other guests and does not bother to inquire.2. After checking in we find, we (husband-wife) have been provided two single beds instead of one double. After several calls and an hour of wait, the house-keeping joins the beds together and the manager assures we will have double bed room the next day.3. The room is full of mosquitoes on the 7th floor and hotel offers to spray pesticide while we are staying there instead of offering good knight etc, as requested.4. No extra blanket which we needed for our 70 yrs old mother. And when it comes, the maintenance/house-keeping head instead of handing it over to us, walks straight into her room and spreads it over her. Boundaries please! We are your guest not your family.5. The breakfast time - 10 staff members moving about but not one bothers to lead you to a seat, offer you water or any other help.6. Limited options in breakfast - even an omelet is not made on order. You pick one from a stack of stale ones cooked sometime in the morning7. We ask them if we can have breakfast outside in the lawn and they are clearly reluctant, the lady on duty telling us "how will you take the stuff outside... you will have to come in again for refills..have it here only" So what was the staff for?8. The pool looked nice from our floor but was dirty, full of bird droppings.9. The changing room, for the pool, was full of water and unkempt10. The a-la-carte menu was fairly good but over-priced. We preferred walking to "Little Italy" nearby for dinners the rest of the days11. We consume a lot of water and it was irritating explaining it to housekeeping every time we needed more bottles.For a so called 5-star tag and price, this place was a big let down.... a total "sarkari" way of doing things.

stayed here for two nights before changing to our "trek" hotel.  Would stay here again...hotel was well located to Thamel, the grounds had so much charm - the marigolds were in full bloom, the ducks and geese just wandered around.  We stayed in the Club room facilities, although pleasant, did not think it was worth the extra money at this stage.  I would really like to see the gym facilities improved with more up to date aerobic equipment - as guests would like to use these to stay fit for upcoming treks.

I stayed in yak yeti for 3 days the location of the hotel is what it should be given priority it's just in the heart of the city kathmandu, but the rooms are not so good there's no feeling of a 5 star hotel... the rooms are now old and humid ac is also poor

We stayed two nights at the end of a trip through Tibet and Nepal.  A great way to end the trip as the rooms and public spaces were terrific, as was the food.  The rooms are in a new building; the public spaces are partly in the new building, partly in an old palace.  We had breakfast and dinners there, and the food was excellent, as was the service.  The hotel is well located; you can get to a lot of places in Kathmandu by walking.

We've stayed at this hotel three times in the last two years and standards seem to be dropping.Friendly customer service has disappeared and staff seem a little aloof.Breakfast has opened late on our last two stays meaning we've been rushed to keep to schedule. The staff seem to struggle to keep the buffet restaurant clean and tidy. The floor and bases to the tables are filthy.The refurbished rooms are good but watch out for the large numbers of dirty pigeons who coo, sleep, fight and poop on many of the window ledges (see photos). In most countries health inspectors would close a decent hotel down for this because of the bacteria that could easily be transmitted from the vast amounts of bird poop.We complained and asked to be moved rooms. We were, but to another room that had the same pigeon problem. So we moved again. Staff acknowledge the problem but don't apologise or do anything about it. The duty manager was difficult to reach to help resolve the issue.My companion obtained the email address for the general manager although staff were reluctant to provide his card. He responded to say cleanliness is something they have a programme for but said the pigeon issue hasn't been a cause for complaint before.Loyalty hasn't been rewarded here. You'd think the management could see that we've stayed three times now so might have waived the cost of our evening meal or massages given the inconvenience. Alas, this hasn't happened but as we paid by credit card, if the management see this, they may make a gesture of goodwill and reverse the charges. That may restore some confidence in me. Otherwise, we wouldn't be looking to come back.

We recently spent 4 nights here during a 2 week trip to Nepal, a couple of nights at the begining and at the end. It was a lovely place to relax, chill out, escape the hussle and bussle. It is a lovely old / yet modern setting with lots of history. The rooms are very nice, the beds super comfortable and the staff very welcoming. The breakfast buffets were highly diverse with all sorts on offer whatever your palate. The bar is a bit $$$$, but lovely space to chillout and relax. The girls enjoyed an afternoon round the pool and the gardens. Overall great place to stay.

If you have an event, this is the place to have it!  Hotel Management, food, catering, and atmosphere are all top notch!  The staff truly made our event our huge success.  It seemed to me that the staff and management had as much as stake in the success of our event as we did.  They helped out in so many ways to planning, to helping, and advising.  I've never had the management and staff be so very helpful and going above and beyond to help us be successful.  We have run many events in many different hotles in countries around the world, and this hotel was the best.  They even remembered specifics such as room numbers and other info from an event we had with them three years prior.  They pride themselves on service and running a well organized hotel.  That was evident in everything that was done.The food was excellent.  I especially enjoyed the pasta part of the lunch buffet.  The catering was well done.The renovated hotel rooms were well done and designed to still appear to be antique and authentic Nepali.  I really enjoyed it.Thank you to all at the Yak and Yeti for making our event a true success!

When detaching the crowded city what we need is the hotel.An experience of many stars and a kitchen that will remain long in the memory of our taste buds.A stroll through the gardens takes you to the era of kings and makes you feel part of these!

I am travel agent based in Delhi. I had organised a conference in the m/o Feb 14 for 5 nights for around 35 pax. The service was excellent, rooms were good / spacious. Food had unlimited variety and quantity. It was zero error conference. I liked it so much that planning to organize one of our next conference in the m/o Nov (on the side line of SAARC summit).Special thanks to their Director Sales - Mr Surendra, for making my conference, successful.

This hotel has a great advantage due to its centralized location. Malls, eating joints, markets are just a hop-skip and jump away. One might actually forget to tour the city of Kathmandu as this hotel binds the guests to its scenic campus. The early morning tea at the picturesque gardens along side a small pond with swans wondering adds to the beauty of the hotel. Rooms are spacious with luxurious amenities, food is delicious and staff hospitality is something to mention about. The fitness centre, spa and other facilities make this place a complete package.Booked the hotel with some expectations after browsing the website but expectations were exceeded soon on check in. Carried some wonderful memories from Hotel Yak & Yeti. Kudos to the team!

The hotel has excellent location and the service is also very good . The upholstery definitely needs a makeover , the carpets in the rooms seem to be very old and never ever cleaned.. The windows were very dirty from outside due to the bird droppings. The housekeeping staff is very rude , they just knock once and then straight away open the door with master keys. The food quality is average , the buffet does not suit every palette . Overall it is not worth the money .The hotel does offer complimentary pick and drop from the airport.

Staff service was good and attentive, and I also enjoyed an excellent massage session there. One concern I have with the hotel is the poor gym area; the equipment provision is simply too outdated, and the room is too small. Jacuzzi and steam room/sauna use were for extra charge, which I found unreasonable as they come standard in every other hotel I have stayed in. it'd also be good to have more variety in the breakfast buffet other than Indian! most time I found myself having just boiled eggs and fruits. Pancakes were good though. As mentioned elsewhere the hallways in upper floors could use renovation; it was dimly lit and the carpets looked old.

Slowly but surely Kathmandu's famous Yak and Yeti Hotel is getting a well-deserved facelift.  The old wing, now the Heritage Wing, is being redone with traditional carvings, wood floors and new linens that brighten up the rooms.  The newer wing has been spruced up, and looks quite nice also.  For many reasons, the  Yak and Yeti has been my preferred hotel in Kathmandu both for myself and my Myths and Mountains guests.  Top of the list is "location, location, location. " The hotel is tucked away off of Dhurbar Marg, lined with nice stores, and not too far from the former palace.  It is a 10 minute walk to the crowded Thamel area with its tourist shops and restaurants and very near the beautiful Garden of Dreams, a restored palace and park dating back to the 19th century era of the Rana rulers.  Here one can also find a lovely restaurant frequented by Nepalis and tourists for both lunch and dinner.  There may be other hotels that are fancier or more expensive, but none can boast the location.Secondly, I love the feng shui of the grounds.  In the back, the hotel has a small pond, complete with geese and ducks and  backed up by a hill and tiny shrine.  There is a nice, green lawn area lined with colorful flowers and boasting a good-sized pool.  To sit or dine outside is a relaxing pleasure.Third, I have always appreciated the warmth of the staff, from the concierge staff, to management, to those in the restaurants.  They have always been welcoming, courteous and helpful - willing to go the extra mile or prepare a delicious cup of homemade Nepali chai.  Food is good in both the buffet and restaurants, and during cocktail hour and evenings, there is a piano bar.The hotel boasts a spa, beauty parlor, exercise room, shops and there are tennis courts available for those who wish.  Parking is easy, something much appreciated in crowded Kathmandu today .

I stayed in yak and yeti last week and was pleasantly happy with my stay . I have stayed in other hotels of the same level which are in near vicinity and its easily better than the rest.The hotel can do a lot better if it wants to , some of the areas seem bit old but overall its a good hotel with a good price. Food was good and internet was also zippy. The hotel staff was nice and welcoming.I enjoyed the stay and would recommend it

I stayed here for a week on business and occupied a front room on the 5th floor.The room was large, comfortable clean bed and a clean large bathroom. Only let down by the age you have to leave the water on to get it hot. A big waste of water IMHO.The staff are friendly and customer focused, even the security guards are helpful,smart and polite.The location is good near the old palace and set back from the manic roads. Easy access to the city and beyond and the shopping in Thamel is only a 10 min 200SR ride away. If you don't end up in an accident...Food in the hotel was average and maybe not up to the room price tag. Especially with such amazing food available locally cheaper.A decent gym is located in the basement and a pretty tranquil garden too.A good visit in a nice hotel.

We stay in this hotel for 3 nights at the start and end of our Nepal Holiday. This hotel offers a welcome respite from the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu (which is a noisy, gridlocked and fumed filled city). Stepping into the hotel is like an Oasis of calm after a days sightseeing. There is a nice lobby area which serves drinks and a restaurant which offers breakfast, lunch and dinner although the service is extremely slow and hap hazard and meal times can be somewhat chaotic at peak times. The rooms are adequate with very comfortable beds and clean albeit small bathrooms. Although the hotel boats 5 stars it would not be up to the perceived 5 star standard. Overall we enjoyed our stay here, there are limited options for comfort in the City and this offers a good alternative. The large grounds offers escape from the noise of the city so sleep quality is excellent. There is a small pool, a casino and a fine dining and Nepalese Restaurant at the back of the Hotel, both of which were very good. The hotel is 30 minutes from the airport by car.

I stayed 24 hours in this lovely hotel. Its location is great. We had free WiFi.Nirvana Spa, breakfast at Chimney Restaurant, post lunch a free airport drop,and helpful guest relation executives, made my stay pleasant and memorable.Casino Royale / casinos in Kathmandu have been closed for last 3 months.

After having a complete marriage of a relative and staying in the hotel YAK & YETI for 7 days consecutive days its been like a home to be. The hotel managers are very cooperative and helpful. They have tried to make the best of their resources. The new GM Mr Phillipee is a cooperative person but very new to this hotel. The hotel is run very well by its owners but it does need an upgrade. Though nothing is broken or un kept but still it feels old. The entire staff and the hotel tried their best to help us in all possible ways and were successful in doing so.A THANK YOU TO  ALL YOU GUYS. But as always there are some who always play the spoil sport namely  MR PRAN CHAND AND CHINNIYA KAZI and living in their own world and need an urgent course in hospitality. Because the word hospitality is not existing in their vocabulary. Please check or the rotten apple will spoil the entire basket.

My family and I have just gotten back from our vacation at the Yak and Yeti Kathmandu. We were there for 4 nights between the 26th June and 30th June 2014 and had 2 rooms . My reviews for the property are as under:(1) The Hotel s location is easily the best in Kathmandu. It is strategically located.(2) The Staff at the Hotel is polite, well turned out and very friendly (3) Mr Philip the GeneraL Manager deserves a special mention he is always taking rounds and asking on his guests if they are comfortable etc .. This for me is always a special quality where the guests suggestions and inputs are taken into account. considering he has been there just 5 weeks a lot of complaints and suggestions seem to have been implemented upon . For example the internet connectivity was working just fine in the rooms, there were complaints of smell in some reviews which I did not encounter (and mind you my sense of smell is very good) so hats off to you Mr Philip for taking care of these complaints in previous reviews.Last but not the least I would like to just make a suggestion as I had personally made to Mr Philip, a lot of attention needs to be diverted towards the swimming pool the floor of the pool is very very slippery at places and needs to be cleaned up on war footing. Also my suggestion to Mr Philip would be to restrict the number of members using the Hotel Facilities drastically. The first right of the swimming pool and the gym and other facilities should always be of the in house guest and not the local members. I appreciate the fact that more members means more revenue but it compromises on the quality of the service being provided. I hope to visit Kathmandu soon again and will most certainly stay at Yak and Yeti. More power to Mr Philip and his team RegardsRajeev Madan

We stayed 3 nights at this property in June 2014. They have a new wing and an old wing, which we were not aware of. We were given rooms in the old wing on the 2nd floor. All the even numbered rooms face the garden and the other rooms have view of surprisingly a dump yard/ construction site. The elevator is located in one corner making it an extremely long walk for  rooms at the other end through the smelling carpeted  narrow walkway. Rooms somehow did not give a very positive aura maybe because of the old carpets. Bathroom was basic with a stained bath tub. They really have to renovate the rooms in this wing. One of our rooms was a suite which had the addition of a sofa area. There was electricity backed by generators throughout which seemed to be one of our major concerns when planning our Nepal trip. Apparently Nepal has a major electricity shortage. Room service had excellent food. We ordered Indian, Italian and Chinese. Leaving the Italian the rest of the food was tasty. Breakfast on the ground floor was decent with cooperative staff. Their pool area and lawns made for a picturesque setting with many morning and evening walkers. The ducks and goose were an added charm. No free wifi even in the dining/lobby area. Did not purchase the paid wifi so cannot comment. This property is right in the heart of Kathmandu at Durbar Marg, which means very easy and convenient access to shopping and eateries in Kathmandu. Keep in mind that Kathmandu is dead by 9:30 pm so you wind up your day by then. Right outside the hotel is a night club which made the ambience kind of unsafe at night. Your stay over here will be fantastic if you get the good new rooms otherwise can let you down.

We stayed in this palatial hotel in June this year. Not too far(or near) from Kathmandu airport. The shopping area, Thamel is also at walking distance of fifteen to twenty minutes. The outside look of hotel is impressive. We were given twin sharing room. The room are just ok. The carpet is bit worn down, and mild smell of dampness was there. The bathrooms are clean with minimal toiletries and just one napkin. The mattress and pillow are very soft (that at least I could not sleep properly; I need slightly firm mattress). Otherwise hotel is nice with helpful and courteous staff. We could not enjoy swimming because of rains. The swimming pool appeared bit small. The travel desk was very efficient. We booked the mountain flight from this hotel. The hotel provided us with complimentary drop to the airport for this flight.The notable thing is about food. The cuisine at breakfast and lunch is really mouth watering and there are variety of dishes. We were here for conference purpose and the dinner and banquet are at Durbar hall which was a large area very attractive decoration. Again, the food at banquet was very nice. There is no free wifi in this hotel, even at lobby.

Work trip brought me to Nepal and the Yak and Yeti. Most staff, especially the housekeeping team were fabulous! I found the front desk staff to be a bit stand offish at times, e.g., on several occasions, I was standing in front of them for minutes, during non-busy times, before they asked if they could help. The rooms facing the garden are quite nice and maintained spotlessly. Hot water is very sporadic - sometimes bordering on cool and internet is spotty. Also one device can have internet on at at a time so it is not possible to have wireless on the phone and laptop simultaneously. The hotel offers transport to and from the airport. It is supposed to run on schedule however the driver and about 4 others waited for one guest for 15 minutes after the designated departure time. Finally, the Y & Y does not really pay attention to the amenities advertised for packages, e.g., I did not get a welcome drink and the newspaper was not left at my room during any of the days during my stay. All in all, it is a nice hotel but these somewhat small annoyances add up and will motivate me to try another hotel should my work bring me back to Kathmandu.

Is your stay in Kathmandu for business, this hotel will be an excellent choice, offer a very good breakfast, nice rooms, good meeting places. Better MO-MO around the corner…A bit on the pricy side, but offer good value for money

I visited this property in the Month of April this year. What to say about this hotel......The place, the ambience, the staff and the food....everything seemed so perfect. This was my truly international experience. The place has some nicely done rooms with all modern facilities. Highly recommended for families and even business travellers. The gym, pool and the garden were simply superb.

In truth, it's an average hotel, with slightly below par facilities, probably deserving of a three star rating. I gave it four because the staff are just so nice, and everything about the place so far has been easy - from airport pickup, though check-in, bars, meals, room service etc. I'm a business traveller in Kathmandu for a week, and have needed to spend quite a lot of time in the hotel. The rooms are fine - spacious, good bed, modern TV and cable, only slightly rundown (tip - don't stare too closely at the water you've just showered in ...). I admit i don't have much frame of reference for comparison with other hotels in Kathmandu (first visit), but I've been overwhelmed with how friendly everybody is, and genuinely helpful. They seem very surprised if you tip them, and grateful - amazing considering how poorly I tip. The building itself is nice enough, although the pool is disappointing, but people make this place. I'd recommend it, on balance.

We didn't stay here but met friends in the garden for drinks. Considering it is right in the middle of crazy Kathmandu, it is an oasis of peace and tranquillity and I can't work out how they've managed to screen the car horns and other city noises. Beautiful garden area where there are covered tables and chairs to sit out on the lawn. We had a tour of the communal areas and it looks like a very decent hotel with a blend of history and old culture as well as new rooms and a refurbed block.

Perfect location for exploring Kathmandu; lovely garden area, good internet speed, decent service. Buffet food really lacking, though breakfast was fine. Nice bar area. Decent internet service, generally charged extra.

We stayed at the Yak and Yeti for 3 nights - one night when we arrived in Kathmandu and two nights at the end of our holiday.  It was a welcome retreat from the city which is busy and noisy and an attack on the senses!We had interconnecting rooms.  The rooms on the garden side of the hotel have a nicer outlook.  The beds were the most comfortable of our trip.  The rooms were clean and although the hotel is quite "old fashioned" we liked that.  The buffet restaurant was good - a great selection of food.  We had breakfast there. The dinner there is also good - lots of choice, even able to satisfy three hungry boys.Tee gardens are lovely.  here is a pool and tennis courts.  Pool was clean and cool.  Don't leave without checking out the Yeti footprint in the rock in the garden!

An Oasis in a busy city. Good breakfast and nice bar. Lots of activity and plenty of interesting people coming and going. We were upgraded to a suite due to non pick up from the airport, but other than that it was a great hotel.

Good Place to live based on Location & Cleanliness.Breakfast is good also.Our Dining Experience is also good  at "The Chimney" they have taken time to serve the food but the food quality & Taste is awesome must recommended.

I liked the Yak and Yeti. It is a huge hotel. The lobby is often jampacked with people, especially large tour groups. The front desk was professional and quick. They were not exceptional in terms of warmth. That's because the place is enormous and they have thousands of guests passing through every day. The location can't be beat. The service is not like a small Nepalese hotel where they treat you like a member of the family. Go elsewhere if that's what you require. The Sunrise had wonderful breakfast and dinner. I am amazed anyone is complaining about the sunrise restaurant. The doormen, bellhops, and room attendants are quite friendly. The hotel has old world charm. I liked the gym and the hot tub in the mens locker room. The Casino Royale was great to have attached. It is a fun casino to relax, play, and meet people. The massage therapist was pretty, but the massage was just okay. Room attendants doing turn down service is a nice touch. It's a nice oasis in such a busy packed city. I like getting room service late at night. Late at night there are only 4 items available to order. This is completely unsatisfactory. Everything should be available at all hours. I am used to this even from cheaper hotels with restaurants. The room was fine. The beds are comfortable, but not exceptional. The bathroom is quite strange. There is a glass wall, and it is not completely frosted. So if a friend visits, you can see them going to the bathroom inside. Why isn't the glass frosted or black? Why not? This is a very strange idea I have never seen before. See my pictures and you'll understand. My stay here was pleasant. I would consider staying here again. It is a bit pricey, but not too much so. I am surprised this hotel is not rated higher. Although not perfect, it's still pretty nice.

I recently stayed here. The hotel was expensive buthe services were of great value. I was informed that the hotel had a Renovation and it looked quiet attractive with its newly colored buildings. The hotel had a lovely ambience. I loved the Heritage deluxe rooms. It was very comfortable and so were the bathrooms. Small but very clean. The staffs at the hotel were very helpful. I loved the place and I will definitely recommend it to my friends if they visit Nepal.

The staffs are great; the room are very simple yet beautiful; added garden view from the room is cherry on top. The restaurant facing the garden with the pool view is also nice.  Location is at the centre on the city. I will definitely visit this place again nd stay here.

We stayed at Y &Y early March 14 and were so glad we made the choice.  It is a good central location. Kathmandu is so hectic it was such a joy to return to the very civilised and peaceful atmosphere of the hotel. Having a bedroom overlooking the garden is to be recommended - very attractive! The room wasnt huge but the beds were just wonderful- very supportive and yet soft - quite simply the best we have ever had in any hotel. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The breakfast extensive and the same restaurant really went out of their way to fulfill our dietary requirements in the evening. We were most impressed and would definitely stay there again.

This Hotel is perfectly located Durbar Marg, Kathmandu. I had mixed feelings about my decision for choosing to stay here but I realized that I had made the right decision. It’s a great 5 star hotel for a country like Nepal. Health facilities, cleanliness, and food everything is up to the mark. Breakfast is at Sunrise was delicious with varieties to choose from. It was a great holiday

I was in Kathmandu for two day and I chose to stay at this Hotel, as it is centrally located. I loved the Heritage Deluxe room as it is new built plus has a great ambience. I was quiet happy with the decision that I had made. I will stay here again if I come back to Nepal. I found a homely environment here.

This hotel is located in the centre of Kathmandu, near to Thamel district and the airport. It was an old palace which was converted into a hotel. It is situated in a quiet part of town. The rooms are large and the bathrooms are of average size. The hotel provides airport transfer on arrival and departure free of charge.

Really feel at home here. The masala tea is a must. Just ask them ready made Chai and you'll be pleased. Enjoy a cool waok at the Garden and you will love the tranquility there for sure. Anyways just make sure that your bed has been clear of bugs

We stayed for 6 nights and the hotel at first seemed a bit awkward. It's location though proved to be great for exploring Kathmandu sights and valley. And then we came to find the hotel staff and amenities great for service and support with a very comfortable room, good food and an escape to plan the next trip. It was our first time in Nepal and nothing can prepare you for the feeling walking down the narrow streets which shout out an unchanged culture going back thousands of years but so accessible from the hotel by foot which we did mainly but always with little taxis to pop you back. You can also get out to all the main sights quickly and cheaply within 30 mins, I went walking in the hills a few days and was able to get to some great views of the high Himalayas in less than an hour by car. I was sad to leave our room at the end of our stay.

While I agree with a couple of other reviewers who have expressed that the place is looking a little aged, this was still a wonderful experience with fantastic service!  In the middle of Kathmandu, it has its own campus that makes it an oasis of peace and relaxation in a bustling city.  The kids loved the pool and the geese and ducks that roamed the expansive lawn; and the prices were fantastic.  A comparable hotel in America would be three times as expensive.  We stayed on the Club Level (Shangri-La floor, as they call it) and definitely appreciated the extra service and the breakfast and evening meal service.  Their website guarantees best rates and has good "specials" as well.  Additionally, they were repainting the entire place while we were there (January 2014) so it should soon be back to sparkling glory.  The in-house restaurants were both also terrific; and the tennis and message were a vacation delight after a cold week in Tibet.  The Everest flight is highly recommended as well!

When booking our trip to Kathmandu, we wanted to make sure we stayed in a modern, attractive hotel. Looking at the pictures on line and on the hotel site we were truly deceived and a little disappointed. The reception area and restaurants are very nice and modern, but he rooms were disappointing to say the least. Small, dingy, old fashioned. Our first room had furniture and fittings that were falling apart and the room smelled of smoke and mould ( as though it hadn't been used for a long time. We asked to be moved and were kindly accommodated by front end staff. The second room was a little better but still small and old. The grounds were nice but needed greater maintenance.The staff were helpful when required. The food and service was good. the location was central.Charging to use the business centre should be a no no. This is a reasonable hotel but by international standards not a 4-5 star as advertised.

I stayed there for 2 nights, from 1st jan 2014 to 3rd jan 2014. A/c was not working properly n bathroom was not up to mark n many more thing that i dont like. staff dont know how to talk. This was worst hotel i have seen in my nepal trip

The stay was amazing  i enjoy stay the  un this property i really wanna one  name from front muskaan was really helpful and  very attentive and   All the staff were  very nice and sweet  to us I highly recommend this property to visit . I  will surely visit again and enjoy this property more next time beautiful place.

The stay here was really beautiful, all the staff were really helpful from the time of arrival till now everyone helped us. Mr. Janak, Pramis Specially Ms. Shreeya, she helped us much, she assist us upto the room and helped us connecting wifi and provided each and every thing we wanted. Thank you everyone for everything.

Excellent gym and spa, vast selection of massages for a very good price. Breakfast and restaurants were excellent and the service is top notch, a special thank you to Pempa in the reception and Salikram for outstanding service in the Spice room

My stay was very beautiful  and highly  recommend Muskan from Front she was excellent and  very attentive and highly recommend people to visit this beautiful property. And overall I  am in love with this property. Will visit very soon and very good hospitality.

My stay was really  nice in  hotel  property   was very beautiful. I really  wanna  mention  Muskan for her helpfulness . She introduced us the hotel and their facilities. Feels like second home. Good service. Good hospitality. Beautiful garden and rooms.
Great place to Stay with Good people to serve you. Good ambience, Good Food, Good vibes. Recommend it to all.

I stayed for three days. A friend recommended this hotel to me. It was exactly what I expected. Everyone was friendly and offered lots of hospitality. The building is very nice and clean. There is a beautifully landscaped garden in which you can take a walk. It was a very relaxing experience.

Fantastic stay. Loved the breakfast and the swimming pool. Prinshu at the front desk was most helpful. She suggested some excellent outings including a hike in the National Park to a waterfall. Thank you for a wonderful stay. I’m sure we will return in the future!

Excellent hotel. Ms. Prinshu and Mr. Binaya were very helpful with excellent advice about what to visit and where to eat. They also were willing to accommodate all our requests. The place is clean and well maintained. I’d come back for sure.

Yak and yeti’s Kesan (Bartender)recommended me Barahsinghe beer to have when you are in summer in Kathmandu and sure enough it was one of the best beers I’ve had since my college days…..Do visit secluded hotel Yak and yeti, especially the the bar where Kesan will make sure you have a great time with Barahsinghe.

Hotel is in center location, love the environment of the hotel.Services were up to higest standard.staffs were very helpfull among them Mr. Bhola Thapa Magar, Bell Boy is amazing for his excellent communication skill.He is an asset for this beautiful hotel.

Well i have to admit among mine list it is one the finest hotel in kathmandu located in heart of the city and during mine stay had a very comfortable experience. The staff were exceptionally hospitable, humble, and always ready to assist. Breakfast at the Sunrise Restaurant was quite delightful, and the beautiful garden provided a peaceful atmosphere. The view from the room's balcony was stunning, and the quiet space was perfect for jogging. I highly recommend this hotel to other travelers looking for a welcoming and enjoyable stay.

Very comfortable stay. Beautiful ambience. Very helpful staffs. Special mention to be made of miss Dolkar of front office who helped us in every small needs during our stay. Love to stay in this hotel again whenever we visit Kathmandu. Thank you.

The was amazing and room is so nice and the gentleman from front desk sachin was so nice and humble….. everything was perfect and I will suggest my friends to stay here.The food in the chimney restaurant is amazing and the vibes over there. I love it

Poor room maintain ence.carpet had stains.ac was not working.billed for complimentary wifi.There are many better hotels in Nepal..look elsewhere.Billing was not transparent.House keeping was non existent Had to change room twice due to issue with room odour and moulds

The property and staffs were stupendous. everything was top notch and the atmospere there itself is mesmerizing. we were there for couple of nights and the experience was phenomenal. it lives up to the expectations felt like a truely heritage property in the heart of kathmandu. will be back soon for the next visit in nepal.
The hotel staff are so approachable and responsive to issues. It is a hotel that I would want to stay there again if I were to visit Nepal and Kathmandu
Excellent location and excellent services Very friendly and helpful staff Well maintained pool and surroundings Love to stay again
It was ok. Breakfast was open till 10, it can be extended till 12 for people coming in mid night. Coffee/tea and water can be made more accessible at restaurant
Our event in the ballroom was meticulously organized and ambience was fabulous. Truly enjoyed the excellent hospitality.
Stayed for a short Business Trip. Great location, value for your money,  good food and friendly staff. All good to go !!
I have an amazing and memorable experience at Yak and Yeti Hotel. The most attractive thing was its architecture and the services provide.
very beautiful building structure, location is very good, like royal traditional filing. Room rent & food costing should be minimize. Hope see u next time.
A very centrally located hotel in Kathmandu. Major locations including Narayanhiti Palace within walking distance. Staff very friendly and helpful. Food is excellent. Rooms were good.

Had heard of Yak & Yeti when I was a young boy and always wanted to visit Nepal and stay at the Yak & Yeti and Soaltee ---- which I finally did at age 75. The hospitality is outstanding and the staff all smiling. helpful and courteous. Ms. Shreeya at  the reception deserves special mention.

I called from the US one month prior to request additional nights be added to our reservation (10 friends traveling, 5 rooms.) I offered to book and pay but was told these could be added when I arrived. When I did arrive, I was told the hotel was booked and no more nights could be added. I tried to speak with management, no reply. The representative at the desk answered the phone during our conversation and passed the call to the second representative. They clearly had no interest in the complete inconvenience they caused our entire party of 7 physicians and their families. Go elsewhere. The hospitality in Kathmandu is exceptional.  This hotel is a frustrating outlier. Wish I had known.
A great find.  Will definitely return. Expansive garden and Nepali inspired decor. Food choices were fine but not outstanding. Service was impeccable

The staff are very friendly. Very nice breakfast. Good coffee.  Excellent omelet. well served. I tried the dosa. For Indian breakfast. It was an enjoyable experience. The rooms are comfortable. Nice bathroom. Nine pool for hot days. I will definitely come back.

After eating in the chimney, the staff showed us around the facility that used to be a royal palace, which was very impressive. I was also very happy that the hotel staff talked to me every day.I want to use this hotel again!

fantastic property in the center of the bustling city. Staff, food and facilities are all wonderful.The on site dining was excellent and the grounds are stunning. Have stayed there each time I visit and never disappointed.

A beautiful oasis of kind, thoughtful staff, beautiful grounds and accommodations and wonderful food. Don’t miss the buffet breakfast and the Chimney Restaurant had exceptional food. Service was impecable.

Absolutely delighted to share my experience at the Yak and Yeti hotel, Nepal. The standout feature of my stay was undoubtedly the exceptional service provided by the staff. Their sweetness and attentiveness truly made me feel like a welcomed guest. The ambiance of the hotel was equally impressive. The blend of traditional Nepali aesthetics with modern comforts created a cozy atmosphere. I wholeheartedly recommend this establishment to anyone seeking a memorable and comfortable stay in Kathmandu, Nepal. Special mention goes to my favourite staff member of Yak and Yeti, Kumar who was super charming and surely a gem!

The staff is very cute and adorable there way of being as a friend is toooo cute I just fell in love them specially  artuta and nirzla they are the most beautiful and adorable girls I saw there those who had the best service

Great experience! All the staffs were friendly and approachable, ensuring a pleasant experience for guests. They are very attentive to detail and special shout-out to Salikram for his efficiency and professionalism!!

We had a wonderful stay here at hotel yak &yeti where everyone felt home. Special thank to spice team Mr.dewan,saksham, sujan& Ms. Jessica were they served with love and happiness with delecious food and  wonderful ambience.

Today we were in event of IPPAN in yak anf yeti hotel. The food ,setup and environment was perfect. Mine personal favourite was mutton pannu and chiken tikka. The best part of our event was the service and delivery of the staff was spectacular. My special regards to the kamal, saurav ,dewan ,sakshyam and rest entire team of banquet for great showmanship. What a night. Thank u all for it. Cheers.

Amazing staff everywhere with special mention to staff at the Front desk- Anamika and Artuta Spice restaurant - Naresh, Sirjana, Sujan, Charas,Swostika, Sonika,  Nirjala, Rocky and all other data serving guests at breakfast time Chimney Restaurant- Numa Housekeeping- Binita,Aastha and the team Food was great, thanks to the chefs.I only wished I could adjust the aircon temperature in the room. Everything else was great.

Excellent experience. Definitely will stay here if visited Kathmandu again. Nice staff. Room is clean and peaceful. Food is great. Right in the center. Close to Pasupathinadh temple. We really enjoyed our stay.

While staying in yak &Yeti hotel for four days  we thoroughly enjoyed the hospitality of the staff inthe spice room restaurant of the hotel. Staff is well behaved very serviceable and serves you with warmth. Binod, Saksham, jesica and Anisha needs special mention. They possess all attributes which are expected from a staff of a 5 star hotel. Wonderful experience.

The front desk so corporative every thing on just one click ( Amishan , artuta  ) .   the chef mandeep sing  personally take care of the guests like and dislike … the entire staff everyone’s name but spice room staff ( saksham , dewan , Jesica , nirzala , Mr Kiran Thapa came personally to our table 4 times in the dinner get complete . Entire spice room staff .. they serve with so much love and simple like a family , felt like I am at my own home … Special thanks to RIKESH TAMANG who guide us what to do in Nepal and we’re to go … very nice person .. Rikesh make us feel so special and make us have yummy yummy food … Thank you spice room & yak yeti hotel

wonderful  experience, nice  hospitality , spice  team was  execlent  in  service specialy  Sujan, Dewan, Binod,  Rikesh ,Sakshyam ,Nirjala and The  Chef Mandeep , Deserts  and main  course  हस many  veriety. .

We have enjoyed our holidays in yak and yeti , I would like to thanks hotel staff to provide good services.Specially enjoyed the food and test more over the staff persons severed with love , it’s is awesome experience. Mr Dewan , Saksham ,Vinod , Sujan and Mandi Safe served us delicious food and awesome hospitality. Really enjoyed my trip in the hotel

I have been visiting this hotel for years and I really love it. I have visited almost all the so called 5 star hotels in Kathmandu, however I like Yak & Yeti most.There are completely different restaurants there, but each has its own charm.The waitresses and waiters there are exceptionally friendly and accommodating.Today I was greeted by a receptionist with the name tag "Nirzala" in the main restaurant. I have rarely experienced such a warm and hearty welcome and such a lovely smile - then the very tasty food there tastes double delicious.I also like the mysterious (real?) Yeti footprint on a stone in the beautiful garden of the hotel.

I stay here on business visit regularly..The staff go extra mile to make you feel that this is your second home.. It’s just exceptional All staff from bell desk to front office to restaurant etc..I would like to make special mention about Mandy , the chef and Binaya in front office.. they are really customer focussed and travel manymiles to ensure customer delight Best wishes to all staff & management

Stayed here before and after my Everest Base Camp trek, many other climbers, trekkers, and business travelers here.  I had very friendly service from all their staff from front desk, bar, breakfast, and spa.  They have a basic fitness center, his/hers spa areas with lockers, massages, steam rooms, and jacuzzi.  The breakfasts were terrific buffet style of Hindi/Nepali plus omelette/eggs station.  The little cinnamon rolls are very tasty.  Service was great albeit not super fast American style but not super slow French style either, ha.  Rooms are nice and beds were comfy.  This is not a high end hotel but very nice for trekking groups for sure.  Hard Rock Cafe is around the corner, many souvenir shops and cash changing out the front door.  Short taxi rides to tourist sites.  Great spot and inexpensive.

My review of this hotel is a bit devided. On the one hand this is by far no 5 star hotel, even it claims it is; on the other hand, comparing with what we saw in Kathmandu and compare it with the overall impression of the city it is clearly one of the best.What we liked- good breakfast- nice quite location- good infrastructure (good, but expensive restaurant nearby, taxis always available, everything in (a bit longer) walking distance, but no chaos like in Thamel- some very helpful people (at breakfast, in restaurant, security)What was not as expected- no flexibility in terms of changing rooms- old fashioned equipment - pool was dirty (but nice to see, great garden)- extremely overpriced pick up serviceWould we go there again? Probably not, as we thing there are better places what offers a better value for money

A fantastic stay at the Yak and Yeti and an amazing meal at the Spice Room, Anisha was exceptional and more than welcoming , talked us through all the dishes and recommended many dishes for us which turned out to be fantastic 👌I’m would definitely return to this hotel and restaurant,.

Rooms are not spacious but the Heritage interiors compensates the space. Spice room their inhouse restaurant offers amazing breakfast spread including wide Indian delicacious to choose from.......Pool is averge and their spa, sauna and jacuzzi is average.

Did not meet my expectation Of a high end hotel, slow responses and processing of requests and not bring able to accommodate even small requests like extending beyond usual checkout times. Not much variety in food

So loyal and helpful staff we found most helpful staff at breakfast room chief , and service team anusha Bohora and manisha they made my stay like at home , if you are looking Royal kind of service yak & yeti is on of the place in ktm as well great location for office work as well many Ministery and Embassies  located less than 5 Km’s range

I would like to comment on Bhola Thapa for his excellent communication and room service while we were leaving hotel, absolute please to meet him, all the services were upto highest standard by all the people from room service

Wonderful staff--very considerate, friendly and concerned with making your stay nice.  Anisha, our waitress in the Spice Room for a few dinners was charming and wonderful with our group--she's a special employee!  The rooms could use a bit of a face lift but they were comfortable and clean overall.  The Spice Room served excellent food throughout the day.  The Chimney restaurant was just okay.

Yak and Yeti is in a great location but the rooms were tired— worn carpet, mold in tub caulking and we had to switch rooms to avoid viewing a construction site and all of its accompanying noisiness and smells.  Make sure to inquire about non smoking floors as the smoking floors reeked into the adjoining rooms — even if you were not a smoker.   Also disappointed as our initial stay was rooms booked with a trekking company and we then stayed an extra two nights per our guides recommendation.  The only option for our personal pay rooms was to switch to a higher different room from these lower grade rooms.  We opted not to move but were not compensated for staying in this lower grade rooms.  They also made us “check out— and check back in at the front desk.  A seemingly unnecessary set of steps.  Take note- most books and sites that profile this Hotel for pDirect booking say breakfast included but in fact was not.   They undersell their Chimney restaurant which has superb food, beautiful setting  and a welcome break from the buffets.  Our in room guide to their services was missing 80% of its contents— so we didn’t know about chimney restaurant until late in our stay  (we only learned our book was incomplete because we kept being told info was in the book and discovered it was not.) Also take note trekking groups- The “private room” buffet was lower quality food and a massive impersonal space -  we were only a group of 10 and found this space hollow, including our first meal  shared with another group — BLARING music for their celebration and I think for both of our groups- uncomfortable.

We had an amazing time in Kathmandu, and the Hotel Yak & Yeti was the cherry on top. BEAUTIFUL rooms, grounds, facilities, & staff! Kamal, at the Chimney restaurant, was very friendly, profesional, and attentive!

Our stay was for 2 days from 13th-15th august for 8 person.The reception ppl were quite friendly and assisted us in best possible ways for any request.The room service was beyond expectations and would def refer them for ppl visiting kathmandu.

We stayed for 1 night. We had a great time. The environment is very peaceful. The food was great. The room was spacious and had all the facilities. The Interior of the hotel was classic and remind us of the old times.

We were initially confused about where to stay in Kathmandu during our trip to Nepal. The options were Hyatt, Dwarika and Yak&Yeti. The modern city-type rooms of Hyatt with no local decor and no heritage tag did not excite me. Dwarika seemed better, but seemed like a very compact resort. The lush green lawns and the heritage of Yak & Yeti led me to this property finally. And must I say that I've never been happier with my decision, which was spot on !!The property is a fabulous 5 Star Deluxe resort located in the heart of Kathmandu. Very close to the happening area Thamel and located on the high street with plenty of superb clubs and shopping all around, it was a delight being there ! It has the distinction of being Kathmandu's first 5 Star Hotel and retains that heritage even today with its lovely Nepalese Darbar decor. With heritage artefacts and so much of history all around, you are actually staying in a grand palace. I happened to see their convention halls and was simply stunned with the magnificent murals, the paintings, artefacts and the decor ! We chose to book a package called 'Tour de Kathmandu' which also included dinner sightseeing directly from their site. And we really felt it was super value for money. The check-in was smooth and we were escorted to our lovely room overlooking the mesmerizing gardens !! The room was very comfortable and spotlessly clean with a large LED TV ! The hotel has 2 wings and both seemed equally great to stay at. There is also a large lawn tennis court and a terrific spa !! The best part of the hotel is its lovely garden. It's like an oasis in the middle of the city. There's a lovely Buddha temple, a pond with fishes and ducks and it's simply unbelievable !! I've never seen a lawn so well landscaped and manicured. It was always a delight to walk there after every meal or in the mornings.  The service at both the restaurants (Chimney and Spice Room) was top notch ! I particularly fell in love with the ambience of Chimney Restaurant which was so cosy !! Special thanks to Mr. Rojesh for his warm service and his chefs Mandeep Singh, Jitendra and Prabhat who made some fabulous dishes, especially the deserts (Baked Alaska, Bailey's Rasmalai etc.) !! The Travel Desk also was very efficient and is highly recommended to book through them. I felt they were really very reasonable. Special thanks to Mr Raju9860971021 who arranged everything so well !! The artefacts shop in the hotel was also quite good and surprisingly affordable (infact cheaper than Thamel) which is often not the case.Finally, hats off to the special lady - the General Manager of the resort Ms. Monica Scheiblauer who truly deserves a standing ovation for managing the resort impeccably. She is truly a very charming lady ! Very warm and hospitable, I always saw her at talking to guests personally ensuring their comfort. Unlike other GMs who are mostly confined to their cabins, she was everywhere taking care of every minute detail !! A special thanks to her assistant Mr Sumit Bhandari also who was very hospitable and courteous. Overall, it was one of our finest stays ever and we left with a heavy heart leaving a piece of ourselves there ! Highly recommended..just close your eyes and book !! Can't wait to be back again !!

I had an amazing experience.  I had inadvertently left my cell phone at a nearby ATM machine.  By the time I had realized it missing I returned to the place and of course the phone wasn’t there anymore. I had given up on it and made all arrangements to suspend services to my cell phone. Nonetheless I decided to go to the concierge to ask for help the next day which was a holiday.  They said to return the next day and would accompany me to the bank to ask if someone had returned it.  The next day I went to the concierge again and they said they had already inquired and found my phone. Apparently the next person who went into the ATM booth happened to be a hotel employee. He left a note to the bank (as it had already closed for the weekend) and told them that if anyone had lost a phone to have them call him at home. So when the hotel concierge enquired on my behalf they found out that one of their own employees had found my phone.  What I appreciated was that they went out of their way to help and thank goodness for an honest employee who did what he did.  All’s well that ends well. I commended the employee to the GM who was very appreciative that this had happened and hopefully rewarded the employee as well. The employee meanwhile became my Facebook friend. Go Hotel Yak & Yeti!

Almost everything is super bland, but that's becoming common everywhere. 4 star ambiance, 1 star paper napkins, 2 star food, 1 star self-awarenessI've been eating at the dinner buffet for 30 years off and on.

You gave me a peaceful experience in a country I have never been to. I enjoyed the food, drinks, hospitality, weather and general reception. Thank you very much. May be one time, when I return to Kathmandu, Yak & Yeti is my preferred choice. NOAH MUSOKE from Uganda

An excellent property within the City, well placed location. Being amist proper City location, the Entrace Exit gates aren't pleasent to feel great.Hospitality + Service befitting a 5 Star Property. Travel / Car is damm costly, including Airport Pick up. This needs to be rationalised. Room Service is prompt + impressive presentation of all add ons Guest can car for with the ordered Food / Drinks. Casino is however independent of the Hotel. Morning / Evening time pathway for Walks is Feel Good.

I had stayed in the hotel in May 2017. The place was really neat clean and well maintained. The staff service and hospitality was just amazing. Little did I feel away from home and had Nepalese hospitality to enjoy.The rooms were neat, tidy and regular cleaning was done promptly. The breakfast was really good and had a huge spread to indulge in. However, the Hotel wifi speed was slow.Overall, whenever I go back to Kathmandu, Hotel Yak and Yeti would be on my list.

We spent a few days at the iconic Yak and Yeti recovering in May. The facilities are everything you would expect from a hotel of this standard. Our room was comfortable and clean and quiet, the staff were helpful and courteous, the restaurant is good and serves a satisfactory breakfast.The gardens are lovely and the outdoor pool was a bonus.it lost a star because the decor is beginning to look a little tired in places and the shower in our room was poor.

We stayed at Yak & Yeti before and after our Everest trip. The rooms are spacious, clean and comfortable. There is a nice pool area to relax during the day that is surrounded by a green garden area (which was much appreciated after 2 months in the Khumbu Valley!). The restaurant has a delicious buffet that is good for any meal of the day. Next door there is a spa where we had massages and a pedicure after our trip. They offer basic services such as haircuts as well. The hotel is also located off the main roadway in Thamel which is a nice break from the chaos. I would recommend this hotel to anyone traveling in Kathmandu. Coming from the US, this is not 5 star, but for Nepal, I would definitely rate 5 star.

Was booked into this hotel by my travel agent. Despite being a five star, hot lukewarm (not hot) water in shower. Aircon barely functional does not cool room effectively. Fixtures and fittings dated. When taking shower in the bathtub (no other option), water does not drain properly . No mini fridge in room. No cookies or fruit either. No free WiFi!! Breakfast spread inadequate, not enough choices. In short, a 5 star hotel of 1990 vintage which would not pass for a 3 star today.I saw many similar reviews on tripadvisor, which elicit the same standard response from Monika someone. Basically they say1) Thank you for your feedback2) sorry for the problem faced3) we are 5 star and customer satisfaction is important to us4) we will fix the problemI suspect this review will meet the same fate. The problem cannot be fixed with the hotels ageing infrastructure. I complained on the phone and to the duty manager Mr Harsha but to no avail.Had prepaid, no option of cancellation or refund so stayed put for 2 days, no choice.Will not return. avoid.

We only stayed for 2 nights, but I was a little disappointed that the hotel doesn’t look as grand as per photos. Hotel guests are staying in a newer part of hotel that feels a bit dark and lacks many original features. Room was spacious and comfortable. An older part of hotel was beautiful and had a great heritage ambiance, but it is mainly used for casino, conference and event rooms and Chimney restaurant. We had a delicious lunch and dinner in a Chimney restaurant.

The hotel is beautiful with a luxurious swimming pool and gardens.  When I visited an Indian wedding was in full swing...an extra treat!  I wanted to go to the Chimney Restaurant and order the beet borscht as I'd read about the fascinating White Russian Boris Lissanevitch in Lonely Pplanet.  Quote from Lonely Planet: "He was a friend of Ingrid Bergman, ballet dancer, chef, tiger hunter, fighter pilot, Shanghai club owner and trapese artist"   His first hotel is now the Yak & Yeti.  Beautiful.  I just went for lunch but it was fun and enjoyable none-the-less.

I stayed here for a total of five non-consecutive nights within a two-week span and was happy with the overall experience. The hotel has a lot of character and attracts a diverse crowd. It was fun for me to people-watch the combination of trekkers, tour groups and business travelers coming and going in this busy hotel. The hospitality was top-notch and staff were gracious at every turn. I had dinner one night at The Chimney which was delicious-lunch at the bar x 1 (nice selection/casual) and enjoyed the breakfast buffet every morning. The rooms could use an update, but were comfortable. The bathrooms were awkward and cramped and I ended up flooding the place a few times when I took a shower. All in all I felt very comfortable staying here and would return without hesitation  in the future.

We are coming for business  purpose and we enjoying our stay here.. staff are very helpful, especially  Sabina, she  help us with the many queries. Centrally  located  easy to get nearest  market. Food are very tasty..

A very good and nice hotel in which I'll definitely come back. The room is nice and affordable. The service is good especially a concierge named sabita,who was very helpful and spoke perfect English, and I enjoyed the food very much.

Yak and Yeti is a very nice hotel. Rooms are clean and comfortable. The restaurant is very recommended, both with buffet and a la carte, and breakfast is very complete. The staff stands out for being gentile.

Having first visited the hotel in 1980, I was curious to see what it was like now. When I told the restaurant staff that I was revisiting, firstly, they were so surprised, but then welcomed me as if I was a long lost friend. My husband and I were treated like royalty with exceptional attention afforded us in the way of a tasty little starter specially made for us whilst we waited for our order and a welcome back chocolate cake before we left. All the wait staff came as a group to welcome me back. We felt very special! The food was excellent and the service outstanding. We live in Kathmandu at the moment and will definitely be returning for more meals. I highly recommend a visit to this very special hotel.

I stayed at Hotel Yak & Yeti before and after my trek to Mt. Everest Base Camp. The staff were very friendly and helpful and the grounds of the hotel are beautiful. There was a pretty sunrise from my window each morning.The food in the restaurant was great; there are lots of choices at the breakfast buffet. There are also shops and restaurants not far from the hotel.

We stayed 5 days in this hotel at the end of February 2019, it was difficult to have good night sleep as the rooms were too hot, the central heater was still on. They offered us fans but they were too old and too noisy. The rooms are clean, the matress too soft. Internet is not free 10 dollars for 24 hours, this is the only hotel in Kathmandu without internet included which is not acceptable for a 5 stars. The buffet is good and offer a lot of variety nevertheless nothing for milk intolerant. We requested substitute of milk, they brought soy milk for our second breakfast. The employees are helpful and friendly. There is probably better option for the same price in Kathmandu.

I came for a conference and found the staff at the business center very friendly and helpful. We had to do some last minute conference room arrangement and printing and the staff attended to us swiftly and made things happen. Definitely recommend!

Namaste! Perfect hospitality and clean rooms. Great conference facility and support. Sabina and Sabita were great. Very friendly ladies. The food was superb. Proximity to town airport is convenient. Excellent choice of hotel for a perfect destination.

Good place for families.  Beautiful property. Good breakfast.  But the restaurant food is overpriced.  Rooms are small for the price paid. The hotel is at the heart of the city. Easy access to many restaurants and shops.

Happy with the hotel. The room has very distinct Nepalese elements. The back yard is very peaceful with impressive design. It is very beautiful. The food from the restaurant is not bad. I am particularly  happy with the service from Sabita at the lobby

Staff is friendly and responsive to all requests. The room is well appointed and very clean. The air conditioning was not very effective and despite our complaints, the problem was not resolved. We had to open the windows to cool the room.Other than the air conditioner issue, we were very pleased with the hotel and location. Good shopping and restaurants are really close by . The pool and gardens are lovely as well.

We spent two separate nights here, one before our Annapurna trek and one after. This is a large hotel complex that boasts 270 rooms and all the amenities you’d expect in a 5-star hotel. Our first night stay was somewhat disappointing. Several outlets in the room didn’t work (in fact one shorted when we plugged in a phone charger) and the bathroom shower grout appeared to have mold. The front desk graciously provided a complimentary upgrade to the Club floor when we returned (although they were quick to add we couldn’t enjoy the Club level amenities, only the room was being upgraded). Much better! Given the age of the hotel, clearly rooms are in various stages of renovation. The grounds are lovely, so make sure you request a room with garden views. No complaints about the bountiful breakfast buffet offering numerous American choices. Served in the Sunrise Restaurant overlooking the gardens and pool, it’s the perfect start to the day.
