Drinks in the Piano Bar and dinner in the Chimney Restaurant are the perfect way to end the day. We ate here both nights. Service was attentive, friendly and the atmosphere cozy and charming. Overall, we looked forward to returning to the hotel after the busy chaotic streets of Kathmandu.

We are in a tour of India and Nepal. We’re looking for a more euRopean hotel witH high grades for cleanliness and service.  This is it.  The breakfast buffet was wonderful and the European style restaurant chimney great

We 4 friends were travelling to Kathmandu and Pokhara in september 2018. One of our friend in Kathmandu suggested us to stay in this hotel. This is a beautiful hotel with lots of open areas to walk and relax with beautifully kept garden with ponds etc.Stay was very comfortable.Friendly and attentive staff ,eager to help. This hotel is located centrally and situated in walkable distance from Themal, the maket place which is always happening.Food is good too and complimentary breakfast spread is awesome.we enjoyed our stay here.

This hotel was recommended to me by a friend who travels to Nepal frequently. The staff are great, they helped in all sorts of ways for the week I was there. There is a nice breakfast and a great lunch if you happen to be eating in the hotel. The Chimney Bar is also very nice.

After an incredible adventure in India, we were beyond excited to visit the magic of Nepal.  And what a beginning when we arrived at Hotel Yak and Yeti!  A sumptuous lobby with nooks and art and statuary and beaming and gracious staff.  Our room was spacious and beautifully furnished - the nepalise lattice work extraordinary.  Our bathroom had nice amenities and oh so hot water after a long and dusty day.  We visited the bar every late afternoon to share our day and relive all that we experienced, and enjoy a libation !  And we weren't the only ones - so many happy travelers and trekkers and businessmen doing the same.  Now, the breakfast! !!!  Where to start !  An enormous buffet with everything you could imagine. Regional and Indian,  western, and Asian.  The most heavenly croissants, rich and aromatic coffee, and my favorite, Mongolian meatballs over basmati rice.  The food choices changed daily which made it fun.  We also enjoyed lattes in the garden around a water feature, peace pagoda, exquisite flowers, and a most adorable family of ducks.  And for shoppers, there are the most wonderful shops right across the street.  We found Nepal crafted folkart, felted jewelry and slippers (mine are sacred cows), textiles, very original tees, and leather.  The shop keepers were so delightful and helpful, with NO PRESSURE.  After we toured Nepal, we returned to the Y&Y for another stay before we returned home.   But we already felt at 'home' the minute we crossed into the beautiful and welcoming lobby.  Nameste.

I have stayed at Yak and Yeti five times in 2018 , and last week as well. There are many things about this hotel that keep bringing me back to it. The hotel is spread over a large area, with a huge garden, a beautiful pond with ducks , many restaurants, a coffee shop, a casino and many , many rooms. Though its a big hotel with all modern amenities, it still retains the charm of a heritage hotel with extremely warm staff. I think the staff they have is their highlight : always smiling and ready to help. I would particularly like to mention Goma (from the sunrise restaurant) for her efficient service. She is always smiling and strikes up a good conversation over breakfast. Always good to see her at breakfast. Also, Ms. Anu and Mr. Netra from the front desk are always helpful. Pratima and Benju from the Travel desk are extremely efficient and helpful as well. Overall, a great property, and I guess I will stay this year as well at least 5-6 times. Keep it up Team Yak and Yeti !

Great location, wonderful staff.   But.    The gym is hidden deep underground which is so 1980s.    That said, if you need 5 star service, I'd highly recommend this hotel.   Note, I travel for business 14 weeks per year.    Stayed at the Y&Y 10 years ago, and glad I made a return visit.   If your budget allows, stay on the Executive Floor;  well worth the extra cost.   Again, amazing service.  Peter

My stay in this hotel was very comfortable and pleasant.I have been assisted in all time in excellent way by Miss Sabita.The restaurant allows you to chose among many different foods both nepali and international types.The staff people are very kind satisfying all needs of the costumers and assisting in them in solving all their problems.

Beautiful hotel, in a central location of Kathmandu, with very kind personnel, in particular at the reception and at the restaurant. The private garden behind the hotel is a plus.  It's always a pleasure to be here, even for business.

Though there are many properties around Kathmandu, honestly this one is the best one to stay at. Given it is a heritage property, the spacious lobby and outdoor is not match for many properties across. Though they have two separate wings, I would suggest to stay in the heritage wing due to the pool view. However, I stayed in the other wing because of the cost factor which isn't much but if you are going to stay for more than a week then do consider it. Friendly staff and very prompt. They do have several power outage (less than 2 mins) and have two restaurants, although The Chimney is my favorite.

My two-week stay at Yak and Tak was excellent. The guest services manager, Sharmila  and the restaurant manager, Bindu,  as well as all the staff from the housekeeping, maintenance, restaurant, door service, and  front desk provided warm, welcoming and professional assistance at all times.  Any little problems I had with the TV were addressed immediately.  The hotel is beautifully maintained and a very enjoyable getaway,  I hope I can return and highly recommend it.

I am staying in hotel yak and yeti a very good hotel with excellent room. Food is very good here and all the staff are friendly... Main things of hotel is garden side. and the lady in front desk Ms Sabita is very nice and kindand always ready to help with smile.

Nice hotel for where it is.  On the front end of our Ebc trek we were overwhelmed with everything and the staff was very friendly and helpful.Same on the back end as we had a little more time to explore.  The rooms are plain but work fine for what you needThe staff and the dining facilities are very good.  We had no problems.  We also tried the spa after our trek and would highly recommend this

Ms sabita very kind and helpful-and room is very good & restaurant nice!many kind of food & taste was very good!all staff are very helpful we enjoyed stay over in hotel yak and yeti and we will be back again

The  stay at yak and yeti always goes very well. The entire team is very friendly and helpful. The food is excellent and the room is very clean and comfortable . Sharmila  from the guest relation team is very good .

We stayed at the Yak and Yeti for six nights.  During that time, the staff could not have been more helpful, attentive, or welcoming.  They were truly fantastic.  It made us relax a bit more in a city that is so different and so far away from home.  The hotel is a 15 minute walk from the old city section of Thamel, a 5-10 minute taxi ride from Durbar Square, and a 15 minute taxi ride to the Boudhanath Stupa or the airport.  The hotel is a bit threadbare at this point, but the service and hospitality more than make up for it.   Furthermore, it is spotless, and the breakfast is good too.  We felt incredibly comfortable here.

My husband and I spent four nights at the Hotel Yak & Yeti on two separate occasions in November, 2018.  We found the hotel to be surprisingly charming, attractive, quiet, and welcoming for all of its large size.  Well situated in Kathmandu, the hotel features a beautiful garden with swimming pool, a pavilion, and lots of blooms behind it.  Next door to a Casino, the hotel boasts an excellent bar and an outstanding restaurant for breakfast or any other meal with good food and an amazingly good and reasonably priced buffetHotel staff were very accommodating, gracious, generous, and pleasant.  The hotel offers an outstanding currency exchange at the front desk, good laundry service, a good baggage check service which we were delighted to use, and a variety of attractive small shops selling local luxury items from cashmere to sculptures and jewelry.  The currency exchange rates were better than the local bank rates.Our first room was huge, with plenty of space for our month's travels worth of luggage, a large desk with writing tools, two huge comfortable beds, a gigantic closet with lots of hangers, a safe, a refrigerator, free bottles of water, excellent WIFI, a big tv with local cable, and an excellent bath with a huge shower, beauty supplies and soap, and everything else we could need.  The room had huge ceiling to floor picture windows overlooking the front of the hotel with blinds and curtains, plus wonderful padded bench seating underneath it for holding your luggage and gazing at the world.My favorite feature of our first room was the beautify local carvings on all the walls, beams, furniture, and features in the room.  The carving showed flowers, plants, animals, and traditional Nepalese people.  it was as if we were actually staying in a lovely museum hall.We were very happy to have had the chance to spend four nights at this charming and elegant hotel.  When we go back to Nepal, we look forward to staying here again.  We highly recommend this hotel.

Not so modern, but the room is very big, and the decoration is very unique with local elements, with parking lot free for guests. Also near to the Kingdom Palace. One quiet garden is behind with nice swimming pool, and plenty of plants. Morning I could hear the live song from Magpie Robin at the garden. There is some casino is just at next door, one big screen at the Bar, good see some football game. The breakfast is good, and the staff very kind

After a 15 day journey through India and Nepal we were more than ready for a little  luxury and our wish came true at Yak and Yeti... a warm greeting and staff determined to meet every need!A big Ahhhh as we snuggled into our comfy bed after a gourmet meal served with great attention!Couldn’t ask for more!Thank you YNY!

Staff is very courteous. Specially The desk lady named Sabita guided us well being on family outing.We are very happy to came again here .Happy to come again with family. Food is very delicious. Service is fine enough.

The Himalayan city cradled in the lap of nature and its bounty just is breathtaking. And never to miss the trips to THAMEL and PATAN ( The Hare Rama Hare Krishna mivie effect  never really went from me ) ...and I also enjoyed the trip to see Mt EVerest at close quarters with the early morning YETI flight .....which is certainly not to be missed

Within 2018 I was traveling to Kathmandu 4 times, each time I was staying with my team at Yak & Yeti Hotel. In my opinion the best place for stay in Kathmandu. Very comfortable and clean, located very close to the city center where you can find pubs and restaurants. Hotel Complex is souranded by garden what makes visitors feel peacfull, out of the heavy traffic jam. Hotel staff was always supportive and polite. All the best to Yak & Yeti personel !

What a terrific place! First time visiting Nepal, and was invited for lunch by some old friends that I have not seen in a very long time. We had a wonderful experience and my taste buds were left with a feeling of pleasure. The staff was very helping and accommodating. Thank you for the harmonious experience

Had a great time at the Restuarant. Manager Bindu and team were very helpful and friendly.Food was great as usual.Went with family for 7+ for lunch. We all had the buffet.Big thanks for accommodating for our grandmother who was in a wheelchair!

Been a regular visitor to this property for last 12 years now - I do a monthly trip here - to meet friends . Kathmandu is 1hr away from delhi (home bass) It’s a wonderful get away for the weekend. The hotel yak and yeti has been only partner in these years. Great location , huge lawns , heritage look with Morden facilities. The staff here is homely , respectful and they all have keep great friends now . Warm and humble always . If In Kathmandu yak and yeti is a must stay . Aditya khatri New Delhi India

Probably one of the older ones maintained reasonably well,  nice and courteous staff.  Rooms were neat and clean and they also have a casino.  Buffet breakfast was good spread. Located off Durbar road nearby markets Thamel and asan .

Nice by its name, decent staff members.Expert in their work but management need more attention, putting forward hidden cost plus adding the value for more money no good aT ALL.Room interiors okay as per charges and what they claim.old interiors and poor management.

We reached Kathmandu airport at around 11 am on 8th DEC 2018. We got hold of a taxi driver / owner Mr Ganesh. Tel : local no 98416 73473. very professional person knowing Hindi, Nepali & little English. WE hired him for all Kathmandu sight seeing & Travel to Pokhara & Pokhara Sightseeing. We recomend this Taxi for economical .Now comig back to Yak & Yeti hotel: The positives: location is good , right on the Darbar Marg, Thamel is about 15 minutes walking distance. The rooms are specious, good WiFi connectivity. Excellent & tasty breakfast spread. The negatives: overpriced , The shower water spills outside bathroom, wrong design of shower room. The wooden windows are not airtight & cold wind comes inside room.

Yak and Yeti has excellent staff specially in the restaurant. They made my stay comfortable. It’s like home away from home. Good amenities and beautiful garden. I will miss you Pindu, Gina, Barrie,Sunil and Bed from the restaurant and Reeta from housekeeping. Until next trip♥️🌼

Had the pleasure of staying at Yak and Yeti while in Kathmandu on business.I stayed on the fourth floor which gave me access to the lounge where every evening a gorgeous man would pour me a glass of wine and ask about my day.The rooms are well appointed and the beds are very comfortable. It’s only a ten minute walk into Thamel for shopping fun and there are always taxis outside the gates.Only down side would be the light in the bathroom. I don’t know how many hotelsForget that women need good light for their makeup.Apart from that will stay again

This is a classic 5star old style hotel, with charm, elegance and something different.  The look and feel of the places is wonderful; that being said it has a few issues, all of which are cosmetic and small in comparison.  The service offered was second to non, the food was high quality, and the services within the hotel were well delivered.  A colleague found the spar to be of low quality, with staff ill trained and prepared; the gym was small but adequate, the equipment was newish and serviceable.The hotel grounds were well maintained and spacious for the middle of a city.  Minor issues were found in terms of poorly working air conditioning units and a badly chipped dish on the bathroom counter top; it just needed to be thrown away and a new one in its place.  In places tiles were chipped, although I did notice that maintenance were always busy repairing and running replacing bricks and tiles right across the hotel.All,in all a great day, I would come back again, and the staff and food make the place.

We had a family stay here. Heritage property with excellent service. Very caring team. Staff were helpful. Food and room was equally excellent. Also thanks for the support in arranging for tours nearby. Keep up the good work! 5 stars :)

I recently stayed at the Hotel Yak and Yeti after trekking to Everest Base Camp. After such a tough trek it was revitalizing to stay in a quality Hotel who provided helpful and friendly service. We are now refreshed and ready for our trip home.

A really enjoyable stay with all the comforts. Were looked after very well. Enjoyed the Nepali food and hospitality of staff. The bar facilities and dining facilities were also very satisfactory. The arrangements at the meeting rooms and behaviour of staff was also comendable

I appreciate the service at Yak and Yeti hotel. I enjoy staying here...the food is good ...the hospitality. It was an amazing stay at yak and yeti. Conference hall was very good with the beautifull decorum.

I havr stayed for 5 nights in Yak and Yeti. Excellent location only few minutes to Thamel, the tourist area. Service is great and wifi is fast. One of the few standard service hotel. Thanks to the hotel management.

First I will give a shout out to Sabita and Anamika for being so awesome. The two and the staff know the value in creating the best stay ever.  What made it awesome is they continue to check to make sure all is awesome.  Accommodations were over the top. Second night I was upgraded just because!  Staff is what makes this place the best!

Very friendly staff, specifically sabita, great hotel and restaurant for a reasonable priceThe food was great, the room was nice, with warm hot water, and always clean, the internet worked and the grounds were welcoming, I felt safe and welcomed

We stayed at Hyatt on the way in and the Yak and Yeti after our EBC trek. Yak and Yeti was nicer and friendly and good character as a historic hotel. Breakfast buffet was good and the kids liked the room service as well as they relaxed after the trek. Easy to get over to Thamel for shopping and dinning.

The location of the hotel is among the best in Kathmandu, in the heart of Durbar Marg. The property is spread across a large area and has lots of open spaces. The rooms have been renovated and are well equipped. The breakfast spread is pretty good, though probably not as good as at Hyatt Regency.

Meeting sharmila at guest service desk was a delight and very helpful. She is a good PR person. Also enjoyed hotel ambiance and food. Will bring my family next spring season and will definitely stay at the hotel

Located within a 20 minute walk to shopping in Tamal the Hotel Yak & Yeti offers a wide range accommodations designed to fit every pocket book. The staff, from management to doormen, are eager to be helpful and insure your stay is memorable. Room rates include a buffet style breakfast. An evening buffet is also available or you can order ala carte, either way you can't go wrong . . . the food was always fresh and tasty. On premise services are numerous and reasonably priced. The hotel grounds offer a pleasant and relaxing space.

Had a fantastic stay at this oasis of calm among the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu! The staff were friendly and helpful, room was spacious, clean and had a very comfortable bed. The  grounds and garden were beautiful and well kept even had a well attended jazz concert during our stay and everything was packed up and cleared away without disturbing guests. Filled with trekkers and climbers and it wasn't difficult to see why this hotel was so popular being only a 10 min walk from the main tourist area of Thamel. Highly recommend staying here if you are visiting Nepal.

I needed a doctor and the hotel had one on call who came there and took care f me.  I ws impressed!  Rooms were fine.  Main restaurant was OK but buffet not so good.  There is now another restaurant on the premises which is supposed to be better.

My group and I stayed at the Yak & Yeti for a couple nights before and after an Everest Base Camp trek (October/November 2018).  Both times our rooms were in the older part of the hotel, conveniently close to the front desk area and main restaurant. On our first visit, the room had a strong musty smell and we noticed, what appeared to be, mold/mildew residue on the air register.  Given how accommodating the hotel staff was during both our stays, I suspect we could have changed rooms had we complained, which we did not.  Our room on our second visit, after our trek, was again in the older section on the first floor, and still had a bit of a musty smell, but not as bad as the first.  As other reviewers have mentioned, the musty odors might be coming from old carpets that need replacing.  Our beds were very comfortable and we rested comfortably during both our stays.The hotel is conveniently located, and within walking distance, to a variety of businesses and Thamel. A complimentary breakfast buffet was included in our room cost and was excellent, with lots of options to suit a variety of tastes... Not sure why some reviewers thought it was a negative to have too many options?  We found all the hotel staff to be very pleasant and helpful.  Our group was allowed to store our baggage on site, at no cost, while we completed our trek, as well as after checkout on our return while waiting to leave for a late plane departure.  Our baggage was well secured and we had no issues leaving and/or retrieving it.  There are a couple very comfortable lounge/sitting areas where we were able to "hang out" while waiting to leave for the airport. Food/beverage service was available throughout the day while we waited with no pressure to purchase.All in all we had a very pleasant stay at the Yak and Yeti.  The only reason this is not a 5 star review has to do with the musty smell in our rooms.  Should we visit in the future we would ask for rooms in the newer section.

My husband and I stayed at the Yak and Yeti for three nights before heading off to trek. While the building and furnishings are tired and need updating, we were very comfortable. The breakfast is great. The staff were exceptionally friendly and helpful.The hotel is close to the Tamel area and the old Royal Palace with everything an easy walk.We enjoyed our stay. Thank you!

Stayed here for approximately 7 days, some with a group and some solo. The hotel is about a 10 minute walk from Thamel. The rooms are a good size and have all you need. The grounds (garden area) are huge with a  large pond and water feature, complete with hotel ducks wondering around. A really wonderful escape from the hustle and bustle of the streets of Kathmandu. Also ate at the newly reopened Chimney Restaurant...had the Salmon and it was delicious. The hotel also allowed me to leave luggage in their storage room for well over a week and at no cost.While I do agree that the hotel could do with a revamp, but this in no way detracts from how wonderful my stay was

We stayed here 3 times in the space of 2+ weeks as part of a tour group.  The first stay was for several days and the next two stays were for a single night.  During our first stay, we had one of the newer rooms which was comfortable, overlooked the courtyard and was quiet.  The second stay was in the older section of the hotel (where the club rooms are located) and that room had seen far better days.  The carpet was very old and the room smelled musty (most likely from the carpet).  The furniture was dated  with dings and nicks prevalent.  The pigeon poop on the railing outside the window was pretty gross.  I also didn't care for the fact that I needed to kill a roach in the bathroom.  On our last trip, we saw exterminators at work in the hallways so maybe that issue has been resolved.  Our third stay was again in the newer part of the hotel so the room was decent.  While there are thermostats in each room, it appears that there is a pre-set cooling temperature which you cannot make any cooler.  Breakfast is included and maybe tries to cater to too wide a range of guests.  There was always a mixed bag of some western type foods and some Nepali type foods. No matter what time we showed up for breakfast, the "hot" food was at best lukewarm.  I saw that there were burners underneath the chafing dishes, but perhaps they were not lit.  Although the coffee was great each morning.  The most stressful part of our trip was when we returned to the hotel after a week in Bhutan.  We had left a bag at the hotel along with many others of our tour group.  On our return, our bag was not part of the returned luggage.  Our concerns were met with, "I'm sure someone from your tour group took your bag."   Even if the bag was sent to a room by mistake, no doubt it would have been returned.  We asked if we could help look for the bag as clearly the hotel didn't have a clue.  We were led to several different storage rooms all to no avail.  The bellman who was helping us said there was one more room we could check.  We found the bag.  The "tour" tag had been taken off or fell off.  What really angered us was when the bellman helping look for the bag said, oh, that bag had been there since our tour group checked in and was never claimed on our original arrival.  Given the bag we left at the hotel, was an extra bag that we brought along so we could leave things at the hotel meant it was impossible for the bag to have been there from the beginning.

We ended up staying here by surprise (the surprise is a much longer, and slightly embarrassing story). The service was exquisite, from the moment that we arrived. This was the perfect way to spend our final 24 hours in Nepal. After trekking and staying in much less comfortable accommodations, we enjoyed the plush linens, well-appointed room, great shower and amenities, wonderful breakfast and dinner buffets and great cocktails. The pool and outdoor landscaping and divine and the downstairs spa offered a delightful surprise: a eucalyptus steam room. Our group of 4 was so pleased with the surprise pampering we received at Yak & Yeti. The staff provided service that is on par with any luxury hotel in the world. I will definitely stay here again at the end (and maybe also the beginning) of my next trip to Nepal.

The hotel is very old built perhaps in the 70’s. Buts right in the heart of the city and one of the few with gardens. The food is good and the staff very friendly. It’s an old style hotel but needs a bit of renovation in the bathrooms etc but still very good

Love this place returning again from a year ago it’s like walking into a bar where everyone knows your name Also used Vespa valley for a trip search for them on google really great firm to use The guide I always use for city trips I use Uttara most excellent through himex

Not the sort of hotel I normally stay in but two nights either end of a trek were part of the package. I imagine once upon a time this was a magical place. Sadly it is now lack lustre and many areas need attention. My bathroom had been semi-renovated but the creaky stained bath, cracked tiles and rusted faucet did it no favours. My bedroom door lock failed and this took a long time to sort out. Bedroom carpet stained and furniture needing updating. Fridge was empty despite the list of drinks on offer. The staff I must stress were delightful. Helpful and courteous. All of them. No tonic to go with gin in the bar!  Internet (charged daily) is very erratic. Very busy hotel full of tourists which is great for the hotel and Kathmandu but if you like smaller, more relaxed accommodation I’d suggest looking elsewhere.

I was really looking forward to staying here but it was very disappointing, we booked for the regular rooms and they were very old, with the dirtiest carpet I've seen in a long time and the bathrooms were only just bearable.  The breakfast buffet had very little choice and poor quality food, however the staff were very friendly.The only plus for this Hotel is the location - walking distance to some great bars & restaurants. Sorry but I wouldn't recommend this Hotel at all!

stayed for an extra 3 nights at the end of our tour, grand hotel in the middle of kathmandu but very quiet location, nice room as you would expect from this type of hotel, breakfast was ok but quite limited in choice, ordering poached eggs was a struggle and we ended up with fried instead, ran out of orange juice but no one seemed bothered to top it up even after asking for it twice to be done, one issue was wifi, although not a major problem this was the only hotel that charged for it and at quite a price. the transfer to the airport was also very expensive for the amount of time it took, it seems that the hotel think they can charge you high prices because you appear to have money to stay here. not disappointed but also not happy

This hotel was very disappointing. It’s expensive but not at all worth it. The air conditioning doesn’t work. They are renovating so there is a constant sound of drilling. The rooms are very average. Bathrooms not great. The staff are friendly but the service is not good.

This once grand hotel is now a lacklustre shadow of its former glory days and I say that as someone who visited the hotel regularly when I was a Kathmandu resident 20 years ago and on the basis of 3 recent visits. It could, and should, be so much more.It is true that some of the rooms have been renovated, but it is very much the luck of the draw as to which you are allocated on arrival. Many of the bedrooms are tired, with insufficient electrical sockets to charge the plethora of gadgets and accessories that most of us travel with nowadays and the lighting and fixtures are poor, particularly in the bathrooms. On the positive side the staff are good ambassadors and the beds very comfortable. Also, the bar can be fun, albeit very noisy if a big tour or trek have descended on the hotel and the food is also of a good quality, but both the bar and restaurant are ridiculously overpriced. If you have the time and inclination you should look further afield for a night out if staying at this hotel; you won't regret it.

This was my 7th visit to Kathmandu and thought I would stay at Yak & Yeti for a change as I usually stay at the Radisson. Firstly the location is great with some fantastic restaurants nearby. The problem starts with the unfriendly reception staff. Having flown in from Australia and being extremely tired, a pleasant smile would have gone down a treat, not an abrupt request for my passport. This also was my husband's  check out experience with no thank you for staying at the hotel. If you are looking for a delicious breakfast well you may be disappointed as the hot selection was miediocre.  With the number of 5 and 4 star hotels being built in Kathmandu I would hope the management of the Yak and Yeti address these problems.On the plus side, the gardens are lovely as were the majority of the staff.

When you google this hotel, you get the sort of British Raj splendid building, but this is not where you are going to stay. It is worth paying USD 20 extra to get in the so-called heritage rooms which at least give a glimpse of Nepalese style. Rooms are ok, breakfast is passable but the hotel is over-rated. I guess the current rating of 7,8 is just about right..The best thing is a nice large garden.

My son and I stayed at the Yak and Yeti during our recent trip to Nepal. The accommodations were very nice. Our room had two full size beds with a view of the back garden area. It was also equipped with a stocked mini-fridge, coffee maker, and just about everything else we needed. While at the hotel we also visited the buffet a few times. The buffet had pretty much the same food options every time we went. It would have benefited from more variety. The staff was very friendly. Wifi was slow like most hotels in Kathmandu but we were able to get online to check email and connect with family at home. We would definitely stay here again.

We arrived back from 10 days of trekking and found this hotel online and booked a room.We were very impressed with the service, staff, hotel room and Spa. At check-in , a staff member walked us to our room and showed us the room features. The buffet for lunch and dinner was incredible!! Highly recommend eating there. The property was tucked away and very secure. The best part was you could not hear any of the hustle and bustle of Khatmandu. It’s about a 10-15 minute walk to the Thamel District. Highly recommend the Spa and Massage!!We received a nice gift in our room which was a nice little touch. The airport shuttle was very nice and got us to the airport on time the next morning. Overall, exceptional property and stay!!

Kathmandu is a crowded, overpopulated, dirty city. People are wonderful and most all trekking in eastern Nepal starts with a flight from Kathmandu to Lukla.  Nice clean rooms and bathrooms.  Really great buffet 3 meals a day. Peaceful courtyard and grounds with pool.  Good location for walking to nearby shopping area of Thamel.

Very nice hotel catering to western visitors. Friendly staff, particularly Rashmi Ghimire - a hostess in the restaurant and Damador, the chef who went out of his way to make sure guests are content with their meal.

This although may not be the fanciest, is a very cozy hotel. Good sized rooms and what is great is the fact that the location is good and convenient. The staff is helpful and perhaps the only let down was the fact there there was no wifi connectivity. Which in all honesty did not matter.

This hotel is very well laid out and the rooms are a good size and well maintained.  Housekeeping is good.  Staff is helpful.  The food in the Chimney Restaurant is excellent.  Lots of choices even for a picky eater.  Only thing that upset me was that though they say free wifi, that is not the case.  I was part of a group that was travelling to Mt. Kailash and we had to pay for the wifi while some other group that was in the hotel at the same time and going to Kailash as well had it for free.

We stayed one night here. Food in the bar was mediocre and the hotel room was very tired. Sheets were stained. Few towels and sporadic hot water. The wifi was spotty. This is supposed to be the best hotel in Kathmandu.  I would not want to stay at the others.

The setting and ambience was stunning. I loved the garden area and the breakfast was great too.My only 2 complaints are:1. No complimentary Wi-Fi not even in the lobby. Wi-Fi is very expensive2. Rooms were really smelling bad.Otherwise we had a good experience. The hotel as such is beautiful.

The hotel has a historic feel. But the facilities are also dated and jaded. The maintenance of the infra not great.The good thing is that it is centrally located and easily. The staff was reasonable. The rooms were large.

One of the best hotels in Kathmandu because of its location: Location: Very centrally located (~1km from Thamel) but still far off from the hustle bustle of ThamelFood: Breakfast spread is good, food in general is okRoom: Clean and well maintained Service: Decent  enoughFacilities: Pool where they can serve drinks/food etc,

Here are my reasons for the above title;--centrally located--beautiful and colourful gardens together well manicured lawns--extremely polite, courteous and respectful staff--great choice of shops in the arcade--has an amazing heritage PALACE that is being restored--Large Banquet halls that cater to shapes and sizesYes, there are a few negatives but I wish to only focus on the POSITIVES as stated above and below.Now I can go on and on but in my humble opinion, I must say the LEADER of this 40 year old ship is the GENERAL MANAGER, Monika. In my brief meetings with her she came across as a true professional, VERY POLITE in her dealings with ALL GUESTS, really passionate about her position and extremely caring for her "A" team of humble staff. Believe you me, if YOU need to experience 5* hospitality, THIS IS THE HOTEL TO STAY AT.Coming from the land of EDMUND HILARY, I certainly recommend this beauty to my network of friends in New Zealand, Australia and around the globe.Overall--9/10

A large hotel in the centre which appears to cater to the conference trade (why I was there) and the trekking trade. Each morning a bunch of suits head for the breakfast bar whilst a bunch of nervous looking youngsters wait in the lobby to be bused our to the mountains! Decent enough rooms, a little jaded and faded. Food good but expensive. I suspect there are better. Steamy small gym and a pleasant outdoor pool.

We stayed here for 3 nights . This is a 40 year old  5-star heritage hotel located in the city centre of Kathmandu .It is probably one of the best hotels in the city, but be aware that the 5 -star standard here is not the same as other major cities . The landscaping around the hotel grounds is lovely . We frequented the lobby lounge and restaurant every day . The service staff were all very pleasant . The rooms are ok but are showing their age , especially the bathrooms. What was most disappointing was the hotel spa. Promoted visibly upon check-in and in the rooms, the spa is at most a 3 - star standard but priced 5 -star pricing . Upon walking into the spa room, I wanted to cancel my massage . I felt bad for the therapist and reduced it to a 30 min massage . The therapist was good, but the decor ( or lack of ) in the room is a huge embarrassment for a 5 star hotel . When a hotel has a spa on its premises, it must make sure that the spa reflects its standard . I was planning to go to the spa daily until I saw it .The same applies for the beauty salon . I didn't go there as it is also  3 star . I would still recommend the hotel for its location and history . There are shops on the hotel premises and rows of shops outside the hotel . Do drop by the scarf shop in the hotel On the lobby level . Having visited many pashmina / cashmere shops in Kathmandu , this hotel shop offers best value and a variety of scarves of various quality . The boss is genuinely friendly and taught us so much !

we were disappointed in the condition of the room of this 5 star hotel. The white headboard was badly stained, and the carpets old. We were also very surprised to be charged for a daily internet charge on checkout. On the positive side the buffet breakfasts were very good. The kitchen did not seem to refill dishes timeously when there was a large group eating at the same time. The baggage storage was a huge bonus as we left them while we had  an 11 day trek. All round it was fairly comfortable but not 5 star standard.

Hotel has a lovely garden and decent outdoor pool. The food was excellent and staff all very friendly and attentive. It is certainly in need of updating in places - the spa area was very old and dated. Hotel was busy during my stay. It seemed to be used by several tour company’s as a meeting place for people and kit so foyer often packed with people and luggage all day. Also hosts business conferences so getting lunch could be tricky if it coincided with conference lunchtime when the restaurant was struggling to seat everyone. Overall a good hotel in good location but perhaps does not live up to the grand photos and expectations of a 5 star hotel.

This hotel was a former palace, and the ambience is lovely. Staff are friendly and the food is excellent. The rooms are pretty, with traditional woodwork. But they look a little tired and slightly run down for a 5 star. The location is also great, close to Thamel.

This is a tired old hotel that is in desperate need of redecorating. I can tell it was nice in its day, but its day has come and gone. It is dated and didn't feel clean. I would look for other options if in the area again.

I don’t see this hotel to be a 5 star hotel.Property is good but not maintained well. Need improvement to meet 5 star expectations. Breakfast menu is pretty much same every alternative days. There was no bathtub in the room. They have desk in the room but no office chair. I was in bathroom and power gone generator took 5-10 min come online. Equipment in the Gym are very old and sticky doesn’t feel good only one ellipticals and which is of no use and very congested gym. No paper in the washroom, sink is getting old.

The rooms are not worth the money spent. Have stayed in all 5 star properties in India and abroad, and these people call their rooms good. I have changed 3 rooms, and its 7pm already and its really pathetic. The hospitality is bad and the management really have a perception of having a good hotel, but trust me its just the pictures which are deceiving. Room 308 has no water to flush, Room 446 is just small and chaotic. Room 336 is rugged and old.Don’t go for this hotel. Just an over priced property with bad rooms and hospitality.

Spent a couple of days here on a quick business trip to KTM.  The Y &Y is an experience, in a good way, if your expectations are not too high.  It is perfectly comfortable and functional, but it does not have all mod cons.  Its in a quiet location and  has some old world style.  The service is pretty average, the garden is nice, as is the pool.

Denied us food in their restaurant even though we had prior booking. We were a group of about 15 couples some of them 60+ year old people and they denied us admission in their restaurant on no reasonable ground. For two hours we waited, yet the hotel staff, lacking complete empathy, did not allow us admission eventually. Their lack of hospitality was appalling. Not recommended at all.

Though it is the oldest hotel ( 40 Years ) but kept in a very good condition. I did suggest to get renovate old block rooms to save lots of money in terms of Electricity and water consumption. Any way staff is very good and behave like owner. Always ready to help with smile and courtesy. May Almighty blessed them all the happiness as they make their guests happy.

Initially the hotel seemed nice - away from the main road and with a garden and clean swimming pool. However when we were first dropped off by the taxi, exhausted from trekking, none of the staff milling about came to help us with our luggage. The bed was comfortable, but the advertised sound-proofing is a lie - the fountain and pump in the garden switch on at 6am and can be heard in the room, as well as people in the hall and in the adjoining room (only separated by a locked door) and their tv that was blaring until 11:30pm. The bathroom was smelly and the shower small - over a bath that was tiny and stained. The breakfast was terrible - too much sugar and stodgy, rubbery, over cooked  food. The spa was awful - inbearably not sauna and steam, and a very rough unprofessional massage that the masseuse talked almost constantly through. Finally, the laundry service damaged my clothing, that was returned to me with holes in it. They refused to accept responsibility, making out like I was trying to mislead them! I’m leaving here feeling ripped off and pissed off - not exactly what you’d hope for from a holiday, especially not when staying in a “5 star” hotel!

The Yak and Yeti rests on its laurels as a 5-star hotel. In reality it's extremely run-down with out of date bathrooms, rooms and most facilities. Staff are nice, but when this is priced as one of the most expensive properties in Kathmandu something's not right. Buffets are extremely marginal, AC is barely functional. Bathrooms feel like they're decades old. If you want real luxury, go to the Hyatt for basically the same price. Or stay at one of the many hotels offering basically the same amenities for a fraction of the price.

The Yak and Yeti is a large hotel in Central Kathmandu just a 15 minutes stroll from the tourist area of Thamel. Very grand when arriving. Beautiful grounds. Friendly and efficient staff. Great buffet breakfast or dinner.Yet it seems to lack character. Perfect for business or conference travellers but for a tourist wanting a unique or different experience, this is not the place. It could be a business hotel in any city of the world. Nothing wrong with the hotel at all but tourists (with reference to the trekking touist) could find other hotels at lower prices with more of a feeling of being in Kathmandu. Am probably being harsh as there is nothing whatsoever wrong with the hotel, the staff or service. All excellent. But once inside, you could be anywhere.

This is the only place to stay in Kathmandu. I’ve been lucky enough to stay here 4 times now. The staff are fantastic, the tranquility of the gardens is wonderful, I love the ducks in the pond that get out to bed safely in their little duck houses every night. I love the historic grand building and the quiet but friendly and efficient service. A peaceful oasis in all the crazy chaos and dust of Kathmandu. Luxury linen and the most comfortable beds make  your stay an unforgettable and relaxing experience. I love this hotel. I highly recommend you stay next time you’re in Kathmandu!

This hotel has almost everything like good location, nice staff, huge property etc but still in my opinion it is slightly overrated and overpriced. Like if you open your room window and there are piegons sitting (it is ok) but if its their home (including toil**) then perhaps it is not so nice :) I was told that the iron station will be provided on request n need basis (that too to me doesn't rate a property 5 star). I couldn't do bench press (bench was not available) at the gym that was a bit disappointment. Overall its a nice and warm place with good food and service - there is a casino as well round the corner and tennis court inside hotel. Don't miss to see a big foot (that locals describe as foot of a Yeti) in the outside area (near pool).

Visited Kathmandu on business tour & stayed in this hotel. The rooms have centralized AC with temperature control switch. Has a flat TV, minibar and all such amenities in the room. Garden facing rooms have excellent view. In all excellent experience.

The location is great - it's quiet, fresh air, and the palace wing looks nice. Breakfast is good both for local food lovers and "bacon&eggs eaters'. Staff is helpful, halls and rooms are clean. Bathroom feels not very well maintained. But the feeling of the place, the atmosphere is still there :-)

I have been travelling to Kathmandu for Business. Have stayed in this hotel more than once. Best thing about this hotel is the Casino. after a long day working you can comfortable relax and unwind at the casino.Food at the hotel is quite good. Buffet is very well laid out with lot of variety to choose from. Overall an amazing experience every time.

I gave this a 4 star because for a country like Nepal I would rate it differently than hotels in the US.   For this country I thought the hotel was decent.  we stayed here 3 different times during our trip.  There were issues with the elevator and when we stayed on a low floor ended up using the stairs a lot.  The room was basically clean.  on our first stay the guy was late picking us up at the airport.  we found another rep and they did apologize once we got to the hotel.  The breakfast was adequate.  They stored our luggage for us in between visits.

Stayed here for 2 nights on a business trip in March after staying further south in the country in Lahan.Can’t praise this hotel enough on every aspect; service, food, rooms, cleanliness and gardens were excellent!I will be back to this lovely country and it’s welcoming people and when I do, I won’t hesitate to stay in the Yak and Yeti.

Yak & Yeti gets a 5-star for its architecture, location, staff and its lovely gardens. A place that resonates elegance and comfort. We booked this hotel last minute during our trip and were skeptical about it first with its name "Yak & Yeti". We stayed in a Nepali architecture room with a lovely private terrace on the 7th floor which overlooked 360 degree of Kathmandu valley surrounded by ancient temples. The most amazing view was the view of UNESCO World Heritage Site, Swayambhunath in the evening from our terrace was truly magnificent.Guest services were very friendly and informative and so were the front desk team. I always felt that the Yak & Yeti staff went out of their way to provide comfort and convenience. Staff at Sunrise restaurant during breakfast were courteous. Delicious array of International cuisine changing everyday at the restaurant was just something we couldn't miss on.The gardens of Yak & Yeti is the most beautiful place you can be in Kathmandu. With geese running on the grounds to the fishes on the large pond in the garden made me feel we were on a far off resort than a city center hotel.The convention center meetings at Yak & Yeti were busy with large conferences during my stay and they served lovely buffet at the poolside garden; which was a gathering of global audience from all over the globe.It took me not more than a minute to get to the downtown street at Durbar marg, which had many good shopping and dining outlets, though I was cautious not to take meals outside the hotel just to be careful with otherwise the hygiene of street side restaurants.This was my first visit to Nepal and I am sure, it will not be the last time. I will surely return back to Nepal with my family next time during a leisure trip and will stay again at the Yak & Yeti; an amazing piece of architecture.

I had an amazing experience staying at the Yak and Yeti. One of the best hospitality that i had experienced. The Property was maintained very well, excellent amenities - Gym/Pool and the garden was the best part .And the staff were ready to go beyond the norms to help make my stay comfortable. Jatin was an absolute call out, he made sure to fulfill my odd-ball requests time and again. Great customer service experience starts with the personal touch!Breakfast and Lunch was great. Really enjoyed the food and made me eat more.Location is great for the stay and everything around feels wonder staying here.Thanks for the wonderful experience. I am sure to come back again and stay!

A beautiful hotel with a lovely garden and swimming pool.  The rooms are clean and spacious.  Great service from all the staff.  A very nice buffet breakfast.  Location is also good. Close to the Ason bazaar.

Hotel Yak and Yeti provided for us a few days of quiet luxury and rejuvenation amidst a hectic holiday in Nepal and Bhutan. The moment we entered we were greeted with cold lemonade and a warm reception. The staff were efficient and generous always doing their best to help in whatever way possible. The rooms are very comfortable and air conditioned. The bathroom was clean. Ask for a garden facing room if possible as the grounds an oasis of green with hundreds of colourful flowers and a small stream with ducks and geese. A tranquil swimming pool is nearby. The meals can be ala carte or there is an excellent buffet for breakfast or dinner. After a few days of hectic travelling it was a very welcome respite.

We found the hotel comfortable and clean. Bathrooms are ideal. Rooms are adequate but very tired and in need of renovation. The staff are exceptionally helpful and pleasant with floor staff coming to see if you need anything at approx 5pm each afternoon - if you are in!Absolutely great location with excellent restaurants nearby.Our first two rooms were in floor 5 had decent views and the air con worked well. We found the restaurants to be excellent with really good choices at all times of day. Of course there are some busy times. Outside you can sit near the grass but the pool area is very overlooked with very few loungers so not a brilliant atmosphere. The flowers in March are exceptional and make the garden look beautiful. On our return to the hotel 5 days later we were give rooms on floor 3 which were not so good. Air con didn’t work, windows seemed a bit dangerous and the view straight onto a roof was a shame.WiFi was free for us and always worked!! Maybe it depends where you are in the complex.Anyone about to book should be aware that you are not going to be staying in the hotel pictured in the main photo, there are two modern blocks attached to this, in fact next door, and you will likely be in here, certainly heritage rooms are in the new parts.

A great place to stay prior to tracking in Nepal. Central to shops, has good restaurants, hairdressers, massage, gym, pool and a lovely out doors area/gardens. Safe to leave your excess bags while tracking. Rooms are spacious and have all the modcons either single or twin share at good prices. If tracking in Nepal I would recommend staying at the Yak and Yeti.

The Yak and Yeti made my stay in Kathmandu very comfortable. First class hotel! Everything is clean and spotless. Wonderful varied buffet breakfast we started our days with. Behind the hotel is their pool which is in a quiet garden setting and nice to relax around. All the staff were very attentive to my needs. For a small amount more, I extended my check out 8 hours longer due to my late flight out.

I recently stayed at Hotel Yak and Yeti for 4 nights. The hotel is very well maintained. It is spread over a huge area and the fact that its this huge a property in the heart of the city (Durbar Marg), is amazing. There are various good places to eat at 2 mins walking distance, and thamel is just a 8-10 min drive by a taxi.The rooms are well kept, the staff is very efficient and very courteous. There is a huge garden , a well kept swimming pool, geese running around the garden and a fountain. Overall, this is an amazing hotel which has modern facilities, a lot of space as well as a nepali touch to it  which is great. The food is good too and the breakfast spread is pretty good. The travel desk is very efficient too. I would definitely be going back to this hotel again and again, and I highly recommend it to everyone.

The building is very nice and quite impressive when you reach the hotel.However the standard rooms are very average, as well as food and serviceGreat location though, being walking distance from Thamel.

This is a large heritage hotel, now celebrating 40 years, but I wouldn't have guessed it to be that old.  Everything looked modern and updated to me.  It is a large hotel, with a surprisingly large lobby and garden area for being in such a busy, crowded, downtown location.  While on the hotel grounds you don't really feel "downtown".  The staff was great, always helpful and friendly.  My room was clean and well appointed.  The restaurant was wonderful, with a lovely breakfast buffet.  It is an easy walk to shopping and restaurants, and not too far a drive to the airport.  Wifi is available for a price.

I like the Yak and Yeti for many reasons:It is set in a very nice large garden;It is located in the heart of the city;It is walking distance from Thamel;It offers a nice entry with a pleasant feel;It has great staff who are very helpful;It has a good “Nepali Feel;”Now the down side-This “modern” hotel seems to date from the late 1970’s and nothing has realty been updated, though in all fairness everything works;The rooms are below the standard size for a 5 Star hotel;The toilets lack sanitary hoses (a must for traveling Asians);There are only three fixtures in the bathroom rooms, and one has to climb into the bathtub to take a shower!The bathroom fittings are out dated!BUT I STILL PREFER THIS HOTEL ABOVE ALL OTHERS

I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at Yak & Yeti this year! The hotel is an oasis amidst the bustling Durbarmarg in Kathmandu city. It is pretty close to the airport and the location is perfect. Team is superb and extremely warm. I stayed here for more than two weeks and every day I felt relaxed and taken care of. You can feel the warmth from the moment you step inside the hotel.  People would sincerely greet and welcome you. Food is delicious. Team is very warm and helpful. Service in the restaurant is by far the most quickest service I have ever come across. This is generally missing in most of the new age swanky hotels, where one feels intimidated. The most enchanting part of the hotel is the gorgeous flower garden and a beautiful pond with fish and ducks swimming around. I could sit there all day :). All in all, a great place to be!!

I was there with my brother and 2 other friends to celebrate his birthday. We arrived at 12:00 AM and stayed up till 04:00 AM ( Friday ). The bar was beautiful with an awesome bartender. I like the hospitality and specially the drinks. Thank you

This is a good hotel for a few days before or after visits outside of Kathmandu, and I would probably be happier with it if I'd stayed in that situation. I've stayed there twice for business, each time for roughly a week, and neither stay was wonderful. The only reason I stayed there the second time is because the nature of my work required it.First, the good - the reception, concierge, and lounge staff go out of their way to be helpful. They tried their best to help me with lost items. Sometimes a shift change would mean messages were lost and I would have to wait a day to get them, but they were sincere in their attempts to help. The garden is beautiful despite the birds, and I do think the location is good if you want to get to many different areas of Kathmandu during your stay. The lunches and dinners I had at the Sunrise restaurant were decent. Now to the not so good. The entire hotel needs to be renovated- bathrooms have mold, there are regular electricity brown-outs (though after the earthquake this is probably not the fault of the hotel), fixtures fall off, and all of the water in brown at all times - do not drink the tap water. They restrict the number of bottles of water and the number of devices on wifi for each room, which is unusual for a luxury hotel. The wifi is weak at best - remembering this I brought an ethernet cable for the second trip and learned that there are no actual wires in the ethernet ports. I was very tired of the breakfast buffet early on, and noticed that I was often eating lunch around the crumbs left by breakfast guests. And yes, the birds are loud even at night and can be very disruptive if you have jet lag.In short, the Yak and Yeti is a nice place for a few days, but if you are staying longer or need things to be easy to get business done, it's probably not for you.

This hotel is in a beautiful building in the center of town, however it's upkeep is not as good as it should be. The location is perfect, walking distance from Durbar Marg with a lot of restaurants and about 10 minutes walk to Thamel. The grounds are well landscaped with a pond and it is a peaceful oasis in the middle of chaotic Kathmandu. However the maintenance of the hotel is definitely as good as it should be, and the bathrooms need updating. Our AC and heating did not work right, the power outlets were unique and the hotel did not offer any plugs. The bathroom was very basic. Our room was a suite and had a large sitting room and a good sized bedroom, with a very comfortable bed.

Wow..... Is the expression I have for this place, ready made Masala Tea is my number one preference when I am here....... Lots of memories and the morning walk at the garden is out of the world. Maha shivaratri for us and HYY are a bonding whenever we are in Nepal 🇳🇵

Very friendly people with delicious food. We had a chance to taste only lunch and tea. Because I didn't stay in the hotel our workshop held in this hotel. It has nice history one of my napalee friend told me. Good outside environment.Good place to stay. Easy access.

as the title says this is my home from home while in Nepal as ever I love this hotel returned in 2017 for Dashain festival time as ever my guide was Uttara fantastic lady also used Vespa valley for a vespa ride around Kathmandu fantastic food safariAs a footnote this is the hotel Beck Weathers used to recover after the ill fated climb on Everest

My significant other and I stayed at the Yak and Yeti hotel for a week while we were in Kathmandu and we absolutely loved it! The location was perfect as the hotel is located in the center of the city and was walking distance to many sights including the busy streets of Thamel, it is located minutes from the Royal palace and is close to many restaurants with delicious food. The service we received is unlike any other, we truly appreciate everything the staff did to accommodate our needs. We would definitely recommend staying at Yak and Yeti to anyone who is visiting Kathmandu. Thank you to all people who made our stay such a wonderful experience!

As went in Yak and Yeti for lunch it was awesome  food arranging with many verities of taste. i enjoyed a lot. i felt that who are in Kathmandu  go for lunch hours there for your lunch. you will have best moment of lunch hour in your life as I got  there.

The hotel is is definitely the best in Kathmandu. It is located @ Durbar marg which is the heart of the city and its poshest area, right next to the Narayanhiti Palace museum. It is within 5 mins walking distance to the city's biggest shopping area with all the high-end stores and restaurants. Its a 15 mins walk to Thamel which is also the city's larger shopping districts. The hotel is a heritage property. The whole facade is inlaid with wood carving and magnificent architecture, you can't be at a better place. My room was large and very comfortable. The heating was excellent, even though there were almost zero degree temperatures outside. The shower and WC were excellent too. Bed was super comfy. Right outside the hotel are shops for handicrafts etc. Didn't try, but useful for last minute shopping and souvenirs.Internet is chargeable at NPR 750 for 24 hours and 3 devices at a time. Speed is ok,  but generally these days wifi is included as a standard, hence that's something Y&Y could look into. Its an industry norm. Housekeeping was very efficient and maintained the room spic & span. I locked my self out with the safe, the technician was quick to attend to the issue and efficient in re-opening it for me. Room service was efficient. Food was good. The breakfast could do with some improvement. Food quality was good, but the spread could be better, with more variety. Coffee was pretty standard, the hotel could put in a good machine and offer options like lattes, cappuccinos and espressos with the breakfast. The hotel has a complimentary shuttle to the airport every hour, which is great and the airport is a 10 mins drive in non-rush hours and about 25 mins during rush hours. We also attended an event in one of their convention centres, I think it was the Royal ball room or something. The space is really large for gatherings of about 500 people. Buffet was really nice. The overall service in terms of hospitality and staff friendliness is very high.There is a famous 5-star hotel across Y&Y also on Durbar Marg, I visited there for an event. Was not impressed at all. Y&Y is highly recommended.Will go back.

It is just as wonderful as we remember and a lovely way to end our Nepal trip. Great food, comfortable rooms and friendly helpful service. A special thanks to the room attendant who gave us the name of  a shop that sold Indian silk saris. We hope to return soon.

We had a lovely time at this hotel, which was made even better with the great service, hospitable staff, and wonderful hotel style and decor. We had in another "high end" hotel in Kathmandu the last time we were there, and it pales in comparison to the Yak and Yeti.The breakfast (included for us) was pretty good, and the food delivered by the room service was also quite tasty. Cocktail hour at the Shangri-la lounge was delightful, and the butlers there are absolutely the best! They were super helpful suggesting things to do, restaurants to try out along with a variety of other things. Bhakta Raj went out of his way to show us a nearby restaurant, personally showed us a short-cut to get there, and most surprisingly, even brought me a special batch of masala chai right before our departure simply because he noticed on the prior day that I really enjoyed drinking masala chai! Talk about making me feel special! Thank you, sir! I will never forget that!He was quite definitely the highlight of our stay there, and if we do go back to Kathmandu, we will most definitely stay there, simply because of him! All the other staff was super helpful and kind, too. The housekeeper, for example, was SUPER nice about getting us water whenever we asked for it (I need to drink lots of water due to kidney issues), and did it with a smile every time.

Admittedly I was attending a 3-day conference here and not staying in one of the rooms, but if they take care of their guests in any way similar to how they handled the conference, I don't have great news. Arrived at first lecture (not early) and the staff had only just started putting out chairs. Started 15-20 mins. late. At lunch - which was outside and very lovely - they hadn't put out 1/2 of the tables, linens or chairs. There weren't enough tables and chairs for lunch or for most lectures. Major renovations were taking place over the conference which were sometimes disruptive. Wifi was spotty and weak, staff seemed to know very little, and generally speaking, a big disappointment after the photos of the front of the hotel make it look so grand.

Highly dissapointing hotel. Bad slow service . Terrible housekeeping and maintanence. Still here and very dissapointed. Food is good . Reception staff are nice but the general living experience is horrible. The faucet setting is only on super hot. Does not work. No one comes to repair for over 30 minutes. In a cold place they give you house slippers only on asking. The bathroom products are crap. Service is slow. One coffee mug. And not so clean glasses in the room. Seriously poor experience given their rates and promises. Urge no one to waste their time here getting frustrated on a holiday .

Hotel Yak and Yeti is very centrally located in Kathmandu, situated walking distance from Durbar Marg and Thamel. Also there are good restaurants nearby. The architecture is old style and its a fascinating heritage building with modern amenities. There is a garden at the back with the swimming pool and a walkway. The rooms are comfortable with wooden flooring and brick walls. Renovations were going on in part of the hotel. I guess attempts to modernize the facilities.

Just loved the experience..the ambience the decor the service the helpful people of Nepal all constitute my reason for adoring to live in this hotel. special mention is the Durban at the main entrance gate who was so very caring ...."Ma'am be careful you will catch a cold "

An iconic hotel living up to its reputation. Excellent service and delicious food. Love the buffets. Extensive choice of freshly made food. Yum yum. Just what one needs before and after an expedition. Friendly and very helpful staff. We will be staying there again when we next go to nepal.

Our stay here was extremely pleasant.  The rooms were beautiful, comfortable and clean!  Top rate.  The food at the restaurant was good was a little more expensive than eating out.  Great location.  We were able to walk to almost everywhere we wanted to go. The grounds were beautiful too.

In need of renovation. Rooms should be cleaned better as carpets are still left dirty. There are no toothbrush, shaving kits or bedroom slippers provided. Breakfast is also subpar. WiFi connectivity is expensive and doesn’t work that well.

I expect a monetary refund if the hotel has ruined my belongings, not a discount!I requested a manual receipt and the hotel staff said they don't issue one. My company picks up my tab. So, If the hotel ruins my belongings , who will compensate me?No cotton buds, no hairdryer, no dental kit, very stingy with soap

This hotel is an old palace with a beautiful garden. The room are comfortable and cosy. It would be great to do some refurbishment and renovate some rooms. A bit more cleaning would not be bad either. All in all, very pleasant and comfortable stay.

Stayed three nights in this hotel and I think that it is one of the best in Kàtmandu.Facilities are good : garden and pool very nice to relax, large and comfortable rooms and very good restaurant.Only one negatif point : you must pay for the wifi, and this is not usual nowadays and less in a five stars hotel.

The stay was perfect and relaxing in the Yak and Yeti. We enjoyed Nepal. The hotel is in a nice area where you can reach a lot of places by walking. The rooms are spacious and very good equipped. There is currently a wish tree to help children- very nice touch. We will come back with our children.We are happy that we had the opportunity to join the animal welfare conference in the hotel. The facilities where the conference took place are in a palace.

Great service and hospitality!! Fantastic location, environment and great food options. I'd highly recommend staying at Yak and Yeti. Great view and easy in and out from airport shuttle. Internet speed is good too. Bathroom could be better thats all for now.

Excellent meeting facilites (indoor / outdoor).  High floor meeting rooms.  Elegantly appointed.  Outstanding Security staff:  One day, I've requested the doorman / security officer to help call a taxi for me.  The driver overcharged me.  When returning to the hotel, I expressed my disappointment to the same security officer who got the taxi for me.  He then took the initiative and ownership of the case, tracked down the driver and requested the driver to refund half of the money I had paid.  The following day, the hotel staff informed me that they were able to track the driver and got him to refund!  I was amazed by the diligent efforts from the hotel staff. Amazed by their honesty and great service!  In return, I offered the refund as a tip to the great officer.

In the middle of a dusty and busy Kathmandu you will find the Yak and Yeti hotel surrounded by a large well-kept garden with swimming pool, tennis courts and a jogging trail. The old part, where I stayed, is slightly rundown but kept clean and the newer rooms are apparently in better shape. The hotel restaurant serves all meals as buffet with very little left to the imagination after a couple of days. The food is of good standard though. The bar area still have individuals smoking which is unreal as it is part of the larger hotel foyer.The hotel is one block away from a busy street with a number of restaurants to choose from but quite a walk from downtown Thamel and if the traffic is not too bad about 15 minutes from the airport.I attended business meetings at the hotel with very good facilities for conferences and meetings in the old palace building.

The Yak & Yeti is a great hotel with a nice facade and traditional Nepali decor (which does require some sprucing up). Stayed for 2 nights in mid November. Our check in and out was efficient for a busy lobby. Service is good throughout our stay.The room and bed/ensuite was clean, quiet and comfortable, with sufficient room and storage. The room overlooks the extensive garden, grass area and pond. There is a small walking track around the border of the garden to exercise or admire the plants. The breakfast has a reasonable range to suit anyone's taste with plenty of seating. Breakfast can be served at a designated room on each floor if you don't want to be at the main ground floor eating area. We did not have lunch or dinner at the hotel or use any other available facilities,  other than the room.Helpful information to visit Places of interest from tours desk lady at the hotel lobby.Why 4 stars and not 5. The hotel is a fast 15 minute walk to the edge of Thamel district and longer to any sightseeing areas or restaurants. You have to pay for WiFi at a 5 star hotel!!. 900 NPR for 4 hours we where told by the busy suit&tie and unattentive 'Buisness center ' staff of the hotel. Obviously we did not measure up to the pompous requirements. This would rate as a 3.5 to a 4 star hotel in another country.

Due to Medical issues on our Hike, we unexpectedly had to find a hotel in Kathmandu for a couple nights.  Luckily we got into the Yak and Yeti and were very happy.  Although just a short walk to Palace Museum, Garden of Dreams and the Thamel Pedestrian Zone, the hotel it's self is in a quiet area and the garden was very peaceful.  Spa is a bit lacking in ambience, but the service we got was excellent.  If you have to get stuck anywhere, this is the place!  also it is a 15 min walk from CIWIC hospital if you have follow up appointments.  My only suggestion is if you have to grab a cab, walk out to the main street first.  Outside the hotel they wanted 1000 rupees where as we normally could get a ride to the hospital for 200-400 rupees.  Bfast Buffet has lots of options and was convenient.  Chimney restaurant was under renovations while we were there, but they let us order off the menu still and we had some excellent dinners as well.  Overall we were happy with this hotel!

Stayed at the hotel for a single night as I was on business and ‘this was the second stay after a gap of three years. Saw considerable improvement in the services. It was a welcome surprise to see the General Manager  I think a German lady escort to the room. I have not seen this happening for along time during my travel. The rooms were well appointed and the breakfast buffet was a lavish spread. Staff seem to be concerned of my needs and willing to help.The location of the hotel was prominent and a major factor for the decision to stay there. Would surely go back and recommend this hotel.Can’t ask for better treatment.

we were at the Yak and Yeti 2 times, be8for and after our trekking tour. we enjoyed both stays. the one after the tour even more as we could totally relax and enjoy the beautiful garden. the staff is very attentive, which is probabky the result that the manager is very visible and has a desk in the lobby- first time for us to se a General Manager who is really interested and accessible for the guest, this is a very nice touch. if we have the chance to come back to Nepal we will choose again the Yak and Yeti.all the best.

this place has not lost its grace. it has maintained itself. but nw it needs renovation for a sharper look. specially the toilets needs major renovation. the tap doesnt stop no matter how tight u hold it

My second stay after over 10 years and we were decidedly underwhelmed by the service, facilities and maintenance / condition of rooms. Yes the grounds are lovely and on first appearance the hotel gives an impression of being “5 star” with large lobby and larger than average rooms.  This is where the 5 star description should end. Service is mediocre to downright poor (upon checkout my bill was pushed towards me with no eye contact, no thank you and no questions re whether we required assistance for onward travel - we had stayed for 4 nights!). There was no recognition or greeting from any staff when we were entering or leaving (sometimes the door men would be nice but that’s it).  The rooms themselves are dated and not maintained well.  Our phone didn’t work, the tv is a joke and the shower curtain smelled and water leaked.  The travel desk at the hotel was poor - I was better off planning most things myself.  All of this I could somehow accept - this is after all a very poor country with limited infrastructure.  However, as a hotelier, don’t charge 5 star prices and then spend nothing on maintenance, updates, staff training.  Because then you are taking advantage and don’t deserve to call yourself 5 star.

They charged me whatever they can, i dont get any good service from the hotel. Requesting scissors 3times no replied so i had to go concierge, house keeping took my extra room key without saying anything..   i feel very insecure. Water.. one day not enough hot to take shower, one day too hot. No cold water at all... it is weird ...The last i paid $30 private car to drop hotel amd they provided me $10 hotel big old van... 5 stars.hotel does not.provide free wifi... after check out they said i need to pay extra using wifi at the lobby ....

A lovely place to stay and a refuge from the chaos that is Kathmandu.  As a 5star property I felt the room was a little small but it had everything we needed.  The shower was over the bath which I find awkward and power points were scarce. I stayed there 20 years ago when it had much more local charm, now it is a hotel that could have been anywhere. I guess that is progress.  but the service was good and the people were lovely.

Loved the Yak and Yeti. The staff went above and beyond to make you feel welcome and comfortable. My father and I stayed there 6 nights in early May 2017 and I would definitely recommend it. Even though the wifi wasn't amazing, their desire to make your stay as enjoyable and seamless as possible really was wonderful.

Recent stay in late October before heading off to Pokhara for motorbike trip was alright.. Ok but quite pricey relative to other more local options. The massage after a long flight from India, was very good and recommended. Good gym for workout including swimming pool. Quiet safe and secure location. Staff were excellent

This is our 2nd visit to Nepal and the 1st time staying at this place. This hotel was booked by our work therefore didn't have a choice. The staff are mostly courteous but  but services certainly are not at par to be classified 5 star. No slippers or robe, no newspaper delivered to your room and no complimentary wifi and even when you pay, the speeds are very slow and you can only connect two devices. The room temperature is centrally controlled so goodluck if it's too warm or cold for you. On the positive side  the beds are comfortable and meals do offer a range of dishes to select from and they offer an airport shuttle service @$10 per person.My request to hotel management is to please take my feedback on board. Having stayed at countless hotels across Australia, Nepal, UAE, Thailand and Taiwan  this is probably my 1st negative expereince and review.

Me and my family have a wonderful experience with the hotel, specially the hotel staff/management. The hotel staff are very accommodating, friendly, and they love kids.  The hotel are so neat and our room is quite spacious and lastly the food in the hotel is very tasteful and very well presented.We will visit the hotel again for sure!!! Highly recommended!!! 👍👍👍👍👍

During my journey through Nepal, I spent four days at Yak & Yeti while in Kathmandu. My first room where my journey through Nepal began, #423, was comfortable with a king sized bed. While the bathroom could probably use a bit of updating, everything worked well and complimentary toiletries were provided. My second room, #445, which I stayed in prior to my flight to Delhi, had obviously been upgraded. The bathroom had modern fixtures and appointments and the rest of the room had upgraded lighting and wood appointments as well.I was happy to pay for the WiFi at Hotel Yak & Yeti. This is a country that is still recovering from a devastating earthquake. It is a testament to the people of Nepal and Kathmandu, in particular, that the Hotel Yak & Yeti can provide Internet service which works so well. The aggregate cost was approximately 900 rupees (approximately $8USD) per 24 hour period. During my stay, breakfast was included at the Sunrise Restaurant. There was an excellent buffet which served Nepalese dishes as well as western offerings. I very much enjoyed the puri, curried beans and the variety of fresh baked items as well as the fruit juices (watermelon juice!) that were offered. I also had a lunch buffet one day which was equally as delicious. At 1800 rupees (approximately $15USD), it was not inexpensive. However, the food was plentiful, fresh and very tasty.The hotel is within walking distance of great shopping, restaurants and ATMs. I felt safe walking to and from the hotel, even at night. The hotel is gated with guards posted, but I was always welcomed and even saluted by a couple of the guards each time I returned to the hotel.I very much enjoyed my stay at Hotel Yak & Yeti and hope to return one day during a future journey to Nepal and Bhutan.
