No free wi fi which we battled to get as it was on our itinerary. No help with heavy deck chairs even after asking for assistance. No towels around the pool area. I would go somewhere cheaper and get better.

Historic and comfortable in every way, this is the place to stay in Kathmandu.  The Shangri-La Executive Lounge is a particular haven. Goma, Bakhtar, Deepok, and Khin make every visit there memorable and warmly friendly.I've now stayed at the Yak and Yeti in multiple visits for nearly a month in total nights.  I wouldn't stay anywhere else!

Stayed 2 nights and was upgraded to the Club floor, Excellent service   Booked a city tour through the Hotel desk and although the guide was very nice, it wasn’t as interesting as I️ had hoped. We could have taken a cab and Read signs at the temples we visited for a lot less money. But right outside the door was an amazing $13 massage-

This is a nice hotel. 4 1/2 Star.  Not quite a 5 Star but I would still recommend.  Efficient staff.  Renovated rooms are clean and well equipped.  Renovations are ongoing.  Nice buffet breakfast.  Great location if you like the bedlam of Thamel.

Modern hotel, good location, close to Thamel. It's quiet and provides good services, although some of them not included in price, makes it a little expensive, Internet should be included. Breakfast is good but also should be included, as there are no other options close by.

I was a bit disconcerted when I arrived at the airport, having confirmed my arrival and pickup only the day before, to find I was absent from the list. I was even more disconcerted when we finally arrived at the hotel, and there was no reservation for me, even though I produced their emailed confirmation.  Having travelled for over 24h, all I wanted was a shower and a bed - and after about an hour that was finally produced!My room was spacious, comfortable, and looked down on a pleasant garden and swimming pool.  Curses! I had not thought to bring a costume, and there was no dressing gown. In fact, in 10 days, I never once saw anyone swimming.Dinner was a buffet, which sounds boring, but was really, really good. The service was quite over the top - leave the table for an instant, and everything was cleared away, and someone might well have grabbed your seat by the time you had collected the next dish! There were some delicious soups to start; a range of curries with rice and papadums and other fixings; quite often a roast with a wide range of vegetables; salads galore; and puddings to die for.  Suffice it to say that I put on 4kg during my stay.The location was great, a quiet paradise down an urban alley. There were occasional curiosities - the lifts sometimes hiccupped; the carpets were vacuumed regularly but really needed a good scrub; and the light switches in the bedrooms needed an expert Pelmanist to remember what did what. There was a lot of dust in the air from the reconstruction of the conference facilities - which really need reconstruction, beautiful as they are. In the Regency room there were two plug points.  Have you ever seen grown men weep in frustration as their cell phones die for lack of power? And the internet was decidedly underwhelming.

We spend several days at the hotel.  Located in a good area, easy to access, and the hotel was nicely decorated and everything worked well.  Decent breakfasts and menus were also easy to read.  Be careful of the garlic bread---really good but covered in garlic cloves!   Rooms were spacious, easy to find, and had all the amenities.  A good experience.

I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights at the end of my trip after time in the mountains as I expect a lot of people reading this review might, so let me start with they do have warm large showers with good water pressure!The hotel is set within a gated enclosure and has an old world regal air to it. The staff are friendly and helpful kindly facilitating early check in for me.My room was spacious and had air con, tv, internet, room safe (strongly suggest this is used) and all the usual comforts one would expect of a hotel of this caliber.The hotel is set in spacious grounds with a pool, tennis courts, running track, pond (with some noisy geese) to allow you to escape from the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu.There is a bar and a couple of restaurants. I went to the restaurant (name escapes me) by reception. A buffet is available daily for breakfast lunch and dinner. There is also an a la carte menu available. The buffet was good and this was my choice for breakfast (included) and lunch once but at US$25, only once!. The dinner buffet was very similar to the lunch buffet but there was still plenty of selection however I opted for the a la carte most nights having fallen in love with the (boneless) murgh kastoori (try it!!).I cant vouch for what is in the immediate area as I did not venture from the hotel instead spending my time round the pool where i was dutifully cared for by a young trainee working the pool bar, thank you young lady (take note Yak & Yeti!).At the end of my trip I was also provided a complimentary ride to the airport which is probably 15 minutes.I do have 1 minor peeve which annoying and something I have never experienced before. At around 10am ish a member of staff would go from room to room knocking on doors to inspect the mini bar, this was a daily occurence. A very minor thing but annoying none the less.In conclusion I would stay there again and would recommend it

Stayed for a total of 3 nights - bookending our Annapurna trek. Large comfortable rooms, bathroom may need an upgrade but was more than adequate.  The breakfast choice was huge and what I ate, very good.  Lovely grounds. Very friendly and helpful staff.Unlikely to retutn to Kathmandu any time soon but would have no hesitation staying here again - far ahead of the two hotels I have stayed in previously.

The Yak & Yeti was the hotel chosen by our outfitter as the start and finish of our Khumbu trek, and, as such, more than adequate for that task. The rooms,  particularly in the newer wing are comfortably well-appointed. The venue is popular with conventions, as we learned a bit about cardiology, architecture, and the U.N. mission in Nepal while here. The staff is friendly and attentive. The property is extremely well-secured should that be of any concern. The breakfast, lunch and dinner buffets in the Sunrise Restaurant are nothing short of sumptuous. While heavy foot traffic caused by a succession of exhibitions have impacted the garden and pool area somewhat, the outside areas provide needed serenity from the busy central city neighborhood.

Great location, just walk out the gates, and walk the streets, into another's world 🌎!!! Everything is close to hand, and people are extreamly helpful and friendly, if you ask for directions, they will leave what their doing, and take you there!

This old palace turned hotel holds much of Kathmandu's climbing history. I wanted to stay here to experience what climbing parties for decades have experienced. I was only a trekker but the history bound up in this hotel seemed iconic with Kathmandu. The staff is very friendly and helpful (especially the bellmen), the breakfast buffet was something I looked forward to each morning (even though it is a bit pricey $15) and the garden is a lovely place to unwind and gain back a bit of piece and quiet. I was able to leave an extra duffle bag at the hotel while I trekked out of Pokhara. For me, the Yak and Yeti was worth the price I paid to stay there.

This is the famous old hotel in town and we booked here to join a group. The staff is extremely attentive, the breakfast is great and the rooms are nice, although somewhat tired. It is not a great value for your money, but it is the most famous hotel in Kathmandu!

we have been at the hotel yak and yeti already 4 times. we have always chosen the hotel because of its location. in the future we will again choose yak and yeti, as the service has improved a lot compare to our last visit in April. it is a different feeling, you get a smile a welcome and you feel welcome. we heard from and saw that there is a new manager who is literally everywhere, we saw her quite some times taking care about everything, as we are owners of a small guesthouse we figured out she must be the one. we did not have the chance to talk to her, as we have been with a group of people and always on the move. we love the yak and yeti and will always recommend it to our friends. we wish the team at yak and yeti all the best, especially for the upcoming renovation. the hotel will renovate one wing of hotel, i think it is the one with the carpet in the rooms. we stayed on both sides of the hotel. there are heritage rooms available which are nicer, they cost a little bit more, but it is worth and compare to other cities still affordable and good value for money. looking forward to be back in kathmandu at yakandyeti. if you are there, do not miss to have a lok at the palace part of the hotel where they do conferences. it is partly already under renovation, but still worth to look at it.

Stayed here for 5 days and the outside structure it all that looks impressive. The rooms really need a revamp; toilets are old; toilet amenities are old fashioned and pretty much nothing was that impressive.The hotel staff are good but only that does not help much. They need to upgrade now because they have the best location in town.

Stayed for 10 days here. Made very welcome by the staff who were very helpful and quickly replaced broken hairdryer. Service was very efficient. Great location for both business and tourist customer. WiFi isn’t brilliant as others have said but who needs to download movies if you’ve come to Nepal! Food and drink on the expensive side was my only niggle but had dinner out most nights. Would certainly stay here again.

The hotel needs major renovation and improvement to the rooms with proper 5 star facilities especially in the bathrooms.  Tea & Coffee facilities with a filled mini fridge would be advantageous. Breakfast spread and Lunch buffet spread is good but very expensive. Entertainment for night life would be good to have a dance bar or a disco.

The Yak and Yeti has all the trappings of a 5 star hotel but doesn't live up to expectations- shower water is tepid- they charge 10 bucks a day for sluggish wifi- you'll be charged more for a beer than you would pay on the Everest Base Camp trail (and more than you'd pay in London) and then you'll be hassled to drink up so they can close the bar at 11 o'clock- the toaster doesn't work and breakfast is lacklustre- the bedroom walls are paper-thin and the plumbing antedeluvian ie noisy - laundry wasn't ironedOverall the Yak and Yeti is not value for money and certainly not 5star. Next time I'll stay in a mid-range hotel closer to Thamel.

It is a nice hotel because of it palatial looks. Rooms are good. Food is very average. Breakfast room is too small for the number of people and service leaves a lot to be desired. Being season the hotel was very crowded.Well located and convenient to go to Thamil etc. Check out was very quick. Overall did not see value for the kind of money that we paid.Maybe does well due to limited alternate options.

Many annoying things which could be improved:- Wifi is not free: i thought this was 2017 though- No airport shuttle: Hyatt has one- Deceptive pictures: look at the one i attached: i booked a "deluxe heritage" which turned out to be quite different from the pictures online - staff acknowledged that the "deluxe heritage" i had was not up to online pics standard though and changed me to one which was closer to what i booked- Slow service: not specific to Yak&Yeti, but hey. Standards.- Staff pointing at stuff and waiving when giving indications: not bringing you to facilities and pretty much leaving you on your own- Double payment checkout: staff asked to pay room charge again when i had already paid online. Fortunately i checked on the spot, but could have been very annoying if not. I am sure it was not done on purpose, but still worsen the experience.Overall, all these things add up to an average experience at best."Lawn is nice though" as one other comment says.

The hotel is nice, heritage one, location is good, nicely done - trying to preserve the heritage. But signs of aging are quite clear and needs a lot of maintenance. For example, flushes not working in toilet (and i had been reading this as a consistent feedback). The maintenance team was prompt to address it though! If maintenance is improved, this hotel will be a five star for me.

Good rooms. I got a free upgrade. However they messed up a bit on the accounting part while settling the bills. Not a major issue though. Buffet breakfast was good. The Gym a bit small and people queued to use the treadmill.

Terrible management, I blocked two rooms and while checking in they told me that the amount was for one room which is nearly 840 US dollar, however I asked them to change my booking to two rooms for on night and they charged me almost 440$ per night for every room, I called the manager to assist understanding the massive charges while their available online charges are between 130 and 200$ he was not helpful, extremely rude and said he will not be able to change my room or offer any discount on my high charges! Will never recommend this hotel or stay again here!

Quite a good place to stay. The room and the decor of the Hotel is a bit dated and that is a let down but overall it is quite decent. The hotel biggest USP is the location, right on Darbar Marg and that means all the important locations are nearby. the breakfast buffet was quite decent and in the evening though we did not go for the Buffet - the spread seemed very lavish. there is a nice garden behind the Hotel and it is a serene spot and worth taking a stroll in the morning or evening alike. The Hotel is more suited for tourists and not much for business travellers like me. Food seemed a bit overpriced. Overall a good place.

The location is excellent, in the heart of the city. I suggest to pay a few Dollar more and get a heritage room. It is a historical hotel, with local flair. I definitely go back there. Shops for souvenirs in walking distance. Only around 5 km from airport

The difference between most hotels and the Yak & Yeti are the people working for this hotel who provide outstanding customer service.  Bandana, the representative at the customer service desk in the lobby, went out of her way on a number of occasions to help me. Surnita, the greeter at the Sunrise Cafe, impressively remembered my room number and name after the frist day.  The attendant in the Business Office helped me find a magazine on local crafts and arts and helped copy a number of assignments for me.  These memories of my time spent at the hotel are the reasons why I go stay there on my return visits to Kathmandu.            (Dr. D.McKinney, CA, USA)

The room air conditioner was not working and room was changed. In the changed room, the toilet flush was not working properly.I would strongly recommend the maintainance to check all the facilities in room to be on working condition before the room is allotted to any guest.

Have gone down way below standard from checking in to check out everything has gone down considerably poorLast year it was superb but now the hotel and staff both r in miserable condition Food and service WORST ever

1. Check-in and check-out was best part in the 3 day stay, please see below the improvement areas apart from this I found the staff to be courteous and helpful2. The room stinked as if it was not opened since ages - suggest to request a room on the higher floors3. The TV in our room was not operational and it was learnt that the subscription was expired, I took an hour to get it renewed4. The carpet in the room was visibly dirty5. Swimming pool was not clean and could see a lot of rubbish in it

For all the hype around this place, found this place very average for the price I paid. The rooms are basic, our toilet did not have a latch to lock from inside. Food is average. Staff is friendly but need training. The hotel has a beautiful lawn but that's about it. I was a little disappointed

A very well run hotel with lovely grounds. The staff were friendly and helpful. Excellent breakfast buffet.Our room overlooked the garden and was very peaceful. Cleanliness was of a high order. It is in a good, central position.

not for average traveler, unless you book a bigger rooms. Amenities are good with beautiful garden. Service staff were good. Can't comment on food as we were out most of the times. Casino Royale is quite decent.

I was here last December and loved all about the place. It was centrally located yet was removed enough from the noise of the city to be a calm stop.Food was amazing.. I loved everything they had to offer, the rooms were cozy and clean. Fantastic! I would love to visit again!

We stayed here on an official trip for 3 days, food was pathetic, infact I would say worst, tasteless.Staff was corporative, issues with Wifi each space has different wifi connections so you can't take your phone independently to the premises, rooms are just fine with dampness on wallsWould not recommend any one looking for a 5 star, at this price its fine to opt for a 4 star with better amenities

The hotel can cater to large groups. It has a big banquet hall. It has a small hall area in the lobby. The staff at the reception counter is very helpful. It is walking distance to the bazar. The breakfast and dinner is lavish and serves vegetarian and non-vegetarian food. The breakfast hall is quite large. The garden and swimming pool create a pleasant surrounding. The rooms overlook the garden. Ample parking space is available.

I've stayed at Yak and Yeti a couple of times now.  It's a great hotel, and has a wonderful Nepali ambience.  The staff is incredibly warm and helpful.  It is worth getting the executive level - Bhaktaraj ("Peter") and his crew take great care of you (he'll also teach you some Nepali, if you're interested!).  Protima and Protap will help you find a great adventure in the Kathmandu area as well.  It's a great place for a get away, but also provides every advantage for the business traveler - business center, wifi, etc.  Yak and Yeti also has great food at the Sunrise Cafe and the pub.  The only aspect that falls a bit short is the gym.  It has a great sauna and whirlpool (and a wonderful outdoor pool as well), but the fitness center is a bit dated.  As someone committed to fitness, that made it a bit challenging to get a good workout in (but creativity helps!).  Finally - it is centrally located.  You can get anywhere you need to be in town very easily.  You can't go wrong with this hotel!

Fairly priced heritage hotel with some deferred maintenance (especially noticeable at room level where guests expects high standards and spend the most time in). It does however provide a wonderful  escape from the hustle and bustle of the city, with its manicured gardens and serene surroundings. Buffett variety and front desk professionalism can be improved. Overall I like the idea of preserving the historical aspects of this hotel.

Nice location, with a well maintained garden and an enjoyable swimming pool.Attentive staff , large rooms and a continental breakfast with quality and abundant food selection.Recommended for couples and families

Wooow ! Stunning heritage hotel, will take your breath away ! Rooms are great, decor, interior, ambiance everything is perfect. Outside of the hotel there is a good handicraft shopping area, can spend good half day on shopping on this street. I personally felt staffs are bit old school type. Rest everything is outstanding ! must experience stay !!

This is a lovely luxurious hotel in Kathmandu. It's very grand, quite expensive for Nepalese standards but a lovely treat. The hotel staff are fabulous and everyone I came into contact with was very friendly, helpful and super professional. The building itself and the grounds are beautiful and kept spotless. One of the wings is currently being renovated / restored but that didn't affect my stay. My room was very nice and well laid out, the bed was big and very comfortable. There was an in room safe, hairdryer and good air con. The bathroom was nice with a lovely powerful shower, there was a nice selection of toiletries. The Chimney restaurant is currently closed but the Sunrise restaurant was nice for breakfast and dinner. The dining room staff were great and paid such attention to detail. The location is good, about a fifteen minute walk into Thamel (close enough but far enough away!). There are a few shops very close and a couple of supermarkets a few minutes walk away. The only thing that was slightly disappointing was the wifi access - there is complimentary wifi but limited to a certain time,  I stayed in five hotels in Nepal (from budget to higher end) and this is the only one where there wasn't full complimentary wifi access.

Though it might have been a nice hotel in the beginning, deteriorating standards of maintenance and a lackadaisical attitude of the management have trapped the hotel in a rut. On my first trip here, I was given a room whose bathroom door wouldn't even shut because the wood was suffering from water retention. On my second trip a week later I got a better room. The buffet breakfast was alright. The housekeeping staff, the restaurant staff are quite polite and helpful. But the biggest problem is the management of the hotel. They are neither helpful nor polite and can be quite disrespectful. The reasons I gave this hotel a 3/5 is because of the beautiful lawn and the chimney restaurant otherwise I would be tempted to give it a 1/5. Will definitely not be in a hurry to return.

this hotel was stayed for prince harry of england. the good hotel. but very cold. out of the hotel have lot of shop, japanese restaurant.  wifi need to pay if you book through travel agent. no tour board. good view of surrounding.

A nice hotel well located in Kathmandu. The breakfast is good and so is the dinner buffet. It feels like a corporate hotel or group-friendly hotel. The rooms could be cleaner. Over all, good value for money.

Hotel staff are friendly and cooperative. Foods are well balanced and service are goods.But suttle bus service are little bit late. Room service ia also good. Environment and conference halls are good.Pradeep

I had two night stay but hotel Maintanence is v bad.  It was not a nice experience to stay their. From our side it looks nice but rooms are not up to mark. They need to improve a lot in every respect for room.

非常好的地理位置。有歡迎飲品，還有熱心的職員。有乾淨的泳池和美味的早餐。每天有免費報紙，房間乾淨。有免費機場接送。Good location and safe.welcome drink and nice staff.swimming pool and good breakfast.everyday free newspaper.clean room free Shuttle to airport.

I was very happy with the service provided by the Yak & Yeti Hotel. I stayed here during a short business trip to Nepal, and the hotel staff could not have been more professional. My group used the executive lounge every evening to conduct post-meeting follow-ups, and the 4th Floor lounge team was incredible. They are some of the most professional and attentive employees I've ever seen. They made the stay feel very special and treated our group very well. You could not want for more food/coffee in the morning and snacks/drinks in the evening. The staff on the 4th floor alone made this a 5-star trip! The staff of the guest service desk were as equally impressive. They helped me book a restaurant for my team, organized transportation to the airport, and extended my room stay with a helpful, friendly attitude.We will certainly stay at the Yak & Yeti Hotel on future business trips. They made my first Nepal experience an outstanding one. Thanks!

I went here with my family and friends for a meal. The location and the gardens are lovely. The food was very average and the service was terrible. We have to call the waiters a couple of times to get attention and they all seemed very laid back..

This is a large hotel popular with tour groups and for government meetings etc.Its getting a bit old and rooms need a renovation. Our room, 336  was OK but some lights burnt out, window dirty - they should do better.The hotel grounds are large with nice pool and its in an enclosed area off the street. Nearby are some shopping areas and a large busy street with many restos shops etc. Breakfast buffet is good, can be busy though.Front desk service is a bit aloof and not friendly.Wifi is extra charge.

I was at the Yak and Yeti for two nights for a work related trip and had an amazing time! They upgraded me to the executive suite which was large and spacious. The hotel is old but well maintained and beautiful with lovely garden surrounding the hotel.

It is one of the oldest hotels in Kathmandu and it does not disappoint you also. The staff is very friendly and the heritage ambience is very pleasing. Though rooms need little more attention in terms of upkeep. However it was a good experience.

I stayed at Hotel Yak and Yeti for 4 nights in July of this year - on a work related trip. The hotel itself is clean and comfortable. The staff are very helpful and friendly. There is a high level of security - as you might expect for one of the smartest hotels in a relatively deprived city. I ate in the restaurant one evening - and I was slightly disappointed. It was relatively expensive (£10 for a curry) - and not particularly tasty. I definitely had better food at much lower prices elsewhere in Kathmandu. However, the range of food available at breakfast was good and the staff were excellent. I attended a large international conference - and we did experience some difficulties accessing wifi during the event. I don't think their servers were set up for hundreds of people trying to get online at the same time. The staff were also initially reluctant to serve hot drinks outside of the allotted timings - but did become more flexible as the week progressed. The food provided at lunch time was good and they were very well set up for catering for large numbers. Overall - I would say this hotel was good and I would stay there again. If I was organising a large event in Nepal I would consider this venue - but would also investigate other options!!

The Yak and Yeti has a lot going for it and much to recommend it. Great location and outstanding physical layout, including a nice garden and a spacious lobby and bar area. The staff are well-trained and professional. At the same time, the hotel is showing its age and suffers from wear and tear, which appears in the form of stained carpets and dirty bathroom grout. So, as long as you keep in mind that this is a luxury hotel by Nepalese standards, not necessarily international standards, you shouldn't be disappointed. The wifi and restaurant both seem reliable.

Lovely place!  Everyone was so friendly and helpful and the garden was beautiful.  Also it seemed to be out of the way of the terrible air pollution in the city, but close enough to be able to walk to the old town and the shopping district

Mixed feelings. You go to Nepal not expecting international standards and need to take that into consideration...that said...Initially upon check in we were offered a ground floor room and told that there were no others available unless we took a twin alternative. Naturally this made us question what was wrong with the room being offered and he said nothing just that it's on the ground floor. So we continued to check into this room. Upon seeing the room we understood the issue immediately. It was on the ground floor facing a path with an old arched room height window which wouldn't close and a bathroom from the 1970s that wasn't well kept.... at all. We returned to reception immediately and the receptionist was extremely helpful and after talking to the manager (who just happened to be passing) he upgraded us to a Heritage room. This room was lovely and I'd recommend if staying you only stay in a heritage room. Overall the standards here do not match international standards so a heritage room is a nicely decorated standard room really. But charged at club Pros1. Location relatively good2. People at the hotel were quite gracious and generally helpful3. Breakfast range is ok/good but a simple upgrade to include a egg station would help update the hotels offering4. Umbrellas are available upon request5. Easy check outCons1. Whilst we were there a 7 day conference was running. This had a significant number of delegates which naturally took over the hotel - grounds segregated and blocked for them limiting access for other guests plus with the buildings works on the old building this really limited enjoyment of the grounds. 2. Breakfast -suggest a delegated area rather than allowing the delegates to take a table each and making other guests wait and feel second class. 3. Gym/ tennis courts -not up to international standards- small and dated equipment - really needs refurbishment 4. Whilst not being at international standards in every way - the costs for any service was at international costs - certainly comparable to London pricing e.g. Dinner at the restaurant, spa, drinks - they should really reduce this as more people may use the facilities. So overall I'm giving the hotel a 3 rating but this is based on hotels in Nepal otherwise would be significantly lower. Also note this is a 3/4 star not 4/5 in reality

The Yak & Yeti Hotel has a very housewarming feel to it. Exquisite art, woodwork, decor, etc. Room are fairly large with a nice view (at least mine did). Every staff member constantly greets you with a smile and a loud Namaste greeting.  They did this every time I walked past a staff member, server, manager, etc. They knew me by name. The restaurant even memorized my order after my 2nd visit and confirmed if I was going to eat the same type of omelet. The 4th Floor lounge servers were simply the best. They are the most competent, professional, and understanding gentlemen I've ever seen in a hotel environment. Mr. Bhakta Bharati and Mr. Khin Karki were complete professionals. They were very courteous and worked with our group to accommodate every one of our wishes. They stopped at nothing to ensure we were happy. Even when I wasn't feeling well, Mr. Bhakta brought snacks/ginger ale to my room. Great work guys!!The management were equally professional. Mrs. Neeta Thapa and Ms. Anju Kunwar were extremely accommodating. Whenever I needed them (even on their day off), without hesitation, they called me back and worked out the issue. I couldn't be happier with Mrs. Neeta and Ms. Anju. They worked with me as if I was the only guest in the hotel. They sat down, we drank tea/coffee, explained the situation, and worked diligently to meet our needs. I will always come back to the Yak & Yeti Hotel as long as these professionals are working there. They made my Nepal experience an outstanding one. Great Job!!!

I dined in the iconic Chimney at the Yak and Yeti in 1984, so for a very special occasion I decided to return.  Unfortunately "The Chimney" was closed for renovations, so I was offered the Sunrise Restaurant as "they offer the same menu"! Possibly the same menu, but not the same ambience or service.  Clearly being located in the "new building" adjacent to the lobby means that it must serve a broad clientele, and the convenience of a buffet is added. My medium rare beef was cooked to perfection and was certainly the best steak I have had in Kathmandu.  The wine list is extensive covering all important bases, at prices you would expect (USD60 for a good, slightly aged French Pinot Noir).So a good restaurant, but lacking the wow factor of the Chimney, and short of delivering a true fine dining experience.

The hotel is situated in Durbar Marg, best location in Nepal 🇳🇵 where you can just walk by the road to shop, eat, dine, and do many more things. This hotel has acceptable service standards, not as good as Indian hotel standards but still the best in Nepal. Better hotel than Annapurna, Durbar Marg.

It was a pleasure to stay in this hotel after a terrible hotel in Kathmandu. Rooms are comfortable, clean, and spacious. The common areas are a delight. Chef creates wonders at the kitchen. Food is delicious and of rich variety. Staff is very nice and helpful. Hotel has a very good location. It also has a wonderful backyard with a pool.

I stayed in the hotel during official meeting. The staffs were very friendly and provided their assistance when needed during meeting and cocktail dinner reception. The rooms were also good and maintained well. Though there was some delay while billing in the reception section due to crowd and the staff was feeling irritated.

We got a refurbished pool facing room. Wooden flooring, no carpet stench. Location is good. Casino not much to talk about. Food is good for Indians, but, sometimes may not be very fresh. People are friendly and helpful

Property is too old and its showning. Cannot call this even 4 stars. Staff is not that polite.They do provide free shuttle from airport but one need to inform them separately as they don't read booking details.Travel desk is ripping money, their prices are too high. I know in hotel travel companies charge more but charging 3-4times is not worth. When asked why urprices are soohigh lady responded security....... not sure for you profit u need to defame ur country.

Excellent experience. Service with smile!  Enjoyed our stay from 6/11 through 6/17 and back again from 6/29 through 7/1.The rooms were clean and comfortable.. The room service was fantastic!Buffet Breakfast was also great... Welcome change after long trip to Tibet.Individuals like Gopal, Basu, Khrisna, became friends. Shanti and Damodar in the cafeteria -- Thank you! for lovely Masala tea and your lovely smile!

Awesome hotel in Nepal. Awesome Architecture.Food is delicious. people at concierge are quiet helpful. Rooms are more than expectation. hotel has everything that you expect like Swimming pool, Gym (of international standard), Sauna, Jacuzzi, Steam.Hotel has pick and drop facility also.

Rooms are large & comfy if a little dated. We had early start so asked for packed breakfast which was OK. Seems to be in a reasonable location & the old part of the hotel (mainly used for weddings & functions) looks great

Once a reputed hotel. But perhaps bad management has reduced it to an ordinary one. Where much lesser properties do not charge at all or charge just a nominal amount for free wi-fi, this hotel charges 170 rupees per hour for the same. Quite shameful. Plus the sullen faces at the reception does very little to help matters.

very comfortable and relaxing, food at restaurant was very tasty, garden was really nice and peaceful, receptionist was very cordial, over all good stay. love to stay again. pool was clean. lifts were little old and make more noice.

We stayed twice once in May and then again in June after coming back from Pokhara the garden landscaping is beautiful and nice comfortable beds. The staff was very courteous and took good care and specially Dinesh in reservations was very helpful. The Narayanhity Palace Museum and Thamel are walking distance. I would definitely stay here again whenever I go next.

Needing to take the wife somewhere for her birthday, I decided on Nepal.The Yak & Yeti seemed a good compromise between Kathmandu's number one and the others (vouched for by the taxi driver).Albeit we spent a mere 4 nights there we enjoyed it...but need to draw attention to the poor quality of the food.The hotel is set in its own grounds, replete with the token wildlife in the form of geese, and security. It even has its famous casino and splendid wing that has survived the country's colonial past and the 2015 earthquake.The room was very good, not "in spite of the host country" but on its own merits.The pool and ground were picturesque.The restaurant and other bits were...well, fine.Food was a problem. From the onset when I asked for diary and gluten free products for my wife. Unfortunately, they (mis)informed me when they said that the lavish buffet spread would cater to her needs.To compound my angst, the duty manager pretended that such new-age requests were extraordinary to his ears.Exacerbating the absence of such needs, we partook of the breakfast buffet. Sadly, the quality was a let down. Stale is not a term I have ever used to describe a restaurant's food. However, sad to say that it was apt for the YNY.I need to emphasize that the food was not the only feature of the hotel and that everything else was fine with us but, the food did leave a bit of an aftertaste.Would I return? The jury is still out.(If I could, I would have given them 3-1/2 out of 5 - better than "Average" but less than "Very Good".)

Spent a very comfortable 2 weeks at the Y&Y for a business trip. Was on the 4th floor in the Shangri-la Club rooms, which I highly recommend especially if you're staying more than a few days. Can't comment on the value as my company paid, but you'll have access to the Club Room on the 4th floor including a nice breakfast spread (fruit, cereals, yogurt, cheeses etc as well as eggs made any way you like). In the evenings there's a happy hour with a snack buffet that can serve as a light dinner, and free drinks. But the best part is the wonderful staff on the 4th floor, who will make sure you're looked after and enjoying your stay. Room was very spacious. I was overlooking the city (really, my view was a wall but it didn't make much of a difference to me) not the garden and didn't find it noisy as some reviews have reported. Bathroom also spacious and very clean, with a hair dryer.  The water pressure in the shower was incredible. Nice in-room amenities including a water kettle and instant coffee/tea, fruit plate delivered daily, and a large flat screen TV though I never turned it on so can't comment on channel selection. The minibar was mostly alcohol and expensive compared to street prices, as you'd expect for the convenience. Same for room service, but the food is very nice. Laundry was always prompt, and same day return is standard if you get it to them by 10 am. Housekeeping did a great job of keeping things clean daily.The grounds of the hotel are gorgeous, and there's a track which is nice for a walk in the morning since the streets of Kathmandu are pretty dusty and not so nice for walking or running. Location is convenient, 5 minute walk to the Palace museum and easy 10-15 min walk to Thamel. There's a great little market called Bluebird market just down the alley, for snacks and toiletries.  Plenty of restaurants and stores in the area, as well as ATMs (including a Standard Chartered which seemed to be the only ATM that worked for everyone in our group, but there are plenty of banks with international networks). I didn't run into any problems during my stay, but feel confident that if I had the staff would have taken care of me. I will definitely come back to Y&Y when I return to Kathmandu.

My first impression of the Yak and Yeti was that they had doctored the picture on their web site because the hotel doesn't look anywhere near as grand as the picture suggest (almost like the best marigold hotel).However, putting aside facade, the rooms are comfortable and the service is excellent . The hotel is also in the heart of Kathmandu so relatively well placed and secure. A four star hotel but with charm and great service.

Its a local five star hotel so I'd probably class it as a four star - but post trek when you need clean sheets, hot shower and a little bit of comfort its the perfect place! The rooms are nice and big and the bathrooms too - its a huge hotel so you should be able to ask for good rooms with better views!

I love the service at the door and the breakfast! Especially the chocolate bread! Relaxing and beautiful garden. Last time I got an older room on the ground floor and there was some smell of moisture. But clean rooms always!

Heritage hotels are often trade-offs between awe-inspiring historical buildings and shortcomings in moderns amenities. The Yak&Yeti does not even hold this low standard. The historical royal palace has been violated with ugly elevators, the contemplative pond is next to a jet engine noise level machine, and the boxy concrete wing fits in this ensemble like a fist in your stomach. All of the aestethetic violations, even the dated and shabby interior could be forgiven would the hotel keep hygenic standards. Dirty glasses, mouldy water, broken handdryers and the ever pervasive smell are warning signs that things are not in order. Several food bugs in our group are simply unacceptable. Few minor headaches: install plugs to charge phones, fight the dengue carrying tiger mosquitos descending on the poolside, give out wifi coupons that don't just simply run out without any explanation and please serve some breakfast which deserves the name.

Nothing about the hotel is good other than its outside appearance. Apparently it is a Old palace converted into a hotel 20 years back. It may have qualified to be a 5 star hotel when it was built but it needs serious up gradation now. It is a shame to be keeping heritage properties in such poor condition. They should learn from the Taj Group of hotels, who maintain heritage properties so well.The breakfast was horrible. They need to shut down to renovate. I don't understand why do they still have 5 star rating. This would be a good 3 star hotel. Just being big does not make it 5 star.

Travelled with family when going on trekking trip to Nepal. Hotel states it is a 5 star - not the case, low 4 star perhaps. However it does have good grounds, the location is excellent and after trekking in Nepal the showers and aircon were welcome after the trekking and hours in a vehicle. Their Wifi policy of only allowing 2 devices per room is a bit outdated and surprising for an establishment that bills itself as 5 star. Food and beverage are rather pricey, however overall i would recommend and will stay there again on further trekking holidays

The hotel seems to forgot about renovation and upgrade since last 15 years. Property smells of old moist furniture and carpet, customer service nearly non-existant, staff and front desk untrained to handle groups, need to shout for attention in the dining hall

The hotel is centrally located and an easy walk to restaurants and shops.  At the time we were there, they were remodeling.  The noise in our room was unbearable from the jackhammering.  We asked to be moved and were assured that we would be when we returned from our outing.  When we returned nothing had been done. The manager indicated he would move us the next morning (we were leaving the next day). He finally very reluctantly moved us to a room above the dining room where we got to smell the food.  Other than that, the restaurant was good with a full breakfast and the rooms were a decent size and clean. Friends who had booked a suite were given a larger room but no suite.

I had the opportunity to stay here one night, and was not pleased with the staff at the front desk. There was an overbooking at my hotel, and to accommodate me, my company placed me here generously. The hotel staff was not very pleasant. I would stay here again assuming this incident was isolated. The breakfast was fantastic, a large variety and lots of light from the garden windows. The grounds were lovely, but the hotel had little to offer in their shops area. I did break out in a rash from the soap, possibly not used to it, but it was overwhelmingly fragranced.

Very nice hotel with classic appointments, clean, comfortable rooms and pleasant staff. The restaurant is very good, other than the breakfast buffet is the same each day. However, a la carte dining is not publicized but they will prepare some of the basics if you ask them.  The pain au chocolat are the best ever when they come out of the kitchen first thing in the morning. Lunch and dinner buffets provide a nice selection of Indian/Nepalese classics.  Also on the premises is The Chimney, which once you dine there, will become your regular spot. The MUST HAVE is the classic Chicken Kiev, rumored to be the finest in the world and I AGREE!  Equally fantastic is the Borstch.

Staff and particularly in terms of safety was brilliant.  I had forgotten my passport, substantial amount of cash, and other valuables in the hotel safe when I checked out and only realised in the following morning.  I was assured by the hotel security staff and I was able to collect all my belongings first thing the following morning.  Overall I found all staff to be professional and helpful.

Based on documentaries and news reports I had a totally different expectation of Kathmandu and their facilities. One has to keep in mind that this is a very poor country but the people are honest and very friendly. And while this is the best hotel in Kathmandu it cannot be compared to other metropolitan accommodations. It is clean and comfortable. The dining room offers great meals. It is centrally located and the gardens are beautiful and well kept and quiet. There were a couple of very short electrical interruptions but nothing major. I would certainly stay there again.

I recently stayed at the Yak and Yeti and on checking into my room, I was surprised to find that the room smelled like a toilet. We immediately went to the reception and asked them to give us a change of room. Unfortunately, the hotel staff were far from hospitable and informed us that they didn't have another room until later. We were thus forced to go on our sightseeing tours without even being given privacy to change or freshen up. A really disappointing start to our holiday. Upon return, we were given our new room key without even an apology or any sense of remorse.

My son and I stayed at the Yak & Yeti for a four night stay. We found it extremely clean, with good facilities and very comfortable and in a very good location. The breakfast and evening meal options were wide and varied and well presented and tasty. We felt very safe and very much enjoyed our stay.

Oldest still the best hotel to stay in Kathmandu , big rooms , big gardens , well maintained , service is good , all basic amenities are provided in room , The dining area is too small for in house guest , especially during breakfast it becomes fish market and the quality of service and food goes down. The only thing which was pinching was no free WiFi , the charges were 935 Rupees Nepali for 24 hours. which is very steep for local Nepali standards , here you get 1 GB data on N cell mobile for 500 Nepali Rupees.

Lovely location everything in walking distance from shopping to restaurants and popular clubs .. premises was clean and safe, staffs were very attentive and always attended us from bell boys to guest services.

we stayed here at two different times during a recent trip to Nepal.   We enjoyed the hotel very much.   The location is good.   It is close to restaurants and good shopping and pretty close to the historic sites of Kathmandu.  The rooms were nice.   The food at breakfast and in the lobby bar was very good.   The service was also quite good.   We would stay again if we return.

The best calm hotel in Kathmandu, away from hustle bustle. The hotel is so beautiful and well maintained and well planned. Swimming pool adds to it's value. The staff is really very nice and helpful.  Good food is available here.

I stayed here for 1 night before my Himalaya trek and 2 nights after my trek. Good guest rooms and grounds. Very good breakfast. However, I was surprised that a hotel of this standard charges its guests for Wi-Fi. Also, as I booked this hotel as part of a package, the gym facilities were not included. This is very poor practice and does not promote the hotel in a positive way.

I have stayed at this hotel twice. Here are the good and bad things:The breakfast is average, the rooms are average and so is the washroom with the room. However, the property itself is a boutique hotel property, there is outdoor pool seating and the restaurant serves good food (especially Mughlai). The staff is very helpful.However do not book a car from the hotel's travel desk. They will fleece you to the extent of paying 20 USD per hour. Or 20USD for a trip that will be hardly 4-6 kms. Take a cab that is easily available out side the hotel.The hotel is located at Durbar Marg (very close to Thamel) which means you have plenty of options to eat out.

We stayed a few nights both before and after our EBC trek. Rooms were comfortable, as was the beds, but the room was warm and the bathroom plumbing was quite old. We enjoyed an expensive but delicious buffet lunch. Compared to the rest of the city, the Y+Y offered a nice respite from the dust with a very pretty garden area in which to enjoy the outdoors. Staff was very friendly. Hotel was conveniently located to the DarbarMarg area for good dining options.
British-style historical hotel.The garden was beautiful.Closed to bustling shopping and entertainment district、Kingsway、but the hotel area is quiet.Souvenir shops are also available around the hotel.

I stayed here in January 2017 for a couple of weeks on a business trip. The hotel has a very convenient location within Kathmandu. This is a good hotel for business travelers, but I did find the hotel a bit outdated. There is no air conditioner, just a heater. Housekeeping did provide me with a fan. The buffet food at the hotel is good, but I did tire from it pretty quickly. There are several very good restaurants within walking distance for lunch/dinner. We did hold conference events and the hotel did an excellent job. The conference facilities are within an old palace, so it is a very nice location and venue.

After our 10 day trek to ABC, we decided to treat ourselves to a fancy last night in Kathmandu.  The Yak and Yeti is an older hotel, but is well maintained. Our room was very comfortable and big. We had a nice little living area and spacious bathroom. There is a swimming pool and outside area but we did not get a chance to have a dip. The hotel restaurant is a bit pricey compared to what you can get in Thamel which is a 10 min walk away. The breakfast was also nice with a variety of food options. 'There was also a Casino called Casino Royale on the hotel grounds which our guide told us was for foreigners only. We did not go in so not sure what it is like. We had some lovely cocktails at the Piano Bar to celebrate our ABC trek and they gave us some snacks also. It is a very laid back and relaxing hotel and we almost did not leave the room to go out for dinner!

Hotel reasonable value for money. Staff friendly and helpful. Rooms rather dated and air conditioning not upto much. Reastuant quite good.. Hotel seemed to Ben having work done so oneumatic drills all day...unwelcome

For my travel reason, I will leave at 6:00 am in the next morning. but my package is include breakfast, when we talk to the reception they tell us may be we can not have the breakfast in the hotel. So, I ask what is they can do if I want to have breakfast. After them discuss they told me will prepare the breakfast box for me. the Breakfast box only include one apple, two bread, no boiled egg, but the inside is very simple. The hotel with great luxury deco, beautiful view, but service quality I believe have a great room to improve!

We have stayed at the Yak and Yeti for 9 nights, 2 before our trek to EBC and 7 after.  The staff, particularly the Sunrise Cafe staff, and the Guest Services staff (Shimila) have given us excellent service throughout our stay. They have gone above and beyond to make our stay a happy one.The rooms and bathrooms are clean and well appointed, the food is excellent, the swimming pool is clean and well maintained. The Yak and Yeti is very highly recommended if you are spending any time in Kathmandu

I stayed two nights in this hotel . Hotel lobbey and breakfast is awesome but rooms are quite old now and toiletries are very poor , even no comb is there and whatever you need you have to call them to provide in the toilet .Airport pick and drop facility is also not good . At the time of departure we reached 10 minutes late at hotel due to traffic jam in the city and hotel denied us to give the drop facility  to airport which was very bad experience from a five star hotel  . We called taxi and paid to taxi to drop us airport . casino is very very old and all machines are quite old . Inside casino service to players is also poor they don't care the orders .  Rollet machine is very poor and old even not visible board . We enjoyed in Radision which is new and fantastic service .

We did not stay at this hotel, but having heard so much about it,  went for lunch.  It turned out to be a luxurious buffet with a huge spread of delicious breads, cheeses, meats,  soup, fish, meat, a full dessert buffet and every kind of cuisine.  We sat overlooking the beautiful pool and gardens and were pleased to be seated between two tables of apparently senior monks.  When they finished, the staff bowed and made it clear they were very pleased o have e served these individuals.  They were very solicitous of us, too, but without the bowing.  It was a great place to have lunch in the midst of some serious shopping close by.  Very secure, delicious food.

On the first stay the AC in the room did not work. While this was fixed the manager was extremely dismissive of the issue. On the second stay we were upgraded to a suite, which smelled like cigarettes and did not have any international adapters. Nor were any available upon request from the front desk. The front desk assured me they could charge my device and after returning after 1 hour my device had not been charged and had in fact lost power. Finally the Wifi Cost 10 US dollars for 24 hours which is outrageous, considering that each of the 7 hotels we have stayed at within Nepal offered free Wifi at much higher speeds. I would not recommend this hotel

The hotel is located centrally with easy access to the main areas of Darbar Sqaure and Thamel...the Hotel is one of the old property with huge out areas including pool and landscaping with walking  tracks and also has an In House Casino for the ones interested in it.The room i stayed was the park /pool facing and hence enjoyable. I felt the hotel needs to upgrade/change the carpeting of the floor as they have become really old. The house keeping, rooms and food were fine .The Hotel has a spa but slightly overpriced for the services offered.The front staff could be slightly more responsive to the guests .Overall good for few days of stay in Nepal.

Yak & Yeti is a great hotel located a short walk from the Thamel district and down the street from the Palace Museum.  Both worth a visit. It would be nice if the wifi was free but otherwise the hotel staff was very helpful and the rooms were very nice.

we had just complete our Nepal trip and got a this hotel to spent our time. this hotel is in perfect location. full of facilitates with friendly staffs are recommendation. Next time this hotl will be in my first choice.

I have now stayed four times at the Yak & Yeti. I love this hotel, its style, history, food and quality of service. The breakfast buffet is amazing, with a mix of local, regional and international foods. The restaurant has views of the garden, an oasis in an otherwise busy and polluted city. Make sure you book one of the heritage rooms with the beautiful Nepalese wood carvings. They are worth the additional money.The hotel used to charge for WiFi, but this is now provided free of charge, which is a great improvement.

The location is very good. Easy to get to all the attractions. Nice restaurants nearby. The garden is very peaceful and pretty. The service at the hotel is very good. The rooms are nicely decorated in the Nepali style. Niche breakfast options. Also free shuttle service to the airport.

Let me explain my title first - this hotel is really good, but only considered that it is in a very poor location where good and bad have different meaning, so if I compare it to a really good hotel somewhere in the developed world, that one will be average to poor rated by me.What is good - comparatively clean and with a good, central location. Two not bad restaurants, one of which is a fine dining place with a really stunning wine list!!! The personnel are friendly and helpful, though some of the young staff need additional training, on serving and products. There is constant hot running water - a blessing after a trekking in the Himalayas! What is not good - the rooms are old, very old and need renovation and refurbishment. The bar closes very early and the garden is not in its perfect shape. Could be easily improved, the basis is there. The internet connection is payed additionally.

Nice location and ambiance, worth the money spent. Range of breakfast items was excellent, however, daily serving of Mango & Litchi Juice was boring and either orange or mixed fruit should be provided.

Hotel looks great and staff is efficient and dedicated. While the rooms look great their comfort could be slightly improved xoth better Wifi and the usual amenities. Hotel was crowded of groups of trekkers and, in particular breakfast areas was noisy.

All was fine the  only problem  the room was too hot.The thermometer pointed out 26ªC. I report to the reception desk but the situation was not modified.Very good breakfast. Excellent bed . Beatiful garden.

Yak & Yeti is an iconic hotel in the heart of Kathmandu but it has not been refurbished for many a year. The rooms are old and musty. Breakfast is monotonous for anyone with a western appetite. Staff are friendly and courteous.

It is better to be back in this hotel and my guests from Rome were also very happy to be here. Nice room overlooking garden and swimming pool, excellent variety of breakfast and nice people are all add value for money. We also got complementary fruit basket and sauna/zaccuzi facilities but disappointed and found discriminatory to national guests are not offered complementary transport service to domestic airport. People gets bad experience at the time of departure when it will not add any extra cost. In this case Hotel Del Mount Annapurna is much accommodative. Avoid room service -they are expensive and not good. Better to take in restaurant or eat out. The meeting is well managed and social dinner is also well organised in poolside. Shower and toilet pans are improved. Overall no regrets to be back here and the place is quite lively.

I stayed in Hotel Yak and Yeti for the first time to meet my friend who came to nepal to have a trekking. The hotel was good and the staffs were kind. The room was clean and well equipped. But, the toilet flush was not working. I requested the repair of the flush. It was immediately fixed. The restaurant on the first floor serves a variety of foods. The yogurt was too spicy, though. In general the hotel is worth the price and I wat to stay there nstay another time.

Nice location beautiful building and lawns. Nice rooms good bar. The facility is a little used but still functional. Considering its in Nepal it is 5 star. Front desk was strange when checking in but friendly and helpful. Stay there for sure

I loved staying at the Yak and Yeti.  The location is extremely convenient for government, sightseeing, interesting parts of the city for strolls as well as phone stores, banks and cafes.  I must say, my favorite part of this beautiful and comfortable hotel was the wine bar.  They have the most comfortable corners from which you can people watch, read or catch up on emails with attentive staff and great happy hours.  Please do take some time to visit the older parts of the hotel and their very special restaurant. It's a memorable dining experience.

returned last year as part of a month long trip to this part of the world loved the hotel nothing was too much trouble i was back and forth via Bhutan Tibet and Indian,everything from food laundry service to storing my bags was all done in a excellent manner I shall be returning this year and look forward to a cold bottle of beer

I can't say enough about the Yak and Yeti. Anyone around town who we mentioned it to was very impressed that we were staying there. A neurosurgeon conference was being held while we were staying there and then when we came back for our second stay, heads of state were staying there. The staff bent over backwards in every way, extra water, transfers to and from the airport, money exchange, early check in, answering any questions, handing our luggage. By our second stay, we felt like we were coming home to our favorite little hotel. The shops connected to the hotel had surprisingly good prices when compared to around town. And we had a great dinner at the Chimney restaurant in the hotel. But to be honest, the real reason to stay here is the buffet dining for breakfast, lunch or dinner. And I don't usually like buffets. First of all, the breakfast was included in the room price. They have a huge selection of excellent food from all over the world: Mediterranean, Chinese, Middle East, American and more. Salads and fresh fruit abound. Since it was my first time in Nepal, and I wasn't sure about the food, facilities or cleanliness of the places we'd be visiting, it was always nice to know I could count on the Yak & Yeti. On our second stay they even upgraded us to the Business floor that had really nice extra amenities, including a small private breakfast room. The grounds were well tended and beautiful to look at. And the steam, sauna and massage were great after a long flight. I fell in love and I hope you do too.

Excellent stay, little problem with the shower which should be replaced.Would love to come back. Food was very good. Hotel transport charges are very high. Should charge less as people coming for official tours find it difficult.

Good place to stay when you are on a business trip. Food is awesome with a great variety of Indian, Continental and Chinese options for all meals. The high point is the idyllic garden where you can refresh yourself with a drink  or two after a hectic day.

The room that we got after we checked in was a big surprise.  The shower curtain for the tub in our bathroom was not closing properly and the water was flooding out.  When we complained, they moved us to a different and better room.  Except for this initial surprise, the stay overall was very pleasant and enjoyable.  The staff is very service conscious and responsive to every request for assistance like planning travel arrangements, helping map trips around Kathmandu, and literally any request that you have.  One of the staff members, Sharmila, exemplified this by helping us plan a trip to Nagarkot at 10:00 PM in the night!  The other good features of the hotel are an excellent breakfast service with more than 30 items from several cuisines with some of them changing everyday.  And, the best part is their location which has excellent access to Thamel which has great shopping, Durbar Square - a must see old part of Kathmandu, and taxis. Overall, we really enjoyed our nearly one-week stay there.

Excellent hotel. The hotel is very clean. The design is unique. The staff is very helpful. The breakfast is good. Location is very central, many nearby restaurants. Overall, it is a very good and recommended hotel.

This hotel is centrally located and walking distance from Thamel and next to Durbar marg. Its great 5 star property but I feel it's too expensive for facilities it's offering. Per night room rate is USD 240. One can find lot of better places around this place. Staff is helpful , stay was pleasant.  Room service staff was excellent. Front desk experience was average. I was attending an event here & would like to inform hotel management that banquet hall arrangement are POOR.  I would not recommend this hotel at all for any event. Chairs are damaged and bad shape. One of senior citizen fell down while session was going on.. This is  very very sadThis property will be great if priced at USD 100

We had a great time during our stay at Yak and Yeti, kathmandu. The location of the hotel is very convenient, most of the attractions are near by and thamel, by lanes of which I enjoyed tremendously, just10 minutes away. Hotel staff is extremely friendly and helpful. Specially Ms. Sharmila, who went out of her way to make our stay comfortable, and the hotel manager Mr. Harsh, who was always helpful in sorting out any small issues. Food is great with lots of variety, we enjoyed the cocktails. All in all, a very good choice, would love to go back again sometime soon.

quiet and friendly spot in dirty and airpolluted Kathmandu, excellent restaurant with open fire place,  helpful staff, diversified breakfast - breakfast-box unfortunately less good, free newspaper, perfect laundry service

beautiful building and servicesare very good. very nice breakfast. quite and very peaceful inviroment. you can swim or hangout in garden. gardens are so big. perfect stay in kathmandu. comfortables rooms .

High services quality, food and beautiful building and garden. Wide choice for breakfast, silent, clean and comfortable. Wide rooms and bathroom, very clean.Close to Kathmandu centre, rather expansive but it worth the cost.

The Yak and Yeti is a meeting place for diplomats, adventure treks, mountain climbers, business people, and touristsThe holtel's manager and staff take pride in ensuring that the Yak and Yeti provides a cultural window.Great grounds, architecture, and professional staff ensure that no detail is to small for attention.A great hotel!Great people!

Mediocre location with scary busy streets to be crossed to get to Thamel and other more interesting areas of Kathmandu.  I was not impressed with extra charges for things that should be included (gym and jacuzzi).  The water was rusty and/or yellow colored at all times.  Free bottled water was nice and the staff was very attentive and helpful.

I visit Nepal at least three times a year on business and the Yak & Yeti always provides a home away from home. The friendly staff are always there to giving a helping hand whenever asked. Harsh the assistant manager front office is always there to solve any problems and offer advise for restaurants,sightseeing or anything you may need in the hotel.The rooms were recently renovated and offer comfort at a very affordable price.Next time you visit Kathmandu make the Yak & Yeti your choice. Its definitely worth a  stay.

nice facilities. they have a very good breakfast spread, with delicious fresh fruit as well as fresh juice. the staff is very friendly and accommodating, even giving a free late checkout when I asked. they have beautiful grounds, definitely take a walk around the property and relax at a table outside by the pool or on the lawn.

Good location with walking distance to "garden of dream", multiple restaurant choice available near by,  pretty hotel garden, room with beautiful wood carving decoration, no response for inquiry made on website, food is just fine, no travel guild leaflet

I think I have said it all...I would definitely recommend this hotel...also, the location was very convenient for us...and another bonus...free shuttle to and from the airport, with very nice service from the drivers

This hotel was amazing. The staff was amazing. The property was heavily guarded and the guest services desk was great at getting you anything you need. Bar in the lobby with a very wide selection and a great restaurant to match. Free wifi and the pool was very clean and well maintained. Will definitely stay here again when we return to Kathmandu.

Good lifts, bed and room are ok, but as you'd expect the bathrooms are a bit ancient. Breakfast was ok (nothing special) The staff at the bar area and on reception were on the ball. there seemed to be a lot of NGO types or people about to go off trekking or on tours.

Lovely hotel, great breakfasts and nice rooms. We stayed here before and after an Everest basecamp trek. KE adventure booked us in and we upgraded the room for the last 2 nights. Very clean, very quiet.

Great staff ,very helpful going beyond and above to help you in every need!!especially guest desk services ms Sharmila Rai excellent host!!!Cleaningness needs a bit improvement,in spa area,alsoonly on Shangri La level you get amenities.Great location

Nothing wrong at all with this hotel. Super friendly staff, great common areas. Convenient location that is walkable to most places you want to be in Kathmandu...Just be aware that the rooms are a little on the older side - This is not a new hotel.

Good value, well located, very friendly and accommodating staff A long time visitor who would like to see a little upgrading of the facilities and furnishings Staff was very helpful arranging airport pickups

We stayed here at the last day of our stay, I can say you can feel the 5 star in their but not quite what I was expected, I think the place just needs renovations.Big thanx to the Manager Philip for his effort he has done for us so we get the room we asked for.Don't be fooled by the picture of the hotel as the rooms looks a bet older.

The staying in the Yak hotel was very pleasant and enjoyable for me. We liked the location very much. The service people everywhere were very nice and polite. We liked the breakfast very much. I have stayed last year 4 times

Ground floor room with a view over the garden was lovely.  However lots of noise from next room - walls are very thin.  Staff very helpful and polite. Food is good, lots of choices at breakfast.  Lovely kept gardens with a small swimming pool with outside bar but it took quite a while to get a cup of tea and a beer. Good location, private and secure within walking distance of Thamel and Durbar Square.  Short taxi ride to airport.Not much character for a Kathmandu hotel.

I was staying here for 4 nights in January. The hotel is beautiful (minimalist yet comfortable). Day one I found the rooms to be really dark as they don't have enough lights in the room but then eventually you get used to it. For the pricing - it is totally worth it. Big celebs and business officials stay here and genuinely the staff is very welcoming apart from people of Nepal being friendly and nice...

Kathmandu is one of the most vibrant and colorful cities in the world, and anyone visiting should be pleased with the Yak & Yeti. It's distinctive name is surpassed only by it's welcoming environment, wonderful location and the great service provided by a friendly staff, committed to your comfort.  I've stayed in hotels around the world, from zero to five stars, and the Y&Y is every bit as unique and wonderful as any of them.  And the price is beyond compare.  I won't stay anywhere else in Kathmandu, and I don't think twice about booking this hotel.  I'm not so easy to  impress, but I'm always pleased with my time at the Yak and Yeti.  The experience is as unforgettable as the name.

We had such a lovely time in the hotel firstly with the friendly staff who are happy to help, with a smile no matter what your request. The surrounds are well kept and beautiful and despite being so close to the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu, it feels like a quiet oasis away from it all!

Very nice hotel with great staff and comfortable rooms. Great breakfast buffet with many items to choose from. A few things for me were a little off.1: bar shorted alcohol content in drinks.2: dinner staff not familiar with menu or lack of English posed a problem. 3: for a 5 star hotel you have to pay for Wi- Fi.

We been there on last August - it was a wonderful experience as usual.  Nice deco, clean rooms, delicious food and friendly staff member.  It was a good value of money.  Strongly recommend to my friends to stay there if you planning to visit Kathmandu ?!

Not a bad hotel, service minded staff in both the hotel as well as the hotel bar. The restaurant was mediocre though. The breakfast was somewhat lacking of options and for dinner the buffet was a strange combination of foods. The worst part though was that the Indian Curries of some 6 only one contained meat which meant that this dish was constantly empty.

Location is really good walking distance to main site and markets. beautifully grounds and hotel, lovely restaurants and good services. 5 mins walk from palace museam and 2 min walk from brand shop high street and 20min walk to Temple markets and dream garden. very good location as can get round everywhere by walking so good cost saving on transport

Our tour operator, MyTrip2Nepal recommended this Hotel. Found it to be very good in almost every aspect. Nice outside garden with a walking trek. Very nice rooms. The Yak is obvious but the Yeti, threw us off.  Actually, it is a superstitious mythlogical animal.

As compared to the other services that you will find in Kathmandu, Yak and Yeti is definitely a better option. The location is great.. very close to Thamel and other leading food joints.. There's a casino in the same campus so that's quite convenient.. I was specially impressed by the interiors and large lawns to just bask in the sun.. Yak and Yeti mostly has all the basic amenities.. Rooms are clean and adequate for two people.. Room service is slightly slow but again the staff is quite humble.. Also right outside the hotel there are a few shops where you can buy good stuff for a decent price if you want to avoid the crowded streets of Kathmandu.. I managed to get couple of beautiful paintings for a great deal!!

A good four star hotel in Kathmandu with an international standard feel - a rare treat in Kathmandu.The hotel is next to an old palace (which doesn't have any hotel rooms unfortunately) and what is probably Nepal's only casino (give it a miss). The building appears a bit dated from the outside, however the interior has been renovated and is of a high standard. The check in and welcome procedure was seamless; my room had excellent wooden features, and the bathroom was excellent.The only let down was the buffet breakfast, which was too focused on subcontinental and broader Asian cuisine, and didn't have any western favourites like bacon and sausages.All up, a good hotel for the price, and good location - a few minutes walk to the former royal palace, and about 10 minutes' walk to the Thames area.

Excellent service, staff is very sweet and helpful. Chef helps to coook what you want to eat. Close to downtown. It's a home away from home! Very safe place and they take outstanding care of guests. .

Old hotel, still acceptable, but in need of refurbishing. Will definitively select another one for my next visit. Food & beverage at the bar are expensive and not worthy. You have to pay for internet, which is not acceptable for the price you pay for the room alone.

Great staff! Check-in is easy. This is a good, but getting dated, hotel in Nepal. I have stayed here several times.  I have also stayed at the Radisson in Kathmandu as well.If you want to compare to 5 star in Europe or the US, then you have incorrect expectations on both price (much lower here) and accommodation.The bed is very comfortable, the shower is strong and hot, the Internet is good, the buffet is good with western and non-western food. Many types of juices are available for breakfast. If you need laundry done, this is your place!Ask for room on garden/pool side of hotel.

Excellent location for downtown and close to restaurants shops and cultural attractions.  Clean and comfortable rooms with easy check in and check out. Great service.  The food at the breakfast and dinner buffet was excellent. The grounds and pool were beautiful. Only place to stay in Kathmandu. I would have no reservations recommending this hotel for those planning a trek.

Very nice and big hotel special arrangement for meetings and best suited for business meetings.also have casino and open garden for dinners and lunch.really nice place.we have done one meeting here with one of our client.hotel staff is also very customer friendly.its also very near to Indian ambessy .really good place for you also for organising marriage and functions

We stayed at Yak and Yeti hotel, Kathmandu Nepal for one night at the end of December 2016. The hotel shuttle picked us up from the airport.  The hotel grounds are beautiful and the interior is serviceable. It is an old hotel with newer additions.  We stayed in second floor adjoining rooms. The stuff were very friendly.  The breakfast was very good with multiple ethnic choices: continental, Nepali and Indian cuisines. The garden at the back is perfect for morning walk.

The Hotel Staff at the Yak & Yeti were extremely helpful and attentive. Very nice historical hotel, on a gracious property to be explored in itself. Great place to stay while in Kathmandu. The Hotel is set inside of secured gates, making it a bit of a compound. A bit of an oasis inside the chaos of the city traffic and busy streets and shops. The restaurant and lobby bar are also exceptional, with great food and drink, supported by their continued great staff.

I have been guest of Yak and Yeti on several occasions and I will continue to stay there, being in Nepal for my job. The Hotel itself is very beautiful, with its own character and history, very different from that kind of anonymous hotels you can find in other cities of the world and which are often soulless. But the strongest point in this Hotel is - in my opinion - the kindness and the professional competence of the staff. It is due not only to the well known Nepali hospitality, but also to a deep and refined ability to understand the needs of the customers. Absolutely astonishing.

It was nice to retreat here after finishing a hectic tour of India and Nepal. The entire hotel and the rooms are clean and beautiful. The staff were efficient and the included breakfast was plentiful. We didn't realise this was quite an 'up market hotel' and felt a little out of place, but nonetheless we enjoyed our stay here. It is a short walk into the main area of town to access shopping and restaurants (or roughly $2-3AUS to hire a taxi). My only gripe is that we were required to pay an additional $10/day for wifi which was displeasing considering the nightly rate.

I have stayed at the Yak & Yeti on several occasions over the last five years and I have always had a great experience. We were here for business and the rooms were coordinated for ahead of time. At our arrival they collected our passports and we waited in the area that looks like a gazebo. The staff provided refreshments and our whole party was in their rooms within 20 minutes of arrival.The rooms were adequate. I stayed in a room with two twin beds. The room is older, but well maintained. The bathroom was clean and there was plenty of hot water. The room comes with two .5 liter bottles of water and coffee/tea complimentary. There is also a hotpot and tv in the room. The room also contains a travel safe.The staff was excellent. The maid service did an excellent job every day and there weren't too many intrusions. The front desk was helpful with information and their exchange rate was decent.The breakfast was buffet style. They had a good variety. I wish they did eggs to order and that they had the coffee prepared earlier for those of us that rise early.The hotel provides good security with two manned gates at all times.The hotel is also located off the main path, but still close enough to Thamel for shopping and restaurants. It is only about a 10 minute walk.Overall, I would say if you are not on a budget that this is a very nice place to stay if you are in Kathmandu.
