We were in Kathmandu for vacation.Had nice time.Stay was comfortable.Location is excellent it's in center of the city, transport easily available,lots of good cafes and restaurants nearby, walking distance from Thamel the most happening area.

Visited KATHMANDU n stayed in YAK n YETI n was happy to be greeted by sweet n hospitable Mm JANISON. It's a good hotel with good Indian Breakfast n services. Hotel is too old n looks TIRED n RETIRED but has good huge property n with ambience. Needs REFURBISHMENT in true 5 STAR STYLE as it is not befitting for this status. Seems best hotel to stay n KATHMANDU with EXCELLENT location.

I have stayed thirteen times at the Yak & Yeti over a period of seven years: these stays have normally been for a month or more on business.  On every occasion the service has been outstanding: personal, friendly and helpful at all times. The dining room (both buffet and a la carte) has been excellent. Rooms are comfortable and convenient for work or leisure. The garden is a haven in a busy city, with attractive trees and water feature and a convenient three hundred meter jogging track. My wife has often accompanied me and has always been welcomed and comfortable.

This was my fourth visit to this hotel and again it did not disappoint. The staff are very welcoming, friendly and efficient throughout all the services in this hotel. Stayed in the Heritage-Deluxe room and it was fabulous in size and comfort and overlooking the garden and pool area. The breakfast is excellent and a large variety of different foods both hot and cold.A wonderful place to spend the Christmas/ New Year. Excellent location and will definitely be returning

The hotel is in a prime location and is very suitable for family trips. The service is excellent and the hospitality of the staff is very good. The rooms are a little small for families but the maintenance is very good.  We will be visiting there more often.

Needs improvements and customer service & focus. The restaurant, too many heads running around but the main service is ignored . The internet pretty slow. But over all the hotel is warm and friendly. The staff are pretty nice and helpful.

This place is clearly overrated and has seen better days. the rooms have a jaded look and are in need of a renovation. The service is of less than average quality in terms of promptness as well as courtesy. I have seen a constant decline in its standards over the years that i have stayed here. The food quality has come down and lacks freshness. This time, my wife had food poisoning despite the fact that we never ate outside of hotel. It is overpriced for the services that it currently offers. I would avoid it in future visits.

We had a very nice trip in Kathmandu, ppl there are very friendly, I love their smile, the rooms are clean, the food & drinks are great, and I've recommended it to my friends. We are sure that if the price could go down a little bit, it would be more attractive and competitive in the local market. By then more and more groups will choose Yak & Yeti instead of others.

During my recent visit to Kathmandu I stayed at Yak and Yeti . I stayed in many other hotels in Kathmandu but this was my first stay here. Location is excellent , you can take a stroll in the evening ,do some window shopping and try some local food . Staff at the hotel was very friendly and always there to assist . For a traveler like me, a good breakfast buffet set a happy day and surely the breakfast was good starter of the day.  As the entire hotel is not renovated yet, you should ask for the new rooms .

Stayed only one night before flight back to the States. A beautiful property with attentive and courteous staff. Excellent menu options in on site restaurants ND room service. Room very clean ND well appointed. Would stay again. Highly recommend.

I really enjoyed my stay here.  from pick up at the airport to delivery back, everything was great.  The location is excellent as is the gym and spa.  The gardens are a pleasure to walk around in at night and food is good, although expensive. I would stay here again.

I stayed at the Yak and Yeti after my tour to Everest Base Camp was cut short due to illness.  My insurance company put me in this hotel and after a long day of being flown back from Namche Bazar to Kathmandu in a helicopter and being taken to hospital I was pleasantly surprised at how easy it was to check in and how welcoming the staff were.  I was on the business floor and the staff were absolutely amazing, they made me hot drinks with honey and ginger to help with my illness and always asked how I was.  The service was so personalized it was amazing, my flight back to Australia was at 11:15pm and check out was 12pm, I was just going to wait at the airport but instead my check out time was extended until 4pm free of charge.  The rooms were lovely and the food was great, can't talk highly enough of this amazing hotel!

The hotel itself is beautiful, with well-manicured lawns and even a small pond where I met a goose and a duck. There is lush greenery, which would delight guests, amid the dust-filled road outside; thus I guess the word sanctuary might be apt. Breakfast buffet is adequate - descriptions like "amazing, tantalising, wide-ranging spread" do not apply. Every service staff is discrete and courteous, except for one housekeeping staff. Ten feet from my room door was the cart with the staff in front of it. I approached him asking for toothbrush and toothpaste (which was not provided in the bathroom); spoiling for a tip, he insisted that I go into my room and he will bring it to me. As I pointed out the ridiculousness of the situation, he gave me the toothbrush, and repeated his request that I go into the room and wait for him. There I was, toothbrush in hand, arguing with the Housekeeping staff; only did he then, rather reluctantly, give me the toothpaste, which incidentally came from the same place as the toothbrush! However, I must insist that this person was the exception, rather than the norm.What I enjoyed most about the room is the bed, which I found to be very comfortable. However it is an old hotel, and the rest of the room, including the bathroom, is not in the best condition – I would describe it as “fading”. What I disliked most is the water coming out of the shower is light-brownish, and the bathtub is old and stained. I would definitely refer to the rooms as being part of a four-star hotel. Location depends on which area of Kathmandu you want to visit. If you want to shop in Thamel, you can walk there in about 20 minutes. If you want to go to Boudhanath, it is quite a distance away. I booked a van for 6 people with luggage to take me to another hotel in Boudhanath with Yak and Yeti's car service, and they charged US$35.Those with a lot of devices will be in for a disappointment. Free wifi is restricted to 2 devices per room. So if have two persons, you cannot both have your laptops and phones connected. For three persons sharing a room, two phones only!

Hotel is old and I am not quite comfortable with their room. Room facilities  and amenities are incomplete which I believe is not worth with the rate I got. I stay their for 5 nights and I did not even get a toothbrush and toothpaste. Would you not believe that I am using one piece of bath soap for 5 nights, good thing I have brought some detol soap with me. Hotel staff are not friendly  and they did not even greet you , they will just look at you. My overall hotel staying experience is unsatisfactory. I will not definitely return to that hotel. I will rather stay at Annapurna Hotel.

Simply amazing! From our transfer to the hotel to complimentary drinks and evening canapés, yak and yeti did not disappoint. We stayed here before embarking on Everest base camp and our stay was just what we needed before the long trek. If you want to enjoy uncompromising customer service with friendly staff and amazing fascilities,  I highly recommend a night or two at this Nepalese gem. A big shout out to Bhakta - an amazing man with incredible knowledge!

Love the service, GREAT staff, & public spaces. We got the old deluxe wing room, bed was comfortable..next stay booked the heritage room in the new wing. Piano Bar Lounge is great to just chill & relax & have a drink! Breakfast was 👌🏼

My husband and I stayed 2 nights at Yak & Yeti, when arriving and when leaving Kathmandu. We enjoyed very much Yak & Yeti for its quietness, good location, clean rooms and helpfulness of the staff.The first room we have was a small studio/suite, which was more modern and clean than the 2nd room with a queen bed, in the older portion. We had twice the Saturday brunch, with an impressive choice of Indian, western and arabic foods. We were stunned by the level of variety and attention given to prepare this buffet.

Good hotel, with all facility, nice people, food was very nice specially vegetarian, natural fruits was available. Location is very nice, we can enjoy with family in swimming fool, calm and quite area, best for Yoga and meditation even your not in this mood it will give you peas.

Our National Geographic Expedition tour of Tibet and Nepal wound up at the Y&Y.The staff of the concierge floor was welcoming and responsive. The Chimney restaurant hostedour farewell dinner ad the food and service was outstanding.. I recommend the hotel highly, it wasan oasis in the teeming bustle of Katmandu.

peaceful and comfortable stay, superb room services, quality of food was very good, room was very nice decorative, well managed, honest management of casino, cooperative staff, i was very impressed during the welcome moment, love to visit again very very nice and lovely stay.

This is a wonderfully done flagship hotel in the city. The rooms are good and some of the facilities such as conference rooms are done in very elegant way in gothic style. The quality of services varies. For example, the food served during lunch in its Sunrise restaurant was average on day 1 but much improved on day 2. I was a bit surprised how such drastic variation happens. Day3, it was fine. The items they do well are Indian Dals and Cottage cheese preparations but breads are dampener. Menu, again repeated. The sweets are quite a few but almost similar. The cost of stay is high but the price offered for buffet lunch and dinner are very reasonable.

Comfortable, friendly and very clean. The staff was extremely helpful and was always looking to improve my stay. The breakfast was included in the cost and was outstanding. Felt safe and secure at the Yak, right in the middle of the hustle and bustle of the crazy traffic in Kathmandu.

Yak & Yeti is perfectly located, has a nice ambiance of platform for departing and returning upscale trekker. Was there for a fair and everything was perfectly organized.I was upgraded because my room category was not available. Nice room, though looking a bit oldish.

Yak and Yeti hotel is great for getting away from the hectic streetlife of Kathmandu.The private park with pool and walking path is nice. The food is good (bufé restaurant) and breakfast is really good.Coming back from a trek in the Everest region, sleeping in good beds and eating good food was excellent. The staff was really helpful and the location good (15 min walk from Thamel district).Shopping street right outside the hotel.

First visit to this hotel and will definately recommend it to everyone. Being a single lady traveller i didnt actually feel alone. All the staffs here since the beginning as they werr there to pick me frm airport and till the end of my check out date were very helpful, always with a huge smile in there faces to welcome everyone. Definately will be back with family.

Good hotel with great location. Was there for marriage function couple of days early, the hospitality was superb. Landscape of garden and swimming pool is great. Will definitely come back again for fun time with family.

The staff in front desk are friendly and polite and they made us feel very welcome. We had a nice stay.  we are a breakfast lover. The hotel served a great breakfast. The front desk staffs made us feel very welcome and comfortable. We will definitely visit it again.Thank you hotel Yak and Yeti.

The room was very spacious. i really like the room of this hotel. And the GRE of hotel are very good. They really help me out during my stay. Even i had smartphone, I asked them the direction of places and they explain it so well. One of the GRE had help me alot. I missed my shuttle service to airport, and i was bit panicked, But she calm me down and arrange me the another one. I really wanna to thank everyone of yak and yeti. And I would like to stay there when i visit next time too.

Yak and yeti is centrally located. Room are clean and nice decorated. Front desk staff are very nice, friendly, cooperative and  helpful. We had dinner at chimney resturant which was classic and suberb. Garden is beautiful with jogging track. Satisfied with service and hospitality. Will definately stay this hotel on next visit.

Stayed as part of trek group in Nov 2016. Rooms vary a lot from being  in need of a spruce up (ground floor) to very respectable (4th floor Club VIP), but all are clean and linens fine (a rarity in Nepal). Staff v attentive, good breakfasts, great location. Sadly no free WiFi, which I find incredible for a hotel that aims to be luxury.

The hotel's location their staffs and the services was top of the pack. Everything was positive and the stay went perfect and as planned. We loved the experience,specially the guest relation was very helpful.

I was there to meet one of my clients. I found that hotel staff are very friendly and helpful. i love the location and the way they responded was simply great. I definitely recommend for business visit.

My trip to this hotel was marvelous. Actually I was not expecting that quality services and rooms. But i was amazed by the services and rooms that the hotel has. The staffs were so good, room was spectacular and the quality of food, it was amazing. I would love to visit this hotel again. soon very soon

My stay at the Yak and Yeti began with a complimentary upgrade to a suite and continued to exceed my expectations throughout my stay.  The hotel is peaceful, well equipped and the staff helpful and the bed was so comfy!  As a woman staying alone, I felt safe at all times.    Would not hesitate to recommend.

Very nice  hotel.  All the staff were friendly and attentive. Very clean through out. Would  definitely recommend. The surrounding area of  kathmandu is in my opinion quite unique. You must  go walk about to take in the local  way of life.

i stayed here for couple of days and i had a great time. the food, the service and everything else. i must say its one of the best hotels in kathmandu to stay. if you guys plan to visit Nepal and want to stay in this hotel its the best.

We spent several nights at The Yak and Yeti during our stay in Kathmandu.  The rooms were spacious, clean and well appointed.  The entire staff was friendly, attentive and went out of their way to accommodate any request.  There is a beautiful garden and pool out back.  It was quiet and yet centrally located.  We really enjoyed our stay.

We had a night here at each end of our trip to Bhutan. It is a big, smart hotel but the first room we had was a little bit shabby ....possibly because it was in the older part of the hotel. The second room, on our return 3 weeks later, was bright, clean and very pleasant. It was also in the newest part of the hotel.The hotel is well placed centrally in Kathmandu within easy walking distance of the main sights. It also has an excellent garden and outdoor pool if you just want to relax after the chaos and noise of Kathmandu.The service is excellent. The food is a multicultural buffet of good quality or you can go a la carte for your evening meal - again very high quality anda  good choice range.My only gripe that the wifi is not free ....unless you happen to spot the tiny sign on the piano near the bar that states you can have 2 hours free wifi if you buy 2 drinks, excluding tea! Given that this is a 4* hotel which is excellent in every other way, not having free wifi was not a good move on the part of the mangement!

As various reviewers have noted, this hotel is centrally located, expansive, and convenient. It has restaurants, pool, spa, health club, convention center and a Casino as well. However, the wing I stayed in was looking slightly run down; possible because it is an old hotel. The service levels were excellent and the staff was very responsive. Allin all, it is a very good hotel.

Good hotel staff, very friendly.specially staffs in  executive lounge are very much helpful. They have distinctively answered my inquiries  without being reluctant. Which generated a very positive vibe in me untill the last day of my stay. Really enjoy.

Had a wonderful and remarkable stay  Service was superior and beyond expectations. To be more specific, staffs in club lounge were completely professional and Generous. Loved the Hotel! Best hotel to feel good on your stay.

The property is tremendous. The hotel staffs are very friendly and attentive. The hotel has a serene vibe and the garden is truely beautiful. A perfect holiday destination with delicious food, good location and wonderful staffs.

I stayed in this hotel for three nights.Built on a huge premises and in the heart of the city , Kathmandu.The infrastucturae is very commendable.Best suited for conferences,seminars,workshops and meetings.A variety of Social and business events can be very comfortably organised.The special attraction is Casino Royal within the hotel premises.The hotel is equipped with Fitness centre and Pub bar.The hotel maintains Business centre to cater to the business needs.Check in process is very smooth due the pre arrangement made by the local contacts.My room tariff includes complimentary breakfast,free wi-fi,complimentary two way airport transfers etc. Fruit basket in the room on the day of arrival,daily news paper on demand,Tea/coffee making facility in the room are added advantages.I was offered to upgrade to Heritage Deluxe at the time of booking,But that was not honoured at the time of check in.Regular Deluxe room is allotted.I was satisfied with the size of the room,bed linen,two complimentary drinking water bottles etc. But I was thouroughly disappointed with the very old Bath Tub which give indecent look and torn Bath towels.( I am resisting from uploading these two photos of Bath tub and towels.)I am not satisfied with the amenities in the room.Bat soap is not replaced for three days.Of course i did not look for any additional amenities.There is a great scope for the house keeping and room service to improve their services.Sunrise restaurant offers breakfast.Well spread over.Caters to different tastes.Excellent jogging track is available.Out door swimming pool is also added attraction..Well maintained lawns prompts to organise evening parties and get togethers.I enjoyed my stay there.

Very nice hotel which after trekking in the Himalayas for three weeks felt like a ten star hotel ! Nice staff and spacious bedrooms with good bathrooms, bar area nice with good gardens and a swimming pool though not many chairs and tables in the garden. The hotel is in very spacious grounds away from the chaos of Kathmandu but ask for a room overlooking the gardens at the rear to avoid the nightclub which plays loud music at the front.

A great stay as always. I've used this hotel fir many years and always remained completely satisfied. The rooms are niw vey nice after the rennivation and the staff always polite and helpful. A special thanks to Bhadri in the restaurant who aleays looks after me and Harsha the duty  manager always willing to go that extra mile to help. Many thanks and see you again in a few months on my next visit.

We stayed right in the heart of Kathmandu near (but not in) the bustling touristy area of Thamel. Yak and Yeti was perfect as it was a quiet respite with a large gated courtyard with trees and flowers and a pool. An island in the midst of chaos. all day buffet offered fantastic choices of food with fresh fruit, vegetables and different ethnic cuisines. Slightly expensive but well worth it. Excellent service.

As a member of the Nirvana health club, and a local resident, I can say that as far as 5-sstar hotels go in KTM, this is my favorite. All the facilities are here, but what makes the place is the great staff. Fantastic! .

There is no free wifi. To get wifi, buy a bar drink and get an hour free. Or pay $9 for 24 hr usage. Several times one of the two elevators was out of service. Hotel gift shops are expensive but prices are negotiable.  Shops are also close by the hotel and can easily be walked to.  Easy to get money exchanged at front desk. Breakfast lacks many standard American breakfast items, so get ready to either limit yourself to cheese and rolls, or take a chance on spicy regional foods. Take some time to explore the older hotel with its great staircase. Swimming pool was okay. To get a towel, you have to walk down a stairs into a darken area that becomes their spa. Watch your step so you won’t fall. And expect power outages lasting for several minutes- these are apparently very common in Kathmandu and everyone just expects it.  Don’t panic if you are on an elevator when it stops the elevator- it will only last a few minutes.  Bathrooms were not as clean as we normally expect for a high end (or even mid-range) hotel in the US.   There was a “conditioning shampoo” but no separate hair conditioner so bring your own if you want some (we wanted separate conditioner).

in Yak & yeti cofee shop, every night is a food festival,with a great buffet at free service.a great variety of plates, for vegetarian, non veg,continental, chinese and of coursenepali food. you can enjoy to select from appetizer to main courseand you can also try a good fresh bread homemade. at the end wait for you mani sweet and fresh fruit.a good coffee can ultimate your experience for 2300 rupees with tips (about  20 euros)They have european standard in comfort and clean. Medium quality of thestaff.

Kathmandu is a difficult city to visit, so it was very nice to come back to the oasis of the Yak & Yeti at the end of everyday.  The entire staff is very helpful, particularly Guest Services.  Always, with a smile they dealt with all my impossible requests

The Yak and Yeti is my home away from home. I visit twice a year, and am always welcomed by their warm and friendly staff. Great central location, but better hospitality; never pushy, and always available.

Staffs are always with a smiling face and much professional. Located at the centre of Kathmandu. Beautiful interior and exterior. Variety of foods are there. Guest relation personnels are really helpful !

I really didi not know what to expect getting into Nepal on a business trip. What pleased me the most what the attitude of the employees. Gentle, helpfull, calm, not pushing. The location is great. You can find all you need nearby. Pleasant atmosphere inside the hotel, always something going on downstairs for enterteinment. Nice outside garden. Good food, good breakfast. I fully recommend!

Hotel Yak & Yeti is THE place to stay while in Kathmandu if you want to have the best possible services, warm friendly and welcoming with an A+ location and the most relaxing and comforting garden area in the Kathmandu city centre!Rooms are spacious and well equipped, the lobby is open and welcoming, and as mentioned the garden is a nice safe haven just a few steps away from the centre point of Durbar Marg and Thamel. But foremost of all the spirit of the entire staff at Yak & Yeti is what makes this Hotel so unique in my mind. Everyone of the staff no matter where they are are so warmly attentive, very affectionate to provide their best services always, with a smile that reveals their true passion and enjoyment for their work.It is a bit like stepping into a big family of compassion, care and friendship which will make your stay so enjoyable!

Rooms are perfectly designed in a heritage style. staffs are very much helpful and friendly. Guest relations people are excellent. their beautiful smile and attentive attitude is the bench mark of this hotel. Breakfast is very good and it has a variety too with different cuisine. My overall experience was excellent and I highly recommend this hotel to those people who want visit in kathmandu...

Really good people, from the second I enter the hotel i really get the positive vibes. Guest relation people made my life really easy out there. Morning breakfast is great. And most importantly hotel is really clean. And if you have problem,staff are ready and prompt to fix any inconvenience. I highly recommend this hotel.

Rooms are comfortable, Food is great and people are really helpful and friendly. Perfect choice if anyone is visiting Kathmandu. The location of the hotel is also very nice. I recommend Yak and Yeti to everyone who is visiting Kathmandu.Thank you

We only stayed 2 nights , having a little time to kill before starting a trip to Bhutan. The Hotel is set off the main roads and therefore quiet and secluded - yet close enough to walk to places like Durbar Square. The grounds were delightful and my wife enjoyed jogging there in the morning - however the Tennis court was overgrown, whether awaiting repair - I don't know. Although everything functioned well, there is a rather worn feeling, so doesn't really reach 5-stars. Nevertheless, the service was impeccable and the buffet breakfast very good and there is a free shuttle service to and from the Airport - some thing I had not realised until we left. Although there are other  'chain' hotels that are probably as good albeit more expensive, I would definitely stay here again - it has character.

The Yak and Yeti is not a 5 start hotel but is fine in most ways. We have stayed in hotels across the world and have  never been asked to pay $10 per day to access wifii. The gardens are nice and the hotel staff are helpful. We stayed in two different rooms - the first one at the start of our trip was old and a bit damp/musty smelling - the second room at the end of our  trip was modern, bright and welll appointed - overlooking the gardens. I would stay again if the policy of charging for wifii is changed by the manager to free access. Otherwise I would choose another hotel. This was the only Hotel accross Nepal and Bhutan we had to pay for wifii.Communication is important for travellers and $10 per day is an uneccessarily high charge.

I used this hotel to hold a large-scale meeting (over 100 people) including lunches and room accommodation for the guests. The hotel was extremely accommodating with arranging and including airport transportation and allowing for accommodation changes. I could tell they are used to event management, and were very professional. We worked with Neeta on arranging meeting logistics, and she was extremely helpful. Downsides: There were multiple meetings going on at the same time, and the overlap made things chaotic-- we were continually running into each other, and the central spaces were often full when we needed to use them. Our meeting attendees also had to walk across the conference center to reach the coffee break, which was somewhat cumbersome. They also provided limited internet codes for meeting attendees.The hotel is very well located, walking distance from many areas and with easy taxi accessibility to others, and has both renovated and un-renovated rooms. It has a nice courtyard. The food is good, though the service at the cafe is often very slow. Overall would recommend, as their professionalism was excellent.

The photos were a bit deceiving. The hotel itself is an add on to the right of the old Rana place. The service was good but the mainlanders on the place was poor in parts.Carpets were very old and worn, the tennis court was unkept and overgrown with weeds, the pool didn't have enough water in it for the pool to work properly, despite having a full time life guard on it. The buffet was of a good standard for Nepal but like everything else, just wasn't five star. That being said, neither was the price and I may be a little hard in my review and I would give an extra half star if I could. The location was good and the free pick up and drop off at the airport was appreciated. I would stay here again, especially as the Hotel Shanker is currently undergoing major renovations after the earthquake.

The hotel is well located for visiting the city. It has rooms of different standard so be sure to get a renovated room: we had to change ours at arrival because the one allotted was not good. Huge breakfast spread, huge gardens, though not so well kept. Vicinity if some good restaurant and curio shops.

I have visited Kathmandu on several occasions for solo or small group trekking expeditions. Normally I would stay in a 'local' hotel in Thamel as these work well enough for my budget.  This time I spent 2 nights at the Yak and Yeti (one before and one after) as part of a large group trek to Bhutan. It is a lovely hotel with beautiful grounds and pool area. I felt pampered and well taken care of.  A very different experience from my usual accommodations, yet close enough to walk into Thamel for shopping!

A well positioned hotel within walking distance of the major shopping area, and yet nice and quiet with beautiful garden and pool.  A great choice for the travel weary needing a little down time. The cosmopolitans slip down very nicely too!

We spent 3 days in Katmandu waiting for the clouds to lift - never happened but what a wonderful hotel. The hotel was situated in the center of the city so all sights within easy reach. The hotel was an oasis of calm and beautiful grounds. The room and beds were very comfortable and we had excellent service and food.

We have stayed at the Yak & Yeti twice in the last three weeks. When you walk in the front doors you are greeted with a welcome drink, air conditioning, and very hospitable staff. Both times we were in a standard heritage room. The rooms are big by European standards and come with a queen size bed, TV, ensuite, closet (with safe) and desk area. Be sure and ask for a newer/renovated non-smoking room though. Our first room had not been renovated and it was dark, a bit damp, and had terrible carpet. Rooms overlooking the pool are also quiet and have a nice view. The hotel check-in staff are quite good. It is better to book online rather than in person. If you book online you get free wifi and free breakfast. If you book in person you have to pay $10/day for wifi (two devices only). The hotel is large with lots of common spaces to relax and unwind. The breakfast buffet is fantastic with a huge selection of cuisine to choose from. We will be back here for sure.

The Yak and Yeti is the best hotel in Kathmandu. The staff is wonderful and the room is well maintained. The bed is the most comfortable in any of the Nepalese hotels I've stayed. The humidity level was also very good compared to other hotels. Toiletries are nice, except they don't give you conditioner, which is an annoyance.I didn't get a chance to visit the pool, gym, or business center due to my schedule.Shopping tip: 10-15 minute walk: Walk out the little gate to the right of the hotel. You'll go straight until it ends and then turn right and take the very first turn. Continue till the Main Street, Durbar Marg, and cross. Find someone also crossing and mimic them it looks scarier than it is. Walk to the right and keep walking (pass the fancy shops and a KFC) till you get to a stairs overpass cross the stairs and veer left and you'll be in a local marketplace. Good prices and bargain hard. Think 15-25% less and if you can get 50% you're a pro.

A beautiful property from the outside, with lovely lawns and spacious interiors, its rooms could do with some much-needed refurbishment. Being a five-star establishment, everything was too damn expensive. :)Breakfast was sumptuous, with Chinese, Indian and continental spreads.Good for a business trip, otherwise you are better off staying in a smaller, cheaper establishment (there are plenty in Kathmandu's Thamel district).

A good hotel that offers all the facilities. Room was good. Internet was good and they didn't have power problems like a lot of hotels in Kathmandu. Only negative was a mild case of food poisoning. This was the only place we had eaten was the hotel.

Very comfortable. Clean. Spacious public areas and rooms.  Solicitous staff.Some nice though over-priced shops on premises.  Only a short walk outsidethe gate to town with a myriad of offerings. Excellent buffet restaurant on premisesserves all meals.  Lovely garden, pool and shrine out back.  Calming.

I stayed in the Club Lounge at this hotel on business and really enjoyed my visit. This is one of the first upmarket hotels in Kathmandu and that sense of history meets the present day is present throughout the hotel. The location is good and the service excellent, especially in the Club Lounge.  I have heard from colleagues of guests who only stay in the Yak and Yeti when they come to Kathmandu and now I understand why. Despite the hotel being very busy with a conference, the service in the Lounge was always great and the place did not feel crowded. In particular Bhakta Raj Bharati in the lounge was always very happy to help and provided exceptional service. I would recommend this as a place to stay.

Yak and Yeti is a beautiful Heritage Hotel. The Palace and garden view rooms are spectacular . The rooms are beautiful equipped with all modern amnesties. The staff is very courteous. Hotel has a greatly jogging path, tennis court, swimming pool (which got damaged due to earth quake).The hotel is best in its class and I will surely consider this in my next visit as well. The only thing is the breakfast menu is almost the same every day. People staying longer may find it boring. Still a great place to stay and experience luxury.

I spent three weeks in the Yak and Yeri while I was house hunting for a more permanent accomodation. Very nice hoetl and staff are just wonderful and frindly. The hotel has all amenites one would need and the rooms are tidy and comfortable.

One of the great things about being a nerd is sometimes you get asked to go to great places to talk to other nerds. Such was the case with the Y&Y, where I was lecturing on economics.The hotel is in a fantastic location, close to the tourist-y bit of Thamel, but also the proper local markets & shops. Amenities were good - the garden is pretty spectacular, and although the wifi could have been a bit stronger it generally worked ok. Staff were fantastic - I cannot speak highly enough about them. Downsides? Food was ok, but nothing special. But there are so many places to eat nearby, that doesn't matter much.All in all, this was a great place to stay - thoroughly recommend this place for any other visitors.

Stayed for 7 days whilst attending a conference at the hotel. Rooms were clean and lovely, I stayed in 546 which overlooked the pool and gardens. The staff were always friendly and helpful. The hotel is in a central location for Kathmandu and it's only a short walk to the market and a short drive to the airport. We booked some excursions through the hotel travel company and they were fantastic. It's expensive but the best hotel in the area.

Yak and Yeti is simply mind-blowing! The entrance creates the aura and you are not at all disappointed once you enter the lobby greeted by warm smiles! We took a heritage wing room since we wanted to live in that era and it was amazingly complemented by the feel of the era as well as latest technologies. The service was exceptional and we thoroughly enjoyed our days. View from the room was so pleasant - greens and blues everywhere! Loved the large garden area where you could just sit and relax or just swim around. Another good part is its at the heart of the city and you can just walk around the area, walk to Darbar Marg and just take a short ride on a taxi to Thamel. Extremely pleasant experience I must mention and would look forward to going back!

I went with my family on Father's day to treat my father. Ambience was average , service was good, food was top notch,from soup to dessert. Especially Croquembouche and strawberry cheese cake were outstanding.  Hats off to chef! I think the interior needs face lift, it looks little boring, it could be more interesting

Recently, I was in  Kathmandu for a conference and stayed at the Hotel Yak & Yeti. The conference was held there as well. What really stood out was the service. Front desk, guest services, travel, housekeeping, restaurant, bar, bellman, front door, lobby attendants -- they were all beyond superb! The conference facility is actually an building that previously served a royal palace -- so there is a historic Nepalese feel to the place. One of the conference rooms was once the queens dressing room and its opulence and beauty is incredible. My room appeared to have been renovated fairly recently. The bed was very comfortable. The pillows appeared to be very new and bed linens were clean. This hotel utilizes washable duvet covers instead of the old comforters -- which is another plus. I really slept well here.  Built-in LED nightlights that can be switched on or off was a nice touch.  The electronic controls above the desk area include two outlets that have built in adapters -- another plus for the business traveler as I had work to do that week. My room had a view of the pool and garden which was very pleasant. Each day a local newspaper was provided. Laundry service was prompt and efficient. Climate controls in the room were new (digital) and easy to operate. The brick and carved wood trim in the room gave the setting a Nepalese charm reminiscent of nearby historic Bhaktapur Durbar Square.The buffet in the restaurant was quite good. Contrary to some other comments here, I found there to be a great selection of food. There were regional offerings (Indian style) as well as Western, Asian, and some made-to-order foods (such as pasta during lunch). A wide variety of salads and breads complimented the meal. Service in the restaurant was outstanding as well.  I mentioned I was there for a conference.  The hotel knows how to host a conference quite well -- there were a couple being held simultaneously.  Conference coffee and snack service was excellent as was conference support. One part of the conference facility includes the former dressing area for queens. The beauty and opulence of this room cannot be overstated. It really reflects old Nepalese royal charm. There were several items that kept me from giving this a 5 rating. First, the water in the bathroom is discolored -- a bit yellow. To the hotel's credit, two, one-liter bottles of water are provided gratis. However, the discoloration can be a bit of a turn-off. Second, the Wi-Fi was slow and sometimes difficult to connect.  It seemed to be even slower during peak times. My Wi-Fi was part of our conference package, but for normal travelers, it is not free. In 2016, Wi-Fi should be complimentary. Lastly, there are some minor things that separate 4 and 5 ratings.  The do-not-disturb/ make-up room sign was very worn. Likewise, the hotel information book was worn and had some outdated information in it. I bring these up as constructive criticism that can assist the hotel in making improvements that make a difference.Overall, my experience at the Hotel Yak & Yeti was simply outstanding.  As I mentioned in my opening comments, the service is beyond reproach and some of the best I have experienced anywhere in the world. I would certainly stay here again and look forward to the opportunity to do so. Happy Exploring!Ferdinand Magellan

What a beautiful hotel located near the center of the city. I looked forward to our time in our room and on the grounds because it was so quiet and elegant. Our room was an amazing mix of luxury and traditional Nepalese style. The hotel apparently was a royal palace in the past, and it felt like we were treated like royalty. The restaurant offered wonderful local cuisine that I always looked forward to. If in Kathmandu, this is the place to stay if you want an oasis of comfort and Nepalese culture.

It's about a 10 minutes walk from Yak & Yeti hotel to Thamel in Kathmandu. This gives the hotel an excellent location from where you can walk easily to the shops and restaurants. The hotel itself is very clean, nice and cozy. The room I stayed in (shangri-la room) was terrific. The staff are very friendly and helpful and the hotel has anything you would expect (swimming pool, fitness, shops, business center etc). One area of improvement would be the fitness room; this does not have air conditioning (making it very warm when exercising) and some of the equipment is a bit old. Overall a great place to stay in Kathmandu.

A 6-night stay at Yak & Yeti provided a very welcome oasis of peace and quiet in contrast to much of Kathmandu outside of the hotel's compound. The room was clean, with some traditional décor (e.g., wood floors, Tibetan carpet along the room-wide window seat (perfect for sitting and for luggage), and quiet. The breakfast buffet is enormous and features many types of cuisine (Nepali, Chinese, middle eastern, western, etc.). The concierge staff was extremely helpful negotiating prices for taxis to several sites that would wait for us and provide a ride back to the hotel. The price per night seemed very reasonable.

Overall, I had a pleasant stay at the Y&Y.  I am only giving it a 3 star because the hotel itself feels a bit dated and could benefit from renovations.My room was nice and comfortable for the most part.  Bathroom shower appeared to have been updated at some point but the room must not have been used in some time.  The first morning I showered I had to let the water run a little before getting in because it was brown.  Every morning after it was fine.  Bathroom could use more lighting. The staff had to replace a bulb in the bathroom but it is too dark still.I think at this point high end hotels should be able to provide filtered/cleanish water.  It's a pain to have to brush one's teeth and rinse with bottled water constantly. I recommend providing more complementary water bottles, you only get two per day.Breakfast buffet was decent.  Nothing to write home about but they have all the basic breakfast essentials and some more.  Dinner buffet was also pretty good if you don't want to walk anywhere.  I had it twice and the Indian was pretty good.  The bar was a bit dated and could use an update but it was an ok place to get a beer and chill.What I will give the hotel props for is the customer service and friendliness of the staff. From the door man, to the front desk, to the waiters and hosts, all were eager to please and very friendly.Overall a nice hotel! It could just do with some updates.

The Hotel is located located in the center of one of the most happening town of Nepal, not far from Thamel, if you like to shop. The rooms are good, staff is very humble and helpful. Breakfast served is really amazing.

Well friends if you are planning a trip to kathmandu then definitely dont miss to stay in yak & yeti as the services provided here are really good and the best thing to enjoy your free time is the casino of this hotel its lovely

Verry nice hotel I will be come again in this hotel.staff are friendly.thanks all of you.one of my friends say for me I will come with my wife when I married . Very nice service they're flowing the them roils.out side view verry nice.Theri is no traffic at that time.i am so happy and my friends also .

We drove from the airport into the city on its bustling streets and as we turned into a noisy narrow side street I began to be apprehensive about wether a hotel  located in this environment could be a a decent one.I need not have feared .As soon as the gate closed behind us,we were ushered into a beautiful quiet and serene environment.The Yak and Yeti has an old elegant building with traditional Nepalese motifs,artworks and presentations adorning its wall and grounds.With a lovely garden and beautiful landscaping ,the hotel is a picture of olde worlde charm.My room ,located on the sixth floor was clean and the beds soft and cosy.The only draw back was the bathroom arrangement. It has a partially enclosed shower and water tended to spill over into the rest of room.My room had a good view of the garden and swimming pool and at night pigeons kept me quiet company outside on the window sills.The wifi was fair and consistent.But it is the restaurant that takes the cake. I sampled the breakfast lunch and dinner.It was all buffet. But what offerings,what spread,what variety, what  culinary delights!And what is more the menu kept changing ,offering more opportunities to the curious and the adventurous like me.As in all Kathmandu,there were frequent power challenges but but in the Yak,they were not prolonged as an alternative power source usually kicked in in a matter of seconds.The staff were ever friendly,ever courteous.One of the them Janison at the concierge desk went out of her way to ask after our welfare and encouraged us to visit some tourist sites including a plane flight to view Mount Everest.Alas the weather was hostile and we had content ourselves with a visit to the Monkey temple.The Yak &  Yeti is indeed  charming and lovely place.NAMASTE!

Despite the corny name, suggesting backpacker style and quality, this is actually one of the top hotels for Kathmandu. Located close to airport and big tourist attractions. Staff is helpful and basically great, breakfast and lunch superb, the bar has a great selection of cocktails. Rooms are OK, bit old but acceptable. Enjoyed the Finnish sauna at the spa and a shave at the barbershop.

The Yak & Yeti is a hotel located about 15 to 30 minutes away from the international airport (depending on traffic conditions). I had a room on the 4th floor which had its own lounge where you can have a nice breakfast and snacks/happy hour drinks in the evening. The staff here are amongst the best you will encounter - friendly, always with a smile and always going the extra mile to help you with tour options, etc. There are some shops within the hotel as well as shopping options outside the gates of the hotel. For those who want to try their hand at games of chance, the Casino Royale is located within the older part of the hotel. As in most locations within Kathmandu, power shedding is an issue and you need to be prepared for temporary outages. The free wifi within the hotel can be somewhat patchy. The room which i had on the 4th floor was very nice, clean & with modern fixtures in the bathroom. Will stay here again for my next visit.

While the hotel is older, I think it is the best option based on the quality of the hotel and location. It is within walking distance to many of the top sights and there were always taxis waiting to get to future out locations.  I found the rooms clean and the service very good.

We had a group needing 21 separate rooms from May through June.  The staff at the Yak and Yeti were super supportive of our group's unique requirements while the big American chains had no flexibility or concern.  I would absolutely stay at this hotel again!

The room is small. Toiletry cheap. No comfortably located electric points in room to charge your devices. Basin had cracks. Bathtub enamel was coming off. Breakfast just about ok. Feels an ordinary hotel

First of all I would like to thank the general manager who despite his broken arm ensured all guests were looked after as best as possible. All other staff members were really helpful and looked after my wife who had a broken nose and arm. Thank you very much and we look forward to returning next week. Mr H Pandya

Had spent a night at this hotel. Beautiful and humongous property. We had a conference there and arrangements were nice. The rooms need little more maintenance and careful supervision. There was no room slippers which one expects in such a big hotel. The jet washer next to the pot didn't work!

Spent 3 nights at the Yak & Yeti and it felt like a cocoon in Kathmandu to me. The complex itself getting old, however is filled passionate and courteous people. The garden is a retreat. The food at the Sunrise Cafe was so good that I ate all my dinners  there.

It was a best experience stay on the star hotel  yak and yeti. Our visit was easy because of reservation management  by Ms Karuna Khadka thanks to her for easy booking.We really enjoyed sauna and jacuzzi which was included in room cost.Moreover breakfast was also awesome. We had two rooms with friends 310,311 my next visit will probably be with my family.Thanks once again management team.

The few things going for this hotel are the location, the garden, and the service. Otherwise hotel seems tired, dated and unkempt. Showers are sad, rooms half decent. But the service is exemplary. Food is good, maybe not the buffet, but a-la-carte is fine. For the longest time I remember, they serve poori/aloo and Chana/bhatoora on alternate days.  Both being North Indian food delicacies. Hope the management refurbishes and focuses on this hotel.

This hotel is a landmark in Kathmandu. However the rooms are tired. Beds are not as comfortable, bathroom is extremely basic. Modern travellers with tons of gadgets will struggle to charge their devices. The biggest let down was the breakfast. The spread is pretty wide but lets not talk about the taste. What works for this hotel is its location, Durbar Marg. This is the heart of Kathmandu and a step away from all the activities. Will I return? Most definitely not.

The hotel is very centrally located in Kathmandu with walking distance to the market and eating joints. Not to forget..one can walk down to the Darbar.However, it seemed that it is slightly expensive with its architecture and room comfort.

As a frequent user of hotels i like a simple check-in, stay and out. At Y & Y you have to buy username and password and then struggel to log in with max 2 units. Please increase the room rate with some dollars and let us log in whith room number and name. Then I may come back

Stayed in this five star hotel for 2 days....must say the best experiance...staffs are good and cooperative ....rooms are clean and spacious ...price is very affordable....all in all best place in this price....enjoyed the stay...must insist people to stay in this hotel once in a lifetime as it is really very cheap....

Very popular with Westerners this hotel is pretty average. The rooms were clean and pleasant enough, but nothing special. The breakfast buffet offered a variety of food including eggs, fruit, bread and regional dishes. Dinner buffet is over priced and the deserts which looked palatable were terrible. Internet may or may not be included with your room fee--find out because it will cost you about $4/24hrs.

Hard to get consistency in Kathmandu. However, this is about as close as you can find. $109/night. there is an old part and a new part. the old part is tired and need a deep cleaning. The new part has a VERY strong smell due to the laquer on the floors. Pick your poison. Ask for a view of the pool area. internet costs $10/night. It is close to sovenier shops.

After one week of treking , we have been happy to stay 2 nights in the comfort of yak and yeti . Here nothing has really change over the last 30-40 years . You smoke inside . People read paper , not Ipad. Red brick design so common in Nepal . Travel agent arrange your Trip by phone . Surprise . We realise that Prince Harry was also in the same hotel . Good Experience in the curious Russian French restaurant the chimey open by a Pioneer of alpinist and first owner of the hotel . Will definitely remember my journey in yak and yeti . Please don t renovate yak and yeti . Keep the old good charm .

Enjoyed a very comfortable 2 night stay in a spacious twin room located in the older part of the hotel so we benefited from beautiful wood carved furniture. Our room had tea/coffee making facilities (but I wish they had provided larger cups!), Wi-Fi (but ask about prices), A/C, plenty of towels and a wonderful shower!! Breakfast was a very comprehensive buffet including pancake station. The lobby was a relaxing area to enjoy a drink or snack and the gardens were beautiful. The hotel is well situated for a short walk to the Thamel area of Kathmadu but if you need a shopping fix there are many shops located just outside the gates. The hotel appears to be very popular with people preparing or returning from trekking so offers a good opportunity to exchange information

Great location in central Kathmandu with helpful and friendly staff. The room was clean and comfortable and I had a pool and garden view, which was great to wake up to. Enjoyed my stay here and wish I had stayed longer just to enjoy the hotel amenities!

Room was great - lots of space- comfortable bed- hotel beautifully kept - plenty of communal areas. Was here for 5 days on mixture of leisure and business. Very convenient for centre of Kathmandu. The country and city is very much in early recovery from the 2015 earthquakes - hotel not affected. Restaurants fine - staff ultra efficient! Only thing to say against is the very noisy night club which is just outside the hotel and affects one part of the hotel until late.

Checked into the hotel on April 21, 2016 for a night. The check in was smooth and the front office team were relatively prompt in the checkin. However once I entered the room and settled in - I could not help but notice the finer details. I had checked into their deluxe room and the overall look was definitely tired. The bath towels had definitely seen the good days and the bathroom was definitely dated. The washbasin had a crack!! I hope it was not as old as the hotel itself. Same with the bath towels. Has a strong chlorinated smell. The lamp shade in the room was tilted which went to prove that the housekeeping team definitely did not have a keen eye. However, on the other hand, the hotel team were extremely helpful and friendly. I guess the team needs to look into the basics in the room as that would definitely help in pushing the property up several notches.

The place is located in the heart of the city. The staff at the reception are so polite and helpful. The market is just walking distance, where you can get KFC, Pizza Hut, Baskin Robin etc. Not only that there are variety of hotels Nepali, Chinese, Japanese, Indian if you have a flavor for them.

The location of the hotel is very good it's in the middle of the market everything is near you like Pizza Hut . Kfc , baskin Robbin, very friendly staff , clean and good service food is good , although many things need to be improved , shisha is very bad don't smoke it .

The Hotel is situated in the heart of town 500 metres from the scenic lake, walking distance to all the shops and restaurants needed. The lake is worthwhile taking a canoe ride on and you get your own oarsman for 2 people. Lifejackets are provided and it takes about 45 minutes or more if your oarsman is happy. It is a most serene and beautiful ride and you look back at the city with its temples showing above the skyline. Reception when you arrive is quaint but very friendly and all is explained about the hotel but quite well English speaking staff. The 1st floor is recommended as you do not hear any staff or guests wandering around the lush gardens. Rooms are well appointed and include Tv, WiFi and the usual assortment of teas etc. The queen size bed is most comfortable with plenty of extra blankets as it can get cool some nights. A short walk to the well equipped restaurant for breakfast or meals or you can choose to eat outside in the lovely garden area adjoining it. My wife is a vegetarian but that was no problem at all as the food is very similar to our visit to India prior to coming here and plenty of choice for non-meat eaters. I was more than happy with my choices of pork, goat, chicken and beef though not a huge variety of seafood but adequate .Drinks are very cheap for beer and cocktails but a bit expensive for wines and a "stubby" of beer was a 600ml bottle which my wife enjoyed. We also went to the top of the mountain at 5am the second morning to watch the sun rise over the snow capped mountains, something worth doing. There are plenty of temples, squares, shops and sites within walking distance but other out of town tours are readily available. Light clothing is all that is need though a jacket was needed for the morning sunrise trip.

Yak and Yeti is very well located in the heart of Kathmandu. The hotel infrastructure is a little old and the age shows.I found the hotel service outstanding. The staff was always happy to engage with the guests and go the extra mile to help out. One feels very welcome.The room I stayed in was quite adequate in size. The bed was comfortable. The other thing that I enjoyed was an in-house walking track. Morning walks were very pleasant.

Named after two mythical Nepalese creatures (although my children tell me that one of them is real 😂), the Yak and Yeti is a very pleasant and centrally located hotel, providing all the facilities you could need if you weren't adventurous enough to rough it at the cheaper end of the local hotel market. Restaurant and bar are both well stocked but probably cater for the 'bus tour' tourist rather than the mountaineers or back packers that are drawn to Kathmandu. Staff were very friendly and more than helpful. Good wifi and comfortable rooms - upgraded to a suite which provided plenty of space and smiles from the family. Great gardens for a relaxing walk or you can spread your wings and walk to Thamel for a coffee or meal (10 mins away). Sadly no Yetis or even Yaks seen - perhaps my kids were pulling my leg! Recommended stay.

Great staff!  Check-in is easy.  This is a good hotel in Nepal.  If you want to compare to 5 star in Europe or the US, then you have incorrect expectations on both price (much lower here) and accommodation.The bed is very comfortable, the shower is strong and hot, the Internet is good, the buffet is good with western and non-western food.  Many types of juices are available for breakfast.  If you need laundry done, this is your place!Ask for room on garden/pool side of hotel.

Plenty of space - big rooms and garden, a bar area and a restaurant area - makes this place a comfortable stay. Location is also good as it is on the main King's palace road and near to tourist hub called Thamel. Food and drinks average. Wifi connection is to be bought separately and this is definitely a minus since all other htls I visited had free wifi anywhere in Nepal (and around the world)

Nice catchup in daurbarmarg kathmandu, to be true this never changes the bar and everything. I love hyatt but when i am with my family i always be here coz its just so formal and treats all customers accordingly. Has a separate foreigners section and everyting the bar never changes more than that drinks always tastes the same dont it!!!😊

I stayed in the property for 14 days ! So have decent idea about the hotel.Room: I stayed in a pool facing room. The pool however was not working  b/c of earthquake.Location: Excellent. Beyond Doubts. Peer hotels in same tariff would not come even close.Amenities: Host of amenities that are ill maintained.Bottom Line: The Hotel has an excellent infrastructure but its hospitality leaves a great room for improvement. All my co-guests had some or  the other concern on hospitality. I'm sure modern hotels in Kathmandu would definitely fare better.

The stay was not bad, the bed was comfortable and the room clean. Even though people say it is a five-star hotel, just remember you are in Nepal. I think they gave it a couple of extra stars for not falling down during the earthquake. The staff is extremely kind and very helpful.Situated near Thamel Marg you will be able to stroll down some quaint streets and shop for curios. You have plenty of shops to buy your Kukri Knife or any other Nepalese souvenir.

We passed by this hotel for a snack whilst staying with some friends in Kathmandu. It's really pretty and the food was reasonably priced and really tasty! The only downside was the service - it took us 3 hours to have nibbles and a couple of drinks.

This is a nice hotel, good decor, clean, great staff however it is a little run down and not centrally located for tourist Thamel which was disappointing however it is in a nice street with shops you can walk among. The pool was empty but gardens with Geese very attractive. Buffet breakfast really nice first day and samey and tired looking on the second. Rooms were way too hot and windowsills covered in pigeons and their poo.

Torn over my rating of this hotel as it is better than average for it's category but can't give it a very good. At almost one hundred pounds per night it is quite expensive for Nepal and standards should be higher. I felt the hotel lacked polish in every sense of the word. Admittedly, Kathmandu has seen difficult times last year but the hotel needs to pick up from that and should be shown some loving care and attention - it looks definitely faded.Positives are that there are free pick ups and drops from and to the airport. The hotel is situated in a quiet but central area with extensive grounds, once part of a palace complex. The room was large and had a view over the hotel gardens and a window seat to admire them from. The bathroom was also adequate. Two restaurants in the hotel, one for breakfast buffet and then a Russian restaurant, called The Chimney - strange but true. Had one meal here and the room has a large raised hearth in the centre with a huge brass and copper chimney. It was most welcome on a chilly evening. The restaurant was completely empty when I visited and so service as attentive. Had an excellent mountain garlic soup, followed by Chicken Kiev - good job I was sleeping alone!Negatives are that the rooms are starting to look faded and uncared for and in need of a deep clean. The breakfast buffet was OK but suffered from that perennial of tepid food that needs to be hot. Quality of what was on offer was average.Would I stay again? Probably, unless I could afford Dtarika's.

Agree with other reviews that the location is excellent, can even walk to Durba Square, the staff are extremely polite and helpful, but the hotel is not only in need of refurbishment but also also suffers from the national problems, such as powercuts. The grounds offer a relaxing athmosphere!

The hotel has a great location and that is why was choice number one. As for the rooms - it was always cold as heating not working well. Room was pretty big, but dusty. Toiletries - provided upon request. Buffet did not have that much choices of meals that were not spicy. But nice staff and great locations is hotel's advantage. Also, we had an event at this hotel and Convention Center Team were very helpful.

From the minute I walked into this hotel I knew it would be my perfect fit.Nice rooms with a wonderful private lounge that's an intimate place to relax. This is overlooking the grounds and pool.Being a former Palace it just flows through the entire building. The Buffet is exquisite and the curry dishes are the best I have ever enjoyed . I don't just love the country ... I love the people !

The room was good, with nice wood carvings and details rather than trying to be worn modern. There was no heating due to the fuel crisis, however we were provided with an electric heater and were very warm in bed. The biggest disappointment however was the lack of hot water, the shower was luke warm which is not what we expected when other hotels had been providing hot water during our stay in Nepal. During normal times the hotel would be worth the price, but without hot water we felt a bit short changed. The hotel is a good location and within walking distance to Thamel whilst still being quiet.

Arrived on the Sunday to a really nice welcome and a small lemon and mint drink.  Room was ready and everything was already in the system.   Signed and was taken to the room on the 4th floor with a view of the garden and empty swimming pool.    The room is ok.   I had a nice double bed.    The room has no heating due to the problems with india.   So the room was very cold at night and during the day.   Some electricity problems but the backup kicks in under a minute.  The rooms are very clean and staff are friendly.   Breakfast was nice with a huge selection of food.  Internet is ok but if you buy a 24 hour voucher it will cost you 4000 rupees.   A beer in the hotel will cost you 900 rupees.We went out for dinner and found lots of cheaper places to eat.What i didn't like is that they refilled the bottled water in the meeting room and people drink out of it.  Not cool for a 5 star hotel.

first of all this is now not the best hotel in nepal which it used to be. it's casino is not working. even pool is under renovation. staff too cold. and at the price which they are charging you can have shangri la with casino or other five star near by with much better connectivity and facilities. staff is rude, breakfast good .  they don't have al cart in their food restaurant. their buffet they charge approx 1500 nps excluding tax . also they are bit in side road where u have to walk at least 3-4 min to come to main raod while annapurna and shangri la are on main roads.

Its an old hotel with nice service. The rooms are too old though and the bathrooms are not well maintained but they are clean. It would be one of the options you choose when going to Nepal. Close to most attractions though.

big hotel in central location, loved the garden, spacious rooms but everything seemed a bit outdated. food is seriously overpriced for the quality, even espresso was disappointing. Service is very professional . Paying for wifi in the room felt a rip off: seriously, free wifi is everywhere now!

We recently stayed at this hotel after arriving in Kathmandu before flying to Lukla to start our trek in the Everest region, and then again upon completion of our trek. The hotel is rather a mixed experience. There are many lovely decorative touches in the common areas, lifts, lobby, etc. In the past the hotel seems to have come in for a lot of criticism of its breakfast buffet offerings, but I was quite pleased with the spread put on. There were Western, Chinese, and Indian options available, and a tremendous amount of variety. I couldn't fault the hotel at all on this score. Prior to our trek we stayed in one of the Heritage rooms, which was ok and reasonably attractive and comfortable. On our return visit, we were upgraded to a suite on the 4th floor executive wing, which was really nice. The suite was lovely and spacious, with a large living room, spacious bedroom, plenty of closet space and other storage, with our mineral water replenished daily. The bathroom was a bit dated, but certainly adequate. The hotel seems to do a very large convention business and can be quite crowded at times. The hotel bar was marginally adequate, with not a lot of choice, though the bartenders were mostly attentive and one made us very good Cosmopolitans indeed. The front door staff, however, seemed disorganized and under-proficient in the most basic English (basically the international language for all foreign guests). On one occasion they were incapable of organizing a taxi and we ended up simply walking to Durbar Marg and hailing one on our own with much less trouble and aggravation. Overall, the hotel is an average, big establishment with some nice touches but nothing too special. It is comfortable enough, however, and serves its purpose.

Comfortable hotel in most respects. Nice garden with jogging path, and tennis court. Empty pool mars the landscape. Service in hotel is mainly good, with wide selection for breakfast in a room of mainly excited tourists. One night room service woke me up in middle of the night with something I didn't order; that was annoying.

This is a very good hotel with very capable staff.  This is my second time here.  The buffet is good, not great.  The room is clean, the shower is hot, the bed is comfortable.  While very good, it is not a 4 or 5 star by western standards.  Wifi is extra and allows 2 devices to join per each paid ticket.Thamel is only a 10 minute walk.  Fire and Ice Pizza is worth going to and is an easy walk on the way to Thamel.View of garden is preferred but not necessary.

The hotel is just off Durbar Marg, the poshest road in Kathmandu, and only 10 minutes away from the touristic spot of Thamel, full of curio shops and restaurants. The hotel is very large and nice, with its old and quaint looks. Big garden and swimming pool, relaxing spot in the middle of the city.

The look is good with brass in the lifts  dominating the mind. The people are courteous but the food needs lots of effort.  The effort to have freshly cut fruits which are reasonable cannot be more emphasized. It is at the best a 4 star property which is rich in heritage but very average in maintenance. Needs efforts

Yak & Yeti was once, apparently, *the* place to stay for westerners looking to suck the marrow from the bones of a poor, remote, but interesting country. And even now it hosts the headquarters of the World Bank in South Asia. You definitely get a whiff of the British Raj at Yak & Yeti - more than a whiff, in fact - as though this property is stuck in time, nostalgic for an anachronism. Unfortunately, the property seems to believe that it is still the only game in town, which it clearly isn't. The rooms - at least the one I was in - are a bit rough around the edges, badly in need of updating. The Wi-Fi was slow, and the food - especially the breakfast buffet - was completely undistinguished either by variety or by flavor. The service, meanwhile, didn't seem particularly keen to please or meet guest needs; I was left with the impression that they didn't feel they needed to. Additionally, I booked an appointment for a haircut in the hotel barbershop - and while the haircut was okay, I ended up with a cut the barber thought I should have, because he didn't speak any English whatsoever.After I checked out of Yak & Yeti, I checked in to Hotel Annapurna right across the street. The difference couldn't have been more striking. My experience in the latter hotel couldn't have been better, and just made Yak & Yeti look that much worse.

Pros:a. This hotel is very centrally located on Durbar Margb. Very big hotel, c. Used to be Kings palace earlierd. Big Garden and a jogging trek inside the hotele. Fantastic Jacuzzi, Steam bath and sauna bathCons:a. Price is not value for Moneyb. B'fast menu is also very sad, no good options for Vegetariansc. Taste is also not very good.

Even in the most remote village restaurant, ine can get internet. Not in this 5 star hotel. I sat down to eat a buffet lunch, complete with crushed chicken bones in the food, when staff said I'd have to move to a different restaurant. All this in full view of their empty pool.

I recently stayed at this Hotel during my Business trip to Nepal for 03 nights.I chose this because the location is great.But i found the rooms to be too old, they badly need renovation.Also, the some of the staff attitude was rude...Also, their breakfast and food is not something to write about...

The only good thing to say abou this hotel is probably its location (city center). Other than that it fails on all accounts: run down and pretty much dirty (at least my room, note: on the executive floor), service is terrible and the breakfast just awful - almost no choice, tasteless and pretty annoying staff. They have a long way to go and learn how to run a hotel and please their clients. To be more specific: you can't adjust A/C or heating in the room, walls are eyesore, TV signal just unacceptable, one power oulet in a business room (imagine that!), furniture nothing but ergonomic, you can't have coffe for breakfast other that this awful from a big pot, they have no idea how to make pancakes or wafels, swiming pool - don't dare to put your foot in this dirty pot, happy hour in the lounge on the executive floor serves the same snacks all the time (after 2 weeks you can be really tired) and if you ask for sth after 7:30 sharp they ask you to pay; lifts are only for the brave ones - being older than my grandma you just have to believe it will take you to your floor. STAY IN THIS HOTEL ONLY IF YOU HAVE TO.

So we first checked in on the 27th for a night and were upgraded to the club floor. Everything seemed great. The hotel standards were good for Kathmandu. Even though a little renovation would be nice, esp changing the carpet. It was an all girls trip and we felt safe. The location is excellent! The hotel staff is great. Very helpful and friendly.However, when we checked in for the second time on the 30th, we complained about everything! We were put on the second floor, rooms 206 and 208. The rooms were stuffy and smelly. Very little light: just ONE bedside lamp and one ceiling light. Bathroom shower was broken. Overall both our rooms were depressing.The positives of this hotel are definitely the staff and the location. Even though the approach road gets really dark and scary at night. But that's with most roads in Kathmandu. We did have a small incident where there was no guard at one of the 'closed' gates. We didn't know the other way and it was dark. It took over five long minutes of yelling just for a guard to come to help us. But they were extremely nice and helpful later.

Great hotel good rooms but not good in room dining though the breakfast served at the restaurant was good stayed for two nights only had one meal that also in room which disappointed me very good staff spacious rooms neat and clean overall decent not bad

We booked 4 nights direct on the hotel website and got a rate better than booking.com. Big advantage was when we got there we found 3 nights was enough for Kathmandu itself and we wanted to spend a night at a hill station, (Club Himalaya at Nagarkot). Because we were direct with the hotel we could check out early. We were with friends who had the regular room type. The special offer on the hotel website got us into the "Heritage Deluxe" rooms. Having seen both room types we all agreed it was worth the upgrade. Y & Y is 20 minutes in a taxi from the airport. (Pay 700 NPR equiv 7 $ USD at the official pre-paid taxi booth on the right as you exit the arrivals hall). 5 stars are not achieved, but better in Kathmandu will be hard to find. Its secure, clean enough & well located. 10 minutes walk from Thamel  - the main area for bars and restaurants. (We enjoyed dining round the braziers at Northfields then drinks after at the improbably named Tom And Jerrys with a ricshaw ride home for 400 NPR - start price 600). Breakfast buffet is not a thrill, but get round this by ordering an omelette with whatever filling you want and something decent will appear. Similarly, don't accept the tea & coffee already on offer. Order a pot. To see Kathmandu you must have transport and a guide. The reliable concierge will sort one for you. We were lucky and already had been introduced to Mr Rajesh Shahi.  Licensed and 100% reliable with excellent English he can sort transport/sight seeing and accompany you with a know how that brings alive what you are seeing. We even had him plan our itinerary once we got to know him. That's how we found the fabulous but unknown Kirtipur. He can be reached on 984 193 8015. Dealing direct with him will save you money which in most cases you can pay in arrears unless you want him to book hotels/flights.

our initial impression was good with an efficient team at the front desk. The rooms were nice but a little shabby, especially the bathrooms. I was appalled to have to pay for wifi having just been trekking and enjoyed free wifi in the mountains. The prices for just about everything were exorbitant and no coffee machine! The rooms were stuffy and offered nothing other than a bed to sleep on. Breakfast buffet was fairly poor so, of particular note, was the super spread that appeared on Christmas Day for lunch. It's not a bad hotel it's just overpriced and impersonal, just like any business hotel in any city, i expected a more Nepali experience.

This hotel is very nice indeed, however, no hair dryer in the room (when asked, reception sent someone upstairs with one), you need to run the tap 5-10 minutes for the water to heat up (which is such a sad waste of water) and worst of all, they charge $10 a day for wifi!!! Seriously, no hotel that aspires to be 5 star does this kind of thing, you might be a nice hotel but you are not the only nice hotel in Kathmandu, so please adjust accordingly.On a positive note, we had to leave at 5:45 am and even though the breakfast isn't served till 06:30, they packed our breakfast for us. Just stop charging for wifi and i'd have very little negative things to say.

Over the 15 years I have been travelling to Kathmandu I have stated in the Y&Y many times and have seldom been disappointed. This time, in early New Year 2015, my family and I took 4 rooms in what is known as the new "Heritage Wing" . This is a major change in the hotel's lay out  and thus merits a new review (I have reviewed the hotel before)Arrival was as friendly and efficient as ever and we were taken to Room 642 (my daughters in 644/646/648- the rooms in this wing have been cleaned up a bit and given a bit of Newari decor detail to justify the name "heritage" although that, and a little upgrading of the bedroom furniture, is about the only difference between what is there now and the original "trekkers rooms" which is what these rooms used to be nicknamed when I stayed on my first Charity rip to Nepal in 2001.Over the years, my wife and I have normally stayed in the Executive floor rooms in the old wing which, although a bit older, are a cut above the rest so, if you are looking for a quality room with amenities, exec lounge etc, and are prepared to pay a bit more, stay in the old wing - 4th floor. If you want a basic room - go for the "heritage rooms" or the lower floors in the old wing.Ok - back to my review. The "Heritage" rooms, which I will concentrate on, raise the following commentsThere are few amenities - no robe - slippers etc.There is no floor covering - polished wood - some people prefer some form of carpet,There are some nasty elevated lips on the bathroom floor - watch your toes!The power cuts out very regularly and plunges all into darkness - it takes a minute or two to get the emergency generator up and running.The air conditioning does not work, at least it did'nt in January 2015. I am told it is turned off in the winter period to save money - this leads to a roasting hot room at night. The only solution is to open the windows and let the mosquitos in. This is fine if you are not paying the sort of money you are paying the Y&Y.The Wireless internet works fast and well but a voucher costs $15 a day for only two computers. Add this to your room pricing if you are keen to keep in touch but are on a budget.Pigeons park themselves on your window sill and are impossible to shift - charming if you are a flying rat fan but a real noisy nuisance which is prevented in the old wing, but not in the Heritage Room wing, by bird protection strips on the window sills.Lovely big garden and outdoor swimming pool.
