Visited this place for two nights and three days and extended one more day.The most perfect jungle lodge one can aspire to be in.Everything is in perfect synch with nature ,down to the minutest detail.The resort itself is lovely with perfect rooms which though offering all the modern amenities never makes you feel that you are not in the jungle.The food is lovely too which is a rarity in other jungle lodges in this part of the world. We absolutely relished all our meals even though a large part of the group was vegetarians and we also had five kids with us .The activities are well taken care off and activities there are many like elephant safari, jungle walks , elephant bath, jeep safari etc.But the icing on the cake is the staff which tends to all your whims and fancies with a  smile and makes one feel perfectly at peace and at home.7One of the best I have visited and at the moment due to the earthquake in nepal a couple of months back its coming at a steal.Highly recommended for all for an experience of a life time !!!!

We had arrived in Barahi after a somehow long and tiring trip from Lumbini. The lodge is located just on the Rapti River bank across the jungle. Our days were full of activities, which we truly enjoyed. My favorite were elephant safari and elephant shower. It was great to be part of the nature again. The moment we crossed the river, we were in the jungle, seeking permission to be part of the wild life, and also at the mercy of unknown.Recognizing the excellence of Barahi is not a shallow complement. They have been exceptional from the beginning till the end. They re-defined what service and hospitality should be: guessing all our needs before it occurred to us, but leaving us with enough space to adjust; balancing activities with fun and learning; feeding us with exceptionally tasty and well-presented food; and simply making things just easy and comfortable for us. We left Barahi so pampered and indulged that we felt instant disappointment in other hotels we stayed in other parts of Nepal.Barahi is trying hard not to destroy or disturb the nature which we observed with awe. I am hoping that they and every other lodge in the region takes all the steps they can to make Chitwan the best preserved jungle in Asia.I would like to mention the exceptional services of our wise guide Krishna, all-mighty and all-time smiling Vineeta and Rishma, extremely kind and attentive Tej, Megh and Gun. They surpassed all of our expectations. If you stay in Barahi, I hope you will also have a chance to get to know these wonderful people who will always be there for you during your stay, and "lovely animals" of Chitwan (this phrase was being used by Krishna during our walking/jeep and elephant safaris.).

Just spent 2 nights at the lodge and from the moment we arrived until the moment we left we had a smile on our faces.  It was a really wonderful experience, from the elephant riding to the jungle safari drive and then to top it off we watched the sunset after a boat trip down the river.  It was one of the most peaceful places we have ever visited.  The staff were caring, attentive and put so much effort into making the stay memorable.  The food was varied and very good.  We wish the team and the lodge every success in the future and we plan to come back again soon.  Many Thanks

Were two fantastic days in Barahi Jungle Lodge. Staff extremely friendly and helpful, especially Prem and Rishma - fantastic people !! I will never forget this place, I will keep forever in the memory of these great moments. I am very grateful to have known this place and these people. I hope to return soon ...

On our return trip to this exceptional property it felt like coming back to family.  Everything is good about this resort.  The staff is the best ever - from Varun the GM, to Krishna our incredible Naturalist, to Tej who made dining and drinking an event.  Rooms are modern, casual and very comfortable.  WIFI is good for being in the middle of the jungle.  Bedding, showers, services are all first rate.  The jungle safari allows you to see rhinos,deer, peacocks and maybe a tiger if you're lucky and breakfast is served the the jungle.  We were able to go out and visit local villages and assist with some of their basic needs which made the trip extra special.  Our Bush Dinner was magnificent.  The boat ride with drinks and snacks at sunset was a once in a lifetime experience.  The elephants can be brought right to poolside for an amazing encounter (as like so many tourists we do not do elephant riding).  My wife and I have traveled extensively but feel this is the BEST overall experience we've ever had.

This is more then 5 star lodge! Just excellent choice if you want to enjoy all Chitwan activities!The price is much higher then the other hotels in this area but there is a reason for it. You are not paying only accomodation because in the price was included a lot of activities they offer and all three meals per day.  Considering all this the rate was very fair!Lodge is new, the rooms are very nice and original (do not leave open the door because of whild life) and above all very clean.Lodge is not huge rather pretty small so the feeling to be in it is very intimate.The choice of food is just exellent, you can choose which kind of meal do you want and they prepare it for you.The stuff is just too much friendly and very good trained, no complaint.We had during our 3 days stay always the same guide, Giovinda, who was marvelous!There is a very cute swimming pool so we took adventage of the last sunny days before the monsun period to get some ten.There are two sweety lodge's elephantes, our was Ranni Kaly.I would come back any time in this marvelous lodge.

what a great treat, the property is so nicely done suiting to the jungle theme and is a full eco friendly resort.the staff is a feather on the cap....the entire staff is ready for anything you call....very courteous and helpful....Mr Varun the Manager works as if he is a front office staff.....so very kind and helpful in anything you ask for, they all try to adjust if its possible......the River Bank is so lively, the activities are also well planned......only if the approach road is improved, one of the best property to relax in jungle.....

Let me start with the National Park first. Probably the best ever I have visited until now , and I have visited quite a few. The jungle is abundant with flora and fauna. Spotting the one horned rhino was a treat and to top it all a tiger sighting made the trip all the more worthwhile.The resort is located in a serene, beautiful location , right at the banks of river Rapti. Rooms are immaculate and the Nepalese folks are like little gems of human beings. A vacation of 5 days just breezed through and we all were devastated to leave when the time came.For travelers looking for the right mix of luxury and wildlife this resort scores 10/10. Rooms are perfect. All of them face the river. Service is top notch. Mr. Varun and his team are striving hard to make this place a even more fantastic experience and their effort clearly shows.Now for a few observations.Food may be a bit limited in options if you are from India & like your spices. The elephant safari is a bit of a disappointment although the elephant feeding and bathing experience is unparalleled. Expect to spot plenty of wild life & birds and make sure you have Jeet Dai as your naturalist.The road to the resort from the airport is a bit of pain but the journey is worth it.The sunset trip to the Rapti , Narayani confluence is recommended for romantic holiday makers but skip it if you are with a group.All in all a place worth visiting again and again.

A very nice location on the bank of the river with the park just on the otherside. Nice bunglows, good food and most important nice jungle safari with professional staffs.A perfect place only s small drawback the road leading to the property is really bad but once reaching there its a treat.A perfect place for a safari experience.

We stayed for 2 nights at this lodge in March, in the suite, a gorgeous villa with 2 bedrooms, living/dining room, 2 stunning bathrooms with rain showers and a sunken bath in 1 of them, swimming pool, veranda, fire pit, etc., overlooking the river with Chitwan National Park on the other side. Nice furniture, comfy beds, a discreet but efficient butler service which included delicious meals being served on the terrace under a parasol. Sheer bliss. The activities included a game viewing trip in an open-top jeep in the Chitwan National Park but, to be honest, the game there is not in the same league as e.g. Kenya or Tanzania.  There are supposed to be quite a lot of léopards and tigers but they are rarely spotted. We did see a few rhinos during a boat safari on the river, which was great. Bathing with éléphants was also a highlight for our kids. You could tell that the animals are very well looked after and healthy, unlike in some other places we've been to. We warmly recommend this hotel.

The Barahi Jungle Lodge is a wonderfully created property right on the periphery of the Royal Chitwan National Park, the boundaries are only separated by the serene Rapti river. The lodge hence offers superb views of the forest and the river. The attention to detail is perfect, upon arrival you are introduced to your naturalist who schedules your stay in the lodge and plans all safaries and activities. All naturalists have lots of years of experience and they seem to know the jungle extremely well. The lodge has four in-house elephants and spotting a rhino in the grasslands on their back is an experience to remember. One can get real up close with these elephants by bathing and feeding them with the 'mahouts'! The architecture and sensibilities used to build the lodge are very well thought of, use of local elements can be seen prominently all around as they blend seamlessly with the outdoors.The food and beverage is of a very good standard and I'd recommend to try the Nepalese menu.One of the best experiences in the lodge is the morning jeep safari into the park. Once again the naturalists take you by surprise with their knowledge and familiarity of the forest. Our safari ended with breakfast served on the banks of the Narayani river. And talking about experiential travel there is no way that one can miss the evening boat ride. While spotting birds, alligator, crocodile and the rhino it winds up with a sundowner on the river bank as the sky turns orange reflecting on the river.The Barahi Jungle Lodge is without doubt the best wildlife experience in Nepal!

Our first trip to Nepal and Bahari Jungle Lodge just ticked all the boxes. The accommodation, the staff, facilities, food - you name it. We were treated like royalty and given the best possible care and attention. Our safaris were great with our extremely knowledgable guide, Krishna, able to advise us on all the different species of flora and fauna that we saw. Sadly the tigers were being shy and stayed out of sight but there was more than enough to make up for that. Elephant washing (the elephant washed us!) was a fun time after Mrs Jumbo had carried us through the jungle. If you have any doubts about Nepal as a destination because of the earthquake, please put that to one side. This country and its people are really welcoming and need as much tourism as possible. We are looking forward to our next trip and it will definitely include Bahari Jungle Lodge.

To describe this resort is like no where else in the country the beautiful Resort on a very isolated location of Meghauli I had chance to stay almost four different occasions I had my beautiful special First Night stay on my Honemoon & It was a great start of our very beginning of togetherness which was the utmost feelings that a Romantic 5 star property can offer " The flowers on bed champaign on table beautiful candle light dinner Beside the Private swimming poll ( 16 ft by 34 ft) big enough almost a common poll in Hotels I have stayed in Europe or Americas this was just the night start we had our next day waited with full of excitements went for a Hotels jeep Safari & been so damn lucky couple to spot the tiger that was one of our greatest day in the dairy again The staffs at Barahi jungle lodge is attentive helpful & outstanding especially Mr Varun General manager is the jewel of this Laid back high end resort of Nepal . The food always came with surprises fully garnished well presented the service crews were really genuine this had been one of the best hotels / resorts I have stayed in my 20 years of travel experience round the Globe Thank you Barahi Jungle lodge for making our Day as special as it was after wards again I had second chance to stay there on one of their Deluxe beautifully themed design rooms which all in private thatched huts agin exceed my Expectations later again took The suite rooms on recent days with two other friends of mine from Dubai Mr Salman & his brother salim they both were surprised to see kind a Resort in Nepal & said Raj Bhai can't you built some thing like this in POKHARA ??? I wish I could really hands up to Barahi for this beautiful piece of creation on Earth it truly a heaven & gem of a place in Nepla.

This was one of the most perfect places on earth.  It had it all:  great accommodations, thoughtful service, fabulous food and beautiful wildlife.  It also had knowledgeable people who could direct and decipher the wildlife that was all around us.  The naturalist assigned to us was Jitu and he was so in touch with the land, you felt 100% confident with him in the lead.  Krishna was the other naturalist we had and he was also incredibly  knowledgeable.  I also can't say enough about the food- it was 5 star all the way.  I'm a a vegetarian so it was paradise for me but they also cooked meat every night.  As an experience during your time on earth, I truly feel it belongs on the bucket list.  Everyone should experience this place.  The surroundings coupled with a staff who wants to share their love of nature, to the chefs who want you to taste the best food, to the support staff right there always to hand you a heated and scented towel, this place has it all.  It's a long journey to Nepal and then the Barahi Lodge but it is worth it.  I truly sobbed when I left.  Not something I do often!!!

Stayed here last week and really don't know where to start.  The rooms, service, staff, food, entertainment............everything was absolutely flawless.  Service at all levels was par excellence, right from the top Management, down to the golf cart drivers and bell service.  Always a greeting ready with a smile, they made our stay unforgettable!!Thank you so much Varunji, Vinita and everybody at Barahi Jungle Lodge.  Looking forward to our next visit soon.

Not many times do I walk into a hotel and mutter 'wow'! This was exactly my response and that of my husband.  From the infinity pool overlooking the jungle, to the room quality, the food quality, the beautiful bath, the friendliness of the staff, the high standard of the activities.  It made our trip really special.   We live in Nepal and in four years we have never stayed in a place that offers such a service.  If you want to escape, to be pampered, then we would definitely recommend this place.  We have an overactive 2 year old that can be really testing and sometimes difficult, that can sometimes stop us enjoying our retreats. However, as the staff team took a genuine interest in our son, spending time with him, it made the whole experience even more enjoyable and relaxing.  This hotel would normally be out of our price range.  However, having visited a number of hotels in Sauraha that are saturated with tourists, low food quality, and the cost of eating out more - we figured that the extra was probably not that much.  I very rarely write reviews but this is well worth the effort.

Beautiful property  mind blowing location excellent hospitality food was very good especially the breakfast every thing was fresh as they have there own in house bakery only cons was the drive from Bharatpur to meghauli overall we enjoyed our stay n plan to visit again

My sincere apologies, firstly to the Barahi team, for posting this review so late. We, as a family of 5 stayed here for 3 nights and 4 days, and what a time it would be! We were concerned that Chitwan (specifically Sauraha) had become too overcrowded and a bit touristy based on reviews read, and finally came across Barahi lodge, a property which promised to invite you to Chitwan's former glory. Pugdundee Safaris, a renowned safari lodge chain in India had taken over the management of the property and all our requirements were taken care of by their India office through Abhay Sood.The road to Barahi specifically from Bharatpur to Meghauli, is liable to give you a scare,  it is in need of serious repair, so you will have to put up with an hour of a very bumpy ride till things improve (for which Barahi is making efforts) before you get to this little piece of paradise.Location: It is very unlikely any Chitwan property is going to be able to match the location of this lodge. On the banks of the Rapti river, the cottages overlook the river and the national park on the other side. So yes, you might see wildlife from your cottage balcony itself.Rooms: Huge! If you were used to the standard of rooms of the lodges that were inside the national park earlier, you are going to be a very happy camper, because the cottages here are downright luxurious, with lovely bathrooms as well complete with all knick-knacks.Food: Another major advantage, the food is all prepared freshly per order. And though there are some set meals prepared, you can always order something else if the set meals don't agree with you. Everything we had was delicious, special marks to the veg lasagna :)Service: Barahi truly is made of a dream team. A hotel manager with years and years of experience, a proactive operations manager, naturalists of the highest pedigree (you are assigned a dedicated naturalist, in our case Subhash, young but hugely experienced, knowledgeable and a pleasure to be with) and the staff overall which is always looking to help you out. The service when at the lodge never once faltered, and Varun, the hotel manager always found an opportunity to spoil us with his hospitality.Wildlife: Experience it via a rowboat, jeep, elephant and on foot as well. Can you ask for anything more? Lady luck was in her full glory during our trip. So many bird species seen for the first time, a fleeting glance of the Great Hornbill. Mugger and the critically endangered gharial as well. And mammals? We saw plenty of hog deer, spotted deer, langurs and macaques, gaur and of course, the rhinos on every trip. And no, that wasn't the end. We saw a sloth bear shuffling off into the grasslands. And a leopard that zipped off the road to disappear into thick foliage. And the king himself, the Royal Bengal tiger who announced him loudly in Chitwan's grasslands, and rewarded us with a few seconds of a clear sighting, before he too disappeared. Wow!Budget: Barahi is one of the more premium properties here, and hence is a bit heavy on the wallet. But as narrated above, that premium does see you getting your money's worth. It's advisable to book rooms and meals together, if you're going to kick back and relax in the property rather than explore the forest, you can book the activities at the lodge itself. Else go for the full deal, if you're a wildlife nut like me.All in all, my sincere thanks to Varun, Pradeep, Subhash, Jitudai, Vineetha, Krishna and everyone else who looked after us with such great care. Our Nepal trip was special thanks to you guys.

This lodge is brandnew and in the middle of nowhere, away from the tourist crowds in Chitwan. To get there is an adventure itself. Rooms/huts are very nice. The lodge is super quiet, you only hear the jungle voices. Perfect for some wildlife safaris, pool hangouts and a few days to relax.

I am deeply touched by the dedication of the staff, and felt like crying when I had to leave.I stayed for 2 days and got used to being pampered! The staff were very friendly and showed an interest in serving. There was impeccable attention to details. The spa was excellent as well! I enjoyed the elephant safari ride and jeep adventure - we spotted the Indian rhino, hog deer, spotted deer, grey langur as well as heard the barking deer vocalising in the distance. What an adventure in the Terai plains and riverine forests of the Chitwan National Park!

We had stayed there for 2 nights.Great hotel!Excellent service with deep concern for all the very small details.The staff were very friendly and did their best for us.The safari experience was great, especially all the activities with the Elephants.The Restorante and food is excellent.The whole atmosphere and experience was just great and made it Unforgettable stay!!

We stayed at the Barahi Jungle Lodge for two nights last month, and absolutely fell in love with it. It was a family gathering. Each member was very happy that we had selected this lodge to stay. The service was excellent! The staff were super efficient, very courteous, and eager to make sure we were happy. Starting from the general manager down to the dining room staff, every one took excellent care of us! We loved the tastefully done up eco cottages. Every thing spelled out quiet rustic elegance filled with comfort. The food was delicious too. The stay was packed with activities, and each one was carefully planned and charted out. The kids loved the elephant bath! When we left, each family member, especially the kids, was happy and content, and bent on returning. The only thing I would suggest the Barahi team to work on would be to lay pressure on the local government to improve the access road. Sadly, it is in a poor state. Other than that, the lodge is a gem!

Spent 2 nights here and the days were full of activities: boat ride watching wildlife on the river banks, sunset on a sandbar, elephant safaris watching rhino, deer, and wild boars, jeep safari watching rhino in the jungle.  The staff is excellent with wonderful hospitality.  Food was extremely satisfying.  Can recommend to anyone to make sure they spend two full days and nights here.  The only downside is the rough road one hour away to the closest airport.  We did see some guests arrive by helicopter from Kathmandu, so I know that an option. Go enjoy this Nepali hospitality, we did!

We just completed another stay at Barahi and it just keeps getting better.  The staff is incredible and we love the experiences - Bush Dinner, Jeep Safari, Visiting local communities, and the sundown and sun up river boat trip with a surprise ending.  These are all very special and unique to Barahi.  The rooms/cabins are very spacious and comfortable with amazing views of the river and national park (filled with rhinos).  There are great food choices that are delicious.  We love it!HIGHS-Wonderful staff - thanks Krishna, Chandra, Varun, Everyone-Unforgettable experiences - especially the bush dinner -Great food and drink-Spacious rooms-Comfortable beds-Great shower-Nice balcony with beautiful views-Service beyond compare-Sporadic WiFiLOWS-Really there are no lows but the ride from the airport is scenic and a little bumpyIf traveling to this area Barahi Jungle Lodge should be your home.

I rarely give 5 stars but Barahi fully deserves it. The property is beautifully set, spotlessly clean, and has great facilities. But what sets this apart is the staff. They are all just brilliant in every respect. It’s not often that you feel genuinely welcomed and that all staff go out of their way for you. Mr Soobhat the operations manager was extremely helpful and our guide Karaan was knowledgeable and ensured we got the best out of our expeditions. Don’t hesitate to stay here, it was one of our very best holidays.

Barahi Jungle Lodge feels and understands customers and their needs. They have a very well set up 100% customer service orientation and take care of every little detail in a very personal way. The offered activities are super organised and out of the way in every aspect .. early morning boat safaris / jeep safaris .. you couldn’t ask for more special treatment. The food is outstanding and offered all day round and caters to customer specific requests . The naturalists have a fantastic knowledge of the area and each and every staff member goes out of the way and enjoy their work ! Outstanding experience!

This hotel is utterly charming. It has a wonderful location at the edge of the National Park with a stunning outlook towards. Amazing accomadation, clean tidy and comfortable. Food was excellent,plentiful and well presented, Staff extremely attentive,The menu has enough variety. We are staying full board, if we've finished your food more is always offered. The elephant safari was superb, got up close to a rhino with calf, a rare thing to see in the park. Loved the canoe trip and jungle walk. Lots of wildlife, monkeys, wild boar, deer, crocodiles and plenty of birds. We have some amazing photos that we will always look back on. The resort & staff members definitely exceeded our expectations. All tours were excellent & scheduled well. Thank you all for a wonderful trip!

Just spent 2 nights/3 days here with my husband and another couple and we can’t stop raving about the wonderful service we received from the minute we walked in to the moment we left. Every member of staff makes you feel like you are part of their family and they want you to have a great time. All the activities are included as is the food. The only extras are laundry, drinks and spa treatments. Govinda, our naturalist went out of his way to find a tiger for us, but on this occasion we had to settle for rhino, wild boar, deer and numerous kinds of birds. That is the nature of the beast!Feeding and riding bareback on the elephants for me was the highlight but all the included activities are worth it.

I have been visiting Chitwan National Park since my childhood. Since last 30 years I have probably visited more than 15 times and have stayed at more than 10 different resorts available. All resorts are different and gives unique experiences. They are all great! For me and my family Barahi Jungle Lodge was a first time experience. We all were mesmerized! We got more than what we expected. We got more than what we paid for. Its not just for "Customer Satisfaction" - it for "Customer Delight"! I will not write anything in detail not to spoil your experience. I will just describe the Property as "THE BEST among the Best!"

What can I say it was absolutely awesome, food is excellent, the staff are excellent I can’t fault anything we stayed three nights my brother and I and we wish it was a lot longer.On the Safari we saw a rhino that was so close we could’ve touched it, in the afternoon we went down to the elephants that live on site we got to know them and feed them, then we went to the water with the elephants sat on their backs and played in the river getting totally soaked!!

We went as a family of 7 adults and 3 kids. This place was a very nice break in our holiday of 7 days to nepal. It is for people who love safari and natural wildlife. Or for those who want a break. We did only one activity a day and the rest was for relaxation. They have a common room where wifi is available for free and since the entire hotel was almost empty being off season at this time we had all the facilities available for us. We had a blast of the time in the common room as there was no one else to bother us. The staff is very polite and courteous, willing to accommodate our every wish. There is a policy of assigning one person dedicated to each family who will take care of your every need. So we did not need to interact with any other staff. They do request you to provide your food preferences in advance so that your meals can be prepared in advance, so after every meal the food in-charge used to interact with us for our next meal. He was willing to provide whatever we asked.Kudos to them for making our visit a pleasure we will remember for a very long time.

Perfection is the one word that comes to mind, be it the food, service and rooms or the gorgeous poolside lounge and the ethereal fog that obscures the entire lodge in the morning. I arrived in the evening, after two flights (Kathmandu and then Bharatpur) and the riverside lodge was a sight for sore eyes. The earthy cottages are lined up on one side, all offering a view of the Rapti River and blessed seclusion. In the night, I witnessed a beautiful Tharu dance performance, courtesy the talented staff.During the course of three days, I enjoyed an elephant safari where we had an excellent view of the buffer zone and two jeep safaris with the keen-eyed naturalists Saket and Govind, who helped us spot rhinos, Indian bison (gaur), gharials and crocodiles, several birds, moths and butterflies, all types of deer and wild boar. Every time we wanted to go to the forest, we had to take a boat ride and they were magical experiences, allowing us to observe the sea birds closely and soak in the serenity of the river. After a boat safari, I sipped on Shiraz at the confluence of the Rapti and Narayani rivers and watched the sky shimmer in what was one of the most beautiful sunsets I've ever witnessed.While at the lodge, do visit the local Tharu community - they are friendly and their houses and jewellery offer fascinating glimpses into this Nepali tribe. Best of all, you get to partake of the local wine called ruksy.Thank you Varunji and Saket for organising such a beautiful trip for us. I can't wait to return. :)

After a punishing 7-hour ride from Kathmandu (with the last 1.5 hours an absolute hell due to the undeveloped roads leading to Barahi), we arrived at the resort in poor spirits. We were taken to the Welcome area, given cold towels and drinks with one of the staff sitting us down for a quick briefing. Within a few minutes, we were excited again about the experience to come! We stayed for 2 nights.The facilities and hospitality are world-class; in Kathmandu our lodging was not comfortable and without hot water so the Barahi villa (we stayed at No. 32) was heaven! Spa services are good (we tried the Swedish massage) and food is not bad too (although more buffet variety would be good). The chicken momos are excellent! Restaurant staff (and again, all other staff) were very well-trained, attentive and warm.The next day, we went on a 6am elephant safari (with Anjalikali), elephant bathing (with Ranikali) and a boat safari with a wonderful surprise set-up to watch the sun set on the riverbank. Certainly an experience we won't forget. TIP: Check if your naturalist can arrange to buy bananas prior to your elephant safari - we wanted desperately to thank Anjalikali with the elephant bath for bringing us out in the morning, but couldn't get her for the bath due to her schedule (Ranikali, her best friend, was an absolute darling in any case). Buying bananas for her ahead of the safari would have been a good alternative!We were very lucky to have Govind as our naturalist, who was knowledgable, funny and warm. His profound love for nature was prevalent in everything he did (including picking up litter in found in the jungle), and we were very inspired by his volunteer efforts in educating the village community against animal poaching. Govind is a very special person, and we hope very much to see him again!Overall, we didn't want to leave and were very tempted to scrap all other itinerary plans to stay at Barahi. We will most definitely return in the near future, and for a longer stay (one week sounds just about right!) filled with activities so we can catch more animal sightings. Thank you Barahi for the amazing hospitality, and keep doing what you're doing!Travel tip: We recommend guests travel via plane to Meghauli airport vs traveling by road from Kathmandu - apart from the undeveloped roads, the hill roads can get jammed with traffic and are pretty dangerous!

The hotel is located literally next to the river and the jungle. It has amazing views from the rooms, a green property with a very nice and neat design. Rooms are very nicely decorated and clean as well. The staff is extremely helpful,nice and kind. we had an urgent health issue and they did their best to find a solution. The tours that they offer are also amazing. I never felt that close to nature. if you want to run away from city life, this is where you will do a fresh start. Sitting next to the pool or in your room you can only hear birds and the nature nothing else. I saw a wild cat, snakes, weird animals, elephants, rhinos from my balcony. If you are nature lover, you would love the experience. Food and service was also amazing, they had the best food that we had in nepal. One important note is that when they pick you up from the airport, make sure that they go through the longer way, the shorter way is a hell, it is not even a proper road. Before arranging your pick up or drop off make sure you prefer the better way which is also very picturesque.

Let me start from the beginning of the trip. My Wife and I reached Narayanghat late at night and there was a gentleman there waiting to guide us to the resort. In most of the wildlife camps, the resort and the staff retire early since their work starts pre dawn. but i had the privilege of having the resort incharge Mr. Varun and the staff waiting for us. Post a nice drink and Dinner, we retired to our room which was amazingly comfortable. the next morning was a relaxed day as we had not planned anything. the views from the room are out of this world. you are on the edge of the river, with the chitwan national park on the other side. We did a boat safari, a jeep safari and two elephant safaris.  saw two gharials in the river, and NINE RHINOS. the best way to see the rhinos up close and personal is from atop an elephant.To cut it short, the resort is amazingly situated, the staff is the nicest i have come across and food to die for. i even left behind my ipod dock which has been sent to their delhi office to be picked up by me. Would i go there again? without a doubt. i strongly recommend Barahi Jungle lodge for everyone. be it for safaris or to just unwind. you will not come back disappointed. and DO NOT MISS THE ELEPHANT BATHING ACTIVITY. its simply awesome.

This lodge provided one of the best overall experiences imaginable for a trip to this special park.  It is on the northwest corner of Chitwan and just a 2-minute rowboat ride from the Park.  So, no time wasted in looking for game.  The Park made the decision a few years ago to take all the lodges out of the park and relocate them on the periphery.  So, you can't get any closer.  We stayed parts of 3 days and 2 nights and had a fabulous visit.  We started off the first afternoon with an elephant ride into the jungle in the buffer zone this on the lodge side of the river.  No problem--we saw some one-horned rhino as well as other wildlife very quickly.  This ended at sundown and we had time to freshen up prior to a nature program about the park and an excellent dinner.  The next morning dawned early with a 5:30 wake-up call and a 6:00 riding safari into the park.  We really got to see wildlife--in addition to the rhino, we saw large numbers of deer, monkeys, boer, bear and huge numbers of birds.  Don't expect to see the Bengal Tigers.  There is a stable population of about 120 tigers, but they are shy and not likely to be seen during daylight.  We did see leopard tracks, so we considered it to be a successful safari.  We had breakfast at a waterhole where a one-horned rhino was bathing and having a good time, so quite a memorable breakfast.  This trip ended somewhat after 11:00, so we had about a half hour before the next event, which turned out to be the highlight of the visit--even for us older folk.  This was bathing the elephant who had taken us into the jungle the day before.  Not just bathing--we each got to ride the elephant into the river and get really drenched as she bathed herself--and us.  Much fun.  The afternoon activity was a boat ride along the river and a view of the sunset at one beautiful point, with drinks and snacks.  On this trip, we saw crocodile and concluded that the rhino population is doing just fine.  As we were cruising downstream, we saw a male rhino charging after a female rhino, going from our left to right.  A few minutes later, they were much closer, going right to left.  Finally, they emerged not far behind us, going left to right.  We were happy for them and happy that they were behind us.  They charge along around 40 km/hr and they would not have noticed our little boat.  But, exciting to watch.Overall, a great experience.  We  were there early in a week and it was a low point and we had our terrific guide, JItu, all to ourselves.  The night before we left, two large groups came so we were lucky.  The entire experience was near perfect--two long activities each day, but with a break during the real heat of the day.  Excellent rooms and superb food.  We ended our last morning taking an oxcart ride to a nearby village and that was very informative.  We would recommend staying 3 nights, so that we could take the walking safari in the morning of day 3.  The only negative had nothing to do with the lodge, but the roads.  Our drive from Kathmandu to Chitwan took 6 hrs and some of the roads were very bad.  This is particularly true of the road through the mountains to Chitwan, which is also one of the roads to India.  There are many trucks transporting goods, so this road is crowded.  The way back to Pokhara was even worse--took almost 7 hr because of numerous rock slides caused by rain the previous evening.  A big sign tells us that the road is to be completed by April 23, 2017, but I'd add a year to that.  Barahi has a helipad, so I would investigate a helicopter ride one way--the drive is interesting once!

We stayed in the lodge for two days full and it was an exhilarating experience. Owing to the scenic beauty and calm environment, this place is a must visit for anyone looking to relax. We also enjoyed their 3 types of jungle safaris via a jeep, an elephant and a boat.However, the best thing about the resort is it's hospitality and the coziness it offers. The staff was super polite and very welcoming, They served us great food and were always ready with wet towels, snacks and tea every time we returned from a safari. All in all a great experience. Will visit it again.

i had my lesiure stay here for 3 nights. I loved the place. Privacy, elegance, nature, peace, luxury all at same time. Superb Exclusive dinners on prerequest. Wifi only in resturant and swimming pool, no wifi in room. Superb staffs and excellent food. View from room was outstanding, i loved the morning sunrise i could enjoy every morning from my room. But for drinks i wasn't much satisfied, bar tender seems not much trained. and the swimming pool not that clean. i really liked cooperation from binita- a safari guide, she helped us much. But i am definetly going to stay here again next time. I loved the place.

This resort is absolutely incredible. The view, the rooms, the staff, the food.  I honestly cannot fault anything.  The staff think of every last detail to make your trip enjoyable, they really go out of their way to make sure you are happy and you can see they are there because they love their job.  The boat safari with sunset watching was so amazing. I would highly recommend this lodge to everyone! Ps the pool is great as well

It is a beautiful resort, very uniquely decorated, it is one of those boutique hotels that gives you the excitement of not knowing what to expect, but you know it will be good. Five star service, five star facilities, I recall the spa being quite lovely, my boyfriend and I had a good massage experience there. The food was delicious, very fresh and local, which is what we always look for. Close encounter with nature, you could here the rhinos crackling when fighting with one another at night, across the river. Definitely a must if you are going to the Chitwan National Park.

Our experience in Barahi Jungle Lodge is beyond our expectation. We stayed there for 2 nights along with my family in a separate macchan with 5 star amenities. The service that we got from the hotel is superb and the food is so delicious and not to forget safari activities provided by the lodge is excellent.

We stayed 2 nights at the end of our India/Nepal trip and it was an amazing way to finish. We had elephants showering us with water, a fantastic jungle safari, local dancing and wonderful food together with faultless service. Totally recommended.

Barahi is an excellent combination of proximity to incredible wildlife and creature comfort at its best. They are accessible by Heli with their own private landing pad, this is the recommended way to get there. The road option is poor, lengthy and dangerous after sunset. The lodge has a great location with the park just across the river. Facilities are excellent, food is fabulous with great wine selection for a remote location and the staff and service are at the best standards. Our site manager Vineeta was a real pleasure to deal with very professional service. we arrived very late due to weather and transport complications and they were constantly in contact with our driver for direction and preparing for our arrival. Our naturalist Jeetu was excellent, knowledgeable and very familiar with the area. Someone with his skill set and experience can make a safari trip a real treat and we were very lucky to have him as our guide.The huts are arranged around the main building with #24 and #25 on either side. these are the ideal huts, however the resort has golf buggies to drive you around. the resort provide slippers for elephant bathing and it is recommended to have long trousers (elephant skin and hair can be rough)swimming gear is also recommended, they have a great pool.All guest are encouraged to spend time in the main hall as this is the only space where internet (wifi) is available. a great way to bring people together. highly recommended.

From service to facilites to hospitality it was simply too mesmerizingly good. Highly recommend it for vacation and very peaceful and close to nature camp. Each activity is special like the place. i had the best time ever.Thank you barahi team for this wonderful memories i had during my stay.

This place is amazing. Location is gorgeous in front of the river with access to a more quiet part of the national park hence more chances of seeing wild life. Away form the touristy areas with a touch of local culture and delicious food! The staff is incredibly attentive and welcoming, very knowledgeable about local species so wonderful safaris! The hotel itself is beautiful and blends well with the nature. Wonderful service, grounds and staff equals any top safari hotel in Tanzania. I am definitely coming back! Recommend it 100%

I must say that this place is one of the best places I have ever been. Attention to detail is here! My room was exquisite! The people extremely kind, loving and attentive! I felt much taking care of and appreciated everything they had to offer. The jeep safari, elephant safari, canoeing excursion, my guide Vineeta is a most kind and knowledgable girl. The manager Varum has done a great job at making sure the place is well run! Must come!

I stayed for 2 nights at this relaxing treasure in southern Nepal.  It over looks the Chitwan National Park across the river. Each cabin is furnished in a tasteful safari style. It is very new so everything is in pristine condition.  The naturalists are well versed in the animals and land.  Everything is personalized for you.  I was interested in the village traditions, so my naturalist took me on a wonderful village walk.  It was wonderful to see the animals in their natural habitat.  The bird life was plentiful as the winter migratory birds were still there befor their trip north over the Himalays. Don't miss Barahi Jungle Lodge and Chitwan National Park.

Wow.  This place was totally unexpectedly great.  There are individual cottages that are new, clean, and beautifully decorated.  There are architectural details (like the spiral pattern of stones in the showers) that make the Jungle Lodge a luxurious retreat and gateway to Chitwan National Park.  The lodge is located on the river that borders Chitwan.  Our stay included meals and a variety of activities.  Our group had a fun, informative (and bumpy!) jungle safari on which we saw a couple rhinos and lots of other interesting flora and fauna (but no tigers...sigh).  The naturalists who accompanied us were outstanding in their ability to notice and describe the animals and plants.  One evening we had a sunset cocktail hour on a sandbar on the river--glorious.  Another evening, locals came to show us traditional songs and dances--and dressed us in costume to join in.  The food is excellent.  The staff members are unbelievably attentive and helpful.The only downside is that it is quite a (long, bumpy, dusty, and sometimes harrowing) journey to reach it.  Apparently, you can come by helicopter...if that is in your budget.

The lodge was the perfect place to stay in Chitwan. The staff were super nice and really helpful. The food was delicious. Our flight was delayed coming in, but they still managed to squeeze everything in on our schedule without feeling rushed. Our guide for the weekend, Subas, was the best! He and the rest of the staff at Barahi were really patient with us and made our stay that much more wonderful! I wish I could have stayed much longer. Hopefully I'll get to visit again soon!

The best way to visit Chitwan National Park, away from the touristic fuss lies the beautiful Barahi Jungle Lodge. No lack of comfort here, they will go out of their way to make your stay as good as possible. Rooms are perfect and beautiful and they offer lovely presented and tasty meals. The Barahi Jungle Lodge has their own wildlife guides that will take you on boat rides, Jeep safaris, jungle walks and elephant rides and can tell you everything you want to know about the amazing wildlife in Chitwan. The Barahi Jungle Lodge has their own elephants which are taken real good care of, so I took my chance to bath one in the river and it was an amazing experience. Thank you so much, Barahi Jungle Lodge!

My friend and I had an excellent time here. It was my sixth time in Chitwan and probably the best. The lodge is excellently designed and constructed in tune with the jungle environment, placed nicely on the edge of the Rapti River. Mr Varun, the manager, runs a disciplined, yet relaxed outfit with very knowledgeable naturalists, and very pleasant staff, attentive yet not overbearing. Barahi has excellent activity leaders, and very good cafe-restaurant and bar. Food was very good as well, variety being offered, from local Nepali, to continental, chineze, etc. Our naturalist guide, Krishna , was very good, and by the looks of it, so were the others who looked after other small groups. That section of the park (west) has plenty of animals.We saw a large number them, rhinos with babies, etc. I will definitely return here.

Stayed for two nights and didn't want to leave. The staff were amazing and from local villages which has been a great boost to the local community. You are given your own guide for the period of your stay and they organise the programs which are very flexible. Meeting the elephants was a highlight for me. They are such beautiful creatures and it was excellent to be able to interact with them knowing they are being looked after like family. The food was delicious and plentiful and we finished with a glass of wine on the balcony of our room each evening listening to the night noises. Can not recommend this place enough.

Staying on Barahi Jungle Logde is best experience so far. I liked it most because its very close to nature at the same time its really luxurious and comfort. We also got the first class service and hospitality in total. All staffs are very friendly, foods are really good and what a big swimming pool !! I recommend it from the heart to visit once and feel the difference within other similar resorts and hotels.

What a surprise!!  Luxury, eco-friendly, good food, spectacular scenery.  The rooms are beautiful.  The pool is relaxing after a jeep safari.  Be sure to visit the nearby village.  Beautiful people.  The staff couldn't be nicer.

Luxurious comfort and excellent service combined with eco-responsibilityWe cannot recommend highly enough - a brilliantly balanced combination of luxurious resort with excellent amenities and fantastic opportunities for encountering the abundant wildlife of the National Park.From the initial welcome and briefing, through to our departure, we were exceptionally well-looked after throughout our two-day stay. Our programme over those two days included: elephant safari, jungle walk, elephant talk & bathing, river boat trip, local dance presentation and an early morning ride in a ox cart! A fairly busy schedule, but at no point did we feel rushed.Our room was wonderful, with quirky decor - we loved the wildlife cartoons and the pair of duck sculptures on the bed headboard. And aircon and real coffee both contributed to our comfort. The food is excellent, offering a choice between Chinese, Nepali or ‘continental’ (i.e. European) food for lunch and dinner.This is an eco-friendly, top-range resort, really lovely to stay in with superb staff and a very responsible attitude to the ecological mission of the park. We would recommend to anyone thinking of visiting the Chitwan national park.

Service, food, knowledgable guides, and surprise (I won't ruin it for you) were all excellent. Game drive using elephants is a first for me. Cultural dances were unique. Coffee on the trail was enjoyable. One thing, I hope they put gravel on the road for the next time I visit. Definitely a first class experience.

Beautiful lodge - very attractive decor and extremely comfortable.  Veneeta the naturalist was wonderful and very well informed.  She took me on an elephant safari on the back of very placid "Ranikali".  I never expected to see a tiger at all as it is such a rare sighting.  Also saw several rhino up close and personal and also spotted deer.  Helped to bather Ranikali in the river the next day and she made sure that i got as wet as she did generously spraying me with trunkfulls of water!  Roomy villas - well appointed.  Large pool - delightfully warm to swim in

One of the best safari resorts I've stayed in. Cottages are just next to the river, which is next to the jungle where the safari takes place. Jeep safari's are available in the winter, November onward. We took the elephant safari, and it was well worth it! We got to see jackals, elephants, wild boards, deer & a lot of rhinos!The villas are the epitome of luxury. Built in adobe style, the walls are made of clay & the floors are all stone. A great bathroom with a unique stone bathtub.All villas are assigned their own "naturalist" who will take care of you from start to finish of your visit. The management headed by Mr. Varun was there everyday asking about our stay.Each guest keeps their own schedule (meals, tours, activities); even the menu items are individualized. No set menu, the 5-star chef will prepare anything, any cuisine.The management gave us a surprise every day of our visit there, including a riverside catered picnic. You'd be surprised at the variety of menu items that were available. There were even beds on the riverbanks for our relaxation.I highly recommend this to anyone wishing to visit.

I was especially impressed by its service. The staff went above and beyond to make sure my brother and I had a great stay. The primary reason behind my visit to Meghauli, Chitwan was to check out the Chitwan National park. I had heard Sauraha tends to get crowded, hence Meghauli seemed like a better option; located in a very quiet and isolated area. This lodge is about 1.5 hours drive from Bharatpur airport. It costs us Rs 2000 in a cab to get to the hotel from the airport. If you are a good bargainer, I bet you could still do better.I am a curious traveller. For me it wasn't just a fun trip but was equally an educational trip. We were assigned Subash as our naturalist, that man is seriously a wealth of knowledge. Turns out he's had almost a decade long experience working in numerous national parks of Nepal as well as India. Make sure to find out everything that you've wanted to know about the park, the region or Nepal as a whole.  August is not the best time to visit this place, but I still had the best time because of the opportunity to learn so much about this region. From elephant safari to boat ride, absolutely enjoyed it all. A big thank you to everyone at Barahi Jungle lodge for their hospitality. It was a first class experience! Shall be back again.

From start to finish we couldn't have been more impressed; greeted with cold face cloths and a drink on arrival, driven to our cabin in a golf buggy and then blown away with the detail and Luxery of our accommodation. It is beautifully done with an eco friendly touch. The food was fantastic with Nepali, Chinese or continental options. The swimming pool was wonderful for relaxing with a grass land area visible just across the river where you can see rhinos and other animals coming for a splash or a drink. The activities were fantastic, a safari where we saw 12 rhinos, many deer species, some wild piggies, crocodiles and lots of birds. We also got to bath with some  elephants, get an evening boat ride, eat a sunset picnic, dance with the local Tharp people and enjoy lunch by the river!Can't recommend this destination enough. 10/10 in every aspect, especially the staff who are there to meet your every need

The Jungle Lodge was recommended highly by friends and it didn't disappoint!  The service was excellent and trips bespoke  personal and exclusive. We decided on the two and a half day programme which included the elephant safari, culture show, jeep safari, river boat trip, wildlife presentation, elephant bath and ox cart ride, through the surrounding area. The food and staff are all outstanding and the setting and accommodation first class. I cannot recommend enough - we'll be back again with our guests as soon as we can!  Jai Jungle Lodge, Barahi

Our family thoroughly enjoyed every moment at Bahari Jungle Lodge: the rooms are delightfully decorated, the food bountiful, and the activities one of a kind.  We are all still talking about the elephants we rode, bathed, and admired.  A once in a lifetime experience.  You should plan your visit to Nepal now and make sure to include Bahari Jungle Lodge.

Barahi will see us come back for these very reasons. I visited Barahi towards the beginning of this year with my family. I must say this is the place to be if you’re looking for some peace, quiet and close to nature experience. This was the perfect place to relax and unwind. The activities were very well planned as per our stay. Experienced naturalist took us for nature walks, elephant and jungle safaris. We spotted quite a few animals and birds, though probably the tigers saved themselves for us to come the next time! The boat ride along the Rapti river left us speechless. The rooms, they have an interesting wildlife-inspired decor and are very comfortable. From the balcony, there’s a beautiful view of the river.The staff was extremely warm and courteous. All our needs and requests were very well taken care off. And though something small but every time we got back to the resort after any activity, we were greeted with warm towels and drinks, absolutely refreshing!!Food was nice especially the Nepalese meals.Overall, experience we were looking for! Happy & satisfied!

True safari experience:Stayed with my  7 year old son and his cousin of 10 years for 3 nights.Resort is gated and full of  vegetations overlooking the park,the moment we entered inside,we felt like we were in the jungle. Architectures and construction imbibes the local Tharu culture and lifestyle.Location: pristine,set on the beach of Rapti river,built in the style of local Tharu cottage and rooms impeccable furnished with local flavor yet at the same time amenities were well endowed.Rooms:We stayed in the cottage,they were able to put in a  third bed. View from the balcony overlooking the park is to die for.Interior are very much rustic and reminds of being in the park.If you are bored cable is available.24 hour power back up with AC is a respite.Beds are cozy,bathrooms are well designed with a shower but missed a tub.The balcony overlooking the park is a nice spot for two the sit and enjoy the park with  a drink.Infinity pool: Best part of the vacation was chilling out in the pool after a long day inside the park. Huge pool with place for all,starts at a foot and goes closer to 5 feet in depth.Staff:Very much friendly from the moment we arrived to the time of departure. Mr Subash,Naturalist and Mr Pawan,General Manager were able to arrange a Jeep safari inside the park after talking with the park rangers  at our request even though the resort has already closed the safari for the season.This was such a huge thing for us.Mr Subash was great in arranging our plan for the next day every evening and he was of great help.Highlights:Royal Bengal Tiger sighting: Well they say just about 10% of the Safari takers spot the tiger,we were blessed to see a Tiger about 100 yards from our jeep.And what a show he displayed,stayed and stared us for good 5 minutes before the majestic beast got into dense grassland.Jeep safari: Despite monsoon and having closed the safari,Mr Pawan,Manager and Naturalist MR Subash were able to arrange the safari for us.Kids were thrilled.Mr Subash had an uncanny expertise in locating wildlife. After 20 ,kids gave up counting one horned rhinos.Elephant ride and Elephant bathing: We have rode Elephant in Sauraha,the bigger resort town in the park in the past but the experience at Barahi Jungle Lodge was first class.We went for the ride twice,we had plenty of time to photograph,see the rhinos up close.We even saw the rhino duel up close.Boat ride down the Rapti: well worth,another opportunity to see Gharials,Rhinos and deers up close.Food: Order to cook meals were awesome.Local Nepalese food and Indian food  from fresh local ingredient seems to be the specialty.Continental items were delectable,my son was so much thrilled when a Pizza was served to him.We can not wait to get back to this place,truly a family friendly resort for a true safari experience.

We had been there with friends and family to celebrate the AGM of our club BFRT-8. We stayed there for 2 nights and 3 days. We had an excellent time with friends and family members. Kids enjoyed the most. The location is excellent, far from the main city, very peaceful property. Excellent food made as per our requirements. Swimming pool is big, free wifi at the lounge area only. Rooms are good, neat and clean. Service is great. A must visit to all the travelers to Nepal and a best spot for honeymooners. Elephant bathing was a good experience, Tharu cultural dance in the evening made it more exciting. An expensive property.

We stayed in Barahi Jungle Lodge for two wonderful nights in March, 2015. After three weeks of travelling through Nepal, we wanted a couple of nights to enjoy the peace and quiet of the beautiful Chitwan National Park. This is exactly what we found in Barahi Jungle Lodge. It was a true oasis of tranquility and beauty. First, we had the most warm welcome by almost the entire staff and the owner. From that moment on until the very minute of our departure, we felt like royals. Everything was perfect. The staff was very attentive and extremely friendly. The rooms were spotlessly clean and extremely luxurious, with a stunning view and the most relaxing bathtub. As for the activities, we did the Elephant Back Safari, Boating on the Rapti River and Elephant Bathing. Their elephants are very sweet and during the Elephant Back Safari we even saw a tiger, beautifully crossing the river and coming towards us. Furthermore, the food was the best we've had in Nepal. If you are looking for a paradise on earth, we would recommend going to this place.

Me and my husband stayed at the Suite for two nights, three days and we were in paradise! The suite is pricey but the BEST suite Ive seen so far with all the amenities and a private pool! You have to see it to believe it! The property is very quiet, clean and serene by the river and with just enough activities to do for 2-3 days. The staffs are all very kind, at your service and will make you feel at home. We loved the couples massage. Can't wait to go back!

We got there when it was fully booked, but judging from the service we received, it felt like we were the only ones there. The kids enjoyed the stay, as did the parents. Everyone was very friendly and the food was great. Even my youngest, who is a picky eater, enjoyed the food that Pradeep and his team prepared. Everyone who worked there, seemed to enjoy what they did, including the elephants, Ranikali and Sundarkali.Our guide Prem helped us see a lot of animals. My 5 and 3 year olds were captivated by the presentation on wild animals by Vinita and Chinmay. The experience was a lot more fulfilling than we had expected. One of the most memorable new year, and will be visiting there during Feb-March again, when animal sightings are supposed to be high.

Amazing views, beautiful and authentic rooms, fab location, sights and showers. Thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The food was amazing and the staff friendly and helpful. By far the best resort in Chitwan and maybe in Nepal too ! Definitely need to go back there

If you really wish to have jungle safari in exotic way, don't forget to choose Barahi as awesome food, friendly and experienced staffs who will be on your side to awaits you. You will be totally surprised with room as the rooms are beyond your expect ion. Animal sightseeing at Barahi is one of the best you will ever get in Chitwan national park. Last but not  least sundowner will definitely make your trip worthy

Amazing place and amazing people. I was at this resort for a couple of days during new year's. Although at first the bad road condition did dampen the spirit but all was well once we got there.  The people at the resort were very polite and helpful. The rooms were nicely designed and comfy. Overall a very relaxing and great experience. Special thanx to all the staff!

I have had the good fortune of staying in 6 different properties in Chitwan over the last 20 years. The Barahi Jungle Lodge sets a new standard for the jungle accommodation, with excellent views, easy access to the park just across the river, and a GM that was in the Food and Beverage Division for 10 years, so the presentation and the meal are both superb. Couple this with some of the best guides in the park and you have a winning combination.

Can't imagine staying any place more wonderful than this lodge.  The setting by the river and the park is perfect.  Also enjoyed a walking visit to the nearby villages.  Special events can be arranged such as a candlelit garden dinner and breakfast catered on the shore during a canoe trip.  Food is delicious and they do everything right.  This is also a place for weddings and special events.

I had an amazing break here after a really really hectic month at work. The property is just what i looked for. Nestled in a quieter side of the National park, Bralahi lodge served all its purposes. the rooms are beautifully set up, with french press coffee at your disposal in the rooms. they have limited options for food but what every they served was reah and delicious. the pool area is serene and i could spend days here without getting bored. Sagar, the naturalist is a gentle guy and a local with knowledge of everything you could ask for.  The staffs are always ready to help, literally on their toes. I should applaud the management to be able to motivate their staff to this level. My only suggestion would be to improve their spa, good experienced masseur/masseuse is highly recommended and second is more food options for breakfast. The spa is expensive and so should be the service. I would definitely recommend this place and rate it 11/10 :). would love to visit again.

You might have heard about hybridized travel modes like “Glamping” or “Flash Packing”, but I believe the Barahi Jungle lodge has conceptualized & mastered an entirely new breed of travel experience called ‘Glodging”. A tasteful mix of glamorous abode in the wilds combined with regulated indulgence, eco-friendly diligence, and decadent home-style pampering! This is probably one of THE best eco-lodges we have ever stayed in across the globe, and surely deserves to be a part of the ‘elite’ blue-lists and clubs, but unfortunately (or luckily for itself) still flying under the radar!  We couldn’t believe that we were chilling out in one of the most Romantic Jungle Lodges at the edge of a forest in a Himalayan Country! And the fact that we were the ONLY guests in the entire property only made the sweet experience even more Honeyed!Apart from their luxurious settings, The best experiences of the trip were our interactions with Rani-kali, Tulsi-Kali, Shoba-kali and Raj-Kali – the Barahi Lodge’s resident elephant family. The first day we had privileged to chill out with the younger sisters - up close and personal – right next to the pool area while we were savoring chai made with the finest Himalayan tea leaves.The next day the interaction got even more personal (for the pachyderms) as we were allowed to get even closer and feed them, pet them and also give them a bath. Never have we been this close to the moody giants of the animal kingdom – and especially, engage with them directly. One of the most memorable animal encounters we’ve had.LOCATION: Right next to the Rapti River and in the fringe of the core National parkDINE + DRINK: While everything we tasted at the property was excellent, the meal that stood out the most was the Thali we were served for lunch. They were carefully composed combos of fine food whose sole purpose seemed to be endowing one with the ability to tastefully experience heaven on earth!All through our travels, we’ve had the privilege of being able to experience some wicked sundowners – a classic jungle exercise of savoring a surreal sunset while sipping on your favorite drink. But the one in Barahi Jungle lodge was a bit unique. Our Naturalist guide heard about our obsession to always enjoy a new sunset at a new destination in a unique way and decided to do something special to make the Terai Sundowner stand out for us. He got the lovely staff to organize a special table – right on the helipad –with a spectacular view of the Rapti river. And the glowing lanterns around the helipad and the screaming pink sky that was appearing post sunset only made the experience even more supremely special! Suddenly even the light-weight Gorkha beer seemed to taste like the nectar of the Gods!And Just when we thought we have been treated to all kinds of magical surprises, Mr.Varun had something way more surreal in store for us! To make the romantic retreat even more dreamy, he completely astonished us by organizing a surreal dinner in the bush! The greenery that was glittering with dozens of sexy hurricane lanterns, highly attentive staff attending to your needs, the rhythmic buzz of the jungle residents, free-flowing fine wine, delicious local cuisine. My oh my - Words cannot explain what we saw, felt or experienced. So, I will let the pictures do the talking!ROOM: We stayed in the only SUITE bungalow they have, so this review is based on that. While a stay at this wonderful eco-lodge was magical just as it is, the lovely manager of the property made it even more Suite(er) by throwing in a huge surprise for us - since had read about media articles covering our travels. We were upgraded to one of the best Jungle Villa Suites we have ever stayed in - absolutely free of charge!  The suite was so huge, it was much bigger than our apartment back home in Malaysia. It even had its own private party area in the colossal backyard that came loaded with a massive private pool, fireplace sit out, dining table, and a barbecue area! Now, that’s one wicked retreat!FACILITIES: No Gym. But a fantastic Jungle feel POOL right next to the river!SERVICE: Friendly staff that took care of all my needs with a smile and made us feel pampered and well taken care of. Special Shout out to TEZ at the restaurant, SAKET our naturalist and of course the MAN who made it all magical - Mr. VARUNHOW WIRED YOU WILL BE: Free high speed Wi-Fi that works well all over the property. Big Plasma TV screen dishing out dozens of channels spanning sports, news, music, movies and a wide variety of entertainment in multiple languages

Superb resort in all aspects. Entire staff under leadership of Varunji, VP enhance the value of this hotel. Karan, Saket & Anuja are naturalists with good knowledge and pleasant nature. Krishna Didi perfectly manages kitchen service to guests. Chefs cook food of excellent value. Hygiene and ambience is par excellence. Location on Rapti River banks is an asset to the resort.Attitude and dedication of staff complimentarily upgrades the resort for all guests . Bush Dinner offered by management was icing on the cake. A must visit place while on a tour to Nepal.

The rooms here are so well done you don’t want to get out! But once you push yourself out you’re in front of the Rapti where Sava saw an adult and baby rhino getting into the water! Though I missed the sighting, Very happy about the super relaxing hour of reflexology massage at the very pleasant spa managed by tranquility. The staff make you feel like not leaving but you’re off to test out the African luxury tents a new kms away. Also make sure to grab your checklist if birds, animals and trees before heading into the jungle and the bush dinner is a must!

Barahi jungle lodge is a marvelous property. The hospitality and the service is exceptional! The rooms are a complete luxury. The naturalists are knowledgeable. Jeep safari and boat safari are outstanding. The food is delicious. One has to spend atleast 3 nights here. I'm definitely coming back here. I recommend Barahi Jungle Lodge to everyone! If you want to feel heaven and want to be treated like royalty, come to Barahi Jungle Lodge! Cheers!!

Barahi jungle lodge!! Expressing my gratitude for this marvellous piece is difficult. Everything is just perrfect! Staff, infrastructure, location! You name it and they have it! From little surprises to big happiness, barahi jungle lodge gives you love, care and joy all at the same time. I wish i could stay here forever. Mentioning food- they provide you with super delicious food of your choice ( non-veg, veg, vegan, gluten free). The place is perfectly baby friendly and safe. Solo travellers need not worry at all! Being a travel vlogger and having travelled to sooo many places, trust me, there’s nothing like BARAHI JUNGLE LODGE. The flora and fauna around is impeccable ! I saw TIGERS!! Yes! The place with more than 900 great one horned rhino! The animals here are thriving because they are being taken care of perfectly. Having said that there’s nothing like this place. I highly recommend BARAHI to anyone who wants to experience the drops of heaven on earth. I am definitely visiting again and again and again!!! I LOVE IT!! ❤️❤️❤️

We stayed here for 3 nights on our recent Nepal tour.  It is located right across the river from the Chitwan National Park.  We had a bungalow that was a fair walk from reception and the dining room.  They did have golf carts that you could call to pick you up, but we figured the walk helped offset the delicious food they provided.Since we were with a group of 14 they had us place our dinner order ahead of time.  The order was of the type of food, Nepali, Indian, Chinese, or Western.  People in our group were pretty happy with any of the food we ordered.  I was boring and stuck with the Western food, which was tasty.The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because of the *very* bumpy ride getting to it.  Otherwise it would be 5 stars.

A great location for a safari stop in Nepal to see the One Horned Rhino and if you are very lucky leopard and tiger. It’s a wonderful lodge next to the river. Friendly staff, knowledgeable guides and lots of different activities to enjoy. We spent three very enjoyable days at the Lodge and were rewarded on our safari walk with a viewing of Mum and baby one horned rhinos. We were also very close to tiger, as we could smell them and saw their tree markings and paw prints, but we didn't see them. Such a special experience. Amongst other things we went on an early morning boat trip, a jeep safari, walking safari, village tour by bullock cart, we watched dancers from the local village, watched the elephants bathing and learnt how to make a food bundle and feed them.   The lodge is a special place well run by the team and the food was really good. The refreshing pool is a lovely place to relax and read if you have time.

This place deserves its number 1. I was here for work and didn't have any time to take advantage of the attractions but the accommodation was top, with every detail in the room showimg care and love for the environment, the food was absolutely amazing, the pool area divine. The staff could not be any more helpful and happy to show you around. I just wish I could spend 10 days on holidays here. Meet the elephants and just smile. Nirvana.

Wonderful lodge in the  real jungle. Very friendly and very supportive staff. A great place to relax. Excellent food.We really enjoyed the 4days in the lodge as highlight at the end of our Tibet Nepal trip.

We had four superb days with elephant, boot, walk and Jeep safari with beautiful nature and excellent lodge service. Everything you need will be arranged. Jittery was our excellent guide with patience, nature knowledge and real service. We saw more than 10 rhinos and experienced very nice safaris.

Be under no illusion, getting to Nepal from the UK or Europe is not the shortest or easiest trip you will ever make, and that will probably put off many people. When you get to Katmando you may also think this could have been a mistake, however if you stick with it, you will be well rewarded if you choose this resort. They will meet you at the Airport in a fairly meaningful 4x4 which looks as though it actually does whats it was designed for and as the long bumpy transfer continues deeper and deeper into the country side you realise why they did not just pick you up in a saloon car. The first suprise is on arrival when you are met by the General Manager and his passion for the resort and what they do there just washes over you. what you quickly realise is this passion has already been applied to all of the staff. All the staff have what I will describe as 'relaxed efficiency'  as everything just seems to happen without any effort at all. They are an Eco Frienly resort but that does not effect the level of comfort. The villas have quite a unique rustic design which actually fits in really well with the souroundings, but they still come with little touches that you only find in 5* Resorts.You come here because you are next to a National Park and you have chance to see some of the local wildlife, and this is what makes this place so special, on arrival you are assigned a personal Naturalist for your group ( even if you are travelling solo) who will be with you on every excursion you do. The first trip I did was an Elephant Sarfari, this does not actually go into the the National Park which is accross the river. the first rule of this is listen to what the naturalist tells you, they are not tour reps, they really are qualified and really know there stuff. They normally offer the trips early in the morning or late in the afternoon, but due to the time of year i was told if I wanted to see wildlife go early morning, I did and was not dissapointed, So I had 1 staf member in charge if the elephant and the naturalist using his knowledge to say where the animals will be and pointing them out. The trip was stunning. The next trip I tried was a boat safari which was magical seeing the sun rise over the river and seeing the abundant wildlife. The surprise was at the end of the trip where breakfast was all set up with all the trimings on the bank side,  - wonderful trip This time there was a crew for 3 not including my self. I also tried the Land Rover Safari which got me very very close to a rhino in particular, it wasnt planned, howerer the proffesionalism o fthe team i was with not only ensured I was kept out of danger, but also helped out a large family group who only had a driver and had were on foot and there vehicle was parked too far away to provide any security. Luckily our truck was exacly where it it was needed. They like giving you little surprises like bringing one of the young elephants to see you as you sit by the pool  - just because they can. You might find another resort that offers a higher level of comfort or a lower price, but check their reviews, this place gets 5* for a reason, some of the other resorts close by seem to have upset quite a few of their guests.

I visited Barahi Jungle Lodge for (a too brief) two nights in late June, and cannot recommend the lodge and Pugdundee Safaris highly enough. From the moment I entered it was as if all of the stress of the drive from Bharatpur - in an ill-advised sedan - disappeared. Lodge staff and the lodge's local and sustainable ethos were introduced upon entry, and a personal naturalist was appointed, who helps schedule activities based on your preferences and time - certainly no imposed packages here. I was lucky to have Ashma, a second-generation naturalist, with me and found her enthusiasm and advice about timing valuable for my short stay. Different members of the Pugdundee naturalist team are around the lodge throughout the day and evening, and I found they welcomed questions, are clearly passionate about Chitwan's flora and fauna, and are pragmatic, but positive about possible sightings. I enjoyed the company and knowledge of Ashma and Jitu-ji for a long jungle walk in the late afternoon which, along with deer and monkey sightings, was enriched by their keen eyesight and depth of their knowledge about insects, birds, medicinal plants and animal markings. The quiet walk ended in a close encounter with a rearing sloth bear, thankfully very ably managed by the two staff and their sticks! An early morning paddle down the Rapti river was well worth an early rise - it should be mentioned that the hard-working dining staff were up and ready to provide a much needed cup of tea before the 5am start - as this was the best time to see dozens of rhinos grazing in the water - we even saw two pairs of mothers with their calves. Gharial, turtles, and extensive birdlife were in abundance, and a memorable view was of the resident elephants wandering down through the mist for their morning drink.
