A 3hr afternoon jeep safari with Gobinda took us through several of the park's diverse environments and associated wildlife, but the highlight was sitting in the Sal forest watching a large troop of Hanuman macaques - although startling a rhino a couple of metres from the jeep in the grassland comes a close second.Everything at the lodge runs to time and appears effortless - a credit that must go to the management team. The staff interactions, both hospitality and naturalist, felt genuinely guest-focussed without being cloying. I found the selection of all-inclusive meals well-balanced, and large - you will not go hungry here - but the staff were also happy to accommodate lighter versions if three three-course meals a day are too generous. The cottages are beautifully designed and in harmony with the naturally-landscaped surroundings. Despite the heat the resort is well-provisioned with strong air-conditioning and fans in all cottages, dining, lounge and presentation areas. I would suggest that this is a challenging time to visit for anyone unprepared for heat and humidity, however safaris are scheduled in the early morning and late afternoon to suit both humans and wildlife, so it is manageable if this is the only time you have. I can only look forward to returning to Barahi and the Pugdundee team in the future during a cooler season.

Mostly this was a very good experience. Room was very comfortable and jeep and boat safaris were interesting and as advertised.  We saw rhino, crocodile, wild boar, lots of deer. Guide was knowledgeable, attentive, concerned about the environment.  Pool was refreshing and attractive.  Downsides were that guide and staff hovered a bit too much and pressed their agenda a bit strongly.  Partly we were there for their knowledge and guidance, of course, but partly were were there for family time, and they were a bit overly present, especially at meals.  We would encourage them to keep in mind that many guests are traveling partly to spend time together as a family or couple, and value space and privacy.

We've had a most enjoyable 3-days stay at this rather new lodge: excellent food and service and a wide range of activities such as Jeep Safari in the jungle, riding elephants safari, jungle walk, boat safari, lecture, local ethnic dances and many more. With the help of our excellent guide, Jitu, we were able to watch the diverse wildlife of the national park, including many rhinos, 4 deer species, boars, monkeys, crocodiles and a lot of exotic birds. The room was spacious, clean and beautifully designed, including wi-fi. The lodge is eco-friendly, and employs local people.

Of all the amazing experiences in Nepal our stay at Barahi was definitely the highlight..from communications with their office in Kathmandu months before hand which were so warm and genuine right through to saying bye to our wonderful naturalist ..it wasn't about ticking a box ..it felt like a series of very special moments shared with family.We stayed in the suite for four nights and had our 9/7 year old with us..the room, beds, design ..was just perfect..loved the sivit in the trees on our final BBQ dinner evening by our pool and the jungle cat outside on our last morning..A special mention ..all four of us freely drank the water from the glass bottles in the room and the restaraunt and not only was it delicious but there was no issue at all with any of us..the lodges treatment process and also initiative in plastics reduction was well noted, respected and one could only hope further developed with support from future guests.The food was oh so delicious ..and the lengths to please one small person of ours fussy eating was so caring and never too much trouble.All of the staff were amazing...and one thing ..in our whole trip..so many places in Nepal and Singapore were about ohh please write a review for us blah blah which was at times ridiculous..the beauty of Barahi...all the staff were so lovely and genuine..and no one asked for anything..as mentioned it felt like family..attentitive and warm but never invasive or fake..Whilst the lodgings, food and staff were amazing we were here for the wildlife..and we were not disappointed ..it's so important to note...the elephants were so well loved and treated by the lodge..and we all fell in love with them..hugging an elephant and making and feeding it sandwiches with its mahout will be an experience that will stay with us forever.We did all the activities the lodge had to offer and standing on new year eve at sunset where the two rivers meet was so special ..and we were blessed on the first day of the year to witness a bengal tiger pop out of the bush...go for a swim and just be total boss and disappear on the other side with total swagger was for us..our naturalists and driver on jeep safari a very incredibly experience..one can only hope the military protection of the park allows the wildlife to flourish.. but it just wasn't the tiger...we saw so many rhinos, deer, ghariels and so many amazing birds ..we were left so happy to witness without being invasive so many wonders of nature..If we didn't have our children with us at this age..I definitely would have done the long walk into the jungle and we didn't see a sloth bear but we live life embracing the moments that present not the moments that don't..and our stay at Barahi was so perfectly wonderful to indulge all of our senses with so many very special moments that did..so wildly wonderful was our stay...

As soon as you arrive you are welcomed by gracious staff who offered us a cup of tea. We were instructed of how eco-friendly this place is and how safe the tap water is. The bungalows made it felt homey. The room was spacious and decorated with natural material. While on the balcony you could see elephants pass by. Early in the morning and also late at night you could hear all the fauna dancing and singing. The staff provided us with leech boots to prepare us for the river cruises and the walk in Chitwan National Park.The meals at the restaurant were ordered ahead of time and made fresh. The soup was so delicious that one of our friend requested some for breakfast again before we left.I cannot wait to go back.

Picking up Chitwan National Park was always in the itinerary. But choosing Barahi Lodge was the best decision. I don't think we would have liked the place if it wasn't for this property. Right from stepping into the property till check-out, the warmth, hospitality and care shown was impeccable. The place is nicely done, rooms are up to the mark, and the views of the jungle is remarkable. The two Naturalists Giri and Saket made our trip delightful and insightful. These two young chaps need a pat on their back for knowing the jungle and wildlife at the tip of their fingers. The jungle walk,  jeep safari, breakfast in the middle of the jungle, boat ride and the surprise element of sundowner- set up by the banks of Rapti river (where you enjoy watching the sunset with evening snacks and drinks of your choice) was the highlight. Highly recommended and worth what we paid.

This is one of its kind of a place. Beautifully designed and spacious, the rooms are built like huts. The decor is rustic but no compromise haa been made on comfort. The interior is beautiful. A common theme is followed throughout the property spread in 23 hectares of land. Situated on the banks of Rapti river, it offers good view of the river and jungle. All the jungle activities like elephant ride, jungle walk, boating, jeep safari are available.The food was delicious and freshly prepared. The bar was well stocked. The swimming pool is beautifully designed and looks fabulous at night.Last but not the least, the staffs were very courteous and ready to help with a smile. Will definitely visit again.

We spent 5 days, 4 nights at the lodge and would recommend that trip length. By having a longer stay than most guests, we were able to do most of the activities twice, once in the morning and again in the late afternoon.  This matters due to the activities of the animals, and also ensures that you will see lots of them.  Our favorite adventure was a late afternoon jeep safari where we saw two rhinos fighting over a pond, with a troupe of monkeys and deer as spectators ( as well as us), but it was only one of many great experiences we had while there.  Our guide, Juti was very knowledgeable and did a marvelous job of determining what activities to do when.  The lodge staff were very friendly and would often sit around and chat with us in the evening about their day, or their best, most amusing adventures ever.  Our package included three meals a day, with a large selection of items, do try the Nepalese dinner ( but European or Indian selections were also available).  Our natural tendency is for light dinners, which the restaurant was quick to accommodate us on, which was very kind.Our room was very nicely decorated and comfortable ( we had the standard room), and had all the mod cons.  The lodge generator would start up after a few minutes during power outages, which do happen.  I enjoyed sitting out on the deck watching the world go by in our free time,it was very peaceful.  If staying here, I would recommend a small flashlight to help you get back to the right room at night.If you want to see rhinos, this is the place

We stayed at Barahi this past weekend and it was a wonderful experience.The hotel is very well situated bordering River Rapti, the start of the National park. The activities start right outside the property which means that you never have to leave the property to start an activity. They have impeccable customer service which I think has a lot to do with the very detail oriented Mr. Varun Kumar the General Manager of the property. He greeted us personally on our arrival and gave us a brief of the hotel and its activities which was much appreciated. He makes each one of us feel important. The highlights of our stay was the Canoe ride (they have a wonderful set up with drinks after the ride is over and you can watch the sun set, do not miss it! The jungle safari is also a must do, they had packed up breakfast and set it up for us overlooking the river. The food is amazing with three different cuisines  to choose from. We were never disappointed. Over all our stay was made very comfortable by the staff who were extremely hospitable and accommodating.

We ( a group of 18 including kids )were here at Barahi to welcome the new year 2017 and if our stay here is something to go by it should be a fabulous one for all of us !!My second time here and it was nothing short of spectacular.Right from our arrival to our departure the service offered was immaculate and the team deserves a big Pat on the back for that.The ambience is perfect for a jungle lodge and everything seems in perfect synch with the surroundings.The rooms are fantastic with all the required amenities and the feel of the rooms is unique.The common areas are well done and are really cosy which is important as a lot of ones time is spent here during the stay.The naturalists here seem to be in love with what they are doing.A special mention here for Saaket !! Thanks man for everything .Govinda was also very good !!Tej with the F&B was brilliant and led the department with aplomb.The menu is good and what they serve is seriously good.The new year eves gala was well organized with the highlight being the elephant show.The highlight of the trip was jungle lunch during the jeep safari and the arrangement they did at the sunset view point.Mr Varun the manager is the man behind the show and deserves a pat on the back for motivating his team to perform the way they do," you have asked for it sir and so it will be done" is what he has to say to all the demanding demands put to him!!Definitely by far the best property in Nepal and is highly recommended.A trip to Nepal without a stay at Barahi is incomplete!!

My Husband and I stayed in Barahi for 3 days 2 nights. Overall this lodge provides impeccable services, facilities and activities but as we were on the full board plan. Both my Husband and I had food poisoning subsequently on our day 2 and 3. While the room is nicely decorated just like the picture; the sewage smell from the toilet is really bad though they tried to fix it after the first day it slowly came back throughout the night.

It was a pleasure visiting your resort – Barahi Jungle Lodge.  We are very thankful for all the services you have provided us during our stay. From the time we reached Barahi Jungle Lodge, we were very much impressed with the professionalism and responsiveness of your staff members - assets and beauty of your resort. Your GRO Mr. Subash Gurung was very Humble & Professional. Also, our Naturalist Mr. Gobinda was very helpful and friendly. He knew how to deal with the situation. All the staff members were outstanding, friendly and attentive, made our stay very enjoyable.We are in love with your property which has been constructed so simple yet beautifully keeping all the small details in mind. The huts are so cozy, luxurious & ECO friendly. The bathrooms including the shower were impressive. The overall property is attractively decorated, perfectly clean and well maintained. We noticed that you offer Ala-carte instead of buffet which makes your resort different than the rest. We went on 3 safaris – Elephant Safari, Early morning Jeep Safari with breakfast & Canoe ride with sunset. My husband and friends love the surprise after our canoe ride – barbeque set and sundowner drinks. Truly Special :)… During safari, we saw about 6 rhinos (including baby rhino), many deers, monkeys, wild boar, crocodiles and lots of birds including Peacock/Peahens. We also spent an hour in Tharu village tour on Ox-cart, which was a once in a lifetime experience and my son enjoyed it a lot. The spa/massage facilities were comfy and perfect way to end the safari filled days. Even though the road to Chitwan is very tough one as you know, the moment we reached your place, we forgot all the bumps and problems we faced on the way. Everything was utterly perfect throughout our stay.  We are very much obliged for all the extra services you have provided us during our stay. Special thanks to Varun Sir for treating us like a family member.

My wife and I have been doing "Glamping" (glamorous camping) travel for several years now, and frankly, the quality of the wilderness lodges varies widely. If only they were all like this one: the rooms, food, guides, and service were absolutely fantastic and had we only known we would have booked all of our time in Chitwan here! The location is great - right on the river that forms one of the borders of the National Park, and even our jungle trek in the "buffer zone" rewarded us with a number of great wildlife views including the Indian Rhinoceros. If any of you are birdwatchers - the jungle is of course full of birds, but so is the hotel garden, so bring your binoculars to every meal! All the service personnel were wonderful, but I was also very impressed with the guides. Naturally the nature guides knew the mammals and plants, but I was also excited to discover that they were real experts on the local birds and butterflies (particular interests of mine) and which isn't always the case. All in all, as far as we could tell, this is THE place to come to experience the amazing nature of Chitwan NP´and easily the best place we stayed in Nepal.

This place is a must visit when in Nepal. I will not ruin the experience by telling all the details but this is an extremely well run property with fantastic staff taking care of the guests in every possible way. We enjoyed the stay, the safaris, the food and the experience in general. Thanks to Barahi Jungle Lodge for a great stay.

Even though the road to barahi jungle lodge is a tough one, the moment you reach there you will forget about the multiple bumps you had on your way and you will feel that it was worth it! beautiful and luxurious room with amazing small specifications, very helpful and friendly staff, interesting activities and scrumptious food!A must visit!

We had a great 3 night stay at the Barahi Jungle Lodge. We arrived on our wedding anniversary and, unbeknown to us, our guide Rajeev from Dharma Adventures (a great company to show you the sights of Nepal) called ahead to let the lodge know - as a result we were upgraded to a suite. It was awesome - two double bedrooms, lounge/dining room, rain shower and its own private pool. What a treat!  We were then surprised and delighted with an anniversary cake and dinner outside in the jungle surrounded by lanterns and fairy lights. And I haven't even started on the excursions and activities yet..... Our guide for our time there was Krishna who was excellent. He took great delighted in ensuring that we had a great time - elephant safari, Safari walk, boat safari with a sundowner at sunset, ox and cart ride to the village and best of all feeding and bathing the elephants. We saw lots of rhinos, crocodiles, birds, wild boar and deer. No sightings of the elusive tigers but we had a fantastic stay. Thank you. We would definitely recommend a stay here - you will never want to leave!

The journey to Barahi Lodge was arduous due to poor road conditions but once you enter the ages of Barahi, every minute is magical. Special mention to our naturalist Govind for making the experience amazing!

We'd been to the Chitwan area before some of the new hotel developments and previously there were very basic hotels so we were thrilled to find a true luxury (but very comfortable and low keyed) hotel/resort.  Our stay started with a very warm greeting from the manager and staff and then we visited our room.  The rooms are incredible comfortable with great showers and a balcony with views of the river and park.  The bed was very comfortable and we had a free mini bar.  Also very quiet and private.  The meals are included and the staff makes them to your request.  We are vegetarian and all meals were creative and delicious.  The service was always warm and supportive but not invasive.  For our three days we had the best of guides (Krishna) who took us on a safari through the park and served a great rivers lunch.  We saw lots of wildlife.  At our request he took us into some of the local communities where we were able to assist with some of their basic needs (e.g. building a well for only $250.00).  We had a beautiful river ride one evening culminating in a wine and cheese party at the end while enjoying a magnificent sunset.  Also enjoyed an extended outside dinner in the brush around the hotel all lit with torches.  Fantastic!  This is a small, luxury, well managed, hotel with a wonderful staff and I can't wait for our return now planned for March 2017!

Bahari Jungle lodge had exceptional service and was a truly beautiful spot to relax. My sister and I went on several safaris in to the jungle by boat, jeep, elephant and on foot. Our guide Krishna was so informative, helpful and excellent company. We experienced more than I could've possibly imaged. The private dinner that was organised for my 30th was an experience I will never forget as was the sunset on our boat trip. I came back feeling truly blessed and the luckiest girl in the world. Thank you to all the staff who invested so much in making this the trip of a lifetime!!!

Exceptional service, great facilities, helpful staff, good array of activities from elephant safari through keep safari to boat safari. Food was also top notch. Kids had fun, good pool with shallow zone, loads of space and loved the elephants! Only challenge was booking where we used the central booking system which was time consuming and inefficient. For the next visit, we will call direct.

The lodge was the best place to stay in Chitwan. The staff and people there were super nice and really helpful. The place had it all:-fantastic food-great accommodations-beautiful view-fun activities-rooms are very spacious-great and helpful staffIt's was like heaven (well for me). The activities they planned for my dad and I made this trip the most memorable trip. I recommend everyone to come and stay here. The Barahi Jungle Lodge has its own wildlife guides and naturists that will that you on boat rides and elephant rides. They also take you on jeep safaris and jungle walks to tell and show you everything you would want to know about the spectacular and amazing wildlife in Chitwan. The Barahi Jungle Lodge has their own elephants which are taken well care of. Thank you so much for the amazing experience, Barahi Jungle Lodge. Special thanks to Vineeta Didi and everyone else who made my stay AWESOMEEEEE....

We stayed in Barahi for 3 days and every moment we spent there were quality time. Food was amazing and they cooked anything we asked for. It was quiet period there because of earthquakes and political disturbances but they never made us feel that. Best staffs.. always smiling and providing assistance with everything. I am from Nepal and I feel so proud to have such place back home.

Staying at the lodge is a fantastic enjoyable experience - beautiful comfortable private rooms, superb service with a smile, a pool and spa, plus views of the jungle.Staying here is a real treat!  They offer jeep safaris, elephant rides, and boating on the river to spot the animals of the quiet jungle.  Good guides and staff to teach you about the jungle and the animals living there.They took us to a local village to meet the lovely people that live in the area.A very worthwhile stay!

Barahi is everything we expected and more. It is a top notch jungle lodge that is focused on its wildlife program without compromising on the rest of the experience that makes any stay memorable. From the moment we arrived until the moment we left, the staff was extremely attentive and responsive to our needs -  The accommodation is individual cottage style and are all designed to mirror the rural setting so nothing feels out of place. Once inside it is all luxury with great attention to detail.  The common areas are great with a pool overlooking the river and the forest reserve. The full safari package includes an elephant safari in the community forest (it is as experiential as the main jungle with lots of Rhinos and other wildlife sightings to be had) a river boat experience with a wine and cheese sundowner (weather permitting), jeep safari in the main jungle, village walk and birding. We choose all of the above sans the jeep safari as the season did not permit jeeps to ply in the jungle due to monsoon season. We have stayed in other properties owned by Pugdundee Safaris  - Tree House Hideaway in Bandhavgarh, Ken River Lodge in Panna, Earth Lodge in Kanha. Barahi shares the same commitment to providing top notch wildlife experience as its sister properties without any compromise on comfort and luxury.The only reason Barahi does not get a 10/10 across the board is because there were moments when we were not sure if what we were getting was included in the full package or was charged extra. e.g. on the sundowner following the river cruise they laid out some cheese and wine and only later did we know that the wine was on a chargeable basis. Incidences such as this apart, I would highly recommend Barahi Jungle Lodge for those visiting Chitwan. Location: 9/10Property: 10/10Food: 10/10Service: 10/10Safari/Naturalists: 10/10Value for money: 9/10

We were greeted at reception with a cool drink and cold face washer along with a warm welcome and smiles from all the staff. I thought I was in heaven when I saw the room. The design is unique and has so much detail, like pottery animals, hand made chairs and tables, organic soaps, bath robes, beautiful cushions on the beds; I could go on. The air con was already on so we stepped into a cool welcoming room. The view from the balcony of our room looked across the Rapti River into the Chitwan National Park. The dining and pool areas were furnished with the hand made furniture and cushions and the decore has an attention to detail. Service was top rate, nothing was too much. We could call for a lift in the golf cart at any time. Activities included jungle safari, cultural show, information sessions about the park and wildlife, lunch by the river - in another location, tour of a Tharu village and this included all meals! Highly recommended.

I had a 2-night, 3-day stay in Barahi Jungle Lodge last week and I still can't get this place out of my head. No matter how hard I tried, I could not fault the place one bit, even the rain didn't stop me from loving every second!I arrived by bus from Pokhara and was greeted by a member of the Barahi Team and taken by car to the lodge. Upon arrival the manager of the Lodge amongst other staff met me and briefed me on everything from the interior of the lodge, to the food and of course the jungle activities.The room was breath taking, a combination of traditional and contemporary, the bed was incredible, as was the enormous bath tub. All lodges have balconies look out on to the Rapti River.The food was sensational, there is no menu system, only you tell the staff what you want to eat. Each meal consists of a number of courses including salads, soups, fish, meat etc. all very freshly prepared and healthy. I never once felt hungry as the snacks and drinks flow all day long, without even having to request anything.I enjoyed several jungle actives such as jungle jeep safari, river safari, elephant safari and a trip to the local Tharu village. Each activity was a private one with at least two guides at all times so you feel very safe and extremely well informed about the the surrounding area and of course the animals. If you get Vineeta or Krishna as your guide you will be very lucky because as far as I'm concerned - they are the best!All of the other staff are absolutely delightful and attentive beyond belief. They all appear to be very good friends too which makes for a very relaxed and comfortable environment. The only thing I didn't do was try out the pool as the weather wasn't that great but it still looked amazing!All in all it was the best trip ever, I will never forget it and that's not only because of the amazing things I saw, but because of the beautiful location and the kindness of the people that work there. Thank you to everyone at Barahi Jungle Lodge for going above and beyond for making my stay such a special one.

If you are looking for the best from the best providers- look no further. We stubled into this resort through an arrangement from a  friend's recommendation. Boy, he nailed it. Its is simply breathtaking. I would say this is one of a kind, at least in and around Nepal. Having travelled around the world and been to many hig end resorts, Barahi actually rubbed shoulders with many and excelled in certain areas. They make you feel so special that, you feel homesick after your departure. We were there for a coupla days right after Chistmass 2014, it seemed like the X Mass gifts kept coming. If you aver plan to stay at the jungle corridor of Nepal in Chitwan vicinity, please do yourself a favor and pick this resort. You will thank yourself!!! I can go on and on on how pretty and well organised everything is there, I can go on and on. Thanks again to the world class team at Barahi!!!!

Two nights at the Barahi Lodge was a great way to finish off our holiday. We had changed our accommodation only a few weeks before and we are so glad that we did, we couldn't have dreamt of anywhere better to enjoy an adventure in the Terai. From the time we were met at the lodge the staff were all very hospitable, friendly and very informative. The lodge itself is very is a recent, and most welcome, addition to the accommodation available in Chitwan. The traditional style bungalows offer the comfort you'd expect in a modern high quality hotel, with a few quirky additions. And the hospitality doesn't stop there, there's plenty of lovely food for breakfast, lunch and dinner. And should you find some time to relax between the superb activities, you can take a dip in the infinity pool where it almost feels as if the basking local Gharial and Mugger on the banks of the Rapti river are in ther with you. Or you could sit and enjoy a Gurkha beer sitting comfortably at the poolside bar.What makes a visit to the lodge so special are the many activities that are provided, we only stayed for two nights but managed to cram in a number of excursions. Firstly we were escourted on a tour of a nearby Tharu village, where life carries on as it has for centuries in mud and reed houses (some with satelite dishes), we thought that this would feel quite intusive, but their natural hospitality, especially the children, overcomes this. The walk takes you down to the confluence of the Narayani river to see the sun set, the journey back to the lodge is taken in the back of a cart drawn by two waterbuffalo. An early morning elephant ride through the forest and the elephant grass allows you to get up close to one horned rhinos, and the shy spotted deer. Later we got to meet one of them and get close and personal, even the chance to take a bath with her. Late afternoon saw us take a boat trip down the river, before walking through the National Park. Whilst everyone who goes to Chitwan wants to see a Bengal Tiger, one nearby roar was enough to convince our group that we may not wish to get too close. (We also saw evidence that a Tiger had wandered through the grounds of the Lodge the previous night) We did however get up close to some rhinos, being on foot near these wild animals makes you realise how small we really are, and it certainly gets your heart beating. That evening we were entertained by a troop of local dancers performing traditional Tharu dances, which we were encouraged to join in. If there is one negative about the Barahi Lodge it is the VERY bumpy hour's drive to get to the lodge from Baratpur, but there is a positive to this in that it keeps most of the modern world at bay.If you are considering a couple of days in Chitwan, this is the place to stay. I hope you enjoy it as much as we did.

Certainly the best quality hotel we stayed at in two weeks in Nepal.The standard of the rooms would be entirely acceptable anywhere in the world.The resort consists of a number of separate lodges, each with air conditioning and a view across the river to the jungle proper.The heart of the resort gathers round the pool - a great place to relax in the heat of the day. Food was good, and a number of tours are available - I can particularly recommend the elephant ride through the jungle and down to the river where rhino, deer and crocodiles can be seen.The only downside to this resort is that access is the quality of the access road. Like many roads in Nepal it may have been surfaced once, but is now endless stretches of potholes and gravel. Probably only twenty miles, but a very slow and tedious hour's journey from the nearest town.

Wow! That was amazing trip to Chitwan with Barahi Jungle lodge. I would like to recommend Barahi Jungle lodge to the entire higher-class tourists who want to visit Chitwan National Park. It is well located from National Park on the bank of Rapti River. You can see National park view from every cottage. Room have AC, TV, and Tea/coffee maker with well inertial design to make maximum nature friendly. I think you cannot find any other Jungle lodge in Chitwan similar with Barahi Jungle Lodge. I am planning to send all of my high-class tourists to Barahi Jungle Lodge.  Best of Luck ! Thank you for your homely service.

The pick up vechicke for which I paid 80 usd was a lousy  jeep  in which the air conditioning  was not working  and the temperature  was 110 F outside! The price of 500 usd  per person including  food, which was basic is a rip off. At best worth  half the price. The real highlight  was a friendly  staff, very  obliging.

This place is amazing- knowledgable and informative friendly guides, professional friendly staff, great sunrise, great food- spoilt really! The safaris are some of the best- do the walking safari for a truly enlightening experience! The owner / manager incredibly down to earth- Loved the program- definitely come back!

Stunning place to completely switch off. Staff are fantastic. Grounds and lodges are idyllic. The trips were great and I joined the lovely girls in the morning for yoga before they started their work. A great way to set yourself up for the day.

I am a frequent traveller and love exploring different tourist destinations . But without exaggerating I have to say my 3 days stay at the Barahi Jungle Lodge was by far the best holiday I ever had . The place is beautiful , rooms are perfect but what made our stay beyond expectations was the hospitality extended to us by the entire staff .. the General Manager Mr. Prakash made this stay for us a memory of a lifetime . The entire staff arranged a birthday surprise for my husband in a very Nepali traditional way which I could have never imagined ..”Absolutely  Brilliant” is the word for the food served which is also made to order with personalized expectations which makes you feel at home .. the naturalist who took us across for all the activities Mr. Rajesh is extremely professional and we enjoyed every activity we did right from Village tour , Honey Farming , Jeep Safari with Sun downing … everyday evenings are filled with a festive mode with the local tribal villagers who come over and perform their traditional dances and engaged us as well to participate with them .... this place is a must must must visit for everyone who loves nature and want to feeel like a King because that’s how we have felt in the past 3 days by the perfect management of Mr. Prakash and his team … keep it going and wishing you all the best .We are surely coming again .

We stayed for 2 nights and 3 days at the Barahi Jungle Lodge on 17-19th March, 2022. To be honest, prior to our experience, we were half-hearted about shelling out the 28000 NPR nett per couple for a night and wondered if the comparatively steep cost would be really worth it.We checked-in at the lodge to a very warm welcome from the staffs with fresh wet towels and a refreshing lime drink. After a quick briefing regarding the property and our upcoming jungle activities, we were transferred to our cottages in their electric golf carts. Traversing the pebbled track to our rooms itself felt like a journey through the jungle as the massive property is immensely filled and surrounded with well maintained greeneries and trees of various kinds. Interestingly during the evenings, all the key areas in the property are beautifully lit with hundreds of kerosene lanterns that create a very warm, romantic and cozy ambience under the starry nights. The ecological cottages blend well with the jungle environment and interior design inspirations have been taken from the local Tharu culture. There is a balcony set-up as well which beautifully overlooks the Rapti River just a few meters ahead and the dense Chitwan National Park across the river. Surprisingly, amidst all the well set-up in-room services and amenities, the rooms do not have mini fridges on them. But that seemed the least of our concerns even in the hot and humid weather, as the hotel bar happily chilled our beers/juices and we could enjoy them freely anywhere in the property without any added cost. They also thoughtfully waived the corkage charge for bringing our own alcohol. While at the property before or after the jungle activities, the well-designed Infiniti pool area overlooking the jungle is the perfect place to relax or soak in the hot afternoons. During the evenings, this area is abuzz with the cultural Kumal and Tharu performance shows.Our Jungle Plan package had a Boat Safari with a relaxed sundowner experience scheduled for the arrival day and a half-day Jeep Safari for the next day. Since we were travelling with a 2yr old kid, the naturalists humbly adjusted the tours to our suitable timings. The Boat Safari was a thrilling experience with a crocodile swimming near our boat and another swimming past just below. There was a plenty of fascinating bird sightings as well. The sundowner experience with complimentary light snacks, BBQ and soft drinks provided a mesmerizing view during the beautiful sunset hour at the Golalghat confluence point of Rapti and Narayani River. It would have been an icing on cake though, if they added a limited complimentary offering of wine and beer as well, because it's very easy to misunderstand the set-up as complimentary. The afternoon Jungle Jeep Safari the next day was the best we have experienced by far with close sightings of various animals in their natural habitat. Thoughtfully, they also packed afternoon tea/coffee and biscuits/cakes to be enjoyed in the jungle during the safari. Amongst the regular encounters with Deers, Rhinoceros, Wild Boar, etc we were extremely lucky to spot the elusive Royal Bengal Tiger as well. Our naturalist and driver skillfully spotted the rare Royal Bengal Tiger taking a dip in one of the watering holes in the Jungle and we enjoyed the unforgettable sight for a good 25 minutes.To sum it up, our stay at the Barahi Jungle Lodge was unlike any of our numerous trips to the Chitwan National Park. BJL in Meghauli initially might seem remotely isolated compared to the heavily commercialized Sauraha for most people, but the the charm of the lodge is in being the ultimate jungle destination itself. Once inside the main gates, we didn't really need to get out until departure, since every activity begins from inside the property itself. The food buffet spread is pretty good as well and you really don't go hungry with the full board plan as all meals are set up on time with a variety of offerings everyday and stay open till late, well beyond the stated timings. Also, the very hospitable and welcoming staffs are very kid friendly as well. We were travelling with our 2yr old daughter and they always served us unhesitantly whenever we had special request for baby meals and drinks beyond what was being regularly served.Overall, Barahi Jungle Lodge is definitely a 10/10 property. It's no doubt worth an experience...PS: My only suggestion to them would be to have the housekeeping department pay little more attention to cleaning the spider webs in some of the hidden spaces and corners in the room. I agree its a jungle in there, but I believe this is an avoidable problem at least in the rooms.

We used Barahi Lodge as an extension to our 6 days in Kazaringa (Assam). It is a large lodge, some 35 rooms. Our room (No 2) was of a good size and comfortable. WiFi, TV, tea/coffee facilities, AC, adequate hanging space/drawers for clothes. Safe. Balcony with 2 chairs. Decent size bathroom with a large bath, shower within bath. All amenities. Charging board for 3 units. There is a large swimming pool. Outside bar with comfortable seating. Large restaurant. Excellent food and the F and B Manager (Dej) looked after us very well. Not a huge choice but what we had was always hot and flavoursome but not as spicy as India. Access to Chitwan NP was by a small boat across the river and safari jeep. There is a Sundowner Cruise available and also all day safaris with picnic lunch (also very good). Tiger, Leopard, Sloth Bear are here along with limited numbers of 1-horned Rhino. Excellent bird watching (167 species seen). I'm not keen on large resorts but this was very good and with limited numbers staying it was quiet. Long drive from Kathmandu (5-6 hours depending on traffic). Our guide was Karan Giri who did a great job for our 6 night stay. Keen to please and knowledgeable. Really worth a decent length stay - 3 nights minimum.

Very good property. Rooms are big and nice. Staff are friendly. Food is very good. The activities are great fun. The naturalists are well trained and guide you through the safari well. Definetly recommended.

We stayed for two nights and had a fantastic stay.  The grounds and accommodation were lovely and very comfortable.  All of the staff was very friendly and communicative. The food was good, but probably the weak link in the operation. Our guide Rajib was excellent. They pair you with one guide throughout your stay, which was very nice. For most excursions it was just the 2 of us and him, on the Jeep ride we rode with another couple and their guide.  It didn’t feel like group travel at all, instead it was individualized. We saw lots of animals, including a Tiger!!  We also really enjoyed a bike ride through the neighboring village. Highly recommend!

everything about the lodge oozes class. from the well laid out, river facing bungalows, tastefully done up with all the comforts..and stocked with amazing cookies!!to the quality of the game drives, the elephant rides, the efficiency of managing your agenda, the meals, the entertainment..and the sheer abundance of wildlife available..especially rhinos!! a must do!!

Our trip to Nepal included two nights at barahi and wish we could have stayed longer.  We felt we were treated like royalty.  The staff are ultra professional, knowledgeable about the area, the animals and make sure you get the best experience possible.  The food was the best we had on our trip, it was exceptional.  The lodges are so comfortable and quirky and I love their values on saving the environment.  From the moment we arrived we felt very cared for, from the welcome talk from the manager to the day and night activities which were all exceptional.  I loved our travels around Nepal and staying at barahi was certainly the highlight.  Thank you to all the amazing staff for their care, fun and knowledge of particular mention is our personal naturalist Rajeb, he was a superstar and looked after my friend and I with the utmost care to attention to ensure we Had the best experiences and made lifetime memories.  I can't praise this place highly enough it is romantic, fun, comfortable, quirky and outstanding.  We stayed in lodge 9 and loved the home comforts provided including the pick ups to take us to the main complex.  The little touches made all the difference, i.e. Returning from elephant safari and a young lady waiting for you with hot towels to freshen up, we had no idea how she knew what time we were to be there!  Breakfast on the river was a huge welcome surprise as well as the evening special bush meal.  Keep up the amazing experience you work so hard to achieve, it is a gem.

The word "Lodge" does not adequately describe this place. The accommodation, food, and, service are as good as any 5 star hotel in London. Hot showers, very comfortable bed, air conditioning, a balcony, superb housekeeping. The food was varied and well cooked. Sometimes a buffet other times a pre order. The staff are, to a man and woman, attentive but not intrusive. In addition you get to go on safaris and see wild life. Boat/jeep/walking/elephant or all four. We saw crocodiles, 8 rhinoceros, monkeys, deer, and many birds over a period of three days. Hari our guide was knowledgeable and a good spotter.The treat of the stay, indeed in my view, the entire time in Nepal, was being able to ride an elephant in the river for its morning shower, of it and me, and then to feed them. I was sorry to have to move on.

3 days were the best vacation we have ever had! The best part about barahi isn't their gorgeous location or delicious food or their cosy rooms - it's their service and attention to detail that will make you fall in love with them. We thoroughly enjoyed their jeep and boat safaris and highly recommend to try them along with the jungle walk. And the best memory we have is of the sun downer at the confluence of two rivers. It's was such a stunning sunset and we enjoyed their BBQ. The gm and their staff are always looking forward to besting your experience the previous and go the extra mile to take care of you. And yes if you are staying for more than two nights something very interesting awaits you.

Everything from start to finish was spectacular. As someone who is pretty picky and have travelled extensively around the world, I am amazed that I don’t have any critique for the resort (maybe the first time). Food was some of the best food I’ve had. Lodging was spotless and well-designed. Jungle activities we went on were top-notch. Staff members were always so kind and willing to assist. In addition, the owner offered us many complementary activities, upgrades, and wonderful surprises (e.g dining in a lantern-lit, and private area). I travelled with 4 other friends and we all truly had an amazing time. Highly recommend and will try to return back as soon as I can!

Excellent accomodation. Delightful staff who couldn't have been more helpful. Delicious food. And jungle safaris in jeeps, boat trips etc were all well organised, fun & interesting.. It was all over too quickly!

From the moment I was met at the airport to when I was dropped off at the airport, I was treated with sterling service! Perched right on Chitwan National Park, Barahi is privileged to be in a gorgeous location as it is nestled alongside the river with stunning views far and wide. The resort in clean, professionally run and there is always a warm smile to greet you.Subhash the operations Manager took me through the resort and its amenities and was most gracious and accommodating throughout - I could not thank him enough for all the unexpected touches that he and his staff provided to ensure that my stay there was a happy, relaxing one. On the eve of my birthday, the staff had all got together and presented me with an amazing birthday cake and placed a beautifully printed scarf around my neck. I was treated like a princess throughout and I knew that I had made the right choice to choose Barahi. The staff are observant, ready when you need them and they also know when to leave you alone. I chose to have an evening Bush meal and was stunned by the 150 lights that the staff had lit in the forest. Of highest commendation next to the service,  is the food -  the grilled fish and steak was mouth-watering, juicy, fresh and astoundingly delicious. I am still craving these as I traverse the streets of Kathmandu looking for the same or better. No such luck.So if I could give Barahi all the stars in the world (not just a rating of 5 stars), it's only because they truly deserve them.

We stayed at Barahi Jungle Lodge, Chitwan National Park, Nepal, in May 2019 for a few days.  This lodge has it all; wonderful accommodations, well-planned excursions and all the food and cultural experiences you could ask for.  Would have loved to stay for 5 to 7 days, but our tour moved on.

If you are going on a Safari in Chitwan this is the place to stay.  Quite, peaceful, close to the key places, 99% of possible experience offered by lodge. The service was excellent and we had a lovely time.  The best part was our excellent guide that was with us during the whole stay.  He worked with us and was flexible.  We had so many experiences, elephant bathing, feeding bananas, jungle jeep ride (saw tigers, bird, rhino, etc.) sunset experience, elephant rides, dinner outside under the stars with light by lantern, visit to village and dancers from the area.  Ask for guide 'Gavinda' he is wonderful.  It was worth the cost to have such a once in life time experience.

We spent 4 wonderful days at Barahi Lodge.The rooms are spacious, comfortable, eco friendly, and have a porch with a river view.The safari options include boating the Rapti river, where birds and rhinos hang out, a jeep ride through the jungle where boars, monkeys, rhinos, birds, deer, elephants, and bears entertain the quiet observer; and elephants who walk silently through the woods where you thrill to the sight of a jackal or resting rhino.The food is fresh, locally sourced, and prepared to please any palate.  The staff never stop smiling, helping and watching over you.The spa service is excellent.Don't miss this marvelous location for a pampered jungle experience.

We stayed at Barahi Jungle Lodge, Chitwan National Park, Nepal, in April, 2019 for a few days. We have traveled internationally before and let me tell you, this lodge was the best lodge at which I have ever stayed! The food was amazing (5 out of 5),the service was amazing (5.5), the property itself and room, amazing (5 out of 5), and I could go on and on. We went on 2 safaris with our wonderful naturalist, Krishna Poudel, who could not have been any nicer or more knowledgeable. Krishna and the rest of the team (Subash) made the trip so wonderful. They let us spend as much time as we wanted interacting with their elephants one on one. No limit. One morning I wondered where the elephants were and before you knew it, the manager made a call, and all of sudden, an elephant shows up poolside with its handler, just for me. I spent as much time as I wanted. How nice.  We also went on a jungle walk on the elephant (will never forget it), and also, we took showers in the river with the elephants, a total surprise. Speaking of surprises, the lodge set up numerous surprises for us at every turn (went on a river boat ride at dusk, then they set up a full bar and full hot appetizers, cooked on the Bar-B-Q that they brought there, right at the end of the ride, on the side of the river, with tables, tablecloths, flowers, etc. ! How nice is that? Then on the last night, they surprised us with a dinner outside, just for us, in an area of the lodge. The birds at the lodge were amazing (I'm an avid bird watcher), saw about 20 rhinos in and around the lodge.  It was the experience of a lifetime, in an enchanted setting.  Again, best food and service, ever. Will never, ever forget Barahi Lodge! Thank you!!

Ambience of the place is close to nature. If you are a nature lover then this is the place to be in chitwan. Pool and breakfast area by the side of river makes you feel close to nature. New variety of food buffet everyday 👌

Very good experience will not hesitate to go there again.Service excellent staff very helpful.Personal attention by the Manager made a big difference.Location and amenities good.Rooms were a good size.

It is difficult to be as perfect as Barahi Jungle Lodge. Not only are they practicing and promoting sustainable and responsible travel but outperform service and hospitality. First, my room was fantastic. It was clean, more than sufficient with great sleep quality. The cookies in the room deserve a special mention. The hospitality is impeccable. They are attentive and remember food preferences. Special thanks to Abinash and his colleagues (I'm forgetting a couple of names) for making every evening memorable and wonderful. The spa services are also great. Lakshmi happily accommodated by request for a short therapy session, as opposed to a long one. She is a very good therapist. Barahi Jungle Lodge has four sets of meals and guests can state their preferences accordingly. Their Continental preparations are as good as Nepalese dishes. However, by its very nature, the Nepali preparation can be quite a large portion!Most importantly, their naturalists are sensitive and well informed. It was a pleasure to have someone as knowledgeable as Saket (Saki) take us for the many safaris. Chitwan is a birder's paradise. Barahi Jungle Lodge go out of their way to make our stay and experience in Chitwan special. And I am so glad I got an opportunity to experience their hospitality which has magnified my travel to the national park as a whole.

I don't really know where to start. From the second we arrived we have been treated perfectly. The hotel manager runs this business with unbelievable efficiency and every single member of staff is perfectly trained, courteous and simply can not do enough to help you. The trips are amazing, the chance of seeing wildlife is very high (we saw rhino bathing from our window on day one) the rooms are modern and exquisitely decorated as are all the communal areas. There is 24 hour assistance and nothing is too much trouble. The food is so wonderful that you barely notice you've eaten your own body weight every day and everything is cooked to order and fresh. I could go on for days but it would be much better if you came to see yourself! You will be assigned a guide (Ours was Karan who was delightful) but all of whom are knowledge, patient and thoughtful. VISIT THIS PLACE - YOU WILL NOT REGRET IT!!

This luxury five star property is unique. The staff are exceptional as is the service. VERY professional in every way. Our naturalist, Karan, was wonderful and very knowledgeable. Subash Gurung. Operation Manager,  is outstanding. The rooms are beautiful. The staff found out, quite by accident, that it was our 35th anniversary and they prepared a table in the woods with 100 candles lit. We dined in style and truly, it was our most special anniversary ever. The Resort offers such a variety of opportunities: A visit to the Tharu village (indigenous tribe), jungle walk, boat safari or jeep safari, bathing with the elephants or just watching them bathe. Education by the naturalists and a floor show featuring local cultural dancing. We will return but next time for a week. The last picture is part of our headboard in our room, so special. The resort has won awards for their eco-conscious efforts. Varun, VP is also very knowledgeable and helpful.  Front desk staff are excellent. Sarmila & Juna are a delight. Tej, F & B Manager, very good. We cannot say enough good things about this property. Don't wait, book now.

We stayed here for 3 nights at the beginning of February and from the minute we arrived until we left the lodge our experience was fantastic. The staff and attention to detail are second to none. We would like to send huge thanks to Saket who was our guide for our duration. He made us feel so welcome and his enthusiasm for wildlife is amazing. All the activities that we done was excellent especially the jungle walk and our rhino experience. Barahi Jungle Lodge really is a special place and is first class. We have memories to last a lifetime. If you are thinking of going to Chitwan this is definitely the place to stay, you really will not be disappointed.

It was an amazing experience. The entire staff was so warm and compassionate. We felt welcomed each day of our stay. This place and the people are determined to make your stay a memorable one. Our Naturalist, Karan was a friendly and fun. We had a great time exploring the jungle with him. It is definitely a must visit for both experience and hospitality.

I would love this place 7 stars if I could. The key over and above features are as followsWelcome from the managerEvening lecture about wildlifeMany sightings of rhinosEvening tribal songs and danceThe rooms are beautiful and in keeping with the surroundings.No clinical minimalism here. The food and service were first class. The grounds are vast and because there is no barrier animals do roam around..take care and I’d recommend taking a buggy at night...I could go on and on. I would strongly recommend this hotel...just go!

We recently stayed for 3 nights at Barahi and couldn't have been more pleased with the overall experience. The kind, hospitable and knowledgeable team made for a wonderful stay. The setting on the banks of the River was beautiful, the food was excellent (and plentiful) and the guides were extremely enthusiastic about conservation and the wildlife.There were some nice touches (surprises) organised by the team but I won't spoil them by telling you here, better you experience them yourself.We weren't lucky enough to see Tigers but it was exciting to know that as you trecked the Jungle the recent prints in the tracks told you that they weren't far away!I couldn't fault any part of the stay. Thank you to Karan (our guide) and the rest of the team at Barahi.

Experience of a lifetime. Many things to experience on various types of safari, amazing wildlife to see, also amazing & caring service, lovely unexpected turnes in the standard schedule. We loved it all to bits, especially the early-morning elephant  ride.

The time we check in till the time we check out, every thing was simply awesome. we could not expect more than that. We choose Barahi Jungle Lodge for our 1st anniversary, they made it so memorable. Most importantly, the last dinner, it was awesome. There is surprise in every step. From room to jungle safari Breakfast, to sunset view, to boating, to dinner. I would highly recommend this hotel. Best to visit as a couple.Thank you Barahi Jungle Resort to make our time so memorable and special.

Excellent experience. Everything is at top notch and the resort is perfectly managed. Rooms are lovely. The restaurant staff took very good care of my wife's food alergies and overall the only criticism is that we had just too much food! The safaris have been unforgettable. Congratulations to the team.

From the moment we arrived to the second we left - we just loved everything about Barahi. The staff is friendly and always smiling. Our child had the best time, and they were playing with him and giving him icecreem. Wonderful pool. The rooms are romantic and very nice. The only thing we missed was a fridge, but it was easy to call room service, and they where quick. The food was excellent. One day we took the bikes and had a really nice trip around the villages. Highly recommended. We met a lot of nice people and were even invited into a home. We hope to come back to this wonderful place! Special thanks to manager Kumar, Subhash and Tej.

From the moment we arrived and were met by the Manager and  General Manager to the moment we left to be waved off by the same pair we had a truly fantastic time.For whatever reason we were upgraded to a Suite and fair to say in all our years traveling this has to be the best.Everything at this Lodge was outstanding and the attention to detail was incredible.Usually one or two members of staff spring to mind for a mention, but at this Lodge everybody from the Mahoot to the Manager made sure everything you wanted was provided.The trips which included, River Safari, Jeep Safari, Elephant Safari, Jungle Walks we’re so well organised that all we had to do was turn up.Great sightings of numerous Rhinos, especially from the Elephants.    The food was excellent and we ate once in the restaurant, once on the terrace outside our suite, and the last night in a clearing adjacent to the lodge lit by a hundred lanterns.Nothing is to much trouble to these guys, their aim is to ensure that you have a great stay and they go the extra mile to achieve this.If ever you get the opportunity to visit Chitwan National Park there is really only one place to stay.   Our group saying is “. Did we like it,   No we loved it”Thank you to all the staff that made it possible.

Went with my family for a 3 night stay and it was just fantastic. The set up is great with spacious surroundings and golf carts to take you around! The rooms are spacious and comfortable. The highlight has to the great and attentive staff and the Eco friendly policy. Everything is recyclable and eco friendly and the commitment to this is superb! It was refreshing and inspiring!

We 2 persons had been there in Oct 2018. Stayed from 17/10/18 to 20/10/18. Initially we wanted to reach in late June, but anyhow we could not visit at that time. Rescheduled our stay . They made the change without any extra charge or cancellation fee. In our earlier schedule we booked for 5 persons, but later we were 2 only. This Resort is fabulous. In my view it is a Boutique Resort. They customize service as per requirement of guests. Right from Chef to Management everyone with smiling faces, always ready to offer their best. We were extremely happy . Even for a critic of highest category it will be difficult to find out any loopholes. Want to highlight some points which may prove helpful for others.1)   It is located Megholi side of the national park. Just cross the river by boat to do jeep Safari.2)   wifi is available in Reception and Restaurant area. Little week but fine workable in room as well. 3)  Good to do a boat safari till sun downer point.4)   It is advised before reaching pay maximum amount otherwise one has to carry lots of cash. Because sometimes card payment option fails due to network. Nearest ATM is about 35 km away.5)   All the cottages are surrounded by trees. And view by the river Rapti.  Beautiful ambiance, wide spread greenery, organic farm, singing birds.In our view this is probably the best stay in Chitwan. That is why I can differentiate with other places where I stayed for earlier 4 occasions.

wow, what a place to stay, in a secluded area right on the river this is a must do, the staff are exceptional, nothing is too much trouble, there is always someone willing to help, we had a welcome committee and they also came to wave us off. you stay in a lodge that is bright clean and everything you could wish for.if your lodge is a long walk away they will come and pick you up in an electric cart. food is amazing and plentiful. there is a swimming pool which is just about the right size, however you are so close to the river that to just stand and stare is perfect, do not swim in the river!!. the excursions are superb and are led by knowledgeable and enthusiastic staff. my only complaint, i wish we could have stayed longer

Located on the bank of Rapti river , Barahi Jungle Lodge is a perfect resort for a quiet sojourn in the lap of nature . Across the river is the Chitwan national park . There are many attractions such as Jeep Safari, Boat safari , Elephant safari and others. The accommodation is simply superb ..interior decor inspired by nature but with all the amenities and cleanliness of a seven  star luxury hotel . But what is outstanding is the hospitality which I would say is the  best ever in Asia or maybe the world  . Mr Varun, the Vice President of the resort and his team pamper you from the moment you step into the lodge .. They are extremely sweet and caring . The staff derive immense and genuine pleasure in serving you . Your smallest needs are promptly taken care of with a smile . They deserve much more than five star !

Our stay in the Barahi Jungle Lodge was a gift from friends to celebrate our 21st wedding anniversary. Our hosts could not have done more to embellish this gift and make our stay truly memorable. The welcome was warm and generous, introducing us by name to the members of staff. Not only were we treated like royalty, but it genuinely felt as if we were being welcomed into their family - a family who were striving to conserve a beautiful part of the world and share it in a sustainable way, both with visitors and locals alike. We were upgraded to the Suite (which defines comfort and luxury), entertained by traditional dancers and musicians, dined in a secret garden wrapped in the warm glow of lanterns and presented with a cake. The Lodge has been carefully designed using natural materials and blends seamlessly in with its surroundings, well-kept pathways are edged by shrubs and trees (labelled) and all the individual lodges look out onto the river that separates it from the nature reserve. The suite was equally furnished local natural materials and exuded rustic charm and comfort. The food was delicious and the service was faultless. However, it is the team, the family, who make Barahi an unforgettable destination. Their enthusiasm, passion and drive to protect this precious part of the world and generously share it is an inspiration.

Barahi Jungle Lodge is sooooo fantastic that, no words I can use to describe how good it is.You will be welcomed by some staff and the hotel manger at the 'Welcome Home' first, explained everything to you.  A very lovely smell in that room, lemongrass, because they  mop the floor with lemongrass essential oil , so as in your room.Staff are super friendly, knowledgeable, helpful and thoughtful, as I have frog phobia, they always protect me for that.  My naturalist, Govinda, is so knowledgeable, funny, thoughtful, I had a good time with him. Manager, Subhash, also a senior naturalist is super nice and caringRooms are all individual cottage, super clean with lemongrass scents.  Room is well designed that presents all things dedicatedly, make all things look as nature as possible, even using effort to make soap, shampoo, tissue roll, etc  min order to make you feel you are in the jungle. Kept refilling the home made cookies biscuits and water in your room, seems like they make your room few times a day, every time you went back to your room, you would  be surprisedFood were super yummyPool with a lovely viewThere is a notice to tell all the guests about their schedule, so thoughtful.  I enjoyed all the activities over there, well planned.Food was super yummy and presented in excellent ways I enjoyed my stay there , 300% enjoyment.

This place is absolutely stunning, a blend of somewhere between Jurassic Park meets the Flintstones. The staff is amazingly friendly and helpful. Food is ok but then there aren't any real alternatives for many kilometres. Make sure that you book a 4wd to get there as the roads are rough. Like anywhere in the Chitwan region there is an issue with mosquitoes

Look no further - this is the place to go. We stayed here for 4 nights and in that time did 2 jeep safaris, a boat safari, a jungle walk and joined elephants bath time. We also had a slide presentation about the park and saw traditional dancing. It was all fantastic. The staff are wonderful - we were made to feel like royalty. Our guide Krishna was so wonderful, we felt like friends. His knowledge, unfailing enthusiasm and deep love of nature comes straight from his heart - being in his company was a joy. We were so pleased to see the lack of plastic - water is in flasks when you're out and all toiletries are hand wrapped in paper etc. (I would suggest the hotel stops using plastic straws though). The rooms are beautiful, as are all the public areas - the pool, the deck, the library etc, the restaurant and food are wonderful and the spa too, I highly recommend a massage or two! We were very sad to leave. This place is incredibly special indeed.

Stayed here for only 2 nights which was no were near long enough. Stayed in lodge number 15 which was just perfect. The lodge is very safari rustic and they think of every tiny little thing to ensure your stay is pure bliss. The little touches with everything was just perfect. The lodges are decorated extremely tastefully to enhance every ones stay. The shower room was absolutely stunning with a pebble stone base which when standing in provides your feet with a gentle massage as you move around the shower. The soaps sitting wrapped in natural paper and string on a rock all added to the tasteful and appropriate decor. The beds extremely comfortable and rooms spacious with a lovely balcony.The fully inclusive lodge provided excellent meals and we never wanted for anything. Dinner by the pool was surreal with lanterns lighting the way and candles on the table. The activities provided at the Lodge are also wonderful - we did the Canoe Safari which was very enjoyable finished off with canapes watching the sun go down over the river - exquisite! We also participated in a Jungle Jeep Safari and had the most amazing experience with wildlife a plenty and a lovely breakfast served in the jungle.We also had the opportunity to see and participate in the cultural dancing which certainly was an experience!The resort is large and the staff are absolutely wonderful and help and assist in anyway possible to ensure your stay is incredible. They have golf carts which run you around the lodge if need be. The resort also has a very nice pool area with bar and the waiters are happy to serve you in the pool which was just wonderful.Would definitely recommend this property for anybody looking for a piece of paradise!

Our family of four stayed for five nights at the Barahi Jungle Lodge in Chitwan and we were simply blown away. The style and comfort of the rooms were the standard you would expect in the best 5 star resorts internationally. They managed to achieve this with a very low environmental footprint, with the furniture all produced locally, from natural materials.The staff really made our stay special for us, nothing was too much trouble. Their guides went out of their way to tailor our programme to suit our interests and needs. The different types of safari - elephant backed, boat, jeep and on foot - meant we got to experience the wildlife and jungle from lots of different perspectives. The kids adored the elephant bathing and elephant ‘sandwich’ feeding. Our guides ‘Ashma’ and ‘Hari’ were extremely friendly, helpful and knowledgable about the local wildlife and made our stay so fun and interesting. The meals were amazing and vast amounts of food seemed to be delivered constantly. There was a huge amount of choice between local Nepalese, Chinese/Thai, Indian and continental.  The meals hosted by the pool side in the evenings, lit by lanterns were just magical. Lounging by the pool side was the perfect way to relax after a day of adventure in the jungle. We can’t recommend the Bahari Jungle Lodge enough - it’s a must visit if you are planning a visit to Chitwan! Thanks so much to all of the staff at Bahari for our amazing stay! We will definitely be returning.

If a thrilling adventure, excitement of mother nature - all of it coupled with TOP CLASS hospitality, comfort and eco-sensitive practices are what you may be interested in, then Barahi Jungle Lodge certainly must be in your top options.The booking process by itself sets the pleasant and courteous tone. I booked Barahi through Pungdee Safaris. Prompt communication and flexibility puts "service" already in top gear. We did the 3 Night / 4 Day package and every minute was worth it. Every part of the Jungle lodge - The welcome room, the ambiance and facility in each room has a flair. Food as well is excellent ! Every guest (group) get a naturalist assigned who would care for the entire stay and every activity. This approach builds relationship, and makes the entire stay a lovely experience. This operational strategy is something I loved - Kudos to Varun (Manager). Even the daily activities and evening cultural activities are briefed and planned with the guest and their interest and limitations.Our nature expert Karan Giri was a perfect fit for us. His friendliness and love for nature was clearly visible in his knowledge about the flora and fauna. Also his interest in photography was an added bonus for us! Knowledgeable, on time, not overbearing but being there when needed and friendliness are few highlights for Karan - 5/5 stars in our book !Chitwan is a great place to watch wildlife in nature - Rhinos, crocs, boars, deers, bears and a lot of different birds - Leave behind everything that belongs to nature - Take with you the memories and  photographs !Barahi Jungle Lodge is ABSOLUTELY RECOMMENDED. Waving goodbye to the Barahi team made me think just one thing...When could we go back again. Kudos to the entire team for their care and making our experience memorable !

I rarely rate 5 in TripAdvisor, but Bahari Lodge and especially its staff absolutely deserves it. As soon as you arrive (after a terrible bumpy road) into the lodge, you are personally welcomed and permanently spoiled by the excellent members of the team . Congrats to the Management. Leadership not always is the case in the hotels in Nepal.PROS: almost everything ! The room, the cleanliness, the smiles, the service, the jungle activities, the in-house elephants, the naturalists, the location ...CONS: almost nothing ! If I really try to find one, I would say that the front yard garden between the river and the bungalows could be better. But well ? everything else is so great that I quickly forget it :-). And we are in the jungle, aren't we ?

Barahi Jungle Lodge is an excellent place to stay. The place seems very eco friendly. The cottage we stayed in was very warm and comfortable on the inside and the bathroom had the necessary modern amenities. The a la carte menu was excellent and the Nepali thali was scrumptious. Even the pastries were totally up to the mark. They have a beautiful pool for the summer and their own elephants that u can feed along the river side. We were given a bush dinner which was very well presented and made us feel very special. The staff was excellent and their naturalists were highly knowledgeable. We did an elephant safari, a jeep safari and a nature walk in the jungle and loved every minute of all of it. A hotel staff would be waiting for us after each safari with a cold/hot towel which I really appreciated. Very well maintained property. And the activities were also well conducted and professional. It’s a must go to place.

I loved my two days here. Beautiful lodge with wonderful staff.  The food was absolutely excellent, the culture events were amazing and views from the lodge were spectacular. I highly recommend this lodge as your get away.

We stayed 2 nights at this lodge in early Nov.  Our stay was just great.The traditional looking cottages were thoroughly modern inside & clean. The food was very good and they ensured availability of our special requirements (many vegetarians & a Jain).There were many things to do apart from lazing around the lodge buildings and pool.We enjoyed a thrilling early morning elephant safari where we saw an Indian Rhino, Jackals, many Peacocks and some deer. We also indulged in a "shower with the elephants" experience (see photos). We enjoyed the river boat ride to view an excellent sunset at the meeting point (confluence) of 2 rivers. One night we had the pleasure of seeing traditional dances by the local people,Saw a big snail & a "Spiderman" spider (see photos)Overall an excellent stay at this lodge and we would strongly recommend to all who would like to visit the Chitwan area.

Barahi is a very well appointed lodge on the edge of Chitwan National Park overlooking one of the large rivers that cross the forest.Nestled in the proximity of beautiful Taru villages, the lodge is of superior standards and yet managed to maintain contact with nature, personable staff and a feel of authenticity.The staff is extremely dedicated and take excellent care of guests at any time. Obviously the key highlight is the forest and the unique species that it conserves including endangered Asian Rino, a fishing crocodile, tigers, leopards, beautiful Royal white monkeys, deers and over 650 species of birds.Compared to African parks, sightings here are harder due to dense vegetation, so you have to be prepared for patient watching and possibly some big misses (like elusive tigers and leopards). Nonetheless it is all very fascinating, calming and seducing thus a visit is certainly worth it, also to see a completely different Nepal from the Himalayan trekking sites.We spent two nights at Barahi doing two Jeep safaris and one canoe trip on the river; upon leaving we all felt that an extra day would have been worthwhile to focus on forest walks and possibly another attempt to see a tiger....only fresh footprints found during our stay!

This resort was just awarded the best in all if south east asia and is for a very good reason . It’s simply the best there is. Excellent service .. cozy and beautiful rooms all decorated according to tharu culture. The view of the national park along the Rapti river is simply breathtaking. The place will just relax you once you set foot in there. Just visit it once and you will love it.

The Barahi Jungle Lodge gets named to many of the “best of” lists for hotels in the Chitwan area and it more than lived up to the hype!  It is expensive (particularly for Nepal) but it was more than worth it.  Everything is included in the rate (except alcohol!) including your own personal naturalist for your entire stay, Jeep safaris, canoe safaris, walking safaris and elephant safaris and bathing (where the elephants bathe you!).  Our naturalist, Anu was wonderful and one of the best highlights of our stay was having her guide us through our various adventures.On the safaris we saw plenty of wildlife - rhinos, monkeys, gharial, other crocodiles, plenty of deer and birds.  We weren’t lucky enough to see tigers but others who visit do get lucky enough for sightings.  There was also a brief tour of the local village, including one of the houses which was lovely.You could choose to do as many of the activities as you wish or just lounge by the pool with the occasional visit from the baby elephant, Tulsi.The use of elephants is controversial but at Barahi Jungle Lodge they really seem to focus on the well being of their elephants so there was no signs of any of the cruelty that you hear about at other places in Chitwan - quite the opposite in terms of their care and well being.  The lodges were wonderful.  We were upgraded to the family lodge - including a very spacious two bedrooms, pool,  fire pit and the best rain shower I’ve ever experienced!  The food was fantastic and included a choice of local Nepali, Indian or Chinese cuisines.  As a vegetarian, it was a dream in terms of choices and quality.Highly recommend!

Loved this place. It's right on the edge of Chitwan National Park, so the safaris into the park for wildlife viewing are easily accessible. The room was very unique - made of natural materials, really fit into the surroundings, and yet it had AC and all the other amenities. Food was good and it was also fun, in addition to all the wildlife viewing (via jeep, boat and elephant back), to visit the nearby village. The real standout was the staff, who were friendly and attentive. In particular, the manager Saki took care that all was going well and continually asked if anyone needed anything, and our naturalist Anuja was exceptional. She was so kind, thoughtful and friendly and went out of her way to ensure the entire experience was going well. She was also very skilled at spotting wildlife and was a wealth of information. Great place - highly recommend if visiting Chitwan.

I wanted to take a moment to compliment some excellent staff members and send my sincere appreciation for the superior service my son and I received when we visited the Barahi Jungle Lodge in November.  This luxury jungle lodge is one of the best I have seen and well worth a visit.  It's on the waterfront, on the banks of River Rapti in the heartland of Rhinos in Nepal's Chitwan National Park, opposite the wildlife reserve.  This was a first class experience from start to finish.  The activities offered are varied with something for everyone, at every age to enjoy.  The meals included quality foods that were delicious.  Daily menu options are split into categories like Nepalese and Indian - or traditional favorites as well.  We sampled several type of cuisines and everything was excellent, with prompt table service.Everyone we encountered was polite, friendly, helpful and eager to make us feel comfortable, welcomed and happy.  All staff, especially the well-trained and experienced naturalists - were wonderful people.  But it is the exceptional treatment we received from the naturalist that was assigned to us - MISS ANUJA JOSHI - that made this the most memorable experience of our 2 week journey throughout magical Nepal.  She had such enthusiasm, patience, kindness and desire to make our visit tremendous in every way.
