The location is beyond amazing with the river floating by and you feel like you live inside the jungle! We realised that this was not far from the truth, as it's only a 50 meter boat ride across the river away. We got to experience both a boat safari and a jungle safari with a jeep. The guides are very knowledgeful, especially our guide Mr Harry who shared openly about the nepali culture, the people of Nepal and way of living, as well as all that there is to know about the jungle. When you're not at a safari life is very good by the pool.If you're planning a trip to Nepal, please do not miss out Chitwan and Barahi Jungle Lodge. It's worth every penny and it's our best hotel experience EVER!!

Barahi Lodge is a special place, the setting is truly inspiring, coupled with our extremely knowledgeable naturalist Krishna who was always ready with a smile and the very attentive staff made our stay wonderful, thank you Barahi Lodge!

Visited the Barahi Jungle Lodge in March 2019 as part of our 12 day visit to Nepal. Would have loved to spend more time here. The Lodge offered first class accommodation together with caring service and set in wonderful wildlife surroundings. Could not fault the place. Impressive too is the care and practice of eco sustainability.

I have been a resident in Nepal for 20 plus years and have visited the Chitwan National Park at many occasions, being one of my favorite destinations to escape Kathmandu once in a while. This was the first non-work-related visit to the Meghauli area though and the first time to the Barahi Jungle Lodge. And we loved it. The hotel is lovely, well located at the banks of the Rapti river. Staff were very nice and attentive, food was great. The jungle safari by jeep and the boat trip on the river with sundowners was very enjoyable. The swimming pool is great to cool off after a jungle trip or walk, or just to relax. We saw many bird and deer varieties, including many peacocks, kingfishers, spotted and barking deer. plenty wild boar and an incredible 19 rhinos in a single day, definitely my record for the park. Right across the hotel, on the banks of the river, we spotted crocodiles, including the gharial.While there are many good places in Chitwan National Park to stay, Barahi for me stood out because of the excellent organization and the little extra touches, like the cold face towels when arriving or returning from an activity, real ground coffee available in the rooms and served in the restaurant.So a great stay, highly recommended and many thanks to the lovely staff .

Barahi Jungle Lodge was the highlight of our trip to Nepal. Not only are you surrounded by stunning wildlife, this place ticks every box from excellent food and accommodation, exceptional staff and hospitality, it promotes and practices sustainable eco-friendly methods, and having our own personal guide, all of which made our stay very special. If you're thinking of visiting Nepal, Barahi Jungle Lodge is a must!

I never thought to have an experience of old colonial Indo-Asia, but you'll find it at Barahi, but without the dark side of that history. You're graciously greeted by a group of people who give information about the facility, food services and naturalist services, and from that moment on you're held in exquisite care by a staff who work together well as a team and who seem to really like one another - not a small thing just in itself.After discussing activity options with the naturalist assigned to you for the duration of your stay, that information is on a whiteboard in the common area, and each time you're out on an activity (river safari, jungle walk, jeep safari, elephant encounter/feeding/safari, village visit - might have forgotten something!), staff will replenish the provided drinking water and the jar of cookies in your room and tidy anything requiring attention. You'll be asked at lunch what food option you'd like for dinner so it's ready for you (Nepali, Indian, Chinese, Continental). The food was all quite good, and very fresh. There's a coffee/tea station that's always open. I bemoaned that they didn't have anything decaffeinated as I can no longer drink caffeine past early afternoon and still expect to sleep. They went the extra mile to order in decaf coffee crystals for my use and both had some available in the restaurant and put some in my room by my kettle. Wow.I was blessed to have Saket as my naturalist. His passion for nature, his appetite for and ability of wholehearted engagement with the environment, the animals and every person he encountered were extraordinary. Because of him and the activity options, I was able to see different deer species, gharials, crocodiles, wild boar, bar-headed geese (they fly OVER Everest!), a mongoose, two kinds of monkeys, many of the one-horned rhinos, and... we got a rare sighting of a sloth bear. My memories of being poled downriver in that peaceful environment, observing the animal life and just feeling blissful about experiencing deep country in Nepal will remain among my life's significant experiences.Go for a unique experience of true graciousness and luxurious care. I can't imagine anyone being sorry they stayed here! I stayed 3 nights and wished for 4.If it had been in the warmer months, the pool looked VERY inviting. As it was, it was perfectly cool (I can't handle heat so chose to go in early March) and I didn't have spare time for pool lounging anyway.There are other surprises that shouldn't be spoiled in the telling. Enjoy!! ;)The one difficult note was that in the room information material was a note to please not give tips to any individuals during your stay, but to use the lobby tip box at the end of your stay. So I configured what my tip would be for the wait and service staff and my naturalists and put that all into the tip box - and then before leaving had an encounter with the latter that seemed clear was the time to tip the naturalist..... so I gave more, which of course skewed my trip budget. Just to be clear, I didn't feel pressured, but my experience was extraordinary and I did want to reward that - and just got mixed messages about how to do so, thus costing me more $ than I'd planned. It would be a kindness for the resort management to clarify that for future guests.Truly a lifetime experience, and one that might drive me to return to Nepal!

What an incredible experience. We had 2 nights at the jungle lodge and the amount we packed in made it feel like a week.The customer service is impeccable. From the moment you arrive at the welcome lodge to the staff waving you off on your departure this hotel knows how to treat guests like royalty.Each group of guests is assigned a personal naturalist guide for the duration of their stay who plans with you your itinerary of jungle experiences and meals etc. Our guide was Jitu who has worked in and around Chitwan National Park for over 40 years. His wealth of experience and deep knowledge of the jungle and its inhabitants was breathtaking. He truly made the experience so much richer with his guidance. He was attentive but not overbearing and allowed us the space to have our own experience of the lodge. He was an absolute delight to spend time with and I personally learnt a tremendous amount from him.Chitwan National Park is incredible and we experienced fantastic sightings of Greater One Horned Rhinoceros, Monkeys, Crocodiles, so many amazing birds and close encounters with Leopards. The tour packages are exceptionally run with such attention to customer service detail. Morning excursions have delightful breakfasts served at wildlife lookouts. Evening trips have sunset drinks and local delicacies served as you watch the sun go down.Note to Barahi Jungle Lodge - The one downside for us, this does not detract from the 5 star rating, is the use of Elephants in tourist activities. We completely understand that Elephants have been used in lodges and jungle activities for decades and there is absolutely a place for them in the workings of national park maintenance and there is still a demand from tourists for physical interactions with Elephants but we feel that as a hotel who prides themselves on eco tourism the elephant activities should be limited to non physical interactions and if possible phased out. There is enough natural beauty and close encounters with incredible creatures to satisfy any curious soul without the need to ride an Elephant.Despite the above comment we would recommend this experience to anyone. It is truly an unforgettable trip.

Words can barely describe the wonderful experience that I had at Barahi Jungle Lodge. One of the rare solo travellers to visit this unique property. From the moment that the lovely Anuja found me on the bus to Chitwan to the moment I left I felt as if I had stepped into a world of luxury, where you become a member of the family not just another customer going through the doors. I don't want to go into too much detail and ruin your experience here, but from the moment of arrival you really are transported into the wildneress of the jungle, accompanied with a good side serve of luxury. My room was spacious. Perfectly serviced during the day and the turn down service at night. Just a hint - enjoy the cookies, as the staff will top up the jar during the day for you. Food was magnificent. Being there for a 4 days - 3 nights -  I tried Nepali, continetal and Indian. So much delicious food.The true highlights of Barahi Jungle Lodge is there committment to the environment & the local community. You won't find plastics in your room, with fresh filtered water in glass bottles being delivered. And I dare you to try to not fall in love with the bars of delicious soaps in the bathrooms. Along with the unique Jeep safari and boat rides that you should not miss. Enjoy experiencing the jungle life. I for one, can no wait until I can return to Barahi Jungle Lodge to once again become a member of the lodge family.

We stayed in Barahi jungle lodge three days and it instantly felt like home. Staff is always friendly and caring about your needs. Also, they all are native Chitwan people. The place is amazing: remoted, jungle is across the river, pool is melting in the jungle colors...Chitwan National Park is 10 meters in front of the hotel : therefore, it is the place to be. The hotel is of course ecofriendly, it serves veggie food, it respects nature and animals. The + of this place is that for any activities, you will be with a local naturalist that is willing to share his knowledge. With him, you will be sure to see beautiful animals and get the right info about it. To sum up : 1) eco friendly place, 2) best staff, 3) remoted place, 4) savory food!Do not hesitate, you will love it.

Although it has nice rooms, with verandahs, and a swimming-pool, and absolutely excellent food (too much of it!), and the staff's attention to detail is faultless, the real reason for coming here is to do the safari trips into the Chitwan Reserve - we were not disappointed, with numerous encounters with Indian rhinos. Also the grounds themselves are lovely, and good for birdwatching

We spent two nights at the Barahi Jungle Lodge and loved every minute of it! The rooms and grounds were beautiful. The service was excellent with an attention to detail. The staff went above and beyond to make us feel special. We especially enjoyed the boat trip down the river, followed by drinks & the sunset. Saket was our naturalist for our stay there and he went above and beyond. We did one of the longer jungle walks and he ensured that we had the chance to see a black rhino. He was super knowledgeable! If you feel like relaxing the spa is beautiful as well.

We went there for a casual lunch thinking we will have one and return back to Kathmandu but we couldn't resist ourselves to spent  three more days there because of such a mesmerizing environment, magnificent beauty of that place and such a warm hospitality.I have all my heart for their room, amenities and their staff. I am so so so in love with them and they are just outstanding and very very creative.Talking about their amenities, I really appreciate BARAHI JUNGLE LODGE for empowering local community to produce all the toiletries for them. I really admire their thought of working together with the community because they not  just utilizing the resources and the skills they have but making them realize their worth. Truly speaking it is such a good effort.Keep up the good work always.Sending you lots of love.

Wonderful stay here. Amazing food. Great personal attention with our own guide from arrival until we left. Facilities were very comfortable, a little unique and very clean. The whole staff were fully engaged in client comfort. There were a range of activities arranged including safari tours, local village walk, local entertainment and a special dinner.This was part of a tour for me so unsure of the cost but a great way to finish my hotel. Only negative would be that the roads to get there are pretty rough.Great experience I’d recommend to all .

Simply no words. Service perfect, food out of this world! Don’t miss the river cruise where you get to see these exotic animals. The majestic One horned Rhino and the Ghariyal. Then travelling to a secluded location where Rapti RIU and Narayani rivers meet for an amazing barbecue With a perfect Sunset.

We were in Barahi Jungle Lodge in July 2018 for a couple of days.  The staff were friendly - from the room service to the General Manager. Special mention goes to Saket who brought us on the boat trip and the jungle safari.  We were really back to nature with the boat ride, the jungle safari and the "Elephant Bathing".  I was really tricked by this:)

Took a group there for three nights, which is just enough time to participate in all the activities: jeep ride, elephant ride, bathing elephants, canoe ride on river, Tharu village visit, and more. More nights would be even better to give you more chances to spot wildlife. Very good food, great service, fabulous rooms. We loved everything about the place.

From the moment we arrived we were made to feel part of the Bahari Lodge family. We were lucky enough to have Saket as our own naturist who loved his job so much that you could not help being fascinated by his enthusiasm. Every single member of staff were unique to this property. The accommodation had everything you could want in a room. Filtered water in glass bottles, handmade soap, hair and conditioner. filtered coffee and tea station. We had a huge bed with pure cotton bedlinen, lovely outdoor space overlooking the Rapti River. There was a great swimming pool with loungers and sun umbrellas to relax inbetween our safaris. We done two river sundowners as we loved them so much. We washed and fed the beautiful resident elephants every day as it was so special spending time with these gorgeous animals.We were lucky enough to see crocodiles and Rhinos on our safaris and so many beautiful birds and butterflies are around the lodge. The breakfast and dinners were first class.If you have one trip left in this world make it to this lodge. You will not be disappointed.Thank you so much Bahari of a truly magical experience.

To start with : Barahi is really fantastic.There is a lot mentioned about the safari's already in the reviews.I travelled my entire life over the world ( mainly for business ) but i really never faced a hospitality like they offer in Barahi Lodge .Maybe not 5* waiters or waitresses like the big Hotels offer you, BUT this is MORE than compensated by the hospitality and kindness of staff and waiters/waitresses .Our private naturalist Sakhë and masseuse Sophyia are BOTH TOP OF THE RANGE.The offered food and drinks are excellent but don't expect a huge menu card .Simple dinner but all fresh and very tasty .The " safari " is a bit misleading to my opinion .They offer super lovely and interesting trips BUT don't be surprised when you don"t see animals ( tiger , crocodile , bear or monkey ) during the trips .Because we had Sakhé the whole week , we were very lucky to see even the tiger .

A very good base to stay in from which to explore the nearby rural area and the National Park. The food was excellent and the staff team friendly and very helpful. The lodges are beautifully decorated and comfortable with the bathrooms containing organic soap, shampoo and hair conditioner bars. Lovely touch! Guests are ferried to and from their accommodation after dark in a golf buggy. A beautiful pool that is probably no more than 4 feet deep at the deepest point is family friendly, with the outside bar and adjacent verandah both sited nearby for relaxation. A small shop sells local craft items. Take a river trip and hope to see the one horned rhino, watch birds or go into the jungle on safari.

Amazing hotel complex, individual secluded thatched cottages which were well equipped. Delicious food, excellent service. Lovely pool overlooking the river. Boat, jeep and walking safaris were all exciting. Washed elephants in the river. Could not fault this hotel...the highlight of my touring holiday!

Very nice place to stay. Very friendly and helpful staff. Very rich and good food. Rooms and bathrooms nicely built and clean, equipped with air conditioning. Excursions interesting with lots of animals to be seen. Guide with broad knowledge of flora and fauna.Lodge pool clean and beautiful.

Although the National Park was closed but Pradeep & krishna made sure we enjoy our 3 days stay! Loved every single thing there! The food was so good, too many activities and amazing view! Thank you so much guys!

being there is a nightmare as the connecting road are in very poor condition, But once you reached there is gives you a feeling that your entered in other world, Experience is so overwhelming that can't be expressed in words. Likely to visit in future with my Family.

Wonderful place on the river bank overlooking the Chitwan forest. The waiting area is impressive. Briefed by the manager (he is always around) on arrival. The whole place is made from natural and locally sourced materials. I loved the room design. Even the shampoo etc are ecofriendly and in paper packaging. Dining area is beautiful. So is the pool. Sunrise provides beautiful views at riverside. Bush dinners can be arranged on request. Apart from the usual jeep safaris and elephant safaris, you can enjoy boat safaris (early morning are best). We even had a complete breakfast atop a machaan during our jeep safari. Boat cruises are followed by snacks and sundowner. Elephant bathing can be fun, but it's easier on the elephants if you don't ride them, because the mahouts then prod them into doing the chhop and this i didn't like. So we dropped the elephant safari next day. Reading room has some good coffee table books. I liked one about the tiger (photographer was , surprise, an Amdavadi). Enjoy Tharo folk dance and village visit, don't miss tasting rice wine.Staff is very hardworking and we saw them on duty since 6am till late into the evening. Rhinos can be spotted frequently. Minimum 2 days and 2 jeep safaris is recommended. The place went through some difficult times during the earthquake and fuel blockade. Again there was flooding few months back. But the people have done a wonderful job to get it up and running. They employ local people and give them livelihood which is a good thing.God bless.

Stayed at the Barahi Jungle Lodge for just 2 nights (and repented like anything for not having planned for at least 4 nights).12 people - including 2 kids and 3 above 60.The road from Bharatpur airport to the hotel is a bit of a nightmare in patches. It took us about an hour plus a few minutes to cover under 30kms. Don't think of driving down from Pokhra or Kathmandu - best option is to fly into Bharatpur and then take this 1 hour ride.Check-InMr. Subhash - the in-charge, Mr. Jitu - our designated naturalist and Ms. Kabita - at the reception, welcomed us with a traditional drink and warm smiles. The introduction to the resort and activities was thorough and detailed. They surprised us with an upgrade for our kids (twin boys - six year Olds) - an individual room inter - connected to our cottage.The Property:There's a big welcome area right at the entrance and down about 100mts from there is the main building which houses the reception, restaurant, library, the bar, the deck and the swimming pool. The rooms are a fair bit away from this building but they also have electric carts to pick up and drop you to and from. They also offer bicycles to ride around the resort. The resort also has a spa and souvenir shop to boot.Rooms:Each room is an individual cottage - with loads of privacy and a spacious balcony facing the river and overlooking the jungle.The interiors are done very tastefully - rustic and natural items used in every nook and corner. They have tried to incorporate as many local items as possible into the room.The shower area and bathroom are also very neatly designed. The toiletries are top of the line too.The hotel uses glass bottles for drinking water in the room instead of plastic bottles which was a nice touch.Food:The resort is an all - inclusive kind and they consult you before fixing the menu - specially in our case since we have informed them about our dietary restrictions. We had a minor issue on the first day regarding repetition of items from lunch time to dinner but it was sorted out and the other meals went on well. The continental, Nepalese, Indian and Chinese dishes were all authentic and tasty. The service was top notch too. Activities:This part is what excited us the most. The naturist Mr. Jitu briefed us about the various options available - boat safari, jungle walk, elephant interaction, elephant safari, jungle safari and village tour. He also understood the interests of all the members of our group and then drafted the plan to our complete satisfaction. He was very well informed and ended up being a great asset for us throughout our stay at the resort, especially during our jungle walk. We ended us seeing rhinos up close and personal during our boat safari, jungle walk AND elephant safari. Didn't use the swimming pool much since it was peak summer and there were a lot of insects around. We left a satisfied lot and with a feeling that at least a couple more nights would have been lovely to spend at this beautiful property. A lot of thanks to the entire staff and especially Mr. Jitu.Would highly recommend this one with full conviction and without a shadow of doubt.

My husband & I and the small group we were traveling with had a great stay at Barahi Jungle Lodge.  The facility is very nice in all respects including the rooms/cottages, dining and lounge.The customer service in particular is outstanding.  I am disabled and the staff went way out of their way to take great care of me.  Krishna in particular kept an eye on me and was there whenever I needed anything.If you have difficulty walking as I do, Barahi Jungle Lodge does present some challenges.  The rooms can be a fairly good walk from the main lodge, but they have golf carts to take you back and forth which are prompt and speedy.  There are some stairs which presented a challenge for me, but the staff carried me up and down the steps in their wheelchair that they loaned me.The biggest mobility challenge at the lodge is getting to/from the boats that take you across the river for the safaris.  To get to the boats, there is a long set of steps down the river bank that are manageable if you can walk.  To get to the jeeps on the other side of the river, it is a long walk in loose dry sand.  I could not do this and had to be carried to and from the boat both ways.  Mostly some men in our group carried me, but the lodge staff was quite willing to carry me when needed.On safari, we saw lots of rhinos and peacocks.  We were near a tiger, but did not see it.  We also did the sunset boat ride one night which was very nice.  And we went into the village one morning and got a tour of one of their houses which was quite interesting.  Some of the guys in our group went for a run along the river bank and also borrowed bikes from the lodge and road into the village.  In addition, there is a talk or performance each night before dinner.  So there is a lot to see and do.  At the main lodge, they have wifi, so you can stay connected.Barahi Jungle Lodge is a great experience in all respects.

I couldn't recommend this hotel enough! From the moment we arrived, the customer service we received was like no other. The members of staff were welcoming, helpful, inspiring and they couldn't do enough for us. The accommodation is of exceptional quality and the activities on offer are some of the best we have done. We were fortunate to get engaged during our stay here and the hotel manager went above and beyond in order to help me prepare for the big moment. I would be sad if I never stayed here again. The easiest 10 out of 10 I've ever given.

Stayed here for 4 nights.Very luxurious lodges . Superbly well run with very good attention to detail.Very good value for money as cost per night is full board including tea, coffee etc and virtually as many safari type activities as you can fit in. Very knowledge guides. We were lucky enough to see a tiger at 12 midday on the road back towards the hotel at the end of a Jeep safari. We are very privileged to have seen this.Do not miss the elephant bathing it’s wonderful. You can go on a cycle tour of the local villages too. Everyone is so friendly it’s infectious.Our daughter was ill for a few hours when we were there and the guide was phoning us to ask if we has medication and if she was feeling better.I’ve never experienced such genuine generous service before. Can not recommend this place highly enough- just wonderful and so many unique memories to take away from just one place makes this hotel truly specialThank you

The staff here = incredible: Friendly, accommodating, funny. Barahi Jungle Lodge's team will plan your daily activities according to your interests. I enjoyed two nights of the perfect blend of adventure and relaxation! Massage, swim, elephants, boating, beautiful sunsets, candle lit dinners. Go!

I just read through several reviews and it IS all that.  A fantastic, beautiful location on the river just across from the jungle with clean, comfortable and beautiful accommodations.  The staff goes way out of their way to make sure every detail of your trip meets your expectations and more!  They keep an activity board in the lobby that details all your activities and of course, they will change it upon your request- which is what they did for me.  I arrived after several days of trekking and was wiped out.  I did an elephant ride into the community jungle and instead of dinner and a native dance, I turned in for the night.  Of course, they noticed that and wanted to make sure everything was okay and I reassured them I just needed a rest!  They also provided a very knowledgeable guide (Asma) who spoke good English.  I really enjoyed the jeep tour into the jungle, the bike ride through the villages and relaxing by the pool.  Overall- a really great experience that I would do all over again in a heartbeat.  (No tigers seen on my trip- just fresh paw prints!  Lots of birds, rhinos, deer)

The entrance sign says it all “it’s a jungle out there and you’re going to have wild time” Yes, you are in the jungle and so much beauty here. Clean, spacious, beautiful rooms with all shampoo and body soap. Food is oh so good, all meals. The beef is a must try, so drooling. WiFi works everywhere. Staff are friendly and go above and beyond to make you happy. Swimming pool if you like to take a dip or just grab your book and read outside. Leave the balcony door in your room open at night to hear the sound of creatures and birds.Such a Zen place to stay.

Our family of 5 just enjoyed a superb 2 night stay at the Barahi Jungle Lodge nestled in the heart of Chitwan National Park. What a find! All thanks to Himalayan Holidays.The rooms were immaculate, all in keeping with the Eco environment and finished with organic linen. The service was second to none, food plentiful (needed to ask for smaller portions sometimes) and jungle activities delightful. The highlight being 'Bathing with the elephants', a truly magical experience. Riding bareback on elephants whilst they bathed (and showered us!) in the river. We also enjoyed an elephant jungle safari as well as jeep safari to spot rhinos and other wildlife though sadly the Bengali tigers remained elusive. Our naturalist guide, Saket, was very knowledgable, fun to be with as well as being extremely courteous. Our final night was a river exploration by local boat to enjoy the amazing sunset with sundowners on the bank side followed by a farewell dinner in the bush which was lit by over 350 lanterns. Just magical. Overall highly recommended for a 2 or 3 night stay. Easy access in and out of the local airport (25 min flight to Kathmandu). My only small recommendation to the resort is to consider introducing rose wine to the drinks menu for a spot of lunchtime indulgence!

This lodge is up there with the best. It has the prime location right on the river. The service was fantastic and management (Subash and his team) are extremely active in planning the best stay possible. What I really liked was the sheer variety of activities in my 2 1/2 day stay. I really felt I got the most out of this stay. They make all their guests feel special. The naturalists are a great group of individuals. Special thanks to Jita Ram and Sakit.  Plenty of great birds right around the lodge. It was the highlight of my stay in Nepal. If you come here stay 3 nights to allow for all the activities. I did not see a tiger this trip but hope to return some day. Plenty of rhinos and other wildlife.

We came here as part of the G Adventures tour for two nights. We were so impressed with the setting and the decor of the lodge, and the staff were so friendly and attentive, really went out of their way to be friendly and talk to us. We had amazing rooms, with lovely natural decor, balconies overlooking the river and all the essentials in the room. The main lodge was spacious, catered for everyone and the pool was just stunning. We enjoyed the safari tour and the boat ride and Saket (our guide) was just so valuable and helpful and made our stay along with the other staff members.

We had the most enjoyable 2-day stay at Barahi Jungle Lodge. Not only the place is amazing, every little detail being looked after by the team, but the fact that the lodge also pays attention to its ecological footprint, on the edge of Chitwan National Park, was a plus, for us. Our naturalist (guide) was excellent, always pending of our needs and providing insightful knowledge about the area, its culture, fauna and flora. Spotting rhinos during our elephant ride was a unforgettable moment, and the jeep safari was also fantastic. Besides the "official" activities proposed by the lodge, our guide even brought us for a bike ride around the lodge, to discover the Tharu culture and way of life. All in all, an amazing experience at Barahi Lodge. Thank you very much for everything!

My husband and I recently stayed at Barahi Jungle Lodge and we were so pleased with our experience. I did a lot of research before our trip because I wanted to make sure we booked with someone who had good conservation practices and would be knowledgeable. I have done cheaper tours in other places that are greenwashed and where guides are not as familiar with the flora and fauna. While this was a splurge for us (it is a luxury lodge after all and we were treated as such!), it was worth every penny to know we were supporting sustainable practices and the local community. It was clear to us that this was an integral part of the lodge's mission and practice. We were assigned a naturalist for the duration of our stay. He was very experienced and when he learned we were interested in birds, took extra care to help us find and identify them. We used the lodge's handy animal list to track that we spotted over 100 species of birds during our stay. We also enjoyed our boat, walking, and Jeep safaris (where we were very lucky to get a great look at a tiger!). The lodge ambiance is lovely and the lanterns at night make it feel magical. The staff was so kind and attentive, and we felt truly pampered. We appreciate all their good work, and highly recommend Barahi Jungle Lodge to anyone looking for a conscientious and relaxing visit to Chitwan.

Wow! From the moment I arrived I was warmly welcomed by the General Manager  who showed me around and introduced me to all the staff.  The place is simply stunning sitting on the edge of the Jungle separated only by a river.  The staff are all from the local villages, with excellent English, all of whom go out of their way with kindness to make your stay comfortable and enjoyable. The hotel is beautiful, warm cosy rooms with jungle views, a variety of delicious food at every meal time, complimentary tea/coffee, reliable hot water, electricity and WiFi.  The team also helped my arrange onwards flights and hotel in Kathmandu for the next part of my journey, much cheaper than the online websites. I stayed for 3N and enjoyed many of the jungle activities on offer, each being tailored to individual preferences.  Jeep Safari, walking Safari, river cruise , village visit, elephant encounters, local dance show.  A special thank you also to my Naturalist Guide - We were lucky and saw so much wildlife...rhinos, deer, gharials, monkeys, elephants, birds.  No tiger but the signs are there and some have been seen in recent months.  A simply amazing 3 days, my only regret is not staying longer!

My stay at this property was a added value with magnificent view and vibration of natural surroundings of rivers and wild jungle. Really peaceful and a quality service far from city. Your stay at this property will definitely be worthwhile. Recommended.

Barahi Jungle Lodge situated in the pacific Chitwan, reflects the serenity of the National Park. Chitwan’s tranquility and the lodge’s peace very well complement one another. Experiencing refined luxury in the panoramic jungles adorned with the Rapti River when viewed from Barahi’s vantage point is a parallel universe retreat. We take immense pride in strengthening the bond of nature and mankind through our experiences.

On returning to Nepal I decided to visit Chitwan. It is really a nice experience of a different landscape and wilderness compared to the mountain region. This lodge is very isolated and directly facing the jungle. They offer many excursions inside. Really enjoyable. The cottages are nice and built to suit the jungle theme. Only problem is getting there from the airport: the road is terrible.

We had a great stay at barahi jungle lodge...the staff were well trained and very friendly...we loved the food and surprise breakfast at riverside after a lovely early morning boad ride...we will surely be coming back again

Home away from Home....They treat you like GOD...full of enthu....active...never tired of smiling....excellent service....awsome cottages...Wow factor food....blessed with outstanding property in Nepal...lot of activities to keep you occupied...they truly make u feel that property is our home and bleong to us.

We came here with a GAdventures trip and were blown away by, well, everything.  The staff, especially the naturalists, are wonderful human beings.  They genuinely care about your experience, which is clear right from the start when you meet the property's owner and are greeted with fresh lemonade.  Our naturalist, Govinda, knew we were interested in local wildlife and culture, and was so knowledgeable about both.  When others in our group went to rest, he took us down to the river and we spotted the first of several crocodiles we saw in the two days we visited.  The safari was amazing, too!  We followed the calls of a barking deer and came across a sleeping black rhino, only 50 yards away from us.  Earlier that day, we had the opportunity to walk through a Tharu village and learn about local life.It was also really neat to have our own individual bungalow.  It was spacious, well decorated, and had a neat stone shower.  The food was hands down the best we had in our two weeks in Nepal, with a wide variety of traditional Nepali dishes (including desserts) and continental options.When we talk about our trip to Nepal with friends and family, we usually start with Chitwan because it was an unexpectedly wonderful place.  It's unique in that you can be standing in a humid jungle, surrounded by wildlife, and turn the other direction to see some of the world's largest snow-capped mountains in what seems like the not so far distance.  The Bahari Jungle Lodge was a big reason this region of the country stood out for us!

The overall experience at Barahi Jungle Lodge was fabulous. Staff couldn't do enough for us.  The game rides were interesting albeit not a lot of animals. Washing the elephants was the highlight of the trip. Hotel rooms were little round houses which were beautiful, creatively designed and well thought out. The grounds are exceptionally well maintained and plants are very lush.  The food was great, all dietary requirements were taken into consideration. I could go back tomorrow.  October was very hot still.

After a very rough ride from the airport (roads are notoriously poor in Nepal), we were stunned by the beauty of this safari resort.  We were greeted by the manager, Varun, and treated like royalty - they even had a beautiful local woman there to add some sparkle to the greeting.  Our room was quite lovely - a short walk from the dining room (bring a small flashlight; though the path is lighted, it's useful to have).  We went on an elephant safari, fed the elephants, watched the elephants bathe other tourists (they call it elephant washing, but the elephants really splash water on those on their backs - we declined), and went on a jeep safari - we saw one-horned rhinos, birds, deer, and tracks from panthers and tigers (sightings are quite rare).  Our local guide, Krishna, was fun, helpful, and quite knowledgeable. In part because I cook and in part because we had a short time on a runaway elephant (no harm to us or the elephant), Krishna arranged for some cooking lessons for me just before a wonderful lamplit dinner outside the lodge's dining room.  I was shown a bay tree.  I asked if I could have a few of the bay leaves to take home for cooking - Varun arranged for three large packs of the leaves to be delivered to me before I left.  Very nice!

Excellent services! The beauty of the facility and all its amenities were wonderful. The staff are so helpfuil and kind. The food very yummy with safe water available at all times. The mornings with their coffee off the beautiful wrap porch n rocking chairs over looking the river, elephants n nature are cherished in our hearts.

Beautiful place. Very cozy. Beautiful location. The rooms very cozy. We especially loved the elephant ride. Food also very excellent. Staff very very helpful.  Lovely boat ride, small treks and jungle safari.

We had a wonderful 3 night stay at Barahi Lodge in October. The lodges are beautiful, very comfortable and the service from all the staff was outstanding. The hotel sits on the river bank opposite the wildlife reserve. You are looked after by a naturalist who organises your trips - safari, boat, walks into the jungle and ensures that you have a good time. We were lucky to see Rhino, crocodile, monkeys, deer and, in the distance, tigers ( unusual and very lucky).The road to Chitwan from Pokhara is difficult but it was well worth the journey. We flew back from Bharatpur (about 1 hour from the lodge) to Kathmandu and can recommend that.

After staying in tented accommodation and a well worn Lodge then travelling for 10 hours on very bad roads we arrived at Barahi Jungle Lodge....a piece of paradise.The quality of the accommodation was fantastic...with a real safari feel. Peaceful view from the patio of the river and the wildlife. Spotted a crocodile on the river bank...other side from our room. The room was very well appointed....great bathroom and the beds were very comfortable.The food on offer was either the set Nepalese Indian Continental or Chinese or we also had a buffet when there were more guests. We were also treated to a Jungle dinner...this was amazing. Water which is filtered by their own system is provided in reusable glass bottles which were regularly replaced.Our guide Govinda was extremely knowledgeable and passionate about his environment. On our first safari we saw 11 Rhino 🦏 both in the river and walking the tracks.We have so many fabulous memories of our time here.

The Barahi Lodge exceeded all our expectations.  There are so many activities offered but you can opt for as many as you want to do.  There is an elephant ride safari (a once in a lifetime experience), bathing with the elephants (so fun!), a boat safari (gorgeous, peaceful), jeep safari (we got up close and personal with so many animals and rhino babies!), a jungle walk, educational nature talks, a native dance performance, and village visits.  Even if you just want to hang around the lodge, you can take advantage of the lovely spa and massage like we did or relax by the pool or partake in magical outdoor dining by lanterns.  We loved just walking through the eco-friendly gardens on the property.  The room is comfortable and well-appointed but with character like a boutique hotel with a safari theme.  The food (Nepalese, Indian, Continental, and Chinese) was prepared perfectly.  But what impressed us the most about this lodge was the staff.  Anuja, our guide, was truly outstanding.  She shared her love of nature and animals with us and we learned so much from her.  She was gentle and attentive.  Everyone we encountered there was hospitable, knowledgeable, committed to the environment, and possessed a great sense of humor.  We came for the animals but will leave with fond memories of laughs and great times with the staff and other visitors.

Barahi Resort has been the absolute best experience in luxury eco-lodge staying we have ever experienced.  We stayed for 5 days with our 2 children under 3 years of age, and it was an absolute delight.     Service: The service was impeccable.  Every attention to detail is made.  You are greeted with a lemon grass scented cool washcloth and juice upon arrival, then are introduced to the resort by the general manager Varun Kumar, who could not have been any nicer.  You are assigned a personal naturalist who attends to your schedule, what time you wish to begin your day, organizes your activities, and accompanies you on them all, from when you wake up in the morning until the evening.  We had Anuja Joshi, a delightful and caring person who we felt became very much a member of our family immediately!  Her love for the environment and the animals is truly inspiring. When you watch her interaction with the elephants you can see they love her as well.  The naturalist arranges your daily activities but Anu played with our children before and after our activities, she joined us for breakfast and walked us back to our hut every night. She didn’t have to be so kind and attentive to all of us but she was. She made us all feel at home and we learned so much from her about nature from the trees to the wildlife. She is truly a passionate, kind and intelligent person and we highly recommend her!! She made our stay one of the most memorable family experiences we have ever had.   Elephant rides – you can ride a very gentle, female elephant as many times as you wish.  You are situated on the bank of the Rapti river that separates you from Chitwan National Park.  When riding the elephant you can view down to the banks of the river and over to the other side, where you can view rhinos, crocodiles, and jackals, just to name a few of the wildlife.  The elephants are treated very well, with personal attendants. You can go and see where they sleep at night as well.    Feeding the baby elephant – there is a 4 year old baby elephant named Tulsi who comes to the hotel 1-2 times per day and you can interact very intimately with her.  She was wonderful with our two young children, they were able to feed, touch, ride her.  You can feed Tulsi little snacks that are prepared.  It is an incredible experience.  Many people just spend as much time with the elephants as they can.  Elephant Bathing – don’t think you will be bathing the elephants, in fact they bathe you with water from their trunk!  You climb a full grown elephant (who lifts you up with her trunk), are seated on her neck while she wades into the water and sprays you down!  A once in a lifetime experience. River cruise.  At the bank of the river you can take a peaceful (sunrise or sunset) cruise to view rhinos, crocodiles, and jackals, along with an assortment of birds.  At the end of the boat ride there is a surprise waiting for you!  I won’t give it away, but it’s wonderful.  Food: is put simply, top notch.  We enjoyed every single dish.  There is buffet option or ordering off the menu.  There are Indian, Nepali, Chinese and Continental cuisine options.  We had two children adjusting to jet lag so we ordered many meals in our room, so room service is also available.  Everything is included except for additional drinks, such as alcohol and soda.  Please try the Nepal Chai tea!  We met the visiting chef who comes in to maintain the highest quality of the food preparation. We never once were ill. All water is filtered through their system and we drank this, even though they will also provide bottled water upon your request.  Access:  We were arriving from the USA so after a long international flight we transferred to the Kathmandu domestic terminal for a short 20 minute domestic flight to Bharatpur Airport. The airport in Kathmandu can be very hectic but it was all worth it. You can also consider an overnight stay in Kathmandu, but we wanted to get all our traveling done up front to maximize our time in Barahi.  Landing in Bharatpur (the airport to access Barahi Resort) we were picked up by the hotel staff (we paid for airport pickup, which was well worth it) and there is about a 60 min drive to the resort. Pool:. There was a beautiful pool in which you can swim and look out over the banks of the river and into Chitwan National Park. We enjoyed a swim everyday with our children (some parts are very shallow so our 2 and a half year old could stand and play in it) and when looking out we could see the visiting elephants!  A magical experience, truly.  Dancing:  Every other night there was traditional Nepali dancing which was very inclusive, and a beautiful sight to see. Our children loved being involved, and they were warmly welcomed! Village Tour:  We took two village tours on an ox drawn cart, where we met local villages, tried rice wine, and visited with them, and were given Tikkas.  We took two because we enjoyed the first one so much! Jungle Activities:  Other guests ventured deeper into the jungle on jungle treks but with our children being young we chose to do the shorter, more relaxing activities.  These seemed to be great though, and other guests highly recommended them.  We were able to do all activities except the jungle tour with our kids.  Rooms:  beautifully designed, with a very natural feel, excellent air conditioning, extremely comfortable beds, beautiful hand made stone showers, with tea/coffee makers. There is a small porch off the back of each room which looks over the water of the river and into Chitwan National Park.  At night you can hear the sounds of the jungle!  An immersive experience! Lastly, the night before our departure, the domestic Nepal airlines canceled our flight.  The Barahi lodge staff went above and beyond to get us on another flight and this was during a very busy holiday time. We know this was not easy and we appreciate their genuine kindness and care for us.. We are truly thankful for the help of the General Manager Varun Kumar and Anuja Joshi, our naturalist.  The Barahi Resort was the most incredible experience we have had as a family in resort staying.  We felt pampered but were able to have very intimate animal and ecological experiences in the jewel park of Nepal.  We cannot recommend it highly enough.

Fantastic lodge. We stayed for 3 days / 2 nights. Saw lots of wildlife including several rhinos, Gaur and a tiger. Rooms are great and well equipped. Food is great. The location on the river is stunning. Most important however was the team. Guides were super knowledgeable and service in the lodge the best I have experienced. And the pool great when traveling with kids. If we were to go again the only thing we would do different would be to stay a day or two longer.

One of the best jungle lodge of its kind in Nepal, I think after Taj. Stunning ambiance, services are outstanding, staffs are knowledgeable, courteous, decor is excellent ! Location is outstanding, maximum wildlife sighting is possible from this place. Resort has its own jeep & highlight is its Elephants...We had a great time interacting with Tulsi & Rani (Elephants) . Must visit, wonderful experience...Many activities can be arranged for groups

The rooms are very individual with a lot of local stone and other materials being used.  The rooms are large and spotlessly clean and have a beautiful en suite.  The menu is split into categories Nepalese, Indian etc.  The final product is excellent although the friendly staff do sometimes have a coordination problem with accompaniments sometimes arriving very late.The hotel is right on the river and one morning a rhino and her baby casually swam across in front of the hotel.  There is a swimming pool in front of the dining room.Lots of local activities can be organised. Apart from the safari you might consider a visit to a local agricultural village.

Had been at Barahi Jungle Lodge between 22nd may -  24th May. Though the Chitwan National Park doesn't have diverse wild life that would excite you, the Lodge is excellent. They pamper you a lot. Very competent and pleasing staff who can comprehend your requirements without your saying it. Their coordination is excellent. You never feel lost and there's always someone to guide you. One can opt for safaris (Elephant, Jeep & Boat) organized by the Hotel. Each safari is a different experience. Amenities are very good! An excellent place to relax... Plan a couple of nights in Barahi if you are planning a holiday in Nepal.

Barahi jungle lodge is a perfect place where you can feel the nature.. the perfect calm beauty of jungle (Adjacent is chitwan national park). We went there for 4 nights.. The lodge is situated around 1:30 hours distance from Bharatpur airport (from car). Though it takes quite some time to reach there, but result is definitely fruitful..😊 Ambience n all for lodge is awesome.. large and clean swimming pool.. supportive, cooperative and always smiley staff..😊 Hospitality and treatment provided by staff was commendable.. Stay was perfect. Enjoyed jeep safari, river safari (boat), Elephant safari, Elephant bathing etc..Will recommend the same to dear ones for sure.. Will surely love to visit there again..😊

Made unforgettable memories!The services provided to us by the team of BARAHI JUNGLE LODGE were one of the kind. Incredibly good and happy souls greeted us althrough. People were full of enthusiasm and were always ready to serve us even at the odd timings. The hospitality and mother like treatment will always make us remember them and of course our visit to that lodge. Would love to visit that place again.And i wish wherever i go I get treated by them.Such lovely souls!Thank-you all for making us feel so good and home like at your place.

After gruelling trek to base camp the finale of trip was to Barahi Jungle Lodge Chitwan. This was a fabulous ending to my first visit to Nepal. From the incredibly welcoming knowledgeable friendly staff to all the awesome excursions it was the the highlight of my Nepalese journey! The lodge and amenities are superb and all staff are courteous and passionate about their work and country. I would recommend Barahi to anyone journeying to Chitwan 5⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️plus keep up the great work!Pss food and presentation was superb!Warmest RegardsNancyCanada

I stayed here for a night.Service staffs are excellent.Its so quite and peaceful here.Early morning you come out at the balcony of your hut and you could hear birds chirping.Excellent hotel at the edge of Meghauli Chitwan.

The moment we stepped into the lobby at Barahi Jungle Lodge we were treated like royalty but in a warm and friendly way.  The manager explained all the activities that were planned for us.  Each sounded and turned out to be better than the next.  Our guide and naturalist, Hari, was a wealth of information about the plant and animal life.  He  took great care of our comforts as well as our interests in the jungle.Every meal was an elegant treat.  The preparation and presentation were comparable with the finest restaurants in the world.  The decor in the dining room, common areas, and guest room made us feel that we had found the most perfect place on earth to stay: elegance in a natural setting.  Even the outdoor pool was well maintained and inviting.  The entire staff was helpful and friendly. The activities including elephant safari, jeep safari, boat trip, introductory lecture, and cultural show were each magical and informative.  We saw 16 rhinos in the wild over 2 days.  I can't say enough great things about the entire experience.

This was my first experience at a jungle lodge and thoroughly enjoyed it! Right from the time they received us till the time they said good bye, everything was world class. The very first thing you'll notice about this place is the rustic yet trendy decor that follows the jungle theme throughout the resort. You can see the effort and attention to detail that has gone into every sma thing like the pencil or soap in the room. There is absolutely no plastic used anywhere in the resort. They try their best to be eco friendly in every way possible.The food is mind blowing. I was first feeling bad for not having buffet spread. But after I tasted the pre-plated food, I fell in love with it! We tried Nepali, Indian, Continental and Chinese. The chef did total justice by maintaining the authenticity of each cuisine.There are plenty of activities that the resort will plan for you. The elephant safari, boat safari, elephant feeding, tribal dance and village visit were some of the things we enjoyed. Seeing the rhinoceros was the highlight of our trip. A naturist named Saket was very knowledgeable and gave us a 45 minute presentation on Chitwan National Park which was very informative.The best thing about the resort was a staff named Krishna who took very good care of our infant while we were enjoying the meals. Don't miss the refreshing lemon grass juice which is served as a welcome drink. Overall, it's a great place to spend 2-3 days in Nepal.

I would only write that our family thoroughly enjoyed our two days visit.  I will not repeat all the positive observations other reviewers reported - as these were all true to our experience. Heartiest congratulation to Varun Kumar and his excellent staff who made this such an outstanding establishment.Definitely will visit again.

We had the most wonderful experience at Barahi Jungle Lodge. Quite out of this world - it is a luxury lodge and prices to match, but provided top level accommodation, service and great experiences in the Chitwan National Park.  We had the most amazing family visit with our grown up children and their partners - the wonderful memories will last a lifetime. It's a bit of a 'trek' over rough roads to reach the lodge , but you are more than amply rewarded. Every member of the lodge staff strove to make our visit special - it was! Can wholeheartedly recommend.

We stayed 3 nights at Barahi and all wished we could have stayed longer. Everything here is fantastic. The thatched lodges overlooking the river are very comfortable. Great views from the balcony, A/C, comfortable bed and great bathroom with huge shower. The décor is original and totally in keeping with the jungle location. The centre of the hotel housing the restaurant, bar, library are very tasteful. The restaurant served very high quality meals. Lots of choice and any special request accommodated. The pool is large with wonderful views of the jungle and has a bar nearby. The real stars though are the staff. Very warm and keen to help. We were assigned our own guide for the duration of our stay who tailored a program according to our wishes. Activities included a boat trip down the river which ended at a beautiful spot to watch the sunset. Staff had gone ahead to set up a bbq and bar so we watched the sunset wine in hand. We also went on an elephant safari and spent time with the elephants feeding and washing them. My 10 year old loved this. We had a ride on an ox-drawn cart to the local village to meet some of the villagers. We went on a full day jeep safari through the national park and were not disappointed. We saw lots of wildlife including rhinos, elephants, python, deer, and a Bengal Tiger. The tiger was the highlight without doubt.

Everything was really good. The service was impeccable; everyone was friendly. The food was excellent and catered to suit all of us. The guide we had was fantastic. Sakith, our naturalist, was good with the children as he took them on an extra activity, and was very enthusiastic. The activities we did were fun and exciting, ranging from game safaris to playing with the elephants. Overall the lodge is an amazing place to stay and I would definitely go again. They are a jewel in the crown of Nepal. A huge thank you to Arun Kumar and his team. As they said, it WAS a home away from home.

We totally loved our stay at the Barahi Jungle Lodge, a little oasis in the middle of nowhere. Bungalows are equipped with A/C and in boutique style. Bathroom nice and clean, in stone appearance. The room was big, including a small balcony. No universal plugins, so bring an adapter. Meals were delicious and there was lots of options. In between meals, one could always visit the tea lounge where tea, coffee, and cookies were served all day.Use the opportunity to do a boat trip and a jeep safari (You might spot a tiger! Rhinos are spotted for sure!), their naturalists are great and will share their knowledge about the lical fauna & flora with you. The lodge has also a great outdoor pool (limited shade though) incl. sunbeds, a conference room (incl. A/C), and a veranda (suncovered). WiFi at the veranda only. Bungalows are a short walk away from the dining salon but for those who can't or don't want to walk (or are afraid of the wildlife in the dark :)), golf cars will safely drop you off at your room. Every bungalow consists of 2 attachable rooms. Every single time we came home, we were always greeted with fresh, cold towels. Staff was superfriendly - highly recommended for those who want to explore nature but don't want to miss out on some luxury in the boonies.

I visited the resort last month, we were dragged a away the resort.we stayed the villa no 16 the view form the room was so excellent, bathrooms and Bed was so decorated,Room was very spacious and Comfortable. In my view this hotel is very much luxury hotel in nepal . The  Food is very  fresh organic and so much delicious . Multiple cuisine are available in different time The resort staff are so unbelievable because they have deep smile with services, the resort have well minted their staffs with well traning and manners The resort and over all surrounding is very well maintained with ecosystems and Natural ,Swimming pool  is so ausum river views Swimming pool ...overall everything is great survive ,Food ,Swimming pool ,Room  ,Restaurant,jungle Guide, I refer everybody who is planning to travel Chitwan National Park to stay a night at the resort without any doubt.

My wife and I had been wanting to go to Chitwan for awhile now. After searching and going through a number of hotels, we zeeroed on Barahi and all I can say is, we loved it. I usually am far too lazy to write reviews but this experience made me want to write one.From the way their reservation office handled our queries to the actual trip, it was truly impressive. Even our smaller questions were answered. The resort itself is beautiful. It's right next to the river and far away from the general tourist crowd of Chitwan. The rooms are great, there is also a pool and a turtle deck, which was one of our favourite places to relax.The food is awesome, we were welcomed with piping hot momos and even tried authentic Nepali cuisine. My wife too enjoyed the variety of dishes that were offered to us during our stay.The best part was the safari with the naturalists Govind and Saket. They would tell us interesting facts about the wildlife there and made the whole experience interesting. We were also given hot water bottles during the jeep safaris which was quite thoughtful. The best part of the resort is that apart from safaris, there are a whole lot of other activities that they offer : village visit, Tharu culture show, sundowner and bush dinners.Overall, we highly recommend this resort. If you are heading to Nepal, then Barahi is a must visit.

If you want to be a part of the ecosystem of Chitwan National Park - stay at Barahi. Aesthetically built cottages that overlook the Rapti River with all the luxuries that may not even expect in the middle of a jungle, it is a delight to stay at Barahi.The biggest asset of this jungle lodge is its staff, especially its naturalist - who play a mediator between you and the forest. They are your friend and guide who know the jungle, its flora & fauna well.

Barahi's top highlight has to be its vantage location - right next to the Rapti River & away from the crowded Kasara gate. The rooms are gorgeously earthy and comfortable (with a TV for those who like it), a nice pool that overlooks the river and nooks and corners where you can relax ( the library, a deck overlooking the river etc). The Chitwan forest is a dream for wildlife enthusiasts; we saw rhinos, Indian gaurs, heard the growl of a tiger, tons of birds, deer, wild boars etc). I have to say that the experience was amped up, thanks to Saket, the in-house naturalist. His enthusiasm is contagious and he is a treasure trove of knowledge at such a young age. My top experiences were a sundowner at the confluence of Rapti and Narayani Rivers, the walking safari in the forest where a rhino mum-baby duo was so close, seeing the inside of a Tharu tribal house and having a swig of their local alcohol and bathing the gentle elephant Sundarkali. Can't decide which experience trumped the other - all of them were so well thought out.

Absolutely beautiful place.  Staff give you a warm welcome and do anything to make your stay memorable.  Great safari trips with knowledgeable guides.  Beautiful setting to sit back and relax whether you want a boat ride down the river at sunset or just relax by the pool.  Great food selection and endless supply of tea or coffee

I remember the experiences with the Tiger Tops brand in the 80s and early 90s. It was legendary. Ever since I have been looking out for similar experiences. I had altogether given up, thinking it was the excitement of my youth that made these experiences at Tiger Tops lodge and camps heightened. Then I made a visit to Barahi Lodge managed by Pugdundee Safari. Similar feelings and experiences all came back. Hari jee was the naturalist assigned to only us and he was professional and knowledgeable through the elephant, boat and jeep rides. All the staff from the welcome team to the restaurant staff were excellent. The Manager was very warm and welcoming. Besides the bungalows being excellent the little details like placing a hot water bottle and shawl for our jeep ride through the jungle in the morning without us requesting them was what makes this place special. Not to mention the breakfast served for us in the jungle. Wildlife are plenty. We did not get to see the elusive tiger (only fresh prints) but every other animals are well encountered. You will also notice that much of the animals are encountered in the elephant ride on the same side of the Rapti river as the Barahi. This is the new forest of Chitwan and is very young at about 15-20 years only. Across the Rapti is the old Chitwan forest which you can boat along or drive through on your jeep safari. Barahi probably also has the best location for wildlife spotting in Meghauli.

Once i entered the realm it was so peaceful and relaxing after nearly a drive from the chaos city the staff embraced us with their happy faces the jungle safari and the tharu dance with the kind staff along with the great location is what made my trip  to remember it was my first visit and my husbands second will definitely look forward for the third one ;)

Decided to visit this amazing place on earth and I was so mesmerized by the ambience, service, hospitality of all the staffs from operation, f & b staffs, Naturalists. It was a delight and my short visit for 2 nights seems to be very short. I didn't wanted to leave this place in the end. What should I praise, the food on a-la-carte was so much of choice and tasty. The Chef given the local flavor in continental dishes, which makes the dish very unique and authentic. The activities on your visit was adjusted to your time and managed so well. The game we saw was fantastic, lot of Rhinos forgot the counting, different species of Deer, Wild Boar, Sloth Bear, lot of bird species, crocodiles. The ambience and interior blends with the nature and is a very rustic theme which is required in jungle lodge. The area of the lodge at the manager says is 13 hectare of land which is a huge area for the jungle lodge. could be the largest jungle lodge outside the national park in Nepal and elsewhere.

Barahi Jungle Lodge was one big surprise! At arrival there was a whole team welcoming us, the lodges are tasteful and luxurious, the food is outstanding and there is an excellent swimming pool with jungle view. The jungle walk and elephant safari were well organised but moreover the staff definitely made the experience complete: all so friendly and helpful. Our personal guide Krishna was very knowledgeable and funny. In short, we had a great time!

I traveled to the Chitwan National Park for 2 days and stayed at the Barahi Lodge.  I can't say enough about the staff, lodge and experience.  The lodge is small with only 40 rooms facing the park with a ECO style but very comfortable & luxurious .   The food is served in the main lodge that  also has a outdoor bar and a beautiful infinity pool. There is a small spa and the safari activities are the best.  Krishna the resident naturalist was so informative, funny & kind he made seeing the elephants and going on the jungle jeep and boat safari a great deal of fun a & super interesting.  Iti s not easy to get to Chitwan but totally worth the experience.

We could not praise the Barahi team enough. Everything was absolutely perfect throughout our stay. All staff is extremely friendly and attentive, making the stay for both adults and children very enjoyable. All aspects of the property are tastefully decorated, immaculately clean and well maintained. The food is tasty and plentiful, with options for every palate. All in all we had a fantastically enjoyable stay, and the fact that they have rhinos, tigers, crocodiles and lots of animals in their literal back-garden just tops it all off.

If you are going to Chitwan National Park ... You need to stay at the Barahi Lodge! Experience unforgettable jungle and river Safaris with the highly educated guides. Dine and eat the delicious buffet style restaurant. Swim in the refreshing pool overlooking the calm river. Sleep well in the comfy, large, air conditioned rooms available on the property. The staff was beyond helpful and kind ... truly making your stay feel like home.

There so much to say it's hard to find a place to start! Our group was personally greeted by the General Manager and his staff, along with much appreciated sweet lime juice and cold towels. The GM took the time to introduce us to the lodge and it's attendants before we went to check into our cabins.The cabins were absolutely stunning! I've never stayed in a place so beautiful. They were designed to compliment the natural environment on the park - wood finishing and furniture, earthy tones and warm lighting, and stone-tiled bathroom. I had two very comfortable sleeps and loved having the mini French press in the room to wake me up in the morning :) The rest of the lodge property was so lush and green. I walked the gravel pathways and felt like I was walking through the community forest just outside the grounds. It was lovely to have the Rapti river right in our backyard too. The naturalist on-site was a fantastic guide throughout our entire stay. We took a canoe trip down the river, where he began to talk us through the flora and fauna of the park. Once down-river, we hopped out onto the bank and were treated to snacks and drinks to enjoy as we watched set over the river. One-of-a-kind experience!I should also mention that the food was excellent. As someone who is gluten-intolerant, both the chef and waiters where very accommodating and would sometimes guide me through the buffet (when it wasn't a la carte) to make sure I avoided anything with wheat/flour/gluten. I felt very taken care of :) The staff were all so kind and gracious and made us feel like royalty (that's how I felt anyway) I wish I could have stayed longer. One of my most memorable experiences in Nepal. I highly recommend a visit to Barahi!

After a rocky four hour drive from Bandipur, my family was greeted by the most hospitable staff you'll ever meet. Having only arranged rooms and no activities prior to our arrival, the hotel manager was kind enough to sit down with us and offer a special rate for two days of incredible meals and safaris (walking tours, jeep tours, and elephant rides). The lodge is relatively isolated, with only a few villages in the surrounding area, but they kept us fully occupied with forays into the jungle, cultural dance performances, and spa treatments. Although pricey, the stay was well worth it--you won't find the quality of service and accommodations (or a place with four amazing resident elephants) anywhere else in Chitwan.

This place should be reached by plane, the road is far too rough. Other than that, the place is lovely, spread along the river, facing the jungle. One can choose among many activities inside the jungle and there is orientation program by skilled guides. Food is ok. There is nothing else in the vicinity, place is isolated.

As mentioned in other reviews the road to Barahai from the airport is very poor. It took us about an hour each way which was small price to pay for the reward on arrival, a beautiful resort in an amazing location with super friendly and helpful staff. The rooms are little thatched bungalows along the river, air conditioned, private and very comfortable. The food was exceptionally good buffet style, great choices expspecially given remoteness of resort. The trips on the boat, elephant etc were all great, highly recommend staying 3 nights so you get a full day walk in the jungle and maximum chance to see Bengal Tiger, sadly we did not but a baby rhino with mum in the walk made it well worth it.

Stayed only two nights at The Barahi, which certainly was not long enough. The lodge buildings are finished to a very high standard and the pool is incredible, especially at night when its beautifully lit.The accommodation is made up of single and semi-detached cottages, all of which look out over the river and surrounding countryside. I slept very well in the superking size bed.Food is excellent. They offer various activites including elephant safari. We one first thing int he morning, and saw wild boar, deer, peacocks, even some rhino paddling on the other side of the river. the later in the day watched elephant bathtime.Only downside is the road to the Lodge, which is pretty full of large potholes, but the manager mentioned they were hoping to do something about that very soon.All in all highly recommended, and I would love to visit again.

my husband and i stayed here and its always been a nice place to stay. we always got good service from the ladies at the front desk and rooms we've stayed in are pretty nice. Nice place to stay overall. The overpriced definitely no shopping centres nothing outside the hotel you have to drive half hour to main cchitwan to do so

Beautifully located by a river on the edge of the jungle. High-class facility and staff with a very high level of service both in reception, restaurant and guides to activities. Guides very skilled and know the jungle, its animal and plant life. They really care about their customers. Extra thanks to the guide Mr Govinda Thanait.

If you're looking for a place to either be on a vacation or even for business purposes, I think this hotel is the best one to go for in all of Birgunj !The services and management offered by Mr. Vijay Yadav and his team is better than the very best in Birgunj.However good the services may be, there was one thing I did not like at all. My daughter (5 yrs) and I stayed here for whole two weeks for my ethnographic fieldwork. The location of the hotel is very central and I had no difficulty scheduling most of my meetings in the hotel itself. In any case, most of the business houses, government offices and universities I wanted to visit were within walking distance. The border/customs office is only a short ride away.The hotel staff were very respectful to everybody who came to see me, ranging from crime victims and martyrs' families to eminent journalists, businessmen, policymakers and political leaders. This was the aspect I appreciated most about this hotel.This hotel is very new and rooms are comfy and fashionable. I rented a suite to facilitate the meetings while having a young child around: it was spacious and had a lounge attached to the main room. Bathrooms were big and very clean; one had a very comfy bath tub. Central heating worked well too.I must also share that finishing work is still ongoing in this hotel, sauna/steam rooms and rooftop restaurant are not yet operational (but work seems ongoing). Swimming pool is ready although we did not use it in the winter. The rooms on the higher floors offered nice city views. Staff is well-meaning and generous. Occupancy was not always on the high side and so we were offered a la carte breakfast on few days. Servings were generous! This is definitely the most modern hotel in Birgunj and I am pretty sure it will take off once the finishing work is complete. Was flown by Fishtail Air Pvt Ltd for Everest Helicopter Tour collected from hotel at 5am for transport to Kathmandu airport for take off.Being a solo traveler the helicopter takes 5 but was lucky that 2 other couples wanted to fly as well .One  no longer lands at base camp since January 2024 this has been disallowed.One now flies Kathmandu/Lukla(refuel stay in helicopter)/ fly over Kala Pathhhar(5545 metres previously landed  ) /Hotel Everest (3880 metres for breakfast)/Lukla (able to walk around a couple of hours) /Kathmandu.Front seat rotation is practiced so all 5 are accounted for I was also told to have R10000 to pay for national park fee and breakfast which is optional one can just take in the view .Breakfast menu is in $US .The breakfast menu is varied and plentiful and can recommend having while looking at Mt Everest.Even though I didnt land at base camp I was closer than I expected and I thoroughly enjoyed my day .

Sonia, the manager of Hotel Everest View, organised a wonderful adventure for us in November. Everything ran incredibly smoothly from our arrival in Kathmandu to our departure 9 days later. We are both in our mid-60s but trekked for 4 days from Lukla airport and stayed at the hotel for 2 nights. It was incredible to have a view of Everest from our hotel room (we stayed in room 3 and I think rooms 1 to 5 that have the best view so ask for one of those rooms). We loved the hotel although it is cold in November at that altitude. The electric blankets made sleeping comfortable but the electric heaters in the rooms only made a small difference. The staff light a fire and provide heaters near the tables at meal times. Staying there for 2 nights enabled us to appreciate the views and facilities in peace when there were no large groups around (groups tend to arrive around 10am and are gone by 1pm and much of the hotel is off-limits to them). The inside part of the spectacular viewing area on the roof of the hotel was actually very warm in the sunshine. Sonia organised a helicopter to take us back to Lukla with a flight over Everest Base Camp (which was deserted at this time of year) and the Khumbu Ice Fall. A truly amazing holiday. Thank you to Sonia and all the team.

Just that you know it is 31 USD per person no matter what you want to eat/drink. I didn't mind paying 62 USD, btw. It is what it is, if you want to have a coffee with lovely view to Mt. Everest. What bugs me is intentional fraud they tried to get away with. There is no way you can slip in 0 by mistake. If they did swipe 662 or 622 instead of 62, I would have given them a benefit of doubt that it was a double press somewhere and plausible. Anyway, I raised the issue with my bank and they are figuring how to get my refund back as ideally the merchant is supposed to refund it if it was their mistake. If you go here, take cash. NPR. Don't keep your hopes up on whatever they have to offer. Pay for it but don't eat. Just have coffee or warm water and enjoy the view. The view is to die for. Have to say that. These guys got the location spot on.

Sonia at Everest View hotel arranged a private helicopter around Everest, with a landing at the Goyko Lakes  at 16, 500 feet, then  dropping us off at the hotel to stay for two nights. The flight was smoothly organized from Kathmandu to Lukla  to the hotel then back to Lukla and Kathmandu. To say the flight was spectacular is an understatement. We saw where Basecamp had been but has since been removed we saw the route to the climbers took and the phenomenal surrounding mountains. The greeting of the helicopter by the manager and staff was welcoming. We were greeted with warm towels and hot lemonade and then that view. You see it is remarkable in the photographs but it is more moving when you were there. The view from the hotel is a dream. Being at 13,000 feet and then seeing the surrounding mountains from 26,000 to  29,000 feet, 30 miles away, is daunting. Lingering and seeing it from the cozy warmth  of your bed is such a wonderful way to be in the mountains.As others have stated the hotel is cold. But the staff do the best they can with space heaters and heating pads and double quilts so that your stay can be comfortable. Just ask them and they will provide a solution.  The morning is kind of crazy with all the hikers coming in for breakfast but they are in their own area and you can have the peace and quiet of your room, your private outdoor area, and the observation deck.  But the day hikes from there are lovely whether you choose to take a trail or just go cross country. If you go cross country around on the grounds you can get away from the chatter of the people.
