If you can stay two nights the first day you can get a sense of  how you deal with high altitude and then the second day you can go for a day hike. The hotel might seem expensive, but when you think that everything has to be helicoptered in and that you have saved three days of hiking to get there it seems like a small price to play. And after the morning, with only 12 rooms, you really do get you enjoy the quiet and the changing light and amazing fact did you are on top of the world. Sonam Sherpa is a remarkable Manager dealing with our needs; he and his staff really are there to help you from advice about day hikes to dealing with the altitude sickness or the cold, to dealing with a sprained ankle — they take care of everything and really make you feel like a special guest.

We had planned our first trek to Hotel Everest View to see Mt Everest. We opted for Discover Altitude Pvt Ltd. It was an amazing experience. Though it was Pooja Festival time Mr Santosh cancelled his home visit and was with us throughout our trip. Inspite of busy season they managed to provide us with attached bath accommodation everywhere. The porter Krishna and Baktha took care of every need of ours throughout our journey. All of them were like our family members. We were highly impressed by the arrangements made by Mr Kumar the owner of Discover Altitude.

This is one of those places in the world that you have to be there to understand how it feels. No words or pictures can describe the euphoria you experience waking up in your hotel room looking at Mount Everest and other majestic mountains, glowing up from early morning sun right outside your window. You get a rush to see more and get out there, even though paradise is right outside your window. You then run out of your room and go to the rooftop viewing platform reserved for in-house guests. What you see is literally breathtaking: you are surrounded by beautiful snow capped mountains all around you. And these are not just any mountains, these are the among the tallest and the most spectacular peaks in the world. You also see lush green mountains with beautiful little villages nearby and you really you are in the middle of it all. Matterhorn Glacier Paradise or Jungfraujoch viewing platforms in Switzerland absolutely cannot compete with what you see from Hotel Everest view. A big part of the magic of this place is its people. All the staff are really dedicated to making sure you are comfortable and able to enjoy the experience to the fullest. I was particularly impressed by a staff named Buddhi Bahadur Rokka. He was so passionate about the mountains that he explained the detailed story of every single peak and every single ridge of every mountain I was looking at. I had never met anyone who had so much knowledge and passion about the Everest region. I thought he was the mountain expert for the hotel. To my surprise, he told me he is just a maintenance guy! He has my utmost respect.The most difficult aspect of your visit to Hotel Everest View is getting there. Hiking 3 days from Lukla is the fun part and only way to ensure you don’t get altitude sickness staying overnight at this altitude. The worst part is dealing with the helicopter companies that fly you there. In my experience, helicopter tour companies in Nepal are run by the most corrupt, unethical, untrustworthy, and outright criminal organizations. I was supposed to fly out of Kathmandu airport that morning and was told to be at the airport at 7am. When I got there and called the contact person, I realized they didn’t give a damn about me. I had to call them so many times to just get someone to let me inside the airport. It was a chartered flight and they didn’t issue tickets, someone from the helicopter company was supposed to escort me into the airport. After waiting for more than an hour, one extremely rude and disrespectful person came out told me to follow him as if he was doing me a favor. Then they wouldn’t tell me anything and just told me to literally shut up and wait while they kept flying helicopters with other people.After talking to other people and some tour guides I realized a few things. Costumers that have already paid for the flights were the lowest priority for them because they already got the money. They always make those customers wait for hours and treat them horribly. They go after people that have been stranded at the airport first and extort extra money for “emergency flight “. Their second priority is “rescue flights “ which I realized is a huge insurance scam and a very lucrative business. I won’t go into details but you can google “Nepal Helicopter Insurance Scam” and learn how that works. Even after such an stressful start, I enjoyed the trip because as soon as I landed at Lukla airport, the hospitality of my guide Mr. Damber made me forget how I actually got there.To experience the magic of Hotel Everest View you must stay overnight. There are drones of day visitors who go there for lunch only and they experience a crowded touristy place but that is not what it is. Outside the busy tourist lunch hour, this place is absolutely peaceful, gorgeous and beautiful. This is a real paradise.

A HOTEL WITH CELESTIAL BEAUTY ALLAROUNDWe were at this hotel for 2 nights – 21st and 22nd April, 2023 to celebrate 70th birthday of Puloma (on 22nd April). We reached the hotel on 21st after trekking from Lukla to this place. 22nd April is an historic day for this iconic hotel as it was on this day a ground-breaking ceremony for the hotel construction was held in 1970. (refer page 95 of the book “A Ray of Light in the Himalayas” by Takashi Miyahara, the Founder). HISTORY:The hotel was built sometime around 1971 by Mr. Takashi Miyahara from Japan. The founder had written the above book detailing how the hotel idea was conceived and in due course of time implemented. English translation of this book is now available titled – “A RAY OF LIGHT IN THE HIMALAYAS – Building the Hotel Everest View”. The book vividly describes what painstaking efforts were put in by the Founder and all his team members to build this hotel.In this book on page 135 Mr. Miyahara narrates experience of a 71 years old (or, may say, young) grandma who was amongst the first guests at the hotel sometime in April, 1971. We too of around the same age say to the present management and entire staff: “Oh. How beautiful those mountains are! You should know how grateful we are to you all and Mr. Miyahara and his team for building this hotel and offering all required comforts and facilities.”LOCATION:The guests need to thank Dr. McKinnon who was then in charge of hospital at Khumjung village (built by Sir Edmund Hillary) for suggesting this wonderful strategic location to Mr. Takashi Miyahara who later created this wonderful hotel for all the guests to enjoy the celestial beauty of majestic & mighty Himalayas. Undoubtedly, Himalayas offer many such locations and this hotel’s location is one of the best coupled with all possible comforts and facilities the guests need and expect at this altitude – 3,880 meters. ROOMSAll the rooms with en-suite bathrooms are spacious and offer excellent view of the Himalayas. The beds are electrically heated with good quality comforters & linen. We had stayed in room no. 7 which had one single bed in addition to one double bed and attached terrace. We recommend room nos. 1 to 6 which are on an elevated level and may give better views.VIEWING GALLERY:Next to the Bar, there is a small staircase which leads to a covered viewing gallery and also to an adjacent open terrace giving 360 degree views of majestic mountains. We visited this viewing gallery on both mornings at around 5.15 am. Fortunately, it had snowed on 21st April evening and at night and the open to sky deck and all mountains surrounding were covered with fair quantity of fresh snow and clear weather on both mornings. The hotel management can consider keeping binocular and/ or telescope in this viewing gallery for the guests to use to get closer views of the mountains and the ranges. There is also a need for a picture with names of the mountains visible from the terrace.   OPEN TERRACEThe Bar room and the dining room have access to an open to the sky terrace with sit-outs for guests to get unhindered views of the mountains including Sagarmatha (Mount Everest) and many others. FOOD:The hotel serves sumptuous breakfast and all meals served individually to all guests on their tables. Even though one of us was pure vegetarian (no eggs), the hotel served very good vegetarian options on both the days. There is a good system of Happy Hours (5.30 to 6.30 pm) in the dining room with bon-fire. The guests can mingle with each other and share their experiences. The management can consider serving some hot drink like ginger-honey-lemon tea or spices infused local rum Khukari to guests with a starter during these happy hours. In order to make the discussion lively, an experienced staff can be present to start and lead discussions amongst guests and who can also share interesting stories of trekkers and guests’ experiences. A TV can also play videos of various Himalayan ranges, local life, local dances and music etc. STAFFThe staff is courteous and very prompt in addressing all concerns/ requirements of the guests at all times. Considering the altitude and possibilities of high altitude sickness, oxygen level was measured at night on oximeter. The Chef had made special birthday cake for Puloma on 22nd and offered ‘khata’ – a traditional silk scarf given as blessings – to both of us. We sincerely thank the staff and the management for making this important day memorable for us.

This was our last stop in our trekking , and I have to say that ir was the best , the hotel was built on the very best place were you can on a clear day see Everest and stay and the terrace for hours , the manager and staff great , the best cusine on our trekking great Japanese food , Sonia was great and I have to say that I found out that she does not only help me with Hotel Everest View she is one of the most importan trekking companies in Katmandu , she is the owner on Hotel Evers View as well she runs THT trekking company founded by her father , so she arrange every thing for us Helicopter transportation , lodges during the trekking ,Bhim our guide great human being and with a lot of experience he was pacient  with  us and help us mentally to get to destiny HEV its nice , the rooms are. fully furnish with everything it is neededthanks Sonia , Bhim, Sirish for making the trip of our life

Stayed one night on the way to EBC. Very impressive hotel considering the construction materials has to be delivered by yak, mule or humans 50 years ago. The hotel are still in good conditions, well maintained.The room was spacious and clean equipped with small portable heater. Not sufficient to keep all the room warm but considering the location, the small heater was not bad at all, plus each bed is equipped with heated mat for comfortable sleep.The 360 view from observation platform which is restricted to guess only was out of the world - the most beautiful breathtaking view I ever seen from a hotel. Food is not cheap, the Japanese set lunch menu cost USD 34, but understandable since most of ingredients are imported and delivered at site with helicopter.Inclusive breakfast was great, the best among the hotels we stayed on the EBC trek. All in all, good value hotel if you want enjoy the luxury and amazing view Himalayan mountains.

We stopped over at this location for breakfast, as part of a helicopter tour.Whilst the view and ambiance was nice, the food option was disappointing. There were separate menus for trekkers and people who were flown in. If you fly in, you are only offered 1 set breakfast menu, which consisted of a meagre portion of food for a staggering price of $31 USD/4000 NPR per person. The breakfast consisted of a plate with an omelette of your choosing, 2 pieces of sliced tomato, a piece of lettuce, 2 small slices of sausage, and a plate with 2 small pancakes and tea or coffee. Quite disappointing for the price paid. I had even initially requested to see the other menu, however the server had blatantly refused.Can't speak for the other aspects of the hotel, but if you're here for breakfast and you've flown in, don't even bother.

Could anyone please tell me what tea they serve?☺️ Saw the tokla tag but asking for the specific detail and the milk. 'The best tea' in my life (I am a tea person).Thank you for the smiles all the way through serving the breakfast (busier time).I'm in lost of words about the view.I wanted to treat myself and lo, I got the best.

We stayed here for one night at 3880 meters.  Although it was extremely cold in the room and the restaurant, we cas it be choosy to have standard service in the clouds ( literally!) The staff was helpful the best way they could.  The views of the Everest are the best you can get!!! Happy to have experienced this peak!

my second visit after 4 years ,and things chance ,yes i understand is a hotel ,but the only menu they have is a lousy 31 dollars breakfast (dont serve nothing else ) while i notice some people only have a coffee or tea , also the stuff in nasty and they ask us to leave the premises .Bottom line just go out and around the big antena at the right and you will get even better views of the epic mountains in the front

Thank you so much for giving us best service. the location is not easy and you serve the best. The view is stunning from your location. I am glad to recommend your hotel to any travelers those who visit Nepal/

The views of the mountains Everest, Lhotse, Ama Dablam, etc are breathtaking. The hike to the hotel from Namche Bazar is all uphill but not far. The room was comfortable with heated blankets. There was a small heater in the room but prepare for the room to be cold at night which is like every place in the Everest region. The view from my room was incredible.

The views are indeed majestic if it is clear. The staff is great and the food is excellent. But sadly, the physical condition of the hotel is not good. Carpets are worn bare, electrical mysteries abound, and leaks from the ceiling onto our heads at night. The building is ready for a major renovation project.

Wow!Experienced the hotel only for the view and breakfast via a helicopter trip close to base camp (landed at Kalapatthar area).  After the trip to Everest, part of the trip included this stop for breakfast at Hotel Everest View.It is amazing with trails all around if you have time before the helicopter comes back.  Our pilot said 1 1/2 hours but it was actually closer to 4 hours before he arrived back.If you have to stuck some place waiting to be picked up, this is that place!

Arriving by helicopter was unusual, but gave a WONDERFUL view of the Himalayan mountains! Considering it is in the middle of nowhere, they did a great job to make our stay as pleasant as possible. The food was great, they accommodated a vegetarian diet. The views are unparalled  with a 360 degree view of mountains. The rooms are large and well furnished, with a small inadequate heater, made up for with two large comforters and a heating pad under the mattress pad. The carpet is a little tired, but a lot can be overlooked considering where you are!! The last morning there the clouds parted and we had a wonderful view of Mt Everest, 17 miles away!

I stayed at Panorama Lodge in Namche (also excellent but not as high end) as I believe this hotel was already booked and walked here for coffee and the view of Everest on my acclimatization day.I live in New York and think the coffee I had here was the only place in Nepal where I had similar caliber coffee. It is worth the short walk up.If you are a coffee or tea drinker, you won’t regret it!

I had a fantastic 4-night stay at this extraordinary and unique hotel at the end of November at the end of my one-month exploration of the Khumbu including the Everest Base Camp. Had previously visited twice before, once for breakfast and another time for a one night stay, but this was my first chance to settle in on a longer stay and truly relax into the incredible surroundings.  Yes, it definitely was cold, but I’m not sure what else one would expect at an elevation of almost  4,000 meters at the beginning of winter.  The staff were absolutely lovely, and would start the fire in the dining room in the late afternoon, they did so even when I was the only guest in the hotel for two of the four nights I stayed.  The room I had was simple and rustic, but with such luxuries as attached toilet, shower and bathtub, a space heater, and a delightful mattress warmer which actually got so warm overnight I had to turn it off!  Visitors need to understand how luxurious all of this is for high-altitude rural Nepal, and have a spirit of adventure in this very remote place and an appreciation for these amenities.  Every room, the dining room and outside terrace have the spectacular view of Everest peeking over the Nuptse-Lhotse wall,  and in fact there are mind-boggling mountain views in every direction from the hotel environs. I will never forget the sun setting one day casting an unearthly pink and orange light on Everest in the distance, one of the most beautiful things I’ve ever experienced.  I was sad to have to leave, and hope that I will be able to return to this special place very soon for another stay!

Had hear about this hotel from many years, and finally reached last October.Though situated in such adverse & remote place, Owner of this hotel is truly a visionary person who built this iconic hotel some 50 yrs ago!Due to our trek schedule, we only had our lunch there, but explored the facilities well, and planned to stay there again in our returning back.Most probably, I'll visit this heavenly beautiful hotel again during my Gokyo trip next year for sure.

Looking for an exotic place nearest to Everest peak, I was browsing the net. After some search I found this hotel. Either accessible through a 3 day trek from nearest city, Lukla, or a helicopter ride from Lukla. Charmed by its  inaccessibility, and the reviews I sent a mail inquiring the possibilities of visiting with other nitty- gritty of the probable trip. In few hours, Mr. Shirish responded with detailed travel plan and other relevant information. i wanted a package Kathmandu to Kathmandu, covering air fare, Helicopter, hotel at Lukla etc. Shirish gave me the possible options. Though a bit pricey by any standard, we have decided to avail. I made a booking with no advance, but with a promise of paying in full amount on arrival at Kathmandu, Shirish agreed without and security. I was a bit surprised, as all other hotels I booked before and after EVH, had to make advance payment to secure the booking.I was contacted on arrival at Kathmandu and made the payment. Next day early in the morning the expedition started. All went on smooth and as planned. We got best possible accommodation at Lukla, Timely Helicopter ride to EVH with a detour to Kalapatthar (base camp). The helicopter landing and the check in is excellent. Checked in at room no.4, with a direct full time view of Mount Everest from the beds.Nice neat and clean w/c with bathtub and running hot water, everything is just perfect, considering the inaccessibility of the place. We have learnt that from salt to heavy furniture, everything is to be transported either by head carry or helicopter from nearest town. naturally every service is costly comparing to plain land city hotels. This is quite logical.The rooms are perfect, the ambience is just fine, service is simply excellent, food is very good, and the view, needless to mention. Finally I wander, how the owner did this impossible task of building the hotel 50 years back, when it was least accessible by today's s benchmark, with all standard amenities and comfort.Last but not the least, without which my review will be incomplete. Mr. Shirish, (forgot to ask his surname), who from day 1 was in constant touch with us giving suggestions, guiding us to make our stay comfortable, even with matters beyond his jurisdiction. he also helped and advised us on our COVID test, which was a requirement for travel back home. Our fully satisfactory  tour was successful largely due to Shirish. I can confidently certify that, he is an asset for any organization, the organization can take pride for a person like Shirish. We also thank the company for the excellent gift ( a duffel bag with EVH logo and monogram) A little suggestion for the Hotel management. In room toilets, a toilet/commode shower can be fixed to give comfort to subcontinental visitors, as we are used to it.I wish all the best for the Everest View Hotel.

Absolutely terrible value - I have no idea how anyone could stay the night here and rate it more than one star.The rooms and common areas were freezing cool - like being in a cave. Furnishings, carpeting, etc. seems not to have changed since 1968 when it was built.Dinner was served in the room, huddled next to a tiny space heater which did almost nothing to prevent the chill. Down jackets and warm hats a must. Forget about making use of their lavish dining room - no fire was lit, only a tiny space heater offered... bone-chilling cold even in late afternoon.Staff knocked on door to wake me up at 6 AM and again at 6:30 even though I specifically told them I did NOT want a wake up call.When I complained about all this, no compensation offered at all.Always sad to have to leave a bad review, but in this case, I wanted to try and warn others to avoid them having a similarly bad experience.

We weren’t lucky enough to stay here, but we did stop here for a break on an acclimatisation walk.  The hot chocolate was fabulous and it was great to sit in the sun with our first view of Everest! Such a fabulous place.

I recently had a one night stay at the Everest View Hotel at the end of a week-long trek along the Everest Base Camp trail. After a long and tiring hike in from Deboche, it was heavenly to get some hot tea and be shown to my beautifully appointed and spotlessly clean room with a very comfortable bed with an electric mattress pad and thick quilts.  There was also a small space heater in the room to take some of the edge off the chill. The weather in early December was very, very cold so I was not surprised that the hallways of the hotel were a bit chilly, but the dining area had a large heater/fire going which made for a cozy atmosphere.  One of the highlights of my stay was the delicious breakfast outside on the terrace in the bright sun, with the one in a million, mesmerizing views of Everest, Nuptse, Lhotse and Ama Dablam, there is literally nothing else in the world quite like this. Every staff member I interacted with was charming, helpful and friendly.  One night was definitely not enough to savor this very special place, and I am already hoping to return for a longer stay!

Last year I did a short Heli tour to Khumjung to spectate Mt. Everest. For breakfast, I went to Everest View Hotel & was amazed to see such a beautiful hotel in such a remote place. I then had breakfast which was mind-blowing & also knew about the history of this hotel. If you are in Khumjung then do visit this hotel.

A year ago I started to plan a trip to the Himalayas to make some night photographs.I came across HEV Hotel Everest View, and started to communicate and plan the trip of a lifetime. An elitist holiday trip of the non plus ultra-kind of travelling. That required a lot of questions to be answered and a lot of wishes and requests of the rather unusual sorts. There was this only one person I have communicated for over a year by sending almost a 100 mails back and forth. Would it not have been due to the tireless efforts of Shirish Krishna Khatri, I would not be so sure that the trip would have been such an unforgettable experience as it was.Shirish’s coaching since the landing in Nepal till the departure back to where we came from, was unprecedented. We felt like a kind of a jewel he was carrying as a dowry to his future parents in law. His personality is so unbelievable pleasant; polite and humble, calm and thoughtful and to my great astonishment he was so intelligent and well read. This man is only 22 years of age. I am wondering what he is going to be in 20 years!?!The trip was well organized during every minute.The helicopter ride to the HEV was efficient and pleasant, we were greeted by the hotel staff at the heli pad. The hotel is an iconic fortress of hospitality and charisma. You feel right away that these walls have seen and survived a lot, and will stand and remain for a long time to come. The terrace with view to Everest, Lhotse Nuptse etc reminds of typical mountain restaurants in Switzerland; clean terrace furniture and a huge menu to choose from breakfast or à la carte dishes and even Champagne.The rooms are nicely appointed with a private terrace yard to sit outside and to view the mountains. The beds are fitted with Korean heating mattresses to give nicely warm. The food in the restaurant is of exceptional high quality! Exceptional when considering the location and altitude of that place, how the goods get carried up there. The hotel offers European and local dishes such as Filet Mignon, Swiss Röschti with German Sausages, Japanese food at it’s best! And the staff are the ones who made our stay so pleasant. We felt like home there, and very safe as they were always checking for our wellbeing. Even when trekking around the hills, Shirish and some hotel staff would accompany us to ensure our safety and wellbeing. What started as a business deal has become a companionship during our travelling in Nepal. We truly appreciated Shirish’s presence and thank him for his well-done work, but especially to have met him! Last but not least my wife and I do convey our condolences and respect to the family of the passed founder of the HEV. He has passed during our stay at the hotel. It was a privilege for us to have checked in there when he was still alive.

Hlo. We are planning go HEV in 2020 in March. Please help us how to contact the hotel as we are from India? What is the cost in Indian money? Total Tour cost? We cant find any way to get contact with this hotel. Is there any Indian contact no by whom we can get the information about this tour?

Dealt with the legend that is Joshi, and guided by Bhim - both superb and really made our journey an incredible experience we will never forget. The trek to the hotel was amazing, the hotel has simply some of the best views on the planet and the subsequent helicopter around Everest was truly an experience. The hotel is very nice, staff are excellent and is definitely higher spec than most on the mountains. Food is western, but if you ask they make a superb Dhal Bat! Only minor improvement is that the heater they provide in the rooms is pretty tiny, but we loved every minute of our stay.

Seeing Mt. Everest has been on my bucket list for a long time. Hotel Everest View (HEV) and Trans Himalayan Tour Ltd. (THT) made that happen (with a little help from the weather). The hotel is off the grid so has to be totally self sufficient and all supplies are either trekked in or flown in by helicopter. The fact that the hotel was even built is an incredible feat in and of itself. The level of comfort, food and service the hotel provides is amazing. Yes it is cold and you will be wearing your jacket in the hotel but you are nearly half way up to the top of Mt. Everest (the hotel is at 13,000 ft Mt. Everest 29,000 ft). The electrically heated mattresses are unique and with the comforters make for sound sleeping after a day of hiking. We planned on three days at the hotel hoping that at least one day would be clear. We were blessed with three clear days!The actual hotel is only part of the story. The services Trans Himalayan Tour (THT) provides are truly remarkable. I contacted Shambhu Joshi (their chief marketing officer - info@hoteleverestview.com) and asked for his advice about visiting HEV. He created a personalized itinerary for us leaving Kathmandu via plane to Lukla, staying at a Lukla Hotel for a day of altitude acclimatization, helicopter flight to HEV and the entire return trip to Kathmandu. Another member of the staff, Mr. Dumber met us at Lukla airport and guided us all the way, getting us the best possible flights. The hotel has guides on staff and Sanjay Magar guided us on a trek (our first ever) to Khumjung on our second day at the hotel. Impressed with our capabilities during this trek (we are 70 years old) he felt that we could successfully tackle the Namche trek on our third day at HEV and we did! His help and guidance was instrumental in our successfully completing the trek. Joshi also created itineraries to see many of the World Heritage Sites in Kathmandu. Our driver Nati Maharjan seemed to know every back road and short cut allowing us to visit 6 sites in 1 and a half days and our guide that Joshi provided - Kedar Tamang was incredibly knowledgeable - a master class in history and culture at each site. Left to your own devices I doubt one would see more than a fraction of what we saw (no street signs, no traffic lights and traffic that would scare a New York cabbie) in the same time. At each point a THT staff member met us and guided us to our next destination. Joshi kept in constant contact by email and even called us at HEV to check in on us. Joshi and the team at THT made our dreams come true and we left Nepal with great appreciation for the culture, diversity, history and its people.

Was there just to had lunch after checking the viewpoint. The food was OK,  expensive as expected, but the atmosphere was terrible: Entering I was asked if I am alone (not because of the size of the table) - just in a disrespective way. The boss was asking me to make an order, literally throwing the Menue on my table (when I already had ordered). Then he was angry with one member of the staff because of my order (not quick enough). I could see other guests were asked to pay just the moment they put down their fork and knife. Staff was dressed in black pants and leather jackets, all seemed stressed and dissatisfied. I paid right after finishing my lunch and left. If you want to keep a nice atmosphere - just go to the viewpoint and eat somewhere else. Apparently Money is not making you happy.

Amazing stay at the Hotel Everest View, great comfort at 3800m to enjoy the magnificence of the view on the Himalaya’s mountains and the big Sagarmatha. No words to stress the excellent value for money this place is offering, very friendly hotel crew, great chef the food was very good. We were on a full board basis for 2 days, very clean room, hot shower and last but not least the heated mattress pads to add to this incredible comfort level at such a high altitude . Can’t recommend enough this place and can’t wait to get back there again any time soon in the near future. Thanks Everest View Hotel team for this unforgettable experience. Big thanks to Sonia for arranging this trip for my entire crew.

Absolutely amazing views to the nearby mountains, including, of course, Mt. Everest. There is an outdoor terrace where one can enjoy hot chocolate or the wide range of teas. Plenty of tourists. Good service

We have stayed 2 nights in room no 1. The best 2 things were the view from the room and the complementary hot water thermos in the room. Upon our arrival we were informed to turn on the hot water tap and wait 20 minutes!!!We were complaining of how cold it was in the lobby and bar and restaurant areas and were assured heating will be turned on between 10 pm and 3 am in the room. I woke up freezing  at 1am and there was no heating whatsoever. The hotel supplied us with a small noisy heating fan but that is not what I expected for the price. Walking inside the hotel in coat and gloves???Temperatures on both nights were -3 and -5. Better to just stay for a fraction of the price and walk up in the morning. All this said I haven’t even started on the lousy food and fly in my tomato salad.

Electric blanket and real hot shower! Much needed after days on trek, filthy smelly and dirty.The room and beds are comfortable. Clean. Toilet and room are spacious. Outdoor area is beautiful. The view from the hotel outdoor space is absolutely beautiful

I have been to everest view hotel twice now.Both times I went to the cafe and both times the food has been very poor, Bread has been stale and coffee cold. the view was great and maybe I was unlucky with the food, but for the price you pay one would expect a little more attention from the staff when food is prepared

We stayed for 1 night after hiking up from Namche Bazaar. Quite a few people arrive by helicopter which is a stylish way to do it but we prefer the walk. The hotel itself is nice enough. I wouldn’t say it’s luxurious albeit it is very nice by Nepal standards and on par with a good  3 or 4 star hotel in a large city. The food is quite nice, the hotel room is functional but every one of the 12 rooms has a great mountain view. This is the reason to go ( or stay ) here, it’s for  the views.. which did not disappoint. When we arrived around 4pm you couldn’t see anything but clouds and it was freezing cold . But The clouds by magic cleared around 6 pm and we were treated to the magical views and Sunset. Up before 5am the next morning to be treated to the view you hoped you would get. Absolutely stunning and we said it was worth every penny we paid to stay here. At around $350 a couple per night, it’s not cheap but if you can splash out and you are lucky enough to get the beautiful evening and morning views we had, you won’t regret it.

Spent 1 night here for our 50th anniversary. We flew in by helicopter & landed at their heliport. The service is impeccable & the rooms are very comfortable considering the remote location- reported to be the highest hotel in the world, own by the Japanese.The room was reasonable at $194/night but the meals are way overpriced for what you get. I think breakfast & lunch was $22 & dinner was $44. We were disappointed with dinner. They did not give us a choice & just served us chicken Katsu with fish tartar sauce with some cooked vegetables & soup. The chicken was cold- I would estimate the meal to be worth maybe $6 & I would rate it at 2 out of 5 stars. But the view was incredible- each room has a patio sliding door with a view of Everest & other surrounding mountains both for sunset & sunrise Almost everywhere at the hotel there was great views from the dining room to the public patio to the rooms. Luckily our stay had clear skies- it was awesome!I would highly recommend this hotel, but just confirm your meals. There is no other place to eat!

Initially just wanted to visit Hotel Everest View. As result of discussions with hotel manager Mr. Joshi I have decided to trek to the hotel and helicopter back. The booking process was made easy by Mr, Joshi with timely communication. I was met by Mr. Joshi at hotel in Kathmandu and introduced to Guide in Kathmandu and Mr. Bhim who looked after me through out my trip. Overall an excellent experience.

Two weeks ago my friend and I spent two nights at HEV. After a few days of hiking to get there, it was great to arrive. The rooms were very spacious with an incredible view of Mount Everest. It was so nice to have a hot shower. Being from a tropical country, my friend and I get cold easily - the staff did an amazing job at making sure we were comfortable. At dinner there was a lovely fire and space heater, and in the rooms there was a small space heater and electric blanket. There was also extra blankets in the room. At the end of an evening, I would highly recommend a hot chocolate in the sun room (private to those staying at the hotel). Thanks HEV! We would love to come back again soon!

You cannot ask for any better place than this in entire Everest Region. This place has got everything from stunning panoramic views to great accommodation with heating blanketsWe are big group of 11 people stayed here for 2 nights on the way to Everest Basecamp Trek. Its a limited Menu, Food was pretty good for both Vegetarian and Non-Vegetarian.Staff were very friendly and Clean Rooms.I highly recommend to stay at this place if you are visiting Everest Region.

The views here are epic!  The staff are all very helpful and attentive. We had a wonderful stay, the room was large and comfortable with magnificent view of the mountains.  We managed to get a helicopter to fly up to land on Kala Phattar (last minute request).  The food was delicious (particularly the chicken dish we had on our last night there)Will definitely come back.

This hotel’s name says it all! I simple cannot understate the magnificent, spectacular 360 degree view the rooms and patio afford of the mountain range in which the Khumbu valley is nestled. We stayed here for 3 nights and 4 glorious days and were blessed with the clearest days to view the many snow-capped limestone formations that was once at the bottom of the Indian Ocean 50 million years ago.Not being avid trekkers we opted to take the helicopter shuttle from Lukla which was well worth the extra expense, and offered amazing views of the river valley and, better yet, a preview of the breathtaking view we would have as we approached the hotel. But be aware that as well as being notoriously dangerous, the Lukla airport is completely at the mercy of the mountain weather and is often closed, especially to airplane traffic, so be prepared to get diverted to a small town or even be stuck in Lukla until the mercy of the gods provides a window to get in and out.The hotel itself is quite spacious with an amazing patio and inside dining space and has large windows and glass sliding doors allowing for maximum enjoyment of the incredible Himalayan mountain range in the Sagarmatha National Park. The staff is ready to assist in whatever way they can, and the chef makes some of the best desserts we’ve ever had. I brought my wife here to celebrate a milestone birthday and the chef made THE BEST chocolate mousse cake ever to surprise her after dinner. This cake had the best balance of sweetness, chocolate, and unbelievable moistness! And the staff in the Kathmandu office really tried to take care of all our needs, like handling the domestic flights and managing the changes, as the weather dictates, to our bookings.Some words of caution to prospective travelers: be prepared to wait for flights for hours, and possibly days; understand that the hotel gets most of its supplies by helicopter which is why the food is not the greatest and many items come from cans or are rehydrated; the WiFi is practically unusable for anything but text-based email with measured speeds topping off at 300kbps like in the days of dial up (although we found this to be true in all the rural places we visited in Nepal); and most of all, in the cold months there is no heating or hot water at all making the entire place freezing except under the nice electric blankets in each room. This last part may improve after their recently added solar water heater is fixed and hopefully made more durable to survive future harsh winters, but while we were there they brought buckets of hot water which really was the only way to bathe, brush your teeth, or even wash your hands and face, besides using the communal shower located all the way in the lobby, down a long freezing corridor, without any robes provided. Also know that the water in this area is quite mineral laden making the removal of soap a bit more of an effort, especially in freezing cold water, than you may be used to.A final note to readers: do not expect that your needs will be anticipated. Although the staff are very friendly and willing to help, you must be explicit in stating what you expect. A case in point: we booked a helicopter mountain flight with this stay and were told that the price we paid only allowed for the flight to occur on the inbound or outbound flight (the day we arrived or when we leave). I had expressed the significance of this trip to the agent you will deal with while planning and during your entire stay and was concerned about whether the weather might prevent us from enjoying this extra feature. The only assurance I could get prior to arriving was that I’d be refunded fully if we couldn’t get the mountain flight. As luck would have it the weather was not good enough when we arrived and rain was predicted for when we were leaving so I was certain we wouldn’t be able to go. While we were there we could see the many helicopters coming and going with supplies and other guests so I inquired about paying extra to use one of these and was indeed able to book one for the second day. As was agreed when we booked the hotel package, the flight was supposed to include a 15 min stop at Everest base camp for pictures so we assumed this was communicated to the helicopter company when we agreed to pay extra for the new flight, but it WAS NOT! And even though we were accompanied by one of the hotel managers we did not find out about this oversight until we were on our way back to the hotel! Imagine after agreeing to spend nearly $1500 and not getting the biggest reason for taking the helicopter instead of just an airplane flight how upset we were, but nothing was offered to us except some bogus reason about not being able to land at base camp. Then, as we disembarked we overheard the next passengers saying they were going to Kalapathar, another great place to get out for photos of Everest so that really made me feel cheated. So I had to agree to pay another $700 for a SECOND flight to take us to Kalapathar so we could have the full experience I had originally booked, and fully paid for. So the point is that the staff should have offered the possibility of taking the flight on another day and made sure that the pilot knew what was expected, and if it was not possible, then alternates should have been offered.While it was challenging getting here and even staying here, it is still worth it to be nestled in this most beautiful mountain range if you’re not a seasoned hiker. If you go expecting a 5-star resort you will be very disappointed. But if you go knowing all the caveats, and with the goal of finding peace at 13000 feet among the mountains and stars you will be the happiest you can possibly be. We still think it was all worth it!

Location is great. Having breakfast in front of Mt Everest is once in a lifetime experience. It was apart of our helicopter tour to Everest. However, the breakfast was just average and the service was not prompt.

We had a great sunny room with plenty of space and a private courtyard. Room 6. Heaps of bedding and electric blankets. Hotel is slightly tired but then you are up at 3880m. You go there for the views and not the decor. Absolute luxury compared with trekking lodges. Staff were very helpful. Fantastic viewing platform  and sun room on the roof.

My husband and I have just returned from a 3-day trip to the Hotel Everest View (one day to acclimatize in Lukla and helicopter ride to hotel). Our overall reaction is one of gratitude to the staff for their impeccable service from the beginning of our planning last November until the last pick-up on the return to Kathmandu Airport. Sonia and her team were with us at every moment anticipating our every need and helping us through it. Given the remote location (13,000 ft. Elevation), any number of mishaps could have occurred, but we encountered none, leaving us free to enjoy our trip and experience the Himalayas up close, which was our goal. Our room was large and well-appointed, with big lovely windows framing multiple peaks, including Everest. Given recent storm damage, hot water was not available in our room; however, staff made available another shower, which had everything we needed. When you remember where you are, and realize that everything up there is brought in by Sherpa or small helicopter, you appreciate it even more. The food was phenomenal!! It was very tasty, ample and varied. The pasta with tomato sauce was the best I’ve ever had anywhere. The beauty is indescribable, and the hotel is situated in such a way that it enhances every possible angle for viewing the majestic peaks. Even though we are well-seasoned world travelers, this experience at the Hotel Everest View will remain in the top of our list for many years to come. The picture of the Super Moon over the peaks was taken on our way out on our last morning at Hotel Everest View (HEV).

I read the negative review from the Israeli guest. I spent 1 night end of March and it seems they fixed the hot water pb in the bathroom. Electric heating was working and hot blankets, too. The staff is helpful (connections with helicopters), they do great job according to the location and weather conditions. We faced snow storm... The food is good and the view front of the Everest UNIQUE.

It is probably the most luxours hotel in Himalayas and it located in the best location to view Mt Everest and surrounding peaks, and it does has the best facilities of all hotels of the region. But it does not offer happy hours like all yeti mountain home does, that is a free tea hour with one cup small hard liquor, local whiskey or rum. If it does, it will make guest much happy as they can make new friends and exchange informations.

I’d like to write couple of words about this very well advertised place, which supposed to be one if highlits of our jorney!!!!As you know , the EBC track is not the easyest thing to do and one , who decides to challenge it need some points on the way to refresh him/herself.After reading many reviews about many hotels on the way we decided to let ourselfs kind of King’s time out befor starting a really hard and cold part of the track.How surprised were we upon arrival to the Hotel Everest View, when we found out, that the hot shower, which we were starving for is not in the list of services of the place!!!! The hot water was delivered by hotel staff handly!!!Heating in the room was very weak.WiFi, which we were also waiting for, to connect our families  almost didn’t work.As for restaurant....!We were tried to be feeded with concentrated soup and only after making kind of scandal we received kinde of “normal” food.So.... This place is definitely not recimmrnded!!!!The price was $280 per night !!!!This hotel not worth it at all!!!Better to stay in Namchi Bazar for $50 and to have a warm hosts, hot water in the room and nice food and views.

It was a real treat to stay at Hotel Everest View, the views were just glorious.  The staff were very friendly and our room was wonderful with huge windows so we could sit and watch the view as long as we wanted.  We had a lovely lunch upstairs in the observation room which was cozy and warm while we watched the clouds swirl around the mountains, fabulous dinner by the indoor fire pit and a wonderful breakfast severed in our room so we could enjoy the views in comfort as it was -14’C outside !!  Huge thanks to all those who looked after us so well, we had a fabulous time.

We hiked up to the Everest View Hotel on our acclimatization day at Namche Bazaar, and hoped to get our first glimpse of Mt. Everest. Unfortunately, the weather was not in our favour and the mountain was shrouded in some thick cloud covering (it would be two days more until we saw her) but instead, we were treated to some excellent lemon ginger tea and enjoyed a nice warm drink on the patio.The hotel itself seemed very nice. No expenses were spared in the building of this place. The prices seemed expensive when compared to the guest houses we were staying at, but it's the price of luxury at altitude.

We visited the hotel when our helicopter landed here to get refuelled.The views of Mount Everest were breathtaking. The weather was perfect for scenic photos that day. We ordered ginger lemon honey tea but were told there were no lemons that day. We also ordered a serve of fries and they came after some time but were piping hot and delicious.The hotel itself was very cold inside. We wanted to borrow the restroom but decided not to after seeing it was outside in the cold.

We recently did the Everest Base Camp Trek and decided to treat ourselves by staying overnight in one of the highest hotels in the world. The Hotel Everest View is about 90 mins walk up hill from Namche Bazar. Whilst the hotel is somewhat old and dated, it makes up for it so many ways. The view is simply worth a million dollars. Super comfortable beds with electric blankets. What really surprised me was that the meals were very affordable and not at all expensive. Anyone doing to EBC Trek should consider an overnight, or just drop in for a great meal between tea houses on your trek. This was a fantastic stay and one I will not forget. Thanks for the great memories Hotel Everest View,

SUMMARYThis is a hotel/restaurant about 1 hour hike from Namche that offers lodging and an outside patio with really nice views of Everest and the Himalayas.RECOMMENDATIONS:  If Namche is your final stop or you are having a rest day in Namche, then this is a nice hike and experience to get a glimpse of Everest.  If not, then you may want to save your legs for the rest of the trail.

We recently had the opportunity to visit the Hotel Everest View as part of our helicopter tour, which included the EBC, Kala Patthar, Tengboche and an extraordinary stop and delicious breakfast at this uniquely beautiful hotel.  We were fortunate to have absolutely perfect weather that day, and the views of the highest Himalayas from the hotel’s terrace were gorgeous. Nothing like an omelet and masala tea at 12,000+ feet!  Already craving to return to this very special place and actually spend several days savoring the mountains, the crystalline air and the silence.  Highly recommended!

we hiked up from namche for the morning to catch a view of everest...and the views did not disappoint (clear sky for dayssss). you can certainly see everest without going to the hotel, but this gives you the opportunity to have tea/coffee/beer with a view. you're still ~12mi from everest and you can only see the peak but it's a beauty...and you'll be able to see from L to R kyajo ri, khumbi lha, tabuche, phortse, everest, lhotse, ama dablam, thamserku. the drinks/snacks are pricey (~Rs350 for coke) as you'd expect and the spot was busy. we sat outside at a table on the deck in the sun. beautiful!

Trekked up to the hotel during an acclimatization day at Namche. The views were breathtaking... best enjoyed over a hot cup of masala tea... on the beautiful terrace of the hotel. Friendly and willing staff are always ready and willing to assist.

Though it was the first time I had gone to the place but have been hearing about the place since I was a child. Even as a child we used to read about the place as the highest place hotel in the world that hold Guinness world record. When I was there the environment was truly mesmerising. The flow of trekkers also makes it feel the adventure spirit of the place. I didn't spend a night over the place but had a nice breakfast and had a superb awinspiring view of Everest. The place is bit expensive but the fact that every items needs to be supplied through helicopters is good reason the price going high on scale. The best thing about the hotel is all twelve rooms gives you the view to Everest. If you  have time please have a one night stay in the very resort it definitely worth it.

If you are bone weary after a long hike and motivating yourself the last few miles with thoughts of a hot shower - do not stay here. They do not provide a towel for good reason. The shower in the room only has a choice of cold and ice cold. So basically only pretend shower here. A typical hotel scam in Nepal.

This is the highest hotel in the world and way out of the beaten path. At 3,880 meters perched 440 meters above Namche in the Himalayas, this boutique hotel is such a gem.  First, you don’t expect luxury at this altitude but you will find it here. The staff is very friendly and accommodating. I was amazed at the restaurant quality. The night I spent there, the restaurant offered authentic Japanese cuisine prepared y a Japanese chef.  It was excellent and such a nice surprise.  Food, of course, is not why people come here. They come for the views, which are amazing and priceless. On a clear day you are treated to the stunning views of Everest, Ama Dablam, Nuptse, Lhotse and Lhotse Shar. For Himalayan enthusiasts and especially women, you will be amazed the hotel also offers a hair drier in addition to heated beds and a hot bath. A true rarity in this vicinity. I highly recommend spending a night here.

Who would have thought there would be a place to relax and have a tea or coffee in the Himalayans after hiking up from Namche Bazaaar?!  Simply amazing! Of course some people took a helicopter up and back!!

Been there several times and the location itself is in an amazing spot where you get panoramic views of mountains around inculding Mt. Everest and 4th Highest Lhotse. Friendly staffs and great hospitality.

Traveling to Nepal, seeing the Himalayas, experiencing life on top of the world, meeting the people, visiting this land of whispers, dreams, and legends, has always been a dream of mine.  How could I possibly make this happen?  My wife and I have traveled some, but we are not trekkers by any stretch of the imagination.  Both being in our late sixties we have done our share of adventure travel and by no means are couch potatoes. We had been checking out the possibilities of how could we see Everest.        A trip to the high Andes back in 2012 taught us a thing or two about travel at high altitudes. We had some ideas about how we could see Everest...perhaps a 45 minute  flight around the magnificent mountain and other glorious  peaks. Then we came across Hotel Everest View in our research and I sent a inquiry to Trans Himalayan Trekking Ltd.  It was promptly answered and everything changed.        Sure I have heard about Lulka, the worlds most dangerous airport, and Namche Bazaar, the Sherpa town in the sky, but we neither had the time nor the energy to trek several days in the high altitude to get there. Oh, then we learned of this exclusive hotel built high on a ridge at 3880 meters (that's nearly 13,000 feet) with a view of Everest from every room and all the comforts of home!!       Then Joshi emailed. We started our communication at the beginning of February.  We went back and forth until he had answered all our questions and alleviated all of our fears on how we could get to HEV. We told him that we would be spending about 12 days in Nepal. He explained in his email that he could arrange our entire stay in Nepal and after several back and fourths he presented us with an itinerary based on getting to HEV as our priority.       Now let me explain that we have been traveling about 6 years now since retiring and have never gone on a arranged tour. We consider ourselves fairly experience travelers and have been traveling around South East Asia several months a year for the past few years, always without the help of any sort of travel agents or tour experts. However, due to time restraints we booked our round trip flight from Bangkok and let Joshi take over ground control. We had twelve days before our return to Bangkok and home to the USA.        We were met at the Kathmandu airport by Nati, a mild mannered Nepali with a jovial attitude and permanent smile! Immediately we were at ease.  He drove us directly to meet Joshi, who, by the way, spoke perfect English.  We were already like old friends due to our multiple email exchanges and his help with putting my wife at ease (more about that later).  We were given our itinerary and whisked off to our first hotel in Thamel, Kathmandu. The choice of our first hotel was perfect....Fairfield by Marriott, which was right on the edge of Thamel, the high energy, exotic heart of the tourist district in Kathmandu. Perfect!         The next morning we were picked up by Nati, our driver and Nabin, our tour guide, and went to the office of Trans Himalayan Tours LTD. There we met Sonia the daughter of the builder of Hotel Everest View who is a Japanese architect.  We even got to meet her father, the man himself, who at 84 is still going strong!  We had a wonderful two days of touring the Katmandu Valley with Natti and Nabin.  Nabin spoke perfect English and can only be described as a scholar.  He was knowledgeable about all things Nepal and he educated us about Buddhism (Nepal being the birthplace of Buddha).   Now back to my wife .... with all this excitement about going to Lukla and HEV I had neglected to tell my wife about Lukla, the MOST DANGEROUS airport in the world!! Not to mention the helicopter flight up to 13,000 ft between snow covered peaks and bottomless valleys . Not that she isn't adventurous because she have ridden elephants bareback and even entered a tiger cage to pet the felines up close, but flying into a 550 ft runway uphill onto a tarmack carved into a mountain with a wall of granite as a stopping point...well, all bets were off. Several times during our conversations with Joshi she was off to the airline to cancel the flight to Nepal. Joshi assured her that all would be well.  He also keep in touch daily to make sure that we were well taken care of even when we were at HEV. Finally the day came when Nati arrived bright and early to bring us to Katmandu airport.  We were on the first flight, but there were several first flights.  It was exciting to say the least! I had a bruised arm where my wife held on during landing. My wife said "that wasn't to bad". The flight and landing were smooth and the landscape was breathtaking. We stayed in Lukla for one night to acclimate to the altitude.  The staff at the hotel couldn't have been more accommodating. During the day we were given a tour of the town and had a delightful lunch with our sherpa guide. The next morning we were up bright and early headed to HEV.  The staff met us at breakfast and the helicopter picked us up at 7.  The skies were bright blue accented by the snow capped mountain and shear walls of granite . The flight was right out of National geographic, exhilarating hair raising excitement. We came around a mountain and suddenly there was Everest in all her glory. We landed and spent the morning at Everest View Hotel sitting on the deck totally mesmerized by the magnificent mountain that we had come to see and it's surrounding peaks.    The staff were fantastic, the food was excellent being flown in by helicopter every day. The Sherpas who took us trekking treated us with the utmost respect and it was nice to see a culture where the concept of respecting your elders is alive and well. The staff at HEV and Trans Himalayan Trekking are the the best in the business. Joshi,   Sonia and their staff, Nati, Nabin, and our Pokhara friend and guide, Pasang Sherpa, along with the folks at the Fish Tail Lodge in Pokhara were absolutely fantastic!! The best decision that we made in planning our trip to Nepal was having Joshi arrange our tour. Everything detail was meticulously arranged for us and he was always one step ahead to make sure it all went as planned.  It our minds it was beyond our expectations!!     Nepal is one of the most beautiful places on earth and the people are some of the most wonderful, interesting, colorful and friendly people on the planet. We truly fell in love with this fantastic country and will be back soon!!Our deepest thanks go to Sonia, Nati, Nabin, Pasang and all the wonderful staff at Hotel Everest View and Fish Tail Lodge, but mostly we want to thank Joshi at Trans Himalayan Trekking LTD for a spectacular vacation!

We take our clients as an acclimatization hike to this poit and surrounding villages like Khumjung and Khunde. The guest are always happy to see the magnificent view of the giant mountains, This place host as a good location for people who can not make all the way to EBC but want to enjoy the view of Mount Everest and her surrounding.

Hotel Everest View is the experience of a lifetime! You can only get there by helicopter or by trekking 3 or so days. :) When's the last time you could say that about a place you've been?! Because it is so remote, the hotel booking agent, Joshi, was a life saver - coordinating our transportation to and from. But even better, Joshi is a full-service travel agent. I never thought I'd need a travel agent, but boy am I glad I allowed myself to lean on Joshi's expertise! Together, we planned my entire Nepal trip, not just the few days I was at HEV, and there is no way I could have done it without him and his team (esp because we lost our luggage for several days and he navigated that craziness with the local airport authority). They provided private transportation to and from every airport, booked an incredible wildlife lodge and elephant safari at Chitwan National Park, booked expert tour guides for the holy sites in Kathmandu Valley, and a wonderful trekking guide for our trek out from the hotel to Namche Bazaar and Khunde Peak. You could easily use HEV as a stopping off point on the way to Gokyo or Tengboche, but since we weren't doing a full trekking trip, we flew up to and down from HEV by helicopter and let me tell ya, it was the coolest 5 mins of my life! HEV is nestled right in the Himalayas with 360 degree views of 8 of the tallest mountains in the world, Everest being one of them of course. It will take your breath away!The hotel itself was comfortable, clean, and modern. And the food was good - american protein and veggie style with some little Japanese surprises like Teriyaki chicken. They light a fire in this grand fireplace every night during/after dinner and they provide heaters at the food tables which is much appreciated.You have to know what to expect... it's going to be cold so be prepared. Electricity up there is hydro power so the electricity cuts off during the night through early morning to conserve. So while you may start warm with an electric blanket, you won't stay that way. :) And the shower water is mostly super cold, so I just put off taking one truthfully.But all in all, you won't regret a stay at Hotel Everest View! Lean on their expertise and you will be incredibly pleased.(Note: I traveled late March)

A fantastic hotel on the top of the world - officially the highest hotel in the world at 3880 metres. You have to trek there , 3 days from Lukla staying at lodges en-route (we used yeti mountain homes, excellent). The food, rooms, service and views are just spectacular. Top tip —- take a helicopter back to Lukla for a stunning 10 minute ride. How to organise the hike ? Simple: email the hotel and they’ll take care of everything  ( guide , Porter, lodges, flights, helicopter etc.). It’s a tough hike but so worth it — get training.

Pros:- Staff was friendly and helpful- Beautiful view of the Everest mountain right outside the room, with patio- Spacious roomCons:- Bathroom could be cleaner- Heater was very small and basically ineffective- No entertainment within the hotelThis is the best hotel in the Everest region but understand that there will be limited supply of heat and electricity and hot water when you stay in this region.

We spent only one night in this famous hotel. Although the views from the room and dining area are incredible, hot shower and electric blankets are a kind of luxury during the trek, I should say that the hotel rooms and facilities are very outdated, the food is too expensive for the quality of it and the staff was really unfriendly (except for Sonia who was very helpful by booking it). Can’t recommend it for that price.

I went with my husband of 45 years to this beautiful hotel with great food and views that you can't get anywhere else in the world. He planned this vacation with Joshi from hoteleverestview.com whose attention to detail made this a remarkable experience. We were connected with Bhim Magar, our trek guide, whose knowledge and skill enabled us to navigate the rocky terrain with confidence. Planning this vacation with Joshi is the way to go!

We trekked our way to HEV fromLukla Airport and we stayed for 2 nights. The whole itinerary for the trekking and our stay was carefully organised by Sonia at HEV. It was tailored and personalised to our needs.Our guides (Lhakpa and Pemba) were amazing and although we were not experienced trekkers they guided us in the best way.Our stay at HEV was really good, as the facilities and service are great considering the altitude. Highly recommended to everyone!

This is a hotel that has the best views of Mt Everest and surrounding areas. The food is first rate and the service is five star.Joshi, hoteleverestview@gmail.com made all our arrangements and when we asked to change our itinerary, he was able to do it without hesitation. He not only arranged a personal guide and porter for our trek from Everest View Hotel but also a personal guide and driver in Kathmandu, private transfers from the airports, and accommodations at all lodges from Everest View to Lukla. His attention to detail is impeccable.

From Yeti Mountain Home in Namche, it took us 3 hours to climb to Syangboche which is where Hotel Everest View resides. Not only are the views something out of a movie, but the food and lodging was wonderful given how remote the area was. Most people use Hotel Everest View as a acclimatization hike but then trek back to Namche. My family and I stayed here and we are so glad we did! It was amazing to wake up to Everest, Ama Dablam and the other famous mountains. As I said above, the beds were comfortable, the food was delicious, and we had hot showers and warm duvets. What else do you need on a mountain trek? I would highly recommend everyone to stay here when passing through this region. You will be so glad you did!

My wife and I decided to do something different for our 20th anniversary so off to Everest View Hotel in Nepal we went. I had read a number of reviews on tripadvisor before making the choice and I have to say my experience was so similar to those that had a 5 star experience. Sonia took care of everything for us, and in a place that can be foreign to a westerner it was most comforting. The HEV staff met us at Lukla from our flight and then chaperoned us onto our helicopter flight the next day. We had a fantastic stay at the hotel, which naturally is all about seeing Mt Everest with your own eyes. We were not disappointed. The food at the hotel was fantastic. It is remarkable that most of it comes in via helicopter because there is no supermarket for miles. The Japanese dinner was exceptional and the Miso soup is the best I have ever had! The hotel even made us a Happy Anniversary cake!!! We were blown away!!!The views from the restaurant are spectacular. For the return trip the HEV staff then met us again at Lukla after our helicopter flight down from the hotel, and made sure we got onto our connecting flight to Kathmandu ok, before meeting us in Kathmandu airport and driving us to our hotel. To all the staff (and especially Sonia) thank you thank you thank you. That was a trip of a lifetime made into something truly exceptional. I will be recommending you to all my friends and acquaintances and we may even be back for our 30th, 40th and 50th anniversaries!

I went to HEV in January 2017 for my 21st birthday with a friend of mine as I wanted to wake up overlooking Mt Everest for my birthday. This trip was incredible!! Sonia as incredible helped organise all of the details and it ran so smoothly. Our guide Sanjay and wonderful porter were beyond incredible. Taking the time to explain all of the details before and along the way. The team at HEV were utterly amazing too, when we arrived it was winter and we were the only guests in the building. As a result of being winter the water pipes often froze, and each morning we would wake up to fresh buckets of boiling hot water at our door and each of the men were super helpful; always smiling, always asking if we were okay and always asking if they could do anything for us. All of our meals were beautiful and when we arrived at HEV on our first night we were greeted by the kitchen staff signing us happy birthday with a beautiful cake. I could not recommend this trip anymore, in fact i'm currently organising to go back at the end of the year!! This is the most incredible trip, hosted and organised by the most lovely, caring and beautiful people.

My husband and I travelled to Nepal in November 2017 and we were excited but a little apprehensive as to what to expect from this very remote hotel.  However, our stay exceeded all expectations!Sonia was fantastic in organising our whole trip, with lots of emails being exchanged before booking exactly what we wanted. She even met us at our hotel in Kathmandu (as well as greeting us after the trip and taking us back to our hotel again) - a lovely personal kindness.Our guide - Ang Furi Lama - also met us at the hotel and with his expertise we successfully negotiated the airport to get on the plane to Lukla - not an easy task as it's so chaotic.  Ang Furi Lama was the best guide, taking into account our hiking pace (very slow I'm sure), he never hurried us and matched his pace to ours so well. His knowledge of the area was wonderful, we would have missed so much of the history and sights without him.On the way up to HEV we stayed at Yeti Mountain Lodges as arranged by Sonia, and these were all very good, comfortable but of course cold at night.We arrived at HEV after a long day's hike from Thame to be greeted by the wonderful staff and given refreshments, while oggling at the view through the huge windows!  Soon we were shown to our room - huge by the way, with that same awe-inspiring view.  A nice hot shower and we settled in for a few nights.  We were blown away by the remoteness and the beauty of this hotel.  Our stay here exceeded all of our very high expectations.  The bedroom had a heater which made the temperature very pleasant indeed, we had very warm doonas, and unexpectedly, ELECTRIC BLANKETS!  We were not cold at night, which was such a plus.We found the food delicious, and I so appreciate that the chef took care to provide vegetarian meals for me - thank you. We had lots of Japanese food here, and once again thanks to  Ang Furi Lama for his explanation of this yummy cuisine!We spent our few days here doing local hikes - to Kunde Peak and Khumjung and really felt that we had time to relax and enjoy the whole experience of the mountains, while still being able to return to the hotel and relax there too - in comfort.It was cloudy on our first afternoon at HEV and of course we were hoping for clear weather the next day...waking at 3am and looking out of our window to see the incredibly clear skies, stars and towering mountains was one of the most memorable moments of my life.  My husband was up early every morning to take photos from the observatory, while I was able to drink in the same view from my warm bed!!This hotel is amazing.  Sure, it is not a modern five-star city hotel, but that is not what anyone would expect in such a remote location (I shake my head when some of the reviews mention that it is cold - really - get a grip!).The hot water is now available in each room I believe, it was just being connected while we stayed, but having to use a shared shower was not a big deal. We felt privileged to stay here, and we hope to come back.Thank you to all the staff, Ang Furi Lama, and especially to Sonia, for our wonderful memories.

This is part of our acclimatisation day each time we were trekking in The Khumbu. The walk from Namche is enjoyable and panoramic. The view from the verandah (on a clear day) is spectacular. Always a good place to stop. The prices here for coffee and such are very reasonable when you consider exactly where it is.

Myself and two colleagues stayed at HEV ON Sat 27th Jan 2018 in advance of a work visit to India. We arrived by helicopter from Kathmandu. HEV lived up to all expectations. Brilliant, amazing, friendly staff, great food, great accommodation .. we were privileged to stay there. Yes it was cold in the evening, minus 18C but that added to the fun. Yes we slept in our hiking gear and yes I viewed the stars and shooting stars at that at 03:30 in the morning and I was blown away. We were the only guests that night, the staff were amazing. We had a guide for our hike to Namche (we hadn’t really acclimatised flying straight from Kathmandu and it was cloudy on the Sat day).Sunday morning, clear skies and amazing views of the mountains: Everest,  Lhotse, Ama Dablam and so on. Thanks to Sonia for all the arrangements and the rest of the staff for looking after us. If you want to see Everest and are not trekking in the region and you want to stay in a fantastic location/ place then HEV is a must. It was built in the 70’s, it won’t have all mod cons but it has character by the bucket load, go see for yourself. Matthew McIver

A steep climb to Syangboche from Namche takes you to open ridge and hilltop to Syangboche offering amazing view of the higher mountains and low glacial valley below . Sipping hot drinks at the patio with Mt. Everest View is so rewarding after the steep hike to ease the pain .

After my daughter's graduation from college, Celine, my niece and I decided to embark on this adventure. So, here we are in December. Three active but not expert trekkers from New Orleans, which is below sea level, trekking to Hotel Everest View, the highest hotel in the world. We arrived on Christmas Day and spent two nights. The staff made sure we celebrated Christmas dinner with style. The garlic soup was heavenly delicious. The dinner was exquisite. The entire staff made us feel at home.. One of the best Christmas ever. The room was  cozy and warm with views of Mt Everest, Ama Dablam and all the other mountain peaks that I do not remember the names. The next day, our wonderful guide Sanjay took us on a low key trek. We sat down, relaxed, and enjoyed the majestic beauty surrounding us. Took pictures that are now watching me on my desk! I will, definitely go back. Maybe when the rhododendrons are in bloom?

I always wanted to travel to Nepal and visit the Himalaya, everybody should see these incredible mountains with their own eyes.                                     I had a set amount of days left during 2017 to plan a trip, and an important part of that, for me, was to photograph Everest and the surrounding peaks. I needed a base where I could settle down for a few days, take in the views and spend some time photographing the region.I searched for places that would fit my needs, and Hotel Everest View just seemed to tick all the boxes. An e-mail query to HEV was promptly answered by Sonia, the Hotel Manager, and this set the ball rolling for a planned visit in early December. Sonia was fantastic in helping me to customize my trip to suit and since she also Manages a trekking company, it was made so much easier for me to concentrate on flights and other things while she took care of domestic Nepali items like permits, trekking lodges and other essentials.                   After arriving in Kathmandu, and getting to my hotel, it was time to re-pack my belongings into a duffel and prepare for the early morning flight to Lukla. This is quite an experience in itself, and after meeting my guide and porter, Sanjay and Kiran, it was time to start the trek towards Phakding, the following day to Namche Bazaar and the third day to Syangboche and Hotel Everest View.The hotel was everything I had hoped for and more besides. Wonderfully located, but quite hidden by trees until you get closer, this is part of its charm! It just seems to blend into the surrounding landscape and is something of an oasis within the Himalayan hills. The rooms have the most fantastic views of the great mountains, with Everest, Lhotse and the beautiful Ama Dablam dominating. It was a great pleasure to stroll around the outside of the hotel and around the hills with the 360-degree view.I have read some infrequent reviews which have complained about the cold. I think that this is really down to bad planning on the part of some people who simply do not prepare properly. Depending on what time of the year you are travelling, do some research, read a trekking guide and make sure you have the right gear. Sort out your base layers, get a down jacket for the night.                     I believe HEV do a great job in looking after their guests, the staff are so polite and friendly. The rooms are very comfortable, with electric blankets to warm up the beds for a good night’s sleep. I enjoyed the food very much and they take great pride in providing the best ingredients for the guest’s meals.I stayed for 3 nights and would highly recommend Hotel Everest View to anyone who has a passion for the natural world and would like to wake up to a breath-taking view of Everest and surrounding peaks outside their window.

I accidentally discovered Hotel Everest View through Google and felt like I found a new entry in my bucket list. A short email conversation with their super helpful manager Mr Joshi put me (and my friend) on a plane to Kathmandu. This was our first time to this region and I didn’t know what to expect but it turned out to be the best holiday experience I ever had. Everest region is an incredible place. It is as if mankind never invented the wheel. You see nothing with a wheel - not even a toy cycle or a push cart. As a walker/trekker, this is one of the very few places on earth where you feel terrific about walking. Walking is the only way here. You are the highest in the food chain of transportation. There is nobody going past you by mechanical trickery. Well, there are helicopters but you still own the land.We trekked to the hotel from Lukla with everything meticulously arranged by Mr Joshi. He also arranged enroute accommodation (Yeti Mountain Homes) during the trek. All we had to do was just trek for 3 days to reach Hotel Everest View and words can't describe my experience that borders on spiritual enlightenment. I believe some people take a helicopter directly to the hotel but for those who have time on their hands and have reasonable fitness levels (I feel you don't even have to be much fit, just need to love walking), trekking to the hotel would be an extraordinary experience. While Everest base camp trek is the most popular thing to do in this region, it's not for everyone due to lack of decent accommodation once you cross Namche Bazaar. I found trekking to reach 4000m is an amazing experience without being deprived of comfortable accommodation. Of course, you won't get the bragging rights of an EBC trek but for those who can't do without creature comforts there is a lot to enjoy here.The hotel has an amazing location and has earned a reputation of 'must see' places in the region. This place has incredible mountain views anywhere you look and the famous four peaks (Mt. Everest, Lhotse and Nuptse, Ama Dablam) can be seen from pretty much every window in this hotel. They also have nice viewing decks which are great when the sun is out. Ama Dablam is my favourite mountain. The hotel has clean and comfortable rooms and toilets. Very friendly staff and the food was delicious. I casually asked the chef for how long he has been working here and he said 28 years!
