We spent two days by hiking to nearby villages and came back to enjoy the creature comforts that you know are extremely hard to come by at such inaccessible and remote location.I think anybody who has trekked in Nepal can't stop talking about it :) It was a great experience and this hotel made it just perfect. I hope to go there often, anytime I feel like I need a good walk. Highly recommended. Important: read up about altitude sickness and do as advised.A comment on the critical reviews:I think people who have trekked and seen the country from up close and those who have been to EBC develop a sense of perspective about Nepal and what can qualify as a luxury. It’s relative. At times I wished they had heated rooms but then you would never feel like getting out and the outdoors is where the magic is. The rooms, beds, bath and toilets, etc. are extremely clean and offer good value for money. The food choice was excellent and it was very tasty and served by very attentive staff. Don’t go there with the expectations of a Swiss boutique hotel. If you don’t enjoy walking outdoors, you will get very bored.

The Hotel Everest View was what we really needed after a day’s trek. Their staff were very welcoming and we were well taken care of. Their service was excellent and the food was all good. We love their large cozy rooms, tidy and clean. The design of the hotel was well-thought of, they really took advantage of their location because every corner has its stunning Himalayan views. Thank you to the hotel personnel who showed and led us to their sun-room early in the morning just in time for sunrise. It has unobstructed views of the giant peaks and the experience was totally overwhelming. Special thank you to Sonia for a smooth transaction, she was and still is very professional.

I heard about HEV 11 years ago, I saw a brochure before there was a website or really any online advertising and had been dreaming of going to this seemingly fairytale hotel at the top of the world. Of course, I wanted to see the rest of Nepal too but this was beyond bucket list material. Going after the 2015 Earthquake made it all the more special. I am not an particularly outdoorsy person and hadn't even thought I would actually trek, I always assumed I would take a helicopter up and back, but friends who currently live in Nepal decided we had to trek as it would really make the experience. I am mentioning this because HEV also arranged our entire trek via their touring arm; Trans Himalayan Tours (THT). They do not have a separate trip advisor site (yet). So, bear with me because I want to review that experience too.  Both the hotel and THT are Nepali owned and operated. (Mr. Miyahara, who built the hotel, is from Japan but he has lived in Nepal, taken Nepali citizenship, and raised his family in Nepal since the 70s. There are some really interesting articles on him if you are so inclined)Getting to LuklaAny trekker or climber to this region will tell you how finicky the weather can be going from Kathmandu to Lukla.  There were no flights out our initial travel day. Sonia, the manager, and her team at THT kept us up to date all day and worked tirelessly with the airline to see what our options were. Since we were not on a tight schedule, like so many of our fellow travelers, we opted to wait a day. Sonia had us wait in comfort in Kathmandu until we for sure had travel arrangements made instead of sitting around the terminal. We opted for a helicopter, which she not only arranged at the last minute but also made sure she had passengers to share the fare with so it ended up being incredibly affordable (and since I had never been on a heli an amazing 1st flight!).  The views were outstanding. And the heli company Air Dynasty took great care of us.GuidesI don't know who these people are who don't use guides or porters but for the price and the really the safety aspect I don't get why you would not. Our guides were phenomenal. They kept our spirits up and kept my rather out of shape self motivated and excited...even when another staircase loomed.  I learned that THT hires its staff year round, so their guides and porters are not laid off during monsoon. That means they have a reliable livelihood and you get dedicated guides who are committed to your positive (and safe) experience. Our primary guide was a 2nd generation THT guide and a lifelong resident of the area. His knowledge of the people we would meet, the things we would see, and the history of the land was incomparable. He also spoke incredible English. Yeah, yeah, yeah you say, but he was educated in the region at the Hilary School not in Kathmandu or an intl school so it was doubly impressive. He told us that HEV and THT ensure their staff, including guides speak a variety of languages and send them to extra courses if needed. I wish my job took that much interest in my ongoing training. Speaking of our guide, even after he had got us back to Lukla and made sure we were checked in at the airport, he came back hours later to check on us when he noticed the flights weren't coming in. He didn't want his to get stranded & have to sleep in the airport as often happens. He was ready to arrange accommodations if we had to stay and worked with Sonia to get us on a helicopter. He even had our luggage carried over and made sure we were literally on the heli before he would leave us.  We were the envy of the airport lemme tell you. No flights went in or out for three days due to weather.Hotel FacilitiesAfter two nights of very cold teahouses, having to buy drinking water, pay extra for a shower, and absolutely arctic toilet seats HEV rooms were divine. We had comfortable beds, loads of warm covers, and hot water bottles already warming the bed while we were in the lounge. I was sad to go home and find no one warmed a water bottle for mt feet.  And those bottles stayed warm all night, mmm toasty toes. I had read comments about the heating being off between 10pm-3am, we were exhausted and weren't awake that late at all so it did not bother us. It was cold all night in the previous teahouses so 5 hours while I slept wasn't a big deal. We were perfectly warm during the day.  The solarium on the roof was hot enough to need to peel off a few layers, ask the staff if you can't find it. Bonus: Roof top observation platform.We also had hot drinking water in our rooms and could call down to have it refilled at any time if needed. Just sitting in the chairs and staring at the most incredible views (every room has the same breathtaking view) from the comfort of our jammies with hot drinks was worth the long walk (uphill) to get there.  Every morning hot water was sent to us to wash up before breakfast. We didn't have hot water in the room, but I know they were working hard to get the solar system set up to enable it.  We used the shower room which was super toasty and had amazing water pressure. Plus, a full power hairdryer!  Hadn't seen one of those in weeks! The hotel was full but with 12 rooms you aren't waiting on loads of people, in fact we only saw the other guests at meal times.  Which brings me to food.Food and DrinkTwo words: Hot Lemon. I have no idea what the Nepali 's are doing with these two humble ingredients but they make the most refreshing warming drink. And at 14,400ft  the fact they have lemons is something of a miracle.  Instant dry throat relief.  In addition to the altitude the air is super dry so you want to avoid caffeine and alcohol. Kinda like being on an airplane, I was always parched (Tip: bring good thick hand/body lotion for your trek).  Our friends, who live in Nepal, enjoyed the beer selection and suffered no ill effects. The food was delicious and plentiful. You definitely won't starve, seconds anyone? The staff is very friendly and their service is top notch, the tables are set just so and each course is served with care. I could not get over the dishes and silverware. It was made in Japan and had the hotel's logo on it and was carried up-NOT by heli-but by a person, piece by piece. Every single item was clearly chosen with care and when you consider how each item got there it is just incredible. My only regret is that I did not think to order the Japanese set menu. The chef is trained in both Japanese and Continental cooking so you can't go wrong either way.  The Nepali food is excellent as well, we had a proper dal bhat our last night, which I could have happily ate every day. StaffMost of the staff come from local Sherpa villages, many speak more than one language, and they tend to have worked for the hotel and THT for an average of 15 years. Between the hotel and the tour arm there are 65 families that are dedicated to providing you with the best possible care, from carrying bags, guiding you through their home villages, cooking for you, taking care of your rooms, and maintaining the hotel.  We learned that the hotel staff lives on site and their child attend local schools. They are often supporting extended family and not having to move to another country  to do so. In a day and age of sustainability, local eating, and responsible traveling it feels good to know where and to who my travel dollars are actually going.  As the 2015 earthquake showed, without tourism, Nepali's livelihoods were in peril. As an aside, the sad reality is that while the Earthquake was 2 years prior its effects on getting supplies and rebuilding are still felt everywhere in Nepal, including at the hotel. In the immediate aftermath the first priority was ensuring the staff and staff's home villages were attended to. Only after vital supplies and medical care were sent did they start repair work on the hotel. As folks in other reviews have pointed out there is still work to be done but quite a lot of it is directly related to the Earthquake.  There are people in Kathmandu who are still waiting on aid from the government (See Bhatrapur), but HEV made sure their staff was taken care of first and foremost. Personally, knowing the  immense challenges the country and specifically the Everest region has faced, made the trip all that much better and also provided me with valuable perspective.And last but not leastThe toilet seat covers! You can think I am crazy but having clean terry cloth covers on all the toilets was probably my favorite thing (I mean besides the view, the staff, the hot lemon drinks, the hot water bottles). Even in my own home, I often face a freezing toilet seat, and can't seem to convince the husband to get electric heated seats. I don't know who invented these these simple porcelain-warming miracles or who thought to use them at HEV but trust me, if you have to leave your toasty water bottle and thick comforter to use the bathroom in the middle of night you will agree with me they are awesome! In sum, I had never trekked and not spent much time in mountains of any sort so I didn't really know what to expect but still found myself amazed at the level of service and amenities available at 14,400ft.  I doubt I will find more hospitable people in any of my travels.  Thank you HEV and THT for the trip of a lifetime.

We visited as a small group while trekking, unfortunately for the hotel it had one of its frequent power cuts on arrival, so we had to wait for normal service.  I feel for what is paid that the hotel is a little dated and could do with a revamp.  The food was nice but not exceptional.  The communal dining room was a little on the cold side, but obviously the view was fantastic, even from the rooms.A little over hyped but overall a good experience.

We came just to have breakfast and to admire the view.The view of the mountains was fantastic. The breakfast was very expensive, the food was nothing special, I had porridge( the portion was very small and it was cold). The coffee had no taste and the service was very bad.

Well we went for the views and we got them.  But expected a bit more comfort inside the hotel, but it was the same temperature inside as outside which means 1 deg during day and -6 deg at night.  they had great doona,s and electric blankets.  but you were still breathing that cold air  not good.  Food was ok service was very good.  don,t be fooled by the fireplaces as they are never used.   staff try so hard to please. ok for overnight stay at right time of year. don,t go if you have any chest infection head cold (etc)  no double glazing

on day 3 of our trek we mastered the climb up from Namche to this hotel.   Amazing view of Everest.   And an excellent outdoor cafe for tea/coffee/lunch.  Can't miss this one while in Namche Bazaar.  Enjoy!!

We walked to the hotel for sunrise views and were well looked after and catered for considering we had come mainly for the views and after some coffee and a light snack.  Staff were very friendly and took photographs of our group in front of the tallest mountain in the world.We didn't see the rooms or look at the cost, but had to rate to have the review accepted.

My wife and I️ enjoyed a two night stay at HEV on our way up the Everest Base Camp Trekking Route.When we first arrived, we were greeted, then invited to take a seat on the outside patio/deck area to rest from the hike up from Namche. We were then given welcome drinks as well as the WiFi codes set up on our iPhones. After a few photos were taken of the amazing views from the hotel, the chef, manager, as well as some of the employees introduced themselves to my wife and I which was a nice warm welcome.We were then taken to our room by one of the employees. He explained the features in our room to us, like how to work the hot shower, the heater, the thermos of boiling drinking water provided, and the electric blanket on the bed. If ever we had a problem, the HEV employees were prompt about helping us with it.We decided on ala carte menu during our stay, so whenever we got hungry, we would order food and either eat in the dining room or they brought food to our room. The dining room would turn on a fire place at 5pm every night, so many guests gather around and enjoy the warmth from the fire.What my wife enjoyed most was the hot shower, the electric blanket on the bed, and of course the million dollar views of the mountains.I️ spent a whole year planning this trek and stay at HEV with Sonia. She helped arrange the whole customized trek I️ asked for, so I️ was comfortable with the pace and the ability for my wife and I️ to acclimate properly all the way to Base Camp. I️ was provided a awesome guide Sanjay, who proved to be the main reason my wife and I️ were able to make it all the way up. Everything went smooth as planned from the flights to and from Lukla, the trek, the stay at the hotel, to helicopter back down from Gorakshep.Hotel Everest View proved to be an oasis in the middle of our trek. A little luxury before the cold days ahead in high elevation, where hot showers aren’t available, where sleeping bags are a must, and my wife and I️ would look back and wish we were still at HEV. That short stay definitely played a part in us being able to make it to our goal of Base Camp. I️ would highly recommend not to just have an acclimation day here, but stay here, watch the sunrise and set over Everest, Nuptse, Ama Dablam, etc. Enjoy a little luxury on your way to the top of the world.

We were sitting there to give order of medium pot of coffee. Nobody came to took order. After a while we ask to take our order then they reply there kitchen is very busy so it will take a while. Then we just walked away.

When we booked this hotel, we had high expectation that this will be the great hotel in the whole trip, especially with the amount of money the hotel charged me. The hotel does have a great view of Mt. Everest and Ama Dablam. With only 12 rooms available, we booked 10 rooms in this hotel. All the pictures and reviews in Tripadvisor looks great. Until we checked in and find out that there is NO heater in the room. They found all the excuses about electricity instablility etc so that they cannot turn on the heater. Instead, we were given a small portable heater that cannot even warm the room at all. Next was the shower... there was absolutely NO warm/hot shower in the room. The water is freezing cold. They provided a bathtub in the bathroom, but who is going to use it if the water is freezing cold? Instead they gave the option of using a PUBLIC hot shower in the lobby. The staff and the manager was so untrained to handle this situation. How could a hotel that charges so expensively (500% of the best hotel in Namchee charged us, as comaparison) fail to have a heater and a warm/hot shower inside the room. That i cannot understand and refuse to understand. If they charged a regular price like all hotels in Namchee, i would not make any fuss and make this report. But the fact that they charged us heavily and we get nothing in return, left a sour feeling in our mind. And food, yes they over charged us heavily as well (250-300% in fact for the food charges). We have no choices but to eat from the hotel as there are no other reataurant near by. The closest one is 30-40 minutes away. In short, never stay in this hotel. You will NOT get your money worth for both the service and the amenities of the hotel. Go to Khumjung village which is 30 minutes away from this hotel. There are plenty of good and affordable hotels and restaurants there.

We trekked up and stayed for two nights. It was truly amazing and unforgettable when I saw Everest, Nuptse, Lhotse, Ama Dablam when waking up in the early morning. I could see the mountains from room window, the court yard and also the little platform above the cafe.The staff are very friendly and polite. The room is very spacious. Unfortunately the shower in our room did not work properly (water not hot enough), we had to use the shower near front desk. A bit inconvenient but it was not far, so not a big problem.The hotel is very quiet. Because of the location and view (not only the mountains but you can also see wild animals), it really made me feel far away from everyday life and appreciate the opportunity of being there.

Very nice stop for breakfast after an EBC helicopter landing. The hotel has good facilities considering the location. Breakfast pretty good considering the location. Nothing great culinarily speaking. The view is so worth it. Service is OK. Price is fair.

I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights arriving and departing by helicopter from Lukla. Upon arrival i was greeted by the manager who helped me to the hotel with my bags. The staff are extremely helpful and friendly as i have experienced all across Nepal.First impressions of the hotel and its location are mindblowing. You are surrounded on all sides by snow capped mountains and tremendous views. The hotel is actually a lot larger than expected and reminds me of a supervillains lair from an old James Bond movie ( which is cool). The hotel is Japanese owned and as you may expect very well run. The design is classic 60s which again adds to the coolness of the place. The rooms are spacious and offer breathtaking views of Everest and the valley. I was also fortunate to have a terrace. The room included a heater which you will definately need at night, a single and double bed , electric blankets and a flask of hot water to help you stay hydrated ( very important at altitude) and warm slippers. The bathroom includes a japanese style bath/shower with hot water but the pressure is low.My stay included breakfast , lunch and dinner which were superb. 3 course lunch and dinner and a modest breakfast in the dining room which offers pnoramic views of Everest and its cohorts.During my stay the staff ( Jack kindly guided me on a hike to Khumjung ( very close by) and Namche Bizaar which is a 5km round trip ( not far you say) but is a 442m descent and on the return,climb. My guide was very knowledgeable of the area and thankfully very patient as i wheezed my way back up the mountain. The altitude is such that tying your shoelaces leaves you out of breath.In conclusion a stay at this hotel is something you will remember for the rest of your life. I strongly recommend it if you have the chance. The views, food  and staff were excellent and also a special mention to the Sonia and her team who handled the booking and travel arrangements for me and was responsive and attentive to my queries throughout the process.

Arrived by hotel arranged flight and helicopter KTM/Lukla from  for a 2 night stay. Everything was perfectly coordinated and staff couldn’t have been more kind. Hotel sent a guide with us for hikes to the various nearby towns (this was a life saver). The views are not to be missed and the meals were all very good. The only downside is the lack of good hot water- the shower has a gas powered instant water heater... but considering where and how isolated we were, this isn’t bad at all. Overall, an excellent stay with amazing staff. Keep up the good work!

During my Everest Base Camp Trek, I made a rest stop at the Hotel Everest View for a snack at the hotel’s outdoor dining patio.  The hotel definitely lives up to its name with a view of Mt. Everest.  The service was prompt and the staff was friendly.  There is also a small gift shop next to reception desk.  This was the nicest hotel/accommodation that I had visited between Lukla and Everest Base Camp.  I definitely recommend a visit to the Hotel Everest View.

Most people go there for an acclimatization walk from Namche Bazaar and it's worth it. If the weather is good you have a great view on Mt.Everest and the way there is not too bad and helps your body to get used to the hight. Some wealthy people come up here via helicopter. They have a nice terrace crowded by people to come and have the view on Mt. Everest.

I was so fortunate to have Sonia set a visit to her hotel last month as my 60th birthday present to myself.   She is not only extremely knowledgable about the area and hotel but extremely competent.  My relatively complex visit came off without a hitch barring the snow on the last day and fear the helicopters couldn't come get us.   On arrival in Lukla, her staff took good care of me and the following day came and got me for my helicopter flight to the hotel.  I was sad I couldn't trek but happy this alternative is offered so I could get there.  The hotel employees were so nice and I felt very pampered.  I am sure I got the very best room (okay maybe not but it felt like it was to me).   It was gorgeous and so nicely laid out.   I did the package which included meals and the dining room staff also made me feel so special.  I loved that they had a big fire going to meet and chat with other people before and after dinner.   They were very attentive and the food was yummy!   While it was cold in the room, there was a little heater and when bundled up, I was snuggly and warm and slept well.  I took a hike to Khumjung with one of the staff who was quite the photographer and also adapted my walk to help with my knee which was hurting.   He was very kind.   While the view was obscured by clouds the day I arrived, the following morning Everest came out in all its glory and was stunning.  And the second night we had a big snowfall which made things even more beautiful.   Once my helicopter arrived and I got to Lukla, Sonia's team was right there to get me on one of the first flights out of Lukla that day and it was over.   But I will never forget this experience and being so well taken care of.   It was an amazing 60th birthday.

This trip we stayed in Namche Bazaar but just could not go on without a visit to Everest View and what a view it was. Well worth the 2 hour hike up to have a delightful, snack but an even better range of snow capped mountains sprawling our in front of us. Recommended highly!

Really nice and comfortable luxury hotel at altitude of 3880 mtrs.A nice change after trying trek and cold weather. Rooms are good and comfortable, food is very good, service is excellent. The hot water bottle provided in bed was amazingly hot and comfortable for the whole night. The only drawback is hot shower is in common area , which is not expected in such a hotel.The view from this hotel as the name suggest is  is undoubtedly remarkable , you can see all the complete range ( Evrest , Aba dablam , lohatsue, and more )provided the weather is clear and good .

Make sure you get up when the sky is clear, the view is stunning. Amadablam, Everest, Lhotse - all the beauties in the same view. Have a cup of tea and a cheese omelette, enjoy the moment away from home.

The setting and view are stunning - 360 views of the Khumbu Valley (don't miss the sun room and roof patio). Staff are helpful and efficient, the restaurant is quite good, especially the Japanese set meal. Nice warm fire in the large, central fireplace in the dining room, around which guests gather before dinner. The room was spacious with a nice sitting area, and room-service tea arrived within minutes.But - the fireplace is the only place in the hotel to get warm. When we arrived the manager made a point of saying they'd turn the heat on from 10 pm to 3 am (thought it would be better from 7-10 pm, so one could get into bed warm) but I woke up both nights (altitude will do that) and the radiator was as frigid at 1 am and 3 am as during the mornings and evenings. It didn't seem to be due to lack of fuel, as the hallway smelled strongly of kerosene both afternoons.After 3 days of trekking and staying in basic lodges, we were looking forward to a stay in a high-end place with a nice hot shower. But the bath had only a tiny, under-powered flash heater, and a cheap, ancient shower head. We took quick showers, but it was uncomfortable to say the least. Lodges along the entire valley have effective solar water heaters - we finally had a comfortable shower the day after HEV at a simple lodge.In sum, this is a spectacular property in one of the best locations in the world, but physically the hotel is tired, outdated, and not what I expected for a top-end place. With a bit of investment and care, it could be a truly special place to match the truly special location.

I have never and will probably never again stay in a hotel that will steal my heart like HEV has!The views are out of this world and it's impossible to get used to the amazing surrounding beauty.The staff is so accommodating and so lovely. Nepalese people have a reputation for being very friendly and welcoming and you'll understand why after staying here.The food is also delicious which I really didn't expect at 3880m high! Strangely enough, you can have some amazing Japanese food while looking out on Mt Everest. My friends and I trekked for 3 days from Lukla to reach the hotel and I would highly recommend doing this as it's a great way to see the area but you also get an amazing feeling of achievement once you finally see the hotel.The rooms were beautifully laid out and the electric blanket ensured that we all had a good night sleep. After sleeping in freezing and very basic lodges, HEV felt like pure luxury and that's because it is!In one word, GO!! Go to Nepal, Go to HEV and have a once in a lifetime experience that you will never forget!

The Hotel Everest View must be the hotel with the most amazing and awesome view in the world. On a clear day the views of the Everest and Lhotse are just priceless. Located at nearly 4000 meter above sea level the hotel is mostly visited by well-off, fortunate tourists who can afford to rent a helicopter for a few hours. Sure, the hotel is not luxurious and is hardly heated. And yes, the food is not overly good ... but the view makes up for everything!!!!

Sonia, was a wonderful and very helpful manager. She not only arranged our entire Nepal trip, she was extremely detailed and helpful in answering my questions about helicopter and altitude sickness paranoid questions. Apparently, the hotel now has a travel agency in Kathmandu and can plan your entire trip to Nepal with other destinations like the safari. We booked a flight to Hotel Everest and a short flight to the Basecamp. Staying two nights at the hotel as we have lack of acclimatization. They provide oxygen and we are taking medication two days before and after. Overall I am very impressed with the customer service and the kindness of the people especially Sonia. Some other reviews talk about lacking heat or other amenities. It's all a matter of expectations and if you read Trip Advisor Reviews how does one expect something else? The beauty of the place and being at 13K feet is enough to make up for anything else.

This hotel is one of its kind & has stunning views of the mighty Mount Everest!!! :) The full 5 points are purely for the view. Although, the hotel is well-made and well-maintained even at such a high altitude with amazing service & food but the stunning views over-shadows everything about it.Its a humbling experience to see the mighty Mount Everest and nature all around. Places like these make me feel..."What a tiny place I acquire in the Universe"!!!!!!! :)We took a helicopter ride from Kathmandu to Everest view hotel and while the helicopter was climbing up higher altitudes, I was restless, breathless at a point, and speechless all through the journey and when I landed at the Helipad of this hotel, I was stunned. :)A golf-course, greenery at such a high altitude (we visited in June),  giant snow capped peaks all around, a lovely seating space where one can just keep gazing at the Mount Everest while sipping a hot cuppa like we did. We ordered club sandwiches and butter toasts & tea! And believe me you, the bes-test butter toasts I have ever had in my whole life. Such a simple thing like a butter toast but it tasted better than any I have ever had...super thick bread & lots of melted butter!I didn't stay here so can't comment on the rooms but am sure looking at the hotel, that rooms must be well-maintained too! :)Once in a lifetime opportunity this was and I am so thankful, I got to experience this! :)

I passed along a field resembling a golf course green and approached the Japanese-owned Everest View Hotel. Part James Bond baddy lair, and part paradise, this hotel is state of the art. In 2004, the Guinness Book of World Records listed it as the Highest Placed Hotel in the world. The blurb online says, "With a view of Mt. Everest from every room, visitors can immerse in this mesmerizing scene in luxury." That is impressive. I had a milky tea and steak sandwich, taking in the view. It truly is an astonishing location with superior unmatchable panoramic views of the region.

We stayed a night here and thought that the hotel was stunning in terms of location and design. The rooms are spacious and comfortable with private bathrooms with deep Japanese baths. Unfortunately the water pipes were frozen so we had to rely on water being bought in buckets to our room. Water bottles are put in the beds at night.The main  heating system was not on so we had two small heaters in our room. Most of the hotel was very cold including the dining room where we had dinner. The food was pretty good - quite a varied menu with some western dishes and local food.There is a sunroom and viewing deck up top and we had breakfast in the sunroom  which was nice and warm and looked out over Mt Everest. It was a pretty stunning experience.The staff are very helpful - I think that in season this would be an amazing place to stay at and I was glad we had a night here despite the cold.

The view from here is unparalleled. One could watch the Everest on sunrise, sunset and all thru the day. Sonia is great in communicating and very accommodating - incredibly helpful in our trek. The hotel staff are very warm and welcoming too in making us feel comfortable. I'd happily stay here again and strongly recommend to my friends too.

Meant to stay here during our trip to the Khumbu region but it didn't work out in the end. However the manager was extremely helpful, informative and flexible throughout our entire correspondence. We did end up going up from Namche for a day hike and it is an excellent day trek for great views of Everest and its neighbours while you take a cup of tea or lunch. It can be combined with trips to Khumjung and Khumde before returning to Namche (or staying in one of these villages or the hotel if you want to).

So this hotel is all about the view. It is stunning and you can sit and just star at it for hours as the light changes constantly across the mountians.  The room we had was very large with two queen beds and a sitting area. It has a shower with hot water on demand that was very nice. It also had a space heater to sit by during the day. at night, the staff tucks a hot water bottle at your feet in the bed. Wonderful. The only slight negative is that this hotel is really cold. Everyone is wearing down coats all the time. Even the waiters are wearing them. Wood is hard to get so they don't burn fires all the time. The staff is very attentive and when asked, they will light the fireplace. The staff is wonderful and always looking to make your experience better. The food is very good and meals are a multi course set dinner.  Sonia is delightful to work with and her English is perfect. She organized a trek for us that was exactly what we wanted and her choice of guide and porter was a perfect fit. The tea houses we stayed in on the way up where top level. I would definitely stay here again but dress warmly and bring pajamas!

I must admit, I was a bit nervous about arranging an entire trip to Nepal through the hotel but it could not have gone better.  We were picked up in Kathmandu and taken to our hotel for an overnight stay before departing for Lukla the next morning.  The flight to Lukla was smooth and the helicopter transfer up to the hotel provided us with our first view of Mt. Everest.  The hotel is situated in an amazing spot, surrounded by snow-capped mountains and the views from around the property will leave you breathless.  A trek was arranged for us the following day to visit local villages and climb to Rhund Peak at 4200 meters.  The rooms are spacious and comfortable, the food is delicious and plentiful and the staff is there to make sure you stay is top notch.  We were sad to say goodbye after only two nights but the unobstructed view of Everest on our last morning was the perfect send off.  Thank you Sonia, for being such an amazing host and travel agent.  This was a trip we will never forget.

The hotel has an amazing terrace with uninterrupted views over the Everest Summit and Himalayas. Usually hikers stop by to have a drink at the terrace and then continue their journey. I preferred to spend a night at the hotel to enjoy the view properly. You can see Everest from your bed and the view is amazing at night with full moon or in sunrise when the snow caps looking like in fire. I used one of the two rooms that have hot water. The room was very spacious, comfortable and clean but it gets really cold at night and you can't stay up in the room, you have to go in your bed and sleep. The bed is very warm thanks to the hot water bottles. You also have a private terrace looking at Everest. Food was included in the price. Every meal was very delicious and service was excellent. The restaurant has wide windows looking at the Himalayas and Everest.I wasn't very fit for climbing up to the hotel and I didn't have enough time to hike up and down. So I flew from Lukla to the hotel by helicopter. The hotel provides the helicopter charter for $700 one way (so $1400 return). I thought it was super expensive for only a five minute ride and I had to book it just because I didn't have another option. But it turned out to be one of the best five minutes of my life! Even if you are fit enough and have time to climb up, I would recommend you to do the helicopter ride just for the flight experience itself (if you have extra budget to spare of course). I was worried about high altitude sickness when I flew to the hotel directly but I didn't have any problem. As a measure, I had spent one night in Lukla before flying to the hotel and I had started taking Diamox two days before arrival.After I spent one night in the hotel, I started my hike down back to Lukla the next day. I did the hike in two days (first day from the hotel to Monjo, the second day from Monjo to Lukla). The hotel provided me a guide and hiking pole. My guide was Ang Nima and he was an excellent guide, very kind and thoughtful. I definitely recommend him. Normally, Ang Nima arranges the accommodation (tea houses) himself but if you prefer specific more comfortable lodges you can ask the hotel to pre-book them for you. Tea houses are super cheap (around 200 rupees per night I think) but also super basic, I don't think the bed linen was clean in one of the tea houses where I stayed, for example. Sonia who is the manager of Hotel Everest View is very helpful and if you need anything or have any problem, don't hesitate to contact her, she promptly answers your email and makes sure everything is alright.All in all, I'm glad I stayed in this hotel for once in a lifetime experience.

We stayed for 2 nights at the Hotel Everest View. After a long days of trekking, having some rest here is a very good decision.the hotel is very clean, the staff is friendly, the view of Everest, Ama Dablam was truly grand. the scenery and panorama is to die for.mealtime is my favorite ! while waiting for our meal, we sit next to the wood fire and talk to other guests and enjoying the panorama from the window and by the way,  the food was great.our room is comfortable and our balcony was very spacious.and other surprise is... after we finished dinner and go back to our room, the staff already put a hot water bottle in our bed so we can have a warm good night sleep.hopefully i can come back, but maybe with the direct helicopter to the hotel :)

I didn't actually stay overnight at the hotel. Along with four friends we hiked to the hotel from Namche Bazaar as part of a 'rest day'/acclimatization-day, three-days into the standard Everest base camp trek, starting at Lukla, Khumbu. For safety it's mandatory to spend an extra night in Namche Bazaar and to hike to the SoloKhumbu ~~ and the Hotel Everest  View is a wonderful place to stop for a snack, or lunch, or just drinks. The views are incredible so long as the clouds have lifted. The patio is a great place to take a drink but unless you are well covered up the UV sunshine will burn in just 30 minutes.Drinks and snacks all sound and look better on the menu than they are once delivered; but then that is par for the course in the Khumbu since everything has to be man-carried from Lukla. There is no competition for the hotel Everest View. It is sufficiently out-of-the-way and exotically placed that almost whatever was on sale will be something that you would want to buy! Even though cold drinks, simple snacks and comfortable chairs are all provided at New York prices ... The view from the patio or the inside sitting area simply cannot be beaten and will stay with you forever. For all the shortcomings attendant upon what must be the highest hotel in the world this edifice is sufficiently unique that you're guaranteed to leave the place smiling and grateful that it is parked in the most surprising and perhaps even desolate location imaginable.

My short Khumbu trek a fortnight ago concluded with a two-night stay at the Hotel Everest View. It was the perfect setting and exceeded all expectations. The view of Everest and the nearby Himalayan giants (particularly Lhotse and Ama Dablam) was truly grand, and it was beautiful to see the surrounding landscape transform as the light shifted and the snow came and went. The hotel itself was also a pleasant experience. My room was spacious and comfortable; I especially liked the warm, poofy double-quilts and the hot water bottle that the staff tucked into my bed every night! Mealtimes in the dining room were a treat, being seated next to a wood fire and enjoying a surprisingly wide range of cuisine (my favourite was the Japanese dinner the final night). The staff were very warm and attentive and made me feel welcome from the moment I arrived. My only suggestions for improvement are to (a) supply running hot water to every room (currently, some rooms do not have this, and you can either request that the staff bring hot water to the room or use the shower adjacent to the lobby), and (b) install TVs for relaxation after dinner (currently there are none in the rooms).  Last but not least, I have to say I was so pleased with the way Sonia at Hotel Everest View helped to organise my whole itinerary - flights between Kathmandu and Lukla, a guide, trekking permits, accommodation en route to the hotel, and a helicopter shuttle directly from the hotel back down to Lukla on the morning of my return to Kathmandu. It helped a lot to have everything taken care of and brought together seamlessly. The guide, a young chap named Sanjay, was very good-natured and pleasant company. The heli-shuttle was a nice touch, avoiding the need to double-back on ground already walked and so allowing more time to explore the region around the hotel. Thanks very much to all at Hotel Everest view for a memorable experience… I hope to return with friends in the not-too-distant future!

Listed on the Guinness Book of World Records in 2004 as the Highest Placed Hotel in the world (3880m), Hotel Everest View, turns into a landmark in the Himalayas by its own right. With great service, delicious food and out of this world view of peaks like Everest, Sagarmatha, Taboche, peak48, Thamserku and Kongderi mountains, just to mention some of them, turns into a whole new experience for the traveler that always is looking for something more.The access to the hotel is by Trekking (2 days) or Helicopter (5 minutes) from Lukla Airport, which its an adventure by itself. I spent one night at Lukla village for acclimatization and took the helicopter next morning, great ride, takes the whole trip into a VIP level experience.The view from the rooms is outstanding, good size, comfortable beds, and good heaters. The staff is always with a smile and ready to help to any request, which adds value to the experience. I spent my birthday in the hotel and it was a great surprise to received a complementary birthday cake after dinner.One of the best hotels I have stayed, considering service and location.

We stopped here at part of our helicopter tour and ate breakfast. The views are stunning from every room (including the bathroom). I was able to peak in one room, they had floor to ceiling windows so you are not limited on the view. I hope we can come back to stay the night.

Certainly the best stay in this hotel during my EBC Trek. Really glad i made the choice to stay here and check it out. The views here are out of the world. This hotel is a must go if you want to really see magnificent views of the mountains while in comfort. They had a sundeck where i had my lunch overlooking Everest,Lhotse and the surrounding mountains and even a lovely place  with a view to have breakfast or tea time. Their service was also excellent. They always was there to help me out with anything i needed and all their meals which is inclusive of bkfs, lunch and dinner were really good and up to standards. I was more than impressed with their service, room comfort and tasty food at such a high altitude. The staff always smiled and got back to my requests very promptly every time. They were very polite and helpful all the time and The rooms were amazing too, very spacious and had good heating. A real hotel it was up in the mountains. The views were really magnificent. Imagine getting up to an outstanding view of the mountains just in front of you. I practically almost didn't leave my room because the view was just stunning. My stay here was perfect. I would say this was my best hotel stay ever due to its stunning views and lovely hospitality.Thanks to all the staff in Everst View Hotel for everything. Everything was just more than impressive here. Will come back again!!

I am so happy and proud to see and stay at the Hotel Everest View (3880m) and which was listed on the Guinness Book of World Records (2004) as the Highest Placed Hotel in the world at 13000ft with good (food, accommodation and hospitality) .The hotel offers a 360 degree view of the snow caped peaks like Mount Everest, Ama Dablam and many more.

Well worth the hike up from Namche. Unbelievable views of Mt Everest. The cafe is a little expensive but with it being so remote, its kind of expected. An incredible hotel to look through too, they did a great job building it.

I trekked to the Everest Base Camp in October 2015. During the 2 days acclimatization in Namche, we hiked to HEV for brunch, and to check out the view. We did not stay at HEV. Of all the lodges and hotels I passed along the way from Lukla to EBC, I think this is the best acommodation in the area. The food and service is good. The view is breathtaking. There are better views, but you will have to hike/trek higher from HEV. I would like to stay there one day.

Just spent 3 nights at The Everest View after trekking up from Lukla. This was to be our reward.The hotel sits atop a ridge at just under 4000 meters. You can hike up to it from the Khumjung ( approx 30min steepish. climb - for the average fitness ) or hike up from Namche - a steeper climb used for acclimatisation or you can jump a helicopter and fly up. The hotel is perfectly situated with on a clear day...views of many of the major peaks including Everest. We were lucky and had great early morning views but soon after the mists rolled in and you could not see a thing, so luck does play a part if you are coming only for the view.The services at the hotel were a bit disappointing - there was no electricity apart from about 2hrs in the afternoon. Consequently no heating in the hotel, no hot water etc. they did light the fire in the dining room after 5pm and after being asked to but at times I found myself sitting in down jacket, thermals and Beannie with my head light on. Each night we were given a warming pan for the bed ( surprisingly effective  - never cold at night ) Not really what I expected at over $300 per night. Use your generator guys that's what it is there for!! ( I have since hear,d that electricity is restored for peak trekking season).Having said that it is a magnificent experience and you should definitely go there. The rooms are comfortable and all face the mountains.The food was delicious and the service apart from electrical related was very good. I feel rather petty making comments such as this but in the interests of honesty I have told it like it was. It is the experience of a life time and a privledge to be sitting in front of the amazingly beautiful Nepalese Himalayas.The day trip down to the Khumjung was one of the best experiences.

It is nice hike to Everest View from Namche bazzar in the morning. It is really good idea to climb to Hotel Everest view in acclimatization day. Take a breakfast and enjoy the Mt. Everest great view with other peaks is outstanding ! This hotel is superb !

A very well-run company by people who are genuinely passionate about what they do and it shows... from their warm greetings, to ensuring that your stay is as comfortable as possible, making this trip an unforgettable one! The staff made us feel so welcome as if we're their extended families in this foreign country. A trip of a lifetime - will definitely return!

We had trekked for many days to Ama Dablam Base Camp and then back towards Namche Bazar. How utterly delightful to then spend two days at Everest View Hotel. We all loved the little luxuries after camping. Sheets on the bed, lights in the room, delicious meals, and the view! It was however still extremely cold and we looked forward to the little warmth from the log fire each evening. All in all a wonderful experience. Well worth the tricky, half hour walk uphill to get there.

As part of an altitude acclimatization day (Trek EBC), we completed a difficult hike starting from Namche to reach the Everest View hotel. The start of the hike is particularly difficult, very steep and stony. After 2.5 km of walking and 410m of ascent we reach the hotel and its beautiful terrace facing Ama Dablam on one side, Tabuche on the other, Nuptse, Lhotse and Everest further on. . Unfortunately that day Everest and Lhotse remained hidden in the clouds but the panorama offered was nevertheless grandiose. The place is a must, a lot of people occupy the terrace. However, the service is fast. We take the time to contemplate anyway.

Sensational location, rustic furnishings, stylish, everything is there, luxury at 3880 meters, food, service, everything is perfect, if possible you should stay 2-3 days and enjoy the whole thing! It is unique. You also have to see the history of the hotel and look at the whole thing, every bottle of beer has to be carried up the mountain by helicopter or donkey or yak
An impeccable welcome! Rooms in style and attentive staff.Mount Everest presents itself to you in all its majesty!You will not regret every piece of your money.Do not hesitate !

I posted a review late and the date I visited was not an option, so I listed it as 2022, but I actually visited in 2017. For me, it was the best hotel. First of all, the view was great. And the food was delicious. There was a warm shower and room, and the staff were all hospitable, kind, and comfortable. My visit here is a memory I will cherish forever, and I often talk about it with the friends I went with. It was hard to climb up to this hotel, but it was a quick helicopter ride back. It takes quite a while to get to this hotel, so it's not easy to get there, but I would like to go again.

Very nice view, it felt good to warm up on the electric blanket! If the bathroom was heated it would be perfect We stayed there on the way there and back, the breakfast was good and the staff very friendly
