It is a short hotel ferry ride across the water to the hotel. As a result the quiet and peaceful atmosphere exists here. Staff were very friendly and efficient with delivering luggage, to serving meals and providing laundry services to our 10 days of dirty trekking clothes. The views in the morning of Machapuchre and other mountains are unsurpassed. Will return on our next trip here.

Each time we returned to Fish Tail from the hustle and bustle of Pokhara, we joked that it was time to return to our "bubble".  And the quiet serenity of Fish Tail is truly a bubble of reality from the rest of our stay in Nepal.  We were with our three kids and their grandparents so there was an ease to this resort that was worth the extra cash.  My kids could run around with a soccer ball and swim in the pool.  Best sleep in Nepal.  The resort has great views of the peaks - no way you could get that from the lakeside resorts.  The hotel staff knew us all by name and crossing the "moat", especially by moon light, was magical.  This is a true gem.

I read lot of reviews about Fishtail lodge and saw their pictures before I made my booking. What I loved about :It was very interesting and unique way to go to the resort. Whole landscape of the resort was beautifully done. Rooms have old heritage feel which I liked. Staff was friendly and service was excellent. Very cozy feeling. They had a nice swimming pool (which we haven't tried though). Resort offers great view of Fewa lake and Fishtail mountain.Al-carte food was very food, we also tried cakes.Areas which require lot of improvements :Bathroom toiletries were not sufficiently provided, no shower gel (though this is small thing but I would expect such thing from star hotels). They did not top-up toiletries until asked for. Napkins and towels were very old and some of them have holes. Which pissed me off completely. Breakfast spread was not great and 70% of the menu was repeated everyday. We stayed there for 4 nights and after 2 days I was bored of breakfast due to lack of options. Fishtail only provide free wifi to dinning area, if you want wifi in room it will be paid.

Fish Tail Lodge has been the best hotel in the center of Pokhara for quite a long time.  The location is great and the way to the hotel by the boat is quite unique and interesting.  It's just a several minutes walk to the main shopping road beside the lake. We had the palm court room on the 2nd floor which has a nice view of the garden.  The room is a little bit dated and quite normal considering the price, but the view from our balcony is great.  It's better to look outside rather sitting inside the room.We had our dinner in the hotel's restaurant which offers a set menu.  The set menu will make you rather full with starter, soup, main dish and dessert.  The taste is quite good but it's not traditional Nepal food.  It should be a mix of Chinese and Nepal food.This is a good place which worth a visit and stay.

This hotel is the most beautifully located hotel in the middle of fewa lake and overlooking the lake and the machha-puchha peak surrounded by north and south Annapurna peaksThe quaint lake makes your mind relax and wonder about the beauty of the place The staff is extremely cooperative They have these two heritage rooms with a view  of the lake Though the rooms are small , they are worth every penny as you are looking at all the beauty pokhara has to offerThe restaurants are nice and offer wide menBut more important ant are the people who Run this hotel , extremely helpful and cooperative I love this hotel

A short ride on a raft, pulled across the water with a rope, brings you to the lush green grounds of the Fish Tail Lodge.  It has a secluded feeling, even though the town is close by, which made it easy to walk to shops and restaurants.  Rooms are a bit dated but with lots of character.  Most are in attached bungalows, maybe ten to a building.  Need to keep the curtains drawn for privacy, making the room quite dark.  Don't know if queen-size beds are available, but we were given twin beds.  Good service, decent buffet breakfast included.  Free wifi only available in the dining hall.  Not a fan of the big wooden fish attached to our hotel key - can't carry it in your pocket.

Try to book room no 17 and enjoy the excellent view of the greenish blue Lake nestling bright reflection of snow peaks like Fishtail and Annapurna 3!  This is a unique hotel for relaxation, building relationships with humans and nature amidst an island with forest surroundings. The rope ferry to reach the hotel is very special. Cottages and rooms are well appointed with a mention of the international dignitaries who had stayed there. The hammock by the lake or the swimming pool in the garden offer a lot to the visitors. Lots of exotic plants and lawns sooth the eyes and calm the mind. Food is enjoyable. The staff are warm, hospitable and efficient. The hotel is equally comfortable in sunshine as well as in rain which are so characteristic of Pokhara valley.

My boyfriend surprised me with this stay. And it really was romantic. Passing the lake by pontoon was kind of special. Staff is friendly. Rooms are big and clean. Bathrooms are a bit smaller but clean and really hot showers. The views on a clear day can be fantastic. Breakfast was a bit expensive ($20 for 2 persons) but good. The only thing is the wifi. It's not free in the rooms and in 2017 it should be. I would love to come back and enjoy a little bit more.

this hotel has legend that a lot of famous people visited, -  probably it had an excellent management at old times.- current management is bad.they did not renovate for the last 40 years !!.the food i lousy, the service is bad and when u complain they look at u as if u were fallen from the sky.they always try to take u for a ride for small stuff such as charging u for stuff when u were not there..don't use the SPA as it has unqualified massage therapistif u have any other choice (unfortunately there not that many) - just go visit as it has nice view of the lake and mountain,  but don't stay there..

Reached by short ferry trip and on the lake, it looked like a really promising spot to withdraw from urban buste of Pokhara. Comfortable well equipped Rooms located in bungalow style lodges holding about 8, and very friendly and attentive staff, but buffet style restaurant mediocre and serving large parties of Chinese tourists, who appeared to have not eaten for days was disappointing. Offered a welcome break, but keen to move on after 2 days.

This is a magnificent place to stay or just to visit for a meal or snack. The setting overlooking Fewa Lake is hard to beat. You can paddle your own boat to this historic lodge, or take the hotel's own boat. These days it is seriously underutilized, as are most hotels and shops in Pokhara. So, it's a good time to get a better price than ever before.

We arrived there with a kind of canoe, the hotel is ok, the view and location stunning. As said, bit weird, the rooms, the restaurant, the pool.... strange feeling i did not feel comfortable. The food was also ok but something was missing. I thing this place had better time....

Fishtail does not even bask in the shadow of the Fisthtail peak but nevertheless it is perhaps the neatest and the cleanest place in Pokhara. We loved it. The staff are fussy and the management is greedy, but the place is an island of peace and calm. There isn't much in Pokhara apart from the sites, the Tibetan shopping and the adventure sports but Fishtail Lodge is a place where you would want to stay and stay. They are efficient and expensive but if you really don't care about money then they are your first choice, always, and no doubt.

I came here to stay for four days, and I am glad to share about my experience at this lodge as the rooms are very clean and well decorated with immense of support and take care of by the management of this lodge. as we have to reach this lodge through a boat that lies between the fewa lake is also a amazing view.

We were booked into this place by our travel agency and it shows they are good at what they do.  Fish Tail Lodge is accessed only by a 24 hour operated raft.  The operator pulls on a rope whilst coiling it on the deck in a lovely rhythmic display.  The staff are great, concerned with your comfort and happiness.  The restaurant overlooks the lake and if its sunny, you get amazing views of the Annapurna range, including Fish Tail mountain.  Talk a walk around and enjoy the beautifully kept gardens (they even have a vegetable garden) and listen to the birds.  Would definitely go back again.

Luckily we had 3 nights in this beautiful hotel, setting stunning, amazing views from the dining room. Rooms excellent with powerful shower and nice toiletries. Good hairdryer. Beds are hard, not sure if the hotel provide mattress toppers. Breakfast buffet was very good and likewise the evening buffet. Very convenient to the town centre with excellent shops. Very good spa. Luxurious pool area.

On the recommendation of a friend, we stayed at Fish Tail Lodge on our recent trip to Nepal.  We remain ever grateful to this friend for insisting on this place, even though our Tour Operator said that this place was a little run-down and there were better hotels in Pokhara.We were pleasantly surprised to see a book at the reception '1,000 places to see before you die'.  Fish Tail Lodge is listed in this book.  This should be reason enough for anyone to stay here.The experience of accessing the hotel in a hand-drawn barge, to begin with, gives this place an exclusive feel.  Rooms are well-appointed and the service is excellent.  Breakfast spread is huge.  Just outside of the restaurant is sprawling lawns overlooking the Fewa Lake, where one could sit for a quiet and romantic meal or breakfast.The Fish Tail peak is visible from the hotel and photographing the peak, along with its reflection in the Fewa Lake should not be missed for the more serious photographers.  We also tried some trick photographs with a reflective table and got some amazing results.  Hint: wait for passing boats and include in your frame.You can take a (row) boat ride from the hotel to a nearby Temple.  The round trip will take about an hour.

I loved my stay here. From crossing the river to the island with the attentive staff to exploring the beautiful grounds. The service was very attentive and flexible - from enjoying a drink in nature to the quality of the meals - especially an exquisite lunch outside looking at beautiful Annapurna in the distance.

Amazing, bang in the middle of a lake. Quirky ferry gets you to the ‘mainland’! Our room was of the highest standard, with a balcony overlooking the well kept gardens. Nice swimming pool. Busy high street, restaurants and shopping area nearby. Strong WiFi in the room. Excellent hotel restaurant but also try the Lake View restaurant in the high street- about 20 minutes walk from the hotel ferry. Stunning outside breakfast area with a view of the Annapurna range!

I had a great respite stay at Fishtail. I had been in modest Airbnb's and wanted to pamper myself for a couple of days. So I went to Fishtail. As soon as you cross the lake on the raft and walk up the garden path to reception, you leave your cares behind. There is a great, well-cared for pool, a wonderful spa and best of all wonderful gardens. The rooms have international channels to enjoy and you have your own terrace with chairs and beautiful landscaping. The food was average but the waitstaff were excellent at the restaurant and actually throughout the facility. It was a great stay!

I have been in the travel Industry for the last 30 years and have visited & stayed in many places around the globe. “Fish Tail Lodge” in Pokhra is one destination which ranks to my experience as one of the top places to stay. I went with my family and we had an amazing experience.  From the polluted cities, it’s a heaven to stay where you get engulfed in nature. The ambience of the whole resort is amazing where the management has ensured the guest with the best of everything. From entry experience of shuttle floats through the lake,  to the beautiful rounded cottages, flowery gardens, restaurant with a perfect view of the lake with the magnificent Annapurna mountains on the background, warm pool, soothing spa, clean nd green & most important respect to the guest’s privacy that lures one to stay here forever. My daughter just didn’t want to leave. I believe it’s the experienced management with their friendly, polite, committed & always smiling staff that made our stay perfect. Food was great,  ‘try the ‘Momos’ its excellent’. Thank you Fish Tail Lodge Management GM Mr Arun Pradhan & the wonderful staff for giving us a beautiful holiday specially for the wonderful cake made for my daughter on her 13th Birthday.

My Husband and I needed to celebrate our 1st year anniversary and obviously Fishtail Lodge was our first and only choice. The setup done was perfect for us and we thoroughly enjoyed the service.The food was amazing. We had no complains at all as the team together was so great. Special mention and thanks to Mr. Bidur who was very humble and polite.If anybody is looking for a perfect destination to spend some quality time with their partner FishTail Lodge is the ultimate choice. The General Manager of the hotel is an added value to the property.

Lovely venue. Serene view and clean rooms. Friendly staff.Special mention for Sanju Sharma, for her great hospitality and service. Very client friendly and helpful. She made us feel AT HOME. Worth a visit with friends or family.

Wherever you are in this lodge, there is always a guarantee for your room to have an amazing view! I booked this trip last minute with friends from the Middle East and was not disappointed. Fish Tail Lodge, its view, staff, and management ate the epitome of five star luxury in Pokhara. If you’re looking to get away from the hustle & bustle of the city, relax, and escape to an amazing destination with a breathtaking view. The Lodge also has their own travel desk who can organise all the tours and activities for you at a competitive price, so this saves you so much time to book it yourself. It definitely deserves to be in the 1,000 places to see before you die.PS: the pancakes at breakfast are DIVINE! Don’t forget to add bacon and maple syrup.

Outstanding Hotel...overall a fabulous experience. Right from the Raftsman to the GM...the entire team knows what hospitality means and they go above the call of duty to ensure they deliver.The location is the best in Pokhara...you could not get anything better even if you paid more. The rooms are very well maintained and the view from every room in this hotel is gorgeous. The food is very good though they could improvise on the menu options a little bit.Overall, we had a memorable stay and would like to Thank the entire Team at Fishtail Lodge for the same

One could write at length about the rather dark rooms, the old furniture and the empty minibar. Yet, none of this really matters. It is amply compensated by beautiful landscaping and a unique location on a peninsula in the Fewa lake, reachable only by raft. Expect a travel back in time, to slower and perhaps more peaceful days. Would the resort benefit from an uplift of its tired infrastructure? Perhaps, but it it would also risk removing its old-school charme. I'd rather wish it remained true to itself.

Hotel is extremely located in a beautiful area,We were welcomed by a staff and taken in special boat We stayed for two nights and really enjoyed .We were offered an anniversary cake and special amenities in the room  and arranged all best possibilities to make our stay more comfortable.Breakfast was amazing and during breakfast as I had my 4 years daughter with me so they took care of my daughter and offered hot chocolate and asked us on timely basis and that’s  a touch point where we realized that we choosed  the best hotel in Pokhara thought it was busy during breakfast hour.No matter in which room you stay but the view of mountains will not leave you alone and this is the main hallmark of this hotel.Special Thanks to entire team including General manager of this hotel for making our stay more comfortable,More relaxing and keeping the hotel up to the expectations.Hotel was  perfectly maintained and room was shining and didn’t find any gaps related to sevice and product and  I am 100% sure this is the result of the good management teams. I will definitely  recommend this hotel to my friends and  if you are going to Pokhara please book this hotel and stay in a heaven and enjoy some memorable moments.This is really a heaven on Earth.

A colleague recommended the hotel for us. After contacting the hotel i received all answers within 24 hrs to whatever inquiry i had. After arriving, the pleasant experience just increased. The people were fantastic, the service superb, everybody made us feel that they were there only for us. The room was cosy, the water hot (we were really afraid to have cold water only). The restaurant was absolutely great with a fireplace in the bar what the guests could “sit around”. Most nights we had dinner there or just finished the day off with a drink (or two). The Management, led by Mr Arun was attentive and always visible. I could recommend the place to everyone.

The lovely hotel is located on a small island on the lake with great view, beautiful gardens, and nice cottages.  The staff were friendly and provided good services.  Taking the boat ride from and to the hotel is a unique “back-to-ancient time” experience.We appreciated Odynovo Tours for booking this hotel for our trip.

Stayed here after coming back from Annapurna circuit trek. My porter Pawan (Annapurnaporter blogspot com) told me about this hotel when I asked him about best hotel in Pokhara and he was right.I am glad that I choose only Porter instead of going with trekking agency or without guide as this trek is very easy to do it solo. 90% trekkers were solo even without guide or porter.I choose guide because it gives someone a job and earn his living as I can afford it😀I need to treat myself after very hard trekking for last 14 days of Annapurna trekking Hotel is one of the best. To enter you have to go through boat (like Taj Palace in Udaipur), staff is very helpful and buffet breakfast and dinner is very good(but not like Oberoi Bengaluru 😀)Hotel has very good view and very nice garden and it’s very relaxing.That’s why Prince Charles and other kings prefer to stay here.

Arriving here you need to get across Lake Phewa on a punt which is operated by a man pulling a rope.  It is a resort style hotel in an absolutely magnificent location. The room was large and very comfortable with views looking across the lake. The whole area is well maintained and the gardens are attractive. The buffet meals were good. It is a pleasant 15 minute stroll into the township.  I highly recommend this establishment.Although Pokhara is only 204km from Kathmandu, by road it took 9.5 hours to get there allowing for a lunch stop.  The return journey took 9 hours. It is a pity that the Nepalese airlines do not have good safety reputations. Our English tour company would not use the flights.Nevertheless Pokhara is a wonderful place to visit.

To get to the hotel you have to take a pulley system raft type boat over. The grounds are stunning and the food is delicious. The rooms are spacious and clean. There is so much storage. The towels are large and soft, some of the best I’ve used in a hotel. There is a safe in the room as well as a coffee/tea maker. There are basic toiletries. There is a gym and a spa on the premises. The pool area is beautiful. There is also a reading/game area situated in a large gazebo type structure. There are plenty of restaurants across the lake as the dinner buffet is around $18 a person. A 120 minute massage is around $60, and they were fantastic. The Mountain View’s are stunning. You can’t go wrong staying here !! The staff was friendly and helpful. They couldn’t do enough to make sure our stay was perfect.

We loved every minute of our stay at Fish Tail Lodge. It was a welcome oasis after our motor bike ride from Kathmandu. The flowers and the landscape were beautiful. The mountains were being a bit shy, but we enjoyed our coffee on the terrace overlooking the lake. Thanks to everyone who made our stay so special!

We stayed here pre and post a trek. It is a fantastic oasis in Pokhara. The whole resort has a peaceful feeling about it. The staff were great and couldn’t do too much for you. A short chain ferry across to Pokhara town took you back to Nepali reality. All in all just great. This visit was my second and hopefully not my last.

OK.  I rarely write a review of this caliber, but I gotta say that this wonderful and beautiful place in Pokhara is just stunning.  The gardens are lush to the extreme, the service couldn't be better, the breakfasts were ALWAYS wonderful, and the staff simply were exceptional.,  That says it all, except the price was quite reasonable and we want to come back as soon as possible and stay longer.  WHAT A WONDERFUL PLACE

I didn't actually stay at Fish Tail Lodge due to my budget while staying in Pokhara for 10 days from 10/07/18 to 20/07/18. However on Sunday 15/07/18 I took a long walk  from my hotel & headed towards the spot opposite the Lodge & relaxed watching guests come & go on the small transfer boat across the Lake. One of the boatman asked if I was a guest to which I replied No, he mentioned I could still board the boat & take a look around the grounds of the Lodge. The hidden gem looks beautiful with well maintained garden area & accommodation choice + a pool. Stopped for a short while close to the pool and talking to staff & ordered a Cappuccino NR 220.00Certainly a beautiful location in a secluded spot away from the main drag of Pokhara business area.The boat transfer takes just over 5 minutes one way & Free.

This hotel is highly recommended for a number of reasons, those being the location, staff, food and overall hotel grounds.  The staff is just fantastic from the bellmen to the bartenders.  Everyone treats you like you are the most special person on the planet.  This did not apply to one or two members of the staff, but all of the staff including the groundskeepers.  For the area, this lush tropical paradise is a five star resort.  The hotel grounds made me feel as though I was back in Hawaii.  The pool area is quite beautiful with an adjacent bar for poolside drinks.  The room is very nice with air conditioning that keeps it ice cold.  You have a nice outside patio, king size bed, flat screen television with cable (American movies) and good size bathroom.  It has an excellent bar and restaurant with an excellent breakfast. You are just across the river from the tourist area and there are numerous restaurants and shopping areas within walking distance. This is the place to stay!

The hotel is old but very well maintained and run . It’s age actually adds to its character . It’s location on the lakeshore is wonderful . Try and get one of the Heritage rooms right on the lake . They are slightly smaller but the stunning view from your sit out is unbeatable . The fact that you can see Dhaulagiri and Annapurna South from your window is worth paying extra for .

We spent a couple of nights here on either end of our trek, and found FTL to be a beautiful place to relax.  The location is unrivaled in Pokhara and it is located within likely the most beautiful gardens in the city.  The brief boat ride across a narrow stretch oh Phewa Lake insulates you from the bustle and noise of the town.  The staff are friendly and attentive.  Rooms are comfortable and clean.  They offer full amenities such as pool, fitness center, laundry, and massage.  They also have boat rentals if you want to explore the lake.

It's been long time that i have been accommodating my guest in the Fishtail lodge. The best thing about the Fishtail Lodge is the Panoramic view of Annapurna ranges and the Eight thousanders with the lavishing breakfast in the morning. The room should be renovated a little bit.The oher things are perfect in the hotel.

Raise your hand and wave, here cometh the boatman. Get across and it's an eden. Round is the theme. 70s is the feel. Good rooms, great service. Beautiful views from the deck near the restaurant. Food is good. The cook at the live counter can converse endlessly especially with the kids. Small pool but with a waterfall. Spa +. Do go boating or fishing, hike to the peace pagoda, rent a bike and go along the lake road or go ultralight (60 min is best i believe). Sunrise at sarangkot is ok, can be missed. But go there if you want to do paragliding.

Really beautiful place. You need to go there by boat. Nice flora and fauna. Good food. Elaborate breakfast. Good host. Met one Australian Lady who manages the place. She was very helpful as well as the staff. The View from the restaurant is amazing, Picture Perfect.

This hotel can easily rank among the top ones for hospitality. Good, spacious and very clean rooms, several charging points for all our gadgets (this is a luxury in Nepal) excellent room service which is prompt, efficient and staff are very courteous. Made our stay so relaxing and comfortable. They have good airport pickups, they were waiting to pick us up even though the flight was many hours late. Booking a spa was a breeze, and the spa was good too. Room service was just excellent, food was just delicious, they considered all our suggestions for wheat parathas, less oil, no sugar, deliver at a certain time and so on. A very efficient boat service to ferry us to the hotel at all times, yes, even at midnight even though it was raining. Hotel is located near the market centre, everyhting is at walking distance, one can stroll towards shopping, pubs with live bands. Stopping over for only a day after our Annapurna trek was the best decision, this place is so worth it. I hope to come back with family again.

Its an amazing experience to stay at Fish tail Lodge. The cottage is cosy. You are cut off from the rest of the world since the only way to reach the hotel is by a boat. The boat service is 24 hours. Buffet breakfast is excellent. If you go to Pokhara, this is the place.

The only hotel in pokhara with a unique arrival experience. Great location, really pleasant and clean rooms, but the thing that makes this such a good place to stay are the staff. All of the people are incredibly helpful and generous. Great breakfast with an amazing view is one of the many features that will make you fall in love with the hotel. Thank you for the absolutely memorable stay. Will see you again soon.

This hotel is located inside the lake and has to be reached via the free 24 hours boat service. This is located very far from the central point, which is good if you like it that way. The hotel is very clean and nicely maintained.The interiors are little old and needs a changeThe rooms have a wall full of windows and glass doors, which is great for the views if you have lake side views, however is a big pain for the privacy, as keeping your curtains shut throughout the day is impossible.They have free Wi-Fi and a good swimming pool. Bathrooms are extremely small. The doors did not have a handle to operate which turned out to be extremely inconvenient.Staff were very helpful and courteous.Food was very decent and they had a good breakfast spreadThey are very close to many restaurants, you can easily walk to that placeBest place to stay at the lake , as you are on it

This hotel has a great location with beautiful grounds that makes it a pleasure to walk around the hotel. The service is friendly and responsive. The rooms have a good size and are well equipped. Finally the restaurant has good food and the prices are reasonable. Having breakfast lakeside while watching the Annapurna range is a great way to start the day!

The website pictures provide a perfect representation of the introduction to this delightful hotel that is accessed via a pontoon type ferry operated throughout the day. This is a covered pontoon manually moved via a member of staff pulling a rope that is perfectly coiled from the slack in preparation for a return journey - impressive. Just be mindful that in inclement weather you will get absolutely soaked, as we were, however it was wonderfully warm, even if both us and the suitcases got more than we bargained for.  Access from the pontoon to the hotel is via uneven stone slabs and may be difficult for those with  any mobility problems. Lovely location on the edge of Lake Fewa and incredible sight of 6 Egrets in a tree just outside the main building.The well laid out gardens contain both a garden or river view single storey buildings with some two storey buildings. The separate reception is contained in the same building as the dining room, which is airy, well laid out and serves a variety of foods by pleasant and friendly staff.Whilst the garden room type villa is well provisioned and has an outside seated area, a major issue for us was the lack of privacy. The path takes you past all the buildings, however the passers by can see directly into the rooms and could do with blinds. It felt claustrophobic having the curtains closed during the day. The separate bathroom is provided with all toiletries, bath and shower (Do not remember that hooks were provided in the bathroom), with the main room having a comfortable double bed, seating arrangements, television and safe.

We stayed here a few days ago and found it to be perfect. Firstly the setting across Fhewa Lake with the mountain ranges behind is superb. It is reached via a pontoon, which is staffed 24 hours a day, although it is wise to inform the staff if you are going to be very late. The accommodation comprises a modern block or gorgeous bungalow style rooms all surrounded by greenery full of birds and colourful butterflies. The bar and restaurant are excellent, modern Raj style. Very comfortable, spend some time talking to the staff, their stories are fascinating-many famous people have stayed here. And the very best of all is 100% of the profits go to a heart foundation that provides free treatment for those patients in Nepal that wouldn't normally be able to afford it. There is a very well equipped gym and lovely swimming pool. I felt totally refreshed after staying here- both physically and mentally; it couldn't be better!

Staff were amazing and helpful! Service was impeccable and they were always going the extra mile to make you happy!Rooms were a bit smaller than expected, but the views from the windows and staff made it up! A/C works very well.Views of the Lake and Mountains were to die for! You get Best of Both Worlds at this location.Location to Shopping Areas and Airport of Pokhara were convenient.Definitely will stay here again!

Friendly, helpful staff from the raftman to the waiters. Peaceful and relaxed environment, with stunning gardens and views across the lake to Fishtail mountain and the Annapurna range (best viewed in the morning!). We love that the profits go to helping the local population access cardiac healthcare. Thank you especially to Fiona for making us feel at home and going the extra mile to give us helpful tips.

Awesome experience nd great hospitality such warm welcoming staff nd very good food. All the small Things were taken care of ......loved the view with snow peak on  the mountains . Rooms were comfortable.   Quick services in the room. Loved it staying ther.

My family and I stayed two nights at this tranquile and wonderful retreat on the Fewa Lakeside. The most fantastisk place, great food, standard, service and hospitality - Fishtail Lodge is an absolute must for all travellers to Nepal and to the Annapurna-region (though the resort is worth a trip - all on its own). We will come back!

This was our third Hotel on our tour of Nepal with Mercury and probably the best, the trip across the river on the ferry is great and is ready for you 24hrs a day. The Hotel is in a beautiful setting with views of the Himalayas and so quiet, we could have stayed here for two weeks instead of two nights, the rooms which are all bungalows are well equipped and large, there is a fridge(un-stocked), tea and coffee facility with two bottles of water supplied daily, flat screen TV, safe(free of charge), the beds are very comfortable and the staff are really nice and polite, once again the drinks are quite expensive as we found in all the Hotels on our tour. If you are looking for a great base to visit Pokhara then this is the Hotel to choose.

The way to get to the hotel is an experience I've never experienced before, having to actually cross the small stretch of the lake to get to it, and the grounds of the hotel are amazingly beautiful. The staff were efficient. The room I've stayed in was good, but could have done with a lick of paint to freshen it up, as well as with having an updated bathroom. The shower was just a showerhead stuck in the wall, with the curtain dividing the bathroom in half; I didn't mind that whatsoever, as that was part of the charm, I guess, and an experience I was happy to have and have a giggle with friends about, but the whole feel of it was a little...outdated.And, of course, I was disappointed with the fact that I didn't have a plaque near my room to say that I had anyone famous staying in it ;)

The best part of this resort style hotel is its location. About 10 minutes walk from the Lakeside restaurants and shops but a world away from the hustle and bustle. The only way to get to the hotel is by a boat that is manually pulled and operates 24 hours a day. The rooms need updating, but are comfortable. The views of the Annapurna range and Fishtail mountain are awe-inspiring. The grounds are nice with places to sit and admire the view. They have kayaks for rent. The food in the restaurant was very good. The staff are extremely friendly and attentive.

An excellent stay with very friendly staff and clean, comfortable rooms with good food. If ever in Pokhara this is a must. On our last day we even saw the amazing Mountain View’s. Our only criticism is that the travel desk could be more accommodating towards day hiking trips in the region. But still definitely worth a visit.

The whole area is located on an island with bungalow Stile houses. Most of the rooms are beautiful renovated and well serviced.The kitchen is very good and worth the price.Absolutely outstanding is the service: super friendly, competent, quick and always available!!! We are travelling a lot, but we have NEVER had a service of such a quality!!

Fish Tail Lodge enjoys a unique location situated on a peninsula across Fewa Lake. Shuttle-floats or boats transport you across to the resort. With the lake on one side and a forest hill on the other, the views are spectacular. The panorama of Annapurna range and Mount “Machhapuchre” (Fish Tail), and their reflection on the lake soothe your soul and refresh your spirit.

Wellkept lodge in a stunning environment. Restaurant and terrass overwieving the lake and the Annapurna mountain range. The lake with 6000 meter high mountains on one side. A boat trip for no money. Frequent visits from a travel agent made it easy to make arrangements. I had a feeling of beeing very well taken care of by a professionell and genuinly friendly staff. Picked up and delivered at the Airport etc. At last. The ”ferryboat” that took me to the lodge across the narrow part of the lake is memorable. The boatsman made it moove by pulling a rope fixed on each shore. Keep it that way.

Stunning place. Most beautiful nature .Breakast buffet is out of the books and caters for all. Had as well the catch of the day out of Lake Behwa. Was served with a lemoen butter . To die for. Appel Pie also very nice. Rooms comfortable. Bathroom slightly small. Staff is catering for any of your needs. Very friendely and extermly helpful. Can walk to Pokhra. Nice clean town and it offers lots of activities around the area

The fistail lodge is one of the luxurious  hotel and lodge in Pohara by Fewa lake. its offers really a dramatic stay with good food rooms  location  and the magic of the fistail and all mountaion floating on Fewa.

The view is amazing with the Fewa lake and view of the Himalayas. The hotel is rich in nature and very clean. It also has very excellent food. The hotel has relaxing spa and massage and a nice pool. The hotel offers boating, canoying, and other adventures.

This place was magical.  After a long medical mission, it was awesome getting to a quiet room, warm shower, and great amenities.  First order of business was to try the Spa.  The folks there were very professional and the prices were similar to home but was necessary.  The pool was beautiful but cold.  The Fewa lake was pretty.  We were able to hire a canoe and paddler to take us through the lake onto the north side of the lake.  I could see the peace temple from the lake.  The views of the Annapurnas is breathtaking.  FTL also had a fitness room but it was locked at the time.  The staff at the restaurant were pleasant and helpful.  The outside seating for meals was beautiful.  We even got to see part of a wedding on the grounds.

I like the toilet Theme of colour and design. A different World from the basic Teahouse basic toilet in the Cold Wintery Mountains.Soothing and comforting feel after all the roughing it out.I dont like the boating across to the Resort though. I prefer a bridge is built for me to cross over than see 1 to 2 Security Guards pulling the robe to cross to and fro.

This was our favourite hotel on our recent group tour to Nepal. Fantastic views of the Annapurna range of mountains, a lovely lake on which to take a boat ride and the novelty of being ferried over the lake to the hotel on a rope pulled raft. The staff are very friendly, food is good and room was very comfortable. The only mistake was to be woken up at 0530 when we had not booked a wake up call.

Had a wonderful 2 night stay. Huge breakfast included. Lovely room with balcony view looking at anapurna mountain range. Food was very good in restaurant and staff were helpful and friendly. Pool is nice. Water cold. Spa was nice post trek and fitness facilities are basic. The short boat ride is very nice pulled across by rope.

One has to take a short raft ride across the lake about 4 minutes, one stands for the journey, it’s very interesting, luggage goes separately, Hotel is away from any town noise, rooms very quiet and peaceful, and well kept, not as modern as some but one must take accountbof it’s location.any traveller will not be disappointed Staff are really very charming.Recommend this hotel without hesitation.

We enjoyed our stay thoroughly. Very helpful staff and plenty of them to help. Good feeling. Good views. Conveniently located. You can walk to the lakeside market. Only food was very average Would have loved to stay there a few more days.The fact that this hotel is an island and requires a short boat trip to reach and exit the hotel is itself unique.

Stayed only one night  but experiences were fantastic. Comfortable and Clean room I was provided. Food was fine, Service  provided by the staff were excellent. Location of the hotel is very good. I would want to have a booking at this hotel in coming December.

We had a perfectly adequate room; we booked too late to get the larger ones in the octagonal structures. The grounds are beautiful. The restaurant (dining room and patio dining) and bar were a great pleasure, and offered beautiful views of the lake and distant Annapurna range, with Fishtail Mountain the dominant vista. The people who staff the hotel were unfailingly warm and helpful and gracious and friendly. The food was interesting and several dishes were well worth repeating. Our stay included breakfast, which was a well done buffet plus eggs/omelettes prepared to order. Highly recommended.

The views are stunning, the pool area relaxing and the restaurant is amazing. The adventure to the hotel starts by a floating pontoon that takes you across the lake. You then reach paradise! Highly recommend

Beautifull settting on the edge of a lake, you arrive by raft!This hotel had everything going for it. The stunning views so the lake form the various terraces, the magnificently kept gardens and nice pool. What let it down for me was the rooms are "tired" and in need of updating and decorating inside,although they are nicely set in small round bungalows in the gardens. The food from the buffet was OK but if you choose from menu the improvement was very noticeable.We stayed only 2 nights, but plenty to do here. We took a kayak on the lake and were entertained by the monkeys in the trees on the lake edge.

I have just checked out... Hotel is surrounded by very beautiful plants. You feel you're in botanic gardens. Lake view is amazing. It's very peaceful. Rooms are clean, spacious and hotel staff is very helpful. But, we didn't like the meals at restaurant. Some of the dishes we had were OK, they were average, but some of them were really not good, we stopped eating. We had lunches and dinners at many restaurants in Nepal, but the dishes we had at Hotel's restaurant were really one of the worst of them. Additionally, this restaurant was the most expensive one we experienced in Nepal. As a result, I recommend this hotel to everyone who needs a peaceful hotel with a good view, but I don't recommend the restaurant.

Best room, friendly people, the best cuisine in the country. I selected the place by fluke. I wasn't that excited until i got inside the lodge and checked out my room in one of the cottages. Then everything was mind blowing. The best place ever that i've stayed thus far.

A unique experience to take a boat to the hotel... but unlike other months, the water of the lake in rainy season is yellow. Fantastic cuisine, beautiful surrounding, and polite staff. It's the best place to stay in Pokhara.

This is an old charming hotel, across Phewa lake. Location is the highlight, few heritage rooms are overlooking the lake. Personally I liked old rooms being spacious & nice decor. Meals are great with pretty good spread out. This is an ideal option to for leisure stay!

situated on the lake side,about 2 furlongs inside from the main road.A pleasant boatride takes you to the main hotel.It has visitors from the Royal Nepal family and maintains its service.The staff are courteous and the food I tasted vegetarian was good.The ambience with trees and flowers is amazing.provides the comfort as well as privacy for young couples,who will be tempted to visit again

A lovely place in the middle of the lakeThe hotel is a little old-but offers spectacular views of the mountains and fewa lakeNote there are lots of lizards out here 🙈 I used to get the hotel staff help me Chas's the lizards before getting to the roomMy room had a great views of the fishtail peak of the Annapurna mountain range Time to visit is in September / October so you can see clear views of the mountains We didn't try the food here - but I can say a cup of coffee was pretty pricey!Since u changed my arrival date due to a landslide that caused the roads to shut down- the hotel was very flexible to accommodate  our request as well as give us an additional night at the same rate.I recommend this place and try rowing the ferry when going to and from the hotel / its fun and a super arms workout :)

We stayed here for two nights whilst in Pokhara. The rooms are dated but adequate, but what was frustrating was the lack of wifi. We only had a free voucher for one device in the room, and the signal was patchy at best. This lack of connectability has not been an issue in any other hotel or restaurant in Pokhara so it seemed odd to pay this much money and be so limited.Breakfast was adequate but ruined by badly behaved children rampaging loudly around the restaurant; their parents didn't seem to believe in discipline and good manners.The staff were very friendly and were the highlight of the stay, along with the attractive grounds. Expensive for the experience.

The lodge is accessed via a charming hand powered ferry. To be met a great reception staff. The surronds are beautiful almost a relection of the atyke if tge 30s or 40s. The accommodation was comfortable modern with wifi. Looking over the grounds from the veranda! Along with attentive staff the nenu satisfies all taste. Sitting outside the restuarant the views are amazing.

This is the most beautiful relaxing scenic hotel I loved it and did not want to leave...service is outstanding...food amazing... (I have been looking everywhere for 2 potatoes dishes I ate there but cannot remember the name..one a stuffed potato dumpling in a curry sauce ...and another potato dish in a sauce...please can you send me the names of these dishes..or a photo of menu..)besides the food ..a short pulley boat ride across the river far from the hustle and bustle of the streets is a piece of paradise....sit outside in the evening on a clear night u can see himalayas....this place I could call home ..loved it 😊

A charming hotel on a stunning location. The rooms are ok and clean, but basic. You'll need a small boat to get on the hotel's island and that seems to be romantic, but at some times it's queuing when you try to get off to the city. We stayed here 4 days after a trekking around the Annapurna to relax. But 4 days is definitely long for a small town like Pohkara.

What an amazing place. You get pulled across the lake with a backdrop of the Annapurna mountains - absolutely breathtaking.  The rooms were spacious and the staff were very helpful.  The amenities were pretty basic in the room but we didn't spend much time in the room apart from sleeping.  There was a small pool ideal to gray a few rays of sun. The location was excellent across from lots of shops and bars.  There was a good choice for breakfast and a varied selection for dinner - all served hot.  I would definitely go back

We stayed for two nights in a room overlooking the lake.  The location was excellent - close to shopping and the lake.  Lots of shopping and no pollution!  The views of the mountains were excellent.  The food at the hotel was great.

Loved the entry on the boat with man pulling the rope and making 4 circles. What character. Staff was helpful. Wifi could only be used near the lobby. This could be improved easily in today's world. Enjoyed the food and buffet at the restaurant. The wait staff was excellent! The grounds were beautiful and had multiple people maintaining the property. We had to move rooms because there was too much noise from the staff coming in and out the kitchen door. That could be improved. Pool was cold. This a great place to make a memory!

Highly recommended hotel! The view is just amazing and the service is excellent! The location is also great just a couple of minutes walk from the main tourist market, perfect for last-minute shopping and souvenirs. Loved it!

Well known people have stayed in this lodge which has made it somewhat famous (and this can generate a feeling of 'greatness' or 'extra satisfaction' when you stay there!). This is perhaps the greatest selling point. Reaching the lodge by a raft across the inlet of the lake is exciting. Lodge is cut off from the crowded areas of Pokhara. It has an old charm, but needs renovation. Garden is well maintained (nothing special, though), but at the same time you get to see guests drying their laundry out in the open which do not go well with the nice flowers in garden beds. Otherwise hotel grounds are relaxing and enjoyable. Breakfast has an excellent spread. Views of the lake are good from the deck. However, did not see any snow peaks as it was cloudy.  Definitely an expensive place to stay. Wifi should be made free at all places in the lodge. Room well furnished. Place is over advertised. But it has an 'exclusive' flavour of its own. Understand lodge funds go to the Heart Foundation, which is a worthwhile cause.

This hotel is a bit of a novelty when staying in Pokhara. While the raft to get to the hotel is cool, the trade off it is quite a decent walk out of the main bit of the tourist zone. The view across the lake is something really special, especially if you get up early enough to watch the sunrise

Its one of my personal favourite hotel and i prefer to stay in this property for over 8 of my 10 visits to Pokhara.The boat ride to reach the hotel gives a different experience all together and make you feel that you are taking in the middle of a lake. The staffs are courteous and the food is also fine.A small fireplace inside the restaurant and nice arrangement to sit besides the same gives warmth and ambience over drinks in winters.Early morning walk, serene nature views and lake water all around can be the best way to start your day in Pokhara.

This is the place you can relax IN NATURE away from hustle and bustle, very quiet and has amazing view of lake and mountain. Breakfast is good, big restaurant with outdoor seating, very nice view from everywhere. No free wifi in room, only at the front desk and restaurant area and very slow connection. Room is clean and charming yet need update. Staffs are nice but not as friendly.

Fishtail is a great place to stay away from the business of pokhara but within walking distance of everything. The rooms are spacious and the gardens very well looked after. Coming and going from the hotel on the small pontoon adds another little frisson - and adds to the feeling of getting away from it all. It was inter when we were there but the sun in the beautiful gardens in early afternoon was warm enough to take a few layers off. The food was good and the staff were very pleasant and helpful. Top marks for Mr Gopal who helped us plan how to do what we wanted to do including watching the sun rise on machepuchre ( otherwise known in English as fishtail ) Would definitely recommend.

The Fish Tail lodge is situated at the lake and has an interesting way to get you across to the hotel. There is a canoe option else a big raft that takes up to 10persons.The security pulls on the thick rope to get momentum and take you across- fascinating is how he stores the pulled rope into a pattern of circles on the floor. This is available 24X7.The lodge has these little cottage rooms with individual sit out space in front.You can enjoy your morning cuppa watching the Machu Pichu range.Food is delicious both Ala carte & Buffet for break fast lunch/dinner.The restaurant has a sit out with multiple tables that overlook the lovely lake and Snow peaks in the background. Smokers can easily steal one with a cuppa tea at the lakeside watching lush greenery.

A beautiful lodge of which you need to take a canoe or raft across which gives it that much more tranquility from town.  Only a 10 minute walk into the hustle and bustle of Pokhara.  The Heritage rooms are older although the views you have over the lake are incredible especially during sunrise and sunset with the mountains in full view!~

My wife and I stayed at the Fish Tail Lodge this past November and thoroughly enjoyed it.  A quiet oasis away from the hustle and bustle.  Very nice restaurant with buffet breakfast.  Guests take a 2 minute boat ride to/from the hotel.  We could walk to all of the shops and restaurants.  Taxi's readily available for those not interested in walking.  Some beautiful views of the Himalayas from the hotel.  Would highly recommend it.They charge for wifi in the room but wifi was free in restaurant and lobby.  They can also arrange tours for you.

Fish Tail Lodge is one of best locations to stay in Pokhara with family. Very close to Pokhara Airport and main city. The property is located in the middle of lake. You can have an excellent view of Fish Tail and a part of Annapurna Range from the room. Hotel can only be entered through a manually operated boat. Serene atmosphere and well maintained room. Restaurant and Bar is excellently placed in the middle of the property with excellent variety of food on offer. If you are driving on your own, make sure that car is properly secured as it need to be kept in the bank of lake. Pokhara is also an excellent place for paragliding and having some airlite adventures. Overall a very rewarding experience and must visit place of people who loves mountains and trekking. Pokhara is usually the base camp for Annapurna Range which takes about 17-18 days. Apart from Fish Tail Lodge there are number of restaurant by the lake side where you can spend your evening.

We stayed at Fish Tail Lodge in Pokhara for three nights in December 2016.  The location of the hotel is outstanding.  You have to cross a portion of the Phewa lake (Phewa Tal) on a hand-drawn ferry to reach the hotel. There are four circular one story bungalows and a two story structure.  The reception and the restaurant is in another large circular structure.  The hotel grounds are very well maintained.  We stayed in rooms 33 and 34. The rooms are facing the Annapurna Range with a large front yard.  Great view.  But the best rooms are room numbers 16, 17, 18 and 19 with great view of Phewa lake and the snow topped range.  The only issues we faced in this hotel are low water pressure and low lights in the rooms. The rooms had great window seats for reading.  The stuff were beyond friendly.  We had dinner there one evening and breakfast one morning only.  The food was reasonably good. The hotel is located within walking distance from the main shopping/tourist area of Lakeside. We walked there several times.

The most awesome location in Pokhara. Right on the famous lake. Even the entry to the hotel is through a ferry in lake. The resort is full of flowers and gives a stunning view of lake as well as the fishtail hill which is snow clad.

Visited Pokhara a beautiful city with a very good hospitable hotel with best location with family. Had INDIAN DINNER with EXCELLENT SERVICE n BEST QUALITY FOOD with staff amiable n family like attended to us by Mr DEVILAL.Had a grand feeling n feel we shul have stayed there more as Hotel was located in LAKE n background of JUNGLE. Excellent rooms Good Facilities n Prompt Hotel Sevices. Must stay Hotel if anyone visits POKHARA n without it the stay in POKHARA is MEANINGLESS.

Exceptional location, quite, clean with very friendly staff. The view is extraordinary... you have the impression that you are in the middle of  nature.. so peaceful place. The breakfast is very good- there are places to eat outside with the wonderful view  I would like to return to this place again and again....

This hotel is in the most beautiful island setting. Single storey accommodation tastefully arranged in lush gardens. Some overlook pool. There are many amenities here including a spa. The food is the best I have tasted so far in Nepal and is piping hot. Meals can be taken outside overlooking the lake with fantastic views of mointains. The staff are very helpful and the rooms are a very good size and spotless.

Beautiful surroundings, pleasant staff, decent food. Good place to relax between treks. Recommended if you are staying overnights in Pokhara. One can clearly notice that the staffs take pride in their work providing a level of hospitality one can expect from a great hotel. They take pride in keeping the gardens around the hotel really beautiful. Even the 'boat' man takes pride in keeping the skills and tradition in the way lines for pulling the boat are coiled. May seem like a small matter but the small input by the dedicated staff made our stay extremely pleasant.

Quirky, fun way to get there. From bustling Pokara, take a turn off onto a tree lined street toward the lake. Fish Tail Lodge is accessed by climbing onto a floating platform that is attached by rope to both the Pokara side and the Fish Tail Lodge side. A "boatman" pulls the rope into coils as the platform glides across the short stretch of water to the hotel's landing. The hotel is a collection of multi-room villas and 2 story buildings.  It's clean and the staff is very nice and accommodating. There is a swimming pool but I opted not to take a dip in the milky water.

We spent three nights there, as a small group, and were well served. The facilities were in good state and the surroundings are just splendid. I only can imagine what it takes to keep it up.The transport by the person-driven ferry make the arrival each time a special moment, and puts the pace of your stay. And the bustling city is in walking distance too, if you want a change of atmosphere.The fact that larger groups use this little paradise can be a little downside, and the buffet has some delicious dishes, but it's no gourmet experience. The friendly staff make up for a lot though.

Fish Tail Lodge has the best location of any hotels in Pokhara--it requires taking a short boat ride across Phewa Tal (Fewa lake) but boasts a quiet atmosphere, superb cocktails, an impressive view of the Annapurna skyline, and a lovely dining deck that overlooks the lake. The rooms are fairly basic and the wifi barely works, but while in Pokhara we spent most of our days exploring the hotel grounds, the city and surrounding area anyways. The staff was incredibly helpful; they assisted us in arranging a car from Pokhara to Bandipur and from Bandipur to Chitwan, and stored our luggage while we trekked to Poon Hill. Overall, it was a great place to stay.

The hotel is only accessible by boat/canoe ( they have their own canoe for guests) very unique experience with a view on phewa lake, the food and the rooms are decent, they have a spacious pool. located on a small Island which provide you a unique stay in Pokhara.

What a refreshing surprise...admit lush green plants and trees...flowers...with the lake front and mountain peaks beyond....it's paradise.Well appointed rooms and good food.It was a idyllic and scenic break in the himalayasHighly recommended.

Stayed here for 2 nights - first upon our arrival in Pokhara, and the second before our departure from this town...  I didn't book this place hence I was quite shocked when I had my first glimpse of the establishment - it looked pretty darn high-end and luxurious, definitely not the kind of place I would consider staying a night had I been the decision-maker...Fishtail Lodge was truly lush and beautiful...  As this resort sits on a small "island" of a land in the middle of Lake Fewa, it feels very private and exclusive to be staying here...  The way to and fro this resort from the mainland is either via a floating sheltered raft or a small sampan-like boat, both of which were manually and skilfully manovered by one of the resort staff...We were in room 24 (Garden Terrace) during our first visit in February 2016, which was essentially part of a circular cluster of single-storey cottages with a private front porch...  Our clean twin room came complete with an ensuite bathroom and western-style toilet...  On our return stay, we were given a complimentary upgrade to room 61 (Palm Court Deluxe)...  Our room was on the 1st floor, and it came complete with a private balcony...  Evening evening here at the Fishtail Lodge, the hotel staff would make his rounds to every occupied room across the entire resort to help get the clean and snugly made beds ready for the guests to rest in...Daily breakfast here was continental buffet - a wide and tasty spread of cereals and fresh fruits, toast and pastries, sausages and baked beans, vegetable pockets and dhall, various nepalese delicacies and hardboiled eggs, and eggs-to-order, etc...  For those weary from their treks, massage is available at this resort albeit at quite an expensive rate (you can get the same at a much cheaper price on the mainland)...  WiFi was free but was only available in the reception room and in the restaurant / dining room...One thing I've noticed - power outages are more frequent here than anywhere else I've been in throughout Nepal...  For instance just for comparison, while I've experienced it perhaps once (at most twice) in Kathmandu, it happened about 5 ~ 6 times at this resort in one single evening...  One time, it happened when I was taking a morning hot shower - good thing I was almost done and did not get hit by the cold water...

Stayed here for two nights and was very impressed, the rooms were clean, fresh & tidy, restaurant was first class as was the food served there. Access to the hotel was via a quaint raft. Friendly staff enhanced our stay there. A1+

I stayed for two nights at this beautiful lodge.  Really, the setting was beyond my expectation.  Unbelievable views and the whole vibe of the place is so serene. I wish I had stayed there my whole 9 days in Nepal! The staff are helpful, the food was excellent.  The rooms are not super luxurious, but perfectly serviceable and comfortable.  I changed my room from a garden view to a lake/mountains view and was so glad I did.  It was about 9 steps to comfortable seating with a spectacular view.  Definitely upgrade if you can - totally worth it.  If I come back to Nepal, I would spend every night here!

Check in took more than half an our as they had confusion on type of room I booked through Expedia. Eventually room was allotted and was taken to room only to find room is not ready. Hence House Keeping Staff was called to prepare the room which again took almost half hour till the time we were made to wait outside the room.In case you look for Smiling and Happy Faces, certainly FishTail Lodge is not the place to stay, staff never smiles and aren't warm.Untrained waiters in Restaurant is something you have to live with. They will not assist you in ordering food, will keep food basket in your plate, wont serve food in your plates. You will keep looking for them for service and reordering, so please don't mind your food getting cold while you look for waiters. Food taste isn't great but very expensive. Dinning here may be perfect recipe for spoiling your dinner or lunch. Better option can be... take a stroll and you will find plenty of places who serve better food and at 1/4th of price.And at last, please carry your own umbrella, don't expect hotel staff to offer umbrella if it rains rather have trust on your feet and run.Don't expect evening/ turn around service. Room dining plates wont get cleared after waiting for half an hour so putting them out of room may be better idea. Bellboy will not show up at check out time.At the time of booking never thought will have this kind of experience for bomb kind of money (compared to most of the places in Pokhara) I spent.Room Tip: Don't opt for this hotel certainly not value for money you will spend. Location and lawns of Hot...http://www.tripadvisor.in/ShowUserReviews-g293891-d6206380-r261387801-Hotel_Fishtail_Villa_Bed_and_Breakfast-Pokhara_Gandaki_Zone_Western_Region.html#

We stayed here for two nights before and after our trek. The location is fantastic but we found the service, food and overall value to be lacking versus the premium price - fancy the most expensive hotel in the area and no free wifi in the premium rooms?  The decor is ok but feeling tired. The restaurant was fine and reasonably priced - but having stayed here I would probably choose another lakeside hotel in Pokhara. If budget is unlimited then the mountain and lake views and the gardens are certainly lovely.

The hotel is in the best location if you are a nature lover, across the lake. Ferries and boats available all the time. The people are extremely hospitable. The place is well managed, neat and clean. The food was exceptional. Highly recommended. Must go and see. The price was reasonable. My 6 year old loved it.

Positive: The location, quiet, peaceful, on an peninsula, nice garden, everytime you go to the lakeshore market you use a small ferry, very good Chef, food is very tasty. Extraordinary friendly waiters, we like to highlight especially Niraji and Prakash.Negative: Definitely a NO GO was our room, although clean it was shabby and would need a total renovation. Awful brown towels, the small bathroom smells musty. We hope, that they do have better rooms. The Restaurant does not have an atmosphere. There were only a few guests when we stayed here, certainly due to the present circumstances in Nepal it might be very hard to nowadays run a place like this, therefore it was even more not understandable, that we got this terrible room.

I stayed here while backpacking around Asia - I wanted a bit of luxury before returning back to the UK. And what luxury. The hotel is isolated from the shoreline on the lake so you get to the island by raft. Amazing views of the Himalayas. Food was fantastic, my room was wonderful staff were so helpful and friendly. Thoroughly recommend this hotel.

We have plenty of good memories while staying here. We learnt a lot about Nepalist people, food and culture. From the gardener to our concierge, they are very attentive and resourceful. We met our boatmen that took us from the hotel to the nearest temple, then to our jungle trekking to see the World Peace Pagoda. There was zero minute wasted during this trip. The hotels food was amazing! They do room service too if you're too lazy:) which we did. Would love to come back

Fishtail Lodge was a lovely surprise for my husband and I. We enjoyed the little boat ride to reach the lodge and found it a beautiful and relaxing setting at the foot of the mountains. The staff weye very welcoming and excited to have us inspite of the fact that tourist traffic there was heavy. The rooms were exceptional for a lodge...we especially appreciated the window seating. My personal highlights were the buffet breakfast and the nepalese massage I enjoyed at their in house spa. All in all if you're staying at Pokhara it doesn't get any better than this.

Stayed there 2 nights with my family in Feb.15 and had a wonderful time. With Ubud in Bali, I can't think of a better place that immerses you in peace, tranquillity and idyllic landscape (Nepal is blessed in that regard).It is an old hotel but everything was working perfectly & rooms / bathrooms were clean.Great frontdesk team and very friendly staff in restaurant.

Fish tail lodge has pretty much the perfect location - beautiful views of the snow clad Himalayan peaks in the distance and the lovely lake right in front!We loved the property, excellent rooms and excellent food. The service was great!Definitely would love to return to Fish tail lodge.

One of the most blissful place i have ever visited. ..it is truly like heaven on earth!  The best thing about Fish Tail is the location- overlooking the lake and the himalayas...The next best is the wonderful hospitality that you experience even before you step on the property - the staff is polite, very well trained, eager to help you and no, not for tips, as you would find in resorts otherwise...In short, i was a WOW experience!I plan to visit again soon:)

Definitely charming.  On the outskirts of pokhara , this resort/hotel is on a small island on the lake in pokhara. You get there by a small barge, 10 or 12 people only, that moves by the porter pulling rope lines. It takes less than 3 minutes and runs continuously 24 hours. The dining room is circular and the buffet and other food was excellent. The service was also pleasant and helpful. There is free wifi in the dining room and open bar area. The front reception was helpful in getting onto wifi. As in everywhere rose in nepal, the lights periodically go off for a minute or two. Each room has a flashlight. The rooms were pleasant and the bathrooms modern. You can walk around the lake and to the tourist shopping area. There are rental canoes for a ride around the lake. The boatman has life jackets which should be worn. The hotel has a travel desk to arrange yours etc. the view of the mountains is lovely but weather dependent.  Our room looked out to gardens but I think all rooms should be ok. There is a woman on the land side parking lot who has lovely things.

Fish Tail Lodge was recommended to us by our local tour guide. The highlight of our arrival would have to be being pulled (or rowed) across the lake to get to the hotel, this was unique and brilliant! With only one night of stay and fishing being our intention, we could not have asked for a better location. Upon arrival, the staff was helpful in showing us around the area to look for suitable fishing spots. Within an hour, we had for ourselves two jungle perch and a freshwater eel, just by fishing right by the hotel. Though Nepal in General is not highly recommended during the monsoon, we beg to differ, the monsoon rains added to the experience walking the streets of Pokhara and having a delicious hearty meal in Fish Tail Lodge for dinner. Undeniably, one of the best meals we had on our entire trip. We were lucky to wake up to clear skies and a magnificent view of the Fish Tail mountain and all that surrounds it, taking our breath away. Having warm delicious breakfast out in the nature, with a magnificent morning view, we could not ask or imagine anything better. Staff were friendly and ever so helpful, we highly recommend Fish Tail Lodge for your stay in Pokhara.

The hotel is set in a beautiful location and is accessed either via a raft pulled across the lake or a row boat (this can be a trick if your in a hurry to get out or in so do leave time)Food here is in one resturant and was pretty good, will recommend the local dishes as very tasty.The hotel itself is pretty old with all sorts of dignitaries having stayed in the 80's, this also means the hotel will be a little old and lacking a few of the model amenities and look and feel, so come for the ambience.The kayaking equipment was brand new and in super condition, we did a lot of that, plenty room to paddle around and it was great, loads other activity as well.Had a pretty decent stay, it's setting and location is what you will be coming here for.

This is a very quaint hotel accessible by a short row boat ride across the lake. It feels like reaching an island oasis when you land. All of the staff are very charming and extremely helpful form the bell boys to the reception staff and dining staff. The rooms are little lodges and although the beds seems slightly uncomfortable at first we had a very good sleep and felt recharged after the night. The restaurant has lovely views over the lake and it is possible to get a boat to take you on various trips or enjoy some kayaking from the lodge. The grounds are very well kept and the resort has a calm and peaceful air. Overall this hotel was very charming and makes it an ideal base to explore Pokhara. It is a lovely place to enjoy the sights of Pokhara. As an aside; We drove both ways from Kathmandu and we were sorry we did not fly back as there is an airport in the town and the journey back can take up to 6 hours. We stopped on the way down to take the cable car ride in Manakamana but we found the journey back very tiring.

Visited in early June 2014. Undoubtedly the best hotel in our Nepal Trip in terms of service. Mr. Hasta at the dining room, Mr Tiwari at the front office were always smilingly helpful. There were a few unpleasant faces but majority of the staff just personified brilliant service. This lodge is very unique with its ambient, picture perfect, true to nature surroundings. Forest, hills, lake, snow capped Annapurna, beautifully maintained garden. One is right amidst nature. Their raft to reach the hotel itself started of a unique experience. Coming to their rooms, they had very bad damp smell in some of the older non renovated rooms. With their electricity on and off the air conditioner would take ages to switch on or would remain completely off. Our first night was a nightmare. On the second night we shifted to a newer room which one can figure out by the new air conditioner. This room had no issues and even with the fluctuating electricity the air con worked perfectly fine. Both the rooms we stayed at were classic . Renovation for the rooms is underway. The deluxe rooms, very few in number, they somehow were reluctant to give them with many excuses. They do not provide kettle in the room. View from the rooms - there is none.  You have to be around the dining area or in the presidential suite for the spectacular views. Wifi is free at the dining area and is chargeable at the rooms. We had breakfast, lunch and dinner at the property and all our meals were excellent. The staff just made the whole experience more enjoyable. Paragliding and ultra light flight are two not to be missed activities for those even little willing. On the way to Kathmandu the Manakamna temple cable car should not be missed.

Fish tail lodge has a pleasant, warm and wow approach to hospitality.  I visited earlier this month with my mother, being flower lovers, we both enjoyed beautifully manicured gardens and lawns. Being able to admire the snowladden Annapurna mountain range from the hotel patio is breathtaking. Rooms are clean, cozy and chic. Staff are amicable and helpful. Food is tastefully prepared. Definitely will be going back...

stayed on 22nd & 23rd april. Dream Location. Recently renovated & excellently well maintained. Rooms and landscaping nice & well kept. The food is Delightful. The Gym swimming pool  & spa are well maintained. All the  Staff members are very well mannered & hospitable. Overall had  a wonderful stay & experience.

Location was perfect!  Loved riding on the barge to get to the hotel.The rooms were very spacious & clean.  Grounds were beautiful.  The food & service was excellent.  The restaurant/bar area is very cozy w/a fireplace.

The services of the fishtail lodge were very fast and the food also over there was very good.Moreover, the staff was also very cooperative there.The receptionist over there Mr. Manish and Ms. Himani and also the other staff were very friendly and quite helpful. Moreover I would like to share the this lodge with friends.

Great location, first class accommodations and incredible service.  Prakash, Surendra, Zanisha and Haste made our stay even more enjoyable. They always greeted us with a smile, and gave us first class service.  The breakfast buffet was amazing and it was wonderful to sit outside, looking at the lake and the mountains in the background.  Highly recommend Fishtail Lodge.

This is the one off the most amazing place too be Very good food and the place r so so warm and the room r too good too be real 💋💋💋Can’t wait too be back with them We were served by sagun and Ganga 🤙🤙🤙

We stayed at the hotel for 2 days... the ambience was outstandingly beautiful and peaceful... all the staffs were warm... especial thanks to Sagun ji for all the arrangements and her sweet nature... looking fotward to coming back soon!

Stayed for three nights was lucky to get perfect clear weather not many guests due to Covid but more than enough staff to take care.  I like to following things 1. excellent ambience 2. excellent service 3.courteous staff 4. active general manager and 5. very helpful travel desk6. Friendly Chef.  What can be better : 1. Rooms are now aging.  But comfortable. Tips :1. Deluxe rooms are ideal. They have good views from first floor . 2. Heritage rooms are expensive and smaller. But have lake and mountain view.

This is a heritage type hotels in Pokhara. The property is big with a swimming pool, spa and restaurants. I like hanging out in the deck with friends with some drinks and snacks. Great food and excellent service.

We have stayed in this hotel in new year. We can see the lake and mountain just outside our room. Very relaxing and peaceful environment but at the same time, near the downtown area. Indeed enjoyed our stay here!”. Highly recommended!

We are enjoying our 10-night stay at Fish Tail Lodge! The staff is very friendly and if you have a specific wish, they do everything to make your wish come true! Furthermore, Fish Tail Lodge is a peaceful place where one can experience a big variety of flowers and if the weather is clear, one can see the Annapurna or Dhalaugiri! What's more, the restaurant offers a wide range of good quality meals and the restaurant staff is very friendly like Bidur Acharya for example! We highly recommend to stay at Fish Tail Lodge!

The hotel is so famous and I think it’s amongst one of the most expensive accommodations by Phewa Lake, but really don’t think too much of it.It is interesting to get to the hotel by raft of by boat, the garden is well maintained, the staffs are nice and responsive, but the room is old, and when we got in the room we killed 6 or 7 mosquitoes in 5 minutes. We told the reception on our way out and they took care of it, so we only got to kill another 2 in the evening. Bed is old and squeaky, worst of all is, the hot water supply. It suddenly turned extremely hot Sheila in shower, almost got burnt. Anyway, won’t recommend to my friend or anyone plans to go to Pokhara.

When you visit Nepal, Pokhara is a must place to visit which is an 6-8 hours drive from Kathmandu. My husband and I visited Pokhara for a romantic getaway and Fish Tail Lodge was the right place for us. Fish Tail Lodge was located in Pokhara and right in between the Phewa Lake. I mean you will be staying in a place surrounded by water and the mountains. So clean, green and fresh, we had such a good time staying at the hotel. To enter the lodge, we have to park the car near the Pokhara market and then there’s a guest boat ride that runs for 24 hours for the guests to travel to and out of the hotel. Arrival at the reception of the hotel, you will be treated with a welcome drink and a wet towel to wipe of your tiredness from travel. To add on top of that, their food was just mesmerising and it’s such treat for your palette. We had such a fulfilled holiday and spend our time from the lodge by visiting the Pokhara night markets, Sarangkot sunrise and other local tourist spots. Fish Tail Lodge also has their own travel desk where you can make plans with them and arrange activities such as trekking, hiking, helicopter ride, paragliding, river rafting and bungee jumping, etc based on your interests. The staff were kind, caring and compassionate to the work they undertake and we were treated royally by them. We would highly recommended this place for both romantic getaway or for a family retreat to strengthen the bond and communication within yourself and others.

To get to the hotel you cross the Fewa lake by raft (takes 12 people) as the hotel is on a peninsula with the lake on one side and the thick forest behind; it's in a spectacular location. The hotel has quite a few small cottages but we chose a room in the two storey building that had roughly 20 rooms all with balconies. The rooms are not huge but comfortable and has everything you need. Breakfast was included and had a fantastic variety of different food and it was delicious. One night we opted to have dinner at the hotel and it was wonderful. The staff were all very attentive and professional. I loved staying at the lodge and highly recommend it.

Very Nice hotel..Great people..Realy Good food..Great service!!!Special thanks to de waiter surendra thapa for his hospitality;)Met mooi weer kan je o.a. the fishtail zien, en de annapura bergen.Echt een aanrader!!Edwin en Ursula van zijderveld

I am extremely glad we stayed in this wonderful property. The little cottages, the lovely garden and most of all the views of the famous fish tail peak. The whole place is magical. The property is in the other side of the lake. Traveling back and forth on a rope pulled barge was an unique experience.

The hotel can only be reached by a raft which is pulled across the lake by a rope from the mainland.
