Excellent property to enjoy the hill stay in Pokhara Everything in hotel is very nice and lovable Hotel staffs,attendents,Chef, cooks all take personal care and prepare very tasty food Best thing is to cross Fewa lake in manual flat boat pulled by rope I give 10 out or 10 .

I stayed in this hotel with my wife for family holiday from 27.4.22 to 29.4.22. We are sr. citizen. We have vast travel experience outside India. After Covid pandemic, we started travelling afresh and decided to go to NEPAL My booking was made in thos hotelI have stayed so many 4 & 5 star hotels, but this place and the stay i would give it a full 5 star review. The place is more than the worth of the price they took. The hotel follows the covid norm sincerely.The rooms are good. Reception services, room service, in room dining, housekeeping are all excellent. The hotel is handled by Very well trained, experience and responsive staff. The choice of restaurants is also good but we normally eat the buffet. If u have any issue related to housekeeping problem then contact GM of hotel. He is very polite & gentle and take quick customer satisfy decision.The hotel is room is very neat and clean having all facilities, double beds, neat clean bed cover. Bathroom was good with toiletries. Staffs are very courteous. I appreciate the behavior of all hotel staffs and their services. The food provided by the hotel is sufficient during breakfast and dinner. The menu of buffet is as per international standard and taste is good. The food serving staff are very cooperative about your choice of food.THE BEST PART THE HOTEL IS THAT IT IS VIEW PART OF MOUNTAIN, DEEP FOREST AND LAKE I.E TOTAL COMBINATION NATURE WITH FULL DAY BIRD SOUND. FOR THAT YOU ASK FOR HERITAGE ROOM. All rooms are attached with small balcony from where you can enjoy sun & moon set. Surrounding area is cover with forest and mountain. It is a superb place to enjoy nature along with sounds of birds AND FREE LAKE TRAVEL ENJOYMENT BY BOAT MANDETORY.

My husband and I had the pleasure of staying at the Fish Tail Lodge for 4 nights during our recent trip to Nepal.First, you arrive to the hotel via a barge hand pulled across the lake (how cool is that!)!  The front desk team is one of the friendliest front desk staffs we've ever met (and there were several different staff members over the time we were there and the were ALL equally attentive and welcoming.   They really made our stay special.We had a minor issue with our initial room, which could have impacted our experience, but when we presented the situation to the front desk staff, they handled is incredibly well and they made it right.  I know that's what one typically expects, but it doesn't always happen.... and they made the change with such sincerity and care, it really resonated with us.  The front desk team was excellent. We stayed in a cottage which had good space - a little sitting bench inside by the windows & outdoor patio with chairs.  The landscaping on the property is absolutely stunning.  So many beautiful plants and flowers.  The pool was a lovely respite from the heat and the staff was very attentive regarding bringing you food or drinks.Oh my goodness... the spa services.... I typically don't do spa treatments on vacation, but my body was sore from trekking and the prices were very reasonable.  I had a deep tissue massage and a Swedish massage and both were amazing.  The women who did each massage were very skilled and very aware of what your body could tolerate.  What a treat for me and a great experience.Breakfast on the patio overlooking the lake was absolutely amazing..... that view, that peace and serenity.  And the staff!  We like to interact and joke with the staff and there were several staff members that were so friendly and fun..... and also making sure we had everything we needed.  I wish I was there now!At night, sometimes they used a canoe instead of the barge to get you back to the hotel - so much fun!  And so unique.The hotel is a bit older, and not fancy "per se (the cottages appear to have been recently renovated)", but the uniqueness of it being on the lake, the fantastic staff, and the gorgeous views, make it a special experience.

Excellent location if you are looking to relax and enjoy serene and tranquil atmosphere. Great food, very helpful staff and great service. Rooms are very comfortable. Would definitely recommend to everyone.

Such a perfect scenic place to stay you will feel like staying along with the Nature and birds impressive staffs and such a friendly Sagun Thakuri who helped us through out our stay and food prepared by Aga Thammar Murthuza chef was amazing..!

I loved the ambience and the breakfast view. Amazing hospitality by the staff Mrs. Shagun and Mr. Gyan. I had asked them to arrange a surprise for Birthday and they pulled it off well..  Thank you for the stay

It's a very wonderful lodge,we enjoy it very much .hospitality of stuffs very nice. We wish success of its future progress. Natural beauty of it is very fantastic. Food was very delicious. All staffs are very cooperative and helpful.

Absolutely amazing trip with family. The ambience and the mountains were breath taking, wish we had spend some more time there. The greenery, hammock, mountain view, the chills everything was amazing.

It was an amazing experience staying here. Good ambience, tasty food, great hospitality, staffs were very humble. Guest relation officer sagun shahi was very cooperative and cheerful. View of lake and himalayas is superb.Highly recommended Fulfilling experience!!

We were in fishtail resort for 2 nights and the view, the hospitality, the comfort was nothing less than amazing. We will be back for more of Fishtail Resort and thank you for letting me have the best birthday with you guys! The resort itself has everything in it, we didn’t have the need to go around in lakeside Pokhara (been there done that)!

Had our wedding there in December, the food was very good and the staff were friendly. Covid precautions were taken by all staff and eveyone involved. Highly Recommended for destination weddings or functions

Very nice place.service was good and the TripAdvisor is very good for the travelers..it helps travelers to travel in every situation when they r hurry to go anywhere,good hospitality and as well As I like as travel Dex that was very good & specially crew member are polite and I like ur service thanku ..

Such a beautiful store!an amazing selection,an extremely knowledgeable staff coupled with fantastic price!good location,really pleasant and clean rooms.All of the people are incredibly helpful and generous with their and advice.

The Fishtail Lodge in Pokhara is one of the best hotels we have ever stayed in. Very peaceful location, set in wonderful gardens on the shore of the lake. Excellent service, very comfortable room and good food in the restaurant. Sat outside on the deck by the lake, watching the sunset on the Himalayas was a wonderful hour. We only stayed two nights and wished we could stay longer, a very enjoyable and relaxing place to stay.

The Fish Tail Lodge was the the most beautiful place we stayed on our recent trip to Nepal. The views are amazing- lakeside with lovely gardens. This is a real hidden gem! The staff was wonderful, friendly, and professional.

We were recommended to this hotel by a fellow traveller in Nagarkot. No regrets.Polite staff. In the dining room, they should take care of the clients dining rather than chatting around.Well-appointed rooms. scenic and beautiful gardens.In the morning the staff are noisy and is not aware of clients sleeping in the rooms

Led a garden tour group and stayed here and loved it. Great location close to the main street and right on the lake. Superb gardens and very nice rooms in the old raj style. We had quite a few meals in the restaurant and the food was good and service good also. Enjoyed taking the punt across the river each time we departed as it gave an exclusive and secluded feel. Highly recomended.

We were lucky to spend a little time in this peaceful setting in late November and enjoyed every minute of it.  All of the staff made us feel so welcome. Special thanks to Bidur who made an extra effort to show us around and explain the fascinating history of the place.

Catch the punt across the lake to this stunning hotel owned by the Royal family, who contribute the profits to addressing heart disease in Nepal.Stay in one of the bungalow rooms and sit in the afternoon outside watching the jungle or sit outside the restaurant and watch the people on the boats on the lakesSO relaxing. A great spot to base yourself for the activities in the surround area

This was my third time at Fish Tail Lodge. It is simply the best hotel in Pokhara! We had an amazing experience all the way through. The location is fantastic, the hotel area and rooms beautiful and the service is amazing! All staff is very friendly and helpful - at the reception, in the restaurant, the bell desk - they all arrange very quickly what you need. Coming back again!

Very pleasant and relaxing four-day stay at this charming retreat hotel. The travel desk and reception desk staff were particularly helpful and knowledgable. They helped us to enjoy our stay and arrange flights and transport. Thank you, Eneela Rai, first class service.

Had gone on a family trip (August, 2019) to Pokhara and stayed at the renowned Fish Tail Lodge. Have always enjoyed staying at places that have "ambiance and character" and Fish Tail had plenty of these. The kids enjoyed the lush green gardens and swimming pool. We enjoyed beer/cocktails by the pool and in the evening a massage. Breakfast with views of Himalayas, the famous Fewa lake in front wasa great way to start the day. The lake side city itself was just walking distance from the Lodge which is another big plus point. The service was top notch, the ambiance magnificent and we returned home refreshed yet longing to visit again, very soon.

5 stars!!!We had a wonderful and comfortable stay here. The location of this place is very unique. We also got to see the breathtaking view of mountains from the deck. The staffs were helpful and courteous too.We would surely love to visit again.Thank you fishtail lodge for all the good memories.

Hello everybody!There are good hotels with good food and services and then tgere are excellent hotels!Rarely do you get a hotel with a genuinely warm staff which turns a hotel into a home away from home. Fishtale is simply one of those places!A peaceful hotel away from the hustle and bustle yet walking distance from lake side market, this place, its location and the vibes will tempt you to relax within it the whole time.Add to it some extremely delicious food and you are in for an awesome time.No hotel has or ever will succeed without its wonderful staff and this hotel has taken that a notch above the rest. I will not do justice if i do notmention the following:Raftsmen- these ex Nepalese army men are an epitome of grace and discipline. A smile always on their faces, you can feel the warmth in their crisp Army style salute!Reception: what can i say! Genuinely warm staff always ready to help you out with your smallest request. I would not do any justice if dont mention the name of Mr Durga here.A thorough gentleman and ever ready to help us out. Thank you Mr Durga for all your assistance in making it a memorable stay.Restuarant: A lovely restuarant and an able staff which can make you the best masala chai and palak paneer!Housekeeping: cheerful housekeeping staff who will keep your room extremely clean and tidy except that you will never see them. They do their job so quietly and without disturbance Gardeners: The extremely well kept lawns of this hotel will remind you of the old gardens with a variety of flowers and plants. You will have to see it to believe what effort thay are putting in it to maintain it the way they have.A BIG Thank you to the entire staff of this fine hotel especially Mr Durga for making our stay here a memorableo one!

Visited pokhara with family in the month of july 19 . Iam beyond satisfied with the services and the hospitality staff here.The airport’s just 5min from the hotel. The hotel rooms are very clean and the staff is very courteous, polite and professional.  The foods was delicious and tastey. Location was across the lake from the main shopping area accessible by a boat and raft which added to the charm and atmosphere. And also hotel has featured in the bestselling book “1000 place to see before you die” we feel so lucky.One of the highly recommended options in pokhara. We would like to Thanks the entire team of Fish tail lodge.

When we were asked by people at Kathmandu where we were going to stay for two nights atPokhara and we replied that it would be at The Fishtail Lodge, they said that we'll be staying ata very fine property and one of the best in pokhara. Once featured in the book 1000 places tovisit before you die, this picturesque resort managed by the Annapurna hotel was once the primevacation spot for famous people including Prince Charles. Thus with high hopes we proceed toFTL.Getting to the resort is actually fun and gets you into the mood of staying with nature. Yourequire a boat or a raft to get from the roadside to the resort as we have to cross a part of thegorgeous phewa lake. The staff manning the rafts were very friendly people. The raft service isavailable 24×7 as that is the only way to reach the resort.The only downside to this setup is that during the rains there is a good chance that some of yourluggage may get slightly wet as was our case. But the staff were really careful.The resort itself is breathtaking and beautiful. Since it is literally in the lake, you get awonderful view of the Himalayas beyond it. However since we visited during the monsoon seasonwe could only see some distant hills due to the low clouds. Nonetheless, it was still beautiful.It's quite, secluded and peaceful. The resort is laid out in the form of many cottages with eachcottage having a couple of rooms. The main building had the lobby and the restaurant called TheCircle which also has a bar. The lobby had a board with pictures of all the celebrity who havestayed here. We were checked in quickly and taken to our two rooms which were attached.This is where the resort started disappointing us. The rooms at one glance were clean enoughand in good shape although a bit small. But the lack of maintenance supervision showed as westarted using the rooms. To say the least, they were in a very bad state. To start with, onebulb in each of the rooms weren't working. This room had severe lack of lighting when it's theevening and the handful of warm bulbs don't actually brighten up the room much. Add to thatbroken bulbs, then it was almost hard to read books. There were no table lamps or bedside lampseither which, to be honest, is very poor for a resort that is said to be the best at Pokhara. Thewindows couldn't lock properly as the locks were bent and deformed. The TV reception was poorand seeing the TV properly was almost impossible. The cables and even the receiver were justhanging out of the TV with no support. The numbers on the keypad on the phone were almostcompletely wiped out and barely visible. It shows that the phone is very old and hasn't beenproperly maintained. The coasters for the cup were very filthy and stained. The cups were alsodirty and we had to clean one ourselves. The slippers provided in the room in our cupboard wasused as there was sand on it. These may be small things but they show how badly kept this placeis. No wonder the amount of celebrities visiting this place lately has been less. The photos havebeen attached below.After keeping our bags in the room, we went to the restaurant to have some snacks as wehadn't eaten anything since morning at it was about 4. Since it was rainy they provided umbrellasfor us to walk to the restaurant. The restaurant was cozy and warm with a fire place at thecentre. There was also a large screen showing the cricket world cup matches. It also has a bar.The main dining area is further down with views of the beautiful phewa lake. Outdoor seatingis also available. Our server showed us to our table and presented the high tea menu and the allday dining limited menu. We ordered a plate of veg pakoras, grilled veg sandwich, grilled cheesesandwich and some hot and sour soup. The food was excellent. Really good quality and tasty witha sizeable quantity.We left for our rooms and after refreshing ourselves and resting for a while we went to havedinner back to the restaurant. Again, we were shown to our seats and given the dinner menu.We had some Indian dinner which was also great. The one slight complaint that I felt was thatthe restaurant staff, although they were extremely friendly, weren't polished.Breakfast the next day, was in the form of a buffet having various Indian, Chinese andContinental options. Everything was great except the sambhar which didn't even taste likesambhar. Otherwise the spread was big and really good.After breakfast we went for the city tour of Pokhara and came back before dinner. We had lightdinner of various snacks as we were full from the late and heavy lunch. Again, the food wasgood.The next morning we explored a bit around the resort as the rains had stopped. The resortas I mentioned above was beautiful and it also has a pool. We went for breakfast but wasdisappointed that there was no buffet due to the lack of customers there. Instead we couldorder food in an à la carte format. The selection was huge and maybe even more than the buffet.We had a little of everything in the Indian selection and some noodles. All of it was good, exceptthe sambhar. We ordered a bottle of water to drink because we don't prefer the normal water.As we were about to leave the restaurant we were presented with a bill. I was confused becausethe breakfast was complimentary. When I checked the bill, I found out that they charged mefor the water bottle! Usually at buffet breakfasts bottled water is complimentary. Never haveI been charged extra for mineral water for a buffet anywhere where I've stayed across theworld. I don't mind paying for it, and I did because that may be the policy here (but I'd argue thatit is a very weird one). They could've atleast told us that it was chargeable when we ordered itinstead of surprising us with a bill in the end! That was very unprofessional.We went back to our rooms to pack as we were checking out that morning. Before we went wecalled the manager and showed him all the problems in the room. He took it well and accepted itas positive criticism. He said he was sorry and that it was unacceptable that the rooms werein this state. He was very friendly. I appreciate the time he took to hear me out and to accepttheir mistakes. I've had many instances at other places where such criticism wasn't taken well,but the manager was extremely professional.Upon departure, the hotel staff presented us with some souvenir. They gave the women ahandmade pouch with some jewellery and the they gave the men the traditional hat.The only reason I gave this place 2 stars is mainly because of the friendly staff and the goodfood. The rooms were horrible.I also stayed at the Annapurna Hotel at Kathmandu and I found that this lodge had identicalproblems. The rooms were poor but the staff and food were excellent. So is this because of alack of supervision by the officials at the Annapurna group? Maybe. But whatever is the case therenovation and maintenance of the rooms are well overdue.I do not recommend staying here from my experience.

Stuti, Shloka, Tara and Dr. Saroj Basnyet enjoyed comfortable and memorial stay at Fish Tail Lodge, by Hotel Annapurna located in Pokhara, Nepal from 4 July to 7 July 2019.  The view of the Phewa Tal and Mountains from the deck was breathtaking during the morning hours especially during the sun rise.    The location of the Hotel could not be better.  It is surrounded by Phewa Tal Lake and dense green forests. Views of nature are gorgeous and relaxing. Walking on the wide green grasses was very healthy.    We enjoyed the wide varieties of delicious sumptuous breakfast laid out.  Lunch and dinner were delicious.  Swimming pool and gym are inviting and relaxing.  Rooms are cosy and comfortable.   Staffs are hospitable and eager to make guests comfortable.  If you are planning a trip to Pokhara, Nepal it is recommended that you enjoy the luxuries of five star accommodations in Fish Tail Lodge.

Fish Tail Lodge is an absolutely stunning property.  Their location and the romantic raft you must take to and from the property make for a truly special experience.  And while some of the service is outstanding, attentive and warm, some is slow, apathetic and ambivalent.  Despite having some of the poorer service in the poorly air conditioned restaurant, we enjoyed our stay till the final minutes.  When the Lodge had erred and failed to charge us for laundry services after we had paid and were already at the airport, they called us repeatedly even though I offered to email the payment as soon as I returned home.  They even sent someone to the airport despite the fact that I had told them I didn't have enough local currency to pay - which was why I paid my bill by credit card - and would have happily paid the laundry bill too *if* they had included it on my bill.  When their representative came to the airport, my spouse returned through security to meet this person, and offered him all the CAD cash we had with us which was CAD $7 short of the total.  He wouldn't take this money because it was short of the total.  Long story, less long, it was a ridiculous reaction to a mistake THEY made.  It's easy to provide excellent service when things are going smoothly - but we all learn what a business' true service protocol is when things go awry.  Go there and enjoy the uniqueness of the location and raft ride, but be very VERY careful to make sure there are no mistakes or things won't be fun anymore.

An excellent placed Hotel. Staff are prompt, courteous with a smile on face. It's flexible to the needs of the Guests. Small gestures count. When we requested for an Extra bed for our grand child, accompanied came complimentary bottle of water + bath towel. Idea is, taking taking care of need in advance. Would love to come back again with a bigger Group of Us.

My Mum and I came here for a week together after 3 months travelling solo. It was an absolutely gorgeous spot; you felt like you were so far away from anything yet you are 15 minutes walking distance from the town. The restaurant views over the lake are beautiful particularly at sunset. Lovely pool and spa, very very peaceful. The staff were so helpful and friendly; we would definitely recommend!

After an arduous trek our stay at Fish Tail for 5 nights in Pokhara was a perfect rest and recharge. Very tranquil location right on Lake Fewa with beautiful view from our room 18 (heritage room highly recommended).  Staff very pleasant. Location was across the lake from the main shopping area accessible by a 24 hour boat which added to the charm and atmosphere. A really established hotel with great service and good food and a lovely atmosphere. Rooms are simple and well appointed.  The manager Mr Lama was very helpful at all times. We are very glad we were recommended to Fish Tail Lodge and would return next time we are in Pokhara!

We loved this place,  we spent 7 days in Pohkara and this hotel made a diference. The rooms are  very  nice, the place  is  really  charming, the localization  is perfect  and the staff  is very  kindly, we  will come back  for sure.

Family time at the place that has been featured in the bestselling book “1000 Places to See Before You Die” by Patricia Schultz. Located on an isthmus Fish Tail Lodge has the Fewa Lake on one side and lush green forest on the other. One of its unique feature is the shuttle pontoon boat which transports you across to the resort, this novelty is already a start to a great pampering. Machhapuchre- Fish Tail and their reflection on the lake, thus the name Fish Tail, (we weren’t lucky enough to see this due to foggy weather). A place I would recommend as must visit when in Pokhara, an ideal place to unwind & of course tick off your bucket list on 1000 places to see before you die 😊💕👌🏻🏖

Rarely you come across a place like this. A beautiful lakeside resort with the lush mountains and the snow-capped Himalayas as the backdrop, the serene Fewa Lake, the quaint and cozy lodges, the excellent food, but most importantly - the team that makes the experience a truly memorable one. I stayed there briefly but the team made sure that it was exceptional. The Ayurvedic Massage at the Fishtail spa was relaxing - highly recommended. If your travels will lead you to Nepal, make it a point to visit this place and you will never be disappointed. Great thanks to the team led by their very accommodating General Manager Arun. Thank you for taking care of me, and to everyone that visits your property. There will definitely more visits to come. -Eunice

FishTail Lodge Pokhara, Nepal is an excellent lake resort offering mesmerizing scenery and breathtaking views of Fewa Lake and Fish Tail peak. It offers the most luxurious, clean and comfortable living environment in all weathers coupled with the most sumptuous foods and flavours from all continents. Staff at the Fish Tail Lodge is extremely caring and hospitable, particulary Miss Sanju Sharma, the Guests Relation Executive, is an amazing personality who would extend the warmest welcome to the guests besides being always concerned about their comfort and care. She is always running from pillar to post to ensure that the guests are happy and enjoy a peaceful stay at the resort. In a nutshell, this lodge is the best place to stay during visit to Pokhara which is not less than a heaven on earth.

The resort has approx 70 plus room, most are cottage styles and very beautiful architecture. The garden is so well maintained. The best part is the way into and out of the hotel is to cross a small part of the lake, there is a boat which takes 12 people at a time and that part was the best part of the feel of the resort. The food is good too and lots of variety. The service and hospitality were amazing. We were a group of 8 and never had any complaints. Thank you fishtail for making our stay so memorable. P.S. the restaurant is lake facing and on a not so cloudy day we could see the full Annapurna mountain range with all snow-covered peaks from our breakfast table, so make sure to sit outside and watch for the snow covered peaks.

We arrived at Fish Tail Lodge featured in the bestselling book “1000 Places to See Before You Die” by Patricia Schultz and sandwiched between semi natural freshwater Phewa lake , the second largest in Nepal , and the mountains l at 1410 on 11th Nov . Truly speaking ,at that time we were just on the  opposite bank of the lake from where shuttle floats and boats used to  ply to the lodge on a peninsula . We rang a bell and the shuttle float started inching towards us . Two thick nylon ropes were anchored on the opposite banks of the lake . The floatman pulled one rope so that the float moved towards the lodge .Though six months back  I had booked our accommodation in Garden terrace , honouring my one month earlier request the management graciously upgraded our accommodation to Palm Court Deluxe Category .Our room in a quietly tucked away two storeyed Dhaulagiri , was upto the mark as imagined after reading Patricia’s book .  It was very well furnished including electronic safe and other usual amenities . The lodge is visited by not only VVIP foreigner guests but by beautiful , chirping , migrating birds too .  The beautiful gardens , swimming pool , spa , gym , watering hole and Annapurna Base Camp central dining room compete with the serenity offered by the Lake in front and the mountain behind .All the staff were very cooperative and ever smiling . They took utmost care of my 68 years old wife .Whenever we will visit Pokhara , we will stay at Fishtail Lodge only .

Beautiful hotel across the lake. Perfect ending to our week long trek in the Annapurna region.  There is a quick shuttle float ride (sometimes a canoe ride) across the lake to the hotel . You are treated to some of the most spectacular views of the lake and Fishtail mountain.Breakfast is spectacular (loved the freshly squeezed watermelon juice).  Dinner buffet has a wide variety of dishes that will please a wide range of culinary tastes.Neat rooms in little cottages with a lush garden outside.

when you get to this hotel you arrive by a hand pulled ferry,this gives the hotel a quite sense of calm I was lucky enough to stay in room 16 one of the heritage rooms,just wait until dawn when you get great views of Annapurna 2 and fish tail mind blowing.staff and food excellent can't praise it enough would love to return one day

Quite a few descriptions of Pokhara and Fishtail Lodge say its one of the worlds most scenic places. That could be true if your world doesn’t extend beyond the rubbish strewn chaos of Kathmandu or Delhi.The views are good but Pokhara, like most ‘towns’ I’ve passed through in India and Nepal, leaves a lot to be desired. If half built, breeze block, badly constructed houses, terrible roads, huge open quarries and rubbish are termed as scenic then I stand corrected. When we were there mist obscured the distant mountains all the time which may have prejudiced my opinion of the place.The hotel is reached down a side road past parked tour buses to a small jetty where a ferryman transfers you 12 at a time, by hand pulling, across 20 metres of water. The banks are covered in litter. The Lodge is not on an island despite some descriptions. It's just the other side of a small inlet on the lake.Once on the Lodge side a series of steps lead up to a small Reception area. There are nice views along the lake from the lodge.The 'lodges’ are quite poorly built, but adequate, with badly fitting, sticking doors, a minibar fridge that switches on and off all night and a safe that wasn’t bolted down. Duvet was very heavy. However, they each have a small garden at the front with a couple of chairs and a table. Wifi around dining areas was free but in your room was an extra $10 a day. Most hotels now include this for free. Very mean for a hotel with rooms costing an average of $100 a night.Dinner was buffet style in the restaurant and consisted of mainly European food such as crudites, vegetable soup, spaghetti bolognaise, chicken casserole, ratatouille, grilled fish and boiled vegetables. The 'Nepalese’ dishes were boiled rice and the blandest, most tasteless, dahl 'curry’ I’ve ever had. Dessert was chocolate mousse and pineapple gateau. As a visitor to Nepal I felt cheated. Do they really think this is what we want ?Breakfast was similar to most in this part of India/Nepal. Buffet style with an egg counter.Lots of trekking/outdoor shops across the lake, most selling fake North Face etc gear.In summary, quite pleasant but don’t assume its going to be like the English Lake District.

Staying at Fishtail was part of a tailor made itinerary  for us.Getting to it was quite an experience but the setting was beautiful. Just a shame it was beautifully warm...and the pool was not open.....could so have done with a swim. Massage is a must!! Just amazing.....but not a great deal to do and 3 nights was a night too long.....as the food was not brilliant. 5am start to see the mountains was great but the 5am start for the drive back to Kathmandu.......long day.

It was beyond our expectations.The scenic beauty inside as well as surroundings are very exciting and enjoyable. The staff is quite courteous and accommodating. The food in the room was hot and tasty.The breakfast was well laid in the restaurant.

So far ok the location is good. Breakfast is good with lots of choice also dinner is tasty. But the room are so small with wet bedsheets. Ac not work well. Toilet is so small with dirty towels. I won't stay again here.

We have travelled to many Asian countries so we are not naive when it comes to hotels. The location of this hotel is just beautiful. We found the majority of the staff very friendly and helpful. The rooms are a little dark and could possibly do with some sprucing up as they are a little tired looking. So overall we were happy with our stay except for one thing that soured the whole experience. My husband changed some money for me at reception. The first mistake he made was not counting it there and then but he trusted the staff of this hotel. Second mistake I made was not to count the money before I added it to the small amount I already had. I couldn't remember how much I had in my wallet but I had calculated with the money exchange how much I should have and it was well short. We went back to reception and we were not aggressive but polite and my husband told the desk manager I think you have made a mistake. He was adamant that he hadn't and was quite rude. His tone was accusatory and he said this is not the money I gave you. Yes we said I have put some of my own money in the pile. He then gave us a breakdown of the notes he had given us and I was able to work out that he had short changed us 10,000NRP. Maybe he did make a genuine mistake or maybe not. However I did not like his rudeness and unwillingness to help us come to an amicable resolution. My husband had nothing to gain by pretending we did not get the right amount we are honest, generous hard working people. I won't stay here again.

We, a family of three spent 6 days at the Fishtail, nestled in the Phewa lake with the Annapurna Mountains in front and the Raniban forest as a backdrop. This place gives you  a taste of everything. if you are looking for a place to sit back and relax, then this is the one. There are many day treks which can be organised. The travel from the shore to the hotel is thru an interesting rope mechanism on the raft floating on drums.. the staff is extremely courteous and the service is very prompt. Trekked 2 days for birding with Hari who is a very experienced and enthusiastic birder. He made sure that we saw the shiny babbler bird as Pokhra is the only place in Nepal where it is found...do visit the International Museum of mountaineering, which not many talk about but is very informatiive... The month of May when we travelled was a little warm and winter months are preferable for travel. The Fishtail peak and Annapurna snow clad peaks were seen very well from the Palm court rooms and we had the luck of seeing them on a full moon night as well.  The wifi was available for only one device in the room and being three of us, it was a little inconvenient but all in all a great experience...

Fishtail has always been an amazing destination for decades. The entry by log boats, the immaculate service, and the location is absolutely ideal to take in the stuning beauty of Pokhara.The swimming pool, amazing spa, add to the already stunning bit of land on the lake.

We got a great room, loved the service in the property. The swimming pool also is well maintained.But they make a couple of mistakesA) dinner buffet closes at 9 B) the restaurant closed at 9.30C) there is no room Sevice in the night.So if you are hungry and get to the property late you will struggle through till breakfast next morning.Also given that the property is across the lake any need to get some food is atleast a 15 minute river cross + walk across... Fairly a significant effort when you are hungry and sleepy. So you stay in a fancy place but stay hungry. To be fair to them wen we called first time they said kitchen closed and when we calls again and literally begged for food a sandwich was sent our way!But the buffet breakfast is decent.Best property by location on the lakeside

Whilst the location and hotel rooms are pretty and surrounded by well kept gardens, I was disappointed to see the swimming pool empty, have two towels when there were three of us and feel like we were secondary importance to the Chinese tour group. Our desires for dinner were swatted aside and we were limited in what we could choose. It was pretty bland too for curry! Disappointed also by the fact we could not see the mountains due to what we were told was weather but appeared more like pollution because of fuel crisis. Hotel not very central either. It was 15-20 minutes walk (albeit a nice one) to get into heart of town

We stayed here for one night after a 5-day trek in the Annapurna foothills in October 2015.  The arrival by small boat across a narrow part of the lake makes it feel relaxing and other-worldly even before you check in!  We had one of the "Palm Court" rooms on the first floor, which looked out towards the mountains across the gardens.  Although spacious, the room decor was a little dated but this is the only fault in a hotel that offered excellent hospitality and service.  We asked for laundry service at noon to be returned the same day, and it was.  We ate lunch and dinner in the bar and restaurant, where service was good and the food really excellent.  We can recommend the Nepalese curries!  Breakfast also was hearty and varied and with the added benefit of a lake and mountain view from the windows and terrace. We were sorry not to have explored the town but the effects of the trek plus a 3 hour thunderstorm meant relaxing in the hotel was our only option.  Fortunately, it was quiet and comfortable for this!  A very nice place to wind down.

The Fish Tail Lodge is perfectly situated in Pokhara within easy walking distance of Lakeside attractions.  Our stay was fantastic though we found ourselves in a place thinking that it is starting to show its age a bit.  Food prices can be a bit high at times but no one would likely argue that it is one of the nicest hotels in the city.  Service was great but know that there is a short distance you have to travel via a staffed pontoon raft to get from the main hotel to the street.  Our daughter loved that though.

Fish Tail lodge has managed to keep its 1970s - 1980s ambience yet still feel fresh and clean. The location is very peaceful as you need to cross the lake on a raft/ferry to get to and fro. The garden view rooms are part of the original hotel and although the decor is a little dated, the rooms are very comfortable and clean and very charming. The pool is worth a dip after trekking or shopping. The restaurant has great views of the lake.

I have stayed at Fishtail many times and always enjoy the people, the food and the atmosphere. There is very good birding around the lodge and in the gardens. Its a quiet place but with superb morning and evening views of the mountains. I have stayed here every 2 years for about 20 years

We were three of us staying at the hotel, including a 2-yr-old kid. Our experience at this hotel was fabulous - everything from the check-in, to our room service requests, as well as special meal requests for our kid were attended to immediately. The staff was extremely courteous, and this was evident not only in the way they greeted us or attended to us, but also in the way they went the extra mile to always make us comfortable. We were there for new year's and the news years eve dinner was amazing! There was something for everybody! The views from our room were fabulous, the entry to the hotel, and the whole lake-side charm was exactly what we were looking for. Overall, a great hotel, and should without a doubt be the best property in Pokhara!

was in Pokhara for one night to visit friends and stayed at this place, 2nd time in 11 years. it is a high-end place that is quite well maintained and has plenty of options for relaxing, spa, swimming, gym and plenty of beautiful flowers and nice plants to just sit and relax and read. the hotel restaurant is also facing Phewa lake and the Annapurna range

Ideal location, right on the the Fewa Lake, an advantage this lodge has over all the hotels along the lake side.  The rooms with the Lake view is awesome.  The property is well taken care of.  We got very good services from the house keeping staff and especially the restaurant staff.  He made us feel that we are special.   The food is fabulous.  Its highly recommended to stay in this wonderful lodge.

The service is good the rooms are ok as per Nepal standards but can't compare to International 5 Star standards. The breakfast was very basic and needs more variety. The Service in the restaurant and the hotel itself was very good.

Superb location... Surrounded by mountains on the backdrop and lake on the front side... To use a boat to reach the resort... Amazing concept... Restaurant serving some authentic Nepalese n world cuisine and cocktails with a fire place at the centre... Friendly staff... Give u a rating of 4 but wudve been 5 if their pool was functional too... But anyways.. After spending some quality time here I'm completely satisfied with wat I received.... N highly recommend this place..

Whilst somewhat belated, we visited in October 2014, I was glad to see that the hotel was still operating following the earthquake in Nepal. From the gentle raft journey, and the skilfully coiled rope to the beautiful mature landscape gardens, this is the perfect place to relax after travelling around Nepal.A special thanks to the staff at the front desk who sorted out a problem with our booking, the fault of our agent in Kathmandu. We were lucky enough to have one of the rooms in the bungalows overlooking the lake, which I would thoroughly recommend.Whilst it is only a fairly short walk from the hectic centre of Pokhara, much better way of getting there is by one of the small boats which are moored just across the bay.The food in the restaurant is ok, we did have a very hearty thukpa (soup) on one of tables just outside our room with a splendid view across Phewa Lake. Some reviews may state that the hotel is rather dated, but I must admit that I'm glad that it's not had a slick modernisation to turn it in to just another resort hotel.

Had an overnight stay on July 3, 2015 on way back to Kathmandu from Lumbini. I was part of the Press Club of India delegation on invitation from Nepal Tourism Board. It was an exciting experience to board a floating platform on the lake to reach this amazing property. Surrounded by lush green forests, this resort has a serene setting with spectacular view of Fewa lake and  snow- capped Himalayan mountain ranges. A great place to relax and unwind and I enjoyed every bit of my stay. However, my regret was that the stay was too short to thoroughly enjoy the property.Would love to visit again for at least  2N/3D stay.

To escapee the shaking grounds in Kathmandu we booked rooms at Fish Tail for a long weekend and enjoyed every bit of the stay. From the restaurant deck the view of the lake and the mountains  is spectacular and as the food also is both interesting and well done this became a favorite spot. The rooms are nice and clean (and on the ground!) and we really enjoyed the pool and the quick and attentive service by the staff. The short boat ride to the hotel is part of the joy and you do not feel the hustle of the Pokhara night life.

It's a wonderful property, nice location and excellent staff. Each and every staff you meet during the day greets you. Food is okay however they need to add more variety to the buffet breakfast. The resort is located at other side of the lake and you have to board a platform which is towed by a person on the other side to travel to & fro the hotel. Its a resort type hotel with cottages. Though they have one building with rooms but I would prefer a cottage room any day, it is also cheaper than the building's room. If you are in Pokhara you must stay at this property. Having said that I would suggest some points to the management and hope they pay heed to it.Furniture/decor is probably as old as the hotel itself. Bathrooms have been modernised but nothing seems to have been done to the room. It desperately calls for renovation.There are no room slippers. I think it will be unbearable to walk on the floor without a slipper. It must be there in the room.I understand it's more of a resort but so dim lighting in the room at least is not justified. God forbid if anyone has to work/write something.Items need to be added to the breakfast as mentioned before.The resort was quite full when I was there. Some sort of entertainment activity should be organised in the evening as the guest has nowhere to go. Even a simple bonfire could help.The resort, location and staff is so good you just need to fine tune a few things to match the Thai standards, whose resorts I think are fantastic. Me and my kids did paragliding for the first time in our lives in Pokhara and our guides were European. We had a really really good adventure. Being a sunny day view of the mountains from high up in the air was fantastic.I stayed in March'15 before the earthquake. I pray that the hotel and staff were untouched by the devastation.

This has to be the most enviable location in Pokhara. The Fish Tail Lodge offers guests spectacular views across Phewa Lake and the natural forest. This Pokhara Hotel is in a league of its own when it comes to locality.Access across to the Fish Tail Lodge is by boat. Expertly handled by the hotel staff the short trip just sets the tone for what is a most unique setting. With natural forest and spectacular gardens the entrance is just fabulous. But it is the views from the deck that are just unbeatable.The rooms however are in need of a refurbishment. They are adequate but very dated. The guest air-conditioned rooms are en-suite and have the basics but what would place this property in a different league is if they made an investment and jazzed them up. But it is sitting on the deck, looking out over the Fewa Lake with the Himalayan Mountains as a backdrop, when one realises what a special place this really is. Just, simply unbelievable. The restaurant food was good and the service was really great. The waiter staffs were friendly and efficient.The Fish Tail Lodge in Pokhara is definitely a good choice for your stay in Pokhara. Located next to Lakeside you are close enough to enjoy the buzz of the town and later retreat to the solitude of a remarkable location to enjoy a sundowner overlooking pristine bush, a spectacular lake and the majestic Himalayan Mountains.

I was staying at Fishtail lodge when the earthquake struck. I decided to stay until I managed to get a flight out.The staff carried on with their normal routine despite the quakes continuing however nothing was too much trouble for them. This was welcome as it eased the stress of an extremely difficult situation. The lodge is in a beautiful setting and the little bungalows were delightful situated in a lovely garden. The food was very good and views stunning. Thank you for as pleasant a stay as possible, and the delicious sandwiches for my travel to kathmandu, I needed them they fed me for 2 days. I look forward to returning in the future.

We spent 2 nights with family at Fish Tail Lodge in April 2015, and absolutely loved the experience. The lodge sits in the lap of the Himalayas, offering breathtaking sights of various snowcapped peaks of three ranges, Machhapuchchhre (or Fishtail), Annapurna and Dhaulagiri, the 2 latter being 8000-ers.Our first morning, we rushed out at 6.30am for a glimpse of these beauties and weren't disappointed one bit. When we arrived the previous evening, little did we realize the sight awaiting us. The cloud cover throughout the day ensures you see no more that the smaller green peaks. So push yourself that extra bit and catch the morning 7am breakfast service, for a sight that makes the long drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara truly worth the effort.  The breakfast doesn't disappoint nor do the rooms which are clean, well decorated and airy. WiFi services are very limited inside the rooms, so leave behind the office and the outside world before you step in. The reception has better connectivity though.The attached travel desk had the best deal on the adventure sports activities we needed, and handled our queries and planned our afternoon well. We hired the paragliding company the lodge recommended and met some really good instructors, with brilliant stories to share and also restaurant recommendations. All in all a great way to spend a holiday.

This hotel has by far the best view in Pokara! The small boat over the water is a fun way to reach the hotel. The rooms are clean and adequate and the staff helpful. The location is just perfect. Only negative feedback is breakfast is expansive ( for nepal prices) $15 per person and the wifi should be free. It is only free in the dining room, in bedrooms and around the hotel is cost almost $4 per hour. This is something that is now free everywhere you visit and the management should really update their views on giving free wifi.

Check in took more than half an our as they had confusion on type of room I booked through Expedia. Eventually room was allotted and was taken to room only to find room is not ready. Hence House Keeping Staff was called to prepare the room which again took almost half hour till the time we were made to wait outside the room.In case you look for Smiling and Happy Faces, certainly FishTail Lodge is not the place to stay, staff never smiles and  aren't warm.Untrained waiters in Restaurant is something you have to live with. They will not assist you in ordering food, will keep food basket in your plate, wont serve food in your plates. You will keep looking for them for service and reordering, so please don't mind your food getting cold while you look for waiters. Food taste isn't great but very expensive. Dinning here may be perfect recipe for spoiling your dinner or lunch. Better option can be... take a stroll and you will find plenty of places who serve better food and at 1/4th of price. And at last, please carry your own umbrella, don't expect hotel staff to offer umbrella if it rains rather have trust on your feet and run. Don't expect evening/ turn around service. Room dining plates wont get cleared after waiting for half an hour so putting them out of room may be better idea. Bellboy will not show up at check out time.At the time of booking never thought will have this kind of experience for bomb kind of money (compared to most of the places in Pokhara) I spent.

I have been visiting Nepal since 1969 but only recently stayed at the Fishtail (2013 & 2014). It is without question the best hotel I have ever stayed in Nepal and the only one (in my experience) that has local ambiance combined with great location, great food and service for a reasonable price. All considered, this is one of the best hotel I have ever stayed in anywhere!Located on Phewa Lake it is pleasantly quiet with spectacular views of Machhapuchhare (Fishtail Mountain) and the Annapurna range and yet is very close to one of the main tourist shopping areas with a variety of restaurants all within easy walking distance. It is also very close to the airport which gives it added convenience. The hotel is beautifully laid out with different lodges and buildings surrounded by lawns and a profusion of flowers and plants.

Our family stayed at Fish Tail Lodge and were enchanted by the location, the amazing service, and wonderful meals. We kayaked while watching the sunrise and enjoyed an exciting paraglide ride in the afternoon.

I live in Florida and have traveled widely. I came to India to do polio immunizations with members of Rotary, I found the people of Nepal to be the nicest people I have ever met. I enjoyed using the free wi-fi in the restaurant and I loved the omelettes they made for me at breakfast. I liked the breakfast buffet! At 79 and will be 80 in May I appreciated having room 3 near the restaurant. The room was spacious and had a nice clean shower. I had a refrigerator to chill my water. I made instant coffee in the room. i even had a newspaper to read and TV. I didn't have to worry about my large suitcase. The gentlemen took my arm and helped me on and off the raft. I enjoyed watching the sun rise while at the top of the mountain. We took a short flight to Kathmandu. Suggest one go to Chitwan National Park and stay in the new jungle lodge too.

We stayed here for two nights and could not find fault. The welcome, the rooms, the restaurant, the staff were just delightful and nothing was too much trouble. We loved the location and delicious food. We will return!!

Beautiful lodge on the lake with the Annapurna Mountains as a backdrop.  You can see "Fishtail peak" while relaxing on the lovely deck outside the dining room.I was here with friends relaxing after a busy pace with work the 2 weeks prior to coming to Pokara.  This was a great place to relax and shopping, just a short walk from boat landing, was great!

Lovely room well appointed overlooking the garden.  We were extremely well looked after.  Good food and good service.  Enjoyed the spa as well.  Well worth the visit and the long drive to get there.  First view of the himalayas.

To go to this hotel you have to cross the beautiful Phewa lake. It was a wonderful experience! We booked the garden rooms and loved the two days! We were all girls and had a great time. Even used the spa! The view of the Annapurna from the hotel, esp from the restaurant is breathtaking. Decor is really nice. The reception staff, the ladies at the spa, the gardeners; everybody was very friendly and always ready to help with a smile.The only thing that we didn't like much about the hotel was the breakfast menu. All of us thought it could be better. More variety and a little more flavour perhaps.I would suggest everybody going to Pokhara to stay in this wonderful hotel. Whether you're on your honeymoon, with friends or with family!

Like someone said, you can't improve what's already perfect. Fish Tail Lodge has a wonderful and courteous staff who are prompt and extremely helpful. The rooms and the views are breathtaking. What is unique is the way you need to to this property, you need to ride the raft which is functional 24x7 with the most fascinating method of pulling system. The deck outside the restaurant gives you a fabulous view of the range that strangely appears closer from the lodge than sarangkot which is where you visit to see the sunriseThis is a place you need to put your feet your feet up and just breathe. The flora of the lodge is well maintained and beautifully done. If I could live here forever, I most certainly would.

We did not stay at the lodge but visited for lunch, enjoying the beautiful well kept gardens, whilst waiting for the clouds to lift and reveal the majestic Annapurna range. The service was friendly and prompt,the food was delicious and beautifully presented, and portions were generous! If I return to Pokhara, I would definitely also like to stay at the lodge.

Set away from the busy huddle of Pokhara lakeside, the experience begins with a short float ride on the lake to reach the hotel. The first sight of well-maintained greenery; single-storey round buildings with rooms inside; sweeping lawns. However, the highlight is the eternal sight of the mountains of the Annapurna range, and that unique wonder: the Fishtail mountain. The restaurant serves excellent food; the Tandoori Chicken here is amazing! THIS is the property to stay in Pokhara. Why go elsewhere?!

Fishtail Lodge has three things which are unbeatable in Pokhara;1. Amazing Location2. Great food3. Wonderful staffHighly recommended vocation destination for family holiday. Thank you for your great hospitality......

Recently, I spent overnight at Fish Tail Lodge celebrating Birthday with my family. Among several hotels in Pokhara, i found unique experience of warm hospitality and tranquil environment. Moreover, layout of restaurant, bar and dining place is Perfect. In addition beautiful garden, wonderful Spa and plenty of space for a children to move around. Charismatic wider range of mountain view from the hotel rooms feels natural relaxation early in the morning with birds noise. I recommend to spent at least a night to feel the difference of Pokhara.

Great view, great place and above all excellent people. I have never been to such a nice place all my life. There is a some personal and warm touch by the staff especially the guest relation lady manager - Sonu who makes your stay very special. Food is great. You can see some of the world's tallest snowpeaks right from your room/balcony. I could stay here forever....u know its like that Song of Hotel California - you can check out anytime u want but u can never leave :)

This was our third time visiting the Fish Tail Lodge in the last ten years.  We were happily surprised to see that the standard of clenliness and efficiency were kept up, if not improved. Staff were professional, helpful and kind. The spa is excellent, we are massage- lovers, and the massage we had here, before qnd after our Anapurna trek  was definitely the best we had so far in Nepal.The tranquillity and beauty of the Lake make this hotel really worth visiting, as it sits in the middle of the water, surrounded by the  most beautiful tropical garden and with spectacular views of the Mountains.Higly recommended!

One of the best location in Pokhra.Just amazing place to stay, we could see the Fish Tail peak right from our room.Great place and good food!You would need to cross a small lake to get to the Hotel and it adds bit of thrill to the overall experience.

This little "island" resort is definitely an oasis of tranquillity. Peaceful, clean with friendly management - the team ensures your comfort. This is our third visit in a span of 12 months and we love it more n more.

It's the best place to stay in Pokhara with stunning views if the lake. Rooms are comfortable (I won't say luxurious). I would definitely come back and stay here. Food is average but there are many eating options available outside the resort.

I stayed here for 2 nights with my wife and son that is 17/18 Dec.It was most comfortable stay I had ever had.view is amazing .i don't think any hotel has this kind of location in this area..staff were freindly and helpful, food is good.I recommend all the readers to experience the nature at its best.i will definitely be back.

I happened to meet a chef from this hotel (Anil Poudel) who told me about its unique location (on a small island in Fewa Lake) and the dinner buffet and decided to give it a try. Indeed the hotel has a very tranquil environment and cozy ambiance, and the dinner buffer has a nice mix of Western and Asian food. Service is impeccable and the whole experience is quite satisfactory.

Spoil yourself by having lunch in the fantastic garden surrounding this hotel. Across the lake by punt into the lush gardens with a table by the lake looking at the magical mountains. You pay a little extra but an absolute bargain by western standards. Reasonable food , fantastic service and fantastic setting. Just do it.

Perhaps it is one the unique places in the world where one can enjoy the Himalaya as well as its shadow in the lake simultaneously from a hotel. The front side of the hotel is Fewa lake and back side is lush green forest. It is a full of nature. In addition, I found people are friendly. Rooms are beautifully decorated. Food is full of varieties. The hotel is but a bit costly, so is the food. Internet is very costly. It is not a budget hotel. One should stay there who has money.

We arrived a Fish Tail Lodge afer a long drive from Chitwan, tired and grumpy. We were greeted with beaming smiles and were invited to sit on the sun desk. We were greeted by stunning views of the Himalayas!During Nov-Jan the mornings can be very misty, but usually clear up around 10am. Best times to view the mountains from the deck are between 11am and 3pm.The rooms are slightly old in style, but functional. the plug sockets are multi-national and there is a kettle in the room.There is free wifi in reception and on the desk. Paid wifi is available in the rooms.The restaurant does a wide variety of foods both local and international and there are several vegetarian options.Food prices range from NPR200-950. At the time of writing there were 150 Rupee to the British pound.The gardens are peaceful and a haven for birds. Best birding times are 0800-1000 and 1500-1700 when it starts to get dark.

We visited Pokhara as part of a tour of Nepal. It's a great place in terms of views and walks. But what made the stay for us was this hotel with its lovely position, characterful lodges and good service and food. It was easy to relax here and enjoy late afternoon views of the Annapurna massif from the terrace. Many people not staying at the hotel came over to eat and drink on the terrace because it is simply the best place in town (but not noisy despite the popularity)

A stunning location, being pulled across the lake by raft & greeted warmly by the staff, The grounds are lovely with a nice pool to relax. The rooms, most in circular buildings are comfortable with good bathrooms. Good choice of food in the buffet restaurant & fantastic views of Fishtail Peak from the terraces. A great place to stay.

After walking the Everest base camp walk this was the reward to ourselves.Our experience at fishtail lodge was exceptional from the moment we arrived at the lake edge till we left.The location is stunning, the punt to get across the lake feels almost magical, the rooms are fine, the gardens are wonderful. We enjoyed a number of room service meals from our front veranda overlooking the lake, the food was great just watch the spices. We received complementary wine sweet biscuits and fruit, I am not sure if this is standard but a nice practice. The pool is inviting as is the health spa. All of this is contained on what feels like an island overlooking the lake with snow capped mountains in the background.We used the little row boats to explore the lake and had one drop us off at the base of the monastery walk.

We've been here twice for lunch with our twins. The location is beautiful and our children loved the little boattrip to come there. The food is good but nothing special. The staff is nice, but also tried to let us finish asap. Everything ( incl.toilet ) is very clean!!!

This is an interesting property from the get-go. When you arrive at the hectic landing area in the middle fo town, you are then taken by a hand-pulled ferry to the hotel grounds. Neat.The buildings are spread over a large area. Rooms are quite spacious and nicely decorated, Bathrooms are clean, but small. Grounds staff keep things very clean and orderly. Food is quite good, with a large buffet for breakfast, with an omelet station.

The adventure begins as soon as you land in Pokhara, with a short boat ride across the lake to the lodge. You leave the world on the other side and its nature all the way from here. The resort is flanked on one side by the lake and on the other by towering forest trees. The rooms are spacious yet cozy with a seating area by the window, where i lounged and read my book the whole time. There are so many trees and flowers that the photographer in you will not know when to stop. There is a small, clean pool and a pretty good spa. But the icing on the cake is the staff, courteous, yet never in your way. The cleaning of the property goes on all the time and still you feel as if you are the only one around. A safe place for our 8 year old to move around on her own the whole time.We celebrated our daughter's birthday there and they arranged an eggless cake, on the house for us.  The food was awesome all the time, the yak cheese, the banana split ... though vegetarians have limited choices there. We would love to visit again just to laze around the pool, reading or clicking pictures all day.

Fabulous grounds overlooking the lake accessed by a raft pulled by a boatman. Staff very friendly and helpful and breakfast on the lawn overlooking the lake is a joy..The downside is our room was a bit tired and in need of a refurb, but overall a great hotel.

Accidentally stumbled upon this place while in Pokhara. I was booked at another place for 3 days already. But having seen the settings could not resist. Checked out of the other place and moved to FTL. Hotel needs accessing via hotel's dedicated boat. Lake on one side and woods on the other side , the best view all around. Walking distance to townHigh light of entire stay in Nepal

After 5 days trekking to Pool Hill, the 2 nights we stayed in Fishtail Lodge is the best choice! The hotel has an unique way to get to by a raft. Beautiful landscape, lush garden, and ofcourse the best view/set up to the  magnifique Annapurna Range accross the lake. Early in the morning is the best time of the day to enjoy the view. The restaurant just newly renovated. Food price is quite resonable for a good hotel. Staff is super friendly and helpful. Room is clean.The only minus point for Fishtail Lodge is the interior of room which is quite outdated.  It is a bit pity for this beautiful property.Nevertheless, i really enjoyed the stay in Fishtail Lodge.

The boatman hauled us across to the hotel - the only way to get there. Welcome cocktail on arrival, a swim in the pool to wash off trek residue and then a coffee lakeside, looking across the flower strewn lake towards glorious views of sunset on the Annapurnas. Cabanas are great. Big, comfy, clean and well appointed. The food was only average, though OK and with views like this, not worth travelling elsewhere.

we visited this property second time after a long gap. The property is unmatched with any other in town. Very much in the heart of the city but isolated from noise or any other pollution.Lush green area with views of mountains, quiet lake is what people come here for.The restaurant here serves very good quality Indian cuisine.The only thing lacking is room service which should include service of lunch and dinner also which is presently limited only for drinks and snacks.

Fishtail Lodge is the best property in Pokhra. Its location is unique, you have to reach there by boat, surrounded by hills. Very well maintained property with good swimming pool, colorful garden. Rooms are clean with a good view of Mountains and Fewa lake.

We stayed in Fishtail Lodge in Pokhara from June 11th-June14th, 2014. It is an idyllic location with complete peace and serenity in the surroundings. Access to the resort in also only through a tug-ferry , which makes it quite private and protected. The resort's rooms are slightly old and in heritage style, but they are well maintained and clean. The service in the resort was also exemplary and we enjoyed our stay thoroughly. Our kids also enjoyed the swimming pool, which though small, was clean and well maintained.The best part about this resort is its ideal location in Pokhara which I would say is the best compared to any other in Pohkara.It is an oasis of peace and very serene. Fully recommend this resort to others who are visitingf Pokhara with family.

I with my family stayed at the Fish Tail Lodge, Pokhara, Nepal. The place was beyond what I had thought or imagined it to be. The place gives you an experience beyond words. It was just what I needed to relax. The staff is very prompt and curtious and the food is great. I loved it.

Accessible only by rope-pull raft, the Fishtail Lodge in Pokhara offered a few days relaxation and comparative inactivity at the end of a busy tour of India and Nepal. The location is amazing; on a lake with a view of the Annapurna range from the garden and breakfast area. And whilst it is easy to relax in the seclusion of the lodge there are also things to do if you feel like being more active. There are things to do on the lake, there are places to visit and the mountains are accessible. Pokhara town is also worth a visit and compared to the cities in Nepal are lightly populated and tranquil. It was the perfect way to end the trip and I would return to Fishtail Lodge if I happen to be in that part of the world again.

Stayed for just 1 nite which was an excellent experienceThe natural beauty makes the place a must Visit in the intenary for one and all going to KTMOne shud ideally stay back 2 nites and can get a wholesome experience of the place as it has much to offer within the property area itself.Breakfast was quite a decent spread with Good Quality of Meals.However with slight Improvement in the basic amenities inside the room wud do wondersI.e Condition of the fridge for mini bar was worn out, wardrobes have become old.

The drive from Katmandu is arduous and long. You dodge trucks, buses, motorbikes and people. Fly. Fishtail Lodge is a beautiful place on an island in the lake. The people are very friendly and helpful. My wife was ill when we arrived and people went out of their way to assist. Food good  beds comfortable. Don't miss going to the sunrise.

The location is quite secluded, and the surrounding is beautiful and tranquil. The room is quite spacious, and it is the only hotel I stayed in Nepal that provided TV and bathrobe. However, this hotel seems to rely too much on its reputation, being visited by dignitaries in 1980s and way over priced. For the same price, in England we could expect breakfast and more modern room and equipment (when we were there, the button to switch tap to shower didn't work).

It is a lovely property with  nice sized rooms, mattress that were actually comfortable, a lot of staff to help with anything and a nice little ferry to take you back and forth to mainland which is just across a river. in the morning you get the incredible views of the Annapurnas.That being said it is priced exponentially higher then any property in town and I don't know that it is worth it.  The restaurant and spa also charge western/high prices for everything.To get away with being so much more expensive then anything else in town they need to actually offer much better quality then they have to justify it.It is nice for a treat for 1 night after a trek  to relax and take a good hit shower which is hard to come by in Nepal - but not for anything more then that.

It is the second time I chose Fish Tail Lodge, everything is nice as before. You will find yourself in a beautiful garden, which is surrounded by Fewa Lake. You can spend whole day on the lakeside, under the tree,  facing the Fishtail mountain. The staffs here are very helpful. Our requirements were settled timely and perfectly. I still remember one of the staff, Niraj Kummar, a young man with warm smile, who helped us several times. Thanks again. I love here and I'd like to recommend you to stay here and enjoy yourself.

We didn't stay in the resort but went for lunch with my friends. The view from the restaurant garden was amazing, food was great and service was excellent and personalized. The food & beverage manager was so courteous, he showed us the property. Head of the governments and head of the states from several countries have stayed there.

We travelled to Pokhara, Nepal to attend the Annupurna 100 and stayed at the most wonderful hotel. The staff were all gracious and knowledgeable. Nothing was too much trouble and all requests were followed up within minutes. They even gave us a complimentary driver to and from the race venue. At Fishtail you can relax, recharge, and enjoy the majestic view of the Annupurna ranges, I can't speak highly enough of how special they made us feel! The villas and gardens used to be owned by the king of Nepal and its very reasonably priced, just ask when you get there, as if not full they may be able to offer a deal (if you are lucky).

We've just returned from a family holiday in Nepal, which included two nights at the Fishtail Lodge in Pokhara.  Adults and children (ages 8 and 3) had a very good time.  A nice, comfortable and well-appointed room; very good restaurant with excellent selection (although no small portions/reduced prices for children); and an absolutely stunning location on a forested island in Phewa Lake.  Very friendly and courteous staff.  Beautiful gardens.  Highly recommended and a very good base for exploring the surrounding area.

Outstanding location and views.......probably the best views I saw the entire visit with plenty to do nearby and at the location. Like stepping back in time to a different age with all the amenities one would want.

We have our 1st honeymoon and anniversary every year in Fishtail and it has never disappointed us.Me and my husband is so happy and satisfied with the professional service from the General Manager (jb rana if not mistaken)and Manager (Kiren) and also all the staff in the hold fishtail logde to make us feel so welcome.I will surely return.If everyone want to have a perfect holiday definetely please choose fishtail lodge for your accomodation.Once again thank you all the management staff in the Fishtail.See you all next time for our anniversary.

perfect place for a perfect occassion.....The front office staff named Niraj was just simply amazing...He was so helpful and kind....He gave us a great deal for my birthday stay at one of the cottage room(room #7)....He also gave me wifi free for which i'm highly thankful to him....The restaurant rocks...We were not able to find good indian food anywhere in the town....This place on my birthday gave me the best indian lunch and dinner...prices at the restaurant are a little expensive but worth the quality....A must stay here!!!

I did not stay there but decided to visit for lunch. They have indoor & outdoor seatings. It was sunny day in January and I just loved it. Filling up my tummy looking at the Lake & the mountains and the colorful birds chirping away. It was worth it. Friendly restaurant staffs, good service & good food.The ferry takes you to the Lodge crossing the lake :-) enjoyed it.

After a week of roughing it in Nepal, my son suggested we change plans and head to Pokhara. What a great idea!! 5 of us stayed for 2 nights at the Lodge and we loved it! The staff is very attentive. We enjoyed massages at the spa, rented boats, went paragliding, and explored the many shops in town. The rooms are nice and the food and service at the restaurant was excellent. TIP: If you decide to rent a boat, opt for the kayaks! The wooden canoes weigh a ton!!

We stayed in this hotel for two nights.We had lovely vegetarian meals cooked by chef Raj.He came to ask what kind of vegetarian meal we wanted which we thought was very nice.He cooked a perfect Gujarati meal for us.At reception Niraj was very helpful.The raft crossing staff were very courteous and always had a smile even at midnight.We were pointed out to various tropical trees with lovely fruits.The best thing about this hotel is its location.From the garden you have a perfect view of the Fishtail  and we saw paragliders from the terrace.

Very good service and very friendly staff:) The food was great! The view too. We really enjoyed our time here. There were shops very close by and easy to reach.The rooms were also very clean and nice.

You cross Fewa Lake by boat or ferry without a motor to get there. Natural vegetation and very beautiful gardens. In the restaurant, the breakfast that is included is very good as well as the a la carte meal service: a good, excellent presentation. The pool, spa and gym area are also nice. The rooms are comfortable and very clean. There is also a tourist information and services kiosk inside the hotel which is useful because in Pokhara there are several adventure activities that can be done and they can guide you there if you do not want to go to agencies in the city center. Their staff is very friendly and cooperative. World personalities such as members of royal families and politicians have stayed there over time. I recommend it.

The hotel is spectacular! They are all very friendly, the food is very delicious, it would taste and varied. The breakfast is very complete, there is everything and they prepare an omelette for you on the spot. And the best thing is the contact with nature with its beautiful views.

Beautiful location on the lake, boat transport with a raft-like ferry or rowing boat. Great food and friendly staff. Drinks are quite expensive, probably in line with the hotel category. The only downside? The water in the pool is too cold, but that's understandable, it's the end of December and we're in the northern hemisphere at the foot of the Himalayas 🤣. So everything's good 😃🏔🇳🇵

As I have commented in some other cases, for this hotel the five stars in the rating are not enough to express the excellence that, for our taste, it presents.Located in Phewa Lake, Pokhara, to access it you cross a canal by raft or boat, which are open 24 hours a day, allowing a unique environment that provides tranquility despite being close to the busiest area. from the city.The layout of the cabins is very original, immersed in beautiful gardens and with incredible views of the lake and the mountains of the Annapurna Range, highlighting the Fishtail (Machapuchare) that gives its name to the hotel.The spacious rooms, with all the comforts, very clean and comfortable, allowing an excellent rest after the beautiful walks that can be taken nearby.Very good breakfasts and an excellent restaurant with a varied and very rich offering, where the chef himself gave us information about the different dishes, while Prakash was always attentive to our requirements, as were all the waiters, always serving us with warmth. Nepali proverbial.We must also highlight the warmth and attention to the passenger from the rest of the staff, both those who were in charge of cleaning, and the head garden manager who explained to us the characteristics of some of the many plants that make up it, Orson (one of his assistants), reception and I don't want to forget the people in charge of crossing us by raft or boat to the city, all with a common denominator: always with a smile on their lips.I only find one “disadvantage” of this Lodge… it is very difficult to leave it to go out for walks…

Great rooms similar to a small bungalow in the middle of a beautiful garden landscape. Possibility of eating on the restaurant terrace with a direct view of the lake. The breakfast buffet is exceptionally good!
Very pleasant place among birds and flowers on the banks of Lake Phewa. Attentive service especially from Gana Raj, Sagun Shahi, Gam Bahadur and Indu.Very pleasant tea and dinner by the lake.

expensive for Pokhara but you get a rooftop terrace with a panoramic view, air-con that works, cosy when its winter, a good breakfast and quality staff. Choose the upper floors for that view.Repeat visitor for the last 5 years, says it all really...........

The Hotel Glacier is a wonderful value. My boyfriend and I stayed here for three nights and each day we started with a delicious made-to-order breakfast. The omelettes, seasoned potatoes, and lattes were stand-outs and the service was friendly and attentive. Our last evening we also savored a scrumptious wood-fired pizza from the Hotel Glacier Harbor Restaurant and sat out in the delightful patio near a large fire pit. One of the best aspects of the Hotel Glacier is the central location in the Lakeside neighborhood of Pokhara near many boutique shops and restaurants and adjacent to picturesque Phewa Lake. The fantastic location is combined with friendly and knowledgeable reception staff who were very helpful when I needed to use their phone on multiple occasions to adjust flights due to a family emergency.
