The concierge also allowed me to check out late, with no additional charge, which worked perfectly with catching a late afternoon flight. Another standout quality of the Hotel Glacier is the amazing terrace on every floor. We stayed on the sixth level and we took in the sunset each evening. The sunrises were even better as the Annapurna and Fishtail mountain peaks are clearly visible and basking in the morning glow.

The Glacier Hotel is the most modern and up to date hotel in Pokhara. The rooms are of amazing quality with plenty of space and roomservice of highest standard. Their balcony has what I believe to be the best view of Pokhara and the Phewa lake. Definitely the best place to stay when visiting Pokhara!

The Glacier hotel is a very detail oriented establishment. The owner is very present and attentive to your every need. The rooms are very clean and modern. The resturantt serves great food and the best coffee in town. The kitchen lives up to European standards in regards to cleanliness.  Overall this hotel is, in my humble opinion, the best in Pokhara.

The Glacier is a lovely hotel situated on the lakeside. The staff and owner are very friendly and attentive. Nothing is too much trouble. Rooms are spacious and had great Mountain View’s. The bar, restaurant and outside courtyard are perfect areas to escape the huddle and bustle of the main strip. Great food and a selection of local beers made this a perfect place to rest and recovery after our trekking on the Mardi Himal. Pokhara is a wonderful city which we will definitely return to.

Greatly located with very original concept and decoration. Complimentary airport pick with a driver who was of good fun.Very helpful staff, both at restaurant and front desk. We appreciated the help in organizing tour.Finally the room was beautiful, comfortable and with a view on snowcaped mountains. Thank you Rajendra and team

Kudos to all the staff here, especially Mr Sunil the manager, Sushmita & Pushpa at reception, Sharmila and also Shyam who served us  at breakfast (awesome brekkie here) with warmth and smiles during our week stay. They are professional and always proactive,  we even got an upgrade into the Honeymoon suite and deluxe room and we felt completely safe and immensely enjoyed this quaint, beautiful hotel with the lovely rooftop views of the lake and mountains. Only the hot water was a bit fiddly but no other complaints, the bathrooms were comfortable and rooms spacious and clean. It's close enough to the action but comfortably tranquil from the hustle and bustle. Previously, we stayed at Temple Tree but the experience this time at Glacier was far superior. Keep it up!

I can't recommend this place enough. The location was perfect (lakefront but with mountain views from the upper floors), easy walking to shops and restaurants. The hotel itself was clean, well-decorated, and the A/C, wifi, and water pressure were all excellent. And all this is not to mention the kindness and helpfulness of the staff, managers, and owner, who not only made my stay comfortable but also helped to quickly and easily arrange a trek when my original booking fell through. Glacier was wonderful, and I will definitely look to stay here again on my return to Pokhara.

I have stayed at this hotel 3 times in April 2019 and May 2022, and I would definitely choose it again the next time that I visit Pokhara. The rooms are clean, spacious and very comfortable. The air conditioning works great and is very quiet. A big plus is that the bathroom actually contains a full tub with shower, rather than the usual showers in the bathroom at that always flood the entire bathroom floor in most other Nepal hotels. The service staff are always available and very friendly helpful. Wifi works great in the rooms. The food is excellent at breakfast, lunch and dinner. It is superbly located across the street from Phewa Lake and very near a broad variety of shopping and dining opportunities.

We stayed two nights at the Glacier and couldn’t fault the service or the hospitality here. Sunil, the manager, pulled out all the stops: he found us the best room for our needs and helped us arrange our long awaited trip to Muktinath. Nothing was too much trouble. All the staff, including the owner, were a delight to deal with and customer service was excellent. The location was perfect for us - lakeside but in a quieter part of town so we got a good night’s sleep too!

No reason to change the review I made in 2018 - in a good way. Stayed a week here in Jan this year. Scrupulously clean, well equipped with helpful competent staff. Good food. Good value for money, quiet location but near enough to the centre and places to eat to be convenient

Glacier is one the best hotel with spa  in Pokhara. I stayed almost a month there and every morning i woke with a beautiful view of fishtail mountain and fewa lake. I spent my 1 month holiday in a paradise and felt like my home. Hotel and restaurant service was excellent, exceptionally clean and amazing food from Harbour. Staffs were very friendly and hotel manager Sunil even helped me with some paper work that i needed for some official reason. Highly recommend this place and next time as well i will be staying in this hotel in pokhara for sure and still missing Harbour’s menu, esp breakfast.Anyone looking forward for a clean, safe and good hotel to stay in pokhara with amazing food, then this is the one guys. Andrian G.

A beautiful hotel to stay in: decor is stylish yet cosy;  serene view out to the lake; friendly staff; great breakfasts; rooms have everything you would need, including a decent sized bath and oh so luxurious beds...and sunlight. And there was no sound of construction going on anywhere!

I didn’t stay there but during the current lock down time in Nepal they offer free meals for foreign people. You can can have either a vegetarian curry or a panini. It’s simple and delicious food and more than kind and hospitable from the hotel to offer free lunch. I‘m very thankful for that opportunity. The staff who gives out the meals is also very open and kind. Thanks a lot and have a good time, hopefully the situation will get better soon. All the best 🙏🏼

We stayed at the glacier for three nights in mid March. Wonderful hotel. Staff were so friendly, room lovely, tasty food and the bar is great for a relaxing drink at end of the day. We did both the morning sunrise and evening sunset trips. Both were amazing and well recommended. Owner is really friendly and takes a really hands on approach to to running the hotel. Would definitely stay again.

Nice food nice rooms but it is in the insider of lakeBut i love all of the members of hotel they are familiarI love the beds and its very nice its decorative and rooms are so clean and healthy Rooftoo view is nice

Unfortunately no big fire so room was quite cold. Nice design and ambience though . Extensive menu with lots of international choice and food was adequate. Deserts were amazing and good coffee. Very keen waiting staff. Probably one of the better choice restaurants and good central location

The location is on the quieter end of the main road but across from the lake. The hotel is lovely and the staff were wonderful! Can't say enough nice things about the people who work there.The rooms are big, great decor, beds are comfortable, bathroom is okay.The restaurant is great. They say they they specialize in Mediterranean food but their Nepali food is amazing! Omelettes are excellent. They try hard to give guests the best experience.Take advantage of booking excursions with them. They arrange for everything. We enjoyed it so much we extended our stay!

We had a very enjoyable stay at the Glacier during NYE.We had the Honeymoon Suite, which is the only room on the top floor, and it was really nice!There is a convertible AC in the room, which was really important as the temperatures in winter are freezing.We booked the room on the hotel website, and all reservations made on their website have 2 tours included in the package, and we were really glad to take advantage of both tours.The tours are arranged by the hotel's management, and both of them were really enjoyable as they take you to some places you would never have thought of going... And these places are truly beautiful, especially the ones outside Pokhara.The management also kindly organized a last minute Helicopter trip to the ABC, which was the highlight of our trip. Please arrange the ABC tour with the Glacier's team as they work with the best Heli-Company in Pokhara, ensuring your safety. A very smart choice.Cleanliness in the hotel is OK, they should refurbish some parts (bathroom tiles were missing, for example) but nothing really serious to note.Breakfast could be better as there was a very limited choice of pastries.Staff very pleasant, especially the lady at breakfast who would do anything in order to ensure your satisfaction.Thank you for great stay, and we do hope to come back next year!

After staying at a lesser hotel in Pokhara, it was a relief to move to the Glacier Hotel & Spa for two nights.  Our top floor room was clean and comfortable. Appreciated the welcome fruit juice and fruit bowl in room. There was road noise as our room was near the front of the hotel, but not terrible.  Breakfast was tasty and ample.  We enjoyed a lunch and dinner in the Harbor Restaurant, part of the hotel.  Location is convenient to restaurants and shopping, also to the boats for hire at Phewa Lake.  All staff were friendly and helpful.  A person at the front desk provided us some incorrect information about public buses not operating during the regional election day which would have impacted our intended departure date, but fortunately we went to the bus stations and purchased tickets. Would stay here again.

This hotel was delightful! We only stayed one night, and frankly I wish we extended our stay here and delayed our return to Kathmandu! We arrived after an 8 day trek to Annapurna Base Camp. They presented us with a welcome drink of watermelon juice, including a glass for our guide who was still helping finalize a few details and hadn’t left us yet. I found this gesture particularly thoughtful. Our room was on the 6th floor with a lovely (even if foggy) view if Fishtail and other Himalayas. There is a beautiful terrace to the front, and an even better view from the small roof deck. Our room was very clean with nice, simple decor and a very comfortable bed. The shower was spacious and hot. The breakfast (included) was excellent! The location of the hotel is excellent for access to sightseeing at Phewa Lake, or visiting other restaurants or bars. The bar onsite looks fantastic, but we didn’t use it because we were meeting friends. 10/10

I had  one night stay in hotel glacier and spa.This is my second visit this hotel.room and bathroom is very clean .all  staff is very helffulliy.there are all facility which are available in hotel .i stay five floor .

I first stayed here in 2018 and it was great then...it is still an awesome place to stay and if you're looking for a really comfortable nice hotel with good food nice beds and right position, look no further.   the Wi-Fi is not great but thats the same everywhere.... i highly recommend this lovely pretty boutique hotel. Lovely staff as well!

What a fantastic and stunning property. We were so lucky to come across this exquisite hotel in the heart of Pokhara. The hotel has great character and ambience. On arrival we were welcomed with a refreshing fruit drink and in the room was a complimentary fruit platter. The room was large with a queen size bed and a separate large single bed.The bathroom itself was fitted with a spa bath with overhead rain shower and was very nicely decorated throughout. Though it lies on the main road, it remains quiet at night and we had very good sleep throughout our stay.Complimentary breakfast was provided with a great range of delicious breakfast dishes to choose from and the coffee was fabulous. The restaurant has a great selection of meals to tantalise your taste buds.  All the staff from reception, room service and dining were wonderful, always helpful as nothing was a problem. On departure from the Hotel to our bus connection back to Kathmandu the hotel provided their courtesy bus. I would definitely recommend this beautiful hotel to anyone who wish to visit Pokhara! We will be back!

Indulging ourselves in the amazing ambiance of this beautiful hotel after our trek to Annapurna Base Camp was just what we needed and not too expensive to do so either!  Clean comfortable beds, relaxing spa bath and a chance to tantalise the taste buds around a delicious selection of meals available in the restaurant!  The coffee with our complimentary breakfast was amazing aswell!! (I live for good coffee!!!) The staff were very polite and attentive, always smiling, so nothing was a problem from the moment we arrived. On our final day we were escorted to our bus for Kathmandu in the Hotel courtesy bus.  This place is a dream, perfectly presented and a pleasant addition to our stay in Pokhara! We will definitely be back!

We stayed in the family suite. The room was large with a queen size bed and a separate twin bed. There was a complimentary fruit platter to welcome us. The bathroom itself has a Jaccuzi with a rain shower. The room itself was also very nicely decorated with a beach style theme. Though it lies on the main road, it remains quiet at night and we had very good sleep throughout our 3 nights stay.The kitchen and restaurant staff was wonderful. We had complimentary breakfast provided for us. It was delicious and the service staff was always ready to make gluten free and lactose free meals for me. I requested for simple boiled veggies with rice, not in the menu and they were happy to serve it to me.We also had the pleasure to go on a 5-6 hours day hike with Sunil, the hotel manager. It proved to be the highlight of our trip at Pokhara. It was a beautiful hike at Dhampus and everything was so well arranged despite us confirming with him just the night before.In fact everyone at Glacier hotel that I met, the front of house, restaurant staff (the lady who served me in the mornings :)) and the housekeeping team that I met walking up the stairs always have a smile on and are very friendly. Would definitely recommend this beautiful hotel to anyone who wish to visit Pokhara!

I cannot wait to go back. It was an excellent stay. Booked through booking.com and it went smoothly. 5 minutes from airport. Check-in check out were smooth. Domestic flights tend to get delayed a lot, sometimes 8-12 hours, depending  on weather, so if catching an international  flight from katmandu, go one day ahead.Loved the room on 7th floor. Only room on that floor. Lift goes to 6th. Large, clean with superb view. 7th floor terrace was mostly for us and had amazing view on all sides with Phewa lake and mountain range with fishtail mt. Make sure you check the weather for mist/cloud/fog before booking because if cloudy you won't see any mountains. Our sunrise trip was ruined by thick clouds.Jacuzzi, ironing board, complimentary airport trips, fruits and drinks were there (but we don't drink). Staff were very helpful, friendly and not pushy.Loved the breakfast buffet. I am still craving for the mix (chicken cheese and vegetables) omelette. I never had such a tasty omelette before. Tea and coffee were very good. I also loved the water in pokhara. I had gone for a conference, so did not get time for much adventures. But did go site-seeing and boating. If planning a trip to Pokhara, Nepal, (you definitely must) do stay at Glacier hotel.

Newer hotel lakeside in Pokhara. Rooms very nice and spacious. Breakfast was great... many choices and the waitstaff was exceptional... special thanks to Sharmila who took great care of us. The guys were great also, I just don’t know their names. We stayed here on the front and back end of our trip... in the middle, did a 3 day/2 night trek to Poon Hill. Front desk was great in helping us plan our days. There is a great restaurant attached to the hotel also. I would highly recommend staying here when in Pokhara. Take advantage of the rooftop with great views of the mountains.

We stayed 2 nights here recently after some hiking in Nepal. The staff were very friendly in welcoming us. The room was spacious, tidy and modern. We enjoyed the included breakfast each morning up on the restaurant terrace. Not quite as good value as you can get elsewhere in Pokhara however.

The location of the hotel makes its easy to explore both Fewa lake and main town easily. We stayed in a junior suite on the 6th floor and the room was both spacious and comfortable.  Staff was warm and welcoming.  Good option if you want to walk to most things.

Allowed early check in definitely a great point! Thank you! Fulfill almost every aspect of a standard hotel, except the laundry service is not available at night. l chose it for the lake view as it is right opposite the lake entrance but unfortunately the lake was surrounded by trees, plus the electric wires if you try to view it from the hotel.

My husband and I stayed here for 4 nights over our first year wedding anniversary and my husbands birthday. We had such a delightful stay. They were very welcoming and accommodating to our needs. The hotel manager picked us up personally from the bus stop and dropped us off to the bus station. They were attentive to our needs and generous with their time. It was clean and a nice atmosphere. Breakfast was tasty and the coffee the best we had in Pokhara. ❤️

We had a very enjoyable stay in Glacier Hotel. The  hotel is located right by the lake very close to the airport. It has large restaurant and nice bar outside by the entrance. There is also a rooftop where you can chill. The staff are nice and attentive. The rooms are very comfortable and nicely decorated. The price was competitive. We certainly enjoyed our stay and would recommend it.

This place is a thing of beauty! How can I even begin saying how wonderful this place is and how it even made our stay in Pokhara a more memorable one. The rooms here are spacious, super clean, well-thought of. The concept is so pretty. Everything is awe-inspiring. The exteriors are also very beautiful and the location is superb. It is just accross the lake. The rooftop view is bewildering. It is awesome. The food here is delicious and they serve to our heart's and stomach's content. People are really friendly from the security, front desk staff, f&b servers and the shy housekeepers.. everyone was delightful including their ever so accommodating manager Sunil. I mean, we became instant family and friends. So if ever you are in Pokhara, stay here and your stay will be delightful.

Right on the lake. JUst outside the noisy central tourist area. Stayed twice with my four kids and really enjoyed both stays. High comfort, and services.Large rooms, well equipped. Great food at reasonable prices.Free limo service to the Airport.5 stars Nepali standard.Highly reccomended.

We stay two night with my family for deluxe room .room and bathroom was  clean . Excellent location, good lake view ,staff is friendly .Wi-Fi is fine .hot water is available.this place is very attractive.

Excellent location, right next to the Phewa Lake. Great views of the lake from the room. Loved the decor of the room, very cosy and comfortable. The staff went above and beyond. Food at the restaurant was delicious.

The decor of this hotel is extremely modern. We booked a suite via an online travel agency and got a great deal. The room was extremely spacious and well maintained. There was some good coffee to be had at breakfast, which was a big plus !

I stayed at Glacier twice during my tour in Nepal with my wife. On Mar 24th, when I finished a trekking in Annapurna with my wife, we choose to stay again at Glacier cause my wife like this hotel. We did not make any online booking in advance. When we arrived and checked the rate with the reception for a suite room, they told me it's USD100 and I paid by card. Later after my checked-in, I found their rate is only USD70 online for the same room type we stayed. I contacted the hotel staff, and they kindly agreed that I can re-book my room online and they can arrange to refund the USD100 that I paid. I thank them for their kindness and booked once again online. I left the hotel the next day for Lumbini, and they had not arranged the refund yet, but they promised to arrange the refund as soon as possible. I believe their words because I think Glacier is a decent hotel. On Mar 26th, they sent me an e-mail, telling me that they had arranged the refund and attached a refund slip which they sent to their bank. I think this could be an end, but I am wrong.With time goes by, I did not receive the refund up to now. I know it might takes a couple of working days for their bank to handle and transfer, but more than 10 working days is obviously not normal for any refund. I had a similar refund from Buddha Air for my canceled flight, and it only takes 2 working days. During the past one week, I sent three or four e-mails to Glacier, inquiring how it was with my refund. Surprisingly, no one reply me with a word. It seems that I am sending e-mails to a hotel with no person. I really wonder why a hotel like Glacier will treat their guest like this? USD100 is not a big amount, but this is the first and only situation that I have ever and never met in my travel experience. I think Glacier has good accommodation, friendly staff and many other good things, but their way on treating my refund request appears extremly strange and beyond normal understanding.

We stayed at the Glacier hotel for 5 nights. The large room had every facility that we wanted and was very comfortable and immaculately clean.On arrival we were greeted with a glass of cold fruit juice and a cool refreshing towel. Perfect after a long hot journey. All of the staff were very friendly and helpful. We had a great time here and would recommend a stay within any hesitation.

This was our favorite hotel during our month in Nepal.   It is on the expensive side for Pokhara, but you get your money’s worth.   Our room was large, comfortable, and well-appointed, with a small balcony and excellent views of the lake and hills.  And the room was beautifully designed, with a mix of modern and traditional styles that was wonderful.  And a shower plus bath tub!  The staff are kind and very attentive.  The atmosphere in the courtyard restaurant is magical and the food is very good.  Would love to return some day.

We stayed at the Glacier Hotel on route to Chitwan National Park. After the crazy hustle and bustle of Kathmandu it was a welcome, peaceful respite.The hotel is well maintained with tastefully decorated rooms and an excellent restaurant with delicious Nepali cuisine. We had the suite on the top floor with access to a large veranda overlooking the lake which was a real treat. The room was clean and comfortable.The standout for us was the customer service. The hotel offers complimentary sunrise and sunset experience packages if you book directly with them. We were leaving too early for the sunrise package but the owner himself took us on the sunset trip up to a lookout point above Pokhara to enjoy the breathtaking Annapurna mountain range and the sunset over the hills and mountains.The owner also personally drove us for 4 hours to Chitwan National Park for the next phase of our trip (at a cost) which was entirely out of his way and not something he needed to do. Something that was very much appreciated.In all I would recommend this hotel to those that are looking for a relaxing, indulgent experience.

We stayed at the Glacier Hotel last week in the honeymoon suite. It was one of the best hotels we stayed at during our stay in Nepal. It is right next to the lakeside and a 5 minute walk away from the main strip which was great as it was really quiet at night but close enough to get to if you want to go out. The room was large with it's own small balcony with great views, but as it's the only room on the top floor you pretty much have your own large terrace too (although other people can access it too), bed really comfortable, very clean rooms and a large jacuzzi bath. I'd say this hotel definitely meets western standards. The downstairs restaurant is decorated really nicely and the food was very good. I'd say the a la carte breakfast we had on the first day was better than the self service buffet we had on the other days because there's more choice and the food sometimes became cold on the buffet trays. So, it would be even better if the hotel could serve breakfast a la carte all the time, although I know this is tricky with a large amount of guests. The wifi could also be improved on the 7th floor as sometimes we had to go downstairs to connect, but that's a very minor issue. Overall it was an excellent stay, we would definitely recommend staying here if you're in Pokhara.

We (2 adults + 2 kids) stayed in family suite for 3 nights and enjoyed it! It’s definitely more expensive than other hotels in Pokhara but worth it. Room was huge, clean and beds comfortable. Bathroom was huge too, though the bathtub was a bit impractical.Good location, close to the lakeside main shops but not too close We enjoyed our stay there, thank you!

My second stay at Glacier hotel. Stunning,  amazing ambience . Combination of wood and stone , standout.  Food delicious,  most devine bed, well appointed bathroom.  The massage helped iron all those kinked muscles after a trek. Staff ever so obliging. If in Pokhara would strongly recommend staying here.

The Glacier is a splendid hotel, with beautifully designed spaces. It is comparable with European standards and was definitely the best accommodation of our whole holiday in Nepal. In addition, it is in an ideal location in South Lakeside.Our junior suite was equipped with a hot tub and had a nice lake view from the balcony. It was tastefully furnished and very clean. WiFi coverage could be improved, but this was not a big deal during our stay. The breakfast included in our room rate was wonderful and the Harbor restaurant was also a good option for eating in Pokhara. All personnel were extra nice and caring.The only drawback is that this hotel is quite expensive for Nepal. Also the spa is more expensive than other very good options in town. Overall, I would recommend this accommodation for a couple of days of pampering, ideally after a long trekking.

I enjoyed my stay there, room was big as I stayed with my family in a room. Washroom was clean and have all the required amenities.Breakfast could be improved with some Indian dishes for Indian Nationals.Location of the hotel is great, right on the main Street and opposite to Lake.Will surely recommend it and is surely my pick  for next trip

Glacier, as its name; everything matches accordingly. Amazing interior with very basic work gives wonderful result indeed. Quality of service and attention to details are much appreciating. Beautiful and worthy accommodating hotel in Pokhara. Highly recommended.

I have stayed here several times, so many good things I have to say about this place, location is perfect, 100meter to lake and boat rental, 10 minutes drive to Pokhara airport 6 minutes drive to tourist bus station, breakfast is amazing, staffs are beyond professional, rooms are super comfy. whether you are in pokhara for trekking, business trip, just sightseeing, paragliding or just escaping for week from daily grind, hustle bustle, this hotel is your home. Highly recommended... Thank you.

My sisters and I stayed here and it was a perfect, elegant and quiet escape from all the activity that Pokhara has to offer! Glacier Hotel & Spa has a rustic feel and offers a calm and beautiful escape with the warmest staff and perfect location. I would absolutely recommend this property for your next visit. And I especially recommend the Annapurna Helicopter Option offered through the property, absolutely a once in a lifetime chance that we will never forget! Super convenient that we could book through the hotel :)

Nice hotel, definitely higher end for Nepal. Rooms are spacious and staff is very friendly. The homemade pasta and meatballs in the Harbour restaurant are amazing.  We stayed in the honeymoon suite and their standard room on this trip. 4 stars because of a few issues. 1. Lack of attention to deal in cleaning the bathrooms (both times).  There was mould in the corners that had been there for a while.  2. Location. While it is conveniently located on Lakeside, that also makes it noisy. Even with all the windows closed it is loud at night. 3. When in the honeymoon suite on the top floor it would be nice if the rooftop terrace on the top floor was private. Other guests were able to walk up the stairs and use it as well - including one family who let their kid run around screaming while I was trying to read. Overall a very nice hotel, but in the end we opted to change locations to somewhere more quiet (and for half the price). Definitely look online for a deal if you do decide to stay here.

After hiking and sightseeing all day it was great to come home to this hotel.It was as comfortable and safe as my home in Texas USA.The staff welcomes me as a friend. Sushmita at front desk and Himani in restaurant are to be commended.Thank you for loving me as a friend. Right across street from lake. Very comfortable beds, A/C, and American bathroom.I paid $75 USD and will stay here again.I stayed in room 503.

My Mum and I stayed here for 3 nights and we can't recommend this wonderful hotel enough. The rooms are luxurious, well equipped and stylishly designed, all of the staff are helpful, friendly, knowledgeable and genuinely happy and couldn't do enough for us. This is the perfect base to explore pokhara, before or after a trek or if you are just spending time in town. The hotel has the best location, close to everything in town, the lake, shops, restraunts etc We took a tour with the hotel and saw magnificent villages, countryside and of course the annapurna range, which was simply stunning. This hotel really exceeded our expectations, we slept well, ate well and would not hesitate to return again, highly recommend this place, thanks for having us to stay!

We stayed in this hotel from 16th October to 18th October, and enjoyed every bit of it - be it food, courtesy, service, welcoming nature and lend a helping hand. Icing on the cake is the hotel's location - it is just superb and gives excellent views of Fewa lake and the main road. Apart from their own restaurant, lots of other restaurants were nearby. I will definitely recommend this hotel to Pokhara visitors - according to me, this is best hotel with sizable room and excellent location.

I had a room at the top of the hotel with stunning views over the lake. The room was delightful and had absolutely everything you need. The finish and attention to detail was excellent and it had a very comfy bed.  Good A/C. Nice bathroom. Fridge. Water in the room. The whole hotel is very well done and breakfast and restaurant excellent. I highly recommend this hotel for anyone wanting real quality and more upmarket but still affordable. I give this hotel a 4 star rating!

Clean and pretty throughout, comfortable, interesting decor in the rooms. Nice light and view of lake. Staff friendly and helpful. Intermittent internet. Did not try the spa this time. Food at breakfast was  good. Dinner was of excellent quality at a reasonable price. Location in the edge of tourist area was perfect, close but quiet.

Great boutique hotel: nice rooms with unique and very cozy design, good location and very good view to the lake. Staff is very friendly and helpful! Excellent laundry service! Cons: no hot water for bath tub, poor wifiWould definately stay again but please fix your wifi! 😊

This hotel is very nice & in the main area of Pokhara. This area reminds me of Krabi in Thailand, if you’ve been. The lake is directly across the street & you have a view when you eat on the terrace. They have free pick up at the airport. When you arrive, you’re greeted with a fruit drink and cold wash cloth, which was great since it’s been hot. Every one is very nice and accommodating. The breakfast is good, and dinner was great! We ordered the pasta with a mushroom cream sauce & chicken, it was amazing!! The pasta is homemade. I’m a foodie, & my husband loves pasta, it’s the best we’ve ever had. We also had the fish, which was tender & good too. The room is very spacious, with a comfortable bed. I have a bad back & neck, so I don’t sleep well on hard beds. The only bad thing was the WiFi. It was very slow & always buffering. It was a lil inconvenience, but we were only here for a few days, & on vacation so it wasn’t the “end of the world.”

The Glacier Hotel was an exceptionally pleasant place for us to stay after our 5 day trek. While the trek may have lowered our standards or swayed our judgment, it is also a statement of the quality of the hotel, its amenities and the level of service provided by the hotel. Our rooms were large and well appointed. The beds and bathrooms were on par with any international or large chain hotel. The rooms also contained an air conditioning unit and mini-fridges, though our fridge only worked sporadically. The hotel provided us with free large bottles of bottled water and fruit. The amenities at the hotel were similarly well-appointed. We arranged deep-tissue full-body massages at the hotel and, though they were not cheap, they were cheaper than they would have been in the United States. Similarly, the on-site soda shop/ café provided the perfect spot for us to buy a dessert one evening. (We had a slice of cake and some bread pudding.) Breakfast, a buffet which featured a variety of European and American breakfast items as well as local juices, was included with our room and definitely could have served as the perfect fuel for any adventure we could have come up with. (Note that if there are fewer than 12 guests at the hotel, they do not serve a buffet breakfast.) Similarly, the service was excellent. We had dinner there one evening and our waiter proved perfectly responsive without being intrusive. Likewise, when we ordered our desserts from the café, they were (in short order) delivered to our room. We were able to get everything we needed and by the end of our stay here felt extraordinarily pampered. We highly recommend the Glacier Hotel to anyone staying in Pokhara, particularly if you’re looking to indulge a little!

The food was great here. We had the wild boar, the Chicken Chili, some Mo Mos and a couple of beers. Great! Food was spicy, but not overly so. The price for all of this was 3586 nepalese rupees, about 35 bucks.

I spend 3 night in this hotel. I had a so much problem with wifi. It is so slow and not working. When I complain to front desk. They just say OK and never do anything. Other then wifi it was OK. This hotel has a free pic up service from or to airport.

Located on phewa lake in town. Incredible aesthetic architecture. Was upgraded to honeymoon suite, beautifully put together with all those extra touches. Bed was so comfortable,  lots of hot water,  quiet to sleep. Beatiful views of lake and town. Food was fantastic and staff ever so helpful. Very relaxing.   Highly recommend to stay . Look forward to visiting again.

I truly love the stone-wall touch on both outside and inside of the hotel! Having a little balcony (i got a room facing the lake) and 2 more windows make the room airy and bright! Even the hotel is just next to the main road, it is really quiet at night! With the super comfy bed, a good sleep is guaranteed!I especially appreciate one female front desk staff on the morning shift (dang i forgot her name!). she was extremely nice and helpful. We had some trivial requests and somehow kept changing our minds. But she was really patient and polite in dealing with us! Would definitely recommend this place!

Loved there warm hospitality, delicious cuisines from around the world, cozy rooms with the latest interior and scenic view of the Himalayan range and Fewa lake. And experience so delightful that made me fall in love with Pokhara.

I just returned from 3 nights at Glacier Hotel and it is a very good option at bottom of the lake. The rooms are bright, airy and comfortable. The finishing is of stone, however, and in the middle on February the room felt a bit cold. Staff are very helpful and knowledgable. For instance, they will tell you exactly how much to spend on a minicab to certain destinations. The restaurant and cafe were fine but sparsely populated, this is possible due to the hotel being at one end of the 'strip' in Pokara. One thing that lets Glacier down is it's Wifi. It was almost totally unusable on the 5th floor, and this was over a number of devices. Good luck!

I stayed at the glacier hotel for four nights in late January. I was very pleased be given a free upgrade to a suite room on the sixth floor. It was very spacious and had lovely views over the city towards the lake. I had breakfast everyday in the harbour restaurant which is part of the hotel. This was enormous. I also ate dinner there twice. My only little grumble would be that the restaurant was very cold so I had to sit and eat  with a coat on. Other than that nice hotel nice staff nice location

We spent a few nights here over New Years 2018 and extended our stay because it was so wonderful and the staff were so great!  Very clean, comfortable, and beautifully finished rooms.  I would definitely recommend this place to anyone wanting a beautiful escape on lakeside in Pokhara.  Tip: ask for a lakeside room and definitely go to the rooftop terrace for sundowners one day.

Friendly and efficient staff, gargantuan breakfast - porridge, followed by a full fry up???? - I need to get back to a modest start of muesli......Concrete interior to the room so a little chilly in Jan but there is air/con /heating. Like all the lakeside hotels save the old Hotel Fewa you are actually across the main road from the lake but this doesn't matter much. Stayed on the 6th floor which although there is no balcony there is a terrace with a panoramic view of mountains and lake. Good for a post dinner snifter in milder weather and great for an afternoon mellow.

We stayed at Glacier Hotel for 3 nights over the Christmas break in Dec 2017. Our stay was extremely memorable. We opted for the Honeymoon suite, which was absolutely worth the extra cost. Suite is on the top floor (very private), and had a homely feel to the design, with a large bath tub to soak in after a long day in Pokhara. Awesome views of Pokhara from the room, and right outside the room is a rooftop patio that looks directly at the lake - patio is open to all guests but we found ourselves alone most of the time given that the Honeymoon suite was the only room on that floor and the other floors have their patios as well (I think).The service from the hotel staff was delightfully good, and very honestly the best we've experienced our whole trip - all the staff wore smiles on their faces (constantly!), greeted us warmly at any time of the day, and were so polite and genuine when we needed help / had requests. The breakfast spread was also the best we had in Nepal (be sure to get the outdoor seats facing the streets and lake!)We signed up for a very reasonably priced Dhampus sunrise trek (~5 hours) which was the highlight of our trip. Rajendran, the owner of the hotel, was our personal guide for the trek, and he took us on the trek of our lives. We took a comfortable jeep ride (~40 mins) from the hotel to the starting point of the trek (Dhampus hill) where we watched the sun rise and the rays slowly hitting the Annapurna - it was absolutely breathtaking. Rajendran kindly packed breakfast and hot tea from the hotel, and we just ate and sipped while we watched the sun rise - I've been seen some pretty amazing sunrises in my life (Machu Pichu, Chile salt flats, Bali volcano, India ganges etc.), but this is by far the most magical yet... After that, we began a very comfortable (largely flat / downhill) trek from Dhampus - the views of the Annapurna just got better and better with each turn (see my pictures)...We will definitely stay in Glacier when we are back in Pokhara - thank you Rajendran and team for the unforgettable experience.

We stayed bat the Glacier Hotel after our ten day trekking around Annapurna. It was the perfect place to relax and rest after all the hard work. The staff were very nice and professional, the room was very comfortable and they have a nice buffet for breakfast. It is also very well located walking distance from everywhere. I highly recommend this beautiful hotel.

We have chosen to stay at the Glacier Hotel in Pokhara three times now. The rooms, especially the beds, are very comfortable with a good bathroom. The views from the rooms are fantastic, especially those on the lake and northern sides.We really like the location as it’s right on the lake and a fairly short stroll down the main street past the shops - it’s central but away from the noise at night. We also really like the restaurant and the cafe - food is great and we enjoy sitting on the covered verandah watching people walk by. The hotel staff are lovely and helpful. The hotel is also happy to provide airport pickups

Everything was great. - Convenient location (in downtown and very close to the airport)- Friendly stuff- Spacious and clean rooms- Good food with a great variety on the menu- Free airport pick-up and drop-off

Business owner himself involved in serving customers,unique  architecture of building , hotel owner himself involvs in serving customers, proxy to Fewa Lake with Good view of Fewa Lake & Machhapuchhere Himalayas, HARBOR restaurant within hotel property serving delicious foods ect.>>>#one_of_the_very_good_Boutique_Hotel_in#Pokhara#Nepal👍👌

This is a very well built hotel, different decor than usual. Beautiful rooms, comfortable bed and details have been looked into. The decor is fresh and light in the rooms. Views aren't the best as you are surrounded by other hotels and a side road. Breakfast wasn't fresh, was very disappointed. With a lot of tourists in the hotel was hoping for better service.

Despite the of its poor infrastructure  (eg unreliable WiFi connection and poor telecom signals; I think the problem may caused by the local telecom company rather than the hotel), the owner of the hotel is alway there to serve and provides extra care to his clients.He was there when we first arrival at the hotel and he was there when we were departing to the airport.  He provided us  with timely advice when we were in trouble with our transportation arrangement to another city, he was there when we were having dinner at the bar.  He personally drove us to the secret spot to see the sunrise away from the crowd in his 4WD very early in the morning.   He told stories of his life, his hotel and his country.   All told, he cared about his clients and with them a happy stay in whatever way he can do.  His dedication to services has also influenced his entire staff in general.We have planed for 3 day Stay initially but ended stay with them for 4 nights.  We had a choice for other hotels the last night of the journey but decided to stay with them -  the location of the hotel and its friendly services have been the deciding factors.  Yuan & Kwan

At Glacier you get absolute value for the price. The rooms were lovely and clean (although the mattress was not the most comfortable). The service was excellent - including the welcome greetings at the entrance, the check-in and check-out process, the cleaning staff, and the restaurant staff. They were particularly caring and attentive with our young daughter. Our entire experience was pleasant and professional.

I have stayed at the Glacier Hotel and Spa multiple times, and my experience of the facilities and location has me wanting to stay at this hotel time and time again.The design of the hotel is spectacular and relaxing. The hotel restaurant is of great quality. The staff are of tremendous service.I was blessed to meet the proprietor, Rajendra, whose story of developing his hotel, despite many challenges from earthquake to embargoes, was nothing short of inspiring. Rajendra's training as an interior designer is evident in the many visually striking and relaxing choices of decoration and design. His staff's training and natural kindness made my stay a real joy. Rajendra was kind enough to take me on an amazing early morning drive to see the sunrise over the Himalayas. I'd wholeheartedly recommend the Glacier Hotel and Spa for anyone looking for a relaxing and centrally located hotel  in Pokhara. Well done, Rajendra!Craig H.

I believe reviews are always more helpful with a bit of context on the reviewer. I'm an over 60 traveler who's visited 71 countries on business, vacation, and adventure travel. My range of accommodations includes Aman, Relais et Chateaux, and Taj resorts as well as Airbnb homes and Bedouin tents. This was my first trip to Nepal.My partner and I were fortunate to book the Glacier Hotel and Spa. On arriving after 20 some hours of flying from San Francisco, our top floor room in this pristine boutique hotel was very welcome. Glacier's bathroom was beautiful, with abundant hot water, a spacious room and a variety of power outlets for US and other standards. The bed and bedding were lovely. We happened to be just beside the lovely rooftop deck (great place for early morning yoga) overlooking the lake which was just across the street. The Glacier's central location made boating excursions, hikes, shopping and meals an easy stroll. We took many meals at the hotel restaurant and we're consistently impressed with the quality of the food and the service. We were fortunate to meet the proprietor Rajendra whose story of developing his hotel despite many challenges--from earthquake to embargoes--was uplifting and inspiring. Rajendra's training as an interior designer is evident in the many discerning choices on decoration, fixtures, surfaces and paint. His staff's training and natural kindness made our stay a real joy. Rajendra was kind enough to take us on an amazing early morning drive to see the sunrise over the Himalayas and organized a variety of activities including a helicopter ride to Annapurna and a visit to the local Tibetan Refugee organization where we were able to purchase beautiful carpets and help those in need. I'd wholeheartedly recommend the Glacier for anyone looking for a upscale relaxing and centrally located hotel experience in Pokhara. Bravo!

Pros:  Large clean rooms. Comfortable beds. Good breakfast.  Centrally located to lake, restaurants and shops.  Friendly and polite service. Great views from balcony and rooftop terrace. Cons:  shower constantly luke warm despite complaints.  Room on level 2 was above kitchen as a result it was noisy and smelly. Internet in hotel non existent. Spa under renovations. It is overall a good hotel apart from issues mentioned above.

Five of us stayed at Glacier Hotel for several days.  We had a wonderful stay.  The rooms were comfortable, and large in size.  My favorite part was the breakfast area - beautiful sitting area both inside and outside with a great selection of breakfast items.  It was great to start off the day with a delicious breakfast before heading out.  Their coffee was some of the best i have ever tasted! The owner takes out groups for sunset hikes.  We did a four hour hike as well as a sunrise hike with Raj and i think this was the best part of staying at Glacier.  He made sure to take us away from tourist spots so we were hiking through villages and trails and not running into any other tourists!  The trails he chose were beautiful - and he was incredibly patient when we stopped to take pictures everywhere.  Well organized and our favorite part of being in pokhara.  The hotel also arranged for pickup and drop off at the airport.  Excellent location across from lake and in an area with lots of shopping and cafes. The only issue we had was that internet was not always functioning in the rooms but they are in the middle of upgrading and we were able to access wifi in the common areas without difficulty.  Overall incredibly happy with our stay and would highly recommend to others

We’ve been to Pokhara many times and this time decided to stay at the Glacier Hotel & Spa. On the plus side the staff were absolutely fantastic from the front of house to housekeeping & restaurant staff. They were all extremely friendly & helpful.The room was refreshingly different & was bright & comfortable although a bit unfinished in part. My only complaint was the WiFi which was weak and kept dropping out which meant we had to log in multiple times & too weak to steam. The hotel needs to fix this - the WiFi was much better in small local restaurants. I would also not recommend the food in the restaurant.

During my one week travels in Kathmandu, I had planned a side trip to Pokhara, where I had reserved a two-nights stay here at Hotel Glacier & Spa. I booked a coach through Greenline Tours, which was an 8hrs ride from Kathmandu to Pokhara. For the return trip, I took a short 30mins flight back to Kathmandu via Buddha Air.Located in the heart of Lakeside opposite the calm waters of Phewa Lake, Hotel Glacier & Spa is situated not far from the bus station at just 500m away. I was actually unaware the hotel provides complimentary return transfers until my arrival at the hotel reception. Nevertheless, I had paid NPR300 (USD2.90) for the taxi ride from the bus station to the hotel, which I had considered an affordable ride. So if you would like to request for the hotel’s complimentary transportation service, I would recommend that you email the hotel directly in advance concerning this request. For the hotel departure, given its short distance to the airport at 2.3km away and being a small domestic terminal, you can simply allow just an hour for check in before your flight departure.Although I had booked the Deluxe Room, I am grateful for the hotel’s kind gesture to provide a complimentary room upgrade to the Junior Suite (Room No. 6103). The room is comfortably spacious at 25 square metres and has a Mediterranean feel, which comes with stone and wooden elements, creating a natural yet contemporary ambience that is calm and inviting. The room offers a view of the Pokhara streets as well as the scenic Himalayan mountains, including Mount Fishtail and the Annapurnas. During the late morning and noon periods, I can even spot people paragliding from Sarangkot Hill. The suite is situated at the end of the corridor, where it leads out to a terrace offering spectacular views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges, Phewa Lake and the Raniban forest.The bathroom offers a bathtub with a window view of the surrounding nature. However, the showering experience was average, attributed by a weak shower pressure and that it takes a couple of minutes for the shower to get warm. Additionally, you would need to keep the rain shower button constantly pressed to get the water sprinkling from the top. Another gripe is that the Wi-Fi in the room is not very strong and you might experience lagging issues when watching videos. Other than that, it is still generally fine for web surfing and accessing the social media sites. Despite these shortcomings, I had an enjoyable and comfortable stay here.My hotel stay is inclusive of daily breakfast set, which comprises of a wide variety of menu choices such as Continental, English, Vegetarian, Sandwiches, Omelettes, Cereals and Corn Flakes. Amongst my hotel stays in the many countries I had travelled, I must say they serve the most delicious, hearty and filling breakfast. Their breakfast is simply put, awesome! Not to forget, the wait staff was fantastic and always on smiles. Like the saying “Every Great Day Starts With A Hearty Breakfast”, I really looked forward to enjoying my breakfast at the start of each day during my stay here.At Hotel Glacier & Spa, you can expect great hospitality from all its staff. On the morning of my second day’s stay, I woke up to discover many flying insects inside my bathroom. I reported it to the Front Desk and the Hotel Manager immediately came to my room to check and attended to my problem. I later discovered that I did not shut the bathroom window properly, which had thus resulted in the insects flying into the bathroom during the night. I was glad I did not encounter a similar situation on the third day of my stay. I am particularly impressed by the hotel’s attentiveness in ensuring that all its guests had a comfortable stay here.The hotel is also situated close to many of the tourist sites. A taxi ride with return transfers to the World Peace Pagoda taxi costs NPR1,600 (USD15). I had also hired a taxi to Sarangkot Hill to catch the mesmerising sunrise and indulge in the breathtaking views of the Pokhara Valley as well as the Annapurna Himalayan mountains peaks.If you wished to rent a boat in the Phewa Lake, Glacier Hotel & Spa is located very close to the Baidam Boating Point at just 27m away. I hired a one hour ride with a boater who rowed me to the Tal Bahari temple.The hotel is conveniently located on Lakeside Road where the numerous retail shops and restaurants are situated along the 1km stretch. I would highly recommend visiting Caffe Concerto Pizzeria Restaurant situated at less than 100m stroll away, to savour their authentic Italian cuisine.Despite its name Hotel Glacier & Spa, the spa is not operational in the property. Nevertheless, there are massage and spa centres situated in the hotel vicinity if you are in need of some pampering for your body.I would recommend Hotel Glacier & Spa for its great hospitality, beautifully designed rooms and not forgetting its ever sumptuous breakfast. Now my mouth is watering, every time I think of its breakfast.If you find my review helpful in aiding the selection of your hotel stay, I would appreciate if you can give it a “Thumbs Up”.

Recently stayed at this hotel for 2 nights. Pro: convenient location, new hotel was built last year stated by owner, staffs are friendly and professional. Always have smile on their faces, variety of hot breakfast items.Con: INTERNET is unstable and barely able to have stable signal from my room. First room on 4th floor no internet at all, I had to walk to the end of hallway where the elevator located in order to get connection ( and when using YouTube, social media are super slow and unstable). So spoke to manager and changed to 2nd floor close to elevator (during our 1st night stay). It was working for the night but still quite slow to browse the internet.2nd day we were out whole morning and return to room found out internet not working again. So spoke to the owner of the hotel. He is actually a nice guy to speak to, he said for some reasons the internet was not working properly the past two days, and we could use the internet at the ground floor or borrow their computer. I told him that it’s inconvenience to come down in the middle of night due to time zone difference and i think it’s due to the power of internet not strong (I.e. 4G, 5G， etc). Also possible due to the concrete of the building. Anyway, the short version is that I did feel that without internet is a big issue for me. I don’t think it worths the price it lists online. The owner was patient and listening the whole time and he agreed to provide us some discount of the room price. Also, the colour of towels were supposed to be white, but it appeared greyish and we didn’t use it. Would I recommend to friends ? Yes but given the condition that internet issue needs to be fixed and running all the time.I gave 4 points cause the staffs are very helpful and friendly, with the room itself I would rate 3 instead.

Amazing view from the suite and you get your own balcony from which you can see the entire mountain range. Absolutely stunning and quite a bargain for the price!Modern rooms, big TV and very nice bathroom. Too bad the shower doesn't work properly though.

From the first sight of the hotel's distinguished façade in the perfect spot away from the main tourist area, it becomes obvious that Glacier is classy - not in a showy and extravagant way, but in a subtle way, with taste.  Nowhere is this more manifest than the bedrooms, which have been designed and equipped with great care, imagination. and attention to detail.  Rooms are spacious, with a small fridge, desk, and table and two chairs, and lighting is discreet while being sufficient.  Noticeable is the use throughout of local materials for, e.g. floor mats; the bed is extraordinarily comfortable; and the room kept spotlessly clean.The restaurant is certainly the best we've found so far in the city, where many have delusions of adequacy, an oasis of calmness.  It's on two floors, with the upper boasting a wonderful view of the lake (yes, there's a lake in Pokhara).  Credit for the whole set up must go to the owner, Rajindra Dhakal, who adopts the wise approach of staying close to his guests - he runs a frequent sunrise service personally.  Not just that, but he's recruited well: the Hostess, Hirmani, is attentiveness personified, and I as well courteous, friendly, and professional in everything she does.  Similarly, Manisha in reception is extremely helpful and friendly.You get all this for a very reasonable cost.  Pokara is a very special place, and this is a special place to stay while you're here.

My husband and I spent two wonderful nights at the Glacier Hotel following a not so great night at another establishment in Pokhara.  To say that we were thrilled with our change in accommodations is an understatement.  We are not generally luxury seekers when traveling, but the professionalism, cleanliness, and overall attention to detail that we experienced at the Glacier were outstanding.  Upon our arrival we were met by the hotel manager (who seemed to always be on site & always available to help with whatever we needed), a friendly receptionist, and a porter.  We were given cold drinks and shown to our room while our bags were brought up shortly after.  Our Junior Suite was spacious with AC and 24/7 hot water in a beautifully decorated attached bathroom.  The front desk staff were always available to help with anything that we needed from arranging laundry to helping plan day trips.  We opted to take an early morning helicopter ride to Annapurna Base Camp (at the suggestion of the manager) and would could not have been happier with the overall experience and would recommend this splurge to anyone visiting Pokhara.  Also included in our stay was free shuttle service to the airport and a delicious breakfast buffet. We were extremely happy with our stay at the Glacier Hotel and would highly recommend it!

Nice, spacious, clean, newly remodeled after earthquake of 2015!Great location, with Lake Phewa across the street!!Best food in town , and great staff all around!Bed is super comfy, within walking distance to everything!The views of Annapurna’s is very special!Forest has a lot there offer, take a boat ride on the lake!!

Glacier Hotel and Spa is really a heaven on earth. The people working there are so helpfull and do everything to let you have a great stay. The rooms are very pretty and trought the whole hotel you have old and modern art from Nepali artists. The Harbor restaurant has great food and drinks. And the ambiance is beautyfull.I loved my stay, and will sure come again  when I will be back in Nepal.Thank you so much Rajendra Dakhal and personel.

The location is face to lake, you can have a great view if you go to the top level on 6th floor.The bed room is big enough and comfortable. Beds are clean and bath room. We stay two nights in that hotel.Breakfast buffet is excellent and more like western style of food. Their pasta is also taste and favorable.Service is very good and friendly. I will consider to back to thus hotel next time.

Confortable roomIn room safeBreakfast tasteful, good enough 2 goods restaurants inside hotel, with many options in menuwi fi OKHelpful friendly staffLocation excellent beside lake and close restaurants and bars

Pokhara was indeed the highlight of our trip to Nepal, and the Glacier Hotel had a great deal to do with that.  The room was spotlessly clean, with excellent air conditioning (a must), and a lovely, spacious room.  The bath, with it's beautiful glass tiles, was a standout.  This hotel is perfectly located, opposite the lake (we sat on the balcony and enjoyed the views at breakfast and dinner), and near shopping and restaurants.  The staff is lovely and accommodating, and the laundry we sent to be cleaned was returned next day, as requested.

I usually stay in budget hotels, but I started eating in their restaurant and loved the food and service so much I decided to switch hotels.  This is now one of my favorite hotels in the world.  They have a great breakfast buffet, and I've really enjoyed eating on their balcony while people watching on Lakeshore Drive and Fewa Lake.  Everything I've had to eat at dinner has been phenomenal, especially the Nepal Specialities but also their "Continental" food.  Super location, and the rooms are quiet despite being right on the busy rood.  Highly recommend.

Good clean Hotel, wifi is good and staff really friendly...definately do the morning sunrise tour...its the best view of mountains ... the breakfast was also really good...view of the lake is good and right next to boat hire place and couple good restaurants...money change place right next door

We spent two nights to mark the end of one month volunteering in Pokhara. I booked the room via Agoda.com. Upon checking in, we were warmly greeted with watermelon juice and a complimentary upgrade to the honeymoon suite on the top (7th) floor with a large private balcony overlooking Lake Phewa. The upgrade came as a complete surprise. The room was gorgeous, as was the balcony - beautifully appointed inside and out. The only problem during our stay was the bathroom - near zero water pressure for the shower, no hot water most of the time and faulty plug. We raised the hot water issue with the front desk on the first day and water was pumped to the room, but quickly reverted to a luke warm trickle at best. The included breakfast was ok, with a lovely dining room on level 1 overlooking the busy street. Great for people watching. Complimentary bottled water supplied to rooms. Wifi included. No toiletries supplied (ie shampoo etc). Hotel would benefit from having a compendium in rooms. Lovely staff. If you're looking for some AC luxury (in lovely rooms overlooking the green section of the lake) in Pokhara, this is the place. Well located on main tourist trip. And yes...there is a lift in this hotel - services to level 6.

A fantastic and warm-feeling hotel, with unique design and great value. Not on the cheaper end of what you can get in Pokhara, but worth every penny and a bargain for its price. The staff was ultra-kind and helpful; they consistently went above and beyond to ensure we had a pleasant stay. Location is perfect, at the south end of Lakeside, and the attached restaurant has many delicious options, though it is a bit expensive. Highly recommend.

My partner and I spent a week at Glacier Hotel. On arrival, I was pleasantly surprised by the architecture of the building (one of those rare times when the reality is actually nicer than the photos). The hotel is clean and has all the basic comforts required. Rooms are pretty and the decor is simple and pretty. Probably one of the nicest lodgings right by Phewa lake. The staff were helpful and we especially enjoyed the brilliant breakfasts sitting outside. On return from a tiring trek we were given the lovely surprise of an upgrade to a larger suite on a high floor with a beautiful big shared balcony that had gorgeous views of the lake, city and surrounding mountains. Needless to say, we've already decided to come back to Pokhara for another trip in the near future (loved it!) and will definitely opt to stay at Glacier Hotel; which made a lovely home away from home.

This hotel is very unique in the best of ways! It looks like a Mediterranean boutique hotel you would find in Greece. Everything is extremely clean, and very well done. Food is good, service is excellent, and the rooms are clean with nice A/C. For the price, I'd say this is the best value in Pokhara. It's located right on Lakeside and just across the street from the lake. Short walk to all restaurants and shops.

Best Location, very helpful staff, good food , good Wi-Fi ,Hot Shower are the best part of the hotel is very close 20 miter away from Fewa lake and Very peaceful environment. I know where to stay in Pokhara. Its the right place to stay after Trekking and Before Trekking/Tour.

Very nice modern hotel located in central Pokhara.  Airport shuttle service, onsite restaurant and bar, good wifi, A/C in each room, friendly staff.  The hot water can take a long time to get to the shower head, but it gets there.

We loved our two night stay at Glacier Hotel. Entering the room is like instant relaxation!Our room was bright and spacious. We were upgraded to an bigger room on an upper level and had wonderful views of pokhara, the mountains and the lake. The bed is very comfortable. The staff are first class and looked after us well. We were able to organise a late checkout very easily. The wifi didn't work particularly well on the upper levels but seemed to go faster downstairs by the cafe. Breakfast was very good and they know how to make coffee! A wonderful stay which we can recommend to all.

Great Location and comfy room !The service is excellent, the view amazing and the breakfast as well !!They were really helpful and booked for us the zip-line giving us all the needed information.They also provide pick up and drop off from the airport or the bus station.

I stayed here with my wife and brother-in-law when we stopped in Pokhora on the way back from Ghandruk.  It is very conveniently located in Lakeside, and our room (it was billed as a  Deluxe Double online) had a view of the lake and mountains, which was really nice.  You could open a door and walk out onto a balcony, and we were on the 5th floor.The room was clean, quiet, and nicely appointed.  The service at the front desk was great!  We had the included breakfast the next morning -- they had a nice selection and again the service was great.

We stayed here in June 2017.  We booked the honeymoon suite which did not disappoint.  A private terrace with views of the mountains  and the lake every morning.   The manager, Sunil, seamlessly changed our  flights and the next morning drove us to  a private sunrise viewing point.  Excellent restaurant.  Wonderful location. Would not stay any where  else in Pokhara.

We loved this hotel. Right on the lake. Big spacious rooms. Huge bathroom with spa bath. Fabulous food in the restaurant. Beast and dinner were great. Lovely staff and brilliant manager Sunil. They arranged out Annapurna trek and provided the large pack for our porter to carry and poles for me. Highly recommended!!!!!!

Lovely hotel on the lakeside. The pick up was good, the room (4101) was magnificent having three balconies. The room was extremely modern and clean. The bathroom and the Jacuzzi were great. The staff were friendly and helpful. Loved the overall decor and ambiance of the rooms and the hotel. One of the better maintained hotel that I have visited.The only area of improvement could be the travel desk and the breakfast which though plenty was not that tasty.Loved my stay here and would definitely stay here again on my next visit. Thank you for the room upgrade.

This review is more than a year late (we traveled in May/ Jun 2016), but as they say, better late than never. We were doing a trip of Nepal for our marriage anniversary. We spent three nights at the Glacier Hotel and Spa, including the day of our anniversary and we could not have chosen a better place to do it. First off, the location is great. It is bang on the main road, surrounded by a lot of interesting hotels and shops. It is also right opposite the lake. You get gorgeous views of the distant mountains and the lake from the higher floors. On the flip side, you can hear the noise of the vehicles passing by, but overall I would say the advantage of the location outweighs the discomfort from the noise. From the moment we entered, we were treated extremely well by all members of the staff. From the lady at the reception, to the staff at the restaurant, the housekeeping staff, the management, everyone is just so nice and responsive. We mentioned that we were there to spend our anniversary, and they sent us an excellent cake and also upgraded us to a fancy suite. The food was fabulous, the entire property was very clean and well maintained, the cab and the paragliding trip they arranged for us was fantastic, the rooms very comfortable; there was absolutely nothing I could complain about. The manager (Mr. Dhakal) was very friendly and ensured that we had a comfortable stay.  But, the best part was the owner Mr. Rajendra Dhakal. First he upgraded our rooms simply because it was our anniversary. Then he gave us great advice for the trek that we were planning. As we came back after 3 days to collect our bags, he even offered us a free room to freshen up before our journey. I have stayed in a lot of places where the owners/ management is nice, but it is extremely rare to see this kind genuine interest being shown. You may find fancier properties in Nepal, but I seriously doubt you will find a better place to stay.

Great place to stay in Pokhara. Situated right in front of the Fewa Lake, the hotel is clean, offering great services and polite staff. Must stay if you're in Pokhara. Great view from the rooms on the 6th floor. Highly recommended!

I stayed at the Glacier hotel in Pokhara for a total of two nights. The check-in experience was very smooth - they even upgraded me to one of the rooms on the 6th floor. The rooms themselves were very stylish - they told me that they renovated recently. Since the first room they gave me smelled of smoke (they claimed it was a non-smoking room, but in fact there was an ashtray in it), the gave me another room right next to it without any fuzz. Also, the 6th ad 7th floor have an awesome roof terrace. In better weather, the views must be amazing.I also had two meals at their restaurant - the food was really delicious and the service was spot-on. The included breakfast was also good, but nothing special.Overall a very good experience - I would definitely come back if I'm in Pokhara again.

The minute we stepped into the hotel we were treated to fresh watermelon juice and cold towels and greeted like we were family returning from a long journey. The hotel has an amazing vibe about it, making me feel like I was in a cabin high in the mountains. Our room faced the lake and was so spectacular, with a very comfy bed and clean bathroom. The hotel was very environmentally conscious which I liked, using recycled paper for menus and terracotta pots for shampoo. Breakfast was beautiful and the staff were so attentive. We got dropped off to the airport by the manager, as he said the driver was busy. I have never experienced dedicated staff like this. Thank you!

We stayed here one night after hiking Poon Hill and it was a great place to stay and relax after hiking.  Very clean, modern and the staff was very kind and helpful.  The food from the restaurant was very good as well.  Would highly recommend staying here while in Pokhara.

Everything about this hotel was quaint and wonderful. From the moment you step into the hotel to the moment you check out, everyone had a smile and welcoming face. I took the junior suite on the 6th floor and it was huge. I fell in love with the indoor decor. Those circle designs on the ceiling is simple as it is mesmerizing. To the left of my suite was a wonderful terrace overlooking some hills and I had breakfast there every morning. The view of those hills and the call of the birds in the morning was refreshing before I headed out to do my stuff. I loved the place and you would too. Will definitely go there again. Be sure to try out the Harbour Restaurant downstairs as well as the mini bakery place they have near the entrance. On a good cool day, its wonderful there.

From the primly attired, outdoor guard to the cleaners, to the front office desk, everyone just kept beaming. That's hard not to like plus the Glacier Hotel enjoys a good location in Pokhara, is fresh and clean with spacious rooms and pleasing facilities. The sweeping views of the nearby snow-capped mountains on a fine day on the top deck are simply spectacular. Breakfast was also a winner all round with loads of choice and quality. Unless tired though, head out for lunch of dinner. There is so much on offer locally at great prices that it can't compete, but as a hotel it is top dog.

Tastefull decor, cosy rooms, great shower, delicious breakfast and friendly/polite  staff. Location is great with lake view but still in the calm part, few minutes walk from central part of Pokhara. The Harbor restaurant inside the hotel is also very nice.Would recomend this Hotel for sure.

Last year, I helped to organize a rather high-profile technical exchange in Pokhara, Nepal for NASA, USAID, and other colleagues from 20+ countries around the world.  With 95 people in attendance, we split accommodation across Glacier Boutique and two other hotels in Pokhara.  While I didn’t actually stay at Glacier, I was there quite often to liaise with the hotel and meet with colleagues.  Sunil and all others at the front desk were very friendly and professional and did everything that they could to make sure that their guests had a wonderful stay.  We particularly enjoyed the outside restaurant at the front of the hotel that overlooked the main street.  Guests also commented that the food was exceptional and that the view from the higher floors was breathtaking.   I should note that Sunil did an excellent job coordinating with the other two hotels.  With such a large group, it was no easy task.  However, Sunil was very organized which made the pick-up/drop-off process very easy.  We greatly appreciate Glacier’s warm hospitality and we hope to return to Pokhara one day!  Thank you for such a welcoming stay!

We came to Glacier after a few days at an amazing yoga retreat. While on the more expensive side, this place is worth it. The staff were friendly and helpful. Morning breakfasts were delicious. Our room was clean and spacious- bathroom was SO nice and clean as we aren't used to the toilet/shower combos so common in Asia. We loved that it was so close to so many shops and the lake and enjoyed the rooftop lounge area with opportunities for good pictures. Also, we found the bed to be very comfortable and slept very well there. Only negatives would be the wi-fi is spotty and you can find cheaper trekking/attraction options elsewhere. Thanks Glacier!

We had an amazing stay at the Glacier Hotel.  Staff was amazing, property and facilities were terrific and the room was very comfortable.The beds were amazing after having been on a trek for 12 days and the shower was great.  We ate breakfast a few times which was great.The only slightly negative was wifi that was hit or miss.  Not a huge deal just an annoyance. I will stay here again and would highly recommend it to anyone looking.

On Easter morning, we awoke to the smell of burning plastic. We went down to brunch (which isn't bad, btw) and smoke from burning trash across the street started blowing into the restaurant. Trash is constantly burning, but this billowing smoke was ridiculous -- almost as if it was meant to disturb others. To his credit, the manager confronted the men who were burning the trash, and had his very scared looking security man pour water on the fire. When the men defiantly added to the fire, I'd had enough and walked across the street. The men belonged to a local Tae Kwon Do club, explaining, I suppose, the timidity of the security guard (who refused to give me a bucket so that I could finish the job on the smoldering trash). The lead bully (chubby guy with a gold chain who kept rubbing his belly) told me I had no business confronting him about sending plastic smoke into the hotel because this is "the Nepali way." I live in Kathmandu and the constant trash burning, and breathing burning plastic in your own home, is infuriating. The men were giving the manager a lot of grief and trying to be intimidating. I knew there was no point calling the police because they would do nothing unless the men made a direct threat. No matter what I said to the lead bully about being a slob and a disgrace, he would make no threat, and the coward stopped burning trash at least. I was embarrassed that none of the other "environmentally conscious" Westerners in the vicinity got involved. Kudos to the manager for looking out for his guests.

Really recommend staying at Glacier Hotel - it's right on the lake so it's the most perfect location! The rooms are really nice, clean, light and well decorated. The staff are so friendly! Thank you so much for making so much effort for my mums birthday! Will definitely be back!!The only minuses I could say are temperamental wifi and hot water but it's not a big deal at all. The perks way out do these small things!

Fantastic staff, beautiful rooms and a really lovely bath! Loved the decor and ambience. Great location in central Pokhara and a short walk from central lakeside. Helpful, welcoming staff give a personalised and homely yet professional feel.

We stayed in the new wing that was opened after the earthquake - please ensure that when booking a room, you ask to stay in this wing. We booked a standard room and were upgraded to a junior suite, and I have not seen the standard rooms.The staff are polite, courteous, professional and helpful. The rooms are clean and comfortable and the entire wing - due to it being new- feels quite modern and clean and quiet. Each floor has a lovely terrace facing the lake. In the early mornings (if you are lucky) you can walk out onto the terrace, turn your back to the lake and capture some nice images of the mountain range, although the view is obstructed by the building itself as the balconies are facing in the opposite direction. Hairdryer, toiletries, english speaking staff, good location for restaurants and local attractions and experiences- Ticks all the boxes!Breakfast was not great, the pastries especially poor and service is quite slow, but overall a very good place to spend a few nights resting after a trek or visiting around Pokhara.

The Glacier Hotel was probably the best hotel we stayed in over 2 weeks in Nepal. The rooms were spacious with pretty much everything you could need (including mini bar). The staff are great. The breakfast was extensive

We stayed one night here and would have never left! First of all, the building is absolutely beautiful: old stone walls mixed with wooden ceilings, water fountains and art on the walls all given this hotel it's wonderful style. The rooms are great, the staff is helpful and kind, and the location is perfect! Ask for a room with a lake view.

We came to Nepal for our Honeymoon and stayed here a few nights. They were very sweet and covered our room in rose petals. The room had a huge terrace with beautiful views over the lake.
