Nepal to revisit and discover. Excellent food. We spend with my daughter a relaxing and discovering vacation. Visit Nepal👍🌈

Amazing experience. I truly recommend this place. All activities are great (especially the jeep safari) food is good & rooms are spacious and clean. The staff is amazing - they will take care of you from the start until the end of your stay.  I will definitively come back again and spread the word to my friends.

A perfect place for family vacation. Directly connected with nature and well managed property. Loved the food, ambience and friendly staffs. Its' a perfect place for meditate yourself. Thank you for memorable stay.

We stayed 2 night with family. Resport was awesome with friendly staffs . Our guide prem was so knowledgeable with wild life and nature . Swimpool is nice . Food was so delicious and great full to chef shiva.  Only sighting deck is lack to see the nature and wildlife.  Recommend for stay

Amazing experience, the service is exceptional, the food delicious and the place simply outstanding. The safaris were great, we saw lots of different species, and it was quite long so we could take our time (with even a tea break in the middle of the safari). Best experience ever!!

We absolutely loved our stay for our anniversary at Kasara Resort. All the staff were very friendly and best at their service. Highly recommended if you are looking to get away from the hustle and bustle of the city, in a secluded area in Chitwan.

The service is wonderful. They are very accommodating. We were taken on a jeep safari and saw many rhino. We saw the Tharu stick dance-amazing! Great experience and great hosts. Suzan was very knowledgeable as our naturalist.

Stayed here for 2-nights with my family. About 45 minutes from the main city and close to Chitwan National Park, the route to the resort is a scenic one with beautiful mustard fields, small villages and lush jungles. Because of its proximity to the jungle, the resort has a natural look and feel to it. You can hear the animals and birds at night. You will also see parrots on the trees outside the resort which is pretty cool!The villa style rooms are pretty with some modern and open-style elements. The rooms are spacious yet cosy. You can enjoy views of the resort gardens from the room. In the evening, they had organized a “Thaaru Dance” programme by the swimming pool which was interesting and fun. I liked that they served snacks during the show. It did get a little cold out in the open, so good to take a light jacket along. We also signed up for “Jungle Safari” which was about 2.3 hours. This too was exciting and refreshing! I must mention that the WIFI connection during out stay was very good and extremely fast which was very helpful.The staff were also friendly and helpful. The food was good too. Kasara Resort was a relaxing getaway, close to nature, away from the hustle and bustle of the city.Details of stay:Room Type: Deluxe VillaDuration:2 nightsPrice per night: 12,000 Nepalese Rupees

We had just come back from Heli Skiing in the Annapurna Sanctuary and stayed 3 nights here as an add on to our trip. The hotel was quite nice with great service and staff. We did one full day of Elephant riding and Jeep Safari and one full day of Canoe and Jungle Walk.  We were fortunate enough to have Babu as our fearless and knowledgeable guide throughout our stay. Babu was a total trooper...very much in tune with our special needs and always ensuring we got to experience the true Nepal culture. Although we did not see a Tiger (and we put in a lot of extra effort!) we had a fantastic time with Babu and his team. Babu ensured we got (per our request) the most authentic adventure possible both in the jungle as well as significant interaction and special moments with the local people in the village....just WOW! I would definitely go back and highly recommend the resort and the experiences to anyone visiting Nepal.

Fantastic stay. Good food,bar,entertainment,spa treatments,pool etc. Friendly staffs.  Super clean with excellent amenities.me and my frens had an amazingly crazy stay. Jungle safari, elephant shower are some of the activities that shouldn't be missed. Highly recommended. :-):-):-)

We had the privilege of staying at the beautiful Kasara resort this early March. From the excellent staff to the beautiful architecture and landscaping it truly exceeded our expectations. The Rooms and grounds are an excellent blend of modern design, luxury and comfort while blending beautifully with the landscape. The Staff are attentive and kind as it appears there are more of them than the guests. The true highlight of our stay was our guide Babu. His professional warm demeanor and extensive knowledge of the jungle and all it inhabitants from flora to fauna impressed us all. He and his team led our group the jungle with the most intimate knowledge of all that surrounded us reciting the Latin names as well as local of all that we saw and inquired . His ability to navigate the jungle finding ourselves just meters away from Rhinoceros and Crocodiles enhanced our experience entirely. From Lunch in the viewing towers to apres safari in local taverns with his friends, Babu truly made our Kasara experience something to be remembered for a lifetime.He will be missed.

We planned a short and quick one night trip to Kasara. It turned out to be one of the best experiences we have ever had.We were greeted at the Airport by JEET our guide for our entire stay--a very friendly and knowledgeable person.The entire staff and management were very attentive to our needs.A very relaxing environment-- definitely felt like we were one with nature-- seemed so very divine. Never experienced an outdoor bathroom/ shower experience with modern day facility and absolute privacy !The Elephant Safari, Canoeing in the river, visit to the crocodile breeding centre, watching the beautiful native- Tharu dance and a quick bike ride through a nearby village --were some of the things we managed to do in our 24 hr stay there.The staff was extremely friendly .My seventy two year old Mother was able to get on the elephant with ease and felt very comfortable throughout the ride.The whole family was in smiles throughout the trip!A short but extremely SWEET trip indeed.I would highly recommend this to anyone-- experience a piece of nature unlike any other!

The hotel is very new and the rooms are quite good and very trendy.  The downside to them is that the bedroom is connected to an outdoor but very private bathroom, and only the bedroom is heated.  So, when the temperature drops it's a little chilly to use.  Most of the time thought this is not a major issue and shouldn't be a problem.  The food was very nice they seemed to have a nice mix of western and nepalese food.  It seemed like they did table service when the resort was slow and buffet when it was busy so what you get will depend on how many people are there.  The first few nights the place was empty and wonderful.  The last night a group of 40 showed up and while it was still fine it did detract a little from the ambiance of the resort.  They offer elephant rides, boat rides and jeep rides which were all very nice and our guides were superb, but when the resort gets crowded they will bring in guides and trucks from other resorts so if you are not careful you could end up in a truck with 15 other tourists.  Our group never had this but it's something I would check on if traveling alone.

I've visited Kasara Resort twice, my first time was in May and my most recent visit was in August.Kasara Resort offers you a luxurious stay with well air-conditioned rooms, beautiful interior, amazing hospitality and service - the best thing is, you get all of that and you are so close to nature that is Chitwan National Park. Their jeep safari is worth the adventure and I especially loved their open-top jeep! They are quite new for Nepal. The resort has their own elephants so elephant bathing is just a stones throw away from Kasara. It's a wonderful experience, even for me and I have visited Chitwan seven times already.The dining area is open and you have a splendid view of the pool. The bar area upstairs is very cosy with lots of books on offer to read. The way the rooms are laid out is nice and you don't have to walk too far from the reception etc. I especially love the private lobby within each rooms and the open toilet and shower! You can shower under the open sky! Beautiful designs all around topped off by delicious food served by the Kasara kitchen team.

It is highly OVERRATED. We stayed here for two nights. Very good environment. Cottages are too good. Bathrooms are designed differently. As if totally you are in Forest. The whole staff is very courteous. BUT, very sorry to say that management May not be taking personal interest. Entry for Spa at lower ground floor is very risky, without any railing, one of Spa staff was untried.when we complain, they cancel the charges of spa. First time we saw Tea Kattle jar made of plastic, so if we drink hot water from this jar, water smells very bad plastic smell. In such type of luxurious resort, kattle having plastic jar is shameful for them. They don’t provide milk creamer sachet in the room. When we ask for it, they says, we don’t provide this. Anyway, they served hot milk for tea. Pizza is in there Menu, but first day they couldn’t serve. The floor in common washroom area, looks like very unclean. Even some walls near restaurant restaurant requires maintenance. Definitely, it was an excellent stay, BUT, HIGHLY OVERRATED.

We stayed for one night in Deluxe Villa. Rooms are spacious with unique shower facilities. The food and service were top class. Pool is nice and clean. The whole package (All meals, rooms,Elephant safari, canoeing, Jungle walk to Crocodile breeding centre) provided good value for money. Recommended!!!

We have just spent two nights at this awesome resort. The staff are incredibly welcoming. The rooms are just luxury and designed in keeping with the culture. The food is yummy and plenty of it. You can even have an illy caffe latte for breakfast. The safari trips by Jeep or elephant are well organised and the guides are very informative. Every bit of the experience was awesome. We even saw a tiger and sloth bear. I could have stayed much longer but definitely will return. Thank you for the amazing stay

I had a wonderful holiday. I experienced a holiday that I could only dream about. The staff at the resort were wonderful and caring. The accommodation was top class. The guides were so caring and helpful. I highly recommend this Resort.

this is truly of enchanted and an amazing place.  a perfect mixture of modern luxury carefully blent with nature.   accommodations are superb and staff is great and friendly really went out of the way to ensure a great stay.

Bagging all the expectation and temptation, we had planned our trip to Kasara Resort. Over taking the whole thing Kasara gave us a very warm welcome followed by smiling faces all around. Warm hospitality touched our hearts and care they provided to my  11 months old baby just blowed my mind and would like to thank every single person there in Kasara specially Shankar ji, Yadav ji and Gauri ji. Now coming to activities, we enjoyed all the activities so much which also proved to be informative with all the information provided by our guide Babu dai. It was a total fun. And since we were there for Valentine Package, all the arrangements from bbq dinner to the lantern to the romantic dinner was wonderful and secretly made me fall in love all over again. I can say Kasara is the Ultimate Destination to visit again n again.

I spent 2 nights at the resort this week and had the most amazing time. The all inclusive structure of the rates makes it nice and easy, especially for families travelling with children. There is a good variety of activities to choose from and they do their best to accommodate where you want to do something different.The grounds are immaculately kept, the rooms very nicely fitted out with local materials so the resort feels like at one with nature.A special mention to my guide, Jeet, who went over and beyond to make my stay memorable. Nothing was too much trouble and he was completely knowledgable about the surrounds and animals. He even taught me how to ride a motorbike into town so I could buy some soccer balls for the local children to play with. We left super early as the sun was rising on my last morning to ride out on push bikes to some of the poorest villages in the region. We were like the pied piper, with throngs of kids running after us as we rode through. We spent a couple of hours visiting numerous villages playing with the children. It was a very special experience and felt wonderful to do something for the community. I would like to make a recommendation to the resort management about placing a giving box/wishing well next to the gratuity box at reception for guests to make contributions, where funds can used to purchase sports equipment, books, pens, and help install street lights for the communities within which it operates.My only small gripe was having to pay a single's supplement for my room. As the rate was all inclusive (all meals and activities), it hardly felt fair or made sense I had to pay more than had I brought a companion. I was told I was the first lone visitor, so perhaps management need to rethink the fare structure.

Our family of 5 arrived the day before Christmas Eve and were greeted warmly with moist towels and lemongrass drinks - a refreshing way to begin our stay.  No more road dust and bumpy roads.  Kasara was a true oasis for us.  Having enjoyed stays at various 4 Seasons properties around the world, we were pleasantly surprised at the same level of hospitatlity in the rugged countryside farmlands neighboring Chitwan.  The quiet calm of the spacious contemporary lobby set the tone for the clean lines and organic materials used throughout the resort.  We were told that every space, including our suites, sought to incorporate the outdoors with the in.  With 3 boys in tow, from 7 to 14, I was curious if this design plan would be practical.  Let's just say that everyone was happy - and when you have spacious suites (with several distinct areas of bathroom/entry sitting area/bedrooms) we parents were glad to be able to put some space between the boys from time to time.  Comfy beds, high thread count sheets, great wifi = joy.  One son hesitated at the showers since one side is open to the elements (buffered for privacy by a high walled, private, Japanese-inspired rock garden) but my take was: consistently hot water from a personal tankless water heater, strong water pressure, rain head, and pristine white fluffy towels = awesome.  I wondered if I would feel cold but I was so warm from the hot shower, I was able to dry my hair with the in-wall blow dryer and do my make-up without ever feeling chilly.  This, in the heart of winter.  I was wearing the fluffy white robe provided in the closet, though.  I thought the food was amazing.  After raving about the decor and bathroom and layout of the rooms, I might rush through this, but suffice it to say that being a foodie (or really, an 'eatie') I found delicious options at every meal.  I prefer their delicious Nepali and Indian food, and Chinese food, but their Western styled items were excellent too.  With our group of 5, plus another 2 of extended family, over the course of several days, no one complained about any meals.  The buffet was always clean, elegant, delicious and hot.  Two of our kids are pickier than the third, and they were always well sated with enough tasty proteins, veggies, and oh boy their croissant type rolls were delicious.  Service was fantastic - in particular I'm thinking of the restaurant servers and our safari guide.  We tried the Jeep Safari, the Elephant safari (a huge hit for all of us) and the canoe safari (an even huge-er hit!).  Our final morning we had delicious poori / aloo dum aka authentic Nepali breakfast items among the other buffet options and I was a happy camper.  The kids liked the custom omelettes that they grew to love back in the U.S. at family brunches out.  A couple other things: I had a great massage in the spa - in a wonderfully warmed room (my pet peeve is a drafty massage room), and the design lover in me appreciated the numerous light options in the bedrooms - well designed lighting makes such a difference when seeking a cocoon of relaxation, serenity, and respite from a dusty world.  Thank you Kasara, for a high adventure with luxury touches.  We were certainly pampered!

We recently stayed at Kasara Resort for four days and it has provided beautiful memories. The resort was beautiful appointed and the staff very friendly and helpful. A special mention must go to Kamahl our guide, he was very knowledgeable and sensitive to our needs.   We give it the highest recommendation.

I came here recently on a team retreat as a facilitator. I was impressed by the place. Very different vibe from what I expected. Great staff - from the managers to the amazing helpful and knowledgeable guides. Was upgraded to VIP room and had an amazing room. Food was good and had some continental dishes mixed with Nepali food. They organized jungle walk, canoeing and local visit to Tharu village for us...with lots of engagement and professionalism. I think among the 58 people we were was not one critical voice. Just missed some espresso or cappuchino in the morning, but then I am living in Bangkok and I am spoilt. Highly recommended to be the best option when visiting Chitwan National Park or just need some days closer to nature.

2 nights spent at Kasara became a lifetime memories that me and my wife will always cherish, Wonderfully Designed resort from the Lobby to the Rooms , it's so Cozy and Comforting , all of the staffs are so welcoming , friendly and smiling :) , the outdoor activity guides are so good, they can tell us the entire history of the Wild animals to plants of the Chitwan National Park and surroundings , I was amazed to know so much knowledge and informations about our National park , the Guide Baburam even told us the variety of the Grasses and the plants there :O :O :O i have never been guided and briefed like this before :D , We were so much deeply touched when we had a surprise surprise by Kasara resort family ! it was a Elephant written Happy anniversary all over it's body , painted and maked up beautifully carrying the Anniversary Cake :D and all the Kasara Resort family there wishing us , it was little sadening leaving the place today ! Kasara has won our hearts and we will defenetly keep coming back , all the Best wishes for your Success & Achivements KASARA Resort :D God Bless !

Too many problems! We had bought the monsoon package which included some activities and 30 minutes spa for couples. We were so looking forward for this vacation, however, it had been troublesome since the moment we wanted to reserve the package. We had made a reservation on Friday, the reservation staff told us to bank in deposit into their account, however, banks closes at 2 pm and we were unable to bank in the amount. We had also asked for other payment method, which they did not have. They gave us late confirmation due to which we could not pay the deposit, and they were not flexible about it. When we mentioned about this to the hotel staff, we were told that a lot of guests had cancelled their reservation hence had to make full payment before arrival.They only had 1 spa therapist at that time so my partner asked if I could get his time as well which the staff agreed to. However, when it was checkout time we were billed for 1 hour of spa which amounted NRS 5328. When I told the receptionist guy that I hadn't consumed 2 hours of spa he argued that I had. Later, the therapist was called out then she said that I had done 104 minutes of massage, however, they had already inputted 2 hours into the system so I still had to pay for the full hour as they cannot change their system. I don't mind paying but what I found unethical was that I wasn't reminded that my 1 hour had been over by the therapist and why was I only given 104 minutes of massage when they charged me for 120 minutes. The staff said that their previous package consisted of 60 minutes per person therefore, they had made a mistake, however, I still don't see how that is my problem and I had to pay for it.Another thing I found strange was there was no mineral water in the room, however they did provide drinkable water in glass bottles (they said they try to be environmental friendly) which is a good thing. But when we asked for refill of the room water, they brought mineral waters in plastic bottles (which they charge), we had to return the bottled water twice, I was very clear when asking for normal room water refill, so I don't understand how they came with mineral water both times.Since the water came in glass bottles, I wanted to boil the water before drinking it. Sadly, the kettle passed some electricity, which wasn't that serious but I cannot believe that a 3 star hotel can compromise on safety of guest for some reason.We had 3 meals a day included in the package for the first 5 meals we were provided with buffet, however, there was no buffet in the last meal. The staff told us that the other guests had ate and left already so they didn't want to provide us with buffet and were given food by plate even though we had reached the restaurant 30 minutes before the buffet ended. They did give us choices for everything that came in the buffet but it was quite hurting that they would feel some guests are more important than other guests. When we had asked about the checkout time, the receptionist asked another guy (who was in a small room behind the reception) shouted out “tell them to go after breakfast”, breakfasts ends at 9am. I am surprised that the check out time is so early. Small details such as torn bedsheets, missing amenities in the room. We were told during the briefing that there would be a mini fridge/bar in the room which surprisingly wasn't there.(they told us they were giving us their best room)Not everything was bad, some things were good.The hotel is picture perfect. and the staff were polite and amazing. Special thanks to our guide Mr. Madan, he was one of the reason our stay had been pleasant.The menu in the buffet kept changing so it was good for variety. I had the best cake as most of the cakes tend to be too sugary and watered down but the one served by them was the best in all of Nepal. I also had the best scrambled egg in Nepal.Their pool was clean, room has great decorations and had mosquitoes repellent which was quite thoughtful.We had long awaited for this vacation with Kasara due to the hype on Instagram. Sadly, it wasn't worth it. There are far better resorts at a better pricing on other side of Chitwan.

Fantastic resort . Rooms were astounding and well maintained.  They provide mosquito repellent cream and plug in devices. We had a resident millipede in the shower we named Millicent. She was no trouble at all. We were fascinated by her. The butterflies around the resort were beautiful. The food was beautiful. Staff were very helpful and attentive. The activities were well organised and planned. We had suraj as our main guide. He was very good. Saw rhinos, deer, monkeys, boar, mugger crocodile , lots of birds. No tigers but you can’t have everything!  The Tharu culture show was great. The resident cat was very friendly

Loved my stay here. The rooms are huge and have a earthy feel to it. The resort is located in a quiet place and give you a peace of mind. the food they serve are limited in option but manage to serve different cuisine throughout our stay. the guides they have are quite knowledgeable and from the local communities. I would definitely recommend this place to my friends. Just one recommendation to the management, the way out to restaurant and reception is a bit confusing. Out colleagues got mazed multiple times due to lack of proper signs on which direction to follow.

My friend and I visited this resort after two months in the Khumbu area. We loved the room, the pool area, and the large magnificent garden. The room is air conditioned, bug free with a spacious entrance, and has interesting shower area which I liked.The complex was designed by an Australian architect and this shows. The staff are always helpful.The safaris, travelling by boat, jeep, foot and elephant, with a very knowledgeable, polite and helpful local guide, were excellent! We saw a bengal tiger, sloth bear, and numerous rhino along with much more. Couldn’t be better.The only disappointment for us was the lack of fresh fruit and vegetables on the menu. The food was quite stodgy ie lots of carbs etc and it was not possible to purchase any snacks there such nuts, lollies etc. Take some with you.Overall this place was excellent value and I highly recommend it.

Excellent resort.  Design defies description.  It is simplicity itself but undeniably luxurious simplicity.  Staff is excellent and the food is worth writing home about.  I would not hesitate to recommend the resort.  My only criticism is that their elephants are still chained instead of in corrals.

Our family of 5 (2 teens)had a trip booked through Alpine Exodus which included two amazing days in Chitwan jungle at Kasara Jungle Resort. We were so surprised to find the resort to be like something out of Napa Valley, California. We drove up to a luxurious spa resort with a pool, individual bungalows, a water fixture at the entrance that made it feel like you are walking on water. The room was huge with various lighting features i have only seen at the W. The bathroom was the size of a room itself with the shower open to the sky, yet hot. It was incredible. The bed was feather, supper soft. We were totally surprised. The manager took personal care of us, we felt like royalty. He joined us for a talk during dinner and then other guests as well. It was a one on one service. The food was great, the buffet included various dishes from curry to Italian, BBQ and salads. Everything was fresh and the atmosphere tranquil. That night it was new years, but we had classy music that was not loud and yet perfect. The best part of the stay was the Personal guide who took care of us for two days. Kamal Adhikari is a naturalist and knows everything about the jungle and the animals. He took us on an elephant ride and we saw many animals, then we went on a jungle jeep tour and saw rhinos as well as deer, bizzon, peacocks, wild cat, wild boars etc. He told us  a lot of information and spoke good english, he was super  nice and treated us like with personal care. He even took pictures of all of us with our cameras and made sure we felt comfortable. It felt like a personal trip without the crowds or seeing anyone else. It was truly private. The next day, the kids went to wash elephants and then drive them. They were excited beyond belief. We had the best time at this resort, a great guide Kamal and the staff at the resort were top notch!

We arrived on 10th Dec 2015 and stayed 2 nights. From the moment we arrived till departure, there was never a dull moment. Service was exemplary and small details were not overlooked. Rooms were clean and lively decorated. There is always something to discover and  explore.  Miss Gouri and her crew have done a great job to make our stay a memorable one. Well done Miss Gouri!  Oh, I must also compliment the chef and restaurant crew for spinning up a variety of great food. I recommend visitors to experience the wildlife jungle safari. You will be taken to the wilderness by the high spirited and friendly guide Mr. Kamal who knows his jungle like the back of his palm. We could not forget our sending off on the last day, Miss Gouri and her crew were waving ever so passionately. It has left an indelible mark in our memories.Photo: Miss Gouri on rightChia & AnneSingapore

2 nights (3 days) at the end of an amazing trip to Bhutan & Nepal but this was among the best of our experiences in the trip. Open plan nature of the resort and rooms was a joy (and so great after Kathmandu). Jeet our naturalist and guide was superb and so considerate making sure we made the absolute best our of the short stay. The river canoe trip and the elephant washing are musts. 2 nights might not seem much but you will pack so much in. No tigers unfortunately (just a footprint) but crocs, deer, birds and rhinos - don't go with a list just go with the flow and you will enjoy. You need long sleeve t shirts (keep tucked in on jungle walk !), long trousers and shoes for jungle walk (trainers or merrels will do) and swim gear for the pool and the elephant washing. An early (very) morning cycle ride through local village was an added bonus. Food was good for tourist hotel in this part of world, Nepal is not a gastronomic holiday :)  All staff very friendly and helpful. Should not need malarone and malaria risk now v low but use mosquito & fly repellent. The 20min flight from Kathmandu on a 41 seater turbo prob with Yeti Air was interesting. ENJOY - WE DID

A Zen-like oasis beside Chitwan  in the best possible sense as in calming minimalist.  Resort is well maintained and the accommodations are wonderful.  My unit consisted of a small sitting area with a lily pond which was located in the middle with a very spacious bedroom on one side with the bathroom & shower on the other.  The bathroom area partially open to the sky.  Staff are very helpful & friendly.  Activities provided by the resort are very good especially the elephant safari.  If there was a minor quibble it was that at times during meals the service staff not as attentive to needs especially given the quality of this resort.  However, even given that I would highly recommend staying at Kasara.  A most pleasant surprise!!!

Wonderful concept and impeccable service! Very homely feel with friendly and energised staff and the culinary simply commendable. Surely a second visit on the cards with close friends and family. Special thanks to Babu and everyone at Kasara who made our trip memorable! Thanks

Friends and I spent two nights and three relaxing days at Kasara Resort.  Timing wasn't the best as it was during monsoon (early July - exceptionally hot and unpredictable rain) so there weren't a lot of guests but this did not stop the staff from making our trip memorable!  The food was catered to our tastes (we had a vegetarian amongst us and great meal choices were provided, tweaked upon request) and was delicious!  The rooms were beautiful - simple but made to remind you that you are there to enjoy the natural beauty of the area.  When you open the door to your room/villa, you cross over a small bridge/pond into a outdoor sitting area.  The shower/bathroom are open to nature - loved it!  The activities in the Chitwan park were wonderful - our guide, Babu, was AWESOME!!  From elephant-back safari, to the open/tiered safari truck - the experiences were memorable as we saw the exotic one-horned Asian rhino, up close (on elephant back, waded into the marsh where one was casually cooling off), many/many interesting birds, deer, a crocodile and wild boar. This resort is highly recommended!  ALL the staff were attentive, friendly, and helpful...despite what seemed to be a lot of activities, the setting of the resort is peaceful/relaxing....GO! ENJOY!

Our stay and Safari at Kasara Lodge was organised by Ker & Downey who also organised most of the other parts of our Nepal trip. The Kasara Lodge is in a beautiful setting in the buffer zone of the Chitwan National Park and provides a luxurious setting for going off on their organised Elephant, Canoe and Jeep Safaris of which we did all three. The accommodation is first class with a huge swimming pool and restaurant on site. The key is getting a good guide and we had Babu who took excellent care of us including taking to a family members house for drinks when we got caught in a rain shower.  First we went on a 2 hour elephant safari where we came across a huge rhino bathing. The two elephants we had for our group of 6 were lovely and obviously well looked after by their keepers. The next day Babu took us on a canoe trip to see crocodiles in the river of which we saw two.  In the afternoon he took us for a 4 hours jeep safari where he promised us we would see at least 12 x rhinos. We actually saw about 15 some with their babies. Truly memorable. We set him the challenge of seeing a tiger something very rare. Sadly not achieved although the jeep in front of us was filming a rhino when a tiger ran across the track in front of them. We missed this but did hear the tiger and cub growing and pawing in the jungle close to us although not seen.  Babu and the Kasara Lodge staff really looked after us well.  On the last day Babu even accompanied us to the airport to make sure all our luggage arrived safely.  A great location and event.  Thank you K&D for organising this for us.

As three adult couples on a Safari holiday we were thoroughly spoilt and treated like royalty by the brilliant Babu (our guide/host/advisor) and the whole Kasara team. Whether canoeing, washing elephants, or hunting (with our eyes...) for Tigers we were given brilliant insight to Chitwan and its surrounding area. I would thoroughly recommend the resort and the area to curious adults and younger travellers alike. If you do go to Kasara: request Babu as your host! What a gentleman.We will be back.

We stayed there 4 nights during Feb. 15 and enjoyed every aspect of it! Kasara a relatively new resort (18 months we were told) with nice rooms and amenities but mostly great people : warm hospitality & very professional staff from amangement to waiters. Special THANKS to Gayatri ( Mr. smile) and to Kamal the Guide whose knowledge of animals and birds is amazing.Note : the yard behinf the kitchens is used as plastic bottles dump but i was assured it is temporary (awaiting recycling)

My second stay at Kasara was as wonderful as the first. I took family visiting from Australia and we all felt that the service in particular was exceptional. Gayatri Prasad Gautam in the dining room looked after our every need and guides Babu and Jeet were solicitous and knowledgeable. We had a fabulous time.

We spent two nights at the lodge and had a wonderful time.  The rooms are warm and clean with welcome warm showers.  The guide we had, Babu, was amazing and knew everything about the national park, all the animals and, more broadly, Nepal.  He was an excellent host and made sure we got to see a rhino on our last day.  If you visit be sure to ask for Babu - he is an encyclopaedia and a great guy.Service generally is also excellent and the staff are wonderful people.

Very pleasant and attentive staff met us and provided face towels and cold drinks as we registered.  Rooms are large with an open air sitting area in entryway and enclosed open air shower and toilet across the entryway from the closed bedroom.  Free WiFi was available in the central complex (pay-for-use in rooms.)  Very attractive grounds including swimming pool with lounge chairs.  Game viewing in and near Chitwan National Park can include elephant-back, dugout canoe, walking and open jeep. Programme can be tailored to your interests.  Although we did not see any tigers, we did see fresh tiger tracks as well as one-horned rhinos, several species or deer, two species of monkeys, two species of crocs, wild boar and many species of birds.  The guides were very helpful and attentive.  Food was well-prepared and tasty.  The Christmas Eve arrival of Father Christmas with the "Christmas Elephant" wearing a XXXL Santa hat and red and white drape was unexpected and a delight!  The last 18 km of the road is very rough but is to be paved over the next few years.

I researched multiple places in Chitwan on my recent visit to Nepal. I wanted to find a place where I was not only close to nature & wildlife but also a place with quality services. I must say Kasara exceeded my expectations in all areas.  After a lot of research on resorts in the area I was confident in my choice.The architecture was extraordinary & unique among the many resorts in Chitwan.The moment we arrived - we were greeted with smiling faces, oshibori & refreshing herb juice which was grown in their own garden. My little villa with open concept was luxurious & spotless.  Kasara had all the activities well planned. Food was wonderfully cooked and the dessert were to die for. Going off on an eleplant ride was so much fun with a very informative guide. They were knowledgeable about birds & animals to plants in the jungle ( we were lucky to experience close encounters with few rhinos, wild boar, deer, monkey different types of birds & many more) The evening Tharu dance program was well organized and lot of fun. Excellent on-going history of Chitiwan in the nearly 3 hr Jeep safari thru the jungle was thrilling. We thoroughly enjoyed the bullock ride to the historic Tharu Village.The early morning canoe ride with our wonderful guide to see crocodiles in their natural habitat was very exciting & informative. The river was teeming with different types of birds. And not to forget the elephant bath. Make sure you have at least 2 to 3 days to  enjoy this place and take advantage of all the activities. This place is a must, must visit !

What a wonderful resort this is, I had read many great reviews and we were not disappointed.From my first point of contact with Sunaina communication was prompt , friendly and very helpful.We arrived on Christmas Eve for three nights with our two children age 11 and 8 and upon arrival were greeted with fresh towels and drinks. Our accommodation was superb, very private and unique with two small ponds in the entrance hall and the bathroom half outdoors with plants growing.The resort itself is very relaxed and even though they were nearly full it never felt crowded. The grounds are beautiful and well kept. The swimming pool looked very inviting but it was a little too cold to go in while we were there. The whole place is built to be at one with nature, even the restaurant is open . We had read great reviews about Babu the guide so I asked if we could have him take us out on the various excursions, we were lucky to have him assigned to our family for the three days we were there . Babu was fantastic, nothing was too much trouble for him, he was so attentive and very knowledgable. He was wonderful to our two children and we felt in safe hands with him.Christmas Eve was brilliant, before dinner we watched a cultural show performed by the local Tharu people and at the end Santa arrived on an elephant with presents for all the children staying at the resort. It was magical and a lot of fun. We were offered complimentary drinks and snacks throughout the evening.The great thing about the resort is that Babu tailored our itinerary to our wishes, we went on a canoe trip, a guided jungle walk, two elephant safaris, a four hour jeep safari, a trip to a local Tharu village by ox cart, a visit to the elephant stables and a cultural evening of dancing. In between trips we found the resort a great place to relax and drink coffee.The food was delicious and varied for our whole stay and all the staff in the restaurant were friendly and polite.We were lucky enough to see so many animals whilst here, we saw eleven Rhino, sloth bears, all four types of deer, crocodiles, wild hogs, peacocks and many different types of beautiful birds. The elephant safari was a definite highlight especially with the baby elephant tagging along on both our safaris.We had a truly memorable Christmas and our two children are still talking about it.Thank you for a fantastic few days, I hope we can return one day.

Beautiful resorts with lots of activities. We were greeted by the great front desk staff as we arrived, then taken to our bungalow, sporting an entryway with a pond and a sitting area under the sky. The spacious and nicely appointed bedroom was fully enclosed and very comfortable. The bathroom area, on the other side of the sitting area, was also open to the sky with plants growing behind the sink and shower area. The whole thing gave the feeling of a jungle lodge without overdoing the jungle.Activities were great. Our guide, Babu, was very knowledgeable, very nice, and it was obvious that he cared a lot for the flora and fauna he was showing us. His English was excellent. He was constantly on the lookout for animals and signs of animals. We did the elephant trek which was wonderful, the early morning boat ride and jungle walk, the crocodile hatchery, elephant washing and feeding. I loved the elephants, which are the property of the lodge. They were beautiful, gentle and well trained. I just wish they weren't chained to their stable. Food and drink were very good, and the restaurant staff was wonderful. We had one night and 1.5 days, but I would recommend at least two nights, maybe three, to really enjoy everything the resort and the park have to offer.

We are here currently, my parents sister and I in two rooms, and both the Kasara lodge and its staff are great! We booked it based on trip adviser reviews and they were accurate.Our guide Babu is fantastic, being a local with good English as well as a nature expert and experienced guide. He is organised and funny and makes us feel safe as well as guiding us on our adventures. Sounds corny but it's true! He has help from equally talented and friendly drivers, canoers, elephant keepers etc. All of whom go out of their way to make you feel welcome. Overall it's lots of fun with beautiful scenery, wildlife, culture and all in the comfort of a lovely resort.Rooms are clean and luxuriously spartan with open-air bathrooms. Little things like robes and insect repellent are provided. The pool area is gorgeous! Perfect for lounging with your book in between activities.The dining and bar areas are delightful and the food varied but all delicious (too much and too hard to say no!). The waitstaff are excellent, especially the main restaurant host/manager who is extremely warm and hospitable.Don't want to leave!

My family and I (two adults and three children) stayed in Chitwan for three nights and three days, we were actually planning to only stay for two night and two days, because the service and activities were so fun and interesting. We loved the elephant Safari as we got to see lots of animals from the back of a giant mammal, also the second most clever.(dolphins are the most clever.) We also enjoyed the jeep safari and the canoe ride as we got to see other parts of the wide diversity of animals in chitwan national park. We loved everything about the resort, it was very convenient and great roos as they were comfortable and clean, the only thing we found a problem was the pool which was not clean for the first two days that we arrived but the fixed it up on the third day which was really convenient as we had to leave the next day, other than that two thumbs up!

We had a lovely time at the Kasara restart.   It is only a couple of years old so everything feels new and fresh, the bathroom is an open outdoor bathroom so it may be off putting if you do not like creepy crawlies.  The staff were wonderful particularly the general manager Gauri, the were always accommodating to requests.  The food is wonderful despite being a buffet.  Great variety and very tasty, one evening they even laid on some local dancing for entertainment.   Every evening they lay out your next days activities, normally there will be three or four activities the following day made up of at least one safari ride, the guides and spotters were generally very friendly.My big concern was how the elephants were being treated, they were regularly hit with axe like tools by the elephant minders.  Also I got the impression elephants were exhausted by the end of the day.  I have travelled South and South East Asia and have never seen such handling of elephants.  I am not sure if our experience was a one off or a regular occurrence.
Excellent service ! Gréât food . Lovely people ! Alish from the front desk , Sagar at the restaurant and Suresh from activities were extremely hospitable and made our stay enjoyable!! Thanks guys!! !
One of the best swimming pool, and one of the best hospitality ive ever seen Thankyou Kasara for making our stay fun and food is soo delicious here ,we will visit again very soon for our next visit .

It was good experience over all. Food was super good :)… grt hospitality portrayed by internal staffs … just a slight renovation required interms of room to maintain the Kasara standard .. thanx for the grt gesture :)Thanx Pawan for accommodating the needs 😇

We visited Kasara Resort in November 2019 and it was truly a beautiful experience. We stayed in a private villa with a private pool, it was just amazing. Huge huge thank you to all the employees working so hard to make our stay wonderful. Neha dd, always greeting us everyday, gave us all the information about our stays and tours. Suresh dai was our tour guide when you went boating and jungle walk. Sudip dai was very kind while we went boating and showed us the crocodile breeding centre. We had the privilege to see the Tharu dance, another totally amazing experience. Being nepalese it was really nice seeing our diverse culture. Thank you once again to all the villagers who performed and thank you to Babu dai for entertaining us. The restaurant employees made sure we were always taken care of while dining. Everyone I mentioned are a real asset to the hotel, our experience would not have been this amazing if it wasn't for all of them. We will definitely return again, thank you Kasara Resort :)

After a 10 minute flight from Pokhara to Bhuratpur, we were welcomed by Our Kasara driver and driven 30 minutes to the lodge.  A very pleasant welcome awaited. Cold towel and lemon grass tea.  Our room, A2, is beautiful.  Really enjoyed having tea/coffee facilities in the room.  Great food !

We had a most relaxing time at Kasara, the grounds are quite beautiful, the proximity to the Chitwan National Park is great.It feels like a great exclusive resort. They have 2 elephants at the resort, who are incredibly well looked after, watching them their bath in the nearby river was a fantastic experience. Our guide to the park, Suraj Dara made our safari experience very interesting, we were lucky to have him accompany us to the airport and we learned so much about Nepal during that journey. It is rare to see a place where all working there seems to be happy, it was a delight to be there, The food from the restaurant was very good too, my only suggestion for improvement would maybe to try ot make the bar area more convivial and to build on the decoration, it was very plain in comparison to the rest of the resort. Amazing time there highly recommended stop on your visit to Nepal!

My daughter and I stayed three nights at Kasara the end of May.  This was the best part of our trip to Nepal.  From the minute we got off the plane we were treated like family. Bapu was assigned as our guide for this trip and he made the adventure spectacular.  We laughed constantly, enjoyed the animals in the forest, relaxed for a bit by the pool and ate the best food!  This is not just a hotel, it is an experience. We did not want to leave and there were tears in our eyes and also in the new friends we met from the hotel when we left. You should not travel to Nepal and miss this experience.

Best thing of this hotel is warm hospitality. They took care very well.The foods are good, skilled staffs, pleasant environment..Room was spacious, well organized & neat-clean.Wide range of swimming pool is really very amazing..!!

One of the best resort I have stayed in Nepal. Bathroom was phenomenal. Best resort to spend your time with your better half. Pool was also one  of the highlights. Private pool is also available in some villa's so you can ask for it you you want some private space 😁

If you wanna explore Chitwan NP and still looking for some relaxing days, Kasara is the place to be. This resort offers cosy bungalows, a pool and all activities at Chitwan NP. Delicious food (breakfast, lunch and dinner) is offered as well. All staff is super - friendly and helpful. One example: My girlfriend is not a meat-lover but she likes fish. The waiter asked her always if he shall bring her a grilled fish in addition to the buffet. :)The price might sound high if you are booking a 4 days / 3 nights package, however, please keep in mind that this includes all meals and activities / NP entrance fees. Organizing same level of value in Sauraha on your own can easily come more expensive. If you might miss any explanation about flora and fauna during safari, you do not have to worry at all. Babu hold an excellent presentation ("Slide show") in the evening about aninmals and plants in Chitwan NP. Really informative.Another controversial topic are elephant safaris. We appreciated approach taken by Kasara that this is voluntarily excercise. Captive elephants would not survive in the wild, so in our eyes much better if they belong to a resort like Kasara who treat them well.We also liked very much that Kasara tries to employ mostly local Tharu staff and giving people living in this area adequate work opportunities. Our special thanks to Sunaina who handled our booking and ensured that we feel like at home and to Diamond who was our guide on most activities. It was a real pleasure sharing his knowledge with us.

This resort is absolutely breathtaking. From the moment you arrive, it’s like stepping into a beautiful world of rustic nature meets luxury. If you want a true and authentic experience in this part of Nepal then you will love this magical place. The decor of the resort is very Balinese in many ways while somehow not taking away from the natural splendor of the rustic environment. Service and staff are incredible. The food is exceptional as well. They serve traditional quisine in a beautiful modern style. The resort is designed in a very artful way. Perfect for peaceful relaxation as well as outdoor adventures. Looking forward to coming back again for another yoga retreat.

My wife and I recently stayed for 2 nights and wished we had stayed for longer.The rooms and lovely the food was exceptional and the guides did there best to pack as much in as we could.Fabulous staff made this a very enjoyable stay and I would recommend to anyone going to Chitwan.

If you are planning to visit Chitwan this is where you need to stay. I stayed here with my young family and we all fell in love with this place. The resort is well managed and maintained. It has a relaxing atmosphere and the food was amazing. I specially enjoyed the Jeep safari and having coffee & cookies while watching Rhinos and Crocodile in the nearby lake.The staff here are well groomed in hospitality. They made a good itinerary for us. The kitchen staff even made special food order for my 4 year old daughter. She was crying when we had to check-out as she did not want to leave.Special thanks to Sunaina for looking after us.-Raghu

The tranquility of Kasara Resort following a stay in Kathmandu was noticeable. This Lodge may not have the facilities of a top commercial hotel in the capital, but it does exude local character backed by amazingly friendly service. I suggest that the accommodation is more than adequate for the average person who has chosen to be in an area such as Chitwan for the purpose of a holiday. All the staff are friendly and went out of their way to deliver a match to the requirements  of their clients. In our case, food requirements are far from normal, but the efforts  of the kitchen staff to deliver acceptable meals for us was both amazing and greatly appreciated. Were we to be visiting the area again, I would not hesitate to revisit. A very big thank you to the whole team at the Lodge for our memorable stay.

An excellent getaway from the Kathmandu pollution. We traveled by air and fell in love with Kasara from the moment they picked us up at the airport. Our guide, Babu, was exceptional. Mostly self taught, he is knowledgeable, well read, a great communicator, particularly caring, and responsive to needs. The location of the resort and all of the activities they provide were exactly what we needed - combining out door activities with adequate amounts of down time. The food was also excellent. A bit pricey, but well worth the expense - you are really paying for the experience.

Staying at Kasara was a welcoming treat after trekking for several nights in the Annapurna Mountain Range. The grounds, staff, food, and tours were all excellent. My fiancé and I did a two night/three day package, which included the room, tours and all meals. The hotel was beautiful, modern, and clean. They welcomed us with a delicious drink and cool towel. Our room was in our own villa, which featured indoor/outdoor living. The bedroom was completely closed off, easing our minds about mosquitos at night. The bathroom features a partially outdoor shower. All tours were excellent and included an elephant safari, jeep safari, walking tour, canoe ride and visit to the crocodile center. The staff was dedicated and ensured that we had an excellent experience. On the jeep safari our tour guide provided complementary beverages and snacks, which we enjoyed while watching the nearby rhinos! Our guide, Kamal, was very knowledgable and demonstrated a sincere interest about the the animals and history of the park. In addition to the wonderful hotel grounds and tours, the food was excellent. Each meal was delicious. My one complaint re: Kasara was the cost of getting to and from the resort. We took a bus from Pokhara which was relatively cheap (our only other option was a private taxi for ~125 dollars), but landed us far from the resort. We ended up spending approx 40 dollars to get from the bus station to the resort, and nearly that much to get from the resort to the airport. Even though the bus ended up taking more time, and did not end up saving us as much money as we had thought it would, I would take the bus again. Personally, I felt safer on bus due to the poor road conditions (rocky/narrow) between Pokhara and Chitin. In the end, my stay at Kasara was a highlight of my trip and well worth it. I would highly recommend it.

We had 3 days here and enjoyed every minute. We did the elephant safari twice - Mr Buddhi even let us take the reins on one occasion and he pointed out numerous tiger footprints - the jeep safari, the jungle walk and canoe boat cruise. We saw tonnes of amazing rhino, deer, monkeys, crocodiles and even the infamous sloth bear!! Kamal is an absolute star and is passionate about everything in the wild and in trying to make sure every moment you have in the park is memorable. On the transfer down to the resort he even stopped off and showed us a local wedding, he's a pleasure to spend time with. Outside of the activities, the food is great, service top notch and the rooms are beautiful! We were treated like kings and I'd recommend this resort to anyone looking to spend some time in Chitwan. Overall, great experience!

We stopped for 1 night on March 30 Collected from the airport in a clean modern minibus , cold towels and drinks on board30 min drive to the resort , more cold towels and drinks for welcome Stunning resort , pool is first class , rooms are well designed with a courtyard entrance and shower in the open air Air con works a treat Restaurant delivers good food and staff are very attentive, beers are cold The guided us into the park , also arranged an elephant safari and elephant river washing experience which was great Highly recommended

Kasara helped make our 5th anniversary a memorable one. A luxurious abode surrounded by wilderness. Professional staff cater to all your needs including personalized safari packages and timing. Clean rooms, gourmet food and drinks and cultural shows are the icing on top. Best part, an elephant delivering our anniversary cake to the dining area.

I spent 3 wonderfully relaxing nights at Kasara Resort and participated in all of their fantastic activities and programmes. The entire experience was FANTASTIC and I can't recommend it enough.  The rooms are absolutely beautiful - clean, private, and extremely comfortable. The spacious bathroom is separate from the bedroom and makes you feel like you have your own private villa... The meals are all catered for and excellent with wonderful service from the extremely helpful staff. And the highlight above and beyond this was the safari programmes - my guide Tamal was ABSOLUTELY fantastic. He catered to all of our requests and it was clear that he absolutely loved his job and was keen to share his knowledge. We saw rhinos, elephants, deer, crocs and so many birds. I learned so much and had such a wonderful time.

Great place with friendly staff, good food, stylish and comfy rooms.   Having a great time.  The grounds are very pretty, the pool is lovely and the WiFi works well most of the time.  Happy Hour most every night with great drinks.

What a fantastic time we had at Kasara last week.  The resort itself is very discreet, the rooms simply but beautifully furnished, and I loved being able to shower outside whilst ibis flew overhead! We had the opportunity to do all sorts of activities with our fabulous guide, Jeet, who made sure we made the most of every minute. His knowledge of the flora and fauna (including latin names) was very impressive, and he was always able to answer our questions very comprehensively.  I particularly loved spending so much time with the elephants - what a treat to get so close to such beautiful animals. We did a couple of safaris with the elephants, and also went down to the river to wash with them one hot morning. It was fantastic to see them wallowing in the cool water, having a break.Despite the elephant grass being very high, we were lucky enough to see several rhinos, a crocodile, langur and temple monkeys, deer, and a whole host of birds, my favourite being the orioles and brainfever bird. No sign of the elusive tiger of course, but we did hear a deer alarm call on our last night which Jeet thought probably meant a tiger was passing through...Finally, the restaurant staff were so helpful and professional, coming up with little suggestions to help you feel more at home.I can't recommend Kasara highly enough and hope I will return one day to take Jeet up on his offer of a job as a butterfly expert and elephant rider ;)Thank you. Happy days. I was sad to leave.Daisy J

We would like to wholeheartedly recommend this resort for the excellent quality provided to me and my wife during our stay.It is very conveniently located close to the National Park and the activities we have done here were fabulous: trekking in the Jungle, wildlife spotting, elephant grooming (you can also do elephant safari, but we did not go for that). The guides are very knowledgeable and very friendly, they custom everything according to your need. We wanted to walk a lot, so we did everyday in some magnificent and secluded places.The resort itself is New And the bungalows are extremely confortable and well equipped. The food is great, amazing quality and all that you can eat (too much, I should say). The service is so polite and Helpful and they cater to all your needs.They have a pool and Spa as well and everything is so peaceful, green and beautiful, you want to stay there forever!We Highly recommend this resort to anyway looking for adventure and relaxation in the same time!Elena and Adrian

We traveled to Chitwan for the weekend, flying from Kathmandu. A friend recommended Kasara and we were not disappointed. We were met at the airport, given welcome drinks and a nice overview of activity options by Babu, our guide. We can't say enough good things about Babu, he is extremely knowledgeable about he flora and fauna native to Chitwan, and is extremely pleasant. While it is the tail end of the rainy season, there was still a lot to do, including a river canoe ride and nature walk. The food was delicious and they offer both Nepali and Western dishes. Overall, it was a great experience!

A weekend getaway in luxury: Our stay with Kasara was a delightful one. Our rooms, Balinese style, were exquisite. Beds were amazing and the layout and design of the rooms are calming. Everything is planned for you and our guide, Babu, was not only informative and funny, he saved us from a charging rhino, keeping a cool head and walloping the beast with his trusty stick. Please ask for Babu if you go. From airport to airport, Kasara took care of everything. Food is great and the wine selection is pretty nice.

Loved the beautifull modern cool architecture.Extremely helpfull staff.The experience of an open air bathroom was glorious.Thoproughly enjoyed the hot oil massage in the spa.Make sure to go Rhino spotting on the back of the well behaved elephants.Enjoy this jem in paradise.

We stayed for one one night on 3rd Dec due to tight schedule. Check-in was so easy and simple, handled by Gouri ( she already got the message we were going to come in). As other reviews mentioned, a waiter was already there welcoming us with a wet fresh towel and a glass of lime water. As you enter the room, you will see the beautifully decorated lounge and a sofa to relax. Enough space in wardrobe and very comfortable bed. Liked the idea of bathroom and toilet built outside ( kind of new experience i guess) but you have your own privacy. Food ( breakfast/lunch/dinner) were excellent and so the staff. We went for an elephant ( Shanti Kali)  ride in the morning with very well known guide (Babu). Wat a guy. He has a good knowledge about the jungle. We saw the fresh tiger foot print and a rhino wid the baby. Went for river canoing and an elephant shower( wat a memory). Lastly special thank you to Babu, Yadhav (GM) and Gouri for all your warm hospitality and also all the Kasara Resort staff and we will def return on our next nepal visit. Visit Kasara Resort if you are in Chitwan- not to be missed.

Fabulous. Relaxing. Calming. The open feeling upon entering the reception area was just the beginning of things to come. Our "room" began by opening the door into our private open air sitting room complete with water pond, frogs, and comfortable sofa. The lovely bedroom was minimally furnished, but with great beds.

The rooms are very restful as you enter across a bridge over a pond and can sit here comfortably with its open roof or go into your bedroom which is enclosed so protected from any insects that might be around.  The resort provides many activities.  In our day and a half we went on an elephant safari with many sightings of rhino, a peaceful trip in a dugout canoe seeing many birds, a fascinating visit to a crocodile breeding centre, elephant bathing and a trip through local fields and villages in an oxcart.  The local guide was very knowledgeable.  There was also a display by local dancers in the evening.  I'd have liked to be there for longer to have time to enjoy the beautiful surroundings, the pool and the massages available.

We stayed in the resort for 3 days after an expedition in Nepal. We found the resort a wonderful place to relax in a beautiful environment. Babu was the perfect guide in the jungle, whether on elephants, in the jeep or in the canoe. The food was excellent, the staff friendly and alwas helpful. We will surely come back :-)

My husband and I recently spent four nights at Kasara Resort, just outside of Chitwan National Park. As a luxury resort, it is, of course, beautifully designed and decorated. We entered our two-room villa via a wooden bridge across a small, waterlily-filled pond. Our bedroom was to the right, our open air bathroom, with a huge two-person shower, to the right. Our king-size bed was plush and oh-so-comfy! The resort also boasts a lovely pool, open air restaurant & bar and a spa.The staff (front desk, restaurant, bar, spa, housekeeping, drivers, and guides) are exemplary. It is their job to provide impeccable service but the Kasara staff are so warm and welcoming that you feel like a member of a close-knit family. They anticipate, they accommodate and do it with generous, loving hearts. I would like to give a special shout out to the Kasara General Manager, Gauri. I nicknamed her General Mommy because of her unflagging devotion to staff and guests.During our stay we did three elephant safaris (epic rhino-sighting photographic adventures), elephant bathing (so fun) where we rode elephants down to the river, scrubbed them and were, in turn,  showered by trunkfuls of water, a jeep jungle safari, and a sunrise bike ride past verdant rice fields and through small villages bustling with early morning life. The highlight of our bike ride was being welcomed into a home where we drank a sweet, delicately spiced tea and tasted the local rice wine. Special thanks to our intrepid, knowledgable guide, Kamal Adhikari, our talented elephant driver, Bacchu, and our beautiful pachyderm, Roop Kali.I feel as if my words haven't adequately communicated our amazing Kasara experience so please, go experience it for yourself!NAMASTE!!

Incedible two year old facility. Villas are large with open center area and large comfortable bedroom. Restaurant is open air, service was excellent and food, altho excellent was limited. Some guides were better than others

The two of us spent the last weekend at Kasara and the experience was beyond our expectations! We did everything and more: elephant-back safari, stick dance performance at dinner, visit to the Tharu people, jeep safari, canoeing, in the Rapti river, visit to the Gharial Conservation Breeding Center,... and we even took the time to plant some rice in the fields (since it's Monsoon season and we are in the Terai region!). To our tour guide, Mr. Babu, many thanks and just one word more: W-O-W! Great fella. The food was nice, carefully done, the room (not a villa!) was beautifully well-kept and the staff very helpful. We haven't used the pool at all and I made use of the spa facility just once. The only thing I do really regret is that I missed the "tipping box" at the reception when I was leaving in a hurry to take my flight back to overcrowded and dusty Kathmandu. But I tipped heavily those I had a closer contact during our stay and I will definitely remember the others when we come back in next November. So, please, folks, don't go cheap; these people are doing a great job and the deserve some sort of reward! I will see you all in November, because there is still lots more to be seen in Chitwan! Best of luck to everyone. Cheers.

We regret that we spent only one night here.Amazing package with an elephant safari,jeep safari, early morning canoe ride and of course the stunning villas .The staff were all caring and attentive. The pool however was a little disappointing as it was the same depth through out.However it was a super thrilling and comfortable experience.

We stayed at Kasara Resort for 3 days/3 nights on our trip to Chitwan National Park. The lodge was beautiful - there is a nice dining area, a big pool, a lounge/bar area above the dining area, and the rooms are all villa style with an open air bathroom. The rooms were great (comfortable and clean) but as a warning to some, there are bugs in the area (it is in the jungle), and we found some "friends" in the bathroom all of the time. I am not a fan of bugs, but they didn't worry me too much as they kept to themselves. The entire lodge is very clean and well kept. The lodge also has a spa, and we got great massages for a decent price one afternoon. The staff was very friendly and helpful. We were very well taken care of during our stay at Kasara. Our guide during our stay (Kamal) was fantastic! He was very knowledgeable, funny, and helpful. He organized our itineraries every day and worked with us to make sure we were getting what we wanted out of the experience. The food at the lodge was delicious! They served local dishes but always had other options as well (e.g. pasta). All food was included in the price of our stay, but we had to pay for alcohol, which was reasonably priced given the quality of the lodge (about $5 for a big beer or a glass of wine). The best part about the lodge was the activities that are included. We did a full day safari, an elephant safari, elephant bathing, a cultural dance show, a canoe ride, and a village tour. While all of the activities were great, my favorites were the all day jeep safari (the scenery is beautiful and we were lucky to see 39 rhinos, a sloth bear, bison, monkeys, and lots of deer), elephant bathing (the elephants love bathing and it is so fun to get to do this with them), and the village tour (our guide took us on a local bus to the village he grew up in, and we got to see how locals live - it was a wonderful experience!).  I would highly recommend this lodge to anyone that is looking for a fun, relaxing, cultural, and adventurous experience. It was fantastic!!!

We had a wonderful time during our 3 day / 3 night stay! The food, facilities, and staff were great! What we enjoyed most was how flexible the lodge was at catering to our interests. The lodge (and specifically our guide, Kamal) changed several of our original plans. They worked hard to make sure we had a wonderful time. If you are looking for a lodge that specializes in fun activities please consider the Kasara Resort. They offer morning/evening game drives, full day game drives, elephant backed safaris, nature hikes, elephant bathing, village tours, city tours and some evening activities. Thanks again to the Kasara team and to our guide Kamal for making our experience so great!!!! Upon returning home from our trip, we are heartbroken to hear news of the recent earthquake that is devastating the country. Please know that our feelings, thoughts and prayers are with Nepal and the wonderful people we met there.

We stayed 3 days/2 nights in this amazing resort. Brand new, fabulous bungalows. Beautiful pool, very good spa. Plenty of activities, elephant bathing, ox cart riding, visit to typical villages, walks in the jungle... Babu, our guide, made of our stay a wonderful and gorgeous experience we will never forget. Highly recommeded. Thank you Babu!!!

This resort is one of the best in India. The infrastucture of the resort is amazing! The staff is very friendly and service is excellent. There are many facilities in the resort. There is an open pool. There are also trips to chitwan national park. They plan your full day with the best activities to do and best guides with intervals for rest, breakfast,lunch and dinner.The food here is also delicious. They have cultural dance program in the evening and  also provide you with drinks and popcorns during the show. They also have an presentation about the national park. If you are visiting chitwan you should definitely stay in kasara you wouldn't be disappointed.

Kasara sets a high standard across the board - service, accommodations, amenities - but there is something more - an attitude of enjoyment.  I am fortunate to have stayed at other resorts of this level, but I can't think of even one where the atmosphere was so positive and happy!  These people were glad to have me stay with them!  They wanted to do anything they could to make my stay more pleasant!  Any request was their genuine pleasure.  Babu was our guide.  He is beloved on TripAdvisor.  He is knowledgeable and friendly, yes, but again, there is something more - an exceptional human being.  And then there are the elephants.  And the jungle.  We have been so thoroughly spoiled!

A beautiful resort in the middle of the jungle. The most stylish hotel room I've ever stayed in. Its design was refined, simple yet luxurious. Loved the shower and the comfortable bed! The service was great too. The food was delicious, mostly Nepali-Western fusion. Beautiful swimming pool. I loved every minute there! Oh and there was the jungle safari organized by the hotel staff! We saw a TIGER :) And our guide Tulsi was very knowledgeable and affable.In one word, Kasara was AMAZING.

My husband and I stayed at Kasara Resort for three nights as part of our honeymoon in Nepal. The rooms are very clean and we loved the architect design of the resort. It was a little cold in the open bathrooms in the winter but we did not mind this. The staff there are all really lovely and very eager to please. A special mention to our guide Babu who was amazing. He is a walking encyclopaedia about the park and the animals that live in it. Meeting him and heading into the jungle with him on safari (by foot, canoe, elephant and jeep) was the highlight of our time there. We even saw a tiger!! This is very rare so we were very lucky but can confirm that they are in the park! The only negative feedback we have for the resort is the food. This Hotel is one of the most expensive Hotels to stay at in Nepal so we expected the food to be of a very high standard comparable to similar priced Hotels in other countries, even to some of the better restaurants in Thamel Kathmandu. However this was not the case. The food is pretty average for Westerners (who pay twice the price to stay there compared to Nepalis) although perhaps as it is low season they did not have their normal chef there?? We were not provided with a menu, just asked what we would want for dinner and not given many choices. This was pretty frustrating and took a couple of days to figure out what we could order. All in all however the resort was one of the highlights of our trip mainly thanks to the staff, their activities and the modern architecture. I would definitely go back.

This resort exceeded our expectations! It was worth every dollar spent! The service is impeccable, the food divine, the amenities beautiful, the room luxurious & adventures...once in a lifetime! This place ticked our bucket list... Close encounters with rhino, riding & bathing elephants, spectacular scenery & jungle walks & canoe rides... What more could you want in an adventure experience!A very special mention to our guide Babu ( be sure to ask for him!) He was kind, humorous, informative & always obliging... Our experience would not have been as remarkable without him. Also ask for Jee our second guide, he was the best animal spotter & held his wits in the face of a close rhino encounter! A wonderful driver Khem was the most obliging, patient & understanding man... Stopping for any photo opportunity & reversing the jeep at a moments notice. These people make this resort outsatnading & extraordinary!  We hope to revisit in years to come when our daughter is older..the perfect family adventure/ relax getaway!

Beautifully landscaped resort with separate 'villa style' apartments. Water feature lobby entrance with doors to a very comfortable bedroom to one side and bathroom to the other. Bathroom open to the outside air above which can allow bugs and mosquitoes to enter might not be to everyone's taste. A range of jungle activities provides an entertaining and interesting stay. Our excellent and knowledgeable guide, Babu, kept us informed with his friendly humorous style on every aspect of animal life and local customs. The restaurant manger Kapil greeted us warmly and was most attentive to our needs. We found the food very much to our liking served by our friendly waiter Gayatari. Altogether a memorable stay.

Kaiser resort is a great launch pad to explore the Chitwan National Park.  The resort is down a long, rutted track that takes you through poor, traditional Nepali villages.  In a way it's remarkable that they could create a resort in such a location.  The style is simple and natural - outdoor bathrooms, for example, which I personally liked.  You get a good selection of activities included in the price of the stay - jeep, elephant and walking safaris, canoe trip, etc.  We had an excellent guide - Babu - pretty much to ourselves for the two days we stayed.  The food was good, if unexceptional, best when regional rather than international.Everyone is there for the wildlife, so your trip will be strongly influenced by what you see.  We had a good experience - rhinos were the highlight.

overall very good experience. Room was spacious and comfortable. Has an outdoor bathroom/shower separated by the lobby in your room complex. Food was generally very good. Sometimes service can be lacking- didn't get a wake up call first night, had to ask 3 times for extra hangers. Had various tours to go out on. Well run. If you want to take a photo while on a tour, you need to tell them as they usually won't do it on their own. Good choice.

A stunning resort, laid out in modern suite-style bungalows in the jungle.  Delicious food.  Very friendly staff and excellent service, particularly from Babu our guide, and Kapil our principal waiter...............

Kasara is a beautiful resort - loved the water features and the little frogs that were everywhere.The room was very clean and well presented and the sitting area and bathroom opened to the sky and were quite delightful.  The planned activities were great fun and interesting.  Our guide Babu was so informative it really added to the experience - his knowledge and his passion for the park were amazing.  Loved all the activities - the early morning trip down the river was magic, as was the elephant safari. Bathing - being bathed by - the elephants was a lot of fun and we saw a lot of animals and birds on the jeep safari.  Loved driving through the villages with their mud brick and dung houses and the friendly children all waving.  A great three days - would recommend an extra day for checking out the spa and swimming pool.  This is a great place - the staff really made sure we were well looked after and put together an excellent set of activities.

Kasara is a beautifully appointed property with bathrooms and entries open to the sky, lush gardens and in-room water features. The staff are fabulous, from Gayatri Gautam welcoming us for each meal in the restaurant, Gaurie checking that everything was going well, and our wonderful guide Babu. Babu introduced us to the excellent activities program at Kasara. He is knowledgeable and passionate about his environment, the animals, birds and flora. He was attentive to us and ensured that our experiences at Chitwan were enjoyable, safe and engaging. We were very grateful that when the transfer we had arranged was delayed, staff at the Resort, particularly Gaurie and Babu helped us find alternatives and ensured that our wait at Kasari was pleasant and comfortable. We had a magical three days at Kasari Resort.

We were at the Kasara for 3 nights in October.  The rooms are quite nice.  We didn't anticipate the need for air conditioning in the rooms but it was certainly advantageous.  The staff was friendly and attentive and the food was excellent.  We had a very special guide, Tulasi Magar who was available to our group of four the whole time from dawn to dusk.  When we were on the elephants he rode with us and gave us a blow by blow description of the flora and fauna.  He also took us on a jungle walk and a bird watching hike where the depth of his knowledge really came to the fore.  He has studied with the Smithsonian in Nepal and it shows.  I would ask for Tulasi if you have any such option.The only minor negative about the visit is that the internet speed is slow which makes it tough to look things up, but for email it is fine.
