We had an amazing time! It was very well organised with the activity board and the guides were very knowledgable. Really enjoyed the elephant safari, elephant bathing and the canoe ride.  For the jungle walk I suggest a long sleeve light shirt as it was quite humid and for extra protection from branches and mosquitoes. It was my partners birthday and they organised a cake and something special with the elephants.

This place is amazing and I probably can't fully describe it's beauty and uniqueness in words here. Hopefully some of my pictures will help you get an understanding of how unexpectedly cool, modern and relaxing this resort is. Kasara resort, another reason to visit Chitwan. Daaayum!!

This accommodation was absolutely stunning! The rooms were brilliant, the food was excellent and most of all the staff were extremely accommodating and made you feel welcome. The tour guides were very knowledgeable and knew exactly what they were talking about. For this resort there was nothing to small they couldn't help with.Chitwan was very very very hot so drink plenty of water whilst on the tours. Prepare to wake up early for bird watching and safaris. In total we saw 21 rhinos and a sloth bear which is said to be a rare sighting. This place is full of natural beauty and you won't be disappointed. Although this is not a complaint we went to see the elephants bathe in the river with their keepers. For me I would have preferred to watch them bath themselves rather that the keepers give them orders to splash tourists but I understand this attraction to some. Natural behaviour would be extremely appreciated.Going back to the resort they helped with transfers to the airport and the service was spot on. This is an amazing place not to be missed.

We came here under the healthcare hero package. Being a doctor and working in the hospital of the bharatpur city, Kasara resort is the best place in Chitwan to hangout far from the chaos of the city . Food and Hospitality was top notch. Room was clean with complementary amenities. Washroom was clean with essential amenities.
Excellent service. Workers went above and beyond. Safari was also great got to see , crocodiles, birds, Rhino turtles, elephant and a bear.

We had a great time - group of 16 from New Zealand. The team at Kasara were so obliging. We have fiied it safari, elephant ride and canoe trip as well as bird watching.We saw rhino, buffalo, crocodile and many deer and birds.Half our group were Lucy to see a tiger from the elephant.A great experience thank you.

Excellent experience, beautiful rooms and super kind personnel. Raj, the property manager, takes care that everything is perfect! The food, which is a mixture of local delicacies and staples that will please everyone, is delicious and we discovered unforgettable flavours. Our tour guide, Sujan, was very dedicated and put his heart into showing us the local wildlife. Big recommendation for an unforgettable stay in Nepal!

After a 30-minute shuttle drive from the Bharatpur airport, entering the modest gated entrance to Kasara reveals a hidden luxury property. Each stand-alone room has a charming attached exterior bathroom with an amazing and comfortable bedroom. The inclusive breakfast, lunch, and dinner options were delicious, and the property's F&B manager, Raj, was extremely attentive to ensure that we were always satisfied.Daily activities included a serene canoe ride, cycling, bird watching, and the highlight being the reserve drive with ample chances to spot the one-horned rhino among the other diverse wildlife. All in all, a great experience. Be sure to get an assigned naturalist when you arrive - they will assist with organizing the daily activities. Perhaps due to our last minute arrival, we were not paired with a go-to person.

Jungle meets resort at this unique place with outdoor showers!  Beds were not super comfortable and the lighting in the room was this bright fluorescent  bulb - not my favorite for mood lighting.  The AC worked great though which was much needed as it was HOT when we stayed here.  An experience, to say the least!

I enjoyed the novel layout of the rooms and the jungle location, and the bed was very comfortable. Staff were all friendly and helpful, and the programme of activities offered is excellent. We saw a sloth bear and two rhinos on the jeep and canoe rides, although sadly no tigers (wrong time of year for good sightings, I am told). Food was good and the landscaping around the villas made you feel very much part of the jungle.The only drawback of the open shower feature in the rooms is that I had to share my accommodation was a variety of insects and small reptiles. I found a little lizard in the water feature (don't worry, I rescued it), and a millipede and beetle in the bathroom. I am an animal lover and these didn't bother me, but the huge cockroach I found in the shower was a step too far for me! I appreciate there's no way of stopping these sorts of creatures from getting in when you're surrounded by semi-tropical countryside, but I wonder if the open air shower is really the best idea in the circumstances.

Replacement of gas heater with electric one …Dinners found well and awesome ..Hospitality is fabulous ..Environment and nature are quite friendly ..In overall I give four star of all services, hospitality , honesty and welcoming ..

Incredible experience, rooms are super clean, the staff are super nice and polite. They always surpassed our expectations, specially when it came to our meals.Raj and his team were great, hard to find development opportunities.Daily activities are interesting and fun to do.

Welcome- Friendly welcome with a lovely welcome drink. Discussed our itinerary for our time there and explained what was available in the hotel.Room & facilities- lovely modern room, bathroom has an open roof so bugs do get in but I felt this added to the jungle experience and felt more at one with nature. Filtered water and mosquito repellent provided each day.Food- mixed cuisines given throughout stay- Nepalese, Chinese and European. All meals really tasty and good portions given and always offered seconds. Desserts were a highlight.Staff- really helpful and friendly.Experiences-Canoeing- fun experience, saw crocodiles and rhinos by the side of the riverTraditional dance- interesting to see and get involvedSafari- good fun, managed to see deer, rhinos and lots of birds. Were able to get quite close to the rhinos too!Crocodile conservation centre- never seen gharial crocodiles before and was able to see them at different life stages and the work they are doing to protect the species.Plenty of experiences fitted in but still had opportunity to laze by the pool. Bikes also available to explore the local area.

It has been an excellent experience throughout the stay, we found all the service very good. Staff were very, very humble, nice, and friendly. The food was too good. Will miss this stay forever. Thank you.

I travelled nepal for the business propose this resort significants the perfect ambience and i enjoyed here a lot service was good food just amazing server rams was amazing he guided us for the safari.

Staying at Kasara is part of my Nepal trip, my family enjoyed stay at Resort. Especially  thier hospitality and property land scape. Staff is extremely professional,  polite and supportive especially Mr. Raj and Babu. Their safari tour was amazing and we seen 5 Rino's along with other animals.  Resort is very calm and pin drop silence, full of greenery. Nature lovers definitely love staying here. Best Wishes,Anil Kumar

The resort was amazing. A bit isolated from the city area yet the charm was inside itself. They have this beautiful individual villa. The property includes swimming-pool, spa, bar and restaurant. The checkin was smooth. Upon arrival they offered us welcome drink and cold hand towel for refreshment. My God, i must say me and my partner felt like heaven after a long hot journey. All the staffs were very friendly and accommodating. We usually spend our day in the restaurant. Special Thanks to Raj from the Restaurant who was very humble and informative. He and his team accommodated all our requests.

When we arrived, we were greeted by Mr.Sagar, given a welcome drink, we felt so special. We were 3 couples so booked villa with private swimming pool.The staff were friendly and Sagar was there to assist us in case we need anything. The property is located in a jungle area and can feel the nature. I suggest them to improve their breakfast, rest is fine..Thank you for the hospitality.

We stayed for 2 days   It was a wonderful stay with great hospitality extended by the hotel staff.. Esp PREM the naturalist accompanied us for canoeing, safari etc his knowledge about the wilderness was amazing amd very soft spoken person. It’s must go to this place

We being vegetarian they served us chicken soup. This kind of carelessness cannot be accepted at all. Worst service and hospitality ever. It claims it self to be 5 star but 2 star resorts are better than this. Being in Nepal there is no hand shower in the toilet just toilet paper.No tap in bathroom just single shower. No refrigerator and television. Coming to food..... Panner chilly was justifying it's name and it was actually full of chillies...first time  I ate dry Thai green curry...on asking why it's like this they are saying in non veg we have enough liquid.Coming to kids meal.. when i asked what is the option they said generally people here carry there own kids meal... coming to 5 star also I need carry kids meal..so better to stay at some 2 star....then on requesting they bought paneer Paratha...where I had to search for panner in Paratha.people choose 5 star for luxury and service and pay for same...but here I feel I wasted my money.

This is a difficult review, as I wanted to be as positive as possible as there are pluses and minuses to this Resort, mostly negative.  I provided this same feedback to the tour operator who reserved this Resort, in which I recommended that this Resort not be recommended, nor included in their future Nepal tours.Here are the pluses: Restaurant and some hotel staff tried to be helpful.  The hotel grounds and pool area are very nice.  The local villagers who present their nightly show do their best and enjoyable to watch.  The Naturalist assigned to us for the Chitwan preserve safari jungle tour, and bird watching was top notch. Here are the minuses:  Rooms are dated, and at best 3 stars.   The transfer from the Kasara Resort to the airport was a nightmare.  The front desk was extremely unfriendly at check out.  As an example, I pointed out an error in the hotel bill in their favor, but no thanks received.  More importantly, they insisted the night before checkout (interrupting dinner) on the night before checkout a significant charge for airport transport (that was not warranted).  When I inquired with my tour operator via WhatsApp’s and showed the text interchange indicating the additional airport transfer charge was not warranted, the Resort representative persisted and would not relent.  The following morning at breakfast the same representative from the front desk insisted again we owed the airport transfer fee.  Again I showed an updated text message from the tour operator showing the airport transfer fee was already included.  The representative insisted I walk with him to the front desk and discuss with his management.  The front desk management representative reluctantly agreed upon review of the text messages, and I was allowed to continue my morning.   Upon checkout that afternoon, this same management representative was extremely unfriendly (see comments above), and at our airport transfer time he announced the availability of our "jeep” and did not avail any hotel staff to assist with our luggage.  My son and I then proceeded to walk our luggage a considerable distance to the parking lot and place our luggage on the "old truck".  I can only guess as this being retaliatory for questioning the airport transfer fee.Ironically, a management representative (I believe the general manager or executive manager) accompanied us on our transfer trip to the Bharatpur airport for unknown reasons.   Approximately 3.5 miles from the airport the Hotel Truck died.  See photos.    Stranded with only 30 minutes to flight departure, they risked our flight.  The hotel rep did ultimately contact a taxi, that when all boarded with luggage looked like a "clown car".  Stressful and unnecessary.

This was my second visit to Kasara Resort and like the first time, I was amazed at everything they had to offer. They have not only improved and excelled in everything. Where can i start. From the time i was gretted at entrace y Gaurd dai to having a warm welxome by the operation manager Santosh ji and his team. I could see a beautiful ladey in tharu dress with a charming smile. The warm towel and refreshing welcome drink was much needed to me and my team. The guide dai explained

Unethical charge where they said one thing and do another things checkouts time we spent 1 hour without cause and charge they do 2 times then commit so be aware before booking no communication properly and terrible not providingInvoice and more

I honestly have nothing bad to say about this place! From the booking process, all throughout my stay and even helping with my transport back to Kathmandu, all of the staff were incredibly friendly and helpful.I’m typically the type of traveler who stays in hostels, but I chose to treat myself to 4 nights at Kasara over Christmas and I loved it! The food is worth the price alone, so delicious and so much of it. The rooms are super comfy and relaxing. The activities were fun, and my guide Babu was very informative.I can honestly say that the Christmas surprise is something that I’ll never forget! Thanks Kasara :)

We were not fans of the villas as we felt that they were very much 'style over substance' & quite sparse.The villa's entrance is via a wooden walk way over a pond with the bathroom off to one side & the bedroom on the opposite side. As the entrance area is open to the sky when we had a thunderstorm all night, our entrance way & the walk way to the bathroom flooded which meant that it was quite risky getting to the bathroom without slipping over!Our shower was also open to the sky & never got more than luke warm so they became a quick affair!When we visited, there were only a few people staying in the accommodation so it was not worth the restaurant running the usual buffet. The food was of a decent standard but more Continental in style & we missed eating the Nepalese food which we had enjoyed on the rest of our trip.We could not, however, fault the wild life experiences that we had during our stay.Our guide was engaging & knowledgeable about all of the local bird & wildlife so we learnt a lot, especially from the his slide show!We loved walking behind the elephant on safari & more so getting to feed her-she loves molasses!The dug out canoe ride to see the crocodile sanctuary was amazing too but the highlight for us was on the last morning where we had a truly amazing rhino encounter which was the highlight of the whole trip.Unfortunately, the accommodation was not for us but the experiences that we had made our stay!

The resort is captivating on the edge of the jungle offering various activities or you can just relax as time goes by.  The accommodation is spacious  with open air bathroom.  The staff are friendly and knowledgeable, the variety of food was excellent.  Enjoyed the happy hour and the cultural show.  Would have stayed another couple of days if we had of known how wonderful this resort was. Thank you

Was travelling alone but in a group. Long drive from Pokhara. Stunning individual guest chalets with open air solar powered showers, a entrance bridge over a pool and huge bedroom with great air con which kept us cosy when it was cold outside. Great lodge location very close to the forest and had some amazing rhino sightings on our jeep safaris. Excellent food and attentive staff, probably the best place we stayed in the whole Nepal trip. We had wet weather and the jeep safari was very soggy due to a very leaky tarpaulin, but the only other minor critisism was the coffee in the morning. The included coffee was undrinkable so you had to pay for proper stuff. But overall, hard to fault it. Would certainly stay there again.

Comfortable, spacious cottages set in a jungle oasis. Friendly staff, good food and well maintained resort.The staff conducting the activities are very knowledgeable, special thanks to our guide Shiraz.

We enjoyed our stay, the room was clean with a comfortable bed.  The English speaking lady on reception couldn’t do enough to help us, and all the staff were very friendly.  The food was delicious and there was a wide variety.  My only concern is that they have a captive elephant for tourist talks and walks, I completely disagree with this.  I’m not suggesting she’s not well looked after but I believe she should be in the wild or with a pack of elephants which aren’t being exploited.

Stayed recently for 3 nights. Extremely well organised and staff were very helpful. Rooms are spacious and well appointed and the pool and restaurant areas are lovely.First two days we were there were busy but not overly crowded but on our last night a very large group arrived who proceeded to take over! I appreciate that this is good for business but it could have a detremental affect on other guests.Activities were very well organised and guides were knowledgeable. Would definitely stay here again.

We stayed here as part of a group tour.  The rooms were excellent  (open air shower) and quite large.The swimming pool was large and a nice refreshing temperature.It was rectangular so good for lap swimming but a constant  depth of 5'8 which means not suitable for young children who can't swim.We saw two wild  rhinos near the restaurant in the neighbouring National park next door.We did a jungle safari tour from the resort. The guide was excellent and had a passion for the environment.  Part of our group rode through the jungle via elephants (great fun) whilst the rest of the group did a jeep safari in a different National park.For those on the elephants, we saw 2 white rhinos, a wild boar, spotted dear and nice birds.

Had a great stay at the Kasara lodge- staff were extremely attentive and friendly. Food was great and rooms were very comfortable and modern.Everything was extremely well-organised and I was particularly impressed by the hotel manager’s involvement in ensuring all guests were well-briefed on their following day’s activities.Guides were superb too - very knowledgeable and we felt in very safe hands while out in safari.

After 8 days trekking up mountains Kasara was the perfect place to unwind.  Staff were exceptional - nothing was too much trouble. The villas were lovely, rain shower in the elements delightful and appreciated the non plastic ethos in the resort.Food was some of the best we had in Nepal - all freshly made on site, more than you could possibly eat and served by attentive, caring staff.The grounds are lush and well kept, and the jungle is just on the other side of the fence so a rhinoceros visiting at breakfast can be expected.  Well worth a visit to this lovely resort

sabita ! i found a fren in you :) you are an amazing soul ..thank you kasara..n everyone over there .it felt like a home in middle of nowhere and thanks again sabita ji for everything ..u r simply amazing

We initially chose Kasara as they were one of the few resorts in Chitwan who are known for treating their elephants with care and respect, but in the end we got so much more than a clear conscience. From the moment we arrived at the Kasara Resort our experience was simply perfect. The resort staff were polite, eager to please and kept the immaculate grounds, top notch facilities and spectacularly luxurious villas in spotless condition. The chefs and wait staff served us an amazing variety of delicious food from many different cuisines and the cocktails in the relaxing bar area were delicious and affordable. The guides were extremely knowledgeable about every aspect of the park, the local environment and the flora and fauna and made an unforgettable experience even more memorable. The caring and attentive management were always on hand checking that we were happy and that there was nothing we needed, and the genuine authenticity they displayed really made us feel at home and not want to leave. I really could not fault a single aspect of my experience at Kasara and recommend it unreservedly to anyone considering a trip to Chitwan. Don’t be sucked in by the other places that offer a cheaper price, you will not regret coming here for a second. Five stars.

We stayed here as a couple and single Friend in 2 Rooms. We really enjoyed our stay and did the elephant safari, feeding the elephants, canoeing and village visit.  We were very happy to see the Elephants treated so kindly no chains no hitting. The food was above average and all staff were always willing to help and please. The rooms were very comfortable and luxurious

We had a great time staying at Kasara. Personalized service and clean accommodation.  Its always good to see joy in your little one, her first time seeing an elephant, spotted a Rhino 10 ft away during our elephant ride safari, thanks to all the Kasara team.

We were into our 7th day in Nepal and found everything so far to be below standard for what we were paying but Kasara is an all inclusive so nothing extra to pay other than drinks and we found this quite refreshing especially as all the tours are included.  We stayed for a 3 night 4 day package so we were busy but yet relaxed.The rooms are very nice and the staff are wonderful.  the food however is not the best and I really think they need to improve the restaurant food to match the rest of the resorts facilities. The resort pool was great to come back to after our days of activities. The activilites are great and the guides where very knowledgeable. On our first day we went for an elephant trek and straight away we came up and very close to a rhino's which was very cool inded.  That night there was a cultutal show which was most enjoyable we took part by dancing with the group. I beleive the show is on most nights so you really only need to go once.The next day we took a canoe ride on the river to the crocodile breeding centre again very informative. Along the river our guide told us about all the birds and whatever animals we came across .Later in the day we went back to the river to wash the elephants this was so much fun and I would recommend doing this.  You actually scrub the elephant with a stone from the river bed.Next day was a jeep safari trying to find a tiger and what ever else is in the Jungle.  No tigers but we did see heaps of birds and deer, some wild boars, monkeys, a Rhino taking a bath and a bear sloth.  We stopped for the best cookies and ice tea taking in the sunset before heading back to the resort.Next morning we went for a few hours walk through the jungle we did not see tmany animals but still very interesting.  We then relaxed by the pool for a few hours before heading back out again but this time for an Ox ride around the Local Tharu village.  This was another extremly intersting activilty chatting with the locals and seeing how they live.I think that Kasara is a very well oiled machine and is doing everything right we really enjoyed our days here and would recommend it to everyone to spend a few days here.

KASARA Resort is a perfect place as a couple's retreat with a touch of luxury and comfort, resort is located 20-25 mins drive from the nearest airport. this was my 1st visit to Nepal with my better half, we had booked 2 days package which included F&B and Activities. The team at KASARA are very professional, friendly and accommodating.  special thanks to Ms. Sunaina from the Marketing team who was very helpful throughout the Booking/Reservations to the end of our stay. our naturalist Mr. Madan is a very knowledgeable individual and ensured that our activities were well planned for the best experience. these are the real rockstars of KASARA resort. we highly recommend this property for a leisure stay.

We stayed 2 nights as part of a trekking / rafting / wildlife tour organised by Himalayan Social Journey. Beautiful resort; everything very clean and in great condition. Very comfortable room. Food was interesting and varied. One day I had mentioned that it was my wife's birthday and the manager arranged a surprise birthday cake. Wildlife experiences were very good - seeing rhinos, canoe trip, bird watching. Nice pool for relaxing. Very helpful staff and definitely professional. A bit warm in May, so would advise going a bit earlier in the year.

We stayed 2 nights in Kasara Resort as part of an India and Nepal trip organised by Bespoke India. Kasara is a beautiful resort next to the national park offering everything you need to enjoy nature and relax.Our room was great with a partly outdoor shower room, water feature at the entrance and comfortable and roomy bedroom.As we found throughout Nepal, the staff are great nothing is too much trouble.The pool area is lovely with sun loungers and hammocks and the food is delicious.The nature excursions can be adjusted to your interests and we were lucky to see a one-horned rhino on our game drive. Two nights is not enough and we wish we could have stayed longer.

We have had such a wonderful experience, from the manager to all his staff the people were welcoming and caring to all our needs. Annie was a bit ill and they went out of their way to be as helpful as possible, thankyou. The jungle experience was amazing, washing elephants, canoe rides crocodiles, rhinos.... wowIf you are in this beautiful country you must come to this beautiful resort

The room was awesome, beautifully designed with natural feeling. The plants, water and wood makes you feel that you are staying close to the nature. The food was mesmerizing. Above all, the best hospitality and ever cheerful people. I loved it.

First thing that I can say about this resort is the greenery. You find greenery everywhere around and inside this resort. Very peaceful. Restraunt is very clean and the food is also very nice. Pool is refreshing and very clean. There is a lake nearer to the resort. You will find lots of trees and greenery. Hotel is maintained superb clean.I wish to visit the hotel again.

My husband & I stayed here as the luxury upgrade for our tour with Himalayan Social Journey. It was by far the nicest hotel we stayed in during our trip to Nepal & probably up there with one of the coolest resort experiences we’ve had. The villa was just lovely & I really enjoyed the indoor/outdoor bathroom. My husband ran into a huge monkey in the shower so he might have a different view on that (it just ran along the top of the wall- he was fine haha). Along with our guide, we were the only guests at Kasara for our first night. We had extremely attentive service as a result. Dinner was enormous, with numerous dishes on the table to share & regular offers of additional food. We were definitely never hungry! On the second night a few large groups arrived & changed the vibe completely. On our arrival we walked out of our villa & saw a rhino & an elephant right outside the fence. The staff said it’s rare to see a rhino. We were thrilled! We also did the Jeep safari, which was great. Unfortunately our fellow guests were a bit loud & scared away a few animals! But we saw bears, more rhinos, monkeys, peacocks, & lots of deer. I strongly suggest that people do NOT do the elephant safari for ethical reasons. Please do your research about the horrible way these beautiful animals are treated. The Jeep safari is wonderful & you will see far more animals this way anyway. The guide from Kasara is wonderful & very knowledgeable.

Our family stayed at the Kasara Resort and we loved everything about the hotel! It's a well designed hotel with spacious, beautiful rooms. The staff are friendly and went above and beyond to ensure we were well taken care of and food was great. Our safari guide who was with us for 2 days was very knowledgeable and taught us a lot about animal and plant life. If you are planning to go, look at Kasara's website and select one of their package tours which includes airport transfers, accommodation and safari experiences. We very much enjoyed our stay at Kasara and the organized safari tours to explore Chitwan!

Best hotel by far that we stayed at in Nepal. Big rooms, amazing staff, great food and wildlife. We stayed for 2 nights 3 days which is probably the right amount of time to do all the activities. Nature guide was great - we saw rhinos on the walking tour. Manager of the restaurant was the best - we arrived to a buffet that had nothing my husband could eat. He noticed and without being asked made my husband a special meal - and then made sure every meal he was ok or made him a special meal. Highly recommend on a Nepal trip after trekking. Take the flight back to Kathmandu it’s 30 mins compared to 6 hours on a bus.

This was a lovely surprise during our two week tour of Nepal. The rooms are very interesting architecturally, with each individual bungalow divided into two separate entities: the sleeping quarters and the bathing quarters. You enter through a private, locked gate, walk on a bridge over a small pond (in your bungalow entry).There is an outdoor padded bench between the two sections, if you want to contemplate the pond.The sleeping quarters are very large and very nicely appointed. The bathing quarters are also quite nice, except that side is not air-conditioned, as it is open-air. So if you are there during a hot, muggy time, as we were, you have to dash between the shower and the bedroom in order to stay cool and not start sweating again immediately after the shower. In nicer weather, it is probably not a problem. One word of warning: there are rubber flip flops in your room. Definitely wear them when you go into the bathroom, as there are always some kind of creepy crawlies around. It is a jungle, after all, and the bathing area has lots of places for things to meander into. Food was absolutely the best we had on the tour. Nice buffet that changed daily. Also had a nice lecture from someone familiar with the area and excellent entertainment one evening. Very enjoyable over all.

Kasara Resort is SO incredible in every way possible! Food is DELICIOUS, rooms are stunning, activities are absolutely spectacular, the spa and pool are relaxing, and the staff are so awesome and knowledgeable! Absolutely perfect for relaxing, whilst also getting the chance to see some beautiful wild animals and learn all about them!! Seriously could not recommend this resort more. Can’t wait to come back!

What a gorgeous property! Great service, wonderful food, and very luxurious room, with soaking pool. Great naturalist guide and local adventures, including elephant safari, jeep safari, bird watching and nature walks. I highly recommend a visit there!

This was my favourite hotel during my stay in Nepal. They definitely gave the best welcome with cold towels, juice and a speech from the lady at reception explaining about the hotel and their facilities. I believe they cater breakfast, lunch and dinner for all guests as there are little or no other options around to get lunch. They also arrange all your itinerary and guides for you which is helpful.The resort manager is there every meal time checking in on everyone, explaining the itinerary and making sure you like the food. All the staff knew your room number and your schedule and were able to make everything work around this. Having set meals times also met the food was fresh unlike some buffets. This hotel was by far the best with our allergies and dietary requirements having both a nut allergy and gluten free people within our party to cater for. The restaurant manager discussed our allergies/requirements with us at the first meal and I believe tweaked his menu to make sure he catered for us for the rest of the stay. At the beginning of each meal he would come and tell us what we could and couldn't eat and if there was something we couldn't eat he would always offer to make us an alternative and make sure we had a enough food.Although this hotel was a buffet is always had a theme which is much better e.g there was Nepalese, BBQ, Greek lunch etc. It was nice to have a variety of food rather than the standard rinse and repeat of bland 'local' (western twist) on their meals. And to actually make a quantity that got eaten rather than an overload of food trying to please everyone than often goes to waste. They also serve popcorn in the evenings whilst presenting a slideshow or dance performance which is a nice treat! The rooms were beautiful, everyone has their own lodge with their own walkway, a sofa area in front, a bedroom to the right and a bathroom to the left. Some of the bathroom is slightly open air which is a different concept to adapt to, especially when it cooler in the evenings. Once you've adapted it was great and the showers were always hot. You just need to keep the doors shut to keep the bugs out!The only downside to the hotel with them also managing the guides is that they took a slower pace to the day than my family is used to, we like busy days where you feel exhausted at the end, there were lots of great activities like safaris and bathing with elephants, but often awkward one hour gaps between activities or meal times etc. Which felt to me like wasted time. They also grouped together some tours which depersonalised some of the activities which I thought was a great shame. Like washing elephants which I thought would be an intimate experience with my family also had twelve Americans there as well who have a very different holiday approach, this also didn't help our chances of seeing anything on the jeep safari. All said, still the best hotel, beautiful place, nice staff, great restaurant, just wish we had stuck to our own family itinerary as that we could of filled it a bit more.

Kasara is a 20 minute flight from Kathmandu city and quite the convenient getaway for family, couples or solo travelers. We were amazed by the service of the friendly staff. The food is world class. The Nepali Thali is a must try and a huge thanks to Ms. Sunaina, the manager, for being such a wonderful host. Must-go place if you are in Chitwan, Nepal.

Amazing location next to Chitwan np and local village. Our naturalist Madan was excellent jungle guide. Nice pool area too. Evening cultural dance was nice. Food allright. Few power short cuts didn't bother.

Our very friendly and informative naturalist (Babu) picked us up at the airport and stayed with us for our entire visit. Our one full day there was packed full of adventures, with the Elephant Safari, Elephant Bathing and Crocodile Breeding Center among my favorites. Definitely the highlight of our trip to Nepal. Top service was Kasara's key ingredient.

Stayed for two nights as part of the tour package through Himalayan social journey. The staff were welcoming and met all our needs with a smile. It was the perfect place befitting of a national park stay, with a real natural vibe in the resort. Great pool with cabanas and day beds. Food was of high quality for a buffet style service.  Rooms were spacious and memorable with an open their private shower and a bridge over a pond to into your room.  Maybe not quite five star but close to it in a national park in Nepal.

The Kasara Chitwan Resort was picked by our tour company.  It provided a lovely room and grounds for us while touring the area.  The bath areas are a bit open air which means all bugs invited and the jumping spider is no match for the fearless armed with a magazine and shoe.  So you must be prepared for those encounters.  And can you believe I fell into the mote in our suite one night in the dark?  We had not left lights on to keep the bugs away, entered in the dark and had forgot there was a mote!  Room was spacious.  A bit of maintenance could be done (room doors delaminating)  Pool lovely.  We felt the restaurant staff was bending over backwards to take care of my GF diet.  Very nice staff all around.  Great talk by ranger man with slide show to watch one evening and local dancing done another night.

We visited Chitwan National Park and Kasara Resort for a short four day weekend.  The staff were excellent, the outings were exciting and enjoyable, and the Resort grounds were perfect.  Great food, clean pool, lovely open-air bar area, peaceful and  elegant rooms.  I highly recommed Kasara Resort for your stay in Chitwan.

Great villas , Big swimming pool, Luxurious rooms, open roof toilets, restaurant & bar prices are reasonable, friendly staff, great hospitality.BUT complimentary (package included) breakfast was very sad, very few options & small portion breakfast. #disappointedOverall great place to relax and spend your time. would love to visit again.

Kasara is a magical experience. We went with the family and there was something for everyone. Super kid friendly - but us adults had smiles the whole time. The elephant experience was amazing - we still talk about it. We saw a tiger while on Safari. We travel ALOT as a family - and this still stands out. If I could give it more than 5 stars - I would in a heartbeat!

A gem of a place, staff hospitable and prompt to your every needs. The individual rooms are very private  and built in exotic Japanese / Balinese style, Toilet and shower  with open roof, gives the sense of openness and freedom. rooms thoughtfully  and organically furnished. A reading light on the bed  would be really nice.  Very good food and wholesome.  lovely swimming to relax. Perfect place for a relaxing retreat.

The Summer Special Package was Splendid.Thank you Sunaina Di and Lok dai for making  our stay wonderful. Everything was perfect the room , food , the jungle guides was very professional.Associates were very polite n grounded.Thanks to server didi too.She was always having smile on her face while taking care of us in the restaurant made us felt so comfortable.It was worth staying there.Lastly I would like to thank u all for everything.Would definitely share my experience with all my friends and recommend KASARA Resort for the peace and refreshing vacation.

the place is very beutiful. the Room is very big and cozy. at the entrance there is a small bridge on a zen tub, i love these detail. Staff is very kind and redy to help. the excursions are well planned and you have time to relax too. Swimming in the pool massages or practice your yoga session in a big terrace in front of the nature. Food very good, good attention and  good italian coffe... Illy :) .

I recently got back from my 4 week trip to Nepal and although I throughly enjoyed my time everywhere - my 4 days/3 nights at Kasara Resort are definitely a highlight of my trip. I stayed at a wide range of places in Nepal - from trekking teahouses, to basic lodges during transit - but the Kasara Resort was actually my favorite in terms of the quality of accommodations, food, and activities. I made all my travel arrangements in Nepal on my own, and when I reached out to Kasara via e-mail they responded promptly, offered me a good deal (in retrospect, I see now it was a great deal), and made the entire booking process so easy. The quality of the room accommodations were excellent - especially for the value!! Very spacious, modern but not overdone, room with a tranquil outdoor seating area plus pond, super comfortable bed, and the best part, open air hot shower!! The quality (and quantity) of food was great! I usually don't expect much in terms of resort food, but they clearly have a very creative, detailed oriented, and talented chef. But the past part of staying at Kasara is the staff - from the manager who greets who as you arrive, to the wait staff, activities coordinator and jungle guides, Kasara staff were just so helpful, friendly, and professional in every way. My safety and enjoyment seemed as if they were their top priority at all times. Thank you Kasara staff!!

Stayed for 2 nights in a villa with own swimming pool! Amazing experience. Food was above par! Those friendly faces always smiling from the cleaners to drivers and the naturalists made the stay even more enjoyable. Tightly packed retreat program with elephant rides, canoeing and jeep safari. Would definitely recommend to stay here. Top it all with Sherpa beer guys!

We were a 50 strong team for an official retreat here. Around 16kms from Bharatpur, mix of black topped and gravel road. Google map will get you there. rooms are spacious. The bathrooms are really special with an Egyptian feel. Meditation hall provides ample space for activities. The pool is a uniform 5'8" height. Really picturesque. Breakfast nd lunch are both clean and tasty. The jeep safari and canoe ride for 3-4 hours was memorable with lots of animal sightings except the elusive tiger. The chef grilled a whole goat for us which was the icing on the cake. Staff are cooperative. Overall it was good value for the money paid. Would recommend this place for its peace and ambience.

There should be a fancy Nepali word for nostalgia. Like the heartache you feel when you see replays of Michael Schumacher overtake 11 drivers from the bottom of the track to land a position on the podium in his gleaming red Ferrari. If you haven’t left Kathmandu this winter, come summer you’re bound to be overcome with remembrances of the road trip you did when you were in college, memories of your drunk friend sleeping under a very thin blanket and waking up the next morning with dew on their face. So, listen to yourself just this once. It’s not difficult. Just leave your house, drive a few hours, walk a little and spend a weekend outside.There are plenty of places you can go to enjoy yourself in March. Plenty of trails you can hike, villages you can walk through and Instagram-worthy sunrises you can capture in your selfie sticks. I tip my imaginary hat to those places. But when it comes to choosing between what is left on your 128 GB memory stick and what is tweeted from your (hopefully, verified) account, I would strongly urge you to imagine the following scene: a comfortable villa overlooking a national park in the middle of a million square feet of wilderness. A breakfast every morning where you are interrupted by a bunch of Rhinos who get awfully close to you and munch on the greens while you’re mesmerized by the well-done bacon that doesn’t disappoint. In the evenings, crickets make the loud chirping noise and large mean-looking ants unfazed by your presence calmly walking by doing their thing while you lay in your comfortable chairs by the private pool. March is reckless cold in the hills, and this is why God created Chitwan. Although I should warn you that this place is not for the weak of spine or the faint of the heart (and by that, I’m explicitly referring to folks that cannot afford to miss their favorite episode of Koffee with Karan every Sunday). To reach this spot, you must drive from Kathmandu towards Chitwan, past the horribly bumpy roads that never seems to get fixed. After about a few hours’ drive, you’ll have to park your car, and walk through a bunch of friendly looking mud houses for company and fields. Lots of green fields.Else, take the flight. It costs NRs 2,400 per person and 15 minutes to get there. The welcome drink and the friendly reception at the airport will make up for the delay, if any. Every day, you’ll be offered a variety of meals – we’ve been here for three days and have had Mexican, Indian, Nepali Thali and Italian cuisines. Breakfast has fresh fruit juice, and I don’t mean the tetra pack sugary Real. This is complemented by the Happy Hour every evening from 5:30 – 6:30pm (Buy one, get one Free!) where the bartender makes you really nice cocktails. And by that, I mean a Whisky Sour which actually has eggs white in them (unheard of in the fancy bars in Kathmandu where they instead prefer to go overboard on the lemon and sugar syrup). There’ll be pork roast for dinner, while you sip that fine bottle of whiskey you bought along for the trip. All this while you chat with Sunaina, the friendly in-house Manager who always has the answers (I overheard a bunch of foreigners asking her during dinner time if she could arrange for them to see a tiger at 6am). Eventually, a hefty dinner of pork roast washed down by four glasses of single malt whiskeys later (there’s a 15% discount on the whiskeys every evening), you’ll lie on your back and reminisce about the vastness of the galaxy while waiting to spot the falling stars. Then the crickets will get down to business. And if you can’t sleep for all their ruckus, bundle yourself and go back out under the stars. There have never been so many.

What an amazing experience !! The resort is simple but luxurious, the rooms' design amazing and everything is spotless and clean. It's in the middle of the Jungle and we saw a rhyno from the resort.Food is perfect and staff really kind. They tried to accomodate every request we had and our guide Suraz was amazing! Recommended !!

Caring staffs, excellent hospitality from dedicated staffs, comfortable & peaceful environment, Mr. Babu a nature enthusiast from the staff team, the manager & all other staffs ensured we had great time with great package plan to keep us entertained. Christmas Eve was a surprise with the Santa on an Elephant n Tharu Dance. Thank you guys for the 2N3D lovely package. Great Job.😀

Marvelous time of the year to add a safari after a glorious hike to Everest Base Camp. Discovered this relatively new private resort with variety of superb activities, local culture, bountiful cuisine

We came with a family of 6, with two teenagers.  From the time we were picked up to the time we were dropped off, the service was truly remarkable.The staffs are all well trained and with very pleasant disposition.  The rooms are clean and amenities sufficient. There’s no TV in the room,which was a delight as it would have been distracting.Food - Breakfast, Lunch and dinner were all fantastic, menu was changing all the the time and all cuisines - Nepali, Mediterranean and continental were very well done.We were well looked after by the manager and the F&B manager - Mr G Gautam were always looking out for us and always there to see to all our needs.  The staff who took us to the elephant and Jeep safari are are knowledgeable and courteous.  We thoroughly enjoyed our stay and will definitely come back again!!I highly recommend the resort.....

We booked this Resort as a part of the package by Yeti Travels Pvt. Ltd. Its a beautiful Resort with lovely rooms and surroundings. Right from pick up at Bharatpur Airport to dropping us back after our stay, everything was immaculately planned. Rooms are independent villas with a small courtyard and a waterbody, an amazing bathroom with a partial open shower. The staff is ever so helpful & friendly, would specially like to mention Ms. Annapurna in the restaurant. Our naturalist, Babu is a living encyclopedia of the region! He accompanied us at every safari, nature walk, cannoe ride and visit to the crocodile breeding centre feeding us lots of information on the local flora & fauna and also gave us a most informative and entertaining presentation on the wildlife of the Chitwan region. Food was super tasty and the chef catered to our every request. There was different menu for each meal. The last evening culminated with a wonderful cultural program. And yes...we saw lots of Rhinos, crocodiles, wild boars, hog deer and tons of birds...Highly recommend this Resort.

We visited Chitwan after walking to Everest Base Camp – so it was our rest and relaxation. I looked at all the information about the trips organised by places to stay, that were the top places on TripAdvisor, and booked Kasar- and I am VERY glad that I did. My trip involved quite a few changes, but the reservations manageress, Sunaina,  dealt with all the changes and special requests very well.We initially wanted to stay in the same place in Chitwan, to save on packing and moving. But we wanted to see alligators on the river and canoe in a dugout, and that is not possible at Kasara, so I had to reduce it from 3 to 2 nights- but Sunaiana was fine with that.I also decided using TripAdvisor, that we would be better off and more likely to see a tiger, with specialist guides. So, I chose United Jungle Guide Services and I am really glad that we did. It meant I had to ensure that where we stayed, I booked only for accommodation and not for their guiding services, which are the normal rates of accommodation in the park. That is unusual, but Sunaina coped fine with it. Looking at the photos on the website, the tourists do not seem to have seen tiger from Kasara.I really recommend that if you are in Chitwan, you stay in Kasara. Sunaina looked after me very well. I had asked for a quiet room, as I sleep poorly if noisy, and it was quiet. She also heard that I had the Khumbu cough - a problem when trekking at altitude and I had from our trek to Everest Base Camp. She recommended and gave me her own Vic to put on my chest and back to ease the coughing. She also made me ginger with homey tea- and that really helped. As I was trying not to cough, when out in the park looking for wildlife, this was REALLY kind and helpful.I did comment to her on the slightly dirty glass ceiling to the en-suite bathroom in the room. It turns out that it used to be open to the elements. Following complaints from visitors before us in colder times of the year, that this meant it was too wet and cold in the bathroom, they glassed it over, as the bathroom has plants growing in it. I am sure they will address how to clean it soon. I also think they need to ensure that their gardeners look after the plants in the bathrooms better.  Two of the four plants in there were dead.But despite these minor whinges, I still give it 5stars, as thanks to Sunaina, they are excellent.

One of the best resort I have been. Great room, amazing bathroom with a lot of natural light. The facilities are wonderful and the activities great: Riding elephant in the park to better see the wildlife, Jeep safari with our guide Babu who is very knowledgeable and loves what he does. We saw a brand new baby rhino, a week old, with her mother. Lots of birds, crocs, and wild boars. Sunaina, one of the manager, was very good and helpful giving tips of the park activities available. Luke the other manager was also always available to answer your questions. This is a place I would definitely go back and stay more than two nights.

Wonderful location in the heart of nature. Friendly and helpful staff, wonderful food and a great cultural program on the last evening with traditional dancing. Every need was catered for, the room had an open bathroom, giving you a feeling of being closer to nature. Well equipped, top quality rooms. Highly recommendable.

This is a beautiful and immaculately kept lodge.  Lovely pool, stunning cottages and  very lovely garden.The staff are helpful and offer mixed activities.  Our elephant ride was a great way to see the rhinos and other wild life up close.  Less noise than jeep safaris we'd done in Africa although not the same amount of wildlife obviously.  Was a little ambivalent re the elephant ride but it was a good experience.The food at Kasara is the best we have had on our Nepal and India trip - truly amazing, tasty and unique.

We stayed here for 2 nights at the end of our 2-week visit to Nepal. Having done a 9-day trek and then being subjected to the dust and chaos that is Kathmandu and all the domestic airports, we felt like we were transported into a sanctuary of calm when we finally arrived at Kasara Resort! We were greeted by two gentlemen from the resort at the airport who offered us cold towels and drinks (much needed after a 3-4 hour wait at Kathmandu airport!). The resort is a sometimes bumpy 20-30 minute ride from Bharatpur airport. But once we arrived at the resort, which is surrounded by rice fields, we were again offered cold towels and a delicious welcome drink. In fact we learnt that they routinely stock cold towels at the lobby areas so guests coming back from their excursions could refresh themselves! A small but very nice gesture. Our villa was a few minutes walk from the lobby and dining area, but we didn't really mind the distance as the hotel grounds is beautifully landscaped and the weather in October was quite lovely. Our villa was compact, simply but elegantly designed. The airconditioned room was on one side of the villa, and the outdoor shower was at the other side. The bed was big and comfortable (again a very welcomed change from trekking accommodations!), and the room was equipped with an electric kettle, cups, coffee powder and teabags. They even thoughtfully provided a insect repellent cream in each room. The only thing that was less than ideal was the gas-powered hot water shower, which did not stay at a constant comfortable temperature. However most of hot showers outside of Kathmandu were like this.The food provided in the resort was excellent! We took the buffet option every time simply because all the food looks so good. We were very thankful for the high quality of food in the resort given that we had to have all our meals there. They had different themes for each meal (e.g. Mediterranean, Indian, BBQ, etc) so we were never bored of the food. We liked that they use the produce that is grown locally (maybe that was why the food tasted so good!). They also have a happy hour every evening from 6-7pm where there is a one-for-one promotion on some drinks. They even serve each person a small platter of warm snacks and nuts to go along with the drinks!We had taken the bed and breakfast package because we wanted to pick and choose the excursions to go for, and despite there being several bigger groups of guests during our stay, the staff worked hard to make sure that we got to do what we wanted. They even fit in a short complementary bird-watching walk just for the two of us when they learnt that my husband was interested in bird-watching. This is where I'd like to compliment the whole team at Kasara who worked hard to make sure that we were enjoying ourselves during our stay. It appeared to be a small core team, and so it was nice to see the familiar faces everyday. They often approached us to check in on how we were doing, and asked about our experiences on the excursions. Overall we highly recommend anyone who is interested to visit Chitwan National Park and is after a pampering experience to stay at Kasara Resort!

Wonderful people, lovely room and lush grounds. Delicious food, attentive staff. Excellent safari experience and knowledgeable naturalists. I enjoyed a birthday whilst at the resort and the staff made it very special. Possible to view game from first floor bar. Surpassed all expectations - we would love to return.

It was a very peaceful resort.  The people were very helpful.  They all tried to make the trip a perfect vacation.  It addition to the normal activities they arranged private bike rides and a long jungle hike that I wanted to do.  On my birthday they had a elephant bring a birthday cake for me.  The naturalists were informative.  The rooms were beautiful. The pool was relaxing.  The food was excellent.  The bed and pillows were very comfortable with a very well working AC.  Internet connection had a good speed.  I would recommend the location to all.  If you want to see a lot of wildlife March or April is a better time  go.

This is the place to stay in Chitwan - set in the jungle, you can see wildlife from the deck near the restaurant. The grounds are exquisite and the rooms huge with a separate entrance and bathroom. There is a large, airy restaurant and upstairs bar, spa and the hotel can arrange activities if you wish. Big pool.Staff are so helpful and the food is great.

The staff is very attentive (sometimes even too much) but all in good spirit. They make sure you will have the most wonderful experience in Chitwan, and so we did. The room is extremely nice blends well with nature and makes you feel in the right place

Was in the resort again for a second time with my VIP guests from Peru and they loved it. The food, the service, the rooms, the swimming pool and the sundowner that they provide is one add-on service that one should definitely try. They are already planning their next trip to Kasara Resort with their family. Our guide Tulsi had a great sense of humor and made your stay more interesting. Thanks, Lok Dai and Sunena for the great hospitality. Will definitely recommend everyone to stay here if you are planning to visit Kasara.

We went with 5 families. We enjoyed the place. Staff were very friendly. Though it was warm there were no mosquitos or flying insets. Nice rooms. Food was good. Swimming pool with individual cabanas were interesting.

What a great spot on our travels to Nepal.  Wonderful, caring staff.  We did two nature walks, the elephant safari, washed the elephants in the Rapti, took a canoe down the Rapti then went to the croc breeding grounds, and slept really well!  The food was also delicious.   Would have loved to have Wi-Fi in my room, but it forced me to further disconnect - and I survived!   Ask for Babu as a tour guide -- he was so knowledgeable and attentive and he genuinely enjoys what he does as a Naturalist. PLUS, he is a local!

Excellent place to spent. KASARA RESORT: Simplicity with luxurious place that I highly recommend. Interior and exterior of the room is well designed with clever planning, services they provide are all high-end quality and staffs are friendly. Loved the organic food really much and would definitely see Organic Farm in my next visit. Pool area is really nice and big with clean water!!Special thanks to Kanchi and Sunaina for making our stay and experience great!!

This is the place where i can spend quality times with my friends and family. The amazing surroudings which encloses the national park itself visualises the natural beauty. the interior and exterior views consumes astonishing beauty where as pool area is very lavish.The service that they provide is very humble and with a quick response which i admire a lot.Many people might wonder where to go for the vacation with their loved ones, i guess if being myself over there helps others i would highly recommed kasara resort.

I stayed at kasara in june and this is my 2nd visit at kasara in between 5 month which is apparently off season and beginning of the rainy season. The resort is clean and staff polite and welcoming the service was excellent room are nice and cozy I would highly recommend this resort.

Kasara Resort is what you call THE mixture of "Adventure and Luxury". The rooms are super comfortable and clean of course, the staffs are friendly and the food is so good to just set your mood. The clean (and big) swimming pool makes it even better. The Spa was something I looked forward to and was pleasantly surprised (ask for Jenisha because she is too good). Thanks, Kanchi and Sunaina for making our stay great. Definitely going to visit again.

Kasara is more than just beautiful.  As an interior designer, I loved the lush yet modern landscape and rooms. Everyone was very kind that helped us.  More than this, what makes this place incredible are the experiences.  We swam with the elephants!  They squirted us, then we took a ride on them and saw boar, deer and rhinos.  Our guide, Babu, was knowledgeable and funny.  He made sure that we had the adventure of a lifetime!

We spend 3 days in Kasara Resort.Nice and peaceful place with awesome surroundings of Chitwan National Park Excellent food, comfortable rooms and nice and friendly service.And of course best safari guide Kamal :)

Kasara resort was amazing. From excellent rooms and common area, to pristine pool and delicious food. In addition, every staff member was genuine and nice. The jungle package with the elephant safari, elephant bathing, canoe trip, crocodile breeding and jeep safari were all excellent. I would recommend anyone and everyone to stay at Kasara resort.

Kasara was awesome! After time in Kathmandu and a trek out of Pohkara we were looking for some rest and relaxation. This place was just the place. Calm, peaceful and relaxing! The pool is lovely, the rooms are luxurious, and the restaurant has a variety of good food. The staff is attentive, knowledgeable and helpful. The manager Luke took care of us every day easily setting up an elephant washing/viewing, canoe ride and safari jeep ride. We saw a plethora of animals including rhinos and crocs close up, sloth bear and bison. Our guide Kamal had a great eye for the animals and lots of information to share. He also presided over a local dance in the evenings. All in all a great place to stay highly recommend!

I was amazed by the ambient and the way they welcome us as soon as we enter Kasara Resort; kudos to their hard work where the surrounding that they have maintained. I would recommend anyone who wants a luxury trip especially to Terai Region (Hottest part) of Nepal.

I'd like to start by saying that I have travelled to over 30 countries and I make a point of not visiting a country more than once, but I would break that rule with Nepal. Sunaina at Kasara resorts put together an amazing holiday, one that I won't be forgetting anytime soon. Every minor detail was taken care of and nothing was a hassle to alter or change, our guide Jeet would accommodate any request and simply respond with 'no problem'. Every experience was once in a lifetime and I have memories that I will cherish forever. We even booked a helicopter ride, and due to bad weather it was cancelled two days in a row - the owner who felt sorry for us invited us to his restaurant 'Le Sherpa' and treated us to an amazing fine dining experience. Everything that these people did was focused on the customer. I can not praise them highly enough.I would encourage anyone and everyone to go through this company and go on a trip that you won't forget!

This review is long over due. My partner and I stayed at Kasara in September of 2016. Due to a passport situation I had in KTM we missed our flight to Chitwan, but Soinya in the reservation department made sure that Yeti Airlines put us on the next earliest flight. We were greeted at the airport by our guide Babu and driver Pryes. They waited all morning at the airport for us because of our passport situation. They welcomed us with a cool towel and a cold bottle of Coca Cola. I knew then this was going to be a special experience. From that moment Babu personally directed our two night stay and took us on an elephant safari ride where we saw many Rhinos, canoe trip, elephant bath, elephant ride, jungle hike, crocodile farm and bike ride through the country side and local villages. Babu was friendly, kind, knowledgeable and funny. We were always in good hands with Babu.The accommodations at Kasara are the best it Chitwan area. The rooms, pool, and restaurant are modern and luxurious. The food was some of the best we had in all of Nepal. Each meal was fresh, unique and delicious. Our server, Gayatri always made sure we had everything we needed, always friendly and always with a smile. Quite simply impeccable service and excellent food. There is no better Resort in Chitwan Area. Babu, Gayatri, Sionya, Gaurie and Pryus made sure that our stay at Kasara was something we will remember for a lifetime and hopefully one day we will be back to see our friends in this magical paradise. Robert E.

We were totally blown away with the style and comfort of Kasara Resort. We loved the open-air shower and the stylish simplicity of the villa. The guest room was very comfortable with a queen-sized bed. We were sometimes able to reach the reception/restaurant wifi from our villa (C1). There were no TVs in the guest rooms, but that was fine with us. A lovely pool and relaxing pool beds. The resort provides insect repellant for outings. The mosquitoes were not obvious at this time of year, but there were other bugs outside.  The resort naturalist was superb and the elephant safari was a highlight of our time in Nepal. The onsite restaurant served good food and had a decent selection. But, don't miss the happy hour--special drink prices and amazing appetizers! The resort offers airport transfers and is handicap accessible. We had need for a replacement blow dryer in our villa, and the staff responded promptly. They are very intent on pleasing customers. We highly recommend Kasara Resort!

We stayed at Kasara Resort as part of our Exodus trip to Nepal and spent 2 wonderfully relaxing nights at Kasara Resort.   The entire experience was really good and I can't recommend it enough. The rooms are absolutely beautiful - clean, private, and extremely comfortable. The spacious bathroom is separate from the bedroom and makes you feel like you have your own private villa although not so sure about the fact that the shower is open to the elements as this meant sharing my shower with a small gekko.The meals are all buffet style and excellent with wonderful service from the helpful staff. I wasn't too sure about going for an elephant ride at dawn on our first morning but the elephants appeared fairly content and there was no sign of ill treatment. We saw rhinos, deer and many birds but no sign of a tiger. We learned lots and had a wonderful time.We had plenty time to relax back at Kasara and make full use of the sun loungers and pool before we went to the river to bathe the elephants and then went on a dugout canoe ride to spot crocodiles.In the evening we were entertained by some local dancers before another delicious meal.

I spontaneously decided to spend the new years night and weekend in Chitwan.Luckily, I decided for Kasara.It is a beautiful, serene place that quickly let me leave the hectic of Kathamdu City behind.The facilities are excellent and luxurious so that, if needed, you could simply unwind here.I, however, decided to let the staff plan my day and I loved the program they drew up for me.Elephant safari, cycling tour, jeep safari, kanuing - I did it all. And loved it all.This is due to the fact that the surrounding is wonderful and due to the fact that you are very well taken care of.Kasara is a very intimate place where you soon have the feeling of being part of a small community that cares for you.I was travelling alone and not a minute felt lonely.That was mainly thanks to Sunaina, the marketing manager, that organizes everything one needs and brightens one's day with her happy, smiley personality.Thank you, Kasara, for starting 2017 so fabulously for me!!

Everything was good. The architecture is beautiful. The food was very good. Most importantly the staff were very friendly and always helpful. Would definitely go there again soon. A perfect place to get away.

From the time we arrived we we're treated with the utmost care from the transportation to the hotel to every single detail in between.  All of the park guides; most notably Kamal Adhikari we're incredibly knowledgeable on all aspects of nature - it was if we we're on a National Geographic tour - truly.  The Kasara Resort and Chtwan National Park is a must if your going to Nepal.

Was there for the New Years weekend, couldn't believe my eyes when I saw the place how beautifully it was made, green everywhere, rooms were just top class, service was best among I have been in Nepal, food was to die for... overall everything abt this place was best u could get in Nepal. Can't wait to visit them again in my nxt holiday.

Such a pleasure to arrive at Kasara, the last night's stop on our 12 day visit to Nepal. Wonderful hotel, extremely helpful staff, lovely rooms of a much higher standard than we expected. We had an amazing guide, Babu, who took us elephant riding through the jungle on the first afternoon and then canoeing down the river early the next morning, pointing out all the amazing wildlife.  He also arranged for the elephants and their handlers, out for an early walk, to come and pick us up from the river's edge and take us to see 3 rare white rhinoceros up close.  Can not even describe how incredible that was.  Highly recommend a longer stop over than one night!

The room was wonderful and the grounds were perfect, but we will remember Kasara most for how they were able accommodate our situation and provide a personalized experience.We didn't arrive until 10PM, but they were able to provide a very late dinner on our first night and provided a room for our driver.  We had less time than originally planned, but they re-arranged our schedule to include 3 excursions.  When I mentioned that I wanted to visit Tiger Tops 30 years ago, our guide made a special trip to the now closed resort in Chitwan.Next time we plan for a longer stay.

For Nepal this hotel feels like a resort hotel. The rooms are lovely with an outer door, small water area with bridge inside, a sitting area then separate bedroom and large bathroom on either side. The food was buffet style with lots of variety. The bar upstairs was a welcoming place for chatting about the day's events with others.

Five star resort,attached to famous Chitwan National Park,Staff is very good,guide Mr Kamal Adhikari is superb in birds knowledge and guidance in terrain,food is exemplary,management is nice to accommodate small requests to move around, rooms are nature friendly as seen in photosenjoyed stay with support of Yeti Holidays

A beautiful resort with friendly, knowledgeable staff. Delicious food and I must particularly say thank you for catering to my needs, as a coeliac I find it very hard to eat at restaurants/hotels but here they want out of their way to help me.Activities were great and everything really well organised. We managed to fit so much in without feeling rushed.Rooms were luxurious and overall it was definitely worth the price.Would recommend.

Beautiful spacious self-contained rooms with lovely entrance over a small water bridge in a fabulous location with spectacular jungle views. Best poolside beds ever. And blissful spa experience-  those tiny ladies have very strong thumbs.After very mixed experiences previously the charming, chatty and friendly staff restored our faith and were flexible, accommodating and helpful. They couldn't have tried harder. We enjoyed sharing wildlife experiences and appreciated their enthusiasm and knowledge and we had incredible rhino and river safaris.Food is fine(ish), it is what it is for where it is, and our shower experience was patchy but others not. Rooms large with loads of power points and storage.They lose a few marks for their well-intentioned policing of our attendance at the cultural shows/slideshow presentations performed each night - a little over enthusiastic with their keenness to get you involved but they have big hearts and we thoroughly enjoyed our stay.

We stayed two nights at the resort.  The rooms are the best, somewhat unique in design, but quiet and each room is separate from the others.The manager will meet with you at least twice a day.  He is very nice and helpful as are all of the staff.The restaurant food is the best of hotel foods while traveling throughout Nepal.

Visited and stayed for 3 days after trekking and rafting. Able to relax with plenty of pampering and go for elephant safaris, walking in the Chitwan reserve, bird watching, canoe trip,and elephant bathing. First class guide, Babu, who was friendly and flexible, organising early morning trips to maximise animal sitings. Saw leopard, rhinos, deer and crocodiles. As it was October, elephant grass high after the monsoon season, so not best time to see a tiger, but it fitted in with start of trekking season. Very comfortable A/C rooms which kept the mossies at bay. Food usually buffet style, but also wood do early/late meals to suit safari activities. If you're visiting Nepal well worth a visit, especially if you're keen on seeing lots of birds.

If you're planning to go to Chitwan then check out this place. It loves up to its tagline of simple luxury and eco tourism. It's quiet, informal and relaxing and offers a range of great activities from elephant safaris ( unforgettable experience of being in a lake on the elephant 10 feet from a rhino that pulled itself into the bank) , to jeep safaris, jungle walks, crocodile farm, elepgant bathing etc. An hour away is the elephant breeding centre which is a delight. You can get a real taste of local village life without feeling like a voyeur due to the friendliness of the people .  All of this doesn't happen by itself. The general manager Luc runs an efficient and friendly operation with a very nice personal touch taking the time treating each guest as an individual. The restaurant manager Gyatri and his team serve up very good meals throughout the day with a genuine smile. Kamal puts on  good dancing and cultural shows which reinforce the role of the resort locally. Jenisa will massage your aching  muscles and Kim will keep you safe on the dirt track roads. And finally Babu is your man if you need like I did to somehow do all the activities with a damaged back. He looked after me like a 100 year old grandfather which is exactly how I felt. A first rate naturalist and excellent all round guide. We would like to thank the entire staff for the care and attention they showed my wife and I.

From the start to finish it was brilliant, staff were very helpful and well organized. Especially making a reservation was very easy and provided all the service as promised. Great place to spend of your own after day to day life. I especially enjoyed the environment.

I contacted Sunyana of Kasara Resort to organize my solo trip to Chitwan From the beginning she understood what I wanted and advised me to give the good 3 nights package that best matched my idea. I really liked the property and had wonderful time .  In short, both the previous organization, such as attention-site and development of the trip have been excellent. A unique experience, and a visit highly recommended to stay.

I spent two nights at Kasara in September 2016. It was the tail end of monsoon season, so things were relatively quiet. The location is great, right across the river from the national park, and so it was very easy to get to all the different activities. The food was excellent - the kitchen staff asked me what I would like for every meal and were more than happy to bring out second helpings. I also had a massage and facial at the spa, which I enjoyed. As for activities, I did the elephant safari, elephant bathing, jungle walk, visit to the crocodile breeding center, canoeing, and cycling through the local villages. My guide, Jeet, was excellent, although I do think the canoeing and jungle walks are more adventurous/thrill-seeking activities. The room/villa was spacious and lovely. Overall, I felt very well taken care of and would stay here again!

This is a luxurious resort in the Chitwan National Park.  The rooms were huge and had everything one could want. Very clean.  Staff was fabulous.  The buffet was great.  Highly recommend this resort for families or groups.  Free wifi.

This little gem deserves more.  The building is quite contemporary , unique in its own way. Very clean. Love the outdoor shower !  The garden could do with a bit more tender, loving and care. The staffs are very friendly , kind and helpful. They make you feel at home. Food is great but love more vegetarian and fresh fruits. The safari tour is a bonus included in the prices , not sure if everyone receives the same treatment ?  You can easily falling in love here ! Soooo romantic. I will definitely return in autumn.

Two night stay at Kasara was worth it. Its worth every penny you spent to spend quality time with your loved ones. The buffet they offers with changing menu was the best things I ever had.However the cultural show was not so fascinating for me as it was for a very short time.

Already famous as a reputed hotel in Chitwan, we selected this for our family retreat. The whole ambience is amazing with luxury amidst the jungle. There are activities like jungle safari, canoeing, swimming that you are never bored. The food is amazing, the staff is amazing and the best part of the resort is the villas. They have small courtyard in each villa with first class service for relaxation and luxury. This is a must stay place in Chitwan.

It felt like we had escaped to paradise on earth but it did not seem like the resort had been developed to be grand but instead was perfectly respectful to the jungle environment in which it was near. The staff were local and perfectly professional without loosing the genuineness of the community they represented. The rooms combined inside with outside and having the bathroom partially outside was a scary but thrilling experience while maintaining five star standards. The best part was the jeep safari and two trips on the most amazing elephant called roopkalee. The most amazing place I have ever been to with the most incredible customer service I have experienced. We had Kamal who was our tour guide and made this a super special time from the moment he picked us up at the airport with cold towels and cold drinks to the time he brought us back. We even saw two tigers on our early morning jeep safari. The best thing was how the resort was respectful to the natural environment in which it is set and the staff were the same, gentle, polite but welcoming. A first class experience from start to finish. Thank you Kasara and Kamal Will never forget it.

I can't say enough about how wonderful the Kasara Resort and staff are.  The property is stunning in it's indoor/outdoor design for the villas -- you feel like you are really amongst the jungle, but with all the comfort amenities you could need.   The food is delicious, and I really enjoyed the evening cultural show as well. What really made the experience for me was the staff.  They were incredibly willing to help me sort transportation and jungle experiences.  When I didn't see any rhinos on the evening elephant-back safari, they offered to take me out on my own at 5:00 am prior to my outbound flight, at no extra charge.  It was very generous and much appreciated.  The Kasara team went above and beyond to make sure I had a wonderful experience.I cannot recommend this place enough!

Amazing...amazing....amazing !!! We had the time of our life at Kasara which we visited last weekend. We were treated with great hospitality since the time we entered. Everything is so well managed and taken care of....they even take care of waking you up for the safaris and prepare your itinerary as per your convenience. All the staffs treated us so nicely....especially our naturalist DIAMOND dai who was always there to cater to our needs. The rooms are brilliantly made and loved the concept of outdoor bathroom too. Also, a big shout out to the FOOD; the buffet has a wonderful spread. This definitely proved to be a delightful experience for our much needed vacation. We are already planning our next trip there again for the coming year !!!
