The only thing I would criticize is the sometimes not-so-appealing presentation of the food (although it varied - I attached a picture of a very appealing appetizer; but at some other meal, the food was just chomped on my plate by the waiter).- Pool: The pool was just amazing - very refreshing and with great views of the river. Each time I went, the staff was quickly offering me refreshments.- Jungle activities: I had two jeep safaris, a walking safari, a boat safari and an elephant safari. Four out of the five activities were led by Nikita who is an amazing, extremely knowledgable naturalist. I enjoyed most of the activities very much and had several interesting sightings. The only activity I didn't like too much was the elephant safari. The reason for this is that I believe that it is very strenuous for the elephants - it has nothing to do with the staff or with the way it was organized at Meghauli Serai. I know it is a business factor to offer elephant safaris. But other places (like for instance Tiger Tops) stopped the elephant safaris and offer walks / bathing sessions with elephants instead  - and they seem to be doing quite well with this.Overall, it was a superb stay at an awesome lodge with very good facilities and amazing staff. I would gladly come back if I'd return to Nepal in the future.

Staff are amazing and know what they are doing. The rooms are very high quality. Food is excellent. Had a rhino grazing next to the pool. No real downside if you want a luxury safari experience. I would recommend and go back!

Chitin was my last stop during my trip to Nepal and I could not have chosen a better place. The hotel is not only new, but absolutely stunning. It is right next to the river bank and it is decorated with great taste, combining traditional crafts with modern deco. The staff is amazing and will go over the top to make sure that you are having a more than pleasant stay. The activities are great (especially recommend the sunrise boat ride and elephant safari) with very knowledgeable guides. How I wish I could have stayed longer! The hotel is in the middle of nowhere, so it is good to have the transportation previously arranged by the hotel.

After an interesting journey finding the hotel (which is well worth it and out of the way charm added to the beauty of it) we arrived to the hotel with a warm welcome and amazing surroundings. The Villa was stunning, a bathroom with bath, two sinks and two showers as well as a private pool.The Safari experiences; we did the Jeep Safari and the Canoe Safari and the visit to the local village were really enjoyable and our guides were knowledgeable and friendly and we had a fantastic time. The hotel itself epitomises peacefulness. It was calm and tranquil and every need was catered for. The staff were all absolutely fantastic, attentive and friendly. Everything was carried out at a high standard, I was particularly impressed by the fact the Taj Safaris recruit mainly from the local area where the hotel is so upskills the locals.The whole experience was one I will never forget, the little touches and individual attention was second to none. Being a foodie, the meals we had were some of the best I have ever had. We were served a range of Nepali cuisine over the days we were there, showcasing the foods from the different regions as well as international cuisine. You will not go hungry and Meghauli Serai and it really was outstanding. I would go back there just for another meal if I could!

What a fantastic place....from the time you enter till the time you leave the entire visit was magical.Located just off the Chitwan national park ... Which you access by boat , this is truly the gateway to rhino country. The naturalists Arpita, Madan and Mann are not only knowledgable but also extremely enthusiastic and warm. They make the safari truly enjoyableThe boat ride, elephant bath , beautiful dinner setting , the food, are all brilliant.The GM , RItesh, makes you feel like home, with his warm style and little efforts to make you feel extra special. The courtesy he shows flows through the rest of the staff also.Highly recommend the resort...can't wait to go back

What a fantastic experience we had 2 weeks ago at Meghauli Serai.   I was there with my godadughter for 3 nights, and we were treated like royalty.   From the warm greeting upon arrival, the daily surprises by Sanjay, the care to make sure we enjoyed every meal (remembering our preferences) to the amazing daily safaris, it was all magical.The rooms were very comfortable with some of the best bedding of the whole trip.   The private plunge pool was a perfect respite from the hot hot weather.  It was clean, clear and cool.  The food was varied and we always had a choice of western or Nepali food.   The chef(s) made some fabulous meals, and Sanjay and his coworkers delivered them with a smile, with some jokes, and in varied locations (pool, restaurant, bar, river view) so every meal was memorable. I spoke with my goddaughter's mom today and she said my goddaughter was still bringing up Sanjay and his wonderful hospitality.  He really made it so special.The variety and combination of the jeep, boat and walking safari ls kept it interesting and fresh each day.    Speaking of the safari, I had missed an opportunity to do a safari in India to look for tigers, so spotting a tiger here was on the top of my list.   I knew not to be upset if we didn't see one, as the grasses were starting to get high, and a safari isn't like Disneyland- you aren't guaranteed any sightings.   Our naturalist, Santosh, mentioned they hadn't seen a tiger in a month or so.  In our second day, we were so very pleased to get to a vantage point to see a large male tiger crossing the river.   When the locals on elephants mentioned their elephants were getting a bit spooked, Santish knew exactly where we needed to go.  And our (always smiling) driver, Balkrishna, got us up to the lookout place just in time!!  It was magical, and I think our excitement was matched by our guides's excitement.  With bucket list item checked off, i was satisfied.  But when a a tiger is sighted, it's likely to be spotted in the area again in the surtounding days.   So we went back and searched the area.  No luck.   However, later on our way out of the park, I spotted a tiger just off to the right in the grass hanging out.   This time a female and she was glorious.I know we were lucky, and finding all the animals is not guaranteed (we never saw the sloth bear), however, I believe the care, knowledge, and persistence of Santosh helped us make the most of our experience.I highly recommend if you find yourself in Nepal and want to get close to nature, you book a place at Meghauli Serai.   You won't regret it.

After landing safely with Buddha air - I found myself in the jungle at Meghauli Serai, which is the most beautiful jungle resort right by a national park. Being born in the year of the Tiger myself, I've always been fascinated with the tigers and since I've never been to India - I decided to see them in Nepal. The resort is more or less on the border of Chitwan national park - where the last, wild Bengal tigers reside. The saying here goes "Spend 10 hours in the jungle and you'll see a tiger". I spent 20, but sadly they were hiding, snoozing off somewhere. It was super frustrating because we saw fresh tracks and could hear them close - you'll know from the birds and other animals' alarm calls.. It was an amazing, new experience, as I've been spoilt in South Africa where the wild animals more or less almost come into your car during a safari. Here, you need to work for it, be absolutely quiet and sit still. I had this huge safari vehicle to myself with BK the driver and Sujan - tracker. Both excellent at what they do. What an ultra luxurious experience!! The resort couldn't have been more accommodating to my safari needs. And on our last safari, all the other trackers, drivers and villagers were cheering us on as one, big family. They really wanted me to see the tigers as I'd gotten up before 6 am every day for them day after day without luck. The whole village waved and cheered when we zoomed past them. I wonder if I'll forever be known as " The crazy tiger lady of Chitwan. Alas, we didn't see them and a part of me is happy to know that they are smart enough to hide from us humans. I saw an almost extinct Nepalese crocodile species - the Ghiral, heaps of special Rhinos, a wild elephant tons of deer, peacock, beautiful birds and 'water buffalos' :D  I'm still happy with the wildlife sightings and I will be back one day for the tigers and to Meghauli Serai. You need to stay a while to appreciate the jungle properly, it's a very special experience to see these wild animals, and to be able to experience this, should not be taken for granted. The resort itself is beautiful, luxurious and the staff so accommodating. For a couple of days I had the hotel to myself and it felt almost wrong, to have all this and no one else got to share this amazing experience. (I did manage though, lol.) Roomwise, I say go for the villas if you can afford them. There are a few with nice, private plunge pools. They are beautifully decorated and very comfortable and spacious, but the main feature here is that you can see wildlife across the river just from your villa, from your bed if you feel lazy or your plunge pool! Quite an experience. And if you can't afford a villa or they are taken, don't despair, just hang out by their huge, seriously large infinity pool and you'll see the same. I also saw a standard room and it's very beautiful and just above a magical lake with water lilies. If that doesn't make you happy - nothing will. Explore the resort, take a stroll down to the lotus pond, where the stupa and the lotus flowers at sunset are a marvel to behold. And please visit the spa, with the wonderful view of the water lilies. If you are a good explorer - you'll find a hidden path with a secret hammock overlooking the water lilies.. I'm not revealing any more clues :) Gaj Maya took very good care of me in the spa, the spa manager Laxmi as well. All very accommodating. The food was very good, Robin in F&B was assigned to me, and he was always smiling, eager to please and wanting me to be happy. Very sweet. The reception was impeccable, staying in touch before my arrival through What's app. (My flight was delayed 2 hrs.) The camp host Prayatna was very much on top of things, checking for possibilities, cost and more. Amazing service from him. All staff wanting the guests to be happy. The GM greeted me as well, asking if I needed anything or if I wanted anything, I was encouraged to tell him. I was impressed and very comfortable and happy with everything at the resort. A very special place. I feel conflicted to bring this up in my review as what I am about to say has nothing really to do directly with the resort, but I'll say it anyway. I did see another lodge harass and get too close to wildlife (a rhino,) and got stuck in the mud just by the rhino. The Meghauli Serai team did the gentlemanly thing and got the other lodge's truck out of the mud. However, what the other lodge did was inexcusable. There were 3 trucks in the vicinity of a Rhino. The other lodge's truck was very close but wanting to get even closer (why is beyond me..) and revved the engine and got stuck in the mud - the Rhino got scared and stressed by this and even charged them for a few seconds. I wish Meghauli Serai and the other lodges would get together and talk about a common policy about how to behave with these magnificent, wild animals and also set a higher standard for guests wanting to see wild animals. (Like they do in the lodges in South Africa.)I.e guests need to sit still, no talking, no eating, no speaking on the phone, no smoking etc. And for the trucks not to get too close to wildlife for obvious reasons. All of this bad human behavior will scare the animals, and we'll see less in the future. Again, Meghauli Serai had nothing to do with this and I saw only respectful behavior from our lodge. But in an area with other lodges, you are only as good as the weakest link. I hope for improvements here. But dig out your best jungle shirt or attire - be on your best behavior and Meghauli Serai will show you wonderful things in this part of the world!!

We stay there in the villas with the jungle plan , which was included all meals & jungle safari daily once, we celebrate our wedding anniversary thereFor to make our wedding anniversary memorable They made the best arrangements & decorations This is the memorable hotel for us Everything things were best there ie villa, staff ambiance Ext.

We just had a fantastic visit to this amazing property of the taj !! We were a group of six couple and had taken six raptor pool villas !! Hospitality outstanding , well curated meals , outstanding views and extremely courteous staff !! Kiran and his team including sanjay were just amazing !! Although we couldn’t see any big games , but the boat ride and the jeep Safari were an experience not to be missed !! Super experience

This is a wonderful lodge in a truly beautiful location in a remote area at the base of the Himalayas.  Service was superb.  The food was excellent.  The excursions were great, including a boat safari, a jeep safari and an elephant safari in the early hours of the morning. An experience of a lifetime.  We saw numerous rhinos, a crocodile, lots of monkeys and bird life.  Magnificent.

Meghauli Serai, A Taj Safari is exceptional. You will be greeted by music and warmly welcomed to the property. In my stay, half-board and daily a safari excursion was included. First day, we spotted a crocodile and a wild elefant during a short boat safair (with some drink and snack at the river ath the end of it), the other day some rhinos as well as deers, birds of course and some wild peacocks. In the first evening, we were served a local menue after performance of some local dances; the second evening I was served a candle light local dinner on the hotel terrace, lovely and very tasty. The service was incredible and our naturalist accompanying us during the safaris was a very modest and wise young man one could have excellent conversations with. The rooms are well appointed and stylish, mine had a plunge pool I truly loved and the walls of the rooms are painted with motives of local life painted by a local artist. I loved every minute of my stay here and wish I could have been staying more then two nights, just to relax. A big thank you goes to all the staff taking care of the guests.

The very reason we came to Chitwan was because of Taj Meghauli Serai. In fact, I first heard about this serene national park through an article in a travel magazine that was celebrating the launch of this luxury hotel. Unfortunately, after spending a lovely day in Barahi Jungle lodge this place seemed like a runner up in the race to be the king of this jungle! Of course, they were not short on frills and fancy elements – it just felt more manufactured compared to the homely touch of Barahi. With that being said, their spectacular Infinity pool, Riverside Villas with Plunge pools, Characterful Bar where you can exchange travel stories through the night with a Shisha, Surreal Sundowners, Delicious Nepali fare, and Fine hospitality will surely blow you away in any case.LOCATION: Right next to the Rapti River and in the fringe of the core National parkDINE + DRINK:While everything we tasted at the property was excellent, the meal that stood out the most was the THAKALI Thali we were served for lunch and the Newari thali we were served for Dinner. The momo’s and other local food were mindblowing too! We were pampered like crazy all through our trip and probably added on a few extra pounds by the time we left! SAFARI EXPERIENCE: While we had visited in the offseason, the core national park was not open for game drives or Safaris and only the buffer zone was still open. However, we still chose to do a Boat safari, not with any hope of spotting animals but to experience a different kind of sunset. The sweltering heat toasted us severely as we started cruising downstream from the Taj hotel, but it was absolutely worth the trip purely because of what was in store at the end of it.  After an hour or so, the boat pulled off next to a grassland, from where we did a short walk to this magical spot which the staff had already set up a table for us - with all the drinks and snacks – for a classic sundowner.  It was a magical setting - right at the confluence of the Rapti river and Narayani river Meghauli Serai offers several safari options for guests from safari drives, walking safaris, boating safaris and of course the controversial elephant safaris. Since we were against riding animals, we chose to do the game drive on a characteristic Safari jeep. Just like the boat safari, we didn’t spot any of the big guys – except for a teasing sighting of a huge one-horned Rhino. Nonetheless, the drive itself was excellent as we have never been in this close proximity to the greenery and fauna in any of the other safari drives, we had done in Africa and elsewhere. Also, the terrain was so different from what you might get to see in Africa, Borneo or Latin American jungles. - with a direct ringside seat to the spectacular show put up by the great ball of fire as he was signing off for the day!SUNDOWNERS: The key ingredient of any supreme safari drive - no matter how successful the crew has been in spotting wild animals – is how memorable the ending is. And this safari drive was in no way any less than some of the highly-rated safari drives in Africa. The staff had picked a super serene spot that was not just whispering tranquility all around but also felt like a scenery out of a painting! A quiet river streaming below, lush green background of wild fauna, the sun going down at a distance, and the coldest beers and perfectly blended Gin & Tonic! And as we were starting to believe we couldn’t be overwhelmed anymore, they threw into the mix, bowls of spicy potato ‘Chaat’ – whipped up in Nepali style – specially prepared for us just because they heard us in passing mention we love ‘Chaat’!! That is attention to detail and the highest levels of Asian Hospitality for you!To make the evening even more magical, the staff decided to take us back to the Lodge on a Boat instead of an encore of the bumpy ride on the jeep. This was an entirely different kind of boat ride compared to the previous evening. This was journeying down a peaceful stream and reminded us so much of the wooden raft trips in the jungles of the Caribbean or canoe rides in the rivers of Africa.  For a moment we lost our bearings almost and couldn’t wrap our head around where exactly we were! And like the tranquil ride down the river itself wasn’t surreal enough, the departing sun was painting the sky with all sorts of colors like a hyperactive artist on a red bull rush.  Since the setting was unbelievably dreamlike, we couldn’t resist but pipe our own sundowner playlist of African tunes. And that filled in what was missing in this intoxication assault by mother nature!ROOM: We stayed in Rapti River villa number 6, so this review is based on that; VIEW: View of the fields and the river flowing below; SIZE: Very spacious room; AIR-CON: Perfectly functioning cooler that helped in setting the perfect room temperature; BED: Comfortable bed that played the expected part to put me to sleep; BATHROOM: Stand in shower; TOILETRIES: Lovely spa quality cosmeticsFACILITIES: Very lame Gym that was more of a Hot sauna room with broken weights and machines! But the Mind blowingi INFINITY pool more than made up for it!!SERVICE: Friendly staff that took care of all my needs with a smile and made us feel pampered and well taken care of. Special Shout out to SANJAY at the restaurant and ROSHAN at Front desk!HOW WIRED YOU WILL BE: Free high speed Wi-Fi that works well all over the property. Big Plasma TV screen dishing out dozens of channels spanning sports, news, music, movies and a wide variety of entertainment in multiple languages

We got to Meghauli Serai with NatHab for a few days of safari at Chitwan National Park.  We were greeted by all the staff upon arrival (and after each safari trek) with smiles, waves, a cool beverage and moist towel.  The people make this resort very special.  Our room was spacious with a private plunge pool and an outdoor shower.  We woke every morning to the Rapti River and wildlife.  Our treks into Chitwan were excellent with guides knowledgable about the area and how to track local animals.  We even saw a tiger.  The food at the hotel was excellent.  Staff was attentive, especially Arjan in the dining room.  Overall incredible.

One of the best luxury resorts we have been to especially taking into consideration the incredible service and attentiveness exhibited by every single staff in the resort. Everyone goes out of their way to pre-empt and make sure that all your needs are met, and the staff are all really warm and genuine in their desire to make your stay as memorable as possible.The property itself was impeccably maintained and really beautiful, especially the villas. Make sure to get the all-inclusive meal plan, all the meals were very good, but special shout-out to the exceptional dinners served. Every dinner was a feast and truly amazing in showcasing various local Nepali cuisines.In terms of the safari, we did the river/jeep/elephant safari. Our favourite was the elephant safari - we liked it so much we did it twice! Their elephants are treated well and have their own unique personality, and they are such a joy to interact with. Being on an elephant whilst in the jungle also allowed us to get closer to the animals (we got extremely close to many quite a few rhinos during the elephant safaris) than the river/jeep safaris.

As other travelers have mentioned, this is a fantastic property.  We loved riding the elephants on safari to see the one horned rhino , and the ride down the Rapti River at sunset for cocktails and the oxcart ride to the village!  They put on an amazing farewell banquet with entertainment as well.  But it was the genuine concern for our well being and willingness to please that was so terrific.  The people in Nepal are truly amazing, and especially here at the Resort.  Taj really knows how to train and motivate their staff.

Upon arrival after a 45 min drive from airport, we were greeted by the whole team. The entrance and lobby is amazing looking at the beautiful swimming pool. Behind the swimming pool is the river.  Complete silence and  quiet. Rooms are very nice and I have to say the website is under estimating the rooms. Decor is nice  . They have a very nice library next to ten lobby.service is excellent .2 points I would like to mentikn: we did a boat ride over the river.  At the landing point we walked and then they prepRed drinks and a bite but stinks we chargeable. This should not be. Its not suitable for this level of hotel. Doht do it or give drinks you can bear the cost but dong charge.The food at restaurant was ok. But can be improved. Otherwise a real escape. The safari is not as in Adrica bit stil.is a very nice experience.  The naturalists are knowledgeable and its interesting. Very recommended.

You will not find service of this calibre anywhere in Nepal. I visited this property for my birthday and was surprised at every turn by thoughtfulness, consideration, and care. The team here goes above and beyond to make sure guests are satisfied and happy --- as a result, I experienced a magical celebration and an unforgettable stay. If you are celebrating a special occasion, Meghauli can't be beat. Beautiful setting, delicious F&B, top-notch hospitality, and flawless housekeeping. Highly recommended.

We stayed three nights this summer at the Meghauli Serai and it was truly memorable. - the journey to get to the resort is not very comfortable. There are three ways to get there: a 5-7 hr drive (uncomfortable but predictable), a short flight (the 20 min flight is misleading, with the delays it can take 4 hours) and a helicopter ride (comfortable but at ~ 2000 USD for up to 6 people is costly)- I found the naturalists to be excellent, perhaps the best I've seen. They are knowledgeable, articulate and friendly. There is a wealth of birds in the area, as well as the rhinos. I'd like a special mention of Arjun.- The infinity pool overlooking the forest is the best hotel feature- the forest area itself is wonderful. Since Nepal is more relaxed in its forest rules than India, we were able to experience the forest reserve in unique ways: by foot, river, on an elephant- the rooms are thoughtfully designed and very well appointed. We did have a few mosquitoes at night that strayed through the doors. - The food was great at times, but inconsistent. The local cuisine is interesting but probably lacks a sophisticated gastronomic tradition which visitors to the subcontinent expect. Most vegetarian dishes used local ingredients and were top-notch. In the proteins, apart from chicken and one certain local river fish, the rest disappointed. The duck was too gamey and the mutton too tough. Patchy food notwithstanding, this is a wonderful resort. The Taj touch comes out strongly.

Spent 4 nights here relaxing after a surgical mission in Bangladesh and it was the perfect place to come to... amazing staff, incredible food, peace and quiet! loved the wonderful safaris! I’d definitely visit this place again. Short plane ride from Kathmandu and paid a local cab drive $30 US to take us there -

The Meghauli Serai Lodge at Chitwan National Park was overall a very nice experience.  The lodge fits naturally with its surroundings.  The service was excellent and even if we had an occasional language lapse, the staff tried very had to please (their English was much better than my Napalese).  The place is beautiful; the accommodations are top notch.  My husband and I stayed in a villa with private pool.  There were a couple little things that could have been better (The gap under the door to the outside made me nervous - this is cobra country.  My solution, stuff towels under the door at night.  The private pool was beautiful but since it wasn't heated it was rather cool and getting into it was difficult because the first step was very deep).  The pool did bring in a jungle cat one morning and that was neat to see.  Housekeeping refreshed the room several times a day (it was hot when we were there and we took a lot of showers).  Laundry was efficient and returned the same day.  The food was good but there could have been more variety.  They tended to make traditional foods of Nepal but they seemed to have a 3 day cycle and since we stayed 5 days, we got repeat meals (the manager did apologize to us about that, even though we did not complain).  They did have a few a la carte offerings, but "continental" dishes were just pasta and pizza (although they were very accommodating with my requests regarding these).  One evening we were served a traditional meal, along with dance and music, in their "village" - very enjoyable.Safaris were well organized with knowledgeable naturalists and staff.  We saw what we came for   - and more:  32 rhinos!.   We took several safaris, including two boat safaris.  The boat safaris were both the same, ending with a walk to a spot to watch the sunset (beverages were supplied at this point, but someone should have mentioned that we would be charged for these since soft drinks and water on the other safaris were complimentary).  I would have liked some variation in the boat safaris.  Also we should have been warned that we would be doing some walking on the boat safaris - about 10 minutes out to the point to watch the sunset, then another 10 or 15 minutes back to the vehicles that drove us back to the lodge (those vehicles could have been brought closer to us).  If I knew about the walk I would have brought my cane to help with the terrain.  The safari vehicles were rather "beat up" although the naturalist told us they were only a year old.  Jeep safaris often covered some of the same areas, but the routes are determined by the government not the lodge.  Returning from safari we were always greeted by the staff with cool drinks and cold towels.  This was a nice touch, especially since it was quite hot and humid when we were there.We wished all staff, including the safari staff, wore name/position badges. It would have facilitated our getting to know them.   After we returned to Kathmandu I found I had left an item at the lodge.  The staff found it and were helpful in getting it back to me (no small task).  Since this is a relatively new lodge I think some of the concerns I expressed are just growing pains.  They can easily be remedied. If you want a luxury experience in Chitwan, this is the place.

Finest Spot in Chitwan for Safari Lodge for stay. Mayaram Driver ,Pick us up from Bharatpur .Drove nicely with safety, to Chitwan at Meghuali Sarai. Welcome us  very hearty , big and warm cheerful welcome by Staff. Swimming pool is very nice. Location and facility remind me Singita Boulder SA. Nikita & Maan took us on Elephant ,Jeep and boat Safari. Chef Lekhraj and staff gave us best  Cuisine which we like.Rooms view was  very scenic .Love to staff of HOTEL..Stay from 24 th April 2017 to 26 th April 2017: PATEL

Thank you for the good hospitality and making our trip best Roshan Sapkota and Meghauli Serai Team.We loved this place so much. The staff were amazing, very attentive and professional. We appreciated the size of bedroom and bathroom areas. The meals were excellent and the service in the dining room was good. It's been quite an adventure. We are glad we stayed there.

My husband and I booked a villa for our first anniversary after experiencing the wonderful service by andBeyond during our honeymoon. Arriving at Meghauli was such a welcome relief after dusty Kathmandu and a bumpy 7h road ride. The property was absolutely beautiful, the staff was so warm and welcoming, the food was good and the safari experience was amazing (do not expect an African safari though). Even our driver was treated very well! We went for an elephant safari, river safari and a jeep safari and got to know a few rhino up close and personally. The highlight was definitely the staff - our butler, Sanjay, was extremely attentive and even called us when there was a rhino frolicking outside our room and he was delighted to be able to speak Malay to us and our naturalist, Deepkul, was an all-around cool guy who still owes us a tiger sighting. The entire staff team surprised us on our last night by pranking us and it's certainly an experience we won't forget. Our only regret is that two nights was far too short and that we shouldn't have gone here at the start of our trip because everything else just couldn't compare. Definitely looking forward to exploring other Taj Safari/ and Beyond lodges around the world.

The rooms were awesome, I stayed in both the villas and the hotel style room, splurge on the villa - absolutely worth it and so much nicer. The food was great daily. I did the chefs meal every night and each night was a different theme and beyond met my expectations. Even when the hotel was full with the service level didn't fall. I highly recommend the sunset cruise, very relaxing. I did the elephant safari and jeep safaris as well. The property is beautiful! There is a helipad on the property, if there was a next time I would helipad to the property instead of dealing with the airlines/delays and the ride to the hotel. While the reviews say how bumpy it is, I think it depends on the car. My ride in was in a newer car and was fine. The ride back to an airport was older and very bumpy. Highly recommend this place!!

We arrived at midnight after getting stuck in a massive jam from Mugling due to landslide and was promptly served a full course traditional Thakali dinner!  The hospitality was top notch and we were fed way too much. This resort really meant it when it said meals are served on your own time. The menu, including the dinner venue changed every day and they happily whipped out something simple for our kid who refused anything spicy.  Stayed three nights at the villa and wished we had planned to stay longer.  It was such a quiet and peaceful place.  We hardly saw other patrons as everyone were in and out at different time.  Our naturalist, Nikita was a real gem.  Her enthusiasm and love for the wildlife was infectious. The resort's two elephants seemed well taken care of too.  After a tour hour elephant trek, they were taken out to roam and bathe on the river for at least three hours!  As for the rhinos, we saw 8 during the jeep ride and another 4 during the river safari. The highlight of the trip was a rhino right at the outdoor dining area two nights in a row!

I visited the property this past weekend and was blown away by the resort. We stayed at the Villas and were greeted to a beautiful room with great interiors and a plunge pool. Even though we were three of us sharing a room the room was very spacious with the extra bed as comfortable. In my opinion this hotel by far is the most luxurious in Nepal in its segment. The food is very delicious. Different cuisines are served for different meal times. We were served the Oriental cuisine for Lunch which was amazing. The staff are very professional and the Naturalists are very knowledgeable. Overall great food, great swimming pool and great service. I would recommend spending some quality time to enjoy the property.

This lodge is extraordinary in every way. From the moment you arrive the service is topnotch. The views from the main lodge and the river view rooms are breathtaking. We stayed in one of the river view Villas. It was a huge suite with King Size canopied bed facing the river. There is a very large bath that had a claw foot tub, separate shower and two sinks. There was also an outdoor shower contained within a walled enclosure. Each of these villas has a private plunge pool! Plenty of storage. A power cord with two plugs was provided. The hotel has a variety of things to do including elephant, jeep and river safaris. It is a little out of the way but it is worth it.

Once you land at the airport with the small 30 seats airplane you will have a 1 hour ride over bumpy roads and you are wondering if you are going to the right place. The airport pick up is about 80US dollar which is kind of expensive. If the roads are in normal condition the drive would be only 30-40 min.  The arrival at the hotel is just wow and you are greeted by the staff of the hotel which is singing a traditional song before they open the gate into the hotel main lobby to see the spectacular view over the pool and the jungle. After all the check in is done you go to your rooms which are nice and new and see the great view. One thing which is very sad for me is that the rooms have no bath tub which would be nice over the colder months to have. There would have been enough space in the bathroom to have one. All the staff in the hotel are the key and super friendly and welcoming. During our stay there are only 2 other rooms with guests so the staff was for me a bit to overwhelming and checked every 2 minutes if all is ok. You have to always remember that you are a bit far away so even the Internet may not work properly. Food is limited but the staff is always trying their very best to help and accommodate what can be done. If you need anything special for your meals you need to ask them before you arrive so the hotel can try to organize it. Normally thy offer set menus but have a small a la carte menu available as well. We always went with the set which was very fresh and very tasty. Before my arrival I was in email contact with the hotel to make sure the booking and airport pick up was all confirmed. The safari tours are amazing, you will have the chance to see the animals live in action and not in a zoo behind bars. The guide is very knowledgable and experienced. We did a tour with a car and after a boat ride along the river. After the ride we stopped for a small picnic and to watch to sunset. (Drinks will be charged after which we didn't know, would have been nice if they let you know)How many days should you stay? My personal suggestions would be 3 nights, if you are on a tight schedule 2 nights is fine as well, summertime you can enjoy the pool which can be done after your tours to chill out which you can't use over the colder winter months. Prices at the restaurant are very very fair and for sure not overpriced. If you are planning a nepal trip you should plan this lovely hotel in your schedule. I would love to go back one day.

We travelled only for a weekend getaway to Chitwan just to experience the beauty of this resort and must admit it's an upscale resort with personalized service, one of the best in Nepal! Have been to other Taj hotels too but rooms compared to meghauli Serai are quite different, amazing concept, very spacious, we stayed at the Villa with a plunge pool. The only thing that Disappointed us was the road from airport to hotel, almost 1:20 hrs ride and roads are not smooth. Hopefully it will. E taken care of in the near future! Will definitely be back!

I stayed here in mid October 2016 and have to say it's everything it claims to be. From the moment we arrived the staff were friendly and attentive, sorting all of my girlfriends dietary requirements immediately. We stayed in one of the villa's with a private plunge pool and outdoor shower, this I can't recommend enough. The actual safari park is stunning with Pradip guiding you round the park in the Jeep to riding the elephants through the forest seeing many Rhino, monkeys and deer. Overall a brilliant stay with great staff, food and luxury accommodation, if staying in Chitwan Meghauli Serai is a must.

What's unique at #MeghauliSerai @Taj National Park is the entire team welcomes you and sees you off - I can see every member chipping in to make the experience unique and so @Taj - many thanks to the GM of the property Kaustav and his entire team #sayonara and #aufweidersehenEach wall in this property has a story to tell - with a private pool, calm and serene neighborhood and blissful like view of Chitwan National Park- this property is amongst the best places I have stayed

this is a beautiful property. LUXURY in jungle, the approach to the property compels you to think about the choice of property. once you enter  it is fabulous, presidential suit is superb. it is a quiet property. you are in Jungle so you will find insects, frogs and even elephants. must visit for nature lovers. An experience to remember for a lifetime! The hospitality was outstanding, the resort itself is breathtaking. Definitely recommend staying here. Thank you Dipu and Buddi dai for ensuring we had  the best time!

My wife, two kids and myself spent 6 amazing days at the Taj Safari Lodge. Nestled along the banks of the Rapti river, the lodge offers excellent views of the national park which is just a boat ride across the river. We stayed in the Rapti Villas, two of them. These villas are absolutely fantastic and the kids enjoyed swimming in the plunge pools. The lodge, luxurious resort actually, is very comfortable and the entire staff went out of their way to make our stay a truly memorable one. Excellent service and food. I can go on and on about the lodge, but it is a Safari lodge :-). We made numerous excursions into the forest. Watching Rhinos at close range is not an experience that we will forget in a hurry. There were elephant rides and a number of thrilling boat rides as well.  Finally got to see muggers and gharials in their natural habitat. Would love to go back to experience it all over again.Sanjiv Nagraj

We had high expectations for our stay, and the reality exceeded every one of them.  We stayed in a villa that was thoughtfully furnished and decorated and extremely comfortable.  The view of the river was perfect, joyful to sit outside and just relax.The property itself is attractive and welcoming, with lots of places to appreciate the surroundings and to rest and/or socialize.  The dining area takes advantage of the views whether sitting indoors or out.  A shout-out to Chitra and his associates for taking such fantastic and attentive care of us.  A truly amiable host.  It was like being treated by an old friend.  The food was delicious and varied.  Everything was excellent, but we especially enjoyed the Chinese offerings.And the safaris.....  We were going in large part to see a tiger.  We'd failed in our efforts in India, and the odds are even less in Nepal.  Our deep and abiding gratitude to Santosh and Santosh for their extraordinary skills and, as important, their patience, which allowed us to see a tiger on two of our three drives.  Just seeing one would have been a miracle, but two?  Most people will take just one drive and cover a lot of territory.  In our case, we arranged for a private vehicle and were able to sit quietly where Santosh and Santosh identified as highest probability based on their considerable knowledge, and it paid off.  Please keep expectations in check, as sightings are very rare, but worth the effort.  Beyond the tiger, we had exciting sightings of a sloth bear, crocs, rhinos, lots of birds, and many other animals.  I also recommend taking taking the boat ride on the river.  Beautiful scenery and stunning bird sightings.  Many thanks to Amit and his superb staff.  Without exception, they made us feel welcome and appreciated, responding immediately and cheerfully to whatever we needed.  I recommend this property with great enthusiasm and appreciation for all the staff did to make our stay so memorable.

A truly 5-star experience:1) First class property all-round. Tranquil and luxurious.2) Great room - comfy bed, loads of space, huge bathroom with great shower and separate bathtub. Private plunge pool was great too. 3) The staff are friendly and attentive - always smiling and ready to help.4) The food is excellent - just be aware of the set meals with multiple courses - sometimes too much food.5) The main pool is stunning, with a view out over the river (we even saw elephants from the pool one day).6) The safaris (jeep, boat and foot) were excellent. The guides (all from the local area) are highly knowledgeable, and the whole experience was amazing, especially for the kids.

The luxurious experience was amazing. Loved the ambience, extraordinary hospitality, very friendly staff, full exposure of nepali tharu culture, delicious foods, jeep saffari, sunset view diner, boating and more. Will never forget this experience.

Staffs were super friendly especially Sanjay and anil. Stayed there for two night they took care of us very well. Loved the property will definitely recommend friends. But room service needs to be bit active in terms of delivering the goods we need overall amazing stay will be back.

I have visited Megauli Serai around 3,4 times….And still its my favourite place for Vacation in Chitwan…Food,Staff,Ambiance everything is Perfect….Specially the Rapti pool villa is Awesome…..Just taking a dip in plunge pool with your loved ones with the view of Rapti river and Chitwan national park is Amazing…..Highly Recommended ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

The retreat is a perfect mixture of calm and adventure. This coupled with a team that goes above and beyond to ask you at every point about how your stay is going. I remember everyone from the chef to the receptionist to the GM checking on us about our stay. The food was a classic Indo-Nepali affair on Day 1 and a Japanese set menu for lunch on day 2. The jungle safari and boat ride were to say the least, breathtaking. We saw a herd of 6 rhinos with the naturalist giving us interesting  tidbits about the animal and the forest. The evening was a cultural affair with the Tharu dance performance where we danced with the locals over scrumptious food. There's a lot to do and yet one can choose to do nothing. Just sitting at the lawns overlooking the Rapti is a wondrous feeling; self reflective, calming and symbiotic with nature. I've rarely seen a property that combines the beauty of nature in such a perfect setting and makes you miss it terribly once back. Meghaul Serai, A Taj Safari is one of those.

The place was just amazing .. the ambience and food was really good... And the staff were really co-operative and lastly the safari was really good.. did find and spot a few animals.. it's surely a must visit place

Have been to many wild life parks in India,but this experience was simply outstanding-by way of hospitality,service,ambience and the quality of jungle.Breathtaking view from the lobby,as well as the villas,the staff was very very warm and were brilliant in their service

Not being hyperbolic here but this visit was thousand times worth. (Ours was Rapti villa)

Meghauli Serai, a Taj Safari made me get back to TripAdvisor and write a review about them.I had stayed in another Taj property in Aug 2022 and I was not too overwhelmed with that stay. Hence, I was not too sure what to expect as I have stayed in Taj earlier and was always happy.Meghauli Serai takes a blue ribbon when it comes to (a) location; (b) hospitality and (c) service.We were so well taken care of that words fall short fo describe it. From the GM of the property to the naturist, to the driver, to the front office staff, to the guest relations staff, to the chef and to the F&B service staff, all were very hospitable and took great care of us. Never say never at its best.We were in the Rapti River Villa and the villa overlooks the river. Room was great and very well maintained. The other rooms I.e Meghauli rooms overlook a lovely lily pond. There are facilities like a basketball court, badminton court, spa, water safari, jeep safari et al. The naturists have deep knowledge of the area, animals and can communicate very well.The food was great with a continental one day to oriental one day to a traditional Tharu meal one day. A visit to this place is highly recommended!Meghauli Serai, keep amazing your guests! You are great at it!

My visit to this hotel started with Buddha Air sending 2 of my bags to the wrong airport, and went downhill from there. At least Buddha delivered by getting our bags to us only a few hours later.Upon checking into the hotel, we were taken to our suite. Our agent had confirmed a Presidential suite though I saw no particular description of it on the hotel web site. We were just 2 people and this suite had a dining area, living area and 2 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms. We lasted in the room about 3 minutes due to a horrible smell of fresh paint. They moved us to what I guess was a standard room which frankly would have been fine for 2 people for 2 nights. Unfortunately, they gave us no room instructions.Whoever designed the room should go back to school as it’s the craziest layout. You have a walk in from the outside thru gated type doors to the room locked room door. At this point you are still outside. You then open what you’d think was the bedroom door, and you have a hallway thru which you can enter the bathroom. This door locks. Then there is another door to the bedroom which doesn’t lock, which isn’t necessary. So you get the feeling that you can leave the door to the bedroom open to the hallway to the bathroom. This is what we did. But no one advised us to close the bedroom door, and after dark, there were frogs jumping all over the room. The bedroom is somewhat isolated from the frogs, if the door is stays closed, but it was too late. When we complained, we were told that they are harmless and good luck. We didn’t need any good luck charms. The next night, only 1 was in the bedroom as we then knew to keep the bedroom door closed at all times. The bathroom connects to a second shower which is outdoors, and there is a door to the outside that is easy for frogs to come in and then get into the bathroom thru a hole where the swinging door to the outside shower is. I didn’t complain about the ants in the bathroom because it can be expected due of our location. But mold in the shower of an expensive hotel isn’t acceptable. We came here for wildlife. As a veteran of a dozen safaris in Africa including 3 weeks in Botswana 3 months ago, Chitwan is a joke. The vehicles cannot compare to Africa and the posts that are added for the open roof are right by your head when you are sitting. You may get your head bumped on the bumpy road, so be careful. Unlike Botswana, you cannot go off road. So you move along a narrow road and hope to see something. They took us out at 7 am and it was very foggy. So when 2 Rhinos were spotted, it was just a haze of what appeared to be moving rocks even with 8x binoculars. As the fog lifted around 9 am, we could get about 100 yards from the rhinos. On this outing, we saw some spotted deer, 2 rhinos and a few monkeys. The bird life wasn’t there, at least not when we were out. The chances of seeing a tiger is probably slim unless you are out for lots of time, and/or are just lucky. And if you do see one by the water, you may need binoculars to see them in any detail. Our guide even mentioned that it’s easier to see them in India as there is more open area. We chose not to go out again, as it frankly was just plain boring. The hotel staff gets an A for friendliness and effort, but they fail miserably. The food is a few steps step above bad. They cannot even make scrambled eggs correctly. The corn soup was very good as is the fresh orange and watermelon juice and fresh salad. Coffee the first day was excellent, and totally undrinkable the second day, and bread  and muffins are rubbery. The staff has difficulty understanding English. I hate to fault them for that as I basically only speak 1 language, but if you are going to be serving foreigners, you need better English skills.  Even the people answering the phone get it wrong. I asked for fresh towels and 2 boxes of tissues. Housekeeping brought the towels with 2 bottles of water.All in all, this may be a good spot for a novice safari, but not for a veteran. And this is supposed to be the best in the area. Management apologized for the room issue and didn’t charge me for a beer, but no mention of any compensation for the room downgrade was offered due to the paint smell. Needless to say, we won’t be back.

Highly recommended!Whole property is awesome...delicious food and all the F/B staffs are really helpful. You and your family will definitely taken care o! Special thanks to Prayatna for all the arrangements...

The best time I have ever had the team make you like family and the love they give you have no words from the day you get too the hotel you feel like kings and queens I have too say the the villi Is awsome private pool Dinner was so fresh and tasty can not say more

Travelled with my family for a Nepal trip. The rooms and view was stunning! The staff was impeccable and charming, everyone is ready to help and has genuine happiness with them. It is really amazing place to organize  out any events.staff are reloded with full hospitality.place with best hospitality.ambience is so amazing and refreshing and its all due to its natural senerio,rapti river view and care and attentive staff.

What a Lovely welcome culture!! Excellent property!! Friendly staff always willing to help and heartily welcoming!! Great getaway!! Diversity of culture addressed in the property!! Thank you. Recommended, it’s a place to be. One of the best property visited till date!

When we visited it was raining so we couldn't do jungle activities but we were really impressed by the personalized experience they were able to give. Not only they made sure there were no sprouts in my food, but they also made sure we had a very wonderful stay by their food setting.

Rarely can I say that staying at a resort is itself and experience, but for the Meghauli Serai, that it undoubtedly true. I wish I could give this place a 10-star review. The service is the best that I’d had at any resort - they handle everything around your stay in a seamless fashion. The experts that took us into the park for the walking safari were so unbelievably knowledgeable and fun! (I very much recommend the walking safari). And the accommodations are spacious and beautiful and worth the cost. I had an amazing time here.

If my title doesn't say it all then I will illustrate furthermore. Get ready to witness the best service ever in your life! The staff go miles beyond what is expected from them in order to make sure you are happy and comfortable. They honestly make you feel like you are a family. Chitwan is no huge city like Kathmandu or Pokhara. The hotel make sure you get the best experience by offering a variety of activities including: elephant safari, jeep safari, and village safari. The naturalists that accompany you through the tour are extremely knowledgable about almost everything lol. The bedroom and bathroom are clean and nice. I highly recommend you book here if your looking to have a delightful stay in Chitwan.

We spent 2 nights at the resort in one of their standard rooms.  It was spacious and well appointed, very comfortable.  Internet is spotty - if that is a concern.  We did several safaris - river boat, Jeep, and walking.  We saw numerous animals - elephants, rhinos, monkeys, deer, sloth bear (alas, no tigers).  The food was superb with special attention paid to the dinners.  One night was a Nepalese barbecue under the stars.  The other night was a special dinner to show what a special celebration would be like at a local Nepali village - held at a open courtyard with music and dancing from local people.  The breakfasts and lunches were also excellent.  One day we had a wonderful pasta dish with home made focaccia.   The chefs excelled in Asian, Continental, and Nepali food - - just amazing.The other highlight was the warm and attentive service.  Laundry and shoe cleaning is included - fast and thorough.  One of the managers made a special effort to get us different drinks than what was on the menu - really appreciated.  We truly enjoyed our stay at this gorgeous resort.

We were debating skipping Chitwan during our stay because we werent sure we’d have enough time.  We decided to do it anyway despite our tight schedule; I’m so glad we did it and that we stayed at the Megahuli Serai. It was so peaceful and relaxing.  The staff and service was amazing. The food and drinks were exceptional (and reasonably priced for a 5 star hotel). There is not a lot to do other than safari, eat, spa and relax at this stunning property - which was much welcomed after a long trip of trekking and touring. The hotel manager, Roshan was so accommodating and pleasant to speak with each day.  We even got upgraded to a gorgeous, spacious villa overlooking the river and forest.  Both Roshan and is staff (including Anjan) have infectious smiles on their face everyday.  Roshan arranged all our next travels, flights, cars, hotels after we left, which made everything very easy for us. Two additional perks - 1-the hotel employs, educates, and empowers all locals in the local community / village (which is important in a developing country)2- the hotel is making big steps towards eco-friendly operations I highly recommend this hotel and I have exceptionally high standards.

From the first welcoming moment of drums, smiles and clapping to the fond adieu of collective waves by the team, Meghauli Serai is an experience in itself.  The service was impeccable and the villas, utterly luxurious with absolute attention to detail and vignettes that are the quintessence of luxury. The bedroom and bathroom sport large spaces with amazing lookouts over a mini-infnity plunge pool overlooking the paddies.  The scenery is calming as it is serene.  Absolute privacy is guaranteed and if you don't want to go on a game drive, the resort just embraces you in luxurious care.  From a four-legged bath, to an indoor shower and outdoor shower spout that includes a day bed bathed in sunlight, his and her sinks, lots of towels and good quality amenities, the bathroom is just one of those places you can even sit and read a book.The resort prides itself on having team members who are of the Tharu (jungle) tribe, showcasing their cuisine and cultural mores, legends and habits. Meals are plated which is a lovely exception to the buffets that are normal and a full on bar with an expert barman puts you in high spirits.  True infinity is reflected in the massive swimming pool in which panoramic views are echoed.  The architecture and interiors are extraordinarily beautiful, with alot of thought given to the overall look and feel of the resort.  The naturalists are as attentive - taking you through paths, onto rivers and into the forests for your glimpses rhino and if you're lucky, leopard, elephant and tiger.  To me, the entire resort spoke of sincere hospitality coupled with genuine warmth and need to make every guest very special

Where to begin?!? The accommodations are outstanding. We had a suite - each has its own private view to the river and a mini pool. The room was huge and very well appointed down to the hand painted walls. The bath had an outdoor shower option, which is always a plus for us.The main area has a huge negative edge pool, lovely bar, and plenty of comfortable seating. Meals were all delicious! The chefs they have are incredible, especially considering how remote this place is.And the staff!!! Our guide Man was friendly, knowledgeable, and passionate about the environment and animals. Sanjay made sure we were delighted with extras, like the floating bar in the pool and a romantic dinner for two one night. We came back to the room to find a lovely bubble bath drawn in the claw-footed tub and two glasses of wine!The highlights for us (yes, there’s more!) was seeing so many rhinos and taking the elephant bath - they showered us and then we got to bathe them. The elephants are rescues from an Indian park and are very well treated, which made us feel comfortable.I could go on for paragraphs. Do not miss this opportunity if you are visiting Nepal!!

We stayed last week and did the Wildlife Escape Plan, staying in a Maghauli Room and it was such an amazing experience. The service was impeccable, the best I have experienced in all of my travels. The itinerary was busy but they made everything seem so easy with the organisation of all of the activities, the incredible meals and any change of plans were sorted with ease. We were able to swap the elephant safari for elephant bathing and a village visit which were both excellent. I think the river safari was my favourite as we saw many crocodiles within a few minutes of drifting down the river, which was followed by seeing monkeys, jackles and many different types of birds. The guide we had was very knowledgable too. At the end of the trip we were surprised to have a table set up for us to enjoy the sunset. We didn't feel comfortable doing a jungle trek as the guides only carry sticks and sometimes you may have to run and hide (I'm sure it's fine as we saw many people doing it! I just get scared easily) so we paid extra for a jeep safari and we were very lucky to see a leopard! although no rhino's, so if possible try and go on at least 2 safaris at different times of the day to increase your chances of seeing more animals. We had a Maghauli room in the hotel blocks which was beautiful. It had a balcony overlooking a large pond which was great for spotting birds, a very large bed (although the mattress was quite firm for us but we experienced this at most hotels in Nepal), clean well kept rooms with a turn down service and the surroundings of the hotel are very well kept with a lovely pool area. I can imagine the villas are incredible.I would definitely recommend the wildlife escape plan or a plan which includes the meals as they were delicious with excellent service from all the kitchen and front of house staff. We recommend this hotel to anyone staying in the Chitwan Area of Nepal and we ourselves can't wait to visit this hotel again next time we go to Nepal!

EXCELLENT.!!!On behalf of my group thank you for the memorable experience.NAMASTE  Natalia.

Me and seven of my friends stayed here for a night and the experience was awesome. Wish we could stay here for little longer. Roshan was amazing in providing us everything we needed and Sanjay made sure the food served were delicious. Hoping to visit again. The rooms were clean and spacious and the pool was breathtaking.

Me and my wife stayed in Taj Meghauli Serai right after we got married. From the moment we were picked us up at the Bharatpur by Mr Mayaram and Mr. Roshan, we knew that we were in for an mesmerizing experience. The warm welcome by the group of staffs at the hotel gate really touched us even before we stepped inside the hotel.  A short walk around the hotel lobby gives you a hint of the luxury this property offers. The food was really awesome and was served Mr Chitra and Mr Anjan, both of whom were really warm, attentive and were kind enough to give us the information about the hotel and how it has embraced the local Tharu culture as its main theme. We were glad when Mr. Lekhraj, the chef, came to us and asked us if the food was nice. During our stay, we realised that the chef has some really great recipes for the wide varieties of food, ranging from the oriental to continental, including some traditional Nepali dishes which reflect his own trademarks. We want to thank Mr Suman, the naturalist, who guided us during the boat safari down the rapti river. We managed to learn a lot of things from him regarding the traits of rhinos, monkeys, gharials, spotted deers, the birds and the vegetations while enjoying the beautiful sunset in front of us. They even had a surprise for us at the end of the boat safari trip which we would like to keep it secret for the prospective guests. The elephant safari the next day was equally amazing. A couple of hours with the Rupkali, the elephant, took us from the plain glass land of Meghauli to the most dense forest we have ever been. The ride took us through the heart of the jungle where one can have a close up view of the plethora of rare wild animals and birds including the one horned rhinos. We want to thank the helmsmen, the mahuts and the elephants (Premkali and Rupkali) for both the boat safari and the elephant safari. The most touching moment was the private candle light dinner set-up arranged by Mr Anjan and Ms. Pabitra which was as romantic as it can get. We told them that we will remember this dinner forever and thanked them from the core of our heart. The villa that we stayed was absolutely gorgeous: the private pool, meticulous wall sketches depicting the tharu culture and their livelihood, the big bathroom, drinks and the nepali snacks with cute welcome notes. The entire villa was clean and perfectly tidy each time before we returned from outside. We would like to thank Manoj, Januka, Sukhi Tara and the entire housekeeping team for this.I would also like to thank Mr. Mayaram and Mr. Santosh for driving us while receiving and sending off. In addition to the luxury and the amenities the hotel infrastructure provides, we have been truly impressed with the top-drawer service the staffs have provided. It is extremely demanding task for these staffs to deliver the warm and highly personalised hospitality of the highest quality and to be able to deliver that while still maintaining the upmost professionalism is really outstanding.Lastly, we both would like to thank Mr. Roshan, the camp host, for planning and overseeing our journey and stay at the Meghauli Serai. We really appreciate the way he supervised our entire trip to make sure that we are very comfortable. He had truly been a great host during our stay.There are a few things in life which you can not buy with the money and we feel that the experience at the Meghauli Serai is one of them.  -Rajesh

This resort is absolutely amazing in every way. Everything was of very high quality and there was nothing lacking. The staff at Meghauli Serai were so friendly and helpful, and for every detail of our stay they ensured our comfort and happiness. There were a few surprises and extras that really made us so happy. They treated us like royalty!Our room was perfect— clean, cozy and beautiful. The Nepalese food was incredible, and western dishes are also available. The boat safari was an adventure I will never forget (even in the “off season”/ monsoon season, we still saw lots of wildlife!). I learned a lot from the naturalist, who was extremely knowledgeable and answered in detail every question we had! Absolutely heavenly and a must visit! It was precisely the romantic getaway in nature that we were hoping for. Worth more than 5 stars, this kind of perfection is hard to come by!

Amazing hospitality, amazing property! We did canoe safari, elephant safari and jeep safari. There's a spa too! The rooms are beautiful with an ethnic touch. The staffs are very polite, helpful and thoughtful about every detail.

The Meghauli Serai has a fantastic location on the bank of the Rapti River across from Chitwan National Park.  The lodge offers jeep, boat, walking and elephant riding safaris, be sure to understand however exactly what is included in your package price.Beautifully appointed rooms and common areas looking out over an infinity pool to the forests of Chitwan on the opposite bank.  From the moment of our arrival we were treated to first-class hospitality.  The lodge has several naturalists, the three we spent most of our time with (Prayatna in particular, but also Arjun and Ajindra) were exceedingly informative and also just a pleasure to be with.  For us the chance to walk in the forest (once alongside two of the domestic elephants, once just with our guides) were highlights of our most recent visit to the sub-continent.  Food at the lodge ranged from outstanding to good, service from our main server Sanjay was top-notch, we will not soon forget the cold beers he had waiting for us at the riverbank as we returned hot, sweaty and dusty!  Chitwan is not the easiest place to get to by car, and flights from Kathmandu often involve some delays.  But the journey is worth the time, it is one of the very few places left in the world where you can see the one-horned rhinoceros in the wild, in one instance for us while on foot, we took cover behind a tree for a while!  Hundreds of bird species, deer, wild boar, crocodiles and if one is very fortunate a tiger or in our case a sloth bear. If you do go we would highly recommend the Meghauli. Lastly, if you decide to help bath the elephants, count on getting very wet!

If you wish to visit chitwan then this is the place. Amazing property and service. Good food. Dont miss out on the spa either. You will even be served local nepali food which as per me was simple and tasty food. Also we had a night for traditional dance aa well.

We arrived at the small Bharatpur airport and were greeted by our personal guide for our time here. Prayatna was professional and knowledgeable and an excellent guide for our three days at the lodge.  We arrived after an hour drive through the countryside dotted with traditional Thuro villages. The lodge is stunningly beautiful, situated on the Rapti River. Our river front villa was huge and luxurious with a private plunge pool. The bathroom has a claw footed tub, a shower indoors and outdoors. Pure luxury from the soft king sized bed to the lounging cushions. The food was amazing—every meal showcasing Nepali cuisine from different regions— and we had our personal server, Sanjay, who was informative and very sweet. Everyone was exceptionally helpful, kind and delightful. We took two Jeep safaris (at extra cost from our package) but worth seeing a sloth bear and two many rhinos to count, a vast variety of birds and plants with excellent descriptions of flora and fauna from the guides. We enjoyed the boat ride, jungle walk and elephant bath. Note the drinks are an extra charge. Other disadvantages may be the distance to Sauraha, the tourist town with shopping, if one wanted to wander the town. You are definitely far from any tourist area here, which is the advantage of coming here. It’s quiet and isolated and there are very few other jeeps in this part of Chitwan.  We can’t recommend this jungle lodge any more highly and it’s hard to leave. Note temps in the 90-100’s in April. Rooms well air conditioned with all amenities, WiFi a little slow.

It wasn't easy to find but when we arrived there was a team of happy faces waiting by the front of the hotel for us. We had a refreshing drink and we're showed to our rooms. We had a private pool outside our room which over looked the jungle. A massive thank you Sanjay who was our private butler. Nothing was too much trouble. We even visited his village with him.The pool, food menu and safari trips were wonderful. This hotel is a credit to the family who own it. Amazing stay, we can't wait to return x

Our Room was close with a wonderful view of the river. All amenities that you could want was in the room. The room was clean and warm at nights. The bathroom nice and big with lots of space! We did the safari walk; safari drive and elephant back safari. They were all amazing with great guides taking us out each day. We saw many many Rhino; 2 leopard (mother and young) glimpse of a Tiger when tracking on foot; Big forest buffalo; large horn bills; sloth-bear tracks and scat; many types of antelope and many more birds. A big thank you to Marcus and Steph as-well as the Lodge staff and the specifically the safari guides for making our stay once in a lifetime experience! The guides were very informative and engaging, just the way we like it! Nikita you and your side kick (Suman just joking) were great! Thank you for the great team work and the special presentation.

This hotel consists of a centrally located lobby/ lounge area along with restaurant facilities and the large rooms are set off down paths and each one feels very private. Our room was beautiful and has hand painted walls throughout. We had a little private pool set out back for our use only. It overlooked the river and beyond that the safari area. The bathroom is down some steps from the bedroom and has a gorgeous inside shower and a separate tub but also has an enclosed yet outdoor shower attached to the bathroom. The staff was very nice and attentive.  The food was very good. They had a small gift shop.

You arrive at the Lodge after an hours bumpy ride from the airport to be greeted by the friendly staff stood on the steps offering freshening towels and a cool drink.  The main lodge is spacious with windows overlooking the large pool and sitting area down towards the river and across to the national park.  The individual bungalows are delightful with gorgeous views and an infinity plunge pool on the terrace.  The rooms are large and comfortable and the bathrooms huge with tub, separate shower and if you prefer an outside shower.  There is a heli pad for easier access if your pockets are plump!

We planned a trip to Meghauli Serai after reading about it on T+L. The drive from KTM to Meghauli took more than 8hrs on unpaved roads and it was only jet lag induced slumber that rescued us from the misery of the drive. Once at the hotel, the staff was very hospitable and attentive to details. The rooms are very well appointed with large bathrooms. I would rate the rooms better than some of the premium safaris of Africa.In terms of wildlife, we encountered fog in the mornings (not unusual at the Park) which generally cleared up around 8.30-9am. The early morning view of the fauna was limited but we still observed some active birdlife. Rhino, Deer and Gharial sightings were fairly common, we saw some interesting pug marks but did not make any tiger sightings.The resident naturalist, Nikita did an excellent job with her informed commentary on the local flora and fauna. Roshan, who was running the hotel ops during our visit, went out of the way to arrange a return flight to KTM instead of making us endure the return drive back to KTM. The food was very good, esp. the dinner with a strong local cuisine influence was a welcome change from the typical lodging fare. Overall, an excellent customer experience at Meghauli Serai. I hope the industry/local govt. does a better job of building approach roads/connectivity to KTM.

WOW.. what can I say about the wonderful hospitality. From the time we stepped into the hotel, we had  fabulous experiences. Most of the staff were at the Reception greeting us. Before reaching the resort, we were driven thru some very uneven roads and the journey was quite bad. I thought that we actually lost our way as there were no signages to the hotel. But when we arrived at the hotel, all our discomfort just disappeared. I brought along my in laws and parents who are in their 70s. They had the best moments of their lives. I was very impressed with the level of hospitality from all the staff. Special mention to Sanjay Mahato who took very good care of us. He ensured that he made my family happy and words can't describe the level of efforts that he took to take extra care of us. I loved the lemon grass drink that Sanjay makes and everyday, he gets some fresh lemon grass and prepared some chill drink for us... A MUST try...  I have never seen such hospitality in any parts of the world. The services were rendered so genuinely and they were very happy to provide the service. We will NEVER ever forget the hospitality that we received from Sanjay. Roshan from  F & B... was just superb. He went out of his way to ensure that we were well taken care in all aspects. The welcome drink... the hibiscus drink was too refreshing. He even shared with us how to do the drinks. He constantly checks on our well being and my parents and in laws just had a fabulous time. Another special mention to Chef Lekhraj Dangi. OMG.... the kind of cuisine that he came up with... completely mind blowing. We were well fed and loved his fresh baked brownies with ice cream... another must try. We were pampered so much at the hotel and felt as though it was our 2nd home. It is the 1st time in many many years that we felt very sad to leave the hotel. The River cruise by Varun was so well organized. Varun's patience, and humbleness was pure at heart. A great naturalist and he is always with a smile. EVERYONE in the hotel treat their customers as Gods. Special credits goes to the GMs to manage the resort. Watching the sun set during the river cruise was mesmerizing. After the river cruise, we were served snacks and drinks at the river banks. There was a SPA at the hotel and it was really nice to have SPA treatments there. Only feedback I would give is to also have a male therapist at the hotel. We also went for a village visit and because of the festive season, we celebrated with the villagers and it was just amazing to participate in their dances. That was the best moments. The hotel also hosted a Diwali dinner at the site and this was so special as it was organized outdoors. They organized representatives from the nearby village to perform some local dances. Overall the experience at Taj Meghauli was just TOO GOOD. I will definitely return again just to experience the hospitality, serenity, peace and happiness. Well done to the entire staff of Taj Meghauli. We miss all of you!!!!

Meghauli Serai's welcome and service are second to none in Asia.  This is a fantastic place to spend a few nights enjoying safari in Nepal.Accommodation is great.  Food is absolutely fantastic - the chef produced lovely Nepalese food, and there's a staple selection of pizza, pasta and other favourites if the kids prefer.The safari and wildlife options offer something for everybody, from elephant rides, small boat tours, jungle walks, jungle drives, village walks and elephant bathing.  Lots of animals to spot including rhino, crocodiles and the chance of a Bengal tiger.  Suman, Varun and Bhuddi were fantastic guides on these outings.The whole team were extremely welcoming from the moment we arrived at Bharatpur through to checking us in at the airport on the way back.  Meal times were flexible (great for families), and there was always a selection of safari tours and activities for kids.  The lodge has a lovely pool overlooking the river.  It's the perfect place to enjoy a drink and watch the elephants and rhino.Steph and Markus, the management at Meghauli Serai, are always around and keen to help with arrangements and ensure guests are having a great time.  Really attentive restaurant and pool service (thanks Sanjay!). Nothing was too much trouble for the team.Highly recommended.

Truly one of a kind personal service, the staff and team were super friendly and helpful from the moment we walked in the hotel to the moment we left. You can never go wrong with this choice, Wonderful safari experiences and activities. The pool vila is definitely recommend. Will come back one day.

The combination of perfect room, caring and competent staff, delicious food, and wonderful wilderness adventure, made our stay here "top notch in every way!"  The room is truly reflective of being with nature, but in a most luxurious manner.  From our room's outdoor shower option, private outdoor mini-pool, view of the Rapti River and adjacent jungle, to the comfy bed and large bathroom with shower and much appreciated separate tub, the room was beyond our expectation!  More importantly, ALL the staff here were super nice and sincerely caring, in addition to being expert in their area.  The restaurant staff offered a delicious variety of food, served in an attentive and friendly manner.  Expert naturalists provided plenty of insight as we participated in elephant safari, jeep safari, and river float experiences.  I can't say enough positive things about our stay here.  Truly, the staff makes this place a very desirable place to be!  You will love it!

This place is right in the midst of wilderness...the sot out area houses an infinity pool which offers ans amazing jungle view Staff is extremely helpful and Always Willing to offer suggestions to make your holiday even more memorable The safaris organised by them are par excellence Food quality deserves a 5star too

The 5* reviews received are very much deserved. As one approaches the Location one recognises the Lodge is a very special place beautifully in tune with its stunning surroundings in every way The facilities on offer are top notch ; the fixtures fittings,furniture and decor in rooms and public areas are so thoughtfully displayed and just right . The food is truly to die for, plentiful - a work of art in many cases but equally delicious. The infinity pool is stunning and fits in with its surroundings as it looks out onto the countryside and the river. The staff are attentive but not intrusive, informative and reflect enthusiasm and knowledge. The trips down the river and into the jungle were delivered professionally and we were rewarded by many rhino sightings and even a wild elephant which caused staff guests and locals alike much excitement. Our guide Dipsy ( Deepkul) was wonderfully cheery helpful and a joy to be around. Thoroughly recommend Meghauli Serai to everyone.

We were celebrating our 10th Wedding Anniversary @ Meghauli Serai, and looking at the reviews posted here I had hoped for an amazing experience, but, the amazing staff and people at the resort exceeded all our expectations and went beyond to make this an unforgettable experience.
