Very nice hotel, I enjoy staying there fives days delicious food ,good architectural design, nice view to the valley ,staff are very helpful and friendly ,moona in the front disc she is really nice and very helpful  and  also the the boy working with hear forget his name. Deep and Divya working in the bar are exclint also. And acutely all the staff are very friendly. Really enjoyed it and will come again to this hotel.

Good: sound proof room (even if you play the music loud the other room won't be able to hear it, swimming pool, the staff were friendly, amazing view, really good location.There is mini fridge in all the rooms that we booked. Some of the rooms are really spacious.Bad: the food was horrible (Tip: if you can avoid having lunch and dinner please do so, there is a nearby restaurant that have thakali which is way better, breakfast was good though), swimming pool was not that big (if there are about 7-10 people in the pool it would feel as crowded), don't go during june/july if you want to get the view of mountain i guess the better time would be in september or november.

This hotel is built on the side of  steep hill and has a number of serious safety issues caused by the considerable number of stairways and passages in the building.Firstly, the electrical supply in Nepal is a bit unreliable so power outages are common.We were there for 2 nights and there were cuts on both of them. If you are in one of the bars or the restaurant the staff will set up battery powered lights but there is no backup lighting in any of the stairwells or corridors. When the power goes off these areas are left in total darkness. We raised this with the management and they seems unconcerned.Secondly, we identified at least one place in the hotel where it would be possible for smaller children to fall from one floor to the next.In addition to these concerns about safety we were also unimpressed with the level of service.The bedside light in our room didn't work and a maintenance person looked at them but couldn't fix them. On a couple of occasions, the staff were more interested in watching football on the TV than they were in serving the customers.This hotel is in a stunning location and with a bit of effort from the management it could be excellent, they need to get their act together.

My sisters and I stayed here for a few days over Thanksgiving and were so impressed by the very warm and attentive staff, and naturally, the incredible views!!! As noted by other reviews, the ride from Kathmandu is a bit aggressive/bumpy and you have to pay 2 tolls, but we also consider the help our money can provide to the country and it's people (esp since the earthquake) and we are happy to support! (300 rupee per person). We chose to spend our time in Nagarkot enjoying the resort and it's facilities and it will always be an incredibly special memory for us!!! It's a great place to relax, unwind, and take in the irreplaceable beauty of Nepal and the Himalayas!!

Spend a night in a big hole bedsheet that was tuck in to deceive guest, late check-in almost waited for 40 mins, too many bugs inside the room may be because of surrounding, unpleasant smell like water sewage (our room was located near the main walking passage), cobwebs in room and balcony p.s strongly suggest to have an in-room inspection and do a deep clean. Paying around $140 per night (BB plan) was totally not worthy, too expensive for unpleasant stay.Never visiting and recommending this hotel again, what you pay is not worthy. Hotel location is fine but not better than Country Villa or Club Himalaya. First and last visit from us. Thank you!

At the end of a days trek, this place is a haven ! Huge and sprawling over many levels, it has been built into the side of the mountain with every room facing the mountain range and valley. Useable balconies are a blessing, and the dining area is lovely ! The several levels also meant that we were not disturbed while an offsite was in progress. The rooms are very comfortable, and the toilets, though small, spotless and well fitted out. The Nepali massage with mustard oil in the little spa was a treat !The staff was sensitive and considerate and happy, which also spoke volumes about how the place is run. Thank you for a lovely stay !

We stayed couple night at this magnificent hotel and we fall in love with this place. Location is fabulous on the top of the hill and we can see beautiful scenery for 100s of kilometers. Sunset and sunrise is wonderful as well. Friendly staffs and were very helpful, Rooms are nice and cozy. Food was very good specially buffet dinner and breakfast.I would highly recommend this place, you will love it.

The place like heaven and the service was excellent. All the staff are very friendly and helpful. Food are delicious we would like to thank you all the chef for the excellent food with presentation. Room was very nice with natural view. we would like to thank to all the staff specially to Mr. Ajay for his effort.

The place like its name has an aura of mystery surrounding it (May be it is the feeling of being on the top of the clouds, like in a forbidden kingdom). The near perfect ambient impressed me a lot and wonderful staff providing excellent service were always present at call. Also, the food served at the Hotel is wonderfully scrumptious. I found the place a perfect getaway for some quiet "me time" or for some fun time with family and friends, the place caters for both.

Wow. We swam above the cloud at 7200 ft. above the sea level.  We were group of 6 friends and we stayed one night at Hotel Mystic Mountain. This is recently opened new property at Nagarkot with latest modern amenities.  The hotel structure is amazing and it has peaceful ambiance where one can enjoy nature and peaceful environment.

Overlooking the valley beyond, Mystic Mountain has the perfect mixture of modern luxury and healing nature. Guests will be able to enjoy best of amenities and services on the nature's lap. The Hotel gives the perfect blend of luxurious service to be pampered with also to get closer to the nature through nature walks, hiking and other adventurous activities.Odyssey will pamper you with a fine-dining experience. For the gastronomist of food, it is the best destination. The restaurant offers exclusively selected varieties of delicacies. The Bill of fare at Odyssey offers a fusion of vegetarian and non-vegetarian cuisines handpicked by our Award winning Chef and his dedicated team.

Firstly, I’ve noticed that a number of the previous five star reviews are from under five contributors I.e I suspect these are mostly fake. We actually booked time here on the strength of previous reviews and in hindsight, I should have done a bit more due diligence. Just to be aware that the roads on the way to the hotel are pretty poorThe Good+ great views on clear days+ Nice hot showers with good pressureThe Bad- staff lacking training, giving out incorrect information on services or nobody answering the phones- The TV selection is quite glitchy and mostly unwatchable - Staff entering rooms without knocking - Very noisy extractor in the bathroom - some noisy construction close by ruining the serenityThe Ugly- the room and bathroom needs a complete renovation. You can see mold buildup which is quite dangerous - The breakfast buffet is quite poor with bland flavours and low quality ingredients - The overall food is both expensive and poor quality- Charges for self guided hikes. I mean really…- The room heating is quite bad in winter. Your choice is an aircon unit blowing hot air - Leaky bathroom sink splashing water on your feet

This hotel is in a beautiful location, and the vision for it is awesome. After a day trip we returned for a family overnight stay that was quite terrible. Why? Pls read below before you book this expensive hotel:(1) There was an extremely loud group of visitors that dominated the ambience, making it very unpleasant for other guests. None of the hotel staff could control the crowd that was obnoxious — this group checked in early the day before and wouldn’t leave rooms two hours past checkout time. WE COULD NOT CHECK IN on time because of this group’s actions. They also left the rooms filthy dirty. Despite paying steep room fees we couldn’t rahe a nap that my mom wanted.(2) The jacuzzi area was so loud with Tiktok user’s music. Given the mountainous location, the music and obnoxiously loud TikTok crowd could be heard INSIDE our rooms. I tried to run away from the hooliganism, but it was impossible. IF YOU WANT TO HANG OUT WITH VERY LOUD and RUDE TikTok crowd, this is the right hotel for you.(3) Hotel staff was polite, but very inexperienced all around.(4) Despite signs in the pool area, people were not wearing proper swimming costumes (non-cotton clothes) in the Jacuzzi and the pool; they were swimming with the gym clothes and regular cotton dresses, making the water disgusting and dirty. For this reason, we were unable to use the Jacuzzi and the pool, in addition to crowds staying in jacuzzi for 3-4 hours at a time. To sum up, our overnight stay was a major disappointment. If the hotel wishes to attract customers and revenue that match the location, they need major service improvements and an ability to enforce rules around service and comfort for ALL paying customers, not just obnoxious TikTok crowd.

Myself and my partner visited for one night in Feb 23.  We were planning to have a good end to our holiday, and decided to splash out a little for our last night.  The hotel itself is of a reasonable standard, and in good weather would have excellent views.  We ate lunch and dinner here, which was the only food we consumed that day.  Against my better judgement, we had the buffet for dinner.  The food was of an acceptable standard.  My thoughts about food hygiene were raised when I saw one of the chefs cooking out in the restaurant, mixing raw and cooked poultry - clearly a no go!  That night, my partner came down with a severe bout of food poisoning.  As a result, we didn't sleep and spent all night vomiting.  Whilst these sort of things happen, the actions from the hotel are disgusting.  I spoke to the manager the following morning and explained the problem, and that neither of us were happy to take breakfast in the restaurant.  I asked the manager to go and review our bill to see what could be done to rectify it, especially on the basis of a poor night's sleep and feeling sick for 2 hours in a taxi back to Kathmandu.  A few hours later, they returned with a bill which I still didn't find acceptable.  I was able to speak to the owner on the telephone and explained the situation to him.  The owner stated that if the staff "didn't collect the bill", they would have it deducted from their wages - a truly disgusting practice.  We discussed the bill further and stated we were happy to pay for the facilities we enjoyed the use of, but a 20% discount was not acceptable.  As we then tried to leave, the staff became very aggressive, threating to lock us on the premises until we paid.  In the end we had no option but to settle the bill.Such a shame to end our last day of what has been a brilliant trip.

This hotel is located in a very peaceful and secluded place... Rooms are valley facing and have stunning views with blue sky, clouds, snowy mountains, green valley... sitting in balcony was real fun...Rooms here are luxurious... Food it tasty and there are multiple options available... Overall at a bit pricey side however worth to stay due to its excellent location and views...

Excellent views, excellent room, clean and functional facilities.  In such a country that Mystic Mountain Hotel was able to meet such standards - i would say Hats Off o Them !The buffet breakfast and dinner are excellent.   Compliment must go to Chef Pramod who leads his FnB Team.   The quality of food i was surprised - was to respectable standard.   Not forgetting Iwor from front office and the rest of the service staff.   Excellent service.

The ride from Kathmandu can be quite rough but that's a small price to pay for what's waiting for you at the hotel.  The location of the hotel allows it to have truly remarkable views.  Even more remarkable is the level of amenities and facilities that are available at this remote location.  Breakfast is great, heating is great, and all expected facilities work as expected.  Our rooms were big and one of the rooms had a huge balcony.  We stayed just one night but had a great time and really couldn't be happier.

We went with friends. It was nice stay. The interior and the villa designs are very nice. Can view the sunrise direct from the room. Cudn't use pool as some function were going on. Nice food and buffet was heavy. It was a beautiful stay.

I don't understand how this hotel can be travelers ranked #1 for Nagarkot.  There is a serious lack of attention to detail and maintenance.  It does not feel like a 4 star hotel.  I just came back from a 10 days trip in Nepal from Hong Kong, me and my friends stayed at Mystic Mountain for 1 night. We were attracted by the hotel location and the view, and the infinity pool...however, don't be fooled: Pros: Great location high up.Cons: The road to the hotel is very poor, be prepared to be car sick.  Maintenance at the hotel is an issue, things are pretty run down.  The hotel operations has serious flaws/issues...you can see mattresses/mattress covers in the hallway, the balcony in the rooms are great, but when you look down, it's the view of mops, brooms, hanging towels.  The water in the pool is stagnant (so it gets murky).  Food is not great...stick to Nepalese choices.I would not recommend to stay here, there are better options...in fact, there is no need to go to Nagarkot if you plan to go to Pokhara.Suggestion for the hotel: focus on the details and improve maintenance.  The hotel has a lot of potential.

It's an amazing place to be. Mystic Mountain was the perfect place for our hiatus from work. Really amazing service and all around good management. The environment and ambience was one of the most beautiful things I've ever experienced. I can't put into words how great this place is, especially for people looking for a break from the city life. Super worth it! Loved the way it looks after the satisfaction of its guests and treats them as an asset. My words wouldn't suffice to thank the service they offered us at the hotel. Upon our reach at the hotel they gave us a pleasant surprise that our normal bookings were upgraded to  EXECUTIVE DELUXE SUIT, WOW WOW WOW! We were thrilled to get this villa as a surprise 😍😍 We were hopping and jumping around with excitement after having a look at the room. It was a Royal Treat for us ! Thank you Hotel Mystic Mountain for everything 😍 I will definitely visit again and again at your place. And would like to suggest everyone to visit once at this place , I bet you will not feel like leaving the place . Best use of my time and money 😍

I stayed two nights at Mystic Mountain and it is indeed mystically once the fog rises and the peaks of the mountins can be seen from you terrace. This is the huge plus of the hotel: the views. Otherwise it is too big for my personal taste and there is not much love to details in the interior of the rooms and they look also a bit run down already. Breakfast is quite mediocre and the breakfast room is very busy and lacks any charme. The restaurant food however was very good though a bit pricy as well as the drinks. Nothing to complain about the staff and due to the fantastic views down the hills and to the mountains, it is probably the best option in Nagarkot

Great stay ! Amazing views !Loved open air jacuzzi. Breakfast spread was good. The rooms are spacious. Very relaxing location. Only drawback was that the road from Kathmandu to Nagarkot was in bad condition.

We spent a week in Nepal. While Pokhara wasGreat we were pleasantly surprised with the visit to Nagarkot . A short 40 min drive from Kathmandu airport takes you up to 7200 feet . Must stay at the Mystic mountain hotel . It’s only when you get there and see the breath taking view that you correlate the name of the hotel.A must do for a one night stay 😊

Stayed for 4 nights in June 2019. Room was fantastic with a great view of the Mt. Everest. The Sun rise from the balcony is awesome. Breakfast was plentiful with a good selection. We ate in the restaurant every night, there was a varied menu and the food was excellent. Lots to do in the area a 2-3 hours hiking to the Nagarkot Tower is a must as is table tennis, Nepali massage and relaxing in Jacuzzi and swimming pool in this beautiful Mystic mountain. The staff speak English and are very polite and helpful. Sunita from the reservation team helped me to guide about logistics before arriving the property which is really useful. The rooms including bathroom are spotless and relaxing. The architecture and interior are amazing and can easily make you feel happy. I can only suggest to put a pump in the swimming pool to ensure clean water. This is the best hotel on our Nepal trip. We don't stay at real high dollar places but we are not real cheap either. We would definitely recommend this hotel.

A surprising find!Expected a lot less and the place delivered a lot more. Great rooms which all come with a balcony and a view of the ranges. There's nothing to do outside of the hotel, as such.The room was clean. The bathroom was small but clean. Food at the hotel can be improved.I would recommend this property for those visiting Nagarkot.

Positive: Really nice mountain view, welcoming staff, proper dining.Negative: Swimming pool isn't heated, fitness center wasn't maintained, water bottle was empty, expensive hotel for the services offered.

Nothing beats the location and the weather of this place. Because we went in april the view to the mountains was also unobstructed by the clouds.Hospitality was upto the mark and Mr Rohit Sharma gave us a discount on our food also as we had to leave a day early.I recommend it to everyone to come and have a stay here !

It’s located in an isolated spot, and once you are there, there is absolutely nothing to do.So great for those who want to do nothing. You are only limited to what the hotel has to offer.Food was average at best, room less than average.Here are a few tips for the management, refresh the items at breakfast, you can’t have the same salad and cheese platters from the night before. I am not saying waste food, these should be kept away and then reserved if they are still safe to eat. When you see the exact same display with the same exact setting. It shows it was left as is.Rooms should be checked for defects before guests check in, ours had a water problem and a leaky shower head. The shower head was fixed, the water issue wasn’t.We were offered an alternative room, but since we had decided to check out the very next day, we cut our trip short to just one night,  didn’t warrant the hassle for all involved. The reasons for shortening our stay were multiple, no view due to the mist, no activities (all yoga, meditation etc activities were cancelled), so there was really nothing worth staying back for. Rohit Sharma the new manager had just taken over the day we arrived and he seemed like someone with the potential to turn this property around.Here’s hoping it improves, will be watching the ratings and comments closely. Rohit, best of luck to you, it was a pleasure meeting you.

Great view. Unique and impressive architecture. Nice, comfortable and spacious rooms. Food was amazingly tasty and lots of variety.  Very hospitable staffs and great service. Not a single complaint. In one word- “WOW”!

Last weekend we had organized a beautiful night away for us in Nargakot. As this was our first wedding anniversary, we chose for us to stay at Mystic Mountain as we had heard many good things. To ensure our stay went smoothly, we had been in touch with the hotel 1 month earlier to confirm our requests prior to the trip.Unfortunately, we were very disappointed regarding some other major issues. Firstly, the room (no. 112) allocated to us was on the ground floor and directly next to the fitness room. This was very frustrating as we were woken up at 6am by people using the fitness room (we could hear conversations, dropping of weights and the treadmill when operating) and other gym users talking directly in front of our room where a small public courtyard is located. Our plan to sleep in and enjoy the room was ruined and we were forced to leave our room before 7am to escape the noise. Secondly, the bed sheets had obviously not been changed. When we were about to get into bed, we noticed dirty marks and hair all over the existing bed sheets. At 9.30pm approximately, we had to call room service to come and change the sheets for us. In the morning, there was also a terrible smell coming from the bathroom (sewage leakage smell). Finally, the wifi in our room was not working and we were also required to call for maintenance to fix this issue. We did ask for a room change but were told that this would not be possible.  This experience truly impacted our first wedding anniversary and we are both deeply disappointed. We would also like to add that given the cost to stay at Mystic Mountain, we would have expected a much nicer experience.Our reference of Mystic Mountain to our friends and colleagues in Kathmandu and abroad will definitely reflect the experience we shared above and we will most likely not return there for future holidays

After visiting Changu Narayan on 5th Nov . we moved to Hotel Mystic  Mountain on top of quaint village Baluwapati , Nagarkot . The road from Changu Narayan to the hotel was winding around the hills lush with greenery provided by Chilaune ,  Fern ,  Katus , Kafal  ,  Oak ,  Pine ,  Salla ,  Uttis  , etc .   trees . We could see the snow capped Ganesh H IV  , 7102 m ; Ganesh H II , 7150 m ; Ganesh H V , 6950 m ; Ganesh H I , 7408 m ; Langtang , 7246 m ; Gang Chhenpu , 6297 m ; Sisa Pangma , 8013 m ;  Gur Karpori , 6874 m ; Dorje Lhakpa , 6799 m and Phurbi Chyachu , 6722 m along the left side of the road . Hotel Mystic Mountain nestled itself amidst the dense greenery at a very strategic point at a commanding elevation to supervise the Langtang range , Jugal Himal range , Rolwaling range , Everest range and Numbur range . \The hotel had Deluxe Rooms ( US $ 100 – 150 / night without meals )  ,  Super Deluxe Rooms ( US $ 140 / night without meals )  and Executive Suites ( US $ 345 / night without meals ) .   Every room had a balcony terrace facilitating the guests  to enjoy the majestic view of the magnificent snow capped peaks of  Langtang ; Gang Chhenpu ; Sisa Pangma ;  Gur Karpori ; Dorje Lhakpa  ; Phurbi Chyachu  ; Khazane Tippa  , 5647 m ; Choba Bhamare , 5970 m ; Cho Oyu , 8153 m ; Gauri Shankar , 7145 m ; Melungtse , 7181 m ; Lindartsubugo , 6690 m ; Mt Everest , 8848 m ; Chobutse , 6660 m ; Takargo , 6782 m ; Dongiragitao , 6940 m ; Numbur , 6945 m and Karyolung , 6681 m  while  having the sunbath . Alongwith the mountains we had a relaxed panoramic view of themisty clouds ,  surrounding hills , terraced fields and winding roads .Our spacious Deluxe Room had the world class amenities . It had two flat screen TVs . One in the sitting area and another in the sleeping area .  Funny thing about them was , when I would put off one TV another would automatically start . I had to struggle a bit to overcome this problem .  There was a small swimming pool flanked by two baby pools . I dared to dip in it  just for a moment after the sunrise . A small Gym was also available to the guests . Odyssy Restaurant on the sixth floor was a fantastic foody joint . I would like to review it separately . There was a coffee bar too .All the supporting staff was very polite and well mannered . This was the numero uno hotel at Nagarkot .

When I first saw the pictures of Hotel Mystic Mountain, I was instantly drawn towards the infinity pool and the stunning view the hotel had to offer and i could not wait to go there. So, we planned to go there for the weekend and when we reached there, it was exactly like how i had imagined it to be. 'Stunning' does not justify the beauty and the ambiance the hotel has to offer, it is so much more than that. Everything about Hotel Mystic Mountain is just so majestic right from the view, the hospitality, the Infinity pool et al. The aura of the entire place makes one feel truly blissful. I would recommend this place to everyone, and visiting it once is not enough

First of all we had to pay TAX twice coming up to the hotel. Concierge found this funny, we didn't. But we relaxed soon in our beautiful room...the view is worth driving up on a very steep, scary and wobbly road.The food was excellent and the staff is very attentive and friendly. It was very cold at that time of the year and the heating in the room hardly worked and there was no heating anywhere else. People went with winter jackets for dinner.With all my heart I can recommend a Reiki session with Ekant

We had a terrific stay and will be back.  The price is reasonable, the facilities are good, the views are incredible, and the customer service is the best.  We were beyond impressed by Shankar, Ramita, and Binesh, who all helped us greatly.  In fact, it was the best service we have experienced in Nepal and we live here!  Our rate included meals and the food was good and with a large variety.  The trip from Kathmandu is bumpy but took only an hour.  Easy to do a one night stay and back, but you will probably want to stay as long as possible.  Thank you Hotel Mystic Mountain!!

Simply one word to describe our stay. DISAPPOINTING! We had booked 4 deluxe rooms in advance and 1 additional room after midnight; checked in on 4th Oct and checked out on 5th Oct.There was no issue with check in, we were pretty much engrossed with the interior and tired from the long drive from Kathmandu. On that night, after a pretty unsatisfying dinner we were gathered at one of our friends’ room with some music on, chatting and drinking. Around 10.30pm we heard loud banging on our room’s wall from our neighboring room. So we lowered the volume thinking it might have disturbed them and they were sending a ‘message’ to convey that, but the next moment we received a call from the reception asking us to shut down the whole music. We were taken aback as we didn’t think we were making a huge ruckus to be told to do so, it had only stuck 11pm.  The staff tried to reason with us saying that the neighboring guests were complaining, and also that we were given a deluxe room with a much spacious balcony as if it was a complimentary; when in fact we chose that room with the understanding that the room’s rate is much higher and ready to pay for. We could have been out in the open and doing the same thing but we chose to stay indoor so as not to disturb other guests.The issue was not because we were told to shut down and stop with the fun; but the way that the situation was dealt with and what was said. We felt as though as domestic/local travelers, our value was lesser than those of international travelers. Maybe the employee was not implying that, but the damage was already done. The next morning during check out, we were received at the front office with much chilly vibe from the staff. We were not asked how our stay went and if there were any issues. The surprising thing was that they were not wearing any name tag with their designation; which should be part of the uniform and also for accountability purposes. After sorting out the bill and payment, the reception received a message from housekeeping saying that 2 glasses were broken in 2 of the rooms; 1 wine glass and 1 washroom water glass. Both were accidental cases and we accepted that fact. BUT the worst thing that could be done was to charge Nrs. 1000 for those glasses. I just thought that was ridiculous, we are aware that all hotels have damage and breakage policy, but the charge of 500 per glass just seemed ridiculous and unreasonable as we knew how much it would have cost. We had already racked up a bill of 75000 so it was not a matter of having the ability to pay or not but the ethics of it. I said to one of the front office employees if those glasses included VAT and Service Charge; which by the way was a sarcastic and rhetorical question, to my amazement he nonchalantly nodded with a smiled. Despite the negative reaction from us,we felt reasoning with them would be a waste so we felt compelled to pay for it. We did not see or experience any competitive advantage in this hotel and many things were not up to par.Room (504):- Room was spacious with good sized balcony but bathroom was too cramped- no bathrobe/dressing gown- weighing machine was out of order- no vanity mirror on the wall or desk- bedroom slipper was a rubber flip flop- Bathroom floor towel was mixed up with the face and shower towel; only to find it next morning by that time bathroom floor was severely wet- sliding bathroom door seems quite hazardous as it only have the guide at the top and the bottom is left hanging when you try to open the door after closing it goes out of place and bangs the closet on the side- sliding bathroom door was filled with dust and whitish mold- room had the moldy smell when we entered; despite knowing the fact that hotel is situated at a height of 2160 meter, mold is inevitable due to the chilly weather but prevention should have been in place- washroom jet spray’s pressure was too strong (Room No. 504) Food:- given that most guests we saw in the restaurant were East Asian and meal plan are prepared as per bookings/occupancy, the dinner buffet consisted of plain rice and pasta with sauce which made no sense as 9 Pax (our group) were nepali and plain rice needed an accompaniment with lentil(dahl) or any type of gravy item.- Desert was alright as they had sewahi, fruits, mousse and cake- Breakfast was similar, it was pretty limited for vegetarians. The stir fried noodle was burnt at the bottom of the chafing dish.- Buffet dinner and breakfast were not up to par with the rate but F&B staffs were quite polite and efficientOverall our experience as per our expectation it was utterly disappointing, to be honest we received so many queries through social media from our friends in Nepal and abroad about the hotel but we could not put forth much positive feedback besides the view; which goes without saying. Most of us belong to the hospitality/service industry and understand it is inevitable to satisfy and accommodate the needs of every guests/customers but courtesy goes a long way just a smile goes a long way and to only depend on the location/view would be detrimental to the hotel’s image. This was our first and definitely last time in Mystic Mountain; we have been to other similar standard hotels in Nagarkot and could not help comparing against so many aspects on our way back home.

All i want is to relax, rejuvenate, recharge and spend Me time alone when i planned my trip to Nagarkot - Nepal. When choosing a hotel, i always consider peoples review. But i never imagine staff of this hotel will go extra miles just to make their guest very happy and satisfied.Kudos to all the staff who are very nice, helpful, jolly, friendly and accommodating especially to Moona and Bijay who became my instant friends.You made my birthday extra special for doing something beyond your duties. Thank you guys for everything and the memories.In general its exceeded my expectation, from the upgraded big room, comfy bed, huge balconies, awesome and breathtaking panoramic views of Himalayan mountains, food, facility and most of all the friendly staff. Hope to visit you again some day.

Went there is friends for lunch. The view from the hotel is breathtaking. The ambience is very good. At times the clouds are floating below you. The staff are warm and friendly. The Resident Manager, Umesh Thapa took time to sit with us and speak about the hotel and all the facilities available. A very friendly and affable person. Definitely on our bucket list the next time we are in Nepal.

Mistic mountain Plus points Very beautifulAt top of hillAmazing view of HimalayasGood size roomsBeautiful roomsThey have Pool and JacuzziBut these  were not operational during our stay .no one informed us beforehand .Minus Poor availability of hot waterVery limited veg food options.v far from market so one is forced to eat hereToo overpriced for everything plus huge taxes Staff not v friendly .just doing their job no personal touch Spa overpriced underequipped Washroom has some wierd smell We chked in v late ( 5 hrs late )due to long drive and bad roads  . Were v tired .requested the manager for a room upgrade if possible but was denied.We were v tired. Tht night  our room 131 ac broke down znd threw up lots of water at 12 30 am soaking our bags and camera and mobile etc . No hot water at night .no hot water next morning too .so we complained.Finally we were given a new upgraded room ( too late )A gold facial cost 3000 plus almost 25 percent tax . Included just some v basic cream massage .and pack no steam Can avoid .Buffet lunch and dinner costs 1800 plus almost 25 percent  tax Overpriced for vegetarians atleast with very limited food choices.Food is understood bec the hotel is located atop hill so difficulty of supplies . But no hot water and staff indifference puts you off  for the rates they charge .

Stayed a weekend here this February, getting away from work and hectic Kathmandu. It was indeed time well spent! The hotel is set away from Nagarkot town and the road to get there isn't too well made. But once reaching the place, it felt so peaceful. And the view of the mountains was really breathtaking! Rooms are nicely done, spacious and comfortable; bathrooms are also clean with all modern fittings. Our rooms were located away from the main building and that added to the peace and isolation. A good rest, after long hikes through the surrounding villages.Well trained staff; they stand out in comparison to service in most other places in the area! The food was really good, with a significant buffet spread. One of our orders were somewhat delayed, but we put that down to communication hassles! Once sorted out, we were quickly served. Extra service such as late checkout times were also very helpful for us. A very relaxing weekend altogether; will certainly be going back!

Mind boggling location, with superb contemporary architecture at Hotel Mystic Mountain offering exclusive experience to witness the first Ray of the sun as it rises up to glow the snow clad mountain range that faces every room perched on this beautiful valley to transcend you to a Heaven that is above all Heavens.Speaking with the resort manager was quite fascinating. Just a small addendum to make the resort more professional to hotel industry standards and introduce indulging sports to add bigger value to the already magnificent place.

I astonished when I first seen this resort in the afternoon. View the the reception lobby is just wow and I just rushed to the view point open air large well decorated  balcony to enjoy the mountains and greenery.  Before entering the room,  I just mark the resort as 5 star at my first impression.  Large well decorated  rooms with all facilities and balcony viewing mountains is just beyond description.  Earlier I was checking resorts like this and now I am in such resort. Restaurants with balcony,  large badminton court,  swimming pool with viewing mountains,  the open spaces the pavements all makes this resort a well deserved review and thanks.  We have stayed only one night and I regret that.   See you soon Mystic Mountain

We had a great pleasure of staying in this property. Not too far away from Kathmandu valley, this location is peaceful. Waking up with the magnificent views of mountain ranges in a very clean and spacious room can't get any better. I cant wait to go back to this place again.

Well this is the best boutique hotel newly made in a hill side nearby Kathmandu. Its apps an hour thirty minutes drive from the capital. Hotel is just opened this August and is beautifully made. Went there for lunch with friends and family. As I entered the place I fell in love with the property. The view from the rooms, dining , lobby , swimming is so so beautiful. Service and food quality is good too.A visit to this place is must if a person is going Nagarkot. I would highly recommend this place for a night to all honeymooners.Thank you for coming up with such a beautiful property.

The location, the reasonably big rooms, the ambiance all make it a wonderful experience.Sadly the hotel is not yet fully ready.The lifts were not working.Hot water was not proper, and restaurant not on the full preparation.As the rooms are on various levels, proper signs should be put to reach  locations easilyHowever once these hiccups are over it would be an ideal place to stay.

Check-in time was 2PM but had to wait an hour. (Didn't knew this was just a beginning).  After visiting my room I found it worst. Can’t believe 4-star hotel would be in this condition. Bad smell, dusty rooms, grimy switches, dirty windows with dead insects. I booked triple deluxe room but they booked double deluxe instead. They didn't bother to communicate as well and the explanation was they cannot do anything beside adding one extra bed. Maintenance is so bad - empty soap dispenser, broken gym equipments etc. Dinning hall's aisles are narrow, difficult to walk around. You will find huge food menu but taste is no different from other regular good hotels. I don’t recommended this 4-star hotel because of the unprofessional behavior. Add some $$ and you will find other great hotels or go for 3 star hotels. My bad, I didn't went through the reviews. The weekend was ruined.

I decided to swerve the madness of the city after arriving in Nepal and head into the Kathmandu Valley for a few days instead. Hotel Mystic Mountain on the outskirts of Nagarkot was my base, and it was perfect for exploring the surrounding area. Airport pick-up made life much easier (4000Rps each way).It was also a really nice hotel, with a decent bar and restaurant. All my meals were excellent, and the buffet breakfast was ample. Wi-Fi was good enough, although it often dropped out and it was usually better when moving from one network to another. A bit of a faff but bearable.A good proportion of their guests seem to be middle class Nepalis from the capital, and it was a bit crazy when I arrived on a Saturday afternoon. Kids running around, live music, mayhem in the pool…but it was entertaining. People seem to stay 1-2 nts, so I was classed a ‘long stay guest’ by a couple of staff. At check in they gave me an upgrade to a nice room with a huge balcony. The room was very comfortable, but I’d have loved to have a bath after a long day hiking. And it needs some bedside lamps - there’s lots of lights and switches but no combination which works for reading after dark. Similarly, the bathroom has a few lights but there’s a dark spot where you need it most in front of the mirror!All the rooms have killer views of the valley, although unfortunately March isn’t the best time of year for sunrise - it’s too misty. But once the sun was up - wow! Apart from the views, the sky was teeming with sparrow hawks, steppe eagles and vultures - I’m not a twitcher so I had to Google to identify them.I used the spa for massage, steam room and sauna - all good.The staff in particular were great. Always helpful, polite and chatty. One of them even brought me home from a hike on his motorbike as my transport options were too sketchy.

We stayed for just two nights, wished that we stayed longer. Superbly located with ever ending views of valleys, rice fields and Himalaya ranges, simply breathtaking. Very modern rooms are spacious and well designed with all amenities and gorgeous views from your balcony. Good food and Great Service complimented hotel, amenities, and views.

Parts of the road to the hotel are poor and need maintenance.  However, when you reach the hotel, it is all worth it. This place must have one of the best views in the world.  The rooms and grounds are spacious and spotlessly clean. The hotel staff are very helpful: on the last day we had a problem with our taxi which failed to turn up. The reception staff sorted everything out and also made sure we had plenty of free tea and coffee whilst we waited for the car to arrive. The location is great for walking and we hiked to the viewpoint and the local village.The picture shows our balcony which was huge and had the most amazing views. Thank you, Mystic Mountain, for a great stay.

The road up the mountain to the hotel is rough and the ride is slow and bumby.  And finally you arrive at the hotel that seems so out of place.  The hotel has spectacular views of the valley below, and when the clouds allow you can see the snow capped Himalayas.  All the rooms face the Himalayas as do the restaurant, bar, and lounge area.  The room we had was spacious, clean, and well appointed, and had a nice balcony with a couple of chairs and a small table.  The internet worked surprisingly well.  Dinner at the restaurant there, and breakfast the next morning were good.  Would definitely stay there again, but next time would stay 2 nights to increase chances of seeing all of the snow capped mountains.

Modern, clean, quiet rooms, can sleep with sliding doors open to balcony.  But if it’s cloudy and you can’t see the mountains it’s a bit of a bummer. Staff is young and tries hard.  It’s heart warming to see them learning English and working hard to serve guests.  Buffet dinner was expansive given how difficult the logistics of getting food to a hill station is.  One server noted helpfully the fish was frozen which is what I would’ve expected anyway.  Breakfast left me wanting for muesli although nothing to complain about eggs made to order.  Note that this hotel is quite isolated.  $25 taxi into the town of Nagarkot market and return.  And there’s really nothing in town to see.

The resort is about 90 mins drive from kathmandu airport worth the travel the rooms are cosy ,very clean each rooms have balcony to get an amazing sunrise view ,we also stayed in their villa which has a separate jacuzzi, sauna and huge balcony to just relax and enjoy sunrise view where you can see the whole valley and lot of peaks . They have small bar with outside sitting and some really good food . The breakfast buffet was also delicious. Good place to stay over with family and friends and away from hush hush of city life. Loved the hospitality from all the staff they were very helpful and always smiling .will visit soon again .

We had booked one night at this hotel based on recommendation received. We were travelling from Pokhara to Kathmandu and unfortunately the flight was cancelled and since it was supposed to be our only night in nagarkot, we decided to take the bus route so we could atleast reach the hotel by the evening and spend the night. We reached kathmandu only by 930 pm and the hotel had arranged for a shuttle from the city. The shuttle pick up was kind enough to wait for us to arrive since we were originally scheduled to arrive in the morning and even went out of the way to pick us from where our bus dropped us. The hotel is around an hour and half from the the Kathmandu city and the roads are pretty much non existent. We were two girls travelling at around midnight but at no point did we feel unsafe while we climbed the mountainous road. Once we reached the hotel, the staff immediately made us comfortable considering our long ride. We ordered for room service which was good and in good quantities as well. The view of sunrise from this hotel is out of the world. Having travelled a long journey and on not so good roads- all this will be forgotten with the mesmerizing views of the clouds and the mountains from the room. The room we were given was an upgraded one and had a humongous balcony with a small table and chairs and One of those swing chairs. We were unfortunately there on a cloudy day- so by 7am you could no longer see the mountains but otherwise i have no words to describe the beauty of the place. Breakfast is very good and the place has a good crowd. There is not much to do in the area since it is located right at the top of the mountain and you would visit just to feel the place and absorb the views. While we did consider checking out a little late, we were told by the front desk that we should be checking out by the normal hotel check out time itself - so I assume they do not encourage late check outs. Otherwise, beautiful beautiful property and the only regret is that we spent such little time in the hotel. Oh and yes, they have the most amazing hot chocolate. Hotel chocolate on the balcony with the view- best feeling ever!

Hotel Mystic Mountain has an awestruck architectural display amidst peaceful nature... spectacular view. They have exquisite taste of hospitality..staffs are pragmatic in response to any queries. In terms of food they serve exclusive palatable cuisines that really augments their merit list.  I had a great time and their growing popularity elucidates visiting Mystic Mountain is worthwhile...😁

Highly recommended hotel.  Traveling alone I have never felt lonely here. I had more than enough attention from the team. Somraj and Neroz were very kind and professional. Somraj even called to ask why I didn't come for breakfast 😊 Food was great! Breakfast options were different every morning.  My favourite appetizers are Prawn Chaila and Paneer Chilli. Rooms are well located with breath taking view from balcony, super clean and comfortable. Wi-Fi connection was great too. Spa was good with very professional massage therapist. This hotel will be always in my list in future! A small advice to bring alcohol with you as it's a bit expensive. Million thanks to the team and HR who picked the best people, creating a good atmosphere!

We came for lunch at Hotel Mystic Mountain. First impressions was not bad, we ordered food and drinks food was not up to standard, it looked unappetizing my sandwich had mold on that you could clearly see they tried to cut it off, and there are flies everywhere inside and outside the restaurant. I would not recommend this place to anyone.

This is the place for relaxing in the lap of nature / mountains. The property is very well maintained with great rooms, food and of course the very helpful staff. Did not expect much but my visit was just so satisfying and also the Sun rise view from the rooms balcony was just so mesmerizing.

A peaceful place with beautiful view of Mountains. The swimming pool is too small but big enough for relaxation. Nearby pool Jacuzzi is available. The restaurant is located in the 7th floor with beautiful Pano view of the himalayan mountain range. A must visit place nearby kathmandu, just an hour of drive.

This is my third time to Nagarkot - the previous 2 times I have stayed with smaller family run hotels but this time I opted for the number one hotel on TripAdvisor - Mystic Mountain. The hotel itself is nice enough, it’s clean and the bedroom is comfortable and the outside bar area is a nice space to sit with a beer and a book to soak up the mountain spirit.Unfortunately on our visit the hotel was overrun by a certain demographic who had no concept of manners, respect for others or noise control. Due to the nature of the building you can’t unfortunately get away from any loud noise and on this occasion it included hoards of screaming, shouting and misbehaving kids. The dinner experience was horrific as amongst the tables of diners the children dining with their parents were playing tag and hide and seek amongst the tables. Generally meaning they were trying to hide behind my chair or underneath my table whilst screaming and shreaking. In the morning these families were all up at 6am screaming and shouting and banging and generally causing chaos. At breakfast they were taking bacon out of the serving dishes with their fingers and grabbing handfuls of toast instead of using the serving tools provided. They were hanging around in the corridors banging their bedroom doors and shouting to each other down the corridors.I did complain to the hotel management twice during our stay and asked them to speak to these unruly guests...but they wouldn’t...management were just walking around the running/screaming/shouting kids and not speaking to the parents asking them to control their children. It was a bit like staying overnight in a school...or in a train station...Really couldn’t wait to leave and get back to Thamel.Such a shame!!

Two hours away from The bustling Kathmandu lies the sleepy hill town of Nagarkote and settled a little away is this quaint and rather evocative Hotel - Mystic Mountain which transports you to a faraway landUnspoilt natural environs, with Rhododendrons tress in full bloom, mountains just a hand-point away with clouds and snowy peaks, birds chirping, mobile silenced by lack of signals make for a peaceful and serene, restful day at this well managed hotelOnce you have overcome the spoiler of winding mountain roads, you come across a rather simple entrance but once in, you have all that is needed to keep you away from the busy town / city, including wifi if you need to be in touchAll regular need of the international traveller including a swimming pool are available. Good toiletries, clean linen, well maintained washrooms, decently sized rooms and good food. Apart, games, spa, bar, bar be que and a well laid out buffet breakfast make sure you are in for a good time. Look out of your balcony thru the day (almost all rooms face the mountains) and if you have a drink in your hand and look towards the mountains and that skies at night, you could sleep into the starry nightWe spent a barbecue evening and dinner with music at the bar well into midnight and the two local musicians kept us longing for more Nepali music and songs. BlissWill go back for more!They also have a nice meeting / conference room for about 35 / 50 people with a full mountain and valley view

We just loved our stay at this hotel. The hotel is perfect to relax. The view from the balcony is amazing. We enjoyed the sunrise over Himalaya from our balcony. The food of the restaurant was really good. The staffs are very much efficient and friendly. I would love to visit this hotel again!

Visited this hotel for two nights before staying in Kathmandu. Bumpy two hour journey to the hotel from Kathmandu airport but well worth the 'Nepalese massage' as our lovely guide from Cox & King called it.Wonderfully relaxed and peaceful, the ideal place to recover from a long haul flight. It was our 40 wedding anniversary whilst we were there and the hotel upgraded our room and brought us a delicious cake. Breakfast is quite basic but you have to remember that you are 7,200 ft up perched on the edge of a mountain.If you plan on going in winter don't plan on doing anything except read a good book and gaze at the amazing views of the Himalayers.

The view from the hotel was spectacular. The architecture of building was really eye catchy. Staff were very helpful. The way to the hotel was bad. Room was clean. Wonderful restaurant and bar. Highly recommended.

This hotel is located in nagarkot; around 2 hours drive from kathmandu. The hotel room was nice; had great view of Himalayas from our balcony.Lunch was good however I wish the buffet dinner  and general cleanliness of the windwos were better ; other wise 10 on 10.

Last year, my daughter announced that she would be getting married to a wonderful young man and that they had chosen the perfect location for the wedding. I had been to check it out in December and was very pleased with her choice. Now that the actual wedding was taking place and there were going to be over 100 guests so I was a bit nervous. However, I needn't have worried. The hotel, the management and all the staff rose to the occasion and handled every request deftly and efficiently. Everyone always smiled and took care of all requests. And there were many as this was a large noisy, happy group who had come to celebrate the wedding of one of their favourite people. The hotel has lovely rooms , almost all with the most amazing view. At night, one can see the stars as its so clear there. Everything turned out perfect and we must thank the team headed by Satish Shrestha for all their help in making it happen exactly as planned. Would happily recommend this hotel to everyone.

We stayed one night and the view and spa was amazing. But the day we check out, our check out time was 12:00, and we put our privacy “do not disturb” sign for our room. Just around 11:45, when we come back from the restaurant in the hotel, there was 2 house keepers messing around our room. Our room door was wide open and they were touching our luggage and moving them. We pretty much packed our stuff but the clothes and some foods are trashed out. We talked with one of the front desk manager but they just apologized and just did 15% off form our dining fee, not room fee.I stayed at least 50 hotels in my life around all over the world but never never had this situation. I feels super not safe and disturbing our privacy. And our clothes and foods are not 15% of value.I really want them to know there is a people who want to be more private and paying for safe hotel. We are buying safety, if this hotel is not safe, it is not worth to spend $80 or more and our time to stay in Nepal.

pros- great location, on the cliff of the mountain. was able to view the sunrise and the himalayan mountains from my balcony itself. loved it. the food was good. the restaurant, cafe has an amazing view.. i think the view itself it a must stay reason.cons- the road to this place is horrible. and they collect tolls on the way to the hotel twice, which i guess they dont use for the road maintenance. better to keep some nepalese rupee ready with you to pay. the hotel did inform us on booking itself about the toll.

We stayed here for 2 nights in an upper level room one down from the top floor at the far end of the property from the reception. We had a huge terrace out from our room and we could see that those on the floor above us just had small balcony’s. Both mornings of our stay we rose before sunrise & waited outside in order to photograph the sunrise. I’m not a morning person so it took some effort on my part but my efforts were well rewarded on both occasions with a spectacular sight. The light just starting to glow down onto the mist filled valley below, then the red as the sun woke up right until it actually showed itself and last of all the red glow cast on the snow covered Himalayas on the far side of the huge valley. In late October the days were clear and cold first thing in the morning. By 11am the cloud had come up and was starting to cover the Himalayas but it did clear later on in the day once again. You cannot see Mt Everest but several Mountain peaks of a similar height. The location is truly spectacular as is the hotel itself, a feat of engineering clinging to the steep hillside as it does. Our room was larger than an average hotel room and quite comfortable. We had a table and chairs by the window and a sliding glass door leading out onto the huge terrace. The Air Conditioner we only used to heat and it worked very well. The room had it’s own wifi modem tucked away behind the TV & the wifi was excellent, especially considering where you were. We could only use our wifi passwords in the room for internet access, if you wanted to use the wifi in the restaurant I guess you can get a password at reception for that. Everywhere in the Hotel it was clean & all staff were courteous and friendly. The Restaurant was very good, we dined here for both breakfasts, both Dinners (which were buffet or a - la - carte) & one lunch and we enjoyed all the food. You could both see and taste that it was freshly prepared. The view from the Restaurant is absolutely spectacular, one of the best views from a Restaurant we have ever seen in 72 countries visited. As folk have mentioned, the road is a bit rough from Kathmandu to here but this is eclipsed by the breathtaking scenery as you wind up the hills to Nagarkot from the Kathmandu Valley. The road is narrow and winding so you can only travel very slowly but it doesn’t have the huge drop offs you see elsewhere in Nepal. We used the services of Hill Rd Transport to get to and from here hillroad2016@gmail.com because we wanted a private transfer & we didn’t fancy our luggage tied to the roof of a van as sometimes happens to here. I thoroughly recommend this hotel as a “must do” experience whilst in Kathmandu.

I love everything about this hotel. The location is super amazing - nice view of the Himalayan (on a clear sunny day). All the staff were super helpful especially Somraj. From the moment we entered the restaurant, Somraj (the waiter) was there to help us out. He is so knowledgeable not only about the food but the surrounding area as well. It was really refreshing to see a motivated young man like Somraj. The food selection was amazing - we stayed there for 3 nights so we tried almost everything from the buffet to the ala carte menu. I also had a chance to try the spa - I strongly recommend the Nepali massage. I simply love it.

No doubt that this is a hidden gem, and a perfect place to get a glimpse of the spectacular sunrise. The rooms are well maintained with all required facilities. The resort has multiple places to hang out in and around the premises. Recreational activities in abundance includes the pool, table tennis, spa, badminton courts etc. Though they should offer free coupons for spa usage per couple visiting.The only issue we faced was with their restaurant. It's not vegetarian friendly. Even the pizza's, pasta's, deserts contained egg. For the first time, we also learnt that the chole bhature (indian vegetarian dish) contained egg. Surprising!Being the only resort within that vicinity, left us with no option but to only rely upon fruits (some were canned). Though upon our request the chef cooked us an eggless pizza. Very kind of him to do so.We stayed there on 31st December and returned back to Kathmandu on 1st Jan.

It's not hard to get a view in Nagarkot but this place is eye candy itself. It's fairly new, very well spaced out so guests don't feel cramped. Amazing vantage points for photos on the various levels. Infinity pool has a great view too! Food was AWESOME! Chef clearly enjoys presentation of dishes. All in all, we loved it.

Nagarkot is a couple of hours drive from the Kathmandu Airport. The roads are quite bad but manageable in a good car due to the short distance.This property is beyond imagination and even the beautiful pictures on the internet do not do justice to it. It is located on a mountain top and has amazing view of the Himalayas – the widest range of mountains I have seen so far in all the hill stations I’ve been to and we even saw Mount Everest.Mystic mountain – the name does justice to the hotel. It is a small property with limited number of rooms – all very spacious and really well made and one gets a complete 5-star feeling when staying here. Every room has a balcony and the Mountain range is visible from all. The higher category rooms have an even bigger balcony. It gets quite windy and cold so better to get adequate clothes depending on the season. Rooms are well equipped and also have a heater built into the air conditioner. All the rooms are built over many levels which are accessible through lift. The hotel has two buildings but we stayed in the rooms below the lobby so we accessed the restaurant and cafes through the lift and little distance. We also got a great deal on our package maybe due to less occupancy during our stay.The staff is courteous, efficient and well-spoken and service is prompt.We were told there isn’t much to see around and we didn’t need to. The food here is great. We had a nice lunch. We tried a local Nepalese dish called something like Thakla - while enjoying the beautiful view in the heated restaurant. However, dinner - though good too, was not as appealing maybe due to the change in cook. We had not included lunch or dinner in our room package and ordered ala-carte which seemed like a good choice as we could try different things.The hotel has a restaurant, a café and a bar – all of which have a sundeck from where we can have much better views. It also has a swimming pool but we did not use it as it was too cold and water was not heated. We had stayed there for only one night so we didn’t find time to check the entire property but everything is very tastefully done.On our way back – after couple of hours into our drive when we had almost reached the Kathmandu Airport – we realised that one of us had left her purse somewhere. On enquiring with the hotel we were told that is was in the reception. The hotel staff were very very helpful in this matter and due their promptness the purse reached us just in time for the flight. A special thanks to Ms. Mona and her friend for reaching the hotel in double speed in his motorbike – otherwise we would have missed the flight as the purse contained some valuables which reached us safely.One of our most enjoyable and memorable stays.

We live in Kathmandu and needed to go somewhere for a break. We decided on Hotel Mystic Mountain as we had seen a write up in ESC Magazine. On arriving we found the architecture of the hotel stunning and enabled views of the Himalayas from all points within the hotel.The staff, beginning at reception with Moona, were all very friendly, and helpful, they were exceedingly hospitable. We enjoyed the aesthetics and high standard of food. We had lovely walks,the hotel was family friendly. And the price of the package gave great value. Definitely worth another visit.Thankyou one and all.

I stayed at Mystic Mountain with my family. The resort is very beautiful and the view from the room is just awesome. The best part is that all the rooms have the same view. The room was very big and the staff was very helpful. My only complaint is the choice of food for a vegetarian. The breakfast was not great. Overall a great place. Would highly recommend for a day or two.

This hotel has one of the most beautiful mountain view in Nepal, you can stay in heated hot tube or swimmingpool and have amazing view Himalaya peaks up to 27000 feet. Great room, balconey super service from most staff spesialy lady reception, swimmingpool guy and lady the lounge sky bar. Can see sunrise from balconey 6am or sunset have a walk 45 minutes up to view point. Only bad very overprized everthing, but number one of hotels Nagarkot.

It's was very peacefully environment. Rooms are very nice from balcony can see mesmarising view of mountain, cold clouds at the morning and can see the sunrise and sunset. Friendly and helpful staffs. Foods are delicious.

I had a lot of expectations from this hotel so me and my friends were very excited to have a visit “this is gonna be a long one as i am very very dissapointed”. We took 5 rooms in this hotel to have a great night with friends, 4 deluxe and 1 superior deluxe. We booked the hotel through the direct office and from what i was informed the deluxe were told to be 9500++ which turned around to Rs 11800 and the superior which was told to be 14500++ ended up to get around 18000+ with all of the crazy tax and vat included. First of all the information about the prices were not clearly explained when booking the rooms so “you are probably gonna end up with a costlier price than expected with the vats and taxes”. I told them that we were couples staying over so we needed a single bed in all of our deluxe room which the receptionist did not have an idea about, so hence i told her to arrange the beds into one and make the room ready which she agreed to I also informed her that we were a bunch of friends planning to have fun the whole night in the superior deluxe room, so upon the information i provided about what we planned to do on our stay, she selected the rooms and gave us the keys. We wanted to swim but the pool closes at just 6pm. Also pool is such a fake advertisement as it is very small and not at all like what we see in pictures. The hotel is really prettywith good view so we were quite happy to be there. But when we reached our rooms the beds weren’t arranged and the room was not even a deluxe. I have stayed in club himalaya and the deluxe is so much better with better service in cheaper price than this one. The ac didnt work properly in room 404 with dirty water leaking from it the superior deluxe was not spacious enough to be called a superior with no bathtub, the toilet did not have a lock and we could clearly see what the other person in the rest room was doing through such a sheer white sheet. The buffet dinner was not as expected with limited options and not so good taste. But we did not care much as we were planning to have a good time. We finished dinner and went to the superior deluxe room around 10:30pm and started drinking and playing music ,we were decent enough to not use the balcony as it was night time but then we heard a bang in our wall like someone rude had banged the floor and wall loudly with thier feet and hands purposely. Since we had let the hotel know about our night we did not care enough as this room was provided upon all of the requests we made. But then we had a call from the reception that we needed to shut our music which was not even loud i mean how big can a small portable speaker sound? plus it was just 11 pm not even past 12. So the dissapointed us shut the speaker and started talking and laughing like how friends on getaways do but then again the mannerless guests on our side banged the walls i mean if they were that disturbed they could have just knocked our door and requested us to keep it low. The receptionist called again,this time we were furious so we told her about all the deals we had made prior to our stay and demanded a room change which she somehow could not arrange we complained about how these rude guests were banging the walls but she could not say anything to them since they were foriegners??I mean why give us rooms with those kind of guests if they cannot say anything to foreigners? We are also paying customers and maybe even paid more than those freaks witha ll the room service and the numbers of rooms we stayed in but they did not care as we were nepalese. We are working nepalese in kathmandu and nagarkot is just couple hours away so if we had a great experience we would pay a visit here every month or so amd also recommend it to our friends i mean thats more revenue for the hotel than a foreigner who visits Nepal once or a few times in thier lifetime. The way you treat and handle nepali customers compared to foreigners is a disgrace as you give thier requests higher importance. How can you treat a paying customer any less than others like we were just a bunch of nepalese who were staying there for free? We have been to hotels inside and outside the country and town and have never recieved a treatment like this. To feel and be treated less than a foreigner in our own country is what you should expect from this hotel even when you are paying much more. A great night ruined because of a hotel that dont care about customers. Its like they don’t care to earn loyal customers this hotel just takes money and gives no service to its customers. We payed Rs 75000 for one night just to have our night ruined. The billing is not clearly understandable with all the ++ and the billing of the room service we ordered were not clear as it is much easier if you write what we ordered incase of just writing odyssey and room service on it make your bills more clear for the guests to unterstand. The girl and the guy receptionists were awful they did not even cared to ask about our stay no bye bye or thank you i mean even a small guest house has the audacity to greet and talk to thier guests. And even after we payed that much for one night of awfull service and treatment they told us to pay 1000 more for just two glasses that we broke by accident even when we had ordered a decent amount of room service that more than what orders in a night. I own a restaurant and i know how the vats and taxes work the 10 percent service tax that you cut from us you give the waiters and service personnels 77percent of it and the 33 percent is for the restaurant  and for any kind of compensation regarding it. And they did not even care to make a bill for the extra 1000 we paid for breaking their glass as they just wrote broken glass Rs 1000 with a pencil in the bottom of the bill. Also the payment for the glass wasn’t even mentioned on our final bill. I mean how can this service be accepted when we paying this much. Never ever coming back to this hotel or recommending it to anyone. If this hotel wants one time visit customers they probably are succeeding.Such a waste of money and a waste of a great night with friends!!!If you want a good time do not visit this palce as they could not care. I am sure that many nepali people have gone through what we went through in here, but they did not find it necassary to write a review as its not in our culture . It was important for me to write this review to let people really know how they treat local customers as this is the worst service we have ever recieved from a hotel.

Spent 1 night at the hotel. While we were very impressed by the breathtaking panoramic view, we were a bit disappointed by our overall experience mainly due to noise issue. We could hear our neighbours music until 1am, and because our room was next to the stairs we could continuously hear steps in the corridor/staircase. However I would still go back just to enjoy the beautiful view and the great nepali food that we had at their restaurant!

We had booked this place for Monday and Tuesday (probably least busiest day of the week) to celebrate our anniversary. However due to following reason, we had to struggle to enjoy our special day:1) We reached there at about 1pm as check in time was 2pm. When we reached the hotel, reception lobby was in huge mess. There was luggage everywhere and people were cramping in reception. We had to wait for about 30 min to even get check in form. After filling up all formalities, they said out rooms would be ready in 15 mins. But our rooms were not ready till 2:45 pm. I had to go and shout at reception and then only they shifted us in our room at about 3 pm.2) We had booked super deluxe room with big balcony. Room was damp and very cold (even if it was 30 degree outside). Being super deluxe room, we were expecting there would be bathtub. But toilet and bath room was very very small and there was no bathtub. It was difficult for 2 person to even stand in a toilet/bathroom.  Water force from shower was not good. There was very big study table in the room which i didn't find quiet necessary. This had made room smaller. However, bed and pillow was comfortable and a/c was quiet. So sleep quality was good. All basic ammenities (like tea, coffee, hairdryer, freezer. etc) were available in room.3) Food and drinks on the menu were excruciatingly expensive. You could dine in five star restaurant in Kathmandu in that price. Everything was double the price. As we were hungry we ordered momo and spaghetti and decided to skip drink because of price. Taste of food was very average and service was slow.3) Swimming pool was huge disappointment. In that big property with so many rooms, size of swimming pool was very very small. If 5 people are in pool, then its already crowded. Water of the pool was very dirty. When we inquire about that, attendant said it was because of continuous rainfall. Hotel of this level should have taken care of such small issue. Even surrounding near swimming pool was very dirty (photo attached). We dropped our plan to swim.4) There was open Jacuzzi. Water was clean there but it was very small (hardly 5 people could fit in). Force of air was also not strong and it felt like we were just sitting in hot water instead of Jacuzzi.5) Dinner was up to 9:30. We reached there around 9:15. When we reached there, most of the food  trays were already empty. Soup had already finished, desserts were also almost finished and nothing was refilled. When we asked for it, they only manage to bring us soup which was also not the one in dinner. When inquire about dessert, it said that it was already finished!!! (Photo attached). However breakfast was nice with huge selection range. In breakfast, we didnt took risk and reach there at bout 8am even the timing said it was upto 9.30am. 6) Just opposite of our room, there was small storage room. So there was lots of noise of staffs chatting till late night and from early morning.Price of this hotel is very expensive. In this price, you can get same package in Gokarna Forest resort with much more facilities, good room, great food and great environment. In Nagarkot also, Club Himalaya offer good deal in price very less than this (with indoor pool/Jacuzzi and great food and good room). So if you have extra money to spare, then only choose to go there otherwise there are many options available.

I was very apprehensive about the stay here because the previous reviews were all over the place with some troubling details. I kept waiting for something to go terribly wrong, but nothing ever did. The staff were all either at a minimum professionally courteous with many being genuinely friendly. They were super helpful whenever we needed/wanted anything.The food was just amazing. The breakfast and dinner buffets had many options, including a lot of vegetarian items, and the a la carte items we had for lunch were delicious. There are three restaurants along with a full room service menu, the Cliffhanger cafe while having the a limited menu offers a mini-oasis sitting on the cliff away from the 'hub-bub' of the rest of the complex.We mistakenly brought in extra water as previous reviews said only two very small bottles of water were provided. That is not what we experienced, as they were two large 1L bottles given every day, which to go along with the plentiful amounts of drinking water offered at the restaurants (not always the case in Nepal) were plenty for two people.The location is wonderful. The views of the valley and Himalayas is incredible (at least when the Kathmandu smog doesn't infiltrate the area). There are several hiking opportunities straight from the hotel along the very deserted "roads" in the area, and Nagarkot is walkable for the adventurous (45 min) or just a short car-ride which offers more hiking routes. Additionally, they offer bicycles for rent to expand the area available for wandering. The bicycles are adequate for general purpose rides but not to be confused with high-end mountain bikes. Note, however, that if extended walking or taking a car somewhere is not your thing, the location may feel too remote as there are not much other shops/restaurants/entertainment in the immediate area. For us, it was perfect.We splurged and got the Executive Suite which was two stories with a very large private balcony, 1 1/2 baths including huge master bath, two tvs, a jacuzzi, a little day-bed cabana thing that made for heavenly naps, and a sauna. This was a good choice for us, it looked like there were plenty of options to get a nice balcony, but I could see how the standard rooms might not be perfect for a dream vacation.Was everything perfect? No, but the things that come to mind are first-world problems whose nature should almost be expected in Nepal. The jacuzzi was installed backwards so one had to get in it to turn the water on. The hot water was sometimes tempermental. Some of the electrical outlets were a little sketchy. The gym was spacious enough but much of the weight training equipment was dated and in need of repair/replacement. And yes, the pool is not heated as mentioned by others, so a bit chilly. If those things dissuade one from staying here then maybe Nepal is not the place to vacay.FWIW, and I don't really know why, but it is a very popular destination for families. That, as a non-kid person, would be my only concern for others similarly minded. Competing with a lot of kids for hot-tub time or having them use the gym as a playground, etc. was my only actual complaint, and that is not really the hotel's fault.Also FWIW, they do offer arranging car service to the airport for far cheaper than the third-party I pre-booked because I did not know the hotel offered that.

Generally ur flight will be afternoon flight to Kathmandu . Do not waste time and reach the property ASAP cos beauty that u see enroute to this resort is nothing compared to what you will see once u reach the resort !!! Awesome food amazingly designed property !!! All rooms face the valley where you get to see the best sunrise right from ur bed !!!! If in Nepal do not miss this property even if it's a one night stay !!!

The best hotel I’ve ever been best then so called “Marriott”Love the food hospitality + room service even the breakfast verity and dinner 🤌🏻 wallaaa I would love love to visit again soon Thank you so muchHotel mystic mountain feels like home 🙂

Had an amazing satisfying stay regarding food, drinks,view, cleanliness, almost everything what hotel serves. Hotel staffs are so friendly and cooperative with our needs. Met this sweet front desk staff named puja who took care of us and at her best in being professional. Highly recommended if you want to get a quick refreshing getaway trip.

We booked thru agent . Road from Kathmandu Airport is narrow and in bad state. Took over 100 minutes. Hotel welcomed with not a welcome sign : No outside food. Of course we did not carry any but just saying. What we liked : 1. Room size is very good. 2. Has heater and AC.  3. Has balvony for view. All rooms have great view. 4. Good friendly staff. What was disappointing:1. Loud music outside the room2. Strong smell of Barbecue below the room3. V small dining area.  Too crowded during dinner time. 4. Only one Lift and it was out of order.  Old folks were struggling 5. Food was below standard. 6. No Veg NonVeg marking. 7. Spa is lousy. 8. Some Smell of wet carpet in the room which they tried to remove by spraying strong room perfume. 9. Price is v high for the offer.

It was a wonderful celebration. The scenic view the property, the delicious food and the cooperative staff all made the event successful and a memorable one. Everyone was praising the same. Thank you Mystic Mountain!

Everything is awesome Location is perfect pool is great my girlfriend is very happy in this beautiful place  management team is amazing service is excellent we will back next year in this beautiful property amazing super

I really appreciate the type of hospitality i received from every stuff i met. Now talking about the view , it was fabulous  i can't describe it words.Food was 👌 great.I would say it was a power packed trip.

I liked the location of the hotel and the view from the hotel just caught my eyes. I went there with my family and they all liked it there. Especially the staffs were nice and friendly. It's their service which is good.

The food  is not so good ,there are lots of food variety but food quality and taste is not good..too much disturbance in all area and room also ... restaurant menu has only few item and portion is also very low ..
