The food is Nepali and Indian adapted for NorthAmerican and European palates - not authentic but welcome. We were a group of four photographers, so walking around the lake and visiting local homes was rewarding for us for one full day (2 nights). Most of the guests seemed to be doing a lot of hiking. Not much else besides the lake available. Highly recommended if the $$$, the solitude and the activities suit your needs.

We were on a family reunion in Nepal and we decided to go to Pokhara for 3 days . We chose the Begnus Lake resort over the hotels with a bigger name in Pokhara simply because the comments were very good on this hotel . I can tell that those comments were genuine as we experienced the same when we went there between the 30th of Dec 2013 to the 2nd of Jan 2014 . The location is extremely beautiful on lake Begnus with views of the lake in front and the mountains surrounding it . The rooms are cozy and all of them give a good view of the lake . The food and service are of a standard quality .

This is an amazing place which puts you close to the nature and induces relaxation. We were on our hiking vacations in Nepal and The Begnas Lake Resort & Villas was our base near Pokhara.It is not a place for persons who cannot walk. To get in and out of the hotel to the road one has to climb almost 300 steps.The location of this resort is amazing. Gorgeous lakes and mountains. Beautiful views everywhere. Lush nature. Interesting plants. Swimming pool. Hammocks. Opportunity for boating.The cottages are nicely appointed and comfortable. The food was excellent. Breakfast was included and offered great variety of fresh options. We ate also 3 dinners there and they were very good. One evening there was life Nepalese music and dancing. Whenever we sat on the balcony and terrace to read a book or take advantage of better Wi-Fi they immediately offered free soft drinks - water or tea. The Wi-Fi in cottages is poor.We did not partake in the Ayurvedic spa treatments due to lack of time, but we met some European travelers staying for up to 2 months there for a variety of rejuvenating treatments. They loved it and bragged about the perceived health improvements. The treatments are apparently supervised by a physician.The owners are very attentive to their guests. Very interesting, kind and professional Polish-Nepalese couple trying their best to take care of their guests' every need.Given a chance we really want to be back at The Begnas Lake Resort & Villas for more hiking and perhaps the Ayurvedic spa treatments.After one gets up to the road, the hotel is a short walk away from other interesting villages.

Undoubtedly Beautiful resort working on sustainability. Toothbrush was not in part of amenities but separately chargeable plastic toothbrush was available. Bathrobe was also not available upon asked to reception however noticed foreigner guest were wearing dhaka bathrobe.Very limited choice for breakfast  from set menu-not as expected.However, staffs were excellent .

We stayed at this lovely resort for a few days as our friends chose this wonderful location as their wedding venue. We arrived by boat across the lake, which was an exciting start to our stay. After navigating the many steps up to reception (a stay here will definitely keep you fit), we were blessed with a fantastic view across the lake and surrounding countryside. In the mornings over breakfast, to see the views of the mountains were simply the icing on the cake. The food was authentic and fresh. The staff were absolutely amazing, nothing was too much trouble for them. We really tested them (unintentionally) as my partner got sick during our stay. The owners and the staff helped to get medicine, arrange for a doctor to come and provided everything he needed, including their immune boosting soup (highly recommend). I also had a massage there and it was just the tonic to soothe the muscles after our hike. Their organisation of the wedding was also superb , they attended to every detail and it was a magical day to remember. I'll let the lucky couple tell more about that though. I would definitely stay again to relax in a peaceful and scenic place, perfect after a hike in the area.

Worst hotel u can stayWe spent 15 hours without electricity They asked for 2% more because we wanna pay with master cardThey offered food was eaten before as u see cupcakes in photosPool was not clean at all full of insects and frogs Wifi is sooooooo bad Only the view is good Once we arrived didnt drink the welcome drink yet they came , look we will charge 2% Service is not good, but location and view amazing One more thing the staff always looking to us no privacy , they putting there nose in our stay

Overall, the place is excellent, food was okay and service can work more on that, Special Thanks to Amrit( front desk). Most disappointed thing was they charge for wine glass also which was new to us, but it depends upon company policies not hard feelings.

Sailing from a small harbor to the resort is magical. Upon arrival the many steps up are taken while the staff takes one's luggage. The rooms are simple and quite charming in a homey manner (nr. 9 & 11) with fabulous views. The first evening the staff surprised us with a cake as we were together with our newly wed daughter and son-in-law. Food was fine without being fantastic. The place has a very quiet and relaxing ambience, which is wonderful after 3 days of wedding in Katmandu.Unfortunately, there were too many mishaps for a place of this standard. 1. We went for happy hour in the bar three evenings before dinner. Twice there were mice running around us. 2. Due to the beginning of the corona virus many started going home. There is a very large number of staff and instead of putting them to do something sensible that you can't do when the place is busy, they were just standing all over the place, f.ex. at the pool, in the restaurant, etc. This became too much at times, especially because they didn't provide extra service.  In the restaurant service was very slow. No one came automatically with a menu and the likes. At the pool one just wants to relax without 3-4 staff hanging around.3. The manager was here there and everywhere. This is fine, if you are able to converse intelligently with your guests. But constantly having him at our side asking how we liked the place was fairly annoying. He and the staff should instead have asked what we liked to do and come with suggestions on how we could do these things in the neighborhood, for instance visit a nearby village, see monkeys, visit a temple, go fishing or whatever. There were no good detailed maps of the vicinity with suggestions to what to do for 1-3 hr. trips on one's own. The planned hike with a group was cancelled by us due to corona discussions with regards to when to go back home.4. Upon arrival we had paid for the entire stay. When changing a booking (staying there more nights due to the cancellation of hike) we were charged 3 x 150 USD extra. The hotel said this was booking.coms policies and wouldn't take on the responsibillity for this not being reasonable for us being charged both all the nights and cancellation fees. We contacted the owner, who reimbursed 1 x 150 USD. This is not OK. It was a very uncomfortable situation discussing this with the manager and staff - and at the same time paying a large amount cash for food for the entire stay including for a number of our guests.  The manager and a staff member stood looking at us during the time we were counting all the cash. They earned a lot on us as a group, but didn't treat us in a professional manner. This is disappointing as we in many respects loved the place and would go back and recommend it to friends and family,Therefore, the place can only get two out of five points. A shame, but this is due to poor management and a small-minded approach by owner, staff and management .

YOU’RE STUCK THERE. It’s 30 minute boat ride in or 20 minute walk up the side of a mountain. With a menu and decor straight out of 1970, this place will give you the feeling of stepping into a hotel out of a National Lampoon’s movie.  All that was missing was a moose head on the wall. I literally felt trapped. And getting around the grounds requires some agility. The step stones are slippery and uneven. If you have a hard time walking up steep stairs, have a hard time seeing in the dark or have bad balance, this might not be the right choice for you. Good luck doing it with alcohol in your system. HORRIBLE FOOD/ food service I ordered “rogan josh” for lunch.  I put it in parentheses because it was nothing like rogan josh at all... after a 40 minute wait the waiter came with what was a watery yellow soup with hard bits of lamb and coriander floating in it.  I told the waiter that I wanted to order something else but he told me rudely to wait and they will redo it.  I waited patiently and in the mean time tried to flag down another waitress for water.  She responded by rolling her eyes and motioning to a younger waiter to help me. The “curry dish” came out better but FAR off from what I was expecting.  But it’s like calling lasagna spaghetti.That night we went to dinner and had a steak that was like chewing leather. We asked for a sharper steak knife and that same waitress came to deliver it with the sharp side pointing straight at me and a stone face.  Like she was going to stab me. I know the waiters don’t cook the food and I am NEVER rude to them.  This was the first time I’ve experienced such rudeness.  Out room did BEAUTIFUL VIEW of the lake.  HOWEVER you could smell the drain in the shower.  And three times I had to catch wasps from inside our room.  And our windows and screens were closed. The next day we took a morning hike with a worker named Amrit, who was very sweet and made us feel like we were back on vacation again.  The grounds of the hotel and the views are beautiful.  He took us off the beaten path to see a small local village and told us a lot about the local culture. In the afternoon another employee by the name of Bikash Nepali took us to see Pokhara town and some of its sites.  He was very informative and took us to eat at a local restaurant by our request.  As we did not want to dine in the hotel again. He let us take our time and browse the shops a bit after, helping negotiate a good price for us (a big difference from what the store clerk had originally asked for).  These two young men put a smile on our face the whole day.  It’s very sad that the actions of the restaurant staff (particularly one waitress) tainted our first impression of the hotel.  However the two young men’s hard work and the smiles on the other employee’s faces made the rest of our stay pleasant.

Rowing a boat upto the resort, taking a short hike to restaurant, splendid view of Begnas Lake overlapping the beautiful ranges of Himalaya. Beautiful young lady Manju was very attentive who was our server. Nice hospitality extended from management team of Mr. Chhetri.

The absolute WORST!!!First you have to go down FOUR flights of stairs to be presenting with horrible customer service, foowed by THREE MORE FLIGHTS of stairs you will find the pool which was filthy & hadn't been cleaned in weeks & they won't serve you drinks down there despite offering to pay for this service, you can swim in the lake but NOT from their dock so "you have to go to the opposite side to do so at your own risk". Tried to get a spa treatment and they were soooo weird about me wanting just one treatment explaining that "usually they get 7, 14, or 21 day ayurvedic clients". I left SOOO disappointed! I drove 1 hr each way from the Lakeside main town in Pokara to experience this special slice of hell. It is in the middle of NOWHERE and charge $150+ a night.

I brought a group of 10 women to the resort for a week of massages and yoga. Wonderful!  Special mention to the amazing food - a great variety of vegetarian dishes and all group members were catered for beautifully. The front of house staff were always helpful and maid and ground staff welcoming and polite. The resort is so well situated on the edge of the lake and we were able to enjoy fantastic views and great local valley walks. Bar prices are a bit steep and the bar chairs a bit dated but I fully intend to bring another group back to Begnas in the future. Thoroughly recommend it.

One of the best and amazing property in Begnas lake side. Beautifully architect and meaningfully location set up has no words to explain. Sarad who looks food and beverage department provides excellent service. Bikash from front presents wonderful hospitality. Enjoyed the food we had there overlooking begnas lake.

We stayed two days in the resort 4 years ago which was perfect and amazing. We did do any activities as we were a local tour operator but just enjoyed our time there. Me my wife had an amazing time there, all the staff were great, helpful and friendly, Special thanks to Manager who did help us to be in there. If you are looking for a complete Honeymoon place, This is the best place for your idea of paradise. Thank you Begnas Lake, hoping to be there again,

Fourteen days in a little piece of Paradise!Lovely days with treatments, yoga, healthy meals and relaxation at the swimmingpool/sea.The perfect place to relax and optimize your health.Every employee made my stay full of  joy and graditude.From the gardeners, receptionists, waiters to the doctor and therapist.All with smiles and warm personalities, and together with the amazing nature I had an enrishing holiday and only want to come back again.

After a 2 week trek through the Gokyo Lakes region, Begnas Lake Resort was the ideal place to wind down and relax for 4 nights before heading back home.The resort is nestled in bushland away from the hassle and bustle of town and more importantly, away from the sound of barking dogs during the night.The service my wife and I received during our stay were second to none with every need exceeding our expectation. If I'm to be critical of anything, it would be the fact that there was no tea and coffee facilities in your room.

Begans Lake is a very beautiful area just a couple of hours drive from Pokara. When we were there, only a few others had found the way to this place, so we could enjoy the nature and people almost without meeting other tourists. The resort is perfectly situated on the slopes of the banks of  Begnas Tal Lake with a magnificent view of the Annapourna range - when it is not obscured by the mist. Even so, the hills around the lake is certainly also beautiful to watch. Fine possibilities to go for a walk.

This place is a gem! The location is beautiful, the hotel is well taken care of and the staff are super friendly and attentive. We stayed during a quiet time and really enjoyed the serenity and aura of the place. The food was good - try the local fish - and the bar is very cool. Excellent to also walk around the mountains and see the village life. If you are lucky with the clouds, the views to the Himalayas are breathtaking!

I had lunch with a friend in Begnas Lake Resort restaurant. The food taste is lower than its 5-star food standard. We ordered sausage, out of stock. We ordered Buffalo steak, out of stock again. Beer was not cool enough and the restaurant did not bring enough ice.Staffs are very dull and look bored all the time.The restaurant was pretty hot, we requested to get AC switched on, but got refused.We also checked the hotel room, (cottage style) Most of rooms are pretty gone, without good maintenance. Swimming pool seem not to be taken good care.It is off-season in Nepal but I could not imagine the lack of management like we found in this hotel.Our lunch is kind of waste of money and time.

We were very disappointed with staff rudeness and lack of professionalism. They only seem to care about foreign money and foreign guests, which is very sad.The setting is really so beautiful but the environment created by people leaves a lot to be desired. The terms agreed on prior booking were not honored on arrival and my wife was discriminated against based on skin color. What was supposed to be a romantic getaway ended up being a very upsetting experience for us.

Reached Begnas Lake little late in the evening, it was dark but the staff had their boats ready as its one of the primary means to get to the resort. Was little unsure in the beginning of what the property was like surrounded by dense rain forest. We also had my little children with us which made it a little more uncomfortable.Upon reaching we had to climb a little to get to the actual resort. The staff carried all our luggage up hill.However got a sweet surprise next day in the morning when I opened the curtains of my room window. Mesmerising view of Begnas Lake, Green Mountains and glimpse of snow capped mountains afar.The staff made food to our liking. Very polite and courteous. Most of them from Begnas itself.Their Yoga Instructor also took us for almost 2 our trek in the morning through the jungle and nearby villages. In all a very relaxing stay.Would definitely return when in need of a relaxing holiday in midst of nature.

We didn't stay at the resort here but had a fantastic lunch at their restaurant after a boat ride on Begnas Lake. Yummy Indian and Nepalese curries, the kids enjoyed the pasta, nice cold beers and a stunning mountain view from their hillside terrace.

If you want to have a inner healing through nature this is world best location with outstanding service of yoga mediation. Food here is unbelievable tasty , well trained staff . i stayed in luxury suites room .

First of all I would like to thank all the team of Begnas for your great service and making our three night stay memorable & wonderful on our first Anniversary. Top class service, delicious food & beautiful garden. We had stayed in Premier room (Room No# 40) in February which was well furnished, spacious, beautiful overlooking the Lake Begnas & mountain. I would highly recommend this resort for honeymooners.

Resort is located end of Begnas Lake, surrounded by Mountain (like Prison), no air flow, they collect full payment in advance, if you want to pay through credit card they charged you extra. Room with open Bath in entrance, which we didn’t enjoy. Food was Good. Overall not very good stay at Begnas Lake Resort.

We visited this hotel on the way from Pokhara to Kathmandu. The turn off is from Begnas Taal chowk and the road is quite good. Very scenic place, on the bank of Begnas lake. From the top of the road there are quite a few steps down to the reception area, so may not go well with older people or young children. The cottage type rooms are also well laid out along the hill side leading down to the lake. Very scenic view from the restaurant which has outdoor seating. The buildings are set quite close to each other. While this serves to take away the feeling of absolute isolation, it could also feel like there's not enough personal space. We stayed for a meal before heading out on our way back. The food was quite good and the restaurant staff were quite attentive and helpful. We wanted a boat ride but couldnt do that as dusk was already falling. A very nice resort. Well worth a stay.

We visited this resort, very well maintain. Nice environment with a stunning view to the lake. We had our lunch at Jimire Restaurant in this resort. Nice food, i love their chicken and veg briyani rice. Its a nice place to relax and just enjoy yourself. After lunch we went down to the lake and take the boat ride across the lake to the other side where out jeep came and pick us up. Really nice experience.

If you want to escape the hustle and bustle of Pokhara, and spend a peaceful time beside a lake, this is the place to be.Excellent location: there cannot be a better place than this near Begnas.Food: Freshness is the theme here. Simply getting to drink a cup of fresh beans organic coffee grown in the very district makes it all worth. That coconut/cinnamon roll in the breakfast was out of the world. Loved it.

I had the privilege of staying at the Begnas Lake Resort in October 2015. Nestled away on the side of a hill cut into the forest, the resort sits right on the lake side. I found the manager, Arjun and his team to be fantastic taking care of our every need. The location is perfect for those that want to get away from it all completely. It is incredibly quiet and peaceful apart from the odd monkey swinging buy in the surrounding trees. This is not just a vacation but a life experience. I fully recommend a visit.

After trekking in the Annapurna area, Begnas Lake resort was a wonderful, relaxing, quiet and beautiful place to stay. Hidden in the hillside, the slow approach by boat was already soothing and the many steps up to the small village above made sure that you kept up your fitness levels.  A walk uphill to the Begnas Coffee shop (organic) is well worth it.  All staff at Begnas Lake Resort are very friendly, welcoming, helpful and engaging.  The rooms are large, clean, furnished in a rustic style with great views over the lovely gardens, the lake and mountains - if the weather obliges! Highly recommended for some peace and quiet, we would love to return.

What a peaceful, beautiful and caring place to come to for relaxing, regenerating and refuelling! I enjoyed a beachfront bungalow (furnished in tibetan style) with a generous balcony and direct views out of the window onto the lake; sunrise, midday and sunset swims in the warm clear water to the sound of tropical birds & cicadas; professional ayurveda treatment to clear your body & soul from "old stuff"; a wide variety of light, delicious vegetarian food; wonderful welcoming hosts, and a professional service in a familiar athmosphere, where from the second day onwards I felt like part of the family - and not an anonymous guest. Thank you for your wonderful hospitality! I hope to be back agai soon.

If you are not in it for a stay at Pokhara city, then try this beautiful situated Resort, just 30 minutes drive from Pokhara.The resort is placed on the hillside, and over 200 steps leads you from the road down to the resort. If you want, you can book a boat from Begnas Bazar to the resort. That saves you from the steep climb.The houses of the resort are dotted out on the hillside, and on your porch we could enjoy your coffee/tea overlooking the beautiful Begnas Lake and sometimes get a glimpse of the snowy Peaks of The Himalayas. Breathtaking..........The room and bathroom were spacious and clean. The staff made sure that we overall got an excellent service. The food was great, and you can eat all your meals at the balcony of the mainbuilding - also with the greatest views.From the Resort you can enjoy many great hiking-trails. The hotel can provide a guide.I can highly recommend this special place.

I arrived late in night. Mr. Arjun Parajuly waited for me and they had ready dinner. I got an excellent room with a magnificient view of the lake and the montains. I enjoyed the hospitality and generosity, the wonderful massage, to swim in the pool and even in the lake. I would love to come back and stay for more days.

Me and my husband came to stay here for a couple of nights as a special treat for a special occasion. The place is beautifully set on the shore of Begnas Lake with spectacular views (especially the top rooms). The room was very comfortable with nice decor, a little chilly at night but there was a heater so no problem. It was great to wake up to the stunning views from our bedroom window. It was still a bit too cold for us to use the natural pool but it looked really nice and clean. The hotel prepared a delicious birthday cake on my advance request and the food was generally very good so we were very pleased with our stay overall and would recommend this place

Bengas Lake Resort is a glorious little place to relax in. Away from the madness of Kathmandu and even the busyness of Pokhara you take a cab for a half hour ($20) and then we were met by the manager who loaded us onto a lovely little boat and two of the guys paddled us across for 40 minutes until we got to the hotel.We had a waterfront cottage and it was lovely, wifi in the toom, a beautiful view, nice bed and bath and mini bar.the view and tranquility is worth every single penny- it's so calming and so relaxing and the air is pure and beautiful.We only stayed one night but 2 would be perfect. The restaurant was good, food nice (try the locally caught grilled fish), curries good but cocktails not so great, but hey, we're in the middle of nowhere in Pokhara, what do you expect?For the price, room quality and peace and quite this place is a little diamond.

We walked in, no reservations - just to check out the place. We arrived at their drop off point after traversing the side of the mountains. We did not know there was another way out through boats in the river. So we ended up going down some 200+ steps and went up the same way. We were panting but enjoyed the view going down, especially getting the glimpse of the serene lake piece by piece. However, no one helped us to carry our child's stroller going down so we carried it ourselves. We took turns carrying our child going down the winding paved path.We stayed a while in the restaurant, marvelling at the most calm lake, blue skies and fresh breeze as we waited for our food to be served. They offered fresh guava juice straight from the guava fruits abounding in the guava trees. The staff even obliged that we pick some fruits and eat fresh guavas!The staff were friendly and very conversant. We spent a lot of family snaps with the picturesque backdrop. The food is pricey as we ordered some fish dishes and our lunch there was the most expensive bill we paid for in our entire stay in Pokhara vis a vis Lakeside restaurants.Nevertheless the visit was worth it. Next time we will take the boats and not go down/up on foot!

We spent one night at Begnas Lake Resort and went all through relaxing, peacefully. The location of the resort is great as you can scroll down your eyes through the Begnal Lake, surrounding green hills, specially the Himalayas ( Mountain) when the weather is clear. While returning the siling on boat in Begnas Lake was amazing, beautiful which was managed by the resort. The boat man and all the other staffs at the hotel are helpful and always smiling. Please do not hesitate to visit Begnas Lake Resort. We will definately recommened this resort.Kumar Khadka & Anu Shahi( Bardia Jungle Cottage (BJC) & Anu Treks International P. Ltd)

My friend and I spent 2 nights in this resort.  We found it very relaxing, the room was simple and comfortable with a beautiful view of the lake.  There were quite a few steps from the dining area to our room in a little house, but the staff was willing to escort us if necessary.  The restaurant was good with fine fish from the lake which is a very clean lake.  The manager is very personable.  Very courteous staff. I had a very interesting massage which left me totally relaxed and sleeping like a baby that night. We came by car and walked down a lot of stairs to the main building.  We left by boat, a 45 min. boat ride on the beautiful still lake with the Himalayas in the background.  Magic! All in all a very good experience

I was an Ayurveda guest at Begnas Lake Resort for three weeks. It is an absolute dream for nature lovers and people who are looking for peace and security to relax and escape from everyday life. The complex is very well maintained, the rooms are decorated with attention to detail. There are fantastic yoga and meditation classes here. The young Ayurveda doctor is very competent, gets to know the patients and ensures their complete devotion. The treatments were simply great. I would also like to say hello to the kitchen and thank you for the great food. I felt very comfortable here and will definitely visit the resort again. Thank you all!

Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge is my favorite place on this planet.It isn't just the lodge, but also, the natural beauty of the area, and mostly the staff.They are like family after only six days.  So much to do while there including the nature and cultural hikes designed for the individual by Sajan.I'm already planning my return trip and can't wait to be pampered again.

Well i was with my friend and we ordered coffee.We sat outside the coffee was terrible.I was laying on the sofa and was constantly been watched(give me space) later was told not to lay on the sofa ok that's fineBut then when we were taking pictures one of the employee was rude.Later i moved to pay the bills they didn't had qr nor online payment nothing Not so good place very bad

I cannot say enough good things about our stay at Tiger Mountain. When coming to Pokhara, we debated about whether to stay by the lake, or several other venues in the hills around Pokhara, but kept coming back to Tiger Mountain and thinking that while it was by far the most expensive, it would be a special experience. When we arrived, we were the only ones staying that night and were given a room with a direct view of Machhapuchhare and the Annapurna range. The views from the main lodge, the pool, the grounds, and our room were priceless. Sunrise and sundown were especially spectacular, and you receive a wake up call and tea or coffee on your porch to take it all in. The food was fantastic, and we went with Nepali for lunch and English for dinner, and that was a nice mix, and the meals were delicious and fresh. Drinks by the fire in the evening were also a treat with some light snacks provided. The decor is really lovely in the main lodge and in the rooms with items from Nepal as well as other countries. Our room had a comfortable bed, warm shower, and a space heater as well as hot water bottles under the blankets. We turned the space heater off right before bed and felt sufficiently warm. We took several walks with a local guide, ranging from 3-7 hours and saw many views of the mountains, local villages, and so many trees, birds and butterflies. We highly recommend taking advantage of that offer. We did not brave the unheated pool except for dipping our feet in after a long hike, but the views are amazing - from the lodge you can see Dhaulagiri, Annapurna, and Manaslu. We went down to Phewa Lake one afternoon, which was nice, but the refuge of Tiger Mountain is so wonderful we really would not need to leave the area for several days. After the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu, or even the traffic of Pokhara, being in the mountains was the respite we needed. The staff are fantastic - we felt very pampered. Many of the staff have been there from the beginning, some of whom helped build the lodge. If you are in Nepal, we highly recommend visiting Tiger Mountain and experiencing a bit of luxurious tranquility and supporting this special regenerative tourism experience.

An absolutely stunning place to stay. Our room was beautiful with everything you could ask for or need including an amazing, unobstructed view of a piece of the Himalayas from a deck area. Our chalet was Tucked away from the main lodge down a meandering pebbled walkway. Very private and secluded. The lodge itself its beautiful with an open fire pit which vents through openings in the roof. Luxurious dining areas and a bar close to the fire makes for cozy nights with fellow guests if you so choose or you can tuck yourselves away in one of the many seated areas. Sweeping views of both the Himalayas and Pokhara (1000 feet below) offered in the seated areas outside the lodge as well. The well trained staff were extremely attentive and always available to  cater for your needs. The food was first class catering for all tastes. Also a lovely secluded infinity pool which even in winter is a must for a plunge.  Many different activities available including guided walks around the surrounding villages including a photo opportunity under the tree the then Prince Charles sat by during his famous Nepal trek in 1981. Or perhaps a dawn breakfast at a nearby Monastery with fellow guests watching the sun rise. A truly amazing stay.

Wow.  I think I read someone saying I don’t often give five stars. Neither do I.  Can I give this six ?  Fab place. Fantastic location Lovely staff.  Views amazing. Morning cuppa on the patio outside main area. Where staff brought us a welcome cuppa That view through main door. Wow. Fish tail Pool nice. But don’t try to walk there in flip flops. Put walking sandals on.  Fantastic view as you swim. People thought I was mad. But I swim outside in uk until October. So although chilly. Home pools would be worse !Lovely room. Oil filled radiator provided for overnight. Lovely suitcase area with shelves for one case friend left hers in main room Wake up call provided Lovely walk round village  humbling and so special Favourite spot of the holiday could have stayed so much longer Personally hated the freestanding gas fire   A real fire would have been nicer. But we were the only group of 6 staying. So not practical

Amazing location with breathtaking views of the Himalayas - Annapurna range. Rooms and Facilities excellent. All staff were lovely and very helpful going out of their way to make may stay as special as possible. Morning and afternoon personalised Guided walks around villages and local nature were  fabulous. Would highly recommend

Such a beautiful place to stay!  Warmly welcomed by Hari after a very bumpy road trip from Kathmandu. Tiger Mountain has clean and comfortable cottages - all discreetly nestled in the well tended grounds. The flora and fauna was abundant. The tranquility so welcome after the hustle and bustle of the city.The views of the Himalayas on a clear day were stunning. The service from all staff was consistently excellent. And the food of the highest quality. Lots of ingredients locally sourced from nearby villages or grown in the grounds. (The toffee and banana pudding and the ginger ice cream were absolutely delicious!)The Lodge offers guided walks of various lengths and for different abilities. Some FOC, some payable. We opted for the village walk, which was excellent and our guide was so knowledgeable about everything we saw. He really is passionate about his subject and was so interesting to walk with. We were very impressed! Tiger Mountain strives to be a sustainable Lodge with good working conditions and rewards for staff which is commendable and hopefully will encourage more travellers to stay. We throughly recommend it.

I don't really do five star reviews, but I feel like this place merits one for the wonderful location, the superlative Himalayan views, the abundance of bird and insect life around the complex, and the courteous and knowledgeable staff.Tiger Mountain was the fifth hotel I stayed at during a tour of Nepal and it came at a very welcome time after some long, uncomfortable journeys by road and some frenetic days of sightseeing. This hotel offers peace and relaxation in carefully landscaped surroundings, with each room being in a little self-contained villa. They are simply but thoughtfully furnished, with a very comfortable and sizeable bed and a little outdoor terrace area where you can sit and wildlife-watch (there are loads of butterflies and dragonflies to spot).The food was all very good and the reception/dining area had large open French doors along the sides so that the mountain scenery could be seen from almost everywhere.I very much recommend this place for a bit of respite from the higher temperatures of the Terai and the lower-lying hill regions, and for some genuine Nepalese hospitality.

My third (but definitely not last) stay at Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge. This property is so beautiful - amazing view, cozy rooms and the best food! Not to mention the spectacular mountain views in the mornings. Thank you Jhalak and team for always taking such great care of us, see you next time!

Tiger mountain is a beautiful lodge/hotel. High on the hill across from the town of Pokhara. Here you are part of nature but the staff makes sure you are always comfortable. This hotel is set apart from other accommodations thanks to the genuine friendliness of the stuff. The room is spacious and very constable. Super clean. Every room has good privacy, with outdoor seating and great views of the mountains. Also, the food is delicious. Appetizers are served at 7pm and Dinner is served at 7:30. We had a nice time interacting and socializing with the other guests. The pool is nice too.

A magical stay at Tiger Mountain. Our accommodation overlooking the Annapurna Range was spectacular and very comfortable indeed. Breakfast in the sunshine on the terrace overlooking the range was breathtaking each morning. The food is delicious, all organic from their garden and local community and cooked traditionally. Our treks into the Mountains with Sajan were truly memorable meeting the Nepalese families going about their daily lives with spectacular views of the mountains and picnics en route. The River Walk was fascinating watching the birdlife and many Gryphon Vultures in action. We highly recommend Tiger Mountain if you want a holiday that is reasonably intrepid and would like to thank all the staff for making it so memorable for us. Richard & Gaynor Stokes

Just had a really lovely two-night stay here, the property is beautiful and so peaceful, had the best sleeps of my trip here. Love the sounds of different types of birds throughout the day. The team are so kind and the food is incredible - homemade with a lot of love, with local and top quality ingredients, you can definitely taste the difference. Would recommend to anyone visiting Pokhara!

This is was a return trip to Pokhara my first was a trekking  holiday so no such luxury. First this is not for people not too agile as it’s a walk only to the lodge or it was for us the transport drops you at the bottom of a walk up to the lodge. It is also up & down hill to you rooms. But oh so worth it The view is stunning on a good day you can see machhapuchhre. Fantastic to sit on the terrace & look at the view with a sundowner. My room was beautiful large as well as a huge shower. In room safe, charging  , hairdryer etcI loved the food particularly their curry dishes. I am vegetarian this is not a problem In Nepal Grounds good to look around & there is a pool again with a view. Plenty of walking can be done close by. Again loved the Nepalese hospitality. Beautiful people. I would return

This place  is twice the price of the other most expensive resorts in Pokhara and the value does not justify the rates charged. There is no split heating on the room, Vilas have very basic amenities and decor. It gets very cold in the rooms in the winter months and hot water runs out quite quickly. There is no choice in food as it is a set a menu for $25 for lunch and dinner and it is basic food served cafeteria style, with presentation for the food. There are no spas or extra amenities here so we were glad to only stay one night. While we appreciate the resort tries to be eco friendly and save costs from all angles, this must also reflect on the prices charged. Yes the view of the mountains (and that too if you get clear skies) is amazing but not worth the price charged. I would actually give 2 stars, but the manager jalak and  his team ‘s service is the only thing that is saving this place in my opinion. The serenity of the place is lost by the inconvenience caused in not providing enough resources to make sure guests are confortable in the cold months of winter. I would choose a different place to stay in Pokhara next time.

I have travelled extensively for both business and pleasure during the past 40 years but the personal attention to detail and the overall level of hospitality at Tiger Mountain is second to none. It is clear that the entire team take great pride in their work and the service feels thoughtful and personal. It is a wonderful place to stay with the views from the terrace and the nepali food the cream on the cake. Note; I am completely lactose and gluten intolerant which the kitchen team honoured fully.

This was my second visit to Pokhara and my first time staying at Tiger Mountain.  The property is exceptional.  Given reviews we read, we had high expectations for the food in particular, which the Lodge easily exceeded.  The curry was some of the best we’ve had anywhere.  The owner and staff are intuitive and know exactly when to offer a masala tea or leave you alone to enjoy the breathtaking views.  I previously stayed at tea houses and trekked, but the setup at Tiger Mountain Lodge was far superior because I got the opportunity to do some day hikes but still enjoy the creature comforts and even go paragliding in Pokhara (which the Lodge arranged).  The lodge feels lived in and cozy (but not dated) in the best possible way.  Ask for room 9 :)  Highly recommended!!!

Picture yourself sitting in the private courtyard of your secluded cottage, enjoying lemongrass tea, fresh from the garden, while taking in spectacular views of the Himalayan mountains. That vision became our reality when we stepped foot on the grounds of the Pokhara Tiger Mountain Lodge. It doesn’t stop there, though. The food is amazing, the service even better. Everyone here greets you with a friendly Namaste and treats you like you’re a long lost relative coming home after an extended absence. Lastly, a special shout out to Hari who, not only drove us the the airport, but helped us check in. He then handed us a beyond yummy specially packed lunch.

A beautiful place.  Not really fancy, but very intelligently designed with bungalows, a rustic main lodge, great views of the mountains and of Pokhara, even a wonderful outdoor pool..  All very rustic, but with every comfort.Founded twenty years ago by no less than Edmund Hillary (!) with many illustrious guests including Prince Charles and Princess Anne.  Ask the barman for the key to the library to learn more.The hotel has been hard hit by COVID and also now by the monsoon season, and so needs guests.  Please consider a visit, it will be unforgettable.

Exclusive, private, great food, environment friendly, peaceful ambiance. The top of the hill and nearly isolated location ensures cooler temperatures, clean air and a stunning panoramic view of the valley below and snow peaked mountain range beyond the green hills above. Accompanied by a highly trained staff for indoor services as well as for outdoor activities. During our walk through the forest and village we were impressed by the in-depth knowledge of our guide on the local culture, traditional uses of endemic plants, identification of a large species of butterflies and birds.Marcus, the owner, is gregarious, knowledgeable, highly educated with a great sense of humour and slightly eccentric personality, and is a great fun to chat with.

I had the most amazing 3 night stay at Tiger Mountain Lodge! The setting was amazing set up in the hills overlooking the city ( which lit up in the evenings) and in the far distance the Annapurna Range. It felt like alittle bit of magic! Marcus and his team could not do enough. Food was fantastic probably the best I had during my entire stay in Nepal! And that little extra afternoon tea and cake while sitting on the terrace looking at the magnificent view was special!I’m will definitely return!

Having just spent two days relaxing at Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge, after a long trek in the Annapurna region, I can honestly recommend this lovely place to anyone who is looking for that something extra and special- for this place definitely delivers on at least these two qualities!Marcus and his team are so helpful- nothing is too much trouble, there is great attention to detail on so many aspects of creating a unique experience, Hari and his great knowledge on the birds and butterflies not to mention the fauna, during the guided walks we did, and also the lovely meals that were specially prepared for us- many from locally-sourced ingredients!I really enjoyed my stay, which was topped-off by the beautiful early morning views of the Annapurnas!Nirvana!

The setting - with all the flowers, trees, birds and butterflies, and mountain views - is restful and gorgeous.  What I enjoyed most, though, was the delicious food and the amazing staff.  The people who work here are so cheerful and willing to do just about anything to make your stay comfortable and enjoyable.  Thank you, Marcus and all the staff, for making my time there so restful and fun.  I was there for a meditation retreat and the staff really accommodated all our group's unique requests and needs.

Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge is a wonderful place to stay. The panorama of Annapurna and Fishtail mountain from the terrace is genuinely breathtaking; Marcus Cotton (the proprietor and manager) charming and welcoming; the staff attentive and expert; the rooms simple but comfortable; the food excellent and plentiful; and the possibilities for guided walking, birdwatching and relaxing amid unspoilt villages in the clean upland air more or less limitless. I visited as a new year break from my work in a big city in a nearby country and felt completely restored by my four night sojourn. I very much hope to return soon.

This was one of the most enchanting and amazing places I have ever stayed. When you arrive at the lodge and walk through the front door you are instantly transported to the spectacular views of the Annapurna's with Fish Tail Mountain standing proud and prominent in the centre. The Lodge is set up to allow you to enjoy this view from the lounge, the patio and the restaurant. I felt restored instantly by the warm welcome, the rich historical ambience of the lodge and the whole setting. Our room was a good 5 minute walk from the lodge but this was actually quite nice as it was very peaceful and quiet. When we walked back to the main Lodge for early evening drinks and supper the walkways were lit with oil lamps which in itself a new experience. Strolling through the tree lined paths bathed by a warm ambient light.The food and drink along with the service were all of a high standard and the central log fire was always burning from early evening to keep you warm and cosy while you sift through the days pics. On my first night by the fire I was enjoying a nice cold gin and tonic when I was treated to home made light round cheesy biscuits and battered deep fried cauliflower florets with a chilli dip, yummy. Early morning starts can be arranged and if the mountains are clear you will get a tap on the door, some delicious coffee and lovely plate of small tasty homemade biscuits. I got up each morning as it is a truly spectacular experience to watch the sun rise and the mountains turn from the pink glow of early morning to the crisp white and blue bought on by crisp winter sunlight. On day two we went on a nature walk with one of the naturalists from the lodge who showed us the local village where he was brought up, but also spotted some amazing birds for me to capture on camera while we walking. I loved each moment of learning about the people and the wildlife. Nothing at the lodge was too much trouble, the staff were all knowledgeable, friendly and covid safe. From the Manager to the bar staff and the waiter who brought our coffee and biscuits in the morning I could not find any fault, in fact the whole experience would be one that would take a lot to beat. I would strongly recommend anyone thinking of visiting to Pokhara to stay at Tiger MountainLodge as it really is a truly amazing place to stay.

I have been to few eco sustainable lodges or resorts and its looks bit run down and neglected after few years but I got an opportunity to explore Tiger Mountain Lodge, Pokhara which was exceptionally beautiful property, attention to the detail, and keeping the brand up to the standard. I stayed for a night and enjoyed being around surreal green forest, amazing view, homely cottage (away from each other’s), tasty organic homegrown food being served to your table, friendly and attentive staff.Thank you Marcus and his cooperative team member for looking after me well and make my stay comfortable.B. Thapa

A wonderful stay that I would definitely return to. We had been wanting to visit Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge for many years and finally got to go in October. The place has stunning views. The food was wholesome, fresh and delicious. Loved the conversations, stories, food, room and views. The staff were excellent, tending to our needs, while not being intrusive.

Stayed one night in October 2020. The location is wonderful with amazing views of the mountains. The food was incredible and I felt so welcomed and looked after by everyone. My early morning tea and cake on the terrace looking at the mountains at dawn was an absolute highlight. They were very well prepared for guests and it felt absolutely safe - all cleanliness and social distancing measures were followed without diminishing the lovely welcome. Thank you all, it was a pleasure visiting.

Myself and my husband had another dreamy few days here. The staff are superb dn so charming, the bedrooms so comfortable and the curries are exquisite made by a very special, local chef who is famous for his spice blending. I think we will make this a regular trip as it is a great escape in February from the UK winter.

We stayed for three nights at Tiger Tops and it was a brilliant experience.  The lodge is comfortable and reflects the area.  By this I mean that it's more than the standard hotel which you can find in most places.  The view from our room was amazing and the support from Marcus and his staff was exceptional. The food was great - 'real' food which has not been processed to such a degree that it's origins are barely recognisable!We thoroughly enjoyed our stay here and would happily return.

Breathtaking views nestled in the hilltops with direct sight of the stunning Annapurna Range. The location and natural beauty is undeniable which is then amplified 10 fold with excellent service coupled with scrumptious Nepali food (be brave it's divine) and homely rooms nestled in the hilltops. But what defines this lodge is the personal care and attention- Marcus and his team- truly make this place the last Shangrila. Magical.

My boyfriend and i stayed at Tiger mountain lodge for 2 nights in Jan 2020 and we were so impressed with the service and the lodge. I find some of the previous reviews on Tripadvisor unjustifiable and i could not find any fault during our stay. Stunning view of Annapurna range, tasty food and exceptional service- Mana from the reservation team was super helpful and reliable; property staff were very attentive , helpful , proactive and served us with sincere smiles; Marcus the owner, was  approachable and open to talk to guests- made our stay enjoyable!The lodge may not be the typical luxury villas or lodges you can find in europe and north america but you can feel the whole team there is doing its best to support sustainable tourism and provide the best experience to its guests. The stay cost definitely is on the high end per nepal travel standard but we find the moments we spent with the team there worth every penny.Thank you for the team  and we hope to come back soon with our friends and family (thanks for the care given to my boyfriend when he was sick!)

We spent 2 night at this hotel. We were expecting an amazing hotel and we were disappointed. The location is nice, close to Pokhara and has amazing views of the Fish Tail Mountain and Anapurna.The hotel is quite old and outdated, the rooms are nothing special. The restaurant and comune living room  is small, they have also a small bar. The bar is not very well stocked, and the food is preset menu. We were there for NyE, we had a small cocktail before dinner, then dinner. They didn’t do anything special for us.  One of the main issues is that there is no heating(only some electric small heater). I was not expecting to freeze in my room and to get sick going in the bathroom in the morning. If you cant offer heating, i think they should be close in the winter.There is no laundry service(they tell you that they wash only by hand, which i dont believe and they dry it naturally under the sun), no wifi in the rooms, no signal at your phone.Some slowly wifi in the bar. And believe me strangely Nepal has good internet.There is no spa, no gym, massage only in your room but its way to cold to have one.The service was good, but again for a 4*.This hotel is way overpriced and overrated.

Two years ago we visited Tiger MountAin. It was a dream. This was the most beautiful location. It’s set on a ridge surrounded by a local village and a short drive up the hill from Pokhara. We were captivated by spectacular and uninterrupted views of the Annapurnas from our room, from the dining room, from the bar, from the outdoor terrace - everywhere really! Hari met us in Pokhara with a 4WD, cold filtered water and hot towels which was just a taste of the spoiling we received once we arrived at the lodge. Marcus, our host, entertained us with his storytelling and sharp wit and the staff made sure that we got to do whatever we wanted to. We wandered through the village where the kitchen sources most of their raw ingredients from the surrounding farms. We did cooking lessons in the traditional but 5 star kitchen, tours of the local area and beautiful evenings around the open fire before fine dining. Thank you Marcus and team. Take me back!! I can’t recommend this Place highly enough.

We stayed here as part of our tour around Nepal. There was a bit of a hike from the lodges to the communal area but it is in the mountains in the middle of nowhere. The standard of the lodges was fantastic and the staff were really rather lovely. My only complaint is that our driver and his young helper were not given a room for the 2 nights we spent there so they had to sleep in the minibus. We did think this a bit unfair as they have a really hard job.

Good place to stay out of Pokhara up a bumpy unmade road. Outstanding staff, nice rooms and good international food. Birding walk was disappointing. Great view of Fish Tail and Annapurna South from the veranda when the clouds allow.

I am writing to not only compliment the staff of Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge, but to share with everyone about what an amazing place it is, I was just there in Oct. it is simply the best resort to stay in Pokhara.  The morning view of the Himalayan from the lodge is breath taking.The attention to detail is amazing, and the service is impeccable, all the staff are very well trained. Every evening after dinner...beds are turned, guests can walk around and look at up at the stars at night. The food is amazing. The butlers remember your drinks of choice and how you like your tea or coffee. Its like time travel back to the 1800's. Every little touch and detail has made this place that much more special than the rest. Thank you Hari and the entire team, it is a magical place and I will be back for sure.

Recommended by friends, we came up to Tiger Mountain Lodge after our ABC Trek as a treat for two nights.  The perfect place to recharge your batteries.  Totally peaceful with stunning views both from the main part of the lodge, the pool and our room (no. 9).The staff were so welcoming and were always keen to help.  We did a local walk with our guide, Sajin, which was really interesting and beautiful.  The rooms are lovely.  Plenty of space with a  balcony to enjoy your morning tea/coffee that is delivered at your requested time.  Meals are included and the quality of the food is excellent.Would highly recommend this Lodge as part of your Pokhara experience... especially if you can’t make any treks as the views of the mountains are breath taking.Forgot to mention the whole eco-friendly aspect of this lodge... which also extremely important.

It's not just a hotel, but an experience. From the warm and welcoming staff, the food, the gardens, the excursions, the library, the coffee and cake with sunrises, the comfy rooms, eco-friendly and sustainable principles, and beyond. You'll feel great about staying here, and you'll have seen (and supported) and a wonderful part of Nepal.

There's a little hilltop lodging to the north of Khatmandu.Perched above Pokhara with a panoramic view.There, a man called Marcus will take care of all your wishes. Just you relax and sample all the native dishes. If you're lusty for adventure there are mountain trails to take  You can view high Himalayas or paddle in the lake.Or take a wander in the woodlands with the flowers and the birds.Later when they ask about your holiday you'll find you're lost for words.You'll get a wistful longing which is difficult to dodge -For the greenness of the Tiger Mountain Lodge

On a recent trip to Nepal with Saga we stayed there for two nights and I was allocated accomodation about 200 yards from the main building and a 130 steps down a hillside. Fortunately being a reasonably fit 83 year I could cope with the terrain. It was also not well lit at night though a torch was provide, as was an umbrella for when it was raining though the prospect of using both at the same time would make it a hazard for some people.The lodge itself was good and the staff excellent, but a holiday like this is more suitable for the young and adventurous.

This lodge is so comfortable and welcoming. The food is delicious and the rooms are simple and perfect for a holiday in Nepal. It was a real treat to be there. The staff were absolutely charming; nothing was too much trouble. Spectacular countryside. We'll be back for sure.

A much needed break and escape from Kathmandu in beautiful Pokhara. As you walk up to the lodge the views will take your breath away. I enjoyed a relaxing weekend here spent birdwatching, swimming and enjoying the scenery (and a drink) as the sun set. The food was fantastic, the room was so comfortable and the staff were incredibly attentive. Tiger Mountain Lodge is a hidden gem of tranquillity away from the crowds and traffic. A short drive from from Pokhara it's a luxurious base to come home to. I was so comfortable here!Many thanks Marcus, I look forward to coming again.

My stay here with a Saga  group was all too short. It came at the end of a busy tour & the peace & tranquility was just what was needed. Everything, accomodation , service, meals of the highest standard  and the friendliness & eagerness to please of the staff  was second to none.

Tiger Mountain Lodge is certainly a beautiful, serene lodge away from Pokhara. Perfect for those who wish to be completely removed from their busy life and completely relax in this 'Garden of Eden'. The cabins are situated amongst the gardens of the lodge. Beds are comfortable with mosquito nets attached. Showers have plenty of hot water. Free wifi is available only in the bar and common room. A set menu for lunch and dinner and a variety of choices for breakfast. Hikes around the area can be organised through the lodge as well as a village visit which we did and thoroughly enjoyed as we met some of the local villagers and observed their daily activities within the village. For those wishing to visit Pokhara, it is a 40 - 45 minute taxi ride from the lodge.

Pokhara is much more pleasant than Kathmandu, and Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge overlooking the city on one side and the massive Annapurna and distinctive Mount Machapuchare on the other side.  It is stunning to wake up with such a view from the terrace of your room while sipping a freshly brewed tea at 5.30am.Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge  is not only a beautifully run lodge with discreet and attentive staff, it is a great place to rest, to plan day treks, to enjoy good food, it is also a place to interact with locals, understand the culture, totally integrated to the local communities and also very ecologically concerned. AMAZING EXPERIENCE in such a beautiful SECRET RETREAT!recommended to all Nature lovers.

Pokhara itself is beautiful and this lodge, sitting high up in the mountains above the valley and lake, was a surprise and amazing find. Everything about it was literally and figuratively in good taste. They grow their own fruits and vegetables organically, and the meals they served were amazing--yes, we were amazed at the delicate, unique flavors. It's a lovely hotel in a beautiful setting. We were told that sometimes you could see the sun rise on the Himalayas, but we were not so lucky. We didn't see the Himalayas at all. It was still beautiful, though. And the staff were superb. The whole experience is not to be missed if you're in Nepal.

Sheer luxury in the most beautiful, peaceful surroundings.  From infinity pool in its own gardens to immaculate,  beautiful kitchen gardens to gourmet food.  Unobtrusive service all under the superb guidance of Marcus and his incredible team, with a backdrop of glistening snow covered mountains at sunrise with tea and biscuits. I could go on forever, even to the luxury loo paper but there are not enough superlatives!  An absolute must have experience.

Amazing people with heart felt smiles that greets you  always  and ready to help ,  and waking up every morning with  the Himalaya snow mountain view right outside of your window is something else.   The Food is amazingly prepared and freshly prepared daily. The famous drink is  Lemon, ginger and honey tea.    The Lodge is Eco conscious oriented and supporting the local craft community and school.   Absolutely amazing experience.

Lounge outside town, peaceful and wonderful accommodations.On the hills with wonderful view of the Himalayan mountains.Impeccable service. Wonderful food and great comfortable chalés and outstanding views.Very quite and peaceful.Environmentally friendly lounge.Staff super friendly and accommodating.

We stayed 2 nights at Tiger Mountain Lodge after hiking thru the Annapurna range.  It was a lovely place to relax and take in the breathtaking views.   My favorite spot was at the pool at sunrise to catch the reflection off the water -- definitely worth the 6AM wake up call!  The rooms were very nice, big and clean.  The food was also very tasty, had a choice of local or western.    We also loved happy hour every night as the snacks were fantastic!  The reason for the 4 stars vs. 5 was because there were a few misses for the price of this place.  First the staff wasn’t very friendly; second, don’t waste your money on the massage, it was a horrible experience and I was so looking forward to it after my hike; third, our clothes got all stretched out/ruined in the laundry (but do note they make a disclaimer that it is up to your own risk); lastly, their communication on our departure was a disaster – got lots of different details and then they told us our flight was delayed only to have it take off 15 minutes early.     All in all, a beautiful property, but would hope they could improve their services.

Perched on top of a hill overlooking Pokhara, this is far enough away to be peaceful. It's a great place for birdwatching and butterflies, with guides who will take you out as often as you like, and a library full of helpful books. The service and staff are excellent (hot water bottles, early morning tea etc), and the food is very good, and although the meals are set, they are very flexible.

On the day we arrived the sky was clear enough and we could see part of the Annapurna range. The same day we went on a 3-hour hike. the easiest trail, after lunch. It was a nice and relatively easy hike in the mountains. Our guide pointed out different species of butterflies and birds to us. Also saw buffaloes and goats along the way. We got back to the lodge before sunset.Breakfast, lunch and dinner were included in the rate. The meals were sumptuous. For breakfast, we had oatmeal porridge, fruits, eggs, juices, etc and the portion was generous. For lunch and dinner, there were always curry, different kinds, buffalo, chicken, mutton and fish. Great curries they have! We had pre-dinner drinks, alcoholic and non-alcoholic plus canapes. Drinks were chargeable. It can be a bit cold in the room and around the lodge and there is heating system in the rooms. Hot water for showering was only available at certain times of the day, mornings and evenings. Lodge is an eco-friendly lodge so in many aspects we have to help to cut down water, electricity usage. Wi-Fi is only available at the lobby area.I was sick and the owner and staff were very helpful offering medications, suitable food to me, I am very greatful for their help.The whole property is really beautiful. They grow their own veggies, etc. So much wild flowers line the walking path and trees with many species of birds. At times the mountain was covered in fog. A truly relaxing place to enjoy Pokhara.

after a long journey, we arrived in Pokhara. someone from the hotel picked us up at the airport and we reached Tiger Lodge mountain in 45min. From then on, we could just relax and look at the amazing views from the main terrace. The rooms are big, quiet and comfortable. Food is delicious with a choice of nepalese or continental. You can go for short or longer walks with a guide from the hotel. but what makes this place very special is that Marcus (the owner) takes care of you remarkably and you feel like at home. what a great hospitality! we hope to come back soon.

We stayed three nights at this wonderful location recently.  Everything is to a very high standard.  Marcus, the owner, is very much involved and chats to and dines with the guests.  His team are charming and very attentive and are long-term employees so the place feels family-run.  We found the beds comfortable and experienced no lack of hot water.  You do need to be able to cope with steps to get to and from your cottage but if you can't deal with hills you're probably in the wrong country!  This is a 'mountain' lodge!Guided walks are a must do.  We did two and in each case our superb guides (Hari and Sajan) took us through the villages and to meet local people.  You need to be good walkers to get the best out of this location.Two slight regrets: Nepali food was not always offered but we understand it's hard to put on a wide menu and not all guests will like spicy food.  In any case the food was excellent.  And it would have been nice to have a clearer views of the high mountains, but there's not a lot Marcus can do about the weather!All in all, we'd love to go back.

This is an absolutely charming and magical place to stay.  From the first moment until the last, we were made to feel very welcome and very special.  The extremely attentive and friendly staff (most of whom have been here long-term - which tells you a lot) took care of our every need, clearly enjoying our obvious pleasure.  The attention to detail here is quite remarkable - with many surprises evoking delight.The food, snacks and accommodation are all superb.  We also took advantage of several of the treks with the Lodge’s very knowledgeable guides to the local villages and wider environs.  These all took place amid the achingly beautiful and breathtaking landscape.  Although we felt more than a tinge of sadness at leaving, we took away a wealth of wonderful memories from our amazing experiences here - quite simply, we had a fantastic time!  A massive thank you is due to Marcus and his truly excellent staff.

I was back at Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge with my clients. They loved the location, the rooms, the service and the attention to the smallest of details. TMPL is definitely one the few premium hotels in Nepal. Will be sending more clients when opportunities arise.

Marcus, the owner, is a wonderful host who’s engaged in all aspects of the operation.  The Bhutanese food is wonderful, the other options are good.  It’s important to know that if anyone in your party has problems with walking, this is probably not the place for you.  We had 110-120 stairs from our room to the main lodge, and there were others than had even more.  The staff is extraordinarily friendly and helpful, most have been there since the place opened!  Views are wonderful, everyone just wants to make sure you’re happy.  The pool is quite lovely.  We had a hard time with the extreme smell of moth balls in the room, not sure what that was all about.   Also there are other reviewers who mention that the mattresses are hard – indeed they are, and even with the requested mattress toppers, still very hard. It’s very eco friendly- which is a good thing, unless you enjoy leisurely showers with nice bathing products.  The water is solar heated and a small bar of  soap is the included toiletry.

I loved this place! Step into the Lodge at Tiger Mountain Pokhara and you'll find you've left the hustle and bustle of the world behind. Set on a hilltop covered in lush jungle and with views of the Himalayas (especially magical at dawn and dusk) you can spend time being rather than doing. Nothing is too much trouble for the friendly staff team with very detail overseen by Marcus the owner. The guest accommodation is spotless, simply but elegantly furnished and offers a high degree of privacy. Food is superb. Swim in the pool with reflections of the mountains rippling across its surface. Listen to the insects in the trees. Look for animals and birds or curl up in the library, which is convenient sited next to the bar.

Spent 2 nights here as part of a Saga tour. Superb food and service with Marcus, the owner, always on hand. Luxurious individual  cottages. Good walks, birdwatching, infinity pool...even walking to my cottage was a pleasure. Magnificent views of the mountains. Exciting uphill journey on a very bumpy road from Pokhara gave a few thrills. Wish I could have stayed longer!

This was a very, very comfortable lodge - just be aware that it is a good 30 mins outside of Pokhara on a very bumpy road.  We wanted to have dinner and shop in Pokhara, which we did, but had to pay extra to be transported (which is not unreasonable; just be aware).  It is very quiet and quite lovely, which we appreciated, but does not allow easy in and out of town for dinner or whatever.  Each room is in a separate cottage.  We stayed in two different ones and both were lovely though one had a better view of the mountains.  Very comfortable linens and furnishings. Pool - it was hot weather while we were there and the pool was lovely. Food was overall good. Service was very attentive and appropriate. We did't take advantage of any walks or activities from the lodge so can't comment on that.

Fantastic situation , wonderful views over the Annapurna range, brilliant attentive staff, food excellent, Marcus the owner lives on site and is a wonderful host,  The guides were all excellent, knowledgeble and walked according to your ability. Overall a wonderful stay and I hope to return with a friend in November all being well. Highly recommended

My husband and I spent 3 nights at Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge. The staff were friendly and extremely accommodating. I’m a very plain eater, and the staff offered to make me separate meals.My husband fell ill on our second day at the lodge, and spent a night in hospital. The staff were again very accommodating and considerate.With respect to the rooms, they are large and have stunning views of the mountains (when the conditions are right). However, there are no toiletries offered aside from bar soap, with only a homemade bar of shampoo for sale through the hotel. While I appreciate the eco-consciousness, there are certainly biodegradable products on offer. Similarly, there is no air conditioning in the rooms or even a blow dryer (although you can request to borrow one from the reception/bar). While these characteristics are less out of the ordinary for eco-friendly retreats, they seemed somewhat unusual given the price point of the hotel.The bed was extremely hard, as there was no real mattress (it reminded me of sleeping on tatami in Japan). I’m a side sleeper, and so this resulted in very sore hips. The staff tried their best and added two mattress toppers, but unfortunately everything seemed quite worn - the spots where you slept remained quite hard while the outer rim of the bed appeared almost comical - it was deep and fluffy.Overall, how you feel about this hotel depends very much on what you’re looking for. The service was excellent, the food was very good, and the nights were wonderfully quiet, but the rooms appeared tired, and the amenities were lacking compared to other resorts if you typically travel in this price range.

The tranquility of the Tiger Mountain Lodge is a welcome contrast to the chaotic pace of Kathmandu. After a rugged drive to the property's entrance we were greeted by the lodge's amazing staff, most of whom helped build the lodge 20 years ago and remain committed custodians of this unique place. The highlights were the treks through the villages that sharethe same mountain valley. Truly off the beaten path and not amongst the hoards of trekkers on the standard routes in the Annapurna range.

My family and I (there were five of us) stayed here in March and while it was a nice place, it wasn't amazing from my point of view. Let me explain...Rooms - Quite nice, very spacious. The beds were quite hard for our taste, but overall very nice.Food - There are no menus here, so hopefully you enjoy what they serve. I enjoyed the dinners enough, but lunch was chicken sandwiches everyday because we don't enjoy nepali food (I can't have spice), so that was limiting. Maybe adding a few more options for western appetites would be wise?Activities - Now I will preface this by saying that we did not do any of the activities, but partly because we didn't see anything that grabbed us. This is a place for birders, plain and simple. The pool was a little chilly for us at that time of year, so no swimming for us. They had some walks, treks and birding activities, but we had just finished trekking in the Everest region, so we were hoping for something quite different. Overall, I would personally say that the activities weren't too enticing for any of us, so we chose to relax and enjoy the view.Landscaping - I'm an avid gardener back home and found the landscaping to be a huge let down. Plant the area...you have the land!Service - My family noticed that there were no women that seemed to work at this property, but regardless of that, service was good. Overall - I would recommend this property to older, birding couples who enjoy seeing the mountains from afar, enjoy simple treks to see the flora and fauna that the area offers and loves nepali food! Would I go here again? No. But would I recommend it to someone who fit that category? Absolutely.

The lodge is set on a ridge about 5 miles north of Pokhara. There is a central area where breakfast and dinner are served and then accommodation is provided in cottages up to 250 yards from the central lodge. Views from the lodge and many of the cottages are tremendous looking across to Fishtail and the Annapurna range. The cottages were spacious and comfortable with a small balcony. Morning tea was served to each individually. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The food served was mainly acquired locally thus supporting the local population and it was well-cooked and well-presented. Lunch tended to be Nepalese whereas dinner was more continental. Wine was expensive but the local beer [Gorkha] was very drinkable. We had an amazing time there and would recommend it to visitors.

Located at the end of a windy road up the mountain, this beautiful eco-friendly lodge offers breath-taking mountain views on clear days.  Each morning they deliver tea/coffee at your specified time and, if you want them to, will wake you up early if it’s a clear day so you can see the mountains at sunrise.  This is such a nice touch so that you know you won’t miss anything.  The views are spectacular and something that photos just can’t captureThe rooms are set up in cottages spread out over the property.  Our cottage consisted of two rooms – one below and one above which was ours.  We had a perfect view of the mountains right from our deck in cottage 9.  The entire staff at the lodge was fantastic.  The food and room manager Delraj, was particularly helpful in ensuring our stay was a comfortable one.  He even arranged for a surprise birthday cake to help make our stay more memorable.  The food was absolutely amazing!  We opted for the Nepalese menu each meal and were never disappointed.  The lodge made sure that all arrangements for tours and excursions were effortless, including the transportation to and from each function.  We were able to experience ultra-lite flights in the mountains and a walking tour through a nearby village.  The lodge supports local schools and participates in “Pack for a Purpose” where guests bring school supplies to donate.  Hari was our guide for the village tour and was also our contact to meet with the children at school.  Meeting the young students and the school staff was fantastic.  The walking tour through the local village was “eye opening”.  Everyone we encountered was warm and receptive.

This is the best location I have ever stayed in ( and I am retired!). We were in lodge 9 with a spectacular view of the Annapurna range. It is hard to describe how beautiful this is, and we were lucky enough to have superb weather.  Marcus and the team who run the place have created an eco-friendly sanctuary, with well cooked, fresh produce and superb, caring ambience. There are personalised walks, bird watching and butterfly spotting available and a beautiful infinity pool. What a wonderful 2 days we have just spent there - wish it had been longer.

12 days, 8 locations, this was the best/cleanest/most beautiful place of all. We like dirty, camping, roughing it, and this was a nice break from many days of “roughing it.” If you are the upscale traveler, this will not disappoint.I give them a 10!

It is hard to know where to start with a review of this wonderful establishment. The Nepali food on offer was the best we had in Nepal. The staff and management are wonderful. Caring, kind and hospitable. Nothing is too much trouble. We had room 11 and were extremely happy there. Our comfort was paramount to every member of staff. We had the unfortunate experience of my husband becoming quite ill after our 8 day trek and whilst he was in hospital in Pokhara the compassion and concern of the management and staff towards both my husband’s recovery and my well-being was amazing. As well as organising medical care swiftly, they also drove me up and down the mountain daily at my request with never anything but a happy attitude. The management ensured I never felt alone whilst staying there and in fact I felt that I met some truly wonderful people. I can honestly say the experience at the Tiger Mountain Lodge was just like being with family- so comfortable. Thank you all so much - you are wonderful. Adrian and Katie Hollister

We chose this "add on" to our small group Saga tour of India and Nepal. It turned out to be the best possible decision. It is difficult to write about without overdoing the superlatives. So I will attempt to reign myself in. In a way it was the very best kind of late fifties/early sixties time warp. Style, grace and comfort, fine dining without the affectation that can spoil simple first class food. As much as possible was home grown and home made. The jams and marmalades just delicious on freshly baked bread.
