Nothing was wasted, it was an excellent lesson in green, sustainable tourism.Days ended with sundowners in front of a roaring fire.The chef was also kind enough to show me how to prepare one of the very tasty appetisers we enjoyed with our drinks.As we happened to be the only guests for dinner on our last evening we were treated to a table set in the small dining area in front of a log fire. We had five courses all freshly cooked and prepared right down to the final tiny crispy granola bars with coffee. We did enjoy a short walk to meet some of the locals and a great bird watching lesson from Harri.. I intend to start a new hobby now! There was plenty to do but nothing was forced on us. We were really tired after a strenuous tour and mainly wanted to enjoy the peace reading outside in sunshine, and have wonderful food....with choice between continental or local,,,, then tuck up in an enormous bed with hot water bottles at the end of each perfect day. We had three such days and were very sad to leave. Thank you Marcus and please thank your amazing staff.

Location: Great view on the Annapurna and the valley.From the welcoming to the departure day (we stayed 3 nights) we had a great hospitality service (meals, drinks,etc..) , we enjoyed the trek with our guide and the helicopter trip to the Annapurna Base Camp.The cottage was perfect, with heater during this period of the year (and the hot water bottle in the bed as a surprise).Will have love to stay longer.Thanks to Marcus for sharing his knowledge of this beautiful country through the day or at dinner time. You are a real "hotelier" and congratulation to the team for their service.

We have just stayed for 2 nights at Tiger Mountain and we wished we had stayed longer. Our stay was so welcoming and attentive a truly wonderful experience. We enjoyed great food and attentive and faultless staff who really looked after us. Our accommodation provided everything we needed and we like its eco friendliness, the hot water bottles in bed at night were a lovely touch. Pre dinner drinks in front of a roaring log fire with fellow guests was enjoyable. We particularly loved our helicopter trip to Annapurna Base Camp - what an experience (very reasonably priced if you can share the experience with fellow guests like we did) and our birding and village walk was enjoyable and informative. Tiger Mountain has wonderful staff, and great guides. We would highly recommend the experience and let the hotel organise all your activities as they know what they are doing! Outstanding views and a morning wake up call with tea and homemade biscuits to watch the sunrise over the mountains was perfect. DDon’t hesitate just book it! Thank you Marcus and all the team.

Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge was an amazing place to stay. Impeccable service and incredible views. Ask to go for a walk around the local village or enjoy a spot of bird watching. The fire pit is a great place to spend some time in the evening. I would highly recommend the experience.

Walking up the stairs, with Fishtail right in front of you is a great introduction to your stay. The service is exceptional, matched by the quality of the rooms and the views! We did a walk through the village, with out great guide, who was able to give us very interesting insights. An all round amazing experience, would highly recommend.

After a month of trekking and sight seeing in Nepal. Tiger Mountain was a much welcomed stay. Marcus was an absolutely fantastic host along with his staff. Both went above and beyond to accomodate and ensure we were having the best of times. Definitely recommend to anyone travelling Nepal // January 2018

Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge was by far the best place we stayed in our month long trip to Nepal. Marcus was a fantastic host, and the staff went above and beyond to make our stay the best ever. The lodge itself is beautiful and the view will definitely make you want to outstay your visit!

We treated ourselves to a night at Tiger Mountain after a trek in the Annapurna region. The combination of a stunning location, gorgeous stone cottage accommodation and an excellent level of service sets Tiger Mountain apart from other places in Nepal. We were very impressed with the knowledge and service level of the staff, the comfort of the rooms and the excellent food provided. Two of us decided to do the morning guided bird watching tour, which was excellent. We saw an amazing assortment of birds on a short walk around the property, including a very pretty scarlet minivet. The views from the property are superb!

I had the most amazing view of the mountains from my stone bungalow. My 4 poster bed was warmed each night with a hot water bottle. The staff were very helpful and the food the best that I had in Nepal. A bird watcher's dream.

Stayed two nights at this marvelous mountain lodge that sits on a hilltop ridge overlooking the Pokhara Valley.  Your "room" is actually a very spacious, luxurious, comfortable, hand cut stone bungalow blending naturally into their surroundings and sited to maximize the breathtaking vistas of the valley and Himalayas mountains.  Each room has a private verandah and set in private gardens.  There is an infinity pool with unmatched views of the mountains.  The main lodge with both in and outdoor dining facilities and patios to enjoy the valley and mountain views is very, very nice.  Our first night there were just three couples and we enjoyed a lively discussion over dinner.  The second night had a large group of 19 guests which didn't "take over the space" since the bungalows are spread out and all very private.  Most enjoyable stay here after our three days of trekking.  Great place to begin your trekking experience or to recuperate afterwards.  Most relaxing and the restaurant offerings are top notch, as is the staff and the manager, Mark.  Thank you for a wonderful stay!

While the drive up to the lodge is challenging, the lodge itself is an oasis of tranquility. Excellent service by the staff (Jhalak was always present to answer questions), and nothing is challenging for them. There are killer views from almost everywhere, and you can spend your time just gazing !! You can see the Annapurna and Macchapucchare ranges from the lodge, with the sunrise views being particularly awesome (we didn't mind getting up early to see it, especially since there was a pot of tea waiting :-) ). We undertook a short trek, and had a very knowledgeable guide about the flora and fauna that we encountered, as well as the region as a whole. The rooms are clean, and the food, both continental and Nepali, are great ! Marcus is an exceptional host.

Stunning hotel. Nothing is too much trouble. Beautifully clean, wonderful food. If you have a bird watching tour ask for Hari, he's an expert and a wonderful guide. We stayed in room 13 which was the lodge Princess Anne stayed in when she visited and we loved it.

You will feel like you have entered a different world altogether when you arrive at Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge. Firstly, you are treated to the most amazing views, which you never tire of even after spending days in Nepal. The Annapurna range in all its glory can be truly appreciate from the lodge, and you are not to miss the stunning picture opportunity of the mountain reflection on the infinity pool. The lodge itself is very comfortable and relaxing, you can do as much or as little as you like. The staff are incredibly attentive - each and every one of them. Marcus, the resort MD is so warm and friendly and so knowledgeable when it comes to Nepal, and most other things that it makes for a very wonderful stay all around. I would love to return soon, next time perhaps with the entire family when it is winter and there is good excuse to sit in the common area around the fire :)Best, Pramila

After a hectic 2 week tour in India and Nepal this was a perfect place to relax and unwind before returning to UK.  Perched on the top of a steep hill the location is amazing with fantastic views over the Annapurna mountain  range and down into the Pokhara valley.  One didn't mind getting up at 0545 to watch the sun rise over the mountain range, having been woken by the staff with a pot of tea delivered to the room.  At the other end of the day sit on the terrace with tea and home made cakes and biscuits to watch the sun set over the mountains.  In between very knowledgeable nature guides cater for all abilities with short or long walks bird and butterfly spotting.  Alternatively, relax by the infinity pool gazing across to the mountains.Simple but well cooked and presented food with choice between Nepalese or Continental  with most of the food grown locally or on site.  All waiter served, hot and fresh from the kitchen.  Tea and coffee with home made cake and biscuits on tap whenever you want.The staff were extremely friendly and helpful and could not do enough for you.  Marcus, the manager took the time to meet and get to know all the guests.It was such a shame that I only had 3 nights there, I would have liked to spend so much longer and experience more nature walks.Fantastic

This is a truly wonderful place to arrive at after a week of trekking (with sometimes hilarious hospitality conditions!). Or indeed just to arrive at after the hurly burly of Kathmandu! Marcus oversees a superb hotel with glorious views, beautiful lodge-style rooms and simple home-cooking. It is with some reluctance that I left, and to my disappointment now back home, there is no thoughtfully placed hot water bottle in bed at the end of the day, or mosquito net drawn to envelop me and my dreams.

Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge provided the perfect break from the rush, noise and dust in city life in Nepal. From the moment you arrive the staff are attentive and provide helpful information  in a non intrusive way. The rooms, each a cottage on its own, are  spacious, comfortable and every need is catered for. Early morning views of the mountains are spectacular and visible  from each of the rooms. The food is so good at each meal, individual needs having been taken into account, it is worth losing a bit of weight before staying there. A place to be returned to.

Spent 3 glorious nights at Tiger Mountain Pokhara. It is an amazing place and worth the additional expense. The views to the Annapurna range are simply magnificent and waking up to a sunrise over the mountains is very special. The rooms/cabins are very luxurious and perfectly outfitted . The food is wonderful and always the option to have spicier Nepalese or tamer continental fare. The staff couldn’t be more helpful or accommodating whether it was to arrange specialty birding walks or medicine for a stomach ailment. After the hectic world of Kathmandu this place was more than a breath of fresh air. I would encourage you to make time to spend a few days at Tiger Mountain Pokhara!

What a joy it was to arrive at this serene, beautiful place. The staff looked after us to ensure our stay was as wonderful as it could be, nothing was too much trouble. The views are spectacular, it is just perfect in every way and i do so hope to return one day.

Have just spent 2 nights at the lodge. Exceptional stay. The staff are so friendly and helpful. I am a strange visitor to Asia who cannot eat the food!  It was no problem for the kitchen to arrange something I could eat - beautifully served and with a smile.My room was very well presented with mountain views but the breakfast on the terrace, with magnificent views of sunrise over the snow capped mountain range, could not be bettered.The  walk to the main rooms was a little bit of a problem but well worth the effort

Tiger Mountain Lodge is amazing. Though access may be slightly problematic for the less agile such as myself, any efforts are certainly worthwhile. My room (7) had breathtaking views over the mountains and (very kindly ) the weather Gods lifted the clouds enabling the magnificent scene to unfold. Though  this reality was obviously outside the control of the lodge management , the friendly and efficient care that was delivered throughout the stay at the lodge. My food requirements are unusual to say the least, but an understanding staff managed to accommodate those peculiarities very efficiently. All aspect of care lived up to or exceeded expectations and Grateful thanks are due to a very efficient team.

Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge is an intimate boutique hotel that values personalised experience, above all.  It's an institution of tailored adventures and hospitality in Nepal. If only the walls at Tiger Mountain could speak, it'll be of stories within stories of individuals who have been and wrote countless books and tales about Nepal's beauty and serenity. Hands down, the best view from a hotel in Pokhara. Wake up for sunrise and encounter a parallel universe beyond anything you've ever imagined. Truly, a must experience. There is magic in this sanctuary of tranquility that is so healing; it brought me closer to nature, most of all, to myself. The food is exquisite, the simplicity of everything makes moments seem like a painting. If you are looking to book, don't think twice. Spend at least 3 days here, you can thank me later.The staff at TM are the best! It's like walking into a family. I didn't feel like a stranger, it didn't feel like a lodge at all. It was like coming home. Very best,Mr. Raven

Strange as it may seem. But we could not wait for the last four days of our holiday !! This lodge did not disappoint, the attention to detail, to ensure that your stay has the best chance of being a memorable one is impressive. There will always be somebody who will find fault, that is life ! The views are spectacular, the food excellent, ambiance spot on. We decided to have two days trekking, our guide Saajan was informative and considerate, and tailored the routes to suit our abilities, which was much appreciated by my wife who is not always the most sure footed rambler. The packed lunches were something that Enid Blyton would of approved of !! Marcus and his team can be proud of the experience they are delivering to their guests, and we will be returning to enjoy this hospitality as soon as we can. Thanks to all the team at Tiger mountain lodge.

The care and attention to detail I do not believe can be improved at this excellent place. All the staff, and indeed the owner are at hand to make your visit a positive one. I do not eat meat and was given an array of specially made food for my pleasure. The views on clear days are spectacular and to sit with a cup of tea and watch the mountains is a very special experience.

Beautiful. Exceptional level 10 service. To die for views! Quiet get away - absolutely worth the uphill trek to experience. Loved everything about it and will absolutely return next trip to Nepal! Marcus and his team will make you feel welcome, and you will be spoiled!

The staff are first class and look after you very well the bedroom are great and large inside with all you needed Great pool bar and library for us to use Can do early morning walk with a guide to show you around lovely views good food and first class staff well done to all

What more do you want!  Just visit!!!  This lodge is set out of the way with no interruption from anyone or anything.  Grab a book - sit of the ledge and let time just pass - no need to stay here for a week - a day or 2 and you'll be ready for the next part of your trip!

I stayed one night and it was a very pleasant stay. Great service, very attentive and excellent food. My room had a lovely view :) it's is for a relaxing stay and if you want some activities, they will arrange for you.

Marcus Cotton and the rest of the Tiger Mountain family have created a unique oasis in one of the most beautiful spots in the world. Superb food, well stocked bar, appropriately appointed rooms and a morning view from the infinity pool that simply cannot be believed combine to let you relax from the bustle of Kathmandu and enjoy the rest of the country as you continue your trip after a few days. While Pokhara had its pleasures, we found the nature walk, particularly the interaction with locals (particularly children) from the homes scattered nearby, to be one of the highlights of our almost month long trip. We were there prior to the date in the TripAdvisor menu, but our travel agent says the location remains largely unchanged. When we talk about checking off all the bucket list places, and starting round two, Tiger Mountain is always the first location mentioned. We'll be back, Marcus...

What a magical stay this was! With breathtaking views of the Himalayan mountain range right from your balcony any time of day, the views alone are worth the stay.When the skies are clear, and if you ask, the staff will come to your room and wake you up so you can watch the sun rise from the mountains -- a view that will bring you to tears.Meals are included in the price -- the chef cooks the best Nepali curries I've ever had the pleasure of trying.The estate itself is lovely, quaint, lodge-like and smack right in the middle of nature.The hotel itself is also part of the Pack for a Purpose initiative -- where you can pack school supplies and give them to a school at a local village nearby. Another truly authentic and beautiful experience.I'd go again in a heart beat next time I find myself in Pokhara.

My 10the stay at this wonderful, simple and warm lodge. Staff are second to none, food is delicious, the views are simply stunning! Jhalak and Hari made us feel very welcome and spoilt us rotten! The rooms all have a view and are spread over the property in chalets. Morning tea is served there and used as a wake up call. No tv or telephones in room. This preserves the tranquil atmosphere.

I stayed at the lodge with my son and husband for three nights, and it was a highlight in our trip to Nepal. The location of the lodge is high in the mountains and away from the city. It is cooler than Pokhara City, peaceful, and the air is fresh. You will get to see magnificent views and its tranquility is simply inspiring. We stayed at cabin 7 and it was perfect for us in terms of privacy, space, and amenities. It has a balcony from where we could see the Annapurna Himalayas, beautiful sunrises, and get glimpses of birds, butterflies, and all kinds of insects (I got lulled to sleep by insect sounds in the evening). Our stay there was a relaxing pattern of glorious sunrises and sunsets (we were very lucky in this regard), nice but challenging hikes, and afternoons of reading, writing, chess and the Nepali game of “tiger and goats” (which the staff taught my son to play).  We also enjoyed the pool (it is unheated but is a cool respite in the afternoon after our hikes), which has its own surreal view of Machapuchare and the Annapurna ranges.The staff members are wonderful. They are very attentive and accommodating and I really like how engaging they were with my son (who is 8 years old and very inquisitive). When my son found the library and the display it had, one of the staff kindly explained the specimens (e.g. snakes and insects) and tools (e.g. fish traps); and, I appreciate very much that the staff was quite knowledgeable (as affirmed during the hikes we had with him as our guide where he was able to tell us more about the people, places, flora and fauna, etc. in Nepal). You will definitely feel that Marcus and the staff members are doing their best to make your stay as comfortable as possible.My family is vegetarian and one of the compromises we’ve long accepted when traveling pertains to food. However, the food we were served at Tiger Mountain Lodge was simply delectable! I cannot state this enough. Each dish was delicious and I went so far as to ask for a recipe from their kitchen. The juices were always fresh, the ingredients top-grade, and you know you’re not served anything from a can. Aside from the location, service and food, I also want to highlight their advocacy for responsible tourism and accountability to the community where they are (especially within the context of developing countries like Nepal). I am supportive of the various ways in which they lessen the impact they have on the environment (e.g. minimizing the use of water bottles, not using liquid shampoos, etc) and also how they are building relationships with locals and are taking part in improving people’s lives there. I would definitely recommend the Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge to family and friends.

Stayed here for 2 nights on a tour of Nepal and it was the highlight of the trip.  Having stayed here in 2011 I was looking forward to my return visit and was not disappointed.  The staff, as ever, were fantastic.  Marcus was extremely helpful, going out of his way to help a couple of our group who were ill (illness contracted at previous places NOT at Tiger Mountain!).  The choice of activities on offer is excellent, the food wonderful, the lodges superb - I'm looking forward to a return visit.  I can't recommend this place highly enough.

We spent 2 nights at Tiger Mountain but it could have been much more. Superb stay from our first pick up and welcome to our goodbye.From Pokhara it is about 40 min drive up the mountain on a typical Nepali road but then you arrive in an tranquil oasis where you will only hear the birds. Lodge is located on a mountain with sweeping views over Pokhara valley on both sides. Rooms have amazing views towards the Himalayas, perfect for sunrise watching (they will serve coffee/tea and cookies at about 5.30 in your room to accompany the sunrise)Upon our arrival, the lunch table was set on the terrace with a view to the Himalayas and we were served delicious Nepali dishes.Tea was served in the afternoon with home made snacks. Followed by happy hour at 6 and diner around 7.30. Again with delicious Nepali dishes. Had amazing jackfruit curry, some sort of stir fried ferns, spinach dish, home made chutneys, water buffalo curries. I think I would have exploded after a week at the lodge as I had to finish everything. Quality of the food is fantastic, all organic, grown in the area, fresh and everything home made.Even the herbal tea came from their own garden. In the morning there was home made yoghurt with homemade muesli, homemade jams & preserves, honey from Pokhara, homemade bread. Yummy.The lodge offers guides to take you for walks according to your liking. We did a village walk around the hotel and the next day a ridge walk where we had beautiful views over the rice terraces, villages and Himalayas. The guide took us through villages and explained about village life.Staff at the lodge is fantastic: friendly, helpful and offering great service.There is a swimming pool with again magical views, certainly in the early morning you can see the Himalayas reflected in the water.It is a shame it is so far away from Hong Kong otherwise I would be back for a relaxing long weekend.And there is only wifi in the lobby (if it is working, this is Nepal) so relaxing is really good as you can't connect to the outside world!

This is a straight five star stay with lovely accommodation in scattered lodges around the grounds, bird watching and treks available, and a wonderful veranda to sit and look at the Himalayas (if they are clear of mist....)We had mosquito nets (not actually needed) over our beds and hot water bottles can be  requested!The food and hospitality are excellent. The staff are permanently on their toes.We loved our little lodge so much we could have just sat in there all day listening to and watching the birds.A local lady came and did a Reiki massage in the room. Bliss

I had another destination in mind for my Easter holidays, but a friend told me I had to go to Nepal, and especially to Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge.  Great advice.  The lodge is beautiful, in a magnificent location, and very comfortable.  Every member of the staff was exceedingly attentive to me as well as to the other guests.  Tiger Mountain was the perfect centerpiece of my first visit to Nepal.  The staff was ready to make my visit as active as I wanted it to be, with many options for walking and hiking, sightseeing, or simply relaxing at the pool with one of the most fantastic views in the world. The meals were special events in themselves, with a choice of either western or Nepali cuisine.  Yes, Tiger Mountain offers a glimpse of paradise.

Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge manages to knit together the very best in comfort, service and food, whilst making space for nature. A difficult feat to achieve, but one that I and my mother very much appreciated. There is no forced planting of exotic, introduced flowers and tightly strimmed grass, which seems to have become the standard everywhere around the world in boutique hotels and lodges. Instead, the focus is on allowing the smaller but essential things in life to flourish, such as butterflies and solitary bees, without the average guest even knowing these wonderful insects are there.Marcus and his team recognise the importance and value of these pollinators (we would have no coffee or chocolate if it was not for insects pollinating the flowers of these plant species!) and have cleverly crafted and created an environment that allows space for all.This is an ideal place for birding, but even better if you are interested in Lepidoptera. The team's knowledge and enthusiasm is nothing short of incredible, and I am truly in awe that so much time and effort is invested in compiling inventories of what they have found there. It is clear that this is not just a passing interest, or an attempt at green-wash to enhance visitor numbers, but a genuine desire to accurately record the diversity of the lodge. Many congratulations to you all. You have achieved the trickiest of things by providing first class accommodation, food and service without compromising the location.I'm very much looking forward to my next visit.

We visited this lodge for the first time in 2012 and were so blown away by it's most loveliest and most competent staff, stunning location, wonderful food and wide range of acticities. In fact, everything was amazing. So, we decided to return. No doubt at all!And this place managed to blow us away again! Even after all the difficulties they faced since the earthquakes of 2015.We especially loved and still love the day hikes with, our now dear friend, Hari Bhandari. His knowledge of local people and culture, birds, plants, flowers, trees, butterflies etc. is impressive. Combine this with his modest, respectful and calm personality and you'll have the perfect guide. We will be back for sure!! Dear Marcus, Hari and all the staff members: thanks a million for another unforgettable stay!! 💜

The lodge was very comfortable and had the most fantastic views of the valley beneath the lodge and the majestic Annapurna range of the Himalayas. The most incredible views of these mountains was at sunrise across the swimming pool. The lodge sits high on the mountain side and it is a perfect place to relax with nothing to disturb the peace except the sounds of nature; an ideal place for complete relaxation.The standard of the food is very high and interesting menu, each meal was a delicious repast. The main centre of the lodge is very comfortable and outdoor dining at breakfast and lunch was very enjoyable, dinner was served in the main dining room at night when it was a little cooler. ( May ). The staff is very professional, discrete, very helpful and added greatly to the quality and enjoyment of our stay.

A haven of peace after Bhutan and other parts of Nepal--a lazy 4 days where the waistline expanded again, inventive food and yummy....Lalu at his best !! As always, a superb stay, the team surpassed themselves under Marcus's steely eye.The weather was none too good but, hey ho, every visit has given us stunning views of the Anapurna range  so we couldnt grumble( otherwise the Grand Fromage would probably banish us !!  )Looking forward to our next visit and some chilli dishes !!

The views from the property were exceptional and breathtaking. Served a delicious breakfast full of locally produced and cooked ingredients. Beautiful village walk with Hari followed by a superb lunch. Excellent service and generous hospitality. Bvery interesting to hear about the lodges involvement and support of the local community schools. Thank you Marcus and your team.

We arrived late afternoon when 'the view' was in cloud, in fact snow was falling on the mountains.  The following morning we woke with the most spectacular, breathtaking views of the Annapurna range of mountains in the early morning sun with its fresh fall of snow.  Wow.  Our whole experience here was simply bliss.  The attention to detail was good to see from the design to the care and attention given to us.  Marcus and his lovely, friendly team were so helpful and made our stay very memorable, nothing was too much trouble.  The food could not be faulted and the atmosphere was perfect.  It was pretty cold in the evenings, what a surprise when we found hot water bottles in our bed!Our only problem was with our shower which seemed to have a mind of its own!   What a pity it is so far away from us.

Loved this sanctuary at the foothills of the Annapurnas. The host was Super friendly and had dinner with us our first night. We had a villa just near the restaurant/bar which was quintessentially Nepalese. This is not for Budget travellers as the restaurant is on the expensive side and there's no where else in the immediate vicinity to dine.

What an incredible place to stay with stunning mountain views.  We were looked after wonderfully by the staff and also Marcus.  We had some wonderful bird spotting walks around the grounds and found out lots of interesting information about the local way of life. Food was delicious, I think it is usually a buffet lunch but there were was only 2 other people staying our first night and lunch and breakfast was served to our table. The mountain views in the morning were outstanding (we had the benefit of wonderful weather on our first morning there).  This really is a beautiful place to stay if you want peace and quiet and mountain views.

This was my second time at TMPL, and for me TMPL is first of all about this magnificent view. The place itself is so beautifully built, that no matter which way you turn, you are always able to enjoy the spectecular view on the Anapurna mountain range and at the same time feel included in nature without being intrusive. A result of the environmentally conscious approach by its owner Marcus Cotton. The rooms are inviting - spacious, comfortable and in decor beyond any short lived fashion, which can at times be overwhelming. So I felt instantly at home.And the food was just delicious, home made from their own organic garden. It was a treat to chose whatever you wanted, because the guest's well being had priority. The staff is very well trained, attentive, efficent in a gentle way, making you feel very welcome. I thoroughly enjoyed Marcus' warm and generous hospitality sprinkled with a lovely sense of british humour. It was a truly wonderful stay for me and I will be back for more as soon as I can.

Rarely does one find a jewel like this, where staff and owner are welcoming, friendly and nothing is too much. Marcus and his team really go out of their way to make your stay enjoyable, relaxing, rejuvenating. Then comes the view : simply breathtaking. And the cozy rooms in chalets built of local materials, all conscious of the environment and preserving it. And the delicious food : you can have just about anything you feel like, and much of it comes form their own organic garden, simply delicious!Thank you TMPL for a most relaxing holiday, without noise pollution! I will be back for sure.

We had high expectations for this hotel. Sadly due to bad weather we didn't have many glimpses of the mountain, not their fault.What disappointed us the most were the (hidden) extras that resulted in us spending $500 extra (excluding accommodation) over two nights. Lunch / dinner is $25/person when we asked in advance we were told approximately $15/person for lunch and $20/person for dinner which was wrong would you expect them to know the accurate prices. All meals are $25/person then you have to add 10% mandatory service then 13% tax. The food was good but very over priced compared to the food you can get in town for under $5/person, wine was $30/bottle. They also give you a spiel about communal tipping for the people you don't see behind the scenes which i thought was cheeky given they charge 10% service charge on everything. If you choose to go down to the town in their shuttle they charge $20/ person round trip again quite exorbitant. We ordered massages - the quality was very average and on your bed in your room, not ideal. The décor was nice but somewhat dated, the staff were friendly and pleasant but given there were only three couples this was to be expected. If you're scared of spiders, be warned we were greeted with a giant spider in the bathroom one night. If we came back here we would stay somewhere else and get our views outside of our accommodation.

Sorry TMPL, rather behind schedule.  Possibly a combination of -3C welcome home and December overtaking me.Two visits in one year are definitely worth it.  Albeit earlier than expected as in a backhanded way Saga messing up actually did me a favour,  It was great to be back at the Lodge.  Must make it longer next time and hopefully go for walkabouts with Hari.  Must up the exercise regime.I was in need of TLC and was not disappointed.  Looked after by all the guys.  Everything down to a fine art.  Including my escorts home in the dark.  Sunrise at the pool then wake up coffee delivered to my veranda.  Great breakfast on the terrace with Machapuchare and friends looking over.  Fantastic food coming from Lalu and the team in the kitchen.  No continental for me when Nepali is available.  I could do with their help a week Sunday as I'm in charge for the first time in 10 years.  Ouch!  My second attempt at rumble tumble was only just edible.  I hope Lalu's cook book is available at the Lodge.  New Zealand is a long way away.So on that happy note, very many thanks.  I shall wish my life away looking forward to my next trip.  Can't wait!  M

We were there for 3 nights and it was glorious. Everything about this place is perfect: - staff: wonderful, very kind and helpful- rooms: the little huts are just perfect. They are private, wonderfully decorated and have everything one might need. Natural soaps are provided and filtered coffee- grounds: the location is magical. You see the beautiful Annapurna range. MUST DO: get the sunrise coffee and cookies. They will bring it to your room just in time for the sunrise view. Walk up to the pool - there is a beautiful reflection - food- we had all our meals there and everything was absolutely delicious. The Nepalese food is exquisite. Breakfast is lovely. Great coffee and biscuits. Do not hesitate to book this place. You won't regret it. The only danger is that you might not want to leave it. We went for a day to explore Pokhara and kept missing the glorious calm and soothing atmosphere of Tiger resort We will be back!

Having read glowing reviews about this property we were anticipating a really enjoyable stay. First impressions, the car that came to pick us up was not big enough so my seven year old daughter had to sit on my husbands lap for nearly an hour. The view on arrival is amazing. I did not feel that the managers welcome was very sincere. Throughout our entire stay he seemed to be pandering to the British and a big group of American guests. On one occasion a staff member was talking to us and he cut in and took him away mid sentence. The accommodation was really nice. After travelling through Nepal for two weeks I don't believe we had an unrealistic expectation on accommodation services. There were just too many little flaws. On calling for afternoon tea we were told it was too busy and they could not offer it, yet when mentioned to the manager he said he would pull some toenails and get it to us. It said it was available in the compendium. We requested laundry powder 3 times before it was delivered to the room. We had an extra bed in one room and after explaining many times we needed  an extra cup one never arrived. On enquiring about a tour I specifically said I did not want to book, just find out times etc but sure enough we found out at 7 that night they had booked us in. On explaining a problem to the manager he said that the fault lay with the staff, that it was an Asian thing in that they said yes as they did not want to offend by saying no. Although this may be true I felt is was said in quite a condescending manner and we had not experienced this problem anywhere else in Nepal. Seemed a rather pompous attitude. All the staff were friendly and tried to be very helpful. The manager and a staff member both interrupted our breakfast to enquire and write down which travel agency had reccomended us to them, it seemed that they were more concerned about that than letting us eat breakfast. So overall beautiful property, caring staff but management not running smoothly. If you like mediocre service and being fawned over this is for you. Would not go back.

This is a great place to stay if you dontvwant to be in Lakeside. It's takes a while to get up there but when you do it's a haven of tranquility. The grounds are beautifully kept and the rooms eco friendly. You can be woken up in time to watch the sunrise over the Annapurna range which we did 3 days running with the view improving each time. Awesome place to have breakfast! I was suffering with a damaged back. Marcus, Jhalek  and the  team looked after us with a nice blend of low key care and concern and practical advice. The food is a clever blend of local and international .  They have a good hotline to the local clinic. The longer you stay the more the place gets into your bones. I'm so glad I spent an entire day doing nothing just relaxing the only time on the trip. We would recommend Tiger Mountain to all our friends.

I have visited Tiger Mountain several times and I now regard the staff there as 'friends'. The team led by Marcus, Jhalak and Dol Raj are very friendly and helpful. The food is some of the best available in Nepal. Local curry is excellent and the Western dishes are wholesome and tasty. The hotel focuses on ecotourism and so tries to use local organic produce as much as possible. The large garden is full of birds and butterflies and the naturlist team available for nature walks are very experienced. The swimming pool has possibly the best hotel swimming pool view in the World. I shall return!

We lived in Nepal for many years and now visit quite regularly. This has and will always been one of our most favourite spots thanks to Marcus and his team as well as it's most lovely location above Pokhara, in the hills with fabulous mountain views and walks.The local staff are a delight and nothing is too much trouble. The atmosphere is informal and comfortable.The rooms(with attached bathrooms) are tastefully but simply/appropriately decorated and with very comfortable beds. The food is now exceptionally good and there is a choice of meals, which are either enjoyed alone or with other guests and friends. Computers and phones are discouraged in the main reception/dining/living areas which is a breath of fresh air!We spent five nights there on this visit(post high altitude trek) and walked every morning with one of the lodge naturalists, whose knowledge , particularly of the birds, butterflies and trees  is exceptional.The local villagers are very welcoming.Thank you all! We will be back!

This is the first time I have reviewed any accommodation on any website, but I am moved to do it following a lovely stay at Tiger Mountain.I went there in a poor frame of mind as all my trips to Nepal in the past have been trekking holidays, but this time I was prevented from treking long distances due to injury.  My wife and daughter had gone off on the trek leaving me feeling a little grumpy. But it didn't last. Tiger mountain lifted me from the moment I arrived. There is an air of tranquility about the place which is hard to describe, but it is soothing, warming and embracing. All the staff are fantastic. They are attentive but not overbearing. They are helpful and take the time to understand you, and then offer ideas which enhance your stay. I did some lovely walks guided by in-house staff who knew the area and people so well. It just makes the walk so much more enjoyable. I was also carefully steered away from an idea for a walk which I had, which with hind site would have largely been a waste of time, ending up doing a superb replacement instead. This approach to guests runs through the organisation from top to bottom, and also rubs off on the guests. Although traveling alone I couldn't have wished for better company, I had my meals with other guests who were great company and became friends. On top of that Marcus, (the owner), found time to join us and added to some very enjoyable evenings. And what of the accommodation, well the setting is great, my verandah affording terrific views of the Annapurna range, what better way to enjoy that early morning coffee delivered to your door. And inside there are all the ameneties you would wish for, provided in an environmentally thoughtful way. The food is delicious, fresh ingredients and an imaginative chef combine to produce fantastic meals. And I think it is the staff which is Tiger Mountains greatest asset. On talking to them, most have been here for years, some since it opened, and that means visitors benefit from staff who are knowledgeable and work as a team to provide an unparrelled experience. Yes, I did enjoy my stay immensely. A big thank you to Marcus and ALL his staff.

Worth every penny. Hands down the best food and best service you will have in Nepal. Situated on top of a big hill the lodge boasts views of the Pokhara valley and the imposing Himalaya in the backdrop. Pure luxury and class but never flashy.

I stayed at this lodge and loved it. The whole set up is fantastic from the staff, the food and the views. I truly enjoyed the kind hospitality of the owner. He is a very warm host. The food is organic and out of this world. Will definitely return.

It's unreal that you wake up to the panoramic views all around you. As the sun rises the white peaks covered with snow make an appearance. Some days you are actually " above the cloud ". The food is amazing. Home grown organic veg. The swimming pool is fab. The path from lodges to the main building could improve - a bit dangerous at night. I'd love to return if the price is not too steep. All in all - my favourite place.

Our stand-alone bungalow was delightful, decorated in local handicrafts. It had its own patio, where afternoon tea was served. Be sure to do the bird watching tour in the local area if you have time. The service and food were impeccable, the staff will treat you like royalty. The views are to die for!

They don't make hotels like this anymore.  Which is a pity,  because a stay at Tiger Mountain is about so much more than just 'physical' luxury.  It's enriching - visually, intellectually and emotionally.  First things first - it's a fantastic property, perched high up on a mountain overlooking the Pokhara Valley with fantastic views of the Annapurna range. This is eco-luxury at its finest : great views,  great service,  great food but with minimal environmental impact.  The rooms are nice, in a spartan sort of way (no TV, no WiFi, no aircon - not that you need it) with four poster beds, charmingly rustic furniture and a private, sit out balcony.  The food is fantastic - among the best you will ever have, whether it's traditional Nepali fare or the more Western dishes that are traditionally served at dinner.  But many hotels have great views, great rooms and great food.  Tiger Mountain's secret weapon are it's guests and the fact that dinner is a communal meal where all the guests get together over 4 courses and copious amongst of alcohol.  Over the course of 3 nights we met a couple who had driven a Land Rover from London to South Africa and who were currently doing relief work in Nepal, a Scotsman who spent a year living in a campervan with him family and his dog,  and an ex military attache who also oversaw the recruitment of Gurkhas for the British Army.  Simply put, these are things money can't buy.  And that's to say nothing of Marcus, the Managing Director of the place who makes it a point to have a drink with every one of his guests and who has a number of remarkable insights and anecdotes about Nepal, India, England and everything in between to share.  If you're looking for a traditional luxury hotel with every modern comfort, this property probably isn't for you.  But if you're looking for old world charm, delightful dinnertime conversations and a view that just doesn't quit, Tiger Lodge has your number.  It may be a bit pricey, but it's Worth Every Penny.

We came up to the Lodge for supper - what a very special place, amazing views!!  Supper was delicious most of the veggies served came from their very own garden, salad and beetroot, yum!!  To be led back down the path to our car in the rain by the staff holding umbrellas and torches just added magic to a special evening!!

Stayed in April. Our lodge was comfortable, food excellent and the staff and owner very friendly. We were well looked after. Highlights included the resident birdlife and the possibility of seeing the leopard who roams the area. Best of all, was the sunrise casting a pink glow over Fishtail mountain and the others in the Annapurna range. This only happened one of the mornings we were there, nevertheless it was awesome.

It's not often that I come across a place like Tiger Mountain which has such a rich history, character and genuine warmth.  The staff led by Marcus is first class - almost all of them have been with the lodge from the start (nearly 20 years) so there is a sense of real family and connection.   A colleague of mine who has lived in Kathmandu for the past 20 years recommended this gem to me and i can see why.   Escaping the chaos of Kathmandu to the quiet hills and being surrounded by beauty, clean air and the option of relaxed strolls through the local village or an afternoon reading a book with tea while facing the mountains - it was perfect!   But most of the all, the people made it special.  Thank you Marcus and team for making my stay so memorable and for connecting me to such lovely and interesting guests - like Carol below whose birthday i celebrated on my first night there.   I will be back very soon.

What kept me going on the tough 14-day trek up to Lo Mantang in Upper Mustang was the promise of relaxing and recovering in the peace and quiet of TM's Pokhara Lodge.  My four days up at the hilltop lodge, with its chirruping birds and fluttering butterflies, fabulous views of icing sugar mountains in the mornings and twinkling lights at night, were wonderfully restoring.  This was my third visit and, as ever, the staff were so caring and the comfort and cleanliness, delicious meals and drinks were just as I had remembered.  And I really enjoyed the good company of Marcus and the other guests.  Thank you to you all for looking after me and for making me feel very special on my birthday.  Staying at your lodge sums up everything I love about Nepal.

Tiger mountain lodge is amazingly relaxing, an oasis of beauty and organisation and fantastic food in the midst of a fabulously beautiful environment. The chef is splendid, the walks wonderful and the people and enthusiasm for the locale and the villages something to behold. There is a surprising amount to do and you are also on the verge of the Annapurna range and its extraordinary trail.

We stayed here after a grueling six day trek, and what a welcome reward it was! From the moment we disembarked from our jeep, up the steep driveway to the property, our entire group was awed. Literally perched on a mountain top, you have sweeping views from both sides of the mountain. The villas scattered around the property work to maintain privacy, while the beautiful common area has little nooks for privacy, or you can choose to sit on the beautiful verandah, to take in the views, have a drink and rest. The dinner, meanwhile, was delicious, with the tables elegantly set in a non-pretentious way. The villa was beautifully decorated, and again, after our hard work and life in a tent on the trek, the luxurious bed and bathroom was so welcomed!It is truly a retreat - either from the demands that wonderful Nepal asks of you as her traveler, or from the demands that your daily life asks of you. I will certainly return - and might just take in one day in Kathmandu, then come directly back to Tiger Mountain Lodge for three days of beautiful relaxation and rejuvenation.

No other way to describe Tiger Mountain Lodge.  Spectacular setting.  I said I would be back and yes, a very long way for a short cut  but worth all the extra miles for my second visit.  And my room back.  Just like coming home.  Great welcome. Nowhere else will ever be able to come close to the pampering given to all from morning wake up coffee right through the day.  Pre dinner drinks and nibbles get the taste buds going.  Also a good time for a chat.with Dol Raj and Jhalak.Wonderful imaginative food.  Lalu and his team should start cookery lessons.  My attempt at masala rumble tumble went straight in the bin!Hari has infinite patience and steady hands when out walking with non trekkers.  Who needs mountains to climb when TMPL is so close and comfortable?Yes Saga clients seriously miss out.  Such a pity as a two night stay on main tour plus three night extension would be well worth it.Marcus and team.  Very many thanks for yet another fantastic stay.  I will be back, even if under my own steam.M

Beautifully located on a ridge overlooking the valley in front and the mountains above, Tiger Mountain is a perfect retreat for a few days rest. Independent cottages with beautiful sit outs amidst the forest, bird calls and mountain views makes this property special. The eco friendly resort with its own organic vegetable garden and freshly made jams and breads is an experience to be treasured.

We arrived to grey weather and the welcome was as warm as ever! Every single one of the staff here are smiling and welcoming, they treat you like very special guests and the service is wonderful! The chalets each have 2 rooms, so very private...the "wake ip call" come with a person serving you tea or coffee as  ordered the night before...today was early because the mountains" are here"... So in order to enjoy the view you get up really early, it is worth it!The food here is scrumptious, be it Nepali or western...one tends to indulge....

This hotel is super impressive situated on a Hillside of Royal Mountain amazing views of the Mountains Hills listening the Birds music the beautiful individual villas are just stunning as good as the View the service provided was unbeatable to any where else that I were experienced in Nepal food was well presented & tasted the Best ever lovely courtyard to sit on & listen Marcus's stories & contributions for the tourism industries of Nepal is really appreciable & this lodge deserve to be the Top notch High end resort apart from just a Hotel to visit it is very homely & so authentic this property is beyond any stars if you would consider what star this could be look at the Stars on the skies at Night & Count yes indeed a full star Hotel Hands Up to Tiger mountain lodge for Keeping its glory truly a place to visit once in a life time would love to return any time soon THANK YOU ISWOR BASNET manger & all the team really appreciated

I have stayed here a few times before, and it has to be one of my favourite places. This stay just confirmed it as one of my top picks. The Lodge is well elevated above Pokhara where the views are stunning, although on this trip the weather wasn't too kind so we were deprived of the views over the 'Fishtail". However, there is plenty to do from full day walks, to bird watching tours with wonderfully knowledgable naturalists, and of course just plain relaxation. (There is also a pool). The rooms are spread across several acres and are spacious with en-suite bathrooms and balconies.I could go on for an age about the service, which is as good as you will receive anywhere in the world. Breakfast is varied with home made jams and bread. Lunch is a local Nepali fare (absolutely delicious), and dinner is generally roast meat and veg, all served at the table by the wonderful staff. I can't think of any negatives, other than the weather! I have left out so many positives, from the bed tea/ coffee delivered on demand, to the well prepared drinks at the bar. Its an amazing experience where you are bound to meet interesting people coming and going.

At this point in your travels this is the perfect place to be. Whether you've just completed your travels over to begin a trek or are in the middle of your journey you're probably ready for some clean air, beautiful views and sophisticated but understated pampering. The lodge itself sits astride a mountain ridge outside Pokhara allowing views to the north (Himalyas) and south (Pokhara). If your expecting "bling" (flat screens etc) forget it. If your expexting a proper mountain lodge then this is it. Beautiful architecture, natural building materials, total comfort,  privacy and unbelievable scenery. I stayed for 3 days and never tired of the food, on the contrary I was left wondering what's next. Every meal has a local or continental version impeccably prepared and served. The chef and many of the staff have been at  the lodge since it opened and have the food, beverage and service  dialled in. I know this might sound a little ridiculous but I spent 3.5 weeks travelling India and Nepal and this was my favorited place to spend a few days. I guess it was just the perfect place at the right time. Next year we are hoping to do a 2 week trek, this is where we plan to start and end, I can' wait.

Dear Marcus and team, we had such a lovely stay....2 nights just wasn't enough. Fantastic rooms, stunning views, out of this world food, great birdlife, informative nature walks, such friendly locals, a beautiful pool and a world class host. We'll be back.Oli, Sam, Jonathan & Sonya

Another one of a lifetime experience. This is where the British Monarchy stayed for their holidays in Nepal. Managers said this is where Prince Charles decided to propose to Princess Diana. So fine, it feels good. Great view of the Himalayan.

We stayed here for a couple of nights in October 2015.  It was the ideal relaxation before embarking on a trek in the Annapurna region.  The lodge aims to be very eco-friendly and produces much of its own food in the grounds.  Escorted walks are possible; we went on a short 2-hour one and gained an insight into Nepalese rural life.  We stayed in our own bungalow, and took meals and drinks in the main building, which has a bar and restaurant.  The food was excellent!  Our lunches were Nepalese and dinner more European in style, and the breakfasts were huge!  We enjoyed sun-downers and snacks in the evening in the bar, and during power cuts it was romantically candle-lit!  We were woken early with coffee at our room to view the sunrise over the Fishtail mountain - a fabulous sight!  Attentive and friendly staff made our visit perfect.

Having trekked for six days in the hills, Tiger Mountain Lodge was exactly what we needed. We arrived and were immediately offered refreshing drinks whilst sitting on the veranda looking at the stunning scenery.The view was incredible every single day and it was magical to sit out over breakfast and just see the mountains in the distance. The staff were on another level. They were so attentive, willing to do anything (which included making endless amounts of popcorn) and really professional. They knew exactly when we needed something and were polite and chatty. The rooms themselves were fantastic, the beds really comfy and the views stunning. The bathrooms too were much appreciated and the showers were very welcome after the hills!The food was five star: every day was something different and the breakfast especially wonderful. As a vegetarian, they were very accommodating. One more recommendation is to wake up early (around 7am) and go to the pool and look at the view. It was spectacular and such a special way to start the morning. The fact also that the wifi is limited was actually really nice: it was enough to be able to stay in contact but meant that we spent a lot of time together as a family and it was really nice. It really is a place like nowhere else.

Beautiful get-away with friendly staff, I travel often and I had received a service equivalent to a 5 star hotel! The scenery, the food, cleanliness all is way above expectation.Happy hour around the fire and the sunrise wake up service with tea in your lodge was unforgettable 😊It's a must see , I definitely recommend Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge 😊 and the guided cultural walk in the neighboring village is lovely.

Certainly a place to stay in a luxury stile in the Pokhara region.  A well maintained and comfortable place with attention to every detail.  The food is of high quality although the bar is a bit pricey (bring your own booze).  Guided treks and other nature-related activities are on offer.  A good place for bird-watchers, photographers, trekers and generally nature lovers.  Access to Pokhara requires transortation which is a minus and WIFI is not available in rooms.  Otherwise a wonderful stay which wasnot spoiled at all by the fuel crisis - ask for an extra blanket but the hot water bottle provided nightly and morning tea or coffee combined with very hot showers will take care of the cold. A must visit if you are not on a budget

Just outside Pokhara, on a hilltop and away from the blare of the horns, it was just the break I needed in this  stylish lodge in its idyllic setting.  With probably the very best views of the Annapurna mountains the view from my bungalow across the valley to the Fish Tail Mountain was enchanting. It was a lovely clear morning, so certainly a wonderful way to start the day. I'd visited Tiger Mountain Lodge a few years earlier, so I  was delighted to return again  for a weekend. Marcus Cotton, owner of the hotel is excellent company and I enjoyed very much chatting with him over coffee, sitting on the terrace overlooking the magnificent views. As always the food was second to none. Homemade marmalade made from homegrown oranges, salads and creative wraps, local fresh organic coffee, tilapia fish cakes, Moroccan chicken - all the food was delicious and made a welcome change from the usual meals you find in Nepal. On my second morning, I was very glad I'd made the effort to get up at the crack of dawn to spend some time to admire the early morning sun and mountain views, and to stroll around the gardens birdwatching for an hour or so with Hari, one of the Lodge's three very knowledgeable resident nature guides. The staff here are attentive in the nicest, friendlies but unobtrusive way. I felt very spoilt, totally relaxed and was very sorry when I had to leave.

It is impossible to describe Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge.  The scenery is breath taking, the food deliciously superb, the ambiance and staff first class.  As a disabled person I (Allan) greatly appreciated having the bungalow closest to the main building.  Marcus and his staff could not have been kinder or more considerate.  Wish we could have stayed longer. As we are not exactly in the first flush of youth, it is unlikely that we will visit Nepal again but if we do we will certainly visit Tiger Mountain again.  We wish Marcus and his team every success for the future.  Sandra and Allan

Have stayed in TIger Mountain Pokhara Lodge a couple of times and it will be returned to. It is situated in a high position on the top of a hill affording the most wonderful views of the Annapurna range. The lodge is a place of calm, has beautifully designed rooms, a pool in a stunning setting where you can swim facing the Himalayas and the food provided is consistently the best I have had in the area. Various activities are available or you can read by the wonderful pool.

this lodge goes from strength to strength under the management of Marcus ...only had a few days this time after trekking but what a welcome...the crew under Marcus are great and nothing is too much trouble.cannot wait to get back......the road up to the lodge gives you a free massage as well !!!!!!..Saga clients are missing out on a wonderful experience..

Very attractive lodge with a wonderful view of the mountains weather permitting.  Arrived here after a 4 day trek and it was heaven to enjoy a hot shower, delicious meal and very comfortable room.  Very attentive staff providing a great welcome and stay.

You travel outside the city of Pokhara and up into the surrounding hills to get to this lovely property, which is situated high up to give outstanding views of the surrounding countryside and the Annapurna range of the Himalayas.  While it was overcast the entire few days we were at the hotel, we hear the view of the mountains is to die for!  The cabin-style rooms are quiet, clean, spacious, and well-appointed.  The restaurant and lounge area is beautiful, and the service absolutely outstanding.  Breakfast is delicious and served right to your table, while lunch is an outstanding buffet - though we saw others who ordered specific lunch dishes such as salads and sandwiches where they did not want to have the Nepali-style buffet.  Dinners are served family-style at the table, so while there is a "set" menu each night, the staff very easily accommodated my particular dietary preferences, and would have something additional prepared where the main meal was not something I eat (e.g., beef).  There is a pool which is a bit of a short walk through the grass and away from the rooms and main building, but it is nice enough...though cold!  (I'm sure that cold water feels great after some time in hot weather, though!)  You are also able to arrange for guided hikes in the immediate area, with a naturalist staff member who will explain the local flora and fauna.  The only downside to those hikes is not related to the hotel itself - it's that as you walk through the area and some of the little villages built into the surrounding hillside, you still encounter the litter that is endemic to Nepal pretty much everywhere, despite it being a mostly natural area.  It made me wish I'd brought a garbage bag along on the hike, as it truly breaks my heart to see litter in nature.  The staff at Tiger Mountain is also outstanding, including Marcus the hotel manager, who goes out of his way to personally greet new guests and ensure they feel welcome.  We would recommend this hotel to anyone.

Firstly, my apologies, as my review comes in very late. We travelled as a family of 5 and had planned a one-night stay at Tiger Mountain in late March. The moment we stepped into the lodge, its location took our breath away. Looking down at the valley below and the clouds in the distance, my family was instantly taken with the property. I, of course, had ulterior motives, Tiger Mountain is renowned to be one of the best birding destinations in Nepal. We were welcomed very warmly by Jhalak, the property's customer service manager who gave us a complete overview of the property. We had arrived at lunchtime, so after taking our lunch (all freshly made, the highlight of which was the tomato chutney), we retired to our rooms where the view was equally marvelous if not more. However, my birding for the afternoon did not go quite to plan. Heavy rain and hail! My family were enjoying the weather from the comfort of the room though, so I was a happy camper. As soon as the heavens calmed down, I quickly made my way to meet up with Hari, and we made our way to do a quick hour of birding before the sun set. Great and Blue-throated Barbets could be constantly be heard singing around the property. Grey Treepie, Red-Billed Blue Magpie, Crimson Sunbird, Chestnut-bellied Nuthatch, Blue-winged Minla, Golden Spectacled Warbler were some of the other catches as we walked around the property. As the sun set and it grew dark,  and with thunder and lightning, we rested around the cozy fireplace in the main hall, and interacted with a few of they guests regarding their stay. As my family had some specific food requirements, the hotel stage were kind enough us to whip us something when the regular meal choices didn't make sense. At night once the weather had settled, Hari brought me out to listen to the haunting call of the Mountain Scops Owl, and since I had a flashlight, he said I could try my luck to catch the eye shine of a wandering yellow-throated marten (no luck there!). Next morning, I was up again to go with Hari, and after a quick clouded view of the Himalayas, we were off. We saw many more species, including the Khaleej pheasant scurrying away from the owner's bungalow into the forest. Truly a birder's paradise this. Jhalak and all the other staff ensured throughout our stay that we were well looked after (Jhalak, I did mention you to Jitudai at Chitwan, he beamed brightly when he heard yours and Hari's name). All in all, a wonderful stay, cozy, relaxing and for an amateur birder, downright enjoyable :)

Marcus, I said that and more in your guest book.  It's very difficult to put into words what an absolutely spectacular place to spend a few days.  Would have preferred the six.  Wonderful welcome from all.  Tea with home baking on arrival is a very good start. Pampering at best.  Nothing was any bother.  We didn't feel as though staying at a hotel.I know we were lucky weather wise.  Breakfast with that view, oh boy, plus homemade bread. Cannot go wrong.My wildlife pics are thanks to Hari rather than me.  He has good eyesight.My fellow travelers have the same opinion.  We are still swapping pics.I said I would be back and I will.  Perhaps not with the same tour operator as, yes, itinerary has changed.Very many thanks to you and the boys.  Also my cake  and pressie

While visiting this wonderful lodge with it's secluded, private chalet, stunning views and peace and quiet I was out for a walk, slipped and fell and tore a muscle in my leg. The LandRover came to fetch me, the Kitchen staff provided me with a constant supply of carefully wrapped ice packs and Marcus a goodly supply of Ibuprofen. Of all the things that went right that weekend it was the one time something went wrong for me that the true nature of this hospitable lodge, beautifully sited lodge and it's staff came to light.

We stayed here for 2 nights after two great days hiking. Our welcome was lukewarm and the manager very smiley but hesitant.  Our rooms were nice but there was noise all around and horrid smoke fires from the neighbours behind.  We were very tired and sore when we arrived and we were looking forward to the yoga and massages at Tiger Mountain. It was advertised to us as " an oasis so peace and relaxation" but sadly no yoga or massage was available on site. This was blamed on the strike as no workers could be transported to the hotel. We had delicious Nepali lunch but sadly no Nepali dinner choice amongst average European fare. Breakfast on the terrace with the stunning views was the highlight but the mountain lodges provided the same view with cosy and calm atmosphere and no pretence.Perhaps our expectations were set too high.

This was a beautifully positioned property which exceeded all our expectations. The staff could not have been more helpful or pleasant. The food was delicious and there was plenty of it. The views of the mountains were breath-taking and the sunrise over Fishtail Mt will live with me forever. If the early morning was clear,we were wakened with tea and biscuits so we could get up and see the sunrise. How thoughtful was that? The guided walks were slightly challenging but thoroughly enjoyable. Guides were pleasant and knowlegeable and we met many of the friendly locals.The rooms were very clean and comfortable and the grounds were a joy to explore. We were so sad to leave this gem of Nepal.

Visitors to Tiger Mountain Lodge are rewarded with outstanding views of the Annapurna range which alone makes any visit to the Lodge worthwhile and if Macchapucharre happens to be hiding behind a veil of cloud then just relax with a cup of lemongrass tea and cake (or something stronger) and take in the valley until the mountain shows itself again. The team at  the Lodge operates to a very high standard, the care and attention each party receives from the ever mindful Jhalak   is extraordinary. Hiking options include short bird watching walks (there are some impressive looking and sounding birds around), day hikes to some nearby (or distant) villages or longer treks lasting several days. There is an entire menu of activities to choose from including massages but alas our three nights and four days was not long enough to sample everything. We thoroughly enjoyed the 6/7 hour walks to the monastery and Gurung village and other settlements on the other side of the valley. Our guide seemed to know everyone (old and young) in the various villages along the way and this gave us a very special insight into the lives of the people who live up here. Staying at Tiger Mountain felt more like visiting family rather than a lodge. There is no menu, instead the kitchen produces the most terrific dishes at every meal. Any dietary requirements are noted during the briefing when you arrive. The accommodation is clean, private and comfortable and each lodge seems to provide an impressive view of the mountains. Our cottage was some distance from the main lodge down a very pleasant and well maintained route lit by oil lamps in the evening.Supper is preceded by drinks and canapés in the bar where you can catch-up on the day's adventures and meet other guests. Tiger Mountain is run by people that take great pride in what they do and have every reason to be proud of what they have. I look forward to visiting again.

I have been pondering how to make this review useful to other travellers but my views are so coloured by what I considered to be the most wonderful experience of staying here that this review will be blinded by subjectivity.  Our stay started well - we arrived from Pokhara rather too late for lunch but were told to sit down anyway and, as if by magic, lunch appeared.  It was the best meal we had in Nepal – sitting on the terrace in the sunshine looking out over the Pokhara valley (and that was before the mountains appeared out of the clouds!), with the most delicious selection of food.  I will remember it forever. The rest of our stay continued in the same vein, with so many superlatives required at every turn, that it is almost invidious to mention anything: the entrance that is aligned to frame ‘Fish-Tail’ mountain, the infinity pool that perfectly reflects the mountains, the view from our room, the beautifully tended vegetable garden, the bird life, looking at the sun setting behind the Peace Pagoda in the distance, discovering that one could have a perfectly made Pimms to accompany the sunset, with freshly cooked canapes – I could go on….  Marcus and the team made us feel like friends staying, rather than customers, and that their only desire was our enjoyment – the whole stay was a real treat.  Our only complaint was that we had not booked for long enough – two nights was simply not enough.(In an attempt to be slightly helpful, I should perhaps stress that this is a lodge, not a hotel, and the rooms and facilities are excellent bearing this in mind, but if you want glitz go to Las Vegas!)

What an amazing place!! Once you get there you are truly rewarded by excellent service, second to none. Marcus the MD personally oversees your stay from the early morning tea delivered to your lodge through the Nepalise lunch, afternoon tea and the the wonderful dinner and all points in between. The organised walks take you out onto the mountain side and are well tailored to the abilities of the walkers. The best view from a swimming pool ever!

We stayed at Tiger Mountain Lodge for 4 nights and cannot recommend a stay here highly enough. The self contained lodges are comfortable and offer spectacular views of the Annapurnas. Another highlight of our stay was the food - with both Nepalese and continental options to choose from we were spoiled for choice and the quality of the food was excellent and plentiful! I cannot speak highly enough of the Tiger Mountain staff - from their assistance with booking domestic flights, organising yoga tuition and pick ups, nothing was too much trouble. The hot water bottles that were placed in our bed each evening were an added (and much welcomed) bonus. We wouldn't consider staying anywhere else in Pokhara when we return.

We arrived at Tiger Mountain Lodge after a fairly tough 5 days of trekking. We were greeted with cool drinks, home-made biscuits and a spectacular view - we knew we were going to enjoy our time here. The lodge is extremely comfortable with an eco-friendly outlook. The set meals and buffet lunches are simply delicious with most of the ingredients grown in the gardens of the property. Our group - 4 adults and 3 children, (11,11 and 13), enjoyed the large open living room with the central fire where delicious pre-dinner snacks are served as well as unlimited tea, coffee, hot chocolate at any time of the day. We were there in February so the nights were a little chilly which made the appearance of the hot water bottles in our beds upon our return from dinner a very welcome and thoughtful touch. The staff were wonderful and in particular our guide, one of the managers, who took my friend and I on a very informative and fun 3 hour walk one morning. I would love to return one day.

This wonderful lodge with its beautifully appointed, private cottages each strategically positioned for majestic views of the Himalayas was one of the highlights of my entire trip. It is exemplary for creating a high end experience with minimal impact on this pristine environment something that I value and support when I travel.  Here  I was treated like a VIP.  I was traveling alone, but never had to dine alone as the Managing Director made certain that I had company.  My interest was birding and I had two excellent guides who took me birding as often and for as long as I wished.  We got over 90 species in 3 days.  But my "program" could have been tailored to any one of several interests and there was staff available to accommodate a variety of activities. The food was excellent, including the picnic lunch provided for our outings. I stayed three nights and would encourage anyone traveling in Nepal to take the time to enjoy a retreat at Tiger Mountain away from the noise and tourist shops of Kathmandu and Pokara.

If you are going to Pokhara and wondering where is the best place to stay? I would certainly recommend Tiger Mountain lodge. I stayed at Fish Tail for one night and Tiger Mountain lodge for a night, and there is huge difference between these two. It certainly worth the time and effort to drive up to the mountain, it is relaxing with good view, while Fishtail is centrally located but indeed old.Tiger Mountain lodge is run by a british gentleman. You will not find it surprising to find british taste in deco and cuisine.Unfortunitely, it was very cloudy and rainy when I was there and did not get to enjoy the specular view.If you are searching for hotels in Kathmandu and other location, I would highly recommend Dwarika's group.

Away from the bustle of Pokhara town, Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge is perched strategically to offer the most stunning panoramic view of the entire Annapurna Range, including the unique Fishtail which has never been climbed, allegedly. Accommodation is in collection of "cottages" designed to meld into the landscape, allowing you to marvel at the sights of the himalayas, which is exactly why you chose this place. Based here, you can walk in the surrounding hills with a guide and a picnic lunch accompanying you. When the days are warm, the inviting infinity pool will provide a refreshing plunge with the himalayas always within your sight. The food is fresh; no reheated frozen food here. If you are interested in plants, birds and butterflies, you will get plenty of opportunities to observe them.

Just returned from two nights at this wonderful lodge. The view of the mountains is spectacular and the architects have done a super job in maximising the impact. Excellent craftsmanship in the wood work. The attention to detail made our stay extremely comfortable.torches by the bedside and hot water bottles for the night for instance. Staff was always on hand for anything we needed and yet were unobtrusive with their presence. Farm fresh veggies, lake fish,home made cakes and jams and chutneys made for finger licking good meals. We had a gentle walk through the forest and villages with a lot of bird spotting thanks to our guide. The star studded sky at night left us speechless! Thanks to Marcus, Jhalak, Laloo, Sajjan and all the other staff who were so welcoming. Look forward to being back again!

During the stay, we were the only guests in the hotel, which the employees didn't like very much.     During our whole stay we didn't have hot weather to shower.The room is not cozy, and it's very cold, the bed and the blankets smell terrible, and it's not comfortable.      We had a good time because of the place, not because the hotel. Not recommendable.

Beautiful resort set on the top of a hill in a remote place (about 30 minute drive to Pokhara). From the terrace of the hotel you will enjoy a fantastic view on the Annapura mountains. Excellent service and the best food in Nepal, especially the newari cuisine. I really enjoyed staying at this resort.

Tiger Mountain Lodge has to have one of the best locations in Nepal - the views of the Annapurna range are stunning from the main lodge, infinity pool and (in our case) rooms.  The resort is very sympathetically incorporated into the landscape and serious efforts are made to reduce its environmental impact - so don't expect A/c, TVs or minibars.  There is a sense that the lodge is just as it was when it opened 16 years ago and as a result seems a little dated.  Likewise the food, though good, smacks of the institutional, especially at dinner.  With a little updating this would be a five star experience.

stayed 3 nights in villa 16, which unfortunately didn't have the best view. I'd ask for a different room next time. food is served three times a day and are pretty good, at 730am, 1230pm, and 730pm. very attentive staff and you can get complimentary coffee and tea all day. they also have complimentary guided hikes, which I did a short impromptu one and they accommodated quite nicely. best part of course is getting up by 6am to see the sunrise hit the mountains. from certain spots, you can see the whole Annapurna circuit and it's pretty awesome. I spent most of my time with a book outside staring out at the mountains. I also took advantage of a massage and a meditation session, which I found to be both quite good, costing $62 USD + tip. another highlight is at dinner, since I was traveling by myself, you are seated with others or can sit where you like.
