I had the fortunate luck of sitting with the owner of the lodge, Marcus, who is very interesting and nice, as well as other very nice guests.

We spent three nights here.  The setting is amazing, the views unforegettable and the whole team provide a service level that is superb.  It really is a pleasure to stay here.  The lodges are a good size, clean cormfortable and charming, the food tasty and interesting, beer and wine were right on the mark and the guides excellent.  The pool must have one of the best settings on the planet.  iI the foothils of the Himalayas, with the clouds below you and the snow capped mountains above it does feel like a small piece of heaven on Earth and the comfort is certainly  more than anybody could reasonably want.  Great place for Children I think especialy if teamed up with a trip to Tiger Tops in Chitwan.  My tip and I didnt get as far as I would have liked would be at some point to walk out of the lodge and turn left and walk a little or catch the local bus for a few stops and head back.  One of the great pleasures as well as the mountains is the local people. Such a well run place and the staff so good in such an amazing location.  You will have guessed that we liked it !

We had an unforgettable 4 days with Marcus and his team. This is a lovely place to relax. Accommodation is in cottages with full amenities including a balcony with spectacular views of the Annapurna range. The best view is from the beautifully landscaped swimming pool. We enjoyed the imaginative cuisine and the lovely gentle service from all the staff. Worth putting up with terrible local roads to reach this little oasis of peace

We stayed for 2 nights during a tour of Nepal.  This hotel is managed by a British gentleman who is very much hands-on and this is reflected in the excellent service and attention to detail.  Lodges are dotted around the area and very private.  The location is amazing, peaceful and quiet and we had a great view of the Annapurna range from the seating area outside our lodge.  It is quite a surreal experience to bob around in the pool in the warm sun surrounded by palm trees, and to see huge snow-covered mountains in the distance!  And don't miss sunset from either the terrace or the pool area. The room was huge with a good shower and lots of hot water.  The room has a fan but it was cooler in the evenings so it was not used.  Our room had both a king-size bed and a single and there was still plenty of room to move around.  The beds are very firm and had mosquito nets but we also used a plug/tablet as an extra precaution.  Torches and umbrellas are provided for getting to the main dining/bar/reception area; and large thermoses of purified water are left in the rooms.  The staff are attentive, friendly and polite; nothing is too much trouble and we really enjoyed a 3-hour local walk with our guide on the second morning .  The food was a definite highlight for us - breakfast is cooked to order along with home-made bread, lunch was a delicious Nepali curry with assorted vegetables and freshly-made breads, and dinner was a choice between Western and Nepali - we chose Nepali once again as it was so good.  However, the extras set this hotel apart - tea/coffee and cakes on the terrace every afternoon, plus our favourite - delicious snacks with pre-dinner drinks.  On the first night we had cheese biscuits warm from the oven, cauli pakoras with spicy dip and handmade crisps and on the second, aubergine pakoras and momos.  They were all irresistible and we were almost too full to appreciate our dinner!  Free Wi-Fi in the bar area but don't bother - just enjoy the peace and quiet, relax and be looked after.

Stayed here for 2 nights after 5 days hiking what a treat .The rooms were large and comfortable with bathrooms with lots of hot water.Tea/coffee was brought to your room every morning at your stipulated time .Breakfast was a delight with amazing views followed by a Nepalese curry at lunchtime,then afternoon tea and cakes followed by dinner which was western food or you can request Nepalese food, all excellent.The infinity pool has amazing views and never too busy.It was the ideal place to rest and relax highly recommended.The staff were all helpful and attentive and the grounds immaculate.

After Trekking in Bhutan and before embarking on a "Tea House Trek in Nepal, our group  of three stayed here for one night. We wished we had more time to stay longer. The staff was extremely attentive and Markus went out of his way to welcome us to his retreat. The cabins were well appointed for such a location. The food was first rate. The sunset and sunrise views were spectacular, especially by the pool. Getting up to the lodge was a bit of an adventure given the bumpy road, but that has to be expected when one wants to "get away from it all" in Nepal. The location was convenient to Pokhara and to the starting point for our Tea House Trek.

We very much enjoyed our stay at Tiger Mountain Lodge. The peace and quiet is lovely for a couple of nights. The gardens and pool are beautiful and the views stunning. We did not go on any of the walks as we had just returned from a trek but other guests told us they were very enjoyable.The staff went out of their way to provide us with a Nepali meal on our last night which was much appreciated. If there were any power outages we diddn't notice and who needs a television when there are spectacular views.

This place is run like clockwork - almost a military operation with staff who are uniformly happy, friendly and knowledgeable. Nothing was too much for them.We arrived at the mountain lodge to a spectacular view after four and a half hours on the road. Nothing more to do that day than eat a Nepali lunch of curried eggs … wonderful food. Evening meal was served in the main lodge, indoors, and was a European meal, of lamb stew which was excellent, and then it was off to bed for an early night, as tomorrow we planned to get up at 0530 to watch the sunrise and the light come down the mountain tops if clear. The bed has nets but we hardly saw an insect at all at this altitude.0530 came all too quickly, and we were awaken by tea and hot chocolate delivered to our room by a steward - he confirmed that the sky was cloudless. Ten minutes later we were up sitting by the pool, with a few other hardy souls, watching the sun come up behind us, and light up the face of the Annapurna range. We stayed up watching the light moving until about 0700 when we went to the lodge for more tea and chocolate before returning to our room to shower before breakfast. After breakfast, we headed out around Tiger Mountain for a three hour walk through the countryside and villages,  it was a mix of flat and gentle hills and nothing strenuous. We passed along tiny footpaths around the edge of fields, through farms and fields with the guide pointing out all the wildlife en route. We arrived back at the lodge, somewhat sweaty and ready for a shower as it was very hot at times with the occasional cool breeze. Three miles loop and not too much steep climbs.Lunch was the usual Nepalese curry - our last, as we decided that having curry at lunchtime didn't agree with us. We did nothing in the afternoon but watch the scenery and sit in the lounge looking out. The rooms are very well decorated and remote from the main building - wind up torches helfully provided as you will need them to move around the paths.Plenty of hot water (the usual warnings), and the quietness of a remote hillside.

What an absolutely wonderful place. Waking up in the morning to freshly delivered tea to our villa then sitting and watching the dawning light on the Anapurna mountains is just idyllic. The staff are abosultely wonderful. Our guide Janek who is also the customer relations manager took care of every little detail. We were really spoiled.Great treks configured to what we could deal with. Loved going through the little villages.Great job Marcus and your entire team.

This hotel comes as near to perfection as I can imagine. The most magnificent views, lovely lodges and wonderful staff who are totally committed to making your stay as enjoyable as possible make a stay here an unforgettable experience . An important tip: this hotel has truly wonderful staff and several sightseeing tours and the journey to and from the airport are included in your room rate. So if you decide to stay here contact the hotel direct to arrange your sightseeing in the Pokhara area, rather than using  local tourist agencies.

While this resort is a little way outside Pokhara, don't be in the slightest put off.The location is magnificent and you will be wonderfully well looked after by Marcus and his team whose sole focus is to anticipate and address your very need.Granted, there may be brief power outages before the generator kicks in after minimal delay, and alright there is no TV. But, apart from very minor possible quibbles, this is a great place at which to spend a few days.Finally, make sure you take full advantage of the resort's included packages of guided activities, transportation etc.An Excellent rating is quite clear.

Don't even consider staying somewhere else! This is the place to be. We loved our little cottage #13 on the corner with an awesome view. The Mosquitos were fierce so we didn't get the chance to enjoy sitting on our porch as much as we would have liked. We did walks around the villages and on various trails and saw lots of birds and butterflies. The sun rise view at the pool is so incredible! There is nothing like watching the sun light up the Himalayas peak by peak. The kitchen staff did a great job accommodating us for gluten free meals and we really enjoyed the fresh food with lots of greens. The hotel even packed us a box lunch on the day we left that included a cucumber stuffed with curry chicken salad...delicious. We were sad to leave this place.

There are many reasons to recommend Tiger Mountain, views of the mountains and surrounding valleys, the pool, the lovely rooms each with a unique view, and the attentive staff that will wake you early (if you wish) to see sunrise strike the peaks. Special guides will take you through the hills to see birds, butterflies and villages. It is a very quiet place and you can enjoy a good rest or be out walking every day. The lunch and dinner offer of dal bhat is very basic and needs more variety but if asked to do so I am sure they will make what ever you want. Also on offer is a western meal for lunch and dinner that varies every day, here too some innovations would be desired. Fruit and vegetable selection will vary on the time of year since everything is seasonal.

The lodges are natural and well equipped, Nepali mountain top style. The food, which is all inclusive, is all made onsite - homemade breads, toasted rice muesli, paneer, dahl. Sustainability is key and vegetables are grown onsite to serve the menu. More than that, however, is the feeling of peace and tranquility, high up in clear air with bird song around, staff unheard along the grass paths. Service is gentle and personal.The 5.30am rise to sit and watch the sun rise over the Annapurna Range....you have to do it!! Utterly breathtaking and will remain an unforgettable experience. This place left me a little tearful to be leaving.

Was not too happy! Maybe because it was off season they didn't have the best staff may be!I almost lost it when the manager pulled a chair and sat at our table when me and my huaband were having a quite lunch by ourselves. Found the staff too intrusive. Would linger around for way too long . Maybe they should just close down the space for the off season!

First of all, the location of the property is gorgeous. Secondly, a very well designed ground plan. From all the cottages, the view is beautiful. Very tasty food and a wonderful kitchen staff - friendly, polite and efficient. The infinity pool has a surreal view of the Annapurna & Machapuchare range, almost surreal. Surrounded by birds, insects. flowers and a wide range of plants and trees, the place is therapeutic. Okay, those were the positives.Now the not so positives. Our cottage was not serviced - a horrible musty odor greeted us. The washroom trash wasn't cleared and the room not dusted at all. The housekeeping needs some serious socks pulling, funnily though our cottage was being spruced up the day we were checking out. Anyways, in that tariff category, one would expect a more professional housekeeping department. Definitely worth a visit though....carry some room deodorizers....just in case.

Spent 3 nights at Tiger mountain lodge, and this was sheer delight. A true haven for the ultimate relaxation and peace of mind. Very well kept lodge and very well run. Most of the produce comes from the very well kept vegetable garden and this adds to the excellence of the food served. From breakfast to dinner one is not left disappointed. Rooms are spacious with a nice shower, however hot water not always guaranteed. The lodge is very Eco-friendly and using solar, heisting, mains and generators. Wifi is a bit temperamental but Ncell units available at NR500 per day for usage in rooms. Lovely swimming pool with awesome view but water is cold, so brace yourself! Torches, walking sticks and hats available. Daily activities arranged to suit your needs. Staff very attentive and service very personalised . The only suggestion I would like to make is to provide a daily menu specifying the price for lunch and dinner, as breakfast is included. Now this is not a big deal, but I personally don't like not knowing what to expect when the final bill arrives.  This place is a real gem, so close to nature and it is well worth the money. Highly recommended. Ps bring comfortable walking shoes, no place for your gorgeous CL's!

No matter how long you are able to stay here, it will leave you wishing it had been for longer. Words cannot begin to convey how special this place is. From its breathtaking location at the top of a ridge with views that will simply leave you spellbound, to the warmth and friendliness of the staff who make you feel completely at home. The tastefully furnished and decorated cottages dotted around the grounds cater for all your needs and are extremely comfortable. But it’s the attention to detail that can even take you by surprise as desires you hadn’t yet thought of, have already been preempted. My personal favourite was the hot water bottle found in my bed on a chilly night. The quintessential service is highly professional and yet personal. The cuisine is not only organic and plentiful but utterly delicious.  There’s lots to do with wonderful guided walks, or you can just relax by the infinity pool with its amazing views of the Himalayas. I’ve always held the opinion never to go back to the same place twice when there are so many new ones yet to see.. but for Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge, I may have to make an exception…

We spent 2 nights here truncated by 2 nights of trekking a few hours from Pokhara. The Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge is a lovely getaway /  relaxing venue with first class service, food, and location. Enjoyed soaking up the mountain air, mountain views, early morning sunrises, birdwatching, and getting away from the big cities. This Lodge is highly recommended for at least 2 nights stay. You always meet interesting fellow travellers and the staff are delightful.

One of the highlights of Pokhara is staying at Tiger Mountain.  It is a beautiful property with awesome views of the Himalayas.  A must is experiencing sunrise by their infinity pool.  The Himalayas slowly come to light and their reflection appears in the pool.  The individual cottages are comfortable with private verandas and views.   There are a lot of walking trails around the property, where you can visit local village and get an idea of life in the imountains. Their staff, led by Marcus Cotton, is very friendly and professional.  The food is all organic and much of it is grown in gardens on the property.  I expressed an interest in ingredients and preparation and they arranged for me to meet the chefs and have a cooking class.  It does take about a half hour up a very poor road to get to Tiger Mountain.  It is well worth the ride - once you get there you won't want to leave

I have been traveling to Nepal for over 15 years for business and on my recent trip I brought my wife and friends for some leisure travel outside of the Kathmandu valley.  We were looking for comfort, adventure and eccentricity and we found it in one of the best hotels on earth.  There is nothing that can be said about the views, you must be woken by the exceptional staff with a pot of coffee or tea to watch the sunrise over the Annapurna range with your own eyes.  The natural beauty of the area is enhanced by the cottages that give you privacy, a sense of living in a local village, and luxury.  How they pull it off is simply amazing.  The food was perfect, the guides knowledgable, friendly, welcoming, and well known in the local villages allowing you to take hikes through the area and be greeted with smiles and joy by everyone.  There is something amazing about the comfort and luxury of this destination hotel, nestled at the end of a very rough road with views that are out of this world.  The dichotomy of rustic living (limited power and unlit pathways) and totally pampering by the staff is what makes this hotel worth the price and the trip.  Thank you!

We stayed at the Tiger Palace resort on a recent family vacation in May, 2019.  Tiger Palace bills itself as a 5 star resort.  It is certainly a nice place to spend some time, but "5 stars" is a bit of hyperbole.  The resort has a great pool, a casino and a spa; however, there are limited dining options and the resort is isolated.  The overall ambiance in the lobby and guest rooms is more aligned to mid-tier business hotels in the United States (e.g., Marriott Courtyard) vs. a luxury resort (e.g., Ritz Carlton). In general, the resort is nice and clean.  The rooms are a reasonable size with modern decor - they come complete with a bed, desk, dresser, flat screen TV, etc.  The overall room is reminiscent of a Marriott Courtyard or a Four Points by Sheraton, rather than a luxury resort.  The plug points are "universal", where they can accept plug points from India, the United States, Europe, etc.  However, the US plugs did not work well as the outlets were too "loose" and the plugs would not stay put.  The Indian plug points worked OK and I suspect that the Indian plug points loosened the outlet contacts making other plug points more difficult to use.Although the resort reports 3 restaurants - Cabana Avenue (pool bar), Ramro Chowk (main cafe) and Jackpot Buffet (buffet in the casino) - the actual options were a bit more limited.  Ramro Chowk, the main restaurant, specializes in Indian / Nepali cuisine.  Ramro Chowk had buffets available for breakfast, lunch and dinner along with a la carte items.  The buffet was much more economical than the a la carte items.  In general, the quality of the food was good and had decent variety.  The seasoning of the food skewed towards Indian / Nepali standards and western palettes may find it a bit spicy.  The Jackpot Buffet was in the casino and seemed to have some of the same items from Ramro Chowk.  I had dropped by a couple of times and found the buffet in Ramro Chowk to be much more diverse and appetizing.  Cabana Avenue, the pool bar and cafe, had a limited menu and was aimed primarily at drinks / snacks for the pool area.For a resort, the hotel had two primary amenities - a pool and a casino.  The pool is rather large and has a depth of about 5 feet.  They have a lifeguard on duty for most of the day.  The Casino had the usual blackjack, slot machines, roulette, etc.  The roulette table had a tv screen with the statistics from the last 100 spins (e.g., red / black split, even / odd split, etc.) to help with betting.  Tiger Palace also had some entertainment in the resort, such as singers and dancers.  The resort also has a spa, which some of the party enjoyed using.Service at the resort was quite good, whether in the restaurants, catering or front desk.  The staff has solid English skills.  I had to call the hotel to get the address for a Nepali visa and they were helpful in helping me get the form filled out.Tiger Palace is located about 0.5 kilometers from the road and there are limited shops and restaurants in the vicinity.  The resort is not directly accessible to any natural scenery, such as a beach or mountains.  As a result, one will likely spend most of their time at the resort.  If one enjoys gambling or being at the pool, then Tiger Palace will be a great place to spend some time.  If one is looking for more amenities, greater luxury or more dining options, then they may find Tiger Palace a bit limiting.

When I found this resort online, I really wondered if it was as good as they claimed, and the pictures represented. I was really shocked, it was better. It was a pleasure to explore, from the beautiful lobby to the giant, winding swimming pool. Didn’t go into the spa, but used the fitness center every day, which wasn’t huge, but very adequate. The all-you-can-eat restaurant in the hotel (Not the one in the casino) had both Asian and Western dishes, and they were both high quality. The desserts were off the charts. It was like a whole pastry shop, just take what you want. The rooms were sizable as I looked at both the deluxe room and the suite before choosing. I took the suite because it really wasn’t that much more. Both rooms had everything you’d expect from a four or five star hotel: a safe, laundry bag, numerous bathroom amenities, a patio, and plenty of bottled water. The customer service was excellent, with people constantly asking to help you. The casino was sizable and the bar there seemed to be open 24 hours, but get this: all the drinks appear to be complimentary. No playing bartop slots, no players card to show. I had three glasses of wine while working on my phone, and was shocked when the bartender said I owed nothing. If I have any complaint about this excellent property, it is the gift shop, which looks more like a bargain clothes store than a hotel gift shop. A sign does indicate that the shop is not associated with the hotel, but not a single souvenir that says “Nepal” or “Tiger Palace”. I would have bought anything that had the nice, Tiger logo this place has. All in all, a great property that doesn’t cost much.

There are a multitude of places in Nepal that you can take some much needed rest and recreation but none so far have matched my experience at this Australian brand resort facility.From its clean line architecture that blends well with vast compound setting far from the main highway, to the sincere intent of the all-Nepali staff to please their guests, the very well-appointed rooms, the expansive lagoon pool, the Cabana and Ramro Chowk restaurants and the availability of the casino for foreigners, this facility is A+.Yes, this is not a faultless review but whatever fault one may find it is somehow compensated with something else. For example, when we arrived at 2 pm for our check-in, our suite was not ready due to full occupancy the night before. The front desk manager placed us temporarily to a Deluxe King Room. 3 hours later the suite wasn’t quite ready and as I made my way to speak with the manager again, to compensate for this inconvenience, we were given a late checkout option which we took on our last day. That was a good compromise I must admit. Operational improvements are necessary though.The suite has a direct pool access which was a delight for all of us including our 2-year old fearless boy who was ready to jump into the pool anytime! The amenities are plenty and the one I love in particular is having the quality iron/ironing board inside the cabinets (this is a room essential for me), and hairdryer too. The sofa was very comfortable and the extra bed had quality mattress as well. Satellite channels are wide-ranging on a large LED tv.Saying no further, this is a MUST try in Nepal. The price range is $$$ (and can go higher) which is beyond the local public’s affordability but a 3days-2nights experience is a minimum take in this facility.I would love to come back. As usual, I recommend tipping the room cleaning staff tandem as always. As foreigners, meet them (they are our Nepali hosts as well) and address them by their names because that is an encouraging gesture.

My wife and I needed a break from the summer Terai heat and had seen many of Tiger Palace’s enticing facebook posts, so we decided to try it for a night. I noticed the room price in person, on their website, and at online 3rd party travel agents varied some. I usually like to book directly and give 100% of my money to the hotel, cutting out the middleman, but that didn’t seem to matter at Tiger Palace. Next time I might spend some time in advance researching the best room price and where to book.  We opted for the standard room which was well appointed and extremely clean. The AC was wonderful. Wi-fi in the room averaged around 3mbps. Great lighting and a beautiful TV. Off of the room service menu, we ordered two Ramro Lamb Burgers. They were fantastic! The burgers even came topped with extra ingredients which weren’t listed on the menu. Wanted to try the Mediterranean pizza for dinner, but was too full from lunch, so now we have an excuse to go back. The pool and swim-up bar were clean and relaxing.  At the poolside Cabana Avenue restaurant, we both ordered the Thai Basil Sangria which was delicious, and surprisingly very strong. We took the server's recommendation and ordered the volcano prawns which were tasty and lived up to the hype. After a good night's sleep, we thoroughly enjoyed the breakfast buffet. The occasional calls to the room to check on our stay were a nice touch. Everyone was so eager to offer assistance or a warm smile. It would have been nice to have an information book somewhere in the room outlining the times and locations of restaurants and amenities around the resort. However I had fun exploring, and there was always someone nearby to answer a question if necessary.  Can’t wait to go back. The service from check-in to check-out was very professional and intuitive. I’ve seen many Hotel and Restaurant employees become almost mechanical even after hospitality training, serving guests as a computerized machine would.  Happily that wasn't the case at Tiger Palace, however, the rigid computerized billing system still slows things down a little and leads to a few hiccups here and there.  Tiger Palace offers so many delicious flavors that in my opinion can’t be found anywhere else in Nepal, I’ve looked! We are looking forward to trying the cream brûlée next time too.

This is my fourth time visiting this award-winning eco lodge in Chitwan. (Tiger Tops won the “Most Inspiring Eco Lodge” award in 2018.)Tiger Tops is also Nepal’s first elephant-friendly venue which completely stopped elephant rides and released them from chains after building beautiful and spacious solar-powered corrals for them. It is also the only lodge in the country recommended by World Animal Protection USThey cater to different diets, including vegan. They’re also low emissions venue so there is no AC.  They provide you with filtered water during your stay as they  avoid the use of plastic bottles. The facilities are rustic yet comfortable. Walking in the jungle with happy healthy elephants is something you won’t want to miss. Highly recommended! I also loved the boat safari at sunset. It is such a peaceful thing to do, especially because motorized boats are not allowed in the river. Keep in mind that this is a place for resting and exploring nature, so there is no TV in the rooms (or in the lodge). Bring a nice book or a board game for the evenings after your activities.A special thanks to Sambu. He is an amazing and extremely knowledgeable naturalist and guide. He always takes good care of us.

We stayed at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge for two nights during our trip to Nepal.  This is a VERY rustic lodge with minimal amenities.  They are committed to being eco-friendly and supporting the community.The main "tent" is a large, round structure where everything takes place: meals, meet ups for tours, check in and check out.  During check in, the various excursion options will be explained to you.  This is the only place you can get wifi.  The bar is here as well.  A decent selection, but everything is expensive: at least $6 per drink.Rooms are spacious and equipped with a ceiling fan and mosquito netting.  We asked for a standing floor fan as well, which really helped during the hot nights. Watch out for critters (spiders) in your room!All meals are served to you, but as if from the buffet.  The helpful staff will bring each dish to your table and ask what you would like and how much.  You can have more of anything.  Very generous portions and also quite tasty.  We enjoyed all of our meals.Our jeep safari, unfortunately, was underwhelming.  We saw little and had more people in our jeep than we were told we'd have.  Disconcerting during these pandemic times.  The best excursion for us was the sunset river safari with sundowners near two elephants that the lodge protects.  It was very peaceful to travel the river in a boat with no motor and watch fishermen at work and simply enjoy nature.  PS--you will pay for the sundowners.  Our river guide, Sambu, was excellent.While we'd give Chitwan National Park a pass, Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge is a comfortable choice.

The accommodation is amazing and from the first moment the treatment was incredible. The room was beautiful and in addition to cleaning it every day, every time we had dinner they took the opportunity to leave it ready with the mosquito net so we could sleep. The staff was attentive to you at all times, and served you delicious non-alcoholic cocktails upon arrival of each activity, as well as tea, coffee, popcorn and snacks. Very detailed and pleasant. We had a very friendly guide who did not hesitate to explain everything to us and answer any of our questions with patience, even though our English is not very good. They organized a walk through the jungle for us with elephants (very adventurous) where we saw a rhino next to us, ending at the river where we could see the sunset while having a picnic (although the elephants decided that they did not want to bathe). There I was able to propose to my girlfriend, thanks to the hotel staff, with whom I had spoken personally. During dinner they also had the detail of preparing us a very delicious cake. In short, Tiger Tops is a very special place to visit in Nepal and one that I absolutely recommend!!

We stayed here for three nights and had two days of 'trips'.  We had the boat trip down the river to see the wildlife and also watch the sun set which is beautiful.  We also did the walking trip through the jungle with the elephants (I found this a bit scarey but it was great) and we also did the safari drive.  Finally we were guided around the village and surrounding area which we really enjoyed.  The guide for this was Danny who is exceptionally experienced.     Our room was built in the style of local accommodation and was clean and comfortable.The food was varied and we were able to eat outside as it was still warm - later in the day it could get cold but we were able to go into the main lounge and sit beside a lovely log fire.Staff were helpful and there were two Deputy Managers as the main Manager was away.  The deputies were exceptionally welcoming, friendly and efficient .. if we were ever concerned about any aspect of our stay they were able to respond to our queries.We had a great time and would definitely return.

We loved everything about Tiger Tops. Our family room was fantastic, the meals superb and most important Danny our experienced guide made all the activities come alive. Thanks to everyone at Tiger Tops, our boys will never forget walking between the beautiful elephants. Tiger Tops does not chain the elephants and there are no rides, just walks...ethical, sublime and highly recommended,Michael Racheal Osh and Rubin from Australia

We took a short flight from Kathmandu to Bharatpur where we were picked up by a land rover and our guide Shambhu who remained our guide over the next few days. The journey to Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge was an experience in itself, I had known the roads were not good but that was an understatement, they have to be experienced to be believed. On arrival the bumpy road trip was soon forgotten as the staff made us feel incredibly welcome. We meet the manager and took an early afternoon beer before settling into our lovely spacious room, with all the amenities we could wish for air a jungle setting. Before we knew what was happening we had arranged to go for a walk in the jungle with our guide and two of the elephants that were kept by the lodge. We ordered our wine for our sundowner experience and we were on our way. On day two we had a jeep safari and a river trip in one of the large dugout canoes, and on our final day we went and fed the elephants and made them sandwiches, saw some amazing owlets on our way to the elephant compound and in the afternoon had a final safari. With Shambhu's help we never missed any of the wildlife, we saw Rhino (5 times), Gharial crocs on a number of occasions, so many wonderful birds including some beautiful king fishers, a serpent eagle, the wonderfully playful Ruddy Shell Ducks and many more. My personal favourite were the vultures on the final day. Oh and we saw a jackal, unfortunately we got to tiger footprints and not a tiger (next time maybe).The food was excellent, with a good variety, excellent service and lots of it. The central fire was lit each night and provided a social space to chat through the days activities either with other guests or in my case with our guide Shambhu who helped me identify all of the birds we had seen that day. If I lived closer I think a trip to Tiger Tops would have o be an annual event, as I left wanting to see more, do more, go back and look for tigers or more birds or any of the wild life that thrives in the jungle. If you are passing this way or taking a trip to Nepal stop of at the Chitwan and at Tiger Tops you won't be disappointed it is an amazing experience and they are very socially and environmentally aware.

I was hesitant to make the trip out to chitwan because it was a 7 hour journey from where I was staying in Kathmandu but I decided to gamble and hope for the best... ....This was so much better than the best. I have never been treated so well, so professionally and so completely than by the amazing staff at this lodge/camp. Their knowledge during all the tours and while hanging at the dining hall is astounding. The food is AMAZING and we stayed in the tents which I highly recommend, even in the winter. The heavy blankets and hot water bottle lull you right to sleep. This is the epitome of glamping. We hung out with the elephants and saw 5 rhinos, 2 of which were babies. I love that I got to experience all the nature knowing I was doing no harm because it truly is ethical. Thank you for the most beautiful experience I had in Nepal, and probably the world.

Overall, the lodge was good.  We had hot water for showers and a comfortable bed. The mosquito netting needs to be re-engineered.  Ours did not stay closed and it had 2 small holes in it.The food was very good; drinks were reasonably priced.  We very much enjoyed the walk with the elephants to the river for sunset; the visit to the elephant camp to feed the elephants some treats.  The canoe trip was a waste of time unless you are really into birds.  We skipped the full day safari because we did one in Bardia NP and could not stand to sit in a jeep for 12 hours.  We did do a 4 hour safari during which we saw rhinos up clase.  Four hours is about the correct length of time for this activity.Shopping at the Tiny Store ws fun, too.

We stayed a week here both in a room and in a tent. Both were fantastic, i loved the natural setting of the tent in the greenery where I could see bird life, while also having the luxury of a hot water bathroom.The staff are really friendly and go out of their way to make you comfortable with delicious meals and friendly service.The best part was being able to walk with the elephants who are so well looked after. To be so close to such an incredible creature as it goes about its daily life was amazing. There is no riding which I was happy to see and each elephant had a special bond with its guide which was very heartwarming. We were able to see Rhinos up close with the protection of the elephants beside us. Our guide Dannae was fantastic and very knowledgeable with lots of good stories from years of working in the jungle!The gardens and pool were prefect for relaxing after jeep safari and we saw hornbills and many other birds every day.The elephant camp is well thought out and you can see the animals are happy, going out into the wild frequently and bathing in the river at sundown.wonderful to see them living as close to the wild as possible.All in all a fantastic experience thanks to the river tops team.

I've done a great deal of traveling, including internationally, and this lodge was the BEST i've ever stayed in.  Not quite perfect, but very few flaws, and so very, very warm and welcoming, with the kindest, most helpful staff (each and every one of them).  As examples, they had not received advanced word about eating restrictions, yet we were accommodated.  The manager, who is called BC (as an abbreviation of his Nepali name), should truly be called A+, and he even went out of his way to find me artificial sweetener (which is apparently not common in Nepal).  They were also very accommodating about our safari requests in terms of time allotments, which was also greatly appreciated.  And I am making these very positive comments about the lodge despite the disappointment of not having seen a tiger!  (although we did see 2 leopards, which was very cool!)  Definitely the place to stay.

This lodge is rustic but all you need is there. Rooms have plenty of space , simple but everything you need large beds mosquito nets etc. staff delightful & food varied & mostly good. Enjoyed my stay there. Don’t expect too much of the wildlife difficult to see there & maybe because of lockdown very shy. I just love Nepal & all in all this lodge did not disappoint

My recent stay at Tharu Lodge can't be described in any way other than perfect. Upon our arrival we were warmly welcomed by the Tharu team who are superb at all they do. They go an extra mile to ensure you are comfortable, happy  and well informed throughout your stay. The restaurant serves delicious meals including the most delightful traditional Dhal Bhat and curry. They also cater to different diets, including vegan!The rooms are beautiful; extremely clean, well-kept and come with hot water, which is a real treat in the winter! One of my favourite things about Tharu Lodge is their elephants and their strong focus on animal welfare. They are the first and only company in Nepal to offer responsible elephant experiences. They no longer offer elephant-back safaris due to the stress it causes elephants, don’t use chains and have also built larger corrals for stabling. Hopefully other companies will soon follow suit!Tharu also offers truly wonderful jungle and wildlife experiences, giving you the chance to see some of Nepals most treasured animals in their natural habitat up close and personal. For instance, elephant walks, jeep and boat safaris and bird watching. On all of these excursions you are accompanied by very knowledgeable Naturalists who are experts in all things Chitwan National Park. They clearly love what they do and care deeply about the animals and nature they work among. On this particular trip we got extremely lucky on our jeep safari and saw two tigers! However, this wouldn’t have been possible without Dani, one of said naturalists! Thank you Tharu Lodge for an unforgettable stay! I will be back!

We've stayed in early March 2020 in Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge and are still so amazed by the serene beauty of this place, the lovely people there and the fantastic experience we've had - it's garden eden! We've booked several tours, our guides Shambu and Puspa were super knowledgable, fun to be with and patient with us. Also loved to walk besides the elephants to their grass-cutting activities or the sundowner at the river. Food was most delicious (best on entire trip!) and lunch underneath the mango tree simply spectacular. However most special are the people working there with their pure friendliness, taking the wonderful care of their guests and allowing insights in their lives and Nepali culture. Still daydreaming about this place!

We recently returned from a month long trip to Nepal with a stay at the Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge.  We have stayed at several of the Tiger Tops Lodges including the now closed Tiger Tent and original Tiger Tops Lodge that were in the Chitwan Park.  We also have stayed at the Karnali Lodge  next to Bardia National Park and Tiger Mountain near Pokhara.This organization and these lodges are the BEST and most ecologically friendly of all of the lodges near either the Chitwan or Bardia National Parks.  The organization has stopped giving elephant rides but participates in elephant research in conjunction with Hong Kong University.  The experienced naturalist guide ( Shambu) helped us identify 87 birds, see 9 rhinos (including mother and baby), 10 crocodiles, 4 different species of deer, evidence of wild boar and helped us identify many different plants and trees.  All of this within 2 days of essentially a private tour in the park and on the Tharu Lodge grounds.   We were able to visit the school sponsored by Tiger Tops and watch as the researches conducted their elephant studies.  In our previous visits to the Chitwan and Bardia we have had the opportunity to see tigers and wild elephants and even follow tigersas they hunted.  I do not believe that you can find similar experiences with any other resort in either park.

Loved my stay. The food was delicious, the communal vibe was lovely and they catered to my food allergies without any fuss. The safari tent was luxurious and the elephants are well looked after as is the whole venue. Not a plastic bottle or single use paper towel in sight which I adored.

We had a fantastic time at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge and experienced things we'll remember for the rest of our lives.The accommodation is really nice. We stayed in one of the rooms (rather than a tent) and had plenty of space. There's no TV or radio in the room, but you're not here for that so you won't miss it! Food is delicious and the staff are fantastic. There's a pool you can enjoy and some nice grounds/gardens to go for a wander in.The real highlights at Tiger Tops are the excursions / experiences on offer. I honestly think we'll remember these forever. We enjoyed a morning jeep safari with an excellent guide and saw a variety of animals (but sadly no Tigers). But the elephant experiences are really where Tiger Tops shines.They have a small herd of elephants there which they look after and care for. There are no elephant rides at Tiger Tops, but there's plenty more on offer. My favourite was walking through the jungle with two elephants, down to the river, where they bathe and you enjoy a refreshing drink as the sun sets. In fact we enjoyed this so much we did it twice.We also enjoyed the early morning trip to gather food with the elephants and the opportunity to help make their snacks / feed them. The chance to get that up close and personal with elephants in this way doesn't come along very often.

Amazing experience. All the staff took very care of us. They knew how to adapt the program with our constraints (our litlle son was one year old).  We crossed the river with a pirogue to reach the Chitwan jungle, we explored the jungle by car but also by walking , protected by two elephants. We took an apero with the staff and the elephants by the river with an unforgettable sunset. We spent one day with the elephants, walking with them, feeding them ... We will never forget our stay there !

We have just returned from 3 exceptional days at Tiger Tops,  Don't expect to see Tigers as the area is vast although on the Jeep Safari we did see Rhino, Our best excursion was walking with Elephants,  Tiger Tops for the past 8 years do not allow guest to ride the Elephants however you get to walk between them allowing a magical experience. We came across 3 Rhinos and had a stand off with the 2 elephants either side of us, To say the moment was insane is an understatement. So good infarct we went again the next day and again came across Rhino again,  The walk ends at the river where sun downers are served and the Elephants get to go for a wash and cool down.  Food at the lodge was great catering for both western and local tastes. We staid in the Tents which was great however I think the Rooms would have been just fine.

Wow wow wow. What a great stay. My friend and myself were well taken care of and had a blast. The service is exceptional, so well done and the grounds are beautiful and well taken care of.  The food is fabulous and quite delicious, you will not go hungry. We participated in safari tour, elephant camp, elephant walk, river excursion, and vulture restaurant. I loved going into the jungle in the jeeps and all the guides were amazing. There are many excursions you can choose from as well as half day/full day. We also enjoyed a lazy day by the pool and walking into tharu Village. Tiger tops will take care of you and help arrange everything. Loved this place. Hoping to be able to comeBack again.

Atmospheric accommodation on the terrai. Very helpful staff and welcoming us back from excursions with a cooling flannel was a lovely touch. The food was delicious and all the arrangements were made and executed perfectly. Sam is a brilliant and conscientious guide while Prem is a most able and safe driver on very rough tracks in a recalcitrant vehicle. Altogether a lovely experience from beginning to end. Unforgettable and highly recommended.

I've dreamed about coming to Chitwan National Park since I first heard about it over 30 years ago, and following Tiger Tops leading the way in care and protection for elephants within the tourist industry I knew there was nowhere else to stay! The serene atmosphere, attentive and professional staff, delicious food, and unique activities exceeded all my high hopes and expectations. Best of all was walking with elephants and watching them bathe in the river at sunset, learning to make their snacks from the mahouts and even being allowed to feed them, and going on a jeep safari where we saw lots of birds and animals in their natural environment - just magical!  Our guide throughout everything was naturalist Puspa who was very knowledgeable, enthusiastic and great fun to be with.  We learned so much!  We will never forget our experiences at Tiger Tops.  Thank you to Puspa and all the staff for making our stay so special.

Fabulous people, lovely lodge and great foodThe people make this place! Everyone was so helpful, the Manager, the guides the drivers, the lodge staff and chef!The walk and sundowners with the elephants was a first and the game drives excellent, even though we did not see the elusive tiger so we saw plenty of prints so guess they were watching us!

Outstanding  lodge. Staff were attentive to our every need. Food and service was excellent. The elephant camp is a must visit as well as sundown elephant walk and river side cocktails. Hang out at the main lodge by the fire at night.

We had a fantastic visit. We visited in mid-March and I think we picked the perfect time. The temps were starting to ramp up in the afternoon but the mosquitoes weren’t much of an issue at all. Our guide Sam was wonderful, ensuring our elephant walk, park walk and Jeep tour of the park were thorough. We saw almost all of the animals mentioned, however I had to settle on only hearing two leopards kill a deer and then argue over who was going to get the best parts. The staff at the resort were great and the lodge rooms were large and really very comfortable. I would recommend this experience to families with older children and couples….so much adventure for a very affordable price. Don’t miss the sunset elephant walk or the opportunity to feed the elephants. We learned a lot!

After staying in the village and being horrified by the treatment of elephants there, I moved to Tiger Tops for a much quieter, more pleasant experience. The place is beautiful and peaceful, and elephants are not being ridden, which was very important for me. Delicious food and friendly staff, lots of things to do. I wish I had stayed longer.

This place is simply magical. The rooms are really comfortable and the food and service is impeccable. The lodge operates on an ecological, zero waste policy which is reflected in their menus and that they don't use plastic water bottles, instead providing safe filtered water. The guides are magnificent and are great at spotting and finding wildlife. There is a bar and internet is available in the shared space.

Tiger tops were fantastic! Booked through Reshmi in Kathmandu. Excellent staff, clean and comfortable tent. Safari was great - wild elephant, rhinos, heaps of birds and other animals despite large tourist numbers. Couldn't recommend Tiger tops more (From reservation and both lodges).

Outstanding two days here as part of a Nepal trip. Managed to fit in a walking safari, elephant camp and jeep safari. Incredible guiding by Dan who is a living encyclopaedia of the jungle. Yes, the elephants are not wild and some may be uncomfortable about this, but it’s got to be 100% better that the lives they have been rescued from. The food was superb, as was the service. All the staff seemed genuinely happy and could t do enough to help. Would definitely recommend.

This is a must do if you're in that part of the world. I could hear Tigers at night and say lots of rhinos.  It's eco friendly with great food. The rooms are pretty good and the tour guides really know their stuff. The best part was playing in the river with a baby elephant.

Exceptional service!  I wish I could return as an annual vacation.  One of the most memorable vacations.  The staff was amazing and extremely helpful.  The only thing missing was a tiger sighting.  We saw several Rhinos and tracked tigers tracks.  The elephants were magical and beautiful.

This was my first truly solo trip to a completely new country. The staff at Tiger Tops Tharu lodge went above and beyond to make sure my stay was comfortable and that I was able to make the most of my experience. Each day, the Guest Relations Officer helped me to plan an itinerary for the day, based on my personal preferences. My Guide/Naturalist was also wonderful throughout. The room was clean and comfortable. The food was excellent - especially the lunches which consist of local food. The veggies are all grown locally. I had some wonderful jungle treks in Chitwan. My favourite and most unforgettable part of the trip was definitely meeting the elephants in the elephant camp and walking with a couple of them in the forest (accompanied by the naturalist and their mahouts). Completely smitten. Encountering rhinos on foot is amazing too. Every single part of the experience was joyful and I received such warm hospitality and was so well looked after, that I really can't wait to visit again. Highly recommended.

Tiger Tops is truly the place to be if you visit Chitwan. We initially chose it because they do not chain their elephants and support the local community, but it turned out to also be much superior to any other accommodations in the area. While the facilities and food are really good, we came for the safaris and were more than impressed. They tailor your personal plan for the day according to your interests and own wishes. We went for one safari through the national park and one through the buffer zone. Our guide Gyan was fantastic!! Very knowledgeable and friendly. It was obvious that he loved his work and we enjoyed his company a lot. We saw rhinos, a leopard, sloth bear, crocodiles and lots of monkeys and wild chicken. Their elephants are well kept, friendly and simply awesome!! We stayed at the safari tent. Before making up your mind about what to book or if you have any questions, just call or email their sales office. They were extremely helpful, explained everything and responded instantly. That saved us a lot of headache, as we were travelling to Chitwan between Lumbini and Kathmandu and hence needed to plan our drives, itinerary etc well. We called them from Pokhara and booked directly through them as a result. As checkin is at 12 pm, try to arrive around noon for lunch to take advantage of the afternoon safari or other afternoon activities. The safari leaves at 2 pm. They also have a great swimming pool if you rather relax. On your departure day, leave after lunch to fit in a morning activity, such as a safari or walk with the elephants etc. As a piece of advice, one safari per day is included only with the safari tent or the rooms, but not with the elephant camp. If you don`t plan on going on a safari every day, then staying at the elephant camp right next to those amazing animals and pay for the safaris separately would be a good choice.

On arrival at the camp we were immediately swept away by the free, relaxed and casual luxury feeling of the camp. Entering the camp 3 elephants were walking around playing in a huge enclosure – and on the top of the hill side was the open dining hall with the most incredible view to the nature and the elephants. Our tent was super charming – a double bed, a separate room for dressing – and a beautiful bathroom on the backside. When changing I looked out of the backside of the tent and found one of the elephants standing right behind in an other of the huge enclosures. The special attraction here is to not do touristic activities, but to watch and follow the life of the elephants. During Lunch – excellent Nepali food served in the open dining hall with white cloth tables - we enjoyed watching the elephants - communicating, eating, playing - at very close hand, Then time was up for the elephants for a bath and we walked with them through the beautiful river bed and fields to the river banks, where chairs was set up for us and we enjoyed a drink while watching the elephants enjoying them selves taking a bath for hours. Next day started with a jungle walk where the elephants could choose their own breakfast from the trees, and - had we been up an hour earlier - we would have met the rhinos. Now we only saw the watering hole that they had left shortly before we arrived. Later we made ‘sandwiches’ for the elephants – corn wrapped in straws - they were hungry after moving a tree felled by a lightning the previous afternoon. In between watching the elephants we relaxed at the pool at the nearby lodge. This place and experience is so peaceful, beautiful and extraordinary, that I will highly recommend to everybody who wants to relax and experience nature and natural wild life. My only regret is that we only stayed for 2 nights – I’ll highly recommend staying 3 nights.

The Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge was a fascinating experience. After the noisy and crowded cities this was a quiet and serene place to enjoy nature and the excellent staff. We took a flight from Kathmandu to Bharatpur and were met by our guide who remained with us throughout our visit. After an hour on the road we arrived at the lodge in time for lunch. An outdoor buffet with an excellent choice of foods was served and the lodge manager joined us for lunch. Since there were only 7 guests we had the place to ourselves. Our room was #12 which was a corner room with three sides with windows. This provided light during the day and in summer would provide more air circulation. The furnishings were basic but comfortable. The bathroom was small and contained a shower. Solar-heated water was available but be patient it takes a while to get warm.  Hand-made herbal soap was furnished but that was the only amenity so bring your own toiletries. Light at night was from electric oil lamps and could be a challenge for those who like to read in bed. We were so surprised the first night when we returned from evening activities to find hot water bags wrapped in flannel in our bed! The weather is very cool at night and these felt great. Every morning, coffee  and tea were brought to the room. Forget about keys/locks. You could secure the room from the outside but not inside.The resort was totally self sufficient. Organic gardens furnished fresh vegetables and fruit trees provided fresh fruits in season. Meats were provided by pigs and chickens. Cows provided fresh milk. The staff of 70 were friendly, efficient and courteous.  There was a mushroom house for daily use and an interesting place to see.An activity that you should take was the elephant safari into the jungle. Here we saw one-horned rhinos, monkeys, mongoose, wild boar, peacocks, "barking" deer. Crossing the river on top of a very large elephant was a challenge but not to fear since river was shallow. We also selected an oxen cart drive through the fisherman's and farmers' villages. One evening we took a river cruise at sunset which was very relaxing. There were 8 friendly, female elephants in the resort. One morning we visited this area and were given an explanation of elephant characteristics and care. Feeding an elephant an "elephant sandwich" was fun! Straw with a variety of grains were wrapped into bundles which you feed to the elephant. They really liked this treat.There is a small gift shop called the "Tiny Shop". It is a separate building on the property and has a limited selection of items. I purchased a unique necklace and a small box for a very reasonable price. US dollars were accepted.The food was very good and breakfast and dinner were served in the dining room building. This is also the main gathering place during the day and evening since there is an open pit fire burning at all times. One evening a group of local dancers and musicians came to the Lodge to perform for us.We highly recommend the Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge to future travelers. It was such a low key and relaxing place which we really enjoyed. Our personal guide was with us the entire time. He was excellent and so enthusiastic about  meeting our needs. He loved photography and often took pictures of the two if us. He was a credit to the company.

I have stayed at the Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge last November for a week. It has been a blissful stay in Nepal. Tiger Tops is an eco Lodge where luxury is natural and sustainable. The Lodge also supports environmental education among the people who live in the nearby villages.The kindest staff made my stay even nicer if possible. And excursions in the Chitwan jungle with naturalists, is something I will always treasure. Thank you.

I was delighted with wildlife experiences, comfort, new friendships and hospitality like no other for 7 exceptional days. Stepping out of the vehicle and into the beautiful tropical garden settings I was greeted with a glass of cold lemonade and a refreshing facecloth. And as I followed the path past the chain free elephant corals and organic gardens to my safari tent, a smile quickly swept across my face knowing the elephants here are well cared for and so too are the guests. The following days and evenings I spent eating delicious meals, chatting around the dining room fireplace, grass cutting with the elephants and their carers by the river in the early morning, swimming in the relaxing and glorious pool, exploring the buffer zone and national park from a variety of options - walking with the elephants, jeep safari and jungle walks with the exceptional and knowledgeable TT naturalists. As a keen naturalist and former zookeeper myself I was very impressed with the commitment of TT to the ethical treatment of their team of domesticated elephants and the sincere relationships the handlers have with the elephants. All elephants are chain free 24/7 and confined only when in camp within the spacious corals. Walking with the elephants on the ground gives you an exceptional jungle perspective - if not the best....and due to their presence enables close encounters with rhino.

A wonderful lodge that caters to green and environmentally conscious travelers with great tours and experiences.  Food is outstanding and the service is even better as the price would suggest, this is an excellent place to use as a home base when visiting Chitwan National Park.  Be sure to visit the nearby Tharu village and eat a meal and purchase some local wood carvings that originate in the community managed sustainable forest of the Chitwan buffer zone.  Rooms do not have AC but have powerful ceiling fans.  I stayed during the hot and humid monsoon season and no trouble with temperature, mosquitoes or humidity.  No internet in rooms but wifi is available in the dining area and main lodge.

I cannot recommend Tiger Tops highly enough! What a wonderful experience we had with the elephants, Molly, Danny, Gan and the other members of the Tiger Tops staff.  The tents are so cosy, the ensuite bathrooms are fab and the location, next to the elephant corrals, is one of the best places on earth!  Walking through the jungle with elephants and watching them bathe in the river is an experience my family will never forget. The food served in the dining hall was delicious and plentiful. The staff are fantastic. The guides are very knowledgeable and make you feel very safe even when you are just metres away from some very large rhinos. Tiger Tops are doing a fantastic job with the elephants while also supporting the local schools and economy. Please go there and support their wonderful pioneering work!

This was my second visit to Tiger Tops but first in this location. It was clean, huge, all the staffs were friendly, we felt like we were in our own home. The staff take care us as if we are the owner of the place. We went in January, so it was cold, every time we went to kitchen area, they asked us for tea/ coffee/ hot chocolate and the best thing is it was all complimentary, we do not need to pay extra. Evening walk around the river stream with elephants was a good experience. Champaki, is the only name i remember though. The jungle ride was thrilling, the guide was very enthusiastic in finding wild animals more than us, he was looking though binoculars if he could see some and show to us. Those two nights we stayed at Tiger Tops were our best experience so far. We booked a tent room, and while booking for it (around august) we told them our purpose of coming to Nepal was because of our anniversary. They remember it!!!! The day we checked into Tiger Tops the manager repeatedly told us, since this is your special time, we would want you to have a good time, so if we feel cold in tent he gave us a privileged to change into room for free (which is more expensive). We could not understand at first, we thought maybe there are less people at the place so we were given this offer. But at our last meal, they prepared us a surprise cake. And the day we check out, they dropped us to the nearby bus station, but did not left us until we could get into the bus safely. Very impressed by the whole team. Would like to thank all the for making our stay wonderful.

We spent 3 nights at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge which was the perfect length of time for a family of 4 including two boys aged 12 and 9. This allowed time to participate at least once, sometimes twice in the activities which included Elephant Safari, Jeep Safari, Elephant education/washing, birdwatching, and chilling out by the pool. The staff were very friendly, professional, and the food was excellent. Although not as varied as African wildlife, Chitwan national park provided plenty of animal viewing including plenty of Rhinos, Monkeys, Deer, Wild Boar, Crocs and interesting birdlife. Leopards and Tigers are there but tough to find. Very impressed.

We spent three nights at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge in the last week of March and the whole experience was exceptional. The lodge setting is beautiful and relaxed, with plenty of space for our children to run around. Our guide Krishna was an absolute gem with an extensive knowledge of all the jungle creatures and plants. All the staff were friendly, helpful and patient. We walked around the village, rode on an elephant, washed the elephants by the river, took a jeep and riverboat safari and visited the local pre-school, and enjoyed every minute. The food was excellent. We did see three very big scary spiders while we were there, but I guess that's to be expected! Excellent place.

Our family of three spent three nights at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge and had a terrific time. The staff are welcoming and knowledgeable. Staying here allowed us to have some nice wildlife experiences as well as a chance to learn about village life. A visit to the village school was a highlight. Our other activities included two elephant safaris, a jeep safari, a river safari, a visit to the elephant center, a guided village walk, elephant bathing and birdwatching--all of which were great.We were especially grateful for how accommodating the staff were regarding our child's food allergies; they even made separate dishes for him as needed (and did the same for a guest who was a vegetarian). I should note that we did communicate with them about our needs when booking and again before our arrival, and I had cards printed in Nepali explaining the allergy. Traveling with food allergies is not always easy, but the staff at Tiger Tops made it possible. We all found the food enjoyable.A few practicalities: make sure to bring your own shampoo and conditioner as those were not included. The room includes a flashlight, so we never even used ours. The electricity is not on all the time, so charge your camera and other devices before the batteries are completely empty. Bring a refillable water bottle to use on your outings.We highly recommend Tiger Tops and hope to return there some day. It is a very peaceful place.

We stayed two nights at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge and loved every minute of it.  The staff could not have been more accommodating and welcoming, or more knowledgable.  The rooms we had in the main building were fantastic. As an interior designer, I was wowed by the linens on the gorgeous beds, the hot water bottles at night, the fantastic plaster walls made with most interesting composition, ask the staff! It was like being in another time, Colonial feeling, with just the right amount of luxury.   The main dining room in the lodge with the giant roaring and deliciously smokey fire, going at all times, was wonderful and chic and charming.  The first night we had a performance by local dancers which eventually included us, usually my least favourite thing, and it was so fun!!!! Beautiful dancers dancing beautifully and teaching us all to dance too.  Quite hilarious.  The grounds and pool are fantastic, and the tour we had of the farm and the elephant stables was lovely.  We also loved our elephant safari and got up close and personal with one rhino. We thoroughly enjoyed the ox cart journey and the river boat trip.  Just wish we could have stayed longer, it was all too rushed.The food could possibly be improved by sticking more to local Nepalese dishes rather than emulating more European food.  It was fine and certainly substantial but slightly misdirected.Overall I would recommend this adventure to anyone wanting "Glamping" in Nepal, would love to go back.

A perfect getaway from the intensity of the Kathmandu Valley and the madness of Nepali roads. Rustic and fairly basic but somehow it has everything you would need and the service was just excellent (never before have I had hot water bottles put in the bed as part of the turn-down service!). A highly recommended little jungle oasis!

I am sharing this review after my second stay at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge and both stays were amazing. There is something magical about this place and it has earned a spot in my heart. This is not the same safari experience you have in Africa so managing expectations is important. Chitwan National Park has a lot of vegetation and available water so animal sightings, while plentiful, are not as easy as in Africa.The lodge rooms are large and very comfortable but rustic, without AC or TV, but you don’t miss them. The food is plentiful and delicious, served homestyle. The staff are fantastic, warm, attentive and very accommodating with food allergies.The elephant sandwich making and late afternoon elephant walk/sundowner are a must. Words can’t describe the thrill of encountering a momma rhino and baby, on foot, under the protection of two majestic elephants. The jungle jeep safari is thrilling and Sam is a wonderful guide, making sure we spotted almost every animal except the shy tiger and sloth bear, even though he tried very hard to locate them. He does not use a radio for animal spotting like they do on an African safari but instead relies on the warning calls of jungle animals and he seems to know them all. This knowledge netted two leopard spotting, one on each stay. I am honestly still amazed he was able to find one lazy leopard napping on a fallen tree which was covered in thick vegetation. Even though I knew where it was I still had trouble finding it again each time with binoculars. When we returned from the jungle safari we were greeted with warm smiles an ice cold towel and a delicious cold drink. Make sure to take a refreshing swim in the pool to cool down before you enjoy snacks and then a delicious dinner in the lodge.

Stayed at Tiger Tops for 2 nights in December halfway through a trip through a Nepal and mostly had a great stay as knew what to expect. However for those planning a visit do not expect the lodge/safari experience etc to be like an African or even an Indian safari experience. Food - for the price (and being Pescatarian) did find the food slightly lacking in variety. The meals that were served were nice (with lovely desserts) but would have liked more variety.Rooms - Rooms are rustic chic and are in keeping with the surroundings.  The room was clean and comfortable and although could get cold on an evening the hot water bottles put in our beds each evening was a lovely touch.  The beds were also very comfortable and loved the wildlife pictures on the wall and cushions on the bed.Facilities - did not use the swimming pool.  There is a small gift shop on sight with a few branded products but would have liked a wider variety than just tote bags, caps etc.Activities - this is where you will need to check what is included in your package.  Having done many safaris around the world (as well as paying the amount we did to stay at Tiger Tops) we presumed most things were included in our package (which is not the case).  We did the safari drive, elephant walk (which was a highlight of our stay as got very close to rhinos on foot), a boat ride and the elephant interaction.  All of these were great. Wildlife - we did not see the elusive tiger but saw lots of rhino (both on foot, in the safari vehicle and from a boat) as well as lots of birds, boar and deer.Staff - most staff we came across were very welcoming especially the serving staff at lunch and dinner who always provided service with a smile.  The guides were also very informative about the local area and it’s wildlife.We did have a slight problem (see below) and was not impressed by the attitude of the management but apart from that we were happy with the staff.ConsThe main issue is that we took part in the activities offered as we thought all were part of the package that had been organised (I.e had more than 1 safari drive etc) and not once did anyone say these were not part of the package etc or advise these were at an extra cost.  On our final night we were then presented with a bill for the extra drive etc (which was expensive) of which we were baffled as no one had mentioned this was extra.  We found the manager a bit condescending and abrupt (as well as doing this in front of others) when we mentioned this as nowhere on the premises/our paperwork etc did it state what was extra. After explaining the situation (and refusing to pay the extra)he said that he would take it off but again this left a very unpleasant taste on what had up to that point been a nice stay.  No safari lodge I have ever stayed at limits Safari drives to once per stay! As a lodge focused on conservation would have liked more information about their initiatives (books, wildlife talks on an evening etc) as we are passionate about wildlife and thought something like this would have been offered.  Most of the elephants at the lodge seemed healthy and happy and the mahouts on the elephant walk had a good relationship with them. When taking part in the interaction there were a few elephants that were swaying/pacing but this may have been because of their past.On speaking to some guides (mostly the younger ones) about elephant welfare, the local wildlife etc they did not seem to know a lot/could answer questions.For those that are older/less mobile you will have to walk up and down stairs to get to the safari vehicle to go anywhere so bear this in mind if planning to visit.———————-Would recommend as a place to stay but be aware of what package you are staying on otherwise you will be limited in what you can do.  It is expensive for what you get but for a 2 night stay in the middle of a Nepal trip it is a nice break from the hustle and bustle from the cities.

Love our stay at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge. We stayed for 3 nights and wish we could have stayed longer. Our flight into Baratapur was delayed by 3 hours but once we arrived, the Tiger Tops staff were there to greet us and whisk us to the lodge. The lodge itself was beautiful and rustic. We loved the simple decor but a pity they didn’t sell the cushions and lotions as souvenirs. They had an almost non-existent souvenir shop and we had to get someone to open the doors to it after seeing it close perpetually.We really enjoyed the jungle trekking and was able to see rhinos, deers, crocodiles, Elephants, monkeys, wild boar and many species of birds.The kitchen and restaurant staff was excellent. The food served were varied, very fresh, creative and delicious!! As I am gluten and lactose intolerant they made it a point to provide me with an alternative. For eg our first lunch, while the rest was served creamed cauliflower soup, mine was cooked with coconut milk. And they always asked whether I needed anything extra and offered to make boiled veggies or grilled tomatoes for me. Thank you!!I would like to specially mention Puspha. We had the pleasure of having him as a guide twice. Very energetic young man who is so enthusiastic about sharing his knowledge on wildlife with us. On the last day, I got a little ill and miss our afternoon Jeep safari time slot. He was so kind to arrange a shorter private safari for just me and my hubby. It turned out to be the highlight of our trip. Thank you so much!

Amazing lodge! Excellent food and attentive staff. WiFi in the main area only. Rooms rustic but clean with tiny basic bathrooms, adequate and appropriate for the environment. Tea and coffee served by staff to the room as a wake up call. Day and half day outings of all sorts but the highlight was sundowners with the elephants - watching them wallow and bathe in the river with so much delight- similar to us humans sinking into a hot bath.. very knowledgeable guides and drivers - mostly 50 year old British Land Rovers used! We were nearly charged by a rhinoceros mum with her baby, only feet away! We  also saw a crocodile, deer, monkeys and another group spotted a leopard. All terrific and highly recommended

After the bustle of Kathmandu this was a welcome chill-out, especially as it has a pool. An eclectic bunch of guests during our two night stay added to the  evening conversations.Highlight was a walking tour of the three adjacent local villages, in the late afternnoon, watching different aspects of village life.The jeep safari was a relaxing interlude, but for those who have been on African safari, the wildlife aspect is pretty minimal so don't expect much. Everyone seems to see tiger tracks, but the beast itself is as elusive as the Yeti.Our tour operator had booked tented accomodation, but as the place was not fully we got a complimentary upgrade to a room.

Tiger Tops is a serene and beautiful place to stay. I personally stayed in one of the tents. It was very nice and spacious and I never felt too hot sleeping. The bathroom is separated and very beautiful and has hot water. There is always water in reusable glass or metal bottles. WiFi is in the main lodge only. I think the most underrated part of the lodge is the food. The lodge grows vegetables and makes their own yogurt for breakfast (which is really good). The dinner meals were especially delicious and I enjoyed wonderful conversation with other guests (you can be at a separate table if you choose). The guides were friendly and knowledgeable and the staff was incredibly accommodating. I love this place.

We stayed here for two nights and had a wonderful experience. Beware that you are staying in the middle of the wilderness and the accommodation is not be as luxurious as some of the ultra high-end safari lodges in Africa (for example). The walls between rooms are thin and we were able to hear *everything* (yes, everything....ahem) from the room next door, shower temperature was cold except for late afternoon, and because of the high humidity bedsheets and towels felt damp. HOWEVER, everything was spotlessly clean, the food was fantastic, the experiences (especially the walking safaris) with the elephants were truly memorable (just proving that you absolutely don’t need to ride them in order to enjoy them!), and every single staff member was welcoming and warm. We had an amazing time and especially loved our safari with Sambhu!! Thank you, Tiger Tops! (One tip: be sure to wear long pants tucked into your socks on the walking safari if you want to avoid leeches.)

My fiancé and I stayed here for three nights between Christmas and New Year. As we try to be ethical and responsible tourists, we chose Tiger Tops as from what I could gather from extensive internet searching and Lonely Planet info, TT is the only safari provider which no longer offers elephant rides (which turned out to be correct), and for the ethical and socially responsible way they conduct their business with strong links to the community, a school they run, and a free clinic which they open once a month.We were not disappointed. We stayed in a safari tent which, though not heated, was equipped with an extremely toasty electric blanket which kept us more than warm enough in the cold December nighttime temperatures. The bathroom was very nice, and the water was hot enough to shower comfortably by the afternoon.As other reviews have mentioned, the food was incredible, free-flowing at breakfast and lunch, with 3 course dinners!The activities were brilliant, with cutting elephant grass with the mahouts and making and feeding them elephant sandwiches being extremely special.
