We also took two walks in the jungle accompanied by two elephant bodyguards (as the owner kristian says, why sit on an elephant when you can walk WITH it), which we were EXTREMELY glad for both times as we came across Rhino both times, which approached us to within about 4 metres, and the elephants are there to ensure they don't charge you! We also saw a lot of wildlife on the jeep safaris, though unfortunately not the elusive big cats as the colder winter temperatures and long grass make sightings at that time of year much rarer (March and April are the best apparently). The guides are seasoned pros (one of the two we had has worked as a naturist in the park for over 30 years!) and can track and find a rhino from the crack of a tree branch, or a tiger from the warning calls of deer. Even if you don't spot the big cats, the amount of information they can share with you along the way is incredible! Perhaps one of the nicest parts of our stay with sitting around the lodge fire in the evening and talking to the other guests. Owner Kristian was also around a couple of nights, and it was extremely interesting to hear all about the history of the lodge from him, right back to when it was first set up by his father and his business partner in the 60s.Overall, a magical, unforgettable experience.

We had two overnight stays in Tiger Tops. We booked a room / accomodation in a tent. We were very happy about it, as it turned out to be really hilarious. We've never before slept a night in a tent.The property is next to national park, which we found great. The interrior and garden are kept rather simply but -according my opinion- with good teste. We loved the desing of our tent. The tents have got own bathrooms (shwoer) and toilets, which are modern, so we did not have to give up any conviences. The staff in the hotel is friendly and polite.  It is very much service. All meals are served to table, there is no buffet. They have a good bar. We really enjoyed it. Transfer service to the Airport was excellent and to recomend. We had a driver and a guide for it. We were very happy about it,  as the check-in process differs a lot to that what we have used to. We participated in some activities, whcih were all great experiences. We took a Jeep Safari to jungle / national park.  We were lucky enough to see rhino mother with her "Baby", some deers, a crocodile, monkeys and lot's of birds. Later the day we went againg for a walk with elephants and were able to see again a male rhino. We visited also elephants and saw how they are accomodated. Also we went one evening to see when elephants went to swim, which was nice as well (and to recomend). All in all, we learnt a lot about jungle, elephants, rhinos and the Nepal and nepales during our stay there - thank you to our wonderfull guides. The only thing what I missed a bit, was a Wifi but for a two nights we were also able to live without it. Therefore we did not ask extra for it. We can recomend this place. It is great place to relax. If we return to Nepal, we will book a tent again Tiger Tops.

We stayed at the end of March with our 3 children aged 5-10. We all loved our stay. We had considered booking a cheaper option but were so glad we didn’t. Tiger Tops was excellent. Very comfortable, lovely staff and great food. The trips were well organised and our guide was brilliant. Typically you wake up early and have a leisurely breakfast served to you at your table. Then there is a choice of morning activity and late afternoon activity. Dinner is Western style, 3 course also served at your table. Lunch is Nepali buffet, which was great and gave flexibility so that people could eat when they returned from activities or arrived at the lodge. All the food was delicious. The middle of the day you could relax or swim. Our kids loved the pool and hammocks. They also loved going to feed the elephants one lunchtime. The treatment of the elephants is much better than other places. One couple complained that you can’t ride the elephants- we knew this and that was part of the reason we booked this place. It is on any email they send you. If you want to do an elephant riding safari, this is not the place for you. We walked with elephants, watched them bathe and graze, fed them and had more than enough elephant time and felt they were far better cared for (although still domesticated obviously) than those being ridden. Their handlers do still ride them though. We did not feel we missed out by not riding elephants. The Jeep safari was great (I did it twice! my family had a morning off the second time as we had already seen so much the first time around). We saw a lot of rhino, different types of deer, monkeys and it’s heaven for bird watchers. We saw snakes, wild boar, gharial, a dead python, countless butterflies and a jackal, but not the elusive tiger (or leopard). The safari was well organised with boats and jeeps all standing by for transfers. We felt it was a perfect mix between activities, relaxation in comfortable surroundings (not deluxe but much more than adequate) with great food and service.  Flying is much easier than driving. The road is a construction zone and we saw 3 accidents. We drove from Pokhara but wisely broke up the trip and stayed a night in Bandipur on the way (which was a great detour) We flew back to KTH but our flight was cancelled due to bad weather. A Tiger Tops representative stayed with us (despite us saying he could leave) and offered to drive us back or help us find accommodation- as the next flight was very early the next morning, we didn’t go back to Tiger Tops and they helped us find somewhere else to stay. What service- not just a bus transfer to the airport but actually staying to make sure we got on our plane and helping us when we didn’t. Highly recommend and am so glad we booked.

There is something about Tiger Tops that reminded us a bit of Disney World in the States.  It is magical.  But unlike Disney World, Tiger Tops and the jungle are authentic.  Disney is known for its customer service, Tiger Tops is even better at this.  And while both Disney and Tiger Tops are high end adventures, leaving Tiger Tops we felt that our money was well spent in helping to reverse the shortsighted tourism abuse of the jungle that has obviously occurred in the past.  The staff at Tiger Tops treat their elephants well, with no chains and by eliminating the cutting saddles the other lodges still use.  Knowing this, we had a grand time walking through the jungle with the majestic giants, as they protected us from potential threats (such as rampaging "momma" rhinos with calves).  We were up close with the elephants but not in a circus sort of way.  Another positive was our food, well prepared and good quality.  The lodge dining and meeting hall with a huge in-door campfire was the perfect place to hang out (and to get wifi).  But as noted above, in addition to the the elephant experience Tiger Tops soars with hospitality of their staff.  We effectively had a personal assistant to help us with every part of our stay and experience.  From our "personal assistant" to our jungle guides to the waiters and even to the bar tender, Tiger Tops is tops at customer service.The next level for Tiger Tops can be reached with a eco-appropriate improvement to the lodge, with the addition of other activities (bicycles to ride through the village would be nice), and by somehow making a visit to the elephants (making elephant sandwiches) something more than it is now.  But this would all simply be reaching excellence from an already very good lodge and jungle experience.  We will be returning to Tiger Tops and only Tiger Tops in the future and are assured that no other lodge can match its eco-sustainability and customer service.  A final note, it is worth researching two Tiger Tops founders, A.V.Jim Edwards and Dr Chuck McDougal, to understand this place and how deeply imbedded it is in sustaining the Nepali jungle.

Just completed an incredible 6 day stay at Tiger Tops.  This is a most remarkable and wonderful place and like others, we chose to stay here because of their humane treatment of the elephants.  You won't be disappointed and you will see that the opportunities to walk with and experience the elephants without riding them is memorable and once in a lifetime experience.  This approach extends itself to everything at Tiger Tops.  The lodging (we loved the tents) is extremely well appointed with comfy beds, lots of purified water and many pillows.  The attached bathrooms provide amenities including toiletries and fresh dry towels.  The food was superb.  All the meals are provided fresh and there are always vegetarian alternatives.  And while the local food is somewhat spicey, it was never too spicey for my limited western taste.  Coffee and tea and also hot chocolate were always readily available.   You won't go hungry.  As for the activities, during the time we were there in early November there were maybe 10 - 12 people and incredibly they arranged different full days of activities for each couple or party.  Each itinerary was customized for your individual interests, whether it was spending time with the elephants or birding.  The guides are very knowledgeable and were able to communicate well with us in English.  As for all of the staff, they couldn't possibly be nicer.  No matter what you wanted, they were there to provide to all of your needs.  Even at the end, we were taken to the airport and they helped us navigate the confusing local airport.  After waiting with us for 4 hours, our flight which was the last of the day was canceled and they quickly mobilized and helped us get on the last flight of a different airline.  We were extremely grateful.  I can't say enough about how wonderful this stay was.  I would recommend and encourage you to go here and be sure to try and stay for at least 3-4 days.  The longer you stay the better!!

Tiger Tops are pioneering elephant friendly, environmentally responsible tourism which is why we chose to stay here. We stayed three nights in the most wonderful luxurious tents set in the grounds.The property is immaculately clean, the food delicious and plentiful, and the staff absolutely wonderful. A variety of safari's are on offer and everything is tailored to meet individual needs and wishes. The sundowner safari walking to the river with the elephants and watching them bathe as the sun went down was an absolute highlight. The elephants here are treated with such kindness, they live in small groups, they are not chained nor ridden on by tourists, never have I seen such happy looking elephants. Other animals kept here such as oxon also look very well cared for and much of the food for the hotel is grown on its own organic farm. A word on costs; Having stayed just one night in Sauraha and done one jeep safari there I can honestly say that Tiger Tops, which is all inclusive is excellent value for money. The safari's are fantastic and the guides attentive and knowledgeable.  If you care about elephants and ethical tourism please please stay at Tiger Tops when you visit Chitwan, they are pioneering the way forward and it is up to us the tourists to support them. You will not be disappointed.

If you want a perfect location, with a calming environment, delicious food....and elephants who are treated kindly then this is your destination.  The elephants stay with other elephants that they have bonded with, there are no chains here.  Large corrals that they roam as they wish..  You can so spend time with elephants but there is no riding. Take a journey with them into the jungle, go with them to the river and see them bathe.

Bhim Thanet, naturalist, personally picked me up from the bus station and was so informative even on the drive to the Elephant Camp.  There he gave me a tour of the camp and the staff had a lovely lunch waiting for me even though my arrival was a bit late.  Tara of the mgmt team also came by and the two of them helped me plan my 3 days to the fullestBhim was able to create a visit exceeding any expectations. Even that first afternoon we went walking and located a rhino rolling around in secluded stream. We were able to observe her up quite close but from the safety behind trees above the bank of the stream. I particularly appreciated our conversations with the local people that Bhim would meet along the way.  Once we talked to a family about their farm and what they were preparing that evening. Another time we met families at the sacred river and they explained to me their special offerings and rituals. It was very special when they blessed me and dotted colors on my forehead.I took advantage of all opportunities with the elephants on a jungle walk, down to gather grass, and to the river for bathing. Within the bounds of being part of the camp, you have a natural experience and insight into how they interact with each other without much constraint in a reasonably free environment. The contrast I saw in comparison to an obviously upset Bull elephant on a chain in a natl park outpost was profound and sad. The Elephant Camp provides the opportunity to spend your free time being close to the elephants watching their behavior and occasionally watching them watching youBhim gave me so many memorable moments. We saw rhino over 40 times and he spotted the big Bull Elephant for me across the grassland. It was exciting when he pointed out fresh tiger tracks from earlier that morning and then the drag track where the tiger took its kill into the forest.  Crocodile, wild bore, deer, and many beautiful birds such as the most magnificent white / brown hornbill I'd ever seen.  At the river I found the dance of the peacock really cool.  Sure enough after an appropriate circular dance showing his magnificent feathers the pea hens came out the forest to check him out.A highlight to my particular trip was when a powerful, really powerful, lightning and rain storm blew though. Rest assured the tent accomodation was more than up to the task and I was dry on my porch watching the show. All of the sudden a large shadow passed over my tent. I was totally surprised and looked behind me through the tent. A lightning strike exposed the massive shadowy outline of an elephant just beyond my tent in its enclosure. I laughed out loud as it first had been a bit scary when the shadow crossed the tent.  Then in just a few moments when the next lightening strike occurred it had vanished. Surreal as though a scene from a Hollywod movieTiger Tops Elephant Camp, a rich and intimate experience and the hardest part will be departing.  Food good, service excellent, tent accomodation clean & comfortable

I cannot tell you how awful my experience was.  They spent 3hrs showing me deer and ignored me when I told them I have deer in my yard at home daily-I have actually wondered if they ignored my comments because I am a woman.  The jeep broke down 3 times-the driver was able to fix the battery and the fuel pump but the 3rd time he was stumped so we sat in the jungle 2 hrs waiting for another jeep when the guide had told me it would only take 30 min to walk out?  Needless to say when we finally got back at 7, I was too upset to do anything else and was thrilled to leave today.

After a nightmare road trip from Pokhara we were met by very friendly staff at the lodge. Our room was basic but clean and comfortable.  We then had lunch with the ever helpful Molly who suggested the best ways of making the best of our two night staff.  An evening walk in the jungle with the elephants then the Jeep safari the next day finishing with an ox cart ride through the local villages.  Sambu was our guide for our stay and we really couldn't have wished for anyone more knowledgeable and helpful.   We loved the whole ethos of the lodge and the passion of the  staff towards the elephants, local villages , food etc.  Really recommend staying here you won't be disappointed!

Tiger Tops is truly an unforgettable experience. The lodge itself is beautifully designed, and despite staying in the tents, I felt like I was in a luxury hotel. The staff is so friendly, and even joined us for drinks by the fire on some nights. There is an abundance of activities you can choose from, so you surely won't get bored, and you cannot go wrong in your selection. From watching the sunset over the river with a drink in your hand, to taking a nature walk with elephants, to cruising through Chitwan in a jeep safari, these were memories I'll take with me for the rest of my life. Stay at Tiger Tops-- you will not regret it!

A very good place to stay and relax your time in Nepal. People are very helpful, each and every people were very helpful. Polite and had a good discipline. Place was very quiet and it is far from city, but there will be a hotel pick up, but will charge you some extra cost. Foods were delicious, all the meals were super super delicious. Also it is not only toast, or cereals for the breakfast, they change every day. Same with the lunch and dinner. Lunch was basically typical Nepali menu, rice, lentil soup, meat, vegetable and pickle. Once you get into hotel compound you feel like you are at your own home. There are various activities, like walking with an elephant. This was a very special moment, where you can walk with 3 friendly elephants. A guy who was guiding us told the three elephants were best friends. Wish we were there for Summer, we could have swam along with the elephants, but we missed that opportunity as it was winter. We can walk with elephant to river sunset view where hotel takes you and you will already have a table and chair to relax and enjoy the sunset. Also hotel did not allow riding in an elephant, because they want to give freedom to an elephant. This is very good thought. morning boat ride where you could see birds. Jungle safari was thrilling, as you go into the dense forest, and all you could hear is sounds of different birds and animals. If you are lucky enough, you could see rhino, tigers or maybe more.2 nights were not enough at Tiger, wish i could have stayed longer at least for a week. If i ever go to Chitwan, I will definitely be staying at Tiger again. Thank you all the Tiger teams for making my stay wonderful.在尼泊爾旅行中讓你非常放鬆也非常好的一個住宿地點，每一個人員都非常熱心助人非常禮貌也有良好的紀律。飯店地點遠離市區很安靜但有市區接送，不過會收取一些額外的費用。早午晚三餐都超級好吃。早餐不是只有烤吐司或麥片，而是每一天都有不一樣的變化(午餐和晚餐也是)。午餐基本上是典型的尼泊爾式料理，米飯，扁豆湯，肉類，蔬菜和醃菜，這一切讓你覺得你在自己家一樣的感受。飯店會安排各種活動，像和大象一起散步，這是一個非常特別的時刻，可以和三隻友善的大象一起散步。引導我們前進的嚮導說這三隻大象是最好的朋友。真希望我們是夏天來到這裡，這樣我們就可以和大象一起游泳，但我們在冬天來到這裡錯過了這個機會，和大象走到河邊看日落美景，當你抵達河岸時飯店已經布置好桌椅讓你在此放鬆享受日落。此外，酒店不允許騎乘大象，因為他們想給大象的自由，這是很好的想法。早上安排划船，可以看到鳥。叢林探險非常令人驚奇，你能聽到的是不同的鳥類和動物的聲音。如果夠幸運，你可以看到犀牛老虎或者是更多。在Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge 2個晚上是不夠的，希望下一次我可以停留至少一個禮拜。如果我去奇特旺，我一定會再次住在虎。謝謝所有的Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge team成員，使我這次的住宿非常精彩。

To echo previous reviews, I chose to stay at Tiger Tops due to their sustainable outlook and ethical elephant treatment. There is no doubt that they are completely committed to this and the relationship they have with the elephants is beautiful to witness. Walking in the jungle alongside the elephants is an unforgettable experience, supplemented by the exceptional knowledge of the experienced naturalists that have been with Tiger Tops for decades. Both the facilities at the lodge and the service from the friendly staff are also excellent. I visited at the start of the winter season in Nepal. The mornings were slightly chilly, but quickly warmed up with the sun. Wildlife viewing in the park is only slightly impacted, but there are fewer tourists - an great time to visit! Visiting Tiger Tops is not just a fantastic addition to your time in Nepal, but is helping to fund one if the few organisations in the area that is fully committed to the conservation of the national park and strives to protect its wildlife.

If you go to Nepal don't miss Tiger Tops! You will have an experience of a lifetime. The staff is amazing and what they teach you and show you is unforgettable. I loved spending time with the elephants. We trekked with them in the preserve and watched them bathe and drink in the river while enjoying the sunset and a glass of wine-magical ! Also had exciting jeep and boat safaris looking for rhinos, crocodiles, monkeys, tigers deer and birds. The food is very good and plentiful and they cater to all dietary needs. Perfect for families, couples or groups.

It's a long and bumpy journey to get there but it is worth it for the overall experience. The accommodation is simple but adequate, and the food is OK but this is sort of incidental as you don't travel all that way for the room and board. The place has a great vibe and the people there make you feel very welcome from the moment you arrive. They help you select activities that suit your interests from a wide range of options. Watching the mahouts helping the elephants bathe was very special and the jeep safaris into the jungle were excellent (spotting rhino each time) with very attentive Rangers/naturalists. There are plenty of activities to fill the day, but also a nice pool to relax by if you have some free time. Despite the lodge name, tiger or leopard sightings are incredibly rare so this should not be the reason to come here - but if you are looking for a great overall experience of the natural side of Nepal then this place should be a great option to consider.

From the very first welcome drink to the final drop off at the bus station, TigerTops Hotel and lodge exceeded our expectations. We stayed in the relatively new elephant camp, where you are immersed in the daily life of elephants through a natural observant perspective rather than elephant safaris. The staff are so welcoming and friendly, they fulfil your every need and more. The safari tents are very comfortable, with adjoining private bathrooms with hot showers. Every day our beds were made, complimentary drinking water is provided and our tents prepared for bed every night during dinner. We went and watched elephant bathing in the river, the mahouts cut grass in the mornings while the elephants graze, and jungle walks in the afternoon with the elephants to spot rhinos and tigers. I left my phone charger behind in the tent, and the staff phoned our bus and asked for my address in Kathmandu to send it to me. So kind. It Would be great to see more lodges take TigerTops as an example and give their elephants a more natural experience in captivity. Well done TigerTops 👍

I was fortunate to be able to participate in an elephant Footcare workshop led by elephant expert Carol Buckley Sept. 10-15, 2016 at Tiger Tops Elephant Camp.  It was the end of the monsoon season and so TT elected to house us in the lodge instead of the tents.  I can't praise this establishment highly enough! This goes for every aspect of the experience: the spacious, relaxing common areas of the lodge, the large comfy rooms with private baths, the beautifully landscaped grounds with walking paths and a (totally unexpected) swimming pool, the fascinating and informative nature tours, the plentiful healthy and delicious meals, and BEST of all - THE STAFF.  They treat each guest like the most important person in the world.  Every single encounter was delightful; whether with a member of the wait staff, guest relations, maintenance, grounds keeper, tour guide, or mahout.  All are friendly, exceedingly courteous, knowledgeable and eager to help.  The guides are locals who have a vast storehouse of knowledge about all the surrounding flora and fauna.  I came simply to be with elephants.  I came away with so much more.  Tiger Tops has been doing eco tourism for a very long time.  They are now leading the way for providing  even better living conditions for elephants.  The elephants in their care are all chain-free and the mahouts have embraced gentle humane methods of guiding the elephants. Tourist rides are no longer offered; instead, visitors are treated to the unique experience of following the herd throughout the day as they walk to the river, bathe, and gather grass.  What could be better than watching elephants that are free to simply be elephants?In my humble opinion, you simply can't do better than this.

If you want to do something different in a pristine environment and escape the crowds, then this is for you. Their accommodation is pleasant, their food is delicious as well as sustainably, seasonally and organically grown and to excite you even more...their elephants are off the chains. Our jungle walk was beyond our expectations. We were walking alongside with the elephants (who are no longer doing rides by the way, but who are enjoying their retirement by naturally socializing with other elephants) and we saw rhinos, wild birds, mongoose. Tiger Tops has excellent customer service with very comfortable beds. The only thing we would have appreciated was having a stronger fan at night. Other than that, we were very comfortable during our stay. The children had a fantastic time as they were able to learn how to prepare "elephant sandwiches" and to see them bathing in their natural habitat. Book today! You won't regret it.

This is a brilliant place to stay and experience what Chitwan National Park has to offer. All activities are included and you get to decide exactly how you want to experience everything. Take a jeep safarie with an expert guide to look for Rhino, tiger, leopard, sloth bear, wild boar, 4 species of deer, mongoose and over 400 species of birds. The staff are great, cool of in the pool, go on elephant walks to see Rhino up close, village tours, river tours. Meals are all tasty and use organically grown food from their garden. All other guests believed this is the best place to experience Chitwan.

I spent three days at Tiger Top Elephant Camp and I can't put a finger on anything that wasn't just excellent: waking up to the sound and smell of elephants, who were there right in my backyard of my tent, very good food, very nice employees and all the walks with the elephants: to the river and in the most exciting junglewalk, where I met two rhinos, but never felt scared since the elephants protected me.All I can say: if you consider going there, just do it and you will not regret it 😄

I'm an elephant lover and have traveled all over the world the last 25 years to be with them - on several safaris in Africa, on elephant trekking in Thailand/Myanmar, I've seen them in India, Sri Lanka and at least 5 times in Chitwan Sauraha in Nepal. My visit to Tiger Tops Tharu Elephant Camp has been my biggest experience so far. Opposite all other elephant experiences I have had you're not supposed to touch, feed, ride or swim with the elephants at Tiger Tops Tharu Elephant Camp. You're 'only' supposed to be with them which is the whole idea behind the elephant camp. We stayed in one of the furnished tents (with super bathrooms attached) that are located in the middle of the 3 huge open 'jungle spaces' where the animals lives unchained, as close to their normal surroundings as possible. We spend our time watching them. From our tent, from the restaurant, from the benches around the camp, walking with them in the jungle or sitting on the river bank  watching them bath and play in the sunset or preparing their food. I don't know if the 'no touching' rules also apply to  the elephants. If they do - the elephants give a s*** about them :-). After a couple of hours the curious animals start communicating with you. Either with sounds (they fart as crazy) or by getting as close to you as possible and just communicating through the eyes - or even shake 'hands/trunks' which happened to me. Sauraha the village in Chitwan most travelers visit is very touristic (almost like Thamel in Kathmandu) with souvenir shops, restaurants, tour operators and beach bars everywhere. So if you are that kind of traveler Sauraha is the right place for you. Tiger Tops Elephant Camp in Tharu is located in a very picturesque, peaceful and colorful village in the most beautiful nature that exist in Terrai - perfect for a short walk if you need a break from the animals. So if that-s what you like Tharu is the place to go.Opposite the continental food in Tiger Tops Lodge (500 m from the camp) the food we had at the Elephant Camp (included in the price) was Nepalese. BUT in a super quality.Our biggest mistake was that we 'only' stayed 2 nights (one whole day). We really needed at least one more day with the animals.The place is absolutely fantastic if you travel with kids.We will be back.

We visited Tharu Lodge in March 2014.  It was an amazing experience!  The sleeping accomodations for comfortable, clean and nice.  We were expecting them to be far more rustic than they were and were pleasantly surprised with the shower and water pressure.  The food was outstanding and the staff was second to none!  Everyone was very attentive and kind.  All of our needs were met with a smile.  Feeding, bathing and riding the elephants was so much fun.  Our guides on our river trip and elephant rides were excellent.  They all got us up close with many different birds and animals.  On one elephant ride we came nose to nose with a rhino  and the respect these animals had for each other was easily witnessed.  The lodge manager was very hands-on and checked-in with us several times to make certain our stay was better than we expected.  Tharu Lodge is a perfect place to relax, learn about Nepal and the jungle and be waited-on as much or as little as one desires.  I would return in a heartbeat!  Loved this place!!!

Staying at Tiger Tops was the highlight of my trip to Nepal. It's quiet and beautiful with great food and good guides. I decided to go to Sauraha to sample the difference and, although my room there was very luxurious the area seems much more of a package experience. At TT the elephants go deeper into the forest and the whole experience is more personalised- well worth the cost. Many people have also complained about the elephant breeding centre at Sauraha. Please don't support it - do your homework first.

Staying at tiger tops is truly an amazing experience. I was staying at one of the safari tents in tiger tops tharu village lodge. The tens are spacious and well maintained. The bathrooms attached. I think the only thing I would have missed was shampoo and conditioner to be provided by the lodge.Tiger tops really made my stay a unique and personalized experience. Compared to other lodges where you have a fixed schedule of activities, tiger tops tailors the activities as per your request and wishes. The activities range from elephant, boat and jeep safari to jungle walks and elephant bathing. You can also get guided tours through the tharu villages and to some of the environmental and community projects tiger tops funds and supports. I had the chance to get close to rhinos, see deers and crocs and many birds on my safaris. Apparently we were very close to a tiger but couldn't spot it. The price for tiger tops is not cheap. However when you consider that their price includes the room, all meals, and any activities tailored towards your liking than this is a pretty good deal. Also keeping in mind that some of your money goes to the awesome local projects tiger tops supports, than that's even more good news. I really enjoyed my stay and felt very looked after. The day I left they even provided a lunch pack for my 6 hr road trip. The passion of all staff including guides and management for nature and conservation is just incredible. Facilities and service are very good and of high standard. one might find the food a bit simple but it's very yummy. I can't wait for the jungle lodge to reopen again and experience tiger tops right in chitwan.

Our family of 5 (14,12,5) stayed at Tharu Lodge for 3 nights enjoying Elephant back safaris, Jeep safaris and canoe trip and elephant bathing activities .  Everyone was very professional there, making sure all in our parties were well taken care of.  The lodge is constructed using local materials which made up of dung,clay and dirt.  It is very interesting for our kids seeing such basic construction and serving the community well!  We went to bed early as there is really nothing to do in the night and u would like to get up early to make the most of the day.  Lots of open spaces for my 5 year old to run around, climbing tree houses which I think they use as a lookout .NAture guides were all very experienced in educating us on all the wildlife found in chitwan.  We also had the opportunity to visit a local school sponsored and built by the lodge for underprivileged children in the vicinity.  We also brought stationaries for the kids to use in school, they were overjoyed with such a simple gift.Every detail was looked after very well. We loved the huge fireplace for cool evenings. Chitwan is at a lower elevation, it gets hot during the day and cool off in the evenings.

Our experience at Tiger Tops was nothing short of fantastic, in every respect.  From the time we arrived, the professional and very friendly staff made us feel relaxed and comfortable.  They take care of everything and are not only very knowledgeable but also very, very friendly.The excursions, whether riding on or bathing elephants, to the jeeps and boats, morning hikes, or village tour were always fun and educational.  I recommend all the activities to any visitor.We cannot speak highly enough of the entire Tiger Tops organization.  If you are looking for a relaxing, fun, and stimulating experience in Nepal, we strongly recommend you visit Tiger Tops!

We stayed at Tiger tops for two nights. Had an amazing time. It is perfect get away from busy streets of Kathmandu or a relaxing place after you are back from trekking. We stayed in Safari tents  and they were so good. Sleeping in those tents was so warm and nice and waking up to the sounds of birds in the forest was amazing. The elephant safari and the jungle were good. We spotted few rhinos and few birds. Elephant orientation was good, learnt a lot about Asian and African elephants. The boat safari was the highlight of all, we got to experience amazing sunset from the river side. Food was amazing and the staff is very friendly. Saarc countries get 50% off on hotel book so check for the prices before you book.

Tiger tops are clearly the best jungle safari team at Chitwan, and with higher prices than most, you expect it to be good, but our experience at Tiger Tops just blew us away.  Gorgeous luxury tent (complete with hot water bottles tucked in after they turned down our beds,) delicious food, highly attentive service and very well organised and interesting activities. We stayed three nights and I think many of those who we met (staying two nights) were jealous of our extra night in paradise! The staff were also overwhelmingly friendly and hospitable, as well as truly knowledgable and passionate about the wildlife. Talking with the elephant trainer about his experiences with the elephants and their individual stories was a real highlight. When it came down to it through, it was really the finer details that sets this place apart. Every possible need was considered for us and arrangements made to ensure we were comfortable. A perfect example of this was the surprise we received on arrival back to Kathmandu to have a car waiting for us to take us to our new hotel courtesy of tiger tops. We had only mentioned arranging a taxi at the other end to a staff member who hen arranged this car to be waiting for us when we arrived. What outstanding service!

We were so looking forward to our time at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge! From start to finish, they provided a magical experience, from when Sam picked us up from the Bharatpur airport, to when we sadly departed after our 3 days/2 nights. The lodge itself is stunning and remote, and you really feel like you are in a secluded and peaceful place. The staff were all lovely and attentive, and the food was absolutely outstanding. We loved feeling like were in a proper jungle safari lodge with set meal times, jungle safaris, and sundowners. Of course, the highlight was the "walking with elephants and sundowner" which we did two evenings. It is no secret that in Asia, there is the practice of riding elephants, capturing them, etc. which we would never condone. Tiger Tops, however, has improved their beliefs and offers amazing lives for the elephants they currently have. The herd they have is made up of around 10 middle-aged females ages 40-65, who had already previously been domesticated (in India). They still have the herd that they now will care for so they can live out their lives comfortably. They each have reasonably large enclosures for sleeping/overnight (not chained up like other places) and during the day they go to the jungle with their handlers to feed. At the end of the day, a pair of elephants will walk with the tourists (namely to protect from the rhinos) which can bring in some money to help pay for their care. The handlers really understand and love their elephants, and even let two of them stay in the same enclosure because they are best friends and prefer to be together (so sweet!). During one sundowner, the handler convinced the elephant to go fully submerged into the river, so he could give her a proper scrub down and he really got into washing and scrubbing her head. The morning visit to elephant camp to make sandwiches is also such a treat. The elephants were so friendly and gentle and always loved a cuddle and an elephant sandwich!Our guide, Sam, was excellent, kind, and ever so smiley! One day, we saw a season record for him of 10 rhinos during one walk! The staff all seemed to work there for a long long time, which goes to show what a great place it is. The food was outstanding, with lovely vegetarian options as well, and the food and beverage staff were excellent. I highly recommend Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge.

Words really fail me as I try and adequately represent the beauty of my experience as a guest,  and the Lodge itself-which is only surpassed by the beauty of the staff and management. Every guest is regarded as a VIP in their approach to hospitality here. This is very obvious from the moment you arrive. The food far exceeded any expectation (or quite honestly, apprehension) I had knowing I was staying at a Lodge in the middle of Nepal. Frankly, the food and service for all meals were on par with the very best international resorts for which we have  stayed. There was never a moment I felt unsafe, unwelcome, or unappreciated. Their elephant program with very spacious chain free corrals was truly the impetus for what I consider now to be the most meaningful experience imaginable. The owner of the Lodge demonstrates his unsurpassed level of care and commitment to these magnificent and deserving animals, through his collaboration with world renown elephant expert Carol Buckley of Elephant Aid International. To have this caliber of experience and know that as a guest you are supporting extraordinary efforts in the lives of these animals is second to none. From the mahouts (who are rock stars) to everyone affiliated with hospitality here, you will be convinced that you are as special as they believe you are. Oh, it truly shows. Walk side by side with the elephants to the river each night....yeah, dreams are made of this. Go.....and then you’ll spend time figuring out how you will be going back. Wow.

Tiger Tops is amazing. I was very impressed at the excellent way Tiger Tops cares for their elephants. They are in spacious corals instead of on chains like most of Nepal's captive elephants. Instead of offering rides on the backs of the elephants, which is very harmful to them, Tiger Tops offers a wonderful experience of walking next to the elephants  as you explore, together, the natural areas. The best part of the day is watching the elephants swim in the river each evening.

We stayed here for two nights at the elephant camp. It was absolutely amazing. The price included three meals a day (the food was delicious!) and we stayed in one of the tents in the Elephant Camp. The beds were comfy and we were surprised by the lack of “wildlife” inside the tent! We saw rhinos and elephants. The sunset elephant walk is the best experience. This place comes highly recommended!!

Absolutely incredible experience. Walking with the elephants and seeing rhino in the wild was a highlight. The staff are super friendly and knowledgeable. Comfortable safari style tents with private attached bathrooms. Great food. Don't stay anywhere else !

When looking for somewhere to stay in Chitwan is was incredibly important to us to find somewhere that matched shares our ethos when it comes to the care of the animals. Pioneers of environmentally responsible tourism, Tiger Tops was the first in Nepal (and still one of very few) to ban elephant riding and chains. The 14 elephants that live here were rescued from exploitative commercial industries in India and are now lovingly cared for by their keepers - individuals who have worked alongside the elephants for many years to develop trusting, mutually respectful relationships. Here you live among the most amazing wildlife in the most beautiful setting. We let them know we were vegan before we arrived and accommodating isn’t the word, they bent over backwards!! The food is all included as part of what you pay and everyone has the same meal and rather than give us a second rate option - just missing out on the main and having the side veg - they created totally new dishes. They made vegan puddings and had them as the dessert for the whole place so everyone ate the same - they even made their own almond milk for us! The safari lodge and pool area is gorgeous and the activities like the sunset drinks with the elephants bathing are just insane. Wil 100% be returning despite the fact I am very scared of spiders and you really can’t eacape them here - especially in your bathroom!! In all seriousness though, if anyone is interested in sustainable tourism and amaaazing food and service, this place is a MUST

Undoubtedly the leader in responsible tourism practice in the jungles of Nepal. Tiger Tops pioneered eco practices and everyone follows them. Their dedication to the principle of conservation first is highly commendable. Wish more companies had the same vision and action .Our first ever sighting of a Tiger in the wild, enhanced this trip even more, that too on our first Jeep Safari into the jungle. Sambhu, our naturalist rocks big time, as his patience, experience, and eagle eyes sighted the male tiger first as it made a river crossing. Wow. What an achievement!Thanks for everything. Truly memorable stay and what a lovely place.

I have been living in Nepal for many years. When I need to get away from the bustle of Kathmandu I dream of going to Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge. For me it has always been a piece of Heaven, but this time it was even more wonderful. The jeep safaris and joining the elephants on their daily excursions to gather their fodder and bathe in the river as well as sharing the silence of those moments with only the rushing of the water were so serene. The team of staff is all amazing, kind and always available. The rooms are so comfortable and cozy; you have the feeling that you are indeed in the jungle of one of the most beautiful countries in the world. Here you share your space with Elephants, Rhinos and Tigers (this time I did not see any but I have been spoilt in the past) as well as leopards, vultures, deer, monkeys, sloth bears and wild boar. Tharu is also a paradise for bird watchers. In the mornings you wake to a delicious breakfast, lunch is the best Nepali food, which even Kathmandu cannot offer, and the candlelight dinners are hosted under the mango tree.  I cant wait until I return in a few weeks when the weather will be warmer flycatcher birds of paradise will be back to amaze us.Thank you THARU LODGE!

Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge is located just outside Chitwan National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. We choose to stay at Tiger Tops because of their ethical elephant treatment, environment friendly practices and partnership/support of the local villagers. But there are many more reasons why we enjoyed our 3-night stay and wish it had been longer! The staff is friendly, helpful, and welcoming. We were provided personal attention from the minute we arrived until our departure (including waiting with us at the airport when our flight was delayed). The lodge accommodations, while simplistic, are comfortable despite being in the middle of the jungle. Three delicious meals are provided daily and include produce from the lodge’s own organic garden. Meals are served either in the dining hall or outdoors if the weather is pleasant (we loved having lunch al fresco). Dining provided a wonderful opportunity to mingle with other guests and chat about the day, especially around the evening fire with a drink. And finally, there’s numerous activities to choose from! We especially enjoyed getting up close and personal with the lodge elephants. Encounters included a jungle walk alongside these gentle giants, grass cutting by the river, and learning how to make elephant sandwiches (kuchis) with the mahouts. We also thoroughly relished the jeep and river safaris. The finely tuned eyes and ears of our skilled naturalist guide Shambhu were always on the lookout for wildlife. What a thrill to come within feet of the endangered one-horned rhino! If you want a glamorous and glitzy environment, then Tiger Tops is not the place for you. But if you’re looking for an intimate, authentic jungle experience, you’re going to love it here! Many thanks to the lodge staff for all that they did to make our stay a memorable one.

The excellent: all nature/wildlife guides, mahouts, and other lodge staff were attentive, responsive, and kind; food was great all around; LOVED the elephant jungle walk, river safari, AND elephant sandwich making (which was quite fun & interesting although I first thought it sounded a bit hokey)Room for improvement: front-office communication. It felt at times that the replies to my questions during booking process were piece-meal instead of full answers.  Instead of problem-solving in a given situation, they'd also resort to literal reaction. For example, I asked why our flight to Kathmandu was booked for 11:55am when I was previously told that we'd be on earliest flight out around 10am.  The front office then said they rebooked our flight to 10:10am but took more than a day and a half to confirm flight info, which made us suspicious that they actually hadn't rebooked our flight until much later.  Our 10:20am Yeti flight then did not leave until way past Noon, *AFTER* all other Buddha Air flights (including 11:50am Buddha Air flight) departed, and this messed up our plans in Kathmandu.  It would have been better if the front office explained a) about morning fog situation & resulting flight delays (this seemed to be well understood by all lodge staff as they told us about morning flight delays as we were leaving the lodge) , b) that Buddha Air is more reliable, and c) acted promptly to rebook us on mid-morning Buddha Air flight instead of 10:20am Yeti flight just because I happened to mention that flights around 10am were still available online.  Tips: safari tents can be interesting if never experienced before, but here one does not get the benefit of closeness to wildlife since the entire lodge ground is well protected and away from wildlife; we were in tent 3 which is closest to the dining hall (& kitchen facility) and found a rat munching on our bar soap at night - the lodge staff quickly & thoroughly cleaned our bathroom so we weren't too concerned however; good bathroom facilities & amenities especially considering the location, but the shower water can been less than lukewarm late at night or early in the morning in December - better to shower in the late afternoon immediately after last safari activity of the day; DO NOT expect to see tigers or clouded leopards here - tigers are nocturnal (there's no night safari & early morning has dense fog), and clouded leopards are mostly in the Himalayan foothills

As a seasoned traveller in African safaris I knew this would be very different. The National Park is dense and tracks through it limited in access so game spotting is much more difficult but a good experience. Our tracker did find excellent Rhino with baby and footprints of a huge Tiger but little else from two safaris in a very old and uncomfortable basic land rover with the roof cut off. Walking with the elephants in dense woodland / grasses was a great experience (be aware of leeches).Accommodation basic and tired, food reasonable (served Nepalese style at dinner if requested). Met by a volunteer who settled us - never found out who was in charge and customer service could have been much better.

We stayed at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge in October 2018, in a group of four.  The lodge is located at the far western end of Chitwan National Park - which necessitates a 1 hour (plus) private vehicle ride from the airport.  But the benefit of this is that it's away from the main tourism centres of Sauraha.  You're unlikely to see any other lodges or their guests during your stay at Tiger Tops.   Yes, you can drive 8 hours from Kathmandu to the lodge, but we were certainly glad we opted for the 20 minute flight instead.Yes, you'll find cheaper Chitwan accommodation - particularly around Sauraha - but you'll be hard pressed to find any resort that's as committed to its guests, and to preserving local wildlife and culture.  And - this is a big one - a resort that's as committed to elephant welfare.  Their team of mahouts are  passionately dedicated to their elephants, and it really shows.  The animals are well cared for - never chained or beaten - and just so gentle.  Watching them bathe in the river at the end of each day (with a drink in hand!) was worth the price of our stay alone!Tiger Tops really is leading a new wave of responsible tourism in Nepal. There are lots of cut price operators catering for budget backpackers, giving them elephant rides and a mass-tourism experience.  But if you really care about elephant welfare - and that means NOT riding them - head to Tiger Tops.  You get to spend much more time with their elephants than at other resorts - helping care for and feed them if you wish - and spending precious hours escorted by them on jungle walks.  Seeing a rhino ON FOOT protected by two elephants is an experience you'll never forget.Our jeep safaris were very generous - and we saw lots of additional wildlife, including deer, monkeys, 9 rhinos, wild peacocks and more.  The river safari was totally relaxing as well.The other thing you'll notice about Tiger Tops is its close relationship with the local Tharu Village, which helps provide the resort staff - and in turn gets support for education and health facilities.There's nothing glossy and shiny about Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge - and you wouldn't want it any other way.  The resort really nestles into the jungle, and we saw a snake and plenty of hornbills really close to our accommodation.  Not to mention millions of frogs!  You do feel like you are on safari. We opted for the safari tents, and loved the experience.  It was a warm time of year, but the fans in the safari tent made life comfortable.  Keep the zips done up tight though - unless you want a visitor in the night.  The daily activities mean you'll sleep like a log, whichever accommodation you choose.  The food was really great for the duration of our three night stay - although if anything, we'd prefer some more Nepali food options.  But in all servings were generous and tasty.A big thank you to Marie, Reshmi and Jack for helping organise our stay, and ensuring it was comfortable and enriching.  Thanks also to our guide Gyan for his attention and knowledge.We will be back, and can't wait to share it with our friends :)

Wonderful location and even the garden boast over 300 species of birds - including an extremely noisy pair of hornbills. The staff are knowledgeable and enthusiastic abut the wildlife and great at organising trips into the great range of habitats in the Park. Don't just go for the rhinos - although you'll probably get grid up-close encounters, but enjoy the smaller wildlife too!

The service in the hotel is excellent, the food is delicious and served by people that likes to make you feel at home. Molly was there to be sure we were confortable all time. As the weather is cold in this part of the year, the put hot water bags in our beds to have it warm for us. The jeep safari was awesome, our driver and guide really know about how to hit those roads in the jungle and how to find the animals. We saw rhinos, elephants, monkeys, crocodiles, deers, birds, buffalos, etc. At the end of the safari in the beach of the river there were personnel from the hotel waiting for us with the elephants so we can see them playin gin the water, chairs and tables with peanuts and beverage so we can enjoy the sunset too. The walking tour with Elephants was amazing too. I highly recommend to stay in this hotel if you are going to Chitwan in Nepal.

I visited Tiger Tops in early Dec 2018. The lodge accommodation was fantastic, though they do also supply a glamour-camping experience. Our room included Tiger Tops bathrobes and take-home aluminium water bottles. The food was excellent, varied and plentiful. I especially enjoyed the lunches out on the lawn. The grounds were beautifully kept and the customer service was astounding. The best thing however was the fact that they have removed elephant riding, which is both physically and psychologically harmful to elephants. They are the only place in Nepal that have done this. You still get to be up close to the elephants and walk in the jungle with them. Tiger Tops have also done away with chains by installing a fencing system. The fenced areas are quite large. Well done, Tiger Tops, if only other elephant camps in Nepal would follow your lead.

We spent 4 nights at Tiger Tops and we were very impressed with all aspects of the tour. We were collected and returned to the airport in air conditioned vehicles. the meals were interesting and plenty of variety to cater for a range of tastes. There were several very interesting activities that you could choose from. Im my case I chose to to do the same walk with the elephants three times! The guides were very helpful, and our guide went out of his way to find a Hornbill because of my interest in seeing one! Despite the very heavy vegetation after the wet season we saw many examples of wildlife such as Rhinos, Gharials and barking deer.The grounds and recreational areas are extensive so if you choose to have a quiet time there are plenty of relaxing choices. Overall a very pleasant and interesting experience.

I just spent two nights at the Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge after the Asia for Animals conference.  The place is amazing! The moment I stepped over the threshold I literally felt the stress pouring out of my body. Besides the tranquil environment, delicious food, comfortable accommodation and the friendly staff, the experience interacting with the lodge elephants was the highlight of my stay. Walking with them into the forest, watching them bathing in the river, hearing them talk with each other at night from my tent. Congratulations to Tiger Tops for giving these elephants a chain free life. Thank you for giving us tourists the opportunity to enjoy their company cruelty free.

We stayed for 3 nights at the Tiger Tharu Lodge and had some amazing safaris whilst there.  Our guide Bim made sure we had an exciting timing and ensured that each safari was tailor made to what we wanted to do.  Although we did not see the elusive tiger we certainly found plenty marks of them. We were so close!!The rooms were lovely and there appeared to be enough hot water for a decent shower.  We were our most days and were provided with a packed lunch which was delicious.  Staff were wonderful, polite and friendly at all times.  We had a wonderful time here.

We flew in to Baratpur and our brief 48 hour trip quickly got started. We were met by Danny, who was to be our guide for the entire trip, and were quickly whisked off to a waiting vehicle for the hour long transfer to our lodge accommodation.It is true to say that the transfer will not feature as a highlight but it is best described as interesting. A decent description would put it as a typical Indian subcontinent road journey with pedestrians, cycles and motorbikes all competing with cars, trucks for safe passage.Our arrival at Tiger Tops was very efficient with us being greeted and issued with instructions for lunch and activities. We were quickly shown to our lodge which was very well appointed with plenty of space. One striking feature of the rooms was the absence of locks on the doors!After a quick freshen up we were off to lunch where we enjoyed a pleasant out doors meal with our host, Tara, who quickly appraised us of our activity options. After agreeing our programme we met up with Danny who took us along to walk with elephants in the buffer zone, outside the Chitwan National Park itself. The highlight of this afternoon walk was an encounter with two rhinoceroses who were enjoying the afternoon sun in a mud hole! Danny made sure that we did not miss any action and demonstrated his extensive knowledge of the wildlife.On return to the lodge we quickly spruced up for dinner which was served in the main building around a roaring fire.The next day followe a similar format with a boat trip on the river in the morning followed by a safari in the National Park in the afternoon. The highlight was the chance to observe the wildlife in natural surroundings but the manner in which everything was presented and organised was without blemish. The staff was friendly and knowledgeable with the lodge providing beautiful surroundings.All in all the trip was brilliant if only a bit too short. Still it gives us a reason to return.The return trip to the airport was again quite interesting and possibly not for the faint hearted but this should not detract from the Tiger Tops experience, made possible by wonderful accommodating staff and genuinely luxurious lodge accommodation.

We had always wanted to visit Chitwan, and scoped possible family-friendly lodges with access to the park.  We wanted to see animals, explore and speak with locals to get a sense of life on the edge of the park.  We opted for Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge as it provided this option for comfortable, responsible tourism with a sense of how locals live.  Among the highlights of our trip: a jeep safari to see wildlife in the buffer zone, rhino spotting, bathing elephants, walking in the jungle, and the large swimming pool! Important to note, while other providers also have elephants, Tiger Tops elephants are not chained and have a large area to roam around freely.  The lodge is trying to limit their ecological footprint, serving delicious locally grown food, and attends to your every need.  A great stay with little ones in a gorgeous natural setting.  We highly recommend!

We had heard about Tiger Tops for a while, so we really wanted to visit it during our first trip to Chitwan. What they have done here is *exceptional*  It is a great place for the elephants (which are not chained and have a HUGE area to roam around freely in their corrals) and to learn about their daily routines. We took a jeep safari to see the wildlife in the buffer zone. We saw rhinos (twice in a day!), spotted deer, barking deer and mongoose along with various wild bird species. This is a great place for birdwatchers also! The staff is very friendly and uber competent. Our activities were planned in advance with flexible time slots. They made sure each one of our needs was addressed. If you have dietary restrictions, rest assure that the food will be provided accordingly (and it will be delicious). I am a vegetarian and I loved everything they prepared. We hope to see more resorts like Tiger Tops where there is harmony between elephant welfare and nature appreciation. You will remember your stay here for many, many years!

I was there for 2 days at March 3rd 2016 and March 4th 2016. I had awesome time with Tiger Tops Family at Nawalparasi. It can’t be compare with the other company Tiger Tops has a won reputation. Your hospitality, your food, and your location everything is perfect with name and fame. The best part of your company which I really impressed that was Local organic food. I really appreciated those staff performance who involve in food and beverage department. You guys have a really great management system and experienced team, I enjoyed a lot with you activities package (jungle walk, River trip and Jungle Safar) with our guide Sambhu. Thank you Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge , Thank you Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge Family.Every penny is worth it.

You "glamp"( camp in style) in tents surrounded by chain free elephants . The elephants are truly respected and cared for.  they are not performing for you , you just get to be with them being elephants. From the minute they pick you up until they drop you off the staff of tiger tops takes care of everything you need during your stay.

It was difficult to sleep knowing that feet from my tent an entire herd of elephants surrounded me. It was heaven. There is nothing that compares to being immersed in the the world of elephants instead of them entertaining us in our world. Tiger Tops offers a unique experience like no other. At Tiger Tops Elephant Camp you live, breath and sleep with the elephants. A life changer for sure.

When I was told I would be camping with the elephants I was excited, however when I got to Tiger Tops Elephant Camp I became ecstatic, as this is the most luxurious camping I have ever encountered!  The beds were comfortable, hot water bottles at the ready for cold evenings, and bathrooms that rival many hotels I have stayed in.The staff were extremely knowledgeable when it came to the elephants and other wildlife in the area, and they were very helpful whenever we needed anything.  The food was also delicious and provided a variety, which can be hard to find in Nepal.   The time spent watching elephants from a respectable distance was incredible, keeping both guests and elephants happy.  We were able to see the mahouts were connected to their elephants and took great care of them.  Falling asleep to the sound of elephants rumbling is incredible.I hope to spend more time here in the future.  Thanks to the Tiger Tops Elephant Camp team for such a fantastic experience.

Stayed for 5 nights in late November with some family and friends. This was an unforgettable experience and am already planning to return in 2016.The accommodation was good and the service provided by the staff is to be commended.We went on the river cruise as part of our trip and to watch the sun go down sipping on some red wine really ended that day perfectly.Great to see the Elephants and how well taken care of they are.

We stayed 4 nights in this beautiful and very quiet place. This was one of our Highlights of the 4 week Nepal trip. We enjoyed the peaceful place with lots of nature in the lodge park and of course even more in the National Park. The good food based on local and organic products, the cozy Dining room with the fireplace (it can be quite cold at night in December!). The lunches under the trees in the park were also great.Tiger Tops has a great excursion Programme! In the evening we could always set the next days excursions together with the Manager or a Senior guide. The Elephant lecture, the Elephant ride, the oxcart and river excursion, and also the Jeep tour within the National Park with a visit of the old lodge within the park boundaries were all great. Thank you Noon for your enthusiastic guiding.Definitely a place to visit and fully worth the Price to pay.

Tiger Tops Tharu is a fantastic eco lodge right on the edge of Chitwan National Park. The whole experience exceeded our expectations. The accommodation is very comfortable and consistent with eco lodge approach e.g. no air conditioning (not an issue though), basic but clean bathroom. The main lodge building was comfortable and the three of us were made to feel very welcome. The quality of the meals was high and almost all food is apparently locally grown. A good example of nepalese food. A birthday cake was even found. The lodge has a huge warm pool and is set within beautiful grounds just above a river. All of the staff were very good, friendly and always helpful. Eva and Gabriel as client relations made us very welcome and first rate. Our guide was very informative and worked well with our preferences. The activities (all of which are included in the tariff) were fantastic. The Elephant safari and subsequent bathing in the river was a highlight and it was a delight to see the way "our" elephant (Hira Kali) was treated and responded. That we were able to get very close to a Rhino and her "baby" was special. the boat trip, the walking tour (for me), the bird walk (for Kathy), the village tour by bullock cart were all well worth doing. Even found time for a high quality yoga lesson from Eva and Gabriel.We were at the lodge for 48 hours which is just enough - I'd suggest a three night package though to fit everything in. Don't hesitate to come here!

If you want to visit the Chitwan Park, discover the nature on an elephant back, see unicorn rhinos, crocodiles and a lot of birds, meet wonderful people, GO TO THIS BEAUTIFUL TIGER LODGE !You will have a very environmental, confortable room made as the local houses. Don't be afraid everything is perfect, you will feel as an explorer in the jungle. Everything is done to preserve the nature.The staff is very nice, you can ask almost everything, they can do it with kindness and competences. All activities in the jungle (elephant ride, tracking, boat, jeep, ...) are included.If you really want to live like an explorer, they have also very confortable forest tents in the parc of the hotel as they had inside the Natural Park before (Nepalese Gov rightly decided to close the forest camp and keep the hotel at the border)

We stayed 3 nights and that felt the right time.  Accommodation is good, comfortable and homely it's not luxurious but its certainly very good with charachtor Staff are at worst good and mostly excellent.  Food was good and we loved the alfresco lunches and dinners.  The activities which are the reason you should come here are hugely enjoyable.  We managed 2 elephant safaris, a jeep safari, a 4 hour walking safari, and a combined ox cart and river boat trip.  On top of that helping wash the elephants is a real treat.  We also did the ox cart tour of nearby villages and whilst we loved it I did wish that we had walked to be that bit closer to the local people and their children who are a real real pleasure.  When I get grandchildren I'm bringing them here. We saw rhinos deer monkeys etc but no tiger although we did think that we heard one on the walking safari, good job we had the big sticks with us.

We spent 2 wonderful days and nights at the Tiger Tops Lodge.The lodge is set in an area of jungle adjacent to the Chitwan National Park (Hotels no longer allowed in the park).   The entire facility is built in the traditional Tharu style and set in  extensive  grounds - including swimming pool and outdoor eating areas.  We would not normally stay at an Eco hotel.  We are not interested in trekking, bush walking or bird-watching and I cannot remember the last time we went to a zoo.   We were booked into Tiger Tops as part of a package tour of Nepal.  We had some trepidation about the stay, but it turned out to be one of the highlights of our trip. On our first day we took an Elephant safari through the jungle - getting very close to a rhino.   Second day we started with a guided walking tour of some traditional local villages, followed after lunch with an ox-cart ride though the jungle and return to the lodge via canoe.  On the second night we were entertained by a group of local dancers and musicians - not a grand professional production, but thoroughly charming.     We stayed a tent-room (there are standard hotel rooms also).  The large tent was pitched under a high thatch-covered awning and amid dense trees/shrubs.   Inside the tent was a full king bed in one section and a dressing/storage area in another section.  The bathroom was a separate fixed structure adjacent to the tent, but under the same thatch awning.   It is not luxury by hotel room standards, but very good as tents go.   It was a little inconvenient having to zip/unzip the tent's screens whenever we moved in/out of the tent and more particularly if we went to the bathroom during the night.  All part of the experience of 'camping' in the jungle.  All parts of the 'room' were spotlessly clean and kept that way by frequent housekeeping visits.Our stay was ' full board'.  There was a set menu for each meal, but with enough dishes to satisfy all.   Every meal was excellent - Nepalese themed food, prepared largely from food grown/raised in the Lodge's farm.  Lunch and dinners were served on tables set out in the grounds by a small army of staff who made sure we were never left waiting for anything. The staff at Tiger Tops seemed enthusiastic about the Lodge, the park and providing good service.  We could have not asked for better.Internet is available free of charge via Wifi in the foyer areas only.  Worked well.  Like all parts of Nepal, power outages are common.  We had our share, but they did no really impact our stay. Overall, we had an unexpectedly great time at Tiger Tops.  We would recommend it to anyone wanting something a little different that affords a real insight into rural Nepalese life.  We would however suggest that as fun as the tent room was for two nights, if we had stayed longer, we would have been shifting into the standard rooms (which other guests told us were excellent).  If you have kids, as some of the guests did, they will be fully occupied having a great time.

We arrived after a very long drive from Kathmandu and were greeted wonderful cold towels and drinks. We were shown to our room, which was good and lunch was served in the garden, with the exotic birds flying from fruit tree to another. This is a paradise for bird lovers. The garden with tree platforms to relax, the pool and the hammocks were a wonderful way to relax. We had our elephant safari in the afternoon on Hera Kali and had various sightings of rhinoceros, deer. This was a very pleasant way of travelling through the buffer zone of the national park. Loved Hera and the way she lumbered through the jungle selecting her favourite leaves to snack on. The boat trip across the river early morning was like meditation and than jeep safari through the National park was great. Saw monkeys, deer,wild boar but alas not the tiger or the leopard but very happy to see what a great park it was for these animals.The Staff were great and had the best meal here.

After having stayed at Tiger Tops in Bardia National Park we had another fantastic experience in the Tharu Lodge in Chitwan. Staff, rooms, meals and safaris were all excellent! Also, the availability of a swimming pool was much appreciated. If you go to celebrate a birthday, Tiger Tops staff arranges amazing surprises if you coordinate with them beforehand.

I ended my trip to Nepal by spending two days at the Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge which on the edge of the Chitwan reserve.  The lodge offers a number of nature activities on the reserve, and I had a really great time on an elephant safari and a jeep safari (I saw a number of rhinoceros, monkeys, deer, wild boar).  The staff is very attentive, and the guides are very knowledgeable about the flora and fauna on the reserve.  The grounds are beautiful, and the food served is terrific.  Overall, an excellent experience, and a nice way to end my trip.

For nearly two decades, I had dreamed of visiting Tiger Tops with their elephant safaris--which we ventured straight upon our arrival! We loved the elephant safari (in buffer zone), jeep safari (in core zone), river safari with ox cart ride, and even the Vulture Restaurant conservation project in Tharu Village! The kids enjoyed most feeding and bathing the elephants, the swimming pool and playing in the grounds with other traveling kids. I enjoyed sleeping in the tents (which are much cozier, quieter and private than rooms in the main lodge), bird watching, and seeing the rhinos. Staff were so friendly and knowledgable, meals were served by candlelight in the gardens, and the cultural dance was entertaining. We look forward visiting Tiger Tops again, although we might try their sister lodge at Bardia NP. Consider entering Tharu Lodge by way of river raft expedition!

Outdated rooms, need a good cleanup and to be refreshed.The meals and the service were good.The knowldge of the tour guide and the driver for the jeep safari were outstanding. They could spot an animal (rhino, monkey, deers, wildboard, etc...) very easely.

Cons:This is not an elephant sanctuary! Elephants are brought here from India or born here and DOMESTICATED (ie broken in) for tourist purposes including the “walking with elephants” and feeding activities. Wild elephants would not tolerate these interactions with humans. We were also shocked to see elephants CHAINED UP within the conservation park. We were told that these elephants are used by the park anti-poaching soldiers to deter other wild animals like tigers when they go on patrol. It’s heartbreaking to see. Pros: The lodge staff is wonderful and professional, the food delicious and plentiful - and catering very well to vegetarians - and the other activities like river canoeing and wildlife safari were excellent. And the lodge itself is idyllic. I recommend for the lodge to close the elephant activities and focus on the wonderful natural environment within the conservation park. We were thrilled to see rhinos, crocs, deer and peacocks.

I had a truly wonderful stay! The staff were warm and friendly and our guide on the safaris communicated loads about the wildlife of the area. I was lucky enough to see a tiger, several rhinos, monkeys and deer. I shall definitely be back to try to see a sloth bear!I spent a lot of time with the elephants and it was heart-warming to see how well taken care of they are. The elephant trek and elephant sandwich making (elephant camp visit) is an absolute must! I also really enjoyed seeing the organic farm where food is grown for the lodge. I had such a great time and I can't wait to go again!

This is the fourth time we’ve visited Tharu Lodge and we just love it. The staff are very helpful but unobtrusive and the food and service is second to none! It’s a ‘get-away-from-it-all’ place so you won’t find tv or air con but we didn’t miss either as there’s so much to do. The traditional construction of the rooms in a longhouse means they stay pretty cool.

I naver had before this kind of service in my life we are staying one night with family the staff are local varey help full food was delicious local food and very fresh organic from one farmhouse nice swming pool thank you so much all of you see you soon

Our stay with Tiger tops at chitwan was fine and mostly impressed by the passionate and knowledgable guides for our safaris and elephant walk. Head naturalist Dan worked 50 years for tiger tops and he knows everything here at chitwan national park. Even though we were not so lucky this time for seeing closely a rhino or tiger but we have seen many other wildlife in a close distance. The property itself is nice and can be nicer if weather is warm since you can then use the pool area. Apart from safaris, the chain free elephants here are happy and walking with them definitely is more meaningful than riding on them. I hope more players in the tourism industry will follow them and say no elephant safaris.I will definitely come back to tiger tops but i think there is still  room for improvement on the communication from its reservation team in kathmandu since they were not very responsive and provided wrong information during the booking process( i had to involve its MD to make sure my emails and requests were acknowledged)and when we tried to settle the payment at the property the amount on the bill was not correct too.

I stayed with my son in Tharu Lodge . We loved every minute of our stay here . The staff were so helpful and friendly . Lunch was served for us despite our late arrival. All the food excellent and plentiful.We did all the activities on offer starting with the Sundowner by the river with the elephants.. magical .We did a jeep safari where we encountered “Valentino”a local huge Wild elephant , a leopard 🐆, a sloth bear as well countless birds, monkeys and deer . It was a holiday to be treasured . Can highly recommend.

Sometimes you visit places where everything just seems to fall into place. Tiger Tops is one such place. Everything works so well into the smallest details, that the totality is just a smooth wonderful experience. Park guides, cooks, waiters, staff and all work together to make sure you can live your dreams. I visited here very long time ago, and it’s still top rate. Apart from the amazing nature experience I was so impressed by the food quality. I’m not a vegetarian, but this was the first time that I really enjoyed the remarkably good and tasty veggies. And the rest of the food was equally impressive. We will for sure return.

Just visited Tiger Tops Tharu for the second time (first visited in 2016) and again it didn't disappoint! This place is a must see!!Walking with the elephants is a magical experience, and the jeep safari and river safari were also outstanding. Every outing was accompanied by very knowledgeable guides who clearly love what they do and care deeply about the animals and nature around them.The staff in general are really what sets Tiger Tops apart. The team definetly like what they do and always were ready to help with a smile. Many have worked there for 20+ years and are even the second and third generations in their family to do so, so their knowledge and commitment to the lodge, guests and park are authentic and inspiring.  We also had a great time chatting with Kristjan and Jack, the brothers who own the place, who also shared their long family history with the lodge and their passion for conservation. All in all the trip was perfect.  This really is a special place you should not miss.

Thank you, Tiger Tops, for a wonderful trip. We were a party of 23, and Tiger Tops was wonderful in accommodating all us, from beginning to end. Starting with our contact with Reshmi from the US, everything was arranged, from our pickup to drop off at Kathmandu. She managed to keep us together. Everything was smoothly ran: our luggages were picked up in Kathmandu and delivered to our tents/rooms without us lifting a finger; the food was fabulously prepared (even prepared box lunches for our day tour to Lumbini); and a Jeep was readily available to transport my elderly parents without having to request. And everyone at Tiger Tops seemed happy to be there, always greeting us with a smile!

I cannot speak highly enough of my overall experience whilst staying in Tiger Tops' Elephant Camp in Tharu, Chitwan NP. My tent and the spacious ensuite was devine. The food was amazing. The Manager DB and staff were very attentive, kind, friendly and respectful. Their choice to care for elephants and the environment, rather than other organisations in the park that still offer elephant rides, is admirable and the main reason I chose Tiger Tops.
