The choice of jungle experiences was great, and my favourite time was walking with the elephants and then watching them bathe in the river and the end of each day. 4 nights was not enough and I would love to go back some day. I have had several different wildlife experiences in different regions of Borneo and Africa. I was very pleasantly surprised with my Nepal experience here. Would highly recommend this to anyone, along with Tiger Tops' lodge at Bardia National Park as well. It was very sad to leave. Leisa - Brisbane, Australia

Our recent brief stay at Tiger Tops and visit to Chitwan National Park truly was a once in a lifetime trip. We had a fantastic time, so many experiences and adventures. The staff were excellent, from Reshmi in the office who arranged the details of our booking including flight, to each person we met in Chitwan; with such attention to detail throughout out stay, from drinks in the cooler on the journey from the airport, to being handed refreshing face cloths whenever we arrived back at the lodge.Each trip was so well organised, the guides and team so helpful. We were fortunate to see many animals and birds, as well as a turtle and freshwater crocodiles. Only tiger prints, alas, but even our guide was excited as we spotted two endangered wild dogs! A highlight was definitely walking with the elephants to the river to watch them bathe and play, with a glass of wine in hand as the sun set...!The lodge is beautifully furnished, again with great attention to detail, and the meals were lovely.Thank you to the whole team for enabling us to have a true once-in-a-lifetime visit to this stunning part of the world.

The Tiger Tops Thuru Lodge was a very comfortable place to stay with excellent service. I stayed in one of the tents of which allowed me to wake up to the view of their beautiful elephants. Their service to their customers was impeccable, leaving the guests to want for nothing. The food was very good too and alot of it. You definitely have to do the "Sundowner" which is a walk with the elephants down to the river. That memory will last you a lifetime if you love elephants. We also did the jeep Safari which was very good. We saw 4 Rhinos, monkeys, crocodile and dear. Highly recommend. I am very happy with my trip.

Each time I stay at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge I appreciate it more. Since their elephants have gone chain-free I have seen a progressive improvement in elephant health and mahout care. It was not bad before but now the care and facilities for elephants far exceeds anything you'll experience anywhere in Nepal. I am honored to return each year with Elephant Aid International's Foot Trimming Workshop. Together we can make a better life for Nepal's hard working captive-held elephants. Thank you staff and management of Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge!

Tharu Lodge should not be open in December without clients being made aware of the ever-present morning mist that makes wildlife-viewing impossible. We were advised that there was no point venturing out till 9am and the mist didn’t clear till after midday. That eliminated the chance of us seeing any birdlife and a rhino we sighted across the river was barely visible.A total disaster at Chitwan was only averted by our guide doing his utmost (and succeeding) in getting us close to a rhino down by Narayani River. The manager does a great job from a customer service perspective. The staff are all very friendly and obliging. The lodge catered well for my wife’s onion intolerance.This weather pattern (mist every day) has been constant for the last ten yearsThe safari vehicles are unreliable. When our driver switched off the engine, it would not start until he got out, went under the vehicle and hit something (I assume the jammed starter motor). That meant we could not follow the few animals we saw or reposition the vehicle for a better photography angle. We were also delayed when we were finally being taken into the park itself. Both our vehicle and canoe had been redeployed to rescue another group whose vehicle had broken down.Maintenance in the rooms is also poor, with the staff unable to sort out a dripping tap. The rooms at Chitwan (we had no.7) are ghastly. You can hear every word spoken by guests in the rooms either side, not to mention the snoring and electronic interruptions. The bathroom is tiny and scruffy and the toilet doesn’t flush properly.The bed linen was very damp and we had to ask for hot water bottles. The bed had been equally damp in Karnali, but at least they had the sense to provide hot water bottles without being asked.The owners responded very promptly and positively when we pointed out all, these issues, but I do hope they will warn potential guests about the weather.

After trekking in the Himalayas my boyfriend and I stayed at the Tharu Lodge to celebrate my birthday in a calm and relaxing but nevertheless adventurous surrounding.We chose the Tharu Lodge because the elephants are very well treated there and you can‘t do elephant rides. They don‘t have chains or anything and every elephant lives together with her best elephant friend. You can even prepare elephant sandwiches which is a lot of fun.Everything from booking, to the warm welcome, the tent we stayed in, the food, the staff and the jungle activities especially with the elephants and the jeep safari were amazing!I had one of the best birthdays there, going to the river with the elephants and afterwards having a nice dinner outside. Thank you Tiger Tops for organizing a birthday I will never forget.Even as a vegan there were many options available and the food always tasted fresh and original.The activities that you can do there are all great and the guides are nice and funny, well experienced and can answer all your questions. The area where the Tharu Lodge is located has exceeded our expectations. The tents are almost hidden in the Jungle and when it gets dark you can hear the chirps. The tent itself is really comfortable with a really nice bathroom attached.We can‘t recommend the Tharu Lodge enough. The money you spend is more than worth it! Thank you so much Tiger Tops!

This trip was fantastic and with the help of the good people at Tiger Top it excited all my expectations and more. We all (a group of 12 elegant ladies from Iceland) felt very safe but in the same time thrilled with the pure spirit and nature Nepal has to offer! Would definitely use their services again.

How wonderful it is to be able to walk with the elephant down to the river and follow them to the woods. Their safari trip to the jungle was just wonderful. But the highlight of the trip was the the hospitality of the staff servicing us all along with a smile on their face.  We went there ,12 woman from iceland, planned by Reshmi Parajuli from the tiger tops travel agency. And from the behalf of 12 of us thank you for a truly wonderful time.

My partner and I spent four days at Tiger Tops Elephant Camp. From the moment they picked us up at the airport (and I would recommend everyone fly in) it felt like being welcomed home after a long absence. The staff were consistently warm and attentive. Every meal was splendid and I know they are very intentional about trying to accommodate dietary needs, which is a unique offering in this region. They maintain a garden! The lodge is styled in a way that allows guests to come together to engage in rich conversation with other guests, but we also had plenty of time to relax on our own and enjoy the absolute silence (minus jungle noises). I can't begin to articulate the time you spend with elephants. Each exchange was so intimate and the staff work hard to incorporate you into every aspect of the elephants day. These being are SO well taken care of!

Had an absolutely beautiful stay at Tiger Tops! Luxury and peaceful accommodation, very friendly staff, delicious meals and adventurous safari trips. We really recommend this place!Lots of love Mark & Charlie

The trip advisor box does not have enough space for me to write the many wonderful things about Tiger Tops Elephant Camp!!! We arrived shortly after the season started and were treated like royalty!  The staff at Tiger Tops are so accommodating and make you feel like you are at home in their world.  The way they have the program set up to teach you about elephants is the closest you can get to being in the "true wild" with elephants while not fully disturbing their space.  We learned so many things about elephants along with true jungle plants and animals.  I wanted to stay longer and longer! Sambu is an amazing GUIDE, NATURALIST & TEACHER! All of the staff at Elephant Camp deserve the best recommendation there is! Everyone is professional and KIND! We enjoyed every meal, walk, lesson, sundowner, grass cutting, feeding & meeting everyone! The mahouts are amazing men who care for these majestic creatures around the clock.  And if you are worried about being in the middle of the jungle with food you are foreign too... NO WORRIES! They serve a 10 Star meal at every meal! Catering to your food allergies & preferences.  I can not say enough AMAZING things about Elephant Camp! My HEART is forever stamped! xx

We had an amazing time in Tiger Tops. Since our arrival at the airport, when they picked us up there. The reception was great! All the staffs were very kind to us! We took the complete package with the safaris included and we not regret! The safaris were amazing and the guides are very good!!! The walking safari with the elephants was incredible! We were so close to the rhinos!!!! The food was delicious!!! And the accommodation very comfortable and beautiful. We hope we can come back soon!!!

Tiger Tops it's the place you want to go to rest and enjoy nature. It's away from the chaos of Katmandu, deep in beautiful rural Nepal. The Lodge is well equipped, plastic free, and all eco-friendly. Staff is kind, professional and helpful.Special mention to our naturalist guide Sambu, who accompanied us for two days safari trips and walks in the jungle, showing us and telling us everthing about animals, plants and Nepali traditions.1 hour trip from Bharatpur.dont' forget to visit the TIny Shop in front of the lodge. A Wonderful family runs it and you can buy nice souvenirs.

I had booked and planned this trip in advance and had been speaking with Reshmi via email. Unfortunately, I got sick from trekking to Everest Base Camp. Reshmi was so helpful and understanding during the whole process and a massive credit to the establishment. Thank you Reshmi, I am really hoping to be back!!

Please go and visit this excellent and exceptional lodge on the edge of Chitwan National Park. This is the first and only lodge to treat elephants ethically in the area. So many activities to choose from.... Sundowner with the elephants is a “must do” watching them bathe, play with joy in the river. The food, staff , and accommodations are 1st class ♥️

Definitely worth staying at Tiger Tops. It is relaxing, beautiful & like stepping Back into bygone eras. The elephants are such an experience. To be so close to such a huge animal is certainly a memory I will cherish. To touch them is quite unlike anything I have ever felt. We didn’t see so much on the jungle safari but it was still fun watching the monkeys following us for a better look in the tree tops. The food was lovely. If you have the opportunity to go then don’t hesitate to book.

We spent 3 nights at Tiger Tops and loved the entire experience!   First the property is massive so it never feels overcrowded.   We enjoyed our afternoons relaxing at the pool. Our room was large and very clean.  And the food was very good. Only feedback is that would have liked more local cuisine vs. western.   Second the staff was great from the lodge to the guides.  A special shout-out to Leaha, guest manager, as she was fantastic!!  Really brought the different groups together.   Also the passion for conservation of the guides/team is infectious -- they really believe in what they are doing.   And this importantly was reflected in the activities we did.  They do not allow riding of the elephants and shockingly they are the only lodge in the park that believes in this.  Instead of riding the elephants we spent the day working with the elephants, cutting grass, making elephant sandwiches and feeding them and finally bathing them in the river at sunset.   A magical day!  Also enjoyed the elephant walk as spotted 6 rhinos on foot?!?!   If you are heading to Chitwan national park, this is a must stay!!

its amazing seeing animals specially wild animals. this camp was for elephant and whoelse wouldnt go there. elephants were trained and tamed here. there was small baby elephant named nani is so cute . i wish i had that baby elephant

Beautiful Tharu style accommodation with deluxe tents. Truely a glamping experience, with proper beds in the tents. At night there is an electric blanket that is turned on which is between the mattress and mattress sheet so you get into a warm toasty bed even in the winter! You have your own bathroom directly behind the tent. The staff are so helpful and friendly and the food is wonderful.The jungle experiences with my guide were fantastic, and the elephants seemed very happy and well cared for.

My husband and I spent 7 days with the Tiger Tops crew, some of which was spent at Elephant camp and then we had two amazing nights camping out on the Narayani River. The whole experience was exceptional, the staff and service was unlike anywhere else, the food was delicious, being with the Elephants was incredible! We had some beautiful close encounters with Rhino and our Jungle guide Bhim was so wonderful! I literally cried the day we left, it felt like a home away from home. Thank you and we will be back for sure. Much love Greg and Bec’s

We spent 3 nights at Tiger Tops at the end of our vacation.  We were supposed to spend 2 nights, but it was so amazing we spent 3.   We stayed in the tents outside of the gate, past the elephants.    The bed was super comfortable.  It was nice and quiet.   It was perfect. To answer a few questions I’ve seen people post.  Yes there are insects, but at long as you don’t leave your tent door open, they are not in the tent.  Your private washroom, with plumbing and electricity is about 3 steps from the back of your tent.   We had a visit from a large spider in our washroom as there a gaps along the top and bottom.  It didn’t matter, the spider isn’t venomous, it just surprised us.   You are in the wilderness after all :-) Waking from the lodge to the tent was amazing as we got to pass the elephants every morning and evening.  The only bad part about location of tent was we didn’t really have enough time to go back to the tent between activities.   But, we did have enough time to have a beer in the lodge which was always a treat :-)The food... the food was absolutely amazing.  It was there best food I had eaten during my entire vacation excluding Singapore, Taiwan, Bali and Istanbul.   Part of staying an extra day was to eat more.At the end of eat day sitting around the camp fire visiting with other guests was lovely.  We made many new friends. If you didn’t wish to visit you didn’t have to, youbhad options for privacy but meeting people from all over the world and sharing some whiskey was fantastic. The day activities were magical. Walking with the elephants was such a special thing to do, we went out 3 x with them.  We also did the Jeep safari twice.   The Jeep safari isn’t anything like doing it in Kenya where you have animals everywhere, but it was nice.  We did get to see a couple of rhinos and various types of monkeys.    Our main purpose of our visit was to hang out with the elephant, everything else we saw was just a bonus Thank you for an amazing time. I hope to visit again one day!

My partner and I stayed at Tharu Lodge in one of the safari tents in November 2018. We we so thrilled with the entire experience that we have gone to the effort of writing our first trip advisor review. We went to Chitwan with the understanding that we may or may not see any wildlife so Tiger Tops was a good option in the fact that we knew we would be able to spend some time with the asian elephants they have in their elephant camp. This was truly an amazing experience, walking along side them through the jungle as body guards, seeing them swim in the river at sunset - overall incredible, as I said to the owner Christian, you would have to be an idiot not to enjoy!! We were also completely thrilled with the effort the staff went to, in all aspects to ensure we enjoyed our stay and optimised our time to see and do everything. We were fortunate enough to see many rhinos and jungle wildlife and for this we are truly thankful. Another big drawcard for both of us was the community involvement and sustainable way they conduct their business, something more companies across the globe should be doing.  Food was great, tent was great, staff warm, friendly and incredibly knowledgable. We would go back in a heartbeat.

My partner and I stayed here for 1 night 26-27 November and the experience we encountered was phenomenal ! The elephants were extremely well taken care for and the activities they provided were very special. The service from staff were top quality and the environment was well looked after!We only wished we could have stayed longer!!! Some activities we did:making the elephant sandwiches (kuchi)doing a jungle trek with elephants! (no riding services!! which is great!)jeep safari across the river (if you're lucky, you'll see Rhinos and tigers!)overall 10/10!! Thank you Tiger Tops for this wonderful experience!

We stayed three nights at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge in October 2018. We chose them because of their switch from elephant-riding safaris to elephant walks in the jungle. It was great each morning to walk with, watch, and touch these amazing creatures, as well as to watch them frolic in the water with the sundowners at the beach (a must do).The lodge itself is nice, considering you're in the middle of the jungle, and the food and service was outstanding, as was the correspondence before and after our arrival.Tips: -For morning (or any walks), wear gators or thick socks pulled over your shoes, since there are tiny leeches in some of the marshier areas.-A booklet in the room advertised Oxcart Rides, which hopefully is as outdated as some other marketing materials. These rides are oxen pulling tourists on the rural roads, and they don't look kind to the animals (or in line with Tiger Tops' shift in other areas). So confirm if that is a concern for you.-Rooms near the dining areas were a bit loud if groups stay up drinking, but it actually was never really a problem for us. But request rooms further away if you're worried.

It’s difficult to capture the Tiger Tops experience in a few mere words, on so many different levels an incredibly unique experience from the elegance of elephants to warmth of geniue heartfelt hospitality. You sense that Tiger Tops are really leading the way in terms of sustainable nature based tourism with importantly a real connection with the local villagers. There support to the local school typifies this connection. Coming from an Australian national parks background, Jack and his team are to be commended. Brilliant. An outstanding experience.

We are a family of six. Children ages 8-15yearsWe stayed here after our week trekking /Pokhara. It’s an absolute treat staying at TigerTops. There was nothing they could have done better. Staff were outstanding. Our guide was a gem and awesome with the children. We felt we had fair value. I recommend you stay here at the end of your trip.

My partner and I stayed at the Camp for three nights and every moment was amazing. The stand-out highlight was walking through the jungle with elephants from the camp leading the way and following behind. We encountered a rhino on one of these walks and the mahouts skilfully manoeuvred the elephants between us and the rhino. Meaning we could safely stand watching the rhino while it was only interested in the elephants' presence. Other highlights were a boat trip spotting wildlife down the river, passing by the bathing elephants, spending time watching the elephants in their spaces around the camp and talking with the very knowledgeable staff.The camp itself was superb; with very comfortable tents and the most amazing food we ate in Nepal. Lastly, the elephants themselves seemed, at least to my untrained eye, to be living the most wonderful life. They were playful and full of energy, healthy and clearly well loved by all the staff. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this place to anyone and everyone possible.

We've just left Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge after we got married at a beautiful spot on the Narayani river. Tiger Tops helped us realizing our dream. We have stayed with 49 people at this amazing resort for four days and on the last day we got married. The staff was simply amazing. We've learned that there where 98 people working very hard to give all the guests a lifetime experience. The activities where very interesting, beautiful and full of excitement. Walking into the jungle searching for Rhino and Tigers being protected by at least 2 elephants is an unforgettable experience. We really encourage their ethos about wildlife and their decision to no longer ride the elephants (Only the Mahout, or elephant driver, is allowed on the elephant). We really recommend this lodge to anyone looking for an authentic experience with the right amount of luxury.

I visited the lodge a few days with my father. We were really positivley suprised by the way the Tiger Tops lodge handle nature and luxery tourism in a way the two can exsist in a suistainable and carefree manner.  Dispite this wonderful intent we never felt compromised in our enjoyment of the Lodge and the serounding nature. The service is just absoluteley outstanding. It is mainley because of this we could enjoy Nepals nature in the best and guiltfree way I can possible imagine.The lodge offers a wide variety of activities in the nearby National Park. You can walk through the jungle alongside the (happy) elephants like we did for example. The feeling of seeing a wild endangered rhinos whilst you are being protected by an alephant is just something I will never forget. We had a really good time and hope the Lodge wil continue in their ways. If only there were more initiatives like this...

I want to wholeheartedly recommend Tiger Tops and their entire staff. We have used Tiger Tops twice and in both instances they arranged wonderful tours for us, including a stay at beautiful Tharu Lodge In addition, the Tiger Tops staff helped us out of difficulties that were unexpected during both of our trips to Nepal. In 2015 we were in Paro when the earthquake happened. Tiger Tops staff took unbelievable care of us given the tragedy that had occurred, particularly in Kathmandu. And this spring, they helped us navigate the treacherous road from Kathmandu to the Tibet border. We had not realized what a long, hard road it was since the Friendship Bridge border crossing is still closed. Tiger Tops arranged a car, driver and guide for us within a day of us asking for help. Thank you Tiger Tops for a wonderful experience in Nepal and for your wonderful care in time of need!

Our Clients had a Chitwan extension for 3 nights after successful Island Peak climbing in Everest Region. The nature guide at the resort are well experienced, the scenery, Tharu culture and wildlife excursion made the holiday even better.

Stayed for three nights, two at the Tharu Lodge one at elephant camp. This was our second visit to Tiger Tops after seventeen years. I’d have to say the magic is still there. For those who visited before, You will notice some changes in the activities. Nevertheless, they are well thought through, forward thinking in terms of ethical treatment of animals and enjoyable thoroughly. Staffs are amazing and very helpful to your every needs. Stay at the Legendary Tiger Tops, you’ll love it!

Not easy to get to, but Tiger Tops is worth it.  The rooms are spacious and charmingly appointed, the food was excellent and served with the right combination of professionalism/home hospitality. The swimming pool was beautiful and the perfect respite after a day of safari looking for rhinos, monkeys, tigers, elephants and more. The highlight was walking with the elephants to the river, then watching them play in the water while being served 'sundowners' as the sun set over the horizon. Lunch under the trees in the garden, with over 300 species of birds makes you feel you are in another world. We loved it and would have liked to spend more than two nights.Excellent, dedicated owner and staff.

This is a special place. The staff are very attentive and friendly. You get to see elephants as they would behave in the wild. The jungle walks with elephants are interesting. They eat such a lot! You walk through the jungle with them partly for safety, as there are rhino and other creatures. The walk ends at the river and you can watch them in the river having a really good time while you have a cup of tea and watch the sun go down. Do take the Jeep trip in the jungle. We saw rhinos, bison, wild boar many different types of deer. We were very lucky to see a tiger! It is worth taking a trip to the vulture restaurant. It is not as gruesome as it sounds but you can see several different types of vulture. It is an excellent conservation project for vultures and the village. Spend at least two days there to see the elephants and the other activities. It is the future of wild life tourism. The guides are very knowledgeable and seem Tonkin's where the animals are. The place to stay in the national park

Situated right next to Chitwan National Park, this well organised and atmospheric haven is managed by specialists. We stopped over for a few glorious nights hosted by Molly and Mazza who as creating a warm ambience over excellent dinners, provided advice on which tours to take to optimise the wildlife and birdlife. This proved to be extremely valuable guidance. Food mostly veggie but very very tasty.

Everything about our stay was wonderful. The accommodation, the food, the surrounding, the friendly staff. Shambu, the naturalist who took us on safari and walking in the jungle, had absolutely impeccable knowledge and was open to all questions. He has an amazingly keen eye and was able to spot an impressive array of wildlife and birds - even right at the end of our safari: his efforts for maximising our experience were ceaseless. Elephant activities were amazing and I am very happy to have spent the last 3 days at Tiger Tops.

We have just spent 2 nights at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge which is just outside Chitwan National Park. We arrived after a long and arduous drive from Pokhara, owing to a 36km stretch of roadworks the the journey was uncomfortable. With proper advice the time of booking we would have taken a 20 min domestic flight rather than waste hours in a car.On arrival we were warmly greeted by Muzza and the team and introduced to Sanbu as our guide. A walking safari with 2 elephants as our guardians was truly memorable and the memory will last a lifetime.  It was amazing to walk alongside these beautiful creatures and within close proximity to Rhinos. We loved the fact that the ethos at Tiger Tops is eco friendly and they do amazing work with elephants - no chains, no saddles and no tourist circus. On our last day we went to the elephants home and helped to feed them - a wonderful experience.Our days safari in Chitwan was brilliant and we saw 15 rhinos close up as well as other numerous species. The ride across the river in between the buffer zone and park in a long traditional canoe was amazing in the morning mist.We loved the whole Tiger Tops experience and would highly recommend it. The accommodation was in keeping with the setting and philosophy

A chance to stay next to a natural park in cosy cabins with delicious food and be well looked after whilst exploring the wildlife. Molly and Muzz manage the elephant, river and bird "trips" and were quite charming hosts during our short visit.

We visited Tiger Tops in December 2017 as part of the group from the Asia For Animals conference. We appreciated the efforts that the management and staff made for us, preparing vegan meals and working to meet the needs of a large number of people. It was wonderful for us to see the various species of wildlife (monkeys, deer, rhinos, crocodiles) and to walk through the jungle with elephants. All our guides were very nice, friendly and made an effort to give us a memorable experience. It is great that Tiger Tops is moving away from the elephant-riding practices of other tourist businesses and we are glad that their initiative was recognized at the AFA conference. Obviously, the elephants are still in captivity and do not live as they naturally would, but the lodge seems to be trying to make things less oppressive for these animals. All of our group especially enjoyed accompanying the elephants for their bath in the river at sunset. We were also happy to learn that the lodge not only employs local people but contributes to the community by providing food and medical care. Local people put on a nice cultural show for us featuring traditional dances, supported by the lodge dogs (including the charming Bottle) who enthusiastically joined in. We stayed two nights in a tent, which was fun for us. It was a bit damp but the hot water bottles supplied by the lodge helped. We enjoyed our visit very much and will always have good memories of our time there. We believe that all members of our group enjoyed the visit and we would recommend this to anyone with an interest in wildlife.

I came with a large group of three buses, but the guides organised us very well into smaller groups. Jeep safari, boat on the river, elephant jungle walk, sundowners on the beach (with the elephants taking a leisurely bath!), cosing around the fire by the bar and a perfect stay in village homestay cottages - well worth the long bus ride along a somewhat scary road from Kathmandu (yes, there's a flight option, too, not too expensive as I understood it).Jeep safari requires warm clothes if done in the morning. Takes you through the fascinating jungle, my group spotted a rhino with baby :)Boat trip really soothing for the soul, such stillness! Lots of birds and little crocodiles (they only eat fish) and we spotted another rhino with baby! Safety vests are provided, the little boats are surprisingly steady.Elephant walk nice and slow, easy terrain. You walk by the elephants, only the mahouts ride, very good to cease tourist rides which are often not paired with good animal welfare. One wish though: more information about the nature, geography and plants and trees we saw as we walked. Tiger Tops Lodge also very nice, but I chose the cheaper option of staying in the village. The eco-sustainable programme between the village and Tiger Tops is an initiative I agree with very much, and the cottages were well equipped. We got a warm welcome and having the meals with 'our' family and being in the village are experiences of a great bonus, that I presume would be hard to find on your own.

For a return visit to Chitwan, we wanted to focus on the bird life, the river trips, the varied forests and scenery. (Have ridden and visited elephants before. ) The KTM Tiger Tops office made our reservations and arrangements very convenient (Ms. Shrestha delivered our tickets) and offered a reasonable deal. We were the only guests, and felt welcome and indulged- with access to all the facilities and staff assistance, comfortable room (hot water bottles in bed!), convivial central fire and only a bit self-conscious during meals. Loved outdoor lunches. But the very best part was our excellent, thorough, skilled and kind guide. All arrangements were seamless: walk to boat to vehicle to boat to vehicle to canoe, etc. A great pleasure to enjoy as much or as little as we chose without worrying about costs, time limits, others' priorities: a true luxury! Wonderful.(We were surprised to find non-Nepali and non-Nepali speaking hosts. Really? in 2017?

My family and I visited Tiger Tops after the AFA Conference.  It was wonderful to witness how well cared for the Elephants were and the extent the Lodge has gone to ensure their humane care by discontinuing elephant riding and re-designing their enclosures so they have much more space and are not chained at night.  I particularly enjoyed visiting the National Park where my party was privileged to sight a leopard in addition to other animals. Another highlight was the sunset cocktail-party on the river as we watched the Elephants bathe (photo). The staff and tour guides at the lodge were friendly and knowledgeable. The Lodge itself, while not modern was very comfortable and had a notable relaxing and peaceful energy about it. For anyone looking for an ethical ecotourism experience with Elephants and park safaris; I can highly recommend Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge. I will also suggest that you commute from Kathmandu by air rather than bus as the road trip is long and extremely bumpy.

We had the most amazing time at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge! Most of all we enjoyed the elephant walk safari! We managed to get really close to Rhinos with the elephants protecting us. On the Jeep safari we saw a great deal of wild life and Tiger foot prints. The river safari was very tranquil and great to see all the crocs, Rhinos and birds. A special thanks to the most amazing staff! They are highly professional and so so friendly! Most of them working here for over 30 yrs!!! Truly a great Jungle experience.

We had the most wonderful 4 days at Tiger Tops Elephant camp. We saw lots of wild life! The most exciting part was the elephant safari walk where you can enjoy wildlife just meters away with the elephants  protecting you. A special mention goes to the amazing and very professional staff. We had a great time!

I was there 2 weeks back after the AFA Conference for 2 days and the experience was amazing.As an animal communicator, I could speak with a couple of elephants.They don't allow tourists to sit on the backs of the elephants and they really respect themThe place is wonderful and the beds were very comfy with a hot water bottle each night in your bed..it was winter.The rooms are perfect and the food was great and the staff very heartwarming and competent.I will be back for sure and that time for longer!

I just came back from 2 night tent stay at Tiger Tops.  I so wished I could have stayed for a full week.  The 1 hour walk with the elephants, having my feet on the same ground as theirs, just a little bit in front and in back was a very moving experience. Being with the elephants as they forage, selecting choice branches, stripping the leaves, taking pieces with them to munch on the way - was fascinating.  It was also so important and heartwarming to know that at Tiger Tops, their elephants get to live off chains and in a much more natural life,cruelty free and we, as visitors were part of this!   I am so glad that Animals for Asia, choose this as our post conference trip as it added to the meaningfulness of the theme - Changing Human Behavior.   Everything at Tiger Tops is taken into consideration -  the tent bed was super comfortable, the bathroom simply beautiful, the nighttime hot water bottle under the blanket was a welcome surprise, the food is delicious, the nighttime elephant bath and drinks on the beach just incredible, and everyone who worked there is so knowledgable and hospitable in every possible way.  I have only 2 wishes, the first is wanting to return for a longer stay - to take it in with a slower deeper breathe; and the other is for more people to embrace walking with the elephants and thus allowing them a better life.  Will try my best on both wishes!

I recently had the opportunity to visit Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge as part of an excursion for a conference (Animals for Asia) I was attending. This was a wonderful experience. 5 star service in the middle of the jungle. Tiger Tops is home to a special group of elephant ladies that are treated and cared for with the upmost respect! The elephants were very well cared for and housed in a pasture setting in groups. It made for morning walks a big treat to visit the elephants having breakfast. The mahouts had an extraordinary bond with their animals and it was apparent in how the two communicated by the lightest touch and soft vocal commands just like dance partners across a ballroom floor. Tiger Tops is an innovative and progressive entity that is moving forward in providing excellent service for both people and animals. I highly recommend visiting Tiger Tops and walking through the jungle with an elephant and toping off your day with a glass of wine or the Tiger Top punch while watching the elegant elephants bath in the river as the sun is setting. Truly an extraordinary experience! Can't wait to return!

I just spent two days at this amazing place. The staff was incredible, knowledgable, and tons of fun! After spending 5 days in Kathmandu at at the Asia for Animals conference it was so lovely to see these elephants unchained, well cared for, and able to behave like elephants instead of circus animals for people's entertainment. I hope more places follow Tiger Tops philosophy and discontinue rides and let the animals have freedom. I also LOVED the food, and every event, from the safari to the happy hour watching elephants swim in the river was magical.

I recently attended Tiger Tops as part of the field trip after a conference (Animals For Asia). I was so interested to spend time talking with the managers about the transition to more ethical ways of meeting tourist demand to be with elephants that also doesn't drive the capture of more wild elephants. The elephants currently are in chain free corrals, which is great to see. It is still a far cry from the life of a wild elephant but for these elephants is a defnite improvement and gives them some autonomy. The tourists are not allowed to touch them, which I feel makes the experience of being close to them much more special as they are treated as sentient beings and not as props. The tourists no longer ride them, but can accompany them on elephant walks, which again is a much more impactful and respectful way of interacting with the elephants. The mahouts ride the elephants, although without ankuses, this could also be phased out but from a welfare point of view one rider is probably less compromising than the restrictions on their behavioural repertoire from confinement. The managers were happy to talk about these things when asked but I feel could celebrate them, not just when prompted. The transition is to be proud of and a business niche - leading the way in more ethical tourist experiences. I look forward to keeping in touch with the development of the new business model and elephant management practices. Finally, thanks to all the staff, who were a fountain of knowledge and very keen to share it. Scored a tiny bit less than maximum as would like to see the new ethics in place for longer before can gain that score.

The folk working with the elephants have made huge positive changes in the way that they are worked and trained. As a tourist it is crucial that we choose places like this that have made an effort to change, please support them.

Tiger Tops takes it to a whole new level for service including hot water bottles in the evening to cuddle with. Staff is exceptional, food is good and the gardens lovely. The Lodge should also be commended for taking an ethical approach to the elephants as  it no longer allows Elephant rides but provides an opportunity to spend time with the elephants as well as lean about them. Nepal is not Africa sir do not expect to see the same diversity of animals as one would there. Overall a good experience.

So loved our 3 days here! Didn’t know what to expect but we loved it. Kind of an eco lodge with an ethical approach to supporting the local community. The facilities were great and we loved the lodge style rooms . Lunch and dinner were included and they even baked us a cake to celebrate an anniversary which was so kind.Loads of nature walks treks boat trips etc included. It was wonderful. Our guide Sam was a real star and showed us great wildlife - sadly no tigers but baby rhinos and lots of other animals. We will remember our stay here for the rest of our lives - it was amazing!!

Elegantly rustic, peaceful, 5+ Star Service from care of room, meal staff, kitchen staff, naturalists and management helping with travel arrangements. Rooms were comfortable and clean with plenty of hot water and lots of provided drinking water. All day Jeep Safari and sundowner wooden boat safari were comfortable with amazing wildlife sightings. Naturalists were knowledgeable, and the ethical treatment of the elephants was a clear priority.

Built in 1980, a family run and privately owned elephants.  12 hectares of land with 12 elephants and organic farm.  The lodge opens a medical clinic once a month and fund the Tiger Top Swissair School for disadvantaged  kids in need. At school the children receive 2 meals a day, uniforms and supplies for free.  Parents are encouraged to work in the organic garden to grow vegies.  It gives them a sense of involvement and a new skill to use at home.The lodge is committed sustainable travel and responsible tourism.  They use solar to help reduce energy.  Locals are employed.Rooms.  Large with own shower and toilet. Ceiling fans. Drinking water, soap, shampoo & condition supplied.Food.  Breakfast, lunch & dinner was included & very nice with different variety changing over the 3 nights we were there.  Dining staff spoke English and were happy to have a chat.Pool, tennis and badminton available.Activities - bike riding, bird watching, elephant encounters, elephant jungle walk, river walk with elephant swim, fisherman village visit, jeep safari, sunset walks.  Plenty to keep you busy.  You can also do a day trip to Lumbini Buddha's birthplace. US$60 ea.Free wifi in dining room.We were collected/returned to the airport.There is also a tented camp available.  The tents were being erected again after the monsoon.  We arrived 6 Sept, so they  were just coming out of summer and were the first to stay for the season.  Naturalist was very knowledgeable.  Manager was very friendly and worked with us as to what we would like to do.We were advised that Feb/March are the best viewing for wildlife as the grass is quite as high.If going on a jeep safari I would suggest you to take a cushion from the dining room for extra padding for the long drive.  We did some one horned rhinos.

This camp is adjacent to the tharu lodge. This family owned lodge has pioneered chain free elephants and also do not have tourists ride them. Instead enjoy a walk in the jungle with them browsing in content. Great comfortable tents and lovely food. Fantastic choice for naturalists and conservationists and all of the Safari activities available

We chose TT for the approach to the care of the elephants and were not disappointed. The team here are dedicated to moving forward with conservation and welfare of local species including doing a major neutering and care program for the village and street dogs. This is the only Chitwan lodge that does not chain or have tourist rides on the elephants. Don't worry the guests have a fantastic time too with very comfortable rooms, unique activities, loads to see and talented guides and other staff. Walk in the forest with contented elephants, magical. Float down the river seeing birds. Driving in vintage landys a bonus. Food wonderful. Come stay here for an unforgettable experience

Environmentally friendly lodges with great services. Outstanding meals. The naturalists gave me educational information on rhinos, tigers, and many different wild animals. Immerse yourself in the wonderful tropical jungle and see wild animals right in front of you. Be prepared to fend off the mosquitoes (long sleeve shirts and long pants with a lot of lemon eucalyptus oil)

My wife and I, along with 5 kids, stayed at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge during monsoon season this summer.  We knew it would be hot and humid, and that the national park was closed, but we hoped to catch glimpses of wildlife along the navigable border-zone managed by Tharu locals.  We stayed at the Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge in late July 2017 and were extremely pleased.  There were no other guests, so the entire staff made sure our stay was great.  We occupied 3 rooms on the west side of the encampment.  The excursions were adventurous.  We same mulitple rhinocera (?), a couple of gharial crocodiles, numerous birds, a jungle cat that walked right up to our jeep, and of course our elephant guides.The kids learned to make elephant sandwiches, and we enjoyed a tour of the organic farm along with a sunset over the Narayani River.  The food here was outstanding, the water was as safe as they claimed, and nothing there caused any sickness in the entire group of 7.  We did steer a bit clear of leafy greens in monsoon season, but became more and more daring during our stay as our health was great.B.C. and Gyan were our main contacts during the stay.  Both of them, along with the entire staff, made sure we were comfortable, happy, and entertained.  I could not have been more pleased with this part of our trip.

Closest to river front with terrase for best view of sunrise and sunset ower the forrest and national park. Exiting safaries, nice barbecue, exotic room and cool atmosphere, do to manager and great  employes!!! Peace full and mystic morning mist with tigers and rihnos at the waterfront! :-)

This was our second visit to the Tharu Village. We were so impressed the first time that we wanted to bring our visitors to see for themselves the magic of this place. After seeing first hand the areas where they keep the elephants, we couldn't stop wondering why aren't other resorts doing the same? You can clearly see how happy and relaxed their elephants are since they are not chained or working anymore. The areas in which they are kept are HUGE and they graze and socialize right before your eyes. The food is amazing too. Some of us had dietary restrictions which was not an issue at all. The chef really knows what and how to cook. Someone in our group was vegan, and she said every meal she had was delicious. We love all the activities they planned for us. The only suggestion we have is that they give more information to their guests about all the social work they do for the community. Like the day we were leaving, we learned that there's a clinic open to the villagers that provides medicines and medical assistance.  They also support a local school and the buffer zone, which would be good to learn more about. You're in for an unforgettable experience. We loved their humane approach!

We stayed three nights at Tharu Lodge. The food and service was as brilliant as ever. (We've been twice before.) We really enjoyed the guided morning walks between two elephants (and mahouts). It was so peaceful as there weren't other people in the forest at that time. We love the long house style of the accommodation and enjoyed the pool.

There is the option to stay in 'posh' tents or rooms. The staff are really attentive and almost all get the balance right. The pool is fine and there are loungers but they could be more comfortable. The food is delicious although I was a bit surprised to be served European food in the evening. There are lots of opportunities to see wildlife.For the price it seems strange that there are no massages / treatments available.

From Kathmandu l took a minibus ride down to the Terail. Driving time to the Tharu Lodge was about 5 hours due to traffic and road conditions. I had a reservation for a room, so I was warmly welcomed. No check-in was needed.  The personell informed me of the day plan and activities soon after.I liked my room right from the beginning as it had all necessary items and was decorated in the simple local lodge style. The bathroom was very clean and comfortable. Shower with warm water worked fine. Toilet european style.There were enough plugs to load my electronic devices. Power cuts during the day are normal.Breakfast, lunch and dinner l either had in the main building or in the garden, depending on the temperature. Food is tasty and generous. Tea and water is complimentary. Drinks you get at the bar there.A swim in the pool or just hanging around and reading a book or check emails is easy. WiFi works when power is available in the main building and garden.Activities: I walked over to see the newly built elephant camp and watched the animals in the new corals walking around free. I took an early morning walk with the elephants and later on I could see them taking a bath in the river nearby. My photos are just great. And a little boat ride on the river is a good activity.Took a jungle ride on a Landrover jeep and saw various animals like rhinos, spotted deer, wild boar, birds, monkeys. For a tiger sighting one should do more efforts early morning and later in the day but it is well possible to see one.After check out I was driven to the airport of Chitwan and flew on Yeti Airlines back to Kathmandu to avoid the long drive uphill.

Tiger Tops is a wonderful place to stay.  The staff could not be more welcoming and helpful, and the accommodation is beautiful.  The price includes full board (the food is excellent) and a choice of two activities each day - ranging from spending time with elephants to safari - whether by boat, river, or elephant.  Tharu lodge is located just outside Chitwan national park - approximately a 5 min jeep drive, then a peaceful 10 min row across the river (great for spotting crocodiles!) to the park itself.  We did two jeep, one river, and one walking safari, and saw a fabulous array of animals and birds - including a very close encounter with a curious rhino.  No tigers this time sadly, but plenty of tiger paw prints!  The guides are extremely knowledgeable about all flora and fauna - most have been with Tiger Tops for 10+ years, so know the Park inside out.  The rooms at the lodge are quiet and beautiful, and there is a wonderful swimming pool in which to cool off after a walk in the park.  Nothing was too much trouble for the staff: when we changed our minds about our transport back to Kathmandu, they drove into town for us, booked our flight tickets, and successfully delivered us to check-in with no hassle at all for us.  A wonderful way to unwind at the end of our trip to Nepal.

We had a memorable 3 day stay in the tented camp with the elephants. Everything was well organised, the staff were truly attentive, friendly, and knowledgeable.   The camping  was proper glamping with real en suite toilets and showers and proper beds.   The pool and lodge were a great place to relax with delicious cocktails.   The food was copious and tasty.  We were able to choose from many activities, and tailor them to our own requirements each day.   This included lots of time with the elephants and an exciting jungle safari as well as other things.  The work to enlighten people about the proper care of the elephants is marvelous and very informative.

A different experience. My boss and I stayed in a tent (but with amenities - splendid bathroom.) We got to do all the activities there and interact with the locals and their neighborhood: Rode the elephant thru the jungle, Looked for rhinos and tigers in the woods in a safari 4x4, got to feed the elephants, watched and participated in tharu traditional dances and songs. buffet dinner beneath  the trees. I could go on and on and on. A Very wonderful experience!

Our experience at Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge was beyond expectations.  DB Chaudhary, the manager, did all he could to meet our special requests.  Mr. Shambu, our guide is as learned and educated about the native plants and animals to the extent he even knows the Latin names.  But most of all, it was a great combination between relaxing and going on safaris in the Chitwan National Jungle and down the river.  We were treated by all the staff like Rajas!  The food is also organic with exceptional taste.

We spent two nights in the tented camp. At arrivel, staff was ready with damp cloths and cold drinks for cleaning throat and face after the journey. All food served was delicious and the staff seemed happy, always smiling and serviceminded. The tent was fantastic - never experienced anything like it! It even came with a luxurious private bath room. The experience is made to cater for your every need, even a thermo with cold water was available in the tent along with fan and even hangers for your clothes (which I have never expected to see in a tent). The pool area is really nice and we had a fun day riding elephants and watching them bath in the river. All in all - this is luxurious as well as giving an authentic feeling of living in the jungle.

My wife, my 13 month old son and I stayed 2 nights here in November 2014. We had the most relaxing time here. The rooms were clean and every time we came back from a safari, the bed was set and bathroom towels were replaced. The food was the best we had in Nepal. Everything was fresh, perfectly cooked and organic from their own farms. The staff were very attentive without being overbearing.We thoroughly enjoyed the jeep safaris, boat safaris and elephant rides.When we rode the ox-cart, however, the poor animals were over-burdened. The driver would beat the poor animals to force them to move. My wife could not stand and refused to continue this ride and all the guests agreed to not continue. It was a good decision, as one of the oxen was actually bleeding from the nose because the tether pulled too hard while it was trying to walk.Another thing that bothered us was the mosquitos that would bite you even in the day time. Our 13 month old son was bitten a couple of times, and 2 days later he had high fever and needed to be taken to the doctor. Not much testing was done and he recovered on his own, but we were worried that it was probably a dengue fever.Overall, we felt that our experience there was very memorable and would go back again in the future.

Tiger Tops was a lovely place to stay, the service was great and we had a wonderful local guide. The only way to get to Chitwan National Park is via boat, which is a fun experience, as you are poled across the river. This is a very different experience from India, where you are never allowed out of your vehicle, at Chitwan we walked around the park and witnessed it in a different way. We also went on a boat ride downriver and had the opportunity to visit the "vulture restaurant" where they "feed" the vultures in an attempt to restore their diminished populations. Lots of chances to view rhinos as well.

This jungle loving offers a perfect ecotourist experience in Chitwan.  The elephant and jeep safaris were wonderful fun and the lodge was very nice despite the scarcity of hot water.  The addition of electric blankets made sleeping easy and the service was superb.

What did we expect in the jungle?  The accommodation is fairly elementary. Rooms are basic with no hot water in the morning but only in the evening. No space in the shower room for toiletries. A few mice have even been spotted too!Food gets obviously recycled. But the elephant safaris and bathing are marvellous and the nature guides informative and very knowledgable. Overall put up with the rusticity for the enjoyment of nature. No Tigers had been seen for 6 months but the black rhinos compensated.

We stayed three nights and even though we suffered from 36 hours of rain and 24 hours of thunderstorms, the staff were great and managed to rearrange everyones schedule so nothing got missed out. And they lit the fire in the main lodge room.We arrived by car, after another couple of hours drive over worse roads than before (in places) to arrive at Tiger Tops River Lodge. Now it's starting to rain and hasn't stopped for a couple of hours - but it's still warm. Quick bite for lunch and unpack - laundry facilities available, but they won't touch your socks or underwear. We didn't fancy ox carts or elephants in the rain, so it's time to catch up on things on the communal building wifi. Tina met a Jungle Shrew in the loo this evening. It was difficult to know who was most surprised but Tina won the competition for highest shriek in the forest that night.  It wasn't there when we got back from dinner as a man popped around with a stick to encourage it to leave. It started to rain as we arrived and it's still raining 24 hours later. It was thunderstorms and lightning all night and torrential downpour so the trips for the day are off - so we just did a bus trip around the area as walking anywhere was out of the question.  The roof leaked in places but not enough that you would notice - the weather was worse than monsoon apparently. Plenty of book reading and iPad watching through the day and the promise of a decent weather forecast tomorrow but whatever happens we will be going out for the day as it's our last here. To keep everyone warm, the lodge lit a large bonfire in the centre of the common room, so everyone could fit around it and stay warm and dry. A few more guests arrived through the day, looking ominously at the sky and being reassured that the weather will break. Whatever happens, we are going out.Local guide was SambuGuest liaison were Eva and Gabriel All three were brilliant.So, up again at 0545 for a cup of tea before walking to the start point of the elephant jungle walk.  Thats the nice thing about this lodge - you don;t have to get in a coach to do anything. You get on the elephant from a high platform which the elephant reverses up to and you then sit in the wooden seats facing sideways with your feet on boards, as you go along. It takes a while to get used to, and once you just go with the rocking motion it's fine. We spent a couple of hours going through the jungle, crossing several rivers and saw a rhinoceros and a deer. The elephants take you back to the starting point to dismount. It's then a late breakfast before setting out on the washing of the elephants in the river. You walk through one of the villages to the river where three elephants were waiting and then their Mahout took them into the river and made them lie down. You could then get into the river, up to your waist if you liked, and give then a washing and rubbing by hand across their backs and heads. Once that was done, it's back to the lodge in muddy feet, for a shower and more tea, followed by lunch in the garden, now that things have dried out. By now, the centre fire in the main room is out and cleaned away.In the afternoon, we went for the river boating trip, but as the river had been in flood, the ox cart wouldn't have been suitable transport so it's back on board the elephants for another 90 minutes to get to the river. This time, not a lot to see, but we had to get off the elephant without the use of a platform - all good fun. The river ride back in small boats was nice, with only a single crocodile to be seen, but it was quiet due to the river being so high. After getting out on a breakwater, we got back to camp in a small minibus. The evenings entertainment was the local Tharu stick dance which ended with everyone in a circle dancing. The final evening meal was held outside, under the stars, to candlelight. The following morning, it was breakfast and back into the car for the long drive to Pokhara.Great place, great stay and completely relaxing.

We stayed there for only 1/2 days, weekend breakaway from hustling & bustling Kathmandu city, but it was a dream of peaceful and relax. Staff are very friendly and the room, it is nicely cultured room. The area is very huge and greenery and one can rest and have peace of mind. Rest is perfect! Thank you all!
